These findings suggest that greater snow-process complexity may be associated with improved simulation of runoff timing. Finally, we also find that (3) model performance depends more on systematic and balanced representations of key processes than on model complexity alone. These findings suggest that greater snow-process complexity may be associated with improved simulation of runoff timing but not runoff magnitude. By providing a quantitative and process-traceable framework for assessing model complexity, this study helps identify which process representations are most relevant for improving SMR simulations under complex environmental conditions.

title: Reionization bubbles from real-space cross correlations of line intensity maps
summary: We propose a new way to reconstruct the ionized-bubble size distribution during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) through the real-space cross-correlation of 21-cm and star-forming line-intensity maps. Understanding the evolution and timing o
content: We propose a new way to reconstruct the ionized-bubble size distribution during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) through the real-space cross-correlation of 21-cm and star-forming line-intensity maps. Understanding the evolution and timing of the EoR is crucial for both astrophysics and cosmology, and a wealth of information on the first sources can be extracted from the study of ionized bubbles. Nevertheless, directly mapping bubbles is challenging due to the high redshifts involved, possible selection biases, and foregrounds in 21-cm maps. Here, we exploit the real-space cross-correlation ξ21,ν between 21-cm and line-intensity mapping (LIM) signals to reconstruct the evolution of bubble sizes during reionization. For the first time, we show that ξ21,ν (r) departs from a saturation level for each separation r when bubbles of size r begin to form, providing a handle for the onset of bubbles of each radius. Moreover, we demonstrate that ξ21,ν evolves from positive to negative as the EoR progresses, reaching a minimum (i.e. maximum anti-correlation) when bubbles of radius r reach peak abundance. We show that these results are robust to changes in the astrophysical model as well as the timing/topology of reionization. This real-space observable complements usual Fourier-space estimators by capturing the localized nature of bubbles, offering new insights into the sources driving cosmic reionization.

title: Spectra-Scope: a toolkit for automated and interpretable characterization of material properties from spectral data
summary: Spectroscopy is a central pillar of materials characterization, providing useful information on properties like structure, composition, or excited state dynamics of a system. However, many spectroscopic techniques present challenges in the
content: Spectroscopy is a central pillar of materials characterization, providing useful information on properties like structure, composition, or excited state dynamics of a system. However, many spectroscopic techniques present challenges in the development of interpretable, performant, and reliable supervised learning models due to the wide range of possible nonlinear correlations that can exist between the signal and the response variable (target) of interest. Here, we present Spectra-Scope, an open-source AutoML framework for automatic characterization of material properties from spectroscopy data using interpretable machine learning (ML) models. The software is implemented in Python and a no-code web application. It comprises tools for data preprocessing, nonlinear feature extraction, machine learning model training, and feature selection. Users can easily train different types of simple, interpretable ML models on a set of feature transformations quickly and with modest computational resources. In this work, we outline the methods of Spectra-Scope and its effectiveness across diverse datasets, with applications to materials and agricultural spectroscopy data. We show that Spectra-Scope can reproduce performance of comparable models in the literature, and highlight how our emphasis on interpretability can be used to rationalize the behavior of individual models and understand the physical processes behind spectral features.

title: Tuning Cu/diamond interfacial thermal conductance via nitrogen-termination engineering
summary: Cu-diamond composites are recognized as promising high-thermal-conductivity candidates for electronic cooling, offering tunable properties and competitive cost. However, their performance is significantly limited by the poor Cu/diamond inte
content: Cu-diamond composites are recognized as promising high-thermal-conductivity candidates for electronic cooling, offering tunable properties and competitive cost. However, their performance is significantly limited by the poor Cu/diamond interfacial thermal conductance (ITC). Here, we propose a nitrogen-termination strategy to tune the ITC of Cu/diamond interfaces and unravel atomistic mechanisms by which nitride interlayers tailor phonon transport. Based on the MACE machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) framework, we fine-tune the pre-trained MACE-MPA-0 foundation model by incorporating customized C-N-Cu training datasets. Incorporating non-equilibrium molecular dynamics with MLIP-driven lattice dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that anharmonic effects contribute ∼60% to the ITC, and simply introducing N-termination on the diamond surface enhances the ITC by 10% compared to the bare Cu/diamond interface. However, the enhancement of harmonic phonon transmission contributes ∼80% of the ITC improvement. Mode-resolved phonon spectroscopy reveals that the LA phonons with frequencies above 4 THz and wavevectors near the Γ-X and Γ-U directions are selectively modulated by N-termination engineering. Analyses of local vibrational states and interfacial bonding further indicate that the N-termination on diamond tunes the interfacial heat conduction via surficial mass modification and chemical bonding regulation, as evidenced by variations in LDOS overlaps and COHP spectra. These findings open venues for tuning heat transfer across Cu/diamond interfaces via non-metallic modification-which avoids the graphitization issues associated with metallic coatings-and provide novel guidelines for upgrading the phonon-mediated heat transfer in Cu-diamond composites.

title: Physics-informed offline reinforcement learning reduces worst-case fuel risk in maritime routing
summary: International shipping produces approximately 3% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet voyage routing remains dominated by heuristic methods. We present PIER (Physics-Informed, Energy-efficient, Risk-aware routing), an offline reinforceme
content: International shipping produces approximately 3% of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet voyage routing remains dominated by heuristic methods. We present PIER (Physics-Informed, Energy-efficient, Risk-aware routing), an offline reinforcement learning framework that learns fuel-efficient, safety-aware routing policies from physics-calibrated environments grounded in historical vessel tracking data and ocean reanalysis products, requiring no online simulator. Validated on one full year (2023) of AIS data across seven Gulf of Mexico routes (840 episodes per method), PIER reduces mean CO2 emissions by 10% relative to great-circle routing. However, PIER's primary contribution is eliminating catastrophic fuel waste: great-circle routing incurs extreme fuel consumption (>1.5x median) in 4.8% of voyages; PIER reduces this to 0.5%, a 9-fold reduction. Per-voyage fuel variance is 3.5x lower (p<0.001), with bootstrap 95% CI for mean savings [2.9%, 15.7%]. Partial validation against observed AIS vessel behavior confirms consistency with the fastest real transits while exhibiting 23.1x lower variance. Crucially, PIER is forecast-independent: unlike A* path optimization whose wave protection degrades 4.5x under realistic forecast uncertainty, PIER maintains constant performance using only local observations. The framework combines physics-informed state construction, demonstration-augmented offline data, and a decoupled post-hoc safety shield, an architecture that transfers to wildfire evacuation, aircraft trajectory optimization, and autonomous navigation in unmapped terrain.

title: Two-parameter analytical model for paralyzable radiation detectors
summary: Certain radiation detectors are 'paralyzed' with high input count rates. When applied to count rates close to the event discriminator working rate the one-parameter dead time model fails. Here we present a corrected paralyzable detector mod
content: Certain radiation detectors are 'paralyzed' with high input count rates. When applied to count rates close to the event discriminator working rate the one-parameter dead time model fails. Here we present a corrected paralyzable detector model accounting for the event discriminator's finite response time. This two-parameter analytical model, when compared to the experimental data from a commercial x-ray detector, gives an improved description of the input and output count rate relations. Furthermore, it can independently determine the discriminator response time and the pulse shaper dead time, critical parameters for understanding a detector's performance. Finally, this model also provides a post-acquisition pile-up correction that greatly reduces artifacts in high-throughput spectra. In some situations, applying this model to optimize the acquisition and post-acquisition correction allows a user to acquire data an order of magnitude faster without compromising accuracy.

title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
summary: Abstract Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the s
content: Abstract Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense 5 .

title: Scenario-based forecasting of carbon sequestration and oxygen production in urban green spaces using i-Tree forecast: a case study of Sidoarjo, Indonesia
source: Journal of Environmental Health Science and Engineering
summary: Abstract Transportation is the largest CO2 emission contributor in Indoneisa, followed by industries, waste management, and households. The major greenhouse gas has seen carbon offsetting attempts with varying proposals, one of which is by
content: Abstract Transportation is the largest CO2 emission contributor in Indoneisa, followed by industries, waste management, and households. The major greenhouse gas has seen carbon offsetting attempts with varying proposals, one of which is by implementing Green Open Spaces (GOS), acting as ecological buffers, carbon sinks, and oxygen producers. This study evaluates existing greenery at Abhirama Park (urban core) and Apkasi Park (suburban area) in Sidoarjo Regency (East Java, Indonesia), Utilizing tree planting scenarios to assess CO2 sequestration and oxygen production changes. The methodology integrates field base inventories, vegetation density analysis (GIS-based NDVI), microclimate observations, and i-Tree Forecast modelling from three scenarios (existing conditions, instant greening, and gradual greening). Observations ran for two weeks on select days (Monday, Friday, Sunday) at specific times (Morning, Midday, and Evening) to observe diurnal variatons. The results show Abhirama Park having more complex vegetation structure with a higher tree count (159 trees vs 70 trees), greater carbon sequestration capacity (2.14 tons/year to 0.92 tons/year) compared to Apsaka park. Sequestration values reveal extremely limited capacity of carbon offset abilities from both parks for each respective locations, accounting only 1.33% and 0.5% of total emissions. Microclimate analysis observations found the lowest humidity to be during midday, and is inverse with temperature, driven by increased solar radiation and accelerating evapotranspiration (influencing photosynthetic efficiency). Greening scenarios show better carbon sequestration and oxygen production, yet still insufficient to be said meaningful carbon offset of growing vehicle emissions. While both parks contribute to climate resilience and sustainable urban development, their current capacity remains inadequate to balance urban emissions. Enhancing vegetation structure, Increasing tree biomass, and integrating green space planning with emission control strategies are crucial to optimize urban carbon mitigation.

title: A new method to probe conducting filaments in MoS 2 -based memristors
summary: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂), are emerging as promising materials for next-generation electronic devices. They have proved to be serious candidates for integratio
content: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂), are emerging as promising materials for next-generation electronic devices. They have proved to be serious candidates for integration with memristors in non-volatile memory and radio frequency (RF) applications. However, the physical mechanisms behind their resistive switching, particularly the formation and resorption of conducting filaments, remain unclear. In this study, we present a novel mechanical exfoliation technique that selectively removes the top metallic electrode from MoS₂-based memristors by exploiting the weak van der Waals interaction between MoS₂ and the top electrode. This method enables direct and multi-scale characterization of the MoS₂ surface in different states (initial, ON and OFF) using Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) and Raman spectroscopy mapping. To complete this study, cross-sectional Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) was also performed in different conductive states. Our results reveal that the conducting filament is formed by metallic atom migration from the top electrode into the MoS₂ layer. Additionally, we demonstrate that the choice of metallic electrodes (gold vs. nickel) significantly impacts the switching behavior due to differences in adsorption and diffusion energies. This work not only clarifies the filament formation mechanism and introduces a reproducible approach for in-operando characterization but also represents a real progress in the understanding and optimization of 2D material-based memristors.

title: Role of metastable dicationic intermediates in the breakup of CH 4 2 +
summary: We investigate the fragmentation dynamics of methane dication (CH$_4^{2+}$) produced in collisions with 50-MeV C$^{6+}$ ions using the COLTRIMS technique. The method provides complete three-dimensional momentum vectors of the charged fragme
content: We investigate the fragmentation dynamics of methane dication (CH$_4^{2+}$) produced in collisions with 50-MeV C$^{6+}$ ions using the COLTRIMS technique. The method provides complete three-dimensional momentum vectors of the charged fragments, enabling full kinematic reconstruction of the fragmentation process. The dynamics are analyzed using Dalitz plots, Newton diagrams, and the native-frame method to distinguish between concerted and sequential dissociation mechanisms. The data indicate the presence of sequential fragmentation pathways for the CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ CH$_2^+$ + H$^+$ + H, CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ CH$^+$ + H$^+$ + 2H, and CH$_4^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ C$^+$ + H$^+$ + 3H channels, consistent with dissociation via short-lived dicationic intermediates CH$_3^{2+}$, CH$_2^{2+}$, and CH$^{2+}$, respectively. From the Newton-diagram momentum distributions, we estimate half-rotational periods of approximately 180~fs, 71~fs, and 44~fs for the $\mathrm{CH_3^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{CH_2^{2+}}$, and $\mathrm{CH^{2+}}$ intermediates, respectively, providing characteristic lower-limit timescales for their survival prior to fragmentation. The experimental observations are further supported by comparisons with calculated potential-energy curves.

title: Coherent effects in quantum transport models and their classical counterparts
summary: We analyze the transport properties of quasiparticles locally excited at an initial time moment in several exactly solvable quantum models. It is revealed that, in the investigated quantum systems, the time-dependent probability distributio
content: We analyze the transport properties of quasiparticles locally excited at an initial time moment in several exactly solvable quantum models. It is revealed that, in the investigated quantum systems, the time-dependent probability distribution function (PDF) exhibits behavior similar to that of classical continuous-time random walk (CTRW) models, such as L'evy walks or diffusing diffusivity. For initially excited quasiparticles interacting with the same two-dimensional phonon reservoir, the exact quantum PDF reveals a U-shaped profile due to the presence of a strong ballistic component. This ballistic component arises because the absolute value of the quasiparticle velocity is bounded from above, allowing quantum coherence effects—stemming from the interaction with the common reservoir—to play a significant role. The results obtained for the phonon-assisted hopping quantum model are compared with three alternative approaches: (i) a simple tight-binding model, (ii) a model of a heterogeneous ensemble of chains with Gaussian random hopping amplitude, and (iii) a tight-binding model with random time-dependent hopping amplitude. It is found that the PDF of the simple tight-binding model is similar to that of the phonon-assisted hopping model. For the heterogeneous ensemble of chains with a Gaussian distribution of hopping amplitudes, the PDF transforms from bimodal to monomodal via an intermediate trimodal shape as the parameters of the Gaussian distribution are varied. The spread of the PDF is ballistic for the first and the second models mentioned above. For the model with random time-dependent classical hopping amplitude, the PDF of quasiparticle spreading exhibits universal asymptotics with logarithmic corrections and resembles the diffusing diffusivity model, characterized by diffusive spread.

title: MacroTraits: a global trait data and information system for marine benthic ecology
summary: For a long time, biological trait data have been a bottleneck in biodiversity research. Constraints of data unavailability and challenging analytical implementation are still obstacles to the investigation of functional biodiversity pattern
content: For a long time, biological trait data have been a bottleneck in biodiversity research. Constraints of data unavailability and challenging analytical implementation are still obstacles to the investigation of functional biodiversity patterns. This is especially true in marine zoobenthic ecology where the use of biological traits became common much later than in terrestrial and freshwater ecology. Additionally, most of trait-based marine studies have dominantly been conducted in European waters while large gaps remain in other areas of the world. Therefore, this paper offers a framework to fill this gap by providing the most comprehensive zoobenthic trait data compilation at the global scale. Based on more than 8000 references, 1893 species of marine macro- and megazoobenthos are fully documented for life history, dwelling mode, ecosystem function, habitat and biogeography through 41 traits. Next to this compilation, the paper brings clarifications on research directions by means of these data within the dominant paradigms of modern ecology. In particular, the dichotomous expression that contrasts response and effect traits (i.e. fitness components versus ecosystem function) is emphasised. The database is accessible through an R package in the repository https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24318255 (Beauchard and Soetaert, 2026b) and that facilitates data treatment such as trait selection, cross table construction and label handling.

title: Analysis of scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions associated with electricity consumption at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, India
summary: Abstract Climate change and environmental sustainability have emerged as critical global challenges, highlighting the need to quantify and manage greenhouse gas (GHGs) emissions across various sectors, including higher education institution
content: Abstract Climate change and environmental sustainability have emerged as critical global challenges, highlighting the need to quantify and manage greenhouse gas (GHGs) emissions across various sectors, including higher education institutions. Universities consume substantial amounts of electricity to support academic, research, administrative, and residential activities, making electricity-related emissions a significant component of their environmental footprint. This study assesses the carbon footprint associated with electricity consumption at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) Gorakhpur University, Uttar Pradesh, India, with a particular focus on Scope 2 emissions generated from purchased electricity during the period 2019–2024. The assessment was conducted using the Greenhouse Gas (GHGs) Protocol developed by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). Monthly electricity consumption data were obtained from electricity bills provided by the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL), while emission factors were sourced from the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Government of India. Carbon emissions (CEs) were estimated by applying annual emission factors to electricity consumption data. The study also evaluated the contribution of on-campus solar photovoltaic systems in reducing grid electricity dependence and associated emissions. The results revealed pronounced seasonal variations in electricity consumption and CEs, with peak values recorded during the summer months (May–June) due to increased cooling requirements and intensive campus operations. Lower electricity consumption was observed during winter months. A significant decline in usage of electricity and associated emissions occurred during 2020–2021 as a result of COVID-19-related restrictions, whereas a substantial increase was observed during 2023–2024 following the resumption of normal academic and administrative activities. Annual electricity consumption increased from 2,074,160 kWh in 2019 to 3,181,673 kWh in 2024, reflecting growth in the demand of energy in the campus. Solar Energy Generation contributed significantly to reducing net grid electricity consumption and CEs; however, a decline in solar energy production during 2023 increased dependence on grid electricity and resulted in higher emissions. The findings confirm that electricity consumption represents a major source of indirect CEs within university campuses and highlight the critical role of renewable energy in mitigating environmental impacts. Expanding solar photovoltaic capacity, improving energy efficiency, adopting energy-efficient technologies, and promoting energy-conscious behavior among campus stakeholders can substantially reduce institutional carbon footprints. The study demonstrates that integrating renewable energy with effective energy management strategies is essential for sustainable campus development and climate change mitigation. The find

title: Lightning in global chemistry-climate models: a review of parameterizations, evaluations, and future projections
summary: Climate models are our main tool to project how global lightning activity may change in a warmer world. However, the spatial and temporal scales involved in cloud electrification are too small to be explicitly resolved, so lightning is typi
content: Climate models are our main tool to project how global lightning activity may change in a warmer world. However, the spatial and temporal scales involved in cloud electrification are too small to be explicitly resolved, so lightning is typically simulated using empirical relationships with proxy variables such as cloud top height (CTH), convective precipitation, the product of convective available potential energy and precipitation, or upward ice flux. This review summarizes existing global lightning parameterizations, their skill in reproducing observed lightning patterns, and their projected future changes. We identify 19 parameterizations (including some variants) that have been applied in global modelling studies, with CTH – the earliest developed – remaining the most widely used. Most parameterizations predict total lightning, while cloud-to-ground lightning is rarely computed directly. Several parameterizations, including CTH, reproduce observed spatial lightning patterns reasonably well ( r > 0.7), whereas precipitation-based methods perform worse ( r often < 0.6). Most approaches underestimate lightning over central Africa and in mid-to-high latitudes, while overestimating activity over the Amazon and Maritime Continent. They also struggle to capture the observed land–ocean contrast in lightning activity and tend to underestimate temporal variability from diurnal to inter-annual scales. Future projections show large uncertainty, ranging from an 11 % decrease to a 44 % increase in global lightning frequency per degree global warming. The mean across all parameterizations is +5.5 ± 8.7 % K −1 (one value per parameterization), while the mean across all individual projections (which are strongly biased towards CTH) is +7.7 ± 8.3% K −1 . Although there is a broad agreement that lightning activity will increase in high latitudes, the tropical response remains highly uncertain.

title: Single-blind controlled release testing of vehicle- and aircraft-based methane measurement systems at the TADI facility
summary: Accurate methane emission quantification is critical for climate mitigation efforts in the oil and gas industry. This study evaluates the performance of five academic methane measurement systems through single-blind controlled release testi
content: Accurate methane emission quantification is critical for climate mitigation efforts in the oil and gas industry. This study evaluates the performance of five academic methane measurement systems through single-blind controlled release testing at the TotalEnergies Anomaly Detection Initiatives (TADI) facility in France during June and September 2024. Vehicle-based teams from the Technical University of Denmark, Heidelberg University, and a collaborative team from Utrecht University/LSCE/Cyprus Institute/Royal Holloway deployed mobile in situ measurement systems, while aircraft-based solutions from Empa/UZH and FAAM BAe-146 utilized hyperspectral imaging and airborne in situ measurements, respectively. Vehicle-based systems demonstrated strong detection capabilities with true positive rates of 93 %–95 % and minimum detection thresholds below 1 kg CH 4 h −1 . Quantification accuracy varied significantly, with slopes ranging from 0.38 to 1.04 when comparing estimated versus true emission rates. Aircraft systems showed more variable performance due to operational constraints and limited data availability. Post-unblinding analysis revealed critical insights into systematic errors, including background concentration calculation issues and wind measurement limitations. Low wind conditions (< 2 m s −1 ) particularly challenged quantification accuracy across all platforms. These findings highlight the importance of robust validation procedures and high-quality meteorological data for reliable methane emission quantification in real-world applications.

title: Benefits of multi-target and self-supervised LSTM models for water quantity and quality
summary: Deep learning has become a standard tool for streamflow modelling, but its application to water quality remains challenging due to sparse, irregular, and noisy in-situ observations. Yet, water-quality variables are tightly linked to dischar
content: Deep learning has become a standard tool for streamflow modelling, but its application to water quality remains challenging due to sparse, irregular, and noisy in-situ observations. Yet, water-quality variables are tightly linked to discharge and to each other through shared hydrological and biogeochemical controls, suggesting that jointly modelling water quantity and quality may help compensate for limited data availability. In this study, we compare single-target, multi-target, and self-supervised LSTM models for the joint simulation of discharge and six water-quality variables (NO 3 -N, PO 4 -P, DO, DOC, EC, and WT) across 408 German catchments. Our results highlight that extending the baseline LSTM from single-target discharge prediction to jointly predicting discharge and all six water-quality variables does not substantially degrade discharge performance (across all baseline configurations, median KGE ′ = 0.84–0.87) and yields median KGE ′ values between 0.40 (PO 4 -P) and 0.95 (WT) for the water-quality targets. Interestingly, learning discharge as a co-target matches or exceeds the performance of using observed discharge as an additional input for five of the six water-quality variables, with the clearest gain for DOC (ΔKGE ′ = +0.05). This indicates that jointly learning water quantity and quality can be more effective than using discharge as a predictor. A variable-averaged loss function is key to balance the strongly uneven observation densities of discharge and water-quality variables. Building on this multi-target framework, we further explore whether an alternative training strategy based on self-supervised learning can better exploit the incomplete and heterogeneous nature of environmental observations. Our evaluation reveals that the self-supervised LSTM yields a level of predictive skill comparable to the multi-target supervised baseline LSTM under inference conditions restricted to meteorological drivers and when contextual water-quality data is provided. Thus, while matching the baseline's skill, the self-supervised LSTM gains versatility, as a single model can be applied to many different combinations of available input data without retraining. Besides showcasing the strong performance of LSTMs in water-quality simulations with sparse and irregular data, our results demonstrate that multi-target learning provides an effective framework for coupled water quantity–quality modelling, while self-supervised learning offers additional flexibility for exploiting incomplete and heterogeneous environmental observations.

title: Stochastic multi-segment scheduling of variable-speed pumped storage hydropower for energy and ancillary services provision
summary: Variable-speed pumped storage hydropower (VS-PSH) offers long-duration energy storage alongside ancillary services in competitive electricity markets. However, its operation and scheduling are challenged by head-dependent nonlinearities, di
content: Variable-speed pumped storage hydropower (VS-PSH) offers long-duration energy storage alongside ancillary services in competitive electricity markets. However, its operation and scheduling are challenged by head-dependent nonlinearities, discrete operating-mode selection, and energy-continuity constraints. This study proposes a stochastic framework for VS-PSH that employs a multi-segment bidding structure to generate market-consistent energy and synchronized reserve offers in compliance with market rules. The framework explicitly incorporates physical constraints, including head-dependent capability limits, discrete pumping and generating modes, as well as state-of-charge (SoC) and head dynamics, within a stochastic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulation. Price and reserve-utilization uncertainty is represented through AR(1)-based scenarios generated around the corresponding base profiles and reduced in a normalized joint-input space. The stochastic MILP produces optimal energy and mode schedules that maintain feasible SoC trajectories across scenarios and ensure physically feasible operating strategies. Illustrative case studies under different levels of price variability demonstrate feasible coordination of energy arbitrage and synchronized-reserve provision under the modeled physical constraints. Within these illustrative settings, the results indicate feasible operation rather than converged estimates of economic performance.

title: Access to Diverse Stacking Motifs and Colors in Tetracyanoethylene Charge Transfer Cocrystals with Tetramethoxyanthracene Donors
summary: Abstract Organic charge transfer cocrystals (OCTCs) are an appealing platform for solution processable electronics with tunable properties. Thanks to their modular, molecular composition, OCTC electronics and optics can be varied by the des
content: Abstract Organic charge transfer cocrystals (OCTCs) are an appealing platform for solution processable electronics with tunable properties. Thanks to their modular, molecular composition, OCTC electronics and optics can be varied by the design and selection of electron-donors and acceptors, but to achieve the goal of bespoke properties-by-design, detailed structure−function relationships are needed. One particular challenge is separately interrogating the effects of crystal packing from the effects of donor/acceptor strengths, as it is difficult to find systems where packing can be tuned without meaningfully changing the donor or acceptor strength. In this work, we use a series of easily-prepared 2,3,6,7-tetramethoxy-9,10-dialkylanthracene donors with varying substituent sizes and essentially invariant donor strengths in combination with tetracyanoethylene to probe the effects of crystal packing on OCTC properties. Across a set of five OCTCs, we observe both alternating and slip-stacked segregated stacking motifs. The stacking arrangements are correlated with CT absorbances, related optical properties, TCNE C−C double bond lengths, and corresponding degree of charge-transfer (DCT). Electrical transport under ambient conditions shows no clear trend in relation to molecular arrangement, with all OCTCs being very poorly semiconducting. Using X-ray crystallography and transmission absorbance spectroscopy of single-crystals, we inform structure−function relationships for optical properties of OCTCs with an electron donor platform that may be tuned sterically while holding electronics constant.

title: Vegetation cover shapes community structure and metabolic genetic potential of high-alpine soil microbiomes
summary: Abstract Background Alpine permafrost-affected soils, particularly in the European Alps, remain poorly understood despite rapid warming and projected vegetation increase at higher elevations. We investigated how vegetation cover and physico
content: Abstract Background Alpine permafrost-affected soils, particularly in the European Alps, remain poorly understood despite rapid warming and projected vegetation increase at higher elevations. We investigated how vegetation cover and physicochemical soil properties structure microbial communities across ten high-altitude alpine permafrost-affected sites. Results Soil parameters (pH, soil water content, temperature, and total C and N contents) varied significantly between sites and revealed pH and C: N ratio as key drivers modulated by vegetation cover, highlighting its indirect role in shaping soil environments. Microbial community composition differed significantly across sites, and functional gene profiles mirrored taxonomic patterns, indicating strong coupling between community structure and functional gene potential, with reduced functional redundancy. Microbial abundance increased with vegetation cover, whereas taxonomic and functional gene diversity plateaued at intermediate vegetation cover, suggesting that the presence of vegetation primarily enhances microbial abundance rather than diversity. Genome-resolved metagenomics revealed a shift from generalist-dominated communities in barren soils to increased prevalence of specialist taxa in vegetated soils. Functional gene abundances, particularly for C cycling, were higher in vegetated soils, while N and S cycling gene potentials were associated with soil temperature and water content. A microcosm experiment measuring ex situ CO₂ and CH₄ fluxes from incubated summer soils, identified vegetated soils as modest CO₂ sources. Vegetated soils exhibited lower, pH and C: N ratio, shaping a more abundant microbial community with more specialist members and higher C cycling gene potential. Conclusion Overall, our findings indicate that alpine greening is associated with microbial community turn-over via vegetation-mediated changes in soil properties, with implications for biogeochemical cycling and C emissions under climate warming.

title: Decoding transient X-ray absorption spectra of acetylacetone with multireference algebraic diagrammatic construction theory
summary: Multireference simulations of AcAc time-resolved X-ray absorption spectrum reveal transient signatures of proton transfer and excited-state relaxation.
content: Multireference simulations of AcAc time-resolved X-ray absorption spectrum reveal transient signatures of proton transfer and excited-state relaxation.

title: Pyrrocidines and hirsutellones: distinctive fungal polyketide alkaloid hybrids with intriguing therapeutic applications: a comprehensive update
summary: Covering: 2005-2025Pyrrocidines and hirsutellones are a fascinating class of fungal natural products that possess an intricate chemical structure characterized by a distinctive macrocyclic ring fused to a decahydrofluorene core. Known for t
content: Covering: 2005-2025Pyrrocidines and hirsutellones are a fascinating class of fungal natural products that possess an intricate chemical structure characterized by a distinctive macrocyclic ring fused to a decahydrofluorene core. Known for their complex architectures as PKS-NRPS hybrids, these metabolites are isolated from various fungi and have attracted significant attention due to their potent pharmacological properties, including antimicrobial, antifungal, and anticancer effects. This review article aims to shed light on the structural diversities of 52 fungal-derived pyrrocidines and hirsutellones reported over the period of 2005-2025, providing insights into their chemistry, biosynthetic origins, pharmacokinetic profiles, and structure-activity relationships (SARs). Furthermore, we critically evaluate their promising therapeutic potential, highlighting the opportunities they present for modern drug discovery and development.

title: Phase-morphology evolution and apparent preferential localization of barium titanate in poly(vinylidene fluoride) and epoxidized natural rubber blends with tunable mechanical and dielectric properties
summary: Abstract Non-vulcanized blends of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) with epoxidized natural rubber containing 50 mol% epoxide (ENR-50) in 80/20–20/80 wt% ratios were prepared by melt blending. The PVDF/ENR-50 blends at 80/20 and 50/50 were f
content: Abstract Non-vulcanized blends of poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) with epoxidized natural rubber containing 50 mol% epoxide (ENR-50) in 80/20–20/80 wt% ratios were prepared by melt blending. The PVDF/ENR-50 blends at 80/20 and 50/50 were filled with 5 vol% barium titanate (BT). SEM analysis revealed a change in morphology from PVDF continuity to apparent co-continuity at 60/40–50/50, followed by ENR-50 continuity at higher ENR-50 content. Increasing the ENR-50 content reduced stiffness and tensile stress but increased extensibility, with elongation at break values of about 1000–2200% in the ENR-50-rich blends. Furthermore, the PVDF crystallization temperature increased from 135.8°C in neat PVDF to 139.3°C at the 50/50 composition, whereas normalized PVDF crystallinity decreased from 54.2% at 60/40 to 43.7% at 20/80 due to phase confinement. Relaxation peaks at − 36 and − 9°C indicated phase separation with partial interface compatibility. The novelty lies in the identification of two-phase inversion boundaries and the correlation between phase continuity and mechanical, thermal, dynamic-mechanical, and dielectric behavior. Moreover, BT particles preferentially segregated to ENR-50, increasing the average size of ENR-50 domains in the 80/20 blend from 6.5 to 11.4 µm without altering PVDF continuity.

title: Zerovalent Metallic Intermediates in the Synthesis of InSb Quantum Dots: From Precursor Reduction to Optical Tunability
summary: ABSTRACT Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are transformative for short‐wave to mid‐infrared optoelectronics due to their narrow bandgap and exceptional electronic properties. This work refines the mechanistic framework
content: ABSTRACT Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are transformative for short‐wave to mid‐infrared optoelectronics due to their narrow bandgap and exceptional electronic properties. This work refines the mechanistic framework of InSb QDs formation, demonstrating that the size of zerovalent In 0 and Sb 0 intermediate nanoparticles governs intermetallic diffusion and growth kinetics. By tuning precursor halides (Cl − , Br − , I − ), reducing agent ratios, In/Sb ratios (2:1–5:1), and reaction times (15–180 min), we achieved monodisperse InSb QDs with tunable absorption from 1100 to 2200 nm and exceptional stability. Temperature‐dependent studies reveal that Sb 0 nanoparticles (3–4 nm) template nucleation at 140°C–160°C, while larger In 0 nanoparticles (50 nm) act as an indium reservoir, facilitating diffusion. Validation experiments with pre‐synthesized In 0 and Sb 0 nanoparticles confirm that size‐matched intermediates (14–17 nm) enable complete conversion to zincblende InSb QDs. Spectroscopic analysis identifies a dominant non‐radiative decay channel (τ 1 ≈ 0.12 ns for 9.6 nm InSb QDs) at room temperature, attributed to surface trapping, with the radiative lifetime preserved due to surface oxides. These findings further elucidate the formation and transformation of metallic intermediates and provide practical guidance for controlling the size and optical properties of InSb QDs for SWIR applications.

title: Energy Partitioning in Dust-catalyzed H 2 and HD Formation Revealed by Molecular Simulations Considering Nuclear Quantum Effects
summary: Abstract Molecular hydrogen formation on interstellar dust grains is a key surface process, but the partitioning of recombination energy between the substrate and the nascent molecule remains poorly understood. Here, we use ring-polymer mol
content: Abstract Molecular hydrogen formation on interstellar dust grains is a key surface process, but the partitioning of recombination energy between the substrate and the nascent molecule remains poorly understood. Here, we use ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) with a machine learning force field to investigate energy partitioning during H 2 and HD formation on graphene at T = 25 K, 50 K, and 100 K, focusing on the chemisorbed-H recombination pathway previously identified as the dominant low-temperature channel on bare graphitic surfaces when nuclear quantum effects are included. The desorbing molecule retains approximately 84%–87% of the effective released energy, with only weak variation across the three velocity-initialization temperatures under the present sampling protocol. Within the retained molecular energy, rovibrational motion dominates at 25 K, whereas center-of-mass translation becomes increasingly important at 100 K. H 2 and HD show similar total energy retention, with modest isotope-dependent differences in their internal partitioning. The effective joint rovibrational distributions show a modest positive association between vibrational and rotational excitation. Purely radiative cascade calculations in the optically thin, collision-free limit yield formation-pumping spectra at all three temperatures. From 25 to 100 K, the rovibrational fraction of the emitted energy decreases from approximately 43% to 28% for H 2 and from 41% to 28% for HD, while the strongest lines remain in similar wavelength regions. These results provide an energy-resolved microscopic picture of surface-mediated energy redistribution and formation pumping in H 2 /HD formation on graphene.

title: SWCNTs thin film transistor circuits fabricated on flexible substrates with inkjet-printed silver electrodes for photodetectors
summary: Abstract We demonstrate thin film transistors (TFTs) and PMOS inverter circuit using drop casted single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) as active semiconductor and spin-coated poly(4-vinylphenol) (PVP) dielectric on a flexible polyethylene n
content: Abstract We demonstrate thin film transistors (TFTs) and PMOS inverter circuit using drop casted single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) as active semiconductor and spin-coated poly(4-vinylphenol) (PVP) dielectric on a flexible polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) substrate of 125-µm-thick. All the electrodes were inkjet-printed using silver ink. The fabricated TFTs exhibit a linear field-effect mobility of 2.43 cm 2 V −1 s − 1 , while the saturated-load PMOS inverter achieves a voltage gain of 1.5 at a supply voltage of -15 V. The optoelectronic characteristics of these TFTs are systematically investigated under white-light illumination by monitoring drain-current (I D ) transients at different gate voltages (V GS ). The transfer characteristics reveal a reversal in hysteresis direction between dark and illuminated conditions, indicating that photo-induced charge-carrier recombination governs the device response. Under positive gate bias, the TFTs exhibit a pronounced and fully reversible photoresponse, with the drain current recovering completely after the light is switched off. In contrast, under negative gate bias, illumination suppresses the drain current, and the stretched-exponential transient decay becomes progressively faster with increasing negative V GS , reflecting Fermi-level-dependent carrier dynamics.

title: Reverse micelles as nanocarriers for polar friction modifiers in nonpolar oils: AOT-mediated solubilization and boundary film formation
summary: Abstract Polar organic friction modifiers can form effective boundary-lubrication films, but their limited compatibility with nonpolar oils restricts their delivery to sliding interfaces. In this study, lauroyl choline chloride (LCC) was se
content: Abstract Polar organic friction modifiers can form effective boundary-lubrication films, but their limited compatibility with nonpolar oils restricts their delivery to sliding interfaces. In this study, lauroyl choline chloride (LCC) was selected as a model polar additive to evaluate the ability of sodium bis(2-ethylhexyl) sulfosuccinate (AOT) reverse micelles in n-dodecane to act as nanocarriers for oil-incompatible friction modifiers. Increasing the water-to-surfactant molar ratio, w, expanded the transparent solubilization range of the model additive and increased the hydrodynamic size of the reverse micellar aggregates. Neutron reflectometry (NR) showed that hydrated AOT aggregates formed an adsorbed layer at the FeOx/oil interface, and incorporation of the model additive increased the fitted adsorbed-layer thickness from 3.05 to 3.43 nm under the same fixed-scattering length density (SLD) fitting conditions. Ball-on-disk tests showed lower friction after additive incorporation, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) detected chlorine-containing LCC-derived species on the worn surfaces, indicating that LCC was delivered to and retained at the sliding interface. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were used to observe the structural response of additive-loaded reverse micelles under high-pressure shear. These results support a reverse-micelle-assisted delivery mechanism in which hydrated AOT aggregates solubilize polar additives in the bulk oil, adsorb at the interface, and release additive-derived species under sliding.

title: A harmonised dataset of adult Culex pipiens mosquitoes from 17 administrative Italian regions, 2008–2022
summary: Abstract Culex pipiens s.l. is the primary vector of West Nile Virus in Italy. Despite the availability of abundant long-term surveillance data on adult Cx. pipiens observations in Italy, historical records are often fragmented across regio
content: Abstract Culex pipiens s.l. is the primary vector of West Nile Virus in Italy. Despite the availability of abundant long-term surveillance data on adult Cx. pipiens observations in Italy, historical records are often fragmented across regional repositories with heterogeneous formats and metadata. This work introduces a comprehensive, harmonised dataset of adult Cx. pipiens observations collected across 17 Italian administrative regions from 2008 to 2022. The dataset, compiled from official surveillance programmes conducted by the Experimental Zooprophylactic Institutes network and collaborating institutions, encompasses 58,888 raw observational records of adult Cx. pipiens , corresponding to 37,070 unique trap deployments. To ensure cross-regional comparability, these overlapping local observations were harmonised and spatio-temporally aggregated onto a 9 × 9 km reference grid compatible with ERA5-Land climate reanalysis, providing weekly median abundances. The data were stratified by trap type and mosquito sex, resulting in 50,759 analysis-ready records. Following rigorous quality-control procedures for taxonomic reliability and spatio-temporal consistency, this dataset constitutes an essential resource for spatio-temporal modelling of vector phenology, epidemiological forecasting, and advancing integrated One Health preparedness.

title: Effects of longitudinal gradient on vehicle-emitted gaseous pollutant transport and near-ground accumulation in long highway tunnels
summary: To elucidate the effects of longitudinal gradients on the along-tunnel transport and near-ground retention of gaseous pollutants in extra-long highway tunnels, scaled-model experiments and numerical simulations were conducted to investigate
content: To elucidate the effects of longitudinal gradients on the along-tunnel transport and near-ground retention of gaseous pollutants in extra-long highway tunnels, scaled-model experiments and numerical simulations were conducted to investigate the spatial distribution characteristics of gaseous pollutants under horizontal, unidirectional-slope, and symmetric-slope configurations. Ten combinations of slope types and gradients were examined in the scaled-model experiments. The experimental results show that uphill gradients significantly weaken the longitudinal transport of pollutants. Under a 3% uphill gradient, the near-ground pollutant concentration at the tunnel inlet increased by approximately 120% compared with the horizontal condition. Conversely, under a 3% downhill gradient, the near-ground concentrations at the inlet and middle sections decreased by approximately 60% and 53%, respectively. Numerical simulation further indicate that CO and NO₂ exhibit similar longitudinal distribution patterns, whereas NO₂ is more sensitive to near-ground low-velocity regions. Under the 3% uphill gradient, the near-ground retention index of NO₂ reached 4.40 at x/L ≈ 0.80, exceeding the corresponding CO value of 2.55. Furthermore, longitudinal gradients modify the distribution of high-concentration pollutant zones by altering the longitudinal momentum balance and the extent of near-ground low-velocity regions. These findings suggest that air quality assessment in extra-long tunnels with longitudinal gradients should consider not only the section-averaged concentration but also the near-ground peak concentration and vertical concentration stratification. NO₂ is demonstrated to be a sensitive indicator for identifying near-ground exposure risks under adverse slope conditions. This study provides a scientific basis for optimizing ventilation design and operational strategies in extra-long highway tunnels.

title: High-sensitivity multi-band graphene terahertz absorber and its applications in multi-channel biosensing
summary: Abstract Terahertz (THz) metasurface biosensors integrated with twodimensional materials offer immense promise for labelfree pointofcare diagnostics by exploiting characteristic molecular fingerprinting and nonionizing radiation. However, e
content: Abstract Terahertz (THz) metasurface biosensors integrated with twodimensional materials offer immense promise for labelfree pointofcare diagnostics by exploiting characteristic molecular fingerprinting and nonionizing radiation. However, existing THz sensors frequently suffer from single or dualband limitations that hinder multiplex analyte detection, strong angularpolarization susceptibility, and an inherent compromise between dynamic electrical tunability and high refractiveindex (RI) sensitivity. Here, a multiband grapheneassisted metaldielectricmetal (MDM) terahertz metasurface biosensor operating across 1–8 THz is proposed. By integrating four nested split decagonalring resonators, the metasurface supports three distinct, sharp resonance modes at 2.68 THz, 4.22 THz, and 6.22 THz, with the highfrequency mode exhibiting the peak RI response. Owing to its rotational symmetry, the proposed design achieves polarization insensitivity and maintains robust angular stability under oblique incidence up to 70°. Furthermore, patterned graphene patches—comprising a central circular patch and four corner rectangular elements—impart dynamic electrical reconfigurability via electrostatic gate tuning. Fullwave electromagnetic simulations demonstrate exceptional sensing performance: a maximum sensitivity of 1.34 THz/RIU, a quality factor of 14.82, and an optimal figureofmerit (FOM) of 3.17 RIU-1. Numerical investigations confirm its utility in quantifying hemoglobin concentrations, distinguishing pharmaceutical solvents, and identifying trace pathogens and pesticide residues. This threeband dynamically reconfigurable platform presents a versatile solution for multiplexed, labelfree biochemical sensing.

title: Trait-mediated nutrient resorption reveals element-specific conservation strategies in mangroves
summary: Abstract Background Nutrient resorption is an important nutrient conservation strategy in mangroves. Nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE), defined as the proportion of nutrients withdrawn from senescing leaves before abscission, reflects p
content: Abstract Background Nutrient resorption is an important nutrient conservation strategy in mangroves. Nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE), defined as the proportion of nutrients withdrawn from senescing leaves before abscission, reflects plants’ ability to recycle internal nutrients under nutrient-limited saline conditions. However, how NuRE varies among species with different salt-regulation strategies, seasons, and leaf anatomical characteristics remains unclear. We investigated 10 cooccurring mangrove species, including salt-secreting and non-salt-secreting species, in Dongzhaigang National Nature Reserve, Hainan, China, during the dry and wet seasons. Soil nutrients, green- and senesced-leaf concentrations of 12 elements, and six leaf anatomical traits were measured to calculate NuRE and identify factors associated with its variation. Results The resorption of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), copper (Cu) and zinc (Zn) was positive, ranging from 17.39% to 60.62%, whereas the resorption of calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), boron (B), sodium (Na) and aluminum (Al) was negative, ranging from − 164.91% to − 15.79%, indicating net accumulation during leaf senescence. NuRE varied significantly between seasons and showed element-specific associations with salt-regulation strategies, whereas their interaction was not significant. N and Zn resorption was greater during the wet season, whereas Cu resorption was greater during the dry season. The resorption of Ca, Mg, Fe, Mn, B, and Na was lower during the dry season. Non-secretor species exhibited greater N resorption than secretor species, whereas Na had lower NuRE values in non-secretor species. Green-leaf nutrient concentrations and anatomical traits explained most of the variation in the NuRE (52.0–95.3%), whereas soil nutrients explained 4.7%–48.0%. Green-leaf nutrient concentrations were positively associated with P, Mg, Fe, Mn, Zn, Na, and Al resorption. Guard cell length, epidermal thickness, mesophyll structure, stomatal density, vein diameter and vein density showed element-specific associations with NuRE. Conclusions Mangrove nutrient resorption is highly element-specific, and compared with soil nutrients, variation in NuRE is more strongly associated with internal leaf nutrient status and leaf anatomical traits. These findings suggest that element identity, leaf structural traits, and species-associated differences in salt-regulation strategies are important factors associated with variations in nutrient conservation patterns in coastal wetlands.

title: 1H, 13C, and 15N chemical shift assignments of monomorphic Aβ1−40 at 100 kHz MAS in a diamond rotor
summary: Abstract Amyloid-β (Aβ) fibrils are the principal component of the senile plaques that characterize Alzheimer's disease, and fibrils formed from the Aβ 1−40 alloform are strongly polymorphic, which has long complicated their structural char
content: Abstract Amyloid-β (Aβ) fibrils are the principal component of the senile plaques that characterize Alzheimer's disease, and fibrils formed from the Aβ 1−40 alloform are strongly polymorphic, which has long complicated their structural characterization. We recently reported a reproducible, unseeded, monomorphic Aβ 1−40 fibril grown at neutral pH from supersaturated monomer, together with its atomic-resolution structure and its 13 C and 15 N chemical shift assignments (PDB 12GB; BMRB 31300). Here we extend that reference to 1 H. From a 3D 1 H-detected hCCH (RFDR) experiment and a 2D hNH experiment recorded at 18.8 T and ω r /2π = 100 kHz on approximately 0.5 mg of hydrated fibrils packed in a home-built 0.7 mm single-crystal diamond rotor, we assign 123 1 H resonances, corresponding close to 90% of the distinct 1 H sites of the rigid core (residues Q15→V40), together with sixteen 1 H of the dynamic N-terminal segment. The 1 H-detected data additionally yield six previously unassigned 13 C and three previously unassigned 15 N resonances, predominantly in aromatic side chains and in the mobile N-terminus, and nine 1 H- 13 C and twenty 1 H- 15 N inter-residue contacts that are consistent with the published structure. These assignments provide a residue-level reference for fingerprinting Aβ 1−40 polymorphs and for mapping the binding of antibodies, chaperones and small molecules to this fibril.

title: Combined DFT/GNN analysis of compositional disorder and defects in MeX 2 (Me = Mo, W; X = S, Se) monolayers
summary: Abstract Chemical disorder and point defects critically influence the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials, but their theoretical description is limited by the vast configurational space of possible atomic arrangements, which is int
content: Abstract Chemical disorder and point defects critically influence the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials, but their theoretical description is limited by the vast configurational space of possible atomic arrangements, which is intractable for conventional first-principles methods such as density functional theory (DFT). Here, we develop and validate a method for accelerated assessment of thermodynamic stability of alloyed transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers with and without vacancies. A combination of DFT and graph neural networks (GNNs) is applied across the composition/configuration space (CCS) representing structured collections of symmetry-unique atomic arrangements. First, using the method proposed and convex-hull-based analysis, we show that quaternary alloys are thermodynamically unstable at 0 K. This problem is further addressed by finite-temperature analysis. Second, we demonstrate that random sampling underestimates the configurational entropy contribution for highly defective quaternaries, while considering systematically sampled CCS delivers accurate assessments. Furthermore, structured training data are shown to improve GNN generalization and out-of-domain accuracy relative to random sampling. Third, reconstructing finite-temperature free-energy convex hulls for low-defect alloys, many quaternary compositions become thermodynamically stable. Chalcogen vacancies emerge as the dominant favored intrinsic defect in the studied systems, remaining only ≈20–30 meV/atom above the free-energy hull at temperatures up to 1200 K, whereas metal vacancies stay less favorable (≈70–90 meV/atom). Altogether, these results establish a scalable route for finite-temperature thermodynamic screening of chemically disordered 2D materials with defects.

title: Local mechanical invariance in a recycled biobased vitrimer – evidence from the vibrational density of states
summary: Biobased vitrimers represent a promising class of recyclable thermosetting polymers due to their dynamic covalent networks. In this study, the local mechanical properties of a vitrimer system based on glycerol triglycidyl ether and a vanill
content: Biobased vitrimers represent a promising class of recyclable thermosetting polymers due to their dynamic covalent networks. In this study, the local mechanical properties of a vitrimer system based on glycerol triglycidyl ether and a vanillin-derived imine hardener are investigated before and after recycling. Using inelastic neutron scattering, the low frequency vibrational density of states is analyzed, focusing on the Boson peak (BP) as a sensitive probe of local elasticity. The vitrimer exhibits a pronounced BP, with its position and shape remaining unchanged after recycling, indicating that the local elastic modulus is preserved. Comparison with the BP of poly(methyl methacrylate) reveals a higher maximum frequency of the Boson peak and lower Debye level for the vitrimer, suggesting a higher transverse sound velocity and shear modulus. These findings demonstrate that the recycling process does not compromise the microscopic mechanical integrity of the biobased vitrimer during a recycling process, supporting its potential for sustainable material applications.

title: Spatiotemporal ion flux rectification via femtosecond laser-structured biomimetic shark-skin current collectors for high-performance anode-free zinc batteries
summary: Abstract Anode-free zinc metal batteries (AFZMBs) offer exceptional energy density but suffer from poor reversibility caused by dendrite growth and parasitic reactions. Conventional 3D current collectors and interfacial coatings are often p
content: Abstract Anode-free zinc metal batteries (AFZMBs) offer exceptional energy density but suffer from poor reversibility caused by dendrite growth and parasitic reactions. Conventional 3D current collectors and interfacial coatings are often plagued by weak adhesion and poor scalability. Herein, a monolithic biomimetic shark-skin-patterned copper electrode (Bio-Cu) featuring hierarchical microgrooves is fabricated via femtosecond laser ablation. This non-thermal subtractive manufacturing mitigates native surface defects and exposes a clean architecture that facilitates intimate electrolyte wetting and homogenizes interfacial ion flux. Mechanistically, the Bio-Cu electrode synergistically regulates 3D Zn 2+ transport kinetics and interfacial electric fields. This favors compact Zn deposition with an enhanced Zn(002) orientation, thereby suppressing dendrite formation. Consequently, the Bio-Cu||Zn asymmetric cell delivers a lifespan exceeding 8 000 cycles at 10 mA·cm −2 with a 99.898% Coulombic efficiency. Notably, robust reversibility is maintained even under the stringent condition of 20 mA·cm −2 at a high areal capacity of 10 mAh·cm −2 . The Bio-Cu||Zn x MnO 2 anode-free full cell retains 80% capacity after 800 cycles at 1 A·g −1 , and the assembled pouch cells reliably power an LED display screen. Furthermore, this work demonstrates that scalable biomimetic interface engineering provides a promising route for advancing high-energy-density metal batteries toward practical operation.

title: Analytical and numerical magnetostatic modeling of solid and hollow ferromagnetic structures with complex geometry
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Abstract The accurate prediction of magnetic fields generated by ferromagnetic housings in large-scale engineered systems is essential for magnetic signature (MS) control and magnetic field management. This work aims to provide a general an
content: Abstract The accurate prediction of magnetic fields generated by ferromagnetic housings in large-scale engineered systems is essential for magnetic signature (MS) control and magnetic field management. This work aims to provide a general analytical framework for evaluating the static MS of complex ferromagnetic components by employing a formulation based on the magnetic scalar potential together with volume‐averaged magnetization and effective relative magnetic permeability. The proposed method models arbitrarily shaped housings through equivalent cylindrical bodies that preserve volume and characteristic dimensions, enabling rapid field evaluation in regimes where classical dipole approximations lose accuracy. The framework is applied to two representative structures, a rotating machinery housing and a thin-walled enclosure for energy conversion devices, and analytical predictions are benchmarked against finite element simulations, showing consistent trends and order‐of‐magnitude agreement. Material substitution effects are assessed, and the limiting case of near‐zero effective magnetic permeability is examined, providing a theoretical lower bound for MS reduction and illustrating an analogue of metamaterial-inspired behavior. Results indicate that decreasing both effective magnetic permeability and averaged magnetization yields substantial attenuation of the static MS, approaching two orders of magnitude in the limiting case. The proposed analytical model therefore offers a computationally efficient tool for magnetic field prediction and MS control in complex ferromagnetic housings.

title: Ultrastrong bonded metallization on non-weldable thermoset via additive manufacturing
summary: Abstract The continuously increasing flight speed is the relentless pursuit of the high-speed aircraft (HSA). However, the weak bonding between metals and thermosets in HSA antennas, which are susceptible to peeling and detachment, strongly
content: Abstract The continuously increasing flight speed is the relentless pursuit of the high-speed aircraft (HSA). However, the weak bonding between metals and thermosets in HSA antennas, which are susceptible to peeling and detachment, strongly limits their capacity to bear high-speed thermal-vibrational loads. Accordingly, we pose the question that whether a multiscale interfacial interconnection strategy can provide a high-strength manufacturing solution for this hard-to-weld material combination characterized by vast physicochemical disparities. Herein, using a novel solid-state additive manufacturing (AM) strategy termed screw extrusion–plasticizing friction stir deposition (SEFSD) that allows direct metallization on thermosets substrates, we successfully achieved a multiscale-interconnected metallized thermoset comprising macroscale interlocking, microscale anchoring and nanoscale chemical bonding at the Zn/polyimide (PI) interface. We elucidated the friction-stir-driven in-situ formation mechanisms for connections at each scale and demonstrated that the composite load-bearing effect yields a lap-shear strength of (26.73 ± 2.14) MPa, remarkably surpassing the existing methods. Furthermore, the “integrated forming and joining” nature of this solid-state AM strategy highlights its great potential for fabricating robust, conformal hybrid components for advanced antennas and other related applications.

title: Matrix materials as functional enablers in metabolite sensing: from mechanistic demands to translational potential
summary: The performance of metabolite sensors is strongly shaped by the physicochemical properties of the matrix that governs analyte transport, interfacial stability, and signal coupling, yet the role of the matrix has largely been overlooked, oft
content: The performance of metabolite sensors is strongly shaped by the physicochemical properties of the matrix that governs analyte transport, interfacial stability, and signal coupling, yet the role of the matrix has largely been overlooked, often being viewed as a passive support rather than an active design parameter. This review analyses how matrix architecture controls sensing behaviour across polymeric, inorganic, carbon-based, and supramolecular material classes, examining mechanistic trade-offs between diffusion and binding, conductivity and biocompatibility, and structural stability and responsiveness in the context of electrochemical, optical, and electrical transduction modes. Particular emphasis is placed on operation in complex biological media, where protein adsorption, ionic fluctuations, mechanical mismatch, and dynamic metabolite flux impose constraints rarely captured in buffered laboratory systems. The comparative analysis reveals that no single matrix class universally optimizes sensitivity, selectivity, and stability; instead, sensor behaviour and performance-relevant characteristics emerge from alignment between the matrix architecture and the signal-generating mechanism. By framing matrix selection through these mechanistic principles, this review provides a foundation for rational matrix design toward continuous, multi-analyte, and clinically deployable metabolite sensors.

title: Stress-adaptive manufacturing of a cellulose nanofiber/carbon nanotube-liquid metal dual-functional layer for dendrite-free zinc metal deposition
summary: Abstract Zn plating/stripping continuously reconstructs the anode interface, where uncontrolled metal growth induces current-field distortion, Zn 2+ flux heterogeneity, and stress accumulation, ultimately causing dendrite growth, hydrogen e
content: Abstract Zn plating/stripping continuously reconstructs the anode interface, where uncontrolled metal growth induces current-field distortion, Zn 2+ flux heterogeneity, and stress accumulation, ultimately causing dendrite growth, hydrogen evolution, corrosion, and byproduct accumulation. Herein, a manufacturable cellulose nanofiber/carbon nanotube (CNF/CNT)-GaInZn hybrid interface (CC/GaInZn) anode is reported that couples a flexible conductive fibrous scaffold with a deformable solid‒liquid biphasic interface to regulate zinc deposition across electrical, mechanical, and chemical dimensions. CNF/CNT provides a uniform local reaction environment and current distribution, which results in uniform zinc deposition. GaInZn layer reduces the nucleation barrier, suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction, and dissipates the deposition stress. As a result, the CC/GaInZn symmetric battery operates stably for over 4 200 h at 0.5 mA·cm −2 and 0.5 mAh·cm −2 with low polarization. COMSOL simulations reveal that the CC/GaInZn layer effectively homogenizes Zn 2+ distribution, thereby enabling uniform zinc nucleation and growth. Notably, XRD residual stress analysis reveals a transition from high tensile stress to compressive stress in Zn deposits on CC/GaInZn, providing direct evidence for interfacial stress release and dendrite-suppressed Zn plating. This work demonstrates a strategy for constructing adaptive functional metal interfaces for aqueous zinc energy storage devices.

title: A volatilomics approach for the identification of volatile organic compounds as biomarkers of ventilator-associated pneumonia using GC–MS
summary: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious complication of patients at intensive care units (ICUs), contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Current diagnostic approaches for VAP rely on clinical, radiological,
content: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious complication of patients at intensive care units (ICUs), contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Current diagnostic approaches for VAP rely on clinical, radiological, and invasive methods, which are time-consuming, carry risks, and may result in delayed or inconclusive findings. The need for rapid, reliable, and non-invasive diagnostic tools is critical. Biomarkers and specifically volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose. In this study, we applied gas chromatography-mass spectrometry with solid-phase microextraction to analyze breath VOC profiles in critically ill children and explore their potential as early indicators of VAP. Results reveal significant challenges in breath volatilomics, including batch effects and variability in VOC detection. However, normalization strategies allowed for meaningful comparisons across multiple time points, revealing subtle trends in VOC profiles that could differentiate patients with high and low suspicion of VAP. Notably, VOCs such as o-xylene and pentadecane showed reduced levels in patients with higher suspicion of VAP at Day 3, suggesting potential associations with respiratory infection severity. While preliminary, these findings support further investigation into breath-based VOC signatures as a non-invasive, early diagnostic tool for VAP in pediatric ICUs. This approach could enhance diagnostic accuracy and inform timely clinical decisions, improving patient outcomes.

title: A cold-start self-evolving multi-agent intelligence for closed-loop prediction from materials synthesis to performance
summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to propose materials and plan experiments1–3, but whether they can predict previously unreported syntheses and the structures and performance of the resulting products before exper
content: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to propose materials and plan experiments1–3, but whether they can predict previously unreported syntheses and the structures and performance of the resulting products before experimental validation remains unclear. Here we test this capability using a multi-agent framework of general-purpose, unfine-tuned LLMs that enables cross-disciplinary collaboration, with an AI scientist coordinating chemistry, materials science and electrochemistry agents to performance closed-loop predictions of the reaction process, crystal phase and battery performance of TiO2 anodes synthesized by a previously unreported rapid Joule-heating route. The agents predicted 64 conditions blind in eight rounds and, after each round, rewrote natural-language Skills from the released measurements. A task-matched team predicted the reaction process and phase in 91.7% and 82.8% accuracy, with errors concentrated near sharp transitions, whereas quantitative predictions of rate-capability and long-cycle performance achieved accuracies of 59.2% (72.3% for anatase-rich products) and 68.1%, within ±30% of experimental values. Revised Skills raised accuracy on identical conditions in most matched tests, and rewriting Skills without new measurements did not. A complete prediction chain cost ~US$0.27 per condition. These results indicate that LLM predictions could replace exploratory trials under conditions far away from sharp transitions, pointing to a prediction-first research paradigm.

title: ABA-Mediated Salinity and Drought Tolerance in Plants: Molecular and Physiological Perspectives
summary: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a central regulator of plant responses to drought and salinity, integrating environmental signals with developmental and physiological adjustments. This review examines carotenoid-derived ABA biosynthesis, its turnove
content: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a central regulator of plant responses to drought and salinity, integrating environmental signals with developmental and physiological adjustments. This review examines carotenoid-derived ABA biosynthesis, its turnover during stress recovery, and signal transduction through PYR/PYL/RCAR receptors, clade A PP2C phosphatases, SnRK2 kinases, and ABA-responsive transcription factors. We discuss the mechanistic basis of guard-cell ion transport and stomatal closure, stress-associated gene expression, osmotic adjustment, antioxidant regulation, and root growth responses. Particular attention is given to intersections between ABA and gibberellin or auxin pathways that coordinate seed germination and growth under water limitation. Evidence from different plant species demonstrates both the conservation and context dependence of these pathways. We critically evaluate limitations arising from developmental stage, genotype, stress duration, and trade-offs between water conservation and carbon assimilation. Translational prospects include tissue-specific manipulation of ABA signaling, chemical priming, and field-based evaluation of yield stability. A more precise understanding of ABA dynamics during stress and recovery will support durable crop improvement.

title: Catalyst-Mediated Nucleation Control in Chemical Vapor Transport Growth of Black Phosphorus: A Comprehensive Raman Study
summary: Abstract Black phosphorus (BP) synthesized via Sn–I-assisted chemical vapor transport (CVT) is susceptible to structural inhomogeneity and oxidation-related defects that limit its crystalline quality. We systematically investigate the influ
content: Abstract Black phosphorus (BP) synthesized via Sn–I-assisted chemical vapor transport (CVT) is susceptible to structural inhomogeneity and oxidation-related defects that limit its crystalline quality. We systematically investigate the influence of transition metal additives (Fe, Co, Cu, and Ag) on BP structural properties during growth in the temperature range 600–700 °C. Raman spectroscopy was employed to evaluate vibrational mode positions, line widths, and disorder-activated features across multiple growth conditions.
