Protective challenge studies demonstrated reduced Salmonella Typhimurium fecal shedding and 100% survival against Salmonella Gallinarum infection. These findings highlight PLG-OMV microparticles as a promising strategy for Salmonella control in poultry.

title: Effect of valve opening dynamics on the shock formation and post-shock uniformity in a diaphragmless shock tube
summary: Abstract Diaphragmless shock tubes have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional diaphragm-based systems, offering contamination-free operation, minimal manual intervention, and quick turnaround time between tests. This study inve
content: Abstract Diaphragmless shock tubes have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional diaphragm-based systems, offering contamination-free operation, minimal manual intervention, and quick turnaround time between tests. This study investigates the shock formation and propagation dynamics in a diaphragmless shock tube actuated by a high-speed pneumatic valve. Experiments in a high-pressure diaphragmless shock tube with helium as the driver and argon as the test gas provided time-resolved valve motion data, capturing stroke length and opening speed of up to 28 m/s. The measured valve dynamics were incorporated into axisymmetric CFD simulations, which replicated the experimentally observed shock velocity profiles. Comparisons with conventional diaphragm-driven configuration simulations show that the diaphragmless mode requires up to $$\sim $$ ∼ 40 $$\%$$ % higher driver pressure to achieve the same shock Mach number. The simulations further confirm that the gradual valve opening produces an extended shock acceleration region that results in a longer shock formation length and a shorter test gas length. Notably, the diaphragmless setup yielded lower peak temperatures in the post-shock region, which is potentially advantageous for reducing remote ignition effects in chemical kinetics experiments. To the knowledge of the authors, this study presents the first combined experimental and numerical framework that captures realistic valve dynamics and the full flow evolution in a diaphragmless shock tube, laying a foundation for accurate modeling and reliable operation of next-generation shock tube facilities.

title: Optimizing typical nitrogen application level increases spring wheat yields and mitigates global warming potential in Loess Plateau
summary: Excessive fertilization is common in agricultural practices in the Loess Plateau, China. Spring wheat is a common crop grown in Loess Plateau, China. It is crucial to determine the extent to which nitrogen fertilizer application levels affe
content: Excessive fertilization is common in agricultural practices in the Loess Plateau, China. Spring wheat is a common crop grown in Loess Plateau, China. It is crucial to determine the extent to which nitrogen fertilizer application levels affect greenhouse gas (nitrous oxide, N 2 O; carbon dioxide, CO 2 ; methane, CH 4 ) fluxes and spring wheat yields, and to understand their potential regulatory mechanisms. Two seasons spring wheat field experiment was conducted in Yuzhong County, with four nitrogen fertilizer levels applied: no nitrogen fertilizer (CK), low nitrogen (LN), medium nitrogen (MN), and high nitrogen (HN). Compared with CK, nitrogen application significantly increased N 2 O and CO 2 emission fluxes by 107.47%–217.98% and 9.41%-22.68%, respectively; while suppressed CH 4 absorption by 5.24%-16.51%. The two-year average wheat yield under MN treatment (1322 kg·ha −1 ) exceeded that of CK, LN, and HN by 22.69%, 9.87%, and 13.72%, respectively. Yield formation (thousand-grain weight, number of grains per spike and yield) of MN were significantly higher than those of HN in both seasons, although the global warming potential and greenhouse gas intensity of MN were significantly lower than those of HN. Compared to the HN, the MN treatment reduced greenhouse gas emission intensity by 27.68%. Moreover, principal component analysis and spearman correlation analysis indicated that nitrogen application indirectly affects soil greenhouse gas emission fluxes in spring wheat fields by influencing soil physicochemical characteristics and bacterial community structure. The results showed that an appropriate application level of nitrogen fertilizer (i.e., 105 kg·N·ha - ¹·y - ¹) in the Loess Plateau region can significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions and decrease global warming potential, but increase spring wheat yield.

title: From shade to sustenance: tree species in home and domestic gardens
summary: Introduction Home and domestic gardens are multifunctional systems that support biodiversity, food security, sustainable resource use, and human well-being. However, a comprehensive synthesis of tree species associated with these gardens an
content: Introduction Home and domestic gardens are multifunctional systems that support biodiversity, food security, sustainable resource use, and human well-being. However, a comprehensive synthesis of tree species associated with these gardens and their ecological and socioeconomic contributions remains necessary. This review aimed to characterize research trends and synthesize the available evidence on tree species in home and domestic gardens worldwide. Methods A two-stage approach was applied, combining bibliometric analysis of publications retrieved from the Scopus and Web of Science databases for the period 1978–2024 with a qualitative review of the identified literature. The bibliometric dataset comprised 486 records. The qualitative synthesis examined four thematic areas, including tree species diversity, their uses, and their contributions to ecosystem services. Results Scientific publications increased steadily from 2015 onward, reaching a peak in 2021. The United States, India, and Ethiopia were among the leading contributors to research in this field. Major research areas included ecology, agriculture, and environmental sciences, with prominent themes related to biodiversity, sustainable gardening, and garden management. The qualitative synthesis identified a wide diversity of tree species across geographical regions and highlighted their contributions to food production, biodiversity conservation, shade provision, household resources, and other ecosystem services. Discussion Home and domestic gardens represent important multifunctional systems whose contributions depend on geographical context and local management practices. Integrating tree species into garden management can support biodiversity conservation, household food security, and sustainable resource use in both rural and urban settings. Further research should strengthen the comparative assessment of tree species and ecosystem services across different regions to support context-specific garden management strategies.

title: Evaluating VN Loading and Activation Effects for Energy-Storage through Voigt Deconvolution of Raman Spectra
summary: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is used to evaluate the structure of carbon materials, yet interpretation often depends on metrics that struggle to capture the effects of multiple interacting variables. To address this limitation, an integrated
content: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is used to evaluate the structure of carbon materials, yet interpretation often depends on metrics that struggle to capture the effects of multiple interacting variables. To address this limitation, an integrated analytical approach was developed by combining automated Voigt deconvolution with the linear mixed-effects model to examine the influence of vanadium nitride (VN) loading and activation method on carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrids. Raman spectra of VN–CNF materials prepared with different VN concentrations and activation methods (NH3, CO2, and nonactivated) were analyzed to determine the ID/IG ratio, crystallite domain size (La), peak width, and peak position. Voigt-based fitting enabled physically meaningful separation of overlapping D, G, D′, and D″ bands, while the linear-mixed effects model provided a quantitative means to compare the relative contributions of VN incorporation and activation method to structural variability. Although the statistical effects did not consistently reach conventional significance thresholds, VN loading accounted for a larger proportion of variance across several metrics, with activation method acting as a secondary influence. Trends further suggested that ammonia (NH3) activation combined with moderate VN incorporation favored increased graphitic character (sp2), consistent with enhanced conductivity and reduced charge-transfer resistance (RCT). Overall, the results show that pairing physically informed Raman peak modeling with statistical evaluation offers a practical and reproducible pathway for interpreting complex carbon hybrid systems and guiding the development of electrode materials for energy-storage applications.

title: Direct utilization of prebiotic carbohydrate ingredients by human gut Escherichia coli and Enterobacteriaceae: growth phenotypes and genomic constraints
summary: Prebiotic carbohydrates are food ingredients selected to modulate the gut microbiota, yet their structural fractions may also be directly accessible to non-target facultative anaerobes. We compared the ability of ten Escherichia coli and te
content: Prebiotic carbohydrates are food ingredients selected to modulate the gut microbiota, yet their structural fractions may also be directly accessible to non-target facultative anaerobes. We compared the ability of ten Escherichia coli and ten non- E. coli Enterobacteriaceae strains isolated from healthy subjects to grow on mono-, di-, oligo-, and polysaccharide substrates relevant to prebiotic ingredient design, including fructo-oligosaccharides, galacto-oligosaccharides, xylo-oligosaccharides, isomalto-oligosaccharides, inulin, arabinogalactan, and to hydrolyze starch and resistant starch. Growth data were integrated with genomic analyses of glycoside hydrolases, predicted enzyme localization, and carbohydrate transporters. Utilization was strongly substrate-dependent and decreased with molecular complexity. E. coli grew robustly on mono- and disaccharides but poorly on most oligosaccharides, with galacto-oligosaccharides representing the main exception. Non- E. coli Enterobacteriaceae showed broader strain- and genus-dependent variability, with Klebsiella spp. displaying the widest oligosaccharide utilization profile. Inulin and arabinogalactan did not support detectable growth, and no extracellular hydrolysis of starch and resistant starch was detected under the conditions tested. These findings are consistent with roles for degree of polymerization, glycosidic linkage, and transport compatibility in the direct accessibility of prebiotic carbohydrate ingredients to non-target facultative anaerobes. They further indicate that low-molecular-weight fractions require careful consideration during ingredient evaluation, whereas high-molecular-weight fibers appear poorly accessible to E. coli and Enterobacteriaceae under single-strain conditions.

title: Interfacial reactions and properties of tungsten–silicon nitride composites prepared by spark plasma sintering
summary: Abstract Tungsten–silicon nitride (W/Si₃N₄) composite ceramics were prepared by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1650–1800 °C with W contents of 0–20 vol%. The effects of processing on interfacial reactions, microstructure and properties wer
content: Abstract Tungsten–silicon nitride (W/Si₃N₄) composite ceramics were prepared by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1650–1800 °C with W contents of 0–20 vol%. The effects of processing on interfacial reactions, microstructure and properties were examined by X-ray diffraction, microscopy and property measurements. W₅Si₃ was detected in the specimens sintered at 1650 and 1800 °C, while its peaks were not resolved at 1700–1750 °C. A change in local nitrogen transport during densification is proposed as a possible explanation for this temperature dependence. In the WSN20 specimen sintered at 1750 °C, atomic-resolution TEM revealed a local W/Y₂O₃ contact. The two reported lattice spacings differed by approximately 1.29% in one dimension. This interfacial structure is considered alongside the measured mechanical properties and thermal conductivity. The observations identify a temperature-dependent phase response and an oxide-derived metal/ceramic interface for further investigation; the effects of local nitrogen pressure and interfacial bonding on bulk properties remain to be established.

title: FROM FUNDAMENTAL MODELING TO PROTOTYPE: THE DEVELOPMENT OF A HYDROGEN-POWERED HYDROXIDE EXCHANGE MEMBRANE CARBON CAPTURE SYSTEM
summary: Direct air capture is needed to remove carbon dioxide from ambient air and support net-zero emissions goals, but incumbent technologies remain limited by high capital cost and high-temperature regeneration. To be deployed at scale, direct a
content: Direct air capture is needed to remove carbon dioxide from ambient air and support net-zero emissions goals, but incumbent technologies remain limited by high capital cost and high-temperature regeneration. To be deployed at scale, direct air capture must approach costs below $100/tCO2 captured. Electrochemical direct air capture offers a potential alternative because it can operate at low temperature, use modular stack designs, and integrate with renewable electricity or hydrogen. To realize this potential, low-cost electrochemical direct air capture systems must operate under realistic environmental conditions and achieve high performance, including (i) high CO2 flux, (ii) high CO2 removal, (iii) low device energy consumption, and (iv) low air-side pressure drop. This work focuses on an H2-powered hydroxide exchange membrane carbon capture system, or H2-HEMCC, in which H2 is the energy source; thus, device energy consumption is determined by electron efficiency. Overall, this dissertation advances H2-HEMCC by improving the four key performance metrics for low-cost electrochemical direct air capture, validating operation under realistic weather conditions, and designing, constructing, and automating a direct air capture prototype for real-air operation. In Chapter 2, we experimentally show improved CO2 flux, CO2 removal, and electron efficiency guided by a 1-D through-plane physics-based model. At a fixed air flow rate, CO2 flux and CO2 removal are linked: increasing current density can increase both, but it decreases electron efficiency. To illustrate the importance of electron efficiency, values under 23% would make H2 OPEX alone exceed $100/tCO2, while prior membrane-based electrochemical DAC systems have typically remained below 40%. To overcome this limitation, the model was used to diagnose high-flux losses and revealed that hydroxide leaks across the membrane before fully reacting with CO2. Guided by this insight, a thicker interlayer increased the reactive zone for CO2 and hydroxide and increased peak electron efficiency from 38.7% to a record-high value of 63.8% at higher flux. The model also showed that carbonate and bicarbonate transport losses dominate at low CO2 flux, which was experimentally confirmed by showing that higher membrane resistance improves electron efficiency. Chapter 3 demonstrates that H2-HEMCC can operate across weather-relevant conditions, with performance measured from 5-40 °C and 50-90% relative humidity, in the context of a conceptual green methanol production plant. Lower cathode relative humidity improved electron efficiency, while device temperature had a smaller effect over the tested range. External heating would add energy demand and cost, so ambient-temperature operation is important for practical DAC. Based on this performance and its relevance to realistic operating conditions, 20 °C and 50% RH were selected as the DAC design basis for the green methanol process model. title: Towards Efficient Mangrove Monitoring: Super-Resolution Trained on Paired Low- and High-Altitude UAV Images
summary: Mangrove forests are carbon-rich, yet their dense canopies and intertidal setting hinder ground-based monitoring. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer an alternative but impose a trade-off: high-altitude flights cover larger areas, whereas
content: Mangrove forests are carbon-rich, yet their dense canopies and intertidal setting hinder ground-based monitoring. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer an alternative but impose a trade-off: high-altitude flights cover larger areas, whereas low-altitude flights resolve individual crowns. This study proposes a field-based protocol for super-resolution of mangrove UAV imagery trained on image pairs acquired at two different flight altitudes. Images were acquired at 82 locations in the Ao Kung mangrove forest, Phuket, Thailand, at 80.3 m and 15.6 m to provide low-resolution inputs and high-resolution references, and 64 pairs were retained after registration. A very deep super-resolution (VDSR) network achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) gain of 1.11 dB over bicubic interpolation on six held-out test pairs. In a five-fold spatially blocked cross-validation of all 64 pairs, VDSR outperformed bicubic interpolation on every pair, with a mean PSNR gain of 0.74 dB (95% CI [0.68, 0.80]). However, a brightness and contrast correction of the bicubic image, fitted on the training pairs, reached the same mean PSNR, so the gain of VDSR arose from radiometric correction rather than from recovered canopy detail. The protocol therefore provides real paired-altitude data on which super-resolution models can be trained and tested, and models that tolerate residual misalignment between the paired images should be evaluated in future work.

title: Quantitative Sonazoid contrast-enhanced ultrasound in clinically diagnosed cirrhosis: a prospective exploratory study of associations with liver stiffness and functional scores
summary: Objectives To examine whether quantitative Sonazoid contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) parameters are associated with liver stiffness and clinical or biochemical measures of hepatic function in adults with clinically diagnosed cirrhosis, a
content: Objectives To examine whether quantitative Sonazoid contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) parameters are associated with liver stiffness and clinical or biochemical measures of hepatic function in adults with clinically diagnosed cirrhosis, and to identify which parameters show consistent associations. Methods We prospectively studied 110 adults with clinically diagnosed cirrhosis. All participants underwent sound touch elastography (STE), sound touch quantification (STQ), and Sonazoid CEUS using a standardized single-platform protocol. Late-phase intensity at 1,800 s (BI1800), peak intensity, arrival time, time to peak, and ascending slope were related to liver stiffness measurement (LSM), serum markers, Child–Pugh class, and ALBI grade. Spearman correlations were reported with approximate 95% confidence intervals and approximate Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate q values. Results In the principal analysis, BI1800 was inversely associated with LSM by STE ( r = −0.498, approx. 95% CI −0.627 to −0.343) and STQ ( r = −0.430, approx. 95% CI −0.571 to −0.264; both approximate Holm P < 0.001). BI1800 was also inversely associated with total bilirubin ( r = −0.486) and total bile acid ( r = −0.412), and differed across Child–Pugh classes (A vs. C mean difference 13.49 dB, approx. 95% CI 7.90–19.08; BH q = 0.003). Associations with ALBI grade were non-monotonic and not robust after multiplicity correction (BI1800 approximate q = 0.052). Other CEUS parameters showed weaker or less consistent associations. Conclusions In clinically diagnosed cirrhosis, late-phase Sonazoid intensity was inversely associated with LSM and several functional markers. These exploratory, unadjusted associations do not establish fibrosis staging, direct Kupffer-cell function, diagnostic accuracy, or reproducibility, and pairwise complete-case denominators could not be fully verified. Incremental clinical value was not assessed in this exploratory design. The findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require validation with an independent functional reference standard.

title: Massa Medicata Fermentata (MMF) processed by stir-frying reduces Helicobacter pylori burden in a gastritis mouse model
summary: Ethnopharmacological relevance Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) is the only confirmed pathogenic bacterium that can persistently colonize the stomach and cause gastric mucosal inflammation and related diseases. Massa Medicata Fermentata (M
content: Ethnopharmacological relevance Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) is the only confirmed pathogenic bacterium that can persistently colonize the stomach and cause gastric mucosal inflammation and related diseases. Massa Medicata Fermentata (MMF), a classical traditional fermented Chinese medicine, is commonly used clinically—either unprocessed or stir-fried—to treat gastric disorders such as dyspepsia; however, its pharmacological mechanisms against H. pylori infection remain unclear. Objective To comparatively analyze the antibacterial effects of naturally fermented MMF and its stir-fried MMF on H. pylori in vivo and in vitro . Materials and method Naturally fermented MMF was stir-fry processed for different durations to produce three types: golden-, aromatic-, and charred-MMF; their biochemical characteristics and components were then evaluated. Co-culture experiments assessed the effects of MMF on H. pylori growth in vitro . Finally, a mouse H. pylori infection model was established; interventions with the four MMF types, alone or combined with anti- H. pylori immunoglobulin Y (IgY- Hp ), were administered for 2 weeks, and both H. pylori burden and gastrointestinal function were measured. Results Naturally fermented MMF exerted a direct effect on the growth and infection of H. pylori . Stir-fry processing not only markedly altered MMF appearance and biochemical profiles, but also enhanced its inhibitory activity against H. pylori growth. In H. pylori –infected mice, aromatic- and charred-MMF reduced gastric H. pylori burden, with 37.5% of treated animals (3/8) testing RUT-negative versus 25% for original MMF. Interestingly, combining MMF with IgY- Hp further enhanced the anti- H. pylori activity of MMF; notably, the aromatic-MMF + IgY- Hp group demonstrated a synergistic inhibitory effect on H. pylori growth (FICI = 0.5) and achieved the largest reduction in H. pylori burden in vivo , with 62.5% of treated animals (5/8) testing RUT-negative. This group also showed significantly improved gastrointestinal function, including gastric emptying and small-intestinal propulsion (p < 0.05), as well as serum gastrin, motilin, and somatostatin levels. Further GC-MS analysis revealed that stir-frying markedly altered the chemical components of MMF, such as 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) and 1-Ethyl-2-formylpyrrole, whose changes are consistent with the variation in antibacterial activity of stir-fried MMF. Conclusion Stir-fry processing significantly altered the appearance, biochemical profile, and composition of MMF and exerted a significantly stronger anti- H. pylori effect, especially for aromatic-MMF, compared with naturally fermented MMF. In addition, MMF combined with IgY- Hp significantly increased antibacterial activity in vitro and in vivo and promoted recovery of gastrointestinal function, suggesting a potentially effective and non-antibiotic therapeutic option.

title: Homogenization of daily temperature series: addressing radiation shield biases in the Padua area (1963–2025)
summary: Long-term meteorological observations are essential for assessing climate change and urban microclimates, but they are often affected by non-climatic change-points such as instrumental updates. This study presents the homogenization of two
content: Long-term meteorological observations are essential for assessing climate change and urban microclimates, but they are often affected by non-climatic change-points such as instrumental updates. This study presents the homogenization of two daily minimum and maximum temperature series in the plain area around Padua, Italy, covering the 1963–2025 period. A critical source of inhomogeneity was identified in the 2001–2004 period when metal radiation shields were replaced with plastic ones. To correct this bias, parallel measurements from dual sensors operating with both shield types in a nearby station were analyzed, revealing a seasonal disparity for maximum temperatures—driven by solar radiation overheating the metal shield—and a nearly constant offset for minimum temperatures, both modulated by wind speed. By applying these empirically derived corrections alongside the Climatol R package and multiple homogeneity tests, the reference series for the urban station of Padua and the peri-urban station of Legnaro were successfully corrected and homogenized. The reconstructed datasets confirm statistically significant warming trends for the 1963–2025 period, with the corrected series yielding slopes of ∼+0.4 °C/decade for both minimum temperatures and maximum temperatures. These findings highlight the fundamental importance of accounting for hardware setup changes and radiation shield types to ensure the accuracy of long-term climate trend analysis and urban temperature assessments.

title: Ammonia-Coal Co-firing in a Hybrid Filtration Combustion Reactor
summary: Abstract This study experimentally investigates ammonia-coal co-firing in a hybrid filtration combustion (HFC) reactor, where the packed bed is composed of solid fuel and inert particles. Two different types of coal (Baseline—BLC, Low Sulfu
content: Abstract This study experimentally investigates ammonia-coal co-firing in a hybrid filtration combustion (HFC) reactor, where the packed bed is composed of solid fuel and inert particles. Two different types of coal (Baseline—BLC, Low Sulfur Coal—LSC) under six configurations were tested, where thermal performance and gaseous emissions were assessed to evaluate the influence of fuel composition and bed configuration on reactor performance. Results show that HFC configurations shift the thermal peak downstream, achieving an absolute maximum temperature of 1539 K in the HFC (70% LSC) case. All HFC cases exhibit systematic NOx reductions compared to their nonhybrid counterparts, with reductions of 38.1% (BLC vs. HFC 70% BLC), 38.2% (LSC vs. HFC 70% LSC), and 32.9% (BLC+LSC vs. HFC 35/35/30). Following the same comparison, carbon monoxide emissions decreased in all HFC configurations, and unburned ammonia (NH3) was found below 3.33 ppm for all cases, verifying high combustion efficiency. This work advances the understanding of ammonia–coal combustion in porous media systems, showing that hybrid packed-bed configurations can simultaneously improve thermal performance and reduce NOx emissions, providing insights for the development of low-emission combustion technologies based on ammonia co-firing.

title: Metabolomic variation and pathway analysis of root exudates from Nitraria tangutorum Bobrov. across phenological stages
summary: Introduction Root-associated metabolite profiles may vary across plant developmental stages and seasons, but these variations remain poorly characterized in Nitraria tangutorum Bobrov. This study aimed to characterize differences in root-as
content: Introduction Root-associated metabolite profiles may vary across plant developmental stages and seasons, but these variations remain poorly characterized in Nitraria tangutorum Bobrov. This study aimed to characterize differences in root-associated metabolite composition among three phenological sampling stages. Methods Root-associated metabolite samples were collected from Nitraria tangutorum Bobrov. plants during peak flowering, peak fruiting, and vegetative growth in Alar, Xinjiang, China, with three independent biological replicates per stage. Samples were analyzed by non-targeted ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry in positive- and negative-ion modes. Following peak extraction, missing-value filtering and imputation, and total ion current normalization, metabolic features were putatively annotated using MS/MS data. Chemical-class composition, relative signal contributions based on normalized peak areas, and KEGG pathway mappings were subsequently evaluated. Results A total of 41,972 metabolic features were retained, of which 886 were putatively annotated. Among these annotations, lipids accounted for 23.93%, phenylpropanoids for 17.61%, terpenoids for 14.67%, other or unclassified metabolites for 14.22%, alkaloids and their derivatives for 10.61%, and polyketides for 3.39%. Relative signal contributions differed among the three sampling groups. At peak flowering, phenylpropanoids contributed the largest proportion of the total signal (26.36 ± 1.19%), followed by other or unclassified metabolites (22.87 ± 2.64%) and lipids (19.29 ± 2.61%). At peak fruiting, alkaloids and their derivatives (21.71 ± 0.41%) and amino acids and their derivatives (20.11 ± 0.46%) were predominant. During vegetative growth, carbohydrates (21.98 ± 6.80%) and lipids (21.91 ± 2.52%) made the largest contributions, whereas terpenoids accounted for 11.36 ± 2.09%. Exploratory KEGG pathway mapping revealed several nominal trends, but none remained statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction (FDR < 0.05). Discussion The relative composition of root-associated metabolites differed among the peak-flowering, peak-fruiting, and vegetative-growth sampling groups, suggesting stage- and season-associated metabolic variation in Nitraria tangutorum Bobrov. However, phenological stage was confounded with sampling season and analytical batch in this single-site, single-year study. Therefore, the observed patterns cannot be interpreted as causal effects of phenological development. Validation using larger, randomized, multi-year datasets and targeted quantitative analyses is required.

title: Integrated defense strategies of Chinese chestnut against Oligonychus ununguis: coordinated regulation of morphological barriers, constitutive metabolites, and transcriptome-metabolome responses
summary: Introduction The multidimensional defense mechanisms of chestnut ( Castanea mollissima ) against the spider mite, Oligonychus ununguis , encompassing physical barriers, constitutive metabolites, and post-infestation responses, remain poorly
content: Introduction The multidimensional defense mechanisms of chestnut ( Castanea mollissima ) against the spider mite, Oligonychus ununguis , encompassing physical barriers, constitutive metabolites, and post-infestation responses, remain poorly characterized. Methods This study integrated leaf micromorphology, physiological and biochemical profiling, transcriptomics, and metabolomics to elucidate the coordinated defense architecture of chestnut against O. ununguis . Leaf anatomical traits of six cultivars, comprising three resistant and three susceptible genotypes, were evaluated, while four representative cultivars were subjected to physiological-biochemical assays, widely targeted metabolomic profiling, and RNA sequencing before and 2 days after mite infestation. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to characterize co-expression patterns and metabolite-morphology associations. Results Cultivar-specific anatomical differences were observed among cultivars: the resistant cultivar ‘Likang’ exhibited significantly greater leaf thickness and upper epidermal thickness ( P < 0.05), whereas the resistant cultivar ‘Songjiazao’ possessed a thicker wax layer than the other cultivars. Biochemical profiling revealed cultivar-specific differentiation rather than a uniform resistant-group phenotype. For example, soluble sugar content was lowest in ‘Xujia1’, whereas soluble protein content was highest in ‘Likang’; however, none of these traits varied consistently within the resistant group, while LMM identified significant associations between four biochemical indicators (soluble sugars, flavonoids, lignin and soluble protein) and leaf structural traits, consistent with putative resource-allocation trade-offs. Mite infestation was associated with substantial transcriptional and metabolic reprogramming at day 2 relative to day 0, with commonly shared 406 co-upregulated and 500 co-downregulated genes, and 416 co-upregulated and 281 co-downregulated metabolites. WGCNA identified a cyan module positively correlated with day 2 post-infestation status (day 2 vs. day 0) and a black module negatively correlated with this status; these modules were provisionally designated as defense-associated and immune-suppression-associated based on their KEGG enrichment profiles. Four transcription factor families-AP2/ERF, Dof, C2H2, and PLATZ-showed metabolite-class-specific correlations within the gene-metabolic co-expression network. Disscussion Collectively, these findings support a testable, three-tier defense model- physical structural barriers, cultivar-specific constitutive chemical profiles, and infestation-associated molecular responses-that requires functional validation. This integrated framework advances the mechanistic understanding of mite resistance screening and provides actionable targets for chestnut genetic improvement and molecular breeding.

title: PEG-toughened PPF-DA hydrogels for 3D-printed bone scaffolds with tunable mechanical, degradable and drug-release properties
summary: Poly (propylene fumarate) diacrylate (PPF-DA)-based materials prepared via conventional crosslinking strategies typically exhibit pronounced brittleness, resulting in extremely poor processability and deformability. Under physiological cycl
content: Poly (propylene fumarate) diacrylate (PPF-DA)-based materials prepared via conventional crosslinking strategies typically exhibit pronounced brittleness, resulting in extremely poor processability and deformability. Under physiological cyclic loading, they are highly susceptible to irreversible fracture, which severely limits their application in bone defect sites with complex anatomical geometries and load-bearing requirements. In this study, we propose a novel synergistic toughening strategy. 2-Hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA), which possesses excellent biocompatibility, was ingeniously introduced as a co-polymerization crosslinker, along with PEG segments of varying molecular weights. Through efficient co-polymerization of HEMA and PPF-DA, a uniform and dense crosslinked framework is constructed. Meanwhile, PEG chains interpenetrate and entangle within the network, and by leveraging the differences in steric hindrance and segmental mobility conferred by varying chain lengths, a breakthrough in fracture toughness is achieved, alongside synergistic regulation of degradation behavior, high-precision 3D printing adaptability, and antibacterial properties. The results demonstrate that the addition of PEG enables the adjustment of Young’s modulus (from 0.5 to 50 MPa), fracture toughness (from 8.5 to 200.5 MJ/m 3 ) and degradation ratio (from 53% to 72%) across a wide range and also decides the release kinetics of the PPF-DA-based 3D scaffolds loaded with ciprofloxacin (CIP). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations elucidate the underlying mechanism regarding the influence of PEG chain length on the polymer network mobility and the antibacterial drug diffusion pathways. In summary, this study presents the first construction of a toughened, high-precision 3D-printable modified PPF system, yielding qualified scaffolds with customizable mechanical, degradation, and drug-release profiles ideal for bone defect repair.

title: Monolithic Porous Perovskite Ceramics for Hybrid Sensible/Thermochemical Heat Storage in Air-Operated Concentrated Solar Power Plants
summary: Addressing the materials needs and requirements of next generation concentrated solar thermal (CST) technologies targeted on high-temperature processes for electricity generation and solar thermochemical applications, the present study repo
content: Addressing the materials needs and requirements of next generation concentrated solar thermal (CST) technologies targeted on high-temperature processes for electricity generation and solar thermochemical applications, the present study reports research results on the shaping of porous monolithic structures made entirely out of CaMnO3-based perovskite powder compositions. The approach targets on the eventual use of such structures as hybrid sensible-thermochemical heat storage media, based on their characteristic capability for cyclic reduction-oxidation (redox) in direct contact with air, accompanied by endothermal/exothermal heat effects and complete reversibility of oxygen uptake/release and dimensional changes due to expansion/contraction. Multi-cation perovskite compositions were synthesized by scalable solid-state routes, optimizing the sintering conditions with respect to the desired properties of merit like phase purity of the obtained perovskite, heat capacity, dimensional changes due to thermochemical expansion/contraction and absence of reversible, yet detrimental for the thermomechanical strength and longevity of structured ceramics, phase transformations. Subsequently, monolithic porous structures, namely honeycombs and reticulated porous ceramics (RPCs) were manufactured out of compositions that exhibited a favorable combination of the key properties of merit above. Such monolithic structures of a variety of shapes and dimensions were sturdy and rigid enough to be subjected to several post-shaping (ongoing) tests relevant to the targeted hybrid sensible-TCS application.

title: Development of AC FIRE version 1.0: a mesoscale model with forest canopy and fire behavior submodels
summary: Numerical models are essential for advancing understanding of fire–atmosphere interactions, especially where field campaigns alone cannot provide sufficient insight. Existing wildland fire models vary greatly in complexity and scale, from c
content: Numerical models are essential for advancing understanding of fire–atmosphere interactions, especially where field campaigns alone cannot provide sufficient insight. Existing wildland fire models vary greatly in complexity and scale, from computational fluid dynamics models with detailed combustion submodels, to mesoscale models with empirical or semi-empirical combustion representations, to global or regional models that omit combustion byproducts altogether. However, no existing frameworks simultaneously represent atmospheric responses to wildland fires across scales from hundreds of meters to hundreds of kilometers, incorporate a comprehensive suite of physical parameterizations, and explicitly resolve some scales of atmospheric turbulence within and above a forest canopy. To address this gap, we introduce ARPS-CANOPY/DEVS-FIRE (hereafter, AC FIRE ), a mesoscale model that integrates a canopy resolving atmospheric model (ARPS-CANOPY) with a surface fire behavior model (DEVS-FIRE) and detail its development and preliminary evaluation. Unlike the original ARPS-CANOPY, which relied on a user-imposed fire heat source, AC FIRE employs two-way fire-atmosphere coupling to compute heat release from a surface fire dynamically. We demonstrate the coupled modeling system with a low-intensity prescribed fire conducted in the New Jersey Pine Barrens in March 2019. We compare simulated atmospheric variables to corresponding flux tower observations and simulated fire spread rates with measurements from an array of surface thermocouples deployed during the fire. The 30-m horizontal grid spacing in this preliminary AC FIRE study allows explicit resolution of some convective turbulent motions above the canopy, while turbulence within and near the canopy is parameterized. The AC FIRE simulation generally captures the mean and turbulent flow through the forest canopy and substantially improves upon ARPS-CANOPY with an imposed heat source in its representation of upper-canopy TKE. The simulated spread rates compare favorably to observed spread rates, with differences attributable at least partially to the use of uniform fuels in the AC FIRE simulation. Although the present framework is limited to surface-fire behavior and does not simulate torching or crown-fire propagation, the integration of a dynamically coupled fire heat source represents a significant advance in canopy-resolving mesoscale modeling. Beyond this initial case, AC FIRE provides a foundation for investigating a broader range of wildland fire–atmosphere interactions and for future development of more comprehensive fire–canopy coupling and operational applications.

title: Isolating the influence of aerosols on Arctic cloud radiative effects during a polluted warm air mass intrusion
summary: Arctic warm air mass intrusions are key to the region's energy balance because they transport large amounts of heat and moisture from lower latitudes. The resulting changes in heat and moisture content influences cloud properties, the therm
content: Arctic warm air mass intrusions are key to the region's energy balance because they transport large amounts of heat and moisture from lower latitudes. The resulting changes in heat and moisture content influences cloud properties, the thermodynamic structure of the boundary layer, and surface radiation. Warm air mass intrusions can also carry significant amounts of aerosols into the Arctic, including aerosols from anthropogenic sources at lower latitudes, which could influence the radiative impacts of such events. In this study, we examine the role of aerosol transport during a warm air mass intrusion that occurred in the central Arctic in April 2020. We use a version of the regional chemistry-climate model WRF-Chem adapted for Arctic conditions (WRF-Chem-Polar), to investigate the radiative impact of aerosol-cloud interactions associated with the event. We isolate the effects of the high aerosol burden by running the model with and without anthropogenic emissions. Anthropogenic emissions increase cloud droplet number concentration by 117 % and liquid water content by 52 %. However, the net surface radiative impact of these aerosol-cloud interactions is limited over sea ice. The high albedo of the underlying sea ice limits shortwave cloud cooling, while the longwave effects of cloud perturbations are small. Over open ocean regions, the surface radiative impacts of the aerosols are stronger. Overall, these results suggest that the net effect of an extreme aerosol transport event is sensitive to the season in which the event takes place, due to strong dependence on the surface state and the background Arctic haze conditions.

title: Mechanical friction-reduction strategies in triboelectric nanogenerators for enhancing efficiency and durability: A comprehensive review
summary: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are a promising technology for harvesting ambient mechanical energy, yet their durability is fundamentally limited by friction-induced wear at functional interfaces. Friction in TENGs is inheren
content: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) are a promising technology for harvesting ambient mechanical energy, yet their durability is fundamentally limited by friction-induced wear at functional interfaces. Friction in TENGs is inherently paradoxical: It enables charge generation while simultaneously accelerating material degradation. This review systematically summarizes five advanced mechanical friction-reduction strategies developed to address this paradox, including rolling friction, soft contact, intermittent contact, noncontact, and interface lubrication. Each friction-reduction strategy is systematically evaluated with respect to the corresponding structural design, operating mechanism, and application scenarios in insulator- and semiconductor-based TENGs. Furthermore, a comparative evaluation is conducted to provide a foundational understanding of how friction-reduction methods influence the performance of TENGs and to guide future design optimization. In addition, we outline the emerging trends toward intelligent, integrated triboelectric energy systems and present a roadmap for practical implementation and commercialization. This review offers valuable insights into the path forward for achieving highly efficient and long-term durable TENGs.

title: Tailored isolation and metabolomic profiling of extracellular vesicles in Manila clam (Ruditapes philippinarum) hemolymph and insights into water-derived vesicles
summary: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are evolutionarily conserved mediators of intercellular communication released by cells into biological fluids and the environment. Despite their increasing relevance in biomedical and veterinary research, knowl
content: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are evolutionarily conserved mediators of intercellular communication released by cells into biological fluids and the environment. Despite their increasing relevance in biomedical and veterinary research, knowledge of EVs in marine bivalves remains limited. This study first aimed to optimize protocols for EV isolation from the hemolymph of Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) using density gradient ultracentrifugation (dgUC) or size exclusion chromatography (SEC). EV-enriched fractions were identified and characterized for nanoparticle size distribution by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA), for protein concentration and imaged by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and cryo-EM. Small EVs (<200 nm) were successfully purified with both methods. While dgUC provided higher-purity preparations, SEC provided higher particle-yields and compatibility with metabolomic analyses. Metabolomics performed on SEC fractions and hemolymph revealed a distinct metabolic signature of EV-enriched fractions, characterized by metabolites associated with nucleotide metabolism, glycolysis, redox regulation, and energy metabolism. Secondly, in a separate pilot study, we investigated the presence of EVs in water conditioned by Manila clams. EVs were concentrated by tangential flow filtration and ultrafiltration and characterized by NTA, atomic force microscopy, TEM and by CONAN assay to assess their purity. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of EV-recovery from conditioned water but also the need for methodological refinement and appropriate controls to improve EV purity and distinguish EVs released from clams or from other organisms. Overall, these preliminary results establish a foundation for future investigations into the role of EVs in bivalve biology and their application as minimally invasive biomarkers for aquaculture and environmental monitoring.

title: Enhancing spectral absorption of organic dye sensitizers through ZnSO4 ‑ mediated coordination and protonation for DSSCs applications
summary: Abstract This research examines the spectral improvement of organic-based dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) via the incorporation of ZnSO₄ dual-functional dye additive. In this context, Zn²⁺ ions binds and coordinates anthocyanin molecules
content: Abstract This research examines the spectral improvement of organic-based dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) via the incorporation of ZnSO₄ dual-functional dye additive. In this context, Zn²⁺ ions binds and coordinates anthocyanin molecules to the TiO 2 nanoparticles through its functional groups and stabilizes the flavylium-Zn 2+ -TiO₂ system. Meanwhile, SO₄²⁻ helps boost the cationic resonance through protonation of the dye solution which enhanced the spectral photoactive of the flavylium cation. Then, this consequently stabilizes cationic resonance structure, optimizes orbital conjugation and enhances spectral absorption of the treated flavylium dye molecules. The chemical, morphological and electrical properties of the ZnSO 4 treated samples were characterized through uv-vis spectroscopy (UV-Vis), Fourier-transform Infra-Red (FTIR), field emission scanning electron micrograph (FESEM), cyclic voltammetry (CV), incident photon-to-current efficiency (IPCE), and current–voltage (J–V) measurements. A limited photovoltaics performance was seen in the untreated DSSC (UTD cell), as revealed by the open-circuit voltage (V OC ) of 0.46 V, the short-circuit current density (J SC ) of 0.52 mA/cm2, the fill factor (FF) of 0.44, and the overall efficiency (η) of 0.11%. In contrast, the optimized 8-ZnTD cell achieved a significantly improved V OC of 0.53 V, J SC of 1.74 mA/cm², FF of 0.41, and η of 0.38%. These findings validate the dual functional mechanisms of ZnSO 4 (Zn²⁺ chelation/coordination and protonation through SO₄²⁻) which act in tandem to stabilize the cationic resonance of the flavylium dye, extend conjugation and the enhance spectral integrity of the absorption spectra. This method becomes a synergistic approach to revert natural dye-based DSSCs, which lays the groundwork for future additive design in bio-inspired photovoltaics.

title: Comparison of pharmacokinetic properties of mitomycin C-based regimens for hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy in a rat model
summary: Abstract Mitomycin-C (MMC) is the most widely used agent for hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) in colorectal peritoneal metastases, though dosing and intervals vary across institutions. This study aimed to compare the pharma
content: Abstract Mitomycin-C (MMC) is the most widely used agent for hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) in colorectal peritoneal metastases, though dosing and intervals vary across institutions. This study aimed to compare the pharmacokinetic profiles of three MMC-based HIPEC regimens. Eighteen male Sprague–Dawley rats were randomized into three groups for 90 min of HIPEC at 41–42℃. Group 1 received 35 mg/m² in three divided doses at 0, 30, and 60 min; Group 2 received 40 mg/m² in two divided doses at 0 and 60 min; Group 3 received a single bolus dose of 35 mg/m² at HIPEC initiation. Peritoneal fluid and plasma concentrations were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. MMC concentrations differed significantly across groups over the 90-minute perfusion period ( p < 0.001). Peritoneal concentrations at 90 min were comparable among groups (73.63 vs. 75.92 and 79.58 ng/mL), whereas the plasma concentration was lower in Group 1 (1.59 vs. 2.45 and 2.02 ng/mL; p = 0.043). The peritoneal-to-plasma AUC ratios were comparable among groups (52.1 vs. 47.7 vs. 47.1, respectively; p = 0.849). In conclusion, the three MMC-based HIPEC protocols showed no significant differences in the peritoneal-to-plasma AUC ratio, although Group 1 demonstrated lower plasma MMC concentrations.

title: Magnetic Transition in Nickel-Catalyzed Carbon Nanotube-Alumina Composite
summary: Abstract Carbon nanotube (CNT)/alumina nanocomposites are promising advanced materials because of their superior mechanical, thermal, and magnetic properties. We report on the synthesis and enhancement of the magnetic properties of CNT/Al2O
content: Abstract Carbon nanotube (CNT)/alumina nanocomposites are promising advanced materials because of their superior mechanical, thermal, and magnetic properties. We report on the synthesis and enhancement of the magnetic properties of CNT/Al2O3 nanocomposites via chemical vapor deposition (CVD) using nickel catalysts. Scanning and transmission electron microscopy observations reveal that we have achieved a uniform mixture of CNTs with ceramic powder. The resulting composite contains 7.4 wt.% carbon, as confirmed by thermogravimetric analysis. The average diameter of CNTs is 15 nm, and the crystallinity of alumina remains intact after the CVD process. Magnetic characterization reveals a pronounced transformation in the magnetic behavior following the CVD process. The initial Al2O3 powder is diamagnetic; the CNT/Al2O3 nanocomposite exhibits superparamagnetic behavior, accompanied by a 1300% increase in saturation magnetization, despite containing only 5 wt.% nickel. Zero-field and Field-cooled magnetization measurements clearly show a bifurcation in magnetization curves, with a blocking temperature of 35 K. The enhanced magnetic response may be attributed to the combined contributions of intrinsic magnetic moments associated with CNTs and surface defects or vacancies, encapsulated Ni catalyst particles, and anisotropic magnetic susceptibility.

title: ALPAKAS: Alpine hydrographs and catchment attributes for karst springs
summary: Approximately 40 % of the European Alps consist of karstifiable rock. Due to their distinct recharge, storage, and discharge properties, karst aquifers are key components of the hydrological cycle and water supply in the Alpine region. Howe
content: Approximately 40 % of the European Alps consist of karstifiable rock. Due to their distinct recharge, storage, and discharge properties, karst aquifers are key components of the hydrological cycle and water supply in the Alpine region. However, large-sample datasets enabling comparative and data-driven analyses of karst spring discharge are currently lacking. Here, we present ALPAKAS (ALPine hydrographs and catchment Attributes for KArst Springs), the first large-sample benchmark dataset specifically dedicated to karst springs. ALPAKAS comprises 242 daily and 182 hourly quality-controlled and consistently preprocessed discharge time series from karst spring stations distributed across the EU Strategy for the Alpine Region (EUSALP) area, with stations located in seven countries. The dataset is complemented by both existing catchment delineations and circular catchment approximations, catchment-aggregated meteorological time series at multiple spatial scales, and a comprehensive set of static catchment attributes describing topography, positioning, meteorology, land cover, soil properties, and hydrogeology. In addition, the dataset includes karst-specific indices directly derived from the karst spring hydrographs. ALPAKAS is available via Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19329693 (Joger et al., 2026) under an open-access licence and is accompanied by comprehensive documentation. By providing a harmonized, large-sample compilation of karst spring catchments across diverse Alpine settings, the dataset enables comparative analyses, model benchmarking, and robust assessments of hydrogeological processes and climate change impacts.

title: From dynamic modelling of an experimental Reversible Organic Rankine Cycle towards a digital twin—Validation and remaining challenges
summary: Reversible Organic Rankine Cycle (rORC) systems alternate between high-temperature heat pump (HTHP) and power-generation operation. In geothermal plants, they can cover peak heat demand and convert surplus heat into electricity. Frequent lo
content: Reversible Organic Rankine Cycle (rORC) systems alternate between high-temperature heat pump (HTHP) and power-generation operation. In geothermal plants, they can cover peak heat demand and convert surplus heat into electricity. Frequent load changes, mode transitions, their optimisation and development of advanced control methods require detailed dynamic models, which are not yet available for rORC systems. This work presents the first such model, to the authors’ knowledge, validated experimentally in both modes of a reversible HTHP/ORC test rig. The model is developed in APROS, extended by Python-based sub-models and fitted to experimental data. The ORC net electric thermal efficiency is reproduced with a mean absolute error (MAE) of at most 0.32 percentage points, the control-relevant district heating supply temperature in HTHP mode with an MAE lower than 1 K and the mechanical coefficient of performance with an MAE of 0.31 to 0.44, demonstrating that the model captures the stationary and dynamic behaviour of the test rig in both operating modes. However, absolute HTHP predictions remain limited by a systematic overprediction of the refrigerant mass flow, partly attributed to unmodelled lubricating oil. Within these limits, the validated model provides a basis for control-oriented simulation and the development of advanced control strategies. A continuous bidirectional data exchange with the test rig remains as last step towards a digital twin.
