The mechanics of the GFRP-derived binder are a key finding as it maintained mechanical performance for the duration of the study compared to the Class G cement which showed significant degradation. The scratch test results showed that the GFRP binder scratch-derived strength increased from 14.5 MPa at day 1 to 17.9 MPa at day 90, an increase of 23.4%, and the tensile strength remained stable at about 1.5 MPa. However, Class G cement lost 42.3% of its scratch-derived strength (from 12.3 to 7.1 MPa) with a minor loss in tensile strength. The non-destructive computed tomography (CT) analysis revealed a more homogenous internal damage of the GFRP binder in comparison to Class G cement. Brine chemistry after exposure showed moderate alkalinity (pH 8.0), a large increase in dissolved inorganic carbon and a significant leaching of potassium (from 19 to 12,690 ppm). These results suggest a potential for GFRP derived alkali-activated binders in CO 2 -rich wellbore applications.

title: Marine Exopolysaccharide Diabolican Enhances the Physical Properties of Collagen Hydrogels via a Temperature-Dependent Polyionic Complexation
summary: Collagens and glycosaminoglycans are essential components of the extracellular matrix, providing key biochemical and mechanical properties. Type I collagen and hyaluronan (HA) are therefore widely used in tissue engineering to mimic the cha
content: Collagens and glycosaminoglycans are essential components of the extracellular matrix, providing key biochemical and mechanical properties. Type I collagen and hyaluronan (HA) are therefore widely used in tissue engineering to mimic the characteristics of human tissues. However, native HA does not significantly improve the properties of collagen hydrogels when combined with this biopolymer. In this study, the marine exopolysaccharide diabolican (HE800 strain), which exhibits structural similarities to HA, was evaluated as an alternative glycosaminoglycan for combination with type I collagen. Mixing collagen with diabolican led to the formation of polyionic complexes (PICs), even under conditions of high osmotic strength. Complex formation depended on both the molecular weight of diabolican and temperature. Performing the mixing on ice slowed down complexation, enabling the preparation of homogeneous hydrogels. The interplay between PIC formation and collagen gelation generated composite hydrogels with significantly improved physical properties when high-molecular-weight (HMW) diabolican was used, doubling the mechanical strength compared to pure collagen. Encapsulated fibroblasts remained viable, adopted a spindle shaped morphology, proliferated, and did not induce hydrogel contraction until day seven. Importantly, these advantages were achieved without chemical functionalization or crosslinking. Overall, HMW diabolican represents a promising alternative to hyaluronan for tissue engineering applications.

title: Joint Inversion of Summertime Anthropogenic and Biogenic NO x and NMVOC Emissions over the Continental United States Using TEMPO and TROPOMI Observations
summary: Abstract. Nitrogen oxides (NOx) and non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) are major air pollutants and key precursors to tropospheric ozone. We constrain summertime US NOx and NMVOC emissions by assimilating midday TEMPO and TROPO
content: Abstract. Nitrogen oxides (NOx) and non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) are major air pollutants and key precursors to tropospheric ozone. We constrain summertime US NOx and NMVOC emissions by assimilating midday TEMPO and TROPOMI nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and formaldehyde (HCHO) observations to assess how joint emission inversions and daytime TEMPO observations improve top-down emission estimates. Satellite NO2 and HCHO retrievals evaluated against Pandora show negative biases; notably, TROPOMI HCHO is systematically lower than TEMPO HCHO by 30–40 % over the southeastern US, and a bias correction was applied to TROPOMI HCHO. Top-down NOx emissions derived from TEMPO and TROPOMI are 5–20 % lower than prior estimates. Posterior biogenic NMVOC emissions are reduced by 40–50 %, and top-down anthropogenic NMVOC emissions derived from both satellite datasets are also 20–40 % lower in urban areas. While overall top-down NOx emissions appear underestimated, TEMPO-derived emissions demonstrate better performance than TROPOMI-derived emissions. Updated NMVOC emissions mitigate the prior model overprediction of HCHO and other NMVOC species, with TEMPO data providing stronger constraints while TROPOMI-derived emissions are overcorrected. Joint NOx and NMVOC inversions yield the best O3 simulations compared to NMVOC-only inversions. Furthermore, NMVOC emission estimates are sensitive to the NOx emission inversion, resulting in a 10 % difference in posterior emissions due to complex NOx–hydroxyl radical (OH)–VOC chemical interactions. Our work demonstrates that TEMPO's better midday retrieval quality provides enhanced constraints for top-down emission estimation compared to TROPOMI, laying the groundwork for diurnal geostationary assimilation while highlighting the critical need for multi-species joint inversions.

title: Potential to modulate corneal epithelial repair via nitric oxide-releasing glycosaminoglycans
summary: barrier restoration. A derivative consisting of CS with prolonged NO release and low molecular weight HA with intermediate NO-release kinetics were identified as the most promising materials. The HA derivative enhanced epithelial migration
content: barrier restoration. A derivative consisting of CS with prolonged NO release and low molecular weight HA with intermediate NO-release kinetics were identified as the most promising materials. The HA derivative enhanced epithelial migration even during later timepoints of the migration assays. A carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) gel formulation containing the HA derivative further promoted cell migration. In corneal tissue models, treatment with both the free and CMC-formulated NO-releasing HA enhanced restoration. Barrier recovery, as measured by transepithelial electrical resistance, confirmed restoration of tissue integrity post-wounding, concomitant with a cytokine milieu associated with pro-wound healing. Overall, NO-releasing, low molecular weight HA in a CMC gel formulation represents a promising bioactive strategy for promoting corneal wound repair.

title: Evaluation of marginal and average sectorial GHGs emissions abatement costs using an open-source energy system optimization model: the Italian case study
source: Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies for Global Change
summary: Abstract To achieve a carbon-neutral Europe by 2050, emission reduction efforts must be supported by quantitative tools that capture the interactions among sectors and technologies. This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate system-wide
content: Abstract To achieve a carbon-neutral Europe by 2050, emission reduction efforts must be supported by quantitative tools that capture the interactions among sectors and technologies. This paper proposes a methodology to evaluate system-wide marginal abatement costs and sectorial and sub-sectorial average abatement costs with a multi-sectoral energy system optimization model. The approach compares the total system cost and emissions of a sequence of whole-system optimizations under progressively stricter emission constraints. The constraints are applied along the entire decarbonization trajectory rather than to a single target year. The resulting marginal costs are then allocated to the sectors and technologies that deliver each emission reduction step. Since every point of the curve corresponds to a consistent system configuration, technology interactions and sector coupling are preserved, and each cost level can be traced back to the technology transitions and input assumptions that drive it. The methodology is demonstrated on the Italian energy system with the open-source TEMOA-Italy model, considering emission reduction targets of up to -90% in 2050. The results show that marginal abatement costs rise steeply as the targets become more ambitious, and that abatement costs vary widely across sectors. The power sector is the cheapest to decarbonize, thanks to mature renewable technologies. Transport shows intermediate costs, with marked differences across its sub-sectors. The industrial and residential sectors show the highest costs and contribute mainly at the most ambitious targets. The open-source framework allows the approach to be reproduced and transferred to other energy systems.

title: Regional artificial intelligence development and agricultural ecological efficiency: evidence from Chinese provinces
summary: Existing studies have primarily focused on the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on productivity and carbon emission efficiency, while systematic evidence on whether and through which mechanisms AI improves agricultural ecological eff
content: Existing studies have primarily focused on the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on productivity and carbon emission efficiency, while systematic evidence on whether and through which mechanisms AI improves agricultural ecological efficiency (AEE) remains relatively limited. Using provincial panel data from China for the period 2005 to 2023, this study employs the entropy weighting method to measure regional AI development and a slack-based measure (SBM) model incorporating undesirable outputs to evaluate AEE. A two-way fixed effects model is further constructed to examine the effects of AI on AEE and the underlying mechanisms. AI is conceptually distinct from general digitalization, automation, precision agriculture, and information technology development, as its defining feature lies in leveraging machine learning, intelligent sensing, and algorithmic decision-making to achieve more advanced data processing and intelligent decision-making capabilities. The results indicate that a 0.1-unit increase in regional AI development is associated with an average increase of 0.01078 units in AEE. Mechanism analysis suggests that AI can indirectly improve AEE by promoting green finance development and industrial structure upgrading. Furthermore, agricultural technological innovation exhibits a significant threshold effect, with higher levels of technological innovation strengthening the positive effect of AI on AEE. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the positive effect of AI on AEE is more pronounced in eastern regions, regions with lower levels of urbanization and agricultural modernization, and non-major grain-producing regions. Further analysis identifies positive spatial spillover effects of AI on AEE in neighboring regions, contributing to coordinated green agricultural development across local and neighboring regions. This study provides evidence on the effects, transmission mechanisms, and threshold conditions through which AI improves AEE, offering new empirical insights into the role of AI in facilitating the green transformation of agriculture and extending the analytical perspective of agricultural sustainability research.

title: Measures, Evolutions, and Determinants of Green Efficiency: Evidence from China
summary: This study measures urban green efficiency in 270 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2022 using an output-oriented variable-returns to-scale (VRS) slacks-based measure data envelopment analysis model that incorporates carbon dioxide emissions as a
content: This study measures urban green efficiency in 270 Chinese cities from 2008 to 2022 using an output-oriented variable-returns to-scale (VRS) slacks-based measure data envelopment analysis model that incorporates carbon dioxide emissions as an undesirable output. It then traces the temporal evolution and city-size distribution of green efficiency and examines the factors associated with its variation using two-way fixed-effects models. The analysis further tests whether the relationships of economic openness and economic development with green efficiency differ systematically across city-size tiers. The results show that the national mean VRS green-efficiency score is 0.736 and that efficiency follows a non-monotonic pattern across city sizes, with megacities recording the highest average level and large and medium-sized cities exhibiting relatively lower levels. Over time, green efficiency displays marked fluctuations rather than a sustained upward trajectory. The cross-tier pattern is also sensitive to returns-to-scale assumptions, as the relative VRS advantage of small cities disappears under the constant-returns-to-scale specification. In the second-stage analysis, economic openness is positively associated with green efficiency at the national level, while economic development shows no uniform independent association. Their interaction is positive and significant, indicating that the relationship between openness and green efficiency becomes more favorable as development increases. City-size heterogeneity is pronounced but structurally uneven: differences in the development–efficiency relationship are broad and statistically strong across city tiers, whereas openness-related heterogeneity is concentrated in specific inter-tier contrasts rather than being uniformly distributed across all city-size groups. These findings show that national averages conceal distinct urban trajectories and conditional relationships. Policy design should therefore account for differences in city size, development conditions, and the capacity of cities to translate external economic linkages and development gains into greener production performance. title: Industrial specialization and agricultural green production efficiency: local effects and spatial spillovers
summary: Cross-sector linkages between industrial specialization and agricultural green production efficiency, and their spatial distribution, are important for understanding coordinated industrial and agricultural transformation. Using 3,432 observ
content: Cross-sector linkages between industrial specialization and agricultural green production efficiency, and their spatial distribution, are important for understanding coordinated industrial and agricultural transformation. Using 3,432 observations from 264 Chinese cities during 2011–2023, we examine local and spatial associations with two-way fixed-effects and spatial Durbin models. Efficiency is measured using a global, non-oriented slacks-based measure (SBM) under variable returns to scale (VRS), incorporating carbon emissions from five agricultural input and operation sources. The positive local association retains its direction across alternative measures, sample adjustments, and endogeneity checks. Urban green innovation, fiscal expenditure composition, and urban road conditions provide evidence of positive statistical mediation. The local association is stronger in cities with higher economic development and a stronger initial industrial base. Direct, indirect, and total effects are positive and significant under contiguity weights. Their directions remain unchanged with K = 5, 8, 10, and 12 nearest neighbors, indicating a positive net spatial association. These findings inform budget allocation for agriculture, forestry, and water affairs and coordinated agricultural environmental governance across cities.

title: Challenge of net zero photovoltaic system sizing for residential buildings – a load matching case study
summary: Abstract Mitigation of the carbon emissions of the residential building sector predominantly involves the use of grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems. The core challenge of these PV systems is the load matching problem, the mismatch of
content: Abstract Mitigation of the carbon emissions of the residential building sector predominantly involves the use of grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems. The core challenge of these PV systems is the load matching problem, the mismatch of generation and consumption periods. The topic is actively researched, but less attention is given to the impact of residential building types, heating system types, and PV system specifications. In this paper, using dynamic building energy performance simulations in TRNSYS, three residential building types, two heating and domestic hot water generation systems and various photovoltaic system layouts (orientation and size) are evaluated for self-consumption, self-sufficiency, self-production and grid-liability. The paper reveals a contradiction in load matching improvement and reduction of energy consumption: inefficient solutions, like active cooling instead of shading, or hot water generation with electric heaters instead of heat pump heating can improve load matching indicators. Based on simulation results, the challenge of photovoltaic system sizing is also addressed. Photovoltaic systems sized to balance the electricity needs of the observed households on an annual scale (net zero photovoltaic systems) heavily interact with the electricity grid. The paper proposes an optimal PV system sizing strategy, that is reducing the photovoltaic systems to half of the net-zero sizing, reduces grid-liability by 38 percentage points, as well as improves self-consumption by 15 percentage points and self-production by 6 percentage points.

title: Is Working from Home Good for the Environment? Evidence from Satellite Images
summary: Working from home (WFH) may reduce commuting and congestion, but additional non-work-related trips and household energy use may outweigh such environmental benefits. We examine whether annual changes in WFH prevalence are associated with ch
content: Working from home (WFH) may reduce commuting and congestion, but additional non-work-related trips and household energy use may outweigh such environmental benefits. We examine whether annual changes in WFH prevalence are associated with changes in atmospheric CO2 concentration and tropospheric NO2 column density across U.S. metropolitan areas. We combine U.S. Census Bureau WFH data with satellite observations within 20 miles of each metropolitan area’s downtown center, yielding 216 metropolitan-year observations across 108 metropolitan areas in 2022 and 2023. We find that changes in WFH prevalence are not significantly associated with changes in atmospheric CO2 concentration. For NO2, the pooled regression shows a significant negative association with changes in WFH prevalence, although this association is statistically insignificant after including year fixed effects. Year-specific analyses reveal a more nuanced relation: the association is negative and statistically significant in 2021–2022 but turns positive and marginally significant in 2022–2023. This temporal variation may reflect shifts in the relative effects of reduced commuting and increased non-work-related travel, although we do not directly examine these potential mechanisms. We also caution that these estimates are conditional associations rather than causal effects, and are subject to satellite sampling and measurement limitations. Overall, the findings suggest that WFH’s environmental benefits vary across environmental outcomes and may depend on the extent of WFH adoption and associated changes in travel behavior. The results highlight the importance of considering workplace arrangements and their implications for travel patterns when developing urban transportation strategies to improve air quality.

title: Protein Corona Selectivity on Carbon Nanotube Biosensors Is Driven by Surface Coating and Chirality
summary: Abstract Semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are versatile near-infrared fluorophores that can be engineered to create sensors for biological research and diagnostic applications. SWCNT properties depend on both surface f
content: Abstract Semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) are versatile near-infrared fluorophores that can be engineered to create sensors for biological research and diagnostic applications. SWCNT properties depend on both surface functionalization and underlying lattice structure, defined by the chiral indices (n,m), enabling the development of wavelength-tunable nanosensors. While the principles of specific SWCNT surface modification with biomacromolecules are well studied, the impact of SWCNT surface chemistry and chirality on protein interactions in complex biological fluids remains underexplored. Here, we investigated the role of SWCNT surface coating and chirality in protein corona formation using mass spectrometry-based proteomics. We systematically compared protein corona formation in human blood plasma across single-stranded DNA (ssDNA)- and PEG-phospholipid-coated SWCNTs, as well as across nanotube chiralities spanning (6,4) to (9,4). Our findings indicate that surface coating identity is the dominant factor governing differential protein adsorption. SWCNTs with high binding stability ssDNA sequences exhibited greater protein-corona selectivity, preferentially enriching apolipoproteins and more internally structured proteins, whereas the PEG-phospholipid coating globally reduced, though did not eliminate, protein adsorption. Trends with increasing SWCNT diameter and chiral angle were generally aligned to each other, both associated with preferential adsorption of larger proteins with lower secondary-structure content, while revealing some distinctive protein-property associations, suggesting (n,m)-dependent interfacial differences. Protein corona formation was further shaped by protein–protein cooperative binding effects in a SWCNT coating-dependent manner. Molecular dynamics simulations provided mechanistic support for the experimental finding that proteins with higher glycine content displayed enhanced binding to (GT)6- compared to (TAT)4-coated SWCNTs through distinct glycine-peptide binding modes. Finally, we observed surface modification-specific fluorescence modulation of SWCNTs upon protein adsorption, impacting functional sensing of dopamine as a model small molecule. These insights provide a framework for the rational design of SWCNT-based sensors for protein-profile recognition in complex biological environments.

title: Agricultural land management practices in the conterminous United States from 1980–2023
summary: Agricultural land management practices affect environmental variables including water quality, carbon and nitrogen cycles, and greenhouse gas emissions. To better understand agricultural land management practices, we compiled a land managem
content: Agricultural land management practices affect environmental variables including water quality, carbon and nitrogen cycles, and greenhouse gas emissions. To better understand agricultural land management practices, we compiled a land management history for the conterminous United States (CONUS) from 1980–2023. We used the National Resources Inventory as the basis for our sample-based approach to impute planting and harvest dates, synthetic N fertilizer and manure N and C application rates and timing, tillage systems and intensity, and cover crop adoption on major commodity croplands. We aggregated the imputations to a 0.25° grid and compiled a comprehensive data set detailing the management practices used on agricultural lands across CONUS. From 1980–2023, cotton and spring wheat were planted an average of 12 and 9 d later, respectively, while soybeans were planted an average of 12 d earlier. Nationally, average synthetic N fertilizer rates for corn increased from 122.5 kg N ha −1 in 1980 to 150.9 kg N ha −1 in 2023. Similar increases occurred for cotton and wheat. Synthetic fertilization rates climbed steadily from 1980–2000 and then stabilized from 2000–2023. Conversely, manure N amendment rates increased slowly from 1980–2000 and then more rapidly from 2000–2023. Rates for corn, which had the highest use of manure N amendment, increased from 14.9 to 20.7 kg N ha −1 from 1980–2023. On average, no-till and reduced-till practices for row crops increased by 19.2 % and 26.5 %, respectively, across CONUS, while full till practices decreased by 47.2 %. Cover crop adoption increased across CONUS from 1980–2023, with the highest level of adoption occurring in the Eastern US and covering 10 %–13 % of cropland area in these regions by 2023. The results from this product align with previously published histories, although our work provides a more comprehensive representation of cropland management practices than previous works. Our data set is available on Dryad under public domain license (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23987242, Hoskovec, 2026) and can be used to inform studies of agricultural lands that evaluate processes such as greenhouse gas emissions, environmental impacts, and food production.

title: Accessing Stable Pyridinium Nanohoops with Low-Lying LUMOs by Pyridine-Directed C – H Activation
summary: Abstract Designing stable organic molecules with tailored electronic properties is key to advancing next-generation electronic materials. Cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) and related nanohoops have emerged as promising p-type semiconductors, yet
content: Abstract Designing stable organic molecules with tailored electronic properties is key to advancing next-generation electronic materials. Cycloparaphenylenes (CPPs) and related nanohoops have emerged as promising p-type semiconductors, yet their use as n-type materials remains limited due to inherently high-lying LUMO levels. While pyridine-containing CPPs can be alkylated to lower the LUMO, the resulting pyridinium species are often unstable and unsuitable for practical applications. In this study, we report two complementary synthetic strategies to access bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as stable, electron-accepting organic molecules. A bottom-up approach enables intramolecular cyclization to form the bridged architecture, confirming the stability of this new motif. To streamline access and facilitate structural diversification, we developed a second strategy employing pyridine-directed C–H activation─marking the first example of pyridine-directed C–H functionalization directly on the CPP backbone. The resulting pyridinium-functionalized nanohoops were thoroughly characterized. Electrochemical and spectroscopic studies revealed low reduction potentials (as low as −0.84 V) and red-shifted optical absorption edges for the doubly functionalized di(bridged-pyridinium)[10]CPP. Density functional theory calculations corroborate the observed trends in LUMO energies and support the utility of these molecules as electron-accepting building blocks. Together, these results establish bridged-pyridinium[n]CPPs as a new class of stable, tunable materials with potential for organic electronic applications.

title: The assembly and fate of a giant disc galaxy in a protocluster at z = 3
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Abstract Recent JWST observations revealed two massive (M⋆ ≳ 1011 M⊙), unexpectedly large spiral galaxies at z ∼ 3, both in overdense environments. We focus on one of these, ADF22.A1 at z = 3.09, which hosts an active galactic nucleus (AGN)
content: Abstract Recent JWST observations revealed two massive (M⋆ ≳ 1011 M⊙), unexpectedly large spiral galaxies at z ∼ 3, both in overdense environments. We focus on one of these, ADF22.A1 at z = 3.09, which hosts an active galactic nucleus (AGN), exploiting its extended [CII] emission (∼30 kpc in diameter) with high-resolution observations from the Atacama Large Millimetre Array and JWST. We find a flat outer rotation curve reaching ∼530 km s−1, and perform, for the first time for a system of this type, a rotation-curve decomposition. We infer a dark-matter halo mass of $\log (M_{200}/M_{\odot })=12.9^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$, a baryon-to-halo mass ratio of $0.4^{+0.6}_{-0.3}$ in units of the cosmological baryon fraction, and a ratio between the baryonic and dark-matter halo specific angular momentum of $1.0^{+0.7}_{-0.5}$. Comparing these quantities with those of local galaxies, we find that ADF22.A1 is indistinguishable from z = 0 giant discs, pointing to the inefficiency of AGN feedback in halting disc growth. Using the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory survey, we identify potential z = 0 descendants of ADF22.A1, suggesting it will evolve into an extreme (in either mass or angular momentum) early-type galaxy. Finally, we argue that cold-stream accretion, invoked to explain disc formation at z > 1, is disfavoured as the primary formation channel: while not formally excluded, it struggles to account simultaneously for the observed morphology, size, dynamical properties, high specific angular momentum, and baryon-to-halo mass ratio. Instead, sustained accretion from the hot circumgalactic medium offers a plausible, and possibly favoured, alternative.

title: Sheep grazing within regenerative perennial systems accelerates soil carbon and nitrogen accrual
summary: Abstract Background Global agricultural intensification and crop-livestock decoupling have reduced soil carbon and nitrogen stocks, weakening terrestrial carbon sinks and altering nutrient cycling. Integrating livestock into cropping system
content: Abstract Background Global agricultural intensification and crop-livestock decoupling have reduced soil carbon and nitrogen stocks, weakening terrestrial carbon sinks and altering nutrient cycling. Integrating livestock into cropping systems is a cornerstone regenerative practice, with the potential to enhance carbon and nitrogen storage. However, on-farm research quantifying outcomes of stacked regenerative production models remains limited, and it is unclear how grazing, alone or combined with other practices, affects soil carbon and nitrogen accrual. We assessed carbon and nitrogen stocks (0–60 cm), including mineral-associated and particulate organic matter pools, microbial biomass and plant productivity across 49 California (USA) vineyards spanning conventional to regenerative management, with and without sheep grazing. We evaluated the relative contributions of management practices to carbon and nitrogen pools, accounting for spatial and edaphic predictors, and estimated accrual rates from vineyards with differing management histories (space-for-time substitution). Results Grazing emerged as the most influential management practice for increasing soil organic matter pool stocks, followed by reduced physical disturbance and permanent ground cover. Other regenerative practices, including organic amendments and avoidance of synthetic insecticides, showed positive but more variable associations with soil organic matter pool stocks. Grazing was strongly associated with approximately fivefold higher nitrogen accrual rates (+ 0.04 ± 0.01 Mg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), including plant-available nitrogen (+ 0.94 ± 0.30 kg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), and more than threefold higher soil carbon accrual within regenerative management systems relative to conventional ungrazed systems (+ 0.38 ± 0.13 Mg ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹). Grazing was also associated with greater microbial biomass and plant productivity, consistent with enhanced carbon and nitrogen cycling. Conclusions Under grazing, greater nitrogen availability and more robust plant and microbial communities likely reduced microbial nitrogen limitation while enhancing carbon sequestration and stabilization. Geography and edaphic properties constrained soil carbon and nitrogen accumulation. These patterns proved robust across geographically independent farms, highlighting the value of multi-farm datasets for climate-mitigation assessments. These results demonstrate that integrating grazing within regenerative perennial systems can help meet mitigation targets while building nitrogen stocks and reducing synthetic fertilizer reliance. This underscores the importance of research on commercial operations for translating site-specific results into scalable, climate-smart farming strategies.

title: What two decades of environmental-economic accounting reveal about Guatemala's natural capital and governance
summary: Guatemala is one of the few developing countries to have kept the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) running for more than two decades without interruption. This paper draws together what those two decades produced and what
content: Guatemala is one of the few developing countries to have kept the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) running for more than two decades without interruption. This paper draws together what those two decades produced and what the experience teaches in terms of empirical findings and governance lessons, including the conditions in which SEEA informs policy in a developing country context. The SEEA revealed how much the economy depends on natural capital that conventional statistics fail to capture. Most indicators show that Guatemala has consumed its natural asset base rather than rebuilding it. The paper describes how a long partnership between government and academia turned these accounts into official statistics and put them to work in national planning and forest governance. Four conditions stand out as necessary for natural capital accounts to shape policy in a developing country: (i) the need for a stable institutional anchoring, (ii) a clear demand from live policy questions, (iii) a gradual build-up from simpler to more complex accounts, and (iv) capacity building within the institutions that produce the accounts. This path led the Central Bank of Guatemala to create a permanent environmental accounting unit inside its macroeconomic statistics department. Accounts will be published annually with a fully funded program within the Bank.

title: Niche constraints drive differences between mycorrhizal fungal guilds in future range shifts
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Mycorrhizal fungi are a diverse and ubiquitous group of plant symbionts whose distribution strongly influences ecosystem function across the globe. Yet, until now, we do not have quantitative data on the range sizes of different mycorrhizal
content: Mycorrhizal fungi are a diverse and ubiquitous group of plant symbionts whose distribution strongly influences ecosystem function across the globe. Yet, until now, we do not have quantitative data on the range sizes of different mycorrhizal fungal taxa, limiting our capacity to forecast future shifts in community composition and function. Here, we use 115,924 DNA sequence-derived observations to map the distribution of 651 common mycorrhizal fungal taxa and forecast future changes to their range sizes. We demonstrate that climate, plant cover, and soil factors, particularly mean annual temperature, net primary productivity, and soil organic carbon, exert major control over mycorrhizal fungal distributions. Based on these drivers, the ecological niches of mycorrhizal fungi consistently differ between arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal functional guilds. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal taxa generally occupy a wider niche breadth than ectomycorrhizal fungi, occurring across larger ranges of climate, soil, plant cover, topography, and disturbance conditions. Our models also predict widespread decreases in the suitable range size of mycorrhizal fungal taxa under projected future global climates, with average ranges decreasing by 13.8% or ~2.2 million km 2 under high emissions scenarios (ssp5-8.5). This decrease in projected range size will be most pronounced for ectomycorrhizal fungi, strongly linked to constraints from their smaller overall niches. By generating a global atlas of common mycorrhizal fungi and their associated environmental niche, we establish a critical baseline for widely suspected declines in global fungal biodiversity.

title: Internal conversion in functionalized poly-chlorinated trityl radicals can be tuned by a characteristic high-frequency mode
summary: We provide a theoretical analysis of trends in radiative losses by internal conversion (IC) in a series of doublet radical emitters and triplet diradicals derived from the poly-chlorinated trityl moiety. Minimizing radiative losses in these
content: We provide a theoretical analysis of trends in radiative losses by internal conversion (IC) in a series of doublet radical emitters and triplet diradicals derived from the poly-chlorinated trityl moiety. Minimizing radiative losses in these systems by molecular design is of current interest to opto-electronics and quantum technological approaches. Our results clearly indicate that IC in the doublet emitters as well as in different diradical architectures is governed by a characteristic high-frequency mode, which is associated with a quinoidal distortion. For the doublet emitters, we can establish that deliberate design allows to deactivate this mode as decay channel, resulting in a significantly reduced IC rate and an improved internal fluorescence quantum yield. We propose an analogous design principle for highly fluorescent triplet diradicals, and discuss the role of a high fluorescence efficiency in the context of quantum applications.

title: Interaction of novel imidazolium-based ionic liquids with cholinesterases: an in vitro and in silico evaluation
summary: Abstract The increasing demand for efficient and sustainable CO 2 capture technologies has driven the development of new ionic liquids (ILs) as potential alternatives to established sorbents. However, before large-scale industrial adoption,
content: Abstract The increasing demand for efficient and sustainable CO 2 capture technologies has driven the development of new ionic liquids (ILs) as potential alternatives to established sorbents. However, before large-scale industrial adoption, a comprehensive understanding of the toxicological profiles of these new ILs is essential to ensure human and environmental safety. Thus, in this study, we conducted a toxicological screening of nine imidazolium-based ILs (five previously reported, IL-1–IL-5, and four newly synthesized analogs, IL-6–IL-9), focusing on their inhibitory effects on the activity of human cholinesterase enzymes (acetylcholinesterase, AChE, and butyrylcholinesterase, BuChE). Initial screening at 40 µM revealed that, among the nine ILs, only IL 1-Dodecyl-3-methyl-2-(4-hydroxyphenyl) imidazolium iodide (IL-9), the dodecyl-substituted analog, inhibited human erythrocyte AChE (IC 50 = 3.64 µM) and plasma BuChE (IC 50 = 0.87 µM). When compared with compounds edrophonium and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), only edrophonium inhibited AChE activity (IC 50 = 3.03 µM), and neither edrophonium nor SDS inhibited BuChE considerably. Molecular docking simulations suggested that the long alkyl moiety of IL-9 stabilizes its interaction near the catalytic active site (CAS) and peripheral anionic subsite (PAS) of both AChE and BuChE. While shorter-chain ILs demonstrated no inhibitory effect, the cholinesterase inhibition exhibited by IL-9 indicates that elongating the alkyl chain intr​oduces significant neurotoxic risks. Consequently, future designs of imidazolium-based CO 2 sorbents must carefully balance these structural modifications to ensure environmental and occupational safety.

title: Quality by design development of folic acid–engineered berberine nanoliposomes for targeted triple-negative breast cancer therapy
summary: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains one of the most challenging breast cancer subtypes due to the lack of actionable molecular targets and the systemic toxicity associated with standard chemotherapy. Berberine chloride (BB
content: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains one of the most challenging breast cancer subtypes due to the lack of actionable molecular targets and the systemic toxicity associated with standard chemotherapy. Berberine chloride (BBR), a plant-derived isoquinoline alkaloid, exhibits promising anticancer activity; however, its poor solubility and limited bioavailability restrict therapeutic utility. In this study, folic acid–decorated nanoliposomes were developed to enhance the targeted delivery of BBR to TNBC cells. BBR-loaded liposomes and folic acid–functionalized liposomes were prepared using the solvent injection method and optimized through a Quality-by-Design (QbD) framework. The optimized folate-modified formulation showed a mean particle size of 168.3 nm with an entrapment efficiency of 41.8%, while non-targeted liposomes exhibited a smaller size (95.6 nm) and slightly higher drug loading (47.5%). Both systems provided sustained drug release over 72 hours, with folate-decorated liposomes demonstrating a more controlled release pattern. Cytotoxicity studies in MDA-MB-231 cells revealed significantly enhanced antiproliferative activity of folate-functionalized nanoliposomes (IC₅₀ = 24.72 μM) compared to non-targeted liposomes and free BBR. Increased intracellular reactive oxygen species generation following folate-mediated delivery suggested oxidative stress–driven cell death as a contributing mechanism. Importantly, genotoxicity evaluation using Drosophila melanogaster confirmed the safety of the liposomal formulations. Overall, folic acid–decorated nanoliposomes substantially improve the therapeutic efficacy of berberine and offer a rational, targeted nanocarrier approach for TNBC management.

title: Digitalization, renewable energy transition and the environmental Kuznets curve in GCC economies
summary: This study examines how economic growth, energy use, renewable energy, digitalization, urbanization, trade openness, industrial structure, and oil dependence are associated with per-capita CO 2 emissions in the six Gulf Cooperation Council
content: This study examines how economic growth, energy use, renewable energy, digitalization, urbanization, trade openness, industrial structure, and oil dependence are associated with per-capita CO 2 emissions in the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) economies over 2005–2024. The analysis integrates the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC), STIRPAT, and Ecological Modernization Theory and applies two-way fixed effects with year controls, a formal Lind–Mehlum U-test, Mundlak correlated random effects, panel-corrected standard errors, Method of Moments Quantile Regression, unit-root diagnostics, an energy-exclusion model, and 1-year-lagged regressors. The results support a conditional, sample-specific Inverted-U relationship between income and per-capita CO 2 emissions, with an estimated turning point of approximately US$33,939 per capita (95% CI: US$23,385–US$44,493). The estimate lies within the observed income range but is imprecise and should not be interpreted as a universal development threshold. Energy use is the most consistently positive correlate of emissions across specifications. Renewable energy is negatively associated with emissions in the fixed-effects, energy-exclusion, and lagged models, while digitalization is negative in the main and quantile estimates but weaker in the lagged specification. Urbanization and trade show greater estimator sensitivity, and oil rents and industrial structure lack stable independent effects. Overall, the findings indicate that GCC decarbonization depends on structural transformation of energy and technology systems rather than income growth alone, emphasizing renewable integration, energy efficiency, and digitally enabled low-carbon infrastructure.

title: Unveiling the wide-temperature tribological mechanisms of (MgCoNiCuZn)O high-entropy oxide: The critical role of dynamic CuO precipitation and redissolution
summary: Abstract Rock-salt-structured (MgCoNiCuZn)O high-entropy oxide (HEO) ceramics exhibit great potential for high-temperature applications, yet their tribological behavior across a wide temperature range remains to be fully deciphered. This wo
content: Abstract Rock-salt-structured (MgCoNiCuZn)O high-entropy oxide (HEO) ceramics exhibit great potential for high-temperature applications, yet their tribological behavior across a wide temperature range remains to be fully deciphered. This work systematically investigated the wide-temperature tribological mechanisms of (MgCoNiCuZn)O from room temperature (RT) to 800 °C. The results indicate that the hardness and wear resistance of HEO displayed a nonmonotonic dependence on temperature while simultaneously demonstrating a reversible entropy-driven phase transition. At 400 °C, thermodynamic instability triggered CuO precipitation, which disrupted the high-entropy structure and led to a significant degradation in hardness and an increased wear rate. However, at the elevated temperature of 800 °C, an entropy-driven redissolution of CuO partially restores the high-entropy structure, leading to a recovery in hardness. Concurrently, a continuous, lubricious oxide film was formed on the worn surface. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the low binding energy and high electron activity of CuO underlie its preferential precipitation and its key role in forming the Cu-rich oxide lubricating film. The synergy between phase restabilization and surface film formation results in excellent high-temperature wear resistance, with a minimum wear rate of approximately 0.53×10−5 mm3·N−1·m−1 at 800 °C. This work elucidates the phase evolution and tribological mechanisms of HEO across a wide temperature range, providing valuable guidance for designing advanced wear-resistant materials for extreme environments.

title: Aligning mitigation incentives across technologies under the Paris Agreement's Article 6.4 mechanism
summary: This article examines the incentive structure of the Paris Agreement’s Article 6.4 mechanism and document systematic misalignment of incentives across mitigation technologies and regions. Using project-level data, we estimate levelized emis
content: This article examines the incentive structure of the Paris Agreement’s Article 6.4 mechanism and document systematic misalignment of incentives across mitigation technologies and regions. Using project-level data, we estimate levelized emissions reduction costs across a wide range of mitigation activities and analyze their distributions. A machine-learning clustering algorithm classifies projects into seven global cost clusters, from which we derive relative weights per unit of emissions reduction.Our analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity in mitigation costs across technologies and locations. Yet observed deployment and credit issuance patterns are poorly aligned with these differences. High-cost projects account for a disproportionate share of credits relative to lower-cost activities. Across renewable categories, higher-cost projects issue fewer credits, revealing persistent incentive asymmetries. Estimated relative weights differ sharply across clusters, indicating that emissions reductions from high-cost technologies warrant proportionally greater support. Results are robust across alternative specifications.The findings underscore the importance of accounting for both cost and geographic heterogeneity in the design of climate finance under Article 6.4. By providing a transparent, data-driven, and flexible weighting tool, the framework offers policymakers a practical instrument to improve incentive alignment, maintain technological and regional diversity, and strengthen the integrity and effectiveness of global carbon markets.

title: Volatile dialogues between plants and microorganisms
summary: Covering: up to 2026Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are key mediators of long-distance communication in biological systems. While their roles in plant-insect interactions are well established, emerging evidence highlights their importance
content: Covering: up to 2026Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are key mediators of long-distance communication in biological systems. While their roles in plant-insect interactions are well established, emerging evidence highlights their importance in plant-microbe interactions. In this highlight, we discuss the biosynthesis and ecological functions of plant VOCs (pVOCs) and their impact on microbiome assembly and function. We examine how constitutive and stress-induced pVOCs shape microbial community composition and how microbial VOCs (mVOCs) influence plant growth and defense by modulating hormonal and metabolic pathways. We further address the bidirectional nature of volatile-mediated interactions and the challenges associated with studying complex VOC blends in natural environments. Understanding these dynamic volatile dialogues provides new opportunities for microbiome engineering and sustainable crop production.

title: High roughness and porosity of indoor surfaces increases sorption capacity and may impact indoor air quality
summary: Surface properties impact indoor gas-surface interactions and thus indoor air quality. Specific surface area impacts sorption capacity, while pores increase diffusion and storage in the bulk material. We measured roughness, porosity, and sp
content: Surface properties impact indoor gas-surface interactions and thus indoor air quality. Specific surface area impacts sorption capacity, while pores increase diffusion and storage in the bulk material. We measured roughness, porosity, and specific surface area of eleven common indoor surfaces and calculate the sorption capacity of an authentic office space. The specific surface area of the office is four orders of magnitude greater than the geometric surface area typically considered in indoor studies. Paint decreases the specific surface area for wood and drywall. Due to the substantial sorption capacity, surface films may be patchworks of organic and water-rich layers instead of spatially-ubiquitous, multilayer organic films on top of all indoor surfaces. The pores within surfaces can enhance diffusion resulting in different bulk diffusion equilibration timescales for different surfaces with ceiling tile, carpet and wood require longer timescales (up to years) to equilibrate. Thus, easily cleaned dust and surface films can increase short-term uptake of gas-phase contaminants then be removed to reduce re-emission; however, those contaminants may still penetrate deeper into the indoor building material that cannot be removed by surface cleaning. More solid surfaces with lower sorption capacity and longer diffusive timescales improve air quality in the long term by decreasing the gas-phase contaminants stored on surfaces that can be later re-emitted. Our results imply that building material selection may decrease long-term exposure to wildfire smoke or other air pollutants.

title: Uso de GeoAI e Sensoriamento Remoto Multimodal no Monitoramento da Biodiversidade Amazônica: Uma Revisão Sistemática
summary: A Amazônia desempenha papel fundamental na manutenção da biodiversidade global e na regulação climática, porém sofre crescentes pressões relacionadas ao desmatamento, degradação florestal e mudanças no uso da terra. Nesse contexto, o presen
content: A Amazônia desempenha papel fundamental na manutenção da biodiversidade global e na regulação climática, porém sofre crescentes pressões relacionadas ao desmatamento, degradação florestal e mudanças no uso da terra. Nesse contexto, o presente estudo teve como objetivo realizar uma revisão sistemática da literatura científica sobre aplicações de GeoAI, sensoriamento remoto multimodal e inteligência artificial no monitoramento da biodiversidade amazônica. A revisão foi conduzida conforme as recomendações do protocolo PRISMA 2020, com buscas realizadas nas bases Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, PubMed e IEEE Xplore. Após aplicação dos critérios de inclusão e exclusão, 35 estudos foram selecionados para análise. Os resultados evidenciaram predominância de aplicações voltadas ao monitoramento de desmatamento, biomassa, degradação florestal e estrutura da vegetação, utilizando principalmente redes neurais convolucionais, aprendizado profundo e integração entre sensores ópticos, LiDAR, SAR e drones/UAS. Observou-se crescimento expressivo das publicações após 2020, associado à ampliação de abordagens multimodais e plataformas geoespaciais em nuvem. Os estudos demonstraram elevado desempenho analítico na detecção de padrões ambientais complexos, embora persistam limitações relacionadas à heterogeneidade metodológica, disponibilidade de dados rotulados e validação externa dos modelos. Conclui-se que a GeoAI apresenta elevado potencial estratégico para fortalecer o monitoramento ambiental amazônico e subsidiar ações de conservação, manejo florestal e planejamento territorial.

The results demonstrate that mechanistic emission modelling can help address uncertainty in chemical emission rate estimates and inform decision-making for chemical safety and sustainability.

title: Impacts of combined ambitious marine and terrestrial carbon dioxide removal on major ocean stressors
summary: Abstract Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation are major stressors impacting marine ecosystems. While Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) is necessary to meet climate targets, its potential to mitigate ocean stressors under realistic fut
content: Abstract Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation are major stressors impacting marine ecosystems. While Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) is necessary to meet climate targets, its potential to mitigate ocean stressors under realistic future scenarios remains understudied. Here, we use two Earth System Models to simulate ambitious deployments of Afforestation/Reforestation (AR) and Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) under the high emissions scenario SSP3-7.0. Six experiments with varying CDR magnitude and combination are analyzed. Combined AR and OAE robustly mitigates acidification, deoxygenation and warming, while mitigation on primary production and nitrate declines remains undetectable. Not all mitigation responses scale linearly with carbon removal due to the complex nonlinear interactions among ocean circulation, carbonate chemistry, and biological processes. The early detectability of pH mitigation signal highlights its value for CDR monitoring. Inter-model differences in subsurface oxygen responses appear to be closely linked to differences in mean-state ocean circulation and ventilation. These findings demonstrate that ambitious CDR can measurably alleviate ocean stress, while underscoring that emissions reductions remain essential to limit climate change impacts on marine ecosystems.

title: A Carbon-Linked Trade Finance Framework: A Multidimensional Shadow-Pricing Model for Decarbonizing the Fertilizer Supply Chain
summary: Fertilizer traders face converging pressure from border carbon adjustment regulation and the decarbonization of maritime logistics, yet the price of their trade finance rarely reflects supply-chain carbon intensity. This paper develops a mu
content: Fertilizer traders face converging pressure from border carbon adjustment regulation and the decarbonization of maritime logistics, yet the price of their trade finance rarely reflects supply-chain carbon intensity. This paper develops a multidimensional shadow pricing model that links the cost of trade finance to verified emissions for an anonymized fertilizer trader. Using the firm’s operational shipment records, verified border-adjustment emissions data, maritime emission factors and questionnaire evidence from two banks, the study quantifies logistics emissions across eight shipping corridors, product-level border-adjustment liability to 2034, and the financing consequences of a tiered sustainability-linked structure. In the case studied, avoided border-adjustment cost from shifting to lower-carbon suppliers greatly exceeds the financing margin differential; the participating banks preferred verified over narrative disclosures; and data collection and bank engagement appear best pursued together, not sequentially. The framework may be adaptable, subject to further validation, to other commodity traders with border carbon exposure.

title: Exploring the Origin of Slow-rotating Pulsars: Emission from STARS Simulated White Dwarfs
summary: Abstract An increasing number of slow-rotating pulsars and long-period transients have been observed in recent years. The periods of these sources can be significantly longer than typical pulsar sources, ranging from ∼100 to 1000 s, or even
content: Abstract An increasing number of slow-rotating pulsars and long-period transients have been observed in recent years. The periods of these sources can be significantly longer than typical pulsar sources, ranging from ∼100 to 1000 s, or even longer. The observed periods and period derivatives predict high magnetic fields, higher than the Schwinger field, when we consider conventional pulsar models of dipole-driven emission from neutron stars. Interestingly, the periods of these sources are consistent with the current observations of white dwarfs (WDs). We explore the possibility of magnetic WDs, simulated using the stellar evolution code STARS , as the origin of some of these unusual pulsar observations. We simulate WDs with enhanced magnetic fields due to accretion after their formation. We also briefly touch on the more exotic possibility of super-Chandrasekhar WDs as the origin for these sources. We find that expanding the parameter space to include the possibility of a WD origin provides an alternate and viable explanation for these unusual observations.

title: Effects of hydrological changes on the sources and optical properties of dissolved organic matter in wetlands of the middle reaches of the Yellow River
summary: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) in riverine wetlands is the core carrier of the carbon cycle. However, the dynamics of DOM in large riverine wetlands subject to anthropogenic hydrological regulation remain poorly understood, and the differen
content: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) in riverine wetlands is the core carrier of the carbon cycle. However, the dynamics of DOM in large riverine wetlands subject to anthropogenic hydrological regulation remain poorly understood, and the differences in DOM composition and sources among hydrological periods are still unclear. In this study, water samples were collected from the riparian wetland in the Wuzhi section of the middle reaches of the Yellow River during the dry season (DS), normal season (NS), water-sediment regulation scheme (WSRS), and wet season (WS). Ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) absorption spectroscopy and excitation-emission matrix (EEM) spectroscopy, combined with parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC), were used to characterize the composition and sources of DOM across hydrological periods. Two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy (2D-COS) was applied to reveal the ordered pattern of DOM fluorescent components along the flow direction. The results showed that DOM content, composition, and sources differed among periods. DOC concentration was highest during the WSRS, followed by that during the WS, and was lower during the DS and NS. Three components were identified. Humic-like components C1 and C3 peaked in the WS, whereas the protein-like component C2 peaked in the DS. Within the same season, the water-sediment regulation event caused a significant change in the fluorescence intensity of C2. Spectral parameters indicated that DOM in the WS may have been influenced by terrestrial and autochthonous sources, while autochthonous contributions appeared to be stronger in the other periods. 2D-COS analysis revealed an ordered pattern of DOM fluorescent components along the flow direction, following the sequence protein-like → microbial humic-like → terrestrial humic-like components. This pattern may be influenced by multiple processes including tributary input, agricultural runoff, and sediment release. This study helps to address the limited understanding of DOM dynamics in wetlands under hydrological disturbance and provides baseline data for interpreting the compositional changes and along flow variation patterns of DOM in riparian wetlands across hydrological periods.

title: Embodied multisensory immersive experiences: a perspective into emerging threats and possible solutions
summary: Multisensory immersive virtual reality experiences, encompassing audio, visual, haptic, and/or digital smells and tastes, have been shown to enhance a user’s sense of immersion and embodiment, leading to improved experiences, task performan
content: Multisensory immersive virtual reality experiences, encompassing audio, visual, haptic, and/or digital smells and tastes, have been shown to enhance a user’s sense of immersion and embodiment, leading to improved experiences, task performances, and even clinical outcomes. While the great majority of published works tend to highlight the benefits of such embodied experiences, in this perspective-style paper, we shed light on emerging threats that are often overlooked in the literature. Here, we group these threats into four categories: discomfort, safety, privacy and security, and societal issues. We give examples of such threat vectors and discuss potential solutions. Overall, it is hoped that this perspective will help raise awareness of these emerging threats, such that solutions can be developed from the ground up for future embodied experiences.

title: Toward Transferable Descriptors Linking Formation and Environmental Effects of Microplastic-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter
summary: Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is increasingly recognized as an active product of plastic weathering; however, its environmental effects remain difficult to compare or predict. A major problem is the absence of varia
content: Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is increasingly recognized as an active product of plastic weathering; however, its environmental effects remain difficult to compare or predict. A major problem is the absence of variables that can maintain comparable mechanistic meaning across formation and effect studies. To address this gap, we propose a descriptor-based conceptual framework that uses measurable MP-DOM properties as transferable intermediates. Within this framework, using descriptors as a transferable and standardized language, spanning quantity, optical properties, molecular composition, and reactivity, can bridge diverse weathering conditions with downstream environmental effects. Using E2/E3, defined as the absorbance ratio at 250 and 365 nm, as a representative example, we demonstrate how an optical descriptor can connect MP-DOM formation processes with photochemical reactivity and contaminant photodegradation through its relationship with singlet oxygen generation. This framework highlights the need for transferable descriptors as a standardized framework for MP-DOM, providing a foundation for cross-study comparison, mechanistic integration, and predictive assessment of MP-DOM fate and environmental effects.

title: A bio-digital circular framework for sustainable duck feed production using agro-industrial side-streams and aquatic biomass
summary: Abstract The poultry sector faces increasing environmental and economic pressures associated with agro-industrial by-product accumulation, dependence on conventional feed ingredients, and feed-supply logistics. This study developed the SHIR
content: Abstract The poultry sector faces increasing environmental and economic pressures associated with agro-industrial by-product accumulation, dependence on conventional feed ingredients, and feed-supply logistics. This study developed the SHIREEM framework, a bio-digital circular approach for the valorization of Snack Food Industry By-products (SFIB) and aquatic biomass ( Azolla pinnata and Spirulina platensis ) in poultry feed production. The framework integrates IoT-assisted process monitoring, computational feed optimization, machine-learning prediction, and circular resource-utilization principles. An IoT-assisted pelleting system incorporating a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and real-time sensors was used to monitor and control processing conditions, while a Python-based Least-Cost Ration (LCR) model optimized feed formulations under predefined nutritional and economic constraints. Under the simulated conditions, the optimized formulation reduced the estimated feed production cost from approximately 22,000 to 12,450 EGP ton⁻¹ (43.4%) and reduced logistics-related CO₂ emissions by 93.8% within the defined assessment boundary. Machine-learning models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, with Gradient Boosting providing the best prediction of body weight and Extra-Trees providing the best prediction of feed conversion ratio among the evaluated models. Feature-importance analysis indicated that age and metabolizable energy were major predictors of growth-related performance, whereas Azolla inclusion showed a greater contribution to feed conversion ratio than to body weight prediction. In addition, 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulation indicated that the economic performance of the optimized system remained feasible across the majority of the simulated uncertainty scenarios, with SFIB cost and transportation expenditure identified as important cost drivers. Overall, the results support the potential of SHIREEM as an integrated computational framework for circular feed-resource utilization and localized production. However, the findings represent a computational proof-of-concept and require experimental and commercial-scale validation before biological, environmental, and economic performance can be generalized to practical poultry production systems. To support regional adoption, agricultural policymakers could consider developing appropriate quality-certification frameworks for bio-based feed resources and supportive policy mechanisms that facilitate the responsible upcycling of locally available agro-industrial residues into animal feed.

title: The Use of ESG in Facilitating Eco-Innovation Via Green Innovation: Approaching the Moderated Mediation Role of Top Manager’s Environmental Awareness
summary: Abstract Eco-innovation drives environmental sustainability and creates new economic opportunities, yet how Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance shapes the eco-innovation process remains underexplored. Grounded in the Res
content: Abstract Eco-innovation drives environmental sustainability and creates new economic opportunities, yet how Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance shapes the eco-innovation process remains underexplored. Grounded in the Resource-Based View (RBV), we argue that ESG constitutes a strategic resource that fosters Green Innovation (GI), which in turn facilitates Eco-innovation (EI). Building on Upper Echelons Theory (UET), we further examine how Top Manager’s Environmental Awareness (TMEA) moderates this mediating pathway. Survey data were collected from 371 participants across 29 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in China. Results indicate that ESG exerts both a direct effect on EI and an indirect effect through the partial mediating role of GI. Moreover, TMEA significantly moderates the mediated relationship from ESG to EI via GI. These findings integrate RBV and UET to elucidate the ESG–EI nexus, and provide practical implications for SMEs seeking to leverage ESG engagement and leadership environmental awareness for sustainable innovation.

title: Seafood: processing, preservation, nutrition, marketing, and policy
summary: Abstract Seafood is an essential component of the global diet and economy, with diverse species and products contributing to the nutrition and well-being of populations worldwide. This paper provides a comprehensive review of key aspects re
content: Abstract Seafood is an essential component of the global diet and economy, with diverse species and products contributing to the nutrition and well-being of populations worldwide. This paper provides a comprehensive review of key aspects related to seafood, including processing, preservation, nutrition, marketing, and policy. The processing of seafood involves traditional techniques such as frozen and ultracold, and some new techniques such as high pressure, plasma, pasteurization, which are crucial for maintaining product quality and extending shelf life. Furthermore, the nutritional value of seafood, rich in proteins, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals, is discussed in detail, highlighting the health benefits associated with seafood consumption. The marketing of seafood products involves strategies for promoting and distributing these products to consumers, addressing consumer preferences, trends, and sustainability concerns. Finally, the paper explores the policy aspects related to seafood, including food safety standards, and sustainability initiatives, emphasizing the importance of policy frameworks in ensuring the responsible management of seafood resources.

title: Rising demand for vegetables and fruits reshaped subnational food flows and transport emissions in China
summary: Surging consumption of vegetables and fruits increased dietary diversity and nutritional quality, yet its implications for subnational food mobility and transport emissions remain largely overlooked. Here we simulate 2.9 million city-level
content: Surging consumption of vegetables and fruits increased dietary diversity and nutritional quality, yet its implications for subnational food mobility and transport emissions remain largely overlooked. Here we simulate 2.9 million city-level food flows for 24 crops across China between 1990 and 2020 by integrating spatially explicit supply-demand data, multimodal transport networks, and carbon emission accounting. Results show that food flows increased by 183.5% (from 276 Mt to 782 Mt), with vegetables and fruits accounting for over 80% of this growth, reshaping food flow networks from grain-dominated structures toward more fragmented and spatially extensive configurations. Correspondingly, transport-related emissions rose nearly ninefold, with vegetable transport contributing the largest absolute increase (from 1.1 to 17.6 Mt CO 2 e). Scenario analysis reveals that rising vegetables and fruits consumption contributed more to emission growth than population growth and changing grain demand combined. These findings highlight perishable supply chains as a critical yet underexplored source of emissions.
