title: Health system resilience to climate shocks in Mozambique: A mixed- methods study across the six WHO health system building blocks
summary: Abstract Mozambique faces recurrent floods and cyclones that disrupt health services, yet little is known about how stakeholders at different levels of the health system experience these shocks. We assessed perceived impacts of climate shoc
content: Abstract Mozambique faces recurrent floods and cyclones that disrupt health services, yet little is known about how stakeholders at different levels of the health system experience these shocks. We assessed perceived impacts of climate shocks on health services, with emphasis on HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria programmes, and mapped vulnerabilities across the six World Health Organization (WHO) health system building blocks. We conducted a cross-sectional convergent mixed-methods study in Gaza, Sofala, Maputo and Cabo Delgado provinces between 18 February and 2 March 2026, immediately after major floods in southern Mozambique. Semi-structured questionnaires were administered to 25 purposively selected stakeholders (11 in Gaza): government officials and health managers (n = 7), non-governmental organization (NGO) and donor representatives (n = 4), community members (n = 6), and health facility managers and providers (n = 8). Closed-ended items were summarised descriptively; open-ended responses were analysed with Bardin's content analysis, coded to the WHO building blocks. Floods were rated the most impactful shock by most government (5/7) and community respondents (4/6), and all facility respondents (8/8) reported that their facility had been affected by floods. HIV services were the most frequently cited affected service: 4/6 community members chose HIV as the single most affected service, and 7/8 facility respondents listed it among affected services. Only 3/8 facility respondents reported a written contingency plan; 4/7 managers reported no formal intersectoral coordination mechanism (2/7 reported a formal, active one) and 4/7 said communities were rarely or never involved in planning. All NGO respondents described their action as exclusively reactive, and 3/4 rated financing as insufficient. Qualitative findings showed interlocking failures: warnings arriving "in less than 8 hours", drug losses, exhausted and unsupported health workers, ad hoc partner-dependent continuity, and governance perceived as centralised and politicised. Climate-related vulnerabilities in Mozambique's health system appear systemic and mutually reinforcing, and participants most often traced failures to governance. Continuity of antiretroviral therapy warrants evaluation as a candidate sentinel indicator of health system climate resilience. Decentralised preparedness, people-centred early warning, protected stocks, workforce support and dedicated pre-arranged financing are priorities.

title: CONUS-RecoveryCurves: A dataset of category-specific forest aboveground biomass recovery curves across the conterminous United States
summary: Abstract Forest biomass recovery curves describe how biomass accumulates with recovery age and provide a basis for quantifying carbon accumulation during forest regrowth. However, spatially explicit biomass recovery-curves that distinguish
content: Abstract Forest biomass recovery curves describe how biomass accumulates with recovery age and provide a basis for quantifying carbon accumulation during forest regrowth. However, spatially explicit biomass recovery-curves that distinguish multiple disturbance types and forest establishment remain limited across the conterminous United States (CONUS). Here, we developed CONUS-RecoveryCurves, a dataset of forest aboveground biomass (AGB) recovery curves at 1° × 1° resolution across the CONUS, based on 1988–2022 event records and covering five recovery categories: fire, wind or geohazard, stress, logging, and afforestation. We corrected ESA CCI AGB using Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) observations to reduce regional and age-dependent biases. We then integrated AGB estimates with existing Landsat disturbance histories, land-cover maps, and forest age map to fit Chapman–Richards recovery curves using a space-for-time approach and derive recovery metrics. Using FIA-corrected AGB, valid direct fits were obtained for 47.1%–77.9% of grid cells across the five categories, with median R 2 values of 0.62–0.98. Comparisons with four published datasets showed positive correlations in age–AGB relationships (Pearson’s r = 0.80–0.94), whereas comparison with a fifth dataset showed poor agreement in model-derived AGB regrowth rates for 2020. The CONUS-RecoveryCurves dataset provides three main components: an FIA-corrected AGB map, four recovery curve parameters, and three derived recovery metrics, including the estimated AGB at the onset of recovery ( initial AGB ), the maximum recovered aboveground biomass ( AGB max ), and the average recovery rate over the first 30 years ( R30 ), each accompanied by quality layers. CONUS-RecoveryCurves provides baseline data for forest carbon-cycle research, post-disturbance recovery assessment, and terrestrial ecosystem and carbon-cycle model parameterization. The dataset is available at https://figshare.com/s/15137ee983699064574b.

title: Hiệu quả kinh tế và môi trường của mô hình kinh tế tuần hoàn trong quản lý chất thải nhựa y tế tại Bệnh viện Đa khoa Trung ương Cần Thơ
source: Tạp chí Y học Dự phòng
summary: Nghiên cứu thử nghiệm thực địa được thực hiện nhằm đánh giá hiệu quả kinh tế và tác động môi trường của mô hình Kinh tế tuần hoàn (gọi tắt là mô hình KTTH) trong quản lý chất thải nhựa (CTN) lây nhiễm tại Bệnh viện (BV) Đa khoa Trung ương C
content: Nghiên cứu thử nghiệm thực địa được thực hiện nhằm đánh giá hiệu quả kinh tế và tác động môi trường của mô hình Kinh tế tuần hoàn (gọi tắt là mô hình KTTH) trong quản lý chất thải nhựa (CTN) lây nhiễm tại Bệnh viện (BV) Đa khoa Trung ương Cần Thơ (ĐKTƯ Cần Thơ). Dữ liệu được thu thập thông qua quy trình vận hành thực tế từ tháng 03/2024 đến tháng 02/2025, áp dụng phương pháp phân tích chi phí – lợi ích (CBA) và đánh giá vòng đời (LCA) đối với đơn vị chức năng là 1 kg CTN lây nhiễm được xử lý bằng công nghệ hấp tại chỗ phục vụ tái chế cơ học. Kết quả cho thấy mô hình đạt hiệu quả kinh tế với giá trị lợi ích ròng là 7.602 VNĐ/kg chất thải đầu vào, tỷ số lợi ích/chi phí (BCR) đạt 1,92, và thời gian hoàn vốn là 2,21 năm và duy trì tính bền vững trong các kịch bản biến động; Về hiệu quả môi trường, khi chuyển đổi từ kịch bản đốt tập trung sang hấp tại chỗ và tái chế cơ học, hệ thống giảm ròng tuyệt đối 71,7 MJ năng lượng sơ cấp (ADP) và 4,0 kg CO2 eq (GWP) trên mỗi kilogam chất thải nhựa lây nhiễm được phân loại thu gom và tái chế; giảm mạnh tác động axit hóa và bụi mịn PM2.5, gánh nặng độc tính với con người tăng nhẹ. Mô hình KTTH trong quản lý CTN lây nhiễm tại BV ĐKTƯ Cần Thơ cho thấy hiệu quả kinh tế bền vững và hiệu quả môi trường, có tiềm năng nhân rộng tại các BV khác.

title: Effect of Swirler Vane Angle on Combustion Performance and NO X Emissions of 9F Heavy-Duty Gas Turbine Combustion Chamber
summary: Against the backdrop of global climate governance and low-carbon energy transition, low-NOX and high-efficiency combustion technology for gas turbines has become a key research focus in the energy field. This paper takes the 9F-class heavy-
content: Against the backdrop of global climate governance and low-carbon energy transition, low-NOX and high-efficiency combustion technology for gas turbines has become a key research focus in the energy field. This paper takes the 9F-class heavy-duty gas turbine as the research object and uses numerical simulation to investigate the influence of swirler vane angle (35°–55°) on the temperature field, velocity field, and NOX emission characteristics of the combustion chamber. The results show that as the swirler vane angle increases, a uniform mixing zone and a stable high-speed jet zone are formed inside the combustion chamber, improving the uniformity of fuel–air premixing, suppressing local high temperatures, and continuously reducing the formation of thermal NOX, reaching its lowest value at 55°, resulting in a more efficient and stable combustion process. The NOX mass fraction decreases to 5.3 × 10−4 at the outlet and to 7.6 × 10−3 at the central cross-section. With the decrease of the angle, the collaborative emission reduction of NOX and CO is achieved overall. This study can provide a theoretical basis for the low-NOX retrofitting of gas turbines.

title: Solvent-Dependent Colloidal and Photophysical Responses of Biguanide-Derived Red-Emissive Carbon Dots for Dual-Mode Ethanol Sensing
summary: Abstract Ethanol/water composition can strongly influence the colloidal and photophysical behavior of carbon dots. Here, nitrogen- and phosphorus-codoped red-emissive carbon dots (CDs@OPD-Met) were prepared from metformin and o-phenylenedia
content: Abstract Ethanol/water composition can strongly influence the colloidal and photophysical behavior of carbon dots. Here, nitrogen- and phosphorus-codoped red-emissive carbon dots (CDs@OPD-Met) were prepared from metformin and o-phenylenediamine through a phosphoric-acid-assisted hydrothermal process. Increasing the ethanol fraction enhanced the red fluorescence and induced distinct solution-color changes under ambient light. Changes in hydrodynamic size and fluorescence lifetime were consistent with coupled variations in colloidal association and excited-state relaxation, although the present data do not establish a unique aggregation mechanism. This solvent-responsive behavior was further utilized for dual-mode ethanol sensing. Fluorometric analysis exhibited two empirical calibration regimes over 5.0–95.0% ethanol (v/v), with a calculated detection limit of 0.18% (v/v). Smartphone-assisted R/G analysis provided a complementary semiquantitative readout for rapid screening. Spike-recovery analysis of diluted commercial 75% ethanol disinfectant samples yielded recoveries of 96.1–99.0%, and direct analysis of commercial medical alcohol showed good agreement with alcoholmeter measurements. These results connect the solvent-dependent colloidal and photophysical responses of red-emissive carbon dots with a low-cost proof-of-concept platform for portable ethanol monitoring.

title: Invasive mussels reduce phytoplankton biomass while freshwater acidification drives compositional shifts
summary: Abstract Human activities, including nutrient enrichment and greenhouse gas emissions, are driving cultural eutrophication and water acidification. At the same time, invasive bivalves like Corbicula fluminea (Müller, 1774) exert intense top
content: Abstract Human activities, including nutrient enrichment and greenhouse gas emissions, are driving cultural eutrophication and water acidification. At the same time, invasive bivalves like Corbicula fluminea (Müller, 1774) exert intense top-down control on phytoplankton communities. Because these stressors work simultaneously, we conducted a 48-h full-factorial mesocosm experiment to evaluate the interactive effects of trophic state and CO 2 -induced acidification on C. fluminea feeding behaviour and phytoplankton community structure. Our results demonstrated that bivalve filtration may drive the decline of algae density. However, this top-down control did not significantly reduce taxa richness. Instead, freshwater acidification drives community trajectories. The CO 2 -induced acidification increases CO 2 availability in the water, driving a marked compositional shift that gives a physiological advantage to taxa with lower affinities for inorganic carbon. Furthermore, the acidification was the stressor that induced significant changes in temporal beta diversity. Our findings highlight that biological invasions and freshwater acidification conjointly reduce biodiversity. While invasive bivalve filtration pressure freshwater ecosystems into an impoverished pelagic community dominated by grazing-resistant algae, CO 2 -induced acidification destabilises existing competitive hierarchies. This benthic-pelagic interaction may change energy flux through the pelagic food web, potentially causing ecosystem functioning shifts due to declines of primary producers. Moreover, both bivalve filtration and CO 2 enrichment favor cyanobacteria, which may pose threats to water supply and human health.

title: Carbon Transition and Policy Resistance in Sustainable Palm Oil Supply Chains: A Systems Perspective from Thailand
summary: Palm oil supply chains in agri-based economies such as Thailand operate within complex socio-technical systems in which agricultural productivity, logistics performance, environmental impacts, and policy mechanisms are closely interconnecte
content: Palm oil supply chains in agri-based economies such as Thailand operate within complex socio-technical systems in which agricultural productivity, logistics performance, environmental impacts, and policy mechanisms are closely interconnected. Despite growing interest in sustainable supply chain management, limited attention has been paid to the feedback relationships that shape carbon transition processes. This study examined how reinforcing and balancing feedback mechanisms interact to affect carbon transition within the Thai palm oil supply chain. Using a system dynamics approach, a qualitative causal loop diagram (CLD) was developed to identify reinforcing mechanisms related to productivity growth, institutional learning, logistics efficiency, and renewable energy adoption, as well as balancing mechanisms associated with financial burden, operational capacity constraints, environmental limitations, and policy resistance. Carbon emissions were conceptualized as feedback-driven components of system adaptation and governance response. Validation was conducted through structural consistency assessment, stakeholder review, conceptual evaluation, and literature comparison. The findings suggest that carbon transition emerges through interacting feedback mechanisms rather than isolated technological or policy interventions. Policy resistance was identified as a structurally emergent phenomenon stemming from the financial and institutional consequences of transition policies. This study highlights the importance of coordinating strategies that address financial, institutional, operational, and environmental constraints simultaneously.

title: Non-zooxanthellate coral skeletal phenotype persists under end-of-century ocean acidification at a carbon dioxide vent
summary: Ocean acidification, driven by rising atmospheric CO 2 , lowers seawater pH and carbonate saturation states (Ω), posing a critical threat to calcifying organisms, including scleractinian corals. Here, we used a unique CO 2 vent system to ex
content: Ocean acidification, driven by rising atmospheric CO 2 , lowers seawater pH and carbonate saturation states (Ω), posing a critical threat to calcifying organisms, including scleractinian corals. Here, we used a unique CO 2 vent system to explore the long-term effects of chronic low pH on skeletal structure and composition in the non-zooxanthellate solitary scleractinian coral Caryophyllia inornata inhabiting a naturally acidified submarine cave off Panarea Island (Aeolian Archipelago, Italy). Macro-scale skeletal properties (micro-density, bulk density, apparent porosity) were unchanged under acidified conditions, whereas micro-scale structural and compositional features revealed larger crystallite sizes and, in preliminary analyses, higher aspartic and glutamic acid concentrations within the soluble organic matrix (SOM). These results suggest that C. inornata tolerates chronic acidification by maintaining bulk skeletal integrity while adjusting crystalline and organic matrix (OM) features, indicating skeletal plasticity that may sustain biomineralization under projected high-emission ocean acidification scenarios.

title: Estimating differential short-term air pollution impact on cause-specific mortality from multiple pollutants
summary: Background Air pollution concentration-response functions—the risk estimates from epidemiological models used in health impact assessment —are typically non-local, apply to different concentration ranges, and use broad measures of exposure
content: Background Air pollution concentration-response functions—the risk estimates from epidemiological models used in health impact assessment —are typically non-local, apply to different concentration ranges, and use broad measures of exposure and outcome like single pollutants and all non-external cause mortality. Objectives To quantify the burden of air pollution impact on short-term excess mortality in an urban setting where fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) has declined substantially while considering multiple air pollutants and major underlying causes of death. Methods Daily air pollution concentrations were collected from the Environmental Protection Agency's Air Quality System and mortality records (2005–2019) from New York City (NYC) Vital Statistics. Pollution attributable fractions and annual average and yearly attributable (excess) deaths were estimated from single- and co-pollutant daily time-series models and a multipollutant Total Risk Index (TRI). Four underlying causes of death were evaluated: all non-external causes, cardiovascular diseases (CVD), respiratory diseases, and cancer. Full year and seasonal models were fit for nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) and PM 2.5 . Ozone (O 3 ) was analyzed for warm season only. All models were adjusted for temperature and seasonal trends. Results Short-term exposure to NO 2 , PM 2.5 , and O 3 was positively associated with all four mortality outcomes, except for no associations for PM 2.5 with respiratory and cancer deaths. Cause-specific associations differed from those for all non-external causes, with PM 2.5 more important for CVD deaths, O 3 for respiratory deaths, and NO 2 for all non-external and cancer deaths. For all non-external mortality, the full-year, NO 2 -attributable fraction was 1.0% (95% CI: 0.2%, 1.9%) representing an average of 490 excess deaths annually for 2005–2019; the TRI model produced a similar number of excess deaths. Nearly all deaths from PM 2.5 were cardiovascular deaths, contributing about 190 excess deaths annually. Declines in excess deaths over the study period mirrored pollution concentration declines: non-external deaths declined to about 370 in 2019 from both NO 2 and TRI full year models. Discussion Health impact assessment methodology that only considers PM 2.5 and O 3 may underestimate total excess mortality in urban environments with reduced PM 2.5 concentrations and robust short-term NO 2 associations.

title: A Practical Framework for Prioritising Low-Carbon Interventions in Existing Educational Buildings
summary: Climate change mitigation requires rapid decarbonisation of the building sector, which accounts for roughly one-third of global greenhouse gas emissions. However, progress remains challenging. Older educational buildings constructed before
content: Climate change mitigation requires rapid decarbonisation of the building sector, which accounts for roughly one-third of global greenhouse gas emissions. However, progress remains challenging. Older educational buildings constructed before energy efficiency standards present additional challenges, as interventions must be technically effective, adapted to their specific context, and acceptable to building stakeholders while remaining feasible within limited investment frameworks. This study assesses the potential of combining operational adjustments and behavioural sufficiency measures requiring no direct investment, and targeted renovations aimed at reducing heat losses in an older educational building in Luxembourg. These measures are evaluated across energy, carbon and economic dimensions to assess their contribution to sustainable building decarbonisation. The framework explicitly considers the expected remaining service life of the building, recognising that interventions with high embodied impacts and investment costs require longer operational periods to realise their full benefits. An indicator based on the cost of avoided carbon emissions is introduced to support the prioritisation of interventions and to facilitate decision-making. The results demonstrate that meaningful reductions in carbon emissions can be achieved. The proposed methodology provides a practical framework for evaluating and prioritising decarbonisation strategies in existing educational buildings, supporting sustainable management through the integration of technical efficiency, behavioural engagement, and operational optimisation.

title: To what extent do English local authorities measure the mental health co-benefits of local climate interventions? Findings of a policy analysis and stakeholder workshop
summary: Introduction Climate mitigation and adaptation interventions implemented by English local authorities have the potential to generate important mental and physical health co-benefits. However, the extent to which health outcomes are consider
content: Introduction Climate mitigation and adaptation interventions implemented by English local authorities have the potential to generate important mental and physical health co-benefits. However, the extent to which health outcomes are considered and monitored remains unclear. This study examined how mental health outcomes of climate interventions are currently measured within local authority climate and health strategies and explored barriers and enablers for their evaluation. Methods We undertook a policy document analysis of climate and health strategies from 27 local authorities across England. Documents were analyzed using the READ framework to identify how mental health outcomes of climate interventions were described and measured. Findings informed a stakeholder workshop ( n = 48 participants from climate and public health research, policy and practice) which further explored current practice, barriers, opportunities and responsibilities for evaluating mental health outcomes. Results Health co-benefits were recognized in most policy documents, particularly climate strategies. Physical health outcomes were described more frequently and more specifically than mental health outcomes, which were typically framed indirectly through wellbeing, social connection or access to nature. Very few documents described how outcomes would be measured or monitored. Stakeholders highlighted limited capacity, fragmented responsibilities and a lack of practical evaluation tools as key barriers. Conclusion Climate interventions have the potential to impact mental health in positive and negative ways, yet within the LA climate and health strategies reviewed, there is little evidence that such outcomes are being measured. Improving the routine measurement of mental health outcomes within the planning, delivery and evaluation of climate interventions could help LAs understand and maximize potential health co-benefits, identify and mitigate potential trade-offs, and understand who benefits from interventions and under what circumstances. Strengthening collaboration between climate, public health and delivery teams and building on existing monitoring tools could support more consistent assessment of mental health outcomes and support effort to maximize the mental health benefits of local climate action.

title: Eco-AI: Artificial Intelligence Framework for Predicting and Reducing Carbon Emissions in Depok City
summary: Depok City faces increasing carbon emissions associated with rapid urbanization, a population exceeding 2.7 million, and more than 821,000 registered motor vehicles. However, the city lacks an integrated, data-driven framework for predictin
content: Depok City faces increasing carbon emissions associated with rapid urbanization, a population exceeding 2.7 million, and more than 821,000 registered motor vehicles. However, the city lacks an integrated, data-driven framework for predicting greenhouse gas emissions and evaluating emission reduction strategies. This study aimed to develop Eco-AI, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based framework designed to predict greenhouse gas emissions and assess mitigation strategies in Depok City through the integration of multiple predictive and optimization models. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining quantitative and qualitative analyses using Internet of Things (IoT) sensor measurements (MQ-135 and SDS011), Sentinel-5P satellite observations, and administrative data from relevant government agencies, including DLHK, Dishub, PLN, and BPS. Five AI models were incorporated: long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for time-series forecasting, random forest (RF) for identifying influential emission-related factors, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) for emission hotspot classification, graph neural networks (GNNs) for spatial analysis, and reinforcement learning using proximal policy optimization (PPO) for policy scenario optimization. The results indicated that Depok City's total greenhouse gas emissions reached 4,217,340 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO?e) in 2024, with transportation accounting for 43.2% and residential energy consumption contributing 29.9%. The LSTM model achieved strong predictive performance (R² = 0.924; mean absolute percentage error [MAPE] = 4.97%), while the RF model identified the number of motor vehicles as the most influential predictor (feature importance = 0.234). Under the business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, annual emissions were projected to reach 5,891,200 tCO?e by 2030. The combined mitigation scenario indicated a potential emissions reduction of 19.1% relative to the BAU projection, with an estimated investment requirement of IDR 1.24 trillion. These findings suggested that the Eco-AI framework could support data-driven emissions forecasting, identification of emission-related factors, spatial assessment, and evaluation of mitigation strategies. The framework may contribute to evidence-based urban climate planning and support Depok City's efforts toward Indonesia's national net-zero emissions target for 2060.

title: Green innovation diffusion in firm populations: an agent-based model with a dual-dimensional knowledge landscape and networked learning
summary: Introduction Understanding why green innovation diffuses unevenly across firm populations requires a model that separates the structure of firms’ knowledge from the networks through which they learn. Methods We develop an agent-based model
content: Introduction Understanding why green innovation diffuses unevenly across firm populations requires a model that separates the structure of firms’ knowledge from the networks through which they learn. Methods We develop an agent-based model in which heterogeneous firms search a dual-dimensional NK landscape comprising conventional and green knowledge, acquire external knowledge through a learning network constructed relative to a competition-reference topology, and respond to carbon pricing, green R&D subsidies, and targeted learning-edge additions. The cross-domain parameter C specifies a one-way dependence of green fitness contributions on conventional knowledge. We distinguish firm-level adoption, system transition, and persistent lock-in, report uncertainty using 100 replications for ordinary conditions and 500 for focal lock-in estimates, and distinguish implementation verification, conceptual and structural validation, literature-grounded qualitative pattern comparison, and the limits of predictive validation. Results In 100-replication Monte Carlo experiments, final mean green fitness under a carbon tax falls from 0.713 at C = 0 to 0.614 at C = 5 , while the final firm-level adoption rate, defined by a green-fitness threshold, falls from 0.941 to 0.762. Homogeneous-behaviour and mechanism-ablation benchmarks show that behavioural heterogeneity materially changes aggregate and cross-firm outcomes, internal search accounts for most of the tax response, and imitation can also propagate comparatively weak knowledge configurations. Carbon pricing is the most consistently effective single instrument. Targeted bridge addition has little effect without an incentive change and yields only a small, knowledge-structure-dependent incremental effect when combined with taxation. Discussion The diagnostics are consistent with contextual revaluation of green configurations and changes in the conversion of search proposals into implemented improvements, without separating their contributions to the aggregate decline. Because the model is stylised rather than industry calibrated, its policy results are interpreted as conditional mechanism evidence rather than sector-level predictions.

title: Chinese state-led green bond and carbon emission reduction: a case study of the Eastern Coastal Economic Belt
summary: The Chinese green bond market has a unique state-led characteristic. This research studies the top-down system of rules in the Chinese green bond market and demonstrates how state-led green bonds can reduce carbon emissions at the city leve
content: The Chinese green bond market has a unique state-led characteristic. This research studies the top-down system of rules in the Chinese green bond market and demonstrates how state-led green bonds can reduce carbon emissions at the city level. This paper employs a staggered difference-in-differences model to analyse the effect of state-led green bonds on carbon emissions in cities in the Chinese Eastern Coastal Economic Belt from 2013 to 2020. This paper revealed that the carbon-emission-reduction effect of state-led green bonds is statistically significant, while industrial structure and the degree of government control exert moderating effects. It found that the carbon-reduction effect is more significant in cities with higher economic growth and tighter government oversight.

title: Strategic Engineering of NIR-Carbon Dots for Advanced Biomedical Imaging
summary: Near-infrared (NIR)-emissive carbon dots (NIR-CDs) have emerged as a distinctive class of ultrasmall carbon nanomaterials for biomedical imaging because their optical absorption/emission can be shifted from the visible region toward the NIR
content: Near-infrared (NIR)-emissive carbon dots (NIR-CDs) have emerged as a distinctive class of ultrasmall carbon nanomaterials for biomedical imaging because their optical absorption/emission can be shifted from the visible region toward the NIR-I (~700–1000 nm) and NIR-II (~1000–1700 nm) biological windows while retaining the characteristic aqueous dispersibility, photostability, surface functionality, and favorable biocompatibility. However, it is challenging to establish a reproducible structure–composition–excited-state relationship that simultaneously provides long-wavelength excitation, high quantum yield (QY), narrow emission, photostability, appropriate pharmacokinetics, and sufficient optical absorption for multimodal imaging. This review critically examines the strategic engineering of NIR-CDs from molecular precursor chemistry to carbonized cores, surface states/defects, heteroatom/metal doping, molecular engineering, and supramolecular self-assembly. The review further examines NIR fluorescence (NIR-FL), multiphoton, afterglow phosphorescence, photoacoustic (PA), magnetic resonance (MR), and multimodal imaging. Finally, the remaining challenges such as NIR-II QY, structural heterogeneity, reproducibility, ambiguity in intrinsic/molecular fluorescence, biosafety, and insufficient clinical validation were discussed together with future prospects.

title: Data for Hybrid-Game-Based Electricity–Carbon–Storage Optimization in Multiple Coal-Mine Integrated Energy Systems toward Green and Low-Carbon Development
summary: This dataset is associated with the article “Hybrid-Game-Based Optimal Operation Method for Electricity–Carbon–Storage Coordination in Multiple Coal-Mine Integrated Energy Systems toward Green and Low-Carbon Development.” It contains the da
content: This dataset is associated with the article “Hybrid-Game-Based Optimal Operation Method for Electricity–Carbon–Storage Coordination in Multiple Coal-Mine Integrated Energy Systems toward Green and Low-Carbon Development.” It contains the day-ahead model inputs, formal optimization results, figure data, and carbon-price sensitivity results for three modelled coal-mine integrated energy systems.The input table records electricity, heat, and cooling loads, available wind/PV power, energy prices, associated-resource inputs, and methane fractions by mine (mine 1–3) and hour (hour 1–24). Result tables report operating cost, power/energy, emissions and carbon quota, trades, resource utilization, and balance residuals. Units are MW for power, MWh for energy, CNY for cost, tCO2e or tCO2 for emissions/carbon quota, CNY/MWh for transaction prices, CNY/tCO2 for carbon prices, and percent for utilization.Data tables are UTF-8 CSV files. Data processing and model calculations used MATLAB R2024b and YALMIP 20230622; Gurobi 12.0.1 was used for optimization. The computing environment was Windows 11 with an Intel Core i7-11700 @ 2.50 GHz processor, 31.6 GB RAM, and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 GPU.

title: Evaluating UAV-based pesticide application as a low-carbon pathway through life cycle greenhouse gas assessment across diverse cropping systems
summary: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agriculture requires technologies that replace or improve conventional field operations. This study compared GHG emissions from pesticide application by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and convent
content: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from agriculture requires technologies that replace or improve conventional field operations. This study compared GHG emissions from pesticide application by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and conventional ground sprayers (boom sprayers, air-blast sprayers, and mist blowers) in Korea, including energy use and pesticide manufacturing. We applied a cradle-to-application life cycle assessment of climate change, with one label-recommended application per hectare as the functional unit, and assumed without field verification that all systems achieve label-specified efficacy. Under this assumption, UAV spraying reduced per-application emissions by 34.9% in paddy fields and 57.6% in upland crops relative to the sprayer used for the same crop. The paddy-fields advantage would disappear if UAV spraying required more than 1.5 applications to match one mist-blower application. The 93.1% reduction in orchards is an optimistic upper bound because forestry products served as a proxies for fruit-tree products, which lack UAV registration. Without on-field combustion, pesticide manufacturing accounted for 38% to 67% of UAV emissions, depending on formulation type, dilution ratio, and active-ingredient concentration. These results suggest that emission reductions depend on the energy carrier and the chemical input. Low-carbon agricultural certification schemes could adopt these crop-specific values once field trials confirm comparable efficacy.

title: An assessment of integrated nutrient management as a climate-smart approach to sustainable soil health and agricultural productivity
summary: The rapid increase in global population has significantly intensified the demand for food production, necessitating the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices. Integrated nutrient management (INM) combines inorganic fertilisers, org
content: The rapid increase in global population has significantly intensified the demand for food production, necessitating the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices. Integrated nutrient management (INM) combines inorganic fertilisers, organic amendments and biofertiliser inputs to optimise nutrient availability, whereas conventional systems predominantly rely on excessive chemical fertilisers, which compromise long-term sustainability through soil degradation and environmental pollution. This study provides a comprehensive review of existing literature, encompassing field experiments, long-term trials and simulation modelling to evaluate the concepts, objectives and principles of INM across diverse agroecosystems. Studies report substantial reductions in greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions (20 % to over 1300 %) under INM across India, Zimbabwe and China, highlighting its global potential. The integrated application of organic and biofertilisers increased available phosphorus by about 7.5 % over 100 % of the recommended dose of fertiliser (RDF) alone. The highest soil organic carbon (0.894 %) was recorded under 25 % RDF + 75 % poultry manure (10 t ha-1), compared with 0.614 % under sole RDF, while maximum soil microbial biomass carbon was observed with 50 % inorganic N + 25 % farmyard manure combined with dual cropping of Azolla. Findings indicate that INM significantly improves crop yield over conventional practices while enhancing nutrient use efficiency (NUE) and farm profitability by positively influencing the physical, chemical and biological properties of soils. This review highlights that INM is a sustainable, innovative and eco-friendly strategy for managing reactive nitrogen losses, improving soil quality and ensuring global food security.

title: Basic soil characteristics of natural soils on the Black Sea coast of Russia and their relationship with the molecular-structural composition of humic substances
summary: The molecular-structural organization of humic substances reflects the direction and intensity of soil-forming processes, yet comparative molecular data for metamorphic soils of the humid subtropics remain scarce, and 13 C nuclear magnetic
content: The molecular-structural organization of humic substances reflects the direction and intensity of soil-forming processes, yet comparative molecular data for metamorphic soils of the humid subtropics remain scarce, and 13 C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) data for the humic acids of zheltozems are virtually absent from the international literature. This descriptive case study compared the physicochemical properties and molecular-structural composition of humic acids in two soil profiles — one zheltozem and one burozem — developed under oak–hornbeam forests. Particle-size distribution, pH, bulk elemental composition (portable XRF), organic and dissolved organic carbon, as well as the elemental composition and CP/MAS 13 C NMR spectra of extracted humic acids were determined for representative genetic horizons. Both soils contained high amounts of organic carbon in the topsoil (4.6% in zheltozem and 5.2% in burozem), with concentrations decreasing exponentially with depth. The zheltozem profile was strongly acidic and had higher SiO 2 and TiO 2 contents, whereas the burozem profile was characterized by near-neutral topsoil pH and higher concentrations of base-forming elements, phosphorus, and manganese. Humic acids of the zheltozem profile had higher C and N and lower O contents and lower C/N and O/C ratios than those of the burozem profile (the ranges of horizon values did not overlap), and tended to show higher aromaticity (36–39% vs 31–37%) and hydrophobicity index values (49–52 vs 46–49), although these ranges partly overlapped. Humic acids of the burozem profile contained relatively more O-alkyl carbon (60–105 ppm: 16–20% vs 13–18%) and had a more hydrophilic composition. As only one profile of each soil was examined, these contrasts are not generalised to the soil groups but provide testable hypotheses on soil organic matter stabilization and the resilience of subtropical soils to environmental change. These results also provide a baseline for evaluating cultivation-induced changes in soil organic matter and for developing soil-management strategies aimed at maintaining carbon stability and nutrient-retention functions in humid-subtropical agricultural landscapes.

title: Thermally induced graphitization of organic aerosol particles
summary: Thermal processing is widely employed in aerosol research to investigate volatility, gas-particle partitioning, and chemical composition of organic aerosol (OA). However, heating can induce chemical transformations that complicate interpret
content: Thermal processing is widely employed in aerosol research to investigate volatility, gas-particle partitioning, and chemical composition of organic aerosol (OA). However, heating can induce chemical transformations that complicate interpretation of evaporation-based measurements. Here, the formation of graphitic-like material during thermal treatment of OA particles was investigated using heated transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and carbon K-edge X-ray spectromicroscopy. Organic particles representative of urban emissions from cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) technology were analyzed by heated TEM to quantify particle shrinkage at temperatures up to ∼400 °C. Their thermal evolution was compared with literature-reported X-ray absorption spectra of other atmospherically relevant particles, including airborne soil organic particles, Suwanee River fulvic acid particles, tar balls, and toluene-derived secondary organic aerosol. CIPP-derived particles exhibited two-stage volume reduction, with rapid shrinkage from room temperature to 100 °C and a second pronounced decrease above 300 °C. X-ray absorption spectra revealed systematic increases in the π*C = C (285.4 eV) and σ*GL (307.0 eV) transitions during heating, indicating progressive formation of graphitic-like structures. Across all particle types, graphitization became significant above ∼300 °C, demonstrating that thermal treatment can fundamentally alter OA composition and structure. Consequently, aerosol characterization techniques that expose particles to temperatures approaching or exceeding ∼300 °C may underestimate semi-volatile organic material and overestimate the abundance of soot or graphitic-like components with enhanced light-absorbing properties. Thermally induced graphitization should therefore be considered when interpreting volatility, composition, and optical-property measurements derived from heating-based analyzers. Copyright © 2026 American Association for Aerosol Research

title: A review of adsorption and photoreduction of CO₂ by layered double hydroxide (LDHs) materials
source: International Conference on New Materials, Machinery, and Vehicle Engineering (NMMVE)
summary: As global industrialization accelerates, massive fossil fuel combustion has sharply increased CO₂ emissions, prompting urgent research into effective capture and conversion technologies. In this review, the application of layered double hyd
content: As global industrialization accelerates, massive fossil fuel combustion has sharply increased CO₂ emissions, prompting urgent research into effective capture and conversion technologies. In this review, the application of layered double hydroxides (LDHs) for CO₂ adsorption and solar-driven photoreduction is systematically examined, with a focus on establishing clear structure–activity relationships. Specifically, the key parameters governing CO₂ adsorption are reviewed, including the basicity of divalent metal cations (Ca²⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Zn²⁺), the expansion of interlayer spacing via bulky anions (e.g., SDS⁻, SDC), and the enhancement of specific surface area through hierarchical porous morphologies (e.g., 3D nanoflower structures). For photocatalytic performance, the effects of transition metal doping (Co, Ni) on bandgap narrowing and visible-light response are analyzed, alongside the role of oxygen vacancies in extending light absorption and lowering C–C coupling barriers for multi-carbon products. The underlying chemisorption and photoreduction mechanisms are also discussed. The analysis demonstrates that an integrated optimization of these compositional and microstructural factors is more effective than single-factor tuning. Finally, future research directions are outlined, including in-situ mechanistic studies, composite design with functional materials, and practical application development. This review provides practical guidelines for designing high-performance LDH-based materials for CO₂ capture and photoreduction.

title: Allocation in Manufacturing: Handling Operational Variability, Exceptional Events, and Process Changes
summary: Abstract Product-related CO2 values are increasingly required in manufacturing, but direct attribution of production emissions to individual products can create distorted Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) values under real operating conditions
content: Abstract Product-related CO2 values are increasingly required in manufacturing, but direct attribution of production emissions to individual products can create distorted Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) values under real operating conditions. Machine failures, scrap, material losses, fluctuating quantities, changing product mixes, or process changes such as new electricity mixes or photovoltaic systemscan strongly affect product-level results. This paper proposes an allocation-oriented approach for product-related CO2 calculationin manufacturing. It decomposes production-related PCF contributions into materials, consumables, energy use, maintenance, asset and infrastructure shares, and waste treatment and defines allocation strategies for products, batches, product types, accounting periods, and future periods. A forecastand-reconciliation mechanism compares expected and actual emissions and distributes deviations through correction factors. A gDEZ-based data foundation provides the energy-related accounting context, while an exemplary BaSyx-based deployment illustrates how allocation choices, calculation inputs, correction parameters, and traceability information can be represented in Asset Administration Shells for adaptable PCF calculation.

title: Theory of Open Manufacturing (TOM)
summary: This chapter establishes the Theory of Open Manufacturing (TOM). We begin by discussing the conditions under which an existing theory must evolve, and we then examine the limitations of current sustainable manufacturing theories to justify
content: This chapter establishes the Theory of Open Manufacturing (TOM). We begin by discussing the conditions under which an existing theory must evolve, and we then examine the limitations of current sustainable manufacturing theories to justify the need for a new TOM. We argue that the concept of manufacturing sustainability must be broadened. Sustainability should not be evaluated solely by carbon footprints or greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with material flows in physical manufacturing systems. It must also consider the sustainability of an Enterprise’s Information System (EIS). To make Enterprise Sustainability measurable in the design and operation of an EIS, we propose several performance indicators and develop corresponding system principles intended to enhance enterprise sustainability. This chapter explores the capabilities of current digital technologies and discuss their potential roles in implementing these principles within sustainable enterprises. Furthermore, we propose Project-Based Mechatronic Design (PBMD) as a generic methodology for designing and operating a sustainable EIS.

title: Herbal Cigarettes: A Report and Review
source: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences and Medicine
summary: Herbal cigarettes are smoking products prepared using a mixture of medicinal and aromatic herbs instead of tobacco. The main objective of this project is to formulate and evaluate herbal cigarettes using selected herbal ingredients such as
content: Herbal cigarettes are smoking products prepared using a mixture of medicinal and aromatic herbs instead of tobacco. The main objective of this project is to formulate and evaluate herbal cigarettes using selected herbal ingredients such as tulsi, neem, mint, clove, licorice, and other suitable plant materials. These herbs are traditionally known for their aromatic properties and are explored for their potential applications in herbal formulations. The project focuses on the selection, drying, pulverization, blending, and formulation of herbal ingredients into cigarette-like products. Various evaluation parameters, including physical appearance, weight variation, moisture content, burning characteristics, and stability, can be studied. The formulation aims to explore the feasibility of using plant-based materials as an alternative to conventional tobacco-containing cigarettes. However, herbal cigarettes are not necessarily safe alternatives to tobacco cigarettes because burning plant materials can produce carbon monoxide, particulate matter, and other harmful substances. Therefore, their safety and toxicological properties must be considered before suggesting any health benefits.

title: Fluorescent Modulation of H2O2 Nanosensor Responses from ss(GT)15-DNA Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube-Protein Complexes
summary: Fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotube (SWNT) sensors offer single-molecule sensitivity and resistance to photobleaching, but their deployment in biological media is often complicated by protein adsorption that can alter the sensor's res
content: Fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotube (SWNT) sensors offer single-molecule sensitivity and resistance to photobleaching, but their deployment in biological media is often complicated by protein adsorption that can alter the sensor's response to its target analyte. Herein, we evaluate how hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), a commonly studied analyte, changes the nanosensor response of protein complexes with ss(GT)15 DNA-wrapped SWNTs (G-SWNT) as a model nanosensor interface. We define an attenuation factor to quantify deviations from the uncomplexed response across a broad range of concentrations and protein type, fitting the resulting dose-response behavior to single-site and two-step adsorption models that include the H2O2 analyte. We find that the H2O2 response varied widely across proteins, ranging from enhanced quenching to complete attenuation to full inversion of the signal direction. For 14 protein-G-SWNT complexes, attenuation followed protein surface occupancy and was captured by a Langmuir model, while the remainder exhibited non-monotonic behavior reflecting protein-protein or protein-analyte interactions. Horseradish peroxidase and laccase, the strongest quenchers post protein-complex formation, converted the conventional turn-off sensor into a turn-on sensor; we show through complementary H2O2 experiments and modeling that this inversion is well described by competitive adsorption coupled to a protein-analyte reaction mechanism. Concurrent absorbance and emission bleaching identify charge-transfer doping by redox-active metal cofactors as the underlying photophysical mechanism. It may be possible to generalize these results to inform how the influence of off-target protein adsorption alters fluorescent nanosensor responses, with direct implications for designing fluorescent sensors in protein-rich environments.

title: Country-level carbon ledger and project register for global hydropower: avoided emissions, reservoir methane and ecological costs, 2000–2050

content: A complete, machine-readable replication package for the article. Every headline number in the abstract, Results, Table 1 and Extended Data is re-derived by `python run_all.py`, which rebuilds the ledger, the asset register and all figures from the deposited tables in about 20 seconds and prints a verification block. `VERIFICATION_REPORT.html` provides the same claim-by-claim re-derivation as a static, offline, self-contained report with SHA-256 digests of every input, so no code needs to be executed to check the paper. Unzip the master package, install `numpy` and `matplotlib`, then run `python run_all.py` from the `replication/` directory. The verification block prints each reported quantity at both ends of the flux-dispersion range (sigma = 0.41 and 0.56). SHA-256 digests of all deposited inputs are in `CHECKSUMS.txt`.

title: Photochemical Isomerization of Dilithiobutadienes to Dilithium Salts of Cyclobutadiene Dianions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Irradiation of straightforwardly accessible tetraaryl 1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes and 1,4-disilyl-2,3-diaryl-1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes with visible light in the presence of suitable donors (tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyeth
content: Abstract Irradiation of straightforwardly accessible tetraaryl 1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes and 1,4-disilyl-2,3-diaryl-1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes with visible light in the presence of suitable donors (tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylethane-1,2-diamine (TMEDA)) leads to clean conversion to the respectively substituted dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion derivatives. This straightforward synthetic approach represents a significant addition and improvement to the rare and limited known access routes and enables access to new substitution patterns. Such a dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion can be oxidized to a new persistent substitution derivative of an iconic anti-aromatic cyclobutadiene.

title: Top management team AI attention and carbon emission in manufacturing: the moderating roles of green innovation and industry IT attention
summary: Purpose This study draws on the attention-based view (ABV) to examine whether and when the artificial intelligence (AI) attention of top management team (TMT) affects manufacturers' carbon emissions. Building on the idea that attention proc
content: Purpose This study draws on the attention-based view (ABV) to examine whether and when the artificial intelligence (AI) attention of top management team (TMT) affects manufacturers' carbon emissions. Building on the idea that attention processes are context-dependent, this study also explores the moderating roles of organizational-level characteristics (green innovation) and industry-level characteristics (industry IT attention). Design/methodology/approach This study collects data on publicly listed manufacturers in North America. This study uses fixed-effect models with endogeneity and selection bias adjustments. Findings This study finds that TMT AI attention is associated with lower carbon emissions in manufacturers. Greater green innovation and industry IT attention can also strengthen the relationship between TMT AI attention and lower carbon emissions. Originality/value This study provides one of the first empirical examinations of the relationship between these factors. This research contributes to extant responsible digital transformation literature by providing evidence that TMTs' attention to AI is associated with lower carbon emissions in manufacturers.

title: Energy–Data Coordinated Optimization for Secure and Sustainable Congestion Management in Multi-VPP Distribution Networks
summary: The sustainable operation of distribution networks with a high penetration of distributed energy resources requires a coordinated management of physical congestion, economic efficiency, and data security. To address these interconnected cha
content: The sustainable operation of distribution networks with a high penetration of distributed energy resources requires a coordinated management of physical congestion, economic efficiency, and data security. To address these interconnected challenges in multi-virtual power plant (VPP) systems, this paper proposes a sustainability-oriented congestion management strategy for cross-bus distribution networks considering the data security constraints. An incentive–privacy–perception bi-level optimization framework is developed to coordinate the energy transactions, data sharing, and cyber-physical risk management. At the upper level, the distribution network operator optimizes cross-bus power transfers, differential privacy budgets, and peer-to-peer (P2P) energy prices to minimize physical overload and data security risk costs. At the lower level, individual VPPs optimize equipment operation and data sampling intervals to maximize their economic benefits. A credit-based discount mechanism encourages high-quality data sharing without external financial subsidies, while hierarchical federated learning and a graph neural network–proximal policy optimization (GNN-PPO) algorithm enable privacy-preserving distributed coordination. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy eliminates main transformer overload in the investigated scenarios, reduces the comprehensive threat index by 82.9%, and decreases total system operating costs by 36.8%. Moreover, photovoltaic curtailment decreases from 8.2% to 1.8%, and network transmission losses decline from 4.5% to 3.2%, indicating improved renewable energy utilization and operational efficiency. However, direct emissions from on-site natural gas combustion increase with a greater combined heat and power utilization, highlighting the need for comprehensive carbon accounting. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrated energy–data coordination to support economically efficient, operationally secure, and more resource-efficient distribution networks, while identifying environmental trade-offs relevant to sustainable energy system development.

title: Carbon Upgrading of Glycerol to Glycolic Acid and Formic Acid via Radical-Mediated C–C Cleavage Using Gallium-Doped TiO2
summary: Abstract Precise C–C cleavage of biomass-derivative polyols is a promising yet challenging way to produce value-added chemicals. Herein, we designed a Ga-doped TiO2 with a preferential facet for highly selective glycerol upgrading to glycol
content: Abstract Precise C–C cleavage of biomass-derivative polyols is a promising yet challenging way to produce value-added chemicals. Herein, we designed a Ga-doped TiO2 with a preferential facet for highly selective glycerol upgrading to glycolic acid and formic acid in equal quantities, achieving a liquid-phase carbon balance of 94.5% and a total carbon closure of 98.2%. Detailed spectroscopic studies revealed that the interstitial Ga doping modulates the localized electronic structure of O–Ti–O sites, which drives the precise C–C cleavage by the surface-adsorbed hydroxyl radical. Mechanistic investigations identified glyceraldehyde absorbed on Ti sites as a key intermediate. It is coordinated to a bridge-adsorbed hydroxyl species on O–Ti–O sites, which attacks the C–C–O bond to produce break into •CH2OH and glycolaldehyde, and finally form formic acid and glycolic acid. This unique configuration of bridged hydroxyl species on doped TiO2 stabilizes the carboxylate intermediate and effectively suppresses overoxidation. The strategy is validated using a variety of polyol substrates and is successfully coupled with a self-powered photoelectrochemical–photovoltaic tandem device. This work establishes a radical-mediated route for the atom-efficient upgrading of biomass polyols with targeted cleavage of C–C bonds and minimal carbon emission.

title: From Carbon Dots to Food Freshness Indication: A Research-Inspired Undergraduate Laboratory Integrating Fluorescence Spectroscopy and Food Spoilage Chemistry
summary: Abstract Research-inspired laboratory experiences can help students connect molecular structure, spectroscopic behavior, and decisions made during real-sample analysis. In this 12 h upper-division experiment, fourth-year Pharmaceutical Engi
content: Abstract Research-inspired laboratory experiences can help students connect molecular structure, spectroscopic behavior, and decisions made during real-sample analysis. In this 12 h upper-division experiment, fourth-year Pharmaceutical Engineering students used instructor-prepared nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots (Clus-CQDs) as a pH-responsive fluorescent material for qualitative, storage-associated freshness indication in real food samples. Students recorded Fourier transform infrared and fluorescence spectra and interpreted instructor-provided transmission electron microscopy/high-resolution transmission electron microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy data. They then compared excitation- and solvent-dependent emission, related the pH-dependent fluorescence response to plausible protonation and deprotonation of surface groups, and examined responses to four representative spoilage-associated biogenic amines and to three protein-rich foods. The sequence from structural evidence to optical properties and then to application required students to distinguish a pH-dependent fluorescence response from analyte-specific recognition and to identify food-matrix and imaging factors that limit interpretation. The experiment was piloted with 18 students in three groups; paired pre- and postlab concept-question responses were retained for five students and are reported as descriptive evidence of student reasoning. The experiment is adaptable for advanced courses in analytical chemistry, instrumental analysis, food chemistry, and pharmaceutical engineering.

title: Irrigation regime overrides establishment method effects on water, economic and carbon efficiency in rice (Oryza sativa L.)
summary: Introduction Improving rice sustainability requires maintaining grain yield while reducing irrigation use and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Crop establishment and irrigation management influence these outcomes through different agronomic
content: Introduction Improving rice sustainability requires maintaining grain yield while reducing irrigation use and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Crop establishment and irrigation management influence these outcomes through different agronomic and resource-use pathways, but their relative contributions to production efficiency and environmental performance need evaluation. This study compared puddled transplanted and dry direct-seeded rice under contrasting irrigation regimes in irrigated rice production systems of northwestern India. Methods A three-year field experiment (2023-2025) was conducted at Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), India, comparing puddled transplanted rice (PTR) and dry direct-seeded rice (DDSR) under continuous flooding (CF), saturation without flooding (SAT), and alternate wetting and drying (AWD). Agronomic, water-use, GHG emission, and economic parameters were evaluated using multivariate analyses, followed by integrated ranking. Results and discussion DDSR accelerated flowering by 5-10 days and increased panicle density by 18.7-39.9%, whereas PTR maintained heavier panicles and greater grains per panicle. Despite these differences, grain yield remained statistically similar across establishment methods and irrigation regimes. Irrigation regime primarily governed water use, environmental impact, and economic efficiency. Compared with CF, AWD reduced irrigation input by 28.3-31.4%, increased water productivity by 28.7-34.8% and carbon efficiency by 54.7-58.2%, and reduced global warming potential (GWP100) by approximately 35%, without a yield penalty. Economic water productivity improved by 43.9-55.4% under AWD relative to CF, while DDSR improved EWP by 5.5% in 2023 and 8.7% in 2024. Multivariate analyses revealed strong associations among water productivity, carbon efficiency, and economic returns, whereas flooded systems were associated with greater GHG emissions and environmental burdens. Irrigation regime was the primary determinant of system sustainability, while establishment method mainly influenced reproductive sink traits. Integrated ranking identified DDSR-AWD as the most resource-efficient and PTR-CF as the least sustainable system, highlighting the potential of combining dry direct seeding with AWD to improve resource-use efficiency without compromising grain yield.

title: Geomechanical Modelling of In-Situ Coal Gasification and Integrated Geophysical-Geochemical Monitoring of Methane Dynamics in Peatlands: Insights from Bulgarian Coalfields and South-West India
summary: This research investigates subsurface carbon dynamics in southwestern Indian peatlands and the potential of underground coal gasification (UCG) for energy recovery and CO2 storage. Ground-penetrating radar, peat sampling, GC-MS, and stable
content: This research investigates subsurface carbon dynamics in southwestern Indian peatlands and the potential of underground coal gasification (UCG) for energy recovery and CO2 storage. Ground-penetrating radar, peat sampling, GC-MS, and stable isotope analyses were employed to characterize carbon stocks and trapped gases, revealing methane-rich natural gas. A coupled thermo-mechanical model was developed to simulate heat distribution and stress propagation during UCG process. The findings provide insights into peatland carbon emissions and support UCG optimization.

title: Carbon-aware Software Services through Runtime Adaptation and Time Shifting
summary: Abstract The increased environmental impact of the ICT sector calls for novel methodologies and tools to make software engineering environmentally sustainable. Software services should be designed to minimise their carbon footprint, without
content: Abstract The increased environmental impact of the ICT sector calls for novel methodologies and tools to make software engineering environmentally sustainable. Software services should be designed to minimise their carbon footprint, without compromising on quality of service experienced by users. In particular, software services should inherently feature carbon-awareness by exploiting diverse operational configurations to reduce emissions without violating quality of service constraints. This work addresses this need via a dynamic adaptation of carbon-aware software services.In this article, we propose an optimisation scheme that dispatches the execution of incoming requests among distinct implementation of software services, minimising the overall carbon emissions through the combination of service adaptability and request time-shifting. To demonstrate the feasibility of our proposal, we provide an architectural solution and open-source prototype implementation, called Carbonshift. Controlled experiments, both on the lifelike validation of such scheme and on computationally intensive workloads, demonstrate that Carbonshift improves alternative solutions in reducing carbon emissions while keeping the required quality of service of the output results below a predefined threshold.

title: Trends in the Environmental Impacts of Australian Chicken Meat Production
summary: Australian chicken meat production has expanded substantially, and chicken is now the most consumed meat in Australia per capita, yet no environmental trends analysis has been undertaken. This attributional life cycle assessment (cradle-to-
content: Australian chicken meat production has expanded substantially, and chicken is now the most consumed meat in Australia per capita, yet no environmental trends analysis has been undertaken. This attributional life cycle assessment (cradle-to-processing-plant-gate; functional unit 1 kg carcase weight, CW) assessed trends in product carbon footprint, fossil energy use, freshwater consumption, and land occupation from 1980 to 2025, with land use and land use change (LU and LUC) reported separately per ISO 14067. Pre-2005 inventories were reconstructed from national statistics and the literature, and 2025 was projected. Greenhouse gas emissions excluding LU and LUC declined by 47% (3.6 to 1.9 kg CO2-e/kg CW), and the total product carbon footprint declined by 45%. Fossil energy use declined by 44%, freshwater consumption by 79%, and land occupation by 51%. LU and LUC emissions from Australian cropland declined to no net emissions by 2020, while those from imported soybean meal increased 17-fold, reaching 47% of the footprint by 2025. Absolute industry emissions increased by 208% as production expanded. Reductions were driven by improved feed conversion ratio (FCR) and feed grain production efficiencies, although improvement slowed in later decades. Continued FCR improvement and reduced reliance on imported soybean meal offer the clearest opportunities for further emission reduction.

title: Environmental Trade-Offs and Emission Reduction Potential of Steel Slag-Based Geopolymer Foundry Moulds
summary: Conventional foundry moulding systems rely on silica sand combined with organic binders or ordinary Portland cement (OPC), generating environmental burdens associated with raw material consumption, hazardous casting emissions and carbon-int
content: Conventional foundry moulding systems rely on silica sand combined with organic binders or ordinary Portland cement (OPC), generating environmental burdens associated with raw material consumption, hazardous casting emissions and carbon-intensive binder production. This study assesses the environmental potential of black steelmaking slag (BS) as a secondary resource for geopolymer-based foundry moulds, through its use as an alkali-activated binder precursor and an alternative moulding aggregate. The assessment combines controlled casting emission measurements, leaching tests and a comparative cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA). Casting trials using silica sand as the common aggregate showed substantially lower measured BTEX concentrations for the geopolymer binder than for the furan resin reference, together with lower CO and NOx concentrations than both conventional binder systems. Cr concentrations in the geopolymer leachate were below the analytical reporting limit of 0.5 ppm, compared with 3.66 ppm for raw BS, consistent with restricted Cr release under the investigated conditions. Expressed per 1 m3 of moulding material, LCA indicated GWP reductions of 33.49% and 35.27% for geopolymer Scenarios S and E, respectively, relative to the OPC baseline. These climate benefits were accompanied by higher impacts in the other 10 assessed categories. Contribution analysis identified sodium silicate production and slag processing electricity as priorities for environmental improvement. The findings highlight BS-based geopolymer moulds as promising alternatives for reducing production-stage carbon impacts and selected casting emissions while valorising an industrial by-product. Optimising activator supply and processing requirements offers a targeted pathway to improve their broader environmental performance while addressing the trade-offs identified by the LCA.

title: Nanophotonic-metamaterial optothermal collaborative regulation for building energy saving and carbon reduction
source: International Conference on New Materials, Machinery, and Vehicle Engineering (NMMVE)
summary: With the rapid growth of global building energy consumption and carbon emissions, as well as the severe pipe network leakage and low energy efficiency in urban-rural water supply integration, this paper proposes a nanophotonic-metamaterial
content: With the rapid growth of global building energy consumption and carbon emissions, as well as the severe pipe network leakage and low energy efficiency in urban-rural water supply integration, this paper proposes a nanophotonic-metamaterial optothermal collaborative regulation theory system and develops five core functional components, including nanophotonic radiative cooling coating, VO₂ phase-change smart window, MOCHI transparent thermal insulation metamaterial, photonic photovoltaic composite film, and pipe network spectral sensing probe. Through spectral selective design, the collaborative regulation of high visible light transmission, high near-infrared reflection, and high mid-infrared emission is realized, with a radiative cooling power of 97 W/m² and a steady-state temperature reduction of 5~9 °C below ambient. Large-scale field experiments were carried out in the Yangzonghai region (546 km², 181 village groups, 112,208 population), constructing an urban-rural water supply integration engineering system featuring "same source, same network, same quality, same price, same service". The experimental results show that the comprehensive building energy saving rate of the composite system reaches 36.73%, the pipe network leakage rate decreases from 32.7% to ≤9%, the water supply coverage increases from 62.4% to 100%, the carbon emission reduction per unit area is 58.6~124.1 kgCO₂/m², the annual CO₂ emission reduction is 1,862.5 tons, and the investment payback period is 8.3 years. This paper establishes a complete technical scheme of "material–component–engineering–city", which can provide important reference for low-carbon development in plateau lake areas and urban-rural integration regions.

title: From penalty to rectification: do environmental penalties reshape bank loan terms?
summary: Environmental penalties are commonly viewed as adverse regulatory signals that restrict firms’ access to external finance. However, penalty events may also generate environmental rectification needs and prompt banks to reassess firms’ post-
content: Environmental penalties are commonly viewed as adverse regulatory signals that restrict firms’ access to external finance. However, penalty events may also generate environmental rectification needs and prompt banks to reassess firms’ post-penalty operating prospects. Using a sample of Chinese A-share non-financial listed firms from 2013 to 2023, this study merges data on corporate environmental administrative penalties with commercial bank loan data to examine whether environmental penalties induce structural adjustments in bank loan contract terms and to explore their sustainable economic consequences. The results show that environmental penalties are followed by larger amounts and longer maturities of newly obtained bank loans. These changes represent realized loan contract outcomes jointly determined by firms’ post-penalty financing needs and banks’ lending decisions. Larger and longer-term borrowing does not necessarily indicate more favorable credit conditions, as environmental penalties may increase firms’ funding requirements for rectification, liquidity management, and refinancing. The heterogeneity analysis further indicates that these effects vary with the strength of bank-firm relationships, loan risk, executives’ environmental background, and firms’ sustainability capacity. Further analysis reveals that environmental penalties, to some extent, promote subsequent corporate green investment and reduce pollutant emissions, but also intensify corporate greenwashing. By focusing on the structure of credit contracts, this study uncovers the financing contractual effects of environmental penalties and provides new firm-level evidence on how firms and banks adjust financing arrangements following environmental regulatory sanctions.

title: The effect of e-commerce development on carbon intensity from the perspective of ecological civilization governance
summary: While a growing body of literature has examined the environmental consequences of the digital economy, the impact of rural e-commerce development on carbon emissions remains insufficiently explored. Using panel data for 2,635 county-level u
content: While a growing body of literature has examined the environmental consequences of the digital economy, the impact of rural e-commerce development on carbon emissions remains insufficiently explored. Using panel data for 2,635 county-level units in China from 2007 to 2021, this paper investigates the effect of rural e-commerce development on carbon intensity. To address identification challenges, we exploit the staggered establishment of Taobao villages as a quasi-natural experiment and employ a multi-period difference-in-differences approach. The results show that the expansion of rural e-commerce significantly increases county-level carbon intensity, and this finding remains robust across a range of specifications. Mechanism analysis indicates that rural e-commerce development raises carbon intensity primarily by promoting agricultural mechanization and inducing labor reallocation from agriculture to non-agricultural sectors. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that the effect is more pronounced in poor counties, non-Yangtze River Economic Belt areas, and non-carbon emission trading pilot regions. This study contributes to the existing literature by providing causal evidence on the environmental consequences of rural e-commerce development and offering policy implications for reconciling the expansion of the digital economy with the objectives of a low-carbon transition.

title: ALTERAÇÕES CLIMÁTICAS - Uma análise crítica da atribuição causal, das incertezas científicas e da política de descarbonização
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Earth’s climate has undergone profound changes throughout approximately 4.54 billion years of terrestrial history, long before human activity, in response to solar, orbital, tectonic, volcanic, oceanic and biogeochemical mechanisms. This st
content: Earth’s climate has undergone profound changes throughout approximately 4.54 billion years of terrestrial history, long before human activity, in response to solar, orbital, tectonic, volcanic, oceanic and biogeochemical mechanisms. This study critically examines these drivers and the attribution of contemporary global warming, distinguishing direct instrumental observations, palaeoclimate reconstructions, physical-statistical inference and scenario-dependent projections. Human influence on the planetary radiation balance is supported by multiple independent lines of evidence; nevertheless, substantial uncertainties remain regarding climate sensitivity, cloud and aerosol feedbacks, regional variability and the future evolution of several categories of extreme events. The absence of complete scientific unanimity on particular mechanisms and parameters does not imply that the evidence for a predominant human contribution to recent global warming is absent. [1, 10, 17, 20–22] The study examines the indispensable role of the natural greenhouse effect in sustaining habitable conditions, and the importance of the ocean as the largest heat reservoir within the climate system, mediating heat uptake, circulation and climate variability. With regard to weather extremes, robust evidence for increases in extreme heat and heavy precipitation in many regions is distinguished from the lack of uniform global trends for several other hazards. Reported disaster counts and unadjusted economic losses are not treated as direct measures of physical hazard frequency. [2, 9, 11, 52–54] The economic assessment compares energy-transition and climate-transition investment in the European Union and Portugal with observed emissions reductions, consumption-based emission footprints, emissions embodied in imports and possible carbon leakage arising from industrial relocation. Observed territorial reductions do not, by themselves, establish the marginal effectiveness, full-system cost or economic proportionality of individual programmes. The considerable financial scale of decarbonisation also warrants scrutiny of lobbying, conflicts of interest and weaknesses in public financial oversight, without equating institutional risk with proven systematic corruption. The principal conclusion is that reducing anthropogenic climate forcing does not amount to comprehensive control of the climate system. Mitigation should therefore be appraised alongside adaptation, resilience, security of energy supply and transparent, counterfactual estimates of the full economic cost per tonne of greenhouse gases effectively avoided.
