The study calls for open scientific challenge and evidence-based, economically proportionate public policy. Keywords: climate attribution; natural variability; ocean heat content; greenhouse effect; weather extremes; CMIP6; carbon leakage; European Union; Portugal; system costs; decarbonisation; regulatory capture.

title: Differentiated responses of ecosystem service supply and demand to urbanization across urban–rural gradients: a case study of the Yangtze River Delta, China
summary: Urbanization is closely associated with changes in ecosystem services, but how the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand vary along urban–rural gradients remains insufficiently understood. This study aim
content: Urbanization is closely associated with changes in ecosystem services, but how the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand vary along urban–rural gradients remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to examine the relationships between urbanization and ecosystem service supply and demand across urban–rural gradients and to provide evidence for landscape planning and sustainable management in rapidly urbanizing regions. We assessed the supply, demand, and supply–demand ratios of four ecosystem services—water yield, carbon sequestration, habitat quality, and soil conservation—in China’s Yangtze River Delta region (YRDR) in 2000, 2010, and 2020. Spearman’s rank correlation analysis was used to identify associations between urbanization and ecosystem service supply, demand, and supply–demand ratios across urban–rural gradients. Random forest and SHAP analyses were then used to evaluate the relative explanatory contributions of urbanization indicators and their nonlinear associations. (1) Ecosystem service supply and demand showed marked spatial mismatches across the YRDR. With increasing urbanization, habitat quality deficits deepened and soil conservation surpluses narrowed, whereas the carbon sequestration supply–demand imbalance was alleviated in old urban areas. Water-yield supply–demand patterns were sensitive to the method used to spatialize demand. All urban–rural gradients showed surpluses when sectoral water demand was allocated to the corresponding land-use types. In contrast, supply–demand pressure increased markedly in highly urbanized areas when demand was allocated by population density. (2) Urbanization indicators were generally negatively correlated with ecosystem service supply and supply–demand ratios, with stronger correlations in rural areas. Except for soil conservation, demand for the other three services was mostly positively correlated with urbanization indicators. (3) In 2020, among the seven models that met the spatial predictive-performance criterion, impervious surface proportion had the highest relative explanatory contribution in six. However, conventional urbanization indicators had limited explanatory power in old urban areas and for the supply–demand ratios of water yield and carbon sequestration across most urban–rural gradients. Ecosystem service supply–demand patterns and their associations with urbanization varied with urban–rural landscape context, service type, and the method used to spatialize demand. Landscape planning should consider the spatial configuration of land development and the continuity of ecological spaces, with particular emphasis on development control and landscape connectivity restoration in urban–rural fringes.

title: Sterically Controlled Conformational Gating of Rhodamine Spirolactam Switches for Super-Resolution Imaging
summary: The reversible interconversion of rhodamines between nonfluorescent spirocyclic and fluorescent ring-open states underpins fluorogenic probes and spontaneously blinking dyes for super-resolution imaging. Existing strategies mainly tune the
content: The reversible interconversion of rhodamines between nonfluorescent spirocyclic and fluorescent ring-open states underpins fluorogenic probes and spontaneously blinking dyes for super-resolution imaging. Existing strategies mainly tune the equilibrium between these states through electronic modification, whereas the role of conformational return in ring closure remains less explored. Here, we establish steric regulation of rhodamine spirolactams through amide N-substituents. Bulky substituents generate intramolecular repulsion with the xanthene scaffold, favoring ring opening. Crystallographic observations reveal substantial amide reorientation upon opening, suggesting increased separation between the nitrogen and meso-carbon reaction centers. We propose that substituent-dependent conformational accessibility modulates C-N bond reformation and the lifetime of the emissive state. The tert-butyl-substituted dye 1e exhibits an open-state residence time of 145 ms, despite its lower pKcycl. Calculations also indicate a lower ring-opening barrier for 1e than for less hindered 1a (1.12 vs 1.37 eV). Incorporating this design into HaloTag probes enables SIM, STED, and SMLM imaging. Importantly, N-halo-RBRB enables dual-modal SIM/SMLM imaging with a single fluorophore, integrating the rapid reconstruction of overall cellular architecture by SIM with single-molecule localization information from SMLM. This work identifies sterically modulated conformational accessibility as a design principle for engineering reversible rhodamine switches with tailored imaging capabilities.

title: National Emissions Inventory (NEI) 2020 for County Level Emissions, US EPA, OAR, OAQPS
summary: This polygon feature layer depicts Criteria Air Pollutants (CAPs), Hazardous Air Pollutants (HAPs), Greenhouse Gases (GHG), Particulate Matter (PM) Species and Components, PFAS and Other emissions as reported to EPA's 2020 National Emission
content: This polygon feature layer depicts Criteria Air Pollutants (CAPs), Hazardous Air Pollutants (HAPs), Greenhouse Gases (GHG), Particulate Matter (PM) Species and Components, PFAS and Other emissions as reported to EPA's 2020 National Emissions Inventory (NEI) for counties within the United States and territories. This US EPA, Office of Air and Radiation (OAR), Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards (OAQPS) feature layer depicts annual county emissions for all Criteria Air Pollutants (CAPs), Hazardous Air Pollutants (HAPs), Particulate Matter (PM) Species and Components, Greenhouse Gases (GHGs), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and Other emissions as reported to the 2020 National Emissions Inventory (NEI) within the United States and its territories. Criteria air pollutants within the NEI include: Carbon Monoxide (CO), Lead, Ammonia (NH3), Nitrogen Oxides (NOx), Particulate Matter 10 Particles (PM10), Particulate Matter 2.5 Particles (PM2.5), Sulfur Dioxide (SO2), and Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC). There are 275 unique HAPs included in this inventory, as well as 16 PFAS, 4 GHGs, and 3 chemicals considered "Other". Particulate Matter is also broken down into its individual species and components. Each criteria air pollutant (except Lead) is split into separate fields (sources) representing the amount of Nonpoint, Nonroad, Onroad, and Point emissions for each county. An aggregate TOTAL field is also included for each CAP, representing the sum of all emission sources for each county. Lead only has Nonpoint and Point source emissions reported in the NEI2020. Background The National Emissions Inventory (NEI) is a comprehensive and detailed estimate of air emissions of criteria pollutants, criteria precursors, and hazardous air pollutants from air emissions sources. The NEI is released every three years based primarily upon data provided by State, Local, and Tribal air agencies for sources in their jurisdictions and supplemented by data developed by the US EPA. The NEI is built using the Emissions Inventory System (EIS) first to collect the data from State, Local, and Tribal air agencies and then to blend that data with other data sources. NEI point sources include emissions estimates for larger sources that are located at a fixed, stationary location. Point sources in the NEI include large industrial facilities and electric power plants, airports, and smaller industrial, non-industrial and commercial facilities. A small number of portable sources such as some asphalt or rock crushing operations are also included. Some states voluntarily also provide facilities such as dry cleaners, gas stations, and livestock facilities, which are otherwise included in the NEI as nonpoint sources. The emissions potential of each facility determines whether that facility should be reported as a point source, according to emissions thresholds set in the Air Emissions Reporting Rule (AERR). NEI Point Sources are all included in the EIS Point Data Categor

title: Pareto-based screening of modified high-volume fly ash concrete formulations: Strength, environmental and economic trade-offs
summary: Modifiers can improve the 28-day strength of high-volume fly ash (HVFA) concrete, but additional materials and processing may offset the environmental and economic benefits of cement replacement. This study assembled a harmonised literature
content: Modifiers can improve the 28-day strength of high-volume fly ash (HVFA) concrete, but additional materials and processing may offset the environmental and economic benefits of cement replacement. This study assembled a harmonised literature database of 62 formulations, comprising 50 single-modifier HVFA mixtures, seven combined-modifier mixtures and five ordinary Portland cement (OPC) references. A consistent cradle-to-gate environmental and production-cost framework used 1 m³ of concrete as the principal functional unit, supplemented by GWP and cost per unit of 28-day mean cylinder-equivalent compressive strength. The assessment combined strength screening, strength–GWP–cost Pareto analysis, complementary performance-normalised indicators, OPC safeguards across 12 non-GWP categories and TOPSIS ranking under four weighting scenarios. Technical screening at ≥ 32 MPa retained 29 modified formulations, eight of which were principal Pareto-efficient. The leading slag-modified formulation achieved 55.0 MPa at 292.29 kg CO₂-eq/m³ and A$271.19/m³, with lower impacts than OPC50 in all 12 non-GWP categories. The leading silica-fume formulation achieved 60.3 MPa and the lowest strength-normalised GWP and cost, at 5.15 kg CO₂-eq/(m³·MPa) and A$4.86/(m³·MPa). A hydrated-lime formulation recorded the lowest GWP among baseline-eligible formulations, at 221.92 kg CO₂-eq/m³. At the baseline ≥ 32 MPa threshold, the silica-fume formulation led TOPSIS under balanced and strength-priority weighting, whereas the slag-modified formulation led under environmental- and cost-priority weighting. Both retained the leading two positions across all tested strength thresholds and weighting scenarios. The findings support formulation-specific selection according to performance requirements and priorities. Structural suitability and whole-life performance require project-specific design and durability verification.

title: Response and stability analysis of soil organic carbon in different ecosystems of China under climate warming gradient scenarios
summary: Under the background of global warming, the response pattern of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the stability of carbon sinks have received more and more attention. This research adopts the Space-for-time substitution (SFTS) method to build a
content: Under the background of global warming, the response pattern of soil organic carbon (SOC) and the stability of carbon sinks have received more and more attention. This research adopts the Space-for-time substitution (SFTS) method to build a spatial unit that integrates climate, vegetation and land use factors. These units are used to analyze the SOC spatial distribution patterns along the warming gradients in different regions of China and their related variability. Through linear regression, machine learning and neighborhood least squares fitting, the main driving factors of SOC space changes on multiple scales have been determined. The results show that SOC has a strong correlation with temperature and presents a nonlinear pattern in a higher temperature range. In most areas, the initial SOC content is the dominant factor related to SOC changes, and its constraint effect increases with the increase of soil depth. In contrast, vegetation coverage and precipitation show a stronger correlation on the surface, and there is obvious regional heterogeneity. In areas with low initial carbon content, high vegetation coverage and good moisture conditions, the estimated SOC increase is often greater. With the increase of temperature and soil depth, the content of organic carbon in the soil gradually decreases, and the area of high-content areas gradually shrinks. By establishing a spatial analysis framework that combines ecological units and environmental gradients, this study enhances the regional understanding of SOC change patterns and provides a scientific basis for assessing the distribution of soil carbon in China and formulating regional management strategies. These results should be interpreted as a general response patterns, rather than an accurate prediction of the future SOC dynamics.

title: Effect of Monitoring and Evaluation on Adoption of Internal Combustion Engine to Electric Retrofitting Project in Rwanda
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study assessed the effect of monitoring and evaluation on the adoption of electric mobility projects in Rwanda, with specific focus on the Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) to Electric Retrofitting Project implemented by REMA in Kigali
content: This study assessed the effect of monitoring and evaluation on the adoption of electric mobility projects in Rwanda, with specific focus on the Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) to Electric Retrofitting Project implemented by REMA in Kigali City.The target population consisted of 237 respondents, including project managers, technical officers/engineers, sales and marketing staff, electric fleet operators/drivers, and subcontractors.A sample size of 149 respondents was selected using Slovin's formula, stratified sampling, and simple random sampling.Data were collected using structured questionnaires, semi-structured interview guides, and documentary review.Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS Version 29 through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis.The findings showed that M&E Data had a positive and significant effect on adoption of electric mobility project (B = 0.253, t = 3.892, p = 0.000); M&E Tools had a positive and significant effect on adoption of electric mobility project (B = 0.373, t = 6.661, p = 0.000); M&E Design had a positive and significant effect on adoption of electric mobility project (B = 0.217, t = 3.875, p = 0.000); M&E Process had a positive and significant effect on adoption of electric mobility project (B = 0.176, t = 2.983, p = 0.003).The study concluded that monitoring and evaluation significantly contributed to adoption of electric mobility project in ICE to Electric Retrofitting Project.It recommended that responsible institutions should strengthen data accuracy, completeness, reliability and relevance across retrofitting activities while also strengthening the other significant practices identified by the study.

title: Segments of Sustainability: A Cluster Analysis of Thai Tourist Motivations for Low-Carbon Travel
summary: Low-carbon domestic tourism depends not only on the supply of lower-emission products but also on whether tourists are motivated, normatively committed, and able to choose them. This study segments Thai domestic tourists by integrating norm
content: Low-carbon domestic tourism depends not only on the supply of lower-emission products but also on whether tourists are motivated, normatively committed, and able to choose them. This study segments Thai domestic tourists by integrating normative dimensions from Value–Belief–Norm (VBN) theory, motivational dimensions from push–pull theory, and structural barriers from the hierarchical leisure-constraint model. A non-probability quota sample of 500 eligible Thai adults was recruited online (n = 300) and onsite (n = 200) across six regions. TwoStep cluster analysis of seven dimensions identified Deep Green Committers (n = 150), Convenience-Oriented Pragmatists (n = 190), and Cost-Constrained Travelers (n = 160). Behavioral intention and monetary willingness to pay (WTP), which were reserved for profiling, differed across segments (intention: F(2, 497) = 606.45, η2 = 0.709; WTP: F(2, 497) = 543.40, η2 = 0.686; both p < 0.001), with a mean WTP of 1180, 620, and 260 THB per 10,000 THB trip. All pairwise differences were large (Hedges’ g = 1.51–4.09). Past offset payment and rail/EV use followed the same ordering. Because recruitment included rail, EV, and ecotourism sites and stability was not assessed through bootstrap resampling, the segments are interpreted as provisional profiles of the recruited sample. They provide a basis for product design and for intervention hypotheses that require field evaluation, rather than evidence of causal effects or emissions reduction.

title: Designing the climate agenda in the Global South: selective reconfiguration, institutional scaffolding, and policy entrepreneurship in Brazil’s National Climate Change Policy
summary: This paper examines the agenda-setting of Brazil’s National Climate Change Policy (PNMC) across its first policy cycle (2009–2020) as a case of design-led governance under conditions of complexity. Rather than treating design as a metaphor
content: This paper examines the agenda-setting of Brazil’s National Climate Change Policy (PNMC) across its first policy cycle (2009–2020) as a case of design-led governance under conditions of complexity. Rather than treating design as a metaphor for policy architecture, it foregrounds design as situated practice: the deliberate crafting of governance arenas and instruments, the brokerage performed by policy entrepreneurs, and the selective reconfiguration of governance-design templates as they circulate from multilateral and Global North arenas into a Southern political context. Combining Kingdon’s Multiple Streams Framework with complexity theory and design theory, the argument is formalized as a central hypothesis and five falsifiable propositions specifying the conditions under which circulating templates are selectively reconfigured rather than faithfully adopted, rejected, or symbolically maintained; the operational indicators that discriminate complexity mechanisms from rival accounts (political bargaining, institutional adaptation, policy translation, strategic agency); and the forms of reconfiguration predicted under different actor, resource, and volatility configurations. Empirically, the paper re-interprets a process-tracing study of the PNMC based on documentary analysis and 25 key-informant interviews, deploying the case as a plausibility probe. International influence—disaggregated into multilateral regime institutions, multilateral banks, bilateral Global North funders, and Global South coalitions—operated as a constitutive design variable: external finance exceeding R$20 billion anchored the generation of alternatives, while imported templates (the NDC, MRV systems, REDD+, sectoral plans) were reconfigured, their internationally legible scaffolds preserved and their content reshaped by a cross-ideological pact that pursued resource capture while vetoing domestic costs. A paired within-case comparison shows why SIRENE coupled in the midst of crisis while the NDC implementation strategy never reached the agenda. The same institutional repertoire that built the policy (2009–2018) was repurposed to dismantle it (2019–2020) at a cost inversely related to its institutionalization—a pattern that conversion and policy-dismantling accounts describe but do not predict. The case exposes both Southern agency in remaking circulating design frameworks and the structural asymmetries that constrain it, and derives comparative predictions for other Southern climate agendas.

title: Integrating Microbial Ecology and Sustainability: Linking Agricultural Waste Gas Streams to Microbial Community Shifts in a Photobioreactor
summary: Photobioreactors (PBRs) coupled to animal housing offer potential for mitigating gaseous emissions such as CO2 and NH3 while simultaneously producing biomass. Here, we present a time-resolved characterization of microbial community dynamics
content: Photobioreactors (PBRs) coupled to animal housing offer potential for mitigating gaseous emissions such as CO2 and NH3 while simultaneously producing biomass. Here, we present a time-resolved characterization of microbial community dynamics, with a focus on the genetic potential for carbon and nitrogen metabolism. Using a cone-shaped, helical PBR cultivating Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina) and supplied with exhaust air from a chicken house, we characterized microbial communities over continuous exhaust-air exposure and periodic biomass harvesting. Microbiome and gene-centric profiling revealed temporal variation in community composition and in the representation of genes associated with carbon and nitrogen metabolism. Cycle-based dissolved inorganic nitrogen balances showed that the decrease in dissolved inorganic nitrogen was only partially recovered in harvested biomass, while ammonia-oxidizing microorganisms were associated with structured, low-light niches. These observations indicate ammonia-oxidizing potential but do not establish a quantitatively relevant nitrification flux. Structured carrier matrices provided attached-growth niches harboring microbial populations underrepresented in the circulating suspension, while pre-colonized carriers facilitated biomass development during re-inoculation. Overall, our results show that coupling PBRs to agricultural exhaust streams can support biomass production while sustaining spatially structured microbial communities with taxonomic and functional potential. These findings may inform their further development for emission mitigation and circular biomass production.

title: Nutritional and rumen microbiome determinants of enteric methane emissions in sheep: a systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: Enteric methane (CH4) production in sheep represents both a significant global greenhouse gas challenge and a metabolic energy inefficiency, with energy losses of 6–10% of gross energy intake. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed
content: Enteric methane (CH4) production in sheep represents both a significant global greenhouse gas challenge and a metabolic energy inefficiency, with energy losses of 6–10% of gross energy intake. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively synthesise evidence on the genetic, nutritional and rumen microbiome determinants of methane production and methane yield (methane emitted per unit of dry matter intake, g CH4 /kg DMI) in sheep, and to evaluate integrated strategies for mitigation, including their associated carbon and water footprints. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library databases for peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies meeting pre-defined PICOS criteria (species: sheep; sample size ≥ 20; traits: methane production/yield; study designs: experimental and observational) were included. Data were extracted on methane emissions (g/day; g/kg dry matter intake [DMI]), dietary composition (including starch and water-soluble carbohydrate content, where reported), rumen microbial taxa and heritability estimates. Statistical synthesis employed a random-effects meta-analytic model, with heterogeneity quantified using I2 statistics and publication bias assessed via funnel plots and Egger’s regression test. A total of 67 studies encompassing approximately 12,500 animals from 14 countries were included. A pooled heritability estimate of h2 = 0.19 (95% CI: 0.14–0.24; I2 = 64%) indicated moderate genetic control of methane production. High-forage, low-tannin diets significantly elevated methane output relative to concentrate-based diets, which promoted propionate fermentation pathways and reduced methanogenesis. Rumen microbiome composition, particularly the relative abundance of Methanobrevibacter spp. was significantly associated with inter-animal variation in methane yield (r = 0.58; p < 0.001). Defaunation interventions reduced methane emissions by approximately 11%. Integration of rumen microbiome data into genomic prediction models substantially improved accuracy from 0.42 (genomic-only) to 0.61 (genomic + microbiome). Carbon footprint estimates across production systems ranged from 15.8 to 17.1 kg CO2-eq/kg mutton carcass weight, and water footprint estimates ranged from 140 to 210 m3/kg mutton, tracking the same production-intensity gradient. Methane emissions in sheep are governed by the complex interplay of host genetics, rumen microbiome architecture and dietary substrate availability. Integrated approaches combining precision nutrition with microbiome-informed genomic selection represent the most effective and feasible pathway to simultaneously enhance feed efficiency and reduce environmental impact in small ruminant production systems.

title: Physics-guided multi-scale temporal transformer with dynamic key variable selection for building energy consumption forecasting
summary: Building energy consumption prediction plays a critical role in intelligent energy management, demand response, and low-carbon operation of smart buildings. This paper proposes a novel physics-guided multi-scale temporal Transformer (PMSTFo
content: Building energy consumption prediction plays a critical role in intelligent energy management, demand response, and low-carbon operation of smart buildings. This paper proposes a novel physics-guided multi-scale temporal Transformer (PMSTFormer) for building energy consumption forecasting. First, a dynamic key variable selection (DKVS) module is developed to adaptively estimate the contribution of heterogeneous input variables at each prediction horizon. Second, a multi-scale temporal fusion encoder (MTFE) is designed to capture temporal dependencies at multiple resolutions. Finally, a physics-guided thermal consistency learning (PTCL) strategy is proposed by embedding physical constraints into the optimization process. PTCL is implemented as a set of differentiable soft constraints that jointly optimize data fidelity and simplified thermal-response consistency. It does not require an explicit thermal model or solver in the loop, and is therefore complementary to methods that enforce physical consistency by construction. Extensive experiments are conducted on publicly available benchmark datasets Building Data Genome 2. Comparative studies demonstrate that the proposed PMSTFormer consistently outperforms state-of-the-art forecasting models. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation studies verify the effectiveness of each proposed module. The developed methodology not only improves forecasting accuracy but also offers a practical and reliable decision-support tool for intelligent building energy management systems.

title: How does intercropping perennial grains with alfalfa impact soil physical and hydraulic properties?
summary: Perennial cereal–legume intercropping systems are promoted as climate-smart and resilient alternatives to annual monocultures; however, their effects on soil physical and hydraulic properties remain poorly quantified, particularly for devel
content: Perennial cereal–legume intercropping systems are promoted as climate-smart and resilient alternatives to annual monocultures; however, their effects on soil physical and hydraulic properties remain poorly quantified, particularly for developed perennial cereals; ACE1 perennial rye ( Secale cereale L.) and intermediate wheatgrass (IWG) ( Thinopyrum intermedium ). This study evaluated how intercropping these perennial cereal grain crops (PCGCs) with alfalfa ( Medicago sativa L. ) influences soil physical structure and hydraulic functioning across five field locations in Alberta, Canada. Sites were established in spring 2022, and soils were sampled in summer 2024. Using a split–split plot design, we assessed crop utilization (forage or grain), seeding arrangement, and crop treatment (intercrop or monocrop) effects on soil physical and hydraulic properties at 10–15 and 30–35 cm depths. Topsoil organic carbon (SOC) stock was also measured at 0–15 cm depth increment. Intercropping enhanced soil hydraulic properties in a site-specific manner. Compared to monocultures, PCGC–alfalfa intercrops increased field capacity (FC), plant-available water capacity (PAWC), and meso and microporosity by 6–45 %, with stronger effects at 30–35 cm depth. Unsaturated hydraulic conductivity varied among sites, but IWG-based intercrops exhibited 20–40 % higher values than ACE1 under comparable management. SOC–hydraulic relationships were context dependent; intercrops strengthened SOC water retention linkages, particularly at high-carbon sites. Multivariate analyses associated intercrops with improved water retention, pore connectivity, and S-index, whereas monocrops aligned with increased bulk density and reduced hydraulic function. Overall, intercropping PCGCs with alfalfa improved soil hydraulic functioning, primarily through enhanced water dynamics rather than major structural change, highlighting their potential to increase soil resilience across diverse environments.

title: Does Reducing Relative Income Poverty Carry a Carbon Cost? An Informative Null on the SDG 1– SDG 13 Interface in 25 OECD and EU Economies
summary: ABSTRACT In a balanced panel of 25 OECD and EU economies over 2007 to 2022, changes in the relative income poverty rate show no measurable association with CO 2 emissions per capita. Within‐country changes and between‐country differences ar
content: ABSTRACT In a balanced panel of 25 OECD and EU economies over 2007 to 2022, changes in the relative income poverty rate show no measurable association with CO 2 emissions per capita. Within‐country changes and between‐country differences are both null under production and consumption accounting, in fixed effects and quantile specifications. The production‐based interval confines the association between a one‐standard‐deviation poverty change and emissions to between −0.4 and +1.3%, while the consumption‐based interval of −1.6 to +2.6% is wider and less precise. Westerlund tests give no evidence of cointegration in this 16‐year sample. Subgroup estimates by income, region, energy‐system carbon intensity and welfare regime reproduce the production‐based null everywhere and the consumption‐based coefficient differs across income groups and welfare regimes but offsets to zero when pooled. The presumed SDG 1‐SDG 13 trade‐off finds no support at the country‐year level and the design is associational and cannot exclude offsetting household‐level effects.

title: ‌ Beyond the shortest path: Identifying optimal walkable routes using a street walkability index derived from deep learning and micro-scale pedestrian environment features
summary: Abstract Urban streets are fundamental public spaces that underpin residents’ daily non-motorized travel, and their on-street pedestrian environment and walkability directly shape people’s walking mode decisions and walking experiences. How
content: Abstract Urban streets are fundamental public spaces that underpin residents’ daily non-motorized travel, and their on-street pedestrian environment and walkability directly shape people’s walking mode decisions and walking experiences. However, few existing studies have systematically examined street-level walkability from the perspective of micro-scale pedestrian environment features—particularly its critical role in identifying the truly optimal walkable routes. This study develops a Street Walkability Index (SWI) based on street view image data, deep learning and seven specific street micro-environmental indicators. Leveraging this index, we propose an innovative method for optimal walkable route identification, and conduct empirical validation and performance testing in a historic urban district of Guangzhou. The results show that the average SWI in this district is 35.0638, with 56.25% of the streets scoring below this mean value. Overall, arterial roads exhibit the poorest walkability, while branch roads and internal roads show relatively better walkability. The seven street micro-environmental indicators display distinct spatial distribution characteristics. Branch roads and internal roads perform outstandingly in terms of space vitality, enclosure, pedestrian conditions, and visual permeability. Secondary arterial roads generally have the best street greenery coverage, while arterial roads perform best in openness. For the vast majority of origin-destination pairs, the optimal walkable route is not equivalent to the path with the shortest walking distance. Although the total travel distance of the optimal walkable route increases only marginally, its overall walkability can be improved by a substantially larger margin. This study advances our in-depth understanding of street walkability and optimal walkable route planning, and facilitates their practical implementation in pedestrian navigation systems.

title: Managing healthcare capacity and demand, not just emissions: decarbonization as a purpose-preserving health system sustainability strategy—an Alberta policy case study
summary: Introduction Healthcare decarbonization is increasingly important, yet strategies often focus on emissions from care delivery rather than the climate-related demand and disruption that health systems must absorb. Climate pressures can incre
content: Introduction Healthcare decarbonization is increasingly important, yet strategies often focus on emissions from care delivery rather than the climate-related demand and disruption that health systems must absorb. Climate pressures can increase service use, workforce strain, infrastructure risk, and fiscal pressure at the same time, making healthcare capacity as much a concern as emissions. Methodology We use Alberta Health Services (AHS), 2013–2024, as a descriptive single case and interpret the evidence through Purpose-Preserving Resilience (PPR), distinguishing documented findings from conceptual interpretation. Conclusion Decarbonization can create a triple dividend—population health, workforce, and fiscal benefits—when mitigation and adaptation preserve essential health-system purpose without transferring unsustainable burden elsewhere. Climate action should be embedded in governance, capacity planning, workforce strategy, infrastructure and performance measurement, with system-wide measures of purpose outcomes.

title: EmiMap: Ghana greenhouse gas emissions map, national, regional and district data (2022, with history and projections)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: EmiMap is the Ghana Greenhouse Gas Emissions Map developed by the Net-Zero Carbon Emission Lab (NCEL), Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). This deposit holds EmiMap application 2.0.3 data (dataset 2022-reconciled-2.0
content: EmiMap is the Ghana Greenhouse Gas Emissions Map developed by the Net-Zero Carbon Emission Lab (NCEL), Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). This deposit holds EmiMap application 2.0.3 data (dataset 2022-reconciled-2.0): Ghana's 2022 national greenhouse gas inventory (54,758.6 kt CO2e, IPCC AR5 GWP100, including LULUCF; BTR1) allocated to 16 regions and 261 districts by component and gas, with history from 1990 and the national BTR1 projection cases to 2040. District and regional values are analytical estimates, not official local inventories. Polygon geometry is not included; places carry names and IDs. Every field is described in CODEBOOK.csv. Developed by the Net-Zero Carbon Emission Lab (NCEL) under the Net-Zero Carbon Emissions Project (NCEP), funded by Yinson Production West Africa Limited, in collaboration with KNUST and the Petroleum Commission. Web application: https://emimap.ncelknust.org Provisional status: District and regional values are analytical estimates, not official local inventories or forecasts. Uncertainty ranges are withheld pending joint validation of the ensemble and final estimator. Not peer reviewed. Contact: ncel@knust.edu.gh

title: RepairTax-530: An Energy-Annotated Multi-Turn LLM Code Correction Attempt Dataset Across Five Models and Three Difficulty Tiers
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: RepairTax-530 is an empirical dataset containing 530 detailed attempt records across 150 problem-model evaluation sessions during automated iterative code correction using large language models (LLMs). Unlike conventional code generation be
content: RepairTax-530 is an empirical dataset containing 530 detailed attempt records across 150 problem-model evaluation sessions during automated iterative code correction using large language models (LLMs). Unlike conventional code generation benchmarks that report only functional correctness (Pass@k), RepairTax-530 pairs every individual attempt with: Physically-Measured Hardware Energy: Sub-second component-level energy for both GPU board power (via NVIDIA NVML hardware joule accumulators) and CPU package power (via Intel RAPL MSRs) sampled at 10 Hz. Phase Decomposition: Energy broken down across neural autoregressive generation (E_gen), sandboxed container compilation (E_comp), and automated binary test execution (E_exec). Diagnostic Feedback Tracing: Every correction prompt records the source attempt, failing test case, and failure classification (compile_error, wrong_answer, runtime_error, timeout). Operational Carbon Accounting: Derived emissions in gCO2e grounded in empirical national grid factors. 14 Analytical Tables: Ready-to-use derived CSV tables covering benchmark scorecards, error transition matrices, regressions, and statistical tests. Models Evaluated: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-3B, Phi-4-mini-3.8B, Mistral-7B (4-bit NF4 quantization, temperature 0.2, seed 42). Benchmark Corpus: 30 HackerRank algorithmic problems (10 Easy, 10 Medium, 10 Hard) spanning 6 computer science domains. Isolation: gcc:13.5.0 inside isolated Docker containers (512 MB RAM, 1.0 CPU cap, no network). Associated Publication: Submitted to Elsevier Data in Brief as a companion dataset for the study "An Empirical Study of Energy, Carbon, and Diminishing Returns in Iterative LLM Code Correction". Note: Associated data article is under submission at Elsevier Data in Brief.

title: Beyond depletion: inositol as a candidate endocrine-metabolic countermeasure in psychotropic drug therapy
summary: Inositol’s relevance to psychiatry has rested on the unresolved hypothesis that lithium acts through inositol depletion. Inositol could matter for patients treated with psychotropic drugs through two routes: a central route, which remains u
content: Inositol’s relevance to psychiatry has rested on the unresolved hypothesis that lithium acts through inositol depletion. Inositol could matter for patients treated with psychotropic drugs through two routes: a central route, which remains unresolved, and a peripheral route, in which inositol acts as an insulin-sensitizing agent and as a second messenger in thyroid and gonadal signaling. The peripheral evidence comes from populations without psychiatric illness, is of low certainty, and concerns surrogate measures, not incident diabetes or cardiovascular events. We examine four drug classes, antipsychotics, lithium, valproate, and antidepressants, each associated with weight gain and insulin resistance through partly distinct pathways, two of them also with thyroid or reproductive dysfunction, and grade the rationale in each. The rationale is strongest for olanzapine, which impairs the insulin-signaling node that inositol supports in rat muscle cells and induced weight-independent insulin resistance in a small study in healthy volunteers; this shows that the pathways converge, not that inositol would restore the impaired signaling. For lithium, the rationale is inseparable from the unresolved central mechanism, and a peripheral extension has not been measured. For valproate, reduced inositol synthesis is documented in yeast and mouse cells, while the peripheral finding in patients is reduced hepatic insulin clearance, not a defect at that node. For antidepressants, weight gain is common across the class, and impaired insulin sensitivity is reported mainly for select tricyclics. No controlled trial has tested inositol against psychotropic-induced endocrine and metabolic disruption; small, short trials with mood stabilizers detected no change in drug levels but were not powered for relapse or mood switch. We propose a prospective biomarker study that separates replacement of a depleted pool from a pharmacological effect; a placebo-controlled prevention trial at olanzapine initiation, with insulin sensitivity as the single primary endpoint, psychiatric outcomes monitored for safety, and a dose-finding phase comparing myo-inositol alone with combinations; and, as a complementary strategy, raising endogenous inositol synthesis. Because inositol is expected to be weight-neutral, no effect on adherence can be assumed. This synthesis is hypothesis-generating: we do not claim that inositol is protective, but identify an untested endocrine-metabolic rationale.

title: Climate Policy and Sovereign Debt: The Impact of Transition Scenarios on Sovereign Creditworthiness
summary: Abstract This paper links climate science with sovereign risk assessment to produce a single forward-looking measure of country-level climate change risk. We combine the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) climate scenarios wit
content: Abstract This paper links climate science with sovereign risk assessment to produce a single forward-looking measure of country-level climate change risk. We combine the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) climate scenarios with a sovereign credit ratings model to simulate the impact of climate change on credit ratings, cost of debt and probability of default. For the first time, we extend beyond the physical risks of extreme weather events to explicitly incorporate risks associated with transitioning the global economy towards Net Zero. Across the sample of 48 countries and under a scenario of high (low) physical and transition risks, we find average increases in the cost of debt of 61 (31) basis points and default probability of 4.7% (2.4%). Counter-intuitively, ratings, default probability, and cost of debt appear insensitive to scenarios in some countries, with important implications for the usefulness of NGFS scenarios across central banks.

title: The tumor as a dynamic metabolic interaction network: From the Warburg effect to multi-node collapse as a therapeutic strategy
summary: Cancer metabolism research has long been shaped by a pathway-centric paradigm, in which individual biochemical routes—most prominently aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect)—are studied and targeted in relative isolation. Accumulating evid
content: Cancer metabolism research has long been shaped by a pathway-centric paradigm, in which individual biochemical routes—most prominently aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect)—are studied and targeted in relative isolation. Accumulating evidence from systems biology, multi-omics profiling, and computational oncology suggests, however, that this view is insufficient to explain the adaptive resilience that solid tumors routinely demonstrate against metabolic inhibitors. Here we propose a conceptual synthesis: the tumor dynamic metabolic interaction network, a graph-theoretic framework in which metabolic enzymes and transporters constitute nodes, substrate fluxes define weighted edges, and the system’s overall state is governed by topological properties such as betweenness centrality and eigenvector centrality. Within this framework, we elaborate the hypothesis of dynamic network collapse (DNC)—the notion that simultaneous perturbation of several high-centrality nodes may push the tumor metabolic network beyond a thermodynamic instability threshold, triggering irreversible functional disintegration that cannot be escaped through known compensatory rerouting. We review the three dominant metabolic axes of tumor survival—glucose (GLUT1/HK2/PKM2), glutamine (SLC1A5/GLS1), and lactate efflux (MCT1/MCT4)—and examine how each contributes to immunosuppression through metabolic competition with cytotoxic T lymphocytes and through the acidification of the tumor microenvironment. We further discuss genome-scale metabolic models, flux balance analysis, and graph neural network approaches that may render the DNC concept computationally actionable. The clinical implications of multi-node targeting are considered alongside the limitations of existing evidence and unresolved methodological challenges. Although the DNC hypothesis remains to be tested experimentally in relevant in vivo models, it provides a coherent rationale for the next generation of combination metabolic therapies and for patient-specific metabolic profiling as a decision tool.

title: Contrasting Elemental Composition of Stomatal Complex Surfaces Is Associated With Divergent Gas Exchange Responses to Salinity in Maize and Faba Bean
summary: ABSTRACT Salinity tolerance is commonly associated with whole leaf Na + exclusion and maintenance of K + homeostasis, but whether spatial ion partitioning among functional leaf compartments contributes to stress adaptation remains unclear.
content: ABSTRACT Salinity tolerance is commonly associated with whole leaf Na + exclusion and maintenance of K + homeostasis, but whether spatial ion partitioning among functional leaf compartments contributes to stress adaptation remains unclear. Here, we investigated the relationship between bulk leaf and stomatal complex surface elemental composition and gas exchange performance under salinity using two contrasting genotypes in both maize and faba bean crops. Maize generally maintained higher photosynthesis and stomatal conductance than faba bean under salt stress, which was associated with lower Na + accumulation, stronger K + retention, and distinct ion partitioning patterns between bulk leaf tissue and the stomatal complex. Enrichment analysis revealed that stomatal complex ion composition provided information beyond bulk leaf ion concentrations, with Na + and Cl − showing distinct distribution patterns associated with photosynthetic performance. Integrating physiological and ionomic traits further demonstrated that stomatal‐complex ion traits captured additional variation in salinity responses. These findings reveal distinct surface elemental patterns at the stomatal complex that provide information beyond bulk leaf elemental concentrations and are associated with gas exchange responses under salinity.

title: Incentive-Based Riparian Restoration as A Scalable Model for Agricultural Watershed Compliance
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE
summary: Riparian buffers, vegetated waterways, streambank stabilization practices, and floodplain reconnection projects collectively constitute the riparian restoration toolkit through which agricultural watershed compliance programs address nonpoi
content: Riparian buffers, vegetated waterways, streambank stabilization practices, and floodplain reconnection projects collectively constitute the riparian restoration toolkit through which agricultural watershed compliance programs address nonpoint source nitrogen, phosphorus, sediment, and pathogen loadings from cropland and pasture. Despite decades of federal investment through the Conservation Reserve Program, Environmental Quality Incentives Program, and state-funded buffer initiatives, riparian practice installation remains substantially below levels required to achieve watershed-scale water quality compliance in most priority agricultural watersheds under Clean Water Act total maximum daily loads and state nutrient reduction strategies. This paper develops a scalable incentive design framework for riparian restoration in agricultural watersheds, synthesizing the behavioral economics of landowner conservation decisions, the hydrology and ecology of riparian system function, and the institutional design of multi-level agricultural watershed governance. The framework identifies payment structure, technical assistance quality, social norm alignment, institutional environment, and landscape targeting as the five primary levers through which incentive programs can accelerate riparian restoration at watershed scales sufficient to achieve regulatory compliance. Analysis of program design innovations from the Chesapeake Bay watershed, the Gulf Hypoxia reduction initiative, Great Lakes basin nutrient programs, and Pacific Northwest salmon habitat restoration illustrates the scalability conditions under which incentive-based riparian restoration achieves watershed-scale water quality outcomes. The framework builds on companion analyses of BMP adoption determinants, federal-tribal co-management architecture, and multi-level watershed governance to integrate behavioral, ecological, and institutional perspectives into a unified design approach. Implications for federal conservation program design, state nonpoint source programs, and watershed-scale compliance planning are developed.

title: Best Management Practice Adoption in Nonpoint Source Pollution Control: A Systematic Review of Barriers, Enablers, and SiteSpecific Implementation Pathways
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE
summary: Nonpoint source (NPS) pollution from agricultural, urban, and silvicultural land uses constitutes the leading remaining cause of surface water quality impairment in the United States and a primary driver of aquatic biodiversity loss, eutrop
content: Nonpoint source (NPS) pollution from agricultural, urban, and silvicultural land uses constitutes the leading remaining cause of surface water quality impairment in the United States and a primary driver of aquatic biodiversity loss, eutrophication, and drinking water contamination globally. Best management practices (BMPs) represent the primary technical and regulatory mechanism for NPS pollution control, encompassing a broad array of structural, vegetative, and managerial practices designed to reduce pollutant generation, transport, and delivery at the field, farm, and watershed scales. Yet BMP adoption by private landowners and land managers remains substantially below levels necessary to achieve watershed-scale water quality goals, despite decades of voluntary incentive programs, regulatory requirements, and extension outreach. This paper presents a narrative review and conceptual synthesis of the literature on BMP adoption barriers, enablers, and implementation pathways, drawing on published empirical research spanning 1985 through 2023 across agricultural, silvicultural, and mixed land use contexts. The review characterizes the economic, informational, social, and institutional determinants of adoption decisions and identifies site-specific implementation pathway models that account for landscape typology, landowner profile, and institutional environment as interactive determinants of adoption likelihood and durability. The review finds that adoption is most strongly predicted by program payment levels, social norm alignment, peer network influence, and technical assistance quality, with significant interaction effects among these factors that vary systematically across landscape and landowner typologies. Implications for BMP program design, targeting, and adaptive management are developed. Cross-citations to related governance frameworks developed in parallel work inform the institutional analysis.

title: Tourism demand concentration exposes ecological carrying-capacity mismatches in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
summary: Tourism growth and ecological protection increasingly overlap in large river-basin corridors, but available visitor statistics rarely provide a continuous, cross-regional series and within-city spatial detail at the same time. We therefore
content: Tourism growth and ecological protection increasingly overlap in large river-basin corridors, but available visitor statistics rarely provide a continuous, cross-regional series and within-city spatial detail at the same time. We therefore used a long-term tourism-demand/service-concentration proxy (TD) as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, observed visitation. Across 129 administrative analytical units in the Yangtze River Economic Belt in 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2023, we combined entropy-weight TOPSIS TD and ecological resource-pressure/capacity (ECC) indices with coupling co-development, a directional relative mismatch index (MI), spatial statistics, GeoDetector and 5-km management zoning. TD increased from 0.041 to 0.147, the main-specification ECC averaged 0.131 in 2023, and CCD increased from 0.240 to 0.341. In 2023, 35 units were TD-dominant and 30 were ECC-dominant; global Moran’s I was 0.170 ( p = 0.003), with 26 significant local clusters. MI rankings were highly similar under min-max scaling (Spearman rho = 0.997), and city TD was strongly associated with the area-weighted mean grid tourism-intensity proxy (Pearson r = 0.918; Spearman rho = 0.888; n = 129). ECC rankings remained sensitive to weighting and water-wetland specification. Rail accessibility had the largest single-factor GeoDetector q value (0.202), and potential-cultivation zones covered 54.83% of the study area. The results provide a relative spatial diagnosis for differentiated management, not an estimate of biophysical visitor-capacity thresholds.

title: Does Nationality Matter? Foreign CEOs and Green Innovation: The Role of Institutional Pressure
summary: ABSTRACT Drawing on upper echelons' theory and legitimacy theory, this study examines whether and under what conditions foreign CEOs enhance green innovation in Chinese firms. Using data from firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock
content: ABSTRACT Drawing on upper echelons' theory and legitimacy theory, this study examines whether and under what conditions foreign CEOs enhance green innovation in Chinese firms. Using data from firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges, our multivariate regression results provide robust evidence that firms led by foreign CEOs exhibit significantly superior green innovation performance than those led by local CEOs. Importantly, this advantage is more pronounced in firms located in economically developed regions, firms subject to greater media scrutiny, and firms operating in highly competitive industries. Furthermore, our results show that environmental initiatives led by foreign CEOs are positively associated with enhanced shareholder value. Furthermore, we address endogeneity using firm, year, and province fixed effects, supplemented by lagged specifications and a difference‐in‐differences approach exploiting CEO transitions from local to foreign CEOs. By highlighting the contingent value of foreign CEOs in emerging economies, our findings extend upper echelons and legitimacy theories and contribute to the corporate social responsibility and green innovation literature, while offering meaningful implications for boards, policymakers, and regulators.

title: CropWISE: A spatially explicit and integrated multi-objective simulation-optimization framework for water quality, soil carbon, and economic outcomes in agricultural watersheds
summary: Modern agriculture faces the dual challenge of increasing food production while mitigating environmental degradation. Addressing these coupled issues requires accounting for hydrologic and nutrient processes as well as soil organic carbon (
content: Modern agriculture faces the dual challenge of increasing food production while mitigating environmental degradation. Addressing these coupled issues requires accounting for hydrologic and nutrient processes as well as soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics and their economic implications. This study presents CropWISE (Carbon-Runoff-Optimization for Productivity: Watershed Integrity Simulation and Evaluation), a framework integrating simulations with spatial optimization to balance productivity, water quality, and soil health. A hydrologic module was applied to the Wildcat Creek watershed (Indiana, USA) to simulate the impacts of land use and management scenarios on nonpoint source (NPS) pollution. In parallel, a farm-scale carbon accounting module simulated changes in SOC under different management practices and soil types, enabling the valuation of soil health benefits. These outputs informed the grid-based, stochastic, fractional mixed-integer, multi-objective optimization core of CropWISE to identify spatially explicit optimal management portfolios for each grid cell. This core maximizes agricultural profits and environmental benefits (from improved water quality and carbon credit participation) while minimizing NPS loads, carbon emissions, grey water and total carbon footprint. Results show that the optimized spatial scheme, relative to the status quo, could reduce total nitrogen and total phosphorus loads by 6.35% and 8.39%, while ensuring net soil carbon storage. This comes with an 8.95% reduction in agricultural profit, but monetizing environmental improvements increases total system benefit by approximately 27.90%. These findings underscore the value of grid-scale optimization and economic incentives in aligning farmer profits with watershed ecological goals. CropWISE offers a transferable, spatially explicit approach for integrated watershed management.

title: Supporting ethical engagement with AI in education: Evaluating the ethical coverage of the Scaffolded AI Literacy (SAIL) framework<!--a=1-->
summary: Ethical engagement with AI in education requires more than awareness of risks or compliance with institutional policy. Educators and learners need to recognise, evaluate, mitigate, and respond to ethical issues as AI tools become embedded i
content: Ethical engagement with AI in education requires more than awareness of risks or compliance with institutional policy. Educators and learners need to recognise, evaluate, mitigate, and respond to ethical issues as AI tools become embedded in learning and teaching. This paper examines whether the Scaffolded AI Literacy (SAIL) framework provides a sufficiently comprehensive set of competencies for this purpose. Six cross-sector systematic reviews and mappings of AI ethics are analysed to provide a benchmark of recurring ethical issues identified in relation to AI. The comparison shows strong coverage in the SAIL framework of issues including fairness, equity, transparency, privacy and safety. Human agency, accountability, well-being, human rights, and participation are partially addressed but less explicit. Notably, environmental sustainability demonstrates the clearest gap between emphasis in the literature and explicit coverage in the framework. The analysis supports SAIL as a substantial framework for ethical AI literacy while identifying targeted opportunities for refinement.

title: Green Leadership and Sustainable Healthcare: Distinguishing Organizational Performance from Measured Environmental Outcomes
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS
summary: Healthcare organizations are under growing pressure to reduce their environmental footprint while sustaining safe, effective, and resilient health services. Against this backdrop, environmental and sustainability-oriented leadership has att
content: Healthcare organizations are under growing pressure to reduce their environmental footprint while sustaining safe, effective, and resilient health services. Against this backdrop, environmental and sustainability-oriented leadership has attracted attention as a way to embed sustainability in healthcare governance, workforce practices, and operational decision-making. This review synthesizes recent evidence on how sustainability-oriented leadership is conceptualized in healthcare organizations, which employee and organizational outcomes are associated with it, what mechanisms and conditions shape these relationships, and whether leadership has been linked directly with measurable environmental outcomes. A qualitative literature review design was used to examine scientific literature published between 2018 and 2026 and identified through Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar, supplemented by relevant scholarly and institutional sources. Qualitative content analysis organized the evidence into thematic domains covering leadership constructs, behavioral and organizational outcomes, mediating mechanisms, enabling conditions and barriers, and operational environmental outcomes. Across the reviewed studies, sustainability-oriented leadership was associated with sustainable clinical behavior, employee green behavior, environmental performance, green human resource management, green innovation, and organizational sustainable performance. These relationships were often mediated or conditioned by green psychological climate, employee attitudes, empowerment, self-efficacy, organizational support, and human resource practices. By contrast, direct reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, resource consumption, healthcare waste, and costs were documented mainly in studies of technical or circular-economy interventions rather than leadership studies. The evidence therefore positions sustainability-oriented leadership as an enabling governance mechanism rather than a direct environmental intervention. The review's main contribution is to distinguish leadership-related behavioral and organizational outcomes from objectively measured environmental performance, providing a more precise basis for future empirical research and sustainable healthcare management.

title: Investment allocation and the financial performance of listed insurance companies: A panel data analysis
summary: Insurance companies convert policyholder premiums into investment portfolios, and the composition of that portfolio is widely assumed to shape profitability. Yet, beyond evidence that pools Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries together
content: Insurance companies convert policyholder premiums into investment portfolios, and the composition of that portfolio is widely assumed to shape profitability. Yet, beyond evidence that pools Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries together (Ahmed, 2022) or examines a single neighbouring market without disaggregating the portfolio (Ben Dhiab, 2021), little empirical evidence isolates the separate contribution of each asset class within a single, small, tightly regulated insurance market. This study examines how five investment classes—equities, bonds, fixed deposits, managed funds, and real estate—affect the return on assets (ROA) of the five insurance companies listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange (QSE) between 2019 and 2023 (n = 25 firm-year observations). Using panel data and robust fixed effects and random effects regressions across an allocation model and five asset-specific subgroup models, the study finds that investment in fixed deposits (β = 0.792, p = 0.040) and real estate (β = 0.516, p = 0.037) significantly and positively raises ROA, while equity holdings significantly reduce it (β = -0.449, p = 0.090). Bonds and managed funds show positive but statistically insignificant effects. The results indicate that conservative, liability-matching allocations—not diversification into growth assets—drive insurer profitability in Qatar, with direct implications for insurers’ asset-liability management and investment regulation.

title: A Digital Twin Approach to Integrating Silviculture into Harvester Simulator Training
summary: Abstract Forest machine simulators have been an integral part of forest machine training for several decades. However, the primary focus of this training has been on developing technical machine operation skills, while less emphasis has bee
content: Abstract Forest machine simulators have been an integral part of forest machine training for several decades. However, the primary focus of this training has been on developing technical machine operation skills, while less emphasis has been placed on environmental and silvicultural competencies. In this paper, we introduce new teaching modules that extend training beyond purely technical machine control, enabling the simultaneous development of operational skills and silvicultural decision-making. This is achieved through the use of digital twins of forest stands. We present the methodologies used to capture individual tree data and terrain topography from drone-based inventories and to convert these data into a format compatible with a harvester simulator. We then demonstrate three new teaching modules in which trainees learn climate-smart management of forest edges, selection cutting in uneven-aged stands, and harvesting on erosion-prone steep slopes. In addition, we show how harvester operations can be supported by auxiliary data layers visualized through the onboard harvester computer. We argue that digital twinning of forest sites can elevate harvester simulator training to a new level by integrating environmental and silvicultural considerations into machine operation. Furthermore, it provides an efficient testbed for evaluating which types of map layers most effectively support tree selection, operator training, and the management of information overload in operational settings.

title: Regional governance of the energy transition: A comparison of spatial policies in Germany
summary: The energy transition is a multifaceted and spatially differentiated transformation process that requires effective governance across multiple policy levels. While national and local energy governance has been widely examined, the regional
content: The energy transition is a multifaceted and spatially differentiated transformation process that requires effective governance across multiple policy levels. While national and local energy governance has been widely examined, the regional level remains comparatively understudied despite its crucial role in translating strategic objectives into local implementation and in mediating between policy scales. This paper examines how regional energy transition governance in Germany is shaped through planning and policy instruments in different spatial contexts. This study undertakes a comparative policy screening of 199 formal and informal planning documents related to renewable energy development in three contrasting regions: the Ruhr Area, Western Pomerania, and the Upper Rhine. The analysis focuses on steering modes, degrees of formalisation, style of communication, and patterns of actor involvement to identify region-specific governance constellations. The results reveal clearly distinguishable regional governance profiles. The Ruhr Area is characterised by strategy-oriented governance coordinated predominantly through informal instruments with limited legal binding. Western Pomerania uses a more hierarchical and legally formalised approach, in which the public is addressed comparatively less frequently. The Upper Rhine exhibits a more cooperative and stakeholder-oriented governance profile, with municipalities, civil society, and scientific actors being relatively strongly represented. Overall, the findings suggest that regional energy transition governance does not follow a uniform model but instead is shaped by hybrid, context-specific arrangements. Recognising this difference and strengthening adaptive and learning-oriented forms of regional governance may contribute to improving both the effectiveness and the legitimacy of energy transition processes.

title: Hypoglycemic Effect of Methanolic Extract of Annona Squmosa L. (Seeds) on Streptozotocin-Induced Diabetes in Rats
source: Journal of Pharmaceutical Research and Integrated Medical Sciences
summary: The purity, safety, and long-term therapeutic efficacy of Annona squamosa L. seed extract in the treatment of diabetes were thoroughly assessed. Petroleum ether defatting and Soxhlet methanolic extraction came with the establishment of phys
content: The purity, safety, and long-term therapeutic efficacy of Annona squamosa L. seed extract in the treatment of diabetes were thoroughly assessed. Petroleum ether defatting and Soxhlet methanolic extraction came with the establishment of physicochemical standards (ash values). High levels of total phenolic content (TPC) and total flavonoid content (TFC), which provided notable in vitro antioxidant and anti-glycation properties, were shown by quantitative phytochemical screening. According to OECD Guideline 420 (Fixed Dose Procedure), acute oral toxicity testing verified that the extract has a broad margin of safety, showing no evidence of acute toxicity or fatality up to the highest suggested limit dose. Oral administration of Annona squamosa L. seed extract (200 mg/kg and 400 mg/kg) significantly decreased fasting blood glucose levels and reversed progressive body weight loss in an 8-week in vivo study on streptozotocin (STZ, 50-55 mg/kg)-induced diabetic Wistar rats when compared to untreated diabetic controls. The therapeutic efficacy of the 400 mg/kg dose was similar to that of normal Glibenclamide (10 mg/kg). To sum up, Annona squamosa L. seed methanolic extract is a safe, flavonoid-rich, antioxidant-rich substance that successfully reduces glycation, hyperglycemia, and weight loss in people with chronic diabetes.

title: Phosphorus-Functionalized Carbon Quantum Dot-Doped Alginate Beads for Rapid and High-Capacity Recovery of Rare Earth Elements
summary: Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from waste streams requires adsorbents that combine rapid uptake, high capacity, and effective regeneration. Here, phosphorus-functionalized carbon quantum dots immobilized on alginate beads (P-CQD/ALG)
content: Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from waste streams requires adsorbents that combine rapid uptake, high capacity, and effective regeneration. Here, phosphorus-functionalized carbon quantum dots immobilized on alginate beads (P-CQD/ALG) were developed to integrate REE-binding functionality with a readily separable solid form. First, phosphorus functionalization (P-CQD/ALG) showed substantially higher Ce3+ removal than pristine alginate and unmodified or nitrogen-functionalized CQD composites, suggesting P-CQD/ALG as an optimal adsorbent. Second, P-CQD/ALG also achieved fast, strong, and selective removal of 11 REEs at 78%–95% after 60 min in synthetic solutions at pH 6.8, while uptake of most other common metals was ≤9%. One exception was that Fe3+ outcompeted most REEs, identifying the requirement for iron pre-treatment. Spectroscopic characterization and uptake trends suggest electrostatic attraction and coordination with phosphorus-containing oxygen groups as major mechanisms. Third, Langmuir adsorption capacities reached 301–430 mg/g for Ce3+ and Er3+, 1.1–36 times higher than the existing materials. The capacity-normalized cost (0.05–0.07 $/kg per mg/g) was also 7–3780 times lower than other materials. Lastly, dilute HNO3 (0.05 M) enabled Ce3+ desorption and repeated adsorption over five cycles. These findings identify P-CQD/ALG as a promising platform for REE recovery, with further validation needed in real wastewaters.

title: Changes in Climate, Crimes and Natural Disasters
summary: This chapter summarises climate trends and issues, including its anthropocentric origins, its consequences in terms of risks, harms and disasters, and its acceleration. Compounding problems and crises are identified, as are climate-related
content: This chapter summarises climate trends and issues, including its anthropocentric origins, its consequences in terms of risks, harms and disasters, and its acceleration. Compounding problems and crises are identified, as are climate-related crimes. The intersections between crimes, climate-related events such as floods and storms, and longer-term problems such as prolonged homelessness are briefly touched upon. Events such as natural disasters have special relevance for criminal justice institutions, especially for law enforcement agencies and prisons, and portend new roles, new responses and new responsibilities for criminal justice. Crime trends, law-and-order politics and criminal justice practices are inevitably implicated in the global concerns about, and responses to, climate-related issues. The impacts of global warming are reflected in climate-related crimes as well as greater criminal justice involvement in disasters and emergency management.

title: Supply chain network position and firms’ innovation boundary width: A dynamic capabilities perspective
summary: Supply chain networks have become important channels through which firms obtain external heterogeneous resources, integrate diverse knowledge, and coordinate innovation across organizational boundaries. Using data on Chinese A-share listed
content: Supply chain networks have become important channels through which firms obtain external heterogeneous resources, integrate diverse knowledge, and coordinate innovation across organizational boundaries. Using data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2022, this study examines the relationship between firms' supply chain network (SCN) positions and innovation boundary width from a dynamic capabilities perspective. The results show that firms occupying more central SCN positions tend to exhibit broader innovation boundaries, with the positive association remaining significant after controlling for patent portfolio size and under alternative network-position measures. The mechanism tests provide evidence consistent with knowledge access and absorptive capacity, financing constraints, and market-based innovation resilience, which represent interrelated dimensions of dynamic capabilities. The heterogeneity analysis further indicates that the relationship is stronger among state-owned, manufacturing, and non-technology-intensive firms. These findings extend research on corporate innovation from innovation output to technological boundary width and provide implications for leveraging supply chain embeddedness to support broader technological exploration.

title: Aligning trade and energy policies for sustainability in ASEAN: a regression discontinuity design with random forest-based inference
summary: Reconciling trade liberalization with a low-carbon transition is a central policy challenge for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries. Rapid economic growth in the region has intensified reliance on fossil fuels, desp
content: Reconciling trade liberalization with a low-carbon transition is a central policy challenge for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries. Rapid economic growth in the region has intensified reliance on fossil fuels, despite commitments to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and 13 (Climate Action). However, the extent to which trade openness and energy mix composition jointly shape green economic performance remains empirically unresolved in the regional context. Using a new analytical framework covering 1990 to 2018, we employ the Global Malmquist-Luenberger productivity index to construct an environmental productivity index. To identify the causal effects of trade and energy policy on green productivity, random forest-based quantile control and regression discontinuity design (RDD) were employed to assess policy effects. Our findings indicate that both trade openness and the utilization of renewable energy significantly boost environmental productivity and foster green technology. Biomass energy, in particular, is recognized as an underutilized resource. However, the ongoing reliance on fossil fuels threatens these advancements, as it undermines the potential for biomass energy to contribute significantly to a sustainable energy future. Our analysis highlights a governance gap: while trade policy can drive efficiency, sustainable progress necessitates integrated energy transition strategies. We conclude that for ASEAN to achieve true sustainability, regional economic policies must align with fair transition measures that phase out fossil fuels, promote renewable and biomass energy, and ensure equitable benefits from green growth, thereby facilitating a just transition.

title: Regenerative Design for Built Environment & Urban Voids - Design for Built Environment & Urban Voids. Professional Workshop. Analysis and Conclusions
summary: The "Architectural Experiences" series of conferences is organised by the Faculty of Interior Architecture (UAUIM) and it represents an itinerant scientific initiative that unites scholars, academics, professionals, and researchers from var
content: The "Architectural Experiences" series of conferences is organised by the Faculty of Interior Architecture (UAUIM) and it represents an itinerant scientific initiative that unites scholars, academics, professionals, and researchers from various branches of design research.This third edition is a scientific platform for examining regenerative design in relation to the urban void and the built environment.It aimed to expand the disciplinary lens by integrating strategies that address ecological health, carbon impacts, and human well-being, while incorporating theoretical, historical, and symbolic perspectives.The transformation of the void goes beyond a matter of spatial reactivation but of engaging collective imaginaries, socio-political histories, and the contested dynamics of territory.Traditional sustainability frameworks, while foundational, often rely on incremental metrics that fall short amid compounding environmental crises.Regenerative design, by contrast, articulates a paradigm premised on systemic renewal, prioritising circular resource flows, carbon-sequestering materials, reversible construction systems, and climate-responsive infrastructures.Such approaches enable architecture to move beyond reductionism and toward net-positive outcomes.Yet, regeneration also demands a rethinking of methodological structures.It necessitates performance-oriented metrics that evaluate energy and emissions, biodiversity indices, evapotranspiration coefficients, thermal inertia, and soil permeability.These parameters expand the design brief across atmospheric, hydrological, and ecological dimensions, calling for spatialised carbon intelligence, multi-scalar feedback loops, and hybridised natural-technological systems.In parallel, the void must be read as a cultural and political artefact.Sites of abandonment are typically situated in areas vulnerable to flooding, overheating, or socio-economic marginalisation.Their regeneration offers the opportunity to align ecological adaptation with spatial justice.Moreover, these spaces often carry deep symbolic and affective weight traces of memory, conflict, resistance, or erasure, requiring design to navigate physical transformation and cultural meaning.
