title: Chloroform Occurrence and Drivers of Disinfection By-Product Formation in Drinking Water in the Tropical Andean Region: Evidence from Four Colombian Municipalities
summary: Abstract Chloroform (CF) is one of the most prevalent disinfection by-products (DBPs) generated during drinking water chlorination, yet field-based evidence about its occurrence in Colombian water supply systems (WSSs) remains limited. This
content: Abstract Chloroform (CF) is one of the most prevalent disinfection by-products (DBPs) generated during drinking water chlorination, yet field-based evidence about its occurrence in Colombian water supply systems (WSSs) remains limited. This study quantified CF concentrations and characterized their relationships with key water quality indicators for the first time in four Colombian municipalities: Montería, Cereté, Tunja, and Soracá. Drinking water samples were collected from six points within each WSS during the dry season. Field and laboratory measurements included turbidity (TB), pH, water temperature (WT), electrical conductivity (EC), free residual chlorine (Cl), ultraviolet absorbance at 254 nm (UV 254 ), and CF concentration. TB remained below 1.0 NTU in all municipalities, indicating compliance with Colombian and international guideline values. Cl exhibited spatial variability and frequently fell below the Colombian recommended minimum of 0.3 mg L -1 in Tunja and Soracá. Mean CF concentrations from highest to lowest were Montería (54 ± 8.28 µg L -1 ) > Tunja (33 ± 6.62 µg L -1 ) > Soracá (31 ± 8.07 µg L -1 ) > Cereté (28 ± 8.31 µg L -1 ). Response surface and correlation analyses indicated that CF occurrence was modulated by municipality-specific combinations of WT, EC, Cl, and UV 254 , with WT and EC more relevant in Montería and Cereté and UV 254 more influential in Tunja and Soracá. However, correlations were generally weak to moderate, indicating that CF formation was governed by the interaction of source water, treatment, and distribution system conditions rather than by a single predictor. These findings provide baseline evidence of CF occurrence in Colombian WSSs, and support routine DBP monitoring that integrates water quality, natural organic matter (NOM) reactivity, and WSS conditions.

title: Emission Differentiation as a Self‐Financing Transition Mechanism: The Case of Sustainability in Automotive Repair and Maintenance
summary: ABSTRACT Global commitments to reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions have focused policy and managerial attention on upstream production and use‐phase emissions, leaving downstream repair and maintenance services (RMS) largely overlooked.
content: ABSTRACT Global commitments to reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions have focused policy and managerial attention on upstream production and use‐phase emissions, leaving downstream repair and maintenance services (RMS) largely overlooked. This paper examines whether lower‐emission service provision can become a self‐financing differentiation strategy for capital‐constrained, small‐ and medium‐sized service firms. We develop a price‐competition model where firms choose between traditional and cleaner service offerings, and customers exhibit heterogeneous emission sensitivity. From this framework, we derive a self‐financing condition that links emission‐sensitive demand, market size, operating‐cost variations, and upfront abatement investments. To ground the model empirically, we collect detailed operational data from 13 German and 6 Australian RMS shops, combining these inputs with life cycle assessment (LCA) estimates to map Scope 1–3 emission channels and characterize abatement pathways. The results show that energy‐related measures in heating and electricity provide low‐risk entry points that reduce or stabilize operating costs. Conversely, spare parts and material strategies dominate total lifecycle emissions; while they offer higher absolute abatement potential, they demand greater capital investment and value‐chain coordination. This study contributes to the business case for sustainability literature by demonstrating that environmental differentiation operates not only as a demand‐side premium driver but also as an operating‐cost and investment‐feasibility mechanism. Finally, we offer actionable guidance for RMS managers, insurers, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), and policymakers on sequencing decarbonization pathways within service industries dominated by small‐ and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs).

title: Post-irradiation effects of low-fluence heavy-ion irradiation on AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs)
summary: Abstract We investigated the effects of Ar and Kr heavy-ion irradiation at 1.0 × 10 7 ions/cm 2 on unbiased AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility-transistors. After irradiation, the drain current and transconductance degraded by less than 10 %,
content: Abstract We investigated the effects of Ar and Kr heavy-ion irradiation at 1.0 × 10 7 ions/cm 2 on unbiased AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility-transistors. After irradiation, the drain current and transconductance degraded by less than 10 %, and the threshold voltage shifted slightly for both ions. In contrast, Kr-irradiated HEMTs exhibited much degradation in gate leakage current and off-state breakdown voltage than Ar-irradiated devices, which is attributed to Schottky contact deterioration and defect generation in the AlGaN barrier. SRIM simulations revealed that Kr ions generate more vacancies throughout the HEMT layer than Ar ions owing to larger nuclear energy loss, consistent with these results.

title: Predicting Fashion Sustainability Rate Using Hybrid Models and Sensitivity Analysis for Enhanced Accuracy and Feature Optimization
summary: Fashion sustainability promotes eco-friendly materials, waste reduction, fair labor, and low emissions. This study predicts sustainability rates using Machine Learning (ML) models and sensitivity analysis for improvement. Techniques, includ
content: Fashion sustainability promotes eco-friendly materials, waste reduction, fair labor, and low emissions. This study predicts sustainability rates using Machine Learning (ML) models and sensitivity analysis for improvement. Techniques, including the Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) and Logistic Regression Classification (LRC), benefit from advanced optimization methods like the Tunicate Swarm Optimization Algorithm (TSOA) and the Improved Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (IAOA), which enhance accuracy and reliability. The goal is to identify the optimal model and key features. Sensitivity analysis is conducted on two models to identify the features that most influence performance. This allows for more informed decisions regarding feature selection and optimization. Through analysis, the SGIA model, achieving an accuracy score of 0.987 on the test phase and 0.983 overall, proves to be the most effective for predicting the fashion sustainability rate. Additionally, it appears that brand name and eco-friendly manufacturing practices are the most influential features in predicting sustainability.

title: Preclinical safety evaluation of Vernolac, a commercially available polyherbal nutraceutical comprising Vernonia zeylanica, Nigella sativa, Hemidesmus indicus, Smilax glabra, and Leucas zeylanica, in Wistar rats
summary: Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro stu
content: Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro studies have demonstrated the anticancer potential of Vernolac and its active ingredients, safety data are available only for some of the plant ingredients of Vernolac. In the present study, acute and 28-day repeat-dose toxicity of Vernolac were evaluated in Wistar rats in accordance with OECD guidelines 420 and 407, respectively. Acute toxicity was investigated for 14 days after administering a single oral dose of 2000 mg/kg to 10 animals (5 males, 5 females). A repeat-dose toxicity study was conducted, in which the human equivalent therapeutic dose in rats (HED; 165 mg/kg/day), a mid-dose (2 × HED; 330 mg/kg/day), and a high dose (4 × HED; 660 mg/kg/day) were administered to three separate groups, each comprising 10 naive animals (5 males and 5 females), for a period of 28 days. In both acute and repeat-dose studies, no morbidity, mortality, changes in food and water intake, relative organ weights, microscopic changes in organs, hematological changes, or clinical signs of toxicity were observed. In the acute study, a significant increase in AST and ALT levels was observed in males. In the 28-day repeated dose study, a significant reduction in ALT was observed only in females receiving 4x HED. In summary, the LD 50 of Vernolac is above 2000 mg/kg, and a dose up to two times the therapeutic daily dose is non-toxic in Wistar rats over 28 days. The liver may be a target organ of toxicity when overdosed.

title: Carbon footprint calculation in the framework of the EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542: Implications and challenges
summary: As of 17 August 2023, the European Parliament published the new Battery Regulation, which requires mandatory declarations of the carbon footprint for electric vehicle batteries to be introduced on the EU market. The European Union is curren
content: As of 17 August 2023, the European Parliament published the new Battery Regulation, which requires mandatory declarations of the carbon footprint for electric vehicle batteries to be introduced on the EU market. The European Union is currently drafting a delegated act to complete the new Regulation. This secondary legislation will establish the methodology for calculating the carbon footprint of EV batteries, based on the latest advances in life cycle assessment. This legislation is expected to come into effect within the next few years. The present study examines the proposed draft calculation methodology and applies it to a case study battery pack. The study also examines the impacts of the EU Battery Regulation’s recycled-content mandates and the revised CFF. Because the choice of the functional unit is critical, an additional comparison of different commonly used and proposed functional units is included. Lastly, the main methodological gaps and implementation challenges are identified. Depending on the normalization basis, the calculated carbon footprint under Approach C was approximately 6.24 kgCO2eq/kgpack on a mass basis, 39.15 kgCO2eq/kWh on a nominal-capacity basis, and 0.108 and 0.0815 kgCO2eq/kWh under the two service-based definitions. Moreover, applying the recycled-content targets for 2031 and 2036 shifted the CFF material-input contribution from 0.162 kgCO2eq/kWh to net allocation credits of −0.251 and −0.445 kgCO2eq/kWh, respectively. The results underscore the importance of stakeholder cooperation and alignment across regulatory frameworks to harmonize the calculation and ensure the reliability of the results.

title: The Size Composition of tradable Industries and Local Multipliers: Evidence from Italy
summary: Abstract Do local employment responses depend on how changes in tradable industries are distributed across establishment-size classes? This paper studies whether local employment responses vary with the establishment-size composition of cha
content: Abstract Do local employment responses depend on how changes in tradable industries are distributed across establishment-size classes? This paper studies whether local employment responses vary with the establishment-size composition of changes in tradable industries. Using establishment and personnel data for Italian local labor market areas over 2012-2020, we estimate local employment responses associated with changes recorded in four contemporaneous establishment-size cells. In a homogeneous specification, one additional tradable job generates 1.26 jobs in non-tradable industries. Allowing multipliers to vary by establishment size reveals substantial heterogeneity: employment increases recorded in medium-size cells are associated with the largest non-tradable industries response, followed by small-size cell, while the effect is smaller for large-size cell and statistically indistinguishable from zero for the micro-size cell. We interpret this pattern through two channels: larger establishments strengthen local demand through higher wages, whereas small and medium establishments generate stronger local cost-linkages through denser production networks.

title: Taxonomic and functional reorganization of terrestrial mammal communities under anthropogenic influence in a tropical forest
source: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
summary: Protected areas and national legislation are important tools for conserving biodiversity and maintaining ecosystem services. In Brazil, the 2012 Native Vegetation Protection Law no. 12.651, of 25 May 2012 requires rural landowners in the Am
content: Protected areas and national legislation are important tools for conserving biodiversity and maintaining ecosystem services. In Brazil, the 2012 Native Vegetation Protection Law no. 12.651, of 25 May 2012 requires rural landowners in the Amazon to maintain at least 80% of each property under native vegetation as legal reserves (LRs), including within settlement projects. We compared mammal community structure and trait-based responses between human-occupied LRs and a continuous protected forest (CPF) in the central Amazon. Using camera-traps, we assessed species richness, relative abundance, taxonomic composition, functional traits and ecological attributes in relation to anthropogenic variables. RLQ and fourth-corner analyses revealed similar species richness, but different taxonomic composition and relative abundance patterns between protection types. Herbivores and subsistence-hunted species were associated with the CPF, whereas carnivores, retaliation-hunted species and mammals with large home ranges were linked to LRs. Within LRs, relative abundance increased with forest cover and distance to water but declined farther from roads; in the CPF, species richness increased with distance to roads, while LR mammal communities exhibited compositional reorganization under multiple anthropogenic pressures. These findings indicate that LRs, despite being embedded in human-altered landscapes, can support diverse mammal assemblages and play a complementary role in biodiversity conservation.

title: TRIANGULATE: Trust-minimized MRV for AI normative audits — multimodal triangulation so the answer does not depend on trusting any single measurer
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Measurement–reporting–verification (MRV) is load-bearing wherever claimed contribution must be checked against real contribution — in carbon markets, in the verified-contribution accounting proposed for life-capacity economies, and in audit
content: Measurement–reporting–verification (MRV) is load-bearing wherever claimed contribution must be checked against real contribution — in carbon markets, in the verified-contribution accounting proposed for life-capacity economies, and in audits that classify what objective an AI system appears to pursue. Yet every MRV pipeline rests on a measurer, and a measurer is a trust dependency. The physical world solved a structurally identical problem decades ago: no single satellite, sensor tower, or field plot is trusted to estimate carbon stock; heterogeneous modalities with different bias profiles are triangulated, and disagreement between them is information, not noise. We instantiate the same pattern for AI normative audits. Our pipeline combines three measurement modalities — LLM judge families (remote, scalable, biased), a human gold set (local, expensive, ground-truth), and revealed-preference behavioral tasks — behind preregistered gates that can fail and be reported, a scorer-of-record selected by coded-seed agreement, and a published rejected-instrument exhibit. Applied to a 4,164-record audit of open-weight model objectives, the system localizes exactly which judgment is contested: judge–human agreement is Cohen's κ=0.22 overall, but failure concentrates on the boundary question ("does this text presume an objective at all," κ≈0.19) while direction survives (φ-share 29.8% human vs 25.5% judge on the jointly objective-bearing subset). We therefore report magnitudes as judge-family quantities and direction as a cross-modal finding — decomposition reporting that binds each claim to the level its weakest instrument supports. Part of the LESS–IS–MORE program.

title: The green steel dilemma: capital allocation and decarbonization at Tata Steel
summary: Learning outcomes After completing this case discussion, students should be able to: Case overview/synopsis This teaching case examines the board-level dilemma faced by Tata Steel in 2026 as the company evaluated whether to accelerate inves
content: Learning outcomes After completing this case discussion, students should be able to: Case overview/synopsis This teaching case examines the board-level dilemma faced by Tata Steel in 2026 as the company evaluated whether to accelerate investments in green steel technologies amid intensifying global climate pressures, evolving Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) expectations, rising carbon-related trade regulations and rapidly growing steel demand in India. The protagonist, T. V. Narendran, confronted a complex strategic decision involving competing priorities such as growth versus sustainability, profitability versus long-term competitiveness, Indian versus European capital allocation and technological experimentation versus financial discipline. The case highlights the challenges of decarbonizing a hard-to-abate industry within an emerging-market environment characterized by coal dependence, infrastructure gaps, electricity cost volatility, constrained scrap availability and uncertain customer willingness to pay green steel premiums. Students are required to evaluate alternative strategic pathways available to Tata Steel, including aggressive green acceleration, phased transition, selective decarbonization and conventional growth-oriented expansion. Designed for courses in Strategic Management, Sustainability and ESG, Corporate Governance, International Business, Energy Transition and Emerging Market Strategy, the case encourages executive-level analysis of sustainability transitions, capital allocation tradeoffs and industrial decarbonization within emerging economies. Complexity academic level This case is suitable for master of business administration (MBA) students, Executive MBA participants, Post Graduate Diploma in Management students, executive education programs and corporate sustainability leadership workshops. The case is particularly appropriate for courses in Strategic Management, ESG and Sustainability Strategy, Climate Risk and Governance, International Business, Operations and Technology Strategy and Corporate Governance. Given its emphasis on executive-level decision-making, capital allocation, emerging-market sustainability challenges and long-term competitive positioning, the case is especially relevant for advanced management and leadership-oriented discussions. The case is positioned for postgraduate and executive audiences only, given the depth of financial reasoning, scenario analysis and governance judgment required. Subject code CSS 11: Strategy.

title: Revealed Comparative Advantage and Export Competitiveness of Indian Steel Products in Global Markets
summary: Steel industry has grown its plants in India due to infrastructure demand, investments and industrial policy. However, a higher volume does not necessarily improve export competitiveness. The export performance also depends on product mix,
content: Steel industry has grown its plants in India due to infrastructure demand, investments and industrial policy. However, a higher volume does not necessarily improve export competitiveness. The export performance also depends on product mix, international prices, input costs, logistics, exchange rates, trade measures and the ability to meet the requirements for low carbon. In this paper, an industry specific framework for evaluating India's competitiveness in steel exports based on Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA) beyond a single RCA measure is developed. It involves long-run specialisation in trade, export performance changes, upgrading of products and capabilities of firms. In the new design, the time horizon is extended to the longest time series that are available from official sources, some measures are proposed that are dynamic versions of RCA, some are proposed that are symmetric versions of RCA, and some are proposed that incorporate Constant Market Share (CMS) decomposition to separate market-demand effects from competitiveness effects. The firm level component is based on survey data from 80 steel manufacturing companies in Tamil Nadu. The descriptive statistics provided here indicate a mean production of 309.45 MT, a USD 69.87 million mean export value, a mean capacity utilisation (CU) of 82.31% and a reported mean RCA of 1.52. The numbers do not necessarily represent causal impacts or RCA at the national product level. There is also a recent dramatic shift in India's trade position, as per official industry data, India exported 7.487 million tonnes of finished steel in 2023-24 and imported 8.320 million tonnes, whereas during 2024-25, exports decreased to 4.858 million tonnes and imports increased to 9.551 million tonnes (Annual Report of Ministry of Steel 2025-26). This divergence is a reminder of the importance of considering scale of production and competitiveness of exports separately. The paper's contribution is an integrated, testable framework which connects the concepts of trade specialization with industrial capability and market conditions. To draw inferences, firm-level regression estimates and product-level dynamic indices need to be computed from the underlying datasets.

title: Tích hợp giao thông công cộng thông minh trong phát triển du lịch bền vững tại Hà Nội
summary: Trong bối cảnh đô thị hóa diễn ra nhanh chóng và xu hướng phát triển đô thị thông minh ngày càng được chú trọng, giao thông công cộng thông minh được xem là một trong những yếu tố quan trọng góp phần nâng cao tính bền vững của du lịch đô th
content: Trong bối cảnh đô thị hóa diễn ra nhanh chóng và xu hướng phát triển đô thị thông minh ngày càng được chú trọng, giao thông công cộng thông minh được xem là một trong những yếu tố quan trọng góp phần nâng cao tính bền vững của du lịch đô thị. Nghiên cứu này nhằm phân tích vai trò của giao thông công cộng thông minh đối với phát triển du lịch đô thị bền vững tại Hà Nội thông qua việc đánh giá mối quan hệ giữa giao thông công cộng thông minh, khả năng tiếp cận điểm đến, trải nghiệm di chuyển của du khách và phát triển du lịch đô thị bền vững. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp định lượng với 342 bảng hỏi hợp lệ thu thập từ khách du lịch nội địa và quốc tế đã sử dụng các phương tiện giao thông công cộng tại Hà Nội. Dữ liệu được xử lý bằng các kỹ thuật phân tích độ tin cậy thang đo, phân tích nhân tố và mô hình cấu trúc tuyến tính. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy, giao thông công cộng thông minh có tác động tích cực đến khả năng tiếp cận điểm đến và trải nghiệm di chuyển của du khách, đồng thời góp phần thúc đẩy phát triển du lịch đô thị bền vững. Các giải pháp giao thông xanh kết hợp với công nghệ số không chỉ nâng cao chất lượng trải nghiệm của du khách mà còn góp phần giảm ùn tắc giao thông, hạn chế phát thải và phân bổ dòng khách hợp lý trong không gian đô thị. Nghiên cứu bổ sung bằng chứng thực nghiệm về mối quan hệ giữa di chuyển thông minh (Smart Mobility) và du lịch thông minh (Smart Tourism) trong bối cảnh một đô thị đang phát triển, đồng thời cung cấp cơ sở khoa học cho việc tích hợp giao thông công cộng thông minh vào chiến lược phát triển du lịch đô thị bền vững tại Hà Nội.

title: Nanomaterial-based glucose sensors: detection platforms and highlight applications
summary: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved in
content: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved into a severe global public health crisis. Precise, rapid, and stable glucose monitoring is therefore indispensable for the early diagnosis, clinical intervention, and long-term management of diabetes. Conventional enzyme-dependent glucose sensors suffer from inherent limitations, including high manufacturing costs, inferior environmental stability, short service lifespan, and susceptibility to fluctuations in pH and temperature, which substantially constrain their practical clinical and industrial applications. Benefiting from their unique structural tunability and superior physicochemical properties, nanomaterial-based glucose sensing platforms have emerged as high-performance alternatives to traditional enzymatic sensors, achieving remarkable advancements in detection sensitivity, selectivity, and operational stability, while enabling continuous and non-invasive glucose monitoring. This comprehensive review systematically elaborates the state-of-the-art progress of nanomaterial-enabled glucose sensing technologies, focusing on two dominant detection modalities: electrochemical and optical sensing strategies. We emphatically discuss the rational design of functional nanomaterials, innovative construction of multicomponent nanocomposites, development of flexible wearable sensing systems, and emerging signal transduction mechanisms. Meanwhile, this review comprehensively categorizes and evaluates the performance characteristics and application progress of diverse nanomaterial-based glucose sensors, covering precious/non-precious metal nanomaterials, metal–organic frameworks, carbon-based materials, multifunctional nanocomposites, and molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)-integrated sensing platforms. Furthermore, we thoroughly analyze the current commercialization landscape of continuous and non-invasive glucose monitoring devices. Finally, the core challenges hindering the clinical translation and large-scale commercialization of high-performance glucose sensors are highlighted, and targeted future research directions and development prospects are prospected, aiming to provide insightful theoretical guidance and technical references for the design and optimization of next-generation clinical glucose sensing technologies.

title: Monitoring, Reporting and Verification procedures for soil health: Current landscape, stakeholder dynamics and future pathways
summary: Abstract. To counteract green washing, the effects of the activities that lead to an intended outcome should be quantified and monitored in a scientifically robust way and results should be transparently reported and verified. With this obj
content: Abstract. To counteract green washing, the effects of the activities that lead to an intended outcome should be quantified and monitored in a scientifically robust way and results should be transparently reported and verified. With this objective, Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) procedures were developed and studied in the context of soil carbon credits. However, no broader overview, including other aspects of soils, exists to date. The objective of this study was to fill this gap of knowledge by gathering, describing and classifying the MRV procedures including soil parameters, across the world. As the term MRV seems to be sparsely used by scientists, we combined three methodologies to collect information about MRV procedures: the classical use of scientific article database, web scraping and Artificial Intelligence browsers. We found 96 MRV procedures and partial information was available. Most of the available MRV procedures were applied on a local scale, in agricultural areas, responding to the methodological requirements of voluntary carbon markets standards, which illustrates the hegemony of carbon markets in the soil MRV context. Results were mainly gathered in a classical report and result-based verified. We classified the MRV procedures into six groups. Group 1 was only characterized by the lack of information and thus reflected the main limitation of our study. The five other groups addressed different stakeholders. Four of them targeted stakeholders of the agricultural sector and the last one project developers for peatlands and wetland restoration. The two largest groups demonstrated different strategies: more accurate monitoring and verification methodologies or cheaper ones. We also highlighted the lack of transparency from companies offering MRV procedures. In complement, we developed a decision tool to help future users of MRV procedures to navigate our dataset and select the most adequate MRV procedure, adapted to their context. The next steps are 1) to strengthen the collaboration between scientists and MRV providers and to 2) understand how to transition from carbon-focused MRV procedures to more holistic, soil health-focused MRV procedures.

title: Giải pháp nâng cao hiệu quả xuất khẩu gạo trong bối cảnh thực thi FTA: trường hợp công ty VinaRice
summary: Nghiên cứu được thực hiện nhằm đề xuất các giải pháp nâng cao hiệu quả xuất khẩu gạo của Công ty trách nhiệm hữu hạn Lúa gạo Việt Nam (VinaRice) trong bối cảnh Việt Nam thực thi các hiệp định thương mại tự do. Trên cơ sở Quan điểm dựa trên
content: Nghiên cứu được thực hiện nhằm đề xuất các giải pháp nâng cao hiệu quả xuất khẩu gạo của Công ty trách nhiệm hữu hạn Lúa gạo Việt Nam (VinaRice) trong bối cảnh Việt Nam thực thi các hiệp định thương mại tự do. Trên cơ sở Quan điểm dựa trên nguồn lực, Lý thuyết năng lực động và Lý thuyết thể chế, nghiên cứu xây dựng mô hình đánh giá tác động của công nghệ sản xuất tiên tiến, năng lực marketing điện tử và sự hỗ trợ của chính phủ đến năng lực đổi mới sáng tạo và hiệu quả xuất khẩu. Nghiên cứu sử dụng phương pháp hỗn hợp kết hợp nghiên cứu định tính và định lượng. Dữ liệu được thu thập từ 125 nhà quản lý và nhân sự trực tiếp tham gia hoạt động xuất khẩu tại VinaRice, sau đó được phân tích bằng phương pháp PLS-SEM. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy công nghệ sản xuất tiên tiến, năng lực marketing và sự hỗ trợ của chính phủ đều góp phần nâng cao năng lực đổi mới sáng tạo và hiệu quả xuất khẩu của doanh nghiệp. Đồng thời, năng lực đổi mới sáng tạo giữ vai trò cầu nối trong việc chuyển hóa các nguồn lực và sự hỗ trợ từ môi trường bên ngoài thành kết quả xuất khẩu. Nghiên cứu đề xuất các giải pháp nhằm nâng cao năng lực marketing điện tử, thúc đẩy đổi mới sáng tạo, tăng cường khai thác các chính sách hỗ trợ từ chính phủ và đầu tư công nghệ sản xuất hiện đại để nâng cao năng lực cạnh tranh và hiệu quả xuất khẩu của VinaRice trong bối cảnh hội nhập quốc tế.

title: Mô hình quản trị điểm đến phát huy giá trị văn hóa, lịch sử và tài nguyên tự nhiên tại Trà Vinh (cũ) và bài học kinh nghiệm cho Việt Nam
summary: Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc định hình chiến lược phát triển du lịch xanh và bền vững tại tỉnh Trà Vinh (cũ), nay là Vĩnh Long, một điểm đến đang nổi lên với những giá trị đặc thù tại Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long. Mục tiêu chính của đề tài
content: Nghiên cứu này tập trung vào việc định hình chiến lược phát triển du lịch xanh và bền vững tại tỉnh Trà Vinh (cũ), nay là Vĩnh Long, một điểm đến đang nổi lên với những giá trị đặc thù tại Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long. Mục tiêu chính của đề tài là đánh giá thực trạng khai thác các giá trị di sản văn hóa – tâm linh và mô hình du lịch cộng đồng thuận thiên, từ đó đề xuất lộ trình chuyển dịch từ khai thác tài nguyên thuần túy sang kỷ nguyên du lịch tái tạo. Điểm mới của nghiên cứu nằm ở cách tiếp cận liên ngành, tích hợp đột phá giữa khung phân tích DART (Đồng tạo lập giá trị) và bộ chỉ số ESG để giải quyết các điểm nghẽn trong quản trị du lịch hiện đại. Kết quả cho thấy, thành tố Quản trị (G) đóng vai trò cốt lõi, giúp chuyển hóa vốn văn hóa bản địa và tài nguyên bản địa thành lợi ích kinh tế – xã hội cụ thể mà vẫn đảm bảo sức chống chịu của hệ sinh thái. Đề tài cũng nhấn mạnh việc chuẩn hóa sản phẩm qua OCOP và số hóa di sản là lộ trình tất yếu để xây dựng thương hiệu điểm đến phát thải thấp, định vị Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long trở thành hình mẫu về kinh tế xanh và nhân văn trong kỷ nguyên Net Zero toàn cầu. Về hàm ý quản trị, bài viết đề xuất Việt Nam cần sớm thực thi mô hình DMO thông minh, lồng ghép chính sách tín dụng xanh và cơ chế "đồng quản lý" để trao quyền thực chất cho cộng đồng.

title: Greenwashing skepticism as a selective moderator: how digital environmental content exposure shapes green e-commerce intentions among Saudi university students
summary: Introduction As Generation Z consumers increasingly engage with digital platforms in response to environmental considerations, understanding how online sustainability messaging shapes green e-commerce behavior becomes more pressing. Digital
content: Introduction As Generation Z consumers increasingly engage with digital platforms in response to environmental considerations, understanding how online sustainability messaging shapes green e-commerce behavior becomes more pressing. Digitalization is often assumed to equalize access to sustainability information, yet digital divide research shows that inequalities persist in how online content is converted into outcomes. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), this study examines how exposure to digital environmental content (DECE) shapes green e-consumption intention (GECI) among digitally literate Saudi university students. Methods Environmental awareness and personal responsibility (EAR) and message credibility (MC) were modeled as two parallel mediators linking DECE to GECI, with no hypothesized path between them. Greenwashing perception (GP) was expected to moderate specifically the effect of MC on GECI, and perceived barriers (PB) were examined as an independent predictor of GECI. Data from 305 respondents were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results The model explained substantial variance in GECI ( R ² = 0.603; Q ² = 0.577). DECE had a significant direct effect on GECI ( β = 0.190, p = 0.001). The EAR-mediated pathway was dominant ( β = 0.311, f ² = 0.333), whereas the MC-mediated pathway was non-significant ( β = 0.006, p = 0.823). GP moderated the credibility–intention link (MC → GECI; β = −0.114, p = 0.005) but not the exposure–intention link (DECE → GECI; β = 0.070, p = 0.095), suggesting that greenwashing skepticism acts as a credibility-related barrier. PB was positively associated with GECI ( β = 0.138, p = 0.023), a counter-intuitive association interpreted tentatively. Discriminant validity concerns for two construct pairs are reported transparently. Discussion Exposure-based sustainability communication appears to retain motivational effectiveness even under widespread greenwashing skepticism. Credibility-centred campaigns may require third-party verification (e.g., ISO 14024 Type I eco-labels) to overcome skepticism-driven suppression of the persuasion pathway. Environmental awareness and responsibility appears to be the primary lever for promoting responsible green e-consumption, with direct relevance to SDG 12 (Target 12.8).

title: Carbon-Market Policy Signals, Transition-Risk Perceptions, and Household Portfolio Reallocation in China: A Randomized Experiment
summary: Carbon-market policies can alter the expected costs and financial risks faced by carbon-intensive firms, but less is known about how households translate information about tighter carbon constraints into portfolio decisions. This study exam
content: Carbon-market policies can alter the expected costs and financial risks faced by carbon-intensive firms, but less is known about how households translate information about tighter carbon constraints into portfolio decisions. This study examined whether a standardized carbon-allowance tightening signal changed perceived transition risk and experimentally elicited portfolio allocation among household investors in China. A total of 800 adults were individually randomized to neutral carbon-market information or an allowance-tightening information condition. Participants completed a 100-unit portfolio allocation before treatment, immediately afterward, and 7 days later. The primary outcome was the immediate allocation to global carbon-intensive multinational equity. Relative to neutral information, the tightening signal increased perceived transition risk by 0.79 points (95% CI, 0.70–0.87; p < 0.001) and reduced adjusted T1 carbon-intensive equity allocation by 3.27 percentage points (95% CI, −3.45 to −3.09; p < 0.001). In a participant fixed-effects model, the treatment-by-T2 estimate was −1.22 percentage points (95% CI, −1.48 to −0.96; p < 0.001). The sequential indirect effect through policy-stringency and policy-credibility beliefs and transition-risk perception was not statistically supported (−0.001 percentage points; bootstrap 95% CI, −0.006 to 0.003). Portfolio choices were elicited in a hypothetical 100-unit allocation task rather than observed investment transactions.

title: D-allulose applications in the food industry: sensory evaluation, food safety, and global regulatory approval status
summary: Abstract The global population faces metabolic health complications, a major contributor to which is the consumption of high-calorie foods, particularly those containing high levels of added sugars. The demand for low-calorie sugar substitu
content: Abstract The global population faces metabolic health complications, a major contributor to which is the consumption of high-calorie foods, particularly those containing high levels of added sugars. The demand for low-calorie sugar substitutes has accelerated the use of D-allulose in food products. D-Allulose has been used in various food products, such as cookies, burger buns, muffins, chocolate, starch gels, pectin gels, and yogurt. Foods containing D-allulose often exhibit acceptable or even improved sensory characteristics, including greater freshness and softness, when the replacement level is optimized. Additionally, D-allulose enhances browning in food products owing to its Maillard reaction properties. Moreover, D-allulose effectively reduces the hardening of starch gels during refrigeration. D-Allulose is also relatively stable during storage at lower to moderate temperatures (4–25 °C); however, prolonged exposure to higher temperatures (≥ 40 °C) can cause thermal degradation and the accumulation of degradation products, including 5-hydroxymethylfurfural, vinyl formate, and methyl pyruvate. Animal studies showed no adverse effects in acute, subchronic, reproductive, and developmental toxicity tests at the doses tested. In humans, single doses up to 0.4 g/kg body weight and daily intakes up to 0.9 g/kg body weight were well tolerated. Based on safety assessments, the USA, Korea, China, Australia, and New Zealand have permitted its use in foods, and it is sold in Japan; however, the European Food Safety Authority could not establish its safety in 2025 because of missing data. Current evidence supports D-allulose as a suitable low-calorie alternative to sucrose. However, further studies are needed on matrix-dependent sensory effects, the safety of heat-induced degradation products, long-term human intake, and the gut microbiota.

title: Agromorphological diversity and promising accessions of common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) in the northeastern Peruvian Andes
summary: Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) harbors valuable agromorphological diversity in the northeastern Peruvian Andes; however, local germplasm remains insufficiently characterized despite the risk of genetic erosion. This study characterize
content: Common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) harbors valuable agromorphological diversity in the northeastern Peruvian Andes; however, local germplasm remains insufficiently characterized despite the risk of genetic erosion. This study characterized 80 common bean accessions using 17 quantitative and 14 qualitative descriptors and preliminarily identified promising materials for breeding. The accessions were evaluated under an augmented block design, required because of limited seed availability. Qualitative diversity was assessed in the 78 non-check accessions using Nei’s diversity index (He) and the Shannon–Weaver index (H′), whereas quantitative traits were analyzed using mixed models to obtain BLUEs and broad-sense heritability (H 2 ). Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to identify the main sources of quantitative variation, cluster analysis to define phenotypic groups, and multiple factor analysis (MFA) to integrate morphology, phenology, and yield in the identification of promising accessions. Substantial qualitative diversity was observed, with He ranging from 0.12 to 0.83 and H′ reaching 1.99 for lighter seed coat color. The greatest quantitative variation was observed for number of pods per plant, yield per plant, number of floral racemes per plant, and stem diameter. H 2 ranged from 0.00 to 1.00, with high estimates for D50F and NSP (1.00), NPP (0.98), SW (0.97), and YP (0.96). The PCA identified three phenotypically differentiated clusters, whereas the MFA revealed complementary relationships among morphology, phenology, and yield. Four accessions (UNTRM-335-1019, UNTRM-335-1077, UNTRM-335-1058, and UNTRM-335-1016) met the selection criteria by combining yield higher than the best check with favorable seed weight and harvest index values. These accessions should be regarded as preliminary candidates requiring validation through replicated multi-environment trials. The results provide baseline information for the conservation and use of local common bean germplasm in regional breeding programs.

title: Production-source disclosures, higher-order creative attributions, and audience reception of two-dimensional animation: evidence from a randomized source-disclosure experiment
summary: Introduction Attribution theory explains how audiences use observable information to infer otherwise unobservable agents and processes behind creative work. This study applied this perspective to examine how production-source disclosures in
content: Introduction Attribution theory explains how audiences use observable information to infer otherwise unobservable agents and processes behind creative work. This study applied this perspective to examine how production-source disclosures influence source-role perceptions, higher-order creative attributions, and audience reception of two-dimensional animation. Methods In a randomized experiment, 626 adults were assigned to one of four production-source disclosure conditions—undisclosed, human-made, human–AI collaborative, or AI-led—while viewing the same three animation clips, all of which were actually produced through human–AI collaboration. We examined between-condition differences in source-role perceptions, higher-order creative attributions, and audience-reception outcomes, as well as concurrent associations between higher-order creative attributions and audience reception. Results The disclosures clearly differentiated participants’ perceptions of AI and human involvement. Perceived creative effort was statistically significant before correction but did not meet the α = 0.05 criterion after Holm adjustment ( p = 0.0502); the only corrected contrast indicated lower perceived creative effort in the human–AI collaborative condition than in the human-made condition. No statistically reliable omnibus between-condition differences emerged for perceived authorship, perceived emotional authenticity, artistic evaluation, situational immersion, or viewing and recommendation intention. Higher-order creative attributions were positively associated with all three audience-reception indicators in concurrent analyses, although the strong correlation between perceived emotional authenticity and situational immersion warrants caution about measurement overlap. Discussion The findings indicate that the diagnosticity of a production-source cue depends on the judgment target: the disclosures clearly reorganized perceived production roles but did not yield statistically reliable corresponding differences across most higher-order creative attributions or reception outcomes. The attribution–reception relations represent concurrent covariation rather than causal mediation. Because the three clips were presented in a fixed order, material and order effects cannot be separated, and the equivalence analyses did not establish negligible between-condition differences.

title: PERENCANAAN SUMBER DAYA MANUSIA BERKELANJUTAN: TINJAUAN SISTEMATIS LITERATUR TENTANG DAYA SAING TENAGA KERJA
summary: Indonesia telah mengintegrasikan agenda Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) ke dalam Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Nasional (RPJMN), namun tantangan ketenagakerjaan seperti tingginya pengangguran pemuda dan dominasi sektor informal t
content: Indonesia telah mengintegrasikan agenda Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) ke dalam Rencana Pembangunan Jangka Menengah Nasional (RPJMN), namun tantangan ketenagakerjaan seperti tingginya pengangguran pemuda dan dominasi sektor informal tetap signifikan. Fragmentasi literatur mendorong penelitian ini melakukan Systematic Literature Review (SLR) untuk memetakan dan menyintesis hubungan antara perencanaan SDM berbasis SDGs, keterampilan berkelanjutan, dan pencapaian target ketenagakerjaan SDGs. Penelitian ini menjawab empat pertanyaan penelitian: (1) Bagaimana perencanaan SDM berbasis SDGs memengaruhi pengembangan keterampilan berkelanjutan? (2) Bagaimana pencapaian target SDGs ketenagakerjaan berkontribusi pada keterampilan berkelanjutan? (3) Bagaimana pencapaian target SDGs ketenagakerjaan berkontribusi pada penurunan kemiskinan? (4) Apakah keterampilan berkelanjutan memediasi hubungan antara pencapaian target ketenagakerjaan dan perencanaan SDM berbasis SDGs? Mengikuti protokol PRISMA 2020, penelitian ini mengkaji 35 artikel dan laporan institusional terpilih dari Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, dan MDPI periode 2020–2025. Pendekatan vote counting dan sintesis tematik diterapkan untuk menganalisis pola di seluruh studi. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa perencanaan SDM berbasis SDGs khususnya melalui Sustainable HRM dan Green HRM berpengaruh positif signifikan terhadap kinerja, produktivitas, kesadaran keberlanjutan, dan daya saing tenaga kerja (didukung >80% studi yang dikaji). Keterampilan berkelanjutan berfungsi sebagai mediator parsial antara perencanaan SDM dan pencapaian target ketenagakerjaan.

title: From Industrial Void to Urban Continuity: Regenerating the Bragadiru Industrial Ensemble
summary: The Bragadiru Brewery ensemble represents one of the most significant historical industrial sites of Bucharest, located at a sensitive point in the relationship between memory, urban transformation and regeneration potential.This article ex
content: The Bragadiru Brewery ensemble represents one of the most significant historical industrial sites of Bucharest, located at a sensitive point in the relationship between memory, urban transformation and regeneration potential.This article examines the site not only as an architectural object, but as an urban territory marked by historical accumulations and discontinuities generated by political transformations and large-scale interventions during the late socialist period.The theoretical framework integrates Hannah Arendt's conception of public space as the place of appearance, the ideas of Jane Jacobs and Jan Gehl regarding the human scale, social dynamics and urban vitality, as well as Charles Montgomery's reflections on the relationship between the built environment and wellbeing.The Heideggerian perspective on dwelling allows the industrial heritage to be interpreted as an existential support for collective memory.The analysis traces the historical evolution of the Bragadiru Brewery ensemble, emphasising how the demolitions of the 1980s, which eliminated approximately 5.9-7 square kilometres of urban fabric and resulted in the displacement of around 40,000 inhabitants (Tănase, 2019), profoundly reconfigured its territorial context.The site became isolated and detached from the urban network, losing its natural connections with the city centre.At present, the ensemble is examined as a potential node within a north south green urban direction, capable of connecting the city's major parks into a continuous urban infrastructure that combines vegetation, pedestrian routes and public spaces.Within this framework, the site can become an interface between the centre of the capital and the southern districts, contributing to the rebalancing of the urban structure.The article argues that the regeneration of the ensemble can function both as a local intervention and as a city scale intervention, transforming a fragmented territory into a coherent sequence of the city.can become metabolic catalysts for low-carbon, culturally meaningful urban futures.

title: Tracing Oil Money in the Academy
summary: In public debates, historians often supply historical context or analogies relating past and pre sent.I'll even do so in this essay.But historians should also historicize the debate itself by showing that change over time matters to our eth
content: In public debates, historians often supply historical context or analogies relating past and pre sent.I'll even do so in this essay.But historians should also historicize the debate itself by showing that change over time matters to our ethical calculus.Things were dif fer ent before, what was right then isn't now and vice versa, and things will be dif fer ent again someday.We should even historicize the ethics of oil money in the acad emy.Universities' oil ties weren't innocent in the past, but they were more defensible than in the pre sent.True, many well-meaning academics argue that only by working with oil companies today can universities assist a future green transition.So, let's debate that question, armed with an understanding of how oil money passes through universities, with what results, for whose benefit. 1 Admittedly, my argument that oil ties were once defensible is self-serving: My career owes much to oil.Yours too, prob ably!To illustrate, let's review the institutions I've been associated with, starting with Cornell's Science and Technology Studies (STS) department.Franklin Long, that department's "chief architect," was on Exxon's board of directors from 1969 to 1980. 2 Long was also an influential adviser to the Aspen Institute when that organization was run, and funded, by current and former oil executives.3 While I was at Cornell, the STS department was housed in Rockefeller Hall.One of my PhD advisers, Ron Kline, was Bovay Professor in History and Ethics of Engineering; Harry Bovay was a petrochemical plant designer with Humble Oil and Bovay Engineers.4 After my PhD, I became the Gordon Cain Fellow at the Chemical Heritage Foundation (CHF); Cain was a Conoco vice president and founder of Petro-Tex Chemical Corporation.5 More generally, CHF-its museum, fellows program, art collection, archives-and the historical research it hosted benefited enormously from ties to the oil and petrochemical industries.Then, I moved to Rice University in Houston.Rice's scientists and engineers were naturally immersed in 32 Tracing Oil Money in the Acad emyCyrus C. M.

title: Does the composition of the board of directors impact the implementation of ESG initiatives in Mexican listed companies in the period 2020–2024?
source: Corporate Governance and Organizational Behavior Review
summary: Compliance with sustainability practices extends beyond a mere disclosure of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) actions. Without evidence of consistent implementation, disclosure alone cannot fully demonstrate the organizational co
content: Compliance with sustainability practices extends beyond a mere disclosure of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) actions. Without evidence of consistent implementation, disclosure alone cannot fully demonstrate the organizational commitment to fulfilling its responsibilities in each of these pillars. The present paper examines the effect of two main dimensions of the composition of boards of directors—the number of independent members and its gender diversity on the implementation of organizational ESG practices, measured through an implementation index for the period 2020–2024. Based on a sample of Mexican publicly listed companies and panel data analysis with a two-way fixed effects model, the results suggest a negative correlation with gender diversity, a finding in line with Abdelkader et al. (2024), Husted and de Sousa-Filho (2019), and a negative, though not statistically significant, association with the number of independent board members. In addition, the study identifies a strong positive association between the entities’ trading age and their ESG implementation results in a one-way firm-specific fixed effects test. Further research with a wider sample of organizations is recommended, whereas a cross-country comparative study can uncover novel insights into the effects of legal quotas in gender representation on boards.

title: Infectious Disease Knowledge Graph (IDKG) for Antiviral and Antibacterial Drug Discovery.
summary: Infectious diseases remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, while therapeutic discovery is hindered by fragmented biomedical data and antimicrobial resistance. To address this challenge, we developed the Infectious Disease
content: Infectious diseases remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, while therapeutic discovery is hindered by fragmented biomedical data and antimicrobial resistance. To address this challenge, we developed the Infectious Disease Knowledge Graph (IDKG), a queryable platform that integrates curated chemical, biological, pharmacological, and clinical information relevant to infectious-disease drug discovery. Using a customized ORION pipeline, we integrated 20 data sources, including DrugCentral, SMACC, Heli-SMACC, NPASS, ClinicalTrials.gov, and host-virus interaction databases, into a Neo4j graph containing more than 4.6 million nodes and 26 million edges. IDKG supports graph-based reasoning through Clinical Outcome Pathways (COPs) and incorporates curation workflows for small molecules, biologics, and complex mixtures. Illustrative applications include reconstruction of a literature-supported remdesivir pathway for COVID-19 and graph-based mechanistic interpretation of experimentally observed quorum-sensing inhibitor-antibiotic synergies in multidrug-resistant bacteria. The platform provides an interoperable framework for drug repurposing, target prioritization, and mechanism-based hypothesis generation. IDKG is freely available at https://idkg.mml.unc.edu.

title: Global Trends, Collaboration Networks, and Emerging Themes in Agripreneurship Research: A Bibliometric Analysis (2015–2025)
summary: Abstract Purpose Agricultural entrepreneurship, or agripreneurship, has grown quickly as a field of study, yet its intellectual structure remains fragmented. This study maps the growth trajectory, collaboration architecture and thematic evo
content: Abstract Purpose Agricultural entrepreneurship, or agripreneurship, has grown quickly as a field of study, yet its intellectual structure remains fragmented. This study maps the growth trajectory, collaboration architecture and thematic evolution of the global agripreneurship literature indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (2015–2025) and synthesises the results in an integrative conceptual framework. Design/Methodology/Approach Of 663 records initially retrieved, 190 peer-reviewed articles were retained after a PRISMA-aligned screening procedure. VOSviewer was used for performance analysis and science mapping: publication trends, co-authorship networks (country, institution and author levels), keyword co-occurrence mapping and temporal overlay visualisation. The mapped structure was then interpreted through an entrepreneurial-ecosystem lens to develop the Three-Level Agripreneurship Ecosystem Framework (TAEF). Data cleaning and standardisation protocols preceded all analyses. Findings Annual output rose from 4 articles in 2015 to 18 in 2020, and a further 128 articles appeared in 2021–2025 (about 67% of the corpus). China, India, the United States and the United Kingdom lead in publication share, and collaboration networks are strongly regionally clustered at national, institutional and author levels. Keyword co-occurrence mapping yields three clusters: (1) entrepreneurial behaviour and innovation; (2) agriculture, rural development and sustainability; and (3) institutions, policy and enabling environments. Temporal analysis shows a shift from enterprise-centric studies (2015–2018), through sustainability-integrated work (2019–2021), to ecosystem-oriented perspectives (2022–2025). Research Limitations/Implications The study relies on one database (the WoS Core Collection) and on English-language peer-reviewed articles, so grey literature, conference proceedings, non-English work and records indexed only elsewhere are excluded. The analysis is descriptive-structural, and the proposed framework is an interpretive synthesis whose propositions require empirical testing. Practical/Policy Implications The study identifies the need for standardised ecosystem metrics, longitudinal evidence, greater attention to gender and social inclusion, and stronger South–South research collaboration, and links each gap to a proposed research direction. These carry direct implications for designing evidence-based agripreneurship support systems that combine capability building with enabling-environment reform. Originality/Value Earlier bibliometric surveys addressed rural entrepreneurship broadly or ended before the post-2020 surge in publications. This study maps agripreneurship specifically for 2015–2025, adds country-, institution- and author-level collaboration networks with temporal overlays, and moves beyond description by proposing the TAEF, five testable propositions and an evidence-linked research agenda.

title: Mapping synergies and trade-offs for sustainable intensification (SI) strategies in Europe
summary: Sustainable Intensification (SI) of agriculture remains contested. It is promoted as a pathway to food security, yet criticized for overlooking systemic complexity. This ambiguity leaves uncertainty about the synergies and trade-offs associ
content: Sustainable Intensification (SI) of agriculture remains contested. It is promoted as a pathway to food security, yet criticized for overlooking systemic complexity. This ambiguity leaves uncertainty about the synergies and trade-offs associated with SI strategies in Europe. Through a systematic review of 46 studies, we examine how SI is defined and quantify mentions of synergies and trade-offs across 17 indicators spanning four domains: productivity, environmental, economic, and social. We identify 604 documented effects linked to 25 SI strategies. We find that positive effects are reported more frequently than negative effects, but that this is shaped by uneven indicator coverage. Productivity, efficient resource-use and environmental indicators dominate, while nutrition, food safety, labor conditions, equity and animal welfare remain under-assessed. We therefore interpret the SI literature as indicating potential for positive effects across multiple indicators, rather than demonstrating consistently positive multidimensional performance.

title: Briquetes sustentáveis de biocarvão a partir de resíduos de biomassa: condições de processo e potencial energético
summary: This study evaluated the physical, mechanical, and energetic characteristics of carbonized briquettes produced from banana peels, sawdust, and recycled paper, using cassava starch as a binder. Five formulations (F1–F5) were investigated to
content: This study evaluated the physical, mechanical, and energetic characteristics of carbonized briquettes produced from banana peels, sawdust, and recycled paper, using cassava starch as a binder. Five formulations (F1–F5) were investigated to assess the influence of biomass composition on apparent density, compressive strength, mechanical durability, proximate composition, higher heating value (HHV), and combustion performance. Apparent density ranged from 950 to 1060 kg m⁻³, with F3 and F4 exhibiting compressive strength above 2 MPa and mechanical durability exceeding 95%. HHV ranged from 20.08 to 24.09 MJ kg⁻¹. F4 showed the highest mechanical resistance and durability, whereas F5 exhibited the highest HHV, associated with lower ash content and higher fixed carbon, together with lower apparent fuel consumption and burning rate. These contrasting responses demonstrate that mechanical robustness and gravimetric energy content are not necessarily maximized by the same formulation. The findings provide a basis for optimizing multi-residue carbonized briquettes according to their intended applications and highlight the potential of locally available biomass residues for alternative solid-fuel production.

title: Development of a Lignin-Based Bio-Binder for Particleboards Applications from Organosolv Lignin Extracted from Mixed Cameroonian Wood Sawdust
summary: Abstract This study aimed at developing a lignin-based bio-binder from organosolv lignin extracted from mixed wood sawdust composed of three local wood species, namely Cordia, Iroko, and Passi, collected in Ngaoundéré, Cameroon, for applica
content: Abstract This study aimed at developing a lignin-based bio-binder from organosolv lignin extracted from mixed wood sawdust composed of three local wood species, namely Cordia, Iroko, and Passi, collected in Ngaoundéré, Cameroon, for application in particleboard manufacturing. The mixed sawdust was first sampled and characterized. Lignin was then extracted using the organosolv process, characterized, and modified by phenolation. The bio-binder formulation was optimized using response surface methodology based on a central composite design with three factors (lignin, furfural, and glycerol) and four responses (pH, viscosity, gel time, and insoluble fraction). The optimized bio-binder was subsequently used in the manufacturing process of particleboards produced from the mixed sawdust. The results showed that the mixed sawdust contained 45.6% lignin, with an extraction yield of 55.75% and a lignin purity of 91.1%. The optimized bio-binder exhibited a pH of 5.1, a viscosity of 342 mPa·s, a gel time of 3.35 min, and an insoluble fraction of 79.56%. The optimized particleboard exhibited a thickness swelling of 2.94%, an impact resistance of 100%, and a water absorption of 254%. Finally, the developed bio-binder contains 87.6% wood sawdust. When incorporated at 8.00% into particleboards containing 90.48% sawdust, it results in a final material with a wood sawdust content of 97.28%. These findings highlight the economic and industrial potentials of mixed wood sawdust as an abundant and readily available resource for the development of lignin-based bio-binders and more sustainable particleboards in Cameroon to promot local technology and economic development.

title: Designing for the Future: Sustainability as a Core Educational Principle
summary: This article explores the integration of sustainable practices within the university-level product design education, positioning sustainability as an essential, holistic method in the teaching process, deeply connected to the principles of
content: This article explores the integration of sustainable practices within the university-level product design education, positioning sustainability as an essential, holistic method in the teaching process, deeply connected to the principles of design thinking.The focus is on embedding sustainability throughout the entire design journey -from concept and technical solutions to packaging and transportation -encouraging students to adopt a systems-thinking mindset.Given the current environmental and economic challenges, it is crucial to guide emerging designers to think and act sustainably across all project phases.Sustainability must become an organically embedded principle in product design, not a secondary consideration.The problem -the fundamental driver behind the creation of a design object as a solution -is today inseparable from sustainability considerations.This article examines both the pedagogical methods which have proven effective in fostering sustainable thinking and the challenges encountered during studio-based project work.It further offers a critical reflection on how sustainability is not merely an additive component of the design process, but an inherent and inseparable dimension of contemporary product design practice.Within the educational context, the student-designer is guided to discover the integral role of sustainability as a value-generating element that shapes and informs the entire design process.Rather than being introduced as an optional or external principle, sustainability is revealed as a fundamental aspect of a holistic design approach.

title: Urban avian viromes reveal viral diversity of potential public health relevance across China
summary: Urbanization reshapes ecological interactions at the human-animal interface, yet how it structures viral diversity in urban avian communities remains unclear. Here, we present a pan-urban viromic analysis of avian samples collected across 2
content: Urbanization reshapes ecological interactions at the human-animal interface, yet how it structures viral diversity in urban avian communities remains unclear. Here, we present a pan-urban viromic analysis of avian samples collected across 22 cities in China. We identified 52,314 viral operational taxonomic units, broadly representing species-level viral clusters, revealing extensive and previously underexplored viral diversity. Viral richness varied markedly among cities, largely reflecting variation in bacteriophage diversity, whereas vertebrate-associated viruses showed a comparatively narrower diversity range. Network analyses revealed pronounced geographic structuring of avian viromes, with several cities sharing viral lineages with multiple other cities and acting as hubs of virome connectivity, linked by a core set of widely distributed viral families alongside substantial local heterogeneity. Sequence similarity and phylogenetic analyses showed that 63.1% (2994/4746) of vertebrate-associated viral sequences shared less than 80% similarity with their closest known references, including 65.6% (2718/4143) of DNA virus sequences and 45.8% (276/603) of RNA virus sequences, highlighting pervasive viral novelty across genome types. Further comparisons with reference sequences identified candidate associations with diverse annotated host taxa, including mammals and humans. Functional profiling of auxiliary metabolic genes revealed a highly skewed repertoire dominated by CysH (phosphoadenosine phosphosulfate reductase), a key enzyme in assimilatory sulfate reduction, suggesting that phages may modulate sulfur assimilation in infected bacterial hosts and potentially influence sulfur metabolism in urban bird-associated microbial communities. Together, these findings provide a nationwide view of the spatial organization, evolutionary diversity, and cross-host association patterns of viruses in urban birds, highlighting their role in shaping viral ecology in human-dominated environments.

title: ESG-Related Reporting Breadth and a Development-Oriented Digital-Transformation Proxy: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms
source: International Journal of Business and Management
summary: Adjacent research has linked CSR ratings or practices, disclosure constructs and digitalisation measures, but these constructs are not interchangeable, and their empirical meanings depend on how reporting and digital activity are operationa
content: Adjacent research has linked CSR ratings or practices, disclosure constructs and digitalisation measures, but these constructs are not interchangeable, and their empirical meanings depend on how reporting and digital activity are operationalised. This study therefore asks whether firm-level ESG-related reporting breadth, measured as observable topic coverage with limited report attributes, is associated with a development-oriented digital-transformation proxy among Chinese A-share listed firms. Using 33,000 firm-year observations from 4,679 firms over 2015-2024, the primary specification estimates a linear model absorbing firm and year effects and an archived mixed-vintage industry-category dimension, the documented control set and firm-clustered standard errors. The primary full-panel estimate is positive (β = 0.0381; approximate 95% CI [0.0073, 0.0689]), while a one-standard-deviation increase in reporting breadth, based on overall sample variation, corresponds to only about 1.1% of the outcome proxy’s overall standard deviation. The association is not statistically established in the Bloomberg-covered specifications, the raw-index evidence varies with the estimation window, and the Oster diagnostic indicates material sensitivity to assumptions about unobserved selection. The study’s contribution is therefore construct-specific, measurement-boundary-transparent and evidence-calibrated: it documents a small, proxy-bound and specification-sensitive conditional association without establishing causality, an organisational mechanism, capability formation or a validated disclosure measure.

title: Smart Fume Detection, Extraction, and Filtration System for CNC Laser Machines
source: International Journal of Global Goals and Sustainable Development
summary: This study developed and evaluated a Smart Fume Detection, Extraction, and Filtration System for CNC Laser Machines at Cebu Technological University–Argao Campus to improve airborne contaminant management during laser cutting and engraving.
content: This study developed and evaluated a Smart Fume Detection, Extraction, and Filtration System for CNC Laser Machines at Cebu Technological University–Argao Campus to improve airborne contaminant management during laser cutting and engraving. Anchored in the Cyber-Physical Machine Tool framework, sensor-based monitoring, airflow and filtration principles, Sustainable Manufacturing, and Garvin's Eight Dimensions of Quality, the study employed a developmental research design. The prototype integrated MQ-4 and MQ-135 sensors, microcontroller-based control, automated ventilation, warning mechanisms, digital monitoring, and multistage filtration. Data were collected through 20 controlled operational trials involving plywood and acrylic specimens, technical measurement instruments, observation logs, and questionnaire evaluations from 100 purposively selected respondents. Descriptive statistics and inferential tests assessed technical performance, material-based differences, and contaminant reduction. Results demonstrated 91.7% detection accuracy, 91.2% sensor reliability, a 4.28-second response time, 53.9 CFM extraction airflow, and 77.4% filtration efficiency, meeting all established benchmarks. Mean measured fume concentration decreased significantly from 393.29 ppm to 88.97 ppm, representing a 77.38% reduction (p < 0.0001). Significant differences between plywood and acrylic were observed in detection accuracy, response time, airflow, and fume concentrations, but not in sensor reliability or filtration efficiency. The prototype obtained an overall quality rating of 3.82, interpreted as Reliable. Further sensor calibration, extended testing, and contaminant-specific occupational safety validation are recommended. The study supports Sustainable Development Goals 3, 4, 8, 9, and 12 through occupational health, technical education, safer working conditions, industrial innovation, and responsible production. Its sustainability contribution includes improved fume management, adaptable automation, and institutional operating and maintenance guidance, subject to further validation before broader implementation.

title: Introduction to Geopolitics
summary: This new updated edition keeps the clarity of the overarching theme of geopolitical structures and agents in an engaging and accessible manner. The approach and examples require no previous knowledge of theory or current affairs. It helps r
content: This new updated edition keeps the clarity of the overarching theme of geopolitical structures and agents in an engaging and accessible manner. The approach and examples require no previous knowledge of theory or current affairs. It helps readers understand the geopolitical implications of the history of geopolitical change over the past 200 years, US–China tensions, the relative decline of the US, and emerging environmental conflicts. This book explains the contemporary global power of the United States and the challenges it is facing, the changing foreign policy of China, Iran’s foreign policy, the formation of geopolitical blocs such as the BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, cyberwarfare and geopolitical disinformation through social media, tensions between immigration and nationalist politics, insurgency, the changing landscape of energy geopolitics, environmental geopolitics, competition over resources, including rare earth minerals, and the possibilities of peacebuilding. New and updated examples include the geopolitical significance of Greenland, the geopolitics of “Greater Russia,” an expanded and updated discussion of the Israel–Palestine conflict to include the politics of state recognition and the history of US–Israel relations, and the economic and strategic position of Taiwan. This book raises questions by incorporating international and long-term historical perspectives and introduces readers to different theoretical viewpoints, including feminist contributions. The new edition features margin definitions and 23 new figures, including 19 maps. Introduction to Geopolitics will provide its readers with a set of critical analytical tools for understanding the actions of states as well as non-state actors that act in competition over resources and power. Both students and general readers will find this book an essential stepping-stone to a deeper and more critical understanding of contemporary conflicts.

title: Battery Mineral Value Chains in Africa: Transport optimization model for critical minerals resource allocation
summary: Several minerals found in Africa are critical for the clean energy transition, creating an opportunity for African countries to undertake resource-driven manufacturing instead of an existing extractives driven economic model. To enable Afri
content: Several minerals found in Africa are critical for the clean energy transition, creating an opportunity for African countries to undertake resource-driven manufacturing instead of an existing extractives driven economic model. To enable Africa’s move towards enhanced manufacturing, there is a need to develop methods that provide quantitative insights into how new processing plants could be optimally located in space and integrated with transport networks. A novel method presented in this paper shows how this can be done. We develop and solve a spatial transport optimization problem that: (1) integrates mines, processing locations, urban centers, roads networks, railways networks in Africa with maritime ports globally; (2) maps existing and future global trade of minerals products from originating mines to destination ports globally and cities in Africa; and (3) geolocates future mineral processing plants in an optimal way for maximum aggregation of mine outputs at minimum cost to transport them. The method also considers how planning can be done while accounting for environmental constraints, transport capacities, connectivity to the energy grid and planning polices focused on country-based manufacturing or a more regional integration of manufacturing. The method can be applied to optimizing supply chains beyond the African and critical minerals context.

title: Petromasculinity and Gender in the Climate Crisis (An interview with Cara Daggett, February 22, 2024)
summary: Pawley: We thought we'd start with this kind of central question: What is petromasculinity?Where is it most vis i ble in global political culture?And where is it pre sent and influential but more covert?Cara Daggett: I started thinking abou
content: Pawley: We thought we'd start with this kind of central question: What is petromasculinity?Where is it most vis i ble in global political culture?And where is it pre sent and influential but more covert?Cara Daggett: I started thinking about petromasculinity during the first Trump election in 2016.From ecofeminist theory, I had learned to see how sexual oppression and the exploitation of the nonhuman world are historically and materially connected.Ecofeminism helped me to recognize this pattern in right-wing movements in the US and globally.Two features recur in these movements.First, there is a ubiquitous embrace of heteromasculine domination, which is evident in the overturning of reproductive rights in the US, and in the Right's anti-trans and anti-queer politics.Second, there is fossil fuel boosterism and climate refusal; their only plan for the climate crisis is to accelerate extractivism and militarize borders.These two are mostly treated as separate phenomena in public discourse.Even social movements often counter them as separate prob lems.But it is no coincidence that misogyny and fossil fuel boosterism tend to appear together.Historically, sexual hierarchies have been impor tant in the exploitation of the nonhuman world.Nature and women are both conceived of as needing masculine control, and improvement, because they have been intimately linked as they are devalued; feminized and natu ral bodies are supposedly too chaotic, too passive, too cyclical, or too wasteful when left alone.The practical effect of this ideology is that certain kinds of work, and material inputs, are undervalued or made invisible, or assumed to be freely given by nature-this is work that is sometimes called "reproductive labor" or "care work," although the line between what counts as productive and reproductive is murky.The connection between gender and ecological domination is obvious once you point it out, and it has been gratifying to see a feminist concept like petromasculinity excite public interest.It has excited interest on the Right too.Far-right groups like Turning Point and their followers trolled 13 Petromasculinity and Gender in the Climate Crisis

title: Early In-ovo Sexing of Mojosari Duck Eggs on Day 5 Using Hybrid Feature Fusion and Machine Learning
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
