memory, identity, and environmental adaptation intersect in complex ways.This contribution emerges from a fifteen-year trajectory of field-based research conducted between universities, local institutions and rural communities in southern Tanzania, integrating architectural analysis, historical mapping, ethnographic observation, and environmental interpretation.Due to the limited availability of original architectural documentation-often inaccessible or never formally archived in the Tanzanian context-the analysis does not rely on conventional planimetric reconstruction.Instead, it is grounded in long-term fieldwork, direct observation, and the interpretation of material conditions and contemporary patterns of use.Within this framework, the study examines two colonial-era infrastructures-the Iringa Boma and the Iringa Central Market-to explore how regenerative design can operate as a culturally anchored and climate-adaptive methodology in post-colonial urban contexts.The Iringa Boma, originally conceived as a German administrative complex, has undergone a notable transformation into a museum and cultural centre.Its layered architecture-thick walls, deep verandas, and a courtyard that mediates air and light-illustrates a form of climatic responsiveness that resonates with contemporary ecological concerns.Its current role, shaped through anthropological engagement and communitydriven cultural programmes, provides a compelling example of heritage as an active urban catalyst.Conversely, the Iringa Central Market remains a vibrant yet increasingly pressured infrastructural organism: dense, porous, thermally stressed, and central to the city's socio-economic life.Its morphology offers significant potential for regenerative strategies that enhance ventilation, shading, circulation, and resilience for informal economies in a warming climate.Rather than applying external templates, the paper argues for a regenerative approach grounded in ecological intelligence and local agency.The two case studies demonstrate how residual colonial infrastructures-neither obsolete nor fully requalified-can become metabolic catalysts for low-carbon, culturally meaningful urban futures.

title: “This Was Once Czechoslovakia…”: Memory, Multiple Temporalities, and the Making of the Czech–Slovak Borderland
summary: This chapter examines how inhabitants of the Czech–Slovak borderland construct the meaning of the state border through narratives of the past and how these narratives contribute to the resilience of the cross-border region. It draws on the
content: This chapter examines how inhabitants of the Czech–Slovak borderland construct the meaning of the state border through narratives of the past and how these narratives contribute to the resilience of the cross-border region. It draws on the concepts of border temporalities and borderscapes and on a narrative analysis of interviews conducted between 2023 and 2025. The analysis shows that respondents mobilise multiple temporalities—from Great Moravia and Czechoslovakia to the Schengen Area—not to reconstruct the past, but to interpret the present. The chapter proposes that multiple temporalities can be understood as a mechanism of narrative resilience through which a shared cross-border space is reproduced despite transformations of the state border.

title: “A Process and Not an Institution”: MAC and the Mail Art Exhibition
summary: poesía" (The new poetry), first published in the journal Ovum 10 in 1969, Uruguayan poet, literary critic, and mail artist Clemente Padín characterized the semiotic relationship between signifier and signified as a site of struggle against
content: poesía" (The new poetry), first published in the journal Ovum 10 in 1969, Uruguayan poet, literary critic, and mail artist Clemente Padín characterized the semiotic relationship between signifier and signified as a site of struggle against authoritarian tendencies in poetry.He described how the reader of a poem played an active role in the interpretation of the text, undermining the authority of the artist in a manner similar to that described by Roland Barthes in his essay "The Death of the Author."Using semiotics, "La nueva poesía" outlined an aesthetic opposed to the concept of the "genius-poet" whose work imposed specific metaphors, emotional states, and interpretations on the reader.It proposed that the relationship between the poem and its reader created meaning through a process of communication.For this reason, there could be no correct or authoritative interpretations of new poetry and hence no hierarchies built on such readings.For Padín, this approach opened the possibility of reading texts in ways that were more interactive and less fixed. 1 This development, in which the reader played an active role in the process of creating meaning, occurred at the same time as the transition from first-order to second-order cybernetics, the increasing implication of the observer in the creation of systems, and the growing understanding of information as action discussed in the previous chapter.Padín's ideas had several sources of inspiration that included concrete poetry, poema/processo, visual poetry, and mail art, and paralleled

title: Vegetation changes in Central Asia: uncovering their impacts on regional and Asian climate systems
summary: Abstract Central Asia is one of the most arid regions in the world and is highly vulnerable to climate change. This region has undergone extensive land cover and land use (LCLU) changes over several decades, including the expansion of irrig
content: Abstract Central Asia is one of the most arid regions in the world and is highly vulnerable to climate change. This region has undergone extensive land cover and land use (LCLU) changes over several decades, including the expansion of irrigation during the Soviet era and the subsequent abandonment of cropland after the post-Soviet disintegration. This widespread abandonment represented one of the most extensive LCLU changes in the Northern Hemisphere during the 20th century. Changes in land cover can alter the energy, moisture, and momentum balances, thereby influencing atmospheric processes. However, compared to other Asian regions, significantly fewer studies have examined the impacts of LCLU changes on climate in Central Asia. This study explored the relationships between vegetation changes in Central Asia and climate during the boreal summer through the empirical association (correlation and regression analyses) and causality (Granger-causality test, Convergent Cross Mapping, and Structural Equation Modeling) analyses, supported by the model datasets (multi-model ensemble means). The results showed that a reduction in vegetation significantly decreased latent heat flux, causing sensible heat flux to dominate land-atmosphere energy exchanges and consequently elevating tropospheric temperatures. This thermal expansion in the troposphere elevated the geopotential height, generating an anomalous anticyclonic circulation supported by a significant negative vorticity anomaly in the upper troposphere. The anticyclonic anomaly induced an easterly wind anomaly that counteracted the prevailing wind, thereby weakening the westerly upper-level jet (i.e., the Asian jet) over Central Asia. Our study highlights that vegetation changes in Central Asia can significantly affect not only the regional climate but also the Asian atmospheric circulation.

title: Application of Bacillus toyonensis as a Novel Starter Culture on Nutritional Quality and Probiotic Viability of Fermented Carrot Pickles During Refrigerated Storage
summary: Abstract This study evaluated the impact of inoculated fermentation (IF) using a novel Bacillus strain and natural fermentation (NF) on the physicochemical, microbial, antioxidant, and sensory characteristics of carrot pickle during 13 days
content: Abstract This study evaluated the impact of inoculated fermentation (IF) using a novel Bacillus strain and natural fermentation (NF) on the physicochemical, microbial, antioxidant, and sensory characteristics of carrot pickle during 13 days of refrigerated storage (4°C). The isolated Bacillus strain was identified Bacillus toyonensis by 16s rRNA sequencing. The IF sample showed decreased pH, total sugar, and total soluble solids (TSS), and increased titratable acidity compared to the NF sample. Color (L* and b*) values of both samples decreased during the storage period. The viable count of Bacillus in the IF sample remained above 10 6 CFU/g, whereas the NF sample lower viable count end of 8 days of storage. The total phenolic content (TPC), carotenoid content and antioxidant capacity (DPPH and FRAP) increased in the IF sample, while decreased the carotenoid and antioxidant capacity and increased the TPC in the NF sample at end of storage period. Sensory evaluation further revealed that inoculated fermentation was significantly superior in terms of appearance, fermented flavor, spiciness, texture, and overall acceptability compared to natural fermentation. These findings indicate that using Bacillus toyonensis strain HSTU FPP-1 serves as an effective starter culture to enhance the quality, antioxidant potential, and probiotic functionality of carrot pickles.

title: AI in Food and Agriculture: Ethics from Farm to Table
summary: This book offers the first comprehensive philosophical account of what is ethically at stake as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in agricultural systems, from precision irrigation platforms on the Kansas High Plains to robotic
content: This book offers the first comprehensive philosophical account of what is ethically at stake as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in agricultural systems, from precision irrigation platforms on the Kansas High Plains to robotic harvesters in the apple orchards of Washington State. In the face of changing weather patterns, droughts, and fewer available resources, modern agricultural practices are evolving, embracing AI systems to help increase crop efficiency, production, and yields. However, technological innovation on the farm often comes with environmental and social costs. This book analyzes AI and Information Systems through the lens of contemporary challenges in agricultural processes ranging from farm to table. Drawing on field visits across the Pacific Northwest and sustained engagement with agricultural ethics, the philosophy of technology, and environmental justice, this book develops three original frameworks for evaluating agricultural AI: the Four Pillars of Agricultural Ethics, which assesses AI across its impacts on society, individuals, the environment, and animals; the SEED framework, which translates sustainability into design-stage commitments for responsible AI; and a trivalent environmental justice framework that holds distribution, recognition, and intergenerational responsibility together as inseparable governance concerns. Together, these tools make the case for bringing ethics into the design of agricultural AI before costs become embedded in the landscape. This book will be of great interest to students and scholars of agricultural and food ethics, agricultural technology and innovation, AI and the philosophy of technology.

title: Attributional and consequential life cycle assessment of end-of-life options for flexible pipelines from oil well decommissioning
summary: Decommissioning oil wells in Brazil will generate large quantities of subsea pipelines that require end-of-life (EoL) management. This study evaluated four EoL options for flexible pipelines using attributional and consequential life cycle
content: Decommissioning oil wells in Brazil will generate large quantities of subsea pipelines that require end-of-life (EoL) management. This study evaluated four EoL options for flexible pipelines using attributional and consequential life cycle assessment (LCA) with system expansion: (1) landfill disposal; (2) steel recycling combined with mechanical recycling of high-density polyethylene (HDPE), polyamide (PA), and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF); (3) steel recycling combined with energy recovery from HDPE and PA and mechanical recycling of PVDF; and (4) pipeline reuse. Substitution rates of 100% for recycled polymers and 24% for steel scrap were adopted, and their effects were evaluated through sensitivity analyses. For reuse, the difference between well and pipeline service lives resulted in a Reuse Efficiency Factor (REF) of 37.5%, which was used to calculate the credit for avoided new pipeline manufacturing. Attributional LCA identified landfill disposal as the lowest-impact option, whereas, under the adopted substitution and reuse assumptions, consequential LCA produced the opposite ranking, with reuse showing the lowest impacts, generally followed by mechanical recycling, energy recovery, and landfill disposal. Relative to landfill disposal, reuse avoided approximately 5140 kg CO 2 -eq per t of pipeline for global warming potential (GWP), corresponding to an estimated upper bound of 1.34 billion kg CO 2 -eq from the decommissioning of 261,368.60 t of flexible pipelines in Brazil over the next decade, assuming that all pipelines still within their service lives are available for reuse. These findings show that the modeling perspective can reverse the environmental ranking of EoL options and that reusing remaining pipeline service life can reduce demand for new pipelines.

title: Upcycling of polyolefin and polyester mixtures via a single-atom alloy
summary: Upcycling of mixed plastic waste is challenging due to the complex compositions and high sorting costs, lacking robust catalysts for simultaneous conversion of polyolefins and polyesters. Herein, guided by machine learning, we design a Ru1C
content: Upcycling of mixed plastic waste is challenging due to the complex compositions and high sorting costs, lacking robust catalysts for simultaneous conversion of polyolefins and polyesters. Herein, guided by machine learning, we design a Ru1Cu/CeO2-GR single-atom alloy catalyst that enables one-pot hydrogenolysis of mixed plastics into fuel-range hydrocarbons. Ru single atoms anchored on Cu nanoparticles lower C–C bond cleavage barriers, while Cu suppresses benzene ring overhydrogenation. Under mild conditions (280 °C, 30 bar H2), the catalyst delivers ~75% liquid yield (C5–C22) with 59.5%–62.7% C8–C16 fraction and ~15% aromatic products yield from five-component mixed plastics. Life cycle and techno-economic analyses confirm that this direct upcycling route outperforms traditional sorted recycling with lower environmental impacts and higher economic benefits. This work provides a sustainable and economically viable strategy for mixed plastic waste valorization. Mixed plastic waste is difficult to recycle because different polymers require separate processing. This study develops a catalyst that converts mixed plastics directly into fuel-range hydrocarbons with high liquid yield.

title: The Role of Recycling in the Sustainable Life Cycle of Photovoltaic Power Systems: Approaches to Efficient Resource Use and Local Energy Management
summary: Abstract The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) power plants across the globe has intensified concerns about their environmental impacts and the extensive use of resources throughout their life cycle. Overcoming these challenges is crucia
content: Abstract The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) power plants across the globe has intensified concerns about their environmental impacts and the extensive use of resources throughout their life cycle. Overcoming these challenges is crucial for advancing sustainable energy systems and improving community energy management. This study employs the life cycle assessment (LCA) approach to evaluate the environmental performance of PV power plants, focusing particularly on recycling as an end-of-life management strategy. The assessment examines the major stages of the PV life cycle and identifies module manufacturing, together with the consumption of fossil fuels and mineral resources, as the phases generating the greatest environmental burden. The results indicate that recycling lowers water usage and lessens adverse effects on human health compared with landfill-based disposal options. Recovering valuable materials also contributes to lowering the economic costs of raw material extraction while supporting the principles of a circular economy. Overall, the study demonstrates that recycling should be viewed not merely as a waste treatment solution, but as an essential component of the sustainable life cycle of PV power plants, enhancing resource efficiency and reinforcing the resilience of community energy systems.

title: RETHINKING DEVELOPMENT FINANCE: BRIDGING AID FRAGMENTATION FOR POST-SDG 2030
summary: This article examines the structural fragmentation of development finance as a critical barrier to achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) beyond 2030. The study aims to assess the extent to which current financing architectures are
content: This article examines the structural fragmentation of development finance as a critical barrier to achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) beyond 2030. The study aims to assess the extent to which current financing architectures are aligned with emerging development demands, using an empirical approach that analyzes financing flows, institutional arrangements, SDG performance indicators, and the diversity of development finance sources. The results reveal a significant misalignment between existing aid structures and the complexity of post-2030 challenges, highlighting inefficiencies, overlaps, and gaps in resource allocation. In response, the article proposes evidence-based models for the integration of development finance, alongside practical roadmaps for institutional reform focused on improving coordination and governance. Supported by nine empirical tables and a quantitative evaluation of finance effectiveness, the findings underscore the need for systemic restructuring. The study concludes that enhancing coherence, integration, and strategic alignment is essential to ensure the effectiveness and sustainability of global development financing in the post-2030 agenda.

title: Foreign Assistance and Power-Sector Carbon Emissions in the MENA Region: The Roles of Trade, Foreign Direct Investment, and Foreign Development Assistance
summary: Foreign assistance may help reduce power-sector carbon emissions (PSCE). This study examines the effect of net official development assistance and official aid (NODAOA) on PSCE in 16 Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economies over the pe
content: Foreign assistance may help reduce power-sector carbon emissions (PSCE). This study examines the effect of net official development assistance and official aid (NODAOA) on PSCE in 16 Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economies over the period 1985–2024, within the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) framework. Foreign direct investment (FDI) and trade openness (TO) are included as control variables. PSCE is measured as CO 2 emissions from electricity and heat production. Given the expected spatial linkages among geographically proximate MENA economies, the study applies a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) to examine spatial dependence and spillover effects. The results support the EKC hypothesis, although 14 of the 16 MENA economies remain in its first phase. This suggests that economic growth has not yet been accompanied by a reduction in PSCE in most of the sampled economies. NODAOA is negatively associated with emissions through significant direct and spillover effects, highlighting the potential role of development assistance in supporting cleaner electricity transitions. By contrast, FDI is positively associated with PSCE across the estimated specifications, whereas the effect of TO is statistically insignificant. These findings highlight the challenge of coordinating regional decarbonization pathways in fossil-fuel-dependent MENA economies. They also identify development assistance as a potential channel for improving the environmental performance of the power sector, in line with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7 and 13.

title: Catalytic upcycling of aliphatic polyethers and polyurethanes into α,ω-dichloroalkanes
summary: Aliphatic polyethers are ubiquitous polymers in pharmaceutics and essential building blocks for polyurethanes production. Yet their recycling is underexploited, owing to their strong C-O bond (BDE of ~85 kcal mol-1) as challenging reactive
content: Aliphatic polyethers are ubiquitous polymers in pharmaceutics and essential building blocks for polyurethanes production. Yet their recycling is underexploited, owing to their strong C-O bond (BDE of ~85 kcal mol-1) as challenging reactive handle. Herein, we highlight the exceptional reactivity of gallium or iron catalysis to upcycle these aliphatic polyethers using boron trichloride as a chlorinating reagent, to offset the thermodynamic cost of creating a C-Cl bond from a C-O bond. The reaction can be carried out under mild conditions (low temperature, low catalytic amount of Lewis Acid such as [Fe] or [Ga] salts) to yield the corresponding α,ω-dichloroalkanes (up to 95% isolated). These intermediates are useful organic solvents and essential industrial key intermediates. In particular, dichloroethane gives access to vinyl chloride, whereas dichlorobutane affords adiponitrile upon cyanation: those are versatile precursors of the polymer industry.

title: Collective Stereodivergent Synthesis of the [13]Graphanyl Isomers: Applications as Drug Analogues
summary: Conformationally locked polycycles represent an attractive class of compounds in drug discovery campaigns for medicinal chemists. The three-dimensionality of these scaffolds can result in unique topologies and well-defined exit vectors, enh
content: Conformationally locked polycycles represent an attractive class of compounds in drug discovery campaigns for medicinal chemists. The three-dimensionality of these scaffolds can result in unique topologies and well-defined exit vectors, enhancing pharmacokinetic profiles and protein interactions that lead to the development of clinically approved therapeutics. One such scaffold that has remained largely underexplored is [13]Graphane, as the synthesis of its four stereoisomers is nontrivial. Herein, we describe a collective stereodivergent synthesis of all the stereoisomers of the [13]Graphane, their central derivatization with diverse functional groups for downstream functionalization. From a common epoxide precursor, we exploit dienyne ring closing cascade metathesis and stereospecific hydrogenation to build each isomer. By performing a decarboxylative radical coupling study on all the [13]G–COOH stereoisomers, we report ring inversions of the ccc- and ctt-[13]G radicals and study these by density functional theory calculations. Finally, we leveraged the different centrally functionalized [13]Graphanes to synthesize Adamantane-based drug analogues as examples of applications in drug design.

title: Elucidating the trapping mechanism of underground storage for hydrogen and carbon dioxide via Geomechanical modelling: a case study of the aquifer in Malaysia
summary: Abstract BACKGROUND As a developed technology, underground carbon dioxide storage (UCS) can become the technical reference for the development of underground hydrogen storage (UHS). The same geological criteria can be applied to UHS to ensu
content: Abstract BACKGROUND As a developed technology, underground carbon dioxide storage (UCS) can become the technical reference for the development of underground hydrogen storage (UHS). The same geological criteria can be applied to UHS to ensure its feasibility. The implemented UCS projects in Malaysia can be used as references for UHS development. This study aims to elucidate the potential of UCS and UHS in the Malaysian aquifer, focusing on trapping mechanisms, gas storage performance, gas storage behavior, and the sensitivity analysis of UHS and UCS to geomechanical properties (tensile strength, Poisson ratio, and Young's Modulus). Two CO 2 –H 2 injection strategies are used in the study, i.e., simultaneous injection and CO 2 ‐preinjection. CO 2 is injected as cushion gas with fractions of 60%, 70%, and 80%. RESULTS For cushion gas fractions of 60% and 70%, the total volume of gas injected in the preinjection strategy is higher than in the simultaneous injection. The solubility trapping in the pre‐injection strategy is lower than in the simultaneous injection strategy. The storage volume of UCS is 2.3 times more than that of UHS. UCS shows stronger solubility trapping; 35.32% of the gas has been trapped by the water in UCS at the end of the simulation, which is 16.95% higher than UHS. Furthermore, UHS has stronger residual trapping, 78.02% of gas trapped by residual trapping at the end of the simulation, which is 17.49% higher than UCS. In addition, it was found that the hydrogen equilibrium state in porous medium was achieved after 10 to 15 years of the injection, while the transition among different trapping mechanisms in UCS continued until the end of the 100‐year simulation. One of the major differences between the geomechanical and non‐geomechanical (normal) models is CO 2 dissolution in water. In the normal model, only 29.12% of CO 2 was dissolved in the end of 100 years of storage, but this increased to 35.324% in the geomechanical model. This suggests that the geomechanical effect enhances solubility trapping. CONCLUSION Overall, the findings assess a significant difference in storage capacity and trapping‐mechanism performance between UCS and UHS, which is mainly due to the solubility and the rate of conversion from mobile gas to immobile gas, and from mobile gas to dissolved gas. The effect of geomechanical property is significant in both underground carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and hydrogen (H 2 ) storage, but its impact is larger in CO 2 storage. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

title: Decomposition Mechanism of Organic Sulfide in Heavy Oil during Thermal Reaction
summary: As the proportion of high-sulfur crude oil continues to rise, the transformation behavior of sulfur compounds during delayed coking is of considerable significance for clean fuel production and for controlling the sulfur content of petroleu
content: As the proportion of high-sulfur crude oil continues to rise, the transformation behavior of sulfur compounds during delayed coking is of considerable significance for clean fuel production and for controlling the sulfur content of petroleum coke. In this work, model crude oil systems were constructed using liquid paraffin as the saturate fraction and p-xylene as the aromatic fraction, with thiophene and benzothiophene added separately. Thermal reaction experiments were conducted at 500 °C for 3 h. Gas chromatography with sulfur chemiluminescence detection (GC-SCD) was used for qualitative and quantitative analysis of the sulfur composition in gas- and liquid-phase products, and the transformation pathways of sulfur compounds were inferred in conjunction with free-radical reaction mechanisms. The results show that H₂S predominates in the gas-phase sulfur in both systems, and that the liquid phase contains, in addition to unreacted sulfur compounds, a substantial variety of newly formed sulfur compounds. These findings demonstrate that the thermal reactions in both systems follow a free-radical mechanism centered on C–S bond activation. Furthermore, benzothiophene is converted from a readily desulfurized small molecule into sulfur compounds that are more prone to condensation and coke formation. The results provide a molecular-level basis for regulating the transformation of thiophene-type sulfur compounds and for low-sulfur clean processing in heavy oil thermal reactions.

title: Climate policy packages and support for carbon capture and storage
summary: This project investigates how public support for climate policy packages varies depending on how different policy components are combined, with a particular focus on carbon capture and storage (CCS). In contemporary climate policy, governme
content: This project investigates how public support for climate policy packages varies depending on how different policy components are combined, with a particular focus on carbon capture and storage (CCS). In contemporary climate policy, governments rarely introduce single measures in isolation. Instead, they propose bundles that combine support for specific technologies, timelines for phasing out fossil energy, financial costs for households, compensation schemes, and measures to manage labour market transitions in emissions intensive industries. Public acceptance of such packages is likely to depend not only on each individual component, but also on how these components appear together. Our core aim is to understand how CCS affects the support for broader climate policy packages, and how its effects depend on other elements of the package. To address these questions, we field a choice based conjoint experiment in five European countries: Norway, Denmark, Sweden, Germany and England. In each choice task, respondents are shown two hypothetical climate policy packages, presented side by side in a table, and are asked which package they think the government should introduce. Each package is defined by six dimensions: (1) government support for CCS, (2) government support for offshore wind, (3) the ambition of phasing out fossil energy, (4) household energy costs, (5) compensation schemes for households, and (6) transition measures for industry. Within each task, the levels of these six dimensions are independently and uniformly randomized, and the order of the dimensions is randomized once per respondent and then held constant across tasks. Respondents can choose Package A, Package B, or an opt out option (“Neither should be introduced”), allowing us to capture both relative preferences between packages and rejection of both options. The conjoint design is a cross-national adaptation of the U.S. study by Bergquist, Mildenberger and Stokes (2020). Five of the six dimensions have three levels (e.g., no, some, or substantial government support for CCS), while the industry transition dimension has two levels (retraining and support for new green jobs versus temporary subsidies to emissions intensive industry). Randomization is unrestricted, so all admissible combinations of levels can occur, and each level appears with approximately equal frequency. Norwegian respondents (Norwegian Citizen Panel) complete two choice tasks; respondents in Denmark, Sweden, Germany and England (Norstat online panels) complete three choice tasks. This fully randomized multi attribute design allows us to estimate the average marginal component effect (AMCE) of each attribute level on the probability that a package is chosen. title: Insufficient returns for renewable investments in low- and middle-income countries are addressable at below USD 25 per tonne of CO2
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset contains the outputs of a global geospatial assessment of the risk–return profiles and concessional-finance requirements of five renewable electricity technologies. The model combines spatially resolved renewable productivity w
content: This dataset contains the outputs of a global geospatial assessment of the risk–return profiles and concessional-finance requirements of five renewable electricity technologies. The model combines spatially resolved renewable productivity with technology costs, country-specific costs of capital, and electricity-price data to estimate project-level electricity costs, expected returns, financing gaps, and the grant support required to make otherwise unviable projects financially viable. The outputs support analysis of barriers to renewable-energy deployment in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where high financing costs and constrained electricity revenues can limit investment despite substantial emissions-reduction potential. Model results indicate that fewer than 44% of assessed LMIC locations achieve a positive net return without support. For locations with insufficient returns, the estimated financing gap reaches up to USD 163/MWh globally, with a mean of approximately USD 30/MWh. The dataset also quantifies the cost-effectiveness of closing this gap through grant support, expressed in USD per tonne of CO₂ avoided. The results identify locations where concessional support could enable renewable deployment at costs comparable to prevailing carbon-market prices, while providing greater confidence that the associated emissions reductions are enabled by the intervention. They further enable comparison between renewable-energy support in LMICs and more costly mitigation options for hard-to-abate emissions in high-income countries.

title: Consumer Drivers of Green Supply Chain Perceptions in Selangor, Malaysia: Implications for Sustainable Halal Ecosystems
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: The transition toward sustainable halal ecosystems requires businesses to consider environmental responsibility alongside halal integrity, ethical sourcing, transparency, and consumer confidence. Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) provide
content: The transition toward sustainable halal ecosystems requires businesses to consider environmental responsibility alongside halal integrity, ethical sourcing, transparency, and consumer confidence. Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) provides a practical approach for embedding environmental considerations into product design, procurement, manufacturing, packaging, logistics, and end-of-life management. However, consumer-related factors associated with perceptions of such practices have not been extensively examined in the Malaysian context. This study examines the relationships between environmental concern, environmental awareness, willingness to pay, trust in green claims, and consumers’ perceptions of GSCM practices, and discusses their implications for sustainable halal ecosystem development. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 184 consumers in Selangor, Malaysia, using purposive sampling and a structured questionnaire. Environmental awareness, trust in green claims, and environmental concern emerged as significant positive predictors of GSCM perceptions, while willingness to pay did not make a significant unique contribution when the other factors were considered. Environmental awareness was the strongest predictor, highlighting the importance of consumer knowledge in sustainability evaluation. The findings suggest that consumer perceptions are associated more strongly with awareness, credibility, and environmental concern than with financial willingness alone. The halal relevance is interpretive rather than a direct empirical test. Accordingly, the study offers exploratory implications for halal-oriented businesses by highlighting the value of credible green practices, transparent communication, consumer education, and trustworthy environmental claims in supporting environmentally responsible supply chain strategies.

title: Entrepreneurial Trust and Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence From Chinese Entrepreneurs
summary: ABSTRACT Why do entrepreneurs respond so differently to environmental innovation imperatives? Prior research emphasizes structural pressures, overlooking the cognitive and social frames shaping environmental decisions. Using survey data fro
content: ABSTRACT Why do entrepreneurs respond so differently to environmental innovation imperatives? Prior research emphasizes structural pressures, overlooking the cognitive and social frames shaping environmental decisions. Using survey data from 3163 Chinese micro and small firms, we find composite entrepreneurial trust is positively associated with green innovation. Disaggregating trust reveals a distinct institutional division of labor: Locally embedded in‐group trust accompanies green innovation—particularly local pollution abatement in lower‐pollution sectors—whereas institutional trust is linked to climate‐related innovation specifically among politically connected entrepreneurs. Generalized out‐group trust shows no association. Furthermore, trust aligns with green innovation alongside active behavioral commitments—risk‐taking, employee training, and proactive policy search—rather than passive expectations like future optimism or perceived policy effectiveness. This research advances the microfoundations of environmental strategy by illuminating how distinct trust objects shape responses to uncertainty. Practically, policymakers must lower policy‐information search costs, and entrepreneurs should pair relational trust with concrete capability investments.

title: Industry 4.0 technologies and micro-level circular economy to advance resource equity: Case studies in an automotive industry
summary: Abstract This study investigates the economic, environmental, and social outcomes associated with the implementation of Industry 4.0 Technologies (I4.0 T) aligned with Micro-Level Circular Economy (MLCE) and Cleaner Production (CP) principl
content: Abstract This study investigates the economic, environmental, and social outcomes associated with the implementation of Industry 4.0 Technologies (I4.0 T) aligned with Micro-Level Circular Economy (MLCE) and Cleaner Production (CP) principles, adopting resource equity as an interpretative perspective. A multiple-case study was conducted at an automotive manufacturer using semi-structured interviews, direct observation, and operational data. Environmental performance was assessed using the Material Intensity Factor (MIF) and Circularity Index, while economic outcomes were evaluated through investment, cost savings, return on investment (ROI), and payback period. Social outcomes related to workforce qualification, occupational conditions, safety, and employment were also examined. The findings show that the effects of I4.0 T implementation differed substantially between the two cases. In Case 1, the implementation of an autonomous robotic welding system reduced material and electricity consumption, resulting in a Circularity Index of 20.13%, an ROI of 30.09%, and a payback period of approximately 50 months. In Case 2, the implementation of Automated Guided Vehicles integrated with WMS, RFID, and ERP systems eliminated 10,560 kg of annual natural gas consumption, resulting in a Circularity Index of 7.69%, an ROI of 74.09%, and a payback period of approximately 22 months. Social outcomes were mixed: technological implementation supported workforce qualification and reduced exposure to selected occupational hazards, but workforce reductions were also observed. Overall, the findings indicate that I4.0 T can support MLCE practices and more efficient resource use, although economic, environmental, and social benefits are context-dependent and may involve trade-offs. From a policy perspective, the results may inform industrial innovation and public funding initiatives by encouraging the adoption of measurable resource efficiency, circular economy, workforce transition, and decarbonization criteria in digital transformation projects.

title: Crosslinked Bio‐Based Conductive Composite Films Filled With Carbon Fibers: Fabrication and Electrothermal Properties
summary: ABSTRACT Driven by the booming market of flexible wearable electrothermal and medical sensing devices, eco‐friendly flexible conductive materials are highly demanded. However, traditional flexible conductive films suffer from high brittlene
content: ABSTRACT Driven by the booming market of flexible wearable electrothermal and medical sensing devices, eco‐friendly flexible conductive materials are highly demanded. However, traditional flexible conductive films suffer from high brittleness and poor biodegradability, limiting their applications in sustainable wearable electrothermal systems. Herein, bio‐based composite films were fabricated via solution casting using sodium alginate/dialdehyde cellulose as the matrix and chopped carbon fibers ( CFs ) as conductive fillers. The effects of CF loading and surface modification with 3‐Aminopropyltriethoxysilane ( KH550 ) and polydopamine ( PDA ) on film performances were systematically investigated. Results show that increased CF loading simultaneously improves conductivity and mechanical properties; the 15 wt% CF film achieves optimal conductive and electrothermal performance. All films exhibit stable electrical performance under cyclic bending, with resistance variation below 5% after 60 bending cycles. The two modification strategies exhibit markedly different effects: 1.2 wt% KH550 modification enhances interfacial compatibility, conductivity, and strength while endowing hydrophobicity, whereas 2 g/L PDA treatment improves tensile strength and hydrophilicity yet may trigger CF agglomeration and damage conductive networks. The optimal condition is 15 wt% CF coupled with 1.2 wt% KH550 modification. This work clarifies the regulation of filler content and interfacial modification on multifunctional performances, providing experimental guidance for designing sustainable flexible conductive films.

title: Integrated Agro-Food Waste Valorization and Bioprocess Intensification for Sustainable Tannase Biosynthesis: A Response Surface-Guided Solid-State Fermentation Approach
source: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology
summary: The large-scale processing of fruits and vegetables generates substantial quantities of peel waste; along with STL (Spent tea leaves) that remain underutilized despite their potential for conversion into value-added bioproducts. Tannase is
content: The large-scale processing of fruits and vegetables generates substantial quantities of peel waste; along with STL (Spent tea leaves) that remain underutilized despite their potential for conversion into value-added bioproducts. Tannase is an industrially important enzyme widely applied in food and feed processing, beverage clarification, biochemical industries, and waste treatment. Commercial production of tannase predominantly relies on Submerged fermentation, which involves high operational costs and energy demand. SSF (Solid-state fermentation) represents a cost-effective alternative; however, systematic studies integrating diverse food wastes, statistical optimization, and techno-economic validation remain limited. In particular, comparative evaluation of locally available agro-residues under optimized SSF conditions has not been adequately explored. This study developed a sustainable and economically viable strategy for tannase production using Aspergillus niger under SSF with fruit and vegetable peels, STL, and wheat bran collected from local markets in Kolkata, India. Fermentation parameters; temperature, incubation time, and hydration ratio were initially optimized using a OFAT (One-Factor-At-A-Time) approach, followed by RSM (Response Surface Methodology) with CCD (Central Composite Design). Among the substrates tested, orange peel produced the highest tannase activity (0.0037 ± 0.00018 U/gds) at 30 °C, 9 days, and 1:3 [w/v] hydration ratio, followed by mango peel (0.0035 ± 0.00017 U/gds) and STL (0.0026 ± 0.00016 U/gds). Statistical optimization revealed significant variable interactions and achieved a 1.6-fold enhancement under optimal conditions (8 days, 26 °C, 1:1 hydration ratio; R² = 0.82, p < 0.05). A preliminary techno-economic analysis indicated nearly 14-fold cost reduction compared to market prices, demonstrating strong industrial potential.

title: Mangrove habitat suitability and blue carbon modelling in Soc Trang Province, Vietnam
source: Journal of Applied Life Sciences and Environment
summary: Species selection and spatial assumptions influence mangrove restoration screening, but their effects on the area available for blue carbon assessment are often difficult to separate. This study combined habitat suitability rules for 11 man
content: Species selection and spatial assumptions influence mangrove restoration screening, but their effects on the area available for blue carbon assessment are often difficult to separate. This study combined habitat suitability rules for 11 mangrove taxa with 19 spatial sensitivity scenarios in Soc Trang Province, Vietnam. Sentinel-2 imagery supported mangrove mapping, and distance from an analytical coastline and Copernicus surface elevation provided proxies for species suitability. Five overlapping group summaries were linked to a simplified carbon screening model. In the relaxed marine fringe rule configuration (RF1), the exported group areas summed to 22,727.932 ha, whereas the unique area satisfying at least one species rule was 8931.516 ha. Across the 19 scenarios, group area sums ranged from 18,053.275 to 26,207.868 ha. Using the corrected group inputs and recovered 30-year equations resulted in 10.218 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (t CO₂e) in the RF1 central model run, which was the sum of overlapping group options, not carbon credited to a unique project area. The group areas can inform comparisons among restoration options, while the unique area indicates the land footprint available for further screening. The carbon settings affected group-specific sequestration rates but held biomass, soil carbon stocks and other accounting parameters fixed. Suitability remains a screening hypothesis because the thresholds were not validated against local species occurrence or tidal inundation measurements.

title: UNDERGROUND COAL GASIFICATION: FROM CONCEPT TO COMMERCIAL APPLICATION
summary: Ensuring a reliable and sustainable energy supply represents one of the most critical environmental, economic and societal challenges of the 21st century. Despite the accelerated transition to renewable energy sources, fossil fuels- especia
content: Ensuring a reliable and sustainable energy supply represents one of the most critical environmental, economic and societal challenges of the 21st century. Despite the accelerated transition to renewable energy sources, fossil fuels- especially coal are expected to remain a significant energy component in the foreseeable future. Researches indicates a continued increase in coal demand, underscoring the necessity for more efficient, economically viable, and environmentally acceptable utilization technologies. Underground coal gasification has emerged as a promising in situ technology that enables the exploitation of deep, thin, or otherwise uneconomic coal seams that are not accessible through conventional mining technologies. A lot of researches point to the potential advantages of UCG over traditional coal mining technologies, including higher recovery rates, reduced land degradation, improved economic performance, and potentially lower greenhouse gas emissions, especially when it is integrated with carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of UCG development globally, where we can critically analyze the technological maturity, its economic viability and environmental implications

title: Influence of Viscous Damping on Harmonic-Oscillator Dynamics: Analytical Solutions, Numerical Verification, and Parameter-Recovery Uncertainty
summary: An undamped harmonic oscillator forms an exact benchmark for studying dissipation, regime transitions and inverse parameter identification. In the present study, we offer a replicable analysis of the underdamped, critically damped, and over
content: An undamped harmonic oscillator forms an exact benchmark for studying dissipation, regime transitions and inverse parameter identification. In the present study, we offer a replicable analysis of the underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped cases of a linear mass-spring system with damping. Thanks to the analytical formulas for the displacement solutions, mechanical energy conservation, and the dimensionless damping ratio, as well as the use of the adaptive Runge-Kutta integrator, it becomes feasible to conduct a deterministic synthetic data-based estimation experiment that helps us to estimate the quality of the identification of the damping ratio based on the measured displacement time series. For the oscillator with mass 1 kg, stiffness of 100 N m⁻¹, and the initial displacement of 0.05 m, the natural frequency is equal to 10 rad/s, and the critical damping coefficient equals 20 N s/m. The analytical solution agrees with the numerical one up to the precision of the numerical method used, while the estimation experiment makes it possible to distinguish between the accuracy of modeling and errors in measurement. The study is offered as a computational benchmark without any claims on the new physics.

title: Two Baselines, Two Answers: Screening Kenya's Phase 2 Green Hydrogen Options Under Competing Counterfactual Assumptions
summary: Kenya's Green Hydrogen Strategy and Roadmap identified fertiliser as the Phase 1 no-regret application, now settled by a 165 MW geothermal-powered ammonia facility under construction at Olkaria. Phase 2 names industrial feedstocks, transpor
content: Kenya's Green Hydrogen Strategy and Roadmap identified fertiliser as the Phase 1 no-regret application, now settled by a 165 MW geothermal-powered ammonia facility under construction at Olkaria. Phase 2 names industrial feedstocks, transport fuels and export as successors. Any attempt to rank them meets an obstacle that is rarely made explicit. The cost of avoiding a tonne of carbon dioxide depends on what hydrogen is being compared against, and studies seldom state which comparison they used. This paper screens eleven candidate end-uses twice, once against the fossil practice a site follows today and once against the cheapest lower-carbon alternative it could actually procure, and declines to privilege either ordering. Further gates address thermodynamic substitutability, demand density, project finance risk and additionality. Inputs are classified by data provenance and propagated through 20,000 Monte Carlo draws. Baseline selection matters more than any technical or cost parameter in the model, reordering eight of the eleven applications. Declining to adjudicate does not prevent conclusions. Hydrogen direct reduced iron ranks first under both treatments, at a median of 93 USD per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent, because Kenya lacks domestic gas and no cheaper route exists. Cement kiln substitution fails under both. Transport proves non-additive rather than expensive. On Kenya's low-carbon grid, a battery-electric vehicle abates almost as much as a hydrogen one, so the choice turns on cost. Road freight and mining haulage lose to batteries, while rail is cheaper than electrifying the corridor. An additionality threshold screens out four applications, including the highest scorer on project finance risk, because the market already funds them. For policymakers, two implications follow. Phase 2 support should narrow to applications surviving both comparisons, and any appraisal of a hydrogen project should state its comparison baseline explicitly, because that single unstated choice reorders most of the options.

title: The current macroeconomic situation in Ireland
source: Central European Review of Economics & Finance
summary: Ireland holds the Presidency of the Council of the European Union for the current six months. It is worth taking this opportunity to take a closer look at the state of its economy. The economic outlook for Ireland is optimistic. Assuming th
content: Ireland holds the Presidency of the Council of the European Union for the current six months. It is worth taking this opportunity to take a closer look at the state of its economy. The economic outlook for Ireland is optimistic. Assuming the end of the conflict in the Middle East, which is a bigger problem for the pro-export structure of Irish companies than the war in Ukraine, we can expect new FDI in sectors other than those exploited so far, e.g. AI computing centers, renewable energy (wind farms) or even the agri-food processing sector. Traditionally, Ireland will count on investors from the USA, as well as partial (e.g. in agriculture) financing from EU funds. The economic elites are counting on the success of Trump's policy of strengthening the role of the United States. The Irish government is aware of the importance of the presence of both American and other foreign companies for employment and budgetary policy, and will strive to promote Ireland as Europe's industrial hub in modern technologies of the 21st century. The rapid development of the US economy will generate demand for Irish products, especially in modern technologies (including space technologies – the development of the space conquest program by E. Musk in the next 20 years), and a possible drop in energy prices may reduce the operating costs of industry and transport in the near future. At that time, the political position of the Republic of Ireland in the perspective of 2030. will increase significantly, and the prospect of reunification with the poorer north of the island will be more realistic. After reunification, and assuming the current high immigration dynamics, with a demographic substitutability level of 1.15, there would be more than 8 million people living in a united Ireland – a return to the 1841 value of 8.2 million people. Before we get into the main content, it is important to note a particularly positive feature of the political and economic system of Ireland, where there are no extreme political forces such as the extreme right or the extreme left. The Communist Party does not exist here, and the communist Sinn Fein is more of a nationalist party than a communist one, and being always in opposition to the 2 big centrist parties, Fianna Fail and Fine Gael, it does not pose a serious threat to economic development based on American capital and EU funds.

title: Integration of Blockchain Technology Into Smart Grids Through Adaptive Two‐Mode Energy Management With Teletraffic‐Based Admission Control
summary: ABSTRACT The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources has significantly increased the complexity of real‐time energy management in Smart Grid systems, particularly under emergency operating conditions characterised by transmis
content: ABSTRACT The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources has significantly increased the complexity of real‐time energy management in Smart Grid systems, particularly under emergency operating conditions characterised by transmission congestion and temporary power shortages. Smart Grid energy management increasingly requires adaptive mechanisms to handle variable energy demand, limited available resources and network congestion particularly under emergency operating conditions. This paper proposes a dynamic two‐mode energy management architecture that adaptively switches between normal and emergency operating modes by integrating graph‐based generator selection, blockchain‐enabled transaction validation and teletraffic‐based admission control. Under normal operating conditions, energy requests are processed using graph‐based generator selection and blockchain validation. When the system enters an emergency state, an M/M/8 priority queue is activated to regulate the incoming request flow by prioritising critical consumers before graph‐based generator selection is performed. The proposed framework is evaluated on the IEEE 58‐bus power system using comparative simulations against conventional blockchain‐based and graph‐based approaches. The results demonstrate that integrating teletraffic admission control reduces execution time by up to 24.3%, decreases transaction latency by up to 26.5%, increases throughput by up to 48.9% and lowers blockchain gas consumption by approximately 16% while maintaining priority service for critical consumers during congestion.

title: Peak water: Trends in decoupling regional and global water use
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Water use for human activities, including food and fiber production, energy generation, and residential, commercial, and industrial supply, has grown significantly over the past century, driven by rising populations, expanding economic acti
content: Water use for human activities, including food and fiber production, energy generation, and residential, commercial, and industrial supply, has grown significantly over the past century, driven by rising populations, expanding economic activity, and changes in technologies and consumer demands. Traditional water planning has long assumed that the demand for water, like other resource demands, will grow in perpetuity, shaping infrastructure development, land-use decisions, and water-system investments. However, recent data and analysis challenge this assumption, suggesting that total water use in certain regions and sectors has peaked or even begun to decline, despite continued population and economic growth. This paper's primary contribution is to reevaluate the status of "peak water" and decoupling based on observational and statistical data, as well as multimodel simulations. Data on global, national, and regional water withdrawals indicate that certain peak water-use levels are being reached and the paper discusses past, current, and projected demand estimates; potential drivers of observed water use reductions; and different strategies for managing and modeling water use in the future. These findings indicate that the long-presumed correlation between water-resource use, economic development, and human well-being can be decoupled and that models of water use should reflect this. Decoupling solutions must focus on efficiency technologies, regulatory water-use caps, environmental flow protections, and enhanced monitoring networks.

title: Impacts of Framed Naming on Cross‐Country Acceptance of Cell‐Cultured Meat Alternatives
source: Australian Journal of Agricultural and Resource Economics
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how framed naming influences consumer preferences for cell‐cultured meat alternatives in the United States, China and South Korea, using ground (minced) beef as a case study. Drawing on categorisation and framin
content: ABSTRACT This study examines how framed naming influences consumer preferences for cell‐cultured meat alternatives in the United States, China and South Korea, using ground (minced) beef as a case study. Drawing on categorisation and framing theories, we propose that naming provides category cues and framing provides contextual cues, jointly shaping acceptance through perceived category fit. Using choice experiments and scaled random mixed logit models, we estimate willingness‐to‐pay under two framed naming treatments: one distancing cell‐cultured meat alternatives from the beef category (‘lab‐grown product derived from beef cells’) and the other affirming membership in the beef category (‘cell‐cultured ground beef’). The category‐affirming treatment increases mean willingness‐to‐pay by $10.20 per pound in China and $4.20 per pound in the United States but produces no significant increase in South Korea. Market share simulations further show the largest increase for cell‐cultured meat alternatives in China, limited effects in South Korea and a demand shift in the United States primarily from plant‐based alternatives rather than conventional beef. These patterns suggest that country‐specific understandings of beef may condition the extent to which naming and framing cues shape perceived category fit and consumer acceptance, potentially reflecting differences in production traditions and regulatory contexts.

title: Research on risk hedging efficiency of the ‘Insurance + Futures’ model in China and the United States from the perspective of institutional differences
summary: Against global food‑security pressure and agricultural‑market restructuring, the “Insurance + Futures” scheme has become a vital tool for agricultural risk mitigation. Institutional differences, between China’s government‑led pilot model an
content: Against global food‑security pressure and agricultural‑market restructuring, the “Insurance + Futures” scheme has become a vital tool for agricultural risk mitigation. Institutional differences, between China’s government‑led pilot model and the market‑oriented long‑statute system in the United States, lead to distinct hedging‑efficiency outcomes. Based on institutional‑evolution theory, this paper adopts Super‑SBM‑DEA, two‑way fixed‑effects regression and Monte‑Carlo VaR measurement, and conducts an empirical study using bilateral panel data from 2020 to 2024. The results show that the US model achieves more stable and higher hedging efficiency. Four institutional factors including subsidy continuity, market completeness, farm‑operation scale and risk‑guarantee breadth significantly improve hedging performance. Market‑oriented rules strengthen efficiency gains in the US, while China’s administrative‑dominated pilots produce institutional friction and efficiency losses. Targeted policy suggestions are proposed to promote China’s “Insurance + Futures” transformation from scattered pilots to standardized long‑term operation.

title: Total BIM: Characterization, implementation, and value in construction project delivery
summary: This thesis aims to understand Total BIM and explore what it entails for construction project delivery. In hybrid BIM, models and drawings are produced and maintained in parallel, while construction typically relies on drawings. In contrast
content: This thesis aims to understand Total BIM and explore what it entails for construction project delivery. In hybrid BIM, models and drawings are produced and maintained in parallel, while construction typically relies on drawings. In contrast, Total BIM is an emerging approach in which production-oriented BIM takes precedence over drawings as the contractually binding source of design and construction information, with construction carried out directly from BIM. The thesis examines what characterizes Total BIM, how it has been implemented, and whether it changes how value is delivered.Given the small number of completed Total BIM projects and limited empirical research on model-based construction, the thesis takes an exploratory, predominantly qualitative approach. The appended papers draw on four realized building projects in Sweden and Norway, combining semi-structured interviews, workshops, study visits, observation of on-site BIM use, project documentation, and cost and lifecycle assessment data. The cases are examined through a holistic BIM implementation framework, a digital disruption lens, and a virtual design and construction framework.Implementing Total BIM involved changes in procurement, design, validation, and on-site working methods. Model-derived quantities supported tendering, and designers developed coordinated models suitable for construction. Site personnel worked directly from BIM, generating task-specific views and measurements as needed, and communication and reporting were linked to the model. Implementation mainly used commercially available technology but required project-specific contractual and organizational arrangements, leadership, training, and ongoing support. Responsibilities for quantity accuracy were redistributed, while checking and coordination became more collective. Reported benefits included improvements in cost and schedule performance, logistics, quality, and communication. Model-based information was also used to support material reuse and iterative climate assessments.The thesis provides an empirically grounded account of how Total BIM is implemented and what it requires. Its wider adoption may require standard contracts and permitting processes that accommodate model-based delivery, together with the capabilities and willingness of project participants to change established ways of working.

title: From enterprise regulation to government oversight: The effects of central environmental protection inspections on local environmental governance
source: Energy Sources Part B Economics Planning and Policy
summary: Using panel data from 269 prefecture-level cities for the period 2011–2018, this study employs a staggered difference-in-differences design and deep-learning-based text analysis to examine the effects of central environmental inspections (C
content: Using panel data from 269 prefecture-level cities for the period 2011–2018, this study employs a staggered difference-in-differences design and deep-learning-based text analysis to examine the effects of central environmental inspections (CEPI). The results show that the inspections reduced industrial SO₂ emissions by approximately 15% on average, although the effect was unevenly distributed across regions. The mechanism analysis indicates that environmental administrative penalties with a one-period lag constitute the primary transmission channel. Once lagged penalties are included in the model, the direct effect of the inspections is no longer statistically significant. Although environmental attention increases significantly, its coefficient is not statistically significant when included in the mediation model, while the Sobel test indicates a significant indirect effect. This finding suggests that environmental attention is a necessary but insufficient condition for emission reductions. Environmental protection expenditures receive no empirical support as a mediating channel. The heterogeneity analysis shows that the emission-reduction effects are concentrated in central and western regions and are not statistically significant in eastern regions. Fiscal capacity and technological capabilities both strengthen the effect of environmental inspections, although the moderating effect of technological capabilities is only marginally significant. In addition, the placebo tests support the conclusion that the findings are not driven by random assignments or anticipation effects. Overall, the emission-reduction effectiveness of the CEPI depends on local governments’ ability to translate political pressure into effective enforcement and policy implementation.

title: Fentanyl dabbing with cannabis retail equipment: an ethnographic and drug-checking study
summary: Background: Fentanyl's entrenchment in U.S. West Coast drug markets brought a shift from injecting to smoking illicit opioids. We characterize the next transition: the rise of 'dabbing,' vaporizing fentanyl with equipment sold for cannabis
content: Background: Fentanyl's entrenchment in U.S. West Coast drug markets brought a shift from injecting to smoking illicit opioids. We characterize the next transition: the rise of 'dabbing,' vaporizing fentanyl with equipment sold for cannabis concentrates. Methods: This mixed-methods study combined ethnographic interviewing and participant observation among people who use fentanyl in California and Oregon (2024-2026) with survey data from a Los Angeles drug checking program. After identifying dabbing ethnographically, we added an optional smoking-method item to the survey. Results: Of 108 participants who stated a route of administration, 104 (96%) reported smoking; of 93 who named a smoking method, 81 (87%) reported dabbing. All 11 who first named another method and returned later then reported dabbing. Dabbing was reported at 250 of 405 (62%) encounters with a stated route. We observed participants adapting cannabis equipment. They praised dabbing's discretion, reduced stigma, and convenience, and its capacity for more large hits, more quickly; the same speed led some to call it wasteful, because it went through their fentanyl faster than other methods. Participants described rapidly rising tolerance and frequent dabbing-related burns, which we also observed. Some who had injected said dabbing approximated its "rush." Conclusions: Dabbing has become the dominant way to consume fentanyl among people using drug checking services in Los Angeles, and was observed in every other city where we did fieldwork. Clinicians and programs should ask people how they smoke fentanyl, not only whether they smoke or inject; dabbing may reduce some risks while increasing others.

title: Multi-substrate solid-state fluorescent sensor arrays for synergistic biogenic amine detection across extended concentration windows
summary: Biogenic amines (BA) are important hazard markers closely associated with food spoilage, and rapid, wide-range detection of multiple BA remains a challenging task for food safety monitoring. Herein, we constructed a solid-state sensor array
content: Biogenic amines (BA) are important hazard markers closely associated with food spoilage, and rapid, wide-range detection of multiple BA remains a challenging task for food safety monitoring. Herein, we constructed a solid-state sensor array for synergistic detection of wide-range BA. We then systematically investigated the sensitivity and selectivity of TD-B to various amines and further application potential manufactured multi-substrate solid fluorescence sensor arrays (e.g. film, filter-paper, and cotton thread sensor) for synergistic monitoring the broad-range BA. These observations confirmed that the paper-based sensor can discriminate BA over a concentration range of 0∼540 ppm. The cotton-based sensor and film-based sensor achieve detectable concentration ranges of 0∼1050 ppm and 0∼1950 ppm, respectively. Such multiple detection ranges can compensate for the detection delay induced by signal saturation of individual sensors. Overall, this innovative solid fluorescent sensor array offers valuable insights into the development of readable portable devices for BA detection suitable for diverse concentration scenarios.

title: Sustainable pest management in Africa: Biological control strategies, emerging technologies, and case studies across major crops
summary: Abstract Background : Integrated pest management (IPM) and biological control have become fundamental components of sustainable crop protection in Africa, where invasive and endemic insect pests continue to threaten agricultural productivit
content: Abstract Background : Integrated pest management (IPM) and biological control have become fundamental components of sustainable crop protection in Africa, where invasive and endemic insect pests continue to threaten agricultural productivity, food security, and rural livelihoods. This review synthesizes recent advances, implementation strategies, and emerging technologies associated with biological control and IPM across major African agroecosystems, with emphasis on key pests affecting staple, horticultural, and citrus crops. Methods : A comprehensive review of the scientific literature was conducted to evaluate biological control strategies, IPM practices, and emerging pest management technologies implemented across African agricultural systems. The analysis compared patterns of biological control adoption among different African regions, assessed the use of natural enemies and biopesticides, and examined case studies illustrating the integration of biological control within IPM programs. Results : Conservation biological control (CBC) was the most frequently represented strategy in the reviewed literature, followed by augmentative and classical biological control. Parasitoids were the principal natural enemies employed in augmentative and classical programs, whereas conservation approaches promoted more diverse predator–parasitoid communities. The review identified increasing adoption of microbial and botanical biopesticides, particularly for invasive pests such as fall armyworm and tomato leafminer. Emerging technologies, including semiochemical-based tools, the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT), and genetically modified crops, have demonstrated considerable potential but remain unevenly implemented because of regulatory, infrastructural, and socio-economic constraints. Case studies from citrus, tomato, and maize production systems demonstrated that combining biological control with habitat management, push–pull strategies, and selective pesticide use enhances the effectiveness of IPM programs. The review findings should be interpreted as reflecting patterns in the available literature rather than the actual distribution, adoption, or effectiveness of biological control across Africa. Conclusions : Biological control offers significant opportunities to strengthen agricultural resilience while reducing dependence on synthetic pesticides in Africa. However, wider adoption is constrained by fragmented regulatory frameworks, limited local production capacity, inconsistent biocontrol product quality, weak extension services, and low farmer awareness. Strengthening regional regulatory harmonization, expanding local biocontrol industries, improving farmer training, and incorporating ecological pest management into national agricultural policies will be critical to scaling effective and sustainable IPM across the continent.

title: Double-layer-resolved full-field multiscale simulation unraveling impacts of bubbles on water electrolysis
summary: A double-layer-resolved full-field simulation quantifies the impacts of bubbles on water electrolysis from nanometer to centimeter scales.
content: A double-layer-resolved full-field simulation quantifies the impacts of bubbles on water electrolysis from nanometer to centimeter scales.

title: Beyond active sites: reaction field engineering for heterogeneous CO 2 hydrogenation toward formic acid and formate
summary: Reaction field engineering provides an integrative framework for coordinating active sites, local environments, spatial organization, catalytic functions, and reactor operation in CO 2 hydrogenation toward formic acid and formate.
content: Reaction field engineering provides an integrative framework for coordinating active sites, local environments, spatial organization, catalytic functions, and reactor operation in CO 2 hydrogenation toward formic acid and formate.

title: Understanding of Size and Scale and Order‐Of‐Magnitude Reasoning in Secondary Science: A Teaching Experiment With Worked Examples as Educational Scaffold
source: Journal of Research in Science Teaching
summary: ABSTRACT Understanding of size and scale (USS) and order‐of‐magnitude reasoning (OMR) are considered essential elements of scientific practice and literacy. This study combines intersecting strands of research to develop a rationale and con
content: ABSTRACT Understanding of size and scale (USS) and order‐of‐magnitude reasoning (OMR) are considered essential elements of scientific practice and literacy. This study combines intersecting strands of research to develop a rationale and conceptualization for OMR as an extension of USS from a broad body of research in science and math education. It also considers cognitive prerequisites essential for the development and mastery of USS and OMR. Based on this, the study presents an educational approach to enhance USS and OMR in high school science. Developing these abilities faces major barriers, involving complex procedural skills and strategies for coordinating multiple reasoning steps. Transfer of learning has also been found unsatisfactory in many studies. While there is work on individual activities that can improve this state of affairs, research on systematic approaches in full teaching sequences is scarce for USS and, to our knowledge, nonexistent for OMR. An educational approach for the acquisition of complex knowledge and development of strategies well investigated in the literature is worked examples (WEs). This strand of research found strong evidence for the usefulness of WEs in STEM education, in particular for supporting transfer. The quasi‐experimental repeated‐measurement investigation reported here compares a WE intervention group with a control group using conventional tasks (same content, lesson plan, and teacher). Conducted within regular high‐school science classrooms, the results reveal significant and practically relevant effects on students' procedural and conceptual knowledge regarding USS and OMR, including near and far transfer of learning.

title: Spontaneous spin-selective structural phase transition in chiral crystals
summary: In this Letter, we predict a structural phase transition unique to chiral crystals with screw symmetry. In chiral crystals, the phonon frequency renormalized by the electron-phonon coupling depends on the handedness of circular polarization
content: In this Letter, we predict a structural phase transition unique to chiral crystals with screw symmetry. In chiral crystals, the phonon frequency renormalized by the electron-phonon coupling depends on the handedness of circular polarization. Consequently, the soft mode encoding phonon angular momentum induces spin-selective Peierls gaps in the electronic band, entailing a helical spin density wave and chiral lattice distortion. We also elucidate the chiral signatures and functional implications of collective modes. Our findings offer crucial insights into the emergence of chirality and highlight novel functional aspects of chiral materials and their design strategy.

title: Towards Non-van der Waals 2D Topological Insulators
summary: Abstract Non-van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) materials derived from strongly bonded non-layered crystals have recently emerged as a novel and rising platform for nanoscale research. While uncovering and tuning their (opto-)electronic, ca
content: Abstract Non-van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) materials derived from strongly bonded non-layered crystals have recently emerged as a novel and rising platform for nanoscale research. While uncovering and tuning their (opto-)electronic, catalytic, and magnetic properties has been the focus of intense research, the impact of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) onto their electronic structure has not yet been explored in detail. Studying these effects is, however, particularly relevant due to their surface cation termination and the presence of heavy elements in several representative compounds. Here, we investigate the effect of SOC onto the electronic structure of 2D AgBiO3, NaBiO3, and SbTlO3. While the first two systems show negligible band renormalization upon inclusion of relativistic effects around the band gap, SbTlO3 showcases a large SOC induced splitting (229 meV) for the lowest conduction bands associated with a band inversion. Substitution of Tl with Pb forming SbPbO3 brings the band-inverted feature to the Fermi level. Analysis of topological invariants and investigation of edge states of zig-zag and armchair ribbons within the 200 meV gap confirms the topological nature of the band splitting. Our work thus establishes a foundation for the systematic study of robust non-van der Waals 2D topological insulators.

title: Periplocymarin Suppresses Nonsmall Cell Lung Cancer Progression by Modulating MAPK14 Phosphorylation: An Integrated Multiomics and Preclinical Study
summary: Abstract Nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading malignancy with limited therapies, calling for natural product-derived anticancer candidates with well-defined mechanisms. In this study, Periplocymarin was identified as a select
content: Abstract Nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading malignancy with limited therapies, calling for natural product-derived anticancer candidates with well-defined mechanisms.
