The observed treatment performance likely reflects the combined contributions of physical flotation and ozone-mediated oxidation. Biphasic kinetics were observed, with higher initial rate constants at increased ozone input. Conventional heavy crude oil (CHCO) exhibited faster apparent degradation than very low sulfur fuel oil (VLSFO), likely reflecting differences in their overall composition and physicochemical properties. Post-treatment analyses revealed residual total petroleum hydrocarbon (TPH) concentrations ranging from below 0.1 to 3.5 mg/L, with most of the 16 target parent polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) below the approximate reporting limit of 8 ng/L. The observed pH decline may reflect the formation of acidic oxidation products and nitrogen-containing by-products from air-fed ozone generation. These results demonstrate that ozone nanobubbles enable efficient oil removal and substantial petroleum hydrocarbon attenuation in oil-in-water emulsions under controlled marine conditions.

title: Hijacking Prenyltransferases and Terpene Synthases for the Enzymatic Synthesis of Non‐natural C 19 , C 24 , and C 29 Terpenoids
summary: ABSTRACT The terpenoid substrate analog 14‐ nor ‐farnesyl pyrophosphate (14‐ nor ‐FPP), lacking the methyl group Me14, was synthesized and enzymatically elongated to 18‐ nor ‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (18‐ nor ‐GGPP) and 22‐ nor ‐geranyl
content: ABSTRACT The terpenoid substrate analog 14‐ nor ‐farnesyl pyrophosphate (14‐ nor ‐FPP), lacking the methyl group Me14, was synthesized and enzymatically elongated to 18‐ nor ‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (18‐ nor ‐GGPP) and 22‐ nor ‐geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (22‐ nor ‐GFPP) by GGPP synthase (GGPPS) and GFPP synthase (GFPPS), respectively. Downstream conversion with 20 diterpene synthases (DTSs) and 10 sesterterpene synthases (StTSs) yielded in total 24 new compounds. Surprisingly, in two cases the substrate analogs were converted by GGPPS and a DTS into nor ‐sesterterpenes (C 24 ), while one combination of GFPPS and a StTS yielded a nor ‐triterpene (C 29 ), demonstrating that the lack of just one carbon allows for extension with one more terpene unit than expected, in contrast to the strict product selectivity observed for GGPPS and GFPPS with normal FPP. For certain enzyme‐substrate pairings, the altered reactivity caused by the absence of Me14 unveiled reaction pathways toward di‐ and sesterterpenes with unique frameworks, for which the mechanisms were investigated through DFT calculations. Absolute configurations of the obtained compounds were determined through chemical correlation with stereoselectively deuterated precursors or through a comparison of optical rotations to those of structurally related natural products containing Me18/Me22.

title: Between Ephemerality and Permanence
summary: The textile material, known and used for thousands of years, was and is ephemeral by its very physical materiality: that of the natural raw material from which it is made.The perishability of natural raw materials (whether of plant or anima
content: The textile material, known and used for thousands of years, was and is ephemeral by its very physical materiality: that of the natural raw material from which it is made.The perishability of natural raw materials (whether of plant or animal origin), which degrades relatively quickly, having a limited life cycle, has also led to the disappearance of objects made with them.The 20th century, among its many inventions and innovations, also brought us synthetic textile materials which, through their chemically formulated life, seem to enjoy perpetuity, which is not sustainable and does not correspond to a natural life cycle and therefore, in a way, neither to our transient nature.In recent decades, research has revealed the possibility of having new natural sources of raw materials and possibilities for recycling synthetic materials.The article does not deal with textiles per se, but rather their presence as a variable architectural form.The theoretical investigation dedicated to the connection between architecture and textiles, which has developed especially in the last twenty years after Marc Garcia coined the term Architextiles, together with the technical possibilities and research in the field, have given impetus both to the positioning of textiles on another level of importance and to the multiplication of the use of textiles also at the exterior of the architectural object.Once the field of investigation was opened, it was proven that textiles are very present in architecture, both under the classic uses inside and outside (with new, high-performance materials, with special characteristics) and as a means of communication.For the case analyses, the tent was chosen as the subject of study, as an architectural object which, beyond its materiality, subject to the passage of time, became permanent through the development of its typology as a cultural archetype.

title: Substrate-and defect-induced reactivity of graphene: a theoretical review
summary: Graphene is often regarded as chemically inert, yet its reactivity can be substantially modified through structural defects and interactions with underlying substrates. Here, we review, from a predominantly theoretical perspective, how subs
content: Graphene is often regarded as chemically inert, yet its reactivity can be substantially modified through structural defects and interactions with underlying substrates. Here, we review, from a predominantly theoretical perspective, how substrate-induced charge redistribution, interfacial hybridization, and local structural deformation influence molecular adsorption, dissociation, and covalent functionalization of graphene. Particular attention is given to the interplay between substrate interactions and defects, which can either promote molecular activation or passivate reactive sites. Static first-principles calculations are complemented by ab initio and reactive molecular dynamics studies addressing finite-temperature effects, bond rearrangements, and interfacial stability. We also discuss graphene-based single-atom catalysts (SACs), emphasizing the role of metal coordination, defective carbon environments, and electronic interactions in determining the stability of isolated metal centers and the adsorption of reaction intermediates. Across metallic, oxide, and semiconductor supports, the reviewed studies reveal reaction-dependent modifications of graphene reactivity, including reduced activation barriers for O 2 , H 2 , and H 2 O dissociation, changes in organic functionalization pathways, and stabilization of CO-derived intermediates. Importantly, enhanced chemical activation or irreversible functionalization does not necessarily establish catalytic activity, which requires consideration of complete reaction cycles. By comparing representative systems and theoretical approaches, this review identifies key mechanistic contributions and qualitative principles for substrate and interface design, while highlighting the need for dynamical simulations and experimental validation under realistic operating conditions.

title: Mapping the Barriers to Circular Economy Implementation in Healthcare Waste Produced by Hospitals in Central Java Province
summary: Abstract Healthcare waste (HCW) poses significant environmental and public health risks and is growing by 2-3% annually as populations and healthcare facilities expand. HCW spans hazardous and non-hazardous streams, with sharps and chemical
content: Abstract Healthcare waste (HCW) poses significant environmental and public health risks and is growing by 2-3% annually as populations and healthcare facilities expand. HCW spans hazardous and non-hazardous streams, with sharps and chemicals requiring special handling and incurring high disposal costs. Circular Economy (CE) strategies – reduce, reuse, recycle – could mitigate these impacts, yet remain limited in healthcare, particularly in hospitals. Based on this condition, the purpose of this study examine barriers to CE adoption in hospital waste management in Central Java, Indonesia, and offers targeted recommendations. Twenty-two potential barriers were evaluated by six experts from healthcare institutions, government agencies, and professional associations using a four-point scale; Content Validity Index screening retained 16 valid items. Barrier interrelationships were then analyzed via DEMATEL to map causal links and ISM to prioritize within a hierarchical structure. The integrated DEMATEL-ISM model produced a six-level hierarchy, identifying two root causes – the absence of government legislation and high implementation costs – that drive downstream challenges, including limited incentives and organizational resistance. Mid-level barriers involve insufficient funding and systemic coordination issues, while upper levels reflect knowledge gaps and operational inefficiencies. Addressing policy and financial constraints is essential to unlock systemwide improvements. Findings underscore the need for regulatory development, financial incentives, and public education, guiding policymakers and hospital administrators toward environmentally sustainable and economically efficient HCW management.

title: From Climate Diplomacy to Climate Finance: Assessing Bangladesh’s Diplomatic Effectiveness and International Financing Outcomes, 2015-2025
summary: Abstract This paper studies whether Bangladesh’s climate diplomacy translated into discernible international climate-financing outcomes between 2015 and 2025. It develops a documentary traceability framework distinguishing diplomatic activi
content: Abstract This paper studies whether Bangladesh’s climate diplomacy translated into discernible international climate-financing outcomes between 2015 and 2025. It develops a documentary traceability framework distinguishing diplomatic activity, agenda articulation, collective negotiating outcomes, institutional financing outcomes and Bangladesh-specific financial outcomes supported by process tracing. The analysis covers Bangladesh’s 2020–2022 Climate Vulnerable Forum (CVF)/Vulnerable Twenty (V20) leadership and the Dhaka-Glasgow Declaration, the COP27 Loss and Damage Fund decision, and the COP29 New Collective Quantified Goal. Evidence most strongly supports Bangladesh-linked coalition leadership and agenda articulation during its CVF/V20 presidency. COP27 and COP29 produced consequential shared outcomes, but Bangladesh’s individual causal contribution is not isolated. Financial records identify selected approvals: USD 26.83 million in grants across seven selected GEF-related projects and USD 14.995 million across two identified Adaptation Fund projects. Bangladesh’s interim BTR1 reports USD 9,908.6 million in climate finance received during 2015–2024. Yet a cross-check of eight financing rows across seven standalone GCF projects finds USD 418.300 million in BTR1 amounts matching approximately USD 418.301 million in approved financing, while provider-recorded dated disbursements through 2024 total USD 70.208 million. Nine AIMS profiles were screened but cannot support national aggregation. The analysis shows that agenda-setting is evidenced more clearly than Bangladesh-specific financial causation.

title: Radical Sorting Enables Semiconductor-Driven Redox-Neutral C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Cross-Coupling
summary: Selective formation of C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds from carbon-centered radicals is inherently challenging, because competing radical homocoupling can compromise product selectivity. Here, we combine heterogeneous semiconductor photocatalysis with
content: Selective formation of C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds from carbon-centered radicals is inherently challenging, because competing radical homocoupling can compromise product selectivity. Here, we combine heterogeneous semiconductor photocatalysis with nickel-mediated radical sorting to achieve redox-neutral C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Under irradiation, graphitic carbon nitride (gCN) generates alkyl radicals from carboxylic acids and redox-active esters (RAEs) through complementary oxidative and reductive single-electron transfer, respectively, without the need for stoichiometric oxidants or reductants. A nickel catalyst channels these intermediates towards cross-coupling, providing access to a range of products bearing primary and secondary alkyl fragments, including saturated heterocycles, unnatural amino acids, and late-stage functionalization products. Kinetic modelling, radical-clock experiments, electrochemical measurements, and DFT calculations provide insight into the origin of radical sorting. The results are consistent with sequential radical capture at nickel and identify the suppression of homocoupling between RAE-derived radicals as a key kinetic feature.

title: Ligand-constrained assembly of a quartz-topology metal–organic framework for the uptake of emerging contaminants and trace-level water monitoring
summary: A pyrazolone-based ligand constrains the Zn( ii ) coordination geometry, directing the assembly of a microporous quartz-topology metal–organic framework (MUDEC-4(Zn)) applied to the selective removal of emerging contaminants from water.
content: A pyrazolone-based ligand constrains the Zn( ii ) coordination geometry, directing the assembly of a microporous quartz-topology metal–organic framework (MUDEC-4(Zn)) applied to the selective removal of emerging contaminants from water.

title: Deuteration as a General Strategy to Enhance Small Molecule-Based Photodynamic Therapy
summary: Utilizing isotope effects has a long history in organic chemistry, and has recently been shown to improve fluorophore photophysics and azobenzene-based photoswitch kinetics. Herein, we report the deuteration of methylene blue (MB) and sulfo
content: Utilizing isotope effects has a long history in organic chemistry, and has recently been shown to improve fluorophore photophysics and azobenzene-based photoswitch kinetics. Herein, we report the deuteration of methylene blue (MB) and sulfonated tetraphenyl porphyrin (TPPS), both far-red singlet oxygen sensitizers (SOSs), which boosts the efficiency of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation by >55%. We applied this knowledge to photodynamic therapeutic (PDT) settings by derivatizing deuterated methylene blue as 1) a ligand for the HaloTag protein (HTP) that leads to faster activation kinetics of the ROS-sensitive TRAAK channel, 2) as a fusion to a peptidic agonist of the glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor (GLP1R) to optically induce ablation of GLP1R-expressing cells, and 3) as a lysosome targeting sensitizer to induce spatiotemporally controlled lysosomal damage through lipid oxidation. Taken together, our strategy provides a simple way to improve well-studied singlet oxygen sensitizers through deuteration and leverages the best performing sensitizer across a set of different biological methodologies to study ion channel gating, as well as organelle and cell ablation.

title: Pulmonary Fibrosis Comorbidity Spectrum: Association Mechanisms and a New Perspective in the Context of Occupational Exposure
summary: ABSTRACT Pulmonary fibrosis (PF), particularly idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), frequently coexists with pulmonary and extrapulmonary conditions, including cardiovascular disease, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), pulmonary hypert
content: ABSTRACT Pulmonary fibrosis (PF), particularly idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), frequently coexists with pulmonary and extrapulmonary conditions, including cardiovascular disease, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), pulmonary hypertension (PH), metabolic disorders, lung cancer, and obstructive or emphysematous lung disease. These comorbidities can substantially affect disease course, prognosis, and therapeutic decision‐making. Growing evidence suggests that their coexistence with PF is not simply coincidental, but may reflect overlapping pathological processes involving chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, oxidative and mitochondrial stress, endothelial dysfunction, cellular senescence, metabolic reprogramming, and maladaptive tissue repair. Occupational inhalational exposures may influence PF development and associated comorbidity phenotypes through recurrent alveolar epithelial injury, oxidative stress, and persistent inflammatory responses. These effects may be modified by smoking, aging, genetic susceptibility, metabolic status, and other host characteristics. This review examines the links among external exposures, shared pathological processes, and major pulmonary and extrapulmonary comorbidities of PF, with emphasis on epidemiological evidence, bidirectional relationships, and disease‐specific mechanisms. Particular attention is given to occupational inhalational exposures and their potential contribution to comorbidity heterogeneity, as well as to the clinical value of integrating structured exposure history with comorbidity assessment and disease phenotyping.

title: Grain boundary effects on surface modifications of tungsten under fusion-relevant helium plasma irradiation: Coarse-grained vs. Nano-grained microstructures
summary: Abstract Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tu
content: Abstract Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ~600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.

title: Mitochondria-centered organelle communication network remodeling in osteoarthritis: linking subcellular homeostasis to whole-joint degeneration
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a whole-joint degenerative disease driven by interacting mechanical, metabolic, inflammatory, and age-related stresses. Although mitochondrial dysfunction has long been implicated in OA pathogenesis, mitochondria do n
content: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a whole-joint degenerative disease driven by interacting mechanical, metabolic, inflammatory, and age-related stresses. Although mitochondrial dysfunction has long been implicated in OA pathogenesis, mitochondria do not function as isolated bioenergetic organelles. They communicate dynamically with the endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes, peroxisomes, lipid droplets, and the nucleus through membrane contact sites, metabolic coupling, and bidirectional signaling. These interactions coordinate calcium handling, lipid trafficking, redox balance, mitochondrial quality control, and transcriptional adaptation. Disruption of this interorganelle coordination may therefore provide a unifying basis for the convergence of diverse pathogenic stresses on persistent chondrocyte dysfunction and joint degeneration. Here, we integrate mitochondria-centered communication pathways into a network-level framework linking calcium, lipid, redox, and quality-control homeostasis to chondrocyte dysfunction and whole-joint degeneration. We further propose a conceptual progression from adaptive remodeling through compensatory burden to network decompensation, emphasizing the context-dependent consequences of organelle dysfunction. Importantly, we distinguish mechanisms supported by OA-specific experimental evidence from indirect observations and hypotheses extrapolated from non-OA systems. This evidence-informed perspective identifies unresolved questions and highlights potential opportunities for cell type- and disease stage-dependent therapeutic intervention.

title: The Microbiome in Cancer: Composition, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Implications
summary: Cancer complexity arises not only from host genetics but also from interactions between the host and microbial communities. However, the field remains fragmented, and a systems-level framework is needed to guide precision diagnostics and th
content: Cancer complexity arises not only from host genetics but also from interactions between the host and microbial communities. However, the field remains fragmented, and a systems-level framework is needed to guide precision diagnostics and therapy. We develop the "oncobiome" as an integrative framework linking commensal, pathobiont, and tumor-associated microbial activities to cancer development, progression, and treatment response. We describe how diet, antibiotics, therapy, and environmental factors may shape the shift from microbiome homeostasis to a malignancy-associated oncobiome. An organ-specific overview of the oncobiome illustrates how microbial communities interact with systemic microbial, immune, and metabolic networks. Mechanistically, we examine how microbial signals may influence the hallmarks of cancer, including genomic instability, altered tumor metabolism, and immune evasion, as well as epithelial barrier disruption, metastatic progression, and therapeutic resistance. Finally, we assess candidate microbial biomarkers for cancer detection, prognosis, and treatment-response monitoring, alongside fecal microbiota transplantation, rationally designed microbial consortia, and selected probiotics. We distinguish preliminary anticancer findings from microbiota-restoration and supportive-care applications and highlight the need for prospective validation and contamination control. By integrating temporal microbial variation, anatomical niches, and cancer-relevant functions, this review identifies priorities for development and clinical evaluation of microbiome-based diagnostics and interventions.

title: Vinylcyclopropanes in Rearrangement Reactions
summary: Abstract Vinylcyclopropanes constitute highly versatile, strained building blocks whose unique reactivity has enabled the development of a broad variety of synthetically valuable rearrangement and cycloisomerization processes. Over more tha
content: Abstract Vinylcyclopropanes constitute highly versatile, strained building blocks whose unique reactivity has enabled the development of a broad variety of synthetically valuable rearrangement and cycloisomerization processes. Over more than six decades of development, vinylcyclopropane chemistry has undergone remarkable evolution, particularly in recent years. Accordingly, these transformations have emerged as powerful tools for the generation of molecular complexity through strain-release-driven reaction manifolds involving both homolytic and heterolytic bond-cleavage mechanistic pathways. This Review provides a comprehensive account of the current state of the art in vinylcyclopropane rearrangement chemistry, with particular emphasis on the mechanistic principles governing these transformations and on their synthetic applications in modern organic synthesis. The different rearrangement modes accessible to vinylcyclopropane derivatives are discussed, including stereomutation processes, vinylcyclopropane-cyclopentene rearrangements, divinylcyclopropane-cycloheptadiene rearrangements, vinylcyclopropane-to-skipped-1,4-diene rearrangements, and cycloisomerization reactions involving specifically functionalized vinylcyclopropane substrates. Particular attention is devoted to the influence of substrate structure, stereochemical features, catalyst design, and thermodynamic and kinetic factors on reaction outcome, in terms of efficiency and selectivity. The broad applicability of these transformations in the synthesis of structurally sophisticated carbo- and heterocyclic architectures, including natural-product-related targets, is highlighted together with current limitations and future opportunities for the continued development of vinylcyclopropane chemistry.

title: Glutamine metabolic reprogramming remodels the immunosuppressive microenvironment and modulates immunotherapy response in renal cell carcinoma (Review)
summary: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming, with glutamine addiction emerging as a central hallmark that extends beyond supporting tumor proliferation. This review synthesizes current knowle
content: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming, with glutamine addiction emerging as a central hallmark that extends beyond supporting tumor proliferation. This review synthesizes current knowledge on how glutamine metabolic reprogramming remodels the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and modulates immunotherapy response in renal cell carcinoma. The molecular basis of glutamine addiction is discussed, focusing on the von Hippel‑Lindau/hypoxia‑inducible factor axis, MYC activation and epigenetic regulation. The mechanisms by which glutamine metabolism orchestrates immune evasion are examined, including tumor immune cell competition, impaired effector T‑cell function, expansion of immunosuppressive populations such as regulatory T cells and M2 polarized macrophages, and upregulation of immune checkpoints. Therapeutic strategies targeting glutamine metabolism, from transporter and glutaminase inhibition to dietary restriction, are summarized along with mixed clinical trial outcomes that underscore the need for patient selection. Candidate predictive biomarkers across genetic, metabolic, immune and imaging domains are also reviewed. This review aims to provide an integrated framework for understanding glutamine‑driven immune modulation and to guide future therapeutic development in ccRCC.

title: Extending Axiomatic Design: A Dual-Domain Mapping Framework for Complete Physical Architecture — Co-Generating Functional and Decoupling Components
summary: Abstract This paper extends Axiomatic Design (AD) to address a fundamental design problem in physical architecture synthesis: functional-centric mapping fails to characterize physical field coupling, and decoupling components lack represent
content: Abstract This paper extends Axiomatic Design (AD) to address a fundamental design problem in physical architecture synthesis: functional-centric mapping fails to characterize physical field coupling, and decoupling components lack representation within the existing framework. The core scientific question is: Does functional independence imply physical independence? If not, what representational extensions are required for function-centric design theory to characterize physical field coupling and enabling the systematic recommendation of decoupling components? Existing theories—AD, FBS, TRIZ, and DSM—assume that a valid physical architecture can be obtained whenever functional decomposition is correct and compatibility constraints are satisfied. However, this assumption is incomplete: functionally independent components can still become coupled through shared physical fields, resulting in degraded product performance and quality. Furthermore, decoupling components —elements that implement no functional requirements but serve to suppress physical field coupling—cannot be represented. Consequently, existing theories can only generate functional components and cannot guide the creation of decoupling components, rendering the resulting physical architecture incomplete. Upon integration, problems such as vibration, noise, electromagnetic interference, and thermal failure frequently necessitate iterative redesign and can even precipitate safety incidents. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a dual-domain extension of Axiomatic Design that places physical field interactions and functional logic on equal theoretical footing. The framework integrates residual coupling networks, latent coupling inference, coupling elasticity matrices, positive feedback loop detection, and P0–P3 priority ranking with Constraint Satisfaction Problem (CSP) filtering, Graph Neural Network (GNN) surrogate models, and Pareto optimization. In a high-speed train case study, 2,187 candidate combinations are filtered down to 468 feasible architectures. Scheme 261 (Ω = 1) theoretically achieves suppression rates of 93.2% (implicit) and 74.1% (boundary) . Type I validation and Type II confirmation—including external consistency with published measurement data, retrospective analysis of industrial cases, and sensitivity analysis—substantiate the theoretical merit and plausibility of the proposed extension.

title: Study of the Mechanical Properties of Polymers and Their Comparison Using Epoxy and Polyester Mixtures: Effect of Mixture of Resin and Polyester
source: Pakistan Journal of Scientific & Industrial Research Series A Physical Sciences
summary: This study investigates the effect of varying mixing ratios between epoxy resin and unsaturated polyester resin on the mechanical and morphological properties of hybrid polymer composites. Six different blend ratios were prepared, ranging f
content: This study investigates the effect of varying mixing ratios between epoxy resin and unsaturated polyester resin on the mechanical and morphological properties of hybrid polymer composites. Six different blend ratios were prepared, ranging from 100% epoxy to 100% polyester. Abrasion resistance was evaluated using a Pin-on-Disc device under applied loads ranging from 500 g to 2500 g. The results showed that increasing the epoxy content significantly enhanced wear resistance. Under a 2500 g load, the residual weight increased from 0.3283 g for the 20% epoxy sample to 1.6947 g for the 100% epoxy sample, indicating reduced material loss due to the higher hardness and crosslink density of epoxy. Compressive strength was measured using a bold harris No. 36110 hydraulic press, following ASTM D695. The highest compressive strength was observed in the 100% epoxy sample (6.1 MPa), while the lowest value (0.6 MPa) was recorded for the 40% epoxy / 60% polyester blend, indicating weak interfacial bonding and poor structural compatibility. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis revealed features such as phase separation, particle agglomeration and microcracks in the hybrid samples, suggesting inadequate resin compatibility and non-uniform mixing. Overall, the results highlight that optimizing the epoxy-to- polyester ratio is essential to enhance both the mechanical performance and structural integrity of hybrid polymer composites.

title: Acerihabitans arcticus sp. nov., a first psychrophilic member of the family Pectobacteriaceae and able to reduce Fe(III)
summary: Abstract A novel psychrophilic strain TG2T was isolated from an anaerobic enrichment obtained from a tundra soil sample selected on the Bykovsky Peninsula (Russia). Cells were facultatively anaerobic, Gram-stain-negative, non-spore-forming
content: Abstract A novel psychrophilic strain TG2T was isolated from an anaerobic enrichment obtained from a tundra soil sample selected on the Bykovsky Peninsula (Russia). Cells were facultatively anaerobic, Gram-stain-negative, non-spore-forming motile short rods. The novel isolate grows at 0–25°C (optimum 8°C), pH 6.0–8.0 (optimum 7.0–7.5), up to 1.0% (w/v) NaCl (optimum 0.1–0.5%). Strain TG2T was a chemoorganoheterotroph. Lactate, acetate and formate were the major products of glucose and pectin fermentation. The major cellular fatty acids were С16:1ω8c, С17:0 cyclo and С18:0 cyclo. The polar lipids were phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidylethanolamine phosphatidylglycerol, and four unidentified polar lipids. Phylogenomic analysis based on 81 core gene sequences showed that strain TG2T belonged to the family Pectobacteriaceae. The closest phylogenetic neighbor was Acerihabitans arboris SAP-6T (98.2% 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity). The genome of strain TG2T was 5.3 Mbp in size with 51.1 mol% of G + C content. The average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA–DNA hybridization (dDDH) values between strain TG2T and its closest relative were 78.6 and 22.6%, respectively. Based on the phylogenetic, phenotypic, chemotaxonomic and genomic data, new bacterium represents a novel species of the genus Acerihabitans in the family Pectobacteriaceae, for which the name Acerihabitans arcticus sp. nov. is proposed. The type strain is TG2T (= VKM B-3773T = JCM 39549T)

title: Microplastics affect belowground performance of winter wheat and microbial networks in the rhizosphere
summary: , showed an increased degree and eigenvector centrality in the LDPE treatment, suggesting enhanced co-occurrence and higher influence within the microbial community structure. In contrast, the PES and PP treatments resulted in lower average
content: , showed an increased degree and eigenvector centrality in the LDPE treatment, suggesting enhanced co-occurrence and higher influence within the microbial community structure. In contrast, the PES and PP treatments resulted in lower average node degree and reduced clustering. The PS treatment only had a small effect on the microbial co-occurrence networks. Overall, our data indicate that MP-induced stress can alter microbial network topology, reduce community integration, and drive shifts in ecologically important taxa in the rhizosphere, which are linked to changes in the availability of nutrients for plants. Our findings highlight the complex and variable influence of MPs on soil-plant interactions.

title: Potenziale für Naturschutz durch virtuelle Zäune in der Beweidung
summary: Conservation potential through virtual fences in grazing management // Virtual fencing is an emerging technology with the potential to simplify grazing management and facilitate nature conservation measures on grazed grassland. Based on an
content: Conservation potential through virtual fences in grazing management // Virtual fencing is an emerging technology with the potential to simplify grazing management and facilitate nature conservation measures on grazed grassland. Based on an approved field trial with cattle and artificial nests, we demonstrate that the use of virtual fences is promising for the protection of ground-nesting birds. In areas protected by virtual fences, the rate of nest trampling was significantly lower compared with unprotected areas. In addition to the wide range of practical applications for virtual fencing systems, they also have the potential to simplify the funding of conservation measures on pastures through agri-environmental and climate schemes (AECS), due to the automatic documentation of animal movements. In addition, novel AECS may be established to increase structural diversity or protect particularly vulnerable grassland species. In order to capitalise on the potential of virtual fencing systems for nature conservation, a broad discussion on possible applications and framework conditions is necessary.

title: Multiobjective optimization model for lunar colony logistics based on marginal utility and auction theory
source: International Conference on Machine Learning, Neural Networks, and Computer Software (MLNNCS)
summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of optimizing material transport for lunar colony construction, focusing on the strategic integration of space elevator and launch vehicle technologies. We develop a comprehensive multi-model fram
content: This paper addresses the critical challenge of optimizing material transport for lunar colony construction, focusing on the strategic integration of space elevator and launch vehicle technologies. We develop a comprehensive multi-model framework encompassing four interconnected models: the High-Quality Transport Resource Evaluation (HQTRE) model, the Multi-Objective Programming (MOP) model under non-ideal conditions, the Game Theory-based Multi-Objective Programming (GT-MOP) model for payload transport, and the Environmentally Friendly Reusable Launch Vehicle (EFRLV) model. Our analysis reveals that the optimal hybrid strategy employs a ratio of r=0.05 (5% launch vehicle, 95% space elevator), achieving a completion time of 183.93 years under ideal conditions (194.42 years under non-ideal scenarios) with an economic cost of approximately $4.78 billion for the optimal configuration. The hybrid approach demonstrates significant environmental benefits, reducing carbon emissions by 26-38% compared to launch vehicle-only strategies. Sensitivity analysis identifies the Space System Capacity (SSC≈3.37) as the critical bottleneck. This research provides actionable insights for policymakers and engineers in planning sustainable lunar colonization logistics.

title: Algal laboratory evolution at a cold temperature leads to overproduction of lipid under both cold and warm conditions
summary: Abstract Background Microalgae that both grow fast and overproduce lipids are desirable materials for biofuel production. Evolutionary adaptation under certain stressful conditions is associated with greater levels of lipid accumulation wit
content: Abstract Background Microalgae that both grow fast and overproduce lipids are desirable materials for biofuel production. Evolutionary adaptation under certain stressful conditions is associated with greater levels of lipid accumulation within cells; and the lipid overproduction trait may be maintained even when algal cells are grown under benign conditions where growth rate is high. Therefore, cold-evolved algae and warm cultivation conditions could be a perfect combination for population-level lipid production. Here we test this hypothesis by working with Chlorella sorokiniana isolates from an earlier laboratory evolution experiment, in which algal populations have evolved under either constantly benign (25°C) or constantly cold conditions (15°C). The growth performance and lipid content per cell of each algal isolate were measured at both temperatures. Results The combination of 15°C-evolution algae and 25°C culture conditions gave the highest levels of lipid content per cell as well as a fairly fast growth rate, and not surprisingly, extremely high population-level lipid production. Analysis of evolutionary changes relative to the ancestral strain failed to identify evolutionary trade-offs: adaptation to a certain environment did not cause decreased growth performance in the alternative environment, and an increase in lipid content per cell was not associated with reduced growth rate. Conclusions These findings indicate that laboratory evolution under stressful conditions may enhance environmental adaptability and lipid accumulation of microalgae, offering a potential basis for further improving lipid productivity in biotechnology applications.

title: Global warming extends boreal fire seasons into uncharted territory
summary: Abstract Recent wildfire disasters in communities such as Fort McMurray and Jasper in Canada, and across Siberia, highlight the growing vulnerability of boreal regions to prolonged fire-conducive conditions under a warming climate. Here, we
content: Abstract Recent wildfire disasters in communities such as Fort McMurray and Jasper in Canada, and across Siberia, highlight the growing vulnerability of boreal regions to prolonged fire-conducive conditions under a warming climate. Here, we use 5000-year Earth system model simulations to quantify how quasi steady-state global warming alters the boreal fire-season length across North America and Eurasia. We find that the simulated area-weighted boreal fire season lengthens by $$\sim $$ 12 ± 2 days per $$^\circ $$ C of global mean warming, driven primarily by higher near-surface temperatures and reduced snow cover. Under present-day warming, the mean boreal fire season is already extended by approximately two weeks relative to pre-industrial conditions. The fire-season length spatial pattern remains broadly conserved, but warming shifts the entire boreal domain toward earlier onset and later termination, with the largest proportional increases in high-latitude regions where historical fire seasons were shortest. The area of the boreal forest experiencing fire seasons outside the range of pre-industrial variability increases with warming, leading to increasingly widespread unprecedented fire seasons. Above 2 $$^\circ $$ C of global warming, much of the boreal forest faces unusually long fire seasons. Keeping warming below 2 $$^\circ $$ C could significantly limit the geographic extent and consequences of unprecedented boreal fire seasons.

title: Thermodynamic limits to secondary mineral formation from US enhanced weathering
summary: Abstract It has become increasingly accepted that carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies will be necessary to prevent the worst impacts of climate change. As a result, CDR has been incorporated as a central component of climate policy fram
content: Abstract It has become increasingly accepted that carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies will be necessary to prevent the worst impacts of climate change. As a result, CDR has been incorporated as a central component of climate policy frameworks and projections for climate impact in the coming century. Enhanced weathering (EW), the process of applying finely ground reactive rocks to croplands to accelerate chemical weathering and increase the conversion of atmospheric CO2 to dissolved bicarbonate, has emerged as a promising, scalable, durable CDR approach with clear co-benefits for agricultural systems. However, there remain questions about the extent to which secondary mineral formation may constitute a significant carbon leakage pathway downstream of agricultural deployment. Here, we use an EW field trial and groundwater data from the coterminous US to develop a framework to gauge the likely risk of carbon leakage due to secondary mineral formation. We demonstrate that there are regions across the US with a low risk of carbon leakage through secondary mineral formation, and that these are typically the same regions where the process has the potential to provide the greatest economic and agricultural benefits to farmers. We suggest that this framework can be used to help derisk carbon accounting and crediting through EW in managed lands.

title: Mechanistic and kinetic insights into secondary phenol formation from cresol and toluene: A combined quantum chemical and machine learning study
summary: Abstract Context In this study, the reaction mechanisms and kinetics of four pathways leading to phenol + CH 3 formation were systematically investigated, including the reactions of o -, m -, and p -cresol with H atoms and the reaction of t
content: Abstract Context In this study, the reaction mechanisms and kinetics of four pathways leading to phenol + CH 3 formation were systematically investigated, including the reactions of o -, m -, and p -cresol with H atoms and the reaction of toluene with OH radicals. The results show that the addition of H atoms to the three cresol isomers requires activation energies of 7.6, 8.4, and 8.6 kcal/mol, respectively, leading to the formation of the corresponding intermediates IS1, IS2, and IS3. In the toluene + OH reaction, a pre-reactive complex is formed before the system proceeds via a submerged transition state to generate IS4. All four intermediates subsequently undergo CH 3 elimination to yield the same bimolecular product, phenol + CH 3 . The transition-state energies predicted by the machine learning (ML) model are in good agreement with the corresponding quantum chemical results, with deviations of less than 1 kcal/mol. The calculated rate coefficients indicate that the o -cresol + H reaction is the fastest among the four pathways over the investigated temperature and pressure ranges. In addition, the rate coefficients obtained for the toluene + OH reaction agree well with the previous theoretical results of Wu et al., with a mean absolute relative deviation of 6.3%. These findings provide insights into the competing pathways for phenol formation and their temperature- and pressure-dependent kinetics, with implications for understanding aromatic oxidation and combustion chemistry. Methods The geometries of all reactants, intermediates, transition states, and products were optimized at the B3LYP/6-311 + + G(3df,2p) level of theory. Single-point energies were subsequently calculated using the CCSD(T) method with the same basis set. The ML model was employed to predict transition-state energies and evaluate their agreement with the quantum chemical calculations. Temperature- and pressure-dependent rate coefficients were calculated using RRKM/master equation (ME) theory, as implemented in the MESMER software package. All quantum chemical calculations were performed using Gaussian 16.

title: Co-evolution of microbial mercury cycling genes and Earth’s oxygenation history
summary: Deciphering how microbes co-evolved with early Earth's redox conditions helps us understand life's adaptation to early Earth environments. The mercury (Hg) biogeochemical cycle offers a window into this co-evolutionary process, as Hg was ub
content: Deciphering how microbes co-evolved with early Earth's redox conditions helps us understand life's adaptation to early Earth environments. The mercury (Hg) biogeochemical cycle offers a window into this co-evolutionary process, as Hg was ubiquitous on early Earth and its speciation and toxicity are highly redox-sensitive. However, direct evidence for the co-evolutionary history of microbes and the Hg cycle is scarce due to poor geological preservation. Here, we bypassed this limitation by applying phylogenetic reconciliation to track key evolutionary events across the tree of life for the principal microbial Hg cycling gene systems (the Hg-detoxification mer operon and Hg-methylating hgcAB), including speciation, duplications, transfers, and losses. Our results revealed a two-stage evolutionary trajectory. The hgcAB and core mer operon (merA, merR, and merB) emerged in the anoxic Archean, predating the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and coinciding with intense volcanism, suggesting early microbial adaptation to inorganic Hg(II) under anoxic conditions. Towards the end of and after the GOE, we observed a major expansion of multiple Mer transporters and the negative regulator of the mer operon (MerD), reflecting a microbial adaptive response to the diversification of organomercury species in a progressively oxidizing environment, temporally associated with intermittent volcanic Hg fluxes. The systematic absence of mer genes in hgcAB-containing bacteria, coupled with their distinct ecological niches, points to fundamentally divergent evolutionary trajectories for Hg methylation and mer-mediated detoxification over geological time. This work provides genomic insights into microbial adaptation to early Earth redox evolution and its reshaping of the microbial biosphere.

title: Do rumen microbes use quorum sensing to shape digestion and methane?
summary: ABSTRACT Cattle, sheep, and goats live on plant fiber that they cannot digest themselves. The work is done by the microbes packed into the rumen, which convert that fiber into volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and microbial protein, and along the
content: ABSTRACT Cattle, sheep, and goats live on plant fiber that they cannot digest themselves. The work is done by the microbes packed into the rumen, which convert that fiber into volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and microbial protein, and along the way, release methane. Bacteria in many other habitats coordinate their behavior by releasing and detecting small chemical signals, a process known as quorum sensing (QS). Where QS operates, it switches on the kinds of collective activity that would matter a great deal in the rumen: attaching to feed particles, building biofilms, secreting enzymes, and cross‐feeding. Whether rumen microbes do the same is still an open question. What has actually been found in rumen contents is signal‐like activity of two chemical classes, N‐acyl homoserine lactones (AHLs) and autoinducer‐2 (AI‐2), an AHL‐producing rumen isolate, and genes or transcripts that could build or receive such signals. The parts are present; that microbes use them to regulate fiber digestion or methane output has not been shown. Diet makes the question harder, because changing the ration shifts signal concentrations, microbial biomass, pH, community composition, and fermentation at once. We therefore separate what has been observed directly in the rumen from what is only correlative and what has been carried over from other microbial systems, ask how diet, microbial communication, biofilm organization, feed digestion, and methane emissions might be linked, and set out the measurements and manipulations needed to decide whether QS regulates rumen function, only tracks microbial density and activity, or both.

title: Tree‐Ring δ 18 O Indicates Moisture Variation and Water Vapor Sources on the Eastern Tibetan Plateau
summary: Abstract Under varying atmospheric circulation, the eastern Tibetan Plateau (ETP) exhibits spatiotemporally heterogeneous hydroclimatic changes, for which the tree‐ring cellulose δ 18 O ( δ 18 O tree ) is an ideal paleoclimate proxy. In thi
content: Abstract Under varying atmospheric circulation, the eastern Tibetan Plateau (ETP) exhibits spatiotemporally heterogeneous hydroclimatic changes, for which the tree‐ring cellulose δ 18 O ( δ 18 O tree ) is an ideal paleoclimate proxy. In this study, a newly established 210‐year δ 18 O tree chronology from the ETP revealed that the May‐to‐July relative humidity (RH MJJ ) was its key climatic control. After designing a transfer function, the RH MJJ history was reconstructed, which explained 43% ( R 2 adj = 42%) variance of the instrumental record (1959–2018; r = 0.65, p < 0.001). Our reconstruction revealed progressive southward aridification across the ETP in the latter half of the 19th century and the mid‐20th century. A detailed analysis of spatial correlation, backward trajectory water vapor transport pathway, and water vapor transport flux was carried out. The results indicate that the reduction of the water vapor amount transported from the Indian Ocean propagated a drought signal along the moisture transport pathway over the ETP. Moreover, we found that the δ 18 O tree varied with the contribution ratio of marine moisture, even in the chronology‐climate decoupling years. Based on previous research, we propose a possible response mechanism in which the δ 18 O water and the transpiration intensity dominated by the RH MJJ serve as two independent physiological pathways for the negative correlation between δ 18 O tree and RH MJJ . When the RH MJJ and δ 18 O water were decoupled, the water source information from δ 18 O water served as a main reason for the reconstruction residuals. This δ 18 O tree record revealed the moisture variation and water vapor sources on the ETP and indicated its potential to provide diverse climate information.

title: Plant derived silver nanoparticles from allelopathic weeds as emerging nano bioherbicides for sustainable weed management
summary: The integration of allelopathy and green nanotechnology has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable plant stress management and weed control. However, the evidence concerning AgNPs synthesized specifically from allelopathic weeds re
content: The integration of allelopathy and green nanotechnology has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable plant stress management and weed control. However, the evidence concerning AgNPs synthesized specifically from allelopathic weeds remains fragmented across studies of green synthesis, nanoparticle characterization, phytotoxicity, stomatal responses, and environmental safety. A focused review is therefore needed to connect these currently separate lines of evidence and to clarify the mechanisms by which allelopathic weed-derived AgNPs may function as nano-bioherbicides while minimizing risks to non-target plants and the environment. Allelopathic weeds are rich sources of bioactive secondary metabolites capable of reducing and stabilizing silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), leading to the formation of biologically active nanomaterials. Increasing evidence indicates that plant-derived AgNPs exert pronounced phytotoxic effects, with with stomatal regulation emerging as an important physiological response. This review synthesizes current knowledge on AgNPs synthesized from allelopathic weeds, highlighting their influence on stomatal behavior, photosynthesis, and plant growth inhibition, along with the underlying biochemical and molecular mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, hormonal crosstalk, ion signaling, and ultrastructural alterations associated with nanoparticle exposure. Furthermore, the potential application of allelopathic AgNPs as eco-friendly nano-bioherbicides and the related environmental safety concerns are critically discussed. Overall, this review provides a mechanistic framework for understanding nanoparticle-mediated allelopathic interactions and supports the development of sustainable nano-enabled weed management strategies.

title: The pangenome of the Arctic picoeukaryote Micromonas polaris resolves cryptic ecotypes and identifies a polar-specific gene repertoire
summary: Micromonas polaris is the dominant picoeukaryote of the Arctic Ocean, where it sustains primary production across habitats from sea ice to open water to the subsurface chlorophyll maximum. How a single species maintains this ecological brea
content: Micromonas polaris is the dominant picoeukaryote of the Arctic Ocean, where it sustains primary production across habitats from sea ice to open water to the subsurface chlorophyll maximum. How a single species maintains this ecological breadth has remained unclear. Standard phylogenetic markers such as 18S rRNA are nearly invariant within M. polaris and conceal any internal genomic heterogeneity the species may possess. Here we present a pangenome of 14 M. polaris strains spanning the Arctic basin, integrated with Tara Oceans metagenomes, that resolves the species into two diverged ecotypes invisible to 18S rRNA but recovered consistently by prp8, genome-wide SNPs, ANI, and orthogroup-based phylogenies. The two ecotypes coexist sympatrically, with one lineage consistently enriched deeper in the water column across the basin. M. polaris carries 990 polar-specific hierarchical orthogroups absent from temperate Micromonas, organised around one-carbon metabolism, endocytosis, transmembrane transport, and photo-oxidative stress response. Several components show phylogenetic signatures of horizontal acquisition from co-occurring marine taxa. Atlantification is bringing temperate Micromonas into Arctic margins seasonally, but the polar night likely limits their year-round persistence. M. polaris and its polar-specific toolkit appear positioned to persist through the dark season, suggesting Arctic margins will undergo seasonal turnover rather than stable replacement.

title: Energetic niches of syntrophic methanogens recorded by clumped isotopes
summary: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, an important energy source and a potential biosignature in extraterrestrial environments. Stable carbon and hydrogen isotope (δ13C and δD) and clumped isotopologues (∆13CH3D and ∆12CH2D2) compositions of
content: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, an important energy source and a potential biosignature in extraterrestrial environments. Stable carbon and hydrogen isotope (δ13C and δD) and clumped isotopologues (∆13CH3D and ∆12CH2D2) compositions of methane have been widely used as tracers for methanogenesis pathways. Furthermore, isotopic signatures of methane typically shift closer to equilibrium as the Gibbs energy (∆Gr) of methanogenesis moves closer to the energy limit of life. However, the variations of clumped methane isotope signatures in response to the changes in ∆Gr lack careful examination. In this study, we measure the isotope signatures of methane produced by monoculture methanogens with formate or H2/CO2, and by syntrophic cocultures of hydrogenotrophic methanogens paired with acetate or propionate oxidizers. Methanogenesis by cocultures has lower Gibbs energy yield than monocultures, yet both ∆13CH3D and ∆12CH2D2 values from cocultures are further away from isotopic equilibrium. From these experiments, we identify an energetic niche (∆Gr ~ -35 kJ mol-1 CH4), where δ13C, ∆13CH3D and ∆12CH2D2 values of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis transiently exhibit more disequilibrium. This study presents differential responses of bulk carbon, hydrogen and clumped isotopic signatures to ∆Gr, and highlights their applications in distinguishing methanogenesis under different energy regimes.

title: Genomic blueprints of a dynamic deep sea: contrasting adaptive strategies potentially drive seasonal microbial succession
summary: Genetic variation within marine microbial populations can help reveal how deep-sea communities respond to environmental change. However, population-level genomic variation in deep pelagic waters remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed
content: Genetic variation within marine microbial populations can help reveal how deep-sea communities respond to environmental change. However, population-level genomic variation in deep pelagic waters remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets from ~1,080 m depth in the South China Sea to compare genomic variation between summer and winter microbial assemblages. Among 11 persistent metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) detected in both summer and winter samples, we observed differences in abundance, nucleotide diversity (π), pN/pS ratios, and gene-level differentiation. Two enriched populations showed contrasting patterns, with Sphingobium yanoikuyae enriched in winter samples and Methyloversatilis universalis enriched in summer samples. The winter-enriched S. yanoikuyae population carried winter-associated accessory genes related to restriction-modification and toxin-antitoxin systems, consistent with a defense-oriented persistence profile. In contrast, the summer-enriched M. universalis population showed higher nucleotide diversity in summer samples and divergence in genes related to motility, transport, and cobalamin acquisition. Across persistent MAGs, low pN/pS ratios indicated predominantly purifying selection, whereas gene-specific divergence and flexible accessory gene content suggested population-level adaptive potential under contrasting winter and summer conditions. These results reveal population-genomic differences associated with winter-summer microbial shifts in the deep sea.

title: Nanomalzeme Kimyasında Güncel Yaklaşımlar
summary: Nanomalzeme Kimyasında Güncel Yaklaşımlar, nanomalzemeleri tasarımdan uygulamaya uzanan bir çizgide, kimyasal temeller üzerinden ele alan beş bölümlük bir eserdir. Kitap; yüzey kimyası, sentez yolu ve yapı–işlev ilişkileri gibi nanomalzemel
content: Nanomalzeme Kimyasında Güncel Yaklaşımlar, nanomalzemeleri tasarımdan uygulamaya uzanan bir çizgide, kimyasal temeller üzerinden ele alan beş bölümlük bir eserdir. Kitap; yüzey kimyası, sentez yolu ve yapı–işlev ilişkileri gibi nanomalzemelerin davranışını belirleyen etkenleri sürdürülebilirlik, sağlık ve çevre alanlarındaki güncel uygulamalarla birlikte değerlendirmektedir. İlk bölüm, nanoteknolojiyi yeşil kimyanın on iki ilkesi çerçevesinde ele almakta; bitki ekstraktları ve mikroorganizmalar aracılığıyla metal ve metal oksit nanoparçacıkların çevre dostu sentezini ve bu malzemelerin biyomedikal, tarım, gıda ve su arıtımı alanlarındaki kullanımını tartışmaktadır. İkinci bölüm, metal destekli nanokompozitlerin teranostik platformlar olarak tasarımını; manyetik rezonans ve bilgisayarlı tomografi görüntülemedeki işlevlerini, fototermal, kemodinamik ve radyosensitizasyona dayalı tedavi mekanizmalarını ve klinik aktarımda karşılaşılan güvenlik sorunlarını incelemektedir. Üçüncü bölüm, nanoparçacık–enzim hibrit sistemlerini immobilizasyon kimyası, nanozimlerin yapay enzim etkinliği, katalitik performansın nicel değerlendirilmesi ve enzim–nanozim kaskatları üzerinden açıklamakta; gıda, çevre ve biyokataliz uygulamalarını özetlemektedir. Dördüncü bölümde lipozomlar, polimerik miseller, lipit nanoparçacıklar ve inorganik taşıyıcılar gibi ilaç taşıma sistemleri; biyolojik engeller, EPR etkisi, protein koronası, uyarana duyarlı salım ve salım kinetiği modelleriyle birlikte değerlendirilmektedir. Son bölüm ise hidrojel bazlı adsorbanlarda ağ yapısı, çapraz bağlanma kimyası ve adsorpsiyon mekanizmaları arasındaki ilişkileri, ağır metal iyonlarının ve boyar maddelerin sudan uzaklaştırılması örnekleriyle ortaya koymaktadır. Kitap; kimya, malzeme bilimi, biyoteknoloji ve eczacılık alanlarındaki lisansüstü öğrenciler ile araştırmacılar için temel kavramları ve güncel literatürü bir arada sunan bir başvuru kaynağı olarak hazırlanmıştır.

title: Stage-specific canopy structure is associated with water productivity and evapotranspiration partitioning across China’s major cereal systems
summary: Improving crop water productivity (WP) requires identifying when canopy states are associated with the partitioning of evapotranspiration (ET) and the conversion of water and carbon into yield. We combined harmonized 5 arc-min gridded datas
content: Improving crop water productivity (WP) requires identifying when canopy states are associated with the partitioning of evapotranspiration (ET) and the conversion of water and carbon into yield. We combined harmonized 5 arc-min gridded datasets for rice, maize, and wheat across China with four related canopy descriptors—clumping index (CI), fractional vegetation cover (FVC), leaf area index (LAI), and specific vegetation cover (SVC). WP was decomposed into transpiration fraction (T/ET), carbon gain per unit transpiration (GPP/T), and carbon-to-yield conversion (Y/GPP), and was evaluated using percentile summaries, correlations, LOWESS, XGBoost–SHAP, and structural equation modelling (SEM). Higher-WP systems generally showed higher CI, whereas LAI varied by crop and stage; the most informative stages differed among crops. Direct-flux diagnostics showed that FVC was positively associated with transpiration and GPP and negatively associated with soil evaporation in many crop-stage combinations, clarifying why its relation with T/ET differed from its relation with final WP. The dominant response patterns were highly consistent in a common-period analysis for 2003–2014 and under 10- and 15-arc-min spatial-support tests. LOWESS shapes were generally stable across smoothing fractions, although isolated weak SVC responses were parameter sensitive. Spatial-block cross-validation showed that the incremental predictive contribution of canopy variables was crop dependent and clearest for maize, rather than uniformly large across all crops. Bootstrap path analysis supported the principal signs in the SEM while confirming that these paths should be interpreted as conditional associations, not experimental causal effects. These observational results identify crop-specific canopy windows for subsequent field testing but do not constitute local irrigation prescriptions.
