title: Water-nitrogen coupling reshapes surface rhizosphere microecology to drive water productivity and grain yield of winter wheat under drip fertigation in the North China Plain
summary: Introduction Wheat production in the North China Plain is facing the dual challenges of severe water scarcity and inefficient fertilizer utilization. Although drip fertigation has been widely promoted, the mechanisms by which optimized wate
content: Introduction Wheat production in the North China Plain is facing the dual challenges of severe water scarcity and inefficient fertilizer utilization. Although drip fertigation has been widely promoted, the mechanisms by which optimized water-nitrogen coupling improve water productivity (WPc) and yield via rhizosphere processes remain unclear. Methods A three-year field experiment was conducted with three irrigation levels (maintaining soil moisture at 70-85%, 60-75%, and 50-65% of field capacity, designated as D1, D2, D3) and three nitrogen rates (150, 210, 270 kg N ha −1 , designated as N1, N2, N3). We comprehensively assessed soil microbial diversity, enzyme activities, nitrogen dynamics, root hormonal profiles, architectural traits, plant growth, and yield components. It also systematically analyzed the interactions among WPc, yield, and root-zone microbial dynamics, revealing the relationships among WPc, yield, and core rhizosphere environmental factors. Results The D2N2 treatment (60-75% field capacity, 210 kg N ha −1 ) was identified as the optimal based on a comprehensive evaluation. D2N2 synergistically boosted grain yield by 8.4-18.0%, WPC by 2.0-19.5% compared to other treatments. while maintaining moderate evapotranspiration ranging 501.1-551.4 mm. The yield and WPc advantages of D2N2 were associated with a cascade of rhizosphere and root responses. This regime establishes a favorable root zone microenvironment, increasing microbial alpha diversity (bacteria and fungi) and key enzyme activities (urease and S-NAG) by 0.3-30.2% and 10.7-100.1%, respectively. Meanwhile, this resulted in a 1.3%-31.7% increase in total nitrogen content in the 0-40-centimeter soil layer. Root hormonal profiles were distinctly altered under D2N2, characterized by elevated zeatin riboside (ZR) levels and suppressed jasmonate (MeJA) accumulation, contrasting sharply with the stress‑induced hormone surge observed under water deficient treatments such as D3N1. These hormonal changes were accompanied by improved root architecture, with root weight density increasing by 38.9-47.1%. Multi variable analyses further identified S NAG, fungal Chao index (F Chao), and ZR as the key factors most strongly associated with WPc and yield (p < 0.05). Discussion Our findings indicate that the success of optimal drip fertigation is associated with a bioactive rhizosphere ecosystem that supports root function and resource capture. We conclude that a shift from input-intensive practices to rhizosphere-targeted precision water management is essential for enhancing WPc and ensuring agricultural sustainability in water-scarce regions like the North China Plain.

title: Bidirectional acetate exchange couples ethanol turnover to acetyl-CoA metabolism in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
summary: Overflow metabolism describes the excretion of partially oxidized metabolites into the extracellular environment during rapid sugar utilization. Although these metabolites can later be reused, it remains unclear whether reassimilation also
content: Overflow metabolism describes the excretion of partially oxidized metabolites into the extracellular environment during rapid sugar utilization. Although these metabolites can later be reused, it remains unclear whether reassimilation also occurs during ongoing sugar consumption, and if so, how. Here, 13 C-isotope tracing and metabolic flux analysis of acetate exchange in Saccharomyces cerevisiae during hexose utilization reveal that net acetate overflow is only the small difference between order-of-magnitude larger simultaneous excretion and assimilation fluxes. Unlike ethanol production, acetate exchange is not determined by hexose uptake but depends on metabolic processes downstream of glycolysis. Ethanol oxidation contributes to acetate excretion even during net ethanol production, directly linking the two main overflow pathways. We exploited this understanding to redirect extracellular acetate into the acetyl-CoA-derived product mevalonate. These results establish acetate overflow as a dynamic exchange linking ethanol turnover to acetyl-CoA metabolism, in which acetate is simultaneously an overflow product and a carbon source that can be redirected toward bioproduction.

title: Post-wildfire soil respiration in tundra is driven by plant community composition and soil moisture in the late growing season
summary: Abstract Arctic wildfires are expected to increase carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from soils underlain by permafrost. However, we lack in situ measurements of post-fire soil respiration and its drivers in the Arctic tundra. We measured soil
content: Abstract Arctic wildfires are expected to increase carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from soils underlain by permafrost. However, we lack in situ measurements of post-fire soil respiration and its drivers in the Arctic tundra. We measured soil properties and late-growing season CO2 fluxes in patches of unique plant functional types (PFT) across two years using a chronosequence approach in tundra recovering from repeated wildfires over the past five decades on the Seward Peninsula of Alaska. Soil respiration varied with fire age and number of times burned and was greatest in areas dominated by forbs, declining in areas dominated by shrubs and graminoids. After accounting for PFT, soil respiration also declined as soil moisture increased in already wet systems. Early-thaw season analyses suggested that increased permafrost thaw in burned areas was associated with a denser organic layer. Changes in water availability and plant species composition along post-fire successional trajectories may influence net soil CO2 emissions from Arctic tundra.

title: Development of a folate-conjugated, pH-responsive magnetic nanocarrier based on graphene oxide-g-poly(N-vinylformamide/allylamine) for doxorubicin drug delivery
summary: In this study, a folic acid-conjugated pH-responsive copolymer grafted onto magnetic carboxylated graphene oxide (MCGO) was developed and evaluated for doxorubicin (DOX) adsorption and release. Functionalization of MCGO with allyl alcohol (
content: In this study, a folic acid-conjugated pH-responsive copolymer grafted onto magnetic carboxylated graphene oxide (MCGO) was developed and evaluated for doxorubicin (DOX) adsorption and release. Functionalization of MCGO with allyl alcohol (AOH) introduced vinyl groups that served as initiation sites for free-radical polymerization and grafting of the N -vinylformamide (VF)/allylamine (AN) chains. Subsequent conjugation of folic acid (FA) was designed to enhance the potential for folate receptor-associated cellular interaction. Structural and physicochemical characterization using FTIR, XRD, BET, TGA, VSM, FE-SEM/EDX, TEM, and zeta potential/DLS analyses confirmed the successful fabrication of the nanocomposite. The surface area and pore volume of MCGO-p(VF/AN)-FA were 82.68 m 2 g −1 and 0.21 cm 3 g −1 , respectively, roughly ten times higher than those of CGO. The synthesized composite exhibited high DOX adsorption capacity under selected conditions (pH: 8, temperature: 55 °C, contact time: 45 min), evaluated via a one-factor-at-a-time approach. Adsorption kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order model, while the Langmuir isotherm provided the best fit, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 126.619 mg g −1 at 55 °C. Drug release studies revealed enhanced release under mildly acidic conditions, with 88% of the DOX released at pH 5.6 over 48 h at 37 °C. in-vitro studies implied a formulation-dependent biological response, with the FA-conjugated nanocarrier showing a numerical trend toward greater cytotoxicity against MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells compared with the non-folate system, alongside acceptable biocompatibility toward MCF-10A normal cells (>70% viability). In addition, the competitive inhibition assay utilizing free folic acid resulted in a restoration of MDA-MB-231 cell viability to 98.76%, providing supportive evidence for the involvement of FR-mediated cellular interactions. However, direct quantitative uptake and intracellular trafficking remain to be verified by flow cytometry and confocal imaging in future studies.

title: IMPACTS OF CONTEMPORARY GLOBAL CHANGES ON THE WATER CYCLE OF THE BRESTNITSA KARST GEOSYSTEM IN NORTHERN BULGARIA
summary: Brestnitsa Karst Geosystem (BKG) was formed in the Pre-Balkans in Northern Bulgaria.It is developed in Mesozoic organogenic limestones with a very high carbonate content.A complete karst morphological complex has been formed in the relief o
content: Brestnitsa Karst Geosystem (BKG) was formed in the Pre-Balkans in Northern Bulgaria.It is developed in Mesozoic organogenic limestones with a very high carbonate content.A complete karst morphological complex has been formed in the relief of the geosystem, which is the result of the combination of autogenous and allogenic types of karst.The BKG region is located in the transitional area between the subtropical and temperate climate.The karst aquifer is recharged by infiltration through the aeration zone of precipitation, irrigation and waste household and fecal waters from livestock farms and inflow of river waters and periodic surface runoff of precipitation waters into sinkholes.The specific structure of the karst geosystem is the reason why its water cycle is very sensitive to global changes of both natural and anthropogenic types and is highly vulnerable to pollution (mechanical, chemical, bacteriological).This is a serious problem, because the geosystem drains into the karst spring Glava Panega, which is the highest flow concentrated spring in Bulgaria.Its waters are used for industrial and drinking-domestic water supply.The aim of this study is to track and analyze the consequences of global changes on the water cycle through application of a geosystem approach and the original model for integrated monitoring of karst geosystems (MIKS).Special attention is paid to the sources of anthropogenic pressure influenced by socio-economic changes in regional, national and global aspects and their impact on the pollution of karst waters.

title: Mapping wildfire risks and stewardship opportunities across North Kona and South Kohala, Hawaiʻi Island
summary: Abstract In Hawaiʻi, wildfires represent an escalating crisis for communities, with growing impacts to health and human safety, native ecosystems, vital watersheds, and nearshore coral reefs. Despite increased funding for prevention, suppre
content: Abstract In Hawaiʻi, wildfires represent an escalating crisis for communities, with growing impacts to health and human safety, native ecosystems, vital watersheds, and nearshore coral reefs. Despite increased funding for prevention, suppression, and recovery, the threat continues to outpace responses, culminating over the past decade in some of the largest fires in Hawaiʻi's history. To better understand these trends, we investigated the intersection of resource planning and stewardship, urban development, and wildfire mitigation within the vulnerable North Kona and South Kohala districts of Hawaiʻi Island. Our research integrated three layers of analysis. First, we mapped resource stewardship capacity with a focus on biocultural stewardship defined as conservation that is rooted in Native Hawaiian knowledge, values, and practices. Second, we synthesized spatial data detailing tree canopy cover, flammable non‐native grasslands, and the wildland–urban interface. Finally, we audited existing local, county, and state environmental management and land use plans to evaluate cross‐plan alignment and operational focus on wildfire mitigation. Our findings reveal critical gaps: development plans designate areas for urban expansion that face severe wildfire risks yet funded and enforceable strategies and actions to mitigate these risks are largely absent from official plans. Our spatial analyses also identified powerful, community‐driven solutions: hot spots of active community stewardship—specifically where volunteers plant trees and remove invasive grasses—experienced lower rates of recurring burns over the past 5 years. Ultimately, our research highlights that incentivizing community led stewardship, integrating this stewardship into tiered planning processes, and developing coordinated plans that feature enforceable operational‐scale policies would all represent valuable investments into safeguarding Hawaiʻi's communities and ridge‐to‐reef resources.

title: A Multilayer Cryogel Platform for the Spatiotemporally Controlled Release of Protein Cargo
source: Journal of Biomedical Materials Research Part A
summary: ABSTRACT Biomaterial‐mediated drug delivery systems can improve therapeutic efficacy by extending local drug retention and reducing the need for repeated administration compared to bolus delivery of unformulated therapeutics. Cryogels are m
content: ABSTRACT Biomaterial‐mediated drug delivery systems can improve therapeutic efficacy by extending local drug retention and reducing the need for repeated administration compared to bolus delivery of unformulated therapeutics. Cryogels are macroporous, crosslinked polymer networks capable of releasing hydrophilic cargos; however, many cryogel systems exhibit substantial burst release, resulting in rapid cargo loss. This study investigated whether modifying cryogel architecture through multilayer design of a macro‐sized cryogel could reduce burst release and provide tunable release kinetics while proposing new capabilities such as sequential release of multiple cargoes. Single‐, double‐, and triple‐layer methacrylate‐alginate cryogels were fabricated with fluorescent IgG Fab fragments as cargo localized within a central core layer and surrounded by one or more outer diffusion‐barrier layers. Release profiles were analyzed using the Korsmeyer–Peppas model to characterize early‐stage release and the Weibull model to assess full release behavior. Increasing layer number progressively reduced burst release and prolonged release duration. Approximated times required to achieve 50% cumulative release ( t 50 ) increased from 4.3 h for single‐layer cryogels to 19.9 and 43.3 h for double‐ and triple‐layer cryogels, respectively, demonstrating substantial control over release kinetics through architectural design. Model fitting further revealed systematic changes in release parameters associated with increasing architectural complexity, indicating that cryogel structure can be used to slow and delay release kinetics. To facilitate the rational design of future delivery systems, we developed a new correlation using the Weibull parameters that accurately predicted protein release performance in higher‐order multilayer cryogels. A preliminary prediction of triple‐layer cryogel release based on Weibull parameters obtained from single‐ and double‐layer systems showed agreement with the experimentally measured profile, with a mean absolute error of 4.7 percentage points in fractional release. These findings support further investigation of empirical release models as tools for guiding multilayer cryogel design, although additional independent validation is needed. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that multilayer cryogel architecture provides a simple yet effective strategy for controlling therapeutic release and highlight the utility of extending existing mathematical models for predicting and optimizing biomaterial‐mediated drug delivery systems.

title: TCMFE-Net for robust tree species identification from terrestrial and personal laser scanning data: the impact of feature fusion and sampling strategies
summary: While terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) and personal laser scanning (PLS) provide high-quality forest data, accurate tree species identification remains challenged by the trade-off between geometric detail and computational scalability. This
content: While terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) and personal laser scanning (PLS) provide high-quality forest data, accurate tree species identification remains challenged by the trade-off between geometric detail and computational scalability. This study presents TCMFE-Net, an object-level deep learning framework featuring a general multi-feature fusion and extraction unit (GMFE-Unit), which combines XYZ coordinates with raw reflectance intensity. Evaluated on the TocknerPLS and STPCTLS datasets, comprising major coniferous and deciduous species (including spruce, pine, beech and oak), TCMFE-Net achieves overall accuracies of 94.5% and 94.9%, respectively, yielding competitive advantages over conventional machine learning and state-of-the-art transformer-based architectures. A systematic analysis of sampling strategies reveals that while farthest point sampling (FPS) maintains skeletal quality, random sampling (RS) provides a three times increase in inference speed. The effectiveness of global feature aggregation depends on structural preservation; while global descriptors improve performance under FPS, they may introduce noise under RS. However, the fusion of raw intensity features offsets structural information loss in RS, achieving a better trade-off between precision and efficiency. These results demonstrate the potential of TCMFE-Net for automated single-tree species classification in close-range forest surveys. The implementation is available at: https://github.com/LiTao-0797/TCMFE-Net.

title: Bangladesh's Shrimp Sector: Export Trends, Value Chain Linkages, and Road to Sustainable Growth
summary: ABSTRACT Shrimp is among the most economically significant commodities in global aquaculture, representing approximately 16% by value of globally traded aquatic animal products. Bangladesh has historically been a major producer and exporter
content: ABSTRACT Shrimp is among the most economically significant commodities in global aquaculture, representing approximately 16% by value of globally traded aquatic animal products. Bangladesh has historically been a major producer and exporter, with its industry dominated by black tiger shrimp ( Penaeus monodon ) and giant freshwater prawn ( Macrobrachium rosenbergii ). However, growing structural, environmental, and institutional challenges threaten the sector's sustainability and international competitiveness. This study presents a comprehensive sectoral assessment of Bangladesh's shrimp industry amid post‐COVID market disruptions, accelerating climate‐related risks, and intensifying competition from Litopenaeus vannamei ‐based systems in major competing nations. The analysis integrates 40 years of secondary statistics with large‐scale primary survey data ( n = 8924). The study examines the historical development of shrimp farming, production and export trends, supply chain and value chain structure, post‐harvest losses, and sectoral challenges. Key findings reveal that total farm‐system production has increased through both area expansion and improvements in average yield, although traditional shrimp farming continues to face productivity constraints relative to more intensive systems in competing countries. Bangladesh's share of the global shrimp export market has declined substantially, while post‐harvest losses remain a significant and largely preventable economic burden. Additional constraints include fragmented value‐chain coordination, weak traceability and quality assurance systems, and slow adoption of modern aquaculture technologies. The study also identifies the recent introduction of L. vannamei as both an opportunity and a biosecurity challenge. The findings underscore the need for coordinated interventions by the government, the private sector, and development organizations to restore Bangladesh's global competitiveness in shrimp.

title: Leveraging ODA to advance agroforestry in the Global South: a review of barriers and enabling strategies
summary: Agroforestry systems offer a promising nature-based response to food insecurity, climate vulnerability, and land degradation in the Global South. However, adoption remains constrained by high establishment costs, delayed returns, management
content: Agroforestry systems offer a promising nature-based response to food insecurity, climate vulnerability, and land degradation in the Global South. However, adoption remains constrained by high establishment costs, delayed returns, management complexity, and insecure tenure. This semi-systematic integrative review proposes a framework to evaluate how Official Development Assistance (ODA) shapes agroforestry transitions. The review positions ODA at the intersection of agroforestry adoption scholarship, institutional and governance research, and development finance debates. It argues that ODA matters most when it functions as a de-risking mechanism that relaxes early-stage liquidity constraints, supports technical learning, and strengthens enabling institutions. At the same time, ODA is not a neutral transfer of resources: donor time horizons, reporting regimes, implementation channels, and climate-finance priorities shape whether projects create durable local capacity or only short-term compliance. Across the reviewed literature, ODA is consistently associated with supporting initial uptake, but evidence for long-term post-project sustainability is much weaker. More durable outcomes require longer funding horizons, regionally tailored interventions, long-term operational monitoring frameworks, and stronger local institutional ownership.

title: Heat transport, carbon mass balance and fluids origin in the Matese Massif chain (southern Italian Apennine) inferred from chemical and isotopic data
summary: This study presents a comprehensive hydrogeochemical characterization of the Matese Massif carbonate aquifer system (Southern Apennines, Italy), based on original field samples collected during the 2018–2020 period. Hydrochemical and isotop
content: This study presents a comprehensive hydrogeochemical characterization of the Matese Massif carbonate aquifer system (Southern Apennines, Italy), based on original field samples collected during the 2018–2020 period. Hydrochemical and isotopic analyses were carried out on 109 groundwater samples (springs and wells) to quantify heat discharge and flux of endogenous carbon (C deep ). The heat flux discharged by the aquifer system was estimated at ~250 MW with the primary contribution originating from basal discharge zones. Thermal anomalies, defined by the difference between infiltration and discharge temperatures, indicate a mean geothermal warming of ~2.2 °C, consistent with geothermal gradient interactions during circulation. The deep CO 2 flux was estimated at approximately 540 tons/day, underscoring the magnitude of deep degassing in tectonically active non-volcanic settings. Isotopic signatures (δD, δ 18 O) confirm the meteoric origin of the Matese Massif groundwater, while δ 13 C and noble gases isotope reveal mixing processes between shallow meteoric/atmospheric components and deep-seated crustal/mantle fluids. Specifically, emissions in the northwestern sector of the Matese Massif exhibit isotopic signatures similar to the Roman Magmatic Province, whereas the south-eastern sector aligns with the Campanian Magmatic Province. These findings identify the Matese Massif as a structural and geochemical pivot separating two distinct regional degassing domains. We propose that the Quaternary extensional regime, superimposed on the Apennine subduction structural framework, controls the upwelling of mantle-derived fluids along major lithospheric discontinuities. The carbon and heat budgets of the Matese Massif provide critical quantitative constraints for better understanding the deep degassing mechanisms within active carbonate orogens.

title: Cave ecosystems as drivers of viral diversity, endemism, and ecological function at a global scale
summary: Caves are subterranean ecosystems that host diverse microbial communities involved in key biogeochemical processes. Yet, the diversity and ecological roles of viruses within these systems remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed metageno
content: Caves are subterranean ecosystems that host diverse microbial communities involved in key biogeochemical processes. Yet, the diversity and ecological roles of viruses within these systems remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed metagenomic data collected from 30 globally distributed cave systems, identifying 8,176 viral operational taxonomic units (≥ 10kb size) that have little representation within a recent database of environmental viruses. In addition, cave-specific environmental fingerprints are shown to be a strong driver of viral distribution, reflected in a high degree of endemism both within and across cave systems. Viral-host associations suggest that viruses are primarily associated with Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota lineages, the most abundant groups across all samples and involved in diverse carbon, sulfur, and nitrogen metabolisms. The high proportion of lytic viruses targeting these groups suggests strong top-down viral control, with virus-mediated microbial turnover likely contributing to organic matter recycling. This is further supported by lytic viruses carrying the majority of auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs), with functions related to enhancing viral progeny production by increasing resource availability and reallocating cellular resources toward viral replication. In this study, we highlight how cave environments shape viral ecology and unveil a still yet unknown component of the subsurface virosphere.

title: Ten challenges for modeling and analysis of geothermal thermal energy networks
summary: Geothermal thermal energy networks (TENs) offer a pathway to low-temperature, multisource heating and cooling systems that integrate geothermal exchange, waste heat recovery, and seasonal storage. This paper synthesizes 10 recurring challen
content: Geothermal thermal energy networks (TENs) offer a pathway to low-temperature, multisource heating and cooling systems that integrate geothermal exchange, waste heat recovery, and seasonal storage. This paper synthesizes 10 recurring challenges that limit comparable modeling, techno-economic assessment, and scalable deployment of geothermal TENs. By consolidating insights across disciplines and early deployments, this work identifies barriers and highlights priorities for advancing TEN analysis and implementation, including standardized definitions, cross-sector planning frameworks, validated component models, and improved field data. These insights support consistent evaluation and informed decision-making for TEN planning and deployment.

title: Weathering Flux Calculations From Climate Model Outputs Show a Decrease in Alkalinity Fluxes to the Ocean During the Last Deglaciation
summary: Abstract Variations in chemical weathering rates during the last deglaciation remain poorly constrained, although some studies suggest little net change because climatic and sea‐level changes act in opposite directions. Here, we use climate
content: Abstract Variations in chemical weathering rates during the last deglaciation remain poorly constrained, although some studies suggest little net change because climatic and sea‐level changes act in opposite directions. Here, we use climate model outputs to calculate weathering fluxes with empirical equations, estimating their impacts on the deglacial evolution of riverine alkalinity fluxes to the ocean. With our model ensemble, we obtain a decreasing trend of alkalinity fluxes, resulting from loess erosion and flooding shelves (whose effects are counteracting those of a climate getting warmer and wetter). Such a reduction in alkalinity source could affect the marine carbon cycle, contributing to the deglacial atmospheric increase. Our results also underline the need for further model development to reduce runoff biases and implement evolving coastlines in Earth System Models, as well as the importance of a good representation of lithological data.

title: SSG-GAN: spatial-spectral guided generative adversarial network for hyperspectral reconstruction from RGB images
summary: Hyperspectral reconstruction from a single RGB image provides a practical and low-cost solution for spectral imaging with conventional cameras. However, the task is highly ill-posed because three broad RGB channels must be mapped to multipl
content: Hyperspectral reconstruction from a single RGB image provides a practical and low-cost solution for spectral imaging with conventional cameras. However, the task is highly ill-posed because three broad RGB channels must be mapped to multiple continuous narrow spectral bands. Existing methods, including convolutional, Transformer-based, multi-scale, and adversarial reconstruction models, have improved reconstruction accuracy, but many of them still learn RGB spatial structures and hyperspectral reconstruction features in a coupled reconstruction stream, while adversarial constraints mainly focus on spatial distributions. To address these issues, we propose SSG-GAN, a spatially guided hyperspectral reconstruction framework. The generator explicitly decouples RGB spatial-prior extraction from hyperspectral reconstruction through a dedicated multi-scale guidance branch. At corresponding decoding stages, a Cross-Branch Spatial-Spectral Attention (CB-SSA) module uses guidance-derived spatial weights to modulate reconstruction features and further refines them through feature-channel modulation and channel recalibration. Moreover, the discriminator incorporates a dedicated pixel-wise spectral-vector branch to evaluate joint band responses, providing complementary adversarial supervision alongside the multi-scale spatial branches. Experiments on CAVE, Harvard, and ICVL demonstrate the competitive performance of SSG-GAN. Specifically, it achieves MRAE/SAM/RMSE values of 0.0605/0.0734/0.0177 on CAVE, 0.0393/0.0294/0.0041 on Harvard, and 0.0303/0.0309/0.00101 on ICVL.

title: Radial growth and their responses to environmental factors of four major afforestation species after returning farmland to forest in Southwest China
summary: To elucidate radial growth variation and differences in climatic responses among coexisting tree species, this study, based on 2024 monitoring data of stem radial variation, compared the growing-season phenology, stem radial growth, and env
content: To elucidate radial growth variation and differences in climatic responses among coexisting tree species, this study, based on 2024 monitoring data of stem radial variation, compared the growing-season phenology, stem radial growth, and environmental factors response characteristics of four tree species ( Liquidambar formosana (FX), Melia azedarach (KL), Cryptomeria japonica var. sinensis (LS), and Camptotheca acuminata (XS)). The results showed that: (1) M. azedarach exhibited the longest growing season (168 ± 9.9 days), L. formosana was intermediate (131 ± 4.04 days), and C. japonica var. sinensis and C. acuminata were shorter (117–121 days). (2) In terms of annual increment, KL1 had the highest annual cumulative increment (3.21 mm), followed by FX1 (3.18 mm), whereas C. japonica var. sinensis and C. acuminata were lower (XS2 only 0.38 mm); (3) The growth of L. formosana was primarily driven by air temperature and photosynthetically active radiation (correlation coefficients of FX2 with air temperature, soil temperature reached 0.75–0.82), while KL2, C. japonica var. sinensis , and C. acuminata were more regulated by precipitation and soil moisture. Based on these results, M. azedarach is recommended for sites with stable moisture conditions and strong soil water-holding capacity, whereas L. formosana is suitable for sunny slopes with adequate heat and radiation and good drainage. C. japonica var. sinensis and C. acuminata showed low growth but considerable intraspecific variation, and may possess survival advantages on degraded sites subject to frequent water stress. In terms of planting configuration, the approximately two-month offset in growth peaks between C. japonica var. sinensis and L. formosana suggests that mixed plantations of the two may form a complementary resource-use pattern. This study can provide a scientific basis for the selection and configuration of coexisting tree species.

title: Ecologically safe microplastic removal from saline water via temperature and buoyancy separation
summary: Abstract Although microplastics affect the atmosphere–ocean carbon cycle, the health of marine ecosystems, and pollute the food chain, existing microplastic removal methods cannot cope in the presence of microorganisms, particularly when th
content: Abstract Although microplastics affect the atmosphere–ocean carbon cycle, the health of marine ecosystems, and pollute the food chain, existing microplastic removal methods cannot cope in the presence of microorganisms, particularly when there is an overlap in size. This is a technical challenge for the bio-friendly extraction of microplastics using conventional mechanical methods, such as a mesh. Here, we introduce a mesh-free, ecologically safe method that combines thermotactic and geotactic migration of biological species with controlled hydrodynamics to selectively separate microorganisms and microplastics of overlapping size. The microorganisms were one-day-old Artemia nauplii, an aquatic crustacean, and the microplastics were polyethylene spheres with a similar size range, approximately 307 µm to 450 µm. By controlling the temperature differential in a rectangular channel flow up to 30 K and its flow rate up to 1208 mL min−1, a continuous process was achieved with microplastic removal efficiency and microorganism recovery rates as high as 90.4% and 70.7%, respectively. We report the trade-off between separation performance and the specific energy consumption, the latter being as low as 4.67 kWh m−3. Requiring no additional separation agents or functional materials, our method can provide a simple approach for sustainable, bio-friendly, in-situ microplastic remediation.

title: Territorial performance and policy priorities in Atlantic Canada: A regional attractiveness assessment
summary: This paper applies the OECD Regional Attractiveness framework to four Atlantic Canadian sub-regions, Southeast New Brunswick, Halifax Regional Municipality, St. John's and Prince Edward Island, benchmarking more than 30 indicators against A
content: This paper applies the OECD Regional Attractiveness framework to four Atlantic Canadian sub-regions, Southeast New Brunswick, Halifax Regional Municipality, St. John's and Prince Edward Island, benchmarking more than 30 indicators against Atlantic Canada, Canada and OECD regions. International migration has become the principal driver of population and labour-force growth as new sectoral opportunities reshape the region's economic prospects. The analysis finds a common base of assets, favourable labour-force participation, high tertiary attainment, strong digital connectivity and natural endowments, alongside uneven productivity and innovation and disparities that fall hardest on rural and remote communities. Two thematic deep dives follow: talent migration amid persistent retention challenges, and industrial resilience through export diversification and locally prioritised strategies, drawing on international good-practice examples that demonstrate how policy ambitions can translate into measurable implementation. The paper makes the case for place-based policy that builds on local assets while addressing the barriers constraining communities' capacity to attract and retain talent, investment and economic activity.

title: Antecedent drought exposure weakens vegetation decline without promoting recovery
summary: Abstract Repeated drought can alter vegetation responses to subsequent water stress, but whether reduced canopy decline is accompanied by improved recovery remains unresolved. We analysed global leaf area index and meteorological drought re
content: Abstract Repeated drought can alter vegetation responses to subsequent water stress, but whether reduced canopy decline is accompanied by improved recovery remains unresolved. We analysed global leaf area index and meteorological drought records for 1982–2020 using an event-based framework that separately quantified detectable declines in canopy leaf area, standardized leaf-area losses and recovery to pre-drought conditions. Antecedent drought frequency and cumulative severity were evaluated over five historical windows spanning 12–60 months, alongside the interval since the previous drought. After adjustment for current-drought characteristics and environmental conditions, greater antecedent frequency and severity were associated with lower odds of a clear negative LAI response and smaller losses across all five windows. In contrast, associations with recovery were weak and inconsistent across exposure windows. For the 60-month frequency measure, adjusted predictions from zero to six prior events indicated decreases of 3.7 percentage points in response probability and 0.15 standard deviations in leaf-area loss, while modelled recovery probability within 24 months decreased by only 0.8 percentage points. Associations differed among vegetation groups and forest types, with smaller losses accompanying either faster or slower recovery. Baseline adjustment and recovery sensitivity analyses broadly supported this separation between decline and recovery. These modest observational associations do not establish adaptation or a specific ecological memory mechanism. They show that muted canopy decline alone is insufficient evidence of improved drought resilience and support evaluating impact and recovery separately when assessing vegetation responses to recurrent drought.

title: Phytobarriers reduce the dispersion of particulate matter associated with potentially toxic elements
summary: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) poses risks to human health and the environment because wind can disperse it and carry it far from its emission source. This study evaluated the capacity of plant species to retain PM associated with potenti
content: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) poses risks to human health and the environment because wind can disperse it and carry it far from its emission source. This study evaluated the capacity of plant species to retain PM associated with potentially toxic elements (PTEs). Twenty-six sampling sites were selected along the Peñon–Texcoco and Anillo Periférico Roads to collect soil and leaf samples. In soil, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and pseudototal PTEs concentrations after aqua regia digestion. In plant tissues, PTEs were quantified after sulfuric and perchloric acid digestion. The phytobarrier index (PI) was calculated based on PTE concentrations in washed and unwashed leaves. Species with the highest PI values were characterized using environmental scanning electron microscopy, and particles were analyzed using ImageJ software. The soil had slightly alkaline pH, with EC values ranging from 0.58 to 29.51 dS m − 1 . The mean concentrations of Pb, Cd, Zn, and Mn were 27.8, 1.3, 140, and 278 mg kg⁻¹, respectively. PTE concentrations in plant tissue were consistently higher in unwashed leaves than in washed leaves, indicating atmospheric PM deposition. Micrographs confirmed the presence of particles, predominantly smaller than 10 µm. Tamarix sp. and Eucalyptus sp. showed the highest particle retention; however, site conditions favor Tamarix sp. establishment. The results indicate that vegetation in is a viable alternative for mitigating PM dispersion associated with PTEs.

title: Characterizing autothermal reformer operating conditions for inline integration with a solid oxide fuel cell stack
summary: High-power density solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems running on hydrocarbon fuels warrant compact upstream fuel reforming and reactant preheating to minimize system size and startup time. To that end, this work investigates a CH 4 -fuele
content: High-power density solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems running on hydrocarbon fuels warrant compact upstream fuel reforming and reactant preheating to minimize system size and startup time. To that end, this work investigates a CH 4 -fueled autothermal reformer/heat exchanger (ATR/HX) designed for inline integration directly upstream of an SOFC stack, where mildly exothermic catalytic oxidative reforming simultaneously drives H 2 production for the SOFC anode and air preheating for the SOFC cathode. A quasi-1D ATR/HX model with detailed reforming chemistry guides reactor sizing and selection of operating conditions for controlled partial reforming and effective thermal integration. Modeling results indicate that an in-line reactor length of 3.6 cm sufficiently preheats the anode and cathode streams from 400 ∘ C to 550 -- 650 ∘ C with a cathode air outlet approach temperature of < 30 ∘ C to support high-power-density performance for SOFC cells with thin-film yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) or gadolinium-doped ceria (GDC) electrolytes. Experiments at atmospheric pressure demonstrate stable ATR light-off ≤ 450 ∘ C in a single-cell configuration and near 400 ∘ C in a 3-cell short-stack configuration. These experiments characterize the ATR/HX subsystem in SOFC-relevant hardware but do not constitute validation with an electrochemically active SOFC stack. The model and experimental tests show that the compact ATR/HX operates under residence-time-limited conditions, enabling efficient thermal conditioning while preserving residual CH 4 for downstream internal reforming within the SOFC anode. These results demonstrate the feasibility of compact inline ATR/HX integration and establish operating guidelines for subsequent thermally integrated SOFC systems with reduced startup time and improved system compactness.

title: Gas-phase Formation and Destruction Routes of the Silicon Monophosphide (SiP) Radical
summary: Abstract The silicon monophosphide radical (SiP) was recently reported in the circumstellar envelope of the carbon-rich asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star IRC+10216; however, its chemistry remains essentially unconstrained. Here we present
content: Abstract The silicon monophosphide radical (SiP) was recently reported in the circumstellar envelope of the carbon-rich asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star IRC+10216; however, its chemistry remains essentially unconstrained. Here we present the first systematic study of the gas-phase formation and destruction of SiP through reactions with the most abundant atoms in circumstellar and interstellar gas (H, N, O, and C) and the corresponding silicon- and phosphorus-bearing diatomics. Using explicitly correlated coupled-cluster calculations we map the [Si, P, X] (X = H, N, O, C) potential energy surfaces for all relevant spin states and dissociation channels. We find that SiP forms exothermically and barrierlessly only via Si + PH ⟶ SiP + H and P + SiH ⟶ SiP + H, whereas reactions with N, O, and C destroy it without a barrier, converting it into more strongly bound diatomics, such as PN, SiO, and SiC. Incorporating these reactions into the Nautilus astrochemical code, we model SiP in warm, evolved gas and find that its abundance rises steeply with temperature but that efficient destruction by N and O keeps it well below the value observed in IRC+10216. SiP destruction mechanisms are kinetically competitive, undermining the predicted gas-phase abundance and again pointing to grain-surface formation and nonthermal desorption as necessary formation routes for phosphorus chemistry in interstellar and circumstellar environments.

title: Thermal Transport in Composite Thermoelectrics: From Phonon Scattering Mechanisms to Device Reliability
summary: Composite materials provide a versatile platform for suppressing lattice thermal conductivity through secondary phases and engineered interfaces that effectively scatter phonons while minimizing deterioration of electronic transport, offeri
content: Composite materials provide a versatile platform for suppressing lattice thermal conductivity through secondary phases and engineered interfaces that effectively scatter phonons while minimizing deterioration of electronic transport, offering a promising route toward high‐performance thermoelectrics. Herein, we systematically review how composite architectures manipulate thermal transport and enhance the thermoelectric figure of merit. We begin with classical phonon theory to understand the thermal transport in single phase. By establishing performance benchmarks for pristine matrix, we then compare various reported composite thermoelectric materials across low‐, mid‐, and high‐temperature regimes. The experimental trends are rationalized by the mean‐field theory, interfacial mechanisms (acoustic mismatch model and diffuse mismatch model), and nanostructure‐induced size effects. Next, we examine different compositing strategies to modulate the phononic contribution to thermal conductivity, including porous structure, nanoprecipitates, magnetic phases, crystalline–amorphous hybrid, and superlattice. Extending from materials to thermoelectric devices, we discuss the critical challenges associated with incorporating composite thermoelectric materials into thermoelectric devices, with particular emphasis on non‐uniform heat field, and thermal expansion mismatch for device reliability and operational stability. Finally, we outline practical design principles, highlighting opportunities for reproducible materials fabrication, interface engineering, and synergistic optimization of phonon and carrier transport to accelerate the development of next‐generation composite thermoelectrics.

title: Understanding Nonreacting Substrate Analogs as Potential Scaffolds for Inhibitor Design Against Mycobacterium t uberculosis Cystathionine β‐Synthase
summary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis cystathionine beta‐synthase ( Mtb CBS), a pyridoxal‐5′‐phosphate (PLP)‐dependent enzyme, regulates sulfur metabolism and redox homeostasis, making it a model enzyme for inhibition studies and to understand scaffol
content: Mycobacterium tuberculosis cystathionine beta‐synthase ( Mtb CBS), a pyridoxal‐5′‐phosphate (PLP)‐dependent enzyme, regulates sulfur metabolism and redox homeostasis, making it a model enzyme for inhibition studies and to understand scaffold behavior. Amino acids remains as an attractive scaffold for designing novel inhibitors having reduced cytotoxicity and improved properties for cellular uptake. This study integrates computational, biophysical, and structural approaches to provide for a potential scaffold that could be further modified to inhibit Mtb CBS. Structure‐based sequence alignment of CBS homologs identified seven conserved polar/charged regions critical for PLP‐substrate interactions. Molecular docking of polar substrate analogs (threonine, histidine, glutamic acid, and arginine) at the conserved active site revealed distinct binding modes for histidine, glutamic acid, and arginine. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated persistent binding of histidine, stabilized by hydrophobic interactions relative to other analogs. Experimental studies revealed histidine’s ability to form stable external aldimine adducts, modulating enzyme thermostability (Δ T m ), akin to known reacting substrates. Finally, cryo‐EM‐based structural studies revealed two classes of Mtb CBS, one with extra density suggesting the noncovalently bound histidine and the unbound WT Mtb CBS maintaining internal aldimine. This suggests that exploration of the chemical modification space of the histidine moiety might provide us with a potential inhibitor against Mtb CBS and enzymes of the RTS pathway.

title: Integrated ethanol‐targeted fermentation and methane recovery from the carbohydrate‐rich soluble fraction of municipal organic waste
summary: Abstract Mexico City generates more than 12 400 t of municipal solid waste daily, of which 54% is organic. This waste stream contains 350–620 g carbohydrate kg VS −1 , and volatile solids (VS) account for up to 80% of total solids, making i
content: Abstract Mexico City generates more than 12 400 t of municipal solid waste daily, of which 54% is organic. This waste stream contains 350–620 g carbohydrate kg VS −1 , and volatile solids (VS) account for up to 80% of total solids, making it a promising substrate for biofuel production. Reported yields reach 12 g COD L −1 of ethanol and 545 normal liters of methane per kilogram of VS (NL CH 4 kg VS −1 , at 273.15 K and 101.325 kPa), equivalent to 0.545 m 3 CH4 kg VS −1 , exceeding the average methane recovery from the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW) in other countries. The main objective of this research was to valorize the liquid fraction extracted from OFMSW to promote ethanol‐oriented fermentation and subsequently recover methane through anaerobic digestion. The methodology comprised: (1) water extraction and physicochemical characterization; (2) batch fermentations using Saccharomyces cerevisiae at different concentrations, temperatures, and durations; and (3) anaerobic digestion assays to evaluate methane recovery from the unfermented and fermented liquid fractions. Ethanol production increased significantly with yeast addition, although the effects of temperature and time were dependent on conditions. The highest ethanol concentration (5.5 g L −1 ) was obtained at 37 °C after 72 h with 20% yeast, whereas the most efficient configuration occurred at 30 °C after 30 h with 20% yeast, providing higher selectivity and volumetric productivity while preserving residual chemical oxygen demand (COD) for subsequent methane recovery. Fermentation performed with indigenous microorganisms alone resulted predominantly in lactic acid accumulation (12 g L −1 , 30 °C, 72 h). Methanization assays showed that prefermentation of the liquid fraction for 72 h at 37 °C consistently enhanced methane yields by 48% (683 g VS −1 ) compared with unfermented substrates. These findings demonstrate that controlled, yeast‐assisted fermentation can balance ethanol production with subsequent methane recovery, supporting an integrated biorefinery approach for urban OFMSW.

title: Numerical Prediction of Climate Impacts from Nijgadh International Airport Construction
summary: Serious climatic and environmental concerns have been raised regarding the construction of Nijgadh International Airport (NIA), which would require clearing approximately 2.5 million trees from a pristine flatland forest located about 60 km
content: Serious climatic and environmental concerns have been raised regarding the construction of Nijgadh International Airport (NIA), which would require clearing approximately 2.5 million trees from a pristine flatland forest located about 60 km south of Kathmandu. The potential climate impacts of the deforesting the area have been assessed using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model simulated meteorological fields validated with observed data. The findings, though a short-term assessment during late winter time, indicate that deforesting the NIA development area would lead to increased urban heat stagnation, a drier near-surface atmosphere, and reduced wind speeds. Notably, the near-surface daily average air temperature is projected to rise by 1.5°C, with an even more pronounced increase of 2.8°C in the minimum temperature. These changes, though a part of short-term assessment, suggest a significant shift in the local climate in and around the NIA, underscoring the environmental risks associated with the project

title: Dataset of carbon density and carbon sink potential of Larix olgensis plantations in Heilongjiang Province, China
summary: This dataset is derived from the measured data of 680 fixed monitoring plots of Larix olgensis plantation in Heilongjiang Province, covering three surveys in 2012, 2021, and 2022. The plot area is 0.06 ha. For trees with a diameter at breas
content: This dataset is derived from the measured data of 680 fixed monitoring plots of Larix olgensis plantation in Heilongjiang Province, covering three surveys in 2012, 2021, and 2022. The plot area is 0.06 ha. For trees with a diameter at breast height ≥ 5 cm, each tree is measured and recorded for species, status, diameter at breast height, tree height, live branch height, and crown width. The dataset consists of 9 fields: plot number, forest age, average breast height diameter, average tree height, cross-sectional area, plant density, rank index (SCI), stand density index (SDI), and carbon density (CD), with the region to which the plot belongs (Xiaoxing'an Ridge, Zhangguangcai Ridge, Laoye Ridge, Wanda Mountain, western Songnen Plain) attached. The carbon density is estimated by combining a univariate biomass model with carbon content, the stand density index is calculated by a formula, and the rank index is fitted with a guiding curve for calculation.

title: Synergistic helium trapping at grain/interphase boundaries and intrinsic carbon vacancies in Ti3SiC2-derived TiCx/M6C co-reinforced GH3535 alloy
summary: Helium bubble swelling remains a critical challenge for nickel-based structural alloys in high-temperature nuclear reactors. An in-situ strategy via spark plasma sintering-triggered Ti 3 SiC 2 MAX phase decomposition is proposed to fabricat
content: Helium bubble swelling remains a critical challenge for nickel-based structural alloys in high-temperature nuclear reactors. An in-situ strategy via spark plasma sintering-triggered Ti 3 SiC 2 MAX phase decomposition is proposed to fabricate a GH3535 composite reinforced by carbon-vacancy-rich TiC x nanoparticles and micron-scale M 6 C carbides. 1.2 MeV He + irradiation at 750 °C (fluence: 2 × 10 16 ions/cm 2 ) was used to evaluate irradiation resistance. Compared with monolithic GH3535, the composite exhibits 46 % smaller average helium bubble size and 80 % lower bubble volume fraction in the peak damage zone. Multi-scale characterizations combined with first-principles calculations reveal a synergistic helium trapping mechanism: grain boundaries formed by grain refinement and TiC x /M 6 C/matrix interfaces act as efficient trapping sites, while intrinsic carbon vacancies in non-stoichiometric TiC x serve as additional deep helium traps. Calculations further verify that high concentrations of such vacancies reduce helium migration barriers, potentially facilitating helium redistribution among carbon-vacancy sites. Different from prior studies focusing mainly on interfacial helium trapping, this work highlights the key role of carbide lattice vacancies in suppressing helium bubble coarsening. This defect-engineering strategy via MAX phase in-situ decomposition offers a promising route for structural alloy design in high-temperature molten salt nuclear systems.

title: The OsERF39/OsNAC6 Transcription Factor Module Contributes to Rice Quality and Yield by Maintaining Methylglyoxal Homeostasis
summary: The biosynthesis of starch largely determines rice quality and yield, and is regulated by numerous transcription factors (TFs). Methylglyoxal (MG), a toxic byproduct of glycolysis and the Calvin cycle, accumulates during starch biosynthesis
content: The biosynthesis of starch largely determines rice quality and yield, and is regulated by numerous transcription factors (TFs). Methylglyoxal (MG), a toxic byproduct of glycolysis and the Calvin cycle, accumulates during starch biosynthesis and requires efficient glyoxalase-mediated detoxification for normal grain development. However, how TFs regulate MG homeostasis and modulate rice quality and yield remains largely unexplored. Here, we show that two transcription factors, OsERF39 and OsNAC6, physically interact to form a complex that directly binds to and activates OsGLYI7, encoding a plastid-localized glyoxalase I (GlyI). Loss-of-function mutations in OsERF39, OsNAC6, or OsGLYI7 markedly reduce GlyI activity, trigger MG overaccumulation and redox imbalance in leaves and developing endosperm. These metabolic perturbations compromise transitory and storage starch biosynthesis, reduce nitrogen (protein) accumulation, aggravate grain chalkiness, and decrease grain weight and yield. Collectively, our findings establish the OsERF39/OsNAC6-OsGLYI7 pathway as a critical regulatory node for MG detoxification, sustaining MG and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis to support carbon and nitrogen assimilation in both source and sink organs, uncovering a TF-mediated mechanism linking MG metabolism to rice grain quality and yield and advancing our understanding of its underlying regulatory basis.

title: Lithology Is Strongly Associated With Soil Free‐Living N 2 Fixation in Subtropical Forests
summary: ABSTRACT Free‐living N 2 fixation (FLNF) mediated by soil diazotrophs constitutes a fundamental nitrogen (N) input, critically shaping N availability within terrestrial ecosystems. Despite its ecological importance, the determinants of FLNF
content: ABSTRACT Free‐living N 2 fixation (FLNF) mediated by soil diazotrophs constitutes a fundamental nitrogen (N) input, critically shaping N availability within terrestrial ecosystems. Despite its ecological importance, the determinants of FLNF across distinct lithological types in karst forest ecosystems remain insufficiently elucidated. In this study, we delved into the patterns, predictors, and underlying mechanisms of soil FLNF within two typical karst forests situated on limestone (LS) and dolostone (DS), alongside a proximate non‐karst forest on clasolite (CS) in southwest China. By quantifying FLNF (indicated by acetylene reduction activity, ARA) rates, nifH gene (N fixation) abundance, and an array of soil, rock, and microbial properties, we uncovered significant associations of lithology with soil ARA and N‐fixing microbial abundance ( p < 0.001). Our results indicated that soil ARA in karst forests (DS and LS) was 2.3–4.7 times that in non‐karst forests (CS). Correlation and random forest analyses pinpointed soil reactive minerals (M d and M o ) and N‐fixing microorganisms ( nifH gene) abundance as primary predictors of ARA variability. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS‐PM) further demonstrated that lithology indirectly associated with ARA dynamics through pathways involving soil minerals (M e , M d , M o , M p , and Clay+Silt), N‐fixing microorganisms ( nifH gene) abundance, and microbial stoichiometric C/N balance (BG/(LAP+NAG)). These findings shed light on a comprehensive understanding of the intricate FLNF dynamics, highlighting the pivotal role of lithology in regulating soil N cycling in karst forest ecosystems.

title: Selection of classification methods and quantification of changes in extent of mangrove forests over 6 years (2019 - 2025) in Ninh Binh province
source: Journal of Forestry Science and Technology
summary: Mangrove forests in Ninh Binh Province, a key part of the Red River Delta, provide important ecological services but face significant mapping challenges due to complex land use and tidal dynamics. This study evaluates four classification me
content: Mangrove forests in Ninh Binh Province, a key part of the Red River Delta, provide important ecological services but face significant mapping challenges due to complex land use and tidal dynamics. This study evaluates four classification methods—Traditional RGB, NDVI thresholding, CMRI thresholding, and an Integrated Approach combining spectral bands with vegetation and water indices—using Sentinel-2 imageries (2019–2025) on the Google Earth Engine platform for a coastal area of 23,871.55 ha. Classification performance was assessed using User’s Accuracy, Producer’s Accuracy, Overall Accuracy (OA), the Kappa coefficient and the F1-Score. Findings indicate that the Integrated Approach, powered by a Random Forest algorithm, is the most robust, achieving an OA of 86.27–92.74%, Kappa coefficients of 0.78–0.88 and F1-Scores for the mangrove class of 91.16–99.50%. Unlike single-index methods (NDVI), which are sensitive to tidal submergence and underestimated the mangrove extent at only 2,576.23 ha in 2025, or RGB approaches that misclassify inland crops and overestimated the mangrove extent at up to 7,026.36 ha, the Integrated Approach effectively mitigates spectral confusion and spatial noise. Spatiotemporal analysis identified a stable core mangrove area of 3,750.05 ha out of 4,387.66 ha mapped in 2019, together with approximately 1,344.97 ha gained from non-mangrove areas, reflecting local restoration efforts. These findings underscore the necessity of multi-feature fusion (incorporating CMRI and MNDWI) for accurate coastal monitoring, providing a reliable framework for the sustainable management of Ninh Binh’s mangrove ecosystems.

title: Towards high-performance NiTiCu shape memory alloys: A new de-binding and sintering framework for sinter-based additive manufacturing
source: Journal of Alloys and Compounds Communications
summary: This study establishes a binder-jet additive manufacturing (BJAM) processing framework for NiTiCu shape memory alloys (SMAs), with emphasis on de-binding, contamination control, sintering, densification, and phase constitution. Mechanically
content: This study establishes a binder-jet additive manufacturing (BJAM) processing framework for NiTiCu shape memory alloys (SMAs), with emphasis on de-binding, contamination control, sintering, densification, and phase constitution. Mechanically mixed (NiTi + Cu) and ultrasonic-plasma-atomized pre-alloyed powders containing 3-18 wt.% Cu were investigated. Three static curing/de-binding schedules in argon and air were compared with a fluctuating air-vacuum route. Static argon gave the lowest bulk oxygen (0.27-0.67 wt.%) but relies on inert pyrolysis, whereas static air raised oxygen to 0.88-3.59 wt.%. The fluctuating route produced uniform oxidation, residual carbon of only 0.031-0.050 wt.%, and oxygen of ≈0.8-1.0 wt.% (mixed) and ≈0.5-0.9 wt.% (pre-alloyed), lower than static air in 22 of 24 condition-matched comparisons. Mixed powders densified by transient liquid-phase sintering within a narrow 1170-1180 °C window, with the best shape retention and density (up to 96.0%) at 8-13 wt.% Cu, whereas pre-alloyed powders densified by solid-state sintering at 1250 °C to 97.0% (3 wt.% Cu) and 98.5% (8 wt.% Cu) without Cu pooling. XRD and EBSD showed a continuous B2/B19′ NiTi-based matrix with fine, isolated Ti₂Cu/TiC particles in the optimized conditions. The weak and broadened DSC response of the as-sintered parts is rationalized quantitatively by Ti scavenging by residual oxygen and carbon, the Ti-lean nominal stoichiometry, and local compositional heterogeneity, which defines clear routes towards functional recovery. The observations are condensed into a composition-processing map, and their implications for mechanical properties and for scaling to larger components are discussed.

title: A Lattice Boltzmann-based model for porous domains in electrochemical systems
summary: The performance of electrochemical energy conversion devices depends heavily on the coupled transport and reaction phenomena that occur within porous electrodes. In this study, we present a pore-scale Lattice Boltzmann (LBM) framework that
content: The performance of electrochemical energy conversion devices depends heavily on the coupled transport and reaction phenomena that occur within porous electrodes. In this study, we present a pore-scale Lattice Boltzmann (LBM) framework that integrates incompressible fluid flow, advection-diffusion transport of electroactive species, and Butler-Volmer electrode kinetics into a unified computational model. Focusing on systems with excess supporting electrolyte allows us to neglect migration effects, resulting in a computationally efficient yet physically consistent description. A stochastic pore generation scheme enables independent control of porosity ( 0.1 ≤ ε ≤ 0.9 ), feature size, and anisotropy without relying on tomographic data. We validate the model against analytical Cottrell and Graetz solutions, and we find that concentration field errors stabilize below 1% after initial transients. Cyclic voltammetry simulations reveal a non-monotonic dependence of maximum current density on porosity. An optimum around ε = 0.5 results from the trade-off between active surface area and mass transport limitations. The proposed framework is a versatile, efficient tool for parametric investigations of porous electrode microstructures in electrochemical systems.

title: MgFe-LDHs improve soybean tolerance to saline-alkali stress and yield by enhancing chlorophyll metabolism and photosynthetic carbon metabolism
summary: Soil salinization and alkalization are globally expanding environmental stressors that severely constrain agricultural development. The application of nanotechnology offers new technical approaches for stress-resilient crop cultivation and
content: Soil salinization and alkalization are globally expanding environmental stressors that severely constrain agricultural development. The application of nanotechnology offers new technical approaches for stress-resilient crop cultivation and sustainable agricultural development. In this study, Magnesium-iron layered double hydroxide (MgFe-LDHs), with particles that have average lateral width of 426.5 nm in diameter and a zeta potential of +8.77 mV, was synthesized using a hydrothermal method. Two soybean cultivars with contrasting saline–alkali tolerance, HF50 (tolerant) and HN95 (sensitive), were used. Based on preliminary experiments, 20 mg L -1 was selected as the optimal concentration to investigate the effects foliar MgFe-LDHs application at the V3 stage on soybean growth and the underlying mechanisms. Compared with saline–alkali stress, MgFe-LDHs treatment significantly enhanced antioxidant defense and osmotic adjustment in soybean leaves, reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation, and increased plant dry matter accumulation. In addition, MgFe-LDHs increased chlorophyll content and enhanced light-energy absorption and electron transport capacity by modulating genes associated with porphyrin metabolism and chlorophyll biosynthesis. MgFe-LDHs also regulated starch and sucrose metabolism as well as galactose metabolism, increased the activities of enzymes that play central roles in carbon metabolism, improved carbohydrate accumulation and metabolic balance, and maintained carbon metabolic homeostasis. These physiological and metabolic effects increased the numbers of pods and seeds per plant, as well as yield per plant.

title: Isotope-assisted evaluation of zinc and iron retention and human absorption in processed cereal foods: A critical review
summary: Biofortification increases cereal zinc (Zn) and iron (Fe), but processing determines how much reaches the plate and is absorbed. This critical narrative review examines isotope methods for evaluating mineral retention and human absorption i
content: Biofortification increases cereal zinc (Zn) and iron (Fe), but processing determines how much reaches the plate and is absorbed. This critical narrative review examines isotope methods for evaluating mineral retention and human absorption in processed cereal foods. Enriched stable-isotope tracing follows a deliberately labelled mineral source. Natural-abundance analysis measures small isotope-ratio differences produced by physical or biological processes. We distinguish these methods from radioactive tracing and complementary elemental imaging. Milling and cooking studies quantify mineral losses, whereas human isotope trials assess absorption from the finished food. Published trials show that phytate degradation and improved laboratory bioaccessibility can produce much smaller changes in human absorption. We propose a sequence of mass-balance measurements, food-matrix characterization, label validation and selected human trials. The principal endpoint is the amount of mineral absorbed per consumed serving. This connects manufacturing choices with mineral delivery from the food people eat. Priorities include matched wheat and rice processing comparisons, validation of label exchange in the final food, and shared analytical facilities. Routine compositional assays can screen many products, with isotope studies resolving specific questions about mineral source or absorption.

title: Physiological, shoot mineral-composition, and growth responses of onion to combined microbial inoculation and N-rGO/FCNS exposure
summary: The shallow and sparsely branched root system of onion ( Allium cepa L.) makes crop performance highly responsive to rhizosphere management. An outdoor pot experiment used a factorial design to evaluate the individual and combined effects o
content: The shallow and sparsely branched root system of onion ( Allium cepa L.) makes crop performance highly responsive to rhizosphere management. An outdoor pot experiment used a factorial design to evaluate the individual and combined effects of introduced arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal (AMF) inoculum, Pseudomonas putida S1Pf1, and an intact nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide/Fe 3 Co 3 Ni 3 S 8 formulation (N-rGO/FCNS) on onion ( Allium cepa L.). Responses were assessed through gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, shoot mineral composition, plant growth, qualitative root morphology, total AMF colonization, soil spore abundance, and bulb dry mass. The combined AMF + P. putida + N-rGO/FCNS treatment (MPNG) produced the highest net CO 2 assimilation rate (15.23 μmol CO 2 m -2 s -1 versus 12.16 in the control). Bulb dry mass was greatest under MPNG and AMF + P. putida , with MPNG reaching 23.5 g bulb -1 compared with 16.0 g bulb -1 in the control. MPNG also produced the highest shoot N (4.68% versus 3.25%), P (0.46% versus 0.32%), and Fe (142.0 versus 125.7 mg kg -1 ) concentrations and total AMF root colonization (77.0% versus 44.0%). Significant three-way interactions were detected for net CO 2 assimilation, Fᵥ/F m , NPQ, and soil spore abundance. These results suggest microbial-context-dependent responses under the conditions tested. However, the experiment was limited to a single cultivar, one soil type, and three biological replicates, and lacked separate controls for the individual components of the N-rGO/FCNS formulation. Hydrodynamic particle size, zeta potential, dispersion stability and metal release were not determined; proposed nanoparticle-mediated mechanisms and nutrient-delivery processes therefore remain untested hypotheses. Cobalt (Co) and nickel (Ni) concentrations were not measured in harvested bulbs; their accumulation in edible tissue and associated food-safety risks were not assessed. MPNG should therefore be considered a treatment combination warranting further field and biosafety evaluation.

title: Piezo-Photocatalytic Effect in Biochar-Supported ZnO/TiO2 Nanofibers for Simultaneous Wastewater Treatment and Green Hydrogen Production
source: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
summary: The effluents from textile and dye industries contain organic matter which is costly to be treated, and the production of hydrogen continues to rely heavily on fossil feeds. Both these issues can be tackled by a single material, piezo-photo
content: The effluents from textile and dye industries contain organic matter which is costly to be treated, and the production of hydrogen continues to rely heavily on fossil feeds. Both these issues can be tackled by a single material, piezo-photocatalysis, as mechanical strain and light both work on the same semiconductor. We electrospun ZnO/TiO2 nanofibers loaded with rice-husk biochar (0, 5, 10 and 15 wt%) and evaluated the nanfibers for removal of methylene blue (MB) and hydrogen evolution using ultrasound (40 kHz, 120 W), simulated solar light and both combined. The loading of biochar at 10 wt% (BC10-ZT) showed the most favorable balance with the specific surface area increasing from 38.4 to 148.7 m² g⁻¹, the optical band gap decreasing from 3.05 to 2.88 eV, the photocurrent density increasing approximately 2.5-fold relative to biochar-free fibers, and the effective piezoelectric coefficient d33 increasing from 7.4 to 9.1 pm V⁻¹. The combination of ultrasound and light resulted in a pseudo-first order rate constant of 0.1214 min⁻¹, which is 1.99 times the sum of the two single-mode constants, and 97.4% of MB (20 mg L⁻¹) was removed in 30 minutes. For a mixed system, the rate of hydrogen evolution increased from 1496 µmol g⁻¹ h⁻¹ in 50 mg L⁻¹ MB to approximately 2.4 times the pure water rate, due to dye oxidation removing holes which would recombine. 905 µmol g-1 h-1 of H2 was produced along with 78.6% COD and 96.2% colour removal using real textile effluent. The 10-reuse cycle activity drop was just 12.7%. Biochar primarily functions as an electron shuttle and light-harvesting support that also provides the piezopotential which sharpens charge separation, as suggested by radical-trapping, impedance and statistical (ANOVA, Tukey HSD, regression) analyses.

title: A Perspective on the Capacity of Terrestrial Ecosystems for Carbon Sequestration: Methods, Uncertainty, and Research Priorities
summary: Terrestrial ecosystems are a major component of the global carbon cycle, yet their sequestration capacity is not directly observable as a single quantity. This review provides an overview of methods for estimating carbon stocks, stock chang
content: Terrestrial ecosystems are a major component of the global carbon cycle, yet their sequestration capacity is not directly observable as a single quantity. This review provides an overview of methods for estimating carbon stocks, stock changes, net exchanges, and additional sequestration potential across forests, grasslands, croplands, wetlands, and other vegetated lands. It synthesizes field inventories, eddy-covariance measurements, Earth-observation products, process-based and machine-learning models, atmospheric inversions, and hybrid approaches, emphasizing how pool boundaries and spatial and temporal support shape inference. Uncertainty arises from sampling and allometry, flux processing, sensor retrieval and scaling, model structure and forcing, causal attribution, and counterfactual baselines; these sources can be correlated and propagate across analytical stages. Regional evidence on restoration, wetland management, crop productivity, and soil processes informs the assessment, while studies of engineered carbon materials and contaminated-soil remediation are treated as contextual evidence rather than direct measures of terrestrial sink strength. We identify priorities for defining estimands before selecting data, measuring multiple carbon pools, validating independently across space and time, propagating correlated uncertainty, and reporting observed uptake separately from additional and durable mitigation potential. Integrating inventories, flux observations, remote sensing, ecosystem models, and atmospheric constraints can improve the comparability and decision relevance of terrestrial carbon assessments. Integrating inventories, flux observations, remote sensing, ecosystem models, and atmospheric constraints can therefore support more transparent monitoring and more balanced decisions concerning terrestrial carbon management and sustainable development.

title: Multiparameter additive manufacturing of PETG-carbon fiber gyroid lattices: Compressive performance, microstructural characterization, and property-dependent exploratory machine learning analysis
summary: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid lattices are attractive for lightweight energy-absorbing architectures in additive manufacturing owing to smooth geometry and stress-concentration-free load transfer. However, PETG-CF gyroid res
content: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid lattices are attractive for lightweight energy-absorbing architectures in additive manufacturing owing to smooth geometry and stress-concentration-free load transfer. However, PETG-CF gyroid research focuses on RD, with limited investigation of FDM parameters layer height (LH) and printing speed (PS). Here, a full factorial design of 3 LH × 2 PS × 3 RD levels (54 specimens) was used to compress PETG-CF gyroids and extract eight mechanical properties. Three-way ANOVA showed that RD dominated variation (78–96% for compressive modulus, yield strength, plateau stress, and specific energy absorption), followed by LH (3–14%) and PS (<4%), with significant interactions. Gibson-Ashby scaling yielded modulus and strength exponents of 2.03 and 2.93, respectively, close to bending-dominated wall collapse. SEM confirmed geometry and revealed fiber clustering and extrusion defects. In an exploratory analysis of 18 condition means, power-law Ridge, quadratic Ridge, Gaussian process regression, and linear models were evaluated for four properties using design and as-printed RD configurations. The best models achieved mean R² = 0.962 (0.910–0.992) under leave-one-condition-out cross-validation, with power-law scaling most prevalent for stiffness- and strength-based properties. As-printed RD correction reduced error for modulus and yield strength (17.6% and 24.5%) but increased it for plateau stress and energy absorption (35.6% and 21.9%).
