title: Blue Finance for Coastal Climate Risk Management: Mechanisms, Models, and Implementation Pathways
source: Advances in economics, business and management research/Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research
summary: As the ocean-focused segment of green finance, blue finance draws on ecosystem service valuation, risk diversification, and sustainable development theory. Through blue bonds, climate insurance and other market tools, it internalizes climat
content: As the ocean-focused segment of green finance, blue finance draws on ecosystem service valuation, risk diversification, and sustainable development theory. Through blue bonds, climate insurance and other market tools, it internalizes climate risk costs and improves coastal ecological and socioeconomic resilience. This paper constructs four localized blue finance development paths and tiered policy suggestions, and puts forward a three-phase implementation route. The research proves unified standards and multi-layer risk sharing are core supports for blue finance sustainable operation.

title: Interfacial polarization localization and protection – Transport trade-off in Cr₂O₃-coated O3-NaCrO₂ cathodes
summary: Nanoscale oxide interphases can regulate electrochemical reactions at cathode–electrolyte boundaries, but their protective function competes with the transport resistance introduced across the modified interface. Here, a transient multidime
content: Nanoscale oxide interphases can regulate electrochemical reactions at cathode–electrolyte boundaries, but their protective function competes with the transport resistance introduced across the modified interface. Here, a transient multidimensional finite-element framework is developed to investigate interfacial polarization localization in Cr₂O₃-coated O3-NaCrO₂ cathodes by coupling anisotropic and composition-dependent Na⁺ transport, nonlinear charge-transfer kinetics, finite coating resistance, and controlled interfacial heterogeneity. The simulations reveal a progressive transition from broadly distributed interfacial polarization to increasingly localized electrochemical activity with increasing C-rate. Under the baseline parameterization, the calculated hotspot factor increases from 1.17 at 1 C to 1.64 at 20 C, while the maximum local overpotential increases from 25.1 to 249 mV. However, the absolute predictions at 15–20 C are treated as model-dependent mechanistic stress-test results rather than quantitatively validated high-rate performance estimates because the effective electrolyte formulation does not explicitly resolve concentrated-solution effects, concentration-dependent conductivity, activity coefficients, or salt depletion. Coating-thickness analysis identifies an intermediate 3–5 nm design window in which current homogenization competes with increasing interfacial transport resistance. Higher coating heterogeneity progressively amplifies polarization localization, particularly under demanding current conditions. Experimental comparisons support the model's consistency with measured electrochemical behavior within the examined benchmark conditions, while uncertainty analyses indicate that the qualitative protection–transport trade-off is more robust than absolute hotspot magnitudes. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for understanding particle-scale interfacial polarization and guiding oxide-interphase design without implying fully validated quantitative predictions at extreme operating rates.

title: Towards greener governance? Fiscal decentralization, environmental performance-based promotion incentives, and environmental governance performance: Evidence from China
summary: The impact of fiscal system reform on environmental governance remains contested, while adjustments to the performance-based promotion system provide a useful perspective for understanding this relationship. This study uses the fiscal "prov
content: The impact of fiscal system reform on environmental governance remains contested, while adjustments to the performance-based promotion system provide a useful perspective for understanding this relationship. This study uses the fiscal "province-managing-county" reform (FPMCR) and the revision of the performance evaluation criteria under the National Key Ecological Function Area policy (NKEFA policy) as two quasi-natural experiments. Using a panel dataset of 1848 Chinese counties from 2000 to 2020, we employ a difference-in-differences (DID) model to examine the effects of these institutional changes on county-level environmental governance performance (EGP) and explore potential underlying pathways. The study yields the following key findings: (1) From 2000 to 2020, China's EGP shifted from low to high levels and from negative to positive values, with a marked improvement after 2013. (2) Over the same period, the spatial pattern of EGP evolved from a "strong west-weak east" distribution to a "strong east-weak west" configuration. (3) Baseline results show that FPMCR led to an average 0.54% decline in EGP among reform counties. In contrast, under environmental performance-based promotion incentives (EPPI), EGP increased by an average of 0.84%. Moreover, the effect of FPMCR on EGP is more favorable under EPPI. (4) The mechanism analysis provides suggestive evidence based on indirect proxies. Under growth-oriented incentives, FPMCR is associated with higher nighttime light intensity and more industrial enterprises above designated size, while the effect on vegetation greenness is statistically insignificant. For FPMCR × EPPI, the estimate is positive and significant for vegetation greenness but insignificant for the two economic proxies. (5) Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the incentive-contingent effect of FPMCR is more pronounced in central and western China and among counties designated in the first batch under the NKEFA policy. By adopting a performance-based evaluation perspective, this study sheds light on the relationship between fiscal decentralization and environmental governance, as well as the mechanisms underlying this relationship, thereby contributing to the institutional and environmental economics literature.

title: Food-energy-water screening of greenhouse and data-centre heat integration under a local water limit, with hydrogen and small modular reactor boundaries
summary: Annual food-energy-water balances can conceal seasonal heat mismatch and resource constraints. This study formulates the coupling of a hypothetical 20 ha greenhouse with a data-centre heat source as a design problem with 484 discrete altern
content: Annual food-energy-water balances can conceal seasonal heat mismatch and resource constraints. This study formulates the coupling of a hypothetical 20 ha greenhouse with a data-centre heat source as a design problem with 484 discrete alternatives (two greenhouse heat intensities, 61 IT capacities, two water-recovery rates, dry or evaporative cooling) and solves the same design space at monthly, representative-day and full-year (8,760 h) resolution, the hourly models as mixed-integer programmes with thermal storage. The methodological contributions are a quantification of how temporal aggregation changes coverage, storage and design selection, an upper bound on the premium a heat-efficient greenhouse can carry, and a transferred water-permit quantity used as a feasibility constraint. At 10 MWIT, coverage of an 80 GWhth y −1 load falls from 64.4% (monthly) to 62.1% (representative days) and 61.3% (full year). With unpriced technology premiums the optimum is a 250 kWh m −2 y −1 greenhouse with 90% water recovery, dry cooling and 13–15 MWIT; the monthly choice costs 2.5% more than the full-year optimum. In the monthly screen, annual cost is EUR 1.33–1.77 million y −1 across the tested investment levels, and the efficiency-premium bound EUR 0.60–0.83 million y −1 . A hypothetical 155,000 m 3 y −1 withdrawal cap, the rounded quantity of an anonymised irrigation permit, excludes evaporative cooling above 3.5 MWIT, but greenhouse irrigation above about 4.2 L m −2 d −1 would exceed it without any cooling. Hydrogen and small modular reactors are regional boundary cases. The model is verified numerically but not validated against measurements of a coupled installation.

title: Biological Design as an Interdisciplinary Strategy for Solving Sustainability Issues
summary: This paper explores using biological design as a framework to teach problem-solving in the classroom by integrating it in design inspirations. The field of Sustainability Studies is inherently interdisciplinary and allows for the synthesis
content: This paper explores using biological design as a framework to teach problem-solving in the classroom by integrating it in design inspirations. The field of Sustainability Studies is inherently interdisciplinary and allows for the synthesis of concepts from various fields of study, humanities, social sciences, design, and STEM. Sustainability in innovation is well-recognized in the design world. Designers and engineers are focused on providing low environmental impact in their projects, and design aims are rapidly shifting from Human-centered design to Life-centered design. The concepts of biomimicry, biodesign, materials ecology, etc., are all principles that have been adapted in various technological innovations. In this paper, biological design describes the approach of combining principles of biomimicry and biodesign for finding sustainable design solutions which are the focus of a Life-centered design-based method of problem-solving. The paper presents a case study for developing learning strategies as part of a project-based interdisciplinary course, serving the honors program in the college, to teach biological design to undergraduates. Students explore theoretical concepts of biomimicry and biodesign, which they use in combination to design products to target sustainable solutions to problems addressed by the U.N. sustainable goals. The case studies developed by the student-groups demonstrate the importance of interdisciplinary thinking and further highlight the importance of integrating designs from nature for sustainability in products and architecture. Additionally, experiential learning was paramount in this course. They also developed an understanding of research, experimentation, reflection on their product, its application, economics, and, most importantly, the necessity of converting an abstract idea into a tangible ‘product’. By the end of this course, students were problem-solving theoretical strategies to develop sustainable solutions using information from various disciplines. Furthermore, in this paper, we introduce the concept of ‘observational digestion’ as a relevant responsibility of releasing biological-designed products into the environment, thus, further enhancing the value of the principle of biological design in creating a sustainable future.

title: Agroforestry-Based Mulching as a Climate-Smart Soil and Weed Management Strategy for Sorghum Production in Tropical Agroecosystems
summary: Environmental degradation, declining soil fertility and increasing weed pressure are major constraints on sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L. Moench) production in tropical agroecosystems, particularly under erratic climatic. Agroforestry systems p
content: Environmental degradation, declining soil fertility and increasing weed pressure are major constraints on sorghum (Sorghum bicolor L. Moench) production in tropical agroecosystems, particularly under erratic climatic. Agroforestry systems provide a climate-smart approach to mitigating these challenges by the application of tree-leaf litter as surface mulch to buffer soil conditions and suppress weed growth. This study synthesizes field-based evidence on the environmental and agronomic implications of agroforestry-derived leaf mulches applied to sorghum production in southwestern Nigeria. Leaf mulches from Leucaena leucocephala , Artocarpus altilis , Sesbania grandiflora , and Moringa oleifera , applied at varying rates, and were evaluated for their effects on soil physico-chemical properties, weed dynamics, and sorghum performance. Mulching significantly improved key soil chemical properties such as organic Carbon, Nitrogen, and exchangeable base cations, supporting findings from previous studies on organic residue management. Weed density and biomass were significantly lower in mulched plots than in the unmulched (control) plots, especially at the early stages of crop establishment, suggesting the effectiveness of organic mulches in weed emergence and growth suppression. However, sorghum growth and yield responses differed across mulch species and application rates, suggesting that the agronomic benefits of mulching depend on the balance between soil fertility improvement, potential nutrient immobilisation, and crop nutrient requirements. Overall, agroforestry-based mulching demonstrated strong potential as an environmentally sustainable soil and weed management strategy capable of reducing reliance on synthetic fertilizers and herbicides while enhancing climate resilience in tropical production systems.

title: The effect of particle shape on sunlight exposure in a wind-driven free-surface flow
summary: We investigate how nonspherical marine particles, such as microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice, are exposed to sunlight near the water surface in wind-driven surface boundary layer conditions. We measure the depth and orientation of these
content: We investigate how nonspherical marine particles, such as microplastics, phytoplankton, and ice, are exposed to sunlight near the water surface in wind-driven surface boundary layer conditions. We measure the depth and orientation of these particles in a laboratory wind-wave tank, then use this data to model how much sunlight the particles would be exposed to in an aquatic environment. In particular, we explore how their orientation affects their sunlight exposure in these conditions, since most studies to date do not account for orientation, turbulent shear flow, and wind-waves at the water surface. We find that in all cases, particles prefer certain orientations, and this causes the average sunlight exposure of the particles to be 5 to 40\% higher than would be expected if their orientations were random. Further, we find that the mean irradiance depends on the ratio of the particle mixing length $L_m$ to the light decay lengthscale $λ$, and the nature of this dependence differs between disks and rods. Disks experience disproportionately greater mean irradiance at smaller $L_m/λ$ due to the vertical variation in their orientations. These results have important implications for accurately estimating the sunlight exposure of particles in the surface boundary layer.

title: ADfiRe: An empirical- and CFD-informed advection-diffusion-reaction thermal model for wildfire spread
summary: Real-time wildfire forecasting requires a trade-off between rapid yet physically relevant models and high fidelity but computationally costly models of flame spread over heterogeneous, multiphase solid fuel. The present study introduces ADf
content: Real-time wildfire forecasting requires a trade-off between rapid yet physically relevant models and high fidelity but computationally costly models of flame spread over heterogeneous, multiphase solid fuel. The present study introduces ADfiRe, a hybrid framework that integrates empirical correlations and CFD-informed parameterizations into a physics-based advection-diffusion-reaction (ADR) formulation. The key features of ADfiRe are the use of established fuel databases, the capacity to handle multiple fuels, and a methodology to capture the effect of arbitrary topography. Furthermore, it includes the effect of flame tilting due to wind, thus accounting for the differences between plume- and wind-dominated fire propagation. ADfiRe resolves explicitly the coupled thermochemical degradation as well as heat and mass transport mechanisms of the advancing fire front. The wind field is modeled based on an appropriately defined Byram number. The model is validated against five well-documented experimental field-scale fires in Mediterranean shrublands, showing quantitative agreement with key metrics such as the rate of spread (ROS) and the fireline intensity, through a two-stage, Arrhenius-based heterogeneous reaction scheme coupling solid-fuel pyrolysis and oxygen-limited char/volatile combustion.

title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
summary: Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction. In neuroscience, for example, deep encoding models accurately predict brain activity i
content: Neural networks are powerful predictors, yet their opacity limits their usefulness in science, where the goal is explanation rather than mere prediction. In neuroscience, for example, deep encoding models accurately predict brain activity in response to natural stimuli, but struggle to reveal which stimulus features drive those predictions. Here we introduce interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), a method in which an LLM agent iteratively builds interpretable models by explicitly programming their weights and features in code, without gradient-based training (backpropagation). Without backpropagation to tune parameters, the agent must draw on its prior knowledge and reason over previous trials to hypothesize, hand-craft, and refine human-interpretable computations mirroring the workflow of a human scientist. LLM audits confirm the interpretability of the hand-crafted models. We first validate iWSP by tasking it with constructing transformers for canonical benchmarks such as arithmetic and sentiment classification, finding that LLM agents can successfully craft compact, accurate networks directly. Next, we apply iWSP to build neural encoding models across vision, language, and audition. In the visual cortex, iWSP outpredicts existing interpretable baselines, uncovers distinct computations across early/higher visual areas, and generalizes to unseen data. In language fMRI, iWSP surfaces a confound in the data and in auditory ECoG, it systematically discovers interpretable acoustic features that predict neural activity. Together, these results establish iWSP as a general paradigm for aligning high predictive performance with human-interpretable scientific discovery.

title: Balancing productivity, soil health and estimated greenhouse gas emissions in diversified cereal–legume cropping systems
source: Journal of Agriculture and Food Research
summary: Reconciling productivity and environmental performance remain challenging in semi-arid tropical agriculture. A two-year randomized complete block experiment on one farm in Karnataka’s eastern dry zone evaluated twelve cropping systems with
content: Reconciling productivity and environmental performance remain challenging in semi-arid tropical agriculture. A two-year randomized complete block experiment on one farm in Karnataka’s eastern dry zone evaluated twelve cropping systems with three replicates per treatment. Rainy-season sole crops and intercrops were followed by mung bean, with finger millet–fallow system as the benchmark. Productivity, profitability, soil health, topsoil organic carbon (SOC)-stock change was assessed and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions were estimated using IPCC Tier 1 methods and integrated using a PCA-derived Soil Health Index (SHI) and entropy-weighted TOPSIS. Finger millet + cowpea–mung bean produced the highest system finger millet-equivalent yield (SFEY, 4,271 ± 66 kg ha -1 yr -1 ) and net returns (128,562 ± 3,024 INR ha -1 yr -1 ), exceeding finger millet–fallow by 40.2% and 33.5%, respectively. Intercropping increased mean succeeding mung bean yield by 9–19% and net returns by 26–62% relative to the corresponding sole-cereal sequences. Estimated net GHG emissions were reduced by 9.2–15.3% in maize-based intercrops relative to maize–mung bean sequence, which had the largest mean SOC-stock gain (0.36 Mg C ha -1 ) . Finger millet + cowpea–mung bean had the lowest carbon intensity (0.382 kg CO 2 -eq kg -1 SFEY) and the highest numerical TOPSIS score (0.652). Maize + field bean–mung bean recorded the highest mean SHI (77.75± 1.8) and its TOPSIS score was close to that of finger millet + cowpea–mung bean under equal weighting. Thus, combining spatial and temporal crop diversification improved the overall balance among productivity, profitability, soil health and environmental performance.

title: Reproductive tissues as integrative stress-sensors in food legumes: A proposed molecular framework from perception to yield loss
summary: Food legumes are essential for global protein security, yet their reproductive tissues are highly vulnerable to heat, cold and drought. The mechanisms by which these tissues perceive stress, integrate signals, and generate tissue-specific d
content: Food legumes are essential for global protein security, yet their reproductive tissues are highly vulnerable to heat, cold and drought. The mechanisms by which these tissues perceive stress, integrate signals, and generate tissue-specific developmental responses remain inadequately understood in legumes. We conceptualise reproductive tissues as integrative stress sensors, compartments that concentrate sensing and signal-integration machinery, not discrete sensors in the mechanistic sense. This is framed within a proposed four-tier molecular framework combining evidence from Arabidopsis and model systems with physiological data from chickpea, soybean, cowpea, common bean, lentil, faba bean and mung bean. Tier 1, perception, comprises primary sensors (ELF3 phase separation, phytochrome B thermal reversion, RNA thermoswitches, OSCA1, MSL8, membrane-activated calcium channels), secondary receptors (PYR/PYL/RCAR, which perceive abscisic acid, not stress itself) and ROS-producing machinery (RBOHE, RBOHH/J); their reproductive functions in legumes are largely uncharacterised. Tier 2, signal integration, involves Ca²⁺-ROS feedback, the ICE1-CBF cold cascade, jasmonate-ABA-gibberellin antagonism and ERF networks. Tier 3, tissue-specific responses, includes anther sucrose depletion, pollen tube failure, pod wall transpiration and seed coat invertase inhibition, with direct evidence mainly from chickpea and soybean. Tier 4 comprises developmental outcomes: pollen sterility, fertilisation failure, embryo arrest and reduced seed set and yield. Since most links are inferred from model species, evidence is graded, and the framework is a testable model, not an established pathway. The extent of knowledge is most comprehensive for chickpea and soybean, while it is least developed for lentil, faba bean, and mung bean. The framework offers a hypothesis-generating basis for prioritising candidate targets to improve reproductive stress tolerance.

title: A Review of Emerging Technologies in the Biomass Value Chain: A Clear Path Toward a Green Future
source: Technovations of Electrical Engineering in Green Energy System     فناوریهای نوین مهندسی برق در سیستم انرژی سبز
summary: گذار به آینده‌ای سبز و دستیابی به اقتصادی پایدار و کم‌کربن، مستلزم تحولاتی بنیادین در شیوه‌های تولید و مصرف انرژی است. در این میان، انرژی زیست‌توده به‌عنوان یکی از منابع تجدیدپذیر و دارای پتانسیل بالا برای کاهش انتشار گازهای گلخانه‌ای، از ا
content: گذار به آینده‌ای سبز و دستیابی به اقتصادی پایدار و کم‌کربن، مستلزم تحولاتی بنیادین در شیوه‌های تولید و مصرف انرژی است. در این میان، انرژی زیست‌توده به‌عنوان یکی از منابع تجدیدپذیر و دارای پتانسیل بالا برای کاهش انتشار گازهای گلخانه‌ای، از اهمیت ویژه‌ای برخوردار است. بااین‌حال، چالش‌هایی مانند هزینه‌های بالا، پایداری منابع، راندمان پایین و مسائل زیست‌محیطی، بهره‌برداری کامل از این منبع را محدود ساخته‌اند. پیشرفت‌های فناورانه، به‌ویژه در حوزه‌های دیجیتال، فرصت‌های تازه‌ای برای ارتقای بهره‌وری و پایداری در زنجیره تولید زیست‌توده فراهم کرده‌اند. در این مقاله، نقش فناوری‌های نوین در توسعه و بهینه‌سازی سامانه‌های انرژی زیست‌توده مورد بررسی قرار گرفته است. این فناوری‌ها شامل هوش مصنوعی، سیستم‌های اطلاعات مکانی (GIS)، نوآوری در انتخاب و فرآوری مواد اولیه نظیر پسماندهای پالایشگاهی، جلبک‌ها، پسماندهای کشاورزی و صنعتی، فرآیندهای ماژولار، فناوری جذب و ذخیره کربن (CCS)، روش‌های کاهش حجم لجن در تصفیه‌خانه‌ها و فناوری‌های نوین پیرولیز می‌باشند. رویکرد مقاله توصیفی–تحلیلی است و در آن علاوه بر تحلیل فناوری‌ها، نمونه‌هایی از استارت‌آپ‌های فعال در این زمینه نیز معرفی شده‌اند. در ادامه، وضعیت زیست‌توده در ایران، چرخه عمر فناوری‌های مرتبط و چالش‌ها و فرصت‌های دیجیتالی‌سازی بررسی شده‌اند. یافته‌ها نشان می‌دهند که بهره‌گیری از این فناوری‌ها می‌تواند با افزایش راندمان، بهبود مدیریت منابع، کاهش هزینه‌ها و کاهش وابستگی به سوخت‌های فسیلی، نقش مهمی در آینده انرژی زیست‌توده ایفا کند. این مقاله تلاش دارد تصویری جامع از وضعیت فعلی و افق‌های پیشِ‌روی این حوزه در پرتو پیشرفت‌های فناورانه ارائه دهد.

title: A Collaborative Energy Management in Renewable-based Water-energy Nexus Multi-microgrid System Using Dynamic Demand Response
source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
summary: This paper proposes a collaborative energy management in the water-energy nexus multi-microgrid systems. In this model, several microgrids collaborate together to form a large coalition and perform a centralized energy scheduling in order t
content: This paper proposes a collaborative energy management in the water-energy nexus multi-microgrid systems. In this model, several microgrids collaborate together to form a large coalition and perform a centralized energy scheduling in order to minimize the total costs. In the water section, the microgrids utilize the water desalination unit and underground water sources to supply the freshwater. Also, they operate the water storage tank to enable the water flexibility for the microgrids. In the electrical section, the renewable energy sources, capstone microturbine, and battery storage systems are considered to keep the balance between the generation and demands. In this section, a dynamic demand response program is introduced that calculate the up-ward and down-ward potential of different microgrids based on their load consumption profiles. The numerical results shows that performing the dynamic demand response programs reduces the operating cost and energy not supplied of microgrids by 8.35 % and 91.43 %, respectively.

title: Youth Engagement in Climate-resilient Agricultural Extension Programmes in Siaya County, Kenya
source: African Journal of Food Agriculture Nutrition and Development
summary: Youth constitute a significant proportion of Kenya's population and have considerable potential to contribute to climate-resilient agricultural development. Engaging youth in climate-resilient agricultural extension programmes is very criti
content: Youth constitute a significant proportion of Kenya's population and have considerable potential to contribute to climate-resilient agricultural development. Engaging youth in climate-resilient agricultural extension programmes is very critical for enhancing productivity, food security, and sustainable livelihoods. However, socio-economic and institutional barriers constrain their participation in climate-resilient agricultural extension programmes, including limited access to land, financial resources, and agricultural training, as well as a lack of youth–friendly agricultural extension programmes. This study assessed youth participation and their capacity to engage in climate-resilient agricultural extension programmes in Siaya County, Kenya. A cross-sectional study design was employed using a structured questionnaire administered to 302 youths aged 18–35 years selected from six sub-counties of Siaya through simple random sampling. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression in R Statistical Software version 4.2.1 (R Core Team). The findings from this study revealed that education level (P = 0.022), access to land (P = 0.030), monthly income (P = 0.013), and sub-county of residence significantly influenced participation in climate-resilient agricultural extension programmes. Youths with primary education, those without access to land, and those earning less than KES 10,000 per month were significantly less likely to participate than their counterparts. Before participation in climate–resilient agricultural extension programmes, the respondents generally reported low to moderate knowledge of climate- resilient agricultural practices, particularly regarding renewable energy, water management, agroforestry, pest and disease management, use of climate–resilient crop varieties, crop diversification, and soil conservation. The study concludes that strengthening youth participation requires targeted capacity-building initiatives, improved access to productive resources such as land, youth-responsive extension approaches, and location-specific interventions that address contextual differences across sub-counties. The findings provide evidence to inform county governments, extension agencies, and development partners in designing policies and programmes that enhance youth engagement in climate-resilient agriculture and sustainable rural livelihoods. Key words: Youth Engagement, climate–resilient agriculture, Rural Youth, Agricultural Extension

title: Arginine as a ‘Molecular Glue’ for Robust Hierarchical Supramolecular Assembly
summary: Abstract Hierarchical supramolecular assembly—materials ordered across multiple length scales via weak non-covalent interactions—is nature’s primary strategy for constructing complex functional materials; however, its implementation in synt
content: Abstract Hierarchical supramolecular assembly—materials ordered across multiple length scales via weak non-covalent interactions—is nature’s primary strategy for constructing complex functional materials; however, its implementation in synthetic systems is fundamentally limited by intrinsic structural fragility. While biological systems achieve robustness through embedding their assemblies within dynamic protein scaffolds, synthetic supramolecular architectures often degrade under real-world conditions. Here, we demonstrate that arginine acts as a ‘molecular glue’ to mediate the hierarchical assembly of a cyanine-based model system, resulting in unprecedented structural robustness. Through a combination of optical spectroscopy, cryogenic-electron and near-field scanning optical microscopy, and density functional theory, we show that these arginine-mediated assemblies remain robust even upon dilution in challenging biological environments (cell culture media), or after complete dehydration on solid substrates. Our bioinspired approach overcomes the longstanding stability limitations of non-covalent materials, providing a versatile, robust framework for next-generation organic device applications in nanomedicine, renewable energy, or information technology.

title: Bioenergetic responses to β-adrenergic stimulation in beige adipocytes depend on actomyosin driven forces
summary: Abstract Beige and white adipocytes reside within the same fat depots but differ in their responses to β-adrenergic stimulation. While both activate classical protein kinase A (PKA)-mediated pathways, only beige adipocytes show induction of
content: Abstract Beige and white adipocytes reside within the same fat depots but differ in their responses to β-adrenergic stimulation. While both activate classical protein kinase A (PKA)-mediated pathways, only beige adipocytes show induction of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression and enhanced mitochondrial respiration, suggesting additional mechanisms that distinguish their responses. Here we uncover a parallel, non-canonical biomechanical pathway specific to committed beige adipocytes that is required for the full β-adrenergic induction of their thermogenic activity. Mechanistically, β-adrenergic receptor (β-AR) stimulation induces a rapid myosin heavy chain 9 (Myh9)-mediated actomyosin contraction and stiffening in differentiated beige but not white adipocytes that activates focal adhesion kinase (FAK), which we show to be critical for the expression of oxidative and thermogenic genes including UCP1 and perilipin 5 (PLIN5). These findings reveal an alternative biomechanical Myh9-FAK signaling arm downstream of β-adrenergic activation that distinguishes thermogenic beige adipocytes from white adipocytes.

title: Resource-rich northern Europe experiences persistent wind market value losses as deployment expands
summary: Abstract Wind-power cannibalization, the decline in market value as wind penetration increases, is typically assessed using national averages that can mask important regional differences. Here we show that the economic value of wind power d
content: Abstract Wind-power cannibalization, the decline in market value as wind penetration increases, is typically assessed using national averages that can mask important regional differences. Here we show that the economic value of wind power declines unevenly across Europe, with the largest losses concentrated in resource-rich northern regions. As wind generation shares rise from 10% to 19%, the revenue earned by wind power relative to average electricity prices decreases from 0.94 to 0.78, with sustained declines in many high-wind regions through 2024. Within electricity-market zones, the windiest locations also tend to earn lower electricity prices than other locations in the same market. By combining hourly wind-output estimates derived from atmospheric reanalysis data with hourly wholesale electricity prices from 2015 to 2024, we quantify high-resolution spatial and temporal variation in wind-power value across Europe.

title: Chiral quantum batteries
summary: Quantum batteries (QBs) offer compelling advantages over conventional ones in terms of superior energy density, ultrafast charging, and high conversion efficiency. However, their realization is hampered by decoherence, which causes incomple
content: Quantum batteries (QBs) offer compelling advantages over conventional ones in terms of superior energy density, ultrafast charging, and high conversion efficiency. However, their realization is hampered by decoherence, which causes incomplete charging, rapid self-discharging, and reduced extractable work. Here, we propose a quantum-compatible battery architecture based on a chiral magnonic platform. It comprises two yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spheres, one serving as the charger and the other as the QB, coupled to a waveguide. The unique chiral coupling between magnons and the guided electromagnetic fields breaks inversion symmetry, inducing both nonreciprocal energy flow and coherent interference between the charger and QB. Their synergy endows our QB with a 34-fold increase in energy capacity and a 55-fold boost in extractable work compared to its achiral counterpart in an experimentally accessible regime. Our scheme harnesses the decoherence induced by the common electromagnetic fields, which enables the robustness and wireless-like remote charging features of the QB. Without relying on quantum resource and being representable by classical dynamics, our architecture provides a viable route toward robust and remote-charging of QBs.

title: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack arc
content: Abstract Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RHavg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

title: The P2P-ironing platform: evaluating the software quality and user acceptance of a decentralized cyber-physical marketplace for shore-to-ship power
summary: Abstract Decarbonizing the maritime industry through shore-to-ship power (cold-ironing) requires robust transactive energy systems. However, implementing decentralized peer-to-peer (P2P) energy markets introduces significant socio-technical
content: Abstract Decarbonizing the maritime industry through shore-to-ship power (cold-ironing) requires robust transactive energy systems. However, implementing decentralized peer-to-peer (P2P) energy markets introduces significant socio-technical challenges, including the operational friction of pure Web3 applications and conflicting stakeholder demands regarding billing transparency. This paper presents the software engineering lifecycle and empirical evaluation of the P2P-Ironing platform, a cyber-physical marketplace designed for smart ports. Driven by a two-phase mixed-methods requirements analysis involving key maritime and energy stakeholders ( N = 18, N = 15), the platform utilizes a decoupled, hybrid Web2.5 architecture to abstract blockchain complexity from the end-user. To practically evaluate this cyber-physical integration despite physical infrastructure limitations, the system incorporates a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbed and synthetic vessel-load generation to simulate automated smart-contract escrow settlements. An empirical evaluation ( N = 30) utilizing the Short User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ-S) indicated high pragmatic and hedonic software quality. These findings are consistent with the design objective of reducing the operational friction traditionally associated with decentralized ledgers. Furthermore, descriptive operational metrics indicated stakeholder trust in the hardware-automated settlement logic, a preference for transparent P2P market structures, and perceived alignment with port decarbonization goals. Ultimately, this research establishes a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 architectural foundation, demonstrating a user-centric approach to maritime transactive energy that navigates current legislative constraints while preparing for future physical grid integrations.

title: Addressing Data Imbalance in Operational State Recognition for Photovoltaic and Wind Power Systems via DCGAN-Based Augmentation and 2D-CNN
summary: Accurate state identification is crucial for the safe and efficient operation of renewable energy systems. However, monitoring data from photovoltaic (PV) and wind power systems often suffer from significant class imbalance. This imbalance
content: Accurate state identification is crucial for the safe and efficient operation of renewable energy systems. However, monitoring data from photovoltaic (PV) and wind power systems often suffer from significant class imbalance. This imbalance reduces state recognition accuracy. In this study, we propose one framework to augment fault data and recognize operating states for a combined PV–wind system. The framework first converts signals into images using the Gramian Angular Summation Field (GASF). It then groups samples with K-means clustering. Next, a deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) generates additional fault samples for minority classes. Finally, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) identifies the operating state. PV and wind time-series signals are first mapped into 2D images via GASF to yield richer spatial-feature representations, and K-means clustering is then used to define operating states in an unsupervised manner and generate the corresponding labels. In PV-only, wind-only, and combined PV–wind scenarios, the baseline 2D-CNN trained on imbalanced datasets achieves recognition accuracies of 95.89%, 57.93%, and 81.94%, respectively. To alleviate class imbalance, DCGAN is employed to synthesize images and construct balanced datasets; the best recognition accuracies in the three scenarios increase to 99.20%, 97.08%, and 97.62%, and the model shows stronger robustness in identifying minority classes. This approach supports both single-source applications and multi-source systems such as large-scale wind–solar bases by providing data and algorithmic foundations for generalized fault-diagnosis models, thereby enabling more reliable, data-driven operational monitoring.

title: Sr-anchoring-directed gradient shell architecture in Sr 2 Fe 1.5 Mo 0.5 O 6− δ cathodes for reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells
summary: Abstract Strontium segregation remains a critical challenge for Sr-containing double perovskite cathodes, wherein outward-migrating Sr species accumulate at the surface and severely deteriorate interfacial electrochemical kinetics in revers
content: Abstract Strontium segregation remains a critical challenge for Sr-containing double perovskite cathodes, wherein outward-migrating Sr species accumulate at the surface and severely deteriorate interfacial electrochemical kinetics in reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs). Herein, we develop a Sr-anchoring-driven interfacial catalytic architecture on Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6−δ (SFM) via vanadium-assisted near-surface phase engineering. The incorporation of V introduces Lewis-acidic centers that effectively immobilize migrating Sr species and simultaneously induce the in situ reconstruction of a nanoscale SrMoO4/SrVO3 (SMO/SVO) heterointerface. More importantly, this reconstructed interface functions as a catalytically active region with enhanced electronic delocalization and optimized oxygen defect chemistry, which collectively promote oxygen adsorption, dissociation, and charge-transfer kinetics. The gradient shell architecture not only suppresses detrimental Sr segregation but also establishes fast and continuous pathways for coupled ion–electron transport across the interface. Electrochemical impedance and distribution of relaxation time (DRT) analyses reveal substantially reduced polarization resistance and decreased activation energy, indicating accelerated oxygen electrocatalysis. Consequently, the V-modified Sr2Fe1.5Mo0.5O6−δ-Vx (SFM-V) cathode exhibits markedly enhanced reversible electrochemical performance compared to pristine SFM, delivering a peak power density of 1.23 W·cm−2 at 650 °C together with high electrolysis activity and robust cycling stability, ranking among state-of-the-art SFM-based air electrodes for R-PCECs. This work demonstrates that Sr-anchoring interfacial engineering is an effective strategy to stabilize perovskite cathodes while maintaining fast interfacial kinetics.

title: Annealing induced bandgap engineering and interfacial oxide formation in nanostructured TiO 2 –Ge thin film heterojunctions for photovoltaic applications
summary: Abstract Nanostructured thin films of germanium (Ge) and titanium dioxide ( TiO 2 ) were successfully deposited onto silicon (Si) substrates using a combination of direct current (DC) and radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering techniques
content: Abstract Nanostructured thin films of germanium (Ge) and titanium dioxide ( TiO 2 ) were successfully deposited onto silicon (Si) substrates using a combination of direct current (DC) and radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering techniques. Thickness measurements conducted via Rutherford backscattering spectrometry (RBS) revealed film thicknesses of approximately 484 nm for Ge and 5 nm for TiO 2 slightly below the intended thickness of 500 nm and 10 nm, respectively. The films were subsequently subjected to controlled thermal annealing in ambient air using a muffle furnace at temperatures ranging from 100 °C–600 °C for 2 h. Significant thermally induced modifications were observed, particularly at elevated annealing temperatures of 500 °C and 600 °C. These included visible changes in film coloration from a metallic silver sheen to darker hues, alongside structural alterations and reduction in film uniformity. RBS analysis further confirmed the oxidation of Ge and the formation of interfacial mixed oxides such as GeO 2 and GeTiO 2 , resulting from diffusion and chemical interaction at the TiO 2 –Ge interface. Optical characterization using UV–Vis–NIR spectroscopy revealed a pronounced shift in the optical band gap. Initially measured at 1.45 eV, the optical band gap decreased to 1.25 eV after annealing at 400 °C, attributed to the formation of nanocrystalline Ge domains and quantum confinement effects. At 500 °C, the band gap remained nearly unchanged (1.23 eV) due to the competing effects of crystallization and the onset of oxidation with initial GeO 2 formation, while a significant increase to 1.60 eV at 600 °C was associated with the progressive formation of GeO 2 and GeTiO 2 nanostructures within the multilayered system. These findings demonstrate that the TiO 2 –Ge thin film system exhibits temperature dependent tunability in both structure and optical response. The observed interfacial engineering and band gap modulation position these films as promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications, particularly where engineered heterojunctions and tailored electronic properties are critical for device performance.

title: Green Value Investing in the Banking Sector: The Effectiveness of a Green F-Score Strategy in Poland as a CEE Case Study
summary: The banking sector serves as a critical transmission belt for capital allocation toward renewable energy (RE) projects, yet traditional equity valuation models fail to capture banks’ exposure to energy transition risks. To bridge this gap,
content: The banking sector serves as a critical transmission belt for capital allocation toward renewable energy (RE) projects, yet traditional equity valuation models fail to capture banks’ exposure to energy transition risks. To bridge this gap, this paper develops a novel fundamental–environmental indicator—the “Green F-Score”—tested on 10 major commercial banks listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (WSE) between 2023 and 2025. By synthesizing classical financial efficiency criteria with EU Taxonomy disclosures (Green Asset Ratio), the portfolio sorting methodology reveals how capital markets price sustainable energy financing in Central and Eastern Europe. The empirical results indicate that portfolios with high environmental–fundamental readiness (“Green Leaders”) generate a higher mean annual return of 60.43% and a higher price-to-book (P/B) premium than laggards (15.41%), although inter-group ANOVA differences are not statistically significant (p = 0.215) given the small sample (N = 30). Correlation analysis indicates that the market premium is significantly associated with the ESG sub-score (r = 0.40, p = 0.028), rendering traditional financial metrics an operational hygiene factor. Consequently, the Green F-Score emerges as a promising exploratory tool for institutional investors assessing transition readiness in commercial banks.

title: Использование энергии ветра
summary: В статье рассматриваются особенности использования энергии ветра как одного из перспективных неисчерпаемых источников энергии. Описаны принципы преобразования кинетической энергии ветра в электрическую, а также основные области применения в
content: В статье рассматриваются особенности использования энергии ветра как одного из перспективных неисчерпаемых источников энергии. Описаны принципы преобразования кинетической энергии ветра в электрическую, а также основные области применения ветроэнергетических установок. Проанализированы преимущества ветроэнергетики, а также недостатки. Уделено внимание на перспективы развития использования энергии ветра в современном мире.

title: Из опыта применения вентилируемых труб на примере объектов города Якутска
summary: Обобщены результаты 20-летних натурных температурных наблюдений (2001–2026 гг.) за основаниями двух зданий в г. Якутске, оборудованных системами принудительного воздушного охлаждения с вентилируемыми трубами в подсыпке. Данные получены по с
content: Обобщены результаты 20-летних натурных температурных наблюдений (2001–2026 гг.) за основаниями двух зданий в г. Якутске, оборудованных системами принудительного воздушного охлаждения с вентилируемыми трубами в подсыпке. Данные получены по скважинам внутри и вне контура зданий. Выявлена пространственная неравномерность охлаждения: в одной из скважин спортивного комплекса зафиксировано оттаивание на глубине 3 м (+0,04 °C), тогда как в другой грунт оставался мёрзлым. У жилого дома изотерма 0 °C впервые за 20 лет поднялась до 2,5 м в октябре 2024 г. из-за климатических аномалий, но восстановилась после нормальной зимы. Система регенерирует мерзлоту в нормальных условиях, но необходимо продолжение мониторинга.

title: Assessing the Experience of Vernacular Environmental Sustainability in Desert Settlements of North African Countries
summary: Abstract The research attempts to investigate and evaluate the passive strategies applied in urban pattern and building design of vernacular desert settlements in North African countries. The methodology of the research is based on conducti
content: Abstract The research attempts to investigate and evaluate the passive strategies applied in urban pattern and building design of vernacular desert settlements in North African countries. The methodology of the research is based on conducting comparative studies among vernacular architecture in different desert regions along North African countries to cover adaptation techniques that are climatic responsive and preserve local environmental and cultural significance. The proposed checklist criteria act as a model for applying and assessing environmental sustainability of desert settlements. For international interests it focuses within sustainable desert development, conventional techniques inspected through detailed investigations empowering designers and urbanists for integrating comparable modifications. Such approach support creation of climate-resilient communities, environmentally conscious of local ecosystem, lower footprint and culturally sustaining societies. The research represents an opportunity for using climatic responsive passive design strategies as design alternatives for contemporary household’s developments in arid contexts. The findings from case studies proves that indigenous applied techniques are highly relevant to the context of sustainable development in desert settlements. On the other hand; the adopted passive integrated system reflecting an environmental sustainable design philosophy that prioritizes integration with environmental settings and respect the identity of the local community.

title: How Far Do Kamlet–Taft Parameters and pH Predict Delignification by Deep Eutectic Solvents?
summary: Abstract Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) are tunable, low-toxicity media for lignocellulose fractionation, but their selection for delignification still relies on empirical screening. Kamlet–Taft (KT) solvatochromic parameters (hydrogen-bond
content: Abstract Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) are tunable, low-toxicity media for lignocellulose fractionation, but their selection for delignification still relies on empirical screening. Kamlet–Taft (KT) solvatochromic parameters (hydrogen-bond acidity α, basicity β, and dipolarity/polarizability π*) and pH are the descriptors most often correlated with lignin solubility, yet how far they predict delignification of whole biomass has not been tested critically. Here we report measured KT parameters and apparent pH (pHapp) for 56 DES formulations spanning carboxylic-acid, polyol, metal-salt, amide, alkanolamine, and amino-acid families, together with the softwood lignin removal obtained after a sequential enzymatic–DES fractionation. Four descriptor-to-performance models were compared under identical leave-one-out, repeated k-fold, and grouped (leave-one-cluster-out and leave-one-family-out) cross-validation: a linear correlation, a 15-term second-order polynomial, a random forest (RF), and a Gaussian-process (GP) regressor with automatic relevance determination. All models fit the training set (in-sample R2 up to 0.89 for the RF) but generalize weakly: leave-one-out R2 is 0.10–0.13 for the GP and the RF, the polynomial is overparameterized and generalizes worse than the training mean, and no model predicts a chemical family that is absent from training better than the training mean. Gaussian-process relevance and ablation and random-forest permutation importance rank pHapp as the most informative descriptor, followed by α, whereas β and π* carry little consistent information, and the pKa of the hydrogen-bond donor carries the same information as pHapp; these results point to solvent acid strength, rather than hydrogen-bond donation alone, as the property most closely associated with lignin removal from enzymatically pretreated softwood. The GP provides calibrated predictive uncertainty: 96% of leave-one-out predictions and all four prospectively synthesized blind-test DESs fall within its 95% credible intervals. The results delimit what solvatochromic descriptors can and cannot predict for whole-biomass delignification and provide an uncertainty-aware screening tool and an open data set for DES design.

title: Evaluation of Turbulent-Kinetic-Energy-Dissipation Relationships in the CBL Using a Combination of Doppler Lidars
summary: Abstract This study evaluates parametrizations of turbulent-kinetic-energy (TKE) dissipation (𝜀) in the convective boundary layer (CBL) by analyzing turbulent statistics of TKE (𝑒), vertical wind variance (⟨𝑤′²⟩), and their relationships, u
content: Abstract This study evaluates parametrizations of turbulent-kinetic-energy (TKE) dissipation (𝜀) in the convective boundary layer (CBL) by analyzing turbulent statistics of TKE (𝑒), vertical wind variance (⟨𝑤′²⟩), and their relationships, using high-resolution Doppler lidar data from the Land-Atmosphere Feedback Observatory (LAFO), Stuttgart, Germany. The analysis is based on 25 days with convective conditions in May to July 2021 and 2022. A combination of one vertical-pointing and one six-beam scanning Doppler lidar provided profiles of ⟨𝑤′²⟩, 𝑒, 𝜀, integral time and length scales, as well as CBL depth 𝑧𝑖. The median profiles from 30-min averages between local morning (0900 UTC) and afternoon (1600 UTC) cover the diurnal evolution of the CBL, including its growth, peak, and decay. We found maxima of ⟨𝑤′²⟩, 𝑒̅, and 𝜀̅ at 0.34𝑧̅ᵢ, 0.73𝑧̅ᵢ, and 0.29𝑧̅ᵢ, respectively, which is consistent with previous observations and large-eddy simulation studies. In addition, we also discuss distribution functions, which are very important for future stochastic parameterizations. In the lower half of the CBL, 𝑒 correlates strongly with ⟨𝑤′²⟩ and 𝜀 with r≈0.70, while the correlation is weaker in the upper CBL with r≈0.52. The relationship between 𝜀 and ⟨𝑤′²⟩ follows 𝜀∝(⟨𝑤′²⟩)3/2 throughout the CBL, with r=0.83. We found a significantly higher correlation of r=0.80 when parametrizing 𝜀 with ⟨𝑤′²⟩ instead of parametrizing 𝜀 with 𝑒 (r=0.46). Machine learning models, random forest, and a multilayer perceptron independently identify ⟨𝑤′²⟩ as the dominant predictor, suggesting the use of a ⟨𝑤′²⟩-based dissipation closure in turbulence schemes for the unstable atmospheric boundary layer.

title: A Cardanol-Derived Fluorescent Marker Based on aza-BODIPY for Petroleum Fuel Tagging
summary: Abstract A new petroleum marker (BDPC) was successfully synthesized from cardanol, a renewable feedstock obtained from cashew nut shell liquid, an abundant byproduct of the cashew processing industry. The incorporation of lipophilic cardano
content: Abstract A new petroleum marker (BDPC) was successfully synthesized from cardanol, a renewable feedstock obtained from cashew nut shell liquid, an abundant byproduct of the cashew processing industry. The incorporation of lipophilic cardanol chains enhanced the marker’s compatibility with nonpolar petroleum fuels, facilitating its incorporation into fuel matrices. BDPC exhibited near-infrared fluorescence maxima at 700 nm in hexane and 710 nm in diesel and E10 gasoline, enabling selective detection with minimal interference from fuel matrices. At an optimal concentration (3 ppm), the marker caused no visible change in the fuels while remaining readily detectable by ultraviolet–visible and fluorescence spectroscopy. Fluorescence measurements showed a linear response within the low-ppm range, supporting sensitive quantitative analysis. Physicochemical evaluations by the American Society for Testing and Materials indicated that incorporating BDPC did not substantially alter fuel properties, including volatility, viscosity, density, sulfur content, and cetane index. In addition, the fluorescence intensity of BDPC remained stable in diesel and E10 gasoline for at least 90 days. These findings reveal the promising potential of BDPC as a sustainable, durable, and nondisruptive marker for practical applications in petroleum authentication and traceability.

title: Energy use and the sustainable development goals: A purposive structured review of access, renewable adoption, efficiency, and urban sustainability
summary: Energy underpins most Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet ex-post empirical evidence on how energy use relates to progress across goals has rarely been appraised within one framework. This purposive, structured narrative review examin
content: Energy underpins most Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), yet ex-post empirical evidence on how energy use relates to progress across goals has rarely been appraised within one framework. This purposive, structured narrative review examines how adequate, efficient, renewable, and equitably distributed energy use is associated with SDGs spanning poverty, health, and education (SDG 1, 3, 4); growth and industry (SDG 8, 9); clean energy and climate (SDG 7, 13); cities and consumption (SDG 11, 12); and inequality, institutions, and partnerships (SDG 10, 16, 17). A scoping corpus of 72 documents was screened against explicit eligibility criteria, yielding 29 peer-reviewed empirical studies, each classified by design and appraised for quality. Energy access is consistently associated with better education and health outcomes, supported by one meta-analysis of children's study time. Renewable energy is associated with lower emissions and better air quality in most panel studies, but the size and sign of these associations vary with energy mix, development level, and institutional quality. Evidence on growth and industry is mixed, while equity, institutions, and partnerships rest only on secondary findings. Financing and infrastructure gaps, institutional fragmentation, and threshold effects best explain this heterogeneity. Confidence is highest for education, health, and emissions and lowest for equity and governance, given the purposively assembled corpus. Policy implications remain tentative since this study did not evaluate the proposed measures. A research agenda using threshold, multilevel, cross-country, and quasi-experimental designs is proposed.

title: Forecasting agricultural value added under drought risk in Morocco: a hybrid Fourier ARDL–neural network approach
summary: Abstract Droughts have become longer and more frequent in Morocco, and their effect on agricultural output is now a major source of uncertainty in macroeconomic forecasts. This paper asks how well agricultural value added can be forecast on
content: Abstract Droughts have become longer and more frequent in Morocco, and their effect on agricultural output is now a major source of uncertainty in macroeconomic forecasts. This paper asks how well agricultural value added can be forecast once crop-year rainfall is known, and what droughts of different intensity and duration would cost. We build a consistent quarterly series of agricultural value added for 1998–2025, benchmarked to the latest national accounts, and link it to rainfall and temperature from the ERA5 reanalysis. We propose a hybrid model in which a Fourier ARDL captures the linear relation and gradual structural change, and a small neural network, selected on a separate validation period, models the nonlinear structure left in its residuals. A 10 percent fall in crop-year rainfall lowers agricultural value added by about 4.4 percent in the long run. Over 2020–2025, the Fourier terms improve four-quarter-ahead forecasts by about 30 percent relative to a standard ARDL, and the hybrid model is the most accurate of six models, with a mean absolute percentage error of 5.4 percent against 11.1 percent for ARIMA, although the network’s own contribution is modest. Scenario simulations show that a two-year drought costs more than a single severe one, about 55 against 41 billion dirhams. JEL Classification: C22 , C45 , C53 , Q10 , Q54

title: Toward Practical CO2 to Formate Electrosynthesis: Multi-Dimensional Engineering of Bismuth-Based Catalysts
source: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology Repository (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology)
summary: Converting carbon dioxide into formic acid with renewable electricity offers a compelling route to sustainable hydrogen storage: formic acid is a safe, energy-dense liquid hydrogen carrier, and its electrosynthesis from captured CO2 stores
content: Converting carbon dioxide into formic acid with renewable electricity offers a compelling route to sustainable hydrogen storage: formic acid is a safe, energy-dense liquid hydrogen carrier, and its electrosynthesis from captured CO2 stores intermittent renewable power in a form that releases hydrogen on demand. Bismuth-based catalysts have emerged as the leading candidates for this transformation owing to their intrinsic selectivity toward the *OCHO pathway, yet their journey from laboratory benchmark to practical device remains obstructed by three successive bottlenecks: poor utilization of surface-active sites, cathodic self-reduction of the high-valent Bi3+ active state, and sluggish interfacial proton transfer at high current densities. This thesis resolves these bottlenecks in sequence through multi-dimensional engineering of bismuth-based catalysts, advancing from active site activation through electronic structure stabilization to interfacial microenvironment control, with reactor-level evaluation serving to validate the resulting structure-performance relationships under device-relevant conditions. Three complementary bismuth-based systems anchor this effort: Cu-BOC, in which in-situ constructed Bi nanoclusters and a built-in electric field at the Bi/Cu heterojunction convert catalytically inert planar terraces into dense active domains; metavalently bonded chalcogenide frameworks exemplified by Bi2Te3, whose partially delocalized charge network suppresses cathodic self-reduction of high-valent Bi without sacrificing *OCHO affinity; and Ag-doped Bi2Se3, in which dopant-driven surface and interface engineering constructs a strengthened interfacial hydrogen-bond network that accelerates proton delivery to the *OCHO intermediate. Together, these systems establish stepwise control over active site utilization, electronic structure stability, and the interfacial reaction microenvironment. Complementary evaluation in H-type cells, flow cells, and MEA systems confirms the effectiveness of these design strategies while clarifying how reaction environments modulate activity, selectivity, and stability: the optimized catalysts sustain formate Faradaic efficiencies above 80% at several hundred mA cm-2 and deliver mole-scale formate over more than 100 hours of continuous operation. Catalyst stability and active-phase evolution, this work shows, are not fixed material properties but sensitive functions of the operating environment. By tracing catalytic performance back to active site structure, chemical bonding, and interfacial water behavior, this thesis establishes a comprehensive framework for designing bismuth-based electrocatalysts under practical operating conditions, bridging the long-standing gap between fundamental catalyst design and industrial CO2 to formate electrosynthesis.

title: Compliance with Green Building and Clean Energy for Fashion and Textile Sectors
summary: This chapter investigates various approaches for the fashion and textile industries to fulfil the new demands and voluntary guidelines for sustainable buildings and renewable energy. It discusses the regulatory frameworks and energy-efficie
content: This chapter investigates various approaches for the fashion and textile industries to fulfil the new demands and voluntary guidelines for sustainable buildings and renewable energy. It discusses the regulatory frameworks and energy-efficiency certifications like Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED), Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (EDGE), and Building Research Establishment Environmental Assessment Method (BREEAM). It also analyses how these regulations interact with industry initiatives and corporate climate pledges. Utilizing examples from key fashion brands, it evaluates the degree to which garment and textile facilities implement various sustainable strategies. Further, this chapter also emphasizes the primary factors driving compliance, including buyer demands, consumer focus, and reporting requirements, while also addressing obstacles such as significant initial investments, gaps in technical expertise, and conflicting incentives between brands and suppliers. It concludes by outlining the necessary policy, governance, and financing approaches required to progress from mere symbolic certification to achieving substantial and quantifiable reductions in energy consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions throughout the global fashion and textile supply chain.

title: Fertility, skilled birth attendance, and maternal mortality in BRICS: long-run evidence from heterogeneous panels with cross-sectional dependence, 2000–2023
summary: Background Maternal mortality is a sensitive marker of health-system performance in BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa). This study examines the long-run associations of fertility, female education, and skilled birth atte
content: Background Maternal mortality is a sensitive marker of health-system performance in BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa). This study examines the long-run associations of fertility, female education, and skilled birth attendance with the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), controlling for health expenditure, income, and urbanization. Methods Using data for 2000–2023, we evaluate standard and break-adjusted unit-root and cointegration tests against simulated finite-sample critical values. Long-run associations are estimated with pooled and fixed-effects regressions with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and with mean group, common correlated effects mean group, and augmented mean group (AMG) estimators, all with country-specific COVID-19 dummies. The heterogeneous estimates are summarized with medians, trimmed means, and precision weights and re-estimated in a parsimonious specification, complemented by sensitivity, missing-data, leave-one-country-out, and Dumitrescu–Hurlin analyses. Results Fertility is the most consistent correlate: the AMG elasticity is 0.64 ( p = 0.003), positive in all five countries and in every summary of the country estimates, although it is smaller and imprecise in the parsimonious specification. Skilled birth attendance is negatively associated with MMR in all fixed-effects specifications and missing-data checks. GDP per capita is negative in almost all specifications but significant mainly in the two-way models; health expenditure, female schooling, urbanization, and governance show no association that is stable across estimators. Short-run predictive relationships are absent once common shocks are removed. Conclusion The findings support sustained investment in family planning and in skilled, facility-based childbirth care. Because the MMR series is a modeled estimate that uses fertility, income, and skilled attendance as covariates, the estimates are long-run associations, not causal effects.

title: Upstream CO 2 emissions of renewable electricity supply for heavy-duty road freight – a meta-analysis
summary: This meta-analysis synthesizes findings from 80 studies on the CO2 emission performance and embodied energy of energy supply pathways for heavy-duty transport. To ensure comparability across service-equivalent system configurations, it adop
content: This meta-analysis synthesizes findings from 80 studies on the CO2 emission performance and embodied energy of energy supply pathways for heavy-duty transport. To ensure comparability across service-equivalent system configurations, it adopts a life-cycle-oriented upstream perspective covering electricity generation, fuel supply, grid, storage and the vehicle site. For the functionally disaggregated categories used in the benchmark and case study, photovoltaic electricity supply (PV-direct) shows a median upstream emission intensity of 36.6 g CO2-eq · kWh−1, while wind power (Wind-direct) shows a substantially lower median of 10.3 g CO2-eq · kWh−1. Embodied-energy estimates should be interpreted as indicative rather than definitive due to the limited sample size. Within this exploratory dataset, median values are higher for PV than for wind, at 4,222 and 1,257 kWh · kW−1, respectively. The analysis further indicates that studies excluding storage and grid infrastructure tend to underestimate the CO2 emission intensity of service-equivalent energy supply. The derived upstream parameters are applied in a complementary case study comparing depot-charged battery-electric trucks with electric road systems. For a reference electricity mix of 60% PV and 40% wind, effective upstream CO2-equivalent emissions are estimated at 51.0 g CO2-eq · kWh−1 for battery-electric operation and 34.2 g CO2-eq · kWh−1 for electric road systems. Assuming an energy consumption of 1.85 kWh · km−1, this corresponds to 94.4 and 63.2 g CO2-eq · km−1, respectively. The difference reflects lower storage requirements under dynamic charging and closer temporal coupling between renewable generation and vehicle demand. Overall, the study supports service-equivalent, time-aware upstream assessment and indicates about 50 g CO2-eq·kWh−1 as a conservative near-term planning value for supplied electricity.

title: French Daily Electricity Demand and Renewable Generation Time Series
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This real-world scenario combines four daily electricity time series: residential demand, photovoltaic generation, an additional electricity-consumption series, and wind generation. The tasks belong to the same broad energy domain but repre
content: This real-world scenario combines four daily electricity time series: residential demand, photovoltaic generation, an additional electricity-consumption series, and wind generation. The tasks belong to the same broad energy domain but represent different consumption and production processes, with distinct temporal patterns and variability. Dres: Contains daily residential demand from Enedis’s consommation_telerelevee_residentielle variable, representing average daily power consumption for remotely metered low-voltage residential users, in watts, from 2021 to 2025. Dphoto: Contains daily photovoltaic generation from Enedis’s production_photovoltaique variable, representing average daily photovoltaic power production, in watts, from 2021 to 2025. Dind: Introduces a single daily private household of energy consumption over two years, in kWh. Dwind: Contains daily wind generation from Enedis’s production_eolien variable, representing average daily wind power production, in watts, from 2021 to 2025.

title: A system level review of electric vehicle battery charging technologies and their performance constraints
summary: Electric-vehicle charging is evolving from a conventional energy-transfer function into an integrated electrochemical, thermal, power-electronic, communication, and grid-management problem. This critical review evaluates battery technologie
content: Electric-vehicle charging is evolving from a conventional energy-transfer function into an integrated electrochemical, thermal, power-electronic, communication, and grid-management problem. This critical review evaluates battery technologies, battery-management systems, charging architectures, charging-control strategies, thermal management, renewable-energy integration, bidirectional charging, and wireless charging through a unified technology-to-system framework. Unlike subsystem-focused reviews, the proposed framework evaluates charging decisions against four simultaneous constraints: electrochemical state and degradation risk, thermal headroom, converter capability and power quality, and grid/renewable availability. The review further compares technologies using consistent evidence variables, including charging time, efficiency, temperature rise, degradation/capacity retention, cost, power quality, validation scale, and technology maturity, while explicitly identifying chemistry and operating-condition dependencies. Recent experimental and model-based studies show that extreme fast charging is constrained by lithium plating, temperature rise, impedance growth, and aging-dependent changes in safe operating limits. Worked scenarios demonstrate how the framework changes the preferred charging strategy for overnight AC charging, high-power highway charging, cold-battery operation, PV-rich charging, and V2G operation. The synthesis identifies five priorities: coupled electrochemical–thermal–aging control; experimentally validated AI/MPC methods; interoperable bidirectional charging; renewable- and grid-aware infrastructure planning; and standardized field datasets. All figures are reconstructed as editable Word schematics to improve readability and facilitate modification.

title: Dynamic Security of Microgrids with Penetration of Electrical Vehicles
summary: Microgrids have become a critical component of modern power systems, especially with the rising integration of renewable energy sources and the rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). However, EV penetration introduces significant uncert
content: Microgrids have become a critical component of modern power systems, especially with the rising integration of renewable energy sources and the rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). However, EV penetration introduces significant uncertainty due to their stochastic charging behavior, posing major challenges to microgrid frequency stability and overall dynamic security. This study investigates the impact of EV charging on microgrid frequency deviation using a detailed dynamic model developed in MATLAB/Simulink. The model incorporates renewable sources, EV load profiles, and system dynamics to evaluate microgrid behavior under varying EV penetration levels. Results demonstrate that uncoordinated EV charging leads to increased frequency fluctuations, potentially threatening system stability. However, coordination strategies significantly reduce adverse impacts and improve system robustness. The study highlights the importance of adaptive control strategies and coordinated charging mechanisms in maintaining microgrid stability as EV adoption continues to grow.

title: Policy Brief #2 - PERSIST - From pilot projects to urban policy
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: HIGHLIGHTS + Positive Energy Districts (PEDs), while providing greater potential for accelerating a just transition, face a series of challenges, ranging from technological and technical ones to social, economic, governance and legal barrie
content: HIGHLIGHTS + Positive Energy Districts (PEDs), while providing greater potential for accelerating a just transition, face a series of challenges, ranging from technological and technical ones to social, economic, governance and legal barriers. + PED initiatives are often planned and financed within the timeframe of a single political mandate or a specific EU-funded project, yet the energy transition unfolds over decades. + PEDs should move beyond isolated pilot projects and become part of long-term urban development. + Spatial and urban planning instruments should create conditions that enable PED development, preparing territories for local renewable energy production, storage, sharing and flexibility. + An integrated approach is needed to coordinate energy systems, buildings, mobility, public facilities and urban infrastructure. + Municipalities should establish permanent coordination structures to ensure institutional capacity, cross-sectoral cooperation and continuity in PED development.

title: Prediction of Solar Radiation in Potiskum – Nigeria
source: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF PURE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
summary: Solar energy will remain the most environmentally clean and abundant renewable energy ever on earth surface. Hence, a handy process for predicting the solar radiation is very vital. Meteorological parameters namely; sunshine duration, maxim
content: Solar energy will remain the most environmentally clean and abundant renewable energy ever on earth surface. Hence, a handy process for predicting the solar radiation is very vital. Meteorological parameters namely; sunshine duration, maximum air temperature and relative humidity have been used to develop two model equations (12) and (13) for predicting solar radiation for Potiskum. For these model equations (12) and (13) respectively, the coefficients of determination 𝑹 𝟐 are 97.8 and 98.6, the maximum percentage error MPE are 0.3135 and 0.1177; and the root mean square errors RMSE are 0.8921 and 0.7109. These statistical validation values show that the model equations can be used at the said geographical location for predicting solar radiation.
