title: Geopolitical Rivalry and FDI: Explaining Strategic Investment under Great Power Competition
source: Journal of Business Administration and Social Studies
summary: This study investigates the dynamic relationship between geopolitical rivalry and foreign direct investment, focusing on how competition among great powers, particularly between the United States and China, is associated with changes in glo
content: This study investigates the dynamic relationship between geopolitical rivalry and foreign direct investment, focusing on how competition among great powers, particularly between the United States and China, is associated with changes in global investment patterns. In an era marked by strategic competition, sanctions, and tariff conflicts, multinational corporations and states increasingly view foreign direct investment as a tool linked to both economic opportunity and national security. The research combines political economy and international relations approaches to explain how “strategic investment,” conceptualized as cross-border capital allocation shaped by economic efficiency, political alignment, and institutional trust, evolves under conditions of rivalry, uncertainty, and fragmentation of the global economic order. Using a conceptual–comparative and descriptive approach, the paper examines inward and outward foreign direct investment trends across selected developed and emerging economies, using aggregate investment indicators and illustrative sectoral examples to explore patterns associated with bloc-based economic realignment and friend-shoring initiatives. The analysis suggests that geopolitical tensions may shape corporate investment decision-making and are consistent with broader patterns of global value chain reconfiguration in response to political alignment and changing risk perceptions, particularly in strategic sectors. The study contributes to theoretical understanding by linking realism and liberal institutionalism within a strategic investment framework and by providing an interpretive conceptualization of how geopolitical conditions interact with traditional economic drivers of foreign direct investment. Rather than establishing causal relationships, the study offers an analytical perspective intended to support future empirical investigation and inform policy discussions on balancing economic openness with national security considerations in an increasingly fragmented global economy.

title: Conditions for power-to-hydrogen as electricity storage in the Swiss electricity sector
summary: Abstract Power-to-hydrogen for electricity storage purposes could support the integration of high shares of weather-dependent renewable generation, but its deployment remains uncertain due to early stage of deployment. Using a spatially and
content: Abstract Power-to-hydrogen for electricity storage purposes could support the integration of high shares of weather-dependent renewable generation, but its deployment remains uncertain due to early stage of deployment. Using a spatially and temporally explicit electricity sector model EXPANSE for Switzerland in 2035 and three complementary sets of Plackett-Burman designs for computationally-efficient uncertainty analysis, we investigate the conditions under which power-to-hydrogen could play a more substantial role in the Swiss electricity system and compare it with the role of grid-scale batteries. Under the uncertainty ranges considered, we find that the uptake of power-to-hydrogen and its weight in a mix of storage technologies is mostly sensitive to the improvement in costs and technical characteristics, such as energy-to-power ratio and round-trip efficiency. The uptake is also substantially shaped by the evolution of the electricity generation mix. Under the restrictions of zero net import and no new power plants of biomass and waste incineration, game-changer scenarios for power-to-hydrogen are nuclear phase-out, quicker electrification of energy services, and low hydropower production. Power-to-hydrogen is found to meet different storage needs than grid-scale batteries as power-to-hydrogen addresses the more seasonal differences in electricity supply and demand, while batteries contribute to the shorter-term flexibility needs.

title: ArabAgentHallu: Towards Benchmarking Hallucination Judgment and Attribution in Arabic LLM Based Agents
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Large language model (LLM) based agents execute multi step workflows in which hallucinations at intermediate steps propagate and corrupt final outcomes.Recent work formalized automated hallucination attribution identifying the trajectory st
content: Large language model (LLM) based agents execute multi step workflows in which hallucinations at intermediate steps propagate and corrupt final outcomes.Recent work formalized automated hallucination attribution identifying the trajectory step responsible and explaining its cause but existing benchmarks are exclusively English, where frontier models reach only 41.1% step localization accuracy.To the best of our knowledge, no Arabic benchmark evaluates hallucination attribution at the trajectory step level in LLM based agents.We present ArabAgentHallu, the first study of agent hallucination judgment and attribution in Arabic.Each trajectory is an executable program over a shared state, rendered into Arabic and English from one execution, with injected hallucinations and the responsible step verified counterfactually rather than asserted.The suite comprises 900 items (450 hallucinated / 450 clean) of 7-15 steps across five hallucination categories, balanced over a category × position × length grid.Evaluation is reported for two prompting conditions compared to three reference floors, with the bootstrapped intervals and paired cross lingual statistics appropriately sized to allow for parity claims to be falsifiable.With step localization accuracy 0.396 (Arabic) / 0.438 (English) and judgment accuracy 0.607 (Arabic) / 0.627 (English), the accuracy of the step localization is well above the ceiling of 0.164, while the judgment accuracy is relatively low.The paired Arabic-English difference is -0.042 [-0.132, +0.056]: no difference is detectable above the bound 0.135.With direct prompting the model collapses towards all negative strategy and a small significant gap towards English emerges: without the step by step scaffolding, the gap emerges.The code and generator are open and the data is open.

title: Fluvial Floods in Germany: Multi-region Analysis of Data Sources on the Impact of River Flooding on Transport Infrastructure and its Resilience Management
summary: Abstract Climate change is expected to increase frequency and magnitude of fluvial floods across Europe, posing a growing threat to transport infrastructure. This research project aims to systematically identify and analyse data sources rel
content: Abstract Climate change is expected to increase frequency and magnitude of fluvial floods across Europe, posing a growing threat to transport infrastructure. This research project aims to systematically identify and analyse data sources related to the management of transport infrastructure during river flood events in selected flood-prone regions of Germany: the Rhine-Main area, the Ruhr region, the Elbe region near Dresden, the Danube region in Bavaria, and the Middle Upper Rhine and Black Forest area. The study investigates exposure and vulnerability of critical rail, road, and inland waterway infrastructure to river flooding and provides an overview of flood management practices across all transport modes. This includes collecting and analysing data on early warning systems, alert levels, protective measures, and operational procedures applied during flood events. By structuring this information across regions and transport modes, the project contributes to a cross-modal understanding of flood-related impacts on transport corridors, such as route closures and service disruptions. The findings lay the groundwork for future research focused on integrated risk assessments and adaptation strategies to increase resilience of transport infrastructure. Conducted between January and November 2025, the project contributes valuable insights for policymakers, infrastructure operators, and planners aiming to maintain mobility under growing climate risks.

title: Adsorptive Membranes for PFAS Removal: Current Status, Design Principles, and Research Needs
summary: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are contaminants of concern due to their persistence, occurrence in natural waters, and association with adverse health outcomes. Producing potable water from PFAS-impacted sources require
content: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are contaminants of concern due to their persistence, occurrence in natural waters, and association with adverse health outcomes. Producing potable water from PFAS-impacted sources requires selectively removing PFAS from complex waters. Adsorptive membranes are an emerging strategy for PFAS removal due to their tunable architectures and chemistries, modularity, and high water permeances. However, it is difficult to compare adsorptive membrane performance across studies and identify membrane properties governing PFAS removal due to the diversity of materials, architectures, testing conditions, and reported performance metrics. This review critically evaluates the state of PFAS adsorptive membranes by examining nanofiber membranes, asymmetric membranes, adsorptive nanofiltration (NF) membranes, and ion exchange membranes used for adsorptive PFAS removal. We highlight structure-property-performance relationships, assess current testing strategies, and recommend standard performance metrics to enable cross-study comparisons. We further compare adsorptive membrane performance to conventional reverse osmosis (RO) and NF membranes. Finally, we apply the convection-diffusion-adsorption (CDA) model to published PFAS breakthrough data to gain mechanistic insights into the role of membrane properties and operating parameters on PFAS removal. Overall, this review provides a framework for evaluating adsorptive membranes, identifies key research gaps, and establishes design criteria to advance adsorptive PFAS separations.

title: Connecting Ethnoscience, Augmented Reality, and Inquiry in Science Education: A Systematic Review and the BICK FOUR Framework
source: JagoMIPA Jurnal Pendidikan Matematika dan IPA
summary: The integration of Augmented Reality (AR) in science education has moved from technology-driven visualization toward contextualized, inquiry-oriented, and culturally responsive learning. This study systematically reviews AR studies that int
content: The integration of Augmented Reality (AR) in science education has moved from technology-driven visualization toward contextualized, inquiry-oriented, and culturally responsive learning. This study systematically reviews AR studies that integrate local wisdom, ethnoscience, and ethnopedagogy, and uses the BICK FOUR framework (Building Context, Investigating, Constructing, and Knowledge Retention) as a synthesis lens. Scopus was searched for English-language journal articles published between 2016 and 2026, following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Of 62 unique records, 35 met the inclusion criteria and 32 articles passed quality assessment for thematic synthesis. Fifteen of the 31 primary studies addressed science or STEM subjects, and most originated in Indonesia. The studies reported gains in conceptual understanding, representation skills, scientific literacy, motivation, and creativity when AR was combined with local cultural contexts, but none reported a delayed retention measure. The synthesis positions cultural knowledge within Building Context and links it to Investigating, Constructing, and Knowledge Retention in a culturally responsive BICK FOUR architecture. This architecture is conceptual and requires empirical testing.

title: A Hydrogen-Supported Framework for Detecting Lacunar Infarcts Using Neuroimaging and Deep-Learning Algorithms
source: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
summary: Lacunar infarction is a form of cerebral small-vessel disease (SVD) and is often not identified, as lesions can be small, subtle and morphologically indistinguishable from other white-matter processes. This manuscript introduces a framework
content: Lacunar infarction is a form of cerebral small-vessel disease (SVD) and is often not identified, as lesions can be small, subtle and morphologically indistinguishable from other white-matter processes. This manuscript introduces a framework for detecting lacunar infarcts in neuroimaging data based on medical-image preprocessing, conventional machine learning, convolutional neural networks, and residual neural networks, all with the assistance of hydrogen. There are two interrelated, but analytically distinct branches of the framework. The diagnostic branch collects and processes anonymized MRI or CT data, builds predictive models, and assesses the models using appropriate metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall, F1 score, area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve, calibration and lesion-localisation metrics. The infrastructure branch estimates the electricity consumption for image acquisition, data storage, model training, cooling, and clinical inference, and evaluates the technical and environmental feasibility of using hydrogen as a back-up or long-duration storage method. Hydrogen is not suggested as a substitute for clinical skills or as a treatment or diagnostic signal. Its intended use is for reliable and resilient operation of infrastructure needed for the deployment of medical-AI. This is a proposed framework and not a completed clinical validation study, therefore, the manuscript does not make any claims of the effectiveness of the diagnosis. Instead, it outlines a reproducible design and an evaluation program to use in future empirical research.

title: Nano-enabled neem biopesticides as next-generation agro-inputs for sustainable plant protection
summary: Owing to their inherent toxic manifestations, environmental pollution, and resistance development in pests, conventional pesticides have saturated the farming industry, encouraging researchers to look into alternative options. In this regar
content: Owing to their inherent toxic manifestations, environmental pollution, and resistance development in pests, conventional pesticides have saturated the farming industry, encouraging researchers to look into alternative options. In this regard, Neem ( Azadirachta indica )–based biopesticides offers broad-spectrum pest control with beneficial ecotoxicity profiles. Nevertheless, their commercial scalability has been impeded by the instability of their constituents, including rapid photo-degradation, negligible water solubility, and brief field persistence. Thus, nanotechnology presents an impeccable answer to overcome the disadvantages of these biological pesticides. This review critically evaluates neem-based nano-formulations as next-generation pesticides that address these constraints through rational nanocarrier engineering. The state-of-the-art advancements in polymeric, lipid-based, inorganic, and hybrid nanocarriers are systematically examined. This investigation emphasizes the role of carrier chemistry, interfacial architecture, and matrix networking in regulating encapsulation efficiency, release kinetics, photostability, and biological efficacy. Mechanistic insights reveal that nano-encapsulation enhances bioavailability, prolongs residual activity, improves foliar retention, and preserves synergistic interactions, thereby reducing the need for repeated applications and lowering resistance pressure. Altogether, nano-enabled neem formulations exemplify the practical application of nanotechnology in transforming traditional botanical insecticides into precise, environmentally controlled crop protection measures for sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.

title: How Far Ahead Must a Storage Fleet See? Certified Value of Foresight and the Limits of Information-Relaxation Bounds
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Storage fleets are scheduled by rolling lookahead under forecast errors that grow with lead time. How far is such scheduling from the best achievable, and how much would better foresight at each lead time be worth? The cost under perfect in
content: Storage fleets are scheduled by rolling lookahead under forecast errors that grow with lead time. How far is such scheduling from the best achievable, and how much would better foresight at each lead time be worth? The cost under perfect information (PI) answers neither, because it mixes policy suboptimality with the value of information. We answer both with certificates. Block information relaxations, in which the scheduler sees each block of B hours in advance but remains nonanticipative across blocks, form a monotone family between PI and the optimum, and feasible block policies turn them into certified upper bounds on the value of knowing the future beyond B hours. With PI, a strong policy—scenario lookahead with stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) terminal values—sandwiches the optimum. We also show why the lower bound resists tightening at system scale: when renewable availability saturates at zero, every lower bound that is convex in the forecast-error state, SDDP's included, is vacuous, and penalties built from approximate value functions are arbitraged at first order, with losses that grow with the fleet's energy capacity. On a modified RTS-GMLC system with wind capacity equal to peak load, the best policy is within 0.62% of PI. Rolling deterministic lookahead is therefore certified to lose 2.6–3.2% of weekly cost (14–15% with RTS-GMLC-level wind errors), so most of its gap to PI is policy loss, not value of information. Foresight beyond the current day is worth at most 0.11%, and multiplier errors of a few $/MWh erase the entire remaining gap. Preprint (submitted version) of a manuscript submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Systems. Pages 9–15 contain the supplementary material. Code and stored results: see the related software record.

title: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition for Hydrogen Refueling Infrastructure
source: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
summary: Due to its high energy density and potential for using renewable energies, hydrogen is an ideal energy source for decarbonizing the transportation and industrial sectors. However, hydrogen refueling infrastructure (HRI) is a challenging eng
content: Due to its high energy density and potential for using renewable energies, hydrogen is an ideal energy source for decarbonizing the transportation and industrial sectors. However, hydrogen refueling infrastructure (HRI) is a challenging engineering challenge because it is a complex system with complex safety, reliability, and real-time coordination issues, especially in the high-pressure (350-700 bar) environment. Current approaches with the use of Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) focus on optimizing single components and have a limited focus on control concepts that consider hydrogen specific risks such as leakage, pressure instability, and system failures. In this paper, the introduction of a supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)-based system for monitoring and controlling HRI is proposed for monitoring and controlling HRI. The system combines field-level sensing, PLC/RTU control, and supervisory analytics to provide real-time data acquisition, fault detection, and safety response. It coordinates production, storage, and refueling procedures using multi-sensor fusion, threshold-based fault logic, and emergency shutdowns. The proposed system was found to be more reliable and safer to use where HRI are installed. The modular approach allows for rapid development without impact on performance.

title: Decision learning and strategy optimization for energy allocation under power-hydrogen synergy constraints
source: International Conference on Advanced Optics and Photonics Research in Engineering (AOPR)
summary: The integration of renewable energy necessitates flexible storage solutions like Integrated Power-Hydrogen Systems (IPHS). However, achieving optimal real-time energy allocation while strictly adhering to complex physical constraints remain
content: The integration of renewable energy necessitates flexible storage solutions like Integrated Power-Hydrogen Systems (IPHS). However, achieving optimal real-time energy allocation while strictly adhering to complex physical constraints remains a critical challenge. This paper proposes a constraint-aware decision-learning framework. We formulate the dispatch problem as a Constrained Markov Decision Process and introduce an adaptive Safe Deep Reinforcement Learning algorithm. Crucially, a differentiable safety projection layer is embedded to mathematically guarantee strict boundary compliance. Experimental evaluations on edge devices demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 95.5% nearoptimal economic reward with absolute zero constraint violations under extreme volatility. Furthermore, it operates with a highly efficient 12.8 ms inference latency and a minimal parameter footprint, perfectly balancing algorithmic precision and computational overhead. Future work will extend this framework to decentralized multi-agent topologies for largescale grid coordination.

title: Integrative Optimization and Comparative Analysis of Geothermal-Powered Energy Systems for Sustainable Production of Electricity, Water, and Hydrogen
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: The growing demand for clean energy, freshwater, and low-carbon fuels has intensified the need for integrated and sustainable energy-water systems. Geothermal energy, as a reliable and weather-independent renewable resource with a high capa
content: The growing demand for clean energy, freshwater, and low-carbon fuels has intensified the need for integrated and sustainable energy-water systems. Geothermal energy, as a reliable and weather-independent renewable resource with a high capacity factor, offers strong potential to simultaneously address power generation, water scarcity, and green hydrogen production. This work systematically investigates the integration of geothermal energy with power generation, desalination, and hydrogen production through thermodynamic modeling, techno-economic analysis, multi-objective optimization, and advanced membrane development. In the first phase, geothermal-driven organic Rankine cycle (ORC) systems were evaluated under basic, parallel, and series configurations to convert medium-grade geothermal heat into electricity for desalination applications. Multi-objective optimization using artificial neural networks (ANN) and genetic algorithms (GA) demonstrated that optimized parallel configurations improved power generation by up to 150% and freshwater production by 60% compared to basic layouts, while enhancing exergy efficiency and reducing levelized costs. In the second phase, building upon the optimized ORC frameworks, the system was expanded into an integrated multi-carrier energy platform. The extended configuration combined geothermal energy, dual ORCs, LNG cold exergy utilization, solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC), reverse osmosis (RO) desalination, and proton exchange membrane electrolysis (PEME) to enable simultaneous production of electricity, freshwater, and hydrogen. Through energy cascading and exergy minimization, the integrated system achieved electrical efficiencies exceeding 50%, with exergy efficiencies approaching 60% under optimized conditions. Thermo-economic optimization identified optimal working fluid combinations that enhanced net power output, hydrogen generation, and water production while lowering the levelized costs of electricity, water, and hydrogen. In the third phase, a comparative assessment of geothermal-powered desalination integrated with hydrogen production was conducted to evaluate multi-effect Distillation (MED) and RO under identical operating conditions. Both configurations were coupled with PEM electrolysis, where desalinated water served as the hydrogen feedstock. Results showed that the RO-based system achieved lower levelized costs of water and hydrogen, broader operational flexibility, and superior overall economic performance, while MED demonstrated advantages only under specific thermal utilization scenarios. In the final phase, recognizing that geothermal and thermally intensive industrial streams are often available at elevated temperatures, high-temperature reverse osmosis (HTRO) membranes were developed to directly utilize these hot feeds without intermediate cooling. The membranes were experimentally validated for stable operation up to 120 °C, aligning with typical geothermal brine and SAGD produced water co

title: Geospatial disparities in gray divorce geographies: sociodemographic determinants of late-life marital dissolution
summary: Demographic shifts and technology have impacted family stability, with ‘grey divorce’—marriage dissolution after age 50—emerging as a significant issue. While individualization trends prevail in affluent nations, Kuwait and Gulf Cooperation
content: Demographic shifts and technology have impacted family stability, with ‘grey divorce’—marriage dissolution after age 50—emerging as a significant issue. While individualization trends prevail in affluent nations, Kuwait and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) societies experience tensions between traditional values and modernization. Utilizing georeferenced aggregated data from 2024, this study investigates gray divorce among women aged 50 years and older across urban zones in Kuwait’s governorates. Excess Risk estimation was employed to identify zones that deviated from the national divorce rate. Additionally, Spatial Empirical Bayes (SEP) smoothing was applied to stabilize rates in zones with a limited number of cases, while Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) was used to delineate clusters and outliers. The findings revealed divorce hotspots in northwestern and northeastern neighborhoods, contrasting with cold spots in the southern regions. Higher gray divorce rates occur in areas where women have higher education, housewives are common, and family sizes are larger, a pattern at the neighborhood level may suggest stress on multigenerational family models; however, the aggregate design does not allow for inferences regarding individual couples. This study shows the need for spatially informed policies to address older adults’ vulnerabilities and advocate strategies to mitigate gray divorce impacts within modernizing GCC societies.

title: Katı geri kazanılmış yakıt (SRF) üretiminin çevresel etkilerine yönelik yaşam döngüsü değerlendirmesi (YDD) çalışması
summary: Atıkların biyokütle olarak kabulü ile enerji kaynağı olarak değerlendirilmesi uzun süredir tüm dünyada çalışılmaktadır. Enerji kazanımı ve atıkların yönetiminde çeşitli katı atıklar, atıktan türetilmiş yakıt (ATY) ve katı geri kazanılmış ya
content: Atıkların biyokütle olarak kabulü ile enerji kaynağı olarak değerlendirilmesi uzun süredir tüm dünyada çalışılmaktadır. Enerji kazanımı ve atıkların yönetiminde çeşitli katı atıklar, atıktan türetilmiş yakıt (ATY) ve katı geri kazanılmış yakıt (SRF) olarak hazırlanarak, enerji üretiminde ve çimento sektörü örneği gibi beraber yakma için kullanılmaktadır. SRF’in alternatif yakıt olarak kullanılması ve atık bertaraf yöntemleri yerine kullanılması ile çevresel etkilerinin azaltıldığı söylenebilmektedir. Yaşam döngüsü değerlendirmesi- analizleri (YDD) ile potansiyel çevresel etkilerini hesaplamak ve karşılaştırmak mümkündür. Bu çalışma ile bir SRF işleme tesisi verileri incelenmiştir. YDD açık kaynak programı kullanılarak tamamlanmış ve çevresel etki kıyaslaması yapılmıştır. SRF üretimi aşamalara ayrılarak açıklanmış, 83,62 kg CO2-eşdeğeri emisyon oluştuğu hesaplanmıştır. Küresel ısınma potansiyeline (GWP) katkısının, %65,62 ile en yüksek atık ve SRF taşıma aşamalarından geldiği görülmüştür. Duyarlılık analizi ile taşıma ve tesis elektrik tüketimi değişim % değerleri incelenerek, doğru orantılı değişim görülmüştür. Üretilen bir ton SRF için yaklaşık 500 kg kok kömür ikamesi yerine geçebileceğini göstermiştir. İkame yakıt olarak kullanımı sonucu hem atık bertarafının sağlandığı hem de çimento üretiminde önemli ölçüde CO2-eşdeğeri tasarruf sağlandığı görülmüştür. SRF üretiminden kaynaklanan emisyon değerine rağmen, beraber yakma prosesine bağlı olarak, bu tasarruf ton başına 770 kg CO2-eşdeğerine ulaşabilmektedir. Tesis optimizasyonu ve SRF ısıl değerlerinin çevresel etki değerleri için önemli olduğu belirlenmiştir.

title: Blue and Green Music to the Fear: Centring (on) Periphery through Decolonial Translation
source: ES Review Spanish Journal of English Studies
summary: Disconcerting trends of decline in the use of the Galician language marked a record low ebb in 2024 and saw its degradation to a statistical minority in Galicia for the first time in its modern history. Nevertheless, this article asks not w
content: Disconcerting trends of decline in the use of the Galician language marked a record low ebb in 2024 and saw its degradation to a statistical minority in Galicia for the first time in its modern history. Nevertheless, this article asks not what we can do for Galician, but what Galician can and does do for other languages and for the wider, alternative ecosystem of peripheral epistemology. Specifically, it explores the translational interaction between Galician and Irish English as a source of sustainable, renewable energy for both. The analysis focuses on the poetry collection Diario de Crosses Green by Martín Veiga and its translation into English by the Irish poet and translator Keith Payne.

title: A Short History of Extractivism and Opposition to Critical Minerals Extraction
summary: Phasing out fossil fuels and scaling up a clean energy transition at the pace needed to avoid the worst consequences of climate change has far-reaching implications for frontline communities.It requires increasing the production of raw mate
content: Phasing out fossil fuels and scaling up a clean energy transition at the pace needed to avoid the worst consequences of climate change has far-reaching implications for frontline communities.It requires increasing the production of raw materials needed to manufacture solar panels, wind turbines, electric vehicles, and other technologies.In 2021, the International Energy Agency predicted that keeping the world on a path to hold global warming to 2°C will require expanding critical minerals production sixfold to fortythree million tons per year by 2040. 1 Materials needed for clean energy technologies, such as lithium, nickel, cobalt, and copper, often occur in ore grades measuring less than 1 percent. 2 That means for every ton of finished material, hundreds of tons of ore will have to be mined and pro cessed, with potential ill consequences for local environments and communities.Mining proj ects needed to supply energy transition minerals and metals can compound historical injustices.For instance, a large percentage of active or projected mining proj ects for energy transition minerals and metals are located on or near Indigenous peoples and their territories.3 Perhaps for this reason, Indigenous peoples, among the most adamant advocates for taking action to address the climate crisis, are also among the most outspoken opponents of such mining proj ects.Responding to a proposed lithium mine on the traditional territory of the Shoshone and Paiute people, one tribal member explained that their local water supply was already contaminated with mercury and her people sick from the "last mine."She asked, "[ Isn't] there a better way that we could get clean energy?" 4 For many frontline communities, the clean energy transition appears not so much as the harbinger of a modern era of sustainability as yet another front in a long history of extractivism: putting the interests of outsiders and their claims on land and resources ahead of those of local and Indigenous peoples.In this moment, when efforts to scale up a clean energy transition globally are accelerating, historians can play a key role in considering the 37 A Short History of Extractivism and Opposition to Critical Minerals Extraction

title: Institutions and transformative change in water management: A case study of wetland restoration on the island of Öland, Sweden
summary: Institutions play a dual role in sustainability transformations. On the one hand, they may impede transformative change by reproducing views, structures, and practices that either contribute to environmental damage or fail to effectively ad
content: Institutions play a dual role in sustainability transformations. On the one hand, they may impede transformative change by reproducing views, structures, and practices that either contribute to environmental damage or fail to effectively address such damage. On the other hand, they are also needed to institutionalise new views and practices that enable transformation and the restructuring of society towards sustainability. In this paper, we take a closer look at the dual role of institutions in relation to transformative change through a case study of wetland restoration on the Swedish island of Öland. A key institution for water management in Sweden are so-called ‘drainage enterprises’. As the name suggests, these institutions were originally established to drain water from land for cultivation purposes. While land use and its values have changed considerably on Öland over the past 150 years, the legal status of drainage enterprises has remained intact. Today, this legal status hampers efforts to retain water on land, including wetland restoration. Results from the case study are used to discuss the relation of institutions to sustainability transformations, and what this means in practice for pursuing transformative change in water management, especially during times when the legitimacy and confidence in public institutions stands under pressure.

title: Does AI Readiness Accelerate Sustainable Development? Evidence From 80 Developing Economies
summary: ABSTRACT Progress toward the sustainable development goals (SDGs) remains insufficient to meet the 2030 targets, renewing interest in whether artificial intelligence can accelerate it. Research has concentrated on what particular AI applica
content: ABSTRACT Progress toward the sustainable development goals (SDGs) remains insufficient to meet the 2030 targets, renewing interest in whether artificial intelligence can accelerate it. Research has concentrated on what particular AI applications achieve, leaving national AI readiness, the structural capacity to deploy AI, largely untested. Using panel data of 80 developing economies over 2017–2023, we construct a six‐component readiness index through principal component analysis, validate it against an external benchmark, and estimate effects across the conditional SDG distribution with method of moments quantile regression. Readiness is positively associated with SDG achievement at every quantile, most strongly for countries furthest from their targets, the reverse of the pattern for income per capita. A pooled comparison across income groups shows the same ordering, and Granger tests indicate bidirectional predictive links. The evidence favours technological leapfrogging over absorptive capacity, implying that AI readiness investment yields its largest estimated returns in the lowest‐income economies.

title: Comparison of Maximum Power Point Tracking Algorithms for a 50 W Fuel Cell Stack
summary: Efficient maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is essential for proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells (FCs) to optimize power output under dynamic operational and load conditions. In this study, a thorough theoretical analysis, simulatio
content: Efficient maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is essential for proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells (FCs) to optimize power output under dynamic operational and load conditions. In this study, a thorough theoretical analysis, simulation model, and experimental validation of a 50 W PEM FC system integrated with a step-up DC-DC boost converter operating at a switching frequency of 20 kHz are presented. Two classical MPPT algorithms – perturb and observe (P&O) and incremental conductance (IC) – are evaluated and contrasted to optimize output voltage and current levels. By stepping up a 5 V DC FC input to a stable 12 V DC output, the closed-loop control scheme minimizes current ripple, ensures stable voltage regulation, and enhances overall dynamic performance. Comprehensive MATLAB/Simulink simulations were conducted to assess steady-state efficiency, tracking speed, and power oscillations under transient load variations. Furthermore, a physical laboratory test bench incorporating a 50 W FC stack and a custom boost converter circuit was constructed to validate the theoretical and simulation framework. Experimental results closely match the simulated characteristics, confirming that the IC algorithm achieves superior tracking accuracy, reduced output ripple, and faster transient response compared to the conventional P&O scheme. These findings provide practical design guidelines for developing robust FC power management and conditioning interfaces in low-voltage renewable energy applications.

title: Bio-based nanoparticles for pesticide applications: a comprehensive review
summary: The effectiveness of conventional chemical pesticides has been increasingly undermined by pest resistance, environmental contamination, and non-target toxicity. Nano-enabled biopesticides have appeared as a promising alternative to enhance
content: The effectiveness of conventional chemical pesticides has been increasingly undermined by pest resistance, environmental contamination, and non-target toxicity. Nano-enabled biopesticides have appeared as a promising alternative to enhance efficacy while reducing ecological risks. This review aims to critically evaluate recent advances in nanotechnology-based biopesticides, with emphasis on biopolymer, protein, and plant-derived nano formulations. Chitosan nanoparticles showed strong performance in dsRNA and essential-oil delivery, achieving 2.5-fold higher uptake, 60–67% pest mortality, and up to 96% gene silencing. Cellulose nanocrystal emulsions and alginate carriers enhanced stability and pathogen suppression by >70% while keeping plant compatibility. Protein-based systems, particularly zein nanoparticles, reduced LC50 values by 40–60% with minimal non-target toxicity. Across systems, nano formulation improved penetration, UV stability (2–10×), and controlled release. Nano-enabled biopesticides significantly enhance the efficiency and durability of biological active agents. However, challenges stay in large-scale field validation, environmental fate assessment, and regulatory harmonization. Future research should prioritize safety-by-design strategies and translational studies to support sustainable agricultural deployment.

title: Mind the Gap: Quantifying Wind and Solar Value Through Battery Sizing in Alberta
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Wind and solar generation varies hourly, daily, seasonally, and interannually. Consequently, their value in meeting electricity demand depends not only on the amount of electricity they generate, but also on when that generation is availabl
content: Wind and solar generation varies hourly, daily, seasonally, and interannually. Consequently, their value in meeting electricity demand depends not only on the amount of electricity they generate, but also on when that generation is available to meet the system's demand. Existing resource adequacy metrics do not necessarily characterize both the magnitude of the instantaneous generation shortfall and the duration of an extended energy deficit. This thesis develops a diagnostic metric based on the charging and discharging principles of a hypothetical battery to quantify the temporal mismatch between renewable generation and electricity demand. The metric was applied using historical hourly electricity demand and wind and solar capacity-factor data for Alberta over five April-to-March study periods beginning from 2021 through 2025. Wind and solar generation were scaled to meet total demand, and the hypothetical battery charged during periods of surplus renewable generation and discharged during periods of insufficient generation. Battery power, measured in gigawatts, characterized the largest instantaneous mismatch, while battery energy, measured in gigawatt-hours, represented the cumulative mismatch over time. Wind-only, solar-only, and optimized wind-solar systems were evaluated. Separate minimization cases minimized battery power and battery energy. The analysis also considered a continuous five-year period, renewable curtailment, California as a regional comparison, and additional electricity demand associated with electric vehicle and heat pump adoption. The results demonstrated the importance of evaluating battery power and energy together because they describe different aspects of temporal mismatch. In Alberta, wind generally provided greater value to meet load than solar because its generation pattern aligned more closely with periods of higher electricity demand. However, including both resources reduced storage requirements compared with relying on either resource independently, demonstrating the complementary value of wind and solar generation. Battery power requirements were determined by rare hours of large instantaneous mismatch. In contrast, battery energy requirements were strongly influenced by a small number of prolonged low-renewable-generation events, also known as Dunkelflaute periods. The continuous five-year simulation required substantially greater storage than the individual year cases because it captured a wider range and sequence of generation and demand conditions. Allowing renewable curtailment reduced storage requirement without substantially changing the optimized wind and solar proportions. In contrast to Alberta, the California analysis generally favoured solar generation, demonstrating that the metric responds to regional generation and demand patterns rather than consistently favouring one renewable resource. Electrification scenarios further showed that renewable resource value depends on both the magnitude and ti

title: Influence of Career Guidance on Female Students’ Enrollment in Electrical Engineering Programs in TVET Institutions in Nairobi City County, Kenya
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: Female enrollment in Electrical Engineering programmes in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions in Nairobi City County remains persistently low, despite national efforts to promote gender equity in technical fi
content: Female enrollment in Electrical Engineering programmes in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions in Nairobi City County remains persistently low, despite national efforts to promote gender equity in technical fields.This disparity raises concern given the sector's importance to industrial growth and the underrepresentation of women in engineering careers.The study was guided by the purpose of assessing the influence of career guidance on female students' enrollment in Electrical Engineering programmes in TVET institutions in Nairobi City County, anchored on the Social Cognitive Career Theory, which explains how self-efficacy beliefs and outcome expectations shape career interests and choices.The study adopted a descriptive survey design with a mixed-methods approach.The target population comprised female trainees, trainers, and principals across TVET institutions in Nairobi City County, from which a sample of 211 female trainees, 102 trainers, and 10 principals across 15 institutions was drawn.Data were collected using structured questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and focus group discussion guides.Instrument validity was established through expert review, while reliability was confirmed through Cronbach's alpha (α = 0.857).Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including Pearson correlation and multiple regression, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis.Findings indicated that mentorship, exposure to female engineers, and parental support were associated with higher enrollment interest, while inadequate information, gender-biased counseling, and inconsistent guidance were associated with lower enrollment.The study concludes that career guidance is associated with female students' enrollment decisions and recommends institutionalizing gender-responsive, mentorship-driven guidance frameworks.

title: The relevance of the Joule–Thomson effect to CO2–geothermal operations, with reference to production and injection wells
summary: Abstract The CO2-geothermal (CO2 Plume Geothermal) process has been the focus of research for over a decade. The efficacy of the system in terms of heat extraction has been demonstrated, while its potential benefit in terms of CO2 storage h
content: Abstract The CO2-geothermal (CO2 Plume Geothermal) process has been the focus of research for over a decade. The efficacy of the system in terms of heat extraction has been demonstrated, while its potential benefit in terms of CO2 storage has been highlighted. Nevertheless, further elucidation is required in the context of field applications, including the flow behaviour of supercritical CO₂ within the wellbore, which is directly related to energy extraction. The objective of this study is to demonstrate the significance of the Joule-Thomson (JT) effect in CO2 well flow and to determine its potential impact on the engineering components of such systems, particularly on energy extraction.A theoretical evaluation of the CO₂ flow within a wellbore suggests that temperature fluctuations are also impacted by the JT effect, in addition to variations in kinetic and gravitational energies, and the heat transfer from adjacent formations. The numerical results demonstrate that, although the role of heat transfer from the surrounding formations via the well integrity component is relatively minor, the other thermal components — including the JT effect and gravitational energy conversion — have a significant impact on production conditions at the wellhead. While the extent of CO2 cooling is certainly due to the thermodynamic conditions in the borehole, the temperature may still be low enough to significantly reduce energy extraction performance at the surface. Numerical assessments indicate that energy extraction could be reduced by 80–90% due to enthalpy losses in the wellbore.The thermal effects are also relevant during injection and result in a warming effect. While the warming has been shown to reduce the cooling of the reservoir, it does not offset the negative impact of the JT effect on energy extraction during production. Consequently, the design and engineering of CO2-geothermal systems must incorporate reservoir-well coupled modelling to ensure a realistic assessment of energy extraction.

title: Resilient Adaptive VSG Control of a Renewable-Rich Islanded Microgrid: Dynamic Assessment and Resilience Framework
summary: A resilient adaptive virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control framework is developed and evaluated for a 50-kW photovoltaic (PV)–battery islanded microgrid exposed to significant load changes and renewable-generation variability. The stu
content: A resilient adaptive virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control framework is developed and evaluated for a 50-kW photovoltaic (PV)–battery islanded microgrid exposed to significant load changes and renewable-generation variability. The study employs 15-second dynamic simulations to compare conventional droop control with adaptive VSG control, assessing AC voltage, frequency, rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), battery power, state of charge (SOC), DC-link voltage, efficiency, power factor, current, and a modeled voltage-THD indicator. Results indicate that adaptive VSG reduces the visible peak frequency excursion and RoCoF compared to conventional droop control. However, the current tuning also yields substantially larger AC-voltage excursions and a more pronounced battery discharge response. These findings show that resilience assessment requires considering coordinated frequency, voltage, DC-link, and battery constraints, not frequency performance alone. Accordingly, a multi-objective resilience framework is formulated that adapts virtual inertia, damping, voltage-support gains, and battery support based on renewable/load disturbance severity and battery operating state. This approach establishes a dynamic baseline and a reproducible resilience-assessment framework that can be extended to additional external disturbances in future research.

title: IoT-Enabled Predictive Maintenance for Hydrogen Infrastructure: A Design-Science Framework for Safety, Reliability and Operational Decision Support
source: International Journal of Energy Research Science and Engineering
summary: Hydrogen infrastructure is growing in size and complexity with scale and safety, reliability, leak, compressor degradation, storage integrity and sensor drift/downtime being still significant challenges to dependable operation. The project
content: Hydrogen infrastructure is growing in size and complexity with scale and safety, reliability, leak, compressor degradation, storage integrity and sensor drift/downtime being still significant challenges to dependable operation. The project presented in this paper is developed using a design science and scenario based engineering approach for hydrogen-specific, Internet of Things (IoT) enabled predictive-maintenance framework. The contribution is a conceptual and technical contribution instead of an empirical field implementation, therefore no claim is made with regard to the reduction of downtime, cost or incidents that can be measured in an experiment. It has six layers that are integrated into this framework, namely: assets, sensing, edge processing, secure communications, analytics and maintenance decision support. Also, it implements a clear Hydrogen Asset Health Index (HAHI), a safety-override rule, an asset-failure-sensor-decision matrix, as well as a mapping to the implementation of the hydrogen, functional-safety and industrial-cybersecurity standards. As an application example a medium-scale hydrogen production and refuelling station is considered consisting of an electrolyser, compressor, high pressure storage, dispensers and a safety-detection network. The analysis reveals the possibility of combining hydrogen concentration, electrical measurements, strain, temperature, acoustic emission, vibration and pressure decay with a combination of rule-based logic, physics-based models, machine learning and digital twins for a more timely diagnosis and maintenance based on risk assessment. Those systems are certified and are designated to be used as the primary protection and emergency shutoff device and should not be supplanted by the framework. It is therefore proposed to follow a staged validation roadmap for laboratory testing, fault-injection studies and pilot deployment and multi-site evaluation. The paper characterizes the predictive maintenance as a function of safety and reliability that relies on proven sensing, explainable analytics, cybersecurity, standards and disciplined maintenance practices.

title: Análise das intervenções no mercado de energia elétrica brasileiro sob a perspectiva austríaca: o caso da geração distribuída
source: MISES Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy Law and Economics
summary: Este artigo analisa, sob a ótica da Escola Austríaca, as intervenções estatais no setor elétrico brasileiro, com foco na política de fomento à micro e minigeração distribuída (GD). Com base na teoria do intervencionismo de Mises, Ikeda, Bra
content: Este artigo analisa, sob a ótica da Escola Austríaca, as intervenções estatais no setor elétrico brasileiro, com foco na política de fomento à micro e minigeração distribuída (GD). Com base na teoria do intervencionismo de Mises, Ikeda, Bradley e Barbieri, propõe-se um método para identificar o nexo causal e a direção das intervenções. Estima-se que elas custaram cerca de R$ 130 bilhões aos consumidores em 2023 e quase dobraram a tarifa residencial. A expansão da GD decorreu tanto das tarifas infladas por intervenções anteriores quanto do subsídio do sistema de compensação, pago pelos demais consumidores. Conclui-se que a política é nova camada de intervenção e que o setor se aproxima da escolha, apontada por Mises, entre mercado e controle estatal.

title: Study of Stress-Concentrated Areas in a 600 MW Corner-Fired Pulverized-Fuel Boiler under Flexible Operation: A Knowledge-Based Assessment Framework for Proactive Maintenance
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Flexible operation of coal-fired units—frequent start-ups, rapid load ramps, prolonged part-load running and two-shifting—has become unavoidable as renewable energy penetration grows in India. Large pulverized-fuel (PF) boilers such as 600
content: Flexible operation of coal-fired units—frequent start-ups, rapid load ramps, prolonged part-load running and two-shifting—has become unavoidable as renewable energy penetration grows in India. Large pulverized-fuel (PF) boilers such as 600 MW corner-fired units were designed for steady base-load duty, so their pressure parts now experience thermal, mechanical and chemical cycling for which they were not originally optimised. This paper presents a structured, knowledge-based assessment (KBA) framework for identifying stress-concentrated areas and cracking potential in such a boiler so that maintenance can move from reactive repair to proactive prevention. Seven damage mechanisms (high- and low-temperature thermal fatigue, creep–fatigue interaction, corrosion fatigue, stress corrosion cracking, mechanical restraint and flow-induced vibration) are mapped to boiler components, and a five-phase method—data collection, expert knowledge elicitation, prioritisation of high-risk areas, inspection and monitoring strategy, and preventive and mitigation measures—is described. Pictorials, a mechanism–location matrix and a likelihood–consequence risk matrix are provided so that maintenance engineers can convert plant data into a ranked, targeted inspection plan during planned outages.

title: Evaluating the Compliance Levels of Electrical Safety Rules and Guidelines in Selected Technical and Vocational Education and Training Institutions in Nyeri County, Kenya
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: Electrical safety is critical in TVET institutions due to frequent handling of live circuits, machinery, and electrical tools.This study evaluated electrical safety compliance in selected TVET institutions in Nyeri County, Kenya.Using a des
content: Electrical safety is critical in TVET institutions due to frequent handling of live circuits, machinery, and electrical tools.This study evaluated electrical safety compliance in selected TVET institutions in Nyeri County, Kenya.Using a descriptive survey design, quantitative data were gathered via questionnaires from 290 respondents (234 trainees, 56 trainers) and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics.Qualitative data from six administrator interviews and six observation checklists were analyzed thematically.The results demonstrated moderate overall compliance (M = 3.11, SD = 0.91).Specifically, guideline adequacy recorded a mean of 3.12 (SD = 0.96), compliance with safety rules 3.09 (SD = 0.95), safety equipment 3.14 (SD = 0.95), and safety training 3.11 (SD = 0.94).A significant association was found between safety training and compliance levels, χ²(4, N = 290) = 232.81,p < .001(Cramer's V = .634).Multiple regression revealed that guideline adequacy, safety equipment, and safety training jointly explained 84.7% of compliance variance, F(3, 286) = 527.885,p < .001.Safety equipment was the strongest predictor (β = .370),followed by safety training (β = .305)and guideline adequacy (β = .289).Qualitative and observation findings revealed outdated or generic guidelines, weak routine inspection, equipment serviceability gaps, irregular practical safety training, supervision challenges and budgetary constraints.The study concludes that compliance is moderate and requires an integrated institutional approach combining accessible workshop-specific guidelines, functional safety equipment, continuous practical training, routine inspection and stronger supervision.

title: Ecos do Vigor Econômico Chinês: comércio e investimentos envolvendo o Brasil e Santa Catarina
summary: A proeminência mundial chinesa é um destacado traço da atualidade, em taxas de crescimento ou em comércio e inversões externas. Este estudo, baseado em pesquisa documental e bibliográfica, focaliza a projeção do país asiático no Brasil e em
content: A proeminência mundial chinesa é um destacado traço da atualidade, em taxas de crescimento ou em comércio e inversões externas. Este estudo, baseado em pesquisa documental e bibliográfica, focaliza a projeção do país asiático no Brasil e em Santa Catarina com respeito a comércio e investimentos. Mostra-se forte e progressiva a participação chinesa no intercâmbio comercial tanto do país quanto do estado catarinense, e também se revela crescente a contribuição estadual ao desempenho brasileiro. As pautas comerciais são contrastadas no confronto entre exportações e importações: sobretudo commodities nas primeiras e itens de maior valor agregado nas segundas, abrangendo sobretudo bens de capital e insumos industriais. Parte importante das inversões externas chinesas dirigiu-se ao Brasil no primeiro quartel do século XXI, predominantemente em setores como energia, metais e petróleo, com alguma diversificação recente. Santa Catarina pouco aparece como destino desses investimentos, os principais anúncios referindo-se a logística e energia. Ações promotoras seriam estratégicas para ampliar o envolvimento catarinense no fluxo de inversões chinesas.

title: Smart aquaculture: an IoT-based monitoring and automation system for fish farming powered by solar energy
source: Journal of Electrical Systems and Information Technology
summary: Abstract The growing demand for animal protein highlights aquaculture’s importance for food security, yet conventional practices face challenges in water-quality monitoring, operational efficiency, and energy sustainability. This study deve
content: Abstract The growing demand for animal protein highlights aquaculture’s importance for food security, yet conventional practices face challenges in water-quality monitoring, operational efficiency, and energy sustainability. This study develops a solar-powered Internet of Things (IoT)-based Smart Aquaculture system integrating real-time water-quality monitoring, automated pumps, aerators, and feeders, and renewable energy supplied by a 300 Wp photovoltaic module and a 100 Ah battery. The system was evaluated through technical performance assessments and a 60-day cultivation experiment comparing conventional and IoT + solar ponds. Sensor measurements exhibited deviations of ≤ 5% from laboratory references, while data transmission achieved an average latency of 180 ms and a packet loss rate of 0.8%. Daily energy consumption averaged approximately 850 Wh/day, compared with photovoltaic generation of 1,200 Wh/day, resulting in a 70.8% load-to-generation ratio and an average energy surplus of 350 Wh/day under observed solar conditions. The IoT + solar pond demonstrated a 29.2% increase in average daily fish growth, a 10-percentage-point improvement in survival rate (82% to 92%), and a 17.1% reduction in feed conversion ratio (1.75 to 1.45). One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed a substantial difference in sampled final fish weights between groups (F(1,58) = 2417.16, p < 0.001). However, the absence of independent pond-level replication limits causal inference and broader generalizability. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating IoT-based automation with photovoltaic energy for aquaculture operations, while indicating potential improvements in productivity and energy management. The proposed system provides a practical foundation for developing adaptive, energy-efficient, and sustainable aquaculture technologies, warranting further validation through independently replicated field trials.

title: Cyber-Physical Anomaly Monitoring and Mitigation in Power Distribution Systems
source: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
summary: Power distribution systems represent the final stage of the electric grid, delivering electricity to end users at safe and desired voltage levels. In many regions around the world, core distribution system infrastructure, such as undergroun
content: Power distribution systems represent the final stage of the electric grid, delivering electricity to end users at safe and desired voltage levels. In many regions around the world, core distribution system infrastructure, such as underground cables, was constructed decades ago and is now nearing or exceeding its expected lifespan. As a result, maintenance costs are rising, and the risk of equipment malfunction continues to grow, potentially leading to catastrophic failures. Meanwhile, with the growing demand for renewable energy, an increasing number of distributed energy resources (DERs) equipped with communication and control capabilities are being integrated into the power distribution systems, introducing new vulnerabilities to attacks on communication links. Consequently, cyber–physical anomalies, including both disturbances and attacks, have become a critical focus in industry and academia. In this thesis, we investigate monitoring and mitigation approaches to address cyber-physical anomalies in power distribution systems. Four main research topics are studies. Firstly, root cause classification for power disturbances is investigated, including incipient faults, constant impedance faults, capacitor switching events, and load switching events. Specifically, disturbance models are derived by exploiting their corresponding mathematical formulations or physical characteristics. Then, an estimator is developed for each disturbance model to estimate the unknown disturbance parameters based on the measurement data. Based on the estimation results, a hypothesis-testing-based classification scheme is proposed to identify the root cause by selecting the disturbance model that best fits the measurement data. Case studies based on the IEEE 13-Bus Test Feeder demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only classifies disturbances with a high accuracy rate but also provides insight into disturbance features through the estimation results. After a disturbance is identified as a fault, it is necessary to locate the fault to enable timely maintenance. In the second research work, a fault location scheme based on synchronous waveform measurements is investigated. A fault voltage model is derived through successive calculations using waveform measurements at the substation and branch ends. Based on this model, an estimator is designed to determine the fault distance along each line segment, incorporating a whitening process and a zero-padding technique to improve accuracy. The fault location is then pinpointed using these estimation results. Compared with existing schemes, the proposed scheme provides more accurate fault location results. Beyond power disturbances, securing the communication layer of the distribution system is equally important. In the third research work, an autonomous scheme is developed for the identification and mitigation of man-in-the-middle attacks.
