title: Chevrel‐Phase Mo 6 Te 8 Modulated Pt Catalysts for High‐Efficiency and Durable Electrochemical Methanol‐To‐Hydrogen Conversion
summary: ABSTRACT Electrochemical methanol‐to‐hydrogen transfer catalyzed by Pt still faces challenges of CO‐intermediate poisoning and insufficient activity. Herein, an effective Chevrel‐phase Mo 6 Te 8 ‐assisted Pt catalyst was developed that show
content: ABSTRACT Electrochemical methanol‐to‐hydrogen transfer catalyzed by Pt still faces challenges of CO‐intermediate poisoning and insufficient activity. Herein, an effective Chevrel‐phase Mo 6 Te 8 ‐assisted Pt catalyst was developed that shows an efficient catalytic promotion effect in electrochemical methanol‐to‐hydrogen production by catalyzing the two half‐reactions of methanol oxidation and hydrogen evolution reactions. Theoretical calculations revealed that the synergistic effect between Pt and Mo 6 Te 8 significantly enhances catalytic performance by optimizing the adsorption energies of the intermediate species (CO and H*). This novel catalyst showed a peak current density of 83.6 mA cm −2 , about 3.1 times higher than that of the commercial Pt/C catalyst for anode methanol oxidation, and a low overpotential of 31 mV to drive hydrogen production at the kinetic current density of 10 mA cm −2 . When integrated as an electrolyzer for methanol electrolysis, a low cell voltage of 0.64 V was obtained to deliver 10 mA cm −2 , and good stability for more than 100 h in hydrogen generation. The lower energy input and better performance than the Pt/C||Pt/C system, as well as the water electrolyzer, demonstrated both the advances in novel catalysts and the electrolyzer development for green hydrogen generation.

title: A dynamic engineering wake model for wind turbines under helix control
summary: Abstract. As wind farms increase in size and density, wake interactions between turbines reduce total energy capture and raise structural loads. Wind farm control strategies have therefore become essential for mitigating these effects. The
content: Abstract. As wind farms increase in size and density, wake interactions between turbines reduce total energy capture and raise structural loads. Wind farm control strategies have therefore become essential for mitigating these effects. The helix wake-mixing strategy uses individual pitch control to impose a slowly rotating tilt–yaw moment on the rotor, deforming the wake into a helix and accelerating its recovery. Its power gains have been shown in large-eddy simulations (LES) and wind-tunnel experiments, yet existing engineering models capture only the time-averaged deficit of this intrinsically dynamic wake. This paper presents the first dynamic engineering model of the helix wake: a phase-locked, three-dimensional representation that rotates about the wake axis, enabling dynamic model-based wind farm control and helix-phase estimation. Derived from actuator-line LES of the IEA 22 MW reference wind turbine, it reconstructs the phase-resolved wake from only the actuation amplitude, frequency, and phase, and is validated on unseen test cases. Integrated into the dynamic wind farm framework OFF, the model is applied to a three-turbine row transitioning from free-stream to full wake alignment. With helix actuation on the first two turbines, the framework captures each helix wake arriving downstream only after its convection time and predicts the time-varying downstream power gain and incoming helix phase, about 190 times faster than real time.

title: A hybrid graph-convolutional moving average framework for spatio-temporal voltage prediction in smart microgrids
summary: Accurate voltage forecasting is critical for maintaining the operational stability and reliability of smart microgrids under dynamic load and generation conditions. This paper proposes a novel Hybrid Graph Convolution Moving Average (Hyb-GC
content: Accurate voltage forecasting is critical for maintaining the operational stability and reliability of smart microgrids under dynamic load and generation conditions. This paper proposes a novel Hybrid Graph Convolution Moving Average (Hyb-GCMA) spatio-temporal deep learning framework that synergistically integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Seasonal AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average with eXogenous variables (SARIMAX) for dynamic voltage prediction in an IEEE 14-bus truncated microgrid. The proposed framework very well encompasses spatial correlations between interconnected buses by graph-based learning while sequential learning of temporal dependencies due to time-varying load patterns. To increase the robustness and generality of the model, historical load-flow data under various operating scenarios are preprocessed by normalizing and generating sliding-window sequences. To prevent overfitting, adaptive learning rate strategies and early stopping mechanisms are used to further optimize the model training. The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) per-bus accuracy metrics, along with \(R^2\) , show that the proposed Hyb-GCMA framework makes a significant improvement over conventional standalone deep learning baselines. The RMSE and MAE obtained are 0.0049 p.u and 0.0047 p.u, in squared and absolute error respectively. \(R^2\) value calculated is 0.999993, which suggests the model explains the proportion of variance best fit. The results show that spatio-temporal deep learning methods are providing great potential for real-time voltage stability assessment, anomaly detection and predictive control of next generation smart microgrid systems.

title: Pollutant Removal Efficacy and Bioelectricity Generation of Microbial Fuel Cells from Polluted Water using Different Electrodes
summary: The discharge of untreated wastewater into water bodies creates serious ecological and health problems, highlighting the necessity for a sustainable, energy-efficient treatment solution. Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) have emerged as a promisi
content: The discharge of untreated wastewater into water bodies creates serious ecological and health problems, highlighting the necessity for a sustainable, energy-efficient treatment solution. Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) have emerged as a promising bioelectrochemical technology that can treat wastewater while generating electricity from organic matter. This study evaluated double-chambered MFCs for concurrent electricity generation and wastewater treatment from dairy farm effluent and Turag River water over a 25-day operation. Three anode-cathode configurations: Graphite-Cu (G-Cu), Carbon fiber-Stainless steel (Cf-SS), and Carbon rod-Zn (CR-Zn), were compared for their electrochemical performance and pollutant removal efficiency. In dairy farm effluent, G-Cu produced the highest peak voltage (706.67 mV), current (0.2667 mA), and power (0.1884 mW) with 98.53% COD removal. In Turag River water, Cf-SS produced the highest voltage (676.67 mV) with COD removal (70.59%), while CR-Zn produced the highest current (0.2667 mA) and power (0.1751 mW). COD, TDS, TSS, and turbidity were reduced by the MFCs, although the removal efficiency varied among electrode configurations and wastewater types. Changes in pH were also observed after treatment. In addition, bacterial isolates obtained from the layer formed on the anode electrodes after 25 days of operation were identified using MALDI-TOF MS (Bruker MALDI Biotyper). The identified bacteria included species previously reported to have electroactive potential, suggesting their possible association with electricity generation in MFCs. Escherichia coli was also detected in both wastewater types, which may indicate fecal or domestic contamination. Overall, the study demonstrated the feasibility of using different electrode configurations for treating real wastewater while generating electricity under laboratory conditions. Among the tested configurations, G-Cu showed comparatively consistent electrical and treatment performance, although the highest performance for individual parameters varied among the electrode configurations and wastewater types.

title: Sulphur Trioxide Splitting Catalysts in the Context of a Solid Sulphur-Based Thermochemical Cycle for Solar Thermal Energy Storage
summary: This work is part of a wider project, aiming to demonstrate an innovative approach for the direct storage of solar energy in solid elemental sulphur. The basic idea is to use renewable heat from concentrated solar energy to cyclically drive
content: This work is part of a wider project, aiming to demonstrate an innovative approach for the direct storage of solar energy in solid elemental sulphur. The basic idea is to use renewable heat from concentrated solar energy to cyclically drive a series of chemical reactions that interconvert sulphuric acid and sulphur. Among these reactions, the two-step sulphuric acid splitting, first to steam and sulphur trioxide and subsequently of the latter to sulphur dioxide and oxygen, is the highest-temperature (650-1000oC) endothermic step of the cycle. The heat needed can be supplied by Concentrating Solar Technologies (CST) since these temperatures are within the capabilities of state-of-the-art CST tower plants. The current work presents an integrated approach on catalytic sulphur trioxide splitting (STS) within this perspective. Iron oxide-based compositions - which are the state-of-the-art inexpensive STS catalytic materials investigated - were synthesized, shaped into spherical granules and their performance was experimentally evaluated. Due to practical aspects relating to material availability at sufficient quantities for extrusion, commercial iron oxide was the chosen formulation for shaping into larger-size honeycombs. Subsequently the honeycombs underwent 50 h on stream catalytic testing in a suitably designed test rig and were physico-chemically characterised before and after exposure to the reaction environment. Tested honeycomb specimens demonstrated not only close-to-equilibrium conversion but also phase composition stability and remarkable corrosion resistance.

title: Energetyka jądrowa w trzeciej dekadzie XXI w. – rozdroża technologii i zastosowań
summary: Nuclear power is regaining importance in the third decade of the 21st century as a stable and highly available source of energy, playing a key role in decar- bonization, energy security, and power system stability. Modern nuclear power unit
content: Nuclear power is regaining importance in the third decade of the 21st century as a stable and highly available source of energy, playing a key role in decar- bonization, energy security, and power system stability. Modern nuclear power units provide continuous electricity generation, enabling the replacement of high-emission coal – and gas-fired generating units. Their high-power density (rated power per unit area occupied by the power plant), combined with the possibility of storing nuclear fuel for many years, enhances the resilience of power systems to potential disruptions in the supply of energy resources. Nuclear power is also becoming a foundation for large-scale hydrogen production and for supplying AI data centers, owing to capacity factors exceeding 90% and the possibility of operating in a behind-the-meter model, thereby integrating power system stability with the development of digital infrastructu- re. In future power systems, nuclear power plants will serve as baseload generation sources, helping to balance the variable output of weather-dependent renewable energy sources. The development of grid-forming technology enables inverters and energy storage systems to emulate inertia and provide frequency stabilization, thereby redefining the traditional role of large synchronous generating units, including nuclear power units. Nevertheless, in the 2030s and 2040s, nuclear power will remain one of the most important pillars supporting the secure and stable operation of large power systems.

title: Navigating a Resilient Transition: A Conceptual Framework for Mapping Disruptions to Electrified Public Bus Transport
summary: Abstract Public transport plays a key role in decarbonizing the transport sector, but in Sweden, the sector is challenged by a slow post-Covid recovery. While vehicle electrification can offer new, cross-sectoral resilience services, it may
content: Abstract Public transport plays a key role in decarbonizing the transport sector, but in Sweden, the sector is challenged by a slow post-Covid recovery. While vehicle electrification can offer new, cross-sectoral resilience services, it may also place additional strain on the sector through new infrastructure dependencies and potentially undermine the sector’s long-term resilience. This paper explores how resilience can be conceptualized in electrified public bus transport in Sweden, maps related disruptions and identifies the most critical resilience challenges perceived by stakeholders. Drawing on stakeholder insights, a conceptual framework was developed based on the bus service value chain. In total, 43 potential disruptions were identified through a review of academic and grey literature, as well as Swedish news sources, and mapped onto the conceptual framework. Stakeholders then identified the most critical disruptions and provided insights into vulnerabilities and opportunities for building resilience. A key finding is the need for stronger coordination among public transport authorities, operators and energy actors, across areas of planning, monitoring and technological developments. This framework offers insights for researchers and decision-makers, supporting targeted strategies to enhance system resilience.

title: Enhanced Power-quality Regulation in PV-integrated Systems Using Adaptive Reduced-set Horizon-2 FCS-MPC Systems
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: The increasing use of renewable generation and power-electronic loads makes simultaneous voltage and current power-quality regulation important in distribution systems.Unified Power Quality Conditioners (UPQCs) can address both disturbance
content: The increasing use of renewable generation and power-electronic loads makes simultaneous voltage and current power-quality regulation important in distribution systems.Unified Power Quality Conditioners (UPQCs) can address both disturbance types, but conventional control and full finite-state predictive searches may face tracking and computational trade-offs under changing operating conditions.This study presents an Adaptive Reduced-Set Horizon-2 Finite-Control-Set Model Predictive Control (RS-H2 FCS-MPC) strategy for a matrix-converter UPQC integrated with photovoltaic distributed generation (PV-DG).The controller combines 27-state discrete matrix conversion, reduced second-step prediction, adaptive magnitude restoration, switching-transition and common-mode-voltage penalties, PV power feedforward, positive-sequence synchronization, and a clean-grid deadband.Evaluation uses SEED-PQD-v1 containing 17 power-quality classes and 17,000 signals, with 100 signals reserved for parameter tuning and the remaining 16,900 used for held-out evaluation.Under Protocol A, the six-condition held-out composite evaluation profile comprising Pure Sinusoidal, Sag, Swell, Harmonics, Sag with Harmonics, and Swell with Harmonics conditions, the proposed controller obtains 0.5487% voltage total harmonic distortion (THD), 0.8149% current THD, a power factor of 0.9508, and a power-quality index of 3.9362.The full 17-class assessment is reported separately.Clean-grid operation produces zero series injection and 0% voltage THD.Paired Wilcoxon tests with Holm correction on a 25-trial matched subset support the reported controller differences within the selected disturbance conditions.The results support reduced-set predictive control for compensation under the evaluated balanced multi-disturbance conditions, while the interruption case remains energy-limited without storage.

title: Small language models are agentic but not autonomous in greenhouse climate control
summary: Agentic large language models (LLMs) are proposed for cyber-physical control, yet evidence on how reliably small open-weight models turn sensor context into actuator commands is scarce. We present a reproducible benchmark grounded in an ope
content: Agentic large language models (LLMs) are proposed for cyber-physical control, yet evidence on how reliably small open-weight models turn sensor context into actuator commands is scarce. We present a reproducible benchmark grounded in an operational ESP32-based greenhouse controller: ninety-six generated test cases run against the production tool schema and prompts, scored deterministically, with the controller’s rule-based fallback ported verbatim as baseline. Four quantized models (3–14 B) ran on a pinned llama.cpp stack in two locked environments two months apart (12,000 scored runs). Three findings dominate. Autonomous self-initiation is far less reliable than command execution: models executing 65–100% of chat commands fall to 0.4–64.6% when acting unprompted. Model rankings are environment-conditional: one environment favoured Qwen2.5-7B over the 14B (McNemar p = 0.016; cluster-robust GEE p = 0.084), the other decisively reversed it at identical seeds ( p < 0.001; 77.5% cross-environment agreement), requiring re-benchmarking on the deployment stack. The rule baseline matches the second-best model with the best refusal behaviour: the LLM’s measured value is language-mediated actuation, knowledge capture, and auditability, not superior regulation. Field telemetry and thermal replay show the hybrid controller running unattended through the growing season, rules holding the safety-critical floor. All instruments and both environments’ traces are released.

title: Spinel ferrite nanomaterials: materials science of cation distribution, defect engineering, and structure–property–performance relationships
source: Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology
summary: Spinel ferrite nanomaterials (MFe 2 O 4 , where M = Co, Ni, Mn, Zn, Mg, or mixed cations) have emerged as versatile functional oxides with significant potential in advanced defense and security applications due to their tunable magnetic, di
content: Spinel ferrite nanomaterials (MFe 2 O 4 , where M = Co, Ni, Mn, Zn, Mg, or mixed cations) have emerged as versatile functional oxides with significant potential in advanced defense and security applications due to their tunable magnetic, dielectric, and catalytic properties. These properties are strongly governed by cation distribution, crystallite size, defect structure, and microstructural evolution, which can be effectively controlled through sol–gel synthesis routes. Compared with conventional solid-state methods, sol–gel processing enables molecular-level precursor mixing, improved compositional homogeneity, and reduced crystallization temperatures, facilitating the fabrication of high-performance nanostructured ferrites. This review provides a comprehensive and critical overview of recent advances in sol–gel-derived spinel ferrites, with particular emphasis on crystallization mechanisms, phase stability, and defect engineering strategies that define structure–property relationships. Functional characteristics relevant to defense technologies are discussed, including electromagnetic wave absorption, high-frequency magnetic response, sensing performance, and catalytic activity for environmental remediation. Emerging applications in energy storage and biomedical support systems are also highlighted. Key challenges, including scalability, reproducibility, and environmentally sustainable processing, are critically evaluated. Finally, future research directions are proposed, focusing on predictive defect engineering, green synthesis approaches, and integration into next-generation multifunctional systems. This work aims to provide a unified framework for advancing sol–gel engineered spinel ferrites toward practical deployment in defense-oriented technologies.

title: Self-supervised, physics-constrained super-resolution for wind mapping in the absence of high-resolution training references: a case study in Brazil
summary: Abstract Planning renewable-energy expansion at the national scale requires wind maps far more detailed than sparse meteorological networks and coarse reanalysis grids can typically offer. This study introduces PC-SRCNN, a physics-constrain
content: Abstract Planning renewable-energy expansion at the national scale requires wind maps far more detailed than sparse meteorological networks and coarse reanalysis grids can typically offer. This study introduces PC-SRCNN, a physics-constrained, self-supervised super-resolution framework that lifts ERA5 wind fields over Brazil from a native 0.25° grid to 0.025°, folding in soft regularization terms for horizontal kinematic consistency and the logarithmic vertical wind profile. The model was evaluated against observations from 190 meteorological stations from Brazil’s INMET network across all twelve months of 2024, benchmarked against IDW, Kriging, U-Net, SRCNN, and a variant constrained only by horizontal kinematics (PC-SRCNN𝜑). The full PC-SRCNN was the only model to outperform native ERA5 with statistical significance in every month, cutting MAE by 5.6–11.0%, reaching vertical-profile R² between 0.80 and 0.87, and posting the lowest error at 133 of the 190 stations (70.0%); the PC-SRCNN𝜑 variant, in contrast, performed significantly worse than ERA5, and the purely data-driven models failed to consistently beat it. These findings show that physical regularization aids wind-field super-resolution only when it respects the vertical structure of the atmospheric boundary layer, suggesting the potential of this framework as a computationally lightweight approach for super-resolution wind mapping in settings where conventional numerical downscaling is computationally demanding.

title: A hybrid GWO-PSO-based MPPT controller for high-efficiency grid-connected PV-assisted EV charging under dynamic conditions
summary: Abstract Integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems with electric vehicle (EV) charging is challenging because conventional MPPT algorithms perform poorly under changing weather conditions. To improve the performance of a grid-tied PV-EV chargin
content: Abstract Integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems with electric vehicle (EV) charging is challenging because conventional MPPT algorithms perform poorly under changing weather conditions. To improve the performance of a grid-tied PV-EV charging system, this paper proposes and validates a hybrid Grey Wolf Optimizer–Particle Swarm Optimization (GWO-PSO) algorithm for MPPT control. An integrated system model comprising a PV array, a boost converter, a 3-level voltage-source converter (VSC), and a battery-charging subsystem was developed in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed GWO-PSO algorithm, which combines the exploration capability of GWO with the exploitation capability of PSO, was compared with conventional GWO, PSO, and INC algorithms under step-change and variable-weather operating conditions. For the step-change irradiance case, the simulation results show that the proposed GWO-PSO method achieved a tracking efficiency of 97.979%, an average steady-state PV power of 100.15 kW, and a harvested energy of 41.121 Wh over the post-step interval from 1.00 s to 2.50 s. It also exhibited a post-convergence PV power ripple of 54.31 W and reached the steady-state MPP region within 0.0876 s based on a ± 2% convergence criterion. Under variable irradiance and temperature conditions, the proposed controller achieved a tracking efficiency of 91.57%, an average PV power of 70.543 kW, and a harvested energy of 48.988 Wh over the selected evaluation interval, outperforming the conventional PSO and GWO methods in terms of energy extraction and tracking accuracy. Under grid-only operating conditions, the controller also maintained stable DC-link regulation and effective battery charging performance. This improved MPPT performance contributes to effective battery charging, while the VSC maintains a regulated 500 V DC-link throughout the tested cases. Overall, the hybrid GWO-PSO controller improves PV energy extraction and supports stable PV-assisted EV charging operation under the tested simulation conditions.

title: Evaluating deep learning detectors for thermal photovoltaic fault localization using independent source families
summary: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based automated infrared thermography (IRT) offers a scalable approach to condition monitoring in utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants, but published deep-learning evaluations exhibit persistent meth
content: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based automated infrared thermography (IRT) offers a scalable approach to condition monitoring in utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) plants, but published deep-learning evaluations exhibit persistent methodological weaknesses: frame-to-frame data leakage, unaddressed class imbalance, inconsistent input resolutions, and unstandardized detector benchmarking. This work presents a controlled, source-family-independent benchmark comparing single-stage (YOLOv8s, YOLO11s) and two-stage (Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50-FPN) object detectors on 7,339 cleaned thermal images with 20,995 annotated defect instances from the Thermo-Solar dataset. To reduce evaluation bias, dataset partitioning enforces zero leakage across 2,431 unique source families defined by physical PV module identity, flight pass sequence, and camera telemetry. The single-stage anchor-free detectors clearly dominate the two-stage baseline in a Pareto sense. YOLOv8s and YOLO11s attain similar localization accuracy (0.6958 and 0.6876 mAP@0.50, respectively), with YOLO11s offering a 15.3% smaller parameter footprint (9.43M vs. 11.14M) and lower computational complexity (21.7 GFLOPs). Faster R-CNN achieved lower localization accuracy (0.6542 mAP@0.50), 7.3× slower forward-pass inference latency on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU (75.86 ms/image vs. 10.20–10.40 ms/image), and an 8× higher computational training runtime (7.86 hours for 20 epochs vs. ~1.1 hours for 50 epochs). Despite a raw 119.6:1 class imbalance, the single-stage models retained stronger robustness on minority fault classes (String Reversed Polarity: 0.5817 AP@0.50) than the Region Proposal Network baseline (0.2781 AP@0.50), while spatially dense Multi Hotspots caused severe bounding-box suppression problems (0.4342–0.4781 AP@0.50). This work provides a rigorous and reproducible baseline for operational UAV thermography.

title: What Wide-Area Complementarity Can Actually Deliver: A Realization Ratio for Cross-Regional Renewable Integration
summary: Wide-area complementarity is widely invoked to justify long-distance interconnection, yet resource-correlation statistics do not reveal how much of that opportunity a power system converts into lower operating cost. We introduce the Complem
content: Wide-area complementarity is widely invoked to justify long-distance interconnection, yet resource-correlation statistics do not reveal how much of that opportunity a power system converts into lower operating cost. We introduce the Complementarity Realization Ratio (CRR), which locates a network architecture between isolated operation (ISO) and a lossless copper plate (CU) by the share of the ISO–CU operating-cost opportunity it realizes. We solve four structurally nested architectures for each day of 2020–2022 in a four-region reduction of the Chinese system: ISO, rated corridors without the operational screen (RATED), rated corridors with a MISCR-inspired cross-regional injection screen (STRENGTH), and CU. Across 1096 days and 4384 MILPs, every architecture-day returns a feasible objective and valid dual bound. RATED and STRENGTH realize 0.3667 [95% CI 0.3344, 0.4117] and 0.3481 [0.3162, 0.3893] of the ISO–CU opportunity, respectively. The paired contrast separates the operating-cost effect of the screen from corridor capacity and converter losses. After national resource homogenization, CRR remains 0.3223 for RATED and 0.3147 for STRENGTH, showing that network feasibility and dispatch retain information beyond regional resource geography. Energy ledgers close below 2.658 × 10−6 MWh, and chronological and sub-hourly sensitivities test temporal robustness. CRR provides a reproducible diagnostic for translating resource complementarity into network-conditioned system value.

title: Series compensation for the ride-through of current-limited grid-forming plants: a power ceiling, a planning criterion and hardware-in-the-loop validation
summary: Abstract Grid-forming (GFM) plants limit their current during faults, and while limited they lose much of their ability to stay in synchronism. Many of these plants are connected through long transmission corridors that already carry, or co
content: Abstract Grid-forming (GFM) plants limit their current during faults, and while limited they lose much of their ability to stay in synchronism. Many of these plants are connected through long transmission corridors that already carry, or could carry, a thyristor-controlled series capacitor (TCSC) or a static synchronous series compensator (SSSC). This paper asks when such a device can keep a current-limited GFM inverter in synchronism. For a virtual synchronous machine with current-reference saturation, the power transferred while the current is limited has a ceiling set only by the current limit and the grid voltage. Series compensation cannot raise this ceiling, and inserted inductance can only lower the power curve. What a series device can do is restore the post-fault equilibrium after a line outage. A closed-form minimum compensation for each N-1 outage turns this into a screening map that shows which outages need series compensation, how much, and which need a run-back instead. A coordinated scheme of a virtual-rotor angle freeze and a saturation-aware TCSC boost rode through 1 s faults in all 22 single-machine cases of a phasor study. A switched-thyristor Simulink model, a small-signal resonance study, a modified IEEE 39-bus system and controller-hardware-in-the-loop tests on three microcontroller boards support these findings. The hardware critical clearing times matched a desktop run of the same code within one 2 ms bisection step in 30 of 36 comparisons. On resistive corridors the boost can shorten the critical clearing time, so it should be armed only for the outages the map identifies.

title: Recycling Pathways toward a Sustainable and Inclusive Green Economy in South Africa: A Narrative Review of Institutional and Governance Factors
source: African Journal of Food Agriculture Nutrition and Development
summary: South Africa faces persistent socio-economic and environmental challenges, including high unemployment, poverty, inequality, increasing waste generation, resource depletion, and growing pressure on municipal waste management systems. These
content: South Africa faces persistent socio-economic and environmental challenges, including high unemployment, poverty, inequality, increasing waste generation, resource depletion, and growing pressure on municipal waste management systems. These challenges have strengthened interest in the green economy as a development pathway capable of advancing environmental sustainability, economic growth, and social inclusion simultaneously. Within this context, recycling has emerged as an important mechanism for improving resource efficiency, reducing environmental degradation, conserving natural resources, and creating employment opportunities. However, existing literature has largely examined recycling from technical and environmental perspectives, with limited attention given to the governance and institutional arrangements that shape developmental outcomes. This study addresses this gap by examining recycling through an institutional governance perspective. Drawing on Green Economy Theory, Circular Economy Theory, and Institutional Theory, the study investigates how municipal governance, informal waste reclaimers, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), and recycling value chains interact to influence inclusive green economic development in South Africa. A qualitative narrative literature review was undertaken using peer-reviewed journal articles, government publications, policy documents, legislation, and reports from recognised national and international institutions. The review focused on literature published between 2015 and 2025, supplemented by foundational theoretical works. The study’s findings reveal that recycling contributes to resource efficiency, landfill diversion, greenhouse gas mitigation, employment creation, enterprise development, and poverty alleviation. However, these outcomes depend significantly on institutional effectiveness, governance quality, stakeholder collaboration, market development, and implementation capacity. The review further demonstrates that informal waste reclaimers are central actors within South Africa's recycling economy, while municipal governance remains the primary enabling institution for recycling performance. Although EPR has strengthened producer accountability and resource mobilisation, its effectiveness remains dependent on institutional coordination and implementation capacity. The study develops an Integrated Governance Framework that links municipal governance, informal waste reclaimers, EPR, and the recycling industry within a single analytical model. The framework demonstrates that governance quality mediates the relationship between recycling interventions and developmental outcomes. The paper concludes that strengthening municipal institutional capacity, integrating informal waste reclaimers, enhancing EPR implementation, expanding markets for recycled materials, and promoting collaborative governance are essential for maximising recycling's contribution to inclusive green economic development and So

title: Greenhouse gas forcing dominates the recent strengthening of North Pacific Meridional Mode influence on ENSO
summary: Abstract The North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM) is a key extratropical trigger of El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, and its influence on ENSO has increased markedly in recent decades, offering a pathway to improve ENSO predictab
content: Abstract The North Pacific Meridional Mode (NPMM) is a key extratropical trigger of El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) events, and its influence on ENSO has increased markedly in recent decades, offering a pathway to improve ENSO predictability. Yet, the relative contributions of external forcings versus internal variability to this intensified influence remain uncertain. Using multi-model simulation outputs from the Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project and a suite of numerical experiments, we demonstrate that greenhouse gas (GHG) forcing dominates over internal variability in driving the recent strengthening of the NPMM–ENSO connection, whereas aerosol and natural forcings have minimal impact. GHG forcing enhances the wind–evaporation–sea surface temperature (SST) feedback over the subtropical North Pacific by elevating the background mean SST, which amplifies NPMM-induced westerly wind bursts over the western tropical Pacific and promotes ENSO development. Sensitivity experiments further demonstrate that GHG-induced SST increasing in the subtropical North Pacific enhances the atmospheric response associated with the NPMM. These findings reveal an important role of anthropogenic forcing in modulating the extratropical impact on ENSO and suggest potential opportunities for extending ENSO prediction lead times.

title: Urban Planning as a Tool for Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation in the 21st Century National Development: A Review
source: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF PURE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
summary: Considering the obvious effects of land use on climate change and variability, this paper sought to review the applicability of urban planning as a tool for climate change adaptation and mitigation in the 21st century national development.
content: Considering the obvious effects of land use on climate change and variability, this paper sought to review the applicability of urban planning as a tool for climate change adaptation and mitigation in the 21st century national development. The causes of climate change were identified to include: industrialization and manufacturing of goods, farming activities and food production, consumerism / too much consumption of products, transportation and vehicular movements, oil drilling and gas flaring, power plants / generating power and powering buildings, increased waste generation and management, deforestation, oil and gas usage and overfishing, among others. the main effects of Climate Change include but are not limited to: global warming, greenhouse gas effects, flooding, acid rain typhoons, rising sea levels, rising sea temperatures resulting in depletion of marine organisms, earthquakes, wind storms, land and mud slides, desertification, tsunami, erosion, volcanic activities, hurricanes, pollution, deforestation among several others. It was also found from literature that climate change adaptation can come in the form of defense and fortification, accommodation, retreat, and clean-up; all of which can be achieved through proper urban palnning. It was also found that a well-designed urban planning policy can mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and adapt to anticipated climate change impacts, although there has been limited analysis of the extent to which urban planning policy documents addresses climate change adaptation and or mitigation. There is a need to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions in order to condense warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels by 2100, and to be well adapted to this change in line with the Paris Agreement, we must act now. Since we are still building our cities, we need to be agile to use this moment as an opportunity and plan well to adapt to and mitigate climate change. A regional analysis and assessments that provide the basis for understanding where, how, and why certain regions are affected by climate change is called for. The paper thus recommends that there is need for a platform where discussion and decision making process on the potential aspects of climate change Adaptation and Mitigation issues can become part of National and Local spatial planning policies; need for an integrated, comprehensive, cross-sectoral, coordinating, spatially oriented planning on different scales (from national to local); which is focused on achieving an efficiently and balanced sustainable territorial development; enlistment of multidisciplinary professionals in our planning and designing of modern cities is very important and urban planning policies must do more to include and integrate climate change adaptation and mitigation actions; finally funds allocated to Climate Change mitigation and adaptation projects/programmes should be utilized for that.

title: Shaping a Resilient Future: Schools as Experimental Hubs for Climate Change Adaptation
summary: In line with European policies for ecological transition, this paper reflects on regenerative architecture as a technical and pedagogical tool to address climate change challenges.The contribution investigates the potential of nature-based
content: In line with European policies for ecological transition, this paper reflects on regenerative architecture as a technical and pedagogical tool to address climate change challenges.The contribution investigates the potential of nature-based solutions as devices for both adaptation and learning, capable of combining environmental sustainability, participation and educational innovation.The work presents a participatory, replicable and scalable methodology based on the learning-by-doing approach and articulated in four phases: (1) interactive lesson; (2) experiments and field data collection; (3) coparticipatory implementation of full-scale interventions; (4) maintenance guidelines.This approach was tested through two case studies: in Cavallerleone (CN), the depaving of urban areas and the development of an infiltration basin regenerated underutilized urban spaces and promoted circular economy practices; in Turin, a Living Wall System installed in the courtyard of the "Pertini" Institute was enhanced as a demonstration device, allowing students to directly measure the microclimatic and air quality benefits.The results show how collaboration between universities, local administrations and schools generates measurable impacts on the environmental (soil permeability, water management, microclimatic comfort), social (participation and shared stewardship) and pedagogical (development of technical-scientific and soft skills) levels.The proposed methodology, replicable and adaptable across contexts and age groups, identifies schools as strategic nodes of the ecological transition, capable of combining innovative teaching and urban regeneration, transforming educational spaces into hubs for climate adaptation.

title: Extended Generalized Pareto Models for the Spatial Modeling of Extreme and Bulk Rainfall
summary: ABSTRACT The peaks‐over‐threshold (POT) approach to defining extreme observations is intuitive and less wasteful than other methods such as the block maxima approach. However, POT requires the selection of an appropriate high threshold to d
content: ABSTRACT The peaks‐over‐threshold (POT) approach to defining extreme observations is intuitive and less wasteful than other methods such as the block maxima approach. However, POT requires the selection of an appropriate high threshold to define an extreme observation. In spatial modeling problems, POT requires threshold selection at each location in the study. Threshold selection is usually performed using visual tools and therefore can be subjective and tedious when modeling data from many locations. Extended generalized Pareto (EGP) distributions, extensions of the standard POT model, are more robust to threshold selection and are suitable for modeling extremes using low thresholds, thereby incorporating more data in the analysis and potentially eliminating careful threshold selection by location. This work extends two EGP models spatially using Bayesian hierarchical models to predict rainfall return levels across the province of Nova Scotia, Canada. The spatial models incorporate a forecasting variable as a covariate to account for heterogeneous behavior of extreme rainfall across space and allow for interpolation of inference between stations.

title: Quantifying Thermal Inertia Effect of Permafrost in the Community Earth System Model Version 1.2
summary: Abstract Permafrost's thermal inertia causes permafrost thaw to lag behind climate warming. This is critical for understanding climate sensitivity of permafrost, but has not been well quantified. Using differences between stabilized and tra
content: Abstract Permafrost's thermal inertia causes permafrost thaw to lag behind climate warming. This is critical for understanding climate sensitivity of permafrost, but has not been well quantified. Using differences between stabilized and transient experiments from the CESM1.2, we quantified thermal inertia effect of permafrost in the Northern Hemisphere. The results show that thermal inertia's effect on ground temperature is not apparent in the shallow layers, but enhances with depth. Under the 1.5°C and 2.0°C global warming, thermal inertia reduces warming of ground temperature at 35 m depth by 0.60°C and 0.52°C. It also reduces loss of permafrost extent by 1.8 × 10 6 and 1.7 × 10 6 km 2 , and the corresponding delay times are approximately 19 and 18 years, respectively. Thermal inertia's effect on active layer is small because of its small effect on ground temperature in shallow layer. Magnitude of thermal inertia in different global warming period is related to warming rate in surface air temperature in the transient experiments, a higher warming rate in surface air temperature leading to a greater thermal inertia effect. These results provide important implications for understanding permafrost dynamics and associated thermal change in a warming world.

title: How Is Induced Demand Addressed in Road Infrastructure Planning? An Evaluation of the German Federal Transport Infrastructure Plan
summary: Abstract Given current climate protection targets, the expansion of highway networks has become the subject of a heated public debate. It has long been empirically demonstrated that network expansions induce demand and, in turn, CO2 emissio
content: Abstract Given current climate protection targets, the expansion of highway networks has become the subject of a heated public debate. It has long been empirically demonstrated that network expansions induce demand and, in turn, CO2 emissions, yet transport planning methods still fail to adequately account for these impacts. This paper examines how induced traffic demand is addressed in the German Federal Transport Infrastructure Plan 2030 (FTIP 2030), which has been the subject of ongoing critique in recent years. Based on a systematic literature review on induced demand, the methods used in the FTIP and the appraisal results for its 1,047 road projects were evaluated. The findings show that the FTIP methodology underestimates induced demand by up to a factor of eight and CO2 emissions by up to a factor of four (4.1 Mt/a vs. 1.0 Mt/a). The results highlight the need for integrated transport planning for sustainable mobility that goes beyond road capacity expansion to address accessibility and climate protection targets – particularly in metropolitan areas with high traffic volumes and limited space, yet significant potential to strengthen alternatives to road transport.

title: How far can a surrogate travel? Mapping cross-climate transferability of building energy surrogates considering limited data budget
summary: Machine learning (ML) surrogate models accelerate early-stage building energy prediction by replacing slow physics-based simulation, but a surrogate is often tied to the climate of its training data, and reusing it elsewhere normally requir
content: Machine learning (ML) surrogate models accelerate early-stage building energy prediction by replacing slow physics-based simulation, but a surrogate is often tied to the climate of its training data, and reusing it elsewhere normally requires regenerating datasets and retraining. Transfer learning (TL) offers a potential solution by reusing a surrogate trained in one city for another, yet its reliability under cross-climate weather domain shifts remains poorly understood, and practitioners lack guidance on when it is worthwhile. This study investigates how far an ML building energy surrogate can be transferred across climates under limited target domain data. An artificial neural network trained on Gothenburg data was transferred to five target cities spanning a range of weather domain distances, quantified from hourly EPW data using Maximum Mean Discrepancy. Three TL methods were evaluated through transfer gain, negative transfer rate, and equivalent target simulations saved, across multiple target-data regimes and transfer configurations and compared to multiple linear regression and XGBoost as baselines. The results indicate that TL offers a clear advantage when the source and target climates are similar, whereas for distant climates, a well-tuned XGBoost model trained on the target data alone performs better. The results are consolidated into practical, exploratory maps. By locating a target city on these maps, practitioners can judge when cross-climate transfer is reliable, when it requires validation, and when local retraining is preferable, providing evidence-based guidance for cross-climate surrogate reuse under early-stage design constraints.

title: Operational Resilience of Road Systems When Disruptions Arise
summary: Abstract Climate change driven hazards, including intense rainfall, flooding, and heatwaves, increasingly threaten road transport, disrupting mobility. As infrastructure age faster than they can be upgraded, the inability to respond swiftly
content: Abstract Climate change driven hazards, including intense rainfall, flooding, and heatwaves, increasingly threaten road transport, disrupting mobility. As infrastructure age faster than they can be upgraded, the inability to respond swiftly to emerging threats results in cascading risks across the interdependent services like emergency response and healthcare. This research adopts a systems thinking approach to investigate how operational resilience of the road systems can be enhanced during such disruptions. While previous studies have examined transport resilience to hazards, few have considered system interdependencies, especially in disaster scenarios. This research addresses this gap by placing roads within broader network of societal functions, where localised failures of critical components can lead to systemic breakdowns. Through comparative case studies from the UK and selected Global South countries, we analyse good practices and persistent limitations in resilience planning. The results highlight the importance of data-informed decision-making, inclusive governance and multi-level coordination in building resilient road networks. We propose a four-stage framework - sense, anticipate, adapt, and recover, creating greater adaptive capacity. This work contributes to growing calls urging transport professionals and policymakers to embrace whole system approaches amid pressing climatic, social, and infrastructure challenges.

title: Status loss or control gain?
summary: Die Klimapolitik richtet ihren Blick zunehmend darauf, wie viel konsumiert wird und nicht mehr nur darauf, wie produziert wird. Der Sechste Sachstandsbericht des IPCC beziffert das Potenzial nachfrageseitiger Maßnahmen in den Sektoren Gebäu
content: Die Klimapolitik richtet ihren Blick zunehmend darauf, wie viel konsumiert wird und nicht mehr nur darauf, wie produziert wird. Der Sechste Sachstandsbericht des IPCC beziffert das Potenzial nachfrageseitiger Maßnahmen in den Sektoren Gebäude, Landverkehr und Ernährung auf 40 bis 70 Prozent der Emissionen bis 2050. Ein großer Teil davon liegt nicht darin, anders zu kaufen, sondern weniger. Genau daran entsteht Widerstand und zwar auch bei Menschen, denen Umweltschutz wichtig ist. Diese Arbeit argumentiert, dass dieser Widerstand eine eigene soziale Logik hat: Er wird von zwei Kräften gleichzeitig geprägt, einer symbolischen Statusbedrohung, die daraus entsteht, mit weniger Besitz gesehen zu werden und einem Gefühl von Autonomie, das aus der selbst getroffenen Entscheidung wächst. Die Argumentation verbindet drei Literaturstränge: die Forschung zum Statussignalisieren, die Selbstbestimmungstheorie und die GLORCY-Taxonomie individueller Gewinne und Verluste bei Konsumreduktion. Daraus wurden vier Hypothesen abgeleitet und in einem 2 × 2 Zwischensubjekt-Onlineexperiment geprüft (N = 167). Die wahrgenommene Statusbedrohung wurde über eine kurze Rahmung des eigenen sozialen Umfelds variiert, die wahrgenommene Autonomie über die Bildunterschrift eines Instagram-ähnlichen Beitrags einer fiktiven Person, die keine neue Kleidung mehr kauft. Kleidung diente dabei als empirischer Anwendungsfall. Die Ergebnisse sind in den Hauptbefunden eindeutig. Statusbedrohung senkte die Akzeptanz von Konsumreduktion (H1), Autonomie erhöhte sie (H2). Beide Effekte waren statistisch signifikant aber von bescheidener Größe, was einer einzelnen kurzen Rahmung realistischerweise entspricht. Die vorhergesagte Pufferwirkung (H3) zeigte sich in der erwarteten Richtung. Autonomie half besonders dann, wenn eine Bedrohung vorlag, erreichte aber keine statistische Signifikanz. Die explorative Dreifachmoderation durch die Statusorientierung (H4) ergab keinen Effekt. Die soziale Bedeutung von weniger Konsum ist damit eine reale Barriere und keine Randfrage. Kampagnen, die sie übergehen, dürften an Wirkung verlieren. Das Gefühl der eigenen Wahl ist ein praktisch nutzbarer Hebel. Kommunikation kann beide Kräfte ansprechen, indem sie bewusste Reduktion sichtbar anerkennt und sie zugleich als eigene Entscheidung der Konsumentinnen und Konsumenten darstellt. Ob die Kombination beider Prinzipien wirksamer ist als jedes für sich, bleibt offen und muss in künftigen Studien direkt geprüft werden.

title: Ensemble-based assessment of projected hazard risk: Identification of regions exposed to extreme precipitation in North-Central Europe
summary: Abstract Accelerated transformations in the European hydrological cycle during the early 21st century call for a rethinking of approaches used to detect regions susceptible to precipitation extremes. This work provides a risk map for extrem
content: Abstract Accelerated transformations in the European hydrological cycle during the early 21st century call for a rethinking of approaches used to detect regions susceptible to precipitation extremes. This work provides a risk map for extreme precipitation events, categorizing areas into four risk levels: from no risk to high risk. These were defined based on the direction, magnitude, and statistical significance of trends in extreme precipitation indices, with the highest category representing significant positive trends within the upper percentiles of the precipitation distribution. The study includes 70 years of historical data from E-Obs (1951–2020) and 13 bias-adjusted CORDEX models under two future scenarios, RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, for 80 years (2021–2100). To ensure reliable detection of long-term changes, the analysis employs the Mann-Kendall test with an iterative pre-whitening procedure. The historical risk assessment derived from seven decades of E-Obs observational data shows a heterogeneous pattern across Europe. Elevated risk zones are predominantly concentrated along the western coastal regions of Scandinavia, particularly in Norway’s Atlantic-facing territories. In contrast, continental interior regions (Central European lowlands) generally exhibit lower risk levels. Under the RCP4.5 scenario, some areas, particularly in Scandinavia, show increased risk, although model agreement remains variable. The RCP8.5 scenario presents a noticeable increase in risk levels, with widespread agreement among climate models. Almost the entire study domain transitions into medium to high-risk categories. This broadly shift represents not merely an intensification of existing patterns but a fundamental reorganization of the region’s extreme precipitation climatology. The changes are especially pronounced across the Scandinavian countries, with almost the entire region falling into the high-risk category. The contrast between the two emissions scenarios emphasizes the strong sensitivity of extreme precipitation patterns to greenhouse gas concentration pathways. Overall, the results emphasize the urgency of mitigation and inform adaptation planning in regions likely to face higher extreme precipitation risk.

title: Exogenous brassinolide at different concentrations modulates growth development and physiological indices in Capsicum annuum L. pepper
summary: Abstract Brassinolide (BR), as an emerging plant growth regulator, has shown significant effectiveness in promoting plant growth, enhancing stress resistance, and improving crop quality. This study used the seeds of the pepper variety ‘Chan
content: Abstract Brassinolide (BR), as an emerging plant growth regulator, has shown significant effectiveness in promoting plant growth, enhancing stress resistance, and improving crop quality. This study used the seeds of the pepper variety ‘Changxian Tianxia’ as experimental materials to investigate the effects of different concentrations of brassinolide on the growth and development of chili peppers. Five treatment groups were set up with brassinolide concentrations of 0 mg. L − 1 (CK), 0.1 mg. L − 1 , 0.2 mg. L − 1 , 0.3 mg. L − 1 , and 0.4 mg. L − 1 . Each treatment group had three replicates, and the growth and physiological indicators of the plants were measured to explore the effects of brassinolide on the growth and development of peppers. The experimental results showed that brassinolide can significantly enhance the growth vitality of pepper plants, effectively increase chlorophyll content, enhance peroxidase (POD) activity, and reduce malondialdehyde content; Among them, brassinolide at a concentration of 0.3 mg. L − 1 has the most outstanding effect in promoting pepper growth. This study explores the mechanism by which different concentrations of brassinolide affect the growth and development of peppers, providing a scientific basis for high-yield and high-quality cultivation of peppers and promoting the application of brassinolide in agricultural production.

title: A Two-Stage SARIMA–GARCH Approach to Forecasting Global Monthly Carbon Dioxide Emissions: Trend, Seasonality, and Mitigation Implications
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Accurate near-term projections of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions help governments gauge progress toward the Paris temperature goals and time demand-side mitigation. Most forecasts rely on annual figures, overlook the pronounced within-year
content: Accurate near-term projections of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions help governments gauge progress toward the Paris temperature goals and time demand-side mitigation. Most forecasts rely on annual figures, overlook the pronounced within-year movement of emissions and their reaction to sudden shocks, and rarely model the resulting volatility. Using the IEA–EDGAR v8.0 global monthly fossil CO₂ inventory (156 observations, January 2010–December 2022), this study builds a two-stage model: a seasonal autoregressive integrated moving-average (SARIMA) mean equation selected by an exhaustive search, followed by a GARCH(1,1) variance equation when an ARCH-LM test detects heteroskedasticity. STL decomposition shows a mild upward trend with a strong annual cycle—the seasonal component accounts for 73.9% of short-term fluctuation, with December–January peaks and August–September troughs. The selected mean model is SARIMA(1,0,0)(1,1,1)12 with drift (Ljung–Box p = 0.96), and the GARCH(1,1) removes the remaining ARCH effect (p = 0.27). With MAPE of 1.01% in sample and 2.55% in a held-out 2022 test set and Theil's U of 0.76, it projects 38.86 Gt in 2023 and 39.00 Gt in 2024, a rise of only 0.38% consistent with the Global Carbon Budget's near-plateau. A plateau is far from the rapid, sustained cuts needed for 1.5 °C, so the paper closes with season- and sector-targeted mitigation measures.

title: Aerodyne Lifting and Thrusting Bodies with >90% Decrease in Energy Intensity
summary: Current train, airplane, and motor vehicle transportation is 90- to 300- fold more energy intensity than the basic aerodynamic skin friction of a passenger fuselage. And as an additional consequence; it is possible to reduce energy intensit
content: Current train, airplane, and motor vehicle transportation is 90- to 300- fold more energy intensity than the basic aerodynamic skin friction of a passenger fuselage. And as an additional consequence; it is possible to reduce energy intensity of air and ground transit by more than 90% with substantial reductions in transit cost, time, energy, and environmental impact. A strategic technology for reducing transit energy on railway and highway corridors is ground-effect flight, which displaces most of wheel suspension with aerodynamic suspension and enables higher speeds and multi-modal vehicles capable of seamless highspeed transit between existing highway/railway/waterway/Airway corridors. The combination of highspeed multi-modal vehicles and advances in scheduling would substantially eliminate traffic congestion and favor land-based transit over vastly extended markets. The geopolitical and humanity implications include the ability to rapidly become fully independent of petroleum fuels and the respective funding of wars and other inhumanities with oil revenues. Implementation in a few years is possible because the technology is vehicle based and functional on existing infrastructure. Also, the technology can operate with a near-zero greenhouse gas footprint, which can expedite mitigation of emissions causing global warming.

title: Sustainability Strategies and Practices in the Management of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Narrative Review
summary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 850 million people worldwide and is projected to become a leading cause of death by 2040. Kidney care is resource-intensive, contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water and energy consumpt
content: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 850 million people worldwide and is projected to become a leading cause of death by 2040. Kidney care is resource-intensive, contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water and energy consumption, and healthcare costs. Addressing sustainability in CKD management is critical for aligning kidney health delivery systems with global climate and health goals. A multidisciplinary narrative review was undertaken to qualitatively synthesize literature on CKD management, integrating clinical nephrology, environmental sustainability, and planetary-health perspectives. Studies examining dialysis, kidney transplantation (KT), and preventive kidney management (PKM) were analyzed through the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework, encompassing environmental, economic, and social dimensions. Dialysis, though life-sustaining for people with CKD G4-G5, is the least sustainable option due to its high ecological footprint and cost. KT often provides superior survival and long-term cost-effectiveness but faces barriers such as donor availability, inequitable access, and procedural and pharmaceutical emissions. PKM, including early detection, lifestyle improvements, appropriate virtual care, and optimized pharmacologic management, is important for slowing disease progression and may reduce the need for resource-intensive kidney replacement therapy (KRT). Although the environmental and economic effects of PKM have not been consistently quantified, avoiding or delaying progression to advanced CKD may reduce healthcare resource use, costs, and environmental impacts. Findings support a coordinated, value-based model of kidney care that aligns preventive, interventional, and supportive practices, while recognizing gaps in environmental and economic evidence. Embedding sustainability into CKD care will necessitate technological innovation, policy reform, and equitable access. Future collaborative research should employ long-term life-cycle assessments to guide sustainable, patient-centered kidney care. It should account for variability in CKD pathways and balance effectiveness, sustainability, and equitable access worldwide.

title: Using Game‐Based Experiential Learning With Scenario‐Based Assessment to Measure Climate Change Competence Among Adolescent Students in Pakistan
summary: ABSTRACT Many adolescents are unaware of how unsustainable practices reinforce climate change factors. Although game‐based learning (GBL) is acknowledged as effective, assessing climate change competence often relies on self‐report measures
content: ABSTRACT Many adolescents are unaware of how unsustainable practices reinforce climate change factors. Although game‐based learning (GBL) is acknowledged as effective, assessing climate change competence often relies on self‐report measures that may not capture actual understanding. This study addresses the limited use of GBL for climate change education and overreliance on self‐report assessments. We developed a game‐based experiential learning intervention using a board game simulating real‐world climate factors. To measure its effectiveness, we designed a scenario‐based assessment evaluating systems thinking through open‐ended responses. We compared 24 adolescents under three conditions: GBL, lecture‐based learning (LBL), and control. Findings indicated that GBL significantly improved scenario‐based performance compared with the control group. Game participants demonstrated more advanced systems thinking, identifying more causal relationships and considering more stakeholder perspectives. While self‐reported confidence showed a moderate correlation with scenario performance across the sample, within‐group analysis revealed that self‐reports failed to capture the specific competence gains produced by the game‐based intervention. Interactive board games can improve climate change competence; however, assessment must extend beyond self‐reports.

title: Global greenhouse gas emissions from wastewater treatment plants
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This record contains the data and code accompanying the article “Global greenhouse gas emissions from wastewater treatment plants” (Nature Sustainability). The study compiles a global database of 90,514 wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs),
content: This record contains the data and code accompanying the article “Global greenhouse gas emissions from wastewater treatment plants” (Nature Sustainability). The study compiles a global database of 90,514 wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), infers the treatment configuration of plants without documented process information with machine learning, and estimates their direct CH4 and N2O emissions in 2022 with Monte Carlo simulation, together with projections to 2050. Files Supplementary Data 1 (Combined configuration information.xlsx). Compiled N2O and CH4 emission factors for each treatment configuration, with sources, facility-to-bioreactor ratios, records supplemented from similar processes and IQR screening results, and the parameters of the 2050 mitigation scenarios. Supplementary Data 2 (Combined WWTP information.xlsx). Plant-level database of 90,514 WWTPs, with administrative location, coordinates, served population, reported treatment level and process, and the 26 socio-economic, settlement, land-cover and climatic predictors used for treatment-process inference. Supplementary Data 3 (Region_resolved pollutant flows and GHG emissions.xlsx). Pollutant loads and CH4 and N2O emissions for each administrative region by pathway, the projected values used in the scenario analysis, and the country-level comparison with the EPA inventory. Source Data Fig. 1 to 4 and Source Data Extended Data Fig. 1 to 3. Data underlying the main and Extended Data figures of the article. Figures_code.zip. Python code used to draw the figures. The full code is available at https://github.com/QixiangZ/Global-WWTP-GHG-accounting. Each Supplementary Data file opens with a Dictionary sheet that defines every column.

title: Iot and machine learning for multi-horizon soil moisture forecasting using leakage-free reconstructed sensor data in precision agriculture
summary: Smart agriculture has emerged as an important approach for improving crop productivity, resource efficiency, and climate resilience through continuous environmental monitoring and predictive analytics. This study presents an Internet of Thi
content: Smart agriculture has emerged as an important approach for improving crop productivity, resource efficiency, and climate resilience through continuous environmental monitoring and predictive analytics. This study presents an Internet of Things (IoT) edge computing and machine learning framework for multi-horizon soil moisture forecasting in precision Agriculture. The proposed system integrates a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device with soil moisture, temperature, relative humidity, carbon dioxide (CO $$_2$$ ), and camera sensors to continuously monitor environmental and crop conditions on a cassava farm. Sensor data were processed using an edge-computing architecture and subsequently analyzed using statistical and machine learning techniques. To address prolonged sensor outage, a leakage-free time-series reconstruction methodology was developed that preserves temporal causality by reconstructing missing observations using only historical information available before the outage. Following data preprocessing and feature engineering, four supervised machine learning models including Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), together with Persistence and ARIMA benchmark models, were evaluated for 1-day, 2-day, 5-day, and 7-day soil moisture forecasting. The nonlinear machine learning models consistently outperformed the benchmark approaches, with XGBoost and MLP achieving the highest predictive performance, reaching R2 score of up to 0.94 while substantially reducing forecasting errors. Comparative experiments further demonstrated that leakage-free reconstruction significantly improved forecasting accuracy relative to the non-reconstructed dataset. Feature importance analysis identified cyclical time-of-day information, historical soil moisture observations, and engineered temporal features as the most influential predictors. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of integrating IoT sensing, leakage-free data reconstruction, and machine learning to provide reliable soil moisture forecasting for intelligent irrigation management and sustainable cassava production.

title: FASTMIP-CMIP7: A Coordinated Multi-Emulator Ensemble for Rapid, Spatially Resolved Climate Projections under CMIP7 Scenarios
summary: Abstract. Earth System Models (ESMs) remain the gold standard for translating socioeconomic scenarios into spatially resolved climate projections, but their computational cost limits the number of scenarios and ensemble members that can be
content: Abstract. Earth System Models (ESMs) remain the gold standard for translating socioeconomic scenarios into spatially resolved climate projections, but their computational cost limits the number of scenarios and ensemble members that can be simulated and ties projections to the evidence available when simulations are performed. Climate emulators, which are statistical and machine-learning models trained on ESM output, enable large ensembles and allow projections to be updated as new observations emerge. Here, we present FASTMIP-CMIP7, a coordinated ensemble of seven emulators providing spatially and temporally resolved projections of temperature, precipitation and climate impact indicators for four newly released scenarios from the 7th phase of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP7), spanning very low (VL) to high (H) emissions. Despite scenario ranges having narrowed in CMIP7 comapred to CMIP6, emissions pathways remain the dominant source of uncertainty in regional end-of-century temperature projections, making mitigation the strongest lever for limiting future warming. In 2100, global land temperature reaches 2.3 °C under stringent mitigation (VL), and 3.9 °C under the current-policies scenario (M), approximately 1.4 times the global mean warming. Under M, even the coolest 5 % of years in 2100 are warmer over land than 95 % of present-day years. Precipitation projections are more heterogeneous, with internal variability and regional climate responses often obscuring scenario differences. Nevertheless, robust drying emerges in northern South America and the Mediterranean, where additional drying relative to today is 2.5 to almost four times greater under current policies (M) than under stringent mitigation (VL). Structural differences between emulators and choices in training, testing and validation introduce a new layer of uncertainty to emulated ensembles. Common, streamlined validation experiments are needed to establish confidence in emulated projections and support the broader integration of climate emulators into future climate assessments.

title: Targeted Spectral Threshold Tests for Reducing Cloud Omission in the GOSAT-2 CAI-2 Cloud Mask
summary: Abstract. Cloud detection is a common problem in optical remote sensing, but its consequences vary by mission. In GOSAT-2, missed clouds matter because they can affect greenhouse gas retrievals. This research introduces a targeted omission-
content: Abstract. Cloud detection is a common problem in optical remote sensing, but its consequences vary by mission. In GOSAT-2, missed clouds matter because they can affect greenhouse gas retrievals. This research introduces a targeted omission-recovery approach for the GOSAT-2 CAI-2 Level 2 cloud mask over water. Rather than replacing the operational mask, the method identifies and corrects its errors. True-positive and false-negative cloud footprints are mapped into two-dimensional spectral feature spaces proposed from native CAI-2 L1B ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared radiances. Polynomial logistic regression was used to estimate the probability that a cloud footprint belonged to the detected-cloud group. A Kolmogorov–Smirnov test then compared false negatives at or above the weakest detected TP level with those below it, and the three feature spaces that separated these groups most clearly across granules were converted into probability-threshold tests. Finally, these tests were applied only to pixels labeled no-cloud in the original L2 mask, with additional controls such as sun-glint filtering. Among four overwater granules around Japan, the revised mask reduced cloud omission by 64–83 %, while overestimation increased by 0 to 4 percentage points. Cohen's kappa increased by 5–14 points, reaching 0.88 to 0.93. In the independent granule, the tests recovered 55.4 % of the clouds missed by the L2 mask while introducing false positives over only 2.07 % of cloud-free pixels. Also, an indicator semivariogram showed that recovering the missed clouds improves the mask most at the scales of edges and small and scattered clouds. These results show that missed clouds in CAI-2 contain recoverable spectral structure, which can be used to improve the operational CAI-2 cloud mask over the ocean.

title: Drying the Cradle of Civilization: Water, Food, and Societal Security at a Crossroads in Iraq
summary: Abstract Iraq is facing grave problems and threats regarding the future of its nation, which can be classified into water security, food security, and societal security. These challenges spring from a legacy of past conflicts, unwise admini
content: Abstract Iraq is facing grave problems and threats regarding the future of its nation, which can be classified into water security, food security, and societal security. These challenges spring from a legacy of past conflicts, unwise administrative policies, and complex geopolitical and environmental factors. Water scarcity results from a severe reduction in the abundant flows of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, unfair transboundary sharing, climate change impacts, and haphazard water management. Food insecurity is a natural consequence magnified by agricultural stagnation and population growth. This paper provides an overview of the present situation and outlines proposed solutions, though the future remains uncertain given the fragile economy and the political will required for reforms.

title: Agricultural TFP Dynamics and Ozone-Depleting Substances Panel Analysis in Latin America
summary: Abstract This study evaluates the long-term relationships between ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out policies, land surface temperature anomalies, and agricultural Total Factor Productivity (TFP) dynamics across a panel of 23 countr
content: Abstract This study evaluates the long-term relationships between ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out policies, land surface temperature anomalies, and agricultural Total Factor Productivity (TFP) dynamics across a panel of 23 countries over a 35-year period (1990–2024). Employing a two-stage analytical framework combining an input-oriented Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) Malmquist index with second-stage panel fixed-effects econometric regressions, aggregate TFP growth is decomposed into technical efficiency change and technological progress. Empirical findings reveal that regional agricultural TFP dynamics were primarily driven by shifts in the production frontier and cross-country structural variations. Second-stage econometric estimates demonstrate that historical consumption of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs_IHS) and Methyl Bromide (MB_IHS) did not exert statistically significant negative disruptions on agricultural productivity (β = 0.0160,p = 0.2744; β = 0.0218,p = 0.3691, respectively), reflecting successful technological substitution and producer adaptation during the Montreal Protocol phase-out mandates. Furthermore, annual surface temperature anomalies showed no significant aggregate impact (β = 0.0093,p = 0.9388), highlighting the limitations of macro-level climate averages. Marked cross-country heterogeneity underscores the imperative for targeted policies that bridge technical efficiency gaps and enhance agricultural resilience.

title: Long-term agricultural water conservation under straw and plastic mulching characterized with stable water isotope tracing
summary: Soil health and water resource efficiency are key aspects of sustainable agriculture, and various mulching practices can contribute towards improved soil water conservation and crop yields. A 13-year long-term experiment was conducted to co
content: Soil health and water resource efficiency are key aspects of sustainable agriculture, and various mulching practices can contribute towards improved soil water conservation and crop yields. A 13-year long-term experiment was conducted to comparatively analyze the long-term effects of straw mulching and plastic mulching on soil properties, winter wheat physiological characteristics and yields. Stable water isotope tracing was used to analyze spatio-temporal distributions of soil water fluxes and root water uptake, so that the mechanisms whereby mulching influences soil water conservation and plant water availability can be further characterized. Results showed that both mulching practices increased the proportion of macroaggregates (>0.25 mm) (31.7%-41.6%), water content at field capacity (3.5%-7.9%), saturated hydraulic conductivity (54.9%-89.1%), leaf photosynthesis, instantaneous water use efficiency (WUE 0 ) (13.7%-34.6%), and winter wheat yields (6.9%-19.2%) compared with the control. Straw mulching was more effective than plastic mulching in reducing soil bulk density, promoting organic carbon and total nitrogen accumulation. Plastic mulching led to similar long-term cumulative yields, more consistent annual yields, and less long-term soil quality improvement than straw mulching. Stable water isotope tracing indicated that winter wheat mainly used water from the shallowest 40 cm of soil, and that both mulches improved plant water availability likely by reducing subsurface drainage losses. Additionally, plastic mulching inhibited early topsoil evaporation during the critical jointing stage. Therefore, straw mulching facilitates long-term soil improvement, whereas plastic mulching stabilizes yields under acute droughts. Further research comparing mulch types across different agricultural systems and geographical regions may enhance the generalizability of these single-site findings.

title: THE REBOUND EFFECT: A BLIND SPOT IN LABORATORY EMISSION-REDUCTION EFFORTS
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
