summary: Conference proceedingSF2A 2026 M. Béthermin, K. Baillié, N. Lagarde, J. Malzac, R.-M. Ouazzani, J. Richard, O. Venot, A. Siebert (eds) https://sf2a.eu/proceedings/2026/2026sf2a.conf.999H.pdf Abstract. In an effort to limit global warming, r
content: Conference proceedingSF2A 2026 M. Béthermin, K. Baillié, N. Lagarde, J. Malzac, R.-M. Ouazzani, J. Richard, O. Venot, A. Siebert (eds) https://sf2a.eu/proceedings/2026/2026sf2a.conf.999H.pdf Abstract. In an effort to limit global warming, research laboratories are more and more measuring their greenhouse-gas emissions and taking steps to reduce them. However a cheaper or faster service may be used more, and saved money or time, which then may support other activities that in turn emit greenhouse gases. These responses are called rebound effects. We explain the main types of rebound effect and discuss several examples, namely computing, artificial intelligence, teleworking, and research budgets. Studies in other sectors show that rebound can be large. While efficiency remains useful for both science and emission cuts, we argue that rebound effects is an important, possibly dominant effects, that must be accounted for in any greenhouse gas emission reduction strategy.

title: Livestock farming and soil erosion prevention ecosystem service: a RUSLE-GIS estimation in Italian alpine grassland-based dairy farms
summary: The ecosystem service of erosion prevention (ESEP) becomes increasingly important due to the increasing intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events, particularly in Italy, which records the highest soil loss rate in Europe (24.13% of
content: The ecosystem service of erosion prevention (ESEP) becomes increasingly important due to the increasing intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events, particularly in Italy, which records the highest soil loss rate in Europe (24.13% of total soil loss in EU; average 8.46 t ha−1 year−1). Knowledge on ESEP focuses mainly on farmland, orchards and forests, while grassland managed by mountain dairy farms have been less studied. This study uses a 2017 dataset from 38 grassland-based dairy farms in the Eastern Italian Alps. The aim was to identify the environmental and management factors that most influence soil erosion. The Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) was applied in a GIS-based framework. Monthly variation in the C factor (representing land cover and management effects) was estimated for three plots per farm (113 plots total) using a Generalised Linear Mixed Model. Although estimated mean soil loss (9.48 t ha−1 year−1) is slightly above the Italian average, nearly half of the plots have erosion rates lower than this benchmark. The C factor shows significant correlations with mean monthly temperature, altitude and species richness in the plot, fuel used per hectare and farm area. Higher temperature lowered the C-Factor, resulting in better soil protection, and the other factors increased it, though with a lower strength. This modelling study is a first step towards understanding the relative importance of factors driving mountain soil erosion. Such study could support the assessment of soil erosion in future scenarios, involving livestock farming abandonment in a context of climate change

title: Perspective of euhydration in children: health risk during climate change
summary: Euhydration during infancy and childhood is a complex task and especially gains importance especially during climate change. Euhydration is maintained through neuroendocrine pathways, but heat stress can lead to disturbance in water homeost
content: Euhydration during infancy and childhood is a complex task and especially gains importance especially during climate change. Euhydration is maintained through neuroendocrine pathways, but heat stress can lead to disturbance in water homeostasis, with dehydration being particularly critical in children. Voluntary dehydration is common among children and inadequate water intake can lead to both short-term and long-term health issues. Discussing water excretion mechanisms, including thermoregulation and kidney function potential health impacts can be highlighted. Furthermore, individual aspects potentially impact water homeostasis of an individuum. Climate change exacerbates the risk of dehydration. Current drinking recommendations do not account for these challenges. This overview offers an inside of current research data on hydration principles and increased long-term risks for health due to climate change. It points out deficiency of data in children and is at the same time a call to action for research on climate sensitive drinking recommendations.

title: CLIMATE CONDITIONS, FORMATION FACTORS, AND HYDRO-ECO-GEOGRAPHICAL IMPORTANCE OF NORTHERN SURKHANDARYA
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Ushbu maqolada Surxondaryo viloyatining shimoliy qismi - Hisor tizmasining janubiy yon bagʻirlari va togʻ oldi vodiylari - iqlim sharoitlari, ularning shakllanish omillari hamda gidro-eko-geografik ahamiyati tahlil qilingan. Denov meteostan
content: Ushbu maqolada Surxondaryo viloyatining shimoliy qismi - Hisor tizmasining janubiy yon bagʻirlari va togʻ oldi vodiylari - iqlim sharoitlari, ularning shakllanish omillari hamda gidro-eko-geografik ahamiyati tahlil qilingan. Denov meteostansiyasining 1991–2020-yillar iqlim normalari (Jahon meteorologiya tashkiloti, NOAA arxivi) va nashr etilgan gidrometeorologik ma'lumotlar asosida hududda oʻrtacha yillik harorat 15,6–17,5 °C, yogʻin miqdori tekislik qismida 200–350 mm, togʻlarda esa 790 mm gacha ekanligi, yogʻinning taxminan 85% i qish va bahor oylariga toʻgʻri kelishi aniqlandi. Asosiy iqlim shakllantiruvchi omillar sifatida subtropik kenglik, Hisor tizmasining shimoliy sovuq havo massalaridan toʻsiq vazifasi, janub va janubi-gʻarbning tropik havo massalariga ochiqligi hamda balandlik mintaqalanishi koʻrsatildi. Surxondaryo va Sherobod daryolari oqimi qor va muzlik suvlaridan shakllanadi: Sherobod havzasida aprel–iyun oylariga oʻrtacha suvli yillarda yillik oqimning 55,1% i toʻgʻri keladi. Masofadan zondlash ma'lumotlariga koʻra, Hisor muzligi maydoni 1990–2024-yillarda 8,6 km² dan 5,1 km² gacha (40,7% ga) qisqargan. Suv resurslarini moslashuvchan boshqarish va ekotizimlarni muhofaza qilish boʻyicha takliflar ishlab chiqildi.

title: Bridging Innovation and Ecosystem Resilience: A Regional Case Study of the Seshachalam Biosphere (Tirupati-Kadapa)
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Rapid industrialization and increasing anthropogenic pressures necessitate a paradigm shift from conventional end-of-pipe remediation toward preventive, sustainable, and environmentally benign approaches.The present study explores the integ
content: Rapid industrialization and increasing anthropogenic pressures necessitate a paradigm shift from conventional end-of-pipe remediation toward preventive, sustainable, and environmentally benign approaches.The present study explores the integrated role of green research, sustainable technologies, and green chemistry in promoting regional environmental protection, with particular emphasis on the ecologically sensitive and biodiverse Seshachalam Hills Biosphere Reserve, spanning the Tirupati and Kadapa districts of Andhra Pradesh, India.By incorporating the twelve principles of green chemistry, particularly atom economy, the use of renewable feedstocks, and the development of less hazardous synthetic pathways, the study highlights opportunities to integrate sustainable chemical practices with advanced ecological conservation strategies.These approaches offer potential pathways for protecting the region's fragile dry deciduous and scrub forest ecosystems, conserving threatened endemic species such as Pterocarpus santalinus (Red Sanders) and Cycas beddomei, and preserving its distinctive geological and geomorphological heritage.Furthermore, the study proposes a comparative assessment of the region's biophysical, physicochemical, and conservation indicators in relation to selected Indian and international biodiversity hotspots.It also examines trends in the global green chemistry market and explores the potential of closed-loop phytotechnology, green extraction methods, and phytonanotechnology as sustainable interventions for watershed management, pollution mitigation, and ecosystem restoration.Collectively, these approaches emphasize the importance of integrating green chemistry and technological innovation into regional environmental governance to strengthen biodiversity conservation, promote resource efficiency, and support long-term ecological sustainability.

title: Under-utilized wild varieties: a focus on Vigna vexillate in Africa
summary: Wild varieties can be used to improve genetic diversity in agriculture to enhance food security. Their potential to enhance genetic diversity remains unexplored. This systematic review focuses on the underutilized Vigna vexillata, a wild va
content: Wild varieties can be used to improve genetic diversity in agriculture to enhance food security. Their potential to enhance genetic diversity remains unexplored. This systematic review focuses on the underutilized Vigna vexillata, a wild variety with superior morphological and physiological traits compared to other Vigna species. The agro-ecological, nutritional, and medicinal properties of V. vexillata are discussed in relation to other Vigna species. Agro-ecological, V. vexillata possesses several advantages, including resistance to pests and diseases and adaptability to marginal climates and saline soils. The species' long non-glandular trichomes and the presence of amylase inhibitors in its seeds contribute to its resistance to pests and diseases. The high survival rate and growth capacity of the seeds with mineral concentration in the roots and shoots under saline conditions, suggest its potential for cultivation in marginal environments. Morphologically, it has larger leaves, thicker stems, and greater pod size and number. Nutritionally, grains of V. vexillata contain 25%–38% protein and 50%–60% starch, and sulphur-containing amino acids. Similarities in the reproductive and chromosomal structure of V. vexillata with other Vigna species can advantageously be used to genetically enhance the agro-ecological, morphological and nutritional traits of other Vigna species through research, policy, and advocacy.

title: Xây dựng bộ tiêu chí và chỉ số đánh giá khả năng tích lũy các-bon của cây gỗ phân tán ở cấp cá thể: cơ sở khoa học và thử nghiệm bước đầu
source: Tạp chí Khoa học và Công nghệ Lâm nghiệp
summary: Đánh giá các-bon cây gỗ phân tán tại Việt Nam chủ yếu dừng ở ước tính trữ lượng tại một thời điểm, chưa phản ánh đầy đủ khả năng tích lũy các-bon và chất lượng phép ước tính. Nghiên cứu xây dựng bộ tiêu chí và chỉ số S–Q–R đánh giá khả năng
content: Đánh giá các-bon cây gỗ phân tán tại Việt Nam chủ yếu dừng ở ước tính trữ lượng tại một thời điểm, chưa phản ánh đầy đủ khả năng tích lũy các-bon và chất lượng phép ước tính. Nghiên cứu xây dựng bộ tiêu chí và chỉ số S–Q–R đánh giá khả năng tích lũy các-bon của cây gỗ phân tán theo khung phân cấp tiêu chí – chỉ số – biến kiểm chứng, dựa trên hướng dẫn IPCC, phương trình sinh khối của Chave và cộng sự (2014) và cách tiếp cận UFORE/i-Tree. Bộ gồm ba tiêu chí với bốn chỉ số: lượng các-bon tích lũy – S (kg C/cây); tốc độ tích lũy – Q (mức thay đổi trữ lượng các-bon thuần hằng năm, ưu tiên xác định từ đo lặp, khi chưa có được mô phỏng theo kịch bản – Q_kb) và Q_rel; chất lượng dữ liệu và phương pháp ước tính – R (0–1), báo cáo độc lập. Thử nghiệm trên 44 cá thể thuộc 35 loài tại Trường Đại học Lâm nghiệp cho tổng trữ lượng 14,22 tấn C (khoảng tin cậy 95%: 11,1–18,5 tấn C), phân bố lệch mạnh (trung vị 122,33 kg C/cây; CV 159,1%). Trung vị Q_kb đạt 5,26 và 13,01 kg C/cây/năm với tốc độ tăng trưởng đường kính 0,83 - 1,98 cm/năm. R dao động 0,450–0,810: 20 cá thể ở mức cao, 23 trung bình (chủ yếu do khối lượng riêng gỗ cấp chi hoặc cây bị cắt tỉa) và 1 cá thể thấp. Bộ tiêu chí vận hành được với dữ liệu điều tra thông thường; Q_kb chỉ có ý nghĩa thử nghiệm và cần kiểm chứng trên mẫu lớn, nhiều vùng sinh thái, có đo lặp trước khi xây dựng ngưỡng đánh giá hoặc hướng dẫn kỹ thuật.

title: Can Sri Lanka Become a Regional Hub for Algal Biodiesel Production? A Critical Review of Ecological Potential, Technological Readiness, and Future Prospects
source: Journal of Environmental Professionals Sri Lanka
summary: Sri Lanka's dependence on imported fossil fuels and its abundant aquatic resources have generated increasing interest in algal biodiesel as a sustainable third-generation biofuel. This review critically evaluates the country's potential to
content: Sri Lanka's dependence on imported fossil fuels and its abundant aquatic resources have generated increasing interest in algal biodiesel as a sustainable third-generation biofuel. This review critically evaluates the country's potential to develop a commercially viable algal biodiesel sector by synthesizing evidence on ecological suitability, indigenous algal resources, technological readiness, sustainability benefits, and commercialization challenges. Sri Lanka possesses favorable climatic conditions, diverse freshwater and marine ecosystems, and several indigenous microalgal and macroalgal species with promising lipid productivity. However, comparison with international experience demonstrates that favorable natural resources alone are insufficient for commercialization because harvesting costs, downstream processing, economic viability, and policy support remain major constraints. The review identifies critical research gaps in pilot-scale cultivation, techno-economic assessment, life-cycle analysis, and strain improvement, and proposes strategic priorities including integrated biorefineries, wastewater-based cultivation, industrial CO₂ utilization, and supportive policy frameworks. These coordinated interventions are essential for positioning Sri Lanka as a competitive regional hub for sustainable algal biodiesel production.

title: Associations of Rainfall, Temperature, and Habitat Transformation with Elephant and Giraffe Abundance and Distribution in Meru National Park, Kenya (1995–2025)
source: East African Journal of Environment and Natural Resources
summary: The study investigated the relationships between rainfall patterns, temperature fluctuations, habitat alterations, and the distribution and abundance of elephants (Loxodonta africana) and giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis) within Meru Nation
content: The study investigated the relationships between rainfall patterns, temperature fluctuations, habitat alterations, and the distribution and abundance of elephants (Loxodonta africana) and giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis) within Meru National Park over a thirty-year period (1995–2025). Employing a combination of remote sensing data, climatic records, and wildlife census information, the research explored how environmental variables influence habitat quality and the spatial distribution of these keystone species. The findings reveal significant correlations: declining rainfall and rising temperatures are associated with habitat degradation, notably forest loss and grassland expansion, which in turn affect the movement and population dynamics of elephants and giraffes. While elephants exhibit some resilience due to their adaptive foraging and water dependence, giraffe populations are more sensitive to habitat changes driven by climatic variability. The study emphasises the necessity of integrated conservation strategies that account for climate influences to ensure the sustainability of these species and their habitats in Meru National Park.

title: Perceptions of environmental health education among medical students: opportunities for improving the training of health professionals on planetary health issues – a cross-sectional survey in a French university
summary: Abstract Background Deteriorating environmental conditions directly affects human health and healthcare organization. Although environmental health education in initial medical training appears to be a key factor to implementing attenuation
content: Abstract Background Deteriorating environmental conditions directly affects human health and healthcare organization. Although environmental health education in initial medical training appears to be a key factor to implementing attenuation and adaptation strategies, it remains insufficiently integrated into medical curricula, and the views of students receiving suchtraining are rarely documented. This study aims to identify the methods of integration and teaching deemed most relevant by medical students who completed a compulsory 31-hour module. Methods A descriptive, cross-sectional, survey study was conducted among third-year undergraduate medical students at a French university who had taken the ‘Environmental Health’ module in the 2024–2025 and 2025–2026 academic years. Students completed a 43-item questionnaire one year after the course for the 2024–2025 cohort, or immediately afterwards for the 2025–2026 cohort. Closed-ended responses were analyzed descriptively as counts and percentages; no statistical testing was performed. Open-ended questions were analyzed narratively. Results A total of 140 questionnaires were analyzed, representing a final response rate of 37.3%. Among the respondents, 94 (67.1%) considered the cross-curricular integration of the course throughout the entire program to be more relevant than a standalone module. There were 96 (69.1%) who felt that 30 hours was too long, while 102 (72.9%) believed that all students should take this type of course. Immersion in other contexts (83.6%) and hands-on learning (74.3%) far outstripped theoretical instruction (22.9%) among the tools considered useful for raising awareness, while university courses were ranked last among sources of awareness (28.6%). Finally, 114 students (81.4%) reported that their other teachers never or rarely addressed these issues. Conclusions Students who are among the most extensively trained in environmental health in France consider their course to be too long butbelieve that these issues should be taught to everyone, in a cross-disciplinary manner and through active learning formats. Training teachers in all disciplines appears to be a prerequisite for this change.

title: Global lake synchrony signals rising planetary-scale ecological coupling
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth's surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrien
content: Understanding how localized ecosystem dynamics scale up to influence Earth-system stability remains a major challenge. Lakes, though covering less than 2% of Earth's surface, play a disproportionate role in regulating global carbon, nutrient, and biodiversity dynamics, making them a critical nexus for assessing emerging large-scale environmental coupling. By integrating satellite observations with century-scale sedimentary archives from ~2,000 lakes, we reveal a marked acceleration in global lake synchrony since 2000. This synchronization, coinciding with converging climatic and socioeconomic pressures, signals a widespread erosion of the spatial heterogeneity and regional distinctiveness that historically characterized inland waters. We propose that increasing lake synchrony represents an emergent property of the Anthropocene, transforming lakes from regionally structured, asynchronous waterscapes into dynamically coupled planetary commons. By temporally aligning carbon and nutrient dynamics across broad spatial scales, this synchronization modifies the timing and amplitude of aggregate biophysical fluxes, altering how inland waters interact with larger-scale environmental cycles. Ultimately, this finding motivates a macroscale monitoring framework that jointly tracks synchrony, modularity, and their functional consequences, demanding a shift in governance toward preserving the ecological heterogeneity essential for maintaining long-term environmental stability.

title: Welfare impacts of climate-smart agriculture adoption among smallholder maize farmers in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
summary: Climate change continues to threaten agricultural productivity worldwide, with smallholder farmers in developing countries facing heightened vulnerability due to limited resources and adaptive capacity. This study examined the welfare impac
content: Climate change continues to threaten agricultural productivity worldwide, with smallholder farmers in developing countries facing heightened vulnerability due to limited resources and adaptive capacity. This study examined the welfare impacts of adopting Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices (CSAPs) among smallholder maize farmers in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. The practices investigated included drought-tolerant maize varieties, rainwater harvesting systems, maize-legume intercropping, and crop diversification. Using cross-sectional data from 378 farmers and guided by Random Utility Theory, the study applied an Endogenous Switching Regression (ESR) model to address potential selection bias in adoption decisions. Household welfare was assessed using the Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS) and the Household Food Insecurity Access Scale (HFIAS). Results showed that 47.1% of farmers had adopted CSAPs. Adopters experienced significantly better welfare outcomes, recording lower food insecurity levels (HFIAS score of 7.67 compared to 9.73 for non-adopters) and higher dietary diversity (HDDS of 6.79 compared to 5.39). Treatment effects analysis further indicated that while adopters benefited substantially in terms of food security, non-adopters could achieve even greater improvements in dietary diversity if they adopted CSAPs. The findings underscore the importance of strengthening extension services, improving access to credit, promoting climate-resilient seed systems, and supporting diversified farming practices to enhance resilience and welfare among smallholder farming households.

title: CSR poster A0 ENG
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Climate Smart Research A0 poster representing ESRs (PioneERS and InnovatERS) and the conceptual framework for climate-smart agricultural research.
content: Climate Smart Research A0 poster representing ESRs (PioneERS and InnovatERS) and the conceptual framework for climate-smart agricultural research.

title: Adaptation R&D, Knowledge Spillovers and Stable International Environmental Agreements
summary: Abstract The paper investigates how adaptation research and development (R&D) and knowledge spillovers affect the formation and stability of International Environmental Agreements (IEAs) in a dynamic framework. Adaptation is modeled as a kn
content: Abstract The paper investigates how adaptation research and development (R&D) and knowledge spillovers affect the formation and stability of International Environmental Agreements (IEAs) in a dynamic framework. Adaptation is modeled as a knowledge-based public good generated through cooperative R&D, with knowledge fully shared within the coalition and only imperfectly spilling over to non-members. We formulate an infinite horizon differential game in which countries simultaneously choose emissions and adaptation investments, whereas pollution and adaptation knowledge evolve over time. The open-loop Nash equilibrium is characterized analytically, yielding explicit steady-state solutions for emissions, pollution, adaptation investments and knowledge stocks. The local dynamic properties of the equilibrium are then investigated through a stability analysis and its saddle-path properties are assessed numerically for the parameter configurations considered. Comparative statics reveal how coalition size, adaptation effectiveness, knowledge spillovers, environmental vulnerability, R&D costs and knowledge depreciation jointly influence the long-run equilibrium. The numerical analysis demonstrates that the model generates not only the conventional small stable coalitions commonly found in the IEA literature, but also intermediate self-enforcing coalitions and, under suitable parameter configurations, the grand coalition. Stable coalition size is shown to depend on the balance between the technological benefits of cooperative adaptation and the incentives to free ride on shared knowledge. More effective adaptation technologies enlarge stable coalitions, whereas stronger knowledge spillovers, higher cooperative R&D costs and faster knowledge depreciation reduce participation incentives. The results highlight that adaptation policies may simultaneously strengthen international cooperation and generate moral hazard by weakening mitigation incentives. Overall , the paper shows that the interaction between adaptation knowledge and coalition formation substantially enlarges the range of self-enforcing international environmental agreements as well as the coexistence of medium and large coalitions compared with standard dynamic models.

title: Structuring Firms' Alignment With the Sustainable Development Goals: ESG and Broader Corporate Performance Indicators
summary: ABSTRACT The literature on ESG indicators highlights the relevance of corporate contributions to sustainable development. However, fragmentation and a lack of standardized indicators limit alignment between corporate performance and global
content: ABSTRACT The literature on ESG indicators highlights the relevance of corporate contributions to sustainable development. However, fragmentation and a lack of standardized indicators limit alignment between corporate performance and global sustainability goals. This study examines how the literature has addressed the relationship between Corporate Performance, the SDGs, and ESG indicators in recent years, identifying prevailing approaches, measurement strategies, and reported findings. We conduct a systematic literature review complemented by bibliometric and content analyses. Results suggest a marked increase in publications after 2019 and a predominance of governance indicators in studies linking ESG to corporate performance and the SDGs. Across the sample, more than 300 distinct ESG indicators are identified, evidencing heterogeneity in measurement practices. Based on these findings, we develop a conceptual framework that clarifies structural patterns in the ESG–SDG–Corporate nexus and contributes to greater conceptual integration in corporate sustainability research.

title: From Geothermal Heat to Stored Hydrogen: A Critical Review of System Efficiency, Materials Durability, Life-Cycle Emissions, and Economic Feasibility
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Geothermal energy can supply both the electricity and the heat needed to split water, which makes it an unusual candidate for hydrogen production that can run almost continuously.This review follows the full chain from geothermal heat to st
content: Geothermal energy can supply both the electricity and the heat needed to split water, which makes it an unusual candidate for hydrogen production that can run almost continuously.This review follows the full chain from geothermal heat to stored hydrogen and judges it through four lenses: system efficiency, materials durability, life-cycle emissions and economic feasibility.Coupling options range from electrolysis powered by geothermal electricity to steam electrolysis and thermochemical cycles driven directly by geothermal heat.Heat integration can raise the efficiency of solid oxide systems, but geothermal fluids at roughly 100-250 °C limit the gain and add corrosion and scaling risks.Published life-cycle studies place geothermal electricity at about 10-50 g CO2-eq/kWh, which we estimate at about 0.6-2.6 kg CO2-eq per kg of hydrogen, although gasrich fields can emit far more.Thermodynamic-economic models report production costs of roughly US$1-3 per kg.We identify the main gaps: field-scale demonstrations, durability data under variable and brineexposed operation, and consistent system boundaries across efficiency, emission and cost studies.

title: Modeling Urban Street‐Scale CO 2 in Paris With GRAMM/GRAL and Comparison to Mid‐ and High‐Cost Observations
summary: Abstract Cities concentrate large shares of emissions on small spatial scales and are key actors for climate mitigation, yet substantial uncertainties persist in urban emission estimates. Dense sensor networks are increasingly deployed to r
content: Abstract Cities concentrate large shares of emissions on small spatial scales and are key actors for climate mitigation, yet substantial uncertainties persist in urban emission estimates. Dense sensor networks are increasingly deployed to resolve intra‐urban gradients, but interpreting these observations requires atmospheric transport models that capture the effects of urban topography on flow and dispersion. We apply the building‐resolving GRAMM/GRAL atmospheric transport model at 10 m × 10 m resolution in Paris and evaluate it at 18 mid‐cost and 7 high‐cost measurement sites over two years (2023–2024). The simulations are driven by two anthropogenic emission inventories—a high‐resolution city‐specific inventory by Origins.earth and a European‐scale inventory by TNO—together with a biogenic flux data set constructed from the Vegetation Photosynthesis and Respiration Model (VPRM). We introduce an ensemble‐based transport uncertainty estimate derived from the underlying catalog approach of GRAMM/GRAL. With the Origins.earth inventory, the framework reproduces observed mole fractions across the full diurnal cycle, including the typically challenging nighttime and morning transition periods, with an average RMSE of 10.58 ppm and a mean bias of −2.53 ppm. For the afternoon, the values improve to 6.61 ppm and −0.98 ppm, respectively. The model resolves weekday–weekend contrasts in traffic‐related emissions and identifies systematic differences in the diurnal emission profiles of the two inventories. These results demonstrate that building‐resolving atmospheric transport modeling, combined with high‐resolution emission data, can accurately reproduce dense urban observations. This study provides a foundation for future urban emission quantification based on mid‐ and high‐cost measurements.

title: Zero-Entropy Thermodynamic Cooling Architectures via Trans-Planckian Horizon Lock Mechanics: Mitigating Global Warming Inversions
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This treatise delivers the definitive mathematical physics formulation to resolve the structural paradox of global warming acceleration induced by classical compression-based refrigeration systems, satisfying zero-entropy growth conditions
content: This treatise delivers the definitive mathematical physics formulation to resolve the structural paradox of global warming acceleration induced by classical compression-based refrigeration systems, satisfying zero-entropy growth conditions (\Delta S -> 0). Traditional HVAC cycles exhibit severe continuum mechanics breakdown and localized thermal divergences when cooling macro-scaled closed envelopes, as dictated by standard Second-Law constraints. Operating within the functional infrastructure of Trans-Planckian Horizon Lock Mechanics (TPHLM), we resolve this environmental crisis by executing a rigorous multi-loop tensor regularization under the global metric scale factor of the Khandey Causal Invariant Constant (K_J = 2.02 x 10^26 m). We prove that localized thermal fluctuations can be topologically locked into non-dissipative macro-state boundaries without generating trailing vacuum entropy, achieving a deterministic 0.0000000000000000% computational error baseline for sustainable exascale cooling grids.

title: Tái sử dụng dinh dưỡng từ nước thải biogas trong nông nghiệp theo hướng kinh tế tuần hoàn: Tổng quan và bằng chứng thực nghiệm tại Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long
source: Can Tho University Journal of Science
summary: Livestock production in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta generates large quantities of nitrogen (N)- and phosphorus (P)-rich waste, most of which is not yet appropriately reused. This review synthesizes studies on nutrient reuse from biogas effl
content: Livestock production in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta generates large quantities of nitrogen (N)- and phosphorus (P)-rich waste, most of which is not yet appropriately reused. This review synthesizes studies on nutrient reuse from biogas effluent from three perspectives: the circular economy, nutrient recovery and reuse, and evaluation across experimental scales. Pot experiments show that ammonium nitrogen (NH₄⁺-N) in biogas effluent can partially replace synthetic N fertilizer for rice and upland crops while achieving comparable yields under experimental conditions. Appropriate water management can also reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Field-scale studies, however, remain limited. Large irrigation volumes, risks from pathogens and heavy metals, and the lack of a regulatory framework are the main barriers to scaling up practical application. The review proposes an N flow diagram that marks loss points and control points, together with preliminary indicators of nutrient circularity in biogas effluent reuse.

title: CLEAN TECHNOLOGIES FOR SUSTAINABLE AQUACULTURE IN THE AMAZON: A PRODUCTIVE ECOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVE.
summary: Aquaculture is a rapidly growing global food sector that is essential for food security, but its expansion generates significant environmental impacts. The Colombian Amazon represents a strategic setting for aquaculture development, despite
content: Aquaculture is a rapidly growing global food sector that is essential for food security, but its expansion generates significant environmental impacts. The Colombian Amazon represents a strategic setting for aquaculture development, despite facing challenges such as deforestation and water pollution. Sustainable development in this region requires the implementation of adaptive governance frameworks and clean technologies, such as floating cages, biofloc systems (BFT), and geomembranes, which support multiple UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This research, using a qualitative approach and narrative review of scientific literature and technical documents, seeks to identify strategic prospects for Amazonian aquaculture sustainability. The results highlight that aquaculture in the region contributes positively to SDGs (1, 2, 6, 12, 13, 15, and 17) by promoting economic opportunities, food security, efficient water management, and climate change mitigation. Technologies such as BFT emerge as efficient alternatives by minimizing water exchange and transforming waste into microbial feed. In conclusion, the strategic outlook for Amazonian aquaculture requires a holistic approach that integrates technological efficiency with ecological conservation and social welfare, shaping a future where aquaculture production is a strategic ally for sustainable regional development.

title: In Situ Pore Generation in Clay via Co‐pyrolysis With Biomass Feedstocks: Toward Low‐Cost Adsorbents for Pollutant Control
summary: ABSTRACT Clay is abundant and low‐cost; yet its limited porosity greatly restricts its use in adsorption‐based pollutant control. Here, we propose an in situ pore‐generation strategy by co‐pyrolyzing clay with biomass feedstocks. During pyr
content: ABSTRACT Clay is abundant and low‐cost; yet its limited porosity greatly restricts its use in adsorption‐based pollutant control. Here, we propose an in situ pore‐generation strategy by co‐pyrolyzing clay with biomass feedstocks. During pyrolysis, biomass releases volatiles and undergoes shrinkage, which can create channels and voids within the surrounding clay matrix. To verify this concept, clay was co‐pyrolyzed with sawdust, cellulose, lignin, poplar leaves, banana peels, flour, and bio‐oil at 700°C–900°C. Pyrolysis of clay alone produced a residue with negligible porosity ( S BET = 1.3 m 2 ·g −1 ), whereas co‐pyrolysis with biomass increased S BET to 18.2–287.5 1.3 m 2 ·g −1 and markedly promoted pore development. Biomass composition strongly influenced the pore structure: sawdust, cellulose, and lignin mainly generated microporous composites, whereas feedstocks richer in aliphatic structures favored mesopore formation. In situ DRIFTS showed that the evolution of the clay/char composite was governed by biomass decomposition, and that secondary condensation of volatiles formed hydrophobic carbonaceous deposits on the surface. Overall, this work demonstrates a simple and effective route for converting low‐porosity clay into porous clay/char composites with tunable pore structures, offering promise as low‐cost adsorbents for the control of hazardous organic contaminants and related environmental risk mitigation.

title: Low-Emission Economic Development in Mongolia: A System Dynamics Scenario Analysis of Sectoral Structural and Technological Transitions to 2050
summary: This study investigates the long-term dynamic relationship between economic growth and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Mongolia over the period 2010–2050 using an integrated System Dynamics modeling framework. The model endogenously coupl
content: This study investigates the long-term dynamic relationship between economic growth and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in Mongolia over the period 2010–2050 using an integrated System Dynamics modeling framework. The model endogenously couples macroeconomic production across 18 economic sectors via Cobb–Douglas production functions with sectoral energy demand, IPCC-compliant emission intensity, and a detailed 14-species forest carbon sequestration engine. Economic output is reported as nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at current prices. The Tapio decoupling index, calculated annually from nominal GDP and gross GHG emissions, is used to assess the evolving elasticity between economic expansion and environmental pressure under three policy pathways: Business as Usual (BAU), Mitigation (S2, aligned with Mongolia’s NDC 3.0 and LT-LEDS incorporating 3533 MW across 32 energy projects), and Transformational (S3). The simulation results indicate that under the BAU scenario, nominal GDP reaches MNT 501.84 trillion by 2050, with gross GHG emissions escalating to 93.19 MtCO2e and net GHG emissions reaching 69.70 MtCO2e due to declining forest sequestration (23.49 MtCO2e). Conversely, the Transformational scenario—combining aggressive clean energy expansion (1733 MW of hydro, solar, wind, and storage), legacy thermal plant decommissioning (220 MW), industrial electrification, and active forest ecosystem management—maintains equivalent economic output (nominal GDP of MNT 501.80 trillion) while reducing net GHG emissions to 36.90 MtCO2e by 2050. This represents a 47.1% reduction in net GHG emissions relative to BAU. Furthermore, Tapio elasticity analysis reveals that while short-term structural investments in baseload power infrastructure, renewable grid expansion, and industrial capacity buildouts cause a temporary surge in emission intensity during 2028–2029 (expansive negative decoupling, DI>1.2), the Transformational pathway uniquely achieves sustained absolute decoupling (DI<0, ranging between −0.059 and −0.700) throughout 2041–2050. These quantitative findings demonstrate that structural and technological transitions can successfully decouple economic expansion from emissions in resource-dependent, landlocked developing economies.

title: Smart asphalt materials for future road infrastructure: advances in self-healing, self-sensing, and structural health monitoring in the mexican context
summary: Road infrastructure constitutes a strategic asset for Mexico's economic development, international trade, and regional connectivity. However, pavement networks are increasingly affected by accelerated deterioration resulting from heavy traf
content: Road infrastructure constitutes a strategic asset for Mexico's economic development, international trade, and regional connectivity. However, pavement networks are increasingly affected by accelerated deterioration resulting from heavy traffic loads, environmental aging, and extreme climatic conditions. Traditional reactive maintenance approaches have proven both technically and economically inefficient in addressing the challenges of twenty-first century transportation systems. This article provides a comprehensive review of recent advances in smarth asphalt materials as a transformative solution for enhancing pavement durability, functionality, and sustainability. Attention is given to self-healing technologies, including electromagnetic induction heating and rejuvenator-containing microcapsules, as well as self-sensing asphalt systems capable of traffic monitoring, weighing in motion applications, and early damage detection through piezoresistive behaivor. Additionally, developments in electrically conductive pavements for de-icing applications and Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) integrated with Internet of Things technologies are examined. The review highlights the opportunities for Mexico to leverage locally available industrial byproducts, such as steel slag, and bio-based resources to facilitate the transition toward resilient, intelligent, and sustainable road infrastructure. The findings indicate that smart asphalt technologies have significant potential to reduce maintenance costs, improve traffic safety, extend pavement service life, and support the digital transformation of transportation systems. Particular attention is given to encapsulated rejuvenators, whose field performance is governed by the survival of the capsule through mixing and compaction and by the kinetics with which the healing agent is released and diffuses into the aged binder.

title: Green Resilience: A Community-Based Climate-Smart Vegetable Production Project for Flood-Prone Agricultural Areas in Negros Oriental
source: International Journal of Research in Interdisciplinary Studies
summary: Background: This paper presents the outcomes of the Green Resilience: Climate-Smart Vegetable Production program implemented by the College of Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries of Negros Oriental State University in collaboration with lo
content: Background: This paper presents the outcomes of the Green Resilience: Climate-Smart Vegetable Production program implemented by the College of Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries of Negros Oriental State University in collaboration with local farming communities in low-lying, flood-prone areas of Negros Oriental. Objective: The project aimed to rehabilitate waterlogged farmlands, enhance agricultural resilience, and strengthen community participation through the adoption of climate-smart technologies. Methods: The project ran from October 2024 to April 2025. Guided by a participatory action research approach, farmers most of whom were women successfully adopted raised-bed farming, drainage systems, plastic mulching, and organic nutrient management. Results: The study reported substantial increases in crop yield and household income, alongside strengthened community collaboration. Evaluation findings showed excellent ratings across all indicators and full satisfaction among participants. Conclusion: Overall, the project demonstrates that localized, inclusive, and research-driven climate-smart interventions can transform vulnerable farmlands into sustainable, productive systems and serve as replicable models for gender-responsive and climate-resilient agricultural development.

title: Dispersion Modeling of the 2021 Eruptive Plumes at Mt. Etna by Coupling WRF‐Chem Model With Ground‐Based and Satellite Remote Sensing Observations
summary: Abstract From 20 December 2020 to 22 February 2022, 66 paroxysmal events occurred at Mt. Etna volcano. Among these, the paroxysms of 4 and 12 March 2021 were investigated by coupling a plume dispersion modeling approach with ground‐based fl
content: Abstract From 20 December 2020 to 22 February 2022, 66 paroxysmal events occurred at Mt. Etna volcano. Among these, the paroxysms of 4 and 12 March 2021 were investigated by coupling a plume dispersion modeling approach with ground‐based flux measurements and satellite observations. Both paroxysms generated ash‐ and ‐rich plumes reaching heights of ∼11.8 and ∼10.8 km above sea level, respectively. In this work, we explored the spatial dispersion of volcanic ash and using the WRF‐Chem model. The modeling system was equipped with additional modules to read at each integration time‐step the plume injection height obtained from the MSG‐SEVIRI satellite, the ash Mass Eruption Rate inferred from the plume height and the bulk flux measured from ground by the FLAME‐DOAS network. To evaluate the predictive performance of WRF‐Chem, simulated ash and maps were compared with those retrieved from SEVIRI and TROPOMI satellites, and a quantitative assessment based on statistical metrics was performed. Based on the plume dispersion path, for the event of 4 March additional validation was carried out using downwind observations from an ALC and a sunphotometer located in Messina (Southern Italy). Results from both qualitative visual comparison and quantitative analysis (mostly low errors, Normalized RMSE < 0.1) suggest that this modeling configuration can efficiently reproduce the dispersion of both and ash plumes emitted from Mt. Etna across the Mediterranean region, demonstrating its potential as a tool for assessing air quality, aviation safety, and hazard scenarios associated with the atmospheric transport of volcanic emissions from local to Mediterranean scales.

title: Estimating greenhouse gas emissions and absorption in rice biomass with multi-temporal remote sensing and machine learning
source: Journal of Forestry Science and Technology
summary: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while optimizing rice cultivation is a major challenge for agricultural countries such as Vietnam, which aims to achieve net-zero emissions and strengthen climate change mitigation by 2050. Although r
content: Reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions while optimizing rice cultivation is a major challenge for agricultural countries such as Vietnam, which aims to achieve net-zero emissions and strengthen climate change mitigation by 2050. Although rice production is essential for food security, it is also a primary source of CH₄, N₂O, and CO₂ emissions. Developing and evaluating technical measures and management strategies is therefore necessary to reduce emissions without compromising productivity. This study uses an integrated model that combines multi-temporal Sentinel-1A SAR data with machine learning algorithms to estimate rice biomass carbon emissions and uptake in Hà Nội, Hưng Yên, and Ninh Bình provinces in the Red River Delta. Results from the Winter–Spring and Summer–Autumn cropping seasons indicate that total greenhouse gas emissions (CO₂, N₂O, CH₄) reached approximately 122 thousand tons, while total carbon uptake was estimated at about 354 thousand tons, resulting in a net carbon accumulation of roughly 232 thousand tons. These findings demonstrate that while rice cultivation emits substantial GHGs, rice biomass can sequester significant amounts of carbon. The study provides quantitative evidence to support sustainable emission-reduction policies in rice production. More broadly, integrating remote sensing and machine learning methods offers an effective approach for monitoring carbon dynamics and supporting cultivation practices and policies that balance environmental sustainability with food security.

title: Demand-side pathways for clean air and health
summary: Abstract Conventional air pollution governance relies heavily on supply-side and end-of-pipe controls. While these measures have substantially reduced SO 2 , NO x , and primary particulate emissions, their marginal returns are diminishing.
content: Abstract Conventional air pollution governance relies heavily on supply-side and end-of-pipe controls. While these measures have substantially reduced SO 2 , NO x , and primary particulate emissions, their marginal returns are diminishing. The remaining pollution burden is shifting toward nitrogen-containing secondary aerosols and ozone. This review synthesizes evidence delineating the pathways through which demand-side interventions across diverse sectoral domains (e.g., residential energy, transport, food systems and agriculture, buildings, consumption, and urban form) shape pollutant emissions, ambient concentrations, population exposure, and health outcomes. Three conclusions emerge from this literature review. First, agricultural ammonia is the most cost-effective remaining target for global PM 2.5 mitigation, yet it remains largely unregulated despite high benefit-to-cost ratios. Second, consumption distribution is increasingly decoupled from actual population exposure across spatial scales. Consequently, consumption-based accounting is a necessary complement to effective air quality governance, not merely a peripheral accounting exercise. Third, demand-side measures generate multipathway health co-benefits through physical activity, healthier diets, reduced indoor exposure, and improved energy security. These benefits often exceed mitigation costs and cannot be captured through production-side regulation alone. Future evaluations must trace the full analytical chain from final demand through nonlinear atmospheric chemistry to health outcomes and inequality, with artificial intelligence positioned as a central methodological priority.

title: Predicting farmers' readiness to adopt decentralized renewable energy under climate shocks and power outages
summary: The increasing vulnerability of agricultural systems to climate variability and infrastructural shocks has severely affected the security of base resources, particularly at the critical water-energy-food nexus. This study aimed to predict a
content: The increasing vulnerability of agricultural systems to climate variability and infrastructural shocks has severely affected the security of base resources, particularly at the critical water-energy-food nexus. This study aimed to predict and analyze farmers' readiness to adopt decentralized renewable energy under climate shocks and power outages in Kermanshah Province. The theoretical framework of the study is based on the integration of Protection Motivation Theory (PMT) and Diffusion of Innovations Theory (DOI). Data were collected through a survey method using a researcher-made questionnaire with 50 items. The sample size was determined as 384 using Cochran's formula and selected through stratified random sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that power outage shocks (β = 0.386, p < 0.001), perceived drought vulnerability (β = 0.352, p < 0.001), and perceived relative advantage (β = 0.324, p < 0.001) were positively and significantly associated with readiness to adopt decentralized renewable energy, explaining 47% of the variance (R² = 0.47). Perceived risks were negatively and significantly associated with readiness to adopt (β = -0.156, p = 0.005). Perceived relative advantage played a partial mediating role in the relationship between power outage shocks/drought vulnerability and adoption readiness (β = 0.136, p < 0.001; β = 0.089, p = 0.003), while perceived risks played an indirect-only mediating role in the relationship between self-efficacy and adoption readiness (β = 0.052, p = 0.018). Perceived self-efficacy did not have a significant direct effect, but it was indirectly associated with readiness through reducing perceived risks. The findings provide evidence-based policy insights for water and energy policymakers to facilitate a resilient and sustainable transition to clean energy through a community-centered approach.

title: Reliable synthetic data augmentation for plant stress classification from PTR-MS VOC profiles using a crop–stress factorized variational autoencoder
summary: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) released by plants respond rapidly to biotic and abiotic stresses and serve as important biomarkers of plant health. Proton-transfer-reaction mass spectrometry (PTR-MS), owing to its high sensitivity and ra
content: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) released by plants respond rapidly to biotic and abiotic stresses and serve as important biomarkers of plant health. Proton-transfer-reaction mass spectrometry (PTR-MS), owing to its high sensitivity and rapid response, provides an effective tool for dynamic monitoring of plant VOCs. However, plant VOC data are typically characterized by substantial within-class variability, considerable between-class overlap, and limited availability of high-quality labeled samples. These challenges hinder the development of robust classification models and restrict the rapid, non-destructive identification of plant stress states. To address these challenges, a data augmentation method based on a Crop–Stress Factorized Variational Autoencoder (CSF-VAE) was developed. The latent representation was factorized into crop-specific, stress-specific, and shared subspaces. Crop-type and stress-state supervision were applied to the corresponding subspaces, respectively, while joint-class supervision was imposed on the concatenated latent representation. Candidate synthetic samples were screened for class consistency using quadratic discriminant scores, followed by fixed-size subset selection guided by the empirical energy distance from the corresponding real training samples. Experiments on PTR-MS data from healthy, drought-stressed, and freezing-stressed wheat and maize showed that the CSF-VAE-augmented dataset combined with a one-dimensional convolutional neural network achieved the best classification performance, with mean Accuracy, Macro-F1, and Weighted-F1 values of 87.16%, 87.10%, and 86.34%, respectively. Compared with the original dataset, CSF-VAE augmentation increased CNN accuracy from 73.41% to 87.16% and outperformed VAE- and CVAE-based augmentation. Under equal synthetic-sample quotas, ablation analysis showed a higher mean classification accuracy and a smaller standard deviation after screening across repeated data partitions. The proposed approach provides a reliable solution for intelligent analysis of complex plant VOC data under limited-sample conditions and offers a data-driven route for rapid, non-destructive identification of plant stress states.

title: A Multiphysics Approach for Particle Size Optimization in Shales Using Low-Pressure Nitrogen Adsorption Measurements: Investigations from the Damodar Valley Basin, India
summary: Abstract Accurate characterization of complex shale pore networks is critical for various applications ranging from understanding and modeling pore-level changes in caprocks for carbon capture, utilization, and storage sites to unconvention
content: Abstract Accurate characterization of complex shale pore networks is critical for various applications ranging from understanding and modeling pore-level changes in caprocks for carbon capture, utilization, and storage sites to unconventional energy exploration. However, the reliability of low-pressure nitrogen adsorption (LPNA) remains hindered by unstandardized sample crushing protocols, introducing an analytical paradox between internal pore accessibility and mechanical structural alteration. Limited studies address this gap, particularly concerning shales in the Indian subcontinent. Furthermore, existing investigations typically rely on restricted sample sets. To address this limitation, this study systematically evaluates the impact of distinct crushed particle sizes, namely M-40 (425 μm), M-120 (125 μm), and M-200 (75 μm), using eight representative core samples from two different formations and sub-basins, namely the Barren Measures (BMF) and Raniganj Formation (RF) from the Raniganj sub-basin (RSB) and Jharia sub-basin (JSB) in the Damodar Valley Basin (DVB), India. A unique multiscale multiphysics approach was deployed, integrating crushed-pore-scale quantitative mineralogy analysis via Rietveld refinement on X-ray diffraction (XRD) data and LPNA parameters of the rock with core-scale high-frequency benchtop ultrasonic analysis. The results indicated that the argillaceous BMF exhibited significantly higher specific surface area (SSA) and total pore volume (TPV) compared to the arenaceous quartzofeldspathic RF. It is also observed that a reduction in particle size systematically enhances gas accessibility, with M-200 yielding SSA values approximately 2.1 times and 1.8 times higher than M-40 in the BMF and RF, respectively. Clay-rich BMF largely retained H3 hysteresis across all particle sizes, whereas the mixed clay-sand RF shifted from H4 to H3 upon progressive reduction of particle size. While bulk-scale compressional wave velocities (Vp) correlate inversely with SSA and TPV, as the fractions get finer, the intermediate M-120 fraction provides the most robust linear relationships overall, with intrinsic clay mineralogy (R2 = 0.69) and internal pore cross-plots (R2 = 0.88). Based on our analysis of the DVB shales, we conclude that the intermediate M-120 fraction represents the optimal threshold for LPNA characterization, successfully liberating isolated nanopores without introducing over-crushing artifacts. The findings from this multiphysics approach advance the standardization of adsorption-based pore characterization in shales, especially for the Indian unconventional reservoir rocks.

title: Central Appalachian Partnership for Carbon Storage Deployment Web-Based Tool
source: DOE National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL) Repository
summary: The Central Appalachian Partnership (CAP) for Carbon Storage Deployment Project was a technical collaboration between the Pennsylvania Geological Survey (PAGS) and West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES), focused on acceleratin
content: The Central Appalachian Partnership (CAP) for Carbon Storage Deployment Project was a technical collaboration between the Pennsylvania Geological Survey (PAGS) and West Virginia Geological and Economic Survey (WVGES), focused on accelerating the deployment of carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) in Pennsylvania and West Virginia by reducing barriers for entry to carbon storage project opportunities. This project was funded by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) under Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) 2799 and represents the only such project where multiple states worked together to address CCUS within their region. The Project team has built a free, publicly available ArcGIS Online application that contains essential geologic and technical data alongside area specific map products. The Tool has been designed to provide stakeholders and other interested parties the ability to access, visualize, and download information to assist with their geologic natural resource assessment needs, carbon storage project opportunities, and understanding of UIC activities in the study area. It contains a combination of interpretive mapping products (e.g., structure contours and stratigraphic correlation), downloadable empirical data (e.g., well completion reports, laboratory analytical results), core photographs and imagery-based analytical data, and UIC data.

title: Stage-aware Bayesian-guided evolutionary algorithm for resource constrained serverless MapReduce scheduling
summary: Abstract Serverless computing features instant elasticity and fine-grained billing. It has emerged as a prominent paradigm for big data processing such as log analysis and monitoring. However, scheduling MapReduce jobs under serverless reso
content: Abstract Serverless computing features instant elasticity and fine-grained billing. It has emerged as a prominent paradigm for big data processing such as log analysis and monitoring. However, scheduling MapReduce jobs under serverless resource constraints is challenging because the stateless nature of functions conflicts with MapReduce stage dependencies, which increases scheduling complexity. Existing research has not adequately captured these structural constraints, causing traditional evolutionary algorithms to explore the search space inefficiently. This study addresses the MapReduce scheduling problem under serverless resource constraints with the objective of minimizing the makespan. Accordingly, a stage-aware Bayesian-guided evolutionary algorithm (BGA) is proposed that, unlike traditional evolutionary algorithms, guides evolution through Bayesian learning from elite patterns. First, a mixed-integer programming model is formulated to unify temporal and precedence constraints. Second, a Bayesian probability model for assigning tasks to function instances guides evolutionary sampling using elite patterns, reducing inefficient search. Finally, dependency-aware crossover is integrated with adaptive variable neighborhood search to ensure feasibility and enhance local exploitation. Experimental results show that BGA consistently achieves the lowest makespan among compared methods, with Relative Percentage Deviation (RPD) remaining within 2.40%-3.92%.

title: Single-cell genomics reveals genomic and functional differentiation between freshwater and saline Achromatium populations.
summary: Giant sulfur bacteria of the genus Achromatium reportedly contain extensive genomic diversity within individual cells. Most genomic data (35 assemblies) come from freshwater populations obtained from Lake Stechlin, Germany, alongside four s
content: Giant sulfur bacteria of the genus Achromatium reportedly contain extensive genomic diversity within individual cells. Most genomic data (35 assemblies) come from freshwater populations obtained from Lake Stechlin, Germany, alongside four single-cell genomes from a salt marsh and saline mineral springs. Here, we characterize marine Achromatium from mangrove sediments in Guadeloupe and compare them with freshwater and saline references. Microscopy, elemental mapping, and Raman spectroscopy revealed calcium-rich inclusions, and intracellular elemental sulfur as previously described for this genus. Scanning electron microscopy revealed two cell-size morphotypes. We generated eleven single-cell, four mixed-cell, and two metagenomic binned assemblies from Guadeloupe mangrove. Divergent copies of conserved marker genes revealed extensive intracellular genomic diversity in individual cells of both morphotypes. Multigene phylogenies provided separation between freshwater references and most genomes from saline environments, including the Guadeloupe population. Gene presence-absence analyses further revealed differences in functional potential between Guadeloupe and Stechlin cells across five functional annotation categories including PFAM, KEGG Orthologs, and CAZymes. Differences in genes associated with osmotic regulation, ion transport, carbohydrate degradation, and secretion systems suggest variation in functional potential related to environmental adaptation, interactions and resource utilization. No significant differences in functional potential between Guadeloupe morphotypes were found. Together, these marine genomes reveal genomic and functional differentiation from freshwater populations and suggest that intracellular diversity does not erase freshwater/saline population boundaries.

title: A Manually Curated Metabolic Model of Alteromonas macleodii MIT1002 and its Ecological Implications
summary: Heterotrophic bacteria are a vital part of the marine carbon cycle. They interact with phytoplankton and rapidly process fixed carbon, respiring it back to CO2. Among heterotrophs, Alteromonas macleodii is notable for its colonization of pa
content: Heterotrophic bacteria are a vital part of the marine carbon cycle. They interact with phytoplankton and rapidly process fixed carbon, respiring it back to CO2. Among heterotrophs, Alteromonas macleodii is notable for its colonization of particulate material and its high growth and carbon utilization rates and is commonly used as a model system to study metabolic interactions with the abundant cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus . Understanding how these traits emerge from the interplay of hundreds of reactions requires a formal encoding of the organism’s metabolic network. Here, we present a metabolic model of A. macleodii MIT1002, built in a traceable and systematic way to recreate experimental growth phenotypes on 51 unique media compositions. We used this model to generate testable hypotheses about the role of sodium in the electron transport chain, the catabolic relevance of different glycolytic pathways, nitrogen recycling during cross-feeding with Prochlorococcus , and microbial carbon use efficiency.

title: Mapping class-dependent interactions of electrolyte additives with polysulfides in lithium-sulfur batteries
summary: Lithium-sulfur batteries offer high energy density but suffer from polysulfide shuttling and limited cycle life. Electrolyte additives can mitigate these effects by altering polysulfide interactions and conversion behavior. Here, we use qua
content: Lithium-sulfur batteries offer high energy density but suffer from polysulfide shuttling and limited cycle life. Electrolyte additives can mitigate these effects by altering polysulfide interactions and conversion behavior. Here, we use quantum-mechanical calculations to compare nine representative additives spanning molecular salts, cluster models, and periodic oxide surfaces across the full polysulfide series (Li 2 S to S 8 ). For 54 additive-polysulfide pairs, binding energies range from −7.0 to −0.03 eV and reveal a clear class hierarchy: cluster models interact most strongly, molecular salts occupy an intermediate regime, and periodic oxide surfaces are weakest on average while retaining species- and site-dependent adsorption. Combined binding-energy, electronic-structure, and solvation trends indicate that complementary molecular-oxide strategies merit experimental evaluation under lean-electrolyte conditions, where retention and reversible conversion must be balanced. These results provide a mechanistic framework for rational additive screening and electrolyte design in Li–S batteries.

title: Consequences of cell culture media variation on CHO cells, part 1: Metal speciation changes during media storage
summary: Trace-level metals such as manganese (Mn), iron (Fe), cobalt (Co), copper (Cu), and zinc (Zn) are crucial to the proliferation of Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells and subsequent biotherapeutic protein production as these metals support enz
content: Trace-level metals such as manganese (Mn), iron (Fe), cobalt (Co), copper (Cu), and zinc (Zn) are crucial to the proliferation of Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells and subsequent biotherapeutic protein production as these metals support enzymatic function, redox balance, and metabolic activity. In chemically defined cell culture media (CCM), these metals are formulated to be present at carefully researched concentrations and chemical forms to maximize growth and productivity. It has been suggested that chemical speciation, the form in which these metals exist, changes over time and with different storage conditions, potentially impacting their bioavailability and cellular performance. Here, Mn, Fe, Co, Cu, and Zn speciation and concentration changes are investigated across three types of CCM (basal and two feedstocks) stored at 4°C and room temperature for 3 months, as well as 37°C for 3 weeks. A polypropylene capillary-channeled polymer fiber column is utilized to affect the speciation-based separation of the metals via reversed-phase liquid chromatography. Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry is used to quantify the metal fractions. Findings revealed that Mn, Fe, Co, and Cu speciation is dynamic, dependent on media composition, time, and temperature, while Zn is stable and remains in its intended, inorganic form. Notably, Cu exhibited the greatest change in speciation, with a majority of it transforming from the free ion to a ligated-complex form under increased temperatures and storage times. These findings highlight a critical need for the monitoring of chemical speciation of nutrient metals as a means of quality control.

title: Enhancing Removal of PFAS and Pharmaceuticals from Municipal Wastewater via GAC Pretreatment and StyDex Polishing
summary: Abstract A dual-sorbent system consisting of a granular activated carbon (GAC) pretreatment followed by polishing with styrene-functionalized β-cyclodextrin (StyDex) beads was evaluated for removal of four per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance
content: Abstract A dual-sorbent system consisting of a granular activated carbon (GAC) pretreatment followed by polishing with styrene-functionalized β-cyclodextrin (StyDex) beads was evaluated for removal of four per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS: PFOA, PFHxA, PFBA and PFHxS) and two pharmaceuticals, bezafibrate (BEZ) and diclofenac (DCF), from municipal wastewater. Building on previous pilot evaluations of StyDex as a stand-alone sorbent, this study evaluates its integration into a treatment train with GAC pretreatment, examining GAC replacement frequency and selection of polishing sorbent to more effectively remove mixtures of PFAS and other trace organic contaminants from municipal wastewater. Upstream GAC pretreatment was used to nonselectively remove target compounds, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and other competing background wastewater constituents to enhance downstream polishing performance. System performance was evaluated by comparing individual removal of target compounds by GAC-StyDex and GAC-ion-exchange resin (IXR) treatment trains and assessing the impact of periodic GAC replacement on polishing performance. Combining GAC pretreatment with StyDex polishing demonstrated the highest total removal of PFOA, PFHxS, and DCF over the duration of the pilot, and improved removal of the weaker sorbing compounds, PFHxA, BEZ, and PFBA. However, PFBA was not effectively controlled over the full pilot duration and exhibited substantially lower cumulative removal (55%–62%) in the GAC-StyDex and GAC-IXR trains, compared to the other five target compounds, which all had >93% removal. Extending the GAC replacement interval from 2,500 to 5,000 BV increased sorption capacity by 59.9% (0.177 to 0.283 μmol g–1), allowing greater GAC bed utilization prior to replacement while also maintaining low effluent concentrations after polishing. Compared with GAC-IXR, GAC-StyDex had 87.4% greater sorption capacity (0.283 vs 0.151 μmol g–1) on a mass-normalized basis and similar performance on a sorbent-volume basis, demonstrating StyDex as a high-capacity alternative sorbent for downstream polishing. These findings demonstrate the potential for integrating GAC pretreatment with downstream polishing to improve contaminant removal, maintain low effluent concentrations, enhance sorbent utilization, and inform the design of scalable wastewater treatment systems.

title: Effect of metal salts on the morphology of Mn 2 O 3 hollow spheres and their application for CO 2 fixation reactions
summary: A Mn 2 O 3 hollow sphere was prepared by the hydrothermal method. The Mn 2 O 3 hollow sphere exhibits enhanced catalytic performance for the CO 2 fixation reaction.
content: A Mn 2 O 3 hollow sphere was prepared by the hydrothermal method. The Mn 2 O 3 hollow sphere exhibits enhanced catalytic performance for the CO 2 fixation reaction.

title: AuNP/ZnO-NW/KMO-NF hybrid interface-integrated evanescent-field MMF–SMF–MMF fiber sensor for enhanced pyocyanin detection
summary: Pyocyanin, a harmful metabolite and a representative virulence determinant of Pseudomonas aeruginosa , is the target analyte of a novel crayfish-type MMF–SMF–MMF biophotonic sensor introduced herein, which integrates rapid response with lon
content: Pyocyanin, a harmful metabolite and a representative virulence determinant of Pseudomonas aeruginosa , is the target analyte of a novel crayfish-type MMF–SMF–MMF biophotonic sensor introduced herein, which integrates rapid response with long-term operational stability. Pyocyanin detection is important for preventing ecological damage, ensuring food-chain safety, and supporting rapid clinical diagnostics. The biosensor leverages localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) to enhance the evanescent field and employs gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), zinc oxide nanowires (ZnO-NWs), and potassium manganese oxide nanoflowers (KMO-NFs) to optimize sensor performance and enhance stability. The sensor was functionalized with pyocyanin aptamers to achieve a specific detection. This sensor performance was evaluated with the linear detection range of 0–90 μg/mL, the sensitivity was 28.6 pm/(µg/mL), and the limit of detection (LoD) was 9.13 µg/mL. The sensor also underwent tests for reproducibility, reusability, stability, single-analyte, detection time and pH to verify its practicality and reliability. Real sample detection using tap water, milk, and orange juice indicated good adaptability to complex environments. Compared with existing methods, this method has multiple advantages and offers a pioneering technological pathway for the quick and accurate detection of pyocyanin, potentially becoming a powerful tool in the field of pyocyanin detection, thereby reducing the risk of infection and enhancing public health.

title: Carbon- and polymer-integrated colloidal systems for biosensing: interfacial mechanisms, performance trade-offs, and applications
summary: Colloidal nanoparticles integrated with carbonaceous supports and polymeric matrices provide tunable interfaces for biosensing, but their analytical benefits depend on how hybridization affects charge transfer, analyte transport, receptor a
content: Colloidal nanoparticles integrated with carbonaceous supports and polymeric matrices provide tunable interfaces for biosensing, but their analytical benefits depend on how hybridization affects charge transfer, analyte transport, receptor accessibility, and stability. In this review, we summarize the fundamental principles of electrochemical, optical, and piezoelectric biosensors, and we examine the functional contributions of colloids to signal amplification, selective biorecognition, and advanced interface engineering. We emphasize the growing demand for rapid, sensitive analytical systems in applications such as medical diagnostics, food safety, environmental monitoring, and point-of-care testing. We reviewed major classes of colloidal materials, including metallic nanoparticles, quantum dots, silica colloids, and clay-based structures such as montmorillonite, with respect to their physicochemical advantages and biosensor performance. Integrated analyses of colloid-enriched electrochemical, optical, piezoelectric, and magnetic platforms reveal both the promising aspects and limitations of current technologies. Despite their strengths, practical application remains hampered by issues such as particle aggregation, long-term instability, inconsistent immobilization onto sensor substrates, and fabrication challenges in hybrid or nanoscale systems. Recent advances, such as engineered miniprotein receptors, quantum dot-based electrochemical sensing, and fiber-based metal-enhanced fluorescence (MEF) structures, illustrate emerging strategies to overcome these limitations. This review concludes that future progress will rely on atomic-scale surface engineering, scalable and reproducible fabrication methods, non-enzymatic recognition motifs, and the integration of colloidal materials with smart biointerfaces. Overall, colloids represent a rapidly developing class of materials with the potential to advance biosensor technologies toward more accurate, durable, and accessible platforms for biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications.

title: Volatile Terpenes in Exhaled Breath: Xenobiotic Biomarkers or Misleading Mirages?
summary: Volatile terpenes and terpenoids in exhaled breath have emerged as intriguing candidates for noninvasive biomarker development, yet their clinical relevance remains debated due to their assumed exogenous origin. This Perspective seeks to re
content: Volatile terpenes and terpenoids in exhaled breath have emerged as intriguing candidates for noninvasive biomarker development, yet their clinical relevance remains debated due to their assumed exogenous origin. This Perspective seeks to review the key literature on exhaled terpenes and highlight their potential as xenobiotic biomarkers to monitor a wide range of medical conditions. Through a fusion of breathomics, pharmacokinetics, and an understanding of cytochrome P450 induced metabolism, we argue that terpenes could report on disease-specific enzymatic activities and offer advantages over traditional endogenous VOCs, particularly toward early-stage detection. We propose strategies for identifying novel terpene substrates, biomarker validation, and integration with nanosensor platforms for point-of-care detection. If realized, xenobiotic terpene/terpenoid biomarkers could represent a paradigm shift in breath-based diagnostics by demonstrating that naturally occurring compounds introduced exogenously can function as intentional probes for noninvasive health monitoring.

title: A forest fire multi-scale adaptive attention network for forest fire risk assessment using multi-source remote sensing data
summary: Forest fires pose severe threats to ecosystems, human life and socioeconomic development, rendering effective risk assessment essential for proactive prevention and timely management. Existing approaches generally rely on fixed-scale featur
content: Forest fires pose severe threats to ecosystems, human life and socioeconomic development, rendering effective risk assessment essential for proactive prevention and timely management. Existing approaches generally rely on fixed-scale feature extraction, limiting their ability to simultaneously capture fine-scale spatial details and broad contextual information in complex mountainous environments. This study proposes a forest fire multi-scale adaptive attention network (FMAAN) for forest fire risk assessment. The core multi-scale adaptive module determines appropriate scale combinations and to fuse the corresponding features adaptively, adjusting the effective receptive field for each input sample to capture fire-driving information across spatial scales. Deformable convolutions and a two-stage attention mechanism are further incorporated to enhance geometric adaptability and emphasise critical fire-risk features. The model is evaluated in the Anning River Valley, southwestern Sichuan Province, China. Results demonstrate that FMAAN outperforms all baseline models across multiple evaluation metrics, achieving 90.48% accuracy and an F1-score of 90.99%. Risk maps reveal pronounced seasonal variability and spatial heterogeneity, with high-risk areas concentrated in Xichang, Dechang and Mianning. SHAP-based interpretation further identifies NDII7 and relative humidity as the dominant factors influencing model assessments. FMAAN supports targeted fire prevention and resource allocation and informs forest fire risk assessment in mountainous regions.

title: Microstructure-resolved modeling of fused filament fabrication of lithium-ion battery electrodes
