summary: Lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrode microstructure can be flexibly tailored via solvent-free extrusion followed by fused filament fabrication (FFF) printing. However, the influence of extrusion and printing process parameters on the final e
content: Lithium-ion battery (LIB) electrode microstructure can be flexibly tailored via solvent-free extrusion followed by fused filament fabrication (FFF) printing. However, the influence of extrusion and printing process parameters on the final electrode microstructure, properties, and electrochemical performance remains insufficiently explored and has never been investigated through computational modeling. Herein, we introduce a sequential, particle-resolved framework that transfers heterogeneous filaments from our previously developed twin-screw extrusion model into FFF simulations. The FFF model incorporates solid granules and a viscous fluid, representing active materials and binder/conductive phases, with a material cooling law. Single-strand deposition, one- and two-layer printing simulations, used here as a proof of concept, examine filament feed velocity, printing speed, nozzle-bed gap, cooling rate, strand spacing distance, and interlayer arrangement. Geometrical characterization and through-thickness transport analyses quantify void fraction, tortuosity factors, apparent electronic conductivity, and whole-structure electronic resistance of the final two-layer electrodes. Strand spacing strongly affects layer coverage, surface height uniformity, and inter-strand overlap. Two-layer microstructures with similar total void fractions and tortuosity factors exhibit nearly twofold differences in apparent electronic conductivity. This framework lays the foundation for studying the relationships between microstructure and performance in solvent-free LIB electrode manufacturing via extrusion and 3D printing.

title: Carbonization of traditional Chinese medicines: processing strategies, chemical-material transformations, pharmacological activities and clinical applications
summary: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) processing (Paozhi) is a critical pharmaceutical practice for enhancing the safety, efficacy, and clinical applicability of herbal medicines. Carbonization constitutes a distinctive processing strategy inv
content: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) processing (Paozhi) is a critical pharmaceutical practice for enhancing the safety, efficacy, and clinical applicability of herbal medicines. Carbonization constitutes a distinctive processing strategy involving controlled thermal treatment that carbonizes the external surfaces while preserving the essential medicinal properties. This transformation not only modifies traditional indications but also expands clinical applications, particularly in the management of hemorrhage, chronic diarrhea, inflammatory bowel disorders and toxin-related conditions. Despite extensive empirical use, the material basis and mechanistic underpinnings of carbonized TCMs remain poorly defined. This review systematically synthesizes current advances in carbonization techniques, chemical and structural transformations and associated pharmacological activities. Emerging evidence indicates that carbonization induces coordinated multi-scale alterations, including the conversion of phytochemical constituents, the formation of porous carbon architectures and the generation of nanoscale carbon-based materials such as carbon dots. These physicochemical transitions are closely linked to bioactivities, including hemostatic effects, gastrointestinal mucosal protection, anti-inflammatory responses, antimicrobial activity and adsorption-related toxin mitigation. Accordingly, carbonized TCMs can be reconceptualized as a unique class of therapeutics arising from the interplay between chemical transformation and carbon-based structural evolution. By integrating traditional processing theory with contemporary insights from phytochemistry, pharmacology and materials science, this review identifies characteristic chemical transformation patterns and potential quality markers, summarizes emerging pharmacological mechanisms and proposes a carbon dot- and porous carbon-based material framework to better understand the therapeutic properties and quality characteristics of carbonized TCMs. Such an integrated perspective provides a foundation for process standardization, quality control and the modernization of evidence-based clinical applications.

title: A Stearyl‐Peptide Based Versatile Strategy to Design Enzyme‐Responsive Liposomes for Targeted Drug Delivery
summary: Liposomes are a prominent class of drug delivery nanoparticles. For currently approved liposomal therapeutics, drug is released predominantly via diffusion which has spatio-temporal kinetic and bioavailability challenges, especially in a dy
content: Liposomes are a prominent class of drug delivery nanoparticles. For currently approved liposomal therapeutics, drug is released predominantly via diffusion which has spatio-temporal kinetic and bioavailability challenges, especially in a dynamic environment. Next-generation liposome designs focus on stimuli-triggered enhancement of drug release. One exciting approach here is liposomes that can be site-specifically destabilized by disease-associated enzymes. Feasibility of this has been demonstrated with certain phospholipases or metalloproteases, but a versatile strategy for designing liposomes triggerable by any disease-specific enzyme remains lacking. We report a unique liposome design using enzyme-cleavable stearyl-peptide conjugates. Stearylamine has been explored for cationic liposomes in gene delivery, but the cationic charge poses significant cytotoxicity. We demonstrate that conjugating enzyme-cleavable peptides to stearylamine and assembly of stearyl-peptide conjugates within liposomes mitigates the cationic charge and significantly enhances biosafety. Surface-decorating such liposomes with target-specific ligands enables their active target-anchorage under flow. Exposure of target-anchored liposomes to disease-relevant enzymes renders stearyl-peptide cleavage and liposome destablization, enhancing drug release. We demonstrate the design versatility utilizing microfluidic models of three different vascular pathologies (hyperfibrinolysis, thrombosis and thromboinflammation) and delivering three corresponding drugs (tranexamic acid, tissue plasminogen activator and deoxyribonulease) triggered by three different enzymes (plasmin, thrombin and neutrophil elastase), respectively.

title: Electrostatic Virus Capture and Post-Capture Containment Using Positively Charged Porous Polymer (P3) Beads for Point-of-use Water Treatment
summary: Waterborne viruses remain an important challenge to drinking-water safety, particularly for point-of-use treatment where simple and effective technologies are needed. In this study, we develop positively charged porous polymer (P3) beads th
content: Waterborne viruses remain an important challenge to drinking-water safety, particularly for point-of-use treatment where simple and effective technologies are needed. In this study, we develop positively charged porous polymer (P3) beads that couple electrostatic attraction with swelling-assisted transport for rapid virus capture and post-capture containment. The interconnected porous network provides extensive accessible internal charged surfaces while retaining a large bead size for simple physical separation after treatment. By tuning the polymer composition, the optimized P3 beads achieved nearly 4 log removal of MS2 bacteriophage and maintained high capture performance across variations in pH, conductivity, and dissolved organic matter. Importantly, captured viruses remained strongly immobilized on polymer surfaces, with no infectious virus recovered even after mechanical disruption of the beads. Viral RNA was also efficiently captured and retained, indicating that exposed viral genomes can remain immobilized within P3 network. The beads could be regenerated and reused for both nonenveloped MS2 and enveloped Phi6 while maintaining rapid and effective virus removal in simulated groundwater, with no infectious virus detected even after five reuse cycles. By integrating efficient capture, postcapture containment, reusability, and simple separation, P3 beads provide a promising material platform for point-of-use treatment of virus-contaminated water. Table of Contents (TOC) Synopsis: P3 beads enable rapid, reusable virus capture and post-capture containment for simple point-of-use treatment of virus-contaminated water.

title: Compatibilization and Toughening of PLA Composite via Constructing Dynamic Crosslinked Network
summary: ABSTRACT Preparation of polylactic acid (PLA) materials with good comprehensive performance has always been a popular research direction in this field. In this work, we prepared toughened PLA/poly(4‐hydroxybutyrate) (P4HB) composites with g
content: ABSTRACT Preparation of polylactic acid (PLA) materials with good comprehensive performance has always been a popular research direction in this field. In this work, we prepared toughened PLA/poly(4‐hydroxybutyrate) (P4HB) composites with good strength by introducing dynamic transesterification bonds. Torque, infrared spectroscopy, and gel content analyses confirmed the occurrence of the dynamic crosslinking reaction, which greatly improved the compatibility between PLA and P4HB. The effects of flexible P4HB content and dynamic bond density on the thermal, rheological, and mechanical properties were systematically investigated. When the elongation at break of the PLA/P4HB composite reached 121%, the tensile strength remained at 41 MPa, decreased by 30% as compared with that of pure PLA, and the notched impact strength reached about 8.26 kJ/m 2 . Additionally, the PLA/P4HB composites exhibited good anti‐dripping performance due to the introduction of the dynamic transesterification bonds. This strategy effectively improved the mechanical properties of PLA/P4HB composites, providing a new approach for the development of high‐performance and sustainable PLA‐based materials.

title: An APOA5‐Derived Signature Bridges Cholesterol Homeostasis to T‐Cell Exhaustion and Directs Lung Adenocarcinoma Immunotherapy Response
summary: Immune heterogeneity and metabolic remodeling frequently limit the efficacy of immunotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). To address this challenge, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analyses, pairing machine learning with
content: Immune heterogeneity and metabolic remodeling frequently limit the efficacy of immunotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). To address this challenge, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analyses, pairing machine learning with preclinical models to develop the APOA5-correlated T-cell Signature (ACTsig), which effectively stratifies LUAD patients and predicts immunotherapeutic response. Moreover, We identified apolipoprotein A-V (APOA5) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor linking cholesterol homeostasis to the tumor immune ecosystem. Mechanistically, APOA5 deficiency induced intracellular cholesterol accumulation and MIF production. Cholesterol depletion and replenishment established a causal role for cholesterol accumulation in regulating MIF production, while MIF knockdown reversed APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion and recombinant MIF restored the phenotype. Meanwhile, CXCR4 blockade rescued APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion, supporting the functional involvement of the MIF receptor CXCR4 in this immunosuppressive phenotype. Finally, in silico drug screening identified fenofibrate, which, in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, significantly suppressed tumor growth in APOA5-deficient models. Together, these findings establish ACTsig as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy response and reveal an APOA5-cholesterol-MIF-CXCR4 axis underlying T-cell exhaustion.

title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
summary: ABSTRACT Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report
content: ABSTRACT Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS 1 /CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO 2 ‐to‐*NO 2 H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH 2 O‐to‐*NH 2 OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS 1 /CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO 3 − battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: Tension‐Enhanced Impulsive Launching Using Partially Inflated Pneumatic Actuators
summary: Impulsive actuation, exemplified by launching, has been pursued in engineered systems for centuries. To achieve such actuation, two primary strategies have long been employed: elastic mechanisms that gradually accumulate potential energy, a
content: Impulsive actuation, exemplified by launching, has been pursued in engineered systems for centuries. To achieve such actuation, two primary strategies have long been employed: elastic mechanisms that gradually accumulate potential energy, and equipment that unleashes instantaneous bursts, such as explosive high pressure. In the activity of blob launching, an impact input is transmitted to launch the participant simply using a partially inflated airbag, and such soft transmission may inspire new design principles. However, those airbags' complicated deformation makes the underlying physics hard to understand and exploit. Here, we first investigated the launching dynamics based on multiple tabletop drop tests. In these tests, the launching speed exhibited two peaks at different inflation volumes. Through modeling and simulations, we revealed that the two peaks were respectively dominated by the impact-induced stretch and the pressure impulse. The stretch enhances the membrane tension and synergistically acts with the pressure impulse, leading to the fastest peak. A motor-driven actuator was then designed and proven to strengthen the stretching effort. Building on this mechanism, we developed robotic launchers capable of high-speed vertical and horizontal launching. Beyond advancing the understanding of blob launching, this work offers a soft transmission strategy for achieving repeatable, programmable, and impulsive actuation.

title: Bioactive hyaluronic acid‐polyethyleneimine dynamic hydrogel as a versatile platform for quick‐acting wound management
summary: Abstract Acute trauma management requires first‐aid dressings that enable immediate wound closure, rapid hemostasis, antibacterial protection, and ease of use. In this study, we developed an extracellular matrix (ECM)‐inspired hyaluronic ac
content: Abstract Acute trauma management requires first‐aid dressings that enable immediate wound closure, rapid hemostasis, antibacterial protection, and ease of use. In this study, we developed an extracellular matrix (ECM)‐inspired hyaluronic acid‐based dynamic hydrogel for effective wound management. The hydrogel was formed via a Schiff base reaction between aldehyde‐modified hyaluronic acid (AHA, 1.50 MDa) as the polysaccharide skeleton and polyethyleneimine (PEI, 600 Da) as the crosslinker, yielding a highly absorbent dynamic network within 17 s. The in situ formation of imine bonds between residual aldehyde groups in AHA and exposed amines in tissue ensured strong wet adhesion, enabling rapid seamless wound closure and hemostasis. Moreover, the cationic nature of PEI conferred potent antimicrobial activity, effectively inhibiting bacterial invasion and proliferation. Through direct mixing, both the small‐molecular anti‐inflammatory drug ibuprofen (IBU) and the single‐chain polypeptide human growth hormone (hGH) were efficiently encapsulated within this injectable hydrogel, forming AHA‐PEI/IBU/hGH. The obtained multifunctional hydrogel demonstrated significant anti‐inflammatory and migration‐promoting effects in vitro and markedly accelerated wound healing in vivo. Due to its tunable properties and polysaccharide‐based structures, this hydrogel represents a customizable, on‐demand artificial ECM with great potential for personalized wound management.

title: Site-Specific Enzymatic Radiofluorination of Biomolecules: From Current Methodologies to Emerging Opportunities
summary: Abstract The recent expansion of recombinant biomolecules as diagnostic and therapeutic agents has created a strong need for mild, site-specific, and universally applicable methods to radiolabel them for positron emission tomography (PET).
content: Abstract The recent expansion of recombinant biomolecules as diagnostic and therapeutic agents has created a strong need for mild, site-specific, and universally applicable methods to radiolabel them for positron emission tomography (PET). Fluorine-18 is one of the most widely used radionuclides for PET because it combines a clinically practical half-life, high positron intensity with low mean energy, and a non-metallic footprint in the label. However, the conditions necessary for efficient nucleophilic fluorine-18 radiolabelingbasic, anhydrous media, elevated temperature, and aprotic solventsare poorly compatible with sensitive biomolecules. Therefore, prosthetic group labeling with subsequent conjugation, both site-specific and non-site-specific, and aluminum-[18F]fluoride (Al[18F]F2+) chelation have become essential workarounds. Depending on the radiolabeling site, this can yield heterogeneous products, with impaired tracer target binding and pharmacokinetics. Enzymatic ligation offers a complementary strategy, with radiofluorination done on a robust small-molecule or peptide substrate, and subsequently, an enzyme catalyzes a mild and site-specific conjugation to a genetically encoded recognition motif on the target. This ensures that each step proceeds under its own optimal conditions. This review evaluates the current state of enzymatic and chemoenzymatic radiofluorination of biomolecules, from the early fluorinase work to recent advances with lipoic acid ligase (LplA), peptide asparaginyl ligase, and sortase A (SrtA). It further reviews enzymes and techniques that could extend this toolbox. The field is still emerging, but available evidence suggests that enzyme-mediated radiofluorination can occupy a niche between classical prosthetic-group radiochemistry and kit-like radiometal labeling, especially for fragile recombinant biomolecules whose radiolabeling with fluorine-18 is currently a challenge.

title: Active Targeting Across Scales in Medical Robotics
summary: The diagnosis and treatment of human diseases often involve interventions that target different levels of the body's complex hierarchical organization, from macroscopic organs through microscopic cells, down to nanoscale molecular structure
content: The diagnosis and treatment of human diseases often involve interventions that target different levels of the body's complex hierarchical organization, from macroscopic organs through microscopic cells, down to nanoscale molecular structures such as proteins. These interventions are hindered by challenges, such as biological barriers and dynamic microenvironments, which necessitate the development of more effective diagnosis, therapy, and microsurgery strategies. Multiscale medical robots are an emerging strategy to address these challenges: advances in micro and nano engineering have enabled the development of sophisticated medical robots with size adaptability and hierarchical navigation for active targeting. Such systems can connect organ-level access and navigation with local action at tissue, cellular, or molecular scales. Here, we discuss advances in micro/nano engineering to design and fabricate multiscale medical robots, with focus on their active targeting capabilities in precision medicine. We provide an overview of the current state of these systems, from accurate diagnosis and targeted therapy to minimally invasive microsurgery across the various scales of the human body, and explore how anatomical, biological, and imaging constraints shape their design. Finally, we discuss the practical challenges of clinical translation, including system-level assessment within the intended clinical workflow and the need for collaboration between engineers and clinicians.

title: Measuring digital technology adoption: a multidimensional scale development and validation
summary: Existing research widely acknowledges the significant effects of digitalisation, yet empirical work often treats it as a unified construct, which obscures its underlying technological diversity. This paper addresses that limitation by devel
content: Existing research widely acknowledges the significant effects of digitalisation, yet empirical work often treats it as a unified construct, which obscures its underlying technological diversity. This paper addresses that limitation by developing a psychometrically validated scale of digital technology adoption that captures the multidimensional and functionally distinct nature of digital technologies. Drawing on theoretical insights from innovation studies and digital technology research, we identify four core dimensions that structure firms’ adoption profiles: digital communication technology, digital in situ technology, digital data analytics technology, and digital networking technology. We develop and validate a 19-item scale that operationalises these dimensions and reflects the different coordination, optimisation, data access, and location access functions that digital technologies perform. The resulting measurement instrument offers scholars a more precise means to examine how digital technologies shape organisational processes. It also provides managers with a diagnostic tool for assessing adoption patterns and guiding technology investment decisions.

title: Universal Thermally‐Driven Non‐Noble Metal Redistribution Strategy Boosts High‐Temperature CO 2 Electrolysis
summary: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable CO 2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires cathodes that integrate high activity with robust stability. Herein, a thermally‐driven non‐noble‐metal redistribution strategy is proposed
content: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable CO 2 electrolysis in solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) requires cathodes that integrate high activity with robust stability. Herein, a thermally‐driven non‐noble‐metal redistribution strategy is proposed to overcome the long‐standing limitation in dispersing non‐noble metals on perovskite surfaces, enabling perovskite–ceria composite cathodes with dynamically optimized active sites. Thermal treatment of Cu‐dispersed CeO 2 (Cu 0.05 Ce 0.95 O 2 , 5CC) coupled with Sr 2 Fe 1.5 Mo 0.5 O 6− δ (SFM) induces spontaneous Cu migration and redistribution, which can tailor the electronic structure, increase oxygen vacancies and extend triple‐phase boundaries, thereby enhancing CO 2 adsorption, activation and O 2− /e − transport. As a result, a single cell with 5CC–SFM cathode achieves exceptional current densities of 4.14 A cm −2 at 1.5 V under 850°C, respectively. Owing to strong interaction between the redistributed Cu species and perovskite oxide, the single cell maintains stable catalytic performance for 400 h under harsh high‐temperature CO 2 electrolysis conditions. Moreover, this work demonstrates the extended applicability of 5CC–SFM cathode in reversible solid oxide cells (RSOCs) and establishes the generality and methodological significance of thermally‐driven redistribution in achieving highly dispersed non‐noble‐metal species on oxide supports. These findings offer a general framework for the rational design of next‐generation CeO 2 –containing SOEC cathodes and advanced composite materials.

title: Sustainable diets and post-harvest technologies for enhanced food and nutrition security in East Africa: a systematic review
summary: This systematic review examines sustainable dietary interventions and post-harvest technologies (PHT) for reducing food and nutrition insecurity in East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia). Synt
content: This systematic review examines sustainable dietary interventions and post-harvest technologies (PHT) for reducing food and nutrition insecurity in East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia). Synthesizing 27 studies (2015–2025) via narrative approach, it finds nutrient-dense crops improve dietary diversity and resilience, with superior micronutrient profiles and protein digestibility. PHT innovations such as solar drying and zero-energy cooling reduced losses by 30–50% and raised smallholder incomes up to 50% in individual studies (not pooled estimates). PHT may offset economic risks of perishable crops, while dietary diversification could sustain demand for technological investment; however, evidence for synergy is of very low certainty, resting on conceptual reasoning rather than controlled trials. Adoption barriers include high capital costs (USD 500–2,000), knowledge gaps, and infrastructure deficits, while cooperative-led dissemination and gender-sensitive training facilitate uptake. The review suggests that integrated policies, prioritizing decentralized cold storage, indigenous seed systems, and public-private partnerships, may be essential for scaling these interventions.

title: Service life prediction of reinforced concrete beams under chloride‐induced non‐uniform corrosion using reliability approach
summary: Abstract Chloride‐induced corrosion degrades the cross‐section and yield strength of reinforcement, but existing life prediction models often neglect the strength degradation and lack sensitivity analysis. This study developed a service lif
content: Abstract Chloride‐induced corrosion degrades the cross‐section and yield strength of reinforcement, but existing life prediction models often neglect the strength degradation and lack sensitivity analysis. This study developed a service life prediction model for non‐uniformly corroded reinforced concrete members that accounts for time‐dependent yield strength degradation. Using this model, the effects of geometric dimensions, material strengths, and environmental factors on failure probability were systematically analyzed. Key findings include: (1) Increased cover depth and rebar diameter reduce failure probability, though small‐diameter bars exhibit unique sensitivity to non‐uniform corrosion (NUC). (2) Material strength variations have limited influence on failure probability, though the NUC model consistently predicts higher risk than uniform models. (3) Environmental factors significantly affect service life, with 80%–90% relative humidity identified as the most unfavorable range. (4) Dominant risk factors evolve over time, shifting from multi‐parameter coupling (especially humidity) in early stages to concrete cover depth as the decisive factor later. These findings provide valuable insights for durability design in chloride‐laden environments.

title: Dynamic splitting tensile behavior and failure mechanism of hooked-end steel fiber-reinforced rubberized concrete
summary: Rubberized concrete (RC) has attracted increasing attention owing to its favorable deformability and energy absorption capacity. Introducing hooked-end steel fibers (SF) into RC can enhance its mechanical performance through crack-bridging
content: Rubberized concrete (RC) has attracted increasing attention owing to its favorable deformability and energy absorption capacity. Introducing hooked-end steel fibers (SF) into RC can enhance its mechanical performance through crack-bridging and end-anchorage mechanisms. This study investigated hooked-end steel fiber-reinforced rubberized concrete (SFRC) with a fixed 10% rubber replacement ratio and 0%–2.0% SF through quasi-static and dynamic splitting tensile tests. Dynamic tests used a split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) combined with digital image correlation (DIC) at strain rates of 3.22–10.94 s⁻¹. The results showed that SF improved the dynamic splitting tensile strength of RC, with the greatest improvement among the tested contents at 1.5% SF, increasing strength by approximately 35.78%–39.01% compared with RC at the corresponding loading levels. The dynamic increase factor (DIF) increased with increasing strain rate, while SF incorporation reduced the strain-rate sensitivity of SFRC. An empirical DIF prediction model incorporating SF content was developed and exhibited good agreement with the experimental data. The dissipated energy and energy dissipation coefficient increased initially and then decreased with increasing SF content, reaching their maximum values at 1.5% SF. The DIC-based quantitative damage evaluation showed that SF delayed the evolution of damage degree and reduced the tendency toward damage concentration in RC. Furthermore, the correlations among stress response, energy dissipation, and damage evolution were analyzed. The addition of SF modified the failure characteristics of RC and improved the post-failure integrity of the specimens. These findings suggest the potential use of SFRC in impact-resistant structures.

title: Validation of a Dynamic Process Model of a Thermochemical System for Solar Fuel Production
summary: A dynamic process model of a solar-driven fuel production pilot plant has previously been developed to aid in plant operation and control. This work presents the performance of the model’s key components – a high-temperature thermal energy
content: A dynamic process model of a solar-driven fuel production pilot plant has previously been developed to aid in plant operation and control. This work presents the performance of the model’s key components – a high-temperature thermal energy storage (TES), a solar-absorbing gas receiver (SAGR), and a reforming reactor – on operational data from Synhelion’s DAWN pilot plant. The TES model plausibly reproduces charge–discharge transients. For the SAGR, a data-driven surrogate solar field model was created to provide the unmeasured solar input. The coupled surrogate–receiver simulation captures the receiver’s thermal response well, achieving outlet gas temperatures near 1000 °C in good agreement with experiments. A slight overestimation of ~30–40 K in receiver outlet temperature is observed, consistent with a minor bias in the surrogate model. In contrast, the reforming reactor model, which assumes thermodynamic equilibrium at the reactor outlet, could not be fully validated. Discrepancies in syngas composition (e.g. residual CH4 and lower CO2 conversion than predicted) indicate that equilibrium assumptions are not valid under partial-load conditions. The reactor model overestimates reaction extent and heat consumption, suggesting that a kinetic modeling approach or adjusted equilibrium model is needed for accuracy. Overall, the validated components form a promising digital twin of the solar fuel process, but refining the chemical reactor model is essential for reliable full-process simulation.

title: Assessing Hydropower, Irrigation, and Ecosystem Trade-Offs in the Omo-Gibe Basin: Evidence Synthesis and Work Plan
source: CGSPace A Repository of Agricultural Research Outputs (Consultative Group for International Agricultural Research)
summary: The Omo-Gibe Basin is central to Ethiopia's development objectives and to the livelihoods and ecosystems of the communities that depend on it. Its river system supports hydropower generation, irrigated and rainfed agriculture, livestock pro
content: The Omo-Gibe Basin is central to Ethiopia's development objectives and to the livelihoods and ecosystems of the communities that depend on it. Its river system supports hydropower generation, irrigated and rainfed agriculture, livestock production, fisheries, ecosystems and biodiversity, all of which rely on the specific flow regimes, sediment dynamics and flood pulses. This report presents a rapid synthesis of existing evidence on the basin's hydropower development, agriculture, livestock, fisheries, habitats and ecosystem services, together with the influence of climate variability and land-use change on these systems. The synthesis indicates that several assumptions underpinning earlier analyses warrant reassessment. For instance, lake Turkana, projected to decline following upstream development, has risen in recent years, and climate projections for the basin have shifted from a consistent drying signal to a more heterogeneous pattern of change. Building on previous trade-off assessments, and environmental flows related work, the report proposes a 31-month work plan (June 2026–December 2028) comprising diagnostic stakeholder engagement, data acquisition, trade-off scenario analysis and policy dialogue. The intended outcome is a shared and up-to-date evidence base to inform decisions that balance energy, food security, livelihoods and ecosystem integrity.

title: Photocatalytic control of diamond color center charge states via laser-induced surface oxidation
summary: Color center spins in diamond nanostructures are a key resource for emerging quantum technologies. Their innate surface proximity makes precise control of diamond surface chemistry essential for optimizing their functionality and charge sta
content: Color center spins in diamond nanostructures are a key resource for emerging quantum technologies. Their innate surface proximity makes precise control of diamond surface chemistry essential for optimizing their functionality and charge states. However, conventional surface functionalization methods provide limited control over the resulting surface termination and color-center charge state. Here, we demonstrate nonvolatile tuning of diamond’s surface termination through laser-induced oxidation of H-terminated diamond nanopillars. By tracking negatively charged silicon-vacancy (SiV − ) photoluminescence as a charge-state proxy, we elucidate the carrier-assisted nature of this photocatalytic process through systematic photon-flux and photon-energy analyses, identifying defect charge cycling as a source of photogenerated carriers that drive the interfacial redox chemistry responsible for surface oxidation. Our results suggest that this approach may be applicable to other color centers and host materials for charge-state control and surface engineering in solid-state quantum devices.

title: Comparing the Antioxidant Stability of Lipophilic Compounds from Tomato Fruit in Self-Emulsifying Drug Delivery Systems (SEDDS) and in Nano/microemulsion
summary: Lipophilic compounds encounter dissolution problems when administered orally due to their low solubility in gastrointestinal fluids. To improve dissolution performance, several nanocarriers have been implemented, including lipid-based nanoc
content: Lipophilic compounds encounter dissolution problems when administered orally due to their low solubility in gastrointestinal fluids. To improve dissolution performance, several nanocarriers have been implemented, including lipid-based nanocarriers. Presently, self-emulsifying drug delivery systems (SEDDS) and nano/microemulsions have been used to formulate lipophilic antioxidants from tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) fruit and to compare their stability under ambient conditions. The SEDDS is a 1.6% solution of tomato extract in a mixture of Tween 80, Span 80, propylene glycol, and sunflower oil, with mass percentages of 55, 15, 17.5, and 12.5, respectively. The nano/microemulsion was prepared by dispersing the SEDDS in water (1:50). Subsequently, these systems were filled into a colorless, clear glass bottle with a stopper and placed under reflected sunlight during the day and in darkness at night. The antioxidant activity of the formulations was measured by the ABTS method on 0, 1, 3, 5, and 8 days of storage. The order of activity decrease and the rate constant were determined graphically. The results suggested that antioxidant activity decreased following mostly zero-order kinetics, whereas the average R2 indicated a first-order decline. Three parameters were used for stability comparison, namely zero- and first-order rate constants (k0 in %/day and k1 in day-1, respectively) and t90 (days), in which those for SEDDS are 1.427+0.061, 0.087+0.005, 1.02+0.10, respectively, while those for nano/microemulsion are 1.231+0.068, 0.048+0.003, 2.61+0.15. It is concluded that the antioxidant activity of tomato extract in nano/microemulsion is more stable in nano/microemulsion than in SEDDS.

title: A Carbon-Conscious Fuzzy EOQ Model with Trade Credit Financing
summary: The reduction of carbon emissions and the management of sustainable inventories are significant issues industries face as they work to achieve environmental responsibility and economic efficiency. In this article, a two-warehouse inventory
content: The reduction of carbon emissions and the management of sustainable inventories are significant issues industries face as they work to achieve environmental responsibility and economic efficiency. In this article, a two-warehouse inventory model for deteriorating items with disposal cost, time-dependent demands, one trade-credit period under both crisp and intuitionistic fuzzy environments are developed. Shortages are not allowed and the optimal investment in green technology is included, to capture the costs of carbon emissions of transportation. For the crisp formulation and the intuitionistic fuzzy formulation the optimum total cost and a numerical optimization algorithm is determined. The triangular intuitionistic fuzzy numbers and an α, β-cut based defuzzification method are used for uncertainty of purchasing, holding and disposal costs. Two trade-credit scenarios are considered and variations in optimal inventory cycle time, green investment, and total average cost are illustrated by numerical examples, varying the parameters of the model, and performing sensitivity analysis. Comparative results point out the impact of uncertain cost parameters on inventory decisions. The suggested framework aims to facilitate mathematical and fuzzy decision-making by offering the retailers a foundation to consider replenishment policies, investing in the environment and financing conditions for minimizing the total average inventory cost.

title: Redirecting persulfate-based advanced oxidation from mineralization to oxidative polymerization: Mechanisms, products, and resource recovery for sustainable water treatment
summary: Persulfate-based advanced oxidation processes (PS-AOPs) are conventionally used to mineralize organic pollutants, but this route demands substantial oxidant doses and releases the converted carbon as greenhouse gas. Organic pollutants can i
content: Persulfate-based advanced oxidation processes (PS-AOPs) are conventionally used to mineralize organic pollutants, but this route demands substantial oxidant doses and releases the converted carbon as greenhouse gas. Organic pollutants can instead be redirected toward oxidative polymerization, forming separable polymeric solids under controlled activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and peroxydisulfate (PDS) by photo, electro, thermal, or catalyst stimulus. This review traces the full engineering chain of this polymerization route, from monomer structure and activation mechanisms through product classification, recovery, and high-value upcycling to life-cycle and techno-economic assessment and product toxicity. Recovered polymers can be upgraded into solid fuels, carbonaceous materials, conducting polymers, hydrogels, and composite devices. Practical deployment, however, remains bounded by a monomer concentration threshold, catalyst deactivation through polymer self-inhibition, the selectivity-versus-universality trade-off, and the absence of standardized characterization and continuous-flow data. We outline future directions, including standardized protocols, machine-learning-guided catalyst design, unified sustainability assessment, and hybrid treatment trains. Overall, polymerization is favored wherever a moderate, sustained flux of selective oxidant meets a sufficiently concentrated electron-rich monomer, identifying oxidant control as the primary design variable for wastewater resource recovery.

title: Clustering demand-side flexibility for market participation: A joint assessment of flexibility availability and demand response specific cost
summary: Demand-side flexibility can support power system operation under increasing shares of renewable generation. However, the value of a flexible resource depends not only on the amount of demand that can be adjusted but also on the cost associa
content: Demand-side flexibility can support power system operation under increasing shares of renewable generation. However, the value of a flexible resource depends not only on the amount of demand that can be adjusted but also on the cost associated with providing such flexibility. This study proposes a framework that jointly characterises flexibility availability and flexibility cost in order to identify recurring technical and economic flexibility behaviours. The methodology is applied to a multi-family residential building through 24 case studies combining four building archetypes with six heating system configurations, including air-source and ground-source heat pumps, fan-coil and underfloor heating systems, and thermal energy storage. Two complementary forms of flexibility are considered: passive flexibility, arising from the cost-optimal operation of the system without an explicit flexibility request, and active flexibility, representing the additional load adjustment activated in response to an explicit demand-response signal. Both are quantified over a representative winter week. The resulting flexibility characteristics are subsequently analysed using Gaussian Mixture Model clustering, identifying four representative flexibility patterns. The probabilistic analysis shows that ASHP fan-coil configurations are associated with the high active flexibility cluster with a probability of 96%, whereas GSHP underfloor configurations belong to the low-cost cluster with a probability of 84%. Results show that heating system design strongly influences flexibility availability and specific cost, with ASHP fan-coil configurations providing more than 300 kWh of active flexibility over the representative winter week, compared to less than 40 kWh for underfloor heating. Thermal energy storage and building thermal inertia shape the balance between active and passive flexibility, highlighting the potential of the proposed framework to support aggregator portfolio characterisation and flexibility bidding.

title: Pricing and Extended Warranty Strategies for Echelon-Utilized Batteries with Echelon Utilization Rate in a Dual-Stream Supply Chain
summary: : With the rapid increase in retired power batteries, echelon utilization has become an essential strategy for resource sustainability. However, the commercial application of second-life batteries is often held back by high technical screen
content: : With the rapid increase in retired power batteries, echelon utilization has become an essential strategy for resource sustainability. However, the commercial application of second-life batteries is often held back by high technical screening costs and consumer worries about product reliability. This paper builds an analytical model for a dual-stream supply chain where collected batteries are either repurposed for echelon utilization products or sent for material recycling, based on a specific echelon utilization rate. We jointly optimize the selling price and the extended warranty price, taking into account time-varying failure rates and a cost structure that covers repair, preventive maintenance, and battery replacement. The results show that an extended warranty can effectively lower consumers' perceived risk and increase market demand. We find that the best pricing strategy depends on the echelon utilization rate. As this rate goes up, the echelon utilization provider should raise the product price and shift from a service-led approach to a strategy centered on hardware reliability. In addition, the analysis shows that the revenue from material recycling can help offset the high maintenance costs that come with early-stage screening technologies. Furthermore, we quantify the environmental benefits of the system, revealing that the extended warranty acts as an environmental amplifier that significantly boosts total carbon emission reductions. However, the viability of this strategy is strictly bounded by a frontier dictated by the battery degradation rate and the offered warranty period. This study gives managers a quantitative basis for balancing technical efficiency and service provision to improve the profitability of the circular battery business.

title: How does the remaining thickness of dentine affect the pulp's response to silver diamine fluoride?
source: Otago University Research Archive (University of Otago)
summary: AimTo characterise dentine morphology, age-related variation and silver diamine fluoride (SDF)-associated deposits using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and to determine how remaining denti
content: AimTo characterise dentine morphology, age-related variation and silver diamine fluoride (SDF)-associated deposits using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and to determine how remaining dentine thickness influences diffusion and the response of human dental pulp cells (hDPCs) to SDF in an in vitro dentine barrier model. MethodologyNon-carious human permanent molars were used to prepare 1.0 and 1.5 mm thick discs from coronal dentine. SEM and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) were used to characterise 16 discs from younger (≤30 years) and older (≥50 years) donors and to localise SDF-associated deposits. Dye diffusion was assessed after 7 days with or without 37% phosphoric acid treatment (n = 3). For the cell-culture experiment, 38% SDF was applied to discs positioned above hDPCs (n = 3); disc controls, jig-only, cells-only and direct SDF controls were included. After 24 h, adherent cell biomass and metabolic activity were assessed using crystal violet and PrestoBlue™ assays. Spent media was analysed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and matrix metalloproteinase-2 (MMP-2). ResultsSEM showed young dentine had an open tubular morphology compared to older dentine which had smaller tubules and more prominent intertubular dentine. SDF produced surface-associated and intratubular deposits, while EDS demonstrated a stronger silver signal near the treated surface than toward the pulpal aspect. Dye diffusion was greater through 1.0 than 1.5 mm discs under both untreated and phosphoric acid-treated conditions (p = .03 for both comparisons). Phosphoric acid treatment reduced diffusion through 1.0 mm discs by approximately 35% (p = .05). Cell number and metabolic activity did not differ between the 1.0 and 1.5 mm SDF-treated groups (p = .322 and p = .84, respectively), whereas direct SDF exposure reduced both outcomes (p = .001 and p = .007). Levels of IL-6 protein expression were higher after SDF treatment to 1.0 mm thick dentine (12.16 ± 0.99 pg/mL) compared to the control disc (3.74 ± 1.57 pg/mL; p < .001) but did not differ significantly from the 1.5 mm thick discs treated with SDF (10.41 ± 1.57 pg/mL; p = .325). Protein expression of MMP-2 was lower in the 1.0 mm thick dentine discs treated with SDF (0.53 ± 0.34 ng/mL) compared to the cells-only group (14.01 ± 13.99 ng/mL; p = .03). IL-1β and TNF-α protein levels were below the limit of detection. ConclusionSEM demonstrated age- and specimen-related variation in dentine morphology, indicating that thickness alone does not fully describe barrier characteristics. Remaining dentine thickness influenced dye diffusion, although the hDPC response did not differ significantly between 1.0 and 1.5 mm dentine barriers. Dentine appeared to reduce the cytotoxic effects of SDF, but transdentinal exposure remained biologically active. These findings support mai

title: A framework for standardised characterisation of bulk material handling properties of planetary regolith simulants
summary: Planetary regolith simulants are widely used to support the development of surface systems for exploration, construction, and in-situ resource utilisation. While their geotechnical and physicochemical properties are already well documented,
content: Planetary regolith simulants are widely used to support the development of surface systems for exploration, construction, and in-situ resource utilisation. While their geotechnical and physicochemical properties are already well documented, the characterisation of bulk material handling properties critical to storage, conveying, excavation, and processing operations-remains fragmented and largely non standardised. As a result, experimental data are often difficult to compare across studies, simulant batches, and testing facilities, limiting the transferability of findings to mission relevant scenarios. This paper critically reviews existing approaches used to characterise the bulk handling behaviour of planetary regolith simulants, drawing on established practices from the bulk solids handling, powder technology, and particulate materials communities. Key challenges include the sensitivity of regolith simulants to particle size distribution, shape, surface texture, as well as inconsistencies in test selection, sample preparation, and data reporting. This paper proposes an initial framework for characterising the bulk material handling properties of planetary regolith simulants, combining selected terrestrial test methods with a common reporting matrix. Its application is illustrated using eight simulant materials. Most methods were applied once per material (n = 1); the rotating drum measurements included repeated measurements, as described in the experimental section. The dataset therefore demonstrates implementation of the framework but does not establish measurement repeatability, interlaboratory reproducibility, or batch-to-batch consistency. The framework is intended to support more transparent reporting and future comparative studies. Replicated measurements, testing of additional batches, and interlaboratory comparisons are required before its performance as a standardised characterisation approach can be established.

title: Residue analysis, dissipation dynamics, and risk assessment of cyclobutrifluram in paddy environment by a modified QuEChERS/HPLC-MS method
source: Journal of Food Composition and Analysis
summary: Cyclobutrifluram is a chemical commonly used to control rice nematodes, and its residues in the environment may pose a potential threat to human health. In this study, a modified QuEChERS method was employed for sample preparation, combined
content: Cyclobutrifluram is a chemical commonly used to control rice nematodes, and its residues in the environment may pose a potential threat to human health. In this study, a modified QuEChERS method was employed for sample preparation, combined with HPLC-MS detection technology, to establish an analytical method for determining cyclobutrifluram residues in rice paddy ecosystems. Experimental data showed that when the mass concentration ranged from 0.01-1 mg/L, the concentration of cyclobutrifluram exhibited an excellent linear correlation with the chromatographic peak area, with a coefficient of determination greater than 0.999; the method’s LOD and LOQ ranged from 0.0031-0.0059 mg/kg and 0.0103-0.0196 mg/kg. Recovery tests were conducted using three spiked concentration levels. The intra-day recovery rates ranged from 82.17%-111.73%, and the inter-day recovery rates ranged from 83.54%-110.47%; RSDr and RSDR were 0.37%-5.31% and 0.45%-5.20%, respectively. Dissipation test results indicate that the half-life of cyclobutrifluram in paddy field water is approximately 2 days, and in paddy field soil, it is less than 13 days. In all three treatment groups, brown rice posed a low chronic dietary risk to Chinese residents of different age groups and was acceptable for daily consumption.

title: Hierarchical electricity market optimization for incentive-based demand response: consumer behaviour and strategic coordination
summary: Incentive-Based Demand Response (IBDR) is widely recognized for improving power system flexibility and market efficiency. However, most existing literature focuses on individual market participants or single-level market interactions, offer
content: Incentive-Based Demand Response (IBDR) is widely recognized for improving power system flexibility and market efficiency. However, most existing literature focuses on individual market participants or single-level market interactions, offering limited insight into the integrated operation of hierarchical wholesale and retail electricity markets, particularly when considering renewable energy uncertainty and the economic interests of all stakeholders. To address this gap, this paper proposes a hierarchical IBDR market structure that integrates consumer level demand flexibility with retail and wholesale electricity market operations under Renewable Energy (RE) uncertainty. Consumer responses to incentives are managed by Service Providers (SPs) and Load Serving Entities (LSEs) and then incorporated into system level dispatch, which allows demand side decisions to influence the nodal demand, Locational Marginal Prices (LMPs), procurement costs, and subsequent market decisions. The study further incorporates wind-power uncertainty and consumer comfort while evaluating the economic outcomes of consumers, LSEs, and generation companies within a common electricity market structure. The optimisation problems are solved using Linear Programming (LP) in MATLAB and Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) connected through Stackelberg Game Theory (SGT). The proposed approach is validated on the PJM 5-bus system and larger IEEE 118-bus test system under various operating scenarios that reflect changes in consumer behaviour, market conditions, and wind generation uncertainty. Findings highlight that integrating wind generation with IBDR reduces generation costs by 44%, increases LSE profit by 43%, and lowers peak demand by approximately 10% as compared to conventional DR. The financial interests of all entities involved in energy trading are considered, thereby enhancing consumer benefits by 18%, reducing incentive payments by 22%, decreasing generation costs by 35%, and improving overall Social Welfare (SW).

title: Comfort-constrained chilled-water supply-temperature optimization for a vapor-compression chiller in a hot-climate industrial building: A TRNSYS-Python case study
summary: Cooling dominates building energy use in hot climates, yet chilled-water plants are often operated at a fixed supply-temperature setpoint that does not exploit the efficiency benefit available at higher evaporating temperatures. This case s
content: Cooling dominates building energy use in hot climates, yet chilled-water plants are often operated at a fixed supply-temperature setpoint that does not exploit the efficiency benefit available at higher evaporating temperatures. This case study examines chilled-water supply-temperature (CHWST) adjustment for a water-cooled vapor-compression chiller serving a multi-zone industrial building in Samarra, Iraq. A TRNSYS-18 building-and-plant model was executed from Python over CHWST values from 6 to 10°C. The direct setpoint sweep is the primary engineering analysis, while Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization is a secondary demonstration of the TRNSYS-Python workflow. Over the tested range, chiller electricity decreases and seasonal COP increases monotonically; the unconstrained energy optimum occurs at 10°C. Operative-temperature screening uses a fixed 27°C comparison threshold with pooled P95 and ODH_P90 indicators; the threshold is a study-defined screening reference rather than a standards-based comfort limit. Relative to the 7°C baseline, 8.0°C reduces model-predicted chiller electricity by about 1.3% and increases seasonal COP by about 1.8%, while leaving zone-summed overheating degree-hours essentially unchanged; 8.5°C gives about 1.9% lower chiller electricity and 2.7% higher COP but is a conditional upper bound because office and electrical/IT overheating has increased. The electricity boundary is the Type 666 chiller only; pump, cooling-tower and air-side fan electricity is excluded. No measured building or chiller data were available, so the results are simulation-based and the standalone-versus-coupled comparison is a numerical consistency check rather than empirical validation. Comfort conclusions are limited to operative-temperature indicators and do not constitute a PMV/PPD or humidity-based assessment.

title: Evaluating Simplification Algorithms for Interpretability of Time Series Classification
source: Communications in computer and information science
summary: In this work, we introduce metrics to evaluate the use of simplified time series in the context of interpretability of a TSC -- a Time Series Classifier. Such simplifications are important because time series data, in contrast to text and i
content: In this work, we introduce metrics to evaluate the use of simplified time series in the context of interpretability of a TSC -- a Time Series Classifier. Such simplifications are important because time series data, in contrast to text and image data, are not intuitively under- standable to humans. These metrics are related to the complexity of the simplifications -- how many segments they contain -- and to their loyalty -- how likely they are to maintain the classification of the original time series. We focus on simplifications that select a subset of the original data points, and show that these typically have high Shapley value, thereby aiding interpretability. We employ these metrics to experimentally evaluate four distinct simplification algorithms, across several TSC algorithms and across datasets of varying characteristics, from seasonal or stationary to short or long. We subsequently perform a human-grounded evaluation with forward simulation, that confirms also the practical utility of the introduced metrics to evaluate the use of simplifications in the context of interpretability of TSC. Our findings are summarized in a framework for deciding, for a given TSC, if the various simplifications are likely to aid in its interpretability.

title: L2GTX: From Local to Global Time Series Explanations
source: Communications in computer and information science
summary: Deep learning models achieve high accuracy in time series classification, yet understanding their class-level decision behaviour remains challenging. Explanations for time series must respect temporal dependencies and identify patterns that
content: Deep learning models achieve high accuracy in time series classification, yet understanding their class-level decision behaviour remains challenging. Explanations for time series must respect temporal dependencies and identify patterns that recur across instances. Existing approaches face three limitations: model-agnostic XAI methods developed for images and tabular data do not readily extend to time series, global explanation synthesis for time series remains underexplored, and most existing global approaches are model-specific. We propose L2GTX, a model-agnostic framework that generates class-wise global explanations by aggregating local explanations from a representative set of instances. L2GTX extracts clusters of parameterised temporal event primitives, such as increasing or decreasing trends and local extrema, together with their importance scores from instance-level explanations produced by LOMATCE. These clusters are merged across instances to reduce redundancy, and an instance-cluster importance matrix is used to estimate global relevance. Under a user-defined instance selection budget, L2GTX selects representative instances that maximise coverage of influential clusters. Events from the selected instances are then aggregated into concise class-wise global explanations. Experiments on six benchmark time series datasets show that L2GTX produces compact and interpretable global explanations while maintaining stable global faithfulness measured as mean local surrogate fidelity.

title: FoMo-X: Modular Explainability Signals for Outlier Detection Foundation Models
source: Communications in computer and information science
summary: Tabular foundation models, specifically Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs), have revolutionized outlier detection (OD) by enabling unsupervised zero-shot adaptation to new datasets without training. However, despite their predictive power, t
content: Tabular foundation models, specifically Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs), have revolutionized outlier detection (OD) by enabling unsupervised zero-shot adaptation to new datasets without training. However, despite their predictive power, these models typically function as opaque black boxes, outputting scalar outlier scores that lack the operational context required for safety-critical decision-making. Existing post-hoc explanation methods are often computationally prohibitive for real-time deployment or fail to capture the epistemic uncertainty inherent in zero-shot inference. In this work, we introduce FoMo-X, a modular framework that equips OD foundation models with intrinsic, lightweight diagnostic capabilities. We leverage the insight that the frozen embeddings of a pretrained PFN backbone already encode rich, context-conditioned relational information. FoMo-X attaches auxiliary diagnostic heads to these embeddings, trained offline using the same generative simulator prior as the backbone. This allows us to distill computationally expensive properties, such as Monte Carlo dropout based epistemic uncertainty, into a deterministic, single-pass inference. We instantiate FoMo-X with two novel heads: a Severity Head that discretizes deviations into interpretable risk tiers, and an Uncertainty Head that provides calibrated confidence measures. Extensive evaluation on synthetic and real-world benchmarks (ADBench) demonstrates that FoMo-X recovers ground-truth diagnostic signals with high fidelity and negligible inference overhead. By bridging the gap between foundation model performance and operational explainability, FoMo-X offers a scalable path toward trustworthy, zero-shot outlier detection.

title: Institutional environmental intelligence and high-carbon loans: an intellectual capital perspective on government biodiversity attention
summary: Purpose As biodiversity governance becomes increasingly important for sustainable development, understanding how government-generated intangible knowledge influences financial decision-making remains an underexplored issue in intellectual c
content: Purpose As biodiversity governance becomes increasingly important for sustainable development, understanding how government-generated intangible knowledge influences financial decision-making remains an underexplored issue in intellectual capital (IC) research. Drawing on IC theory, this study conceptualizes government biodiversity attention (GBA) as institutional environmental intelligence and examines its effect on high-carbon loans (HCL). Design/methodology/approach This study constructs a novel GBA index using machine learning and text analysis of 5,726 Chinese local government work reports from 2003–2023. Using a panel dataset of 287 Chinese commercial banks from 2016–2023, this study employs fixed-effects regression models, instrumental variable estimation, propensity score matching (PSM), and placebo tests to examine how GBA influences HCL. Findings GBA is significantly negatively associated with HCL by financial institutions. This effect is more pronounced in cities with well-developed green finance systems and low-carbon pilot policies, among local commercial banks and banks actively engaged in green credit practices. Further channel analyses indicate that the relationship between GBA and HCL is associated with environmental constraints, capital adequacy, and bank risk-taking. Originality/value This study develops a novel machine learning-based measure of GBA and provides empirical evidence of how this institutional environmental intelligence influences HCL. It extends the IC perspective to government-generated intangible knowledge, showing how such knowledge shapes financial institutions' environmental cognition and sustainable credit allocation.

title: Reproduction of the price dynamics during interventions in the foreign exchange market based on an extended dealer model
summary: Although the dealer model developed in the field of econophysics has been able to reproduce the characteristics of financial market fluctuations in calm times, the dealer model needs to be extended to reproduce abnormal price fluctuations d
content: Although the dealer model developed in the field of econophysics has been able to reproduce the characteristics of financial market fluctuations in calm times, the dealer model needs to be extended to reproduce abnormal price fluctuations during government intervention in the foreign exchange market. In this study, we first analysed real foreign exchange market data during the Bank of Japan’s interventions in 2011 and 2022, and report that the intervention strategies were very different in each case. Next, we introduced the concept of volume into this model and further modified and formulated the effects of stop-loss and take-profit, as well as modified the intervention dealer’s strategy to reproduce the market price fluctuations during these interventions. In order to assimilate the abnormal markets, we applied a trend decomposition technique to divide the price movements into upward and downward trends, assuming that the parameters of the dealer model were the same in each trend. The best parameters were searched for, so that the differences between the simulated price changes and the real ones became the smallest. This allowed us to estimate how the intervening dealer would have behaved in each intervention and how the other dealers in the market would have reacted.

title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
summary: Abstract Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors
content: Abstract Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum X Y model and the interacting disordered X X Z chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.

title: Neural Estimation of Crystallographic Orientation from Rotating-Substrate RHEED with Limited Training Data: Application to CdTe Thin Films
summary: We introduce a data-efficient neural-vision method to estimate the crystallographic orientation of a rotating substrate from reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) patterns during molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) growth. We combine
content: We introduce a data-efficient neural-vision method to estimate the crystallographic orientation of a rotating substrate from reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) patterns during molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) growth. We combine single-frame azimuth predictions of a neural network with the known rotation kinematics in a physics-aware postprocessing step. This step detects the rotation direction and recovers a robust reference azimuth, replacing manual frame-by-frame inspection. Trained on RHEED patterns from only 15 independently grown CdTe samples, the model infers the crystallographic directions to within the 0.5° target for 95% of rotations. Under leave-one-structure-out evaluation on all 20 samples, the mean error is 0.18°. High accuracy stems from the postprocessing rather than from the network architecture. A 2D ResNet reaches the accuracy of a 3D ResNet benchmark trained on the same number of samples at approximately one tenth of the training cost. Our work delivers (i) a physics-constrained estimation procedure for rotating-substrate RHEED, applicable to any azimuth regressor that is unbiased over a rotation, (ii) an analysis of why few independently grown samples suffice, and (iii) a trained system validated for online orientation estimation during CdTe growth.

title: Fairness Theatre: Evaluating Post-Hoc Fairness Interventions in Vendor-Controlled Early Warning Systems
source: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
summary: Public institutions increasingly procure AI systems whose design they cannot inspect or change. In higher education, proprietary Early Warning Systems (EWS) leave colleges with few options beyond adjusting model outputs to address inequity.
content: Public institutions increasingly procure AI systems whose design they cannot inspect or change. In higher education, proprietary Early Warning Systems (EWS) leave colleges with few options beyond adjusting model outputs to address inequity. This raises a CSCW question: how is fairness work coordinated among vendors, institutions, advisors, and students with unequal power to change these systems? Using student records from a public college in Ontario, Canada, we evaluate six post-hoc fairness interventions on a research EWS under simulated procurement constraints. We compare fairness, accuracy, and demographic disparities, introducing error-type profiling to trace how interventions redistribute false positives and false negatives. Interventions redistributed disparities without consistently reducing them. Two implementations favoured already-advantaged groups because they used group size to define disadvantage; small, marginalized groups remained poorly served. These findings show how procurement constraints and implementation choices shape the possibilities for fairness work. We call the resulting condition fairness theatre : dashboard metrics converge while groups’ error burdens persist or worsen.

title: The cost of personalization: campaign finance and women's representation in Turkey's closed list system
summary: The increasing personalization of election campaigns shifts the campaign activity and its financing away from parties and onto individual candidates. This paper identifies a critical contradiction in Turkish party law—the candidate-finance
content: The increasing personalization of election campaigns shifts the campaign activity and its financing away from parties and onto individual candidates. This paper identifies a critical contradiction in Turkish party law—the candidate-finance gap—in which the campaign finance of political parties is heavily regulated while private contributions to individual candidates go entirely unaddressed, creating a gray zone. Drawing on a novel post-election survey of 2023 parliamentary candidates, campaign ethnographies and in-depth interviews, we show that candidates run intensive personal campaigns including canvasing, district presence and candidate-branded materials even under Turkey's closed list system. We argue these campaigns are financed in two layers: parties fund the collective campaign (rallies, generic materials and district programs), while the personalized layer is financed privately and outside any regulatory framework. Party money finances the layer the law recognizes; the personalized layer the law ignores relies on private means, where inequality emerges. Because access to private means is unequal, this gap has gendered consequences: women cluster in minimal-budget campaigns and rely on their own resources, while men spend significantly more and draw more on private networks, with implications for who can afford to run.

title: ClimInvestBench: Evaluating Agentic Investment Report Generation and Maintenance
summary: Generated analytical reports can inform financial decisions, so evaluation must check numerical correctness and evidential support as well as content coverage.Existing report benchmarks provide reference reports or grading criteria, but off
content: Generated analytical reports can inform financial decisions, so evaluation must check numerical correctness and evidential support as well as content coverage.Existing report benchmarks provide reference reports or grading criteria, but offer limited support for automatically revising expected calculations and written content when evidence is withheld or updated.Testing generation, missing inputs, and maintenance under the same reporting requirements therefore requires additional reference construction.To address this gap, we define a novel framework for evaluating the quality of structured report generation based on reusable reporting specifications that link structured evidence to required calculations and report content.Pairing a specification with different evidence conditions automatically generates both task instructions and evaluation targets, including unavailable results, revised values, and content to preserve.An automatic test suite combines deterministic checks of structure, tables, numerical results, and citations with LLM judgments of prose coverage and citation support.Using the framework, we build a benchmark, ClimInvestBench, for evaluating the generation of bankability reports for climate mitigation projects.Our benchmark comprises 220 tasks for 20 climatefinance projects across full-evidence generation, missing-evidence generation, and report maintenance.Under this benchmark, we compare six LLMs using whole-report and section-based generation.The experiments show that high structural compliance and content coverage can coexist with numerical errors and gaps in evidential support.Section-based generation uses more recorded response time overall, but its quality benefits depend on the model and task.Specification reuse limits repeated manual preparation, while the set of separate measures expose reporting failures that a single overall score can obscure.These unknown failure modes are of particular concern where the output, as in financial report creation, contributes to high-stakes decision making.

title: Forecasting the future of postal services in Libya until 2030: a strategic analysis of the performance of Libya Post Company in the light of global Directions of the Universal Postal Union
source: مجلة النهضة العلمية بالجامعة المفتوحة سبها
summary: يبحث هذا البحث مستقبل الخدمات البريدية في ليبيا حتى عام 2030 من خلال تحليل متطلبات الاتحاد البريدي العالمي وتوجهاته الاستراتيجية وتقييم آثارها على شركة بريد ليبيا. ويركز على التحول من المراسلات التقليدية إلى تسليم الطرود والخدمات اللوجستية
content: يبحث هذا البحث مستقبل الخدمات البريدية في ليبيا حتى عام 2030 من خلال تحليل متطلبات الاتحاد البريدي العالمي وتوجهاته الاستراتيجية وتقييم آثارها على شركة بريد ليبيا. ويركز على التحول من المراسلات التقليدية إلى تسليم الطرود والخدمات اللوجستية والتجارة الإلكترونية والخدمات المتكاملة رقميا ، إلى جانب المتطلبات المتزايدة لجودة الخدمة والكفاءة التشغيلية والاستدامة وأمن المعلومات. يعتمد البحث نهجا وصفيا تحليليا يستند إلى المؤلفات العلمية الحديثة والتقارير الدولية والوثائق الاستراتيجية للاتحاد البريدي العالمي والمعلومات المتاحة عن شركة بريد ليبيا لتحديد مجالات التوافق الاستراتيجي والفجوات بين قدراتها المنشورة والمتطلبات القطاعية الناشئة. ويشير التحليل إلى أن تطوير الخدمات البريدية في ليبيا يعتمد على تنويع الأنشطة المدرة للدخل ، ودمج المنصات الرقمية مع عمليات الطرود والخدمات اللوجستية ، وتعزيز البنية التحتية التكنولوجية والقدرات البشرية. ويخلص التقرير أيضا إلى أن المواءمة مع متطلبات الاتحاد البريدي العالمي تتطلب ترجمة الالتزامات والتوجهات الاستراتيجية ذات الصلة إلى أهداف قابلة للقياس وبرامج تنفيذ ومؤشرات أداء. تم تحديد ثلاثة سيناريوهات مستقبلية: الاستمرارية المحدودة ، والتحول التدريجي ، والخدمات البريدية الذكية المتكاملة. وعلى الرغم من أن السيناريو الثالث يوفر أقوى مواءمة مع التطورات القطاعية الدولية ، فإن التحول التدريجي يمثل المسار الأكثر جدوى نحو تحقيقه. يوصي البحث باتباع نهج استراتيجي مرحلي لشركة بريد ليبيا ، مع إعطاء الأولوية للرقمنة والخدمات اللوجستية والطرود ، وتكامل التجارة الإلكترونية ، وتنمية القوى العاملة ، والشراكات المؤسسية. وينبغي تقييم التقدم المحرز من خلال مؤشرات أداء قابلة للقياس مرتبطة بأهداف محددة لعام 2030.

title: How do incentive and penalty mechanisms enhance the credibility of blue carbon credit markets? A game-theoretic analysis of multi-stakeholder collaborative governance strategies
summary: Introduction Protecting and restoring blue carbon ecosystems is an important nature-based solution for mitigating global warming and promoting sustainable coastal development. As blue carbon projects enter carbon markets, credit credibility
