summary: The excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance is fundamental for proper neural circuit function, and its disruption has emerged as a convergent mechanism across multiple psychiatric disorders. Primarily, GABAergic inhibitory neurons play essentia
content: The excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance is fundamental for proper neural circuit function, and its disruption has emerged as a convergent mechanism across multiple psychiatric disorders. Primarily, GABAergic inhibitory neurons play essential roles in regulating network dynamics, necessary for physiological, cognitive and emotional processing. This review synthesizes current evidence from genetic, epigenetic, transcriptomic, and cellular studies implicating GABAergic neuron dysfunction in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), major depressive disorder (MDD), schizophrenia (SCZ), and bipolar disorder (BD). We first define the E/I balance and its functional implications for neural circuit dynamics and define the main GABAergic subtypes: Parvalbumin (PVALB), Somatostatin (SST), Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide neurons (VIP) and Lysosomal Associated Membrane Protein Family Member 5/Paired Box 6 positive GABAergic neurons (LAMP5/PAX6+). We then examine GABAergic involvement across distinct neurodevelopmental phases, highlighting critical windows of vulnerability where perturbations can produce lasting consequences. Subsequently, we synthesize and discuss disorder-specific evidence across ASD, MDD, SCZ, and BD, which share substantial clinical overlap and converging genetic architectures. High-resolution single-cell and spatial transcriptomic approaches have fundamentally transformed our understanding, revealing that rather than a uniform global deficit, these conditions exhibit localized, cell-type-specific dysregulations that target distinct interneuron subpopulations in a region- and disorder-dependent manner. Methodological advances now enable integration of genomic risk with cell-type-specific transcriptomic and epigenomic profiles, though challenges remain in translating these findings to clinical applications. Despite promising preclinical evidence, clinical trials targeting GABAergic signaling have yielded mixed results, underscoring the complexity of inhibitory circuit dysfunction and the need for more precise, subtype-specific therapeutic strategies. Leveraging these high-resolution, multi-omic insights holds significant promise for refining psychiatric nosology, discovering reliable biomarkers, and advancing targeted therapeutics and personalized medicine.

title: The Silent Leadership Algorithm: AI as a Strategic Partner for Sustained Growth
summary: The Silent Leadership Algorithm is an essential guide for executives and managers confronting the realities of AI integration in today’s fast-moving business environment. Rather than framing AI as a technical challenge alone, this book show
content: The Silent Leadership Algorithm is an essential guide for executives and managers confronting the realities of AI integration in today’s fast-moving business environment. Rather than framing AI as a technical challenge alone, this book shows leaders how to translate complex decisions into clear, human-centered strategy. Through the powerful WHO–HOW–WHAT–WHY framework, readers learn how to pair AI’s speed, scale, and predictive capabilities with the judgment, restraint, and emotional intelligence required to lead effectively across global, culturally diverse teams. Designed with both senior leaders and operational managers in mind, the book provides practical value at every level of the organization. It demonstrates how to leverage AI to enhance decision quality, identify high-potential talent, reduce bias, and strengthen cross-border coordination while maintaining trust and legitimacy with employees and stakeholders. By integrating micro-level leadership skills such as reflective listening and emotional regulation with macro-level applications such as supply chain optimization and strategic alignment, the authors provide a clear roadmap for turning AI adoption into measurable performance gains rather than organizational friction. At a time when many leaders struggle to balance technological acceleration with human expectations, The Silent Leadership Algorithm offers a distinct competitive advantage: a model for leading quietly yet decisively. It equips executives to move beyond reactive, technology-driven decisions and instead build resilient, purpose-driven organizations where AI enhances but does not replace human insight. For leaders seeking to navigate AI transformation with confidence, precision, and credibility, this book provides both the mindset and the methods to achieve sustained growth.

title: Promotion incentives for local officials and high quality urban economic development
source: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies
summary: Promotion incentives influence local policy choices, but their relationship with multidimensional urban development remains insufficiently understood. Using 3,552 city-year observations for 296 Chinese cities during 2012-2023, this study co
content: Promotion incentives influence local policy choices, but their relationship with multidimensional urban development remains insufficiently understood. Using 3,552 city-year observations for 296 Chinese cities during 2012-2023, this study constructs a promotion incentive index from relative growth, fiscal surplus, and employment performance. High-quality development is measured across innovation, coordination, openness, green development, and shared development. Two-way fixed-effects estimates yield a positive coefficient of 0.0705, significant at the 1% level. This association persists under alternative outcome measures, samples, and controls. Government policy attention, firm entry, and factor allocation efficiency are positively associated with promotion incentives, consistent with the proposed channels. Positive estimates also appear across regional and temporal subsamples and all five development dimensions. City-level wild bootstrap tests support two development thresholds, with the incremental second-threshold test significant at 5%. The incentive coefficients decline from 0.0979 to 0.0676 and 0.0461 across increasing income regimes. These findings indicate that the relationship between promotion incentives and urban development quality varies with cities' economic development levels.

title: Co-developing a human wellbeing-centered, socio-economic framework for small-scale fisheries: The Bahamas’ Nassau grouper fishery as a case study
summary: Most fisheries assessments focus on stock status and economic output but say little about the lived experiences of fishing communities, the cultural value of fisheries, or the governance conditions that decide whether regulations work. Guid
content: Most fisheries assessments focus on stock status and economic output but say little about the lived experiences of fishing communities, the cultural value of fisheries, or the governance conditions that decide whether regulations work. Guidance for broader socio-economic monitoring exists, but no single set of indicators fits every fishery; it has to be worked out in context, with the people whose wellbeing is being measured. Less is known about how this is done in practice. We describe, step by step, how general monitoring guidance was adapted with stakeholders into a wellbeing-centered, socio-economic framework for The Bahamas’ domestic fisheries, using the critically endangered Nassau grouper ( Epinephelus striatus ) as a case study. Twenty-eight participants from government, non-governmental organizations, research, and the value chain took part through meetings, surveys, a hybrid workshop, and interviews. Together they defined the scope, confirmed six wellbeing domains and prioritized 6 research themes. The resulting framework (Framework V01) contains 59 indicators across 20 attributes, including indicators of readiness for a prospective national seafood labeling program. We report the criteria used to select attributes and indicators and the minimum standards set for inclusive participation. T Participation was uneven, which shaped the framework and is discussed as a limitation. Framework V01 has not yet been tested in the field. Its content is specific to The Bahamas, but the documented process, including its compromises, offers a practical reference for others adapting wellbeing monitoring to their own fisheries.

title: BIABooster-based characterization of the cell-free DNA fragmentome in healthy adult blood donors reveals stable reference profiles and pre-analytical influences
summary: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a versatile biomarker in oncology, prenatal testing, and organ transplantation. Although cfDNA concentration and genomic markers are widely used, its fragment size distribution (fragmentome) offers addit
content: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a versatile biomarker in oncology, prenatal testing, and organ transplantation. Although cfDNA concentration and genomic markers are widely used, its fragment size distribution (fragmentome) offers additional diagnostic potential. However, robust reference profiles for healthy individuals—particularly for fragments exceeding 300 bp—remain lacking. We used the BIABooster system to analyse cfDNA from 240 healthy adult blood donors, collected in two French cities of different climate at four different time points over a one-year period. cfDNA concentration and size distribution up to 1650 bp were measured and synthesised in 10 concentration and size descriptors. Potential correlations with demographic and haematological parameters were assessed. For selected samples, cfDNA was also analysed up to 10 kb, and the impact of an end-repair step was investigated. cfDNA size profiles were highly consistent across collection sites and time points and were not significantly affected by the demographic and haematological parameters investigated. In particular, the relative abundances of mono- and di-nucleosomal cfDNA fractions were remarkably stable across individuals. Analysis of longer cfDNA fragments revealed an unexpected peak around 3.2 kb that appeared to depend on pre-analytical conditions. This study establishes a detailed characterisation cfDNA fragmentation profiles in healthy adult blood donors and highlights their limited variability across geographic, temporal, demographic and common haematological parameters. It also demonstrates that pre-analytical conditions, particularly blood collection procedures, can influence specific fragmentome features and should therefore be carefully considered when developing cfDNA size profiling for clinical applications.

title: Decoupling Contamination Detection from Classification Accuracy: A Confidence-based Triage Framework with Explainable AI for Water Quality Monitoring
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Binary classification is the standard approach in machine learning-based water quality monitoring, but its false negative rates remain a practical concern-contaminated samples misclassified as safe go undetected.This study applies selective
content: Binary classification is the standard approach in machine learning-based water quality monitoring, but its false negative rates remain a practical concern-contaminated samples misclassified as safe go undetected.This study applies selective prediction to water potability screening and characterises the resulting Accuracy-Safety Decoupling, demonstrating that contamination detection can be substantially improved independently of overall classification accuracy through a confidence-based triage framework.Rather than relying on binary decision boundaries, the framework sorts predictions into safe, uncertain, and contaminated zones using dual probability thresholds, directing uncertain cases to human review instead of automatic clearance.A Random Forest classifier was trained on 46 features engineered from 15 physicochemical parameters in a synthetic water quality dataset of 2,500 samples generated under controlled conditions to isolate framework performance from dataset-specific artifacts.The model achieved 79.2% accuracy and 86.79% ROC-AUC.The triage system raised the contamination capture rate from 75.21% to 98.3%, a triage-level measure of samples not auto-cleared as safe, an improvement confirmed by McNemar's test (χ² = 26.04,p < 0.0001), A paired risk difference of 23.14 percentage points (95% CI [15.63, 30.65]), and non-overlapping bootstrap confidence intervals.SHAP and LIME analysis showed moderate-to-strong agreement (Spearman ρ = 0.608), with chloramines, turbidity, and pH emerging as the top predictive factors.The dataset was generated under a documented parametric specification with an explicit rule-based labelling function, establishing a controlled methodological baseline against which future real-world deployments can be benchmarked.

title: AGILE У ВІДНОВЛЕННІ АРХІТЕКТУРИ УКРАЇНСЬКИХ МІСТ: ГІБРИДНА МОДЕЛЬ АДАПТИВНОГО ПУБЛІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ
summary: AGILE У ВІДНОВЛЕННІ АРХІТЕКТУРИ УКРАЇНСЬКИХ МІСТ: ГІБРИДНА МОДЕЛЬ АДАПТИВНОГО ПУБЛІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ Анотація.В статті обґрунтувати можливості перенесення цінностей і практик Agile з ІТ-середовища на відновлення архітектури українських міст
content: AGILE У ВІДНОВЛЕННІ АРХІТЕКТУРИ УКРАЇНСЬКИХ МІСТ: ГІБРИДНА МОДЕЛЬ АДАПТИВНОГО ПУБЛІЧНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ Анотація.В статті обґрунтувати можливості перенесення цінностей і практик Agile з ІТ-середовища на відновлення архітектури українських міст та запропонувати гібридну управлінську модель, придатну для органів місцевого самоврядування, служб відновлення й територіальних громад в умовах триваючої воєнної невизначеності.Застосовано системний і порівняльний аналіз, контент-аналіз програмних і аналітичних документів (RDNA5, матеріали URC 2026, посібник KSE зі відновлення, дані системи DREAM), кейс-метод (Scrum на об'єкті в Бородянці; тактичний урбанізм Києва, Львова, Харкова; проєкт TORV) та узагальнення практик адаптивного публічного управління.Визначено, що класична каскадна модель «повний проєктпотім будівництво» втрачає дієвість там, де змінюються безпекові вимоги, демографія, донорські стандарти та фізичний стан кварталів.Обґрунтовано відповідність чотирьох цінностей Agile-маніфесту логіці відбудови.Описано чотири робочі інструменти: incremental urbanism, tactical urbanism, Scrum на окремому об'єкті та гібрид Waterfall + Scrum/Kanban на рівні портфеля громади.Запропоновано каркас із чотирьох епіків відновлення та роль органу публічної влади як власника єдиного product backlog громади.Зроблено висновки про те, що Agile не скасовує стратегію «build back better», зелене відновлення й євроінтеграцію, а змінює спосіб руху до нихчерез портфель коротких інкрементів.Реалістичний горизонт 2026-2028 рр.полягає не в скасуванні нормативної каскадності, а в узаконенні гібриду: експертиза чергами, прийняття інкрементів, тимчасові споруди як офіційна стадія, участь мешканців як user research кожного спринту.

title: Trends in the intervals between and distribution of diagnostic dental visits among adults in Denmark
summary: Before 1999, the recommended dental recall interval for adults in Denmark was 6-7 months. In 1999 and in 2013-2015, two major regulations were made aiming to increase this interval. This study analyzes the use of dental examination services
content: Before 1999, the recommended dental recall interval for adults in Denmark was 6-7 months. In 1999 and in 2013-2015, two major regulations were made aiming to increase this interval. This study analyzes the use of dental examination services for adults in Denmark over the 32-yr period from 1990 to 2021 using national registry data comprising information on 6,894,773 persons (133,811,495 person-years). Overall, 24% of the adult population did not receive a subsidized dental examination during the entire follow-up period, whereas 69% (n = 4,774,716) had at least two registered dental examinations. Median examination intervals increased slightly before 2013, increasing by about 3 months in the period 2013-2015 to 11 months, whereafter they remained stable. Examination intervals increased among 20-59-yr-olds but remained stable for older ages. Lower income, lower education, and immigrant or descendant status were associated with no dental examinations or longer examination intervals. Our analyses show that dental practices compensated for the 1999 restriction on standard examination intervals by use of control examination services, and the 2013-2015 risk-based interval reform was counteracted by increasing use of preventive and supragingival scaling services. Our findings support the notion that dentists working in a fee-for-service system have and exercise market power.

title: Prioritizing the Conservation of Pondok Pesantren as Cultural and Religious Heritage
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: The conservation of Pondok Pesantren as a cultural and religious heritage considers user perception to evaluate the technical aspects. Many building studies are based on technical aspects and rarely involve user perception. Pondok Pesantren
content: The conservation of Pondok Pesantren as a cultural and religious heritage considers user perception to evaluate the technical aspects. Many building studies are based on technical aspects and rarely involve user perception. Pondok Pesantren as an Islamic religious, educational institution was developed by a social and multicultural approach. The results of this study are used to develop maintenance and conservation priorities that benefit in the development of educational institutions, cultural preservation, economic and investment improvement, the application of sustainable buildings, and the development of educational and religious tourism.This research determines the priority of conservation and maintenance efforts at Pondok Pesantren heritage. The priority is determined by analyzing the level of influence and optimisation of building performance factors by implementing green building principles. The method used is multiple linear regression and optimisation by using dynamic programming. Research data is the perception of user consisting of residents and visitors. Residents of Pondok Pesantren include teachers and students.The priority of improving the performance includes: Security protection for residents and visitors; Free from dangerous materials and devices; Function of natural lighting; Aesthetics of park, landscape, and vegetation; Ease of indoor and outdoor circulation horizontally; Performance and reliability of roof structures; Durability of dormitory buildings; Regularity in buildings arrangement; Availability of information and communication facilities for visitors; and Alternative energy from wind sources or Environmental drainage and utility systems.

title: Everyday treasures: Applying product personalities to design user–product relationships
summary: This research applies Transactional Analysis, a theory of interpersonal relationships, to identify people's relationships with emotionally attached and frequently used objects in their daily routines. Through two complementary studies, it i
content: This research applies Transactional Analysis, a theory of interpersonal relationships, to identify people's relationships with emotionally attached and frequently used objects in their daily routines. Through two complementary studies, it investigates both the nature of these attachments and their implications for design. In Study 1, thirty semi-structured interviews invited participants to present their favourite objects, explain the reasons for their attachment, and rate the objects' perceived personality attributes and the emotions they evoke. The findings reveal that attachment to everyday objects is primarily driven by functional aspects and the services they facilitate, rather than aesthetic or symbolic aspects. These “everyday treasures” were most often associated with Adult and Nurturing Parent personalities, along with positive-passive and positive-active emotions. Building on these insights, a conceptual framework was developed to guide designers in creating emotionally resonant products. Study 2 involves a focus group workshop where eight design professionals validated the applicability of the framework in the design process, as a tool for evaluating existing products, generating concepts, and testing outcomes. Together, the studies demonstrate how Transactional Analysis can inform design practice by supporting the creation of products that develop meaningful emotional connections with users. • Explores emotional attachment to frequently used everyday products. • Identifies function and facilitation as key drivers of product attachment. • Shows that users favour products associated with Adult and Nurturing Parent personalities. • Proposes a Transactional Analysis-based framework for emotional user–product relationship design. • Demonstrates the applicability of the framework within design processes.

title: Theological or pedagogic recontextualisation? The Anglican religious education curriculum in Hong Kong
summary: Contemporary schooling is increasingly charged with cultivating wellbeing, citizenship, resilience, and moral responsibility, yet questions of suffering, meaning, hope, and flourishing remain difficult to articulate within the dominant lang
content: Contemporary schooling is increasingly charged with cultivating wellbeing, citizenship, resilience, and moral responsibility, yet questions of suffering, meaning, hope, and flourishing remain difficult to articulate within the dominant languages of secular pedagogy. In Hong Kong, a common state-sponsored social education subject shares a timetable with church-sponsored religious education. Revisiting Bernstein and Wexler, this article compares junior secondary curriculum materials for Citizenship, Economics and Society (CES) and Anglican Religious Education (RE). We argue that the two subjects rest on different principles of recontextualisation, and with them, different pedagogic discourses and anthropologies. CES recontextualises psychology, sociology, and financial literacy through the languages of self-management, responsibility, and adaptation. Anglican RE draws on much the same disciplinary knowledge but relates it to dignity, desire, neighbourliness, vocation, and hope. Shared concerns such as identity, consumption, and life purpose are organised through different codes of meaning, each making some questions thinkable and leaving others aside. Our purpose is analytic: we do not claim that either curriculum is superior. We suggest instead that theology in Anglican RE works less as subject content than as a meta-discourse through which existential questions become educationally intelligible, pointing to an existential dimension of powerful knowledge still undeveloped in curriculum debates.

title: The Impact of Credit Risk Management on the Profitability of Commercial Banks in China
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Banking institutions' credit risk management policies is having a dramatic effect on their financial performance, particularly in the upcoming markets in various markets in China. In China, the credit growth rates, and shifting regulations,
content: Banking institutions' credit risk management policies is having a dramatic effect on their financial performance, particularly in the upcoming markets in various markets in China. In China, the credit growth rates, and shifting regulations, have affected the way financial institutions act and behave. Concurrently, the primary aim for this research is to explore "the impact of credit risk management on the profitability of commercial banks in the Chinese banking sector" by using two key variables of "Non-performing Loans and Loan Loss Provisions to measure" the credit risk exposure that the banks face. Secondary data and regression analysis are applied in order to analyze the impact that these indicators have on "Return on Assets and Return on Equity" followed by comparative assessment. The crucial poor relationship between HNRs and profitability (due to effects on net interest income and provisioning) can be seen from the results. The requirements to provide for loans that could be lost also prevent short-term profitability since it siphons money away from productive lending operations. The discussion entails the essential risk profile differences portrayed in the bigger banks owned by the government and the commercial banks found in the smaller cities, that the former had smaller capital buffers, and fewer advanced risk governance processes, exposing them to greater risk of deteriorating credit. The findings have significant policy, banking management, and banking regulatory implications for China to make its banking system more resilient and profitable. The paper also offers critical recommendations for future research at the end.

title: Challenges and Dynamics of Garo Political Representation in Union Parishad Elections in Bangladesh
summary: Abstract What triggers the Garos’ electoral representation in Union Parishad elections in Bangladesh, particularly in partisan systems after 2015? This article explores the dynamics of barriers influencing electoral participation and the no
content: Abstract What triggers the Garos’ electoral representation in Union Parishad elections in Bangladesh, particularly in partisan systems after 2015? This article explores the dynamics of barriers influencing electoral participation and the nomination strategy in local Union Parishad elections, using a mixed-methods design that incorporates survey and interview data, supplemented by semi-structured interviews, candidate election records, and official election results. Theoretically, this study draws on social inclusion theory, emphasizing the social closure and monopoly paradigm of exclusion as the key drivers shaping the Garos' participation in the electoral transition. The findings demonstrate that economic deterrents, gendered gaps, and regulated political information, as well as institutional and network barriers, are identified as the intersection associated with Garo’s political representation. The findings also show that the partisan local governance competition resulted in the expanded use of party nominations, campaign financing, party political connections, and party patronage, even though the Garos remain underrepresented. Moreover, the electoral advantage is unequal, as the marginalized community faces greater challenges in the new local governance system. By unpacking these processes, this paper contributes to the literature on democratic participation, inclusive local governance, and minority rights, offering a nuanced understanding demonstrating cross-ethnic trust beyond ethnic boundaries.

title: The Nuclear Factory as a Regenerative Paradigm of Industrial Abandonment
summary: An analysis of contemporary cities' satellite images reveals large industrial agglomerations within and near urban centers.The traditional industrial antinomy between operational structures and abandoned sites has led to the clear separatio
content: An analysis of contemporary cities' satellite images reveals large industrial agglomerations within and near urban centers.The traditional industrial antinomy between operational structures and abandoned sites has led to the clear separation between productive functionality and urban "waste".The current climate emergency necessitates an evaluation of this active-passive distinction as a potentially high-risk factor, while also presenting a strategic opportunity for reconfiguring industrial heritage.From this second scenario, the research analyses a borderline case of this possibility within the panorama of industrial heritage: nuclear power plants.From this perspective, nuclear factories are plants that incorporate the principle of planned obsolescence from the outset, necessitating an inherently circular design and meticulous end-of-life planning.The highly significant environmental and infrastructural impact of the plants, combined with the inherent dangers of the sector, prevents their uncontrolled abandonment, which is widespread and marginally controlled by other types of production.Through a comparative analysis, the research identifies case studies of practical application of these strategies to outline best practices and replicable design models.Examples such as those of the Yankee Rowe NPP (USA) and the HDR Großwelzheim NPP (Germany) emerge as representative of post-production environmental recovery processes -"greenfield" regeneration -while cases as the NPP of Fort St. Vrain and Rancho Seco 1 (USA), are exemplary for the post-production reconversion project, where power plants continued to maintain their energy production function trough different technologies.The analysis of the mandatory post-operational planning applied to this architectural typology demonstrates the possibilities of transforming the fate of abandoned factories, even in the case of highly complex industries.These strategies applied to nuclear power plants suggest a project replicability oriented towards the circular management of industrial space, excluding the possibility of abandonment.Introduction.The analysis of contemporary cities reveals the presence of post-industrial reminiscences not only within their urban spaces, but also in their surroundings.The causes that led to industrial abandonment are well documented in the literature, from the oil crisis of the 1970s, the expulsion of factories from the city center to the outskirts, the relocation of production to emerging and more economical markets, to the reduction in demand for goods due to the economic crises of recent years (Aymonino, 1975;Spanedda, 2023; van Neuss, 2018).

title: Re-Centering the Great Acceleration: Fossil Developmentalism in India (An interview with Elizabeth Chatterjee, September 19, 2024)
summary: In articles like "The Asian Anthropocene," you've pushed back against an entrenched narrative describing the rise of what historians have come to call "fossil capitalism."Could you give us a sense of this narrative?Elizabeth Chatterjee: The
content: In articles like "The Asian Anthropocene," you've pushed back against an entrenched narrative describing the rise of what historians have come to call "fossil capitalism."Could you give us a sense of this narrative?Elizabeth Chatterjee: The idea of fossil capitalism is most associated with the human ecologist Andreas Malm, in his 2016 book Fossil Capital.It's useful to realize what Malm is reacting against-that is, the idea of the Anthropocene as coined by climate scientists, referring to our pre sent so-called new epoch in which humans have become the most impor tant disruptor of the Earth system.At the heart of the Anthropocene is the figure of the Anthropos, an undifferentiated human species.And Malm said, "This is not right.First, what does it mean to think of the human species as an agent?It's never active on the historical stage.Second, clearly this masks all sorts of inequalities of class, of nation, and so on."I have a lot of sympathy with that critique.Instead, Malm said, we need to look for the origins of the climate crisis in fossil capitalism, which he traced back to the first Industrial Revolution in Britain, and the takeoff of the steam engine fueled by coal.This is the core of every thing terrible that happens afterward.Previous scholarship had read the takeoff of coal as a product of economics, the scarcity of wood and the relative cheapness of coal.Malm said, "No, that's completely wrong.It really lies in the exercise of class power."He argues that coal and the steam engine took off because British industrial cap i tal ists de cided it was in their interests.They could have continued to use waterpower, which was cheaper than early steam engines, but waterpower is spatially fixed, and therefore gave a lot of latitude to workers to revolt.Steam was spatially mobile.It could defy the seasons, and it enabled cap i tal ists to locate factories in cities where there were large potential workforces so they could pick and choose who

title: Financial Recording First: An Initial Integrated Model for Strengthening Agribusiness MSME Performance in North Jember, Indonesia
source: Journal of Islamic Finance and Economic Studies
summary: Background: Rural agribusiness MSME assistance often addresses financial recording, production efficiency, and digital marketing in separate activities, although enterprises must coordinate these practices under severe resource constraints.
content: Background: Rural agribusiness MSME assistance often addresses financial recording, production efficiency, and digital marketing in separate activities, although enterprises must coordinate these practices under severe resource constraints. Aims: This study identifies configurations of these three conditions associated with high and low enterprise performance and uses the findings to construct an initial assistance model. Methods: Twenty-eight purposively selected enterprises across five subdistricts of North Jember were assessed using a 15-indicator rubric and four performance items. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) examined necessary conditions and sufficient configurations. Nine experts and practitioners assessed twelve proposed model components using Lawshe’s content validity ratio (CVR). Results: Financial recording narrowly met the high-performance necessity threshold (consistency = 0.901); this judgment was sensitive to recalibration. The primary high-performance configuration combined financial recording as a core condition and production efficiency as a peripheral condition (consistency = 0.901; coverage = 0.856). Digital marketing was absent from that solution, but its apparent dispensability depended on borderline cases. Weak financial recording occurred in both low-performance solutions. Following review and revision, ten components were retained or integrated into the model. Conclusion: The evidence supports an initial, financially grounded sequence for enterprise assistance, not a demonstrated intervention effect. Pilot implementation is needed to evaluate whether this proposed sequence improves subsequent performance.

title: The sound of persuasion: Using generative AI to identify gender gaps in political influence
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: Women often experience a deficit in persuasive influence, particularly in contexts like politics, where expectations about women's behavior may conflict with gendered expectations about the domain and role. In spite of this widespread patte
content: Women often experience a deficit in persuasive influence, particularly in contexts like politics, where expectations about women's behavior may conflict with gendered expectations about the domain and role. In spite of this widespread pattern, the mechanisms behind the gender gap in persuasion are difficult to isolate and test in dynamic political conversations. Women may be less persuasive simply because role-based expectations prompt others to afford women less authority when speaking about politics generally or about some political topics. Alternatively, women may be less persuasive because they tend to use linguistic patterns or rhetorical strategies that are less effective. Using an original AI-based approach, we put 4,300 human subjects into realistic, real-time phone conversations with an AI agent. These agents were randomly assigned either a masculine or feminine gendered conversation topic and a male- or female-sounding voice, allowing us to manipulate topic and perceptions of speakers' gender while holding constant other elements of rhetorical content and strategy. After validating the experimental treatments, we find no direct effects of perceived gender of the AI agent, as cued by voice. However, gender affects other important aspects of the persuasive interaction. Research subjects were more likely to be persuaded about the masculine topic (defense spending) than the feminine topic (aid to the poor). Additionally, women research subjects were, on average, more persuaded than men. To the extent that men and women emphasize different topics in political conversations and have different discussion partners, these dynamics are likely to shape women's political persuasive influence.

title: Integrative evidence supports the recognition of a new endangered species of Croton (Euphorbiaceae) from Brazilian restinga
summary: Abstract Croton maci (Euphorbiaceae) is described herein as a new species endemic to the restinga ecosystems of Northeastern Brazil. Its phylogenetic position, inferred from ITS (nrDNA) data, supports its placement in Croton sect. Barhamia
content: Abstract Croton maci (Euphorbiaceae) is described herein as a new species endemic to the restinga ecosystems of Northeastern Brazil. Its phylogenetic position, inferred from ITS (nrDNA) data, supports its placement in Croton sect. Barhamia subsect. Sellowiorum and indicates a close relationship with C. sellowii . This placement is further supported by its laciniate-glandular stipules and the absence of acropetiolar glands. The new species shares with C. sellowii a shrubby habit, glandular stipules, eglandular leaf blades, pistillate flowers with reduplicate-valvate sepals and tetrafid styles. However, it differs by having stellate or sublepidote trichomes, slightly serrate margins in senescent leaves, a pubescent abaxial leaf surface, and slightly oblanceolate pistillate sepals with irregularly serrate margins. Distribution maps, images, and leaf anatomical data are also provided to contrast the new species with its closest relative. Based on its restricted distribution in the Brazilian states of Alagoas and Sergipe, C. maci is preliminarily assessed as endangered (EN) following the IUCN criterion B2ab(iii).

title: DTW-RL: Adaptive Routing Evaluation Interval Algorithm for Stable and Reliable RPL in Mobile IoT Networks
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Routing stability remains a critical challenge in the IPv6 Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL), particularly in dynamic Internet of Things (IoT) environments characterized by mobility, fluctuating link qualities, and fre
content: Routing stability remains a critical challenge in the IPv6 Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL), particularly in dynamic Internet of Things (IoT) environments characterized by mobility, fluctuating link qualities, and frequent topology changes.Although multi-metric routing approaches have improved parent selection decisions, most existing schemes continue to perform routing evaluations at fixed intervals, which may introduce unnecessary overhead during stable periods or delay their adaptation under dynamic conditions.This study presents and evaluates a complete DTW-RL configuration that integrates MMDEW based parent selection with adaptive routing evaluation interval control through an algorithmically compact linear Q-learning mechanism.The algorithm was implemented in Contiki-NG and evaluated using the Cooja simulator under mobility scenarios involving two to five mobile nodes.Performance was compared against the Minimum Rank with Hysteresis Objective Function (MRHOF) and MMDEW using Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), handover count (HO), End-to-End Delay, and Energy Consumption metrics.The experimental results indicate fewer recorded preferred parent changes and improved communication reliability for the evaluated DTW-RL configuration.Under the five mobile node changing trajectory scenario at the 20 s transmission interval, DTW-RL reduced handover events by 97.72% compared with MRHOF and 47.66% compared with MMDEW.Its PDR were 71.28%, 97.37%, and 97.97% at transmission intervals of 10, 20, and 30 s, respectively.Furthermore, DTW-RL achieved the lowest end-to-end delay at transmission intervals of 10 s and 20 s in the five-mobile node scenario, whereas its higher delay in the two-mobile node scenario indicates a trade-off between routing stability and latency.Exploratory paired tests using six matched condition means found fewer handovers for DTW-RL than for MRHOF and MMDEW after Holm adjustment across eight comparisons (adjusted p = 0.0338 for each comparison).Under the evaluated conditions, the complete DTW-RL configuration demonstrated a trade-off between routing stability, communication reliability, and resource utilization.

title: Break‐even reference dependence in crop insurance decisions: Theory and evidence
summary: Abstract We study farmers' crop insurance choices using a behavioral framework in which break‐even status serves as a salient, economically grounded, and empirically observable reference point. The framework nests the standard expected‐util
content: Abstract We study farmers' crop insurance choices using a behavioral framework in which break‐even status serves as a salient, economically grounded, and empirically observable reference point. The framework nests the standard expected‐utility model as a special case and incorporates three forces: risk reduction, aversion to falling below break‐even status, and disutility from paying premiums. It yields sharp predictions about coverage choices, including bunching at the break‐even coverage level (BECL), defined as the coverage level where the insurance guarantee just covers total cost. We test these predictions using a survey of corn producers in Iowa and Kansas that elicits farmers' perceived BECLs, attitudes toward break‐even protection and premium costs, and their actual Federal Crop Insurance Program coverage choices. Coverage decisions display pronounced and asymmetric bunching around the BECL, with a sharp decline in frequency just below it and a smoother distribution above. Proxy measures of behavioral attitudes are also associated with observed choices in the predicted directions: farmers reporting stronger aversion to not breaking even are more likely to insure exactly at the BECL but not above it, while those reporting stronger premium aversion are more likely to insure below it. Using illustrative simulations, we further examine how subsidy changes interact with these behavioral forces and find that aversion to not breaking even may play an anchoring role that dampens the effects of premium subsidy cuts on coverage choices.

title: Market Research and Go-to-Market Strategy for Commercial Vehicles in Selected ASEAN and Latin American Markets: A Study of Tata Motors
source: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
summary: This paper examines how market research can help Tata Motors identify attractive commercial vehicle (CV) markets and develop country-specific Go-to-Market (GTM) strategies in selected ASEAN and Latin American (LATAM) countries. It draws on
content: This paper examines how market research can help Tata Motors identify attractive commercial vehicle (CV) markets and develop country-specific Go-to-Market (GTM) strategies in selected ASEAN and Latin American (LATAM) countries. It draws on a three-month on-the-job training project at Tata Motors Commercial Vehicle International Business and covers nine ASEAN and nine LATAM markets. The study is descriptive and exploratory and uses secondary data only: Total Industry Volume (TIV), growth, segment mix, demand sectors and competitor presence. In 2025, Thailand (381,930 units), the Philippines (368,250) and Indonesia (198,500) were the largest ASEAN markets, and Mexico (378,850) was by far the largest LATAM market. Colombia (41.00%), Cambodia (31.22%) and Vietnam (23.00%) grew fastest, but from smaller bases. Light commercial vehicles (LCVs) and pickups hold 51.8% to 82.3% of sales in the eleven markets with segment data. The study concludes that market size alone is a weak guide to market choice, and that an LCV-led, partner-based and phased approach, supported by fleet sales, financing, after-sales service and Total Cost of Ownership messaging, suits these markets. The recommendations are untested, so primary research is needed before implementation. Keywords: Commercial vehicles; Go-to-Market strategy; market research; ASEAN; Latin America; market prioritisation; Total Cost of Ownership

title: Bond market risk capital charges under the basel standardized duration approach: evidence from state bank of India for sustainable finance
source: Indian Journal of Finance and Banking
summary: Banks' bond holdings expose them to interest rate risk, and the 2023 bank failures in the United States renewed attention to how market risk capital charges are computed. In India, the Reserve Bank of India's 2026 market risk directions ret
content: Banks' bond holdings expose them to interest rate risk, and the 2023 bank failures in the United States renewed attention to how market risk capital charges are computed. In India, the Reserve Bank of India's 2026 market risk directions retain the standardized duration method, yet its mechanics and its link to bond yields remain thinly documented for emerging-market banks, with consequences for financial stability and sustainable economic growth. This study examines how the market risk capital charge on bonds is computed under the Basel standardized duration approach, traces the five-year trend of the market risk capital charge of State Bank of India (SBI), and tests whether the 10-year government security yield is associated with SBI's capital requirement for interest rate risk. The study uses a worked trading-book illustration of 15 debt instruments, SBI's Pillar 3 disclosures for 2015–16 to 2024–25 and Reserve Bank of India yield data, applying duration arithmetic, percentage-change analysis, Pearson correlation and a t-test. The results show that modified duration rises from 0.08 years for a one-month instrument to 6.52 years for a twelve-year instrument, producing a general market risk charge of ₹19.57 crore, a specific risk charge of ₹32.33 crore and risk-weighted assets of ₹576.59 crore on a ₹1,500 crore trading book. SBI's market risk capital charge rose by 106.1%, from ₹21,475.78 crore in 2020–21 to ₹44,252.91 crore in 2024–25, while the yield–capital requirement correlation is −0.30 (t = −0.90, p = 0.40). The findings suggest that residual maturity drives the capital charge through modified duration, that SBI's charge has doubled in five years, and that the yield relationship is negative but statistically weak. JEL Classification Codes: E43, G12, G21, G28, G32.

title: Does Financial Well‐Being Among Low Income Group Contributes in Advancing Poverty Alleviation ( SDG 1)?: A Hybrid Approach
summary: ABSTRACT Financial well‐being (FWB) among low‐income groups is an important but underexplored frontier in the global pursuit of SDG 1 (No Poverty). Despite rising evidence that financial inclusion improves household economic outcomes, the p
content: ABSTRACT Financial well‐being (FWB) among low‐income groups is an important but underexplored frontier in the global pursuit of SDG 1 (No Poverty). Despite rising evidence that financial inclusion improves household economic outcomes, the precise theoretical and empirical mechanisms tying FWB to poverty reduction remain fragmented across disciplines. This study addresses this gap with a hybrid approach that synthesizes and analyses 190 articles published between 2000 and 2025 using the Scientific Procedures and Rationales for Systematic Literature Reviews (SPAR‐4‐SLR) protocols. Employing a two‐study design, Study 1 undertakes a bibliometric analysis to map the intellectual landscape and performance metrics of the field. Study 2 deploys the Theory, Context, Characteristics, and Methodology (TCCM) framework for systematic content analysis. It outlines the findings of both studies, identifying research gaps and offering recommendations to guide future research. Key findings reveal that FWB is studied multi‐dimensionally and is a significant mediator in the relationship between financial literacy, socioeconomic status, and family financial outcomes contributing to poverty eradication among low‐income households in developing countries like Malaysia. Furthermore, there is theoretical reliance on asset‐building and social capital frameworks with limited integration of psychological theories. The review outlines the AMMO‐CV framework as a new theoretical synthesis and outlines a thorough research agenda in theory, context, characteristics, and methodology. The study contributes to policy formulation for governments, financial service developers, NGOs, and multilateral organizations aiming to meet the 2030 Agenda targets.

title: Effect of Public-Private Partnership Practices on Capital Project Performance in Rwanda: A Case of Infrastructure Capital Projects in Bugesera District
source: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
summary: This study assessed the effect of Public-Private Partnership practices on the performance of infrastructure capital projects in Bugesera District, Rwanda.The study examined contract governance and performance monitoring, risk allocation and
content: This study assessed the effect of Public-Private Partnership practices on the performance of infrastructure capital projects in Bugesera District, Rwanda.The study examined contract governance and performance monitoring, risk allocation and risk management mechanisms, stakeholder coordination and institutional collaboration, and financing structure and value-for-money practices.The study was guided by Agency Theory, Risk Allocation Theory, Stakeholder Theory, Value-for-Money Theory, Transaction Cost Economics, and Systems Theory.A mixed-methods approach was applied through descriptive, correlational and explanatory research designs.The target population comprised 150 infrastructure stakeholders, from whom 109 respondents were selected.Descriptive findings showed positive agreement and homogeneous composite responses across all study variables.Contract governance and performance monitoring (B=0.254,t=2.702, p=0.008), risk allocation and risk management mechanisms (B=0.200,t=2.198, p=0.029), stakeholder coordination and institutional collaboration (B=0.270,t=2.784, p=0.007), and financing structure and value-for-money practices (B=0.263,t=2.740, p=0.007) had positive and statistically significant effects on capital project performance.The model explained 79.8% of the variation in capital project performance.The study concluded that coordinated PPP governance, appropriate risk allocation, effective stakeholder collaboration and disciplined value-for-money practices jointly strengthened infrastructure capital project performance in Bugesera District.It recommended integrated contract monitoring, regularly updated risk responsibilities, structured stakeholder coordination and lifecycle-based financing review.

title: Digital Adaptation and Green Human Resource Strategy for Sustainable Infrastructure Development
source: Journal of Infrastructure Policy and Management
summary: Sustainable infrastructure development requires organizations to respond simultaneously to digital transformation, environmental sustainability, and changing workforce requirements. However, digital technology adoption alone does not ensure
content: Sustainable infrastructure development requires organizations to respond simultaneously to digital transformation, environmental sustainability, and changing workforce requirements. However, digital technology adoption alone does not ensure sustainable infrastructure outcomes, while Green Human Resource Management is often examined separately from infrastructure transformation. This conceptual paper develops an integrated framework explaining how Digital Adaptation and Green Human Resource Strategy contribute to Sustainable Infrastructure Development through capability building. Drawing on Dynamic Capability Theory and the Socio-Technical Systems perspective, the framework positions Digital Adaptation as increasing the need for Digital and Green Human Capital. At the same time, Green Human Resource Strategy mobilizes and embeds these capabilities within Workforce and Organizational Capability. Strategic Alignment between Digital Adaptation and Green Human Resource Strategy is positioned as the central mechanism linking these processes. Policy and Governance, Sustainability-Oriented Leadership, and Cross-Sector Collaboration are identified as enabling conditions. Seven propositions are developed to explain the relationships among these constructs. The framework offers a capability-building perspective linking digital adaptation, human resources, organizational capability, and sustainable infrastructure development.

title: Tora (Alpinia allughas) for Sustainable Textiles and Food Applications: Fibre Processing, Blending and Value Addition
summary: Tora (Alpinia allughas) is an underutilized bast-fibre plant with potential for sustainable textile applications. This study investigated fibre extraction and wet processing, evaluated Tora–cotton blended fabrics, and considered opportuniti
content: Tora (Alpinia allughas) is an underutilized bast-fibre plant with potential for sustainable textile applications. This study investigated fibre extraction and wet processing, evaluated Tora–cotton blended fabrics, and considered opportunities for value addition. Tora stems were mechanically decorticated and subjected to water, chemical and enzymatic retting. Water retting for 30 days produced an 85% fibre yield, although the fibres remained stiff and sticky. Chemical retting with 9% NaOH for 3 h yielded 55% fibre with the highest reported bundle strength of 25.5 g/tex, while 3% pectinase produced a maximum yield of 56.2%. Subsequent scouring, bleaching and softening reduced fibre diameter from 100 to 76.4 µm and increased moisture regain from 7.57 to 11.4%. Tora–cotton yarns with blend ratios of 70:30, 50:50 and 30:70 were woven with cotton warp in a plain weave. Among these fabrics, the 50:50 blends showed the highest reported thickness (1.32 mm), mass (466 g/m²), wicking height (1.52 cm warp; 1.98 cm weft) and thermal insulation (3.10 tog). Tora–cEri silk fabrics had a pilling rating of 4. The findings indicate that retting and wet processing can modify Tora fibre characteristics and support its incorporation into woven textiles. Food-related applications are also considered as a potential avenue for integrated utilization. These results suggest opportunities for further development of Tora-based materials within a circular bioeconomy.

title: The impact of advanced manufacturing development on industrial land prices: Evidence from Zhejiang, China
source: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
summary: While existing studies have examined the determinants of industrial land prices, limited attention has been paid to how changes in local government competition strategies shape industrial land pricing. Using data from Zhejiang Province, Chi
content: While existing studies have examined the determinants of industrial land prices, limited attention has been paid to how changes in local government competition strategies shape industrial land pricing. Using data from Zhejiang Province, China, this study investigates how the shift in local government strategies – from a “race-to-bottom” to a “race-for-quality” focusing on advanced manufacturing – affects industrial land prices through market-oriented land allocation practices. Employing regression analyses, the results show that as the land-driven development model becomes increasingly unsustainable, the traditional strategy of attracting investment and tax revenue through low industrial land prices loses effectiveness. Prioritizing land allocation for advanced manufacturing is associated with higher industrial land prices. Further evidence suggests that advanced manufacturing development tends to be accompanied by a higher degree of land marketization, reflecting firms’ stronger preference for transparent and competitive land allocation environments. By clarifying the relationship between advanced manufacturing development and industrial land prices, this study contributes to the literature on market-oriented land allocation and local government competition strategies.

title: Adversarial Risk Management: The Art and Science of Managing Organisation Security in the Hostile 21st Century
summary: Conventional risk management was not built for adversaries. The frameworks that organisations rely upon, ISO 31000, COSO ERM, and their derivatives, were designed for a world of probabilistic hazards, accidents, system failures, and random
content: Conventional risk management was not built for adversaries. The frameworks that organisations rely upon, ISO 31000, COSO ERM, and their derivatives, were designed for a world of probabilistic hazards, accidents, system failures, and random operational disruptions. Against a ransomware operator who studies your disaster recovery plan for weaknesses, a nation‑state actor conducting multi‑year reconnaissance through your supply chain, or an insider quietly exfiltrating intellectual property while compliance scores remain perfect, they fail. They fail because they were designed for a fundamentally different kind of risk, one governed by statistical distributions rather than human decision‑making. An adversary is not a hurricane. Applying actuarial logic to intelligent, adaptive opponents does not produce security. It produces the appearance of security, and adversaries have learned to exploit the gap between the two. This book makes the case for a different paradigm. Adversarial Risk Management (ARM) places the adversary’s decision‑making at the centre of the analytical problem. If a threat actor cannot acquire the intent to harm your organisation, cannot develop or sustain the capability to do so, and cannot identify or create the opportunity to act, the risk does not materialise. ARM works by disrupting that chain, systematically and continuously, across every domain in which your organisation is exposed. The framework rests on two interlocking constructs. The Intent, Capability, and Opportunity model provides the analytical lens through which adversarial threats are deconstructed and understood. The Frame, Assess, Respond, and Monitor cycle provides the operational discipline through which that analysis is translated into action and renewed as adversaries evolve. ARM is applied across six security domains: cyber, physical, information, personnel, personal security, and supply chain, within a single coherent methodology that reflects how adversaries actually operate, without regard to organisational boundaries or disciplinary silos. ARM does not ask organisations to discard existing governance structures. It integrates with ISO 27001, NIST CSF, COSO ERM, and ISO 31000, providing the adversarial layer those frameworks were never designed to deliver, and it gives security leaders the measurement tools to demonstrate genuine outcomes rather than compliance activity. This book is written for professionals who understand that the hostile 21st century demands more than compliance. It demands adversarial thinking.

title: Business Ethics: A Contemporary Introduction
summary: Packed with examples, this book offers a clear and engaging overview of ethical issues in business. It begins with a discussion of foundational issues, including the objectivity of ethics, the content of ethical theories, and the debate bet
content: Packed with examples, this book offers a clear and engaging overview of ethical issues in business. It begins with a discussion of foundational issues, including the objectivity of ethics, the content of ethical theories, and the debate between capitalism and socialism, making it suitable for the beginning student. It then examines ethical issues in business in three broad areas. The first is the market, where it examines what can be sold (the limits of markets) and how it can be sold (ethics in marketing). The second is work. Topics in this area are health and safety, meaningful work, pay, hiring and firing, privacy, artificial intelligence, and whistleblowing. The third area is business and society. Here readers explore corporate social responsibility, business and politics, environmental ethics, and international business. Issues are introduced through real-world examples that underscore their importance and make them come alive. Arguments for opposing positions are given fair hearings and students are encouraged to develop their own views. Major changes to the Second Edition include a new chapter on businesses’ environmental obligations, extended discussion of the ethics of artificial intelligence, and expanded treatment of marketing ethics and shareholder primacy. To aid in teaching, learning, and accessibility, each chapter now provides a summary and list of learning objectives. Examples are updated throughout, and a new a list of cases alongside a glossary of key terms are featured at the end of this book. Key updates to the Second Edition Includes a new chapter on business, the environment, and climate change. Adds features to make the text easier to navigate, including a more detailed table of contents, a glossary of key terms, and a list of cases and examples used in the book. Each chapter now begins with a summary and list of learning objectives, helping students to read more actively. Includes more focused study questions at the end of each chapter, encouraging more engagement with the text. Contains a heavily revised, more nuanced third chapter on ethical theories. Provides additional coverage of AI ethics throughout the book, focusing specifically on issues of bias, transparency, privacy, and safety.

title: The Global Stagnation
summary: The Global StagnationAtomic disenchantment was in the air almost everywhere in the world as the 1970s drew to a close.The original fascination with nuclear fission that had characterized the first postwar decades seemed to belong to a dista
content: The Global StagnationAtomic disenchantment was in the air almost everywhere in the world as the 1970s drew to a close.The original fascination with nuclear fission that had characterized the first postwar decades seemed to belong to a distant past.The antinuclear movement had gained unpre ce dented strength.Governments were growing increasingly skeptical about the atom, as were many utilities.Some remained optimistic about the future, envisioning that the prob lems the industry faced could be overcome.In more and more countries, however, actors began looking for alternative ways to meet their energy needs.What followed was a complex interplay between politics, economics, and technology in dif fer ent national settings, whereby the atom's three troubled marriages meshed with each other in a fierce strug gle for and against an atomic future.
