title: Organization Culture and Employees’ Personality Alignment: Reducing Counter-Productivity Among Early-Career Employees in India’s Private Sector
source: Journal of Management Practices Humanities and Social Sciences
summary: A significant challenge with entry-level or early-career employees in today’s time is the frequent misalignment between their personality and culture of the organization, which in turn may cause adverse effects to their work productivity. T
content: A significant challenge with entry-level or early-career employees in today’s time is the frequent misalignment between their personality and culture of the organization, which in turn may cause adverse effects to their work productivity. This study aims to address how can organizational culture be strategically managed to reduce counterproductive behavior and protect firm performance. The present research studies how personality traits and organization culture jointly impact deviant behavior in the organization, especially among early career employees working in the Indian private sector. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, drawing data from 349 early-career employees (experience of 0-2 years) working in private-sector organizations across India. Standardized measures of the Big Five personality traits, Perceived organizational culture, and counterproductive work behavior were administered. Data were analyzed using hierarchical multiple regression in JASP 0.18.3. Organizational culture emerged as a significant contextual predictor of CWB. Results also indicate that conscientiousness and agreeableness are negatively associated with counterproductive work behavior. The combined model explained substantial variance in counterproductive work behavior, underscoring the need of a supportive and empowering culture to reduce counter-productivity, as well as integrating individual personality dispositions and organizational context when examining workplace productivity among early-career employees. By shifting the focus from obstacles in productivity of newcomer employees to the importance of a culture driven adaptation, the findings offer ground for strategy integration for organizations seeking to cultivate cultures, design effective on-boarding programmes, and retain Generational Z and Millennial employees. This study contributes to the literature by offering an integrated personality–culture framework for understanding counterproductive work behavior in the Indian private sector. By focusing on early-career employees, the findings provide actionable strategies for recruitment, on-boarding, and culture-building initiatives aimed at mitigating dysfunctional workplace behaviors in emerging market contexts.

title: Examining Employment and Export Figures in the Shipbuilding Industry – A Relational Analysis on Türkiye
summary: Abstract The shipbuilding industry is a significant component of the four primary maritime transport markets. In line with recent regulations in the context of green shipping, the development of shipyards in terms of employment is highly va
content: Abstract The shipbuilding industry is a significant component of the four primary maritime transport markets. In line with recent regulations in the context of green shipping, the development of shipyards in terms of employment is highly valuable, as shipowners frequently turn to shipyards for both new construction processes and green conversion and maintenance-repair processes. The identification of factors influencing employment in the shipbuilding industry could serve as a guide for increasing quality production. The present study analyses the relationship between export figures and employment levels of shipyards in Türkiye between 2003 and 2023. Consequently, it was determined that exports in the Turkish shipbuilding sector have a positive impact on employment in both the long and short term. The study's findings yielded theoretical and practical conclusions, as well as policy recommendations for future research. JEL classification: F16 J21, F14

title: Annual report maps for impression management: Weapons of colonialism
summary: Much has been written about Cecil Rhodes and the British South Africa Company (BSAC), which he established by royal charter to colonize Rhodesia. Based on a unique dataset of 24 maps included in the BSAC annual reports 1891–1924, we show ho
content: Much has been written about Cecil Rhodes and the British South Africa Company (BSAC), which he established by royal charter to colonize Rhodesia. Based on a unique dataset of 24 maps included in the BSAC annual reports 1891–1924, we show how the BSAC portrayed its activities cartographically to shareholders in London and to the Colonial Office. Maps were powerful tools of imperialism. We adopt visual reasoning and close reading to interpret the maps. We analyze three aspects: ① the territory the Company claimed to own, ② the minerals the company claimed to control and ③ the communication infrastructure the Company claimed to have developed, together with three map elements overlaid on the maps: ① labelling, symbols and visual emphasis, ② color and ③ inset maps. We conclude that the maps were for impression management with shareholders, creating the impression of immense wealth.

title: Towards sufficiency-oriented urban renewal: Why activating ground floor vacancy requires more than subsidies
summary: :Many cities face the paradox of persistent ground floor vacancy despite unmet demand for affordable commercial space. This highlights the need for sufficiency-oriented urban renewal that promotes the careful use and fair distribution of sp
content: :Many cities face the paradox of persistent ground floor vacancy despite unmet demand for affordable commercial space. This highlights the need for sufficiency-oriented urban renewal that promotes the careful use and fair distribution of spatial resources. In this paper, vacancy activation is examined as a strategy for conserving resources through the reuse of existing buildings while reducing spatial inequalities by improving access for non-profit tenants. It focuses on the challenges faced by associations, one-person- and micro-businesses in activating vacant ground floor premises, and assesses the extent to which funding programs – a common vacancy activation policy – can overcome these barriers. As a city with a long tradition of urban renewal, a mature funding landscape and a commitment to vacancy activation, Vienna provides an interesting case study. The findings – based on a mixed-methods approach drawing on two research projects and additional empirical data – show that affordability and, in particular, the availability of vacant premises remain the main barriers for non-profit tenants in activating ground floor vacancy. While subsidies can provide short-term support, they only partially address existing inequalities in the real estate market, such as rising rents, tax disadvantages and speculation. Thus, they have only limited effect on sufficiency-oriented urban renewal. The paper concludes that regulatory and legal measures are needed in order to tackle the structural causes of limited availability and affordability, and support the redistribution and reuse of existing building stock.

title: Agricultural Knowledge and Innovation Systems (AKIS) and Advi-sory Services in the European Union and Associated Countries: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Achieving the European Union's agricultural sustainability targets depends heavily on reliable advice, coherent system governance and connected innovation networks. Within the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), Agricultural Knowledge and Inn
content: Achieving the European Union's agricultural sustainability targets depends heavily on reliable advice, coherent system governance and connected innovation networks. Within the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), Agricultural Knowledge and Innovation Systems (AKIS) and Farm Advisory Services (FAS) represent the primary macro-systemic and meso-organizational frameworks for sharing knowledge and supporting farm-level decisions. Peer-reviewed literature indexed in Scopus was systematically searched between 2018 and 2026 following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The initial publication title search yielded 408 records. Applying automated filters for English-language peer-reviewed journal articles, reviews and conference papers narrowed the pool to 190 records. Title and abstract screening excluded 109 records (72 outside the European geographic/policy scope and 37 keyword or acronym collisions), leaving a final sample of N = 81 core studies covering EU Member States as well as European countries associated to Horizon Europe or candidates for EU accession. The synthesis reveals a structural transition away from top-down, linear extension toward pluralistic, interactive innovation networks, structured across five analytical dimensions: (a) Macro-level AKIS governance and CAP integration: Member States are not equally ready to put AKIS into practice in their 2023-2027 CAP Strategic Plans, be-cause they differ in funding capacity and in institutional coordination. (b) Meso-level pluralism and market structure: private advisors respond quickly, but advice tied to input sales creates commercial conflicts of interest. Smallholders also lose out because public-good advice is in short supply. (c) Interactive innovation and brokerage: innovation brokers in EIP-AGRI Operational Groups and Living Labs work across boundaries in ways traditional farm advisors do nοt. (d) Digitalization and smart farming: socio-technical bottlenecks and disconnected networks hold back the uptake of Decision Support Systems (DSS) and algorithmic identity friction adds to the problem. (e) Micro-level advisor competencies, wellbeing and microAKIS: advisors now need to facilitate group processes and direct farmers to psychological support. They also have to communicate in ways that fit farmers’ personal knowledge networks. European AKIS needs permanent funding for innovation brokerage and reform of higher agricultural education curricula. It also needs sustained public investment to keep independent, public-good advice available.

title: Perceived age-friendliness in multiethnic and multigenerational Klang Valley, Malaysia: An extended WHO Age-Friendly Cities assessment
summary: Malaysia's transition towards an ageing society underscores the need for context-sensitive tools to assess urban age-friendliness, particularly in the multiethnic cities of the Global South. This quantitative cross-sectional study adapted a
content: Malaysia's transition towards an ageing society underscores the need for context-sensitive tools to assess urban age-friendliness, particularly in the multiethnic cities of the Global South. This quantitative cross-sectional study adapted and extended the World Health Organization's Age-Friendly Cities framework by incorporating additional domains on technology and financial situation to assess perceived neighbourhood age-friendliness across six local authorities in Klang Valley, Malaysia. Incorporating a multigenerational perspective, the study captured perceptions from diverse age and ethnic populations. A bilingual self-administered questionnaire consisting of 15 socio-demographic items and 75 closed-ended age-friendly indicators measured on a 5-point Likert scale was administered to 511 community-dwelling adults aged 18 years and above. The instrument underwent expert review, content validity assessment, and pilot testing prior to implementation. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, one-sample t-tests, independent samples t-tests, and one-way ANOVA. The overall age-friendly score (AFI) indicated that Klang Valley was generally age-friendly, with scores significantly above the neutral midpoint of the 5-point scale (M = 3.36, p < .001). The technology and respect and social inclusion domains recorded the highest mean scores (both M = 3.77, p < .001), while civic participation and employment was the only domain scoring significantly below the midpoint (M = 2.81, p < .001). Significant spatial differences were observed across local authorities for AFI and nine domains (p < .05), with Putrajaya, the master-planned administrative capital consistently reporting the highest scores. Ethnic differences were significant for AFI and eight domains (p < .05). In contrast, age-group differences were largely non-significant except for technology, where young adult respondents reported higher satisfaction than older adult respondents (p < .001). The findings suggest that perceived age-friendliness in Klang Valley varies more clearly by spatial and ethnic contexts than by chronological age. This study provides a multidomain empirical benchmark of urban age-friendliness in Malaysia from a person-environment fit perspective. It highlights the importance of inclusive, multigenerational, and digitally responsive urban planning strategies.

title: New agricultural cooperative economy and agricultural economic resilience in China: the role of factor productivity
summary: In the process of advancing common prosperity and the modernization of agriculture and rural areas, enhancing agricultural economic resilience (AER) has become a key issue for ensuring high-quality agricultural development and strengthening
content: In the process of advancing common prosperity and the modernization of agriculture and rural areas, enhancing agricultural economic resilience (AER) has become a key issue for ensuring high-quality agricultural development and strengthening risk resistance. As a significant innovative form of the basic rural operating system, the New Agricultural Cooperative Economy (NACE) provides a new institutional pathway for improving the quality of agricultural development and enhancing risk resistance by optimizing resource allocation, strengthening organizational coordination, and promoting the integration of production factors. However, existing research has primarily focused on the income-generating effects and governance functions of NACE, with a lack of systematic study on the underlying mechanisms through which it influences AER particularly the mediating role played by Efficiency in the Allocation of Agricultural Production Factors (EAAPF) in this process. Based on this, this paper utilizes panel data from 30 Chinese provinces covering the period 2011–2023 to construct an evaluation index system for NACE. By integrating the progress of collective property rights system reforms, the study empirically examines the impact of NACE on AER and its underlying mechanisms. The study finds that NACE further strengthens AER by enhancing EAAPF; EAAPF plays a partial mediating role in this relationship and serves as a key transmission channel for the transition from factor-input-driven growth to efficiency-driven growth; Heterogeneity and threshold effect analyses reveal that the promotional effect of NACE on AER varies significantly across different regions and under varying factor endowment conditions; simultaneously, the impact of NACE exhibits a threshold effect related to the level of rural financial development, with its marginal effect showing an increasing trend as the level of rural financial development rises. This study provides a new theoretical explanation for understanding how NACE empowers high-quality agricultural development and offers empirical evidence for enhancing AER through institutional innovation.

title: Comparable Efficacy of Clove Leaf Oil Nanoemulsion and Povidone-Iodine on Reducing Microbial and Somatic Cell Counts in Subclinical Mastitis
summary: Effective and sustainable teat dipping strategies are essential to treat persistent mastitis in smallholder dairy farming. This study compared the efficacy of 25% clove leaf oil nanoemulsion (CLON), a natural alternative to post-milking tea
content: Effective and sustainable teat dipping strategies are essential to treat persistent mastitis in smallholder dairy farming. This study compared the efficacy of 25% clove leaf oil nanoemulsion (CLON), a natural alternative to post-milking teat dipping, with 1% povidone-iodine (PV-I) in field conditions in Banyumas, Indonesia. We applied the California Mastitis Test to 138 dairy cows, found 40 mastitis-positive udder quarters, and assigned them to two teat dipping treatments (25% CLON and 1% PV-I) in a completely randomized 2×4 factorial design with five replicates. Teat dipping was applied twice daily for 30 days to measure the total plate count (TPC) and somatic cell count (SCC) on days 0, 10, 20, and 30. Reduction kinetics were estimated using the first-order models and compared using two-way ANOVA and equivalence testing. The results showed that over 30 days, the 25% CLON treatment reduced TPC by 31.65%–64.03% and SCC by 17.52%–45.05% across all mastitis severities, with the highest percentage on trace level. Total reduction or first-order reduction constants were not significantly different between 25% CLON and 1% PV-I, ±10 percentage points, as evidenced by the equivalence testing. Dermal irritation assessment showed no erythema or edema after the 24-h application. Exploratory 16S rRNA sequencing of paired samples revealed a decrease in pathogenic abundance (Epilithonimonas bovis: from 65.04% to 1.51%; Lactococcus garvieae: from 10.03% to 0.09%) and an increase in microbial diversity. Conclusively, 25% CLON was comparable to 1% PV-I, suggesting a feasible natural substitute for post-milking teat dipping in smallholder dairy farming.

title: Does Asymmetric Cost Behaviour Affect Investors’ Heterogeneous Beliefs? Evidence from Egypt
source: Journal of Administrative and Economic Sciences
summary: Objectives This research aims to examine how asymmetric cost behaviour affects investors’ heterogeneous beliefs, with a particular focus on different cost components, based on evidence from Egyptian listed firms. Material and Methods The an
content: Objectives This research aims to examine how asymmetric cost behaviour affects investors’ heterogeneous beliefs, with a particular focus on different cost components, based on evidence from Egyptian listed firms. Material and Methods The analysis is based on a sample of 71 non-financial firms listed on the Egyptian stock market over the period 2014-2023. This study employs panel data regression using the ordinary least squares (OLS) method, complemented by robustness tests conducted using the two-stage least squares (2SLS) method to address potential endogeneity issues, including reverse causality and omitted variable bias. Results The empirical findings reveal that while the asymmetric behaviour of selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) costs exerts a significant positive effect on investors’ heterogeneous beliefs, no statistically significant impact is observed for the asymmetric behaviour of either the cost of goods sold (COGS) or total operating costs. Conclusion The results provide a valuable insight for different sectors in the Egyptian environment. Managers may adopt more flexible cost management practices during sales downturns, investors can improve their interpretation of financial information by considering the asymmetric cost behaviour, and policymakers may enhance market efficiency by encouraging greater disclosure of firms’ cost adjustment policies. In addition, the findings demonstrate that investors place greater emphasis on discretionary costs, which are more directly influenced by managerial decisions, compared to nondiscretionary costs that are largely driven by operational constraints.

title: Sharing the Facts: A Distribution Analysis of Fact-checks During Election Periods
summary: This article investigates the dissemination patterns of political fact-checks during election periods, analysing their spread across news media and social platforms in Norway. While political fact-checking is increasingly recognised as esse
content: This article investigates the dissemination patterns of political fact-checks during election periods, analysing their spread across news media and social platforms in Norway. While political fact-checking is increasingly recognised as essential to informed democratic participation, little research has explored how fact-checks diffuse through the public sphere during elections. Using Faktisk—the sole Norwegian fact-checking organisation—as a case study, the article analyses the distribution of election-related fact-checks published during the 2021 national and 2023 local elections. Results show that the dissemination of fact-checks remained limited primarily within politically homogeneous circles. Ideological leanings significantly influenced sharing behaviour, particularly among far-right groups who engaged actively in hostile interactions, often framing fact-checkers as biased adversaries. Contrary to assumptions that election periods amplify fact-check visibility, findings revealed no substantial increase in overall engagement compared to non-election periods. The study concludes that without deliberate strategies to broaden dissemination and audience reach, fact-checking risks reinforcing polarisation instead of counteracting misinformation. It calls for enhanced focus on distribution mechanisms and audience engagement strategies in political fact-checking practices, especially during critical democratic moments such as elections.

title: Driving Competitive Advantage through Organizational Capacity and Corporate Governance: A Study of Bekasi’s State-Linked Companies (BUMDes)
source: Dinasti International Journal of Education Management And Social Science
summary: This study examines the determinants of competitive advantage in regionally owned enterprises in Bekasi, Indonesia. Specifically, it investigates the influence of marketing strategy, natural resource capital, and organizational capacity on
content: This study examines the determinants of competitive advantage in regionally owned enterprises in Bekasi, Indonesia. Specifically, it investigates the influence of marketing strategy, natural resource capital, and organizational capacity on competitive advantage while assessing the mediating role of corporate governance. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 487 employees from Bekasi’s public enterprises. Data were collected through structured online questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling to assess both measurement and structural models. The results indicate that marketing strategy, natural resource capital, and organizational capacity significantly influence corporate governance and competitive advantage. Corporate governance partially mediates all hypothesized relationships. Natural resource capital shows the strongest direct effect on competitive advantage, while marketing strategy emerges as the strongest predictor of corporate governance. The model explains 54.9% of the variance in corporate governance and 46.8% in competitive advantage.

title: Enablers and Barriers of the Circular Bioeconomy Transition in the Global South: An Empirical Analysis in the Uruguayan Forest-based Bioeconomy
summary: Despite the growing attention paid to circular bioeconomy, limited knowledge exists about enablers and barriers shaping the circular bioeconomy transition in developing regions such as the Global South. This study investigates these factors
content: Despite the growing attention paid to circular bioeconomy, limited knowledge exists about enablers and barriers shaping the circular bioeconomy transition in developing regions such as the Global South. This study investigates these factors from the perspective of different stakeholders of the forest-based bioeconomy value chain in Uruguay. The empirical analysis was based on a survey that involved key stakeholders, i.e., companies, academia, civil society & multilateral organizations, and the public sector. Data was analysed through descriptive statistics and a Spearman correlation test. Findings indicate that efficient technology, recycling capabilities, and the enforcement of good practices are perceived by the stakeholders as prominent enablers of the transition. Conversely, limited technical skills, insufficient knowledge capacity, and weak industrial symbiosis are perceived as particularly relevant barriers that need to be addressed by value chain actors to effectively run a circular bioeconomy transition in the Global South.

title: From paradigms to instruments: ideational constraints on industrial policy and the Dutch National Growth Fund
summary: The resurgence of industrial policy has sparked debate over whether contemporary state intervention marks a break with neoliberalism or rather its reconfiguration. We add nuance by shifting the focus from macro-level paradigms to meso-level
content: The resurgence of industrial policy has sparked debate over whether contemporary state intervention marks a break with neoliberalism or rather its reconfiguration. We add nuance by shifting the focus from macro-level paradigms to meso-level instruments, developing an analytical framework for mapping industrial policy instruments based on two key dimensions: selectivity, the degree to which the state directs investment toward specific sectors, and conditionality, the discipline attached to public support. Neoliberal settings, such as those prevalent in high-income economies, encompass competing ideational currents with different views on these dimensions: Pro-business neoliberals favor selectivity to support competitive firms while placing less emphasis on conditionality, whereas frugal neoliberals prioritize conditionality to discipline public spending but are skeptical about selectivity. Instrument design reflects the negotiation between these competing currents. We illustrate this argument through a case study of the Dutch National Growth Fund, based on 24 semi-structured interviews and documentary analysis. We find that the dominance of frugal neoliberal ideas produced an instrument shaped more by conditionality than selectivity, suggesting that recent industrial policy initiatives have been bounded by intra-neoliberal contestation. The article contributes a meso-level analytical framework for analyzing variation in industrial policy design across high-income economies.

title: Structural and policy barriers to private sector development: evidence from firm-level data in Qatar
summary: This study contributes to the literature by presenting the first systematic evidence on business constraints in Qatar, based on a new firm-level survey of 386 enterprises across eight sectors and three clusters. To measure the challenges fa
content: This study contributes to the literature by presenting the first systematic evidence on business constraints in Qatar, based on a new firm-level survey of 386 enterprises across eight sectors and three clusters. To measure the challenges faced by firms, we construct three indices while distinguishing between structural and policy related constraints using both equal-weight and principal component approaches, alongside polychoric and survey-adjusted robustness checks at the cluster level. Results show that structural obstacles dominate over policy-related ones, with the highest constraints reported in resilience sectors such as food, agriculture, and health. In contrast, policy-related barriers are more binding in enabling sectors including IT, finance, and education. Medium-sized firms tend to report fewer constraints than small enterprises. Firm age is negatively associated with all constraint measures, indicating that experience mitigates exposure to both structural and regulatory pressures. Moreover, firms reporting access to financial support often remain highly constrained, reflecting a reactive rather than preventive role of such support. Comparisons with WBES data, while limited by methodological differences, suggest that Qatar’s structural–policy distinction is broadly consistent with wider international patterns.

title: SMART BANKING SYSTEM (GREEN BANKING) A UNIFIED, SECURE AND INTELLIGENT CORE BANKING PLATFORM FOR CUSTOMERS, COMPLIANCE OFFICERS, AND ADMINISTRATORS
summary: Modern financial operations and digital banking exist in a mission-critical area where security vulnerabilities, unauthorized overdrafts, fraudulent transactions, money laundering risks, and manual credit underwriting delays can profoundly
content: Modern financial operations and digital banking exist in a mission-critical area where security vulnerabilities, unauthorized overdrafts, fraudulent transactions, money laundering risks, and manual credit underwriting delays can profoundly undermine institutional integrity and customer trust. This paper proposes Green Banking (Smart Banking System), a unified, secure, and intelligent core banking platform connecting retail customers, compliance officers and bank administrators through a real-time digital financial ecosystem. The system is focused around an atomic double-entry General Ledger bookkeeping engine, two-step OTP multi-factor authentication, real-time AI Neural Sentinel fraud and anomaly detection, automated Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance monitoring, CIBIL-based loan underwriting with reducing-balance EMI amortization schedules, ISO/IEC 7812 Luhn Mod-10 card lifecycle management and standardized identifier generation (IFSC, UPI VPA and ISO 13616 IBAN). The platform is built using a four-tier architecture encompassing a presentation tier, an Express REST API gateway tier, a business services tier and an ACID-compliant persistence tier utilizing SQLite in Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) mode. Security is enforced through JWT-based Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), bcrypt password hashing and tamper-evident audit logging and the API is documented with OpenAPI/Swagger. The primary aim of the system is to transform every banking operation into an atomic, verified and auditable lifecycle in which no transaction is committed without balance verification, AML screening and fraud-risk scoring. The proposed design also serves as the foundation for future technologies including blockchain-based ESG bond tokenization, IoT smart-meter verification, Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) settlement and biometric authentication.

title: Food Havens: Governing Technological Change for Equitable, Sustainable and Healthy Pacific Food Futures
source: Kōtuitui New Zealand Journal of Social Sciences Online
summary: Background: Global food systems are being reshaped by climate change, nutritional transition and widening health inequities. In Pacific communities, these pressures intersect with colonial legacies and import‐dependent food economies, contr
content: Background: Global food systems are being reshaped by climate change, nutritional transition and widening health inequities. In Pacific communities, these pressures intersect with colonial legacies and import‐dependent food economies, contributing to a high burden of diet‐related non‐communicable diseases. Since 2018, the Food Havens programme has undertaken community‐based research across Pacific settings, emphasising that food‐related health challenges require systems‐wide approaches rather than health service‐centred interventions. Objective: To examine how rapid technological change may reshape Pacific food systems and health equity, and to identify policy‐relevant directions for socially just food futures. Methods: This paper undertakes a qualitative, conceptual policy analysis. Drawing on Food Havens programme insights, it applies the Honest Food Framework to assess current Pacific food systems and to contrast inclusive and extractive future trajectories. Scenario‐based analysis examines the implications of digital, production and governance technologies across agriculture, food markets and nutrition support. Results: Technological change creates both opportunities and risks. Community‐governed pathways may strengthen food sovereignty, nutrition and resilience, while poorly governed technologies risk deepening dependency and health inequities. Conclusions: Technology alone will not produce equitable food or health outcomes. Policy‐makers should prioritise governance frameworks that embed cultural values, community decision‐making and accountability in food‐system innovation. These findings are relevant for countries seeking to align digital transformation with health equity and resilience.

title: Explaining Convection and Instability Scalings in Radiative‐Convective Equilibrium
summary: Abstract In Earth's tropics, stronger radiative cooling enhances convection. Numerical experiments reveal that cloud cover increases nearly linearly with the cooling rate, while updraft velocity remains almost constant. However, atmospheric
content: Abstract In Earth's tropics, stronger radiative cooling enhances convection. Numerical experiments reveal that cloud cover increases nearly linearly with the cooling rate, while updraft velocity remains almost constant. However, atmospheric instability decreases under stronger cooling. We develop a simple two‐layer cloud model to explain how these scalings arise. The cloud cover and updraft velocity scalings follow naturally from mass continuity and an assumption for the dissipation rate. The scaling for instability requires a further closure assumption. Allowing the updraft velocity to depend on low‐level cloud cover is an attractive possibility consistent with cloud‐updraft interactions, and predicts an instability dependence consistent with simulations. Larger cloud cover under stronger cooling compensates for the reduction in instability through cloud‐updraft interactions, allowing updraft velocities to remain approximately unchanged despite lower CAPE. The framework reconciles CAPE‐based interpretations of convection with the observed RCE scalings, providing a physically based foundation for prognostic convective parameterizations.

title: Break‐Even Conditions for HTS‐HVDC in Constrained High‐Capacity Renewable‐Energy Transmission Corridors
summary: ABSTRACT Constrained transmission corridors motivate comparison of high‐temperature superconducting high‐voltage direct‐current (HTS‐HVDC) with conventional VSC‐HVDC under a common receiving‐end service and contingency requirement. This stu
content: ABSTRACT Constrained transmission corridors motivate comparison of high‐temperature superconducting high‐voltage direct‐current (HTS‐HVDC) with conventional VSC‐HVDC under a common receiving‐end service and contingency requirement. This study links three questions: how transmission ratings determine installed reserve, how much additional conventional corridor capital is required for parity and what conductor procurement price permits parity. The calculation purchases complete cable, converter and cooling inventories for independent modules and evaluates lifecycle expenditure and delivered energy. A 2‐GW conventional reference is compared with 2‐, 3‐, 4‐ and 5‐GW HTS planning modules using a common converter–cost relationship. At 2.1 GW receiving‐end power and 500 km, the additional conventional capital required for parity is approximately USD 0.80 billion for equal‐2‐GW modules and USD 1.39 billion for 5‐GW HTS modules. Fewer HTS assemblies can therefore coincide with a higher cost of installed reserve. Conductor‐price thresholds depend on that architecture and the assumed additional‐corridor capital; three heat‐ingress scenarios show their thermal sensitivity. Reliability and input uncertainty qualify these conditions rather than establish commercial feasibility. The calculations use published component correlations and explicit author cost and reliability scenarios. Historical project comparisons do not validate the conventional coefficients, and conductor‐current evidence does not qualify a complete 5‐GW cable system. The outputs are architecture‐specific conditions for further engineering and project appraisal, not estimates of demonstrated avoided corridor expenditure.

title: Moving downstream in responsible innovation: seven building blocks for responsible scaling strategies
summary: Responsible innovation (RI) has mainly focused on decision-making in the ‘upstream’ and ‘midstream’ of science, technology, and innovation, which emphasize agenda-setting for research and development. The ‘downstream,’ in which innovations
content: Responsible innovation (RI) has mainly focused on decision-making in the ‘upstream’ and ‘midstream’ of science, technology, and innovation, which emphasize agenda-setting for research and development. The ‘downstream,’ in which innovations spread and become embedded in society, has received little attention. We argue that RI scholarship and practice should engage in governing the downstream, where decision-making around the scaling of innovations preordains societal impacts. This article introduces the concept of responsible scaling (RS), which denotes practices that reflexively attend to distributed impacts of the implementation of innovations; seek to anticipate unintended effects; involve diverse actors, views, and values; and flexibly steer the spread of innovations in the light of changing circumstances. To promote the development, implementation, and adaptation of RS strategies, we identify seven ‘building blocks’ and discuss their individual merits. Importantly, RS opens up questions as to how scaling is framed and approached to challenge market imperatives and technological determinism.

title: Property rights after flooding: post-disaster land policy in Türkiye and Germany
summary: Flood recovery involves not only rebuilding but reorganizing land, property rights, and long-term development. Yet the role of land policy in post-flood reconstruction remains underexplored. This paper compares responses to the 2021 floods
content: Flood recovery involves not only rebuilding but reorganizing land, property rights, and long-term development. Yet the role of land policy in post-flood reconstruction remains underexplored. This paper compares responses to the 2021 floods in Türkiye and Germany to examine how land policy priorities – land-use regulation, and property protection – shape reconstruction, showing that outcomes hinge on how land-use decisions (allocation) align with ownership and compensation (distribution). Türkiye enabled rapid spatial change through strong state intervention, whereas Germany largely preserved existing settlement structures. The comparison shows how post-disaster land policy influences whether recovery transforms flooded areas or restores them largely as before.

title: Indonesia in the global economy - is institutional change making it more or less resilience to external shocks?
summary: The US-Iran war is the latest adverse development in an external environment that is becoming more challenging for Indonesia. Prabowo’s improbable 8 percent target growth by 2029 will require substantial improvements in productivity and muc
content: The US-Iran war is the latest adverse development in an external environment that is becoming more challenging for Indonesia. Prabowo’s improbable 8 percent target growth by 2029 will require substantial improvements in productivity and much higher foreign investment. Prabowo’s centralised, state-led, universalist, and impatient approach to programs and institutional change lacks planning and prioritisation. Expanded political control of the institutions that promote good governance threatens to weaken the institutions that have served Indonesia well. This survey considers how these trends are affecting the fiscal balance, financial stability and economic depth, which are central to Indonesia’s ability to manage external shocks. Despite investments aimed at increasing self-sufficiency, and changes that could improve the efficiency of State-Owned Enterprises and crowd in private sector activity, it is far from guaranteed. Moreover, the expanding role of the state diverts attention from structural and regulatory reforms and dampens market confidence. The fiscal space to respond to a crisis is under greater pressure, and recentralisation is reducing local institutional capacity to manage shocks. While the economy may be able to recover from most external shocks, the government is vulnerable to the domestic unrest from mismanaging the consequences of these shocks.

title: Model Ekosistem Keuangan Islam Berbasis Rantai Nilai untuk Penguatan UMKM di Kota Tangerang
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan model ekosistem keuangan Islam berbasis rantai nilai yang sesuai dengan karakteristik UMKM di Kota Tangerang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan sintesis literatur dan pemet
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan model ekosistem keuangan Islam berbasis rantai nilai yang sesuai dengan karakteristik UMKM di Kota Tangerang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan sintesis literatur dan pemetaan konseptual terhadap keterkaitan pembiayaan Islam, halal value chain, digitalisasi, penguatan kapasitas, kelembagaan, dan market linkage. Analisis dilakukan melalui proses kondensasi informasi, kategorisasi tema, pemetaan hubungan antarkomponen, serta sintesis model. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa intervensi pembiayaan yang berdiri sendiri berpotensi menghasilkan dampak yang terbatas apabila tidak diikuti peningkatan kapabilitas internal dan akses terhadap rantai nilai. Berdasarkan sintesis tersebut dikembangkan model Tangerang Sharia Economic Link (TSEL) yang terdiri atas enam tahapan, yaitu mapping, assessment, upgrading, linking, scaling, dan impact. Model mengintegrasikan pemerintah sebagai orkestrator, lembaga keuangan Islam sebagai financial linkage, UMKM sebagai aktor pencipta nilai, lembaga halal sebagai penguat assurance, dunia usaha sebagai off-taker, perguruan tinggi sebagai pusat pengetahuan, serta komunitas sebagai modal sosial. Kontribusi penelitian terletak pada integrasi ekosistem keuangan Islam dengan halal value chain dan market linkage pada tingkat lokal, dengan Maqasid al-Shariah sebagai kerangka evaluasi dampak.

title: Notes towards an ethos of repair and the making of other worlds
summary: Our notes towards an ethos of repair emerged from the collective sense-making exercise that took place in Lund, Sweden, where a group of researchers and activists met to discuss notions of repair and retrofitting. Each person shared a text
content: Our notes towards an ethos of repair emerged from the collective sense-making exercise that took place in Lund, Sweden, where a group of researchers and activists met to discuss notions of repair and retrofitting. Each person shared a text reflecting on their engaged research and work on how local knowledges shape forms of making home and repair in underserved neighbourhoods, how this knowledge and practice connects to an ethics of care and how practices expand or contest understandings of urban climate mitigation and adaptation and just transitions. Over two days, we engaged deeply with each other’s texts and brought together our collective thinking on repair.

title: Re-evaluating donor-cell identity after hiPSC-RGC transplantation in mouse models of optic neuropathy
summary: ABSTRACT Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by permanent visual field loss caused by the death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. We investigated the poten
content: ABSTRACT Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by permanent visual field loss caused by the death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. We investigated the potential of transplanting human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived RGCs (hiPSC-RGCs) in two mouse models of optic nerve degeneration: N -Methyl-D-Aspartate (NMDA) and optic nerve crush (ONC), and characterized their ability to survive, integrate, and form synaptic connections in a degenerated retina. Follow-up studies, including immunohistochemistry and patch-clamping experiments, one year after intravitreal injections, determined the location, identity, and function of the donor GFP +ve fluorescent cells within the mouse retinas and their similarity to native RGCs. Upon closer inspection, some GFP +ve cells detected in a few retinal sections did not stain for the human-specific marker and were detected in retinal layers outside the expected ganglion cell layer (GCL)/ inner nuclear layer (INL) regions. These findings highlight complications in the interpretation of RGC transplantation studies.

title: Assessment of a Rural Water Supply System: A Basis for Sustainable Water Resource Management
source: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
summary: This study assessed the water supply systems in the Municipality of Alcala, Cagayan, Philippines, to support sustainable water resource management, focusing on socio-demographic conditions, infrastructure status (groundwater sources, pipeli
content: This study assessed the water supply systems in the Municipality of Alcala, Cagayan, Philippines, to support sustainable water resource management, focusing on socio-demographic conditions, infrastructure status (groundwater sources, pipeline distribution, storage, and treatment), water quality compliance with Philippine National Standards for Drinking Water (PNSDW), and governance aspects such as availability, quality, affordability, and responsiveness. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines surveys, laboratory analysis, statistical tools, interviews, and field observations selected barangays, the findings revealed significant disparities in access, infrastructure, and management. Groundwater is still the main source, but many systems lack permits, monitoring equipment and adequate safeguards against contamination, especially during floods. Many barangays have no formal systems, and there are those that have partial coverage, limited treatment and inconsistent maintenance. Water quality is monitored, but treatment is still inadequate. Communities are concerned about reliability, affordability, and governance. Water resources are available, but sustainability is challenged by infrastructure gaps, weak regulation, climate risks and limited technical capacity pointing to the need for better governance, infrastructure development, better water quality management and climate resilient, community-based approaches.

title: Institutional decoupling in local health-system planning: a cross- sectional study of strategic plan implementation across five Tanzanian local government authorities
summary: Abstract Background Local governments are central to implementing health-sector plans in decentralised systems, but formal adoption of strategic plans does not necessarily translate into operational action. This study assessed the extent an
content: Abstract Background Local governments are central to implementing health-sector plans in decentralised systems, but formal adoption of strategic plans does not necessarily translate into operational action. This study assessed the extent and correlates of perceived strategic plan implementation in selected Tanzanian local government authorities (LGAs), with particular attention to the gap between formal planning, monitoring and corrective action. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 385 officials involved in planning, execution, monitoring, financial management, or stakeholder engagement in five LGAs across four regions. A 17-item, theory-guided and pilot-tested instrument measured four implementation dimensions: awareness and adoption, activity implementation, monitoring and feedback, and stakeholder participation. Descriptive statistics, Friedman and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis tests, and hierarchical ordinary least squares regression with HC3 robust standard errors were used. Because LGAs and respondents were purposively selected, inferential results are interpreted as associations within the study sample rather than population-representative estimates. Results Overall perceived implementation was high (mean 3.770, SD 0.611). Awareness and adoption had the highest dimension mean (3.842), whereas activity implementation had the lowest (3.694). Timely corrective action was the weakest individual item (mean 3.421), despite relatively strong data collection and reporting. No statistically detectable differences were observed across the five LGAs or four regions. In the adjusted model, departmental affiliation accounted for the largest incremental increase in explained variance; health and planning departments reported higher implementation scores than administration. Longer professional experience and direct execution involvement were associated with more critical implementation assessments. These patterns are consistent with, but do not by themselves establish, institutional decoupling between formal planning arrangements and operational follow-through. Conclusions The principal implementation challenge in the selected LGAs appears to lie less in the existence or awareness of strategic plans than in the mechanisms that convert monitoring information into timely operational adjustment. Strengthening managerial decision space, predictable resource flows, cross-departmental coordination and corrective-action routines may improve the connection between formal health plans and service-delivery action. Findings should be interpreted in light of the cross-sectional design, purposive sampling and reliance on self-reported implementation.

title: Explainable Federated Learning: Detecting Drift with Feature-Level Attribution Using SAGE
source: Communications in computer and information science
summary: Loss curves alone provide limited insights into feature attributions and model behavior in Federated Learning (FL), making it challenging to diagnose performance degradation. To address this, we propose a novel framework that leverages Shap
content: Loss curves alone provide limited insights into feature attributions and model behavior in Federated Learning (FL), making it challenging to diagnose performance degradation. To address this, we propose a novel framework that leverages Shapley Additive Global importancE (SAGE) to attribute model performance to individual features by analyzing their impact on the loss. By extending SAGE to a federated setting, we gain a more detailed understanding of feature attributions across decentralized clients. Building on this capability, our approach detects drift by analyzing shifts over time in the distributions of loss and feature attributions contributed by each client. Our approach allows us to pinpoint which features exhibit significant drift and identify those most contributing to model degradation, thereby facilitating targeted interventions. Across six datasets spanning synthetic and real-world domains, our framework achieves an average detection F1-score of 0.97 with an average delay of 1.9 rounds, consistently matching or outperforming standard drift detection methods while retaining fine-grained, feature-level drift interpretability. Furthermore, Federated SAGE approximates centralized SAGE with mean absolute error typically below 0.01, enabling accurate drift explanation in federated settings.

title: Impact Studies of Digitalisation and Digital Transformation on Innovation Management Practices
source: International Journal of Applied Mathematics Computational Science and Systems Engineering
summary: This research examines how digital transformation has affected innovation management (IM) across different industries. The main goal is to look at how integrating digital technologies affects innovation results and processes within organisa
content: This research examines how digital transformation has affected innovation management (IM) across different industries. The main goal is to look at how integrating digital technologies affects innovation results and processes within organisations. To provide a thorough knowledge of the relationship between digital transformation and innovation management, this research uses a mixed-methods approach that combines qualitative analysis of interview data with quantitative evaluation of data. The study emphasises how crucial digital transformation is becoming as an imperative for organisations looking to strengthen their capacity for innovation. Themes from qualitative interviews, including "Cultural Adaptation," "Collaborative Synergy," and "Agile Practices," shed insight on the qualitative aspects of the impact of digital transformation on innovation management. To find correlations between digital transformation activities and innovative success measures, quantitative data analysis involves looking at survey responses from industry specialists, which are then subjected to statistical analysis. The findings highlight the critical part played by digital transformation in forming innovation management strategies. Effectively embracing digital transformation puts organisations in a better position to negotiate the changing terrain of technology disruption, react to market changes, and foster creativity. Insights from this study can help practitioners and decision-makers who want to use the power of digital transformation to support their innovation efforts.

title: “She likes being good, and i like being happy”
summary: During the Gilded Age, happiness, though a private pursuit, was socially codified in terms of wealth and respectability. In The House of Mirth (1905), Edith Wharton presents Lily Bart, whose beauty and charms are treated as assets for secur
content: During the Gilded Age, happiness, though a private pursuit, was socially codified in terms of wealth and respectability. In The House of Mirth (1905), Edith Wharton presents Lily Bart, whose beauty and charms are treated as assets for securing a wealthy husband. Torn between social expectations and her desire for pleasure, Lily admits: “She likes being good, and I like being happy.” Yet her happiness is fleeting, sustained through gambling, parties, and aesthetic enjoyment, rather than through marriage. Drawing on definitions of happiness and affect theory, this essay examines Lily’s evanescent gratifications as strategies to resist society’s restrictive rules, which denies marriageable women the possibility of love and independence. Her social transgressions lead to exclusion from elite circles and descent into poverty. Confronted with new sorrows, Lily gains wisdom, realizing her diversions never brought fulfillment. Her final act of self-destruction emerges as both tragic defeat and defiance of imposed models of feminine happiness.

title: Modelling the Dynamics between Life Expectancy, Economic Growth, Renewable Energy Transition, and Carbon Footprints in BRICS Economies
summary: With rapid economic growth in BRICS, significant concerns about sustainability and climate change have emerged. However, changing demographics, longer lifespans, and the growing adoption of renewable energy have shifted growth’s environment
content: With rapid economic growth in BRICS, significant concerns about sustainability and climate change have emerged. However, changing demographics, longer lifespans, and the growing adoption of renewable energy have shifted growth’s environmental impacts. Using a panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach, robust cointegration analyses establish the long-run relationship between the constructs. The ARDL panel estimates that higher economic growth (GDP) indicates greater affluence, which, along with population growth, has positive long-run effects and therefore increases CO2 emissions. However, these effects were offset by the adverse effects of increased renewable energy consumption, which reflects technological progress, and life expectancy, which reflects demographic transition, in controlling emissions. In contrast, the causality analysis provides evidence of bidirectional causality between GDP and CO2 emissions, suggesting a complex interaction. Furthermore, this study finds that renewable energy consumption, population growth, and life expectancy individually have unidirectional causal effects on CO2 emissions. Robustness estimates using fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) and dynamic ordinary least squares (DOLS) support the ARDL hypothesis. These results support the applicability of the Impact = Population × Affluence × Technology (IPAT) model, with proper consideration of the mutual interactions among population, affluence, and technology in determining the key drivers of ecological impact.

title: Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Thermo-Hydraulic Performance Enhancement of Water-Cooled Photovoltaic Modules Using a Helical Pipe Network with Twisted Tape Inserts
summary: High and spatially non-uniform temperatures reduce the electrical output of photovoltaic (PV) modules and accelerate hotspot-related degradation. While previous research has looked into water-cooled PV/T systems and the use of twisted-tape
content: High and spatially non-uniform temperatures reduce the electrical output of photovoltaic (PV) modules and accelerate hotspot-related degradation. While previous research has looked into water-cooled PV/T systems and the use of twisted-tape inserts as separate solutions, there's a noticeable absence of studies that combine these approaches. Specifically, there is a lack of investigation into optimizing the arrangement of cooling pipes before incorporating internal flow enhancements. Moreover, experimental evidence is essential to confirm if such a dual strategy can genuinely improve the performance without imposing significant hydraulic disadvantages. This research directly tackles these issues by introducing and validating a two-step optimization strategy for water-cooled PV/T modules. Our work commenced with a computational assessment of four different helical pipe arrangements (100 × 150, 100 × 100, 100 × 50, and 80 × 80 mm). After this initial evaluation, the most promising configuration was further refined by adding either four or ten twisted-tape inserts. The best-performing layout was then enhanced using four and ten twisted-tape inserts. Simulations in three dimensions, investigating conjugate heat transfer, were performed using ANSYS Fluent. These simulations were carried out under a heat flux load of 800 W/m², with incoming water at a temperature of 25 °C, and across a range of Reynolds numbers from 5,000 to 11,000. The configuration featuring an 80 × 80 mm layout emerged as the optimal baseline. This setup successfully lowered the average temperature of the PV surface to 45.62 °C when the Reynolds number was 11,000. Concurrently, it achieved an electrical efficiency of 16.05% and an electrical power output of 205.49 W. The subsequent introduction of ten twisted-tape inserts led to a further reduction in temperature, bringing it down to 42.30 °C. This enhancement also boosted the electrical efficiency to 16.44% and the power output to 210.48 W. To confirm these findings, experimental validation was conducted. The results from these experiments showed mean absolute percentage errors of 1.46% for the baseline setup and a slightly lower 1.23% for the configuration enhanced with inserts. An important consideration, the pumping power required for these systems remained below 3 W across all tested conditions. The distinct contribution of this research lies in its comprehensive approach, which unifies several key aspects within a single design framework. This includes optimizing the helical pipe layout, harnessing the flow enhancement provided by twisted tapes, evaluating the uniformity of temperature, and undertaking experimental validation of the thermo-hydraulic performance. This integrated methodology effectively demonstrates that improvements in hotspot management and overall electrical performance can be realized without incurring substantial demands on hydraulic energy.

title: Politička ekonomija zelene tranzicije kao reformskog procesa: pregled literature s osvrtom na EU i Zapadni Balkan
summary: Zelena tranzicija, kao sustavni prijelaz s gospodarstava ovisnih o fosilnim gorivima prema nisko ugljičnim i održivim sustavima, sve se češće prepoznaje ne samo kao tehnološki izazov, već i kao reformski proces pod utjecajem brojnih ekonoms
content: Zelena tranzicija, kao sustavni prijelaz s gospodarstava ovisnih o fosilnim gorivima prema nisko ugljičnim i održivim sustavima, sve se češće prepoznaje ne samo kao tehnološki izazov, već i kao reformski proces pod utjecajem brojnih ekonomskih, političkih i institucionalnih faktora. Ovaj pregledni rad donosi prikaz literature iz područja političke ekonomije zelene tranzicije. Rad je strukturiran oko četiri međusobno povezana analitička stupa: (1) uloge države i institucionalnih okvira u poticanju ili blokiranju zelenih reformi; (2) utjecaja različitih interesnih skupina, dominantnih postojećih industrija i novih koalicija na odabir specifičnih tranzicijskih putanja; (3) utjecaja geopolitičkih turbulencija na brzinu i smjer zelene tranzicije; te (4) specifičnih iskustava Europske unije (EU) i zemalja Zapadnog Balkana kao ilustrativnih primjera međudjelovanja navedenih sila u praksi. Polazeći od uvida iz politologije, institucionalne ekonomije i komparativne političke ekonomije, rad sumira teorijske okvire poput koncepta zelene države, pristupa socio-tehničkih tranzicija, tipova kapitalizma i političke ekonomije reformi. U radu se ujedno i identificiraju nedovoljno istraženi aspekti političke ekonomije zelene tranzicije na Zapadnom Balkanu, uključujući pitanja demokratske legitimnosti i tehnokratskog upravljanja klimatskim politikama te potrebe za sustavnijom komparativnom analizom mehanizama kroz koje različite institucionalne i političke strukture među zemljama utječu na ishode. Mapiranjem ovog kompleksnog istraživačkog područja kroz prizmu političke ekonomije, rad pruža osnovu za buduća istraživanja o tome kako države, interesne skupine i geopolitičke sile oblikuju višedimenzionalan proces zelene tranzicije.

title: Integrated Pinch–Life Cycle Assessment Framework for Energy and Environmental Optimization of Industrial Processes toward Carbon Neutrality
source: Journal of Sustainable Development of Energy Water and Environment Systems
summary: This study presents an integrated framework combining thermal pinch analysis and life cycle assessment to evaluate energy-intensive industrial processes, addressing the need to capture both operational efficiency and environmental impacts.
content: This study presents an integrated framework combining thermal pinch analysis and life cycle assessment to evaluate energy-intensive industrial processes, addressing the need to capture both operational efficiency and environmental impacts. The goal is to determine whether energy savings from process integration justify associated environmental burdens. The method links utility targets and heat exchanger network designs to life-cycle inventory data, while explicitly including heat exchanger manufacturing impacts. Three industrial cases - ammonia, bioethanol, and hydrogen production from biomass-based resources - were analysed. Results show energy use reductions of 62.27–76.05% and cost savings of 45.81–65.38%. Environmental impacts, including global warming and resource depletion, decreased significantly, although minor trade-offs appeared in ozone depletion and mineral resource use due to added equipment. The framework reveals hidden burden shifting and supports transparent decision-making for industrial decarbonization strategies.

title: Adaptive Thermal Comfort and Acceptable Temperature Range in Naturally Ventilated School Classrooms
summary: This study examined thermal sensation and acceptability among secondary-school students in naturally ventilated government-school classrooms in Raipur, Chhattisgarh. Environmental measurements and students' thermal perceptions and preferenc
content: This study examined thermal sensation and acceptability among secondary-school students in naturally ventilated government-school classrooms in Raipur, Chhattisgarh. Environmental measurements and students' thermal perceptions and preferences were collected during classroom surveys, yielding 860 valid responses from students aged 13–18 years. The surveys covered nine classrooms in seven schools during three field campaigns in April, July, and September 2025, producing 17 classroom-by-condition measurement occasions. Classroom clustering was addressed in the reported models, although the small number of classroom-level environmental conditions limits inference. The Griffiths neutral temperature was 30.4 ℃ (95% CI 29.7–31.1) at G = 0.5 and ranged from 29.0 to 30.4 ℃ across the tested constants. Regression gave a comfort temperature of 28.3 ℃, with a sensitivity of 0.194 sensation-scale units/℃. The modelled upper air-temperature threshold for 80% acceptability was 29.4 ℃ (95% CI 28.6–30.4). Mean PMV was 1.68, compared with a mean reported thermal sensation of 0.72; predicted dissatisfaction was 54%, compared with 41% classified as unacceptable using the survey comfort scale. Clothing insulation was negatively associated with air temperature (−0.030 clo/℃). The exploratory socio-economic analysis did not establish a robust association with acceptability after adjustment for classroom differences. These findings provide local indoor comfort and acceptability estimates. They do not validate an outdoor-temperature-based adaptive model or establish a reduction in mechanical cooling demand.
