content: This article compares Uzbekistan’s implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Convention on Biological Diversity and the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification through a review of legislation, official reports and project records. Between 2010 and 2022, greenhouse gas emissions per unit of gross domestic product (GDP) fell while total emissions rose. At Sudochye, legal protection and wetland designation document a change in status. On the former Aral Sea bed, planting records document the scale of restoration work. The study identifies indicators for tracking environmental outcomes, including waterbird abundance and the survival of planted vegetation.

title: Compelled Flexibility and Lock‐in to Dispersion? Imperatives in Japan’s Energy Policy
summary: In the wake of the war in Ukraine, escalating tariff regimes, and instability in the Middle East, rethinking the relationship between energy security and the energy transition has become imperative. This article examines Japan’s energy poli
content: In the wake of the war in Ukraine, escalating tariff regimes, and instability in the Middle East, rethinking the relationship between energy security and the energy transition has become imperative. This article examines Japan’s energy policy as a critical case in which the pursuit of energy security under severe structural constraints can give rise to a form of “compelled flexibility” that drives the simultaneous pursuit of diverse technological pathways beyond mere industrial preference—an “institutionalization of optionality.” It further identifies a risk inherent in this institutionalization: as contractual, organizational, fiscal, and diplomatic commitments accumulate across parallel pathways, institutions intended to stabilize energy security can paradoxically internalize a “lock-in to dispersion,” progressively raising the costs of future convergence. The article argues for governance designs that enable technological convergence in a way that is functional to decarbonization.

title: Swedish Consumers’ Preferences for Tofu Sustainability Characteristics: A Choice Experiment with Information Treatments
summary: For achieving a higher share of plant-based proteins in the diets of people in high-income countries, a better understanding of consumers’ preferences for meat alternatives is needed. Using a choice experiment with around 1,400 Swedish cons
content: For achieving a higher share of plant-based proteins in the diets of people in high-income countries, a better understanding of consumers’ preferences for meat alternatives is needed. Using a choice experiment with around 1,400 Swedish consumers, we investigate preferences for local and organic tofu and examine the effect on preferences when providing information about different aspects of tofu consumption (health, environment, culinary). While we do not find any effects of information on preferences, a latent class analysis indicates the existence of heterogeneous preference classes with a substantial share of consumers willing to pay for tofu and for sustainability attributes. The results contribute to the existing evidence on preferences for meat alternatives and sustainable consumption and can assist policy makers in designing sustainable food policies as well as information campaigns.

title: Epitaxial Ga/ZSM-5@S-1 core–shell zeolites boost CO 2 -coupled propane aromatization
summary: Epitaxial Ga/ZSM-5@S-1 core–shell zeolites spatially separate active sites, enhancing CO 2 conversion and BTX formation in CO 2 -coupled propane aromatization.
content: Epitaxial Ga/ZSM-5@S-1 core–shell zeolites spatially separate active sites, enhancing CO 2 conversion and BTX formation in CO 2 -coupled propane aromatization.

title: Carbon nanotube and graphene-based nanomaterials for perovskite solar cells
summary: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have surpassed 27% power conversion efficiency, yet long-term stability and scalable manufacturing remain key barriers to commercialization. Carbon nanotubes (CNTs), graphene, and their derivatives offer promis
content: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have surpassed 27% power conversion efficiency, yet long-term stability and scalable manufacturing remain key barriers to commercialization. Carbon nanotubes (CNTs), graphene, and their derivatives offer promising solutions owing to their excellent electrical, optical, and mechanical properties. This review highlights their applications in PSC electrodes, charge-transport layers, and interfaces, focusing on charge extraction, interface engineering, and device stability. Key challenges, including film uniformity, reproducibility, and large-area fabrication, are also discussed, along with strategies for developing efficient, durable, and scalable carbon-based PSCs.

title: Binary Ni–Cu metal–organic framework@carbon nanotube hybrid for high-performance supercapacitors and efficient water splitting
summary: for the OER, confirming accelerated charge-transfer processes and efficient catalytic pathways. The NiCu-MOF@CNT electrode also maintained high durability during continuous HER/OER operation for 20 h. Additionally, the overall cell voltage
content: for the OER, confirming accelerated charge-transfer processes and efficient catalytic pathways. The NiCu-MOF@CNT electrode also maintained high durability during continuous HER/OER operation for 20 h. Additionally, the overall cell voltage of the two-electrode electrolyzer was determined using a DC power supply. The NiCu-MOF@CNT/NF‖NiCu-MOF@CNT/NF system required a cell voltage of 2.1 V to deliver a current of 10 mA, demonstrating its effective catalytic activity toward overall alkaline water splitting.

title: Utilization of Shrimp Shell–Derived Chitosan‐Based Activated Carbon for the Removal of Wastewater Pollutants
summary: Water pollution remains a pressing environmental challenge, particularly due to the discharge of inadequately treated industrial effluents that threaten environmental integrity and public health. This preliminary study evaluated shrimp shel
content: Water pollution remains a pressing environmental challenge, particularly due to the discharge of inadequately treated industrial effluents that threaten environmental integrity and public health. This preliminary study evaluated shrimp shell‐derived chitosan‐based activated carbon (SS‐CAC) as a low‐cost biosorbent for improving selected physicochemical parameters of rubber industry wastewater. SS‐CAC was synthesized, characterized by Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and applied through batch biosorption at contact times of 15 and 30 min. Wastewater samples were analyzed before and after treatment for temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), biochemical oxygen demand (BOD 5 ), total suspended solids (TSS), turbidity, chloride, sulphate and copper (Cu). Dissolved oxygen increased from 2.78 mg/L to 5.02 mg/L, representing an improvement of approximately 81% after 30 min; this value is reported as an increase, not as a removal efficiency. BOD 5 , turbidity, TSS, chloride, sulphate and Cu decreased after treatment, with TSS showing the highest reduction of approximately 85% after 30 min. However, Cu remained above the NWQS compliance limit after treatment, indicating that SS‐CAC improved but did not fully remediate metal contamination under the tested conditions. Because independent adsorption controls and commercial activated‐carbon benchmarking were not included, the results are interpreted descriptively as proof‐of‐concept screening rather than a statistically validated treatment claim. The findings suggest that shrimp shell waste can be valorized into a functional adsorbent, while further replicated and controlled studies are required to confirm adsorption mechanisms, equilibrium behavior, scalability and environmental sustainability.

title: Microstructure Engineering of Organic Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors, an Emerging Toolbox for Performance Enhancement and New Applications
summary: Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have attracted growing attention for biointegrated electronics and human-robot interfaces because they can transduce ionic signals into electronic outputs, while offering mechanical complia
content: Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have attracted growing attention for biointegrated electronics and human-robot interfaces because they can transduce ionic signals into electronic outputs, while offering mechanical compliance for seamless integration with soft biological systems. Achieving high-performance in OMIEC-based devices requires precise control over structural parameters across multiple length scales, from molecular-level chemical structure to macroscopic device architecture. Particularly, because OMIECs operate through direct contact with electrolytes and rely on coupled ionic and electronic transport, microstructural engineering provides a powerful strategy to regulate the electrolyte-OMIEC interface, ion-transport pathways, and volumetric doping behavior, thereby bridging molecular design and device-level architecture. In this review, we categorize microstructural engineering strategies for OMIECs across different length scales, ranging from nanoscale phase-separated domains to microscale porous and three-dimensional architectures, and discuss the underlying structure-formation mechanisms and key processing parameters of each approach. Using organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) as a benchmark platform, we summarize how these strategies have been implemented to enhance device performance and enable new functionalities, while also highlighting their limitations and remaining challenges. Finally, we examine applications of microstructured OMIECs beyond OECTs, focusing on electrochromic devices, and discuss future directions for establishing a deeper understanding of microstructure-property relationships in mixed ionic-electronic conducting materials.

title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
summary: Abstract van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies 1–4 . Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstr
content: Abstract van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies 1–4 . Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases 2,5,6 . However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space 7–12 ), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: From Triple Bottom Line (TBL) to Supply Chain Triple Value Bottom Line (SCTVBL): A Sustainable Supply Chain Value Framework
summary: In today's competitive business environment where consumers increasingly expect transparency, quality, and value for money, buying a product means interacting with the entire supply chain. As the modern supply chains become more autonomous
content: In today's competitive business environment where consumers increasingly expect transparency, quality, and value for money, buying a product means interacting with the entire supply chain. As the modern supply chains become more autonomous and interconnected, the effective measurement of their business value necessitates transitioning from the conventional efficiency‐based business models to more holistic, stakeholder‐focused business models. In this regard, although the triple bottom line (TBL) framework offers sustainability of the supply chains via economic, social, and environmental performance dimensions, it does not segregate and comprehensively capture value for the key supply chain stakeholders, thereby disregarding the important stakeholders like employees, customers, suppliers, and partners. Therefore, by evaluating the gaps in the extant supply chain management literature coupled with analyzing, critiquing, and synthesizing the current supply chain performance frameworks, and drawing upon the guiding theories, this research introduces a novel concept, “supply chain triple value bottom line” (SCTVBL), and subsequently presents a SCTVBL framework. While addressing the evolving performance needs of the contemporary supply chains, the proposed framework further extends the conventional TBL framework by offering value‐oriented supply chains perspective. As a whole, by suggesting organizational value creation (via economic value, operational value, and employee value), socio‐environmental value creation (via social value and environmental value), and relational value creation (via customer value and supplier & partner value) as renewed supply chain value dimensions, the SCTVBL framework offers a more stakeholder‐focused perspective for holistically addressing the value creation needs of the supply chain stakeholders. Although the proposed SCTVBL framework is conceptual in nature, it opens new avenues for future theoretical research and empirical practice, thereby paving the way for policy renewals, revitalized industry practices and improved SDG contributions.

title: Solar Radiation Assessment in Guangxi Based on Geostationary Satellite Observations
summary: Surface solar radiation is a key parameter driving the energy cycle of the Earth system and is crucial for agriculture, ecology, climate, and the development and utilization of solar energy. This study compares and validates the high spatio
content: Surface solar radiation is a key parameter driving the energy cycle of the Earth system and is crucial for agriculture, ecology, climate, and the development and utilization of solar energy. This study compares and validates the high spatiotemporal resolution shortwave radiation products from the Japanese Himawari-8 satellite with ground-based observations from three national stations in Nanning, Beihai and Guilin in Guangxi, China. The results show that the shortwave radiation products from the Himawari-8 satellite are highly consistent with the ground-based observations, with a daily mean bias errors (MBE) of 11.20–15.18 W/m2, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 26.59–34.76 W/m2, and a coefficient of determination (R2 of 0.86–0.89. Significant differences in satellite inversion accuracy exist under different weather conditions. The inversion effect is best under clear weather conditions, with R² reaching 0.85–0.96. Based on these validated products, a high-resolution assessment of the spatial and temporal distribution of solar radiation over Guangxi was conducted, revealing that the annual average total solar radiation in Guangxi ranged from 4715.55 to 5873.55 MJ/m2 between 2019 and 2022. Spatially, solar radiation exhibited a clear decreasing gradient from south to north. In terms of monthly variation, a unimodal pattern was observed. This study confirms the effectiveness and reliability of geostationary satellite data for high-accuracy surface solar radiation monitoring in regions with complex topography, such as the karst landscapes of Guangxi. The findings provide important data support and a scientific basis for solar energy resource assessment and severe weather monitoring in Guangxi.

title: De-inking of surface printing ink on waste polypropylene (PP) milk tea cups using nonionic surfactants
summary: Printing ink on waste polypropylene (PP) milk tea cups severely hinders their high-value recycling. A novel aqueous deinking system was developed with alkyl polyglucoside (APG)/Tween-80 (T-80) as composite surfactants and an eco-friendly mi
content: Printing ink on waste polypropylene (PP) milk tea cups severely hinders their high-value recycling. A novel aqueous deinking system was developed with alkyl polyglucoside (APG)/Tween-80 (T-80) as composite surfactants and an eco-friendly mixed solvent of butyl acetate and dipropylene glycol ethyl ether (DPE). Deinking parameters were optimized via single-factor experiments and Box–Behnken response surface methodology, achieving a deinking efficiency of 93.45% under the optimal conditions: 3 wt.% surfactant, 13 wt.% organic solvent, 48°C and 56 min. XRD characterization confirmed the intact α-crystal structure of PP after deinking. Mechanical properties tests showed that the impact strength of deinked PP was significantly recovered, while the bending and tensile strengths were essentially restored to the level of virgin PP. The deinking process followed a synergistic mechanism of solvent penetration, resin swelling, competitive adsorption, roll-up and emulsification. The efficient, low-damage and eco-friendly deinking system provides a promising technical approach for the high-value recycling of printed waste PP, facilitating the development of a circular plastic economy.

title: Data-driven edge intelligence in electric mobility: from battery health forecasting to high-speed autonomous control
source: AMS Dottorato Institutional Doctoral Theses Repository (University of Bologna)
summary: Electric mobility is changing how people and goods move. Both electric cars and autonomous drones face a shared limit: their batteries. Lab tests cannot fully capture how these limits appear in real-world use. This thesis addresses that gap
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: Electric mobility is changing how people and goods move. Both electric cars and autonomous drones face a shared limit: their batteries. Lab tests cannot fully capture how these limits appear in real-world use. This thesis addresses that gap using data collected directly from the vehicles. Human driving behaviors were studied in passenger cars, with over 2.3 million data points collected from a Nissan Leaf using a custom data-logging device. The results show that rapid acceleration and other demanding behaviors raise battery temperature and accelerate cell aging. A Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory model was developed to predict battery temperature, capturing the dynamic effects of real-world driving. These findings were then applied to autonomous drone racing. A vision-only system enables drones to fly at high speed without Global Positioning System localization, and a Reinforcement Learning controller achieves performance beyond human limits. However, such "bang-bang" aggressive control rapidly degrades batteries, with most cells failing in fewer than 20 flights. Building on these insights, the thesis introduces "Energy-Aware Autonomy". A framework that integrates battery prediction with control systems to maintain high performance while reducing the risk of battery damage.

title: A robust machine learning framework for multitemporal bare soil monitoring with high temporal transferability
summary: Accurate monitoring of land degradation is critical for achieving land degradation neutrality, yet multitemporal assessments often suffer from low temporal transferability and threshold-related biases. Here, we present a robust machine lear
content: Accurate monitoring of land degradation is critical for achieving land degradation neutrality, yet multitemporal assessments often suffer from low temporal transferability and threshold-related biases. Here, we present a robust machine learning framework to quantify long-term bare soil dynamics (1985–2020) across tropical drylands in Sucre, Colombia. Using Landsat time series, we evaluated Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and Logistic Regression (LR) ML models under three experimental strategies: year-specific assessment, interannual cross-validation, and combined multitemporal training. A total of 11,308 labeled samples were used for model calibration, and vegetation and soil indices were used as ancillary layers for sample support and quality control. SVM maps were additionally validated with 22,000 independent samples. Our results show a marked expansion of bare soil between 1985 and 2001 (+ 25,504 ha; + 53%), followed by a further increase from 2001 to 2010 (+ 53,351 ha; + 71.7%) and a subsequent reduction by 2020 (–28,475 ha; –22%). Although all models achieve high within-year accuracy, SVM showed the most consistent temporal generalization and external validation performance, with accuracy above 98% and Kappa values close to 1 across decades. Spectral contribution analysis identified Red, Green, and shortwave infrared (SWIR2) bands as the most informative predictors. In contrast, NDVI-based reclassification underestimated persistent bare soil by more than 96% relative to the multivariate ML approach. By integrating interannual validation, threshold-sensitivity analysis, and GIS-based persistence mapping, the proposed framework effectively distinguishes transient seasonal exposure from chronic degradation hotspots. These findings provide a scalable and transferable Earth observation workflow to support evidence-based territorial planning and soil conservation in vulnerable tropical landscapes.

title: The public value in private housing: energy efficiency as a common good
summary: Houses are important components of energy and health systems. They constitute ~33% of energy demand, contribute disproportionately to peak electricity loads, and affect occupant health/wellbeing. Even modest housing quality improvements can
content: Houses are important components of energy and health systems. They constitute ~33% of energy demand, contribute disproportionately to peak electricity loads, and affect occupant health/wellbeing. Even modest housing quality improvements can reduce energy use, peak electricity demand, and carbon emissions, and improve health outcomes and societal equity. However, high-quality housing — with sufficient space, appropriate insulation, draught-proof exteriors, and efficient heating/cooling — is inequitably distributed. We frame building efficiency as a ‘common good’: it can provide net societal benefits substantially exceeding implementation costs and individual benefits. We argue for societal provision up to the point societal costs exceed benefits, which depends on cultural, geographic, economic, political, and infrastructural factors. We also outline a multidisciplinary research roadmap with four focus areas (Building physics; Behavioural and cultural considerations; Appropriate benefit-cost comparison; Economic and political context) to define sufficient energy-efficient housing and acknowledge its potential at the nexus of energy, health, community, and climate change.

title: Copper- and Chromium-Exchanged Faujasite Zeolites: Structure, Acidity and Catalytic Performance in Ethanol Conversion
summary: Cu- and Cr-exchanged faujasite catalysts were prepared by successive ion exchange of hydrothermally synthesised Na-FAU and evaluated for gas-phase ethanol conversion. The effects of metal exchange on the structure, porosity, acidity and cat
content: Cu- and Cr-exchanged faujasite catalysts were prepared by successive ion exchange of hydrothermally synthesised Na-FAU and evaluated for gas-phase ethanol conversion. The effects of metal exchange on the structure, porosity, acidity and catalytic behaviour of the FAU zeolite were investigated using PXRD, XRF, ICP-OES, SEM–EDS, N₂ physisorption, FTIR, Py-FTIR, ²⁷Al and ²⁹Si MAS NMR, NH₃-TPD and TGA/DTG. The FAU framework and characteristic crystal morphology were largely retained after Cu²⁺ and Cr³⁺ exchange, while no separate crystalline CuO or Cr₂O₃ phases were detected. The degrees of ion exchange were 74% for Cu-FAU and 42% for Cr-FAU. Metal incorporation moderately reduced the BET surface area from 721 m² g⁻¹ for Na-FAU to 654 and 628 m² g⁻¹ for Cu-FAU and Cr-FAU, respectively, without destroying the predominantly microporous structure. Py-FTIR showed that Cu exchange produced the largest relative increase in Lewis acidity, whereas NH₃-TPD indicated total acidities of 0.58, 0.84 and 0.91 mmol NH₃ g⁻¹ for Na-FAU, Cu-FAU and Cr-FAU, respectively. At 350°C, ethanol conversion reached 62% over Na-FAU, 91% over Cu-FAU and 79% over Cr-FAU. Cu-FAU favoured ethanol dehydration, providing 76% ethylene selectivity and a 69.2% ethylene yield. In contrast, Cr-FAU favoured dehydrogenation, achieving 63% acetaldehyde selectivity and a 49.8% yield. Cu-FAU also exhibited the highest stability, retaining 88% conversion after 24 hours and 95.6% of its initial activity after five reaction–regeneration cycles. These results demonstrate that ethanol conversion over metal-exchanged FAU catalysts is governed by the combined effects of metal-cation identity, acid-site nature and strength, degree of ion exchange and pore accessibility rather than by total acidity or surface area alone.

title: Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Survey of Foundations, Architectural Paradigms, Core Capabilities, and a Unified Reference Architecture
summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) integrates goal-directed decision-making, state continuity, planning, tool-mediated action, and feedback-driven adaptation into interactive computational systems. Although existing surveys examin
content: Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) integrates goal-directed decision-making, state continuity, planning, tool-mediated action, and feedback-driven adaptation into interactive computational systems. Although existing surveys examine agent capabilities, architectures, and applications, cross-paradigm comparisons often conflate functional capabilities with implementation mechanisms and organizational structures. This comprehensive narrative survey synthesizes foundational and contemporary research on symbolic/classical, neural/generative, neuro-symbolic, and multi-agent approaches to clarify conceptual boundaries and examine how agentic capabilities are architecturally realized. It organizes recurring functions into nine groups: goal and context management, perception and state representation, reasoning and decision-making, planning and replanning, memory and knowledge, action and tool use, evaluation and reflection, learning and adaptation, and coordination and orchestration. The principal contribution is an architecture-capability mapping separating functional responsibilities from computational mechanisms and coordination structures. A complementary conceptual reference architecture integrates goal management, environmental interaction, planning, memory, execution, evaluation, and cross-cutting assurance concerns. Representative cases demonstrate how different systems can realize similar functions using different mechanisms. The proposed taxonomy, formal abstraction, and reference architecture are analytical synthesis artifacts rather than experimentally validated models. They support transparent architectural comparison and identify testable research questions.

title: Foresight Workshop VET 2035: Documentation and retrospective of an expert panel on vocational education and training in the construction sector
summary: In December 2020, an international panel of 25 experts from 14 countries met online for two days to assess developments in the construction sector and to draft road maps for vocational education and training (VET) up to 2035. The workshop w
content: In December 2020, an international panel of 25 experts from 14 countries met online for two days to assess developments in the construction sector and to draft road maps for vocational education and training (VET) up to 2035. The workshop was held as part of the European Vocational Skills Week 2020. Its results were saved as whiteboard exports. This report documents the procedure, the panel and the results. It is based on a complete transcription of all exports, which is included as an appendix. The findings show that the panel used developments in the sector mainly as a starting point to discuss how, where and for whom learning should be organized. Recurring elements are a single access point to training, the recognition of short learning units across Europe, reliable funding and the value of skills for clients and workers. Although the workshop did not set up a group for the dimension „Individual“, the full coding assigns 25 of the 235 original contributions to that dimension, while the category for teachers and trainers as the subject of a contribution remains empty. A retrospective from 2026 compares the results with later developments. Several needs named by the panel have since been taken up in European policy. Generative artificial intelligence, however, does not appear on any board, and the coding of the corpus confirms this: none of the 235 original contributions names analytical or generative AI explicitly, while eight name automation, robotics or data without any method and are therefore technological connection points rather than references to AI. The report closes with the limitations of the documentation and links to related work.

title: Nanoscale Interface Engineering for Steering Charge Carrier Dynamics in Photoelectrochemical Sensing of Trace Organic Pollutants
summary: The precise manipulation of charge separation and transfer at nanoscale semiconductor surfaces and interfaces constitutes the central challenge-and the primary opportunity-for achieving high-performance photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing. T
content: The precise manipulation of charge separation and transfer at nanoscale semiconductor surfaces and interfaces constitutes the central challenge-and the primary opportunity-for achieving high-performance photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing. This challenge is particularly pronounced in environmental monitoring, where trace organic pollutants such as antibiotics, pesticides, and endocrine-disrupting chemicals demand platforms with high sensitivity, selectivity, and portability. Focusing on nanoscale surface and interface engineering that steers charge carrier dynamics, this review examines two interconnected themes: nanoconfined recognition interfaces-molecularly imprinted polymers and nucleic acid aptamers for direct and indirect transduction-and charge transport modulation across engineered nanoheterojunctions and catalytic nanointerfaces. Representative amplification strategies, including heterojunction engineering, electron donor-acceptor alignment, steric hindrance regulation, and nanozyme-assisted catalysis, are critically assessed for their charge-manipulation mechanisms and sensitivity gains. Recent progress in detecting these pollutants in complex matrices is surveyed. Persistent bottlenecks-charge recombination and photocorrosion-are examined alongside a roadmap for device integration and field deployment. By bridging nanoscale materials design with interfacial charge-transfer physics, this review provides a conceptual framework for next-generation autonomous PEC sensing systems.

title: Oxide-side lanthanum regulation enables trap-to-relay conversion of hydrogen spillover at MoO 2 /Ni 4 Mo interfaces
summary: Efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution requires not only rapid water dissociation but also continuous interfacial transport and consumption of hydrogen intermediates. However, alloy/oxide heterointerfaces designed to couple these elementary
content: Efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution requires not only rapid water dissociation but also continuous interfacial transport and consumption of hydrogen intermediates. However, alloy/oxide heterointerfaces designed to couple these elementary steps often suffer from electronic mismatch, leading to localized hydrogen intermediates (H*) trapping and interrupted hydrogen spillover. Here, an oxide-side lanthanum-regulated MoO2/Ni4Mo heterostructure is developed to convert the interfacial H* bridge from an electronic trap into a relay-permissive junction. La is preferentially accommodated in the oxygen-coordinated MoO2-side environment, where it attenuates local contact-potential mismatch, redistributes near-Fermi interfacial states, and strengthens alloy/oxide coupling without forming a dominant La-centered hydrogen-evolution site. This electronic reconfiguration enables a continuous MoO2-to-Ni4Mo hydrogen-relay pathway by lowering the interfacial H* migration barrier while maintaining favorable water-activation and H2-release energetics. Consequently, La-MoO2/Ni4Mo delivers an overpotential of 14 mV at 10 mA cm-2 and a Tafel slope of 31.9 mV dec-1 in alkaline electrolyte. When implemented as a cathode in an anion-exchange-membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), it achieves 1 A cm-2 at 1.74 V and sustains stable operation for 1000 h at 70 ℃. This work establishes oxide-side lanthanum-mediated interfacial electronic regulation as an effective strategy for constructing spillover-active hydrogen-evolution electrodes for practical alkaline water electrolysis.

title: Recontextualizing Circular Economy Principles at the Urban Scale: A Landscape Architecture Based Framework and a Pilot Evaluation Matrix
summary: Circular economy (CE) assessment tools have been developed mainly for products, materials and buildings (micro scale) or for national and regional policy (macro scale). The city tends to appear in this literature as the place where such too
content: Circular economy (CE) assessment tools have been developed mainly for products, materials and buildings (micro scale) or for national and regional policy (macro scale). The city tends to appear in this literature as the place where such tools are applied rather than as a scale with its own assessment logic. This paper asks what the micro and macro scale CE literature actually covers, how far its thematic focuses correspond to the physical, social, ecological, infrastructural and governance dimensions of urban space, and how those focuses might be reformulated as urban scale principles from a landscape architecture perspective. Two Scopus datasets (macro n = 260; micro n = 925) were screened following PRISMA 2020 and analysed by keyword co-occurrence in VOSviewer. The resulting five macro and eight micro thematic clusters were rated against five urban criteria on a Low, Medium, and High scale using pre-defined decision rules. On this basis, five principles of urban circularity are proposed: Spatial Adaptability, Social Inclusion, Ecological Regeneration, Integrated Circular Flows and Adaptive Governance. One of them, Spatial Adaptability, is developed into a pilot matrix of six sub-principles with indicators and qualitative evaluation levels; the other four are outlined but not operationalised. The framework is offered as a starting point for a qualitative urban circularity assessment that can be tested on open-space typologies and refined with practitioner input.

title: Moment-Fourier approach to parallel closures and transport for a toroidally confined multi-ion plasma
summary: We develop a multi-ion closure framework for tokamak plasmas by solving the drift-kinetic equation using the moment-Fourier method. The model extends our previous single-ion formulation to plasmas containing multiple ion species and consist
content: We develop a multi-ion closure framework for tokamak plasmas by solving the drift-kinetic equation using the moment-Fourier method. The model extends our previous single-ion formulation to plasmas containing multiple ion species and consistently incorporates inter-species collisional effects in the moment system. As a representative case, we consider a deuterium-carbon plasma, assuming a common zeroth-order ion temperature on each flux surface while allowing the electron temperature to differ. The first-order fluid moments, namely density, temperature, and parallel flow velocity, are computed for electrons, deuterium ions, and carbon ions. The framework enables a direct comparison of the first-order parallel flow velocities of deuterium and carbon ions, thereby providing a quantitative basis for interpreting charge-exchange spectroscopy measurements and for systematic multi-ion neoclassical transport studies.

title: Making low-clinker cements work: Constraints, chemical activation, and region-specific pathways
summary: Decarbonising cement requires lowering the clinker factor, yet binders in which clinker falls below about half of the binder mass often suffer kinetic and thermodynamic constraints that delay early strength and leave durability performance
content: Decarbonising cement requires lowering the clinker factor, yet binders in which clinker falls below about half of the binder mass often suffer kinetic and thermodynamic constraints that delay early strength and leave durability performance uncertain. Chemical activation, through calcium-based additives, low-dosage salts, hybrid alkaline systems, nucleation seeding, or alkanolamines, is the most direct means of recovering early performance, although each route trades early against later-age behaviour and carries an embodied carbon cost of its own. Because cement production and resource availability vary strongly by region, locally available precursors such as low-grade calcined clays, industrial by-products, and natural pozzolans must anchor regional pathways, even as centralised, traded supply chains coexist with regional ones. This letter argues that low-clinker binders underperform less because a single technical solution is missing than because activation chemistry, the locally available precursor, and the target application are treated in isolation, and that this technical difficulty is compounded by the scarcity of performance-based specifications in many regions and by the hesitancy of practitioners even where such specifications already exist. Since a large share of cement serves unreinforced and lightly loaded applications, low-clinker binders can be deployed there with confidence today, while durability data and performance-based specifications mature for reinforced and structural application.

title: Degradation of Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers Under Shutdown and Open-Circuit Transients: Protocols, Mechanisms, Diagnostics, and Mitigation
summary: Anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMELs) are attractive for direct coupling to variable renewable supply, but their durability under the resulting transients is poorly constrained. This review examines AEMEL degradation under th
content: Anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMELs) are attractive for direct coupling to variable renewable supply, but their durability under the resulting transients is poorly constrained. This review examines AEMEL degradation under the intermittent test protocols reported at cell and stack level, focusing on the shutdown and open-circuit portions of those protocols. We classify the protocols by the electrical route through which the stop is imposed and set out what each reproduces of renewable-driven operation and what it does not. Reported degradation figures are re-expressed on a common per-cycle basis so that studies using different metrics, current densities and cycle counts can be compared. Three recurring losses emerge: oxidation and dissolution of non-noble hydrogen-evolution catalysts, ohmic drift of the membrane and ionomer after dry stops, and structural reorganization of the electrode under repeated reverse current. In the single cells resolved so far, open-circuit and reverse-current stops load the cathode, with a loss that scales with the cathode metal’s stability; severity is set by the boundary conditions at the stop rather than by intermittency as such. Diagnostics and mitigation are assessed on that basis. The evidence base remains small, dominated by single cells, and rarely electrode-resolved, with one anode chemistry tested.

title: XANES-Guided Molecular Structure Generation via Conditional Diffusion and Forward Spectral Prediction
summary: Reconstructing complete molecular structures from X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra remains challenging because the spectra primarily encode local chemical environments, with overlapping contributions from multiple absorb
content: Reconstructing complete molecular structures from X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra remains challenging because the spectra primarily encode local chemical environments, with overlapping contributions from multiple absorbing sites. Here, we develop an inverse-forward framework combining XANES-conditioned diffusion-based molecular structure generation with forward spectral prediction for candidate selection. The inverse model generates atomic species, bond connectivity, and three-dimensional coordinates from C, N, and O K-edge XANES, given only the total atom count without molecular formulas or element-specific atom counts. Combining all three absorption edges substantially improves structural recovery, achieving a best-of-10 exact-match rate of 56.6% across 2,888 test molecules. The generated candidates also reproduce functional groups and structural motifs, achieving a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.951 across 21 categories. Ranking candidates by agreement between input and forward-predicted spectra increases the exact-match rate from 24.3% for unranked top-1 selection to 43.9%. This spectral-consistency criterion also enables atom count estimation, identifying the correct count for 65.6% of molecules among seven tested values. Application to experimental spectra yields an exact structural match for imidazole and recovers characteristic functional groups in two additional molecules, while revealing limitations due to simulation-experiment spectral discrepancies. These findings establish an inverse-forward approach for reconstructing whole-molecule structures from complementary element-specific XANES information.

title: Policy Implications of Singapore’s “City in Nature” Strategy for China’s Carbon-Neutral and Resilient City Development
source: Academic journal of management and social sciences
summary: Singapore has successfully moved from a "Garden City" to a "City in Nature", and its ecological development model in a high-density area serves as a model around the world. By organising the natural environment in the city systematically, m
content: Singapore has successfully moved from a "Garden City" to a "City in Nature", and its ecological development model in a high-density area serves as a model around the world. By organising the natural environment in the city systematically, many good results have been achieved in boosting carbon sinks for the city, strengthening its resilience to climate change, and improving the quality of life for the people living here. This paper will explore four types of cases for Singapore's "City in Nature" plan: policy concept, planning practice, governance model and transferability to China. In addition, based on this experience, it also presents targeted policy recommendations for China's goals of carbon-neutral and resilient urbanisation. Based on the analysis above, it is proposed that the overall approach of "greening" be revised to move closer to integrating "natural systems" in urban areas. It proposes building multi-scale networks of blue-green infrastructure, strengthening cross-sectoral collaborative governance, and improving public participation mechanisms. The above contents provide a reference for building a high-quality and sustainable Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and Xiong'an New Area.

title: Nepenthes‐Inspired Superhydrophobic Porous Lightweight Concrete With a CO 2 ‐Activated Dual‐Level Energy Barrier for Dynamic Anti‐Wetting
summary: Bioinspired porous concrete with a superhydrophobic surface offers multifunctionality for anti‐icing, anti‐corrosion, and thermal insulation, meeting the adaptable demands of modern infrastructure. However, scalable fabrication of robust hy
content: Bioinspired porous concrete with a superhydrophobic surface offers multifunctionality for anti‐icing, anti‐corrosion, and thermal insulation, meeting the adaptable demands of modern infrastructure. However, scalable fabrication of robust hydrophobic microstructures in porous cementitious materials remains challenging. Herein, inspired by the low‐pinning dynamic anti‐wetting of Nepenthes interfaces, an in situ carbonation strategy using CO 2 is developed to construct porous concretes with a dual‐level superhydrophobic energy barrier. Intrinsic rough pores trap air to reduce solid–liquid contact as the first barrier, and siloxane‐coated calcite layers mineralized on pore surfaces act as the second barrier, impeding wetting advance. Under optimal conditions: porous concrete with a density of 600 kg/m 3 , a poly (methyl hydrogen) siloxane (PMHS) usage of 600 g/m 2 , 48 h CO 2 curing (100% CO 2 , and 95% RH), exhibits a long‐term Cassie‐Baxter (CB) state with a water contact angle (CA) of ∼160°, low water absorption of 3.6%, icing delay time of 2350 s at −20°C, low ice adhesion of 15 kPa and anti‐corrosion for reinforced rebar. The ∼1 µm calcite layer theoretically enhances water‐droplet motion by six times compared with the uncarbonated surface. Under coupled water, icing, and elevated‐temperature conditions, the dual energy barrier suppresses heat and mass transfer, making it a promising candidate for lightweight, durable, anti‐icing, and thermally insulating material.

title: Zeleni vodonik u funkciji dekarbonizacije građevinskog sektora - studija slučaja transformacije Dilinger čeličane
summary: Introduction: The paper analyzes steel production decarbonization using green hydrogen through a case study of Dillinger's Power4Steel project, with implications for the construction sector. The Aim: To analyze the technical feasibility and
content: Introduction: The paper analyzes steel production decarbonization using green hydrogen through a case study of Dillinger's Power4Steel project, with implications for the construction sector. The Aim: To analyze the technical feasibility and economic viability of Power4Steel, quantify emission reductions and energy increases, and assess the project's contribution to construction sector decarbonization. Material and Methods: A case study of Dillinger was used. Data were collected from primary and secondary sources. Analysis included a comparative analysis of BF-BOF and DRI-EAF processes, with an additional stoichiometric calculation. Results: Literature data indicate 90-95% CO₂ emission reduction using DRI-EAF with green hydrogen, while the calculation in this paper, based on specific emission values of 1,921 kg CO₂/t for BF-BOF and 339 kg CO₂/t for DRI-EAF, shows a reduction of 82.4%. DRI-EAF requires 8-10 times higher electricity consumption. Stoichiometric calculation confirmed H₂ consumption of 54.1 kg/t Fe. Green steel is 30-54% more expensive (600-850 €/t). Dillinger plans production from 2028 and climate neutrality by 2045 with an investment of €4.6 billion. CBAM analysis shows traditional steel has a cost of 46,82 €/t, while green steel has none. Conclusion: Power4Steel is technically feasible with significant emission reduction, but presents challenges (endothermicity, 8-10 times higher electricity, higher water consumption). Although green steel is currently more expensive, CBAM and EU ETS are expected to make it competitive by 2030. The project is crucial for the sustainable transformation of Europe's construction sector.

title: Tourism Uncertainty and Sustainable Development in Tourism‐Dependent Economies: Nonlinear Evidence on Diversification, Ecological Pressure, and Digital Finance
summary: Sustainable development in tourism‐dependent economies is increasingly challenged by tourism‐related uncertainty, environmental pressures, and structural vulnerabilities. This study examines the relationships between tourism uncertainty, ec
content: Sustainable development in tourism‐dependent economies is increasingly challenged by tourism‐related uncertainty, environmental pressures, and structural vulnerabilities. This study examines the relationships between tourism uncertainty, ecological footprint, the structural/productive dimension of economic diversification, digital financial development, and sustainable development, measured by the Sustainable Development Goals Index (SDGI), across 10 tourism‐dependent economies over 2002–2023. Using complementary quantile‐based, nonlinear, predictive, and relative‐importance approaches, the analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity across sustainability conditions. Tourism uncertainty exhibits heterogeneous relationships with sustainable development but comparatively weak predictive relevance. Ecological footprint displays strong nonlinearity and broad predictive relevance, highlighting the tension between development‐related resource use and environmental constraints. Digital financial development is predominantly positively associated with sustainable development, although its lagged predictive evidence is limited. The structural/productive dimension of diversification, proxied by manufacturing value added, ranks first in the cross‐method relative‐importance synthesis, while its significant short‐run predictive relationships are negative, highlighting that productive transformation is not automatically sustainability‐enhancing. These findings support regime‐sensitive policies that strengthen resilience to tourism shocks, promote sustainable productive diversification, expand enabling digital‐financial capacity, and reduce ecological pressures according to countries' sustainability and institutional conditions.

title: Beyond Acknowledgement: A Strategic Assessment of Decarbonization Measures in Global Steel Firms
summary: Decarbonization of the iron and steel industry is critical to achieving global carbon reduction goals. Existing studies have proposed multiple decarbonization strategies, yet there is limited knowledge on firm adoption of these strategies.
content: Decarbonization of the iron and steel industry is critical to achieving global carbon reduction goals. Existing studies have proposed multiple decarbonization strategies, yet there is limited knowledge on firm adoption of these strategies. In this study, we develop a Decarbonization of Iron and Steel Strategy Classification (DISC) framework for assessing firm‐level strategies for emission reduction based on the transition literature. Using a sample of global steel producers, we evaluate firms' decarbonization strategies under three categories: awareness, planning, and action. We use content analysis of companies' disclosures to score strategies and Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) to estimate relative efficiency within the observed sample. The decarbonization strategy index scores are then compared with the companies' relative efficiency. The results of our study suggest that large steel firms have implemented incremental strategies, but few firms have moved beyond acknowledgement to adopt transformative strategies. The study provides implications for policymakers and steel firms to transition to low‐carbon steel while ensuring long‐term competitiveness.

title: Programmable DNA Nanotechnology as a paradigm shift in targeted therapeutics, molecular diagnostics, and emerging nanotechnologies
summary: DNA nanotechnology has become a programmable platform for building precise nanoscale architectures with applications across biomedicine and materials science. This review examines recent advances in the design, synthesis and biological eval
content: DNA nanotechnology has become a programmable platform for building precise nanoscale architectures with applications across biomedicine and materials science. This review examines recent advances in the design, synthesis and biological evaluation of DNA nanomaterials, including DNA origami, tetrahedral DNA nanostructures and DNA hydrogels. We survey established and emerging fabrication routes, among them chemical synthesis, enzymatic methods, hybridization, microfluidics and machine learning-guided design, and what each offers for scalability and cost. Structural strategies such as scaffold-staple folding are reviewed alongside surface chemistries including PEGylation and lipid bilayer encapsulation, with attention to their effect on stability and biological efficacy. Behavior in vivo is covered in detail: nuclease-mediated degradation, intracellular trafficking, clearance, and the biological interactions set by protein corona formation and physicochemical properties. For targeted therapeutics we cover aptamer functionalization and aptamer-drug conjugates; for molecular diagnostics, aptamer-based electrochemical biosensing and point-of-care formats. Immunogenicity and safety are treated in detail, including innate immune stimulation through TLR9 and cGAS-STING, complement activation and cytotoxicity. By setting out the preclinical evaluation frameworks that matter, among them pharmacokinetic characterization and toxicity testing, the review connects design decisions to biological safety and to what clinical translation of DNA nanomedicines will require.

title: Carbon-based nanomaterials as cutting fluid additives: A review
summary: Metalworking fluids are commonly used in the machining processes of diverse equipment components to provide cooling, cleaning, rust prevention, and lubrication. The incorporation of cutting fluid additives further enhances their performance
content: Metalworking fluids are commonly used in the machining processes of diverse equipment components to provide cooling, cleaning, rust prevention, and lubrication. The incorporation of cutting fluid additives further enhances their performance. In recent years, carbon-based nanomaterials have attracted attention as environmentally friendly additives for cutting fluids. This work reviews the research progress on carbon-based nanomaterials as cutting fluid additives, analyzes the effects of factors such as the dispersibility of carbon-based nanomaterials, cutting fluid types, and cutting parameters on machining performance, and discusses the friction reduction and anti-wear mechanisms of carbon-based nanomaterials. Finally, current challenges and future prospects for carbon-based cutting fluid additives are outlined. This review aims to provide guidance and references for achieving efficient and environmentally friendly machining of difficult-to-process materials.

title: Instabilité des prix et extension des marchés de carbone : une politique climatique européenne sous tension
summary: Le marché de carbone européen, véritable pierre angulaire de la politique climatique de l’Union européenne, peine depuis 20 ans à faire la preuve de son efficacité. Il souffre notamment d’une instabilité des prix historique que des réformes
content: Le marché de carbone européen, véritable pierre angulaire de la politique climatique de l’Union européenne, peine depuis 20 ans à faire la preuve de son efficacité. Il souffre notamment d’une instabilité des prix historique que des réformes récurrentes ne parviennent pas à endiguer. Pour autant, l’Union européenne a décidé récemment son extension à de nouveaux secteurs et la création d’un nouveau marché dédié au chauffage et au transport routier. Cet article montre que l’instabilité des prix est constitutive de ce type d’instrument, à cause notamment de l’incertitude sur la demande et de l’évaluation financière des prix. Alors que ces marchés sont théoriquement censés fournir un signal-prix stable et pérenne, supposé guider les stratégies de décarbonation à long terme, cet élargissement d’un instrument toujours mal maîtrisé pose question. La diffusion probable de l’instabilité des prix à de nouveaux secteurs fragilise toute l’action climatique européenne, mais elle sert l’ambition tenace de voir émerger un prix unique du carbone à l’échelle européenne.

title: Is ESG Performance Priced in the Chinese A-Share Market
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: This paper examines whether ESG performance is priced in China's A-share market using a comprehensive framework by changing ESG measure, empirical approach, and pricing horizon. Unadjusted raw ESG scores do not have predictive power, as the
content: This paper examines whether ESG performance is priced in China's A-share market using a comprehensive framework by changing ESG measure, empirical approach, and pricing horizon. Unadjusted raw ESG scores do not have predictive power, as the gross return of the unadjusted long/short portfolio is insignificant and negative. When the ESG score is controlled for industry and size effect, the composite portfolio obtains a positive and significant annual return of 2.89% with a FF5+UMD alpha of 3.12% (t=4.02). The predictive power of ESG score comes from governance (G) dimension (alpha=2.60%, t=3.57) while environmental and social dimension are insignificant. The Fama-MacBeth regression analysis shows that each year 1 standard deviation increase in ESG leads to a 0.76 percentage point higher return next year (p=0.0093), while next-month return is positive but insignificant. Event study around the 2024 April announcement of the guidelines for the compulsory sustainability information disclosure exhibits an asymmetric response among big firms, which is indicative of relative revaluation. These findings are robust even if the Wind ESG rating is substituted by Sino-Securities ESG rating.

title: Oil and Gas Economics
summary: The textbook is intended for undergraduate students studying economics and management, and is used in the course “Economics and Business Planning in Oil and Gas Companies”. The publication is aimed to provide a systematic overview of the oi
content: The textbook is intended for undergraduate students studying economics and management, and is used in the course “Economics and Business Planning in Oil and Gas Companies”. The publication is aimed to provide a systematic overview of the oil and gas industry functioning as well as the principles of managing oil and gas companies. The first part of the book examines the industry-specific features of the oil and gas economy. It presents the historical stages of development of the industry, analyzes the dynamics of key indicators and reveals the properties and classifications of hydrocarbons. Special attention is paid to the role of oil and gas companies as industry players, the specifics of their interaction with the state, as well as the system of state regulation and taxation. The mechanisms of oil and gas price formation on world markets, the role of commodity traders and price agencies, along with current trends and forecasts for the development of the oil and gas sector are considered. The second part of the book is devoted to business management issues in oil and gas companies. It covers the basics of strategic management, approaches to valuing oil and gas companies, principles of investment portfolio formation, and methods of economic evaluation of projects, taking into account industry risks. Separate sections are devoted to business and financial planning, budgeting, and working capital management. The textbook contains practical examples, assignments, and business cases aimed at developing analytical and management skills. The material is presented with consideration for the interconnection between economic and technological processes in the oil and gas industry, allowing students to form a comprehensive understanding of how companies and the industry as a whole function.

title: THE EFFECT OF PHOSPHORIC ACID ( H3PO4) ACTIVATION TEMPERATURE AND TIME ON THE CHARACTERISTICS OF ACTIVATED NANOCARBON BASED ON OIL PALM BIOMASS WASTE THROUGH PYROLYSIS

content: This study examines the effects of phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄) activation temperature and time on activated carbon from oil palm empty fruit bunches and palm kernel shells through pyrolysis. Dry feedstocks were combined at a 1:1 ratio and pyrolyzed at 450 °C for 120 minutes. Activation at 80, 90, and 100 °C for 90, 120, and 150 minutes was followed by sonication and drying. title: Metastable Olivine-Type Intermediates in Maricite NaFePO4 Cycling Revealed by Operando XRD and DFT
summary: NaFePO4 (NFP) is a potential cathode material for sodium-ion batteries and exists mainly as the maricite and olivine polymorphs. Maricite NaFePO4 (m-NFP) is the thermodynamically stable and synthetically accessible polymorph of NaFePO4, wit
content: NaFePO4 (NFP) is a potential cathode material for sodium-ion batteries and exists mainly as the maricite and olivine polymorphs. Maricite NaFePO4 (m-NFP) is the thermodynamically stable and synthetically accessible polymorph of NaFePO4, with a theoretical capacity of 154 mAh g-1 but is expected to exhibit limited electrochemical activity due to the absence of continuous Na-ion migration channels in its crystal structure. Its reported electrochemical activity has been attributed either to amorphization or to crystalline reconstruction, and previous computational studies have modelled desodiation within the known maricite and olivine polymorphs separately. It has therefore remained unknown whether desodiation of m-NFP crosses polymorph boundaries, and if so, through which intermediate. Here, we combine operando X-ray diffraction (XRD) with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to resolve this pathway. Operando XRD shows that m-NFP retains its long-range crystallinity during cycling, while systematic peak shifts and new reflections reveal an at least partially reversible crystalline transformation. A common convex hull of maricite-, olivine- and alluaudite-type NaxFePO4 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) identifies alluaudite-type Na0.67FePO4 as the thermodynamically preferred intermediate. Calculated voltages exclude a maricite-retaining pathway but cannot discriminate between the remaining candidates. Pathway-resolved simulated XRD fingerprints, however, show that the experimental peak evolution is most consistent with a metastable olivine-type intermediate, lying only about 8 meV/atom above the hull, rather than with alluaudite. Structural similarity analysis indicates that this intermediate retains a more maricite-like local environment, suggesting that structural accessibility, not thermodynamic stability alone, selects the pathway. These results reconcile conflicting reports on m-NFP and show that the electrochemically accessed pathway of polymorphic electrode materials need not follow the lowest-energy intermediate.

title: Treatment of steel slag leachates and the synthesis of calcite via carbon dioxide micro-pressure circulating aeration technique: a pilot study
summary: Steel slag leachate poses significant pollution risks to the surrounding environment. This study proposes a CO 2 -based micro-pressure circulating aeration technique for treating strongly alkaline steel slag leachate. By optimizing experime
content: Steel slag leachate poses significant pollution risks to the surrounding environment. This study proposes a CO 2 -based micro-pressure circulating aeration technique for treating strongly alkaline steel slag leachate. By optimizing experimental research and pilot tests in engineering devices, the calcium-containing wastewater was well treated and met the emission standards. The results show that the effluent of this leachate wastewater treatment project reaches Ca 2+ concentrations of ≤ 80 mg/L, with a pH range of 7.0–7.3. Moreover, the process produces mineral carbonation products of pure calcite particles, with sizes ranging from 5 to 100 μm in an aggregated state. The application of this technology not only solves the environmental pollution problem of steel slag leachate but also facilitates CO 2 reduction and resource recovery of calcium carbonate products. This protocol can be applied to the treatment of high-calcium wastewater and the storage of carbon dioxide in the future.

title: Electrostatic screening and nitrogen-vacancy charge states in boron-doped/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions
summary: Boron-doped diamond (BDD) enables the integration of electrical functionality with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, but the influence of junction electrostatics on NV charge-state stability remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the e
content: Boron-doped diamond (BDD) enables the integration of electrical functionality with nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, but the influence of junction electrostatics on NV charge-state stability remains unclear. In this study, we investigate the equilibrium electrostatics of BDD/nitrogen-doped diamond junctions using self-consistent Poisson-Fermi calculations. The results reveal two distinct electrostatic length scales in the nitrogen-doped substrate: a near-interface region of ionized donors that produces dominant band bending and determines the NV$^{0/-}$ charge-state boundary, and a much longer screening tail associated with weak donor ionization in the neutral bulk. The resulting NV$^-$ depletion depth depends strongly on the nitrogen concentration but exhibits a more moderate dependence on boron doping. At $N_B = 10^{21}$ cm$^{-3}$, varying the interface grading scale $w$ from 0.5 to 8 nm changes the depletion depth by approximately 22 nm, whereas variations in the modeled bulk BDD charge response produce a shift of only 1.27 nm. These results indicate that, under the conditions studied, the nitrogen donor concentration and local interface structure primarily govern the equilibrium NV charge-state profile, rather than the bulk electronic response of BDD alone.

title: Legal Regulation of Digital Agriculture in Africa: From Fragmented National Strategies to a Continent-Wide Framework Law
source: Journal of Digital Technologies and Law
summary: Objective: to study regional and national regulatory mechanisms for digital agriculture in African countries in order to justify the need to adopt a continent-wide framework law aimed at ensuring food security, protecting farmers’ rights, a
content: Objective: to study regional and national regulatory mechanisms for digital agriculture in African countries in order to justify the need to adopt a continent-wide framework law aimed at ensuring food security, protecting farmers’ rights, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Methods: the methodological basis of the work was formed by a doctrinallegal approach combined with methods of descriptive and comparativelegal analysis of normative legal acts, strategic programs, and scientific literature. The case analysis was used to compare the institutional and political-legal models of the agricultural sector digitalization in six African jurisdictions – Botswana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, the Republic of South Africa and the Gambia – in the context of the implementation of the Digital Agriculture Strategy of the African Union and the African Union Agenda up to 2063. Results: the considered sources show that the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, robotics and big data analysis can help increase the agricultural productivity and at the same time reduce anthropogenic emissions of methane and nitrous oxide. The study established that the effectiveness of digital transformation in Africa is limited by the fragmented implementation of national strategies, the shortage of telecommunications infrastructure in rural areas, the high cost of equipment and licensing, low digital literacy, and unequal access to the Internet. Legal gaps were identified related to the uncertainty of the ownership regime for agricultural data, the vulnerability of farmers’ personal information when it is transferred to providers, and insufficient protection of intellectual property rights. Scientific novelty: the article formulates the concept of transition from disparate initiatives and the “soft law” documents of the African Union to a legally binding continent-wide framework law on digital agriculture. It is proposed to consolidate in this act the right of farmers to control the generated data, guarantees for the interoperability of digital platforms, mechanisms for interdepartmental coordination of relevant ministries, and special legal support measures for small landowners and women. Practical significance: the research results can serve as a basis for the African Union bodies and national legislators in modernizing agricultural, information and environmental legislation in accordance with the Paris Agreement and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The implementation of the proposed legal mechanisms can help to reduce regulatory asymmetries between the African countries, protect the property and information rights of agricultural producers, and transit to low-carbon agricultural development.

title: From algorithms to acquisitions: artificial intelligence exposure, organizational intelligence, and firm boundaries
summary: This study examines whether firm-level artificial intelligence (AI) exposure is associated with corporate mergers and acquisitions (M&A), an observable form of firm boundary adjustment. Using more than 7.5 million online job postings in Chi
content: This study examines whether firm-level artificial intelligence (AI) exposure is associated with corporate mergers and acquisitions (M&A), an observable form of firm boundary adjustment. Using more than 7.5 million online job postings in China from 2017 to 2024, we construct a firm-year AI exposure measure that captures firms’ demand for AI-related tasks and capabilities. The results show that firms with higher AI exposure are more likely to engage in M&A. Evidence consistent with several possible organizational channels points to managerial decision-making, organizational coordination, and governance capacity. The association is more pronounced among non-decline-stage firms, firms with stronger digital foundations, and firms facing higher transaction costs. Further analysis shows that AI exposure is more strongly associated with vertical rather than horizontal M&A, suggesting that AI-related capabilities may be particularly relevant for coordinating value-chain activities within firm boundaries. Overall, the findings provide evidence on how AI-related labor demand is linked to M&A-based boundary choices.

title: Bulgaria Country Climate and Development Report
summary: Bulgaria has made remarkable progress in recent years, becoming a high-income country in 2024 and joining the eurozone in 2026. Yet important structural challenges remain. This Country Climate and Development Report (CCDR) examines how Bulg
content: Bulgaria has made remarkable progress in recent years, becoming a high-income country in 2024 and joining the eurozone in 2026. Yet important structural challenges remain. This Country Climate and Development Report (CCDR) examines how Bulgaria can continue converging with the European Union while transitioning to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy. Its central finding is that achieving net zero emissions by 2050 is affordable, supports growth and competitiveness, and strengthens energy security, while targeted adaptation investments can significantly reduce, but not eliminate, future economic losses. The challenge is not a lack of ambition, but the need to accelerate implementation, strengthen institutions, and mobilize public and private financing. At the same time, the report recognizes that the transition must be managed carefully to ensure that its benefits are broadly shared. Poor households, workers employed in emissions-intensive industries, and coal-dependent regions face the greatest adjustment costs. Targeted social protection, reskilling programs, and place-based development strategies will therefore be essential to securing public support and ensuring a just transition.

title: Efficient Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) reach an accuracy close to quantum mechanical reference calculations at a small fraction of the cost. Efficiency is the purpose of MLIPs, yet strategies for efficient MLIPs have not been revie
content: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) reach an accuracy close to quantum mechanical reference calculations at a small fraction of the cost. Efficiency is the purpose of MLIPs, yet strategies for efficient MLIPs have not been reviewed systematically. This review takes efficiency as its guideline. To compare MLIPs on a common footing, we represent them in a complete basis expansion, the Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) and its graph generalization (GRACE). The expansion is canonical, built from products of single-particle functions. Classical interatomic potentials, such as the embedded-atom method, and many modern MLIPs, including equivariant transformers, can be represented within this expansion. Much of the apparent diversity of MLIP architectures therefore reflects how non-linearity, layer coupling and optimization are handled rather than which interactions the models can represent. We show how the cost of an MLIP becomes linear in system size and, at fixed rank of the tensor decomposition, in model complexity, and we discuss the role of machine learning, which provides non-linear parameterizations and optimization. Because efficiency is meaningful only at a given accuracy, we also compare accuracy and cost. On the Matbench Discovery leaderboard, models with three to five layers approach the accuracy of deeper models, and one basis, truncated along the Pareto front of error and speed, spans more than two orders of magnitude in cost. Ultimately, training data determine the quality of any MLIP.
