The system constitutes reusable knowledge for insect farming automation, combining fuzzy logic actuation, multi-parameter sensing, and Telegram-based monitoring within a low-cost embedded platform, applicable to broader smart agriculture and sustainable waste management domains.

title: Quantifying urban heat: A spatiotemporal study of climate change and population growth in Ikorodu, Lagos, Nigeria
source: African Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
summary: Climate change and rapid urban growth are increasingly altering local climatic conditions in cities across the Global South. One important manifestation is the urban heat island (UHI) effect, whereby built-up urban areas experience higher t
content: Climate change and rapid urban growth are increasingly altering local climatic conditions in cities across the Global South. One important manifestation is the urban heat island (UHI) effect, whereby built-up urban areas experience higher temperatures than surrounding less-developed areas. This study examines the relationship between climate change, urban growth, and rising temperatures in Ikorodu, a rapidly expanding peri-urban area of Lagos State, Nigeria. Using simulated but realistic datasets derived from Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NIMET) records, Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) projections, and Lagos State population statistics, the study analyses temperature trends from 2010 to 2024 in relation to population growth and spatial patterns of heat distribution. Findings indicate an average temperature increase of approximately 0.03°C annually, occurring alongside substantial population growth from about 1.0 million in 2010 to over 1.9 million in 2024. The analysis reveals a notable relationship between urban expansion and increasing temperatures, suggesting that rapid urbanisation contributes to the intensification of local heat conditions. The simulated heat map further indicates that the highest temperatures are concentrated in densely built-up areas, highlighting the influence of land-use change, building density, and urban form on heat distribution. The study concludes that continued urban expansion without effective climate-responsive planning could increase public health risks, energy demand, and heat-related discomfort. It therefore recommends expanding urban green spaces, promoting climate-responsive building designs, protecting natural surfaces, and strengthening sustainable land-use planning to enhance climate resilience in Ikorodu and other rapidly urbanising African cities.

title: Evaluation of major livestock feed resources and feeding system in Dalifage district of Afar Regional State, Ethiopia
summary: This study was conducted to assess the major livestock feed resources and feeding systems in the Dalifage district of the Afar Regional State, Ethiopia. Three representative kebeles from pastoral and three from agro-pastoral areas were purp
content: This study was conducted to assess the major livestock feed resources and feeding systems in the Dalifage district of the Afar Regional State, Ethiopia. Three representative kebeles from pastoral and three from agro-pastoral areas were purposively selected, from which 151 households were randomly chosen for semi-structured individual interviews. The major feed resources identified included fodder trees and shrubs (such as Acacia melifera, Grewia ferruginea, Salvadora persica, Cadaba rotundifolia, Dobera glabra, and Ziziphus mauritana), grasses (like Cymbopogon pospischilii and Chrysopogon aucheri), and natural pasture. Coping strategies for feed shortages included destocking and migration. The majority (76%) of the respondents reported a decrease in the status of grazing land/rangeland, with drought being the primary cause of decline. In the agro-pastoral farming system, a few community members supplemented maize stover to milking cows, sick, and weak animals. However, most of the respondents (72.8%) did not use supplementary feed for their animals. The study recommends creating awareness about supplementary feeding and introducing improved forage to enhance the status of communal rangeland and address feed shortages.

title: CottonTrace for Seed to Cloth Traceability with IoT and Digital Product Passports
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Cotton production involves repeated changes in material form, ownership and quantity, making a garment difficult to trace using disconnected records. We present CottonTrace, a web-based prototype that links eight material stages through qua
content: Cotton production involves repeated changes in material form, ownership and quantity, making a garment difficult to trace using disconnected records. We present CottonTrace, a web-based prototype that links eight material stages through quantity-labelled lot genealogy, contract-based validation, an application-managed permissioned-ledger model, off-chain evidence, Internet of Things ingestion and a QR-accessible Digital Product Passport. An explainable detection layer combines robust statistics with domain rules to route suspicious records to auditors. The design is examined against the implementation and the project-reported synthetic evaluation of 18 lots, 61 blocks and 2,488 sensor readings. That evaluation records rejection of invalid operations, detection of edited evidence, eight findings corresponding to planted irregularities, and verification of 12 upstream lots for a garment passport. These observations demonstrate functional integration within the pilot. They do not establish distributed consensus, field accuracy, calibrated fraud probabilities or a complete environmental life-cycle assessment. The main contribution is a transparent workflow connecting deterministic validation, evidence integrity, material attribution and human review in a single cotton traceability prototype.

title: PVC Cable Burning Behaviour and Intumescent Protection: Small-Scale Tests and the Browns Ferry Lesson
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: Electrical cables are present in nearly every building and industrial site. In a fire they can act as the starting point, as a path along which flames travel, and as a major producer of smoke. This paper presents laboratory results for a si
content: Electrical cables are present in nearly every building and industrial site. In a fire they can act as the starting point, as a path along which flames travel, and as a major producer of smoke. This paper presents laboratory results for a single-core PVCinsulated copper cable and a literature review of passive fire protection (PFP), with attention to intumescent coatings. Two standard tests were run: vertical flame propagation under IEC 60332-1-2, and cone calorimetry at 40 kW/m² under ISO 5660-1. Both vertical specimens passed. Flames died out within 5 s of removing the burner, and charring reached only 80 mm and 160 mm along a 600 mm length. In the cone calorimeter the insulation ignited at 125 s, peaked at 114.89 kW/m², gave a total heat release of 70.81 MJ/m² and a smoke production rate of 0.175 m²/s. The material therefore shrugs off a small flame but, under sustained radiant heating, becomes a long-lived source of heat and smoke. The review part explains how intumescent coatings function, the product families available, how they fail, and how the 1975 Browns Ferry fire reshaped cable-protection rules.

title: Spatial and morphological influences on the fatty acid composition of Allanblackia parviflora oils
summary: This study examined the relative influence of location and tree morphology on the fatty acid profiles of manually expressed seed (whole seed) and kernel (seed coat removed) oils of Allanblackia parviflora across its natural distribution ran
content: This study examined the relative influence of location and tree morphology on the fatty acid profiles of manually expressed seed (whole seed) and kernel (seed coat removed) oils of Allanblackia parviflora across its natural distribution range in Ghana. Using the same sampling framework as a companion study on oil stability, oils were extracted from seed and kernel materials collected from 157 trees sampled across 16 communities within three ecological zones. Fatty acid methyl esters were quantified by gas chromatography and evaluated in relation to ecological zone, community, tree morphological traits, soil properties, and oil yield. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) using SPSS version 23 was employed to assess differences in the chemical properties of seed (SO) and kernel (KO) oils among communities. Principal component analysis (PCA), conducted using the Plymouth Routines in Multivariate Ecological Research (PRIMER)/Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance (PERMANOVA) package, was used to explore relationships among oil stability parameters, fatty acid composition, tree morphological traits, and geographical variables. Both kernel and seed oils exhibited similar fatty acid profiles, dominated by stearic and oleic acids. Stearic acid content ranged from 42.8–61.5% (mean 55.3%) in kernel oils and from 42.7–59.9% (mean 54.5%) in seed oils, while oleic acid ranged from 37.4–55.3% (mean 43.2%) and 38.7–55.9% (mean 44.0%), respectively. Palmitic acid (PA) occurred at low levels (0.8–1.6%), whereas linolenic acid was present only in trace amounts (0.3–0.7%). Although substantial tree-to-tree variation was observed, fatty acid composition was not significantly influenced by tree morphology, soil properties, community, or ecological zone. Tocopherols were not detected in bulked kernel or seed oil samples. These results indicate that A. parviflora oil exhibits a stable and highly saturated–monounsaturated fatty acid profile across ecological and morphological gradients. Together with the oil stability findings reported in the companion manuscript, the results suggest that individual tree selection, rather than site-specific factors, is likely to be more effective for the breeding, domestication, and commercial development of A. parviflora as a high-value indigenous oil crop.

title: Spatial Contrasts and Indicator-Based Source-Regime Identification of PM2.5 and PM10 along the Kudenda–NNPC Industrial Corridor, Kaduna, Nigeria
source: GLOBAL JOURNAL OF MODERN RESEARCH AND EMERGING TRENDS
summary: The study sought to determine whether particulate pollution along the Kudenda–NNPC industrial corridor in Kaduna State, Nigeria, is primarily influenced by local industrial activities or regional atmospheric transport, as well as to identif
content: The study sought to determine whether particulate pollution along the Kudenda–NNPC industrial corridor in Kaduna State, Nigeria, is primarily influenced by local industrial activities or regional atmospheric transport, as well as to identify the potential particulate source regimes. To this end, the study adopted a retrospective longitudinal observational research design, using 731 complete daily observations per site for 2024–2025, obtained from atmospheric reanalysis and satellite-informed products. Analytically, the Mann–Whitney U test was used for pooled site comparisons, while Kruskal–Wallis tests and Dunn’s post-hoc comparisons with Bonferroni adjustment examined differences across the four site-by-season groups. In the absence of chemical speciation data required for quantitative receptor modelling, potential source regimes were examined using the PM2.5/PM10 mass ratio, pollution roses and a Conditional Probability Function (CPF) based on sixteen wind-direction sectors. The results of the study revealed that pooled PM10 concentrations were significantly higher at NNPC than at Kudenda (median 152.07 versus 120.89 µg m⁻³; p = 0.043). However, this difference was not sustained after seasonal stratification. Moreover, no significant differences were detected between the sites within either season for either pollutant, whereas all cross-season comparisons were significant at p < 0.001. The results further revealed that during the Harmattan, mean PM2.5/PM10 ratios were 0.2225 at Kudenda and 0.2056 at NNPC, with 74.9% and 92.1% of observations, respectively, classified as mechanical/crustal. During the monsoon, the ratios increased to 0.5220 and 0.4827, while the proportion of days classified as combustion/secondary-aerosol dominant rose to 54.9% at Kudenda and 46.5% at NNPC. The CPF consistently identified the north-easterly sector as the strongest directional association with elevated concentrations at both sites for both pollutants (0.657–0.702), followed by the east-north-easterly sector. On the premise of these results, the study concluded that seasonal variation and regional atmospheric transport were more strongly associated with particulate pollution than monitoring location during the study period, with substantial coarse mineral-dust influence during the Harmattan and a relatively greater contribution of fine particles during the monsoon. The study there recommended the incorporation of chemical speciation in future monitoring to support quantitative source apportionment and validate the present indicator-based findings. Moreso, additional ground-based monitoring locations should also be established at varying distances and directions from major emission sources to identify local concentration gradients that the present two-receptor design could not resolve.

title: Phenylephrine-provoked endoscopy reveals an occult Dieulafoy’s lesion in a duodenal diverticulum: A case report and review of literature
summary: BACKGROUND The diagnosis of a Dieulafoy’s lesion located within a duodenal diverticulum (DD) presents a significant challenge, particularly during nonbleeding intervals. Pharmacological provocation has been proposed for obscure gastrointest
content: BACKGROUND The diagnosis of a Dieulafoy’s lesion located within a duodenal diverticulum (DD) presents a significant challenge, particularly during nonbleeding intervals. Pharmacological provocation has been proposed for obscure gastrointestinal bleeding. However, experience with provocative endoscopy is largely confined to antithrombotic-based protocols, which are associated with a delayed and unpredictable bleeding onset. The use of vasopressors as pharmacological provocation agents for endoscopic localization has not been previously explored. CASE SUMMARY We report the case of a 53-year-old woman with recurrent obscure gastrointestinal bleeding and a haemoglobin level ranging from 50 g/L to 84 g/L. Enhanced abdominal computed tomography showed multiple duodenal diverticula (DDs) in the distal duodenum, with a prominent arterial vessel traversing the wall of one diverticulum. Multiple standard endoscopies revealed fresh clots in the DDs but no definitive bleeding source during nonbleeding intervals. With clinical suspicion of a vascular lesion in the DDs, we administered phenylephrine to induce controlled hypertension for provocative endoscopy, which led to active bleeding from the previously concealed lesion within minutes. Using a colonoscope to enhance distal duodenal visualization, we successfully achieved endoscopic localization and haemostasis in the distal duodenum. The provocation was effective, with no recurrent bleeding or adverse events during a 2-month follow-up. CONCLUSION Phenylephrine-provoked endoscopy assists in localizing quiescent occult Dieulafoy’s lesion in a distal duodenal diverticulum with a colonoscope.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Eustachian Tube Dysfunction Questionnaire-7 (ETDQ-7) in Predicting Objective Eustachian Tube Patency Among Patients with Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Cross-Sectional Analytical Study at a Tertiary Referral Hospital in Bali, Indonesia
source: Open Access Indonesian Journal of Medical Reviews
summary: Background: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) can extend to the tubal orifice and cause Eustachian tube dysfunction. Concordance between ETDQ-7 symptoms and objective tubal patency in CRS remains uncertain. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic
content: Background: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) can extend to the tubal orifice and cause Eustachian tube dysfunction. Concordance between ETDQ-7 symptoms and objective tubal patency in CRS remains uncertain. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ETDQ-7 for objective tubal patency impairment in adults with CRS in Bali, Indonesia. Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study enrolled 42 consecutive adults with CRS at a tertiary hospital from January to March 2026. ETDQ-7 scores ≥14.5 were considered abnormal. Tubal patency was assessed by acoustic impedance tympanometry. Chi-square testing, Spearman correlation, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Result: Mean age was 38.9 ± 11.6 years; 57.1% were female. Abnormal ETDQ-7 scores occurred in 24 patients (57.1%), and objective impairment occurred in 26 (61.9%). Impairment was more frequent with abnormal than normal ETDQ-7 scores (83.3% vs 33.3%, p = 0.002). Scores correlated with impaired patency (r = 0.58, p < 0.001). Abnormal ETDQ-7 independently predicted impairment (adjusted OR 7.84, 95% CI 1.74–35.29; p = 0.007). Conclusion: ETDQ-7 is a useful outpatient triage tool for identifying patients with CRS who need objective audiological evaluation; it should not replace confirmatory testing.

title: Waste-Derived Zwitterionic Bacterial Cellulose Membranes with Enhanced Silica and Scaling Control for Sustainable Nanofiltration Pretreatment
summary: Bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes were engineered via kombucha fermentation with the incorporation of polyethylene glycol (PEG-600 and PEG-1000, 1–2%, w/v) to tailor pore formation and enhance structural stability. Subsequently, the BC mem
content: Bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes were engineered via kombucha fermentation with the incorporation of polyethylene glycol (PEG-600 and PEG-1000, 1–2%, w/v) to tailor pore formation and enhance structural stability. Subsequently, the BC membrane was functionalized with chitosan polyampholyte (CPA) to introduce zwitterionic properties for fouling mitigation. The incorporation of 2% PEG-1000 enhances BC production and mechanical properties, with elongation increasing from 20.3% to 49.7%. The zwitterionic modification leads to reduced pore size and altered surface morphology of BC membrane. The zwitterionic CPA-BC membrane exhibits effective pretreatment performance, achieving accumulated removals of 45% for soluble silica, 35% for calcium (Ca2+), and 19% for sulfate (SO42–), while maintaining a stable flux of 20 L m–2 h–1 over 17 h. CPA-BC pretreatment mitigates surface fouling of the commercial nanofiltration (NF) membrane, as evidenced by optical coherence tomography (OCT) and digital image processing, which reveal reduced surface coverage from 99.4% to 64.8%. This contributes to reducing the rapid flux decline observed with pretreatment, from 42 L m–2 h–1 at 2 h to 29 L m–2 h–1 at 17 h, compared to a rapid decline to 7 L m–2 h–1 within 2 h without pretreatment. The findings demonstrate the technical potential of waste-derived zwitterionic BC membranes to offer an effective and sustainable pretreatment strategy for controlling silica fouling and scaling, enabling improved stability and performance of desalination systems.

title: Ru-Promoted Activation of Ni/CaTiO3/CaO Multifunctional Materials for Integrated CO2 Capture and Dry Reforming
summary: Ni-doped CaTiO3/CaO multifunctional materials couple CO2 capture with dry reforming of methane (DRM), but strong metal–lattice interactions can delay Ni activation during reactive regeneration. Here, Ru was incorporated into Ni/CaTiO3/CaO t
content: Ni-doped CaTiO3/CaO multifunctional materials couple CO2 capture with dry reforming of methane (DRM), but strong metal–lattice interactions can delay Ni activation during reactive regeneration. Here, Ru was incorporated into Ni/CaTiO3/CaO to determine how promotion affects reduction, exsolution, and cyclic integrated CO2 capture and DRM (ICCDRM). XRD and STEM-EDS show exsolution of Ni and Ru from CaTiO3 and preferential spatial association of finely dispersed Ru with exsolved Ni. H2-TPR and CH4-TPR indicate that Ru facilitates reduction and activation of Ni-containing phases relative to the corresponding integrated monometallic materials. At 700 °C, the time to peak CH4 conversion decreased from 6.6 min for both monometallic materials to 3.5 min for NiRu, while first-cycle apparent CO2 uptake remained comparable (5.92, 5.19, and 5.43 mmol CO2 g–1 for NiRu, Ni, and Ru, respectively). NiRu also enabled syngas formation at 650 °C, where the monometallic materials produced negligible syngas. Over 30 cycles, apparent CO2 uptake remained relatively consistent and CO production was sustained. Carbon closures of 99.5% and 98.8% were obtained for cycles 1 and 5, and TPO indicated only ∼0.06–0.07 mmol C per cycle. These results show that Ru principally promotes reduction and cyclic reactivation of Ni, helping coordinate catalytic activation with carbonate-derived CO2 release.

title: Urban freight transition strategies: a multi-criteria assessment of diesel truck alternatives
summary: Purpose Freight transportation has become an important source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly in urban areas where delivery systems are heavily dependent on diesel-powered vehicles. Although a wide range of alternative strat
content: Purpose Freight transportation has become an important source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly in urban areas where delivery systems are heavily dependent on diesel-powered vehicles. Although a wide range of alternative strategies have been proposed to reduce this reliance, existing studies mainly evaluate these options in isolation and with a primary focus on environmental benefits. Such an approach overlooks the broader set of factors, such as costs, infrastructure requirements and traffic-related impacts, that ultimately determine the real-world applicability of these strategies. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review of 112 peer-reviewed studies was used to identify nine strategies and cluster them into three main groups: means of transport, location and infrastructure-based solutions and operational and technological optimization. The study then applied the Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC) method to develop a priority index to compare these strategies based on four criteria: GHG mitigation potential, economic feasibility, traffic congestion reduction and infrastructure requirements. The evidence on criteria values originates from diverse secondary studies and the ranking procedure relies on normalization scales defined by the authors. Findings The analysis reveals that no single strategy performs the best across all criteria, emphasizing the need to balance tradeoffs in urban freight planning. Cargo cycles ranked the highest among the nine strategies, showing their balanced performance across all criteria. In contrast, biomethane trucks with the highest GHG reduction potential ranked lower, emphasizing the important effects of infrastructure and economic barriers. Originality/value By combining the evaluation of evidence with multi-criteria decision analysis, this study offers industry leaders and planners an illustrative basis for comparing urban freight alternatives, moving the discussion beyond simply identifying solutions toward prioritizing them in practice.

title: Coherent state sampling for molecular vibronic spectra
summary: Electronic spectroscopy is today among the most powerful methods for studying chemical systems, and state-resolved (line-assigned) simulations are essential for attributing spectral features to specific vibrational excitations. The standard
content: Electronic spectroscopy is today among the most powerful methods for studying chemical systems, and state-resolved (line-assigned) simulations are essential for attributing spectral features to specific vibrational excitations. The standard time-independent sum-over-states (SOS) route provides line assignments; while effective with truncation and prescreening, it can become computationally demanding as the number of modes increases. Vibronic boson sampling (VBS) offers an event-based alternative, but scaling photonic implementations remains challenging and the required vibronic inputs can be demanding for larger systems. Here we introduce coherent-state sampling (CSS), a sampling scheme for the Linear Coupling Model (LCM), where vibrational modes are independent. This enables a photonic architecture based on a single reconfigurable optical channel with essentially fixed hardware complexity; increasing system size is handled by additional measurement iterations rather than additional optical modes. Using pentacene as a test case, we demonstrate an end-to-end workflow—electronic-structure input, sampling strategy, hardware validation, and comparison to experiment—showing that both a laptop implementation and a superconducting-detector photonic implementation reproduce reference spectra with high fidelity and yield band shapes in good agreement with experiment. While not targeting quantum advantage, CSS provides a practically scalable, state-resolved tool for LCM vibronic spectroscopy and a controlled displacement-dominated complement to more general VBS schemes.

title: KD4MT: A Survey of Knowledge Distillation for Machine Translation
summary: Knowledge Distillation (KD) as a research area has gained a considerable traction in recent years as a compression tool to address challenges related to ever-larger models in NLP. Remarkably, Machine Translation (MT) offers a much more nuan
content: Knowledge Distillation (KD) as a research area has gained a considerable traction in recent years as a compression tool to address challenges related to ever-larger models in NLP. Remarkably, Machine Translation (MT) offers a much more nuanced take on this narrative: in MT, KD also functions as a general-purpose knowledge transfer mechanism that shapes supervision and translation quality as well as efficiency. This survey synthesizes KD for MT (KD4MT) across 105 papers. We begin by introducing both MT and KD for non-experts, followed by an overview of the standard KD approaches relevant to MT applications. Subsequently, we categorize advances in the KD4MT literature based on (i) their methodological contributions and (ii) their practical applications. Our qualitative and quantitative analyses identify common trends in the field and highlight key research gaps as well as the absence of unified evaluation practice for KD methods in MT. We further provide practical guidelines for selecting a KD method in concrete settings and highlight potential risks associated with the application of KD to MT such as increased hallucination and bias amplification. Finally, we discuss the role of LLMs in re-shaping the KD4MT field. To support further research, we complement our survey with a publicly available database summarizing the main characteristics of the surveyed KD methods and a glossary of key terms.

title: Linking Solvation Structure, Activity, and Electronic Structure to Electrochemical Stability in Lithium-ion Battery Electrolytes
summary: Electrolyte stability governs the performance and lifetime of Li-ion batteries, yet a quantitative molecular-level understanding of how salt concentration influences electrochemical stability remains elusive. Here, we combine molecular dyna
content: Electrolyte stability governs the performance and lifetime of Li-ion batteries, yet a quantitative molecular-level understanding of how salt concentration influences electrochemical stability remains elusive. Here, we combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, a lattice fluid theory, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), density functional theory (DFT), and electrochemical measurements to quantitatively link solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure to the electrochemical stability of LiPF6 in EC/EMC (3:7 v/v) across a wide concentration range. We derive simple analytic expressions for species activities, parametrized using coordination numbers obtained from Raman spectroscopy, and validated against both MD simulations and experiment. Increasing salt concentration promotes PF6– participation in the Li+ solvation shell while suppressing free solvent populations, leading to systematic changes in the activities of species and an expanded electrochemical stability window. The lattice fluid theory directly links concentration-dependent solvation structure to measurable shifts in redox potentials via the Nernst equation, in good agreement with both computational predictions and experimental observations. DFT-predicted shifts in the unoccupied electronic states are confirmed by XAS measurements. These results establish a quantitative framework linking solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure to electrolyte stability, enabling the rational design of electrolytes with tailored electrochemical stability windows.

title: Urea-carbon nanotube composites: Synthesis, characterization, and differential antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli
source: Macedonian Journal of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering
summary: This study focuses on the synthesis, characterization, and antibacterial assessment of urea-functionalized carbon nanotube (CNT) composites. Amide nanotubes can be formed through the self-assembly of amphiphilic molecules driven by hydrogen
content: This study focuses on the synthesis, characterization, and antibacterial assessment of urea-functionalized carbon nanotube (CNT) composites. Amide nanotubes can be formed through the self-assembly of amphiphilic molecules driven by hydrogen-bonding interactions; however, previously reported approaches may be limited by aggregation and difficulties in large-scale production. In the present work, CNTs were functionalized with urea and systematically characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and measurement of the zeta potential to evaluate their structural, chemical, thermal, morphological, and surface-charge properties. The results demonstrated the incorporation of urea-derived functionalities onto the CNT surface. Although functionalization decreased the thermal stability of the CNTs, the spectroscopic results indicated the presence of amide-related functional groups in the CNT–urea–CNT composite. Among the characterization techniques, XPS provided direct evidence of urea incorporation through the appearance of the N 1s signal and corresponding changes in the C 1s and O 1s spectra. Collectively, these results demonstrate substantial modification of the CNT surface following treatment with urea, without implying definitive covalent attachment. Measurement of the zeta potential further revealed a substantial alteration in the surface-charge behavior following functionalization. As pH increased, the zeta potential progressively decreased, a phenomenon that can be attributed to the deprotonation of surface functional groups. Pristine CNTs exhibited an isoelectric point (IEP) at approximately pH 7–8, whereas urea functionalization shifted the IEP to around pH 4, indicating a significant modification of the CNT surface chemistry. The urea–CNT and CNT–urea–CNT composites exhibited concentration-dependent antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli at 0.01–0.1 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite was more active against S. aureus at 0.05 and 0.1 mg mL–1, while the urea–CNT composite showed greater activity at 0.01 mg mL–1. The CNT–urea–CNT composite consistently exhibited stronger activity against E. coli, with a maximum inhibition zone of 33 ± 3.01 mm at 0.1 mg mL–1. These differences may reflect variations in surface structure, dispersion, and interactions with bacterial membranes.

title: Layer-by-layer antibacterial coating encompassing silver nanoparticles for infection-resistant BioHole buttonHole device
summary: Most patients in nephrology units require hemodialysis three times per week. Among the available vascular access techniques, the buttonhole method offers distinct advantages, including improved patient comfort and consistent cannulation. Ho
content: Most patients in nephrology units require hemodialysis three times per week. Among the available vascular access techniques, the buttonhole method offers distinct advantages, including improved patient comfort and consistent cannulation. However, its clinical adoption remains constrained by a markedly increased risk of access-related infections. In this study, we present a novel and biocompatible coating strategy for the BioHole buttonhole medical device based on in-house produced silver nanoparticles. These particles were uniform, nanosized and had a narrow size distribution, exhibiting strong and reproducible antibacterial activity. Following mild aqueous amination of the BioHole device surface, a layer-by-layer assembly was applied to deposit a polyelectrolyte multilayer composed of cationic poly-L-lysine and anionic citrate- or citrate/tannic acid-capped silver nanoparticles. The coating demonstrated a strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , while maintaining excellent biocompatibility with L-929 fibroblasts. Overall, this technique provides a versatile strategy for developing antimicrobial surfaces on polycarbonate-based medical devices and establishes a preliminary proof of concept for further research into infection-resistant BioHole devices for buttonhole cannulation.

title: Nitrogen fertilisation reveals contrasting nitrogen-use efficiency and greenhouse gas emission intensity responses in linseed and oilseed rape
summary: Break crops vary in nitrogen (N) demand, yet direct comparisons of their nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity are limited. We compared four linseed ( Linum usitatissimum ) genotypes with one oilseed rape
content: Break crops vary in nitrogen (N) demand, yet direct comparisons of their nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity are limited. We compared four linseed ( Linum usitatissimum ) genotypes with one oilseed rape (OSR; Brassica napus ) genotype in a controlled glasshouse experiment across four N fertiliser rates (0–120 kg N ha − 1 ). Plant growth traits, NUE, daily and cumulative GHG fluxes (N 2 O, CO 2 , CH 4 ) and emission intensity (kg CO 2 e kg − 1 biomass) were quantified. OSR produced greater biomass, chlorophyll content, and NUE than linseed at all N rates. Absolute GHG emissions rose more steeply with increasing fertiliser in OSR. Consequently, CO 2 e emission intensity increased with N rate in linseed but decreased in OSR, consistent with biomass dilution. Fertiliser rate was the dominant driver of GHG fluxes; crop type had no independent effect on cumulative emissions once N rate was accounted for. Genotypic variation within linseed was negligible compared with crop- and fertiliser-driven effects. These results highlight a yield-emission trade-off: OSR maximises productivity but requires careful N management to control emissions while linseed maintains lower emission intensity under reduced N inputs. Linseed offers potential as a lower-intensity break crop in diversified, low-N rotations. Further field-scale evaluation needed to support agricultural decarbonisation.

title: Tens of MeV, collimated, bright fluxes of protons from ordered nanostructured targets in ultrarelativistic laser-matter interaction
summary: Laser-driven proton acceleration from nanostructured solid targets has been extensively studied, yet its performance under realistic temporal contrast conditions at petawatt-class facilities remains an open question. We present an experimen
content: Laser-driven proton acceleration from nanostructured solid targets has been extensively studied, yet its performance under realistic temporal contrast conditions at petawatt-class facilities remains an open question. We present an experimental investigation of proton generation from nanostructured and flat solid targets performed at the ELI-NP facility using femtosecond laser pulses at peak intensities of $\sim 3\times10^{21}$ \wcm. Proton spectra are compared for two contrast regimes: $\sim 10^{-10}$ without plasma mirror and $\sim 10^{-13}$ with single plasma mirror. Importantly, measurable enhancement in the cutoff energy persists for the nanowire targets at both contrast levels, indicating robustness of nanowire targets against moderate pre-pulse intensities. Alongside, study of energy resolved angular distribution reveals that nanowires promote more directional emission with higher flux of high-energy protons along the target normal, while flat targets produce broader angular distributions. The results are well supported and explained by 3D particle-in-cell simulations.

title: Esterified Banana Peel Waste as a Low-Cost Biosorbent for Heavy Metal Removal from Real Paint Manufacturing Wastewater: Effects of Concentration, pH, Contact Time, Dosage, and Regeneration
summary: The discharge of heavy metal-laden effluents from paint manufacturing operations is a significant and growing environmental hazard in industrialising economies, yet few biosorption studies test authentic multi-metal industrial effluent rath
content: The discharge of heavy metal-laden effluents from paint manufacturing operations is a significant and growing environmental hazard in industrialising economies, yet few biosorption studies test authentic multi-metal industrial effluent rather than synthetic single-metal solutions. This study investigates methanol/hydrochloric acid esterified banana peel waste (E-BPW) as a zero-cost biosorbent for removing chromium, nickel, cobalt, and lead from real paint manufacturing wastewater sourced from Brighto Paints Limited, Lahore, Pakistan. E-BPW was prepared by collection, drying, Tyler-standard sieve fractionation (850–1180 µm), and Fischer esterification with methanol and hydrochloric acid at 60°C for 48 h. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed carboxyl, hydroxyl, and ester carbonyl groups as the principal metal-binding moieties. Batch adsorption experiments evaluated the effects of initial metal concentration, solution pH, contact time, and adsorbent dosage, with metal concentrations quantified by flame atomic absorption spectroscopy. Under optimised conditions (pH 6–8, 80 min, 5 g·L⁻¹, 25°C), E-BPW achieved removal efficiencies of 80.3% (Cr), 68.9% (Co), 63.1% (Pb), and 56.0% (Ni). Regeneration with 2 mol·L⁻¹ HNO₃ recovered 99.3% of adsorbed metals, indicating strong potential for circular reuse. These findings demonstrate that waste-to-resource valorisation of agricultural byproducts can deliver technically effective, low-cost heavy metal removal for small-to-medium industrial applications, supporting Sustainable Development Goal 6 and circular-economy principles. The absence of isotherm, kinetic, and surface-characterisation data is acknowledged as a limitation, and a research agenda toward pilot-scale validation is proposed.

title: Correlating Spin and Optical Properties of Quantum Emitters in hBN
summary: Optically addressable spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are well suited for near-surface quantum sensing. They offer bright, wavelength-tunable single-photon emission with high optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contra
content: Optically addressable spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are well suited for near-surface quantum sensing. They offer bright, wavelength-tunable single-photon emission with high optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast at room temperature. Here, we synthesize a high density of visible defects in carbon-doped hBN flakes with a high yield (14%) of ODMR-active emitters. We find that the zero-field splitting parameter D is directly correlated with the zero-phonon line of an emitter, while the ODMR contrast shows no such correlation. We further analyze an individual narrowband defect showing 68% ODMR contrast and enhance its photon collection by ∼40% using a solid immersion lens. By advancing both the practical synthesis of the spin complexes and the understanding of their microscopic origin, our results move us toward the deterministic creation of ODMR-active quantum emitters.

title: Low-background 3D Bi2WO6 enables in situ sulfidation-induced photocurrent polarity switching for highly selective photoelectrochemical detection of sulfide ions
summary: Regulating photocurrent polarity is of significant importance for constructing photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing platforms with enhanced sensitivity and reliability in practical applications. However, the intrinsically high background phot
content: Regulating photocurrent polarity is of significant importance for constructing photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing platforms with enhanced sensitivity and reliability in practical applications. However, the intrinsically high background photocurrent in conventional PEC systems often masks analyte-induced signal variations, thereby hindering reliable photocurrent polarity switching. Herein, we report a low-background polarity-switchable PEC sensing platform based on three-dimensional (3D) flower-like Bi 2 WO 6 for the highly selective detection of S 2- . Benefiting from its intrinsically low background cathodic photocurrent and hierarchical nanosheet-assembled architecture, the constructed 3D Bi 2 WO 6 PEC platform exhibits a wide linear range (0-13.3 µM), a low detection limit of 16 nM outperforming the 2D Bi 2 WO 6 counterpart and most previously reported PEC sensing systems for S 2- detection, as well as excellent anti-interference capability and reliable analytical performance in complex real samples. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the hierarchical 3D architecture facilitates local S 2- enrichment and accelerates the in situ surface sulfidation process, leading to the rapid formation of a direct Z-scheme Bi 2 WO 6 /Bi 2 S 3 heterojunction. This target-triggered interfacial reconstruction dynamically reverses the dominant charge-carrier migration pathway, thereby inducing a distinct photocurrent transition from cathodic to anodic. This work provides an effective strategy for ultrasensitive S 2- detection and offers new insights into the design of low-background PEC sensors with dynamically tunable signal outputs.

title: Ligand Curvature Controls the Size of Self-Assembled Twisted Metallacycles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of metallacycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in co
content: Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of metallacycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in coordination angles. Here we introduce the first twisted metallacycles, in which ligand curvature is tuned through the tether-to-twist approach. Two twistacene dipyridyl ligands with only a 6° difference in the overall bend: the nearly planar Pl (14° twist) and the twisted Tw (34° twist) assemble with (dppp)Pd(II) and (dppp)Pt(II) corners {M} into dynamic equilibria between rhomboidal {M}2L2 and hexagonal {M}3L3 metallacycles. NMR, nanoESI-MS and X-ray crystallography show that racemic ligands self-sort with high fidelity: socially, into heterochiral meso {M}2L2 rhomboids, and narcissistically, into homochiral {M}3L3 hexagons. Van ‘t Hoff analysis shows ring expansion to be endothermic and entropy-driven throughout, with an enthalpic cost rising from 6–10 kJ mol–1 for Pl to 17–18 kJ mol–1 for Tw. This is explained by increased strain energy for mismatched planar ligands in {M}2L2 assemblies. A few degrees of backbone curvature therefore reshape the free-energy landscape of coordination-driven self-assembly.

title: Utilization of Induction-Furnace Slag as a Partial Silica Sand Replacement in CO2–Sodium Silicate Molding: Effects on Mold Properties and Casting Quality
summary: Landfill disposal of induction-furnace slag is a recurring cost for steel foundries, while rising silica sand costs burden CO 2 -sodium silicate molding. This study evaluates induction-furnace slag from AISI/SAE 4130 low-alloy steel melting
content: Landfill disposal of induction-furnace slag is a recurring cost for steel foundries, while rising silica sand costs burden CO 2 -sodium silicate molding. This study evaluates induction-furnace slag from AISI/SAE 4130 low-alloy steel melting as a partial silica sand replacement in CO 2 -hardened sodium silicate molds. Slag was substituted at six levels (10–40 wt.%) using cylindrical specimens rammed and CO 2 -gassed per AFS practice (triplicate, n = 3). Permeability, shatter index, green compression strength, green shear strength and mold hardness were measured, with all levels validated by casting trials at 1600°C. All five properties decreased monotonically with slag content, falling by 27.7–46.2% between the 0% (pure sand) baseline and 40% slag. EDS and sieve analysis identified two independent bases for this decline, slag is chemically lower in silicon and enriched in iron, manganese, calcium, chromium and molybdenum and also substantially finer and richer in fines than the base sand. Within the tested range, 25–30% slag gave the best balance of property retention and substitution level, remaining workable for small-to-medium steel castings. Trial castings showed no visible surface defects across all seven conditions, with surface roughness remaining within a comparatively narrow band and no consistent worsening trend with slag content. Partial slag substitution also reduces raw-material cost versus an all-silica-sand mold. These results support induction-furnace slag as a viable, low-cost partial substitute for silica sand in CO 2 molding, with 25–30% identified as a practical substitution window for industrial by product valorization.

title: ZIF-8-derived Cu–Zn–Zr mixed oxide catalysts for selective electrochemical CO2 reduction to methanol
summary: The selective electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to methanol offers a promising route for carbon utilization, although achieving high efficiency and selectivity remains challenging. In this study, we prepared a series of Cu–Zn–Zr mixed-oxide
content: The selective electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to methanol offers a promising route for carbon utilization, although achieving high efficiency and selectivity remains challenging. In this study, we prepared a series of Cu–Zn–Zr mixed-oxide catalysts by carbonizing a ZIF-8-based precursor containing copper and zirconium at 600 °C under nitrogen. Structural characterization by XRD, SEM, and EDX mapping showed the formation of monoclinic CuO, hexagonal ZnO, and tetragonal ZrO 2 phases, with nanoscale particle agglomerates and a uniform spatial distribution of Cu, Zn, and Zr throughout the catalyst. Among the compositions studied, the catalyst with 15% copper content (CuZnZr-15) showed the most favorable structural features and gave the best performance, reaching a Faradaic efficiency of 48.9% for methanol at a partial current density of 39.6 mA cm −2 . The improved activity is attributed to the coexistence of overlapping distributions of CuO, ZnO, and t-ZrO 2 phases, which is proposed to facilitate CO 2 activation and stabilize key intermediates. These findings show that ZIF-8-derived Cu–Zn–Zr oxide catalysts provide an effective platform for selective electrochemical CO 2 -to-methanol conversion.

title: Synergistic Dual-Modification of Polyurethane Sponge with MIL-53(Al) and Dimethylsilicone Oil for Efficient Oil–Water Separation of Oily Sludge Thermal Washing Wastewater
summary: Developing highly efficient adsorbents is one of the most feasible strategies to achieve oil-water separation. Conventional sponge adsorbents often suffer from limited capacity, poor cyclic stability, and low selectivity. To overcome these
content: Developing highly efficient adsorbents is one of the most feasible strategies to achieve oil-water separation. Conventional sponge adsorbents often suffer from limited capacity, poor cyclic stability, and low selectivity. To overcome these limitations, in this study, we synergistically modified a commercial polyurethane sponge using MIL-53(Al) and dimethylsilicone oil (DMS) via a facile dip-coating strategy, resulting in the M/Si-6@PU sponge. Through the optimization of the synthesis process, the dual-modified sponge evinced a water contact angle of 140° and an oil contact angle of 0° in air. This super-wetting property significantly accelerated the oil absorption process, reducing the absorption time by 48% (2.6 s compared to 5.0 s for the pristine polyurethane (PU) sponge). Meanwhile, this sponge exhibited outstanding adsorption capacities for various oils, including toluene (43 g·g − 1 ), pump oil (40 g·g − 1 ), diesel (39 g·g − 1 ), vegetable oil (35 g·g − 1 ), soybean oil (33 g·g − 1 ), and real oily wastewater (31 g·g − 1 ). Furthermore, the sponge maintained a high separation efficiency (> 99.0%) for oily sludge thermal washing wastewater over 8 cycles, with the efficiency remaining robust at 93.6% after 30 cycles. The composite also exhibited excellent chemical stability, retaining its hydrophobicity after 1 h of immersion in extreme pH environments (pH = 1 and 12). Therefore, the synergistic combination of hierarchical roughness and low surface energy renders the M/Si-6@PU sponge a highly promising candidate for practical and harsh industrial oily wastewater treatments.

title: Ultrasound-activated piezocatalytic microneedles rescue calcitonin gene-related peptide-dependent neuroimmune homeostasis to promote regeneration of infected diabetic wounds
summary: Although chronic, infected diabetic wounds are characterized by disrupted calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-driven neuroimmune signaling, CGRP monotherapy fails to rescue infection-damaged cutaneous sensory nerves. Herein, we develop p
content: Although chronic, infected diabetic wounds are characterized by disrupted calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-driven neuroimmune signaling, CGRP monotherapy fails to rescue infection-damaged cutaneous sensory nerves. Herein, we develop protease-responsive hydrogel microneedles (termed ABC microneedles) that integrate Au-decorated Bi 2 S 3 piezocatalytic nanorods with neuropeptide CGRP. The Au-Bi 2 S 3 interface forms Schottky junctions that amplify ultrasound-triggered piezocatalysis, thereby eliminating S. aureus biofilms, scavenging excess H 2 O 2 , alleviating hypoxia, and consuming surplus glucose in the wound microenvironment. In vitro, ultrasound-treated ABC microneedles protect fibroblasts and PC12 neuron-like cells, restore neurite outgrowth, and trigger paracrine signals that promote endothelial angiogenesis while dampening the excessive proinflammatory activation of myeloid cells. In a mouse model of infected diabetic wounds, this combinatorial therapy eradicates bacterial burden, restores cutaneous CGRP/transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 signaling, activates vasculature-regenerative transcriptional programs, and markedly accelerates wound closure. This study presents a synergistic strategy targeting both infection and neuroimmune dysfunction to treat recalcitrant diabetic wounds.

title: Spin-Dependent Transport in One-Dimensional Mercury- and Silver-Mediated DNA Nanowires
summary: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating disper
content: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second-nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role, the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. In these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin−orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the second-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowires exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-conserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal−metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.

title: Recreational Services of Kazakhstan’s National Parks in a Changing Climate: Economic Valuation and Visitor Dynamics
summary: The study evaluates the economic value of recreational services and the association between seasonal weather conditions and national park attendance in Kazakhstan (2014–2023), focusing on Burabai, Sairam-Ogem, and Karkaraly. Using data from
content: The study evaluates the economic value of recreational services and the association between seasonal weather conditions and national park attendance in Kazakhstan (2014–2023), focusing on Burabai, Sairam-Ogem, and Karkaraly. Using data from 350 survey respondents, it analysed tourist behaviour, willingness to pay for conservation and visitor trends. Results showed visitation peaks in summer (+30%) and declines in winter (-40–50%). The COVID-19 pandemic caused a 45% drop in 2020, with recovery by 2023. Over half (55.5%) are willing to pay USD 22.22 annually for conservation, while tourist spending averages USD 45.56 per trip. Recommendations include infrastructure development, climate adaptation, and sustainable financing mechanisms.

title: Roasting-Assisted Cobalt Extraction from Saprolite Nickel Laterite through Sulphuric Acid Leaching and Cyanex 272 Separation
summary: The increasing use of electric vehicles has driven demand for metals such as nickel and cobalt, which are primarily used in battery cathodes. Rising demand for battery metals drives the need for effective nickel and cobalt recovery. This st
content: The increasing use of electric vehicles has driven demand for metals such as nickel and cobalt, which are primarily used in battery cathodes. Rising demand for battery metals drives the need for effective nickel and cobalt recovery. This study examines the upgrading of cobalt from nickel laterite ore from Morowali, Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. Laterite, common in tropical regions, is a major source of these metals. Cobalt in laterite mineral deposits is often chemically bound to iron, especially in saprolite-type ores with high magnesium content, making its extraction technically difficult. In the chemical process, magnesium oxide reacts more readily with sulphuric acid than cobalt and nickel oxides do, making the extraction process inefficient. In this study, the ore was mixed with carbon and sodium sulfate, compacted, and roasted at 700–900°C for 2 hours. The highest cobalt content (0.188 wt%) was achieved at 700°C with 5% coal, though it is likely trapped in silicates. A leaching process using 2 M H₂SO₄, followed by pH adjustment to 4.5 with NH₄OH, enabled selective precipitation of iron, achieving up to 94.27% iron removal. The selective extraction process using Cyanex 272 showed a tendency to extract cobalt. However, due to the stripping inefficiency, cobalt recovery in this study remains limited and could be further improved.

title: Adaptation of Pinus sylvestris L. to the alpine tundra climate in the Southern Urals
source: Проблемы ботаники Южной Сибири и Монголии
summary: The intensive expansion of tree and shrub species into high-mountain and arctic ecosystems due to global climate change is a pressing issue in modern global science. The rapid invasion of woody vegetation into alpine tundra communities is a
content: The intensive expansion of tree and shrub species into high-mountain and arctic ecosystems due to global climate change is a pressing issue in modern global science. The rapid invasion of woody vegetation into alpine tundra communities is also occurring in all mountainous provinces of the Urals. In recent years, Pinus sylvestris L., a species uncommon in the Ural highlands, re-established and steadily grown on some peaks in the Southern Urals. Therefore, the adaptation of this species to the extreme climate of alpine tundra is of considerable interest. This paper presents the first analysis of leaf functional parameters of Pinus sylvestris in ecotopes of the Taganai Mountain Range (Southern Urals). The increasing of needles surface area, thickness, and density along the altitudinal gradient, with maximum values in trees from the alpine tundra has been shown. It was concluded that altitude-related changes in leaf functional traits of Pinus sylvestris reflect the adaptation to the highland climate, aimed at increasing the assimilating surface, enhancing light absorption efficiency, and optimizing intra-leaf diffusion of CO2. Under extreme climate, Pinus sylvestris develops the leaf structure that provides high assimilation potential creating the basis for maintaining a positive carbon balance, sustainable growth and functioning.

title: Synthesis of Biographite from Starch Biomass Using Additive Assisted Templating Approach
summary: Graphite is a critical mineral with wide-ranging applications in electronics, energy storage, and advanced materials manufacturing. As natural reserves remain limited, there is growing interest in using carbon-rich renewable precursors as a
content: Graphite is a critical mineral with wide-ranging applications in electronics, energy storage, and advanced materials manufacturing. As natural reserves remain limited, there is growing interest in using carbon-rich renewable precursors as alternative feedstocks for synthetic graphite production. Starch, being a widely available, renewable, and carbon-neutral biopolymer, is a compelling, sustainable alternative precursor for graphitic carbon synthesis. However, its inherently nongraphitizable nature requires templating additives to achieve graphitic ordering. In this study, we present a catalyst-free thermal route to produce graphitic carbon from starch-biopolymer-based packing peanuts through carbonization and graphitization, using graphene oxide (GO) and graphene (Gr) as templating additives. The resulting carbon structures were characterized using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), selected area electron diffraction (SAED), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Raman spectroscopy to evaluate the improvements in crystallite parameters La and Lc. At the optimal condition of 2.5 wt % GO loading, crystallite parameters of La = 77.9 nm and Lc = 25.94 nm were achieved, closely approaching those of natural graphite (La = 100 nm, Lc = 24.6 nm). Oxygen content, edge-to-basal oxygen ratio, sp2 π-network, and stacking height are identified as the key factors governing the formation of graphitic or hard carbon from the starch precursor. Unlike conventional catalytic graphitization, this approach requires no metal catalysts, eliminating postprocessing purification entirely. The results establish starch biopolymer as a viable and sustainable precursor for graphitic carbon production.

title: Robust microseismic arrival picking for hydraulic fracturing monitoring using a deep orthogonal collaborative ensemble network
summary: Accurate microseismic arrival picking is critical for hydraulic fracturing monitoring and subsequent fracture characterization. In recent years, deep learning-based pickers have achieved promising performance by automatically learning compl
content: Accurate microseismic arrival picking is critical for hydraulic fracturing monitoring and subsequent fracture characterization. In recent years, deep learning-based pickers have achieved promising performance by automatically learning complex waveform features. However, these pickers still face challenges in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments and in changing monitoring scenarios. These challenges are closely related to the restricted feature representation capability of individual network architectures, which may hinder their ability to capture diverse waveform features. To overcome this issue, we propose a deep orthogonal collaborative ensemble network (DOCE-Net) for robust microseismic arrival picking in hydraulic fracturing monitoring. DOCE-Net employs three heterogeneous base learners, including U-Net, Res-LSTM, and TransNet, to capture complementary waveform representations from multi-trace microseismic data. An orthogonality constraint is introduced to reduce feature redundancy and enhance diversity among different learners. The outputs of these learners are further combined through a semblance-based decision-level fusion strategy, which exploits prediction consistency to improve picking reliability. The proposed method is evaluated using two field hydraulic fracturing microseismic datasets. In the in-domain tests, DOCE-Net consistently outperforms the three individual base learners, particularly under low SNR conditions, and achieves higher accuracy than its single-trace counterpart, confirming the contribution of multi-trace spatial coherence. In the cross-domain tests, DOCE-Net also achieves superior performance after fine-tuning with limited labeled samples from an unseen monitoring domain. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DOCE-Net for robust microseismic arrival picking and cross-domain generalization. This study indicates that DOCE-Net can provide a reliable strategy for developing robust and transferable microseismic phase arrival pickers.

title: Economic and technical optimal sizing and placement of the hybrid energy resources in the electrical grid considering uncertainties
summary: The integration of hybrid energy resources in the electrical grids is essential for improving sustainability and reducing dependence on conventional fossil-fuel generation. Hence, installation of these energy resources is required to maximi
content: The integration of hybrid energy resources in the electrical grids is essential for improving sustainability and reducing dependence on conventional fossil-fuel generation. Hence, installation of these energy resources is required to maximize their technical and economic benefits while maintaining secure and stable grid operation. This paper focuses on a multi-objective optimization framework to identify the best installation and sizing of hybrid energy resources, considering the stochastic characteristics associated with renewable generation, such as photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbine (WT) systems. The stochastic aspects of renewable generation are represented using the point estimate method, enabling the framework to account for variations in renewable resource availability. The multi-objective functions for the optimal installation and sizing of hybrid energy resources are developed with a focus on operational costs, Voltage Stability Index (VSI), and power losses. Two case studies are provided to validate the proposed algorithm, examining different configurations of hybrid energy resources in IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 118-bus test systems. The optimal sizing of hybrid energy resources in the IEEE 33-bus test system result in a 3.68% reduction in operating costs, a 42.89% decrease in power losses, and a 0.19% improvement in the VSI. Also, minimization rate of the operational costs and power losses, and improvement of VSI for IEEE 118-bus test system are equal to 9.3%, 13.23% and 0.3%, respectively.

title: Evaluation of plasticity and damage evolution of welded S355 steel and its heat-affected zone
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: Welded joints are critical regions in steel structures where complex microstructures can reduce local ductility and fracture resistance. Stress triaxiality assessment is essential in welded joint analysis, as it enables the identification o
content: Welded joints are critical regions in steel structures where complex microstructures can reduce local ductility and fracture resistance. Stress triaxiality assessment is essential in welded joint analysis, as it enables the identification of highly constrained regions, such as the weld toe and heat-affected zone (HAZ), where crack initiation and propagation are more likely. These regions exhibit reduced ductility and an increased susceptibility to brittle failure, particularly in the presence of mechanisms such as hydrogen-induced cracking in offshore structures and pipelines. This study investigates the influence of stress triaxiality and microstructural heterogeneity on the plasticity and fracture behavior of S355 structural steel, its heat-affected zone (HAZ), and a representative weld metal. To investigate the material ductility and damage criteria for welded regions with potential difference in fracture strain, triaxiality stress-state, different notched specimens were tested to introduce controlled variations in triaxiality under different loading conditions. Local strain evolution and fracture strain were measured using Digital Image Correlation (DIC), while Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS) were employed to analyses fracture surfaces and identify microstructural and compositional features. The results reveal pronounced differences in fracture strain and triaxiality sensitivity between the base metal, HAZ, and weld metal. The HAZ exhibited the lowest ductility and the highest susceptibility to shear and mixed-mode loading, whereas the parent S355 steel retained higher strain and mixed-mode capacity. SEM observations confirmed that void nucleation and coalescence are highly different over welded regions, with less ductile fracture mechanics in the HAZ. The experimentally derived plasticity and fracture strain–triaxiality relationships were used to calibrate Bai–Wierzbicki (B–W) fracture loci, assessing strain capacity in welded structures. The findings are directly relevant to the plastic deformation regime and to structural scenarios involving low-cycle fatigue, accidental overload, and impact or collision events, where large strains and multiaxial cyclic stress states develop in welded zones. By quantifying the interplay between triaxiality, ductility, anisotropy, and microstructure, this work contributes to improved strain-based design and fracture assessment methods for critical welded steel structures.

title: A label-free domain-knowledge-informed framework for transferability evaluation of synthetic accessibility scoring in energetic chemical space
summary: Synthetic accessibility (SA) evaluation serves as a critical bridge between theoretical material design and experimental realization, and SA scoring has gained significant traction in the data-driven paradigm. However, the scarcity of high-
content: Synthetic accessibility (SA) evaluation serves as a critical bridge between theoretical material design and experimental realization, and SA scoring has gained significant traction in the data-driven paradigm. However, the scarcity of high-quality annotated synthesis difficulty data poses a formidable challenge for cross-domain assessment of existing scoring methods, particularly when transferring models from the pharmaceutical sector to energetic materials. To address this, we propose a domain-knowledge-driven evaluation framework tailored for unlabeled data. A multi-stage screening protocol integrating structural constraints, property calculation, and statistical monotonicity was implemented to construct a statistically controlled dataset of 28,195 candidate molecules. Unsupervised learning was then employed to characterize the distribution patterns of eight SA scoring models within the energetic chemical space, enabling preliminary transferability assessment without labels. Domain-knowledge-based validation, including boundary sample analysis and energy descriptor evaluation, confirmed that SAscore and BR-SAScore exhibit the most consistently favorable transferability. Using RDX as a benchmark, we delineated a high-energy, easy-to-synthesize chemical space, revealing that heteroatom-rich linkages with moderate scaffold complexity are pivotal for novel high-energy-density materials. This work establishes a label-free framework for evaluating SA model transferability in neutral nitro-containing CHON chemical space, providing a robust methodological reference for developing energetic-material-specific scoring models.

title: A Practical Approach to Efficiency Calibration of an HPGe Gamma-Ray Spectrometer for Soil Matrix Measurements Using Reference Materials
summary: In this study, a metrologically traceable and cost-effective efficiency calibration method for a coaxial HPGe gamma-ray spectrometer was developed using the IAEA–312 soil reference material and validated with the IAEA–447 moss-soil referenc
content: In this study, a metrologically traceable and cost-effective efficiency calibration method for a coaxial HPGe gamma-ray spectrometer was developed using the IAEA–312 soil reference material and validated with the IAEA–447 moss-soil reference material. The efficiency curve was derived from selected gamma-ray lines of 214Pb and 214Bi in the energy range 242–1764 keV and fitted using a fourth-order logarithmic polynomial. The fitted model showed excellent agreement with the experimental data (R2 ≈ 0.996), with residuals within ±6%. The calibration was applied to determine the activity concentrations of 226Ra, 232Th, 137Cs, and 40K in IAEA–447. The measured values were in good agreement with the certified values, with relative deviations below 6% and all zeta-scores well below unity, indicating no statistically significant bias and confirming the traceability of the efficiency transfer. A comprehensive uncertainty analysis showed that the uncertainty in the efficiency calibration primarily determines overall accuracy, whereas counting statistics dominate for weaker gamma-ray lines. The results demonstrated that this approach provides a practical, matrix-matched calibration in which geometry-specific effects are inherently accounted for through empirical transfer and verified by reference material validation.

title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
summary: Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound
content: Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. Additionally, T. iboga produces ibophyllidine, a pyrroloindole alkaloid that utilizes the same upstream precursor as voacangine, but is a member of a structurally distinct alkaloid class. Here we use bulk and single cell gene expression from leaf and root tissue to identify the unknown enzymes from these two pathways. We identify two additional enzymes that enable biosynthesis of voacangine in a heterologous host. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.

title: A trait-based vulnerability indicator framework for deep-sea benthic species and ecosystems under multiple climate stressors
summary: Deep-sea benthic biodiversity remains underrepresented in climate-risk assessments because transferable indicators for species- and ecosystem-level vulnerability are still limited. Here, we develop and apply a trait- and exposure-based vuln
content: Deep-sea benthic biodiversity remains underrepresented in climate-risk assessments because transferable indicators for species- and ecosystem-level vulnerability are still limited. Here, we develop and apply a trait- and exposure-based vulnerability indicator framework to assess climate vulnerability in 122 globally distributed deep-sea benthic species and the ecosystems they occupy under end-of-century projections (2090–2100) for SSP1–2.6 and SSP5–8.5. The framework integrates trait-based sensitivity, projected exposure to benthic temperature, pH, and dissolved oxygen change, and ecosystem-level phylogenetic diversity weighting. Vulnerability at both species and ecosystem levels was significantly higher under SSP5–8.5 than under SSP1–2.6. Across scales, ocean acidification generated the highest absolute vulnerability, whereas deoxygenation showed the steepest relative increase under the high-emission scenario. Relatively elevated vulnerability occurred in the Arctic and sub-Arctic, the Mediterranean Sea, and parts of the North Atlantic and continental margins, with broader or more pronounced patterns under SSP5–8.5. Highly vulnerable taxa were generally characterized by calcified structures and limited mobility, indicating strong trait-mediated susceptibility to future climate change. This framework provides a scalable indicator for comparative assessment of benthic climate vulnerability across taxa, regions, and emission pathways, and offers a practical basis for hotspot identification, ecological monitoring, and conservation prioritization.

title: Raw jujube stone and raw hawthorn stone particles as green adsorbents for the adsorption of different organic dyes
summary: In this work, the raw jujube stone particles (RJSP) and the raw hawthorn stone particles (RHSP) as efficient natural and green adsorbents were used for the adsorption of methylene blue (MB), malachite green (MG), crystal violet (CV), and di
content: In this work, the raw jujube stone particles (RJSP) and the raw hawthorn stone particles (RHSP) as efficient natural and green adsorbents were used for the adsorption of methylene blue (MB), malachite green (MG), crystal violet (CV), and disperse red 1 (DR1) dyes. The functional groups, morphology, particle size, surface area, and pore size of RJSP and RHSP were determined using FT-IR, BET, FESEM, TEM, and EDX. The green adsorbents RJSP and RHSP showed high efficiency in the adsorption of MB, MG, CV, and DR1 dyes and showed comparable performance to other reported adsorbents. According to the results, the adsorption of MB, MG, CV, and DR1 dyes onto RJSP and RHSP follows the Freundlich isotherm, while the kinetics are well described by the pseudo-second-order model. Also, according to the Langmuir isotherm, RJSP exhibited maximum adsorption capacities (Q m ) of 145, 124, 114, and 98 mg/g for MB, MG, CV, and DR1, respectively, while RHSP showed adsorption capacities of 84, 111, 102, and 94 mg/g. In addition, thermodynamic parameters confirm that the adsorption of MB, MG, CV, and DR1 dyes is exothermic on RJSP and endothermic on RHSP. Finally, the RJSP and RHSP can be used as affordable, environmentally friendly, and effective natural adsorbents for the removal of various industrial dyes.

title: From isolated component failure to coupled degradation networks in proton exchange membrane fuel cells
summary: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are among the most promising energy conversion technologies for achieving sustainable and carbon-neutral energy systems. Despite remarkable advances in catalyst and membrane materials, the limite
content: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are among the most promising energy conversion technologies for achieving sustainable and carbon-neutral energy systems. Despite remarkable advances in catalyst and membrane materials, the limited durability of membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) remains a major barrier to large-scale commercialization. Unlike previous studies that treated individual component degradation as isolated failures without adequate mitigation strategies, growing evidence shows these processes are highly interconnected. Chemical, electrochemical, mechanical, thermal, and mass-transport phenomena interact across multiple length scales, triggering cascading failure pathways that ultimately govern system-level durability. In this review, we move beyond conventional component-by-component descriptions and present an integrated perspective on coupled degradation networks in PEMFCs. We systematically analyze degradation mechanisms, highlighting how catalyst dissolution, chemical decomposition, carbon corrosion, ionomer degradation, interfacial delamination, water/heat management, contaminants, and flow-field nonuniformity mutually accelerate one another. Furthermore, we critically review recent advances in operando characterization, mechanistic evaluation, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted diagnostics, and degradation modeling to highlight emerging strategies for identifying coupled pathways and predicting long-term durability. This review provides a comprehensive framework for designing durable, next-generation PEMFCs by treating degradation as an interconnected network of failures rather than isolated component issues, while proposing key design principles across materials, diagnostics, and systems.

title: Polyols and Sugars as a Molecular Platform for Prebiotic Evolution: From Mineral Selection to RNA and Cellular Life
source: London Journal of Research in Science Natural & Formal
summary: The emergence of life required the progressive integration of organic synthesis, molecular selection, chemical activation, compartmentalization, and information storage. Although prebiotic research has extensively investigated amino acids,
content: The emergence of life required the progressive integration of organic synthesis, molecular selection, chemical activation, compartmentalization, and information storage. Although prebiotic research has extensively investigated amino acids, nucleobases, lipids, and RNA, the potential role of polyols and sugars as molecular connectors among these chemical systems remains comparatively underexplored.
