Notably, whilst all KPHIS outperform bulk KPHI, the activity varies non‐monotonically with shell thickness and excitation wavelength, whereby the thickest‐shelled sphere ‒ not the one with the highest specific surface area and pore volume ‒ is most active at 365 and 406 nm, with apparent quantum yields up to ∼3.9%. These experiments reveal that the activity is governed not by porosity alone but by the kinetic competition between donor‐mediated hole extraction (least efficient in the most porous sample at low wavelength irradiation) and stabilization of long‐lived reduced states that drive O 2 reduction. Shell thickness should be co‐optimized with light penetration depth and donor‐conditioned charge dynamics, rather than maximizing porosity alone.

title: Probing Formation, Degradation, and Entropic Changes in Lithium-Ion Batteries via a Versatile Reference Electrode
summary: In 2013, Wenquan Lu and colleagues at Argonne National Lab proposed entropy coefficient as a parameter that could characterize the structural changes in lithium and manganese rich (LMR) layered transition metal oxide cathode active material
content: In 2013, Wenquan Lu and colleagues at Argonne National Lab proposed entropy coefficient as a parameter that could characterize the structural changes in lithium and manganese rich (LMR) layered transition metal oxide cathode active materials as voltage fade progresses over life. Subsequently, in 2021, Friedrich and Gasteiger demonstrated entropic changes between the first activation cycle of LMR-NCM and subsequent stabilization cycle. The work seen here demonstrates entropy coefficient as a parameter that tracks structural changes in LMR active materials as voltage fade progresses over life through the use of a versatile reference electrode placed between a graphite anode and LMR cathode. The entropy coefficient of the LMR and graphite are measured explicitly using the versatile reference electrode at three different points during an accelerated degradation study, illustrating the change in the entropy coefficient and associated equilibrium potential shift in the materials due to structural changes. Additionally, by activating the reference electrode (partially delithiating it to the plateau potential) prior to cell formation, the performance of each electrode during the formation process can be studied, offering a picture into first cycle efficiency in-situ.

title: The Last Gasps of a Dying Star: ALMA Observations of the Preplanetary Nebula IRAS 06530–0213
summary: We present high-angular-resolution ( ∼ 0 . ″ 1 − 0 . ″ 5 ) Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of millimeter-wave line and continuum emission (at ∼0.44 and 0.88 mm) in the preplanetary nebula IRAS 06530–0213 (IR
content: We present high-angular-resolution ( ∼ 0 . ″ 1 − 0 . ″ 5 ) Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of millimeter-wave line and continuum emission (at ∼0.44 and 0.88 mm) in the preplanetary nebula IRAS 06530–0213 (IRAS 06530). These data show the presence of an extended circular ring—first evidence of the last thermal pulse preceding the post-asymptotic giant branch (AGB) phase in a carbon star—and a central bipolar nebula (CBN) and torus. The mass-loss rate of IRAS 06530’s AGB progenitor decreased immediately after the thermal pulse, then rose again just before the post-AGB phase, as evidenced by the presence of filamentary arc structures around the CBN. The arc stuctures are likely part of a 3D Archimedean spiral structure generally attributed to the presence of a binary companion. However, we do not find a compact continuum source at the location of IRAS 06530’s central star, such as that associated with the compact dusty disks typically found in disk-prominent post-AGB objects known to have binary companions. The expansion ages derived for the torus and CBN imply that IRAS 06530’s progenitor transitioned to a post-AGB star ≲700 yr ago. The molecular mass of the ejecta in IRAS 06530 is dominated by the filamentary arc region, with a mass M H 2 = ( 0.12 − 0.25 ) M ⊙ . Compared with solar values, the torus of IRAS 06530 appears to be significantly (modestly) enriched in 13 C and 17 O ( 15 N), as well—a pattern of rare-isotope enrichment inconsistent with standard nucleosynthesis models. From the luminosity of IRAS 06530 and the age of its detached shell, while it was still on the AGB, we infer that the mass of IRAS 06530’s progenitor was 1.6–3.4 M ⊙ .

title: An ALMA sub-kiloparsec test of the Kennicutt--Schmidt relation in a strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxy at z∼2.78
summary: Star formation is a key process driving galaxy evolution, but understanding how it proceeds within the interstellar medium (ISM) requires observations that resolve the cold molecular gas and dust on sub-kiloparsec (sub-kpc) scales. At z,∼,2
content: Star formation is a key process driving galaxy evolution, but understanding how it proceeds within the interstellar medium (ISM) requires observations that resolve the cold molecular gas and dust on sub-kiloparsec (sub-kpc) scales. At z,∼,2--3, near the peak of cosmic star formation, such spatial resolution can generally only be achieved through strong gravitational lensing. We present an ALMA study of SMM:J065837.6-555705, hereafter SMM,J0658, a 20 main-sequence star-forming galaxy at z_̊m CO,=,2.7768,±,0.0002 that is lensed by the Bullet Cluster (1E,0657-56; z,=,0.296) into three images. We used 0 and 0 ALMA Band-3 data to test the Kennicutt--Schmidt (KS) relation at sub-kpc scales at cosmic noon. Using a JWST-based parametric strong-lensing model of the Bullet Cluster, we reconstructed source-plane and rest-frame 803 ̆pmum dust-continuum maps down to physical scales of ∼,200 pc. We derived spatially resolved maps of the intrinsic molecular gas mass surface density (Σ_̊m mol), star formation rate surface density (Σ_̊m SFR), and molecular gas depletion time (τ_̊m dep), and quantified the scale dependence of the CO-to-dust flux ratio over apertures from 200 pc to 3.2 kpc across the reconstructed source. CO(3--2) The 0 ALMA data reveal massive (M_̊m mol,∼,10^9 _⊙) and dense star-forming clumps, with Σ_̊m mol,∼,1.3--2.3 times10^3 ̊m M ̊m M ̊m pc ^ -2 , Σ_̊m SFR,∼,0.5--2.3 $ ̊m M _⊙, ̊m yr ^ -1 , ̊m kpc ^ -2 $, and τ_̊m dep,∼,0.82--2.56 Gyr. The observed CO--dust spatial de-correlation produces a strong scale dependence on τ_̊m dep. We find a KS-relation breakdown scale of 0.8,±,0.1 kpc in SMM,J0658, which is consistent with the resolution of individual regions tracing distinct evolutionary stages of the star formation cycle within the ISM. The ALMA and JWST data also reveal evidence of a lensed galaxy pair at z,∼,2.78, although it remains uncertain whether SMM,J0658 is undergoing an early-stage interaction that could contribute to an enhanced star formation efficiency in localized regions of the ISM. Our results show that the apparent universality of the KS relation breaks down once individual regions of the star formation process are spatially resolved, in line with observations from the local Universe to z,∼,1. We extend this picture to z,∼,2.78, opening a new window onto the resolved properties of the clumpy cold ISM and the star formation cycle at cosmic noon.

title: In vitro antibacterial activity and oral epithelial cytocompatibility of myrrh-mediated silver nanoparticles
summary: This study aimed to synthesize and physicochemically characterize myrrh-mediated silver nanoparticles, evaluate their antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and assess their cytocompatibility with n
content: This study aimed to synthesize and physicochemically characterize myrrh-mediated silver nanoparticles, evaluate their antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and assess their cytocompatibility with normal oral epithelial cells (OECs). Silver nanoparticles were synthesized using an aqueous Commiphora molmol myrrha extract and characterized using spectroscopic, diffraction, light-scattering, elemental, and electron-microscopic methods. Antibacterial activity was assessed using agar diffusion against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, with piperacillin/tazobactam as a control. Cytotoxicity in normal OECs, MCF-7 cells, and HeLa cells was assessed in vitro using tetrazolium reduction and neutral red uptake assays after 24 h. Nanoparticle formation was supported by a plasmon band at 416 nm and a face-centered cubic silver structure. Transmission electron microscopy showed predominantly spherical to quasi-spherical particles measuring 4.3-39.3 nm (mean, 17.7 nm); the hydrodynamic size distribution peaked at 210 nm, and the zeta potential was - 27.5 mV. The minimum inhibitory concentration was 10 µL for both bacteria; bactericidal endpoints were 40 and 70 µL for S. aureus and P. aeruginosa, respectively. OECs viability remained above 83% at 100 µg/mL, whereas MCF-7 and HeLa cells were 18.56% and 14.85, respectively. The preliminary results provide on the biocompatibility of myrrh-mediated silver nanoparticles in OECs and antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The study will be applied to odontogenic-related diseases.

title: SiO Maser Line-width Diagnostics of Asymptotic Giant Branch Stars and Red Supergiants: The Red Supergiant-adjacent Region in the FWZI–Luminosity Plane
summary: We investigate whether SiO maser line profiles can distinguish asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars from red supergiants (RSGs) and identify unusual AGB-classified sources near the RSG regime. We compiled 2956 detected SiO maser spectra for
content: We investigate whether SiO maser line profiles can distinguish asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars from red supergiants (RSGs) and identify unusual AGB-classified sources near the RSG regime. We compiled 2956 detected SiO maser spectra for 1551 objects and constructed reference samples of 1068 O-rich AGB stars and 36 RSGs. The full width at zero intensity (FWZI) was reliably measured for 1020 AGB stars and 32 RSGs. AGB stars are concentrated at narrow line widths: 81.5% have FWZI < 10 km s −1 , whereas 81.2% of RSGs have FWZI > 15 km s −1 and none have FWZI < 10 km s −1 . Infrared two-color diagrams provide only partial separation. Combining FWZI with luminosities based primarily on quality-filtered Gaia/Bailer-Jones distances, with independent literature distances for several RSGs, reveals a weak tendency for wider SiO maser lines at higher luminosities but no clean boundary. We therefore define an empirical RSG-adjacent region in the FWZI–luminosity plane, 15 ≤ FWZI ≤ 26.6 km s −1 and 3.9 ≤ log ( L / L ⊙ ) ≤ 4.9 , to characterize the high-luminosity, broad-line tail of the AGB-classified sample. Ten sources fall within this region. Using infrared spectral energy distributions, DUSTY fits, OH/H 2 O maser information, and variability, we find that six are most naturally interpreted as luminous AGB-like objects, two warrant follow-up to assess possible high-initial-mass AGB, RSG-like, or super-AGB-related interpretations, and two are less securely constrained because of poor DUSTY fits. The RSG-adjacent region is therefore a physically mixed screening space, not a definitive classification box, for selecting high-priority follow-up targets.

title: Coulomb screening of the orbital inverse Faraday effect in finite-size diffusive conductors
summary: We study the effects of Coulomb screening on the second-order dc response in finite-size diffusive conductors. Starting from the Boltzmann equation supplemented by the self-consistent electrostatic field, we develop a kinetic theory of the
content: We study the effects of Coulomb screening on the second-order dc response in finite-size diffusive conductors. Starting from the Boltzmann equation supplemented by the self-consistent electrostatic field, we develop a kinetic theory of the inverse Faraday effect for a two-dimensional disk driven by a circularly polarized ac electric field. In this formulation, the first-order charge modulation and the induced electric field are coupled through the Coulomb interaction, and the self-consistent first-order solution determines the nonlinear source for the second-order dc circulating current responsible for the induced magnetic moment. The radial problem is solved numerically using an angular-harmonic expansion and the Chebyshev collocation method. It is shown that in the non-self-consistent approximation the frequency dependence of the second-order dc response has a maximum when the diffusion length associated with the radiation frequency becomes comparable to the sample radius. This behavior is found to be strongly modified by self-consistent screening. We demonstrate that Coulomb screening shifts the maximum of the dc response to a higher drive frequency and suppresses the peak amplitude. This behavior is observed consistently for the area-integrated circulating current and the induced magnetic moment. The obtained results clarify the limitations of the non-self-consistent description of the inverse Faraday effect and show that Coulomb self-consistency is crucial for quantitative predictions of optically induced dc magnetization in finite-size diffusive conductors.

title: Atom-Wise Allocation of Message-Passing Scale for Molecular Property Prediction
source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
summary: Molecular properties depend on chemical structure at different ranges, from local polar groups governing solvation to extended substructures shaping bioactivity, yet graph neural networks usually fix one propagation scale for every atom. We
content: Molecular properties depend on chemical structure at different ranges, from local polar groups governing solvation to extended substructures shaping bioactivity, yet graph neural networks usually fix one propagation scale for every atom. We present PRISM (Per-atom Routing over Intermediate States of Message Passing), in which each atom’s encoded features produce a bounded scalar that positions a unimodal distribution over retained message-passing states and matching circular-fingerprint radii. Because one coordinate translates the whole profile, allocated depth responds to the routing scalar in closed form: at fixed temperature it is nondecreasing, its sensitivity scales with the profile variance, and it saturates in the clipped regions. Beyond providing closed-form analyzability, this constrained one-parameter profile matches or significantly outperforms parameter-matched, unconstrained node-wise gates and Jumping Knowledge attention. Under scaffold partitions with equal tuning budgets against eight graph, fingerprint, and geometric baselines, PRISM trained from scratch without three-dimensional coordinates achieves the lowest mean error on aqueous solubility and hydration free energy and strong accuracy on BACE and BBBP. As a general layer-combination rule, PRISM transfers directly to GCN, GIN, and GAT backbones, reducing hydration free energy error by up to 29% relative to last-layer readout. Applied to a pretrained GIN, it improves on last-layer readout on four of six endpoints and gives the lowest lipophilicity error overall. In trained models, allocated depth differs systematically between atom types in a task-dependent way, and permuting profiles among a molecule’s atoms raises prediction error on several endpoints, so the rule acts as a learned counterpart of atom typing.

title: Continuous UV level estimation using photochromic PLA surfaces: a transformer-based heterogeneous deep ensemble approach
summary: This study presents a high-precision, continuous machine vision system for estimating ultraviolet (UV) radiation levels using low-cost, 3D-printable polylactic acid-based photochromic material (PLA-PCM) surfaces. Filament color transitions
content: This study presents a high-precision, continuous machine vision system for estimating ultraviolet (UV) radiation levels using low-cost, 3D-printable polylactic acid-based photochromic material (PLA-PCM) surfaces. Filament color transitions under different UV irradiance levels were recorded at eight ambient color temperatures, and a zero-padding spatial arrangement protocol was applied to the 252 × 56 images that underwent color changes to extract stable temporal features. The methodology employs a deep transformer encoder with multi-head self-attention, computing global temporal dependencies in parallel within 222 ms and ensuring edge-AI compatibility. Multi-spectral feature vectors from the RGB, HSV, and CIELAB color spaces, augmented with ambient color temperature and DCT components, were constructed for 59 000 frames derived from 236 video sessions at 10 Hz. A strict zero-data-leakage protocol was enforced through video-level holdout, in which each session is assigned to a partition as an indivisible unit. Each fold contained the fast-onset phase and the slow, decelerating approach to saturation of the photochromic reaction, with five-fold cross-validation. The resulting transformer-based heterogeneous deep ensemble (T-HDE), integrating Transformer, SVR, CatBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTrees, and MLP regressors with Nelder–Mead-optimized weights, achieved R 2 = 0.9938 on the held-out test set with a homoscedastic error distribution, indicating that prediction accuracy is with residuals whose spread shows no systematic dependence on the UV level across the measured range. In single-frame snapshot mode, R 2 = 0.9811 was attained, confirming that even without temporal sequence information, the color features extracted from the standardized frame alone provide robust UV estimation. These findings demonstrate that PLA-PCM surfaces, coupled with the T-HDE architecture, can serve as precise, continuous, and cost-effective UV dosimeters for IoT-based environmental monitoring and edge-AI sensing platforms.

title: Flow mechanisms of leading-edge-tubercled hydrofoils and their implications for ship propulsion and underwater noise
summary: Upstream hydrofoils modify the flow approaching a ship propeller, but their hydrodynamic and acoustic consequences depend on how the induced vortices, separation and pressure fluctuations interact with the downstream system. This study comb
content: Upstream hydrofoils modify the flow approaching a ship propeller, but their hydrodynamic and acoustic consequences depend on how the induced vortices, separation and pressure fluctuations interact with the downstream system. This study combines (a) a computational investigation of isolated tubercled hydrofoils with (b) towing-tank experiments on hydrofoils mounted ahead of a model tanker propeller. An unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes campaign covered 31 hydrofoil geometries at seven angles of attack and a Reynolds number of 1.83 × 10⁵. The computed flow exhibits counter-rotating streamwise vortices and an incidence-dependent transition from localised separation to a connected separated region. The experiments assessed 30 hydrofoil configurations using hydrophone pressure spectra and distance per revolution (DPR). The largest single-band pressure power spectral density reduction was 80.2%, while the highest configuration-mean DPR increased by 7.8%; these are separate outcomes and do not establish simultaneous gains. Tubercle effects changed sign with the underlying geometry. Integrating the computational and experimental analysis, the studies support a framework in which upstream flow restructuring produces geometry-dependent hydrodynamic–acoustic trade-offs. The paper shows a series of insights that tubercled hydrofoils can generate counter-vortex flows and this can generate notable implications in ship hydrodynamics and underwater noise control.

title: Forensic BTEX Speciation, Directional Conditional Probability Function (CPF) Plume Characterization, and Concentration-Based Inhalation Carcinogenic Risk Assessment Across 13 Urban Microclimates
summary: Speciated monoaromatic hydrocarbons - benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (BTEX) - govern urban photochemical oxidation while imposing severe carcinogenic inhalation risks. We investigate BTEX speciation, photochemical reactivity, d
content: Speciated monoaromatic hydrocarbons - benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (BTEX) - govern urban photochemical oxidation while imposing severe carcinogenic inhalation risks. We investigate BTEX speciation, photochemical reactivity, diagnostic emission ratios, Conditional Probability Function (CPF) directional polar vectors, and inhalation health risks across 13 continuous monitoring stations in Kolkata and Howrah during 2024-2025 (721,193 valid observations). Monoaromatic loading (total BTEX) spanned from 8.02 ug/m3 at parkland background (Fort William) to 53.64 ug/m3 in heavy industrial corridors (Ghusuri). Toluene dominated mass loading (41.8-54.2%), whereas m/p-xylene exhibited the highest Ozone Formation Potential (OFP) via maximum incremental reactivity (MIR) metrics. Diagnostic toluene-to-benzene (T/B) mass ratios resolved two distinct source regimes: vehicular-exhaust dominated transport corridors (T/B = 1.6-2.4) in central Kolkata, contrasting with heavy industrial solvent, paint, and metallurgical emissions (T/B = 3.2-6.1) across Howrah foundry clusters. Directional CPF polar plots coupled with boundary-layer wind vectors identified localized point-source plumes from western riverbank petrochemical and coating units. Inhalation health risk modeling reveals alarming benzene carcinogenicity: lifetime cancer risk (LCR) exceeds the USEPA statutory threshold (1.0 x 10^-6) network-wide, reaching an extreme upper bound of 5.8 x 10^-5 in industrial Dasnagar and Ghusuri. These forensic findings demonstrate an urgent need for targeted volatile organic compound containment, vapor recovery retrofits at fueling facilities, and mandatory benzene emission controls across eastern Indian industrial clusters.

title: The Disappearing Chemical Signature of Temperate Glacier Ice
summary: Ice-core records of environmental pollution and climate preserved in mountain glaciers are threatened by meltwater percolation and the transition to temperate conditions. Here, we investigate major-ion preservation and redistribution in a 2
content: Ice-core records of environmental pollution and climate preserved in mountain glaciers are threatened by meltwater percolation and the transition to temperate conditions. Here, we investigate major-ion preservation and redistribution in a 221 m ice core from the temperate Adamello Glacier (Italian Alps). A preliminary chronology dates the continuously investigated upper 60 m w.e. to 1901-1985 CE. Ionic concentrations decline markedly with depth, averaging only 11% of fresh-snow values across nine species at 50-59 m w.e. Compared with cold Alpine glaciers, the Adamello ice-core records exhibit lower ionic concentrations and weaker inter-ion correlations, indicating extensive post-depositional alteration. Estimated relative depletion is greatest for SO42-, Ca2+, and Mg2+ (92-99%) and lowest for F- and Cl- (67-69%). F- retains some original temporal variability, consistent with greater resistance to leaching. Preferential elution further modifies ionic ratios, with more than 90% of samples falling outside the range required for conventional marine and crustal source apportionment. Elemental mapping reveals diminishing enrichment of soluble impurities along ice-grain boundaries, consistent with their removal through the liquid-vein network of temperate ice. Together, these findings demonstrate that meltwater-driven self-purification profoundly alters the chemical composition of temperate glaciers, irreversibly compromising the preservation of environmental signals associated with the most soluble and mobile ionic species.

title: A Technology-Driven Maturity Framework for Truck Appointment Systems in Ports
summary: Truck Appointment Systems (TAS) are essential tools for reducing gate congestion at container terminals (CTs). However, the adoption of these systems and the required enabling technologies varies across CTs. This study presents a five level
content: Truck Appointment Systems (TAS) are essential tools for reducing gate congestion at container terminals (CTs). However, the adoption of these systems and the required enabling technologies varies across CTs. This study presents a five level TAS maturity framework, linking technological capabilities to operational, environmental, and economic performance, to create resilient, decarbonised ports. The methodology follows a sequential logic: insights from the literature review and technology mapping are used to define relevant KPIs, which serve as inputs for the techno-economic evaluation. This integrated process enables a structured assessment of the impact of each maturity level on the stakeholders involved. Results show that higher maturity levels improve efficiency, reduce carbon footprint and enable multi-actor coordination and responsive planning. Our findings support the case for targeted investments in digital infrastructure, emphasising both return on investment and community-level benefits. This contribution aims to inform policymakers, terminal planners, and logistics operators who are seeking to implement smart, sustainable, and scalable TAS solutions aligned with resilient and decarbonised port ecosystems.

title: MAGPIE: Navigating to Clean and Smart Logistics to, from and in Ports
summary: The Horizon 2020 Green Deal project MAGPIE employs a living lab approach to demonstrate solutions for smart, green, and integrated multimodal transport. This paper presents overall project results demonstrating technical, operational, and p
content: The Horizon 2020 Green Deal project MAGPIE employs a living lab approach to demonstrate solutions for smart, green, and integrated multimodal transport. This paper presents overall project results demonstrating technical, operational, and procedural energy supply and digital solutions and ensure roll-out through the European Green Port of the Future Master Plan and dissemination and exploitation activities. Results focus on energy supply chain demonstrations such as on-site e-methanol production with a novel membrane, strategic investment decision support tool for smart energy systems, and a hybrid vessel interacting with local grid marketplace to enhance flexibility. Other demonstrations presented focus on ammonia bunkering for deep sea shipping, offshore charging buoy, green connected trucking, and spreading road traffic to reduce congestion and emissions. Furthermore, this paper will give overall results of the clean and smart port related tools developed in MAGPIE being GHG tooling to calculate the emissions of port operations, a tool to match green energy production with port users, and a tool to support smart green logistics. The MAGPIE project is set to be deliver the results in 2026.

title: Parametric Distribution Fitting of Photochemical Oxidants, NOx Titration Regimes, and Leakage-Free Machine Learning Generalization in a Tropical Urban-Industrial Airshed
summary: Ground-level ozone (O3) in tropical urban airsheds exhibits non-linear dependencies on volatile organic compound (VOC) and nitrogen oxide (NOx) precursors. We establish a parametric distributional fitting and machine-learning generalization
content: Ground-level ozone (O3) in tropical urban airsheds exhibits non-linear dependencies on volatile organic compound (VOC) and nitrogen oxide (NOx) precursors. We establish a parametric distributional fitting and machine-learning generalization framework across a 13-station continuous regulatory monitoring network (26 station-years; 16.1 million raw readings) during 2024-2025. Maximum likelihood estimation across 182 spatiotemporal series (seven monitored pollutant variables x 13 stations x two annual cycles) identifies the Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) and log-logistic distributions as optimal models for heavy-tailed ozone exceedances (minimum Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria across 78.6% of station-years), whereas traditional Gaussian and lognormal approximations underestimate statutory threshold breach probabilities. The 13 stations exhibit severe nitrogen dioxide titration and secondary photochemical transformation gradients, dividing the conurbation into urban-industrial NOx-saturated regimes (VOC-limited) in western Howrah and photochemical accumulation hotspots across eastern Kolkata. Random Forest models trained under rigorous spatial block holdout cross-validation eliminate feature leakage between adjacent microenvironments (test R2 = 0.81-0.89 across stations). Spatial feature importance identifies atmospheric boundary layer height, ambient temperature, and non-methane hydrocarbons as primary non-linear drivers of diurnal ozone production. The parametric tail parameters and spatial machine-learning models provide regulatory authorities with an interpretable, transferable decision framework for photochemical risk mitigation, air pollution forecasting, and precursor reduction policy across dynamic tropical megacity airsheds.

title: GreenRide: A Real Time Ride Hailing and Smart Campus Mobility System for Solar Powered Electric Tricycles at a Nigerian University, with Fleet Simulation on Real Campus Map and Solar Data
summary: Many African universities are large enough that moving between hostels, faculties, clinics and gates takes a vehicle, yet intra campus transport is often informal. At the University of Port Harcourt, Nigeria, solar powered electric tricycle
content: Many African universities are large enough that moving between hostels, faculties, clinics and gates takes a vehicle, yet intra campus transport is often informal. At the University of Port Harcourt, Nigeria, solar powered electric tricycles now carry students inside the campus, but riders find them by waiting at a single charging spot, flagging one down or calling a driver whose number they happen to know. This paper presents GreenRide, a web based ride hailing system for campus solar tricycles, and evaluates how well such a system can serve the campus. GreenRide gives passengers, drivers and administrators separate browser interfaces, matches requests through Socket.io broadcast, shares the driver's live position on an OpenStreetMap map, and stores users and rides in MongoDB behind JSON Web Token authentication with email verification. Because no live fleet was available, we built a simulation of a working day from 07:00 to 19:00 on the real campus, using 193 named campus places and the road network from OpenStreetMap and hourly 2020 solar output for the campus from PVGIS. We compared the informal system with three dispatch rules (GreenRide as built, nearest tricycle, and nearest tricycle with battery checks) across 5 to 30 tricycles, 300 to 1,200 requests per day, and 10 dry season and 10 rainy season days. The informal system never served more than 69 percent of requests, however many tricycles were added. With enough tricycles, GreenRide with nearest tricycle dispatch served every request: at 300 requests per day and 20 tricycles, mean waiting time fell from 9.8 minutes to 4.4 minutes. The broadcast rule now used by GreenRide sent tricycles on long empty trips, about half of all kilometres, and more than doubled waiting time compared with nearest dispatch. When demand exceeded what the fleet could carry, battery energy, not matching, limited the service to about 21 to 24 trips per tricycle per day, and rainy season sunshine, 32 percent lower than dry season sunshine, cut the share served by up to 15 points. We give a fleet sizing rule, a dispatch change and an energy aware charging policy for campus solar tricycle services.

title: Adaptation and Mitigation Strategies of Port Logistics in the Face of Climate Change
summary: Climate change poses a threat to global shipping, with ports particularly vulnerable due to their direct exposure to climate hazards. Consequently, ports are implementing emission reduction and adaptation measures. Despite increasing docume
content: Climate change poses a threat to global shipping, with ports particularly vulnerable due to their direct exposure to climate hazards. Consequently, ports are implementing emission reduction and adaptation measures. Despite increasing documentation of individual measures, systematic analysis is lacking. Particularly, linking port specific climate impacts to operational disruptions and potential solutions remain underexplored. This paper addresses this by analyzing how climate change affects ports and suggests adaptation and mitigation strategies. The analysis combines a quantitative evaluation of the most affected European ports by climate extremes and a systematic literature review. The study aims to synthesize key port adaptation and mitigation measures to reduce ports climate-related risks and enhance operational resilience, concluding with targeted recommendations to support strategic mitigation and adaptation planning for ports.

title: Fospropofol disodium for preventing emergence agitation and relevant EEG features : a randomised controlled trial
summary: Background Emergence agitation is a clinically important complication during recovery from general anaesthesia. Preventive intervention before emergence may reduce its incidence and the need for rescue treatment. Fospropofol disodium is a w
content: Background Emergence agitation is a clinically important complication during recovery from general anaesthesia. Preventive intervention before emergence may reduce its incidence and the need for rescue treatment. Fospropofol disodium is a water-soluble prodrug of propofol with a gradual sedative profile. We tested whether fospropofol disodium reduces emergence agitation after video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery and explored the potential electroencephalographic mechanisms. Methods In this prospective, single-centre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, adults aged 18–65 year undergoing elective video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery were allocated 1:1 to receive fospropofol disodium 7.5 mg kg⁻¹ or an equal volume of saline at the end of surgery. The primary outcome was emergence agitation, defined as a Riker Sedation-Agitation Scale score ≥ 5 during emergence. Results All 138 randomised patients were analysed (69 per group). Emergence agitation occurred in 13 patients (18.8%) given fospropofol disodium and 31 patients (44.9%) given saline (risk ratio 0.42, 95% confidence interval 0.25–0.71; P = 0.001). Rescue propofol was given to 13 (18.8%) and 30 (43.5%) patients, respectively (risk ratio 0.43, 95% confidence interval 0.25–0.76; P = 0.002). Extubation time did not differ between groups, but post-anaesthesia care unit stay was longer with fospropofol disodium (median 55 [interquartile range 40–68.5] vs 45 [40–60] min; P = 0.021). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in respiratory or haemodynamic adverse events. Conclusions A single dose of fospropofol disodium at the end of surgery reduced emergence agitation and rescue propofol use, but modestly prolonged post-anaesthesia care unit stay. Larger trials are required to evaluate safety and determine the optimal dose. Clinical trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500106185 (registered 18 July 2025).

title: Fabrication of carbon quantum dots/silver nanocomposite–coated FBG for Pb2 + detection
summary: In this study, a Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) coated with Carbon Quantum Dots/Silver (CQDs/Ag) nanocomposite has been developed for Pb 2+ detection. CQDs were fabricated using the hydrothermal method, while Ag was synthesized using the Pulsed
content: In this study, a Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) coated with Carbon Quantum Dots/Silver (CQDs/Ag) nanocomposite has been developed for Pb 2+ detection. CQDs were fabricated using the hydrothermal method, while Ag was synthesized using the Pulsed Laser Ablation in Liquid (PLAL) method, and the two solutions were combined into CQDs/Ag nanocomposite. The results of XRD analysis confirmed the successful formation of CQDs/Ag nanocomposite, with broad amorphous halo of CQDs at 2θ = 17°–35° and crystalline diffraction peak of AgNPs at 2θ = 38.18°. The formation of CQDs/Ag was also confirmed by the appearance of C and Ag peaks in the EDX spectrum. The bandgap of CQDs/Ag nanocomposite was 2.66 eV. Interestingly, the sensitivity of CQDs/Ag nanocomposite–coated FBG as a Pb 2+ detection was 7 × 10 –3 dBm/ppm, with high selectivity for Pb 2+ and a detection limit of 0.36 ppm. In addition, fluctuations in FBG-based sensors coated with nanocomposite was relatively low, so the sensor has high stability because it was able to maintain a consistent signal without being affected by time changes during each data capture. Therefore, the modified FBG nanocomposite CQDs/Ag nanocomposite-coated FBG can serve as an alternative approach for Pb 2+ detection.

title: Pyrrolysine as an ecologically friendly corrosion inhibitor for zinc in 1.0 M HCl solution: a blend of theoretical and experimental perspectives
summary: The effectiveness of pyrrolysine molecule (Pyl) as an environmentally friendly corrosion inhibitor for zinc in a 2 M HCl solution was confirmed through chemical, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations. The protection efficiency (%I
content: The effectiveness of pyrrolysine molecule (Pyl) as an environmentally friendly corrosion inhibitor for zinc in a 2 M HCl solution was confirmed through chemical, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations. The protection efficiency (%IE) rose with rising Pyl concentration and lowering temperature, reaching a maximum value of 93.82% at 0.001 M Pyl, according to potentiodynamic polarization studies. Pyl functioned as a mixed-type inhibitor by impeding both anodic and cathodic reactions. The inhibition effect of the Pyl molecule is primarily attributed to its adsorption onto the Zn surface, which creates a barrier against corrosive attack. Furthermore, the adsorption behavior matched the Freundlich adsorption isotherm, indicating favorable surface contact between Pyl molecules and the Zn substrate. A single capacitive loop was revealed by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy studies, indicating that a charge transfer mechanism was primarily responsible for regulating the corrosion process. Additionally, the thermodynamic functions associated with the activation kinetics and adsorption process were estimated and thoroughly analysed. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were conducted to examine the adsorption behavior and corrosion inhibition performance of Pyl on the Zn(110) surface. The calculated electronic properties and adsorption energy indicate that Pyl creates a stable protective film on the Zn(110) surface and is a promising environmentally friendly corrosion inhibitor.

title: Evaluasi Kinerja Perkuatan Balok T Beton Bertulang Berbasis HFRP dan CFRP Melalui Pemodelan Elemen Hingga
source: Journal of Infrastructure and Construction Technology
summary: External strengthening using fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) is widely adopted to enhance the flexural capacity of reinforced concrete (RC) T-beams. However, brittle failure modes triggered by premature debonding remain a major challenge in
content: External strengthening using fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) is widely adopted to enhance the flexural capacity of reinforced concrete (RC) T-beams. However, brittle failure modes triggered by premature debonding remain a major challenge in structural modelling. This comparative review aims to evaluate and synthesise the agreement between finite element modelling (FEM) predictions and experimental results for RC T-beams strengthened with hybrid FRP (HFRP) and carbon FRP (CFRP) across varied strengthening configurations. A quantitative assessment was conducted on four parameters: ultimate load capacity (Pmax), critical deflections (δy, δmax, δu), displacement ductility (μΔ), and dissipated energy (Ed). The synthesis confirms that external FRP strengthening consistently increases experimental peak loads (for instance, from 236.0 kN to 291.0 kN), yet exerts opposing effects on peak deflection depending on the strengthening layout and bonded span length. The flexural capacity gains are generally accompanied by a 9-56% reduction in experimental ductility compared with control specimens, whereas transverse strip configurations preserve ductility more effectively and absorb 18-73% more energy (0.91-1.12 kJ) than full-width plates (0.65-0.77 kJ). Regarding numerical validation, FEM simulations predict ultimate load capacities with high accuracy against physical tests (such as 208.5 kN vs. 210.0 kN for BFR1 and 301.0 kN vs. 297.0 kN for SB2), but overestimate initial elastic stiffness, resulting in substantially smaller yield deflections (δy). Owing to the perfect-bond assumption that neglects post-peak brittle delamination, standard FEM analyses overestimate ductility indices (μFEM/μEksp reaching 1.12-2.32) and yield 4.13- 45.89% higher dissipated energy across most specimens. These findings underscore the necessity of incorporating cohesive zone modelling at the concrete-FRP interface to capture actual brittle failure accurately.

title: Multimodal Green Logistics with Cooperative Approach for Peri-Urban Delivery
summary: The rise in parcel volumes across Europe, growing at 6–8% annually, is largely driven by the expansion of e-commerce, faster delivery expectations, and increasing fragmentation of last-mile shipments. Demographic shifts, direct-to-consumer
content: The rise in parcel volumes across Europe, growing at 6–8% annually, is largely driven by the expansion of e-commerce, faster delivery expectations, and increasing fragmentation of last-mile shipments. Demographic shifts, direct-to-consumer models, and digital marketplace dynamics further accelerate this trend. This rapid expansion in urban and peri-urban areas poses major challenges to sustainable logistics. The GREEN-LOG project addresses these challenges with an innovative, cooperative, and interconnected green delivery approach. At the operational level, GREEN-LOG provides cargo-bike-based innovations for sustainable micro-consolidation design and deployment, multimodal parcel deliveries integrating public transport, Logistics-as-a-Service platforms for interconnected city logistics, and automated delivery concepts using autonomous vehicles and delivery droids. This paper presents the concept implemented in the Barcelona Living Lab, combining e-cargo bikes, rail transport, and AMRs (Autonomous Mobile Robots) to enhance efficiency and sustainability in peri-urban goods movement. After an initial round of small-scale trials, a preliminary set of findings has been identified. The work also analyses the challenges, barriers, and drawbacks of multimodal green transport using cooperative logistics strategies.

title: Role of tribolayers in fretting wear in temperature cycling
summary: The role of tribolayers in fretting wear is well understood under isothermal conditions. However, their effects under temperature cycling remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the role of tribolayers in temperature-cycling fretting
content: The role of tribolayers in fretting wear is well understood under isothermal conditions. However, their effects under temperature cycling remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the role of tribolayers in temperature-cycling fretting wear was investigated. Fretting tests were conducted at room temperature (RT, 25 °C), 750 °C (HT), and RT-to-750 °C cycling (TC) conditions. Systematic tribological analyses were performed to characterize the wear scars and tribolayers. The results show that the formation of coherent tribo-sintered tribolayers resulted in a remarkable reduction in both the friction coefficient and the wear rate as the temperature increased from RT to 750 °C. Thermal cycling led to the formation of concentrated cracks and subsequent localized delamination of the coating. Compacted-debris tribolayers formed at RT transformed into tribo-sintered tribolayers during the subsequent HT stage. These tribo-sintered tribolayers were susceptible to cracking and delamination due to their brittleness in the following RT stage. Despite these detrimental effects, the tribolayers maintained relatively high coverage on the wear scar and remained effective in reducing the wear rate under TC conditions.

title: An Evaluation of Ankara Başkent National Garden in Terms of The Design Criteria of The National Gardens Guide
summary: National gardens are extensive public green spaces that enable people to connect with nature while meeting social, cultural, and recreational needs. They generally comprise large open green areas designed for recreation and function as icon
content: National gardens are extensive public green spaces that enable people to connect with nature while meeting social, cultural, and recreational needs. They generally comprise large open green areas designed for recreation and function as iconic urban spaces that preserve historical, cultural, and natural characteristics, reflect socio-cultural life, and enhance the prestige of both cities and nations. This study was conducted at Başkent Millet Bahçesi (Capital Public Garden), located in Ankara’s Altındağ district. The study aimed to evaluate the design of the site based on expert opinions and the design principles presented in the Ministry of Environment and Urbanization’s Public Gardens Guide. For this purpose, a survey was administered to 40 subject-matter experts. The survey questions were developed in accordance with twelve established design principles for public gardens: functionality, accessibility and transportation, sustainability, adequacy, ecology, sense of belonging and identity, cost-effectiveness, innovative design, health, universality, safety, and smart applications. The survey assessed whether these criteria had been effectively incorporated into the design of Başkent Millet Bahçesi. According to the results, accessibility (x̄ = 4.20) and ecology (x̄ = 4.33) received the highest positive ratings, whereas sense of belonging and identity (x̄ = 1.70) and health (x̄ = 1.58) received the lowest positive ratings. The findings were subsequently evaluated in conjunction with spatial analysis and the existing literature. Accordingly, recommendations were developed to enhance the garden’s existing potential, with particular emphasis on the principles of belonging and identity, sustainability, universality, safety, and smart applications.

title: Hyperelastic microfibers as bioinspired proprioceptive artificial muscles
summary: Skeletal muscles combine forceful contraction with built-in sensing of their own length and movement, known as proprioception. Reproducing this combination in soft artificial muscles remains difficult, because added sensors often reduce act
content: Skeletal muscles combine forceful contraction with built-in sensing of their own length and movement, known as proprioception. Reproducing this combination in soft artificial muscles remains difficult, because added sensors often reduce actuation performance, complicate fabrication or limit miniaturization. In natural muscle, specialized sensory fibers are embedded alongside, and mechanically coupled to, the force-generating fibers. Inspired by this arrangement, we pair a hyperelastic, highly stretchable fluid channel with a stiffer, off-center optical core inside a single thin fiber. When liquid is pumped in, the channel wall undergoes a shape bifurcation: a localized bulge forms and propagates along the fiber. Because the core resists stretching, the bulge bends the fiber into a contracting coil, while the core also reports the fiber’s shape through the light it transmits. Here we show that such fibers, produced continuously by a scalable drawing process, act as artificial muscles that sense their own contraction and stretching, supporting self-monitoring movement in soft robots.

title: Activating Interlayer Organic Redox Sites in Hybrid Layered Vanadium Oxides for Li-Ion Batteries via Dopamine-Derived Carbonization
summary: Chemical preintercalation of redox-active organic molecules can enhance the specific capacity of layered metal oxides by introducing interlayer redox sites alongside intralayer redox centers. However, their practical redox activity in hybri
content: Chemical preintercalation of redox-active organic molecules can enhance the specific capacity of layered metal oxides by introducing interlayer redox sites alongside intralayer redox centers. However, their practical redox activity in hybrid electrodes is often limited due to sluggish charge transport kinetics. Here, we show that dopamine (DOPA) carbonization activates 2,6-diaminoanthraquinone (DAAQ) molecules in bilayered vanadium oxide (BVO) hybrid electrodes, resulting in notable capacity improvement in nonaqueous Li-ion cells. BVO preintercalated solely with DAAQ (DAAQ-100) is compared with BVO preintercalated with both DAAQ and DOPA, followed by DOPA carbonization (DAAQ-65/DOPA). We found that DOPA carbonization competes with DAAQ preintercalation, reducing the interlayer DAAQ fraction while increasing hydration, yet preserving hydrogen-bond cross-linking between DAAQ and V–O layers, which enhances structural stability. Notably, DAAQ-65/DOPA exhibits a unique nanoscroll morphology, in contrast to the nanobelt morphology of DAAQ-100. Transmission electron microscopy suggests formation of interlayer carbon domains in DAAQ-65/DOPA and cyclic voltammetry indicates that DOPA-derived carbon domains activate interlayer DAAQ redox sites and enhance vanadium redox activity, which is attributed to improved charge transfer. Consequently, DAAQ-65/DOPA delivers a high initial specific capacity of ∼240 mAh g–1 at 20 mA g–1 and improved rate capability of ∼160 mAh g–1 at 200 mA g–1, outperforming DAAQ-100. Electrochemical analysis, supported by galvanostatic intermittent titration (GITT) and Nyquist plots, reveals fast charge transport kinetics arising from enhanced electron and Li+ mobility. This study demonstrates, for the first time, that DOPA carbonization can activate interlayer organic redox sites in hybrid electrodes, offering a new strategy to enhance energy storage performance.

title: Research on the Daily Frequency Time Structure Components of China’s Real-Time Carbon Emissions —Based on the Prophet Framework Model
source: Journal of Advanced Computational Intelligence and Intelligent Informatics
summary: To accurately characterize the time structure of China’s daily CO 2 emissions, this study uses daily data from the Carbon Monitor database spanning 2019–2025, covering total emissions and six sectoral categories: domestic aviation, ground t
content: To accurately characterize the time structure of China’s daily CO 2 emissions, this study uses daily data from the Carbon Monitor database spanning 2019–2025, covering total emissions and six sectoral categories: domestic aviation, ground transport, industry, international aviation, power, and residential. The Prophet framework is adopted to decompose the emission time series into four components: long-term trend, nonlinear seasonal component, holiday effect term, and COVID-19 impact term. Results show that the model achieves excellent fitting accuracy, with outstanding performance in international aviation and residential sectors, and low error levels across all sectors. In terms of long-term trends, total emissions exhibit a steady decline after 2022, the industry and power sectors are significantly influenced by the “dual carbon” policy and energy structure adjustment, whereas the transport sectors display phased recovery corresponding to changes in travel demand. For seasonal components, periodic peaks are observed in the residential and power sectors, fluctuations in ground transport align with travel demand patterns, and aviation sectors present weak seasonal characteristics with more moderate fluctuations during the pandemic. Regarding event impacts, the negative impact of the COVID-19 peak period on emissions is significantly stronger than that of holidays such as the Spring Festival, with distinct sectoral heterogeneity. The industry and power sectors are the most sensitive, whereas domestic aviation, international aviation, and residential sectors show lower sensitivity. This study provides scientific support for the dynamic management of carbon emissions and the formulation of “dual carbon” policies.

title: Continuous and sustainable multicarbon acids electrosynthesis
summary: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction offers a route to produce fuels and chemicals using renewable electricity. Multicarbon electrosynthesis has predominantly relied on Cu-based catalysts in aqueous electrolytes, achieving high multicarbon farada
content: Electrochemical CO 2 reduction offers a route to produce fuels and chemicals using renewable electricity. Multicarbon electrosynthesis has predominantly relied on Cu-based catalysts in aqueous electrolytes, achieving high multicarbon faradaic efficiencies but facing broad product distributions and substantial carbon loss through carbonate formation. Nonaqueous CO 2 electrolysis offers an alternative pathway to multicarbon synthesis through radical C–C coupling while suppressing carbonate formation. However, the full-cell operation remains limited by sacrificial anodic reactions and poorly controlled proton delivery. Here, we introduce a hydrogen-oxidation-enabled full-cell architecture that couples nonsacrificial anodic H 2 oxidation with continuous nonaqueous CO 2 reduction. Hydrogen oxidation provides a regulated proton flux without disrupting the low-water environment required for radical chemistry. Pairing a PtAu anode with an oxide-derived Pb cathode enables continuous conversion of CO 2 and H 2 to oxalic and glyoxylic acids, achieving a C 2 acid faradaic efficiency of 97 ± 2% at 30 milliamperes per square centimeter and a single-pass carbon utilization efficiency of 72 ± 2%. In contrast, anodic water oxidation promotes water accumulation and shifts cathodic selectivity towards hydrogen and single-carbon products. This approach establishes anodic reaction engineering as a route to continuous, carbon-efficient nonaqueous multicarbon electrosynthesis.

title: Causes of cold-end corrosion in pulp mill recovery boilers: sulfuric acid or hygroscopic deposits?
summary: Corrosion at the cold end of recovery boilers is a well-known issue, although its underlying causes, which may include sulfuric acid condensation and hygroscopic deposits, are not always fully understood. Since the presence of SO 3 (g) dire
content: Corrosion at the cold end of recovery boilers is a well-known issue, although its underlying causes, which may include sulfuric acid condensation and hygroscopic deposits, are not always fully understood. Since the presence of SO 3 (g) directly determines the risk of sulfuric-acid dew-point corrosion, a key practical objective of this work was to determine whether SO 3 (g) is present in recovery-boiler flue gases at cold-end locations where measurable concentrations of SO 2 (g) are found. SO 3 (g) measurements and corrosion-probe tests were carried out under different operating conditions in two types of recovery boilers: a Kraft boiler firing black liquor with relatively low dry-solids content and an ammonium sulfite boiler. In the Kraft boiler, we found that although SO 2 (g) was present in the flue gas, no SO 3 (g) was detected in the cold end. This is because SO 3 (g) reacts with alkali-rich ash, which converts it to solid sulfates and removes it from the flue gas. Thus, the limiting factor in lowering flue gas temperatures in the Kraft boiler was corrosion caused by hygroscopic salt deposits, rather than sulfuric-acid dew-point corrosion. Sodium bisulfate (NaHSO 4 ) can form in boilers firing black liquor with low dry-solids content, and/or with a high S/Na 2 molar ratio in the flue gas. Water uptake by NaHSO 4 was determined to occur at 32–36% relative humidity at flue-gas-relevant water-vapor concentrations (15–35 vol%). In practice, this limits the cold-end carbon steel temperature to around 100–110 °C, depending on the water vapor concentration in the flue gas. In the ammonium sulfite boiler, the situation is different. There, only wood-derived ash is available to capture sulfur, resulting in high SO 2 (g) and SO 3 (g) and a high acid dew point of the flue gas. The measurements make it possible to assess whether flue-gas temperatures can be lowered to recover more energy without causing corrosion in these boilers.

title: Synergy of ternary lubricants and biomimetic honeycomb textures: Stagewise intelligent lubrication and protection from 25 to 800 °C
summary: Wide-temperature adaptive coatings are critical for mitigating tribological failure in marine and aerospace systems. Conventional Cr₃C₂-NiCr coatings offer excellent wear resistance and oxidation stability, but their intrinsically poor self
content: Wide-temperature adaptive coatings are critical for mitigating tribological failure in marine and aerospace systems. Conventional Cr₃C₂-NiCr coatings offer excellent wear resistance and oxidation stability, but their intrinsically poor self-lubrication limits practical engineering applications. Herein, we developed a hybrid “laser-textured reservoir + vacuum infiltration” strategy to engineer biomimetic honeycomb microstructures on Cr₃C₂-NiCr coatings as in situ reservoirs for B₂O₃/Bi₂O₃/C ternary solid lubricant. The coating achieved average friction coefficients of 0.08, 0.14, and 0.12 at 25 °C, 400 °C, and 800 °C, corresponding to 90.5%, 75.4%, and 76.9% reductions relative to the unmodified counterpart, and maintained stable performance after four consecutive wide-temperature thermal cycles. Remarkably, after four thermal cycles at 800 °C, the wear rate of the novel composite coating (0.15 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m)) is two orders of magnitude lower than that of the pristine coating (13.86 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m)). A stagewise intelligent synergistic lubrication mechanism was elucidated: room-temperature graphite sliding, medium-temperature multiphase synergy, and high-temperature dual-glaze-layer protection. The high-temperature stage exhibits fourfold protective functions: fourfold protective functions: liquid lubrication provided by molten B₂O₃/Bi₂O₃; wear-debris encapsulation by the liquid film enveloping wear debris; oxidation barrier by the glaze layer blocking oxygen diffusion into the coating and graphite interior; and structural support provided by the inner nanocrystalline oxide framework. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed the atomic-scale crystalline-to-amorphous transformation of B₂O₃/Bi₂O₃ at elevated temperatures. This work provides a robust fabrication strategy and novel insights into the design of next-generation high-performance, wide-temperature-range intelligent adaptive lubricating coatings.

title: Influence of Molybdenum (Mo) Doping on the Morphology and Photocatalytic Activity of Hydrothermally Synthesized ZnO for Methylene Blue Degradation
summary: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is an inexpensive UV-active photocatalyst, but whether high-valent dopants such as Mo6+ enter its lattice during hydrothermal growth, and how they change its activity, remains poorly understood. Herein, molybdenum (Mo)-dope
content: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is an inexpensive UV-active photocatalyst, but whether high-valent dopants such as Mo6+ enter its lattice during hydrothermal growth, and how they change its activity, remains poorly understood. Herein, molybdenum (Mo)-doped ZnO (2–6 mol% Mo) was synthesized via a urea-assisted hydrothermal route and calcination at 600 °C, and its lattice, morphology, optical absorption and activity were examined on the same samples. The samples were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) with Rietveld refinement, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS). All samples were single-phase wurtzite ZnO with crystallite sizes of 27–31 nm, and the lattice parameters varied by no more than 0.00015 Å in a and 0.0006 Å in c, indicating limited Mo substitution. However, Mo addition changed the particle morphology from porous nanoplatelet aggregates to dense prismatic particles up to hundreds of micrometers in size. The direct band gap decreased from 3.26 eV for pristine ZnO and Mo2-ZnO to 3.22 and 3.23 eV for Mo4-ZnO and Mo6-ZnO, while all samples absorbed the 254 nm excitation almost completely. Under UV-C irradiation, the apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of methylene blue (MB) decolorization increased from (21.8 ± 2.5) × 10−3 min−1 for pristine ZnO to (41.0 ± 1.8) × 10−3 min−1 for Mo6-ZnO, whereas Mo2-ZnO performed like pristine ZnO. The activity gain thus coincided with the small band-gap decrease rather than with the lattice or the morphology, which suggests that Mo acts mainly through a small amount of surface species outside the bulk ZnO lattice.

title: Synthesis and crystal structure of Ta 4 N 20 · x N 2 at megabar pressure
source: Acta Crystallographica Section E Crystallographic Communications
summary: The title compound Ta 4 N 20 · x N 2 (tetratantalum icosanitride dinitrogen), has been synthesized via a direct reaction between tantalum carbide (TaC) and molecular nitrogen (N 2 ) in a laser-heated diamond anvil cell (DAC) at 106 (2) GPa
content: The title compound Ta 4 N 20 · x N 2 (tetratantalum icosanitride dinitrogen), has been synthesized via a direct reaction between tantalum carbide (TaC) and molecular nitrogen (N 2 ) in a laser-heated diamond anvil cell (DAC) at 106 (2) GPa and temperatures above 2600 (200) K. The crystal structure of Ta 4 N 20 · x N 2 was determined by in situ synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction performed on a polycrystalline sample confined in a DAC at 106 (2) GPa and ambient temperature. The Ta 4 N 20 · x N 2 compound crystallizes in the Cmmm space group, with an asymmetric unit comprising two Ta crystallographic sites and five N crystallographic sites. The structure contains four distinct nitrogen species: a lone N 3− anion, a dinitrogen anion, an armchair-type polymeric nitrogen anion, and a neutral dinitrogen molecule. The tantalum cations are coordinated by the nitrogen species, together forming a three-dimensional metal–inorganic framework, within which the neutral dinitrogen molecules are trapped inside channels extending along the c -axis direction. The structure contains at least one N 2 molecule per formula unit; however, the precise value could not be unambiguously determined because of the weak scattering power of nitrogen and likely static disorder of the molecules within the channels. Ta 4 N 20 · x N 2 is isostructural to Hf 4 N 20 · x N 2 – a here-amended model for the previously reported Hf 4 N 20 ·N 2 compound [Bykov et al. (2020). Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. pp. 10321–10326] – and it represents the most nitrogen-rich tantalum nitride reported up to date.

title: Synthesis of Lignans from the Biobased Platform Chemical Itaconic Acid Using Pd-Catalyzed Coupling Reactions
summary: Itaconic acid diesters and monoesters undergo a Pd-catalyzed coupling reaction with arene diazonium salts at ambient temperature and under ligand- and base-free conditions. The products can be further elaborated in two steps to the CL1-subt
content: Itaconic acid diesters and monoesters undergo a Pd-catalyzed coupling reaction with arene diazonium salts at ambient temperature and under ligand- and base-free conditions. The products can be further elaborated in two steps to the CL1-subtype lignans gossypidien and jatrodien or to CL2-subtype lignans with a dibenzylbutenolide or an α-arylidene-γ-butyrolactone structural pattern in three or two steps, respectively. For the synthesis of both CL2-subtype lignans, the Pd-catalyzed Heck-type coupling of α-methylene-β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactones and arene diazonium salts was investigated. While the dibenzyl-butenolide pattern is accessible under base-free conditions with a regioselectivity higher than 98:2, the presence of a base leads to the preferred formation of exo-α-arylidene butyrolactones with an exo/endo-ratio up to 5:1, as determined by 1H NMR spectroscopy. The exo-α-arylidene-β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactone pattern was more selectively synthesized through an aldol condensation-elimination sequence from β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactones. Eventually, the hydrogenation of these α-arylidene-β-benzyl-γ-butyrolactones catalyzed by Pd/C was investigated as a stereoselective method for the synthesis of cis-α,β-dibenzyl-γ-butyrolactones. In our hands, the diastereoselectivity of this method is notably less general than anticipated from literature precedence, but this work enabled us to correct the originally assigned relative configuration of a secondary plant metabolite from cis to trans.

title: Plastic-associated freshwater bacteria promote microplastic aggregation, alter trophic transfer, and serve as chassis for engineered plastic modification
summary: Environmental plastic debris harbors distinct microbial communities, yet the functional traits associated with plastisphere colonization remain poorly understood. Here, we isolated 230 bacterial strains from riverine plastic debris and surr
content: Environmental plastic debris harbors distinct microbial communities, yet the functional traits associated with plastisphere colonization remain poorly understood. Here, we isolated 230 bacterial strains from riverine plastic debris and surrounding freshwater samples and screened their ability to aggregate fluorescent polystyrene microplastics (MPs). Plastic-associated isolates displayed significantly stronger aggregation phenotypes than water-derived bacteria, with multiple environmental strains removing more than 95% of suspended MPs. Comparative analyses revealed that highly aggregative isolates differed markedly from their corresponding type strains and possessed diversified extracellular polysaccharide biosynthetic repertoires. Aggregation dynamics were strongly influenced by hydrodynamic conditions and bacterial abundance, while theoretical encounter-rate analyses indicated that incomplete MP removal was constrained primarily by attachment efficiency, aggregate architecture, and sedimentation behavior rather than by particle encounter frequency. Highly aggregative strains consistently reduced MP availability to suspension-feeding rotifers, whereas effects on phagocytic amoebae were more limited, indicating grazer-dependent impacts on trophic transfer. To explore whether MP-capturing bacteria can be repurposed as platforms for plastic-interacting functions, the highly aggregative isolate Pseudomonas parakoreensis A16 was engineered to express FastPETase, resulting in detectable alterations of PET surface chemistry. These findings suggest that plastisphere-associated bacteria are enriched in traits promoting MP sequestration and may serve as versatile chassis coupling particle capture with engineered plastic-modifying functions. Together, our results identify bacterial aggregation as a central process linking microbial colonization, microplastic fate, and trophic transfer in freshwater ecosystems.

title: Atomic level manufacturing enables ultra-low friction and wear at elevated temperatures
summary: Toward the goal of achieving ultra-low friction and wear under elevated temperatures and high contact pressures in industrially relevant mechanical systems relying on liquid lubrication, we propose a synergistic lubrication strategy that in
content: Toward the goal of achieving ultra-low friction and wear under elevated temperatures and high contact pressures in industrially relevant mechanical systems relying on liquid lubrication, we propose a synergistic lubrication strategy that integrates a close-to-atomically smooth surface as well as atomic-level modifications using a MXene coating and [HMIM][BF4] ionic liquid (IL). The ball-on-disc tribological test results demonstrate that this strategy led to ultra-low friction and wear of engineering steel interfaces at a high contact pressure of 1.13 GPa and an elevated temperature of 300 °C, demonstrating competitive lubrication performance relative to reported traditional oil-based and IL-based lubrication systems. The underlying mechanism enabling the superlative performance is attributed to a solid-liquid synergy since the close-to-atomic smooth steel surface not only mitigates direct load-bearing asperity contact at the sliding interface but also enhances the adhesion of MXenes to form a thicker, uniform composite tribofilm. In contrast, a higher steel roughness induces interfacial stress concentrations, leading to film delamination and failure. This template of lubrication strategy is anticipated to overcome the failure challenge of conventional liquid lubrication in extreme environments and provide a foundational roadmap for designing ultra-low friction and wear sliding systems operating under high-contact-pressure, high-temperature conditions relevant to industrial applications.

title: Wafer-scale transferable hexagonal boron nitride membranes via interfacial engineering for multilevel storage
summary: Two-dimensional materials hold immense potential for memristive devices, offering a pathway to overcome the von Neumann bottleneck. Specifically, hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly promising for low-voltage, multilevel memristors due
content: Two-dimensional materials hold immense potential for memristive devices, offering a pathway to overcome the von Neumann bottleneck. Specifically, hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly promising for low-voltage, multilevel memristors due to its robust physicochemical properties. However, synthesizing wafer-scale, transferable, and thickness-controllable h-BN (tens of nanometers thick) remains challenging, impeding its device integration. Herein, we demonstrate an interfacial modulation strategy via controlled sapphire substrate nitridation to grow high-quality, crack-free h-BN membranes. Introducing an interfacial B–O buffer layer improves the crystalline quality of epitaxial h-BN and facilitates its rapid, damage-free wet transfer onto target substrates. The fabricated memristors with these transferred membranes exhibit a low set voltage of 1.06 V, an ultrahigh ON/OFF ratio of 1.57×10 9 , an ultrafast switching speed of 30 ns, robust multilevel switching and long-term stability. Our study presents a scalable approach for advancing next-generation in-memory computing architectures.

title: Maize-based cropping systems in India: dynamics, drivers, and pathways towards climate-resilient sustainable intensification
summary: Maize (Zea mays L.) is emerging as one of the most significant cereals in India because of its growing importance in food, feed, fodder and industry. Maize-based cropping systems are evolving toward sustainable intensification at an increas
content: Maize (Zea mays L.) is emerging as one of the most significant cereals in India because of its growing importance in food, feed, fodder and industry. Maize-based cropping systems are evolving toward sustainable intensification at an increasing rate, driven largely by climate variability, resource limitations, technological advances, and shifts in market demand. In this review, the status, dynamics, and future prospects of maize cropping systems in India are summarized through a systematic literature review based on the PRISMA 2020 framework. The studies were selected for qualitative synthesis to include a total of 84 studies. This review examines the evolution of significant maize-based farming systems across various agro climatic regions of India, their impact on productivity, resource utilization efficiency, soil health and agricultural profitability. It also highlights the key drivers of cropping system change, including climate variability, soil and water constraints, improved hybrids, mechanization, policy support, and market demand. Recent developments in conservation agriculture, integrated nutrient management, precision agriculture, and climate smart agriculture are discussed for their potential to enhance resilience and sustainability. Despite substantial advances, constraints such as regional yield gaps, resource degradation, lack of labor, and limited market linkages persist. The review identifies certain research gaps and highlights the need for integrated agronomic, technological and policy interventions to ensure climate-resilient and sustainable production of maize in India.

title: Nutritional enrichment of Moina mongolica using different dietary strategies: Effects on growth, biochemical composition and functional nutrients
summary: Moina mongolica Daday is an important live feed organism for marine aquaculture due to its high nutritional value, particularly its enrichment with essential fatty acids such as eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA). However, the nutritional quality
content: Moina mongolica Daday is an important live feed organism for marine aquaculture due to its high nutritional value, particularly its enrichment with essential fatty acids such as eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA). However, the nutritional quality of M. mongolica is highly dependent on dietary composition. This study evaluated the effects of different diets on the biochemical composition, fatty acid profile, amino acid composition, and carotenoid accumulation of M. mongolica . Four dietary treatments were designed: Nannochloropsis oculata (T1), Saccharomyces cerevisiae (T2), N. oculata + S. cerevisiae (T3), and N. oculata + S. cerevisiae + Rhodopseudomonas palustris (T4). The results showed that dietary composition significantly affected the nutritional characteristics of M. mongolica . The T4 group exhibited the highest crude protein content (64.58%), whereas the T1 group showed the highest crude lipid content (28.56%). Fatty acid analysis revealed that the T1 group had the highest levels of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA), especially ω3-PUFA, ω6-PUFA, EPA (C20:5n-3), linoleic acid (LA, C18:2n-6), and arachidonic acid (ARA), while the T2 group showed the lowest PUFA nutritional quality. The combined dietary treatments (T3 and T4) resulted in intermediate fatty acid profiles, with T4 showing improved PUFA composition compared with T3. In addition, dietary treatments significantly influenced total amino acid contents, with the highest amino acid level observed in the T4 group; however, the proportions of essential amino acids and umami amino acids remained relatively stable among treatments. Carotenoid analysis demonstrated that M. mongolica accumulated both astaxanthin and canthaxanthin, and their contents were closely associated with dietary pigment sources. The T4 group exhibited the highest canthaxanthin content, while astaxanthin accumulation was comparable to that in the T1 group. Overall, dietary manipulation significantly regulates the nutritional quality of M. mongolica , particularly its protein content, lipid composition, PUFA profile, and carotenoid accumulation. The combined supplementation of N. oculata , S. cerevisiae , and R. palustris represents a promising dietary strategy for producing nutritionally enhanced M. mongolica as a high-quality live feed for marine aquaculture.

title: Plasma-induced nanocluster structures enhances CO gas sensing properties of n-ZnO/p-CuO heterostructures
summary: In this study, radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering was primarily used to deposit heterostructure thin films of n-type zinc oxide (n-ZnO) and p-type copper oxide nanoclusters. By modulating the surface morphology of n-ZnO, the distribu
content: In this study, radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering was primarily used to deposit heterostructure thin films of n-type zinc oxide (n-ZnO) and p-type copper oxide nanoclusters. By modulating the surface morphology of n-ZnO, the distribution of p-CuO nanoclusters was improved to enhance their characteristics for CO gas sensing applications. After depositing a ZnO seed layer, the oxygen flow rate, etching power, and duration of oxygen plasma etching were modulated to optimize the film surface morphology. Subsequently, p-CuO layers were deposited on the n-ZnO thin film, which not only increased the surface area for gas contact but also utilized the favorable electron transport properties of the heterojunction to enhance gas sensing characteristics. With this structural design, the study also aimed to perform sensing characteristic measurements at a relatively low operating temperature of 100°C, and to further improve CO sensing characteristics by optimizing the film surface morphology. After completing the fabrication process and before packaging, the crystalline properties and surface morphology of the heterostructure thin films were analyzed using high-resolution transmission electron microscope(HRTEM), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and atomic force microscopy (AFM). The absorption characteristics of the film surface were measured using UV-VIS spectroscopy to analyze its surface porosity. The results show that after oxygen plasma etching on the n-ZnO surface with an oxygen flow rate of 10 sccm, etching power of 150 W, and etching time of 15 min, the heterostructure thin film with p-CuO nanoclusters exhibited better gas sensing sensitivity even at the relatively low operating temperature of 100°C, with the response time reduced from 90 seconds to approximately 10 seconds.

title: Proteomic and Metabolomic Profiling and Functional Annotation of Two Drought-tolerant Tef [Eragrostis tef (Zucc.) Trotter] Genotypes During Dehydration and Rehydration
summary: This study aimed to identify proteomic, and metabolomic responses associated with dehydration and subsequent recovery in two drought-tolerant tef genotypes. At the end of drought, proteomic analysis revealed increased abundance of stress-pr
content: This study aimed to identify proteomic, and metabolomic responses associated with dehydration and subsequent recovery in two drought-tolerant tef genotypes. At the end of drought, proteomic analysis revealed increased abundance of stress-protective proteins, regulating protein homeostasis and osmotic adjustment. Gene ontology analysis revealed enrichment of mRNA processing and alternative splicing pathways. Antioxidant responses differed between the two genotypes. RIL44 enriched glyoxal metabolic process whereas, Boni increased L-proline biosynthesis. Metabolomic analyses supported these findings, showing increased accumulation of proline and glutamic acid at the end of drought. KEGG pathway analysis during drought revealed downregulation of secondary metabolism, phenylpropanoid, and lignin pathways. Metabolomic data further showed increased accumulation of arabitol and meso-erythritol, sugar alcohols associated with osmotic regulation and cell wall modification. Recovery induced xyloglucan metabolic process, amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism supporting cell growth and expansion. Moreover, methylation and vesicle budding were downregulated during recovery. RIL44 exhibited earlier downregulation of glucuronoxylan biosynthesis related with lower accumulation of secondary cell-wall and increased accumulation other metabolites at end the of drought, which may be related to its rapid morphophysiological recovery, whereas Boni showed a more gradual restoration. Overall, tef drought tolerance involves molecular chaperone induction, genotype-specific antioxidant strategies, metabolic reprogramming, and dynamic regulation of cell-wall biosynthesis.
