title: Catalytic enhancement of biogas production from organic waste using Cobalt Ferrite Nanoparticles
summary: The improvement of biogas production from organic waste is a key objective in sustainable waste management and renewable energy generation. In this study, cobalt ferrite nanoparticles [CoFe₂O₄-NPs] were synthesized via a hydrothermal method
content: The improvement of biogas production from organic waste is a key objective in sustainable waste management and renewable energy generation. In this study, cobalt ferrite nanoparticles [CoFe₂O₄-NPs] were synthesized via a hydrothermal method and evaluated as catalytic additives in a laboratory-scale anaerobic bioreactor. The effect of nanoparticle incorporation was assessed using 50 g of organic fruit waste in a 2.46 L prototype reactor. Biogas production was monitored over 48 h under natural solar irradiation. The control system generated 12 cm³ of biogas, whereas the addition of 0.5 mL and 1 mL of a 0.1 M nanoparticle dispersion increased production to 126.25 cm³ and 157.81 cm³, respectively. These values correspond to a 10.5–13.2-fold enhancement relative to the non-catalyzed condition. The results demonstrate a clear dose dependent catalytic effect and suggest that cobalt ferrite nanoparticles promote accelerated degradation of organic matter during anaerobic fermentation.

title: Strategic energy efficiency plan aligned with artificial intelligence. Case study: CETis 91
summary: This paper describes the design and implementation of an AI-powered energy efficiency strategic plan aligned with the Project Management Institute [PMI] guidelines. The plan aimed to optimize electricity consumption, reduce operating costs,
content: This paper describes the design and implementation of an AI-powered energy efficiency strategic plan aligned with the Project Management Institute [PMI] guidelines. The plan aimed to optimize electricity consumption, reduce operating costs, and decrease the carbon footprint of a high school. A mixed-methods approach was employed in this research, using a case study at CETis 91. This study was supported by PMI processes, energy management systems [EMS], and data analysis using sensors and artificial intelligence tools to identify consumption patterns. The results demonstrate how a strategic plan allows for the precise identification of opportunities to improve environmental management, from replacing lighting with LED technology in high traffic areas to promoting the adoption of energy-efficient practices by the school community. Finally, the paper describes how the integration of strategic planning, project management, artificial intelligence, and energy management systems fosters systematic, replicable, and sustainable institutional energy management in public educational settings.

title: Yucatan Peninsula Ecosystem: Ecosystem services and tangible cultural heritage
summary: The objective was to carry out a review of the value of the ecosystem services of the Tropical Ecosystem of the Low Deciduous Forest (LDF) of the Yucatan Peninsula and its value as cultural heritage. A review of scientific articles was carr
content: The objective was to carry out a review of the value of the ecosystem services of the Tropical Ecosystem of the Low Deciduous Forest (LDF) of the Yucatan Peninsula and its value as cultural heritage. A review of scientific articles was carried out in the main search engines and those that met the search criteria were used. Human activities have led to a high deterioration in the native vegetation of the Yucatan Peninsula, as a result of the lack of knowledge of the great benefits that it provides to its inhabitants. The LDF provides nutrients for livestock that produces animal protein for the population of the cities and in the same way the hunting of wild species is used in rural communities, on the other hand, large areas are deforested that are used for grain cultivation without knowing the consequences of this change in vegetation. There are tree species in the LDF that have been exploited for use in furniture making, construction or in the charcoal industry and the nutraceutical value of LDF species is not widely disseminated in traditional human medicine and ethnoveterinary medicine for the control of parasitic species that affect traditional livestock. The above must be done in a rational way to continue with the benefit of its ecosystem services and not change the dynamics in this ecosystem of soils, water that can even change air quality.

title: Banking Sector Development and Economic Growth: A Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling Approach
summary: In Pakistan’s evolving financial ecosystem, the banking sector functions as a critical intermediary, mobilizing savings into productive investments and facilitating capital accumulation and economic growth. This study empirically examines t
content: In Pakistan’s evolving financial ecosystem, the banking sector functions as a critical intermediary, mobilizing savings into productive investments and facilitating capital accumulation and economic growth. This study empirically examines the interrelationships among key banking sector dimensions—deposits, loans, and investments—bank capital formation, and disaggregated components of economic growth within the context of Pakistan’s digital banking transformation over the period 2004–2024. The analysis employs Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling (BSEM) to capture complex interdependencies and latent relationships using a panel dataset of 12 banks, including conventional, Islamic, and foreign institutions. The model evaluates both direct and indirect pathways through which banking activities influence economic performance, with economic growth operationalized through GDP components such as private consumption, government expenditure, gross investment, and net exports. The results indicate that core banking activities significantly and positively predict bank capital formation. In turn, bank capital exhibits a positive association with private consumption and gross investment, while showing a negative relationship with net exports, suggesting potential trade-offs in resource allocation. Comparative findings further reveal that Islamic banks demonstrate relatively stronger capital retention, whereas foreign banks exhibit higher investment efficiency compared to conventional banks. This study contributes to the financial intermediation literature by advancing the application of Bayesian SEM in an emerging economy context, offering a comparative perspective across different banking systems, and incorporating the role of digital transformation in shaping financial sector dynamics. The findings provide policy-relevant insights for strengthening capital adequacy frameworks and enhancing the effectiveness of digital banking strategies to support sustainable economic growth in Pakistan.

title: A Bibliometric Systematic Review of Blockchain Integration in E-commerce with Emphasis on Data Privacy and Supply Chain Transparency
summary: Driven by digital transformation and evolving consumer behavior, the e-commerce industry continues to grow rapidly across global markets. Blockchain, as an emerging technology, offers transformative potential for e-commerce operations due t
content: Driven by digital transformation and evolving consumer behavior, the e-commerce industry continues to grow rapidly across global markets. Blockchain, as an emerging technology, offers transformative potential for e-commerce operations due to its transparency, security, decentralization, and traceability features. These attributes enable improvements in areas such as data privacy, supply chain traceability, fraud prevention, and operational efficiency. However, the adoption and integration of blockchain in e-commerce remain in a nascent stage, with significant technological and regulatory hurdles yet to be overcome. This paper conducts a systematic review of blockchain applications in e-commerce with emphasis on data privacy and supply chain transparency by utilizing bibliometric techniques. All relevant publications indexed in the Scopus database were examined to extract and analyze keywords and themes. Additionally, VOSviewer software was employed to visualize co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic clusters. Findings reveal that blockchain contributes to various domains within e-commerce, including data security, supply chain transparency, sector-specific applications, and integration with emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. Key drivers for blockchain adoption include improved traceability, automation, and fraud prevention, while barriers such as scalability, regulatory uncertainty, and high implementation costs continue to hinder widespread integration. The study offers valuable implications for both academic researchers and industry practitioners seeking to adopt blockchain for enhancing e-commerce performance.

title: Altitude-Dependent Climate Effects of Hydrogen Combustion in Turbofan Aircraft: A Comparative Literature Synthesis
summary: Liquid hydrogen combustion eliminates direct carbon dioxide emissions from turbofan aircraft but releases roughly 2.6 times more water vapour per unit of released combustion energy than conventional Jet-A fuel, raising the question of wheth
content: Liquid hydrogen combustion eliminates direct carbon dioxide emissions from turbofan aircraft but releases roughly 2.6 times more water vapour per unit of released combustion energy than conventional Jet-A fuel, raising the question of whether the resulting non-CO2 effects offset the carbon benefit. This study addresses that question through a comparative literature synthesis of 24 peer-reviewed sources, asking under what flight altitudes and atmospheric conditions hydrogen combustion yields a net climate benefit relative to kerosene. A two-stage search protocol combined a date-restricted systematic screen with a targeted search for foundational work published under earlier terminology. Nine standardised variables were extracted from the primary studies and the supplementary evidence was tabulated separately. Altitude was treated as a categorical variable across three bands, with ambient temperature and relative humidity with respect to ice recorded as the underlying mechanism. Hydrogen contrails form at threshold temperatures approximately 10 K higher than kerosene contrails while containing more than 80 to 90 percent fewer ice crystals, which reduces their optical thickness. The altitude dependence is established but is jointly determined by latitude, season and aircraft design, and the direction of the contrail-frequency response reverses between equatorial and non-equatorial regions. The principal gap is not an absence of altitude-resolved evidence but an absence of harmonised comparison under common metrics.

summary: Amaç –Sürdürülebilir finansın piyasa temelli göstergeleri olan ESG endekslerinin geleneksel piyasalarla ilişkilerinin analizi giderek önem kazanmaktadır. Bu çalışma, Türkiye’nin ESG göstergesi niteliğindeki BIST Sürdürülebilirlik Endeksi (X
content: Amaç –Sürdürülebilir finansın piyasa temelli göstergeleri olan ESG endekslerinin geleneksel piyasalarla ilişkilerinin analizi giderek önem kazanmaktadır. Bu çalışma, Türkiye’nin ESG göstergesi niteliğindeki BIST Sürdürülebilirlik Endeksi (XUSRD) ile yerel hisse (BIST 100), küresel hisse (S&P 500), küresel ESG ölçütü (MSCI World ESG Leaders) ve emtialar (Brent petrol, altın) arasındaki statik ve dinamik bağlantılılığı ölçmeyi amaçlamaktadır.Yöntem –5 Ocak 2015–26 Mart 2025 dönemine ait günlük veriler kullanılarak Diebold–Yılmaz bağlantılılık yöntemi ile hem statik hem dinamik bağlantılılık analizleri yapılmıştır. Toplam, yönlü ve net bağlantılılık ölçüleri ile zaman içinde değişen bağlantılılık göstergeleri elde edilmiştir.Bulgular –Statik bağlantılılık sonuçları (TCI ≈ %38,6) ağ içi etkileşimin orta düzeyde olduğunu göstermektedir. S&P 500 ve küresel ESG net yayıcı, Brent ve altın net alıcıdır. XUSRD ve BIST 100 yakın-nötr bir profil sergilemekte ve aralarında güçlü çift yönlü bağ bulunmaktadır. COVID-19 ve 2022 enerji şoku dönemlerinde bağlantılılık belirgin artmakta, özellikle hisse bloklarında çeşitlendirme imkânı daralmaktadır. Normalleşme fazlarında ise TCI yeniden orta banda dönmektedir.Tartışma –Bulgular, XUSRD’nin fiyat-alıcı bir yapıda olduğunu, yerel hisse döngüsünden henüz anlamlı ölçüde ayrışmadığını ve küresel yayıcılara duyarlı kaldığını göstermektedir. Altın çoğu dönemde tampon rolü oynarken, Brent’in etkisi rejime bağlı ve sınırlıdır. Sakin rejimlerde sınırlı da olsa çeşitlendirme olanağının bulunduğu ancak stres dönemlerinde hisse bloklarında senkronizasyonun artmasına ve çeşitlendirme alanının daraldığı görülmektedir. Sonuçlar BIST Sürdürülebilirlik endeksi portföylerde tek başına ayrıştırıcı bir faktör olmadığını, yerel hisse ile birlikte ve küresel yayıcılar erken uyarı göstergesi kabul edilerek yönetilmesi gerektiğini göstermektedi

title: New Challenges, Onboard Carbon Capture and Storage OCCS for Military Ships
summary: The concept of onboard carbon capture (OCC) is based on technology which captures the carbon on board the vessel before the CO2 is emitted to the atmosphere through the exhaust. While it offers flexibility and retrofit potential, some signi
content: The concept of onboard carbon capture (OCC) is based on technology which captures the carbon on board the vessel before the CO2 is emitted to the atmosphere through the exhaust. While it offers flexibility and retrofit potential, some significant engineering, logistical, and economic hurdles remain. Studies show that the technology can be applied safely on vessels, but it still needs to be further developed and optimized for maritime use and integration. Key factors that affect the technical feasibility of onboard carbon capture for a dedicated vessel are the size, operational profile and hull pattern, the machinery capacity for power and heat production, and the space available. This study explores these technologies for naval applications, specifically to reduce smoke emissions from exhaust systems.

title: Inter-Organisational Systems for Circular Value Chains: A Simulation of Digital Product Passport Adoption
summary: Circular value chains rely on effective information sharing to recover materials from waste, reducing dependence on virgin resources and improving industrial sustainability. To support circular value chains, the EU has introduced the Digita
content: Circular value chains rely on effective information sharing to recover materials from waste, reducing dependence on virgin resources and improving industrial sustainability. To support circular value chains, the EU has introduced the Digital Product Passport, an inter-organisational information system for disclosing product information. The effect of the DPP on the sustainability of circular value chains has not been explored, and extant literature focuses only on its technical design. Drawing on organisational information processing theory, we model the DPP characteristics as capabilities that address different information needs in each phase of a circular value chain for the recovery of photovoltaic waste, and simulate 500 random adoption scenarios. The findings indicate that the DPP increases the amount of material processed and improves environmental and social sustainability, while costs grow faster than revenues and the additional material is not matched by proportional downstream processing. These dynamics reveal tensions and trade-offs in both implementation and policy decisions regarding DPP adoption.

title: Navigating Renewable Energy Tensions Through Agentic Human–AI Collaboration
summary: Household decisions about renewable energy technologies involve persistent competing demands, including short-term versus long-term outcomes and individual versus collective interests. These tensions can be reinforced by psychological dista
content: Household decisions about renewable energy technologies involve persistent competing demands, including short-term versus long-term outcomes and individual versus collective interests. These tensions can be reinforced by psychological distance, which makes future and collective consequences less salient than immediate and individual considerations. This research-in-progress paper examines how agentic AI can support households in navigating such tensions rather than resolving them through simple optimization. Drawing on paradox theory, psychological distance, agentic AI, sensemaking, and human–AI collaboration, we derive five initial meta-requirements: surfacing competing demands, counteracting asymmetric salience, providing context-sensitive agentic support over time, supporting ongoing sensemaking, and calibrating human and AI agency. We outline a mixed-method, interpretive design science approach to empirically examine and refine these meta-requirements through qualitative inquiry, artifact development, and scenario-based evaluation. The study conceptualizes agentic AI as support for ongoing paradox navigation in complex sustainability decisions.

title: Defining Green ITSM: A Taxonomy for Sustainable IT Service Management
summary: Despite IT Service Management’s (ITSM) role in digital transformation, its systematic integration of sustainability remains underexplored with no classification of this construct. To address the identified construct-specification and classi
content: Despite IT Service Management’s (ITSM) role in digital transformation, its systematic integration of sustainability remains underexplored with no classification of this construct. To address the identified construct-specification and classification gap at the intersection of Green Information Systems and ITSM, this paper develops a taxonomy-based definition of Green ITSM. An iterative process combines two systematic literature reviews, additional literature, practitioner interviews, practice-oriented guidance, and academic expert evaluation. The resulting morphological taxonomy comprises 16 dimensions and associated characteristics. Green ITSM is defined as the configuration of ITSM beliefs, practices and learning mechanisms – embedded in a management context – that aligns the design, delivery, evaluation, and improvement of IT services and their ecosystems for economic, ecological, and social sustainability outcomes. Evaluation indicates high relevance, novelty, and clarity, while highlighting operationalization and practical validation needs. Overall, the taxonomy provides a conceptualization of Green ITSM and a reproducible classification scheme to assess, compare, and improve sustainability-oriented IT services.

title: How Digital Information Systems Enable Sustainable Procurement: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain, and e-procurement systems, are transforming procurement practices. Firms increasingly prioritize economic efficiency while also adhering to environmental
content: Digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain, and e-procurement systems, are transforming procurement practices. Firms increasingly prioritize economic efficiency while also adhering to environmental requirements and social responsibility to ensure long-term value creation. Despite this, the literature remains fragmented across the domains of purchasing, sustainability, and information systems. This systematic literature review, conducted using the PRISMA method, synthesizes evidence that digital technologies facilitate sustainable procurement across the Triple Bottom Line. Four primary enabling mechanisms are identified: process integration and efficiency, visibility and traceability, supplier assessment and governance, and lifecycle intelligence. Economic and environmental outcomes are more thoroughly addressed than social outcomes, revealing a structural gap in the literature. The review adopts a mechanism-based approach and develops a conceptual research model grounded in socio-technical systems theory and information technology (IT) business value logic, providing guidance for practitioners to align digital investments with procurement sustainability objectives.

title: Perceptual and Behavioral Determinants for Optimizing Energy Performance in Buildings: A Study of Maladaptive Human Interactions
source: Emirati Journal of Civil Engineering and Applications
summary: The persistent discrepancy between predicted and actual building energy performance has highlighted the need to better understand the role of occupants in shaping operational energy outcomes. While technological advances have significantly
content: The persistent discrepancy between predicted and actual building energy performance has highlighted the need to better understand the role of occupants in shaping operational energy outcomes. While technological advances have significantly improved building efficiency, human behavior remains a critical yet often underestimated determinant of actual energy consumption. This study investigates the behavioral and environmental factors influencing lighting related energy use in office environments, with particular emphasis on environmental concern, flexibility of energy-control systems, and responsive occupant behavior. Drawing upon theories from environmental psychology, behavioral science, and architectural research, a mixed-method approach was adopted comprising naturalistic observations, structured behavioral observations, and a survey-based investigation. Fieldwork was conducted within contemporary office environments. Following exploratory observations across multiple workplaces, a case-study office building was selected for detailed investigation. The study involved 77 participants representing a range of professional roles, including administrators, engineers, programmers, and researchers. The findings indicate that environmental concern alone does not adequately explain adaptive energy related behavior. Instead, occupants’ responses emerge through the interaction of personal values, environmental opportunities, spatial perception, and the accessibility of environmental control systems. Flexible lighting-control mechanisms, including adjustable blinds and decentralized lighting controls, were found to encourage greater engagement with daylight and more responsive lighting-related actions. Conversely, social dynamics, workplace norms, and limited environmental control frequently constrained adaptive behavior despite occupants’ awareness of energy-saving opportunities. The study argues that occupants should be regarded as active participants in building performance rather than unpredictable sources of variation. The results demonstrate that improving building energy performance requires an integrated human-centered approach in which architectural design, environmental affordances, and behavioral determinants are considered alongside technological efficiency measures. By supporting environmental awareness, user autonomy, and adaptive interaction, buildings can more effectively reduce the performance gap and achieve long-term sustainability objectives.

title: The Use of Humic Acid in Improving Roughages and to Enhance the Performance of Iraqi Local Black Goats
source: Journal of Animal Health and Production
summary: The present aim to study the effect of humic acid (HA) supplementation on growth performance, nutrient utilization, rumen fermentation and microbial ecology in local Iraqi black goats.Eighteen male goats (4-month-old, 18.6 -0.4 kg BW) were
content: The present aim to study the effect of humic acid (HA) supplementation on growth performance, nutrient utilization, rumen fermentation and microbial ecology in local Iraqi black goats.Eighteen male goats (4-month-old, 18.6 -0.4 kg BW) were randomly placed in three diets control (no HA), 3kg HA t -1DM, and 5kg HA t -1DM for 105 days.Comparison and control with HA supplementation showed that there are significant (p < 0.05) differences in average daily gain (ADG), feed conversion ratio (FCR), and total volatile fatty acids (VFAs).It also altered the molar ratios of major VFAs to raise the propionate and lower the acetate thus causing a lower acetate: propionate ratio and less methane production.The upregulation of cellulolytic bacteria (Ruminococcus albus, Fibrobacter succinogenes, Prevotella ruminicola) and inhibition of methanogenic archaea (Methanobrevibacter smithii, Methanobacterium formicicum) by HA were proved by quantitative PCR and 16S rRNA sequencing.Also, alpha-diversity indices (Chao1, Shannon, Simpson) were significantly higher suggesting a more diverse and stable rumen ecosystem.When combined all these effects of humic on the rumen fermentation, VFA profile and microbial ecology means that it can be used to increase the efficiency of the ruminant digestion and thus the optimum energy efficiency by increasing the fermentations and reducing the generation of enteric methane.Taken together, HA is an eco-friendly additive that enhances productive efficiency, as well as environmental efficiency of small-ruminant systems.

title: The Decoupling Dilemma: Analyzing the CO₂ Delta with India’s Growth and National Action Plan on Climate Change
source: TMP Universal Journal of Research and Review Archives.
summary: The relentless rise in global CO₂ emissions driven by rapid economic expansion poses one of the most pressing challenges to climate stability and sustainable development. Despite technological advances and policy efforts, CO₂ emissions cont
content: The relentless rise in global CO₂ emissions driven by rapid economic expansion poses one of the most pressing challenges to climate stability and sustainable development. Despite technological advances and policy efforts, CO₂ emissions continue to increase, reaching new records in recent years and threatening the achievement of Paris Agreement targets. This study investigates the relationship between economic growth as measured by Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and CO₂ emissions. The primary objective is to examine the nature and strength of this relationship, exploring whether economic expansion inevitably leads to higher emissions or if decoupling is observable in certain contexts. Using a comprehensive dataset from reliable sources, the analysis employs Pearson and spearman correlation coefficients, trend comparisons and detrended Wilcoxon signed-rank test to understand the effect of NAPCC.

title: REAL-TIME ENERGY AND CARBON EMISSIONS MONITORING IN EDUCATIONAL BUILDINGS USING A PLC–SCADA PLATFORM: A CASE STUDY OF AIR-CONDITIONING SYSTEM PERFORMANCE.
summary: The growing demand for energy efficiency has placed higher education institutions (HEIs) at the forefront of efforts to reduce electricity consumption and the associated Carbon Emissions (CE). This study presents the development and impleme
content: The growing demand for energy efficiency has placed higher education institutions (HEIs) at the forefront of efforts to reduce electricity consumption and the associated Carbon Emissions (CE). This study presents the development and implementation of a low-cost real-time monitoring platform based on Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) technologies for tracking energy consumption and associated Carbon Emissions from air-conditioning (A/C) systems in educational buildings. The platform continuously records electricity consumption data, converts them into carbon-emission indicators using the national electricity-grid emission factor, and displays real-time trends through a SCADA-based interface. This enables facility managers and decision-makers to monitor energy and carbon performance and support informed operational decisions.To validate the monitoring system under different operating conditions, two A/C units (5-HP and 1.5-HP) were monitored at four temperature setpoints (20°C, 22°C, 24°C, and 25°C). Results show that maintaining higher temperature setpoints (24°C–25°C) reduced energy consumption and Carbon Emissions, with reductions of approximately 33% for the 5-HP unit and 49% for the 1.5-HP unit when comparing 25°C to 20°C.The results demonstrate the capability of the proposed PLC–SCADA platform to monitor, visualize, and quantify energy consumption and associated Carbon Emissions in real time under varying operating conditions. The temperature-setpoint experiments served as a validation case study illustrating how the monitoring system can detect the impact of operational changes on energy use and emissions. Future implementations may expand the platform to additional building systems and support broader carbon-footprint monitoring and energy-management initiatives. The findings suggest that real-time monitoring platforms can support sustainability objectives and data-driven decision-making in HEIs.

title: Vermicomposting of fallow deer (Dama dama L.) manure using Eisenia fetida (Sav.) earthworms
summary: Given the need to ensure sustainable development in agriculture, waste should be managed properly. This also applies to manure from the breeding of non-conventional animal species. A study was conducted on the vermicomposting of fallow deer
content: Given the need to ensure sustainable development in agriculture, waste should be managed properly. This also applies to manure from the breeding of non-conventional animal species. A study was conducted on the vermicomposting of fallow deer (Dama dama) manure using Eisenia fetida Sav. earthworms. The study assessed the effect of adding cellulose from cardboard and decomposed hay on the properties of the resulting vermicompost. In the study, clean fallow deer manure (FDM), fallow deer manure mixed with cardboard (FDMC) in a 1:1 ratio, and fallow deer manure mixed with decomposed hay (FDMH) in a 1:1 ratio were processed. The basic physicochemical properties of the waste materials and vermicomposts were evaluated, as well as the population dynamics of compost earthworms depending on the substrate used in the vermireactor. The results indicate that E. fetida effectively processed the waste materials. Vermicomposting led to a decrease in pH and a reduction in salinity, indicating the progressive stabilization of organic matter. Compared to the initial material, the resulting vermicomposts were characterized by higher nitrogen, potassium, and magnesium content. The content of the analyzed trace elements in the vermicomposts was low, suggesting their potential use as fertilizer. The most favorable conditions for growth of the E. fetida population were observed in the treatment with cellulose (FDMC) added to the structural materials. The results indicate that fallow deer manure can serve as a useful substrate for vermicomposting, especially when combined with carbon-rich structural components.

title: Cyanide speciation as the determinant of treatment performance: A critical review of removal, destruction and recovery routes for cyanide-bearing wastewater
summary: Cyanide-containing wastewater is a multicomponent system: cyanide occurs as free cyanide, within weak acid dissociable (WAD) cyanide and stable metal-cyanide complexes, and alongside thiocyanate, metals and other impurities. The chemical fo
content: Cyanide-containing wastewater is a multicomponent system: cyanide occurs as free cyanide, within weak acid dissociable (WAD) cyanide and stable metal-cyanide complexes, and alongside thiocyanate, metals and other impurities. The chemical form of cyanide and the composition of the aqueous matrix govern treatment performance, which makes direct comparison between technologies difficult. This review covers physical and physicochemical, chemical, electrochemical, photochemical and biological methods; for each group it examines the process mechanism, the target cyanide species, the treatment conditions, the secondary streams generated, the scope for recovery and the level of technological maturity. Removal, destruction and recovery of cyanide are treated as distinct outcomes, because an identical removal efficiency may conceal a fundamentally different final fate of the pollutant. No universal treatment technology exists, and data obtained on model solutions cannot always be transferred to real multicomponent effluents. For concentrated process streams, the feasibility of cyanide extraction and reuse should be assessed first; where recovery is not viable, destructive processes followed by deep polishing are applied. Further work requires testing on real wastewater, lower energy and reagent consumption, smaller volumes of secondary waste, scale-up of promising processes, and integrated schemes in which recovery, destruction and polishing are matched to the characteristics of the specific stream.

title: Ecological and geochemical monitoring of the soil–surface water system in the impact zone of the thermoelectric power station
summary: This study examined spatial patterns of chemical elements in soils within the potential impact zone of the Burshtyn Thermal Power Plant and compared the soil results with non-synchronous published surface-water data. Instrument screening re
content: This study examined spatial patterns of chemical elements in soils within the potential impact zone of the Burshtyn Thermal Power Plant and compared the soil results with non-synchronous published surface-water data. Instrument screening reported 30 components; quantitative interpretation used ten variables with complete results for 19 sites, while Pb was quantified at 12 sites. Soil conditions were assessed using concentration factors, Al-normalized enrichment factors, the geoaccumulation index, Spearman correlations with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate control, and exploratory principal component analysis (PCA). All enrichment factors for Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, and quantified Pb were below 2. Pb values of 43–77 mg/kg were above the cited 32 mg/kg comparison value, although this screening result requires confirmation by complete analytical QA/QC. Mean Zn was 2.44 times the regional background. After FDR adjustment, significant associations remained for Fe–K, Fe–Ni, Fe–Cr, K–Ni, and K–Cr. No significant monotonic relationship was detected between distance and enrichment factors across all sites or within the six downwind sites. The first three PCs explained 80.1% of total variance. A reduced eight-variable PCA retained the Fe–Cr–Ni pattern and the Ca–Si contrast, whereas the Cu–Zn pattern was less stable. The water-to-soil ratio was redefined as an empirical cross-compartment aqueous-representation ratio (Rw/s, kg/L), rather than a leaching coefficient. Ca and Sr had the highest ratios, Mg and Zn intermediate ratios, and Fe, Mn, Cr, and Cu the lowest. Because soil samples were collected in 2026 and water data originated from earlier studies, the comparison does not demonstrate leaching or soil-to-water transfer. The multielement structure is consistent with a substantial lithogenic or mineral-matrix contribution, while localized anthropogenic contributions to Pb and Zn cannot be excluded.

title: GPS-X modeling of sidestreams elimination for enhanced energy recovery and greenhouse gas mitigation in a full-scale anaerobic-anoxic-oxic plant
summary: The balance between effluent quality, energy consumption efficiency, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions should be well maintained in modern wastewater treatment plants (WWTP’s). In this study, a novel process was employed to eliminate sides
content: The balance between effluent quality, energy consumption efficiency, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions should be well maintained in modern wastewater treatment plants (WWTP’s). In this study, a novel process was employed to eliminate sidestreams from a full-scale anaerobic-anoxic-oxic (A2/O) WWTP, reducing carbon footprint and energy consumption while improving renewable energy production. The integrated plant processes were then modeled using GPS-X simulation, and the model was assessed using comprehensive data from a full-scale WWTP (A2/O) process. The results highlighted that the novel process increased renewable energy by 100 m3/day of biogas, equivalent to 214 kW. It also contributed to a high reduction in energy consumption by about 442.51 kW. Furthermore, the elimination of sidestreams has contributed to a 12 and 13% reduction in net carbon footprint and N2O released into the atmosphere, respectively. These results conclude that treating the sidestreams separately can improve the sustainable management of the A2/O WWTP.

title: Utilization of leached spent vanadium catalyst residue as active silica filler in sulfur concrete: A chemical pathway for industrial waste valorization
summary: This study presents a resource-efficient chemical pathway for valorizing leached silica residue from spent vanadium catalysts as an active mineral filler in dicyclopentadiene (DCPD)-modified sulfur concrete. X-ray diffraction confirmed the
content: This study presents a resource-efficient chemical pathway for valorizing leached silica residue from spent vanadium catalysts as an active mineral filler in dicyclopentadiene (DCPD)-modified sulfur concrete. X-ray diffraction confirmed the silica residue as alpha-cristobalite (ICDD 00-039-1425) with a specific surface area of 15.0 ± 1.2 m²/g and mesoporous structure (6-8 nm pore size). The optimal 15 wt.% loading increased compressive strength by 42% to 68.4 ± 1.2 MPa and flexural strength by 56% to 8.4 ± 0.2 MPa, with water absorption below 0.5%. FTIR spectroscopy revealed enhanced Si-O-Si stretching at 1098 cm⁻¹ and surface Si-OH groups at 3400-3740 cm⁻¹, indicating active interfacial sites. SEM analysis showed transition from adhesive failure (SC-0) to cohesive failure (SC-15) with sulfur infiltration depth of 2-5 μm, as confirmed by EDX elemental line scan (98.2% S bulk → 85% S interface → 45% Si core). Thermal cycling (100 cycles, −20 to +60 °C) demonstrated 92 ± 3% strength retention. Chemical resistance testing over 28-day immersion in 5% H₂SO₄, 5% NaOH, and 5% Na₂SO₄ confirmed 97.2-98.5% strength retention with absolute residual strength of 66.5-67.4 MPa. Thermogravimetric analysis showed 0.12% mass loss at 200 °C, confirming absence of catalytic oxidation by residual vanadium (0.075% V₂O₅). Long-term monitoring over 90 days revealed gradual beta-to-alpha transformation at ~0.08%/day with 94% strength retention. Techno-economic analysis for Kazakhstan (2025) indicated a production cost of 62 USD/m³, representing 27% reduction versus standard sulfur concrete and 5% reduction versus Portland cement. CO₂ emissions of approximately 13 kg/m³ represent 97% reduction versus Portland cement. A unified three-scale stabilization mechanism is proposed, encompassing molecular-level DCPD/Si-OH interactions, microstructural capillary infiltration, and macroscopic void filling. This work establishes a dual waste valorization route for cement-free construction materials with exceptional chemical durability.

title: A review of sewage sludge treatment and management methods in wastewater treatment plants
summary: The purpose of this paper was to review the methods of sewage sludge treatment and management in wastewater treatment plants with particular emphasis on constructed wetland systems as nature-based solutions (NBS). Sewage sludge management i
content: The purpose of this paper was to review the methods of sewage sludge treatment and management in wastewater treatment plants with particular emphasis on constructed wetland systems as nature-based solutions (NBS). Sewage sludge management is one of the major challenges associated with wastewater treatment due to the high associated costs of sludge processing, transport, and disposal, as well as the increasing environmental requirements concerning its safe utilization and overall carbon footprint. This review presented the current state of knowledge on sewage sludge treatment and management, with particular emphasis on technologies suitable for small and decentralized wastewater treatment plants. Conventional methods, including thickening, mechanical dewatering, anaerobic and aerobic stabilization, composting, chemical stabilization, thermal drying, incineration, pyrolysis, and gasification, were discussed in terms of their technological characteristics, environmental impacts, energy requirements, and applicability. Attention was given to NBS, especially Sludge Treatment Reed Beds (STRB), which enable simultaneous dewatering, drying, and partial stabilization of sludge through filtration, gravity drainage, evapotranspiration, and biological processes. The literature indicated that STRB can significantly reduce sludge volume while requiring relatively low energy inputs and limited-to-zero chemical addition. These characteristics make this technology particularly promising for small and decentralized wastewater treatment plants, where conventional sludge treatment technologies are often economically and technically difficult to implement. The effectiveness of STRB depends mainly on the sludge loading rate, feeding frequency, resting periods, filter media properties, vegetation development, and climatic conditions. Despite their advantages, limitations related to land requirements, long treatment periods, seasonal variability, and the risk of clogging must be considered. The review highlighted the potential of STRB as a low-energy and environmentally sustainable approach to local sewage sludge management and identifieed the need for further research on design parameters adapted to temperate climates and decentralized wastewater treatment systems.

title: Photovoltaic modules performance and carbon footprint assessment in agrivoltaic system
summary: We ran a two-month field trial (1 August – 30 September 2025) on a farm near Baghdad to see how lifting PV modules over a crop changes their electrical output, their operational carbon intensity, and the yield of the tomato (Solanum lycoper
content: We ran a two-month field trial (1 August – 30 September 2025) on a farm near Baghdad to see how lifting PV modules over a crop changes their electrical output, their operational carbon intensity, and the yield of the tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) grown underneath. Monocrystalline and polycrystalline modules were each installed in two ways: close to the ground over bare soil (C-PV) and on a 2 m agrivoltaic frame (AV). In total, 720 observations of I–V curves, module temperature, irradiance and energy yield were collected. The AV modules averaged 63.5 °C and the ground-mounted ones 76.3 °C. That 12.8 °C difference is two to four times the 3–7 °C usually quoted for temperate installations, which suggests elevation pays off most where the heat load is highest. In the two-way ANOVA, both mounting and module type affected efficiency, power gain, energy, carbon intensity and temperature (p < 0.001 for most terms). Efficiency went from 11.25% on C-PV to 15.39% on AV; monocrystalline modules gained more (11.26% → 16.45%) than polycrystalline ones (11.24% → 14.32%). Carbon intensity fell by 29.9% on the AV frame (70.26 → 49.23 g CO2e kWh⁻¹). Since we used fixed emission factors for each technology, this drop reflects only the larger amount of energy delivered per unit of embodied emission. Tomatoes under the panels yielded 3.452 kg m⁻², against 3.635 kg m⁻² in the open-field control (C-Ag); one-way ANOVA (n = 144) gave p = 0.053, i.e. not significant, though only just. The results are set against recent agrivoltaic, land-use and life-cycle studies. Over one season, the raised frame gave more electricity with no measurable yield cost, and the layout deserves wider testing in hot-arid parts of Iraq and central Türkiye.

title: Study on air-staging combustion of natural gas-hydrogen blend in high temperature industrial heating process
source: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal
summary: The decarbonization of energy-intensive industrial sectors requires the implementation of low-carbon fuels and advanced combustion technologies. This study investigates the co-combustion of hydrogen and natural gas in an industrial diffusio
content: The decarbonization of energy-intensive industrial sectors requires the implementation of low-carbon fuels and advanced combustion technologies. This study investigates the co-combustion of hydrogen and natural gas in an industrial diffusion burner, with particular emphasis on pollutant emissions and heat transfer. Experimental investigations and theoretical analyses were conducted for fuel blends containing up to 60 vol.% hydrogen over a broad range of operating conditions. A modified burner incorporating staged combustion air, with primary and secondary air supplied separately, was tested in a semi-industrial combustion chamber under high-temperature conditions. The results showed that hydrogen addition increased the total heat flux by up to 3.5 %, primarily because of the higher combustion and flue-gas temperatures and changes in the radiative properties of the combustion products, particularly CO₂ and H₂O. However, the higher oxidation rate of hydrogen reduced the flame length, partially limiting radiative heat transfer directly from the flame. Experimental evaluation of the proposed combustion strategy confirmed stable burner operation with very low carbon monoxide emissions, typically not exceeding a few ppm, even at high secondary air ratios. Although hydrogen enrichment initially increased NO emissions, the application of air staging significantly suppressed NO formation, achieving reductions of more than 55 % at a secondary air ratio of 0.5. The emission-reduction strategy was more effective at lower excess-air ratios. Overall, the results demonstrate that hydrogen–natural gas co-combustion in industrial furnaces is feasible and can maintain NO emissions below 50 ppm under the investigated operating conditions without requiring secondary flue-gas treatment technologies. The proposed approach therefore represents a promising pathway for the decarbonization of high-temperature industrial processes.

title: Transforming shipping in practice : decarbonization, digitalization and Arctic navigation
summary: This book comprises a total of 20 chapters across 3 parts, detailing the maritime digitalization, decarbonization, maritime AI application and seafarers in the era of technology development which including technologies, regulations, and pol
content: This book comprises a total of 20 chapters across 3 parts, detailing the maritime digitalization, decarbonization, maritime AI application and seafarers in the era of technology development which including technologies, regulations, and policies presented during WMU Maritime Affairs Conference 2026. Part 1 focuses on Decarbonization, Part 2 covers Digitalization, and Part 3 addresses Arctic Navigation to convey the key messages from experts speakers of the WMU Maritime Affairs Conference 2026. Part 1 (Decarbonization I and II) contains 7 chapters including 2 keynote speaker’s contribution. Chapter 1 highlights essential of pragmatism for maritime decarbonization and emphasizes taking practical, incremental steps now rather than waiting for a utopian consensus that may never materialize. Chapter 2 introduces maritime sector's dual transformation of decarbonization and digitalization requires a structured Safety Assurance Framework to validate new technologies before large-scale deployment. By combining goal-based criteria, rigorous evidence generation across testing stages, and cross-jurisdictional governance, this approach treats safety evidence as critical enabling infrastructure rather than a mere compliance cost. Chapter 3 highlighted philosophy for selelcting the Green Shipping Corridors to help achieve Paris Agreement and IMO net-zero targets. Chapter 4 Examining synthetic fuels for Mediterranean Ro-Pax ferry decarbonization, this study uses a multi-criteria decision-making approach to evaluate various energy alternatives across safety, technical, and economic criteria. It concludes that while onshore power supply and bio-LNG are most practical currently, operators must maintain technological optionality through resilient, adaptable transition pathways rather than relying on a single future fuel. Chapter 5 examines Onboard Carbon Capture and Storage (OCCS) as a practical bridge technology to help ships comply with the IMO Net-Zero Framework while zero-emission fuel supply chains mature. Chapter 6 Examining alternative marine fuel implementation in Malaysian ports and proposes a four-pillar action framework to strengthen institutional coordination, regulatory readiness, and green energy orchestration for industry-ready bunkering. Chapter 7 Examining liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) as a practical transition fuel for small and coastal vessels in Korea, this chapter evaluates its advantages across technology, regulation, and policy dimensions. It highlights that LPG can serve as a realistic bridge fuel for smaller vessel segments through a phased approach, provided it eventually integrates green-LPG pathways like bio-LPG and e-LPG. Part 2 (Digitalization I and II) contain 6 chapters including 1 keynote speaker contribution. Chapter 8 highlights key technologies like E-Navigation, the Maritime Single Window, and Maritime Autonomous Surface Vessels (MASS) in relation to IMO regulatory frameworks and safety standards.
