summary: Against the backdrop of the deepening of the "Quality Power" strategy and the global industrial transformation, intelligent manufacturing has become the core path for the high-end, intelligent and green transformation of China's manufacturi
content: Against the backdrop of the deepening of the "Quality Power" strategy and the global industrial transformation, intelligent manufacturing has become the core path for the high-end, intelligent and green transformation of China's manufacturing industry. As the lifeline of the manufacturing industry, reliability is a key support for the effective implementation of intelligent manufacturing and the enhancement of industrial competitiveness. Combining typical practical cases, standard system construction and industry research in the fields of domestic intelligent manufacturing and reliability, this paper systematically sorts out the development status of China's intelligent manufacturing and reliability, deeply analyzes the problems in concepts, technologies, standards, talents and other aspects during the development process, and puts forward targeted solutions based on the practical experience and theoretical achievements in existing research, providing a theoretical reference for the integration of China's intelligent manufacturing and reliability and the promotion of the high-quality development of the manufacturing industry.

title: Beyond cost: a critical review of battery trade-offs for just energy transitions in developing and emerging economies
summary: Stationary battery selection in developing and emerging economies involves trade-offs between access to capital, reliable service, lifecycle burdens, and local governance. This review examines how these dimensions affect technology choice.
content: Stationary battery selection in developing and emerging economies involves trade-offs between access to capital, reliable service, lifecycle burdens, and local governance. This review examines how these dimensions affect technology choice. This structured critical review integrates selected technical, lifecycle, and energy-justice literature. Evidence is distinguished by application, geographical transferability, and commercial maturity. The literature is synthesized qualitatively; an illustrative multicriteria template specifies possible weighting scenarios without calculating technology scores or rankings. Lead–acid and lithium-ion batteries have established applications, but their relative whole-life costs depend on operating conditions, usable capacity, replacement, and financing. Evidence on lithium iron phosphate supports its consideration for stationary services without establishing universal superiority. Sodium-ion and iron-based flow batteries offer diversification opportunities with greater uncertainty in long-term field performance. Environmental comparisons depend on lifecycle boundaries and local end-of-life practices. Priorities should be defined for a specified service and jurisdiction with affected users, operators, and authorities. Upfront affordability, lifetime performance, environmental burden, and resilience/justice should be evaluated using explicit indicators, with safeguards for unacceptable health and safety risks. Equal and priority-weight scenarios are proposed only for future testing against local performance data; no optimal weights or rank reversals are demonstrated. Incomplete records of original source identification limit the reproducibility and coverage of this review.

title: Libro de resúmenes del ECI 2027 de verano

title: Cyclic Generation of (Oxy)hydroxides on Bifacial Photoanodes Enables High‐Performing Solar Urea Oxidation With Stability Exceeding 120 Hours
summary: Replacing the conventional oxygen evolution reaction on photoanodes with urea oxidation reaction (UOR) attracts significant efforts to integrate solar‐driven hydrogen production with purification of urea‐rich wastewater. Real‐world implemen
content: Replacing the conventional oxygen evolution reaction on photoanodes with urea oxidation reaction (UOR) attracts significant efforts to integrate solar‐driven hydrogen production with purification of urea‐rich wastewater. Real‐world implementations of this technology require improvements in key performance indicators, including low onset potential, high current density, and long‐term device lifetime; yet no present technology satisfies all these criteria simultaneously. We implement a self‐evolving NiFe hydroxides‐alloy co‐catalyst layer on microstructured Si photoanodes with decoupled photon management from catalysis. The system reports the lowest onset potential of 0.782 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, a saturated current density of 40.7 mA , and stability over 120 hours, an improvement of sevenfold over the closest competitor in Si‐based systems. In situ Raman and reduction‐peak charge analysis demonstrate that the photoanode‐enhanced performance leverages dynamic transition cycles between oxyhydroxides and hydroxides of the NiFe alloy layer, suppressing the steady‐state accumulation of high‐valence NiFe oxyhydroxides. We then engineered bias‐free devices for UOR‐assisted solar hydrogen production, exhibiting a current density of 11.07 mA , representing the highest current density reported among low‐cost, non‐photovoltaic‐assisted PEC devices. This photoanode architecture opens to large‐scale implementations of solar fuel production coupled with industrially valuable reactions, including biomass oxidation and plastics valorization.

title: Glass-Nanofiber-Reinforced Strontium Aluminate/Epoxy Nanocomposite Coatings for Ceramics: Persistent Luminescence and Multifunctional Surface Protection
summary: A multifunctional photoluminescent nanocomposite coating for ceramic substrates was developed using epoxy resin (EPR) as the polymeric matrix, strontium aluminate nanoparticles (NSA; 9–18 nm) as the photoluminescent component, and glass nan
content: A multifunctional photoluminescent nanocomposite coating for ceramic substrates was developed using epoxy resin (EPR) as the polymeric matrix, strontium aluminate nanoparticles (NSA; 9–18 nm) as the photoluminescent component, and glass nanofibers (50–220 nm) as a reinforcing phase. The incorporation of glass nanofibers was designed to enhance the mechanical performance of the epoxy coating while maintaining its optical functionality. The morphological, structural, and surface characteristics of NSA, glass nanofibers, and NSA@EPR-coated ceramic films were systematically investigated using complementary analytical techniques. The resulting coatings exhibited high transparency under daylight, a green emission under UV irradiation, and a greenish-yellow afterglow in darkness. Upon excitation at 365 nm, the photoluminescent coatings displayed characteristic emission bands at 519 nm, corresponding to a strong green emission, and 438 nm, attributed to a weaker blue emission. Increasing the NSA loading progressively enhanced both the fluorescence intensity and long-persistent phosphorescence of the coatings. In addition to their photoluminescent behavior, the nanocomposite coatings demonstrated improved UV-shielding capability, scratch resistance, antibacterial activity, and hydrophobicity. The NSA-containing coatings also exhibited good durability and photostability, indicating their potential as robust multifunctional ceramic coatings for protective, decorative, and optical applications.

title: Meta Life Cycle Assessment, Techno-Economic Analysis, and Risk Assessment of Carbon Mineralization Pathways to Inform Policy Frameworks
summary: Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even th
content: Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even though carbon capture is already factored into all major global climate models, with mineralization (converting CO2 into stable carbonates) representing a major subset. If mineralization is to bolster the suite of climate mitigation strategies, it is vital that academic guidance be provided to inform the currently underinformed policy direction. To address this, this study presents a meta life cycle and techno-economic analysis of carbon mineralization pathways from both academia and industry, normalizing independent techno-economic, life cycle, and risk assessment (Monte Carlo) results within the context of US and EU policy. Results demonstrate that in situ mineralization achieves the greatest life cycle GHG emission reductions at the lowest cost and is the only pathway capable of gigaton-scale emission reductions commensurate with climate goals. Enhanced rock weathering also consistently delivers net-negative GHG removal at relatively low costs, but ex situ pathways achieve lower GHG emission reductions at higher costs, where several proposed pathways are net-CO2 positive as CO2 emitted throughout the process (transportation, electricity use, and natural gas combustion) offsets CO2 sequestered. Risks of leakage, hazards, global capacity, financial impact, and reversal are also quantitatively and qualitatively compared among the mineralization pathways, demonstrating that in situ mineralization has low financial risk when bolstered by state entities, faces uncertainties in non-governmental organization objection, and, ultimately, all pathways are victims of uncharted policy.

title: Waste-to-Energy in Malaysia: Technologies, Biomass Resources, Municipal Solid Waste Management, Techno-Economic Feasibility, Environmental Impacts and Future Prospects
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Waste-to-energy (WtE) technology has emerged as an important alternative for addressing the growing challenges of solid waste management while supporting the transition towards renewable and sustainable energy systems. In Malaysia, rapid ur
content: Waste-to-energy (WtE) technology has emerged as an important alternative for addressing the growing challenges of solid waste management while supporting the transition towards renewable and sustainable energy systems. In Malaysia, rapid urbanisation, population growth, industrial development and increasing consumption have contributed to rising municipal solid waste (MSW) generation, placing considerable pressure on existing landfill-based disposal systems. At the same time, Malaysia possesses substantial energy recovery potential from various waste streams, including food waste, agricultural residues, oil palm biomass, industrial waste and municipal solid waste. This paper presents a comprehensive review of waste-to-energy technologies, with particular emphasis on their suitability, performance, implementation challenges and future prospects in Malaysia. The review examines major WtE conversion pathways, including incineration, anaerobic digestion, landfill gas recovery, gasification, pyrolysis and hydrothermal carbonisation, together with emerging opportunities for biogas, biofuel and hydrogen production. Particular attention is given to the availability and characteristics of Malaysian waste feedstocks, especially organic municipal solid waste, food waste and oil palm residues. The paper further evaluates the technical, economic, environmental, institutional and social considerations influencing WtE implementation, including energy recovery efficiency, greenhouse gas emissions, investment requirements, waste segregation, feedstock sustainability, public acceptance and regulatory support. International experiences are incorporated to identify relevant technological approaches and implementation strategies that may be adapted to Malaysian conditions. The review highlights the importance of integrating waste-to-energy development with circular economy principles, effective source separation, resource recovery and sustainable waste management policies. It also identifies key research gaps concerning technology selection, commercialisation, operational performance and long-term environmental sustainability. An integrated framework is proposed to connect waste resource availability, conversion technologies, energy recovery, economic feasibility, environmental performance and policy development. The paper concludes that WtE technologies offer significant opportunities to strengthen Malaysia's waste management system and diversify its renewable energy portfolio, provided that technology selection, institutional coordination and economic viability are addressed through an integrated national approach.

title: SAHRA ALTI AFRİKA ÜLKELERİNDE İKTİSADİ BÜYÜME, İSTİHDAM, SAĞLIK HARCAMALARI VE HAVA KİRLİLİĞİNİN YAŞAM SÜRESİ ÜZERİNDEKİ ETKİSİ
summary: Bu araştırmanın amacı, 43 Sahra Altı Afrika (SSA) ülkesinde iktisadi büyüme, istihdam, sağlık harcamaları ve hava kirliliğinin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisini panel veri yöntemiyle test etmektir. Araştırma 2000-2023 dönem
content: Bu araştırmanın amacı, 43 Sahra Altı Afrika (SSA) ülkesinde iktisadi büyüme, istihdam, sağlık harcamaları ve hava kirliliğinin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisini panel veri yöntemiyle test etmektir. Araştırma 2000-2023 dönemini kapsamaktadır. Araştırmada yapılan ön testler neticesinde analiz modelleri olarak panel otoregresif dağıtılmış gecikmeli (Panel ARDL) testiyle Dumitrescu & Hurlin panel nedensellik testi kullanılmıştır. Yapılan Panel ARDL analiz bulguları; iktisadi büyüme, istihdam ve sağlık harcamalarının doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkilerinin pozitif, hava kirliliğinin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisinin ise negatif olduğunu göstermektedir. Ayrıca kısa dönemli bulgulara göre iktisadi büyümenin doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi üzerindeki etkisi negatiftir. Panel nedensellik bulgularına bakıldığında, sağlık harcamaları ile hava kirliliğinden doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresine doğru tek yönlü nedensellik ilişkisine rastlanmıştır. İstihdam ile doğumdan beklenen yaşam süresi arasında ise çift yönlü nedensellik ilişkisine rastlanmıştır.

title: Reduced fertilization sustains ecosystem multifunctionality and economic benefit in a temperate agroforestry system
summary: Agroforestry as a sustainable agricultural intensification strategy aims to optimize resource use and enhance the provision of ecosystem services when compared to treeless open croplands. Here, we evaluated the effects of fertilization rate
content: Agroforestry as a sustainable agricultural intensification strategy aims to optimize resource use and enhance the provision of ecosystem services when compared to treeless open croplands. Here, we evaluated the effects of fertilization rates and land use management on ecosystem functions, based on 37 ecological indicators, measured over five years (2019–2023). Reduced fertilization did not significantly affect overall ecosystem multifunctionality in either agroforestry or open cropland, although some indicators differed. This lack of reduced fertilization effect likely reflects a legacy effect of chronic over-fertilization in this agroecosystem. Compared to open cropland, agroforestry enhanced carbon sequestration but was associated with reduced water filtration likely due to spatially unadjusted fertilization rates in shade-affected, low-yielding crops near the trees. Economic performance indicators were collectively comparable among fertilization and land use management systems. Our results suggest that optimized fertilization in agroforestry can sustain food production, while promoting resilient, resource-efficient agriculture.

title: Carbon Credit Marketplace with Multi-Modal Verification for Smallholder Agroforestry - Satellite NDVI, Ground-Photo AI and Soil Carbon
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Smallholder agroforestry plots rarely market, because the measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) step that backs each credit still rests on field visits that are too expensive to run on a one- or two-acre holding, in many respects; i
content: Smallholder agroforestry plots rarely market, because the measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) step that backs each credit still rests on field visits that are too expensive to run on a one- or two-acre holding, in many respects; indeed, the platform is a FastAPI backend, a React web app and an Expo mobile app, with 139 automated tests covering it, to a significant degree. A rule-based fraud engine, role-separated farmer, auditor and buyer portals. The check is fusing satellite vegetation data (NDVI computed from real Sentinel-2 imagery inside the boundary the farmer draws), a ground-photo classifier (MobileNetV3-Small, 98.4% accuracy on 1,420 held-out real photos) and a soil organic carbon (SOC) reading into one weighted score, 0.40 NDVI + 0.35 photo + 0.25 SOC. A score of 75 or above is permitted, 55 to 75 is routed to a human auditor; indeed, we built a working prototype of a carbon-credit marketplace in which a plot can mint credits only after it clears an automated, explainable three-part check. And anything under 55 is rejected; if any single piece of indication is missing the plot stays pending, and no value is ever invented, and an Ethereum-style ledger (Ganache) are logging each credit from issuance, through the transfer to retirement. In an end-to-end run on live data, a real areca plot in Shivamogga, Karnataka created an NDVI of 0.794 from a Sentinel-2 scene dated 27 September 2026, was authorized at 84.9/100, minted a 20 tCO2 credit; and thus, as, well, that credit was then bought and retired.

title: Genuinely Quantum Algorithms for Bio-inspired Meta-heuristic Optimization
summary: Quantum computation offers a promising pathway toward advancing meta-heuristic optimization, particularly in Nature-inspired paradigms such as genetic algorithms and swarm intelligence. This study conducts a systematic literature review of
content: Quantum computation offers a promising pathway toward advancing meta-heuristic optimization, particularly in Nature-inspired paradigms such as genetic algorithms and swarm intelligence. This study conducts a systematic literature review of fifteen major meta-heuristics to assess current efforts toward their quantum realization. Emphasis is placed on identifying genuinely quantum proposals (those that can be implemented on quantum hardware) as opposed to quantum-inspired analogues that remain classically simulable. The review highlights the present landscape, emerging algorithmic strategies, and open challenges that define the path toward truly quantum meta-heuristic optimization.

title: East-West Coordination and Economic Dispatch of Libya's Power System: Economic Value and Transmission Capacity Sensitivity
summary: Independent day-ahead scheduling in interconnected regions can meet the needs of each region, the system-level economic efficiency is low due to the failure to fully utilize the limited exchanges between regions in the scheduling sequence.
content: Independent day-ahead scheduling in interconnected regions can meet the needs of each region, the system-level economic efficiency is low due to the failure to fully utilize the limited exchanges between regions in the scheduling sequence. This paper constructs a 24-hour mixed-integer linear programming model for the Libyan power system to coordinate and optimize unit combination, start-up and shutdown decisions, economic dispatch, and the total east-west exchange variable. Controlled experiments were conducted under three frameworks with the same regional demand, initial state, unit constraints, time constraints, and calibrated cost coefficients: independent scheduling with zero exchange, coordinated scheduling with an exchange limit of 349.6 MW, and a virtually unconstrained mixed baseline. The study is evaluated based on data from 19 authorized operating days starting in 2025, consisting of 25 thermal power plant modules. The MATLAB optimization toolbox provides the main solution, while independent SciPy/ HiGHS reconstructions validate the objective function, completeness, regional balance, ramp-up capability, and minimum time residual. Throughout the sample, coordinated operation reduced the total target capacity from 97.759 million comparative cost units (CUs) to 97.094 million, achieving 86.17% of the combined economic value, reducing the average committed operating units from 9.80 to 9.11, and decreasing the total number of start-ups and shutdowns from 205 to 196. The coordinated operation plan transmitted 105.85 GWh of absolute power and 87.32 GWh of net power from east to west, with model-predicted load shedding at zero. On peak-value days, the target capacity decreased by 1.448%; on peak days of 8166 MW, the decrease was 0.157%. Transmission capacity sensitivity analysis revealed diminishing returns: high-value cases reached saturation near 750 MW, while peak cases achieved almost all available benefits at 500 MW. These results provide a quantitative screening method for prioritizing detailed national grid studies and developing coordinated operation policies.

title: Forecast‐Driven Freight Resilience
summary: Global freight markets are increasingly shaped by rapid, compound shocks. Economic cycles, capacity lags, fuel and carbon cost uncertainty, port congestion, and geopolitical disruptions interact to produce spot-rate volatility that directly
content: Global freight markets are increasingly shaped by rapid, compound shocks. Economic cycles, capacity lags, fuel and carbon cost uncertainty, port congestion, and geopolitical disruptions interact to produce spot-rate volatility that directly affects budgets, service levels, and commercial commitments. This chapter argues that resilience is strengthened when firms treat spot-rates as a real-time market signal and build disciplined, explainable forecasting capabilities that convert turbulence into earlier decisions, rather than later firefighting. The chapter first explains why ocean freight spot-rates serve as a sensitive barometer of supply–demand imbalance and why their swings often precede broader indicators. It then maps the main volatility drivers and illustrates the nonlinear feedback loops that amplify rate moves when shocks collide. Building on this foundation, it translates forecasting into practice. It outlines data requirements, compares four modeling “lenses” from classical time series to machine learning and expert overlays, and shows how to manage uncertainty through validation and probabilistic bands. A practitioner playbook links forecast bands to concrete levers, including hedging and contract strategy, adaptive routing and capacity planning, and S&OP-driven inventory synchronization. A case study on potential Strait of Hormuz closure demonstrates how scenario-based spot-rate forecasts support negotiation, rerouting, and stakeholder communication. The chapter closes with a pragmatic 12-month action plan for implementing forecast-driven resilience at the lane level.

title: MXene and TEGA Compared: Stability, Manufacturing and Scale
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: MXenes, two-dimensional transition-metal carbides first reported in 2011, are again promoted as materials for future batteries, supercapacitors, electromagnetic shielding and water treatment. Before any large-scale use, three practical ques
content: MXenes, two-dimensional transition-metal carbides first reported in 2011, are again promoted as materials for future batteries, supercapacitors, electromagnetic shielding and water treatment. Before any large-scale use, three practical questions decide their fate: how long the material keeps its properties, how it is made, and how much of it can be produced. This preprint compares MXene with TEGA (thermally expanded graphite Arbok), a graphene-like carbon material produced in-house by ARBOK. In water dispersions Ti3C2Tx MXene oxidizes to titanium dioxide, and its conductivity falls to about 7% of the original value in 27 days unless it is stored at −80°C. MXene is made by etching MAX-phase ceramics in hydrofluoric acid, in some protocols for 90-118 hours. TEGA is pure carbon, does not oxidize, withstands up to 1500°C, is made from oxidized natural graphite at 50-100 USD per tonne and is sold at about 50 USD/kg. One TEGA line produces 50-300 kg/h, or 400-2,000 t/yr, against a world graphene output of 3,500-4,000 t in 2023. ARBOK data for TEGA-based supercapacitor electrodes and electromagnetic absorbers are given: 180-250 F/g, 500,000 cycles, more than 60 dB shielding. A scenario estimate puts the saving at 1-2 bln USD a year if one third of the electromagnetic shielding and supercapacitor markets moved to TEGA. Keywords: MXene, TEGA, thermally expanded graphite, oxidation stability, supercapacitor, electromagnetic shielding, scalable production

title: The Missing Link: A View of Food in the Age of Obesity
summary: The most visible form of non-communicable disease is, of course, obesity. Sadly, however, there is also a wide range of autoimmune diseases and, increasingly, of mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions that, all-too-often, are not r
content: The most visible form of non-communicable disease is, of course, obesity. Sadly, however, there is also a wide range of autoimmune diseases and, increasingly, of mental health and neurodevelopmental conditions that, all-too-often, are not recognised by the sufferers themselves. Another characteristic feature of modern disease is onset in ever-younger individuals. Babies may suffer from eczema, children from autism, and cases of type 2 diabetes in primary school. Alongside this, cancer in under-50-year-olds is best explained by an immunodeficiency problem. The view taken in this article is that such a wide range of diseases points to something missing in the intestinal microbiome of vulnerable people and that, rather than exclusively bacterial in origin, this “missing link” is an intergenerational microeukaryote sentinel cell component of the immune system, possibly one that evolved earlier than the vertebrates themselves. In turn, this implies a “dual inheritance” that, alongside the genetic inheritance of a baby, such sentinel cells are transferred from the intestinal microbiome of the mother to the child at birth. Unlike in normal usage, in this article, the word “dysbiotic”, or its derivatives, refers to people having a malfunctioning microbiome from birth, while the corresponding term “eubiotic” refers to the opposite, a person or population who exhibit none of the symptoms of non-communicable disease. Accordingly, a state of eubiosis is best regarded as a theoretical concept in Westernised populations, potentially being restricted to people living outside of modern-dominated environments. In this “missing link” concept it is a failure of a communication network within the growing child, an “immune-gut-brain triangle”, rather than the organs themselves, that define the problem. Food, including probiotics, is at the centre of this “triangle”, having direct effects on the microbiome, the brain, and the immune system. In addition, we should be able to investigate these relationships more closely with the aid of interkingdom messenger-detecting ingestible sensors.

title: Nanofriction strengthened mechanically adaptive electrolytes for safe lithium metal batteries
summary: The expanding application of lithium metal batteries in emerging fields such as unmanned aerial vehicles and humanoid robots exposes them to heightened risks of mechanical abuse, which has become a critical factor contributing to safety fai
content: The expanding application of lithium metal batteries in emerging fields such as unmanned aerial vehicles and humanoid robots exposes them to heightened risks of mechanical abuse, which has become a critical factor contributing to safety failures. To address this predicament, we design a mechanically intelligent responsive multifunctional electrolyte using a “nano-friction-strengthening” strategy to dynamically reinforce its mechanical robustness. The high-polarity carbonate solvents spontaneously infiltrate the hydroxyl-rich poly(hydroxyethyl methacrylate-diethyl allyphosphonate) shell and induce a hydrogen-bond-driven, self-regulated swelling response that enables uniform nanoparticle dispersion. Under impact, the intimate interfacial contact between core-shell nanoparticles instantaneously activates a dense network of dynamic hydrogen bonds within the swollen shell, boosting interparticle friction and adhesion. This molecularly orchestrated nano-friction-strengthening effect endows the electrolyte with impact hardening, driving a 160-fold surge in viscosity and delivering highly effective mechanical protection. Consequently, the electrolyte attenuates impact forces by 73.1%, enabling single Li‖LiFePO 4 pouch cells to endure impact without short-circuiting. Beyond mechanical reinforcement, the phosphate-ester groups in nanoparticles suppress exothermic chain reactions, ensuring safe operation during nail-penetration and ballistic tests in ampere-hour-scale Li‖LiFePO 4 cells.

title: Buckled Silver Microflake Conductors With In Situ‐Generated Ag–O Coordination Enable 3D‐Printed Stretchable Cardiac Bioelectrodes
summary: Metallic pacemaker electrodes risk myocardial injury during implantation, while silver micro‐flakes (AgMFs), despite excellent conductivity, are too rigid for stretchable devices without proper composite/device engineering. Here, we present
content: Metallic pacemaker electrodes risk myocardial injury during implantation, while silver micro‐flakes (AgMFs), despite excellent conductivity, are too rigid for stretchable devices without proper composite/device engineering. Here, we present a synergistic strategy to fabricate fully stretchable, electrically stable, and crack‐resistant cardiac electrodes by integrating AgMF‐based ink with metal‐organic interfacial bonding, biaxial buckling, and wet‐adhesive hydrogels. In situ‐generated Ag–O coordination of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) in the polymer matrix/conductor dissipates stress and suppresses crack propagation, effectively compensating for AgMF rigidity and enabling intact buckled microstructures. The resulting electrodes exhibit high conductivity (∼2.1 × 10 4 S cm −1 ) and stable resistance under 50% cyclic strain, exceeding cardiac motion requirements (15%–20%). The ink is 3D‐printable into mesh electrodes and can be integrated with wet‐adhesive hydrogels to form puncture‐free, stretchable metallic cardiac bioelectrodes with excellent biosafety, offering a promising route toward leadless pacemakers and long‐term wireless cardiac monitoring. A multiscale synergistic strategy integrating metal‐organic interfacial bonding with stretch‐release‐induced buckled architectures enables silver microflake conductors with simultaneously high conductivity and large deformability, demonstrated for 3D printing of bioadaptive, puncture‐free cardiac electrodes and stretchable wireless coils for dynamic cardiac stimulation and long‐term electrophysiological monitoring.

title: Brief communication: Cryosphere ecosystem services and disservices are transforming glaciology into a multidisciplinary research nexus
summary: Glaciology is evolving from a physical science research discipline focused on the properties and processes of ice and snow into a multidisciplinary research nexus. The rapid transformation of the cryosphere is also shaping the ecosystem ser
content: Glaciology is evolving from a physical science research discipline focused on the properties and processes of ice and snow into a multidisciplinary research nexus. The rapid transformation of the cryosphere is also shaping the ecosystem services and disservices (ESD) it provides, connecting glacial processes to freshwater security, natural hazards, biodiversity, economics, and cultural values. Integrating ESD within glaciology provides a unifying conceptual language across the environmental sciences, ecology, social sciences, humanities, and governance. This shift is redefining glaciologists as cryospheric system scientists who combine biophysical data with socio-ecological impacts to address the challenges of climate and environmental change.

title: TransGreen Foundation CSA Dialogue Policy Brief - August 2026 Edition
summary: Can Regenerative Agriculture Feed Africa? is an 8-page policy brief from TransGreen Foundation. It is the second in the Foundation’s Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) Dialogue Series, built from the 20 August 2026 session. Dr. Godwin Atser of
content: Can Regenerative Agriculture Feed Africa? is an 8-page policy brief from TransGreen Foundation. It is the second in the Foundation’s Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) Dialogue Series, built from the 20 August 2026 session. Dr. Godwin Atser of Sasakawa Africa Association gave the keynote, and Dr. Olushola Obikanye of Sterling Bank and Dr. Lindiwe Hayo of South Africa’s Department of Trade, Industry and Competition joined a panel moderated by Jesse Gudah.The brief tests the claim that regenerative agriculture can feed a continent of more than 2.5 billion people by 2050. Its answer is qualified: regenerative practice has moved beyond pilots and is producing measurable gains, but it cannot feed Africa on its own and is not yet at the scale required.It rests on three findings:Finance. The main barrier is “transition risk”. Regenerative farming often brings a yield dip before soil recovers, and harvest-linked loans can push smallholders into default during that dip. The brief proposes patient, concessionary credit with grace periods aligned to biological transition and repayment tied to cash flow.Definitions. Sustainable, conservation, integrated and regenerative agriculture are different things. Blurring them in policy leads to mismatched funding, so Africa needs context-specific definitions.Evidence. Practices that go unrecorded cannot be financed. Measured yields and soil-carbon data are what turn a promising method into a bankable one.It also makes the case that regeneration works best as part of a full system: improved seeds, irrigation, aggregation and processing, extension, markets, and inclusion of women, youth and persons with disabilities.The brief includes three case studies: Sasakawa’s yield gains in Kano (rice above 200%), Sterling Bank’s ecosystem-finance model, and TransGreen Boost. It ends with six policy recommendations, a calls-to-action table by stakeholder group, and a conclusion built around the line “not yet, not at scale, but moving in that direction.”

title: Effects of Particle Size and Functional Group on Spent Engine Oil and Diesel Adsorption by Corncob– Groundnut Shell Nanobiocomposite: A Study for Potential Application in Bioremediation
summary: Spent engine oil and diesel are persistent hydrocarbon pollutants. In bioremediation, corncob and groundnut shell have each been applied as biosorbents/biostimulants, but how particle size and functional chemistry govern the performance of
content: Spent engine oil and diesel are persistent hydrocarbon pollutants. In bioremediation, corncob and groundnut shell have each been applied as biosorbents/biostimulants, but how particle size and functional chemistry govern the performance of their combined biocomposite towards spent engine oil and diesel bioremediation remains poorly understood. This study investigated the influence of particle size and functional chemistry of a 1:1 corncob–groundnut shell biocomposite on the adsorption of spent engine oil and diesel. Corncob and groundnut shell were processed into macro-, micro-, and nano-sizes through mechanical milling and characterized using FTIR, SEM–EDX, DLS, BET surface area analysis, and XRD. The DLS analysis showed a reduction in average particle size from 438.4 d.nm to 45.81 d.nm, while BET analysis reported a specific surface area of 252.67 m² g⁻¹, BJH analysis reported mesopore diameter of 2.115 nm for the nanobiocomposite. SEM images indicated reduced porosity and surface roughness with decreasing particle size, XRD analysis revealed progressive amorphization of the biocomposite following milling. Adsorption experiments demonstrated that pollutant removal efficiency increased significantly with decreasing particle size. By linking particle-size reduction to measurable gains in surface area and removal efficiency, this work provides a basis for designing bio-based adsorbents for petroleum hydrocarbon remediation.

title: Housing conditions, health-related quality of life, and social well-being in urban China
summary: Housing conditions are key determinants of health. However, within the context of rapid urbanization and the proliferation of high-rise residential buildings, how specific housing conditions such as floor level and dwelling size influence h
content: Housing conditions are key determinants of health. However, within the context of rapid urbanization and the proliferation of high-rise residential buildings, how specific housing conditions such as floor level and dwelling size influence health-related quality of life (HRQOL), social capital, and sense of community remains underexplored in urban China. This study therefore aimed to clarify these associations for both women and men. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in Guangzhou, China, from July to August 2025. Floor levels were classified as 1st–3rd, 4th–6th, 7th–9th, and 10th floor or above; dwelling sizes were categorized into 0–50 m2, 50–90 m2, and more than 90 m2. Multivariable linear regression models were applied to clarify the associations. Results from 3112 respondents revealed that, among women, compared with those living on the 10th floor or above, those living on the 4th–6th floors had higher physical HRQOL, while those living on the 1st–3rd and 4th–6th floors had better mental HRQOL. No significant association was found between floor level and HRQOL among men. Regarding dwelling size, men living in dwellings of 0–50 m2 and 50–90 m2 had poorer physical and mental HRQOL. Among women, living in dwellings of 0–50 m2 showed poorer mental HRQOL. In addition, living in a dwelling of 0–50 m2 was associated with lower bonding social capital only in women, lower bridging social capital in both women and men, and a weaker sense of community among both genders. These findings suggest that lower-to-mid floors, particularly the 4th–6th floors, may be associated with better mental HRQOL among women, whereas smaller dwelling sizes were more consistently associated with poorer HRQOL among men and weaker social well-being across both genders. Further research adopting longitudinal designs and broader objective measures is needed to clarify how housing conditions shape occupant health and social well-being across diverse urban and cultural settings.

title: Tectonics and Crustal Thinning Related to the Rise of the Mohorovicic Discontinuity in the Santos Basin and the Migration of Mantle CO2 to Pre-Salt Reservoirs Aristides Perez Frances
summary: The Post-stack seismic reprocessing workflow was applied including Relative Acoustic Impedance (RAI), a band-pass filter with a 3 Hz low-frequency cutoff, spectral whitening, and spectral balancing. That improved the signal-to-noise ratio,
content: The Post-stack seismic reprocessing workflow was applied including Relative Acoustic Impedance (RAI), a band-pass filter with a 3 Hz low-frequency cutoff, spectral whitening, and spectral balancing. That improved the signal-to-noise ratio, and enhanced the frequency content. The better seismic images enabled a more detailed interpretation of the crustal structure, particularly the crustal thinning associated with the uplift of the Mohorovičić Discontinuity (Moho). The improved imaging also allowed the identification of probable migration pathways for mantle-derived CO2 through deep and ultra-deep fault systems, particularly in the areas of the Tupi, Júpiter, Peroba, and Eastern Libra fields in the Santos Basin. These migration pathways provide a plausible explanation for the large variations in CO2 concentrations observed among neighboring pre-salt reservoirs, such as Tupi, Peroba, and Jupiter. The interpretation of the reprocessed regional seismic sections, with appropriate horizontal and vertical scaling, allowed a comprehensive assessment of crustal thinning from the Cretaceous hinge line to the Continent-Ocean Boundary (COB). The results indicate progressive Moho uplift toward the transition zone, accompanied by mantle exhumation. Furthermore, the high-resolution seismic images reveal a high density of deep-rooted flower structures related to transfer and strike-slip fault systems. These faults exhibit significant vertical displacement within the economic basement and at the base of the salt sequence, indicating intense tectonic deformation associated with crustal extension and Moho uplift. They also represent potential conduits for the upward migration of mantle-derived CO2.

title: Cue reactivity and product choice among young adult dual users of combustible and electronic cigarettes: Evidence from the lab and natural environment
summary: AIMS: The aim of this study was to characterize same-product and cross-product cue-reactivity for cigarettes and e-cigarettes and the impact of cueing on choice across laboratory and real-world settings among those who regularly use both ci
content: AIMS: The aim of this study was to characterize same-product and cross-product cue-reactivity for cigarettes and e-cigarettes and the impact of cueing on choice across laboratory and real-world settings among those who regularly use both cigarettes and e-cigarettes. DESIGN: Two-session laboratory experimental design followed by a 28-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA). SETTING: Rhode Island, USA. PARTICIPANTS: N = 70 young adults (age 21-34) who regularly use cigarettes and e-cigarettes. MEASUREMENT: In each laboratory session, we measured craving on a 0 to 100 scale for cigarettes and e-cigarettes prior to cueing, after a neutral cue and after a substance cue. Choice to use cigarettes vs. e-cigarettes was measured across 10 trials and indexed as: (#ENDS choices - #cigarette choices) / (total #ENDS+cigarette choices); scores thus ranged from -1 (cigarette only) to 1 [Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS) only]. In the EMA, we measured craving during random reports and self-initiated cue surveys using the same 0-100 scale. We also measured past-hour cue-exposure retrospectively when cigarette or e-cigarette use was reported. RESULTS: In the laboratory, cue exposure increased craving for the cued substance relative to the pre-cue craving level [cigarette urge: unstandardized coefficient (b)= 14.83, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) = 11.24-18.41; cigarette desire: b = 11.46, 95% CI = 7.76-15.17; e-cigarettes urge: b = 7.64, 95% CI = 3.65-11.63; e-cigarette desire: b = 6.84, 95% CI = 2.92-10.76]. E-cigarette cues statistically significantly increased cigarette desire relative to the pre-cue craving level (b = 3.81, 95% CI = 0.33-7.29) but not urge (b = 2.75, 95% CI =[-0.66 to 6.16). Cigarette cues did not statistically significantly alter e-cigarette craving relative to the pre-cue craving level (urge: b = 1.78, 95% CI = -1.12 to 4.69; desires: b = 0.33, 95% CI = -2.71 to 3.37). Cue exposure did not statistically significantly alter product choice (b = -0.05, 95% CI = -0.19 to 0.10) beyond stated preference (b = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.18-0.49). In the natural environment, cue exposure was associated with increased craving relative to the random report for the cued product (cigarettes: b = 9.57, 95% CI =[7.61-11.53; e-cigarettes: b = 8.70, 95% CI = 6.80-10.61) but decreased craving for the non-cued product (smoking cues: b = -4.54, 95% CI = -6.37 to -2.71; vaping cues: b = -2.12, 95% CI = -4.16 to -0.08). Past-hour smoking cue exposure was associated with increased odds of reporting smoking (reference group = vaping) [odds ratio (OR) = 8.11, 95% CI = 3.73-17.63) whereas past-hour vaping cue exposure was associated with decreased odds of reporting smoking (OR = 0.06, 95% CI = 0.02-0.17). SUMMARY: Same-product cue reactivity effects for cigarettes and e-cigarettes appear to converge across laboratory and naturalistic settings, but cross-product effects do not.

title: Hourly Clean Electricity Tracing and Masked Computation Support Enterprise Carbon Certification
summary: Annual and regional emission factors obscure hourly and nodal variation in clean electricity availability. We developed a consumer-side carbon accounting workflow that combines hydropower dispatch, proportional-sharing electricity tracing a
content: Annual and regional emission factors obscure hourly and nodal variation in clean electricity availability. We developed a consumer-side carbon accounting workflow that combines hydropower dispatch, proportional-sharing electricity tracing and masked certification. In a modified IEEE 39-bus system, nodal clean electricity fractions ranged from 2.95 percent to approximately 100 percent, while three constructed industrial consumers had period-total fractions of 1.96–23.70 percent. A fixed Gaussian mask was shared among trustees and removed before release; a smaller hourly perturbation remained. Across 100 Monte Carlo runs, the released estimates had a mean absolute error of 2.200 MW and a period-total absolute error of 36.08 MWh, compared with 9.272 MW and 240.78 MWh for the tested local-noise baseline. The hybrid scheme also had a 49.24 percent mean absolute percentage error and a 9.33 percent clipping rate. These results support finer spatial attribution and lower absolute error under the selected settings, but do not establish a formal differential-privacy guarantee.

title: A Balanced Amino Acid Supplementation Enhances Myogenic Differentiation, Energy Metabolism, and Antioxidant Capacity in C2C12 Cells
summary: Conventional nutritional strategies for supporting muscle health have largely focused on increasing the intake of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), particularly leucine. However, simply increasing the amount of BCAAs or total amino acids
content: Conventional nutritional strategies for supporting muscle health have largely focused on increasing the intake of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), particularly leucine. However, simply increasing the amount of BCAAs or total amino acids may not be sufficient to elicit optimal physiological effects. Given that individual amino acids exert distinct metabolic and physiological functions, functionally complementary combinations administered at appropriate concentrations may provide a more effective strategy for promoting muscle health. This study investigated whether a combination of leucine, cysteine, glycine, glutamine, and taurine could coordinately enhance myogenic differentiation, cellular energy metabolism, and antioxidant defense in C2C12 muscle cells. After determining appropriate treatment concentrations for each amino acid, C2C12 myoblasts were differentiated for 7 days in the presence of leucine alone or various amino acid combinations. Myotube morphology, the expression of genes associated with muscle anabolism, myogenic differentiation, catabolism, energy metabolism, and antioxidant defense, and intracellular ATP, glutathione (GSH), and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were evaluated. Leucine treatment enhanced myotube formation and increased Akt1 and Igf1 expression. However, combined amino acid treatments generally promoted greater myotube formation than leucine alone. Notably, the half-strength five-amino-acid formulation (1/2 LCGQT) produced the greatest increases in myotube length and thickness and markedly enhanced the expression of myogenic regulatory genes, including Myod1, Myf5, Myf6, and Mef2. Combined amino acid treatments also favorably regulated genes associated with mitochondrial function and energy metabolism, including Cycs, Ucp2, Ampk, and Pgc1a, and specific combinations increased intracellular ATP levels. In addition, the 1/2 LCGQT formulation elicited the highest Gpx1 expression and intracellular GSH concentration, while several combinations significantly reduced intracellular ROS levels. The expression of the muscle catabolism-related genes Mstn and Foxo3 was not significantly altered. Collectively, these findings indicate that combining amino acids according to their complementary physiological and metabolic functions may more effectively promote myogenic differentiation and support cellular energy and redox homeostasis than leucine supplementation alone. Moreover, the superior and more consistent effects of the half-strength formulation demonstrate that optimal amino acid composition and concentration are more important than simply increasing the total amount supplied. This study therefore provides a basis for a function-guided nutritional strategy that shifts from quantity-oriented BCAA supplementation toward the selective combination of physiologically relevant amino acids at appropriately optimized levels.

title: Vitamin B12 fortification in a strawberry and grape pomace matrix with Propionibacterium freudenreichii and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, sterile and non-sterile conditions
summary: The food processing industry generates significant amounts of by-products, such as fruit pomace, which, due to high moisture content and nutrient richness, is prone to spoilage. At the same time, the growing demand for plant-based foods hig
content: The food processing industry generates significant amounts of by-products, such as fruit pomace, which, due to high moisture content and nutrient richness, is prone to spoilage. At the same time, the growing demand for plant-based foods highlights the need for vitamin B12 fortification, as plants cannot synthesize this essential nutrient. This study evaluated the impact of propionic and lactic acid fermentation on the microbiological quality of a fruit pomace-based matrix (strawberry and grape pomace) while enabling vitamin B12 biofortification. Monocultures of Propionibacterium freudenreichii and co-cultures with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum were tested in sterile and non-sterile matrices under different pH conditions. The highest vitamin B12 production was achieved in sterile matrices with pH control, reaching 39.4 μg/kg fresh matrix in monoculture and 48.5 μg/kg in co-culture. In non-sterile cultures, pH regulation also enhanced vitamin B12 synthesis (39.5 and 36.8 μg/kg, respectively), but promoted the growth of Enterobacteriaceae and Bacillus cereus , limiting their application. The results indicate that sterile, pH-controlled fermentation is the most effective strategy for vitamin B12 biofortification of fruit pomace matrices while maintaining microbiological safety.

title: Exposure to Diesel Particulate Matter Aggravates Developmental Toxicity Induced by Cyclophosphamide in Rats
summary: Despite widespread human exposure to diesel particulate matter (DPM) and its recognized health risks, its impact on embryo-fetal development, particularly under conditions of concomitant exposure to developmental toxicants, remains insuffic
content: Despite widespread human exposure to diesel particulate matter (DPM) and its recognized health risks, its impact on embryo-fetal development, particularly under conditions of concomitant exposure to developmental toxicants, remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated whether DPM exacerbates cyclophosphamide (CP)-induced embryo-fetal developmental toxicity in rats and assessed maternal hepatic oxidative stress-related parameters, including malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and catalase (CAT) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activities. CP administration to pregnant rats induced evident maternal toxicity, as shown by increased abnormal clinical signs and decreases in maternal body weight and gravid uterine weight. CP also decreased hepatic CAT and SOD activities in dams, indicating altered maternal hepatic antioxidant status. In fetuses, CP exposure resulted in reduced fetal body weight and placental weight, increased morphological alterations, and delayed ossification. Notably, concomitant administration of DPM further aggravated several CP-induced fetal abnormalities and delayed ossification, although these responses were not uniformly dose dependent. In parallel, concomitant DPM exposure further decreased maternal hepatic CAT and SOD activities, and these alterations accompanied the aggravated developmental findings. Overall, these findings indicate that concomitant DPM exposure can aggravate selected manifestations of CP-induced embryo-fetal developmental toxicity in rats and that these effects are associated with alterations in maternal hepatic antioxidant status. These findings provide experimental evidence of enhanced developmental toxicity under combined DPM and CP exposure and underscore the importance of considering co-exposure scenarios in developmental toxicity assessment.

title: Front-Loaded Innovation, Slow-Moving Level: Climate Policy Uncertainty and the Term Structure of the Green–Brown Return Gap
summary: Climate policy uncertainty determines the cost of capital for the low-carbon transition, yet conventional models mis-measure its transmission to asset prices by entering a single uncertainty index without separating its slow-moving level fr
content: Climate policy uncertainty determines the cost of capital for the low-carbon transition, yet conventional models mis-measure its transmission to asset prices by entering a single uncertainty index without separating its slow-moving level from its transitory innovation. This paper introduces a text-augmented local-projection framework using a news-based China Climate Policy Uncertainty (CCPU) index and green–brown equity returns. We construct time-aligned panel data from the CCPU index and green–brown portfolio returns, decompose each into a standardized level and first difference, and estimate horizon-by-horizon local projections on one sample and controls; a design-based wild bootstrap replaces the conventional 1.96 with horizon-specific critical values. The innovation component is significant: a one-standard-deviation shock raises the green–brown gap by 2.67 points at impact (t = 2.61, clearing its design-earned threshold of 2.21) and contributes nothing thereafter, while the level component reaches − 16.9 points at h = 12, concentrated on the long-duration green leg (− 19.2 vs − 2.3 on brown) and implies 226 basis points of required return. The wild bootstrap establishes that the five-per-cent threshold is 2.21 for the innovation and 3.97 for the level, so the first is an estimate and the second a description; identifying the persistent and transitory innovation as the distinct drivers of the gap. The framework establishes that a single uncertainty index cannot recover both the impact repricing and the term-structure effect, and that the sign disagreement in the literature is a disagreement about the regressor rather than about markets or periods—so component decomposition is necessary to measure climate-policy risk correctly. JEL Classification C15 · C22 · C53 · G12 · Q54

title: Hydraulic performance and vibration response of a centrifugal pump with a 3D-printed impeller under controlled unbalance conditions
summary: Centrifugal pump performance and reliability can be strongly affected by rotor unbalance, while the increasing use of additive manufacturing raises additional questions related to the dynamic behavior of printed rotating components. This st
content: Centrifugal pump performance and reliability can be strongly affected by rotor unbalance, while the increasing use of additive manufacturing raises additional questions related to the dynamic behavior of printed rotating components. This study experimentally investigates the hydraulic performance and vibration response of a centrifugal pump equipped with a fused deposition modeling (FDM) impeller manufactured from polylactic acid (PLA) and subjected to controlled added-mass conditions. The hydraulic performance of the 3D-printed impeller was first compared with that of the original impeller through head–flow rate and vibration measurements, showing similar overall behavior, with an average difference of approximately 4\% between the head–flow rate curves. A controlled unbalance was then introduced by adding masses at a fixed radial position of up to 0.270 g, corresponding to an added unbalance magnitude approximately three times the calculated permissible residual unbalance reference, without removing the impeller from the shaft. Five 15-second vibration measurements were recorded for each condition in both radial and axial directions, and the corresponding power spectral densities (PSD) were analyzed. The vibration response was dominated by the 3X rotational component rather than the expected 1X component. Moreover, the 3X peak PSD amplitude initially decreased with added mass and subsequently increased, which may indicate partial compensation of an existing unbalance of the rotor assembly before additional mass increased the overall unbalance. The dominant 3X response may be associated with structural resonance or the dynamic characteristics of the partially infilled FDM impeller. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using additively manufactured impellers for controlled experimental studies of pump unbalance and vibration behavior.

title: Increased cover crop biomass and exposure time reduces spring emergence of the navel orangeworm in a Mediterranean almond system
summary: Almonds are an economically important specialty crop for the United States, which produces approximately 80% of the global almond crop. Most of this production comes from California, where almond growers have become more interested in incor
content: Almonds are an economically important specialty crop for the United States, which produces approximately 80% of the global almond crop. Most of this production comes from California, where almond growers have become more interested in incorporating winter cover crops to promote soil health and improve orchard sustainability. However, the benefits of winter cover crops could potentially extend to pest abatement as well. The main arthropod pest of almonds is the navel orangeworm, Amyelois transitella Walker, which directly attacks the developing new crop nuts, leading to reduced yield and quality. Crop sanitation is considered the foundation of A. transitella management, as the moths overwinter in remnant nuts and rely on them as a reproductive substrate in the spring. Natural mortality of overwintering A. transitella is known to occur, and there is evidence that this may be enhanced when infested remnant nuts reside within ground covers. However, the effects of functionally diverse ground covers on overwintering A. transitella have yet to be explored. In this study, remnant mummy nuts infested with A. transitella were placed for varied exposure durations into six different cover crop mixtures, along with an untreated, weedy control and a weed-free herbicide control over two winter seasons. Vegetative biomass, remnant mummy nut degradation, and spring emergence of overwintered A. transitella were monitored. Results suggest that plots with greater vegetative biomass, regardless of plant species identity, increased mummy nut degradation, which ultimately resulted in a reduction of A. transitella spring emergence from the nuts. For every gram of weight lost per mummy nut, A. transitella emergence was reduced by approximately 98 percent (95% CI: -6.54 to -1.46). Additionally, results show that A. transitella emergence decreased with longer mummy nut exposure time, with the mean A. transitella emergence per mummy nut reduced by more than half from nuts exposed for 127 days compared to 30 days. While the exact mechanisms by which vegetative biomass degrades mummy nuts and interferes with the A. transitella life cycle remain unclear, this study demonstrates the potential of winter-long ground covers as a novel cultural control tool to reduce the emergence of overwintering A. transitella populations in California almonds.

title: Satellite attribution of trace gases to gas flares in the Niger Delta, Nigeria, 2012–2024: a transport-corrected framework with null tests
summary: Gas flaring in Nigeria's Niger Delta wastes gas and degrades air quality, yet satellite estimates of its emissions are rarely tested for bias. This study combines VIIRS Nightfire flare detections, Sentinel-5P TROPOMI CO, SO₂ and CH₄, and ER
content: Gas flaring in Nigeria's Niger Delta wastes gas and degrades air quality, yet satellite estimates of its emissions are rarely tested for bias. This study combines VIIRS Nightfire flare detections, Sentinel-5P TROPOMI CO, SO₂ and CH₄, and ERA5 winds at the satellite overpass hour in a transport-corrected multi-sensor attribution framework (TCMSAF) with built-in null tests: flare-free placebo points, crosswind controls and fixed compass sectors that cancel static geography. Flared gas in the nine Niger Delta states fell 32% from 2012 to 2024 (9.69 to 6.58 BCM; Theil–Sen − 0.29 BCM/yr, p < 0.001), steepest offshore (− 46% against − 20% onshore), while active onshore flares increased from 103 to 133. Satellite-observed volumes agreed with operator reports to within 6% over 2021–2024 but ran 13–20% higher in 2023–2024 as new onshore flares appeared, a gap worth about US$79 million in flare penalties in 2024. With fixed sectors and placebo adjustment, onshore flare sites carried a CO excess of 78 µmol/m² (95% CI 14 to 142) that was largest within 2 km of flares and decreased with distance, the opposite of what a background gradient produces; it was strongest in the Harmattan season and on light-wind days. Bias-corrected XCH₄ over the flaring zone exceeded a latitude-adjusted background by 5.3 ppb (95% CI 2.4 to 8.1). The null tests also showed that the conventional wind-rotated contrast (241 µmol/m²) overstated the flare CO signal about threefold, because placebo points (− 151 µmol/m²) and crosswind sectors (+ 120 µmol/m²) revealed regional structure of the same size. Flare-attributable SO₂ and offshore CO were below detection at TROPOMI resolution. The framework runs on public data in Google Earth Engine and gives regulators an independent, reproducible check on reported flaring and its air-quality footprint.

title: Energy-Level-Matched Electrocatalysis on Au–Nb 2 O 5 /Histidine-Aspartic Acid-Functionalized B,P-Codoped Graphene Quantum Dots for Selective Bisphenol A Detection in infant care products
summary: Noble-metal sensing materials are limited by poor selectivity and restricted detection limits in complex-matrix trace analysis, because their zero bandgap enables nonselective electron transfer and precludes energy filtering. To overcome th
content: Noble-metal sensing materials are limited by poor selectivity and restricted detection limits in complex-matrix trace analysis, because their zero bandgap enables nonselective electron transfer and precludes energy filtering. To overcome this, an Au–Nb 2 O 5 composite decorated with histidine/aspartic acid-functionalized B,P-co-doped graphene quantum dots (HDBP-GQDs) was designed. HDBP-GQD served as chelating agents and interfacial modifiers, sequentially coordinating Nb(V) and Au(III); two-step annealing at 400 and 900°C then yielded Au–Nb 2 O 5 /HDBP-GQD composite. Lattice-confined Au atoms formed atomic-scale electron-coupling centers, reducing charge-transfer resistance by > 26.7-fold and increasing electroactive surface area by > 9.7-fold. Catalytic activity increased by > 1.9-fold relative to pristine Nb 2 O 5 . HDBP-GQD also enabled multi-heteroatom interfacial band engineering, tuning the band gap and interfacial energy levels to match oxidation potential of bisphenol A. This alignment established a selective electron-transfer pathway, in which energy-level gating favored bisphenol A electrooxidation and suppressed coexisting interferents, enhancing catalytic specificity. Among twenty small organic molecules, only bisphenol A elicited a sensitive electrochemical response, confirming excellent selectivity. The sensor exhibited a linear range for bisphenol A of 0.01–150 µM and a detection limit of 0.0031 µM, with reliable performance in infant care products. Beyond bisphenol A sensing, this electronic-state engineering strategy provides a general route to convert zero-bandgap materials into energy-selective electrocatalysts, with broad implications for trace analysis in complex matrices and beyond.

title: State of orchid conservation in Malaysia
summary: Malaysia is one of the world's most important centres of orchid diversity, supporting an estimated 2,300 species across a wide range of ecosystems, from lowland rainforests to montane cloud forests. This chapter reviews the current state of
content: Malaysia is one of the world's most important centres of orchid diversity, supporting an estimated 2,300 species across a wide range of ecosystems, from lowland rainforests to montane cloud forests. This chapter reviews the current state of orchid conservation in Malaysia, highlighting the ecological, economic, and cultural significance of orchids as a national heritage resource. It examines patterns of diversity and biogeography, ecological functions, industry potential, and the major threats posed by habitat loss, illegal collection, international trade, and climate change. Case studies from the mossy forest of Cameron Highlands and the ultramafic landscapes of Gunung Kinabalu illustrate the conservation importance of high-value orchid habitats. The chapter evaluates existing in situ and ex situ conservation initiatives, including orchid rescue programmes, citizen science, DNA barcoding, and sustainable propagation efforts. It further outlines national conservation strategies, governance frameworks, research priorities, and capacity-building needs. Ultimately, orchids are presented as flagship species for biodiversity stewardship, requiring coordinated national action to ensure their long-term survival.

title: Balancing Seabed Resource Development and Conservation of the Marine Environment—Is a Pause Necessary?
summary: Balancing the development of seabed mineral resources with environmental conservation has become a defining challenge for ocean governance. Deep-sea minerals (polymetallic nodules, polymetallic sulphides and ferromanganese crusts) hold the
content: Balancing the development of seabed mineral resources with environmental conservation has become a defining challenge for ocean governance. Deep-sea minerals (polymetallic nodules, polymetallic sulphides and ferromanganese crusts) hold the potential to provide critical raw materials needed for industrial growth and the global energy transition. At the same time, concerns over ecological impacts have prompted calls for caution, including proposals for a moratorium or pause on exploitation. This chapter examines the competing imperatives of resource demand and environmental conservation while outlining the scale and significance of seabed resources, reviewing current knowledge on potential environmental impacts and conservation measures, while considering the economic and social dimensions of deep-sea mining. Against this background, it assesses if the case for a pause is compelling, or whether carefully regulated development could provide a viable path forward. The chapter argues that the decision ultimately will depend on finding an acceptable balance between meeting future critical mineral needs required by the shift towards a low-global carbon economy and ensuring that all measures and mechanisms exist to protect the marine environment potentially at risk for the benefit of present and future generations.

title: Competitive advantage in biodiesel production: conversion of glycerol and phospholipid-rich gum into value-added streams
summary: The rapid expansion of biodiesel production has reinforced its relevance in low-carbon energy transitions while exposing a critical structural limitation associated with high production costs and narrow profit margins. Under these condition
content: The rapid expansion of biodiesel production has reinforced its relevance in low-carbon energy transitions while exposing a critical structural limitation associated with high production costs and narrow profit margins. Under these conditions, the effective utilization of by-products such as crude glycerol, phospholipid-rich gum, and soapstock emerges as a key factor influencing the overall performance and viability of biodiesel systems. This review repositions biodiesel by-products from residual liabilities to strategic resources by examining their conversion into value-added products, including biofertilizers and biogas, with particular emphasis on phosphorus recovery from degumming gum and carbon recovery from crude glycerol. These pathways offer opportunities to enhance resource efficiency and support integrated biorefinery configurations, although they also face key limitations related to process instability, feedstock variability, pretreatment requirements, and regulatory constraints that impact scalability and environmental performance. Overall, by-product valorization can play a central role in improving both the sustainability and the economic performance of biodiesel systems, supporting the transition toward more integrated and resilient biorefinery configurations.

title: EOM-fpCCSD: an accurate alternative to EOM-CCSD for doubly excited and charge-transfer states
summary: We introduce a new equation-of-motion coupled-cluster method based on a pair coupled-cluster doubles (pCCD) reference, termed frozen-pair EOM-CCSD (EOM-fpCCSD). This approach combines the computational efficiency of the pCCD ansatz with a d
content: We introduce a new equation-of-motion coupled-cluster method based on a pair coupled-cluster doubles (pCCD) reference, termed frozen-pair EOM-CCSD (EOM-fpCCSD). This approach combines the computational efficiency of the pCCD ansatz with a dynamical correlation correction, enabling a reliable description of electronically excited states within the EOM framework. The method has been implemented in the open-source PyBEST software package. Its performance is systematically benchmarked against standard EOM-CCSD and its pair-tailored variant (EOM-ptCCSD), using both canonical Hartree-Fock and pCCD natural orbitals. For charge-transfer (CT) excitations taken from the QUEST database, EOM-fpCCSD yields excitation energies very close to those of EOM-CCSD, outperforming EOM-ptCCSD, as well as to the theoretical best estimates (TBEs). Working within the localized pCCD natural orbital basis allows us to determine the directed CT character, which quantifies the directed charge flow from one molecular domain to another. Numerical results show that EOM-fpCCSD, EOM-CCSD, and EOM-ptCCSD provide nearly identical descriptions of the directed CT character, despite changes in excitation energies. The true advantage of EOM-fpCCSD becomes evident for the challenging QUEST subset of doubly excited states. While EOM-ptCCSD performs similarly to standard EOM-CCSD, EOM-fpCCSD significantly outperforms both methods for these problematic states compared to TBEs. In addition to improving the accuracy of excitation energies, EOM-fpCCSD also converges for several states that standard EOM-CCSD and EOM-ptCCSD fail to converge. These results demonstrate that EOM-fpCCSD offers a promising and computationally efficient route toward a more accurate description of complex electronic excitations.

title: The Effect of Pipe Inclination on the Thermal and Aerodynamic Characteristics of Finned Bundles in Air Cooling Devices
summary: This article presents the results of an experimental and numerical study of the effect of pipe inclination on thermal and aerodynamic characteristics of finned bundles of air cooling devices (ACD). Two four-row staggered beams are compared:
content: This article presents the results of an experimental and numerical study of the effect of pipe inclination on thermal and aerodynamic characteristics of finned bundles of air cooling devices (ACD). Two four-row staggered beams are compared: a horizontal one (Bundle I) and a beam with a slope of 6° for 2-4 rows with an increased longitudinal pitch (Bundle II). It has been experimentally established that the beam tilt makes it possible to reduce its aerodynamic drag by 14% without significant deterioration in heat transfer, which is explained by a change in the flow structure and turbulence from the first horizontal row. Criterion equations for calculating heat transfer and hydraulic resistance of the studied beams were obtained. Additionally, numerical modeling in ANSYS Fluent has shown that magnetic-abrasive treatment of contact surfaces and fins, simulated by increasing heat transfer coefficients, leads to a decrease in the operating temperature of the structure by 5-7°C, which indicates an increase in the efficiency of heat removal. We concluded that it is promising to use inclined layouts and surface quality improvement technologies to modernize ACD.

title: Investigating halogen-bond-mediated through-space activation of CO 2 for electrocatalytic reduction by iron porphyrins
summary: -to-CO electroreduction. Cyclic voltammetry and DFT calculations, combined with a detailed mechanistic analysis, enabled deconvolution of through-bond and through-space effects in these novel XB-capable iron porphyrins and it was found that
content: -to-CO electroreduction. Cyclic voltammetry and DFT calculations, combined with a detailed mechanistic analysis, enabled deconvolution of through-bond and through-space effects in these novel XB-capable iron porphyrins and it was found that σ-hole modulation mitigates unfavourable through-space repulsion at the reduced Fe(0) state.

title: Early-Time Filtrate Invasion Modeling During Primary Drilling-In of Terrigenous Oil Reservoirs
summary: Accurate interpretation of geological and technological data acquired during drilling largely depends on understanding the interaction between drilling fluid and the productive formation at the initial stage of reservoir penetration. One of
content: Accurate interpretation of geological and technological data acquired during drilling largely depends on understanding the interaction between drilling fluid and the productive formation at the initial stage of reservoir penetration. One of the least investigated phenomena affecting the reliability of well logging and gas logging interpretation is ahead-of-bit filtration, in which drilling fluid filtrate invades the formation before its physical exposure by the drill bit. This study aims to develop the scientific basis for a methodology to calculate the parameters of the formation fluid displacement front caused by ahead-of-bit filtration during the primary penetration of terrigenous oil-bearing reservoirs. The proposed methodology combines an analytical description of drilling fluid spurt loss with a two-phase flow model to predict filtrate invasion under downhole conditions. An algorithm was developed to calculate the principal parameters governing the displacement process along the wellbore axis, including filtrate invasion volume, filtrate saturation, penetration depth, and the position of the formation fluid displacement front. The analytical formulation enables laboratory and bench-scale filtration data to be extrapolated to actual drilling conditions, thereby improving the prediction of filtrate invasion during reservoir penetration. The developed approach provides a quantitative framework for evaluating the influence of ahead-of-bit filtration on reservoir fluid saturation and the interpretation of gas logging measurements obtained from drilled cuttings. Application of the proposed methodology demonstrated that the presence of drilling fluid filtrate leads to an underestimation of the native fluid saturation, with the filtrate fraction reaching 4.35% in the investigated case. The proposed methodology offers an effective tool for improving the interpretation accuracy of geological and technological drilling data and supports more reliable characterization of productive formations during the primary penetration stage.

title: Estimating net fixed nitrogen loss in the Baltic Sea from deep-water excess N2 accumulation
summary: We quantified excess N2 accumulation below the halocline of the Baltic Proper using in situ N2/Ar measurements combined with N2/Ar estimates derived from the three-dimensional ERGOM–MOM biogeochemical model. The observed temporal increase i
content: We quantified excess N2 accumulation below the halocline of the Baltic Proper using in situ N2/Ar measurements combined with N2/Ar estimates derived from the three-dimensional ERGOM–MOM biogeochemical model. The observed temporal increase in excess N2 was subsequently converted to nitrogen loss. The analysis focused on the post-2014 Major Baltic Inflow period, when deep-water ventilation effects had largely subsided and stratification with progressive oxygen depletion was re-established. Both observations and model simulations showed increasing excess N2 below the halocline, particularly in the Eastern Gotland Basin (EGB). Observation-based estimates of nitrogen loss amounted to approximately 80.8 ± 22.7 kt N yr−1 in the EGB, ∼15.6 ± 7.8 kt N yr−1 in the Bornholm Basin (BB), and ∼9.3 ± 4.1 kt N yr−1 in the Gdańsk Basin (GB). Model-derived estimates were consistently lower, but basin-specific comparisons revealed no significant differences between observational and temporally matched model-derived excess N2 accumulation trends. The obtained values of net fixed nitrogen loss fall within the lower range of published Baltic Sea estimates, likely because the N2/Ar approach reflects integrated net accumulation of dissolved N2 rather than gross instantaneous denitrification rates. These results demonstrate that deep-water excess N2 accumulation provides an integrative basis for estimating first-order net fixed nitrogen loss in stratified marine systems such as the Baltic Sea.

title: Drivers of ΔN2 variability in the Baltic Sea: Insights from observations and ERGOM-MOM modeling
summary: Excess dinitrogen (ΔN2) is the net accumulation of N2 produced by nitrate-reducing processes in the water column and sediments of oxygen-deficient marine systems. Therefore, biological production and physical processes shape its spatial dis
content: Excess dinitrogen (ΔN2) is the net accumulation of N2 produced by nitrate-reducing processes in the water column and sediments of oxygen-deficient marine systems. Therefore, biological production and physical processes shape its spatial distribution. This study investigates ΔN2 distribution below the halocline in the Baltic Sea using a coupled biogeochemical model evaluated against observations from the Bornholm, Gdańsk, and Gotland Deeps during 2020–2021. Vertical distributions of temperature, salinity, oxygen (O2), nutrients, N2/Ar ratios, and ΔN2 were compared to assess model performance and identify controls on N2 production. A persistent spatial gradient in ΔN2 was observed, with highest concentrations in the Gotland Basin, intermediate levels in the Gdańsk Basin, and lowest values in the Bornholm Basin. These differences correspond to variations in stratification, ventilation, and organic matter (OM) accumulation.
