Seasonal variability was strongest in the Gdańsk Basin, where elevated winter ΔN2 suggests enhanced nitrogen-loss processes supported by OM export and mixing-driven nutrient redistribution. In contrast, the Gotland Basin exhibited relatively stable, persistently reducing conditions, while the Bornholm Basin showed strong interannual variability related to episodic North Sea inflows. The weak relationship between ΔN2 and modeled denitrification rates (ranging from �0.0010 to 0.0200 𝜇mol kg−1 day−1) indicates that ΔN2 should not be interpreted as a direct proxy for pelagic denitrification. Rather, it reflects the cumulative effects of both pelagic and benthic denitrification, together with physical transport processes. By comparison, denitrification rates were more strongly associated with particulate organic carbon (POC) availability. The reported ΔN2 patterns are representative of the investigated post-inflow period rather than a long-term Baltic Sea baseline.

title: An eco-friendly alternative solution to avoid environmental pollution and health damage from wastewater associated with traditional plastics
source: Journal of Natural and Agricultural Sciences
summary: Each year, more than 330 million tons of plastic are produced worldwide. The main consumers are the packaging industry [40%], construction [20%], and automotive [8%]. This generates large quantities of waste, of which less than 10% can be r
content: Each year, more than 330 million tons of plastic are produced worldwide. The main consumers are the packaging industry [40%], construction [20%], and automotive [8%]. This generates large quantities of waste, of which less than 10% can be recycled, while the majority is dumped directly into the environment, causing environmental damage. Bioplastics are a sustainable option, produced from renewable resources such as starch, cellulose, and polylactic acid [PLA]. Water hyacinth [Eichhornia crassipes] is an alternative for reducing conventional plastics. The results of this research showed a 4.41% yield in cellulose extraction from the initial biomass, with samples A2 and A4 standing out for their smooth surface, flexibility, and tear resistance, with average thicknesses between 0.339 and 0.421 mm.

title: Prevalence, familial clustering, and influencing factors of Helicobacter pylori infection in Western Fujian Province households
summary: BACKGROUND The epidemiological status of family-based Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ) infection in Western Fujian Province is unclear. H. pylori infection is a major global public health concern and is closely associated with various gastr
content: BACKGROUND The epidemiological status of family-based Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ) infection in Western Fujian Province is unclear. H. pylori infection is a major global public health concern and is closely associated with various gastrointestinal and systemic diseases. Familial clustering has been increasingly recognized as an important transmission pattern; however, region-specific data are limited. To our knowledge, this study represents the first family-based epidemiological investigation of H. pylori infections in Western Fujian Province (Minxi). We hypothesized that H. pylori infection exhibits significant familial clustering and is associated with modifiable lifestyle factors in this region. AIM To investigate H. pylori prevalence, familial clustering, and infection-associated factors in Western Fujian Province to inform prevention and control strategies. METHODS This observational study used stratified sampling to recruit households from seven districts and counties in the Minxi region between January and December 2025. Overall, 415 households (1427 individuals) were included. Standardized questionnaires were used to collect basic demographic characteristics and dietary and hygiene-related information. All participants underwent the 13C-urea breath test to determine H. pylori infection status. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted to identify factors associated with H. pylori infection, and a binomial goodness-of-fit test assessed familial clustering. RESULTS The overall and household H. pylori infection rates were 34.0% and 56.6%, respectively. Not using communal chopsticks and spoons [odds ratio (OR) = 2.669, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.209-5.895, P < 0.05] and infrequent dishware disinfection (OR = 6.919, 95%CI: 3.897-12.283, P < 0.05) were independently associated with H. pylori infection at the household level. Among adults, insufficient awareness of H. pylori , beer consumption, and frequent spicy-food intake were independently associated with H. pylori infection. No family history of H. pylori infection; low-salt diet; frequent garlic consumption; limited intake of strong tea, coffee, and milk tea; and, adequate sleep were associated with lower infection prevalence. In minors, frequent object biting and dental caries were independently associated with H. pylori infection. No family history of H. pylori infection, independent use of tableware, low consumption of smoked and fried foods, and low-salt diet were associated with lower infection prevalence. H. pylori infection exhibited significant familial clustering (χ 2 = 134.751, P < 0.05). CONCLUSION H. pylori infection in Western Fujian Province exhibits high prevalence and familial clustering and is associated with multiple lifestyle factors. Given the cross-sectional design of this study, causal inferences cannot be drawn; nonetheless, these findings support the need for targeted, family-based prevention and control strategies and warrant further investigatio

title: Ya-Han-Lu-Duan decoction reshapes tumor microenvironment to treat colitis-associated colorectal cancer by regulating arachidonic acid metabolism
summary: BACKGROUND Ya-Han-Lu-Duan (YHLD) decoction is a classical Dai ethnic prescription widely used to treat intestinal inflammatory diseases. However, its ability to prevent colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC), the molecular mechanisms re
content: BACKGROUND Ya-Han-Lu-Duan (YHLD) decoction is a classical Dai ethnic prescription widely used to treat intestinal inflammatory diseases. However, its ability to prevent colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC), the molecular mechanisms responsible, and the active constituents of the formulation remain unknown. AIM To elucidate YHLD’s therapeutic mechanisms against CAC, focusing on tumor microenvironment (TME). METHODS We evaluated YHLD in a mouse model of CAC induced by azoxymethane and dextran sulfate sodium. To elucidate mechanisms, we applied transcriptomic and untargeted metabolomic analyses to colon tissues from treated and control animals. Key pathways identified by these omics approaches were validated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, western blot, and immunofluorescence. We characterized YHLD’s chemical constituents using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS, then performed molecular docking to model interactions between major components and enzymes in arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism, providing a preliminary screen for potential molecular targets. RESULTS YHLD significantly attenuated body weight loss and colon shortening in CAC mice, alleviated colonic histopathological injury, and reduced tumor formation. Transcriptomic analysis showed that genes differentially expressed after YHLD treatment were enriched in TME-related pathways, including Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction and extracellular matrix-receptor interaction. YHLD decreased the expression of pro-inflammatory and pro-tumor growth factors and reduced markers of cancer-associated fibroblasts and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. Untargeted metabolomic analysis further identified AA metabolism as a pathway co-enriched in both transcriptomic and metabolomic datasets. Consistently, YHLD suppressed the expression of key AA metabolism enzymes, PTGS2 and ALOX12. In addition, major components of YHLD, including Pentahydroxybufostane, Clematoside B, Psammosilenin A and Dulcoside A, showed high binding affinity to PTGS2 and ALOX12, respectively, suggesting that YHLD may coordinately regulate AA metabolism through multiple active components. CONCLUSION This study provides the first evidence that YHLD exerts a significant protective effect against CAC. The underlying mechanism likely involves inhibition of ALOX12-mediated and PTGS2-mediated AA metabolism, suppression of cancer-associated fibroblast activation and myeloid-derived suppressor cells infiltration, and remodeling of the immunosuppressive TME, thereby alleviating CAC progression. These findings offer experimental and mechanistic support for the development of YHLD as a preventive agent for CAC.

title: Atıklardan Membran Teknolojileri ile Nadir Toprak Elementlerinin Geri Kazanımı
summary: "Rare Earth Elements (REEs) are essential building blocks of modern high-technology products, defense industry components and green energy transition, yet they are classified as critical minerals with extremely high supply risks due to the
content: "Rare Earth Elements (REEs) are essential building blocks of modern high-technology products, defense industry components and green energy transition, yet they are classified as critical minerals with extremely high supply risks due to the geographical concentration of primary deposits in limited regions on a global scale and the severe environmental costs of traditional mining. This book chapter focuses on membrane technologies as an innovative, eco-friendly, and efficient approach for recovering REEs from secondary sources such as e-waste, mine tailings, coal fly ash, and industrial wastewater instead of primary ores. Within the framework of circular economy principles, transforming wastes from pollutants into strategic raw materials using the “waste-towealth” philosophy is a strategic necessity for global raw material supply security, resource safety, and ecological sustainability. Within the scope of this study, pre-concentration and the enrichment of dilute streams by nanofiltration (NF), high-efficiency separation by reverse osmosis (RO) for high-efficiency separation, forward osmosis (FO) for low-energy enrichment, and membrane distillation (MD) for managing high-salinity streams. Additionally, the highly selective separation of target ions from complex matrices using liquid membranes (emulsion liquid membrane, supported liquid membrane)—which combine traditional solvent extraction with membrane principles— and the use of electro-membrane methods like electrodialysis (ED) and diffusion dialysis (DD) for acid recovery, purification, and ion separation processes are analyzed in depth. Comprehensive evaluations indicate that membrane-based hybrid systems offer lower chemical consumption, a reduced carbon footprint, and superior selectivity compared to traditional methods, directly aligning with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In conclusion, this chapter provides a holistic perspective on the technical and economic potential of membrane technologies, their technical challenges, and their critical role in the REE recovery chain during the transition from laboratory-scale research to industrial applications."

title: Progression of Mineral Transformer Oils, Including Nanotechnology and Property Evaluation Techniques
summary: Mineral transformer oil has long been the industry standard for insulating and cooling power transformers due to its favorable dielectric strength, thermal conductivity, and cost-effectiveness. This paper provides a structured review compri
content: Mineral transformer oil has long been the industry standard for insulating and cooling power transformers due to its favorable dielectric strength, thermal conductivity, and cost-effectiveness. This paper provides a structured review comprising four main elements: (i) the historical evolution of mineral transformer oils, (ii) standard testing methods for evaluating their dielectric (AC, and Impulse breakdown voltages), thermal, and physicochemical properties, (iii) advancements achieved through the incorporation of nanoparticles such as Al₂O₃, TiO₂, SiO2, Fe3O4@SiO2 Core / Shell, AlN, CQD, MWCNT, Zinc Ferrite, Fe₃O₄, etc.., (iv) a comparative analysis of nanofluids in terms of breakdown voltage, thermal conductivity, and long-term performance. The review highlights that nanofluid formulations offer significant improvements in key operational parameters; however, challenges remain, including nanoparticle sedimentation, optimization of particle concentration, viscosity management, and the risk of accelerated oil degradation. This manuscript concludes by outlining essential steps for future research to establish reliable, standardized, and durable nanofluid-based transformer oils.

title: Advances in materials for fog harvesting: A comprehensive review of conventional, bioinspired, and advanced functional materials
summary: Water scarcity is affecting many nations worldwide, and countries including Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and India are among those affected. Fog harvesting has emerged as a promising passive approach for atmospheric water collection, particularly
content: Water scarcity is affecting many nations worldwide, and countries including Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and India are among those affected. Fog harvesting has emerged as a promising passive approach for atmospheric water collection, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions where conventional freshwater resources are limited. The performance of fog-harvesting systems is strongly governed by the material, surface and structural characteristics of the collector, which determine fog-droplet interception, adhesion, coalescence, transport, and drainage. Over the past two decades, research has progressed from conventional mesh collectors toward engineered materials and bioinspired surfaces designed to overcome the limitations of conventional systems. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of materials used for fog harvesting, covering developments from 2006 to 2026. Conventional metallic and polymeric meshes, including stainless steel, aluminum, copper, polyethylene, polypropylene, and nylon, are first reviewed in terms of their material properties, wettability, durability, cost, and water-collection performance. The review then examines advanced material strategies, including surface coatings, hydrophilic–hydrophobic patterns, superhydrophobic and superhydrophilic surfaces, electrospun nanofibers, and micro/nanostructured surfaces. Particular attention is given to bioinspired materials and architectures derived from cactus spines, spider silk, Namib desert beetles, and pitcher plants, as well as emerging fractal and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures. The comparative analysis demonstrates that material performance cannot be evaluated solely on fog-droplet capture; efficient water harvesting requires a balance between capture, droplet mobility, coalescence, shedding, drainage, mechanical stability, environmental durability, and manufacturability. The review identifies the transition from passive interception-based meshes toward multifunctional, surface-engineered, and bioinspired materials as a major technological development in fog harvesting.

title: Comprehensive ecological and microbiological assessment of water quality in selected rivers of Azerbaijan
summary: Assessment of the ecological status of river waters is of great importance for the protection of water resources, their efficient management, and the identification of anthropogenic impacts. The aim of this study was to assess the water qua
content: Assessment of the ecological status of river waters is of great importance for the protection of water resources, their efficient management, and the identification of anthropogenic impacts. The aim of this study was to assess the water quality of selected rivers belonging to the Kura and Araz River basins based on physicochemical and microbiological parameters, as well as to determine the relationships among these parameters using statistical methods. Within the framework of the study, water samples collected from the Lower Kura, Ganjachay, Kurakchay, Tartarchay, Araz River, Hakarichay, Bargushadchay, and Okhchuchay were analyzed for temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, concentrations of ammonium, nitrite, nitrate, and phosphate ions, total microbiota, saprotrophic bacteria, bacteria involved in the nitrogen cycle, as well as the quantitative abundance of oil- and phenol-oxidizing microorganisms using standard physicochemical and microbiological methods. Pearson correlation analysis, principal component analysis (PCA), and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) were applied to evaluate the relationships among the parameters. The obtained results demonstrated that the physicochemical and microbiological parameters of the studied rivers varied both seasonally and among rivers. Higher levels of nutrients and microbiological parameters were observed in the Ganjachay, Araz River, Lower Kura, and Okhchuchay, whereas the Hakarichay, Kurakchay, and Tartarchay were characterized by relatively favorable ecological conditions. A strong positive correlation was identified between total microbiota and saprotrophic bacteria (r = 0.709; p < 0.001). PCA and HCA revealed that the rivers were grouped differently according to nutrient loading, microbiological activity, and the level of anthropogenic impact. The results of the study demonstrate that the integrated application of physicochemical, microbiological, and multivariate statistical approaches provides a reliable framework for the comprehensive assessment of the ecological status of river waters, the identification of river basins associated with ecological risks, and the scientifically based development of long-term monitoring programs.

title: Effect of expanded glass bead particle size on the mechanical, surface roughness and optical properties of low-density polyethylene composites
source: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal
summary: This study investigated the effect of expanded porous glass bead particle size on the mechanical, surface, and optical properties of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) composites. Two granulations of the filler with a range of particle sizes w
content: This study investigated the effect of expanded porous glass bead particle size on the mechanical, surface, and optical properties of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) composites. Two granulations of the filler with a range of particle sizes were inserted into the LDPE matrix at 10% wt. The composites were characterized using static tensile tests, under sudden impact loading, surface roughness measurements, and colourimetric analysis on the CIELAB scale. The results showed that filler significantly modified the mechanical performance, surface morphology, and optical properties of LDPE. The filler reduced tensile properties and increased surface irregularity compared with the unfilled polymer. Clear changes in colour parameters were also observed, including lowered lightness and changes in chromatic coordinates. The magnitude of these changes depended on filler particle size. The results show that filler particle size is an important factor influencing the mechanical, surface, and optical properties of LDPE composites and should be considered when designing materials that require a balance between mechanical performance and surface appearance.

title: Effect of cylinder diameter and unequal loading on the motion asymmetry of two independent pneumatic actuators
source: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal
summary: This study investigates the influence of cylinder diameter and unequal external loading on the motion asymmetry of two independent double-acting pneumatic actuators. The analysis was motivated by rehabilitation-device applications in which
content: This study investigates the influence of cylinder diameter and unequal external loading on the motion asymmetry of two independent double-acting pneumatic actuators. The analysis was motivated by rehabilitation-device applications in which two actuators are expected to perform simultaneous or symmetrical motion despite differences in external resistance. A reduced-order mathematical model was developed in MATLAB and included piston dynamics, nonlinear friction, variable chamber and tube volumes, isothermal pressure evolution, and compressible airflow through effective inlet and outlet restrictions. Two actuator configurations, with piston diameters of 32 and 40 mm and a nominal stroke of 0.4 m, were analysed under two experimentally derived unequal-loading conditions. The results demonstrated that load asymmetry produced measurable differences in piston-rod displacement, velocity, and stroke-completion time. Under the minimum unequal-load condition, both actuators completed the full stroke. The maximum displacement discrepancy reached 15.03 mm for the 32 mm cylinders and 12.88 mm for the 40 mm cylinders. Under the maximum unequal-load condition, the discrepancy increased to 91.73 mm and 71.02 mm, respectively, while the more heavily loaded actuator did not reach 99% of the nominal stroke within the 25 s simulation interval. Increasing the piston diameter from 32 to 40 mm reduced the maximum displacement discrepancy by approximately 14% under the minimum unequal-load condition and by approximately 23% under the maximum unequal-load condition. The results show that a larger piston diameter improves resistance to unequal loading but does not ensure synchronous motion. The developed model can support preliminary actuator selection and assessment of whether an additional pneumatic, mechanical, or electronic synchronization system is required.

title: Expression and role of the long noncoding RNA Linc00909 in chemoradiotherapy for colorectal cancer
summary: BACKGROUND Colorectal cancer is one of the major malignant tumors worldwide. Previous studies have shown that long noncoding RNAs have significant effects on various human cancers, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. AIM
content: BACKGROUND Colorectal cancer is one of the major malignant tumors worldwide. Previous studies have shown that long noncoding RNAs have significant effects on various human cancers, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. AIM To investigate the impact of the long noncoding RNA Linc00909 on colorectal cancer and its molecular mechanism. METHODS Using 196 paired colorectal cancer and adjacent tissues from 30 patients with rectal cancer (19 resistant, 11 sensitive) to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, we assessed Linc00909 expression using real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction and correlated it with survival outcomes. Functional assays in Linc00909-overexpressing SW620 and DLD1 cells—including Cell Counting Kit-8 assays, flow cytometry, and sphere formation—evaluated proliferation, cell cycle, apoptosis, stemness, and 5-fluorouracil/radiotherapy sensitivity. Tumorigenicity was examined in vivo . Bioinformatic and molecular experiments explored Linc00909’s competing endogenous RNA mechanism. RESULTS Linc00909 was upregulated in resistant and tumor tissues and independently predicted poorer overall and disease-free survival. Linc00909 overexpression enhanced proliferation, colony formation, antiapoptotic capacity, stemness, and therapy resistance in vitro and promoted tumor growth in vivo . miR-625-5p was bioinformatically predicted and experimentally validated as a binding target of Linc00909, with its expression decreasing upon Linc00909 overexpression. SOX2 was identified as a downstream target of miR-625-5p and showed increased expression at both the messenger RNA and protein levels following Linc00909 upregulation. CONCLUSION Linc00909 can affect the proliferation, colony formation, apoptosis, cell cycle regulation, spheroid-forming ability, and sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to 5-fluorouracil and radiotherapy. Mechanistically, Linc00909 may regulate the expression of the downstream target gene SOX2 by sequestering miR-625-5p, thereby influencing the sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Therefore, Linc00909 can be considered a potential therapeutic target for treating colorectal cancer.

title: V2I-Based Real-Time Lane Deviation Handling for Automated Vehicles to Face Road Characteristics Changes
summary: One of the main challenges in autonomous driving arises when lane deviations occur due to maintenance works or accidents, diverging from the predefined paths stored in vehicle’s plan. This work proposes a novel solution aimed at preserving
content: One of the main challenges in autonomous driving arises when lane deviations occur due to maintenance works or accidents, diverging from the predefined paths stored in vehicle’s plan. This work proposes a novel solution aimed at preserving a high level of automation in the presence of unexpected lane deviations. To achieve this, a mobile computer vision system placed at infrastructure level has been developed, equipped with dual cameras oriented in both driving directions. This device detects dynamic elements relevant to the driving environment and broadcasts planning and perception knowledge using ETSI-compliant CAM and DEMN messages as defined in the V2X European standard. These messages are enriched with recommended routes as well as conflict zones occupancy for proper arbitration. The entire communication system, which aims to demonstrate the advantages of V2X communication in complex traffic areas, is being tested in simulated and real-world environments.

title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
summary: The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sour
content: The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

title: Correlation-Consistent Gaussian Basis Sets for Copper Solids from Material-Constrained Atomic Optimization
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets enable systematic complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation in molecular quantum chemistry, but their diffuse atom-optimized primitives can lead to severe linear dependence in periodic solids, particu
content: Correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets enable systematic complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation in molecular quantum chemistry, but their diffuse atom-optimized primitives can lead to severe linear dependence in periodic solids, particularly metals and metal-containing compounds. Here, we introduce material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO), which preserves the atomic and correlation-consistent character of Gaussian basis sets while penalizing overlap-matrix ill-conditioning in representative solid-state environments. As a proof of concept, we develop Dunning-style MCAO-cc-pVXZ (X = D, T, Q) basis sets for Cu with nonrelativistic and scalar-relativistic all-electron potential, effective core potential, and pseudopotential treatments. The resulting basis sets exhibit robust numerical stability across bulk Cu, Cu-containing compounds, and Cu surfaces while accurately reproducing plane-wave reference structural properties and electronic band structures. Their correlation-consistent construction enables CBS-extrapolated random-phase approximation calculations for bulk Cu and CO adsorption on Cu(111), providing a systematic framework for assessing basis-set, relativistic, and core-treatment errors in correlated electronic-structure calculations of transition-metal solids.

title: Alternative oxidase in trypanosomatids
summary: Alternative oxidase (AOX) is a mitochondrial terminal oxidase that provides an alternative route for electron transfer, contributing to respiratory flexibility and redox homeostasis under stress conditions. In trypanosomatids, AOX displays
content: Alternative oxidase (AOX) is a mitochondrial terminal oxidase that provides an alternative route for electron transfer, contributing to respiratory flexibility and redox homeostasis under stress conditions. In trypanosomatids, AOX displays a highly uneven distribution associated with extensive diversification of mitochondrial electron transport chains (ETCs). In addition to canonical AOX, many trypanosomatids encode an enigmatic AOX-like protein (AOX-L), whose evolutionary origin and functional significance remain unresolved. Here, we investigated the evolutionary distribution, phylogenetic relationships, structural conservation, and functional divergence of AOX and AOX-L across euglenozoans. Comparative genomic analyses revealed a patchy distribution of both proteins among kinetoplastids, with multiple independent losses during evolution. Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated that AOX and AOX-L represent distinct evolutionary lineages, indicating independent origins rather than duplication-derived divergence. While AOX showed a conserved eukaryotic origin, AOX-L occupied a separate phylogenetic position and lacked key residues required for ubiquinol oxidation. Structural modelling revealed that AOX-L retained the characteristic AOX fold, predicted membrane association, and dimeric organization, but lacked the catalytic architecture necessary for enzymatic activity. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses of four AOX-containing trypanosomatid species showed that AOX expression and activity correlated with mitochondrial ETC organization. Species lacking cytochrome-dependent complexes III and IV displayed substantially higher AOX expression and enzymatic activity, consistent with AOX functioning as the primary terminal oxidase in these lineages. Conversely, species retaining a canonical ETC exhibited lower AOX activity, suggesting a role in metabolic flexibility and redox regulation. Our study provides a comprehensive evolutionary and functional framework for alternative oxidases in trypanosomatids. We demonstrate that AOX and AOX-L are evolutionarily distinct proteins with different predicted functions: AOX maintains respiratory electron flow according to lineage-specific mitochondrial requirements, whereas AOX-L represents a structurally conserved but catalytically inactive protein family that may have acquired an alternative regulatory role. These findings highlight how mitochondrial respiratory components diversify during eukaryotic evolution and provide a basis for future investigations into the biological function of AOX-L.

title: Conflicting-aromatic Ba3B8: a fluxional binary nanocluster rotor
summary: Boron-based alloy clusters represent a fertile ground for exploring exotic chemical bonding and inherent structural fluxionality. Herein, we theoretically investigate the dynamic fluxionality and bonding characteristics of the three-layered
content: Boron-based alloy clusters represent a fertile ground for exploring exotic chemical bonding and inherent structural fluxionality. Herein, we theoretically investigate the dynamic fluxionality and bonding characteristics of the three-layered Ba 3 B 8 cluster via quantum chemical calculations, which adopts an inverted sandwich geometry. The distorted B 8 wheel is sandwiched between an upper Ba 2 dimer and an isolated Ba atom at the bottom. Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics simulation demonstrates that the Ba 2 dimer rotates unconstrainedly and glides atop the B 8 wheel at room temperature (298K). The rotation barrier is only 0.04 kcal mol -1 at the single-point CCSD(T) level. Chemical bonding analyses reveal that this system can be formulated as [Ba 2 ] 2+ [B 8 ] 4- [Ba] 2+ ionic complex, where the [B 8 ] 4- motif exhibits conflicting aromaticity with 8π/6σ electron delocalized. Strong interlayer electrostatic interactions (exceeding 15.8 eV) and fully delocalized π/σ electrons in the B 8 wheel synergistically enable the unhindered rotation of the Ba 2 dimer. The present Ba 3 B 8 cluster expands the library of subnanoscale molecular rotors and provides a novel prototype for fluxional clusters featuring conflicting aromaticity.

title: Local management shapes meiofaunal communities in Balearic sandy beaches
summary: Sandy beaches are highly dynamic ecosystems providing essential services, yet they face increasing pressure from coastal exploitation. While macrofaunal responses to human disturbance are well documented, the impacts on communities for ecos
content: Sandy beaches are highly dynamic ecosystems providing essential services, yet they face increasing pressure from coastal exploitation. While macrofaunal responses to human disturbance are well documented, the impacts on communities for ecosystem functioning, such as the meiofauna, remain poorly understood. This study characterizes the meiofaunal communities of nine sandy beaches across the Balearic Archipelago (Mediterranean Sea) to evaluate the influence of beach morphodynamic zones, regional urbanization (Human Influence Index), and local management and protection ( Decret 25/2018 ). Sampling followed a slope gradient (swash, shoaling and subtidal zones) across four levels of protection, from non-protected beaches to beaches within Natural Parks. Results from meiofauna analyses showed that beach morphodynamic zone was the primary driver of community structure (explaining 15% of variance), with the subtidal zone encompassing the highest taxonomic alpha diversity and density. Local environmental protection displayed a significant positive relationship with community metrics, whereas the human impact, measured as the regional Human Influence Index, did not show a significant effect on the overall assemblage. Beaches under strict management where mechanical cleaning is prohibited and Posidonia oceanica banquettes are preserved in situ , exhibited significantly higher taxonomic alpha diversity and density. Additionally, complementary 18S rDNA metabarcoding successfully captured soft-bodied and rare taxa (e.g., Xenacoelomorpha, Tardigrada) missed by morphological counts, though reference database gaps highlight the necessity of integrated molecular-morphological frameworks. Our findings highlight that targeted local-scale regulations can effectively modulate microscopic biodiversity, playing a vital role in the conservation of interstitial beach ecosystems.

title: Ancient genome of the burial warhorses of the Shatuo leader Li Keyong
summary: The Shatuo-related horse was crucial to the Shatuo people’s emergence in the Central Plains during the Tang Dynasty, and its origin from either the Mongolian or Central Asian steppes and its qualities as a warhorse have long intrigued schol
content: The Shatuo-related horse was crucial to the Shatuo people’s emergence in the Central Plains during the Tang Dynasty, and its origin from either the Mongolian or Central Asian steppes and its qualities as a warhorse have long intrigued scholars. In this study, we analyzed three ancient genomes (0.80–1.79× coverage) of Daixian domestic horses from the King of Jin’s tomb, linked to Shatuo general Li Keyong and dated to the late Tang Dynasty (1046–921 BP). These horses were identified as male and exhibited a close genetic affinity with ancient Mongolian populations from the eastern Eurasian steppe. Our analysis revealed that these Daixian horses carried alleles associated with large body size and athletic performance, phenotypes consistent with their use as warhorses. Furthermore, we predicted their coat coloration to be predominantly bay. Our interdisciplinary findings link Daixian horse genetics to Mongolian horses and reveal Tang elite funerary, military, and husbandry practices.

title: THE ROLE OF AI INHANCING IN GREEN ECONOMY IN ARID ZONES: SMART AGRICULTURE AND ECOTOURISM IN THE ARAL SEA REGION"
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: A move towards green economy, a form of economy characterized by being low-carbon, resource efficient and socially inclusive, is now one of the main guiding principles for development in ecologically stressed regions. The Aral Sea region of
content: A move towards green economy, a form of economy characterized by being low-carbon, resource efficient and socially inclusive, is now one of the main guiding principles for development in ecologically stressed regions. The Aral Sea region of Uzbekistan, especially the autonomous Republic of Karakalpakstan, provides a good example of balancing economic revival with environmental restoration after one of the greatest man-made ecological catastrophes of the twentieth century. In this paper, the mechanisms of how ecotourism – a type of travel aimed at conserving the environment and providing financial benefits to local people – can become an instrument for developing green economy in such an arid and ecologically degraded area are explored. Using data from national-level policy documents, the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism), the World Economic Forum and UNDP publications, peer-reviewed studies and secondary statistical data, this research employs a qualitative case study approach to identify tourism resources of the region, relevant policies and the mechanisms for converting natural and cultural capital into green growth. The findings demonstrate that Karakalpakstan is endowed with unique ecotourism resources – Aralkum desert and ship cemetery, deserts and wetlands ecosystems, rich Karakalpak cultural heritage, and enjoys favorable policy environment with Uzbekistan’s Transition to a Green Economy strategy (2019-2030), and United Nations resolution of 2021 recognizing the region as ecological innovation and technology zone. To unlock its potential, however, requires a system of coordinated mechanisms in the areas of spatial planning, green financing and microfinancing, community building, low-carbon infrastructure, marketing and governance. This paper offers a holistic concept model, which connects these mechanisms to their environmental, economic and socio-cultural effects, as well as identifies the key obstacles – lack of infrastructure, management capabilities, seasonal nature and ecological vulnerability, and policy implications.

title: Critical Role of Wall–Hydrogen Excluded-Volume Interactions in the Freezing of Monolayer Water Confined in Subnanometer Graphene Slits
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Monolayer water confined between atomically flat surfaces exhibits unusual freezing behavior that is highly sensitive to nanoscale confinement and interfacial interactions. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to isolate the role of
content: Monolayer water confined between atomically flat surfaces exhibits unusual freezing behavior that is highly sensitive to nanoscale confinement and interfacial interactions. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to isolate the role of wall–hydrogen interactions in monolayer water confined between graphene sheets by comparing otherwise identical models with and without the C–H Lennard–Jones (LJ) interaction over a range of slit widths. Under strong confinement, inclusion of the C–H interaction markedly increases the freezing temperature, with differences exceeding 100 K at the narrowest slit widths, whereas the two models converge as the slit width increases. The magnitude of this effect is sensitive to the C–H excluded-volume parameter σCH, and this sensitivity decreases systematically with increasing slit width. Structural analyses show that the C–H interaction suppresses hydrogen configurations near the graphene walls and restricts wall-normal O–H orientations, thereby altering the local topology of the hydrogen-bond network. As the slit width increases, comparable out-of-plane configurational freedom becomes geometrically accessible even in the presence of C–H repulsion, accounting for the convergence of the freezing behavior. These results identify wall–hydrogen excluded volume as an important geometrical control of hydrogen-bond network adaptation and demonstrate that its coupling with confinement geometry can strongly regulate the freezing of low-dimensional water.

title: CFD Comparison of Marine Shell-and-Tube Heat Exchangers
source: Journal of Naval Sciences and Engineering
summary: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers (STHXs) are critical thermal management components in marine engineering, where design must balance thermal transport against the hydraulic pressure drop and auxiliary pumping power it demands. Marine-specific
content: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers (STHXs) are critical thermal management components in marine engineering, where design must balance thermal transport against the hydraulic pressure drop and auxiliary pumping power it demands. Marine-specific baffle geometries are rarely evaluated within a single validated framework that jointly addresses thermal performance, dead-zone-driven biofouling risk, nozzle-dominated pressure losses and fabrication-versus-energy cost. This study presents a Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) investigation and comparative thermo-hydraulic evaluation of a marine STHX. The numerical model was first validated against a semi-analytical solution for an unbaffled exchanger, then applied to three baffle configurations under identical operating conditions: a Longitudinal baffle, a Vertical Segmental baffle and a novel inclined XX-STHX design. The inclined design achieved a balanced outlet temperature while reducing pressure drop by 51% relative to the Vertical Segmental design, whose Performance Evaluation Criterion (PEC) of 1.66 confirms that its pressure penalty consumes a disproportionate share of its thermal gain. The swirling flow induced by the inclined baffles also eliminates the recirculation dead zones that drive biofouling in seawater service. An illustrative economic assessment indicates that its higher fabrication cost is justified only beyond a breakeven point of approximately 5.8 years.

title: Class A and Class B Biosolids Under 40 CFR Part 503 and Hawaii HAR 11-62: Pathogen Barriers, Heavy-Metal Loading Limits, Agronomic Nitrogen Balances, and the PFAS Thermal-Remediation Pivot
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Solids stabilization, dewatering, and final disposition routinely represent 30% to 50% of total operations and maintenance budgets across municipal wastewater treatment utilities. This technical brief provides a quantitative engineering and
content: Solids stabilization, dewatering, and final disposition routinely represent 30% to 50% of total operations and maintenance budgets across municipal wastewater treatment utilities. This technical brief provides a quantitative engineering and regulatory synthesis of federal sewage sludge standards (40 CFR Part 503 and RCRA 40 CFR Part 261) and State of Hawaii wastewater rules (HAR Chapter 11-62) governing Class B (PSRP), Class A (PFRP), and Exceptional Quality (EQ) biosolids. It details statutory pathogen ceilings (<2,000,000 MPN/g fecal coliform for Class B versus <1,000 MPN/g or <3 MPN/4 g Salmonella for Class A), Vector Attraction Reduction (VAR) gates, full 40 CFR § 503.13 Table 1 ceiling concentrations, Table 3 EQ concentrations, Cumulative Pollutant Loading Rates (CPLR), and Annual Pollutant Loading Rates (APLR) across nine regulated trace metals, alongside mandatory RCRA TCLP (EPA Method 1311) and Paint Filter Liquids (EPA Method 9095B) screenings. First-principles mass balances demonstrate crop-specific agronomic Plant-Available Nitrogen (PAN) caps under 40 CFR § 503.14(d) (protecting island basal aquifers from nitrate leaching) and wood-chip bulking stoichiometry required to lift nitrogen-rich 5:1 to 8:1 raw biosolids into the 25:1 to 30:1 C:N Class A composting envelope. Finally, evaluating EPA's January 2025 Draft Sewage Sludge Risk Assessment for PFOA and PFOS, the brief explains why conventional low-temperature PFRP composting (60 °C) and thermal pelletizing (80 to 120 °C) leave strong PFAS carbon-fluorine bonds (~485 kJ/mol) intact—accelerating utility transition toward upstream industrial source control and high-temperature (>650 to 850 °C) thermal conversion and biochar immobilization. Prepared with direct relevance to U.S. EPA Region 9 (Pacific Southwest: Hawaii, California, Arizona, Nevada, and the Pacific Islands) biosolids compliance under Clean Water Act Section 405(d), 40 CFR Part 503, and Hawaii Department of Health Wastewater Branch (HAR Chapter 11-62) oversight.

title: Regional sediment characterization and curve reconstruction for hydropower infrastructure design and turbine wear management
summary: Hydro-abrasive turbine wear caused by sediment passage is a severe operational and economic threat to run-of-river hydropower plants (HPPs) in steep, mountainous regions, leading to rapid efficiency decline and high turbine maintenance cost
content: Hydro-abrasive turbine wear caused by sediment passage is a severe operational and economic threat to run-of-river hydropower plants (HPPs) in steep, mountainous regions, leading to rapid efficiency decline and high turbine maintenance costs. This study investigated the spatial and seasonal variability of sediment grain-size distributions (GSD) across 11 HPPs in Rize, Türkiye, to establish a regional baseline and a sediment characterization and GSD reconstruction framework relevant to sediment management. A total of 53 GSD curves were evaluated from regulator sediments during winter and summer periods. Samples were analyzed using conventional granulometric parameters, compositional data analysis (CoDa), principal component analysis (PCA), unsupervised clustering, and paired seasonal tests. The representativeness of composite mixed samples was also assessed at the HPP level to evaluate cost-efficient sampling protocols. Ridge, partial least squares, and Gaussian process regression were compared with regional median and logarithmic interpolation benchmarks under three partial-measurement scenarios using leave-one-HPP-out cross-validation to evaluate reconstruction accuracy at unmeasured sieve sizes. No statistically significant seasonal differences were detected in sediment compositions ( p = 0.650). This result indicates that a consistent winter–summer contrast was not established in the sampled dataset; it does not identify the processes controlling sediment variability or erosive hazards. PCA and clustering identified four exploratory sediment groups with contrasting gravel, sand, and fine-material proportions, providing a descriptive basis for comparing deposited sediment among the sampled locations. Crucially, Under Scenario 2, using measurements at five sieve sizes, logarithmic interpolation reconstructed the unmeasured GSD values with high accuracy (R 2 = 0.978; MAE = 1.706 percentage points), outperforming the evaluated machine-learning models. These findings support a five-sieve reconstruction approach for preliminary sediment screening, although its benefits in terms of testing time, labour, and cost require direct evaluation.

title: σ-complex stabilization shapes enzymatic C-glycosylation and restricts the scope of natural C-glycosides
summary: C -glycosides are valuable compounds containing hydrolytically stable C-C bonds, yet their scarcity in nature and synthetic complexity limit their availability. Enzymes offer a sustainable route to C -glycosides, but few are known to displa
content: C -glycosides are valuable compounds containing hydrolytically stable C-C bonds, yet their scarcity in nature and synthetic complexity limit their availability. Enzymes offer a sustainable route to C -glycosides, but few are known to display C -glycosylation activity and their mechanism remains unclear. Here, we study the intricacies of the maize C -glycosyltransferase Zm UGT708A6 using X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and atomistic simulations. Structural and dynamical analyses reveal two flexible gates that control substrate access and reactive conformations. Combined Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics simulations and mutational data support a stepwise S E Ar mechanism for C -glycosylation of neutral phloretin, mediated by the catalytic His-Asp dyad and involving a high-energy σ-complex that stabilizes through a water-mediated proton transfer. Complementary pH- and substrate-activity experiments, together with Quantum Mechanics calculations, indicate that substrate hydroxylation patterns, protonation states, and σ-complex energetics restrict the scope of C -glycosides. Our results provide a coherent mechanistic framework that reconciles experimental observations across diverse conditions and advances our understanding of enzymatic C -glycosylation.

title: PCET beyond p K a : Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
summary: Photocatalytic oxidative multisite proton‐coupled electron transfer (MS‐PCET) reactions have emerged as a promising tool for the activation of strong O─H bonds in (cyclo)alkanols. However, these methods often require the use of e‐rich arene
content: Photocatalytic oxidative multisite proton‐coupled electron transfer (MS‐PCET) reactions have emerged as a promising tool for the activation of strong O─H bonds in (cyclo)alkanols. However, these methods often require the use of e‐rich arene‐containing derivatives ( para ‐methoxyphenyl (PMP), etc.) — a factor that greatly restricts their broader applicability. In this study, we report the successful implementation of targeted modulation of the base partner in photocatalytic cascade reactions of cyclic alcohols, unlocking previously rather inaccessible, nonactivated substrates. This approach successfully bypasses the prevalent limitations of ring‐opening transformations of cycloalkanols by disaggregation of the bulk alcohol and strategic base selection. As a result, we here demonstrate an operationally simple and widely applicable protocol for the redox‐neutral transformations of cycloalkanols into terminally C(sp 3 )‐C(sp 3 )‐coupled, functionalized open‐chain products. NMR‐based mechanistic studies, comprising in‐depth H‐bond analysis as well as DOSY and ROESY experiments, have elucidated the previously unrecognized crucial role of substrate disaggregation in this multisite PCET, along with (pyridine) base effects surpassing typical p K a ‐related and/or steric effects. Ultimately, our insights, for the first time, reveal the critical importance of the aggregation state and the design of productive alcohol‐base pre‐organization beyond p K a and enabled us to successfully pioneer remote alkylative Giese‐type C─C‐bond formations of previously challenging alkyl‐substituted cycloalkanols.

title: Evolution of entomopathogenicity in parasitic nematodes
summary: Two evolutionarily distant nematode genera, Steinernema and Heterorhabditis , independently evolved an entomopathogenic lifestyle in which they invade and kill insects with the aid of specifically associated pathogenic bacterial symbionts.
content: Two evolutionarily distant nematode genera, Steinernema and Heterorhabditis , independently evolved an entomopathogenic lifestyle in which they invade and kill insects with the aid of specifically associated pathogenic bacterial symbionts. The adaptations underlying the evolution of entomopathogenicity in these organisms and the origins of their symbiotic relationships remain poorly understood. Here, we developed an axenic culture medium that supports robust and sustained growth of Steinernema hermaphroditum while allowing controlled access to nutrients. A survey across nematode species suggests that the ability to feed on this culture medium reflects nematode adaptation to a parasitic lifestyle. Our findings indicate that, among the nematodes tested, only Steinernema and Heterorhabditis independently lost traits that enable survival after hatching in a nutrient-poor environment, an ability that is dispensable for obligate parasites that always hatch within a host. We further show that Steinernema and, to a lesser extent, Heterorhabditis nematodes can invade, develop, and reproduce inside living insect hosts in the absence of their symbiotic bacteria, apparently feeding on the hemolymph. Finally, we show that Steinernema emerging from symbiont-free infections pick up bacteria found within the insect. Our study identifies traits that were acquired or lost during nematodes’ adaptation to parasitism, and suggests that entomopathogenic nematodes were likely parasites before associating with their symbionts and becoming entomopathogenic.

title: Reflectionless modes as a source of topological phase boundaries in multiterminal Josephson junctions
summary: Multiterminal Josephson junctions are a promising platform to study non-trivial topology in engineered quantum systems. Yet, experimentally meaningful insight into what exactly makes these systems topologically non-trivial remains elusive.
content: Multiterminal Josephson junctions are a promising platform to study non-trivial topology in engineered quantum systems. Yet, experimentally meaningful insight into what exactly makes these systems topologically non-trivial remains elusive. In this work, we show that zero energy reflectionless scattering modes (RSMs) of the normal scattering matrix result in topological phase boundaries. By analyzing two different setups, we explain the origin of each topological phase boundary and provide generalizable insight into these systems. The considerations here can be of help for experimentalists as it connects the properties of the normal scattering region to the Andreev bound state spectrum of multiterminal superconducting junctions. In addition, our work provides a way to give meaning to the edge modes of these engineered topological systems with synthetic dimensions by providing a correspondence between unity transmission modes and boundaries between topological trivial and non-trivial phases.

title: Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases drive cancer risk through subtype-specific and shared proteomic mediators
summary: Cancer is associated with metabolic disorders, yet the impact of endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (ENMs) on cancer remains unclear. Here, we show the associations of 25 ENMs with cancer trajectories, from primary cancer inciden
content: Cancer is associated with metabolic disorders, yet the impact of endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (ENMs) on cancer remains unclear. Here, we show the associations of 25 ENMs with cancer trajectories, from primary cancer incidence to multi-primary cancers and mortality, using a multi-state model in a prospective cohort of 405,023 participants. Our findings reveal heterogeneous associations of ENMs across cancer sites and types, identifying 8 cancer-related ENMs that define four subtypes: C1 (iron deficiency/metabolism disorders dominated), C2 (type 2 diabetes dominated), C3 (lipid/lipoprotein metabolism disorders dominated), and C4 (osteoporosis dominated). Subtype-specific and subtype-shared proteomic mediators are identified and their contributions are quantified, with RNASET2 emerging as the major shared mediator. Furthermore, a deep-learning model integrating ENM subtypes and mediators enables personalized prediction of cancer incidence (AUCs = 0.80-0.90) and performs better than conventional Cox models. Our findings highlight the relevance of ENMs to cancer risk, providing mechanistic insights into metabolism-associated tumorigenesis.

title: RF-free control of nuclear spins with color centers in silicon carbide
summary: Color centers that enable nuclear-spin control offer a powerful route towards simplified and scalable quantum devices. Such capabilities are especially valuable for quantum sensing and computing platforms that already find applications in b
content: Color centers that enable nuclear-spin control offer a powerful route towards simplified and scalable quantum devices. Such capabilities are especially valuable for quantum sensing and computing platforms that already find applications in biology, materials science, and geophysics. A key challenge is the coherent manipulation of nearby nuclear spins, which serve as quantum memories and auxiliary qubits but conventionally require additional high-power RF fields, which increase the experimental complexity and overall power consumption. Finding systems where both electron and nuclear spins can be controlled using a single MW source is therefore highly desirable. Here, using a modified divacancy center in silicon carbide, we show that coherent control of a coupled nuclear spin is possible without any RF fields. Instead, MW pulses driving the electron spin also manipulate the nuclear spin through hyperfine-enhanced effects, activated by a precisely tilted external magnetic field. We demonstrate high-fidelity nuclear-spin control, achieving 89% two-qubit tomography fidelity and nearly T 1 -limited nuclear coherence times. This approach offers a simplified and scalable route for future quantum applications.

title: How abruptly did the Holocene Green Sahara end?
summary: Discussion about abrupt changes in the Sahara at the end of the African Holocene Humid Period has generally remained qualitative. Here we move the long-standing debate to a quantitative, metric-driven assessment, and we provide a rigorous f
content: Discussion about abrupt changes in the Sahara at the end of the African Holocene Humid Period has generally remained qualitative. Here we move the long-standing debate to a quantitative, metric-driven assessment, and we provide a rigorous framework to characterize abruptness of vegetation changes in a transient simulation of the MPI (Max Planck Institute) Earth System model and proxy records (dust flux and pollen data) for the last 8000 years. In the simulations, we find the strongest long-term increase in simulated bare surface in a north-west to south-east oriented strip of some 400 to 800 km in north-south direction between approximately 20° N in the west and 15° N in the east. Grid boxes in this region reveal abrupt, step-like transitions with changes in simulated bare surface, or conversely, in the total vegetation cover, which occur on average some 4 times faster than the approximately linear trend in the orbital forcing. The transitions in simulated grass and tropical tree plant functional types, i.e., in the type of the vegetation cover, appear to be up to twice as abrupt and up to twice as fast as the transition in the total vegetation cover. The reconstructed dust flux into the Atlantic shelf area at around 20° N, which we interpret as spatially aggregated changes in the openness of the landscape in the western Sahara, reveal a step-like transition with a much stronger abruptness than the simulated transition in bare surface in this region. The pollen records, however, indicate a rather gradual increase in desert-like conditions (with only one exception), but in many records, abrupt and fast transitions in Guinean, Sudanian and Sahelian phytogeographical groups occur. Hence our standardized, metric-driven analysis of model and data suggests that vegetation composition in the Holocene Sahara can undergo substantially more abrupt transitions than total vegetation cover, and that a gradual expansion of desert areas on a large scale can be accompanied by abrupt, step-like transitions within local ecosystems.

title: Irradiated graphite decontamination: 14C and 3H release–a steam-assisted thermal treatment approach
source: Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry
summary: Germany faces major challenges in disposing of irradiated nuclear graphite due to limited radionuclide inventory data and strict regulatory limits, particularly for 14 C. This study investigates an assisted steam thermal treatment to select
content: Germany faces major challenges in disposing of irradiated nuclear graphite due to limited radionuclide inventory data and strict regulatory limits, particularly for 14 C. This study investigates an assisted steam thermal treatment to selectively remove volatile radionuclides ( 14 C and 3 H) from irradiated graphite while preserving the bulk material. Experiments on irradiated graphite from the FRJ-2 and TRIGA Mainz reactors were performed to study the effects of temperature, treatment duration, and humidity. Under optimized conditions, more than 85% of both radionuclides were removed, demonstrating the potential of high-temperature steam treatment to reduce radionuclide inventories and improve radioactive waste management.

title: The accelerating northward expansion of the South Asian High has slowed regional sea ice melt in the Arctic
summary: Summer Arctic sea ice affects Arctic shipping, the regional ecological environment, atmospheric blocking highs, and even the subsequent East Asian winter monsoon variability; consequently, the mechanisms governing its evolution have receive
content: Summer Arctic sea ice affects Arctic shipping, the regional ecological environment, atmospheric blocking highs, and even the subsequent East Asian winter monsoon variability; consequently, the mechanisms governing its evolution have received extensive attention. This study investigates impacts of the South Asian High (SAH) on the slowdown of Arctic regional sea ice melt through diagnostic analyses and nudging experiments. Results show that the northward expansion of the SAH has strengthened Arctic tropospheric westerlies and intensified the polar vortex over the Arctic Ocean and the Pacific sector of the Arctic. These changes have slowed summer sea ice melt in the Pacific sector of the Arctic by reducing surface net shortwave radiation and enhancing anomalous sea ice drift into the region. More importantly, the coupling between the northward expansion of the SAH and the changing Arctic has systematically strengthened since the early 2000s. This northward expansion acts as the key driver in the dynamical linkage between the intensified Arctic tropospheric westerlies and the occurrence of extreme heatwaves in the region from the Yangtze River basin to the south of Japan. On decadal timescales, this study reveals an identical turning point of both the northward expansion of the SAH and the Arctic summer 500-1000 hPa thickness pattern, which corresponds well to the onset of accelerated oceanic warming in the North Pacific. Simulation experients show that global sea surface temperatures has driven the accelerating northward expansion of the SAH, rather than Arctic sea ice melt. The findings of this study suggest that the northward expansion of the subtropical systems has profound implications for the changing Arctic ecosystem.

title: An overlooked kinetic relaxation in the formation of sesquiterpene-derived criegee intermediates
summary: Sesquiterpene ozonolysis contributes to secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation by producing Criegee intermediates (CIs) via primary ozonide (POZ) decomposition. POZs are generally non-thermalized and thus assumed not to influence the for
content: Sesquiterpene ozonolysis contributes to secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation by producing Criegee intermediates (CIs) via primary ozonide (POZ) decomposition. POZs are generally non-thermalized and thus assumed not to influence the formation rate constants of CIs, yet a fraction of sesquiterpene-derived POZs could be thermalized under atmospheric conditions, which is typically overlooked but potentially affects CI formation kinetics. This study derived a POZ-explicit kinetic model for sesquiterpene-derived CI formation, showing that the CI formation rate constant is initially unstable but gradually approaches a plateau equal to the rate constant of sesquiterpene ozonolysis. Such behavior is called “kinetic relaxation” and the relaxation timescale, as shown by our model, can be extended by cold surges but diminished by heatwaves. Our results revealed that kinetic relaxation occurs mainly in the thermalized POZs; the fractions of thermalized POZs were estimated to be less than 2 % for α -cedrene, up to ∼34 % for α -copaene, and over 90 % for β -caryophyllene. The high thermalized fractions of β -caryophyllene POZs lead to CI formation rate constants at room temperature that are 3–5 orders of magnitude lower than those calculated without kinetic relaxation. Our findings suggest that kinetic relaxation may enable reactions between thermalized POZs and atmospheric radicals, providing a new perspective on the fate of sesquiterpenes in atmospheric ozonolysis.

title: Post-fire soil organic matter stabilization in fire-sensitive patagonian ecosystems
summary: Global change is altering fire regimes worldwide, exposing fire-sensitive ecosystems such as Patagonia’s to unprecedented fire sizes and frequencies, which can result in irreversible soil degradation. A megafire in Torres del Paine National
content: Global change is altering fire regimes worldwide, exposing fire-sensitive ecosystems such as Patagonia’s to unprecedented fire sizes and frequencies, which can result in irreversible soil degradation. A megafire in Torres del Paine National Park (Chile, 2011–2012) created a mosaic of burn severities across contrasting fire-sensitive ecosystems. This setting provided an opportunity to evaluate medium-term post-fire effects on soil organic matter (SOM) stabilization. We assessed the effects of fire occurrence and burn severity across 34 plots within two cold climatic conditions and six vegetation types. Soils were fractionated into free particulate organic matter (fPOM), occluded particulate organic matter (oPOM) and mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM). Chemical composition of fPOM and oPOM was characterized by solid-state 13 C CPMAS NMR spectroscopy, whereas MAOM was characterized by ATR-FTIR spectroscopy. Post-fire analysis revealed that MAOM showed no compositional differences between fire occurrence or burn severity. In contrast, fPOM and oPOM showed clear fire legacies, with high pyrogenic carbon and low carbohydrate contents in burned soils, especially in fPOM. Burn severity had limited effects on SOM composition, but nominal oxidation state of carbon (NOSC) was significantly increased, suggesting thermodynamic changes rather than chemical composition shifts. Associations of carbohydrates with stable aggregates and microbial biomass align with prior research on their role in soil aggregate formation. Our results highlight the subtle effects of burn severity on SOM stability, although post-fire occlusion may occur, increased oxidation leads to more vulnerable compounds to mineralization if aggregates are disrupted.

title: Beyond keratinases: proteomic insights reveals potential oxidoreductase-mediated pathways involved in feather degradation mechanism by Streptomyces sp. G11C
summary: Feather waste is an abundant keratin-rich byproduct generated by the poultry industry that represents an important environmental challenge due to the recalcitrant nature of keratin. Although keratinolytic microorganisms have emerged as prom
content: Feather waste is an abundant keratin-rich byproduct generated by the poultry industry that represents an important environmental challenge due to the recalcitrant nature of keratin. Although keratinolytic microorganisms have emerged as promising biotechnological tools for feather valorization, the molecular mechanisms underlying bacterial keratin degradation remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterized the cellular and extracellular protein repertoire of Streptomyces sp. G11C during growth on feathers using a global label-free shotgun proteomic approach, aiming to identify candidate proteins and associated biological processes potentially contributing to feather degradation. Proteomic analysis of cellular and extracellular fractions collected after 3 and 5 days of cultivation identified 794 proteins, with proteases and oxidoreductases among the most abundant functional groups. An S8 serine protease and an M6 metalloprotease were identified as the major candidate keratinases, and their roles were experimentally validated through overexpression in Streptomyces sp. G11C, resulting in approximately 2.5-fold higher keratinolytic activity than the wild-type strain. Additional components, including lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases and dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenases, highlight oxidoreductase-mediated mechanisms for keratin denaturation and disulfide bond reduction, suggesting a previously unrecognized contribution to bacterial keratin degradation. Sulfite production was detected during feather degradation, although its relatively low concentration supports a predominant role for enzymatic disulfide reduction. In addition, proteins involved in sulfur metabolism, oxidative stress response, protein folding, and cellular adaptation, including γ-glutamyl transferase, catalases, DnaK, and TerD proteins, were identified, indicating coordinated physiological responses during keratin utilization. Our findings support a multistep model of bacterial keratin degradation in which oxidoreductase-mediated destabilization of the keratin structure precedes extracellular proteolysis and is accompanied by metabolic and stress-adaptation processes. This work provides new mechanistic insights into microbial keratin degradation, identifies novel enzymes potentially involved in this process, and expands the current understanding of bacterial keratin utilization, offering new opportunities for the development of sustainable biotechnological processes for feather waste valorization.

title: Beyond Tomorrow—Electrification of Hard-to-Abate Sectors
summary: Reaching net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions requires deep electrification beyond ground transportation, buildings, and conventional industry automation. This article discusses direct electrification pathways for hard-to-abate sectors,
content: Reaching net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions requires deep electrification beyond ground transportation, buildings, and conventional industry automation. This article discusses direct electrification pathways for hard-to-abate sectors, which today account for 30% of global GHG emissions and include steel, cement, chemicals, aviation, and shipping. Whereas indirect electrification via hydrogen and synthetic fuels will remain indispensable for some applications, direct use of electricity is generally preferable from an efficiency perspective. We review selected emerging opportunities for power electronics in industrial process electrification, including steelmaking through hydrogen plasma smelting reduction or molten-oxide electrolysis, electrified cement production, high-temperature process heat, plasma-assisted chemistry, and electrochemical synthesis. Across these examples, power converters must interface with highly application-specific loads, ranging from low-voltage high-current electrolysis cells to dynamic plasma reactors and megawatt-scale induction heating systems. In addition, high-power grid interfaces and in-plant energy management/buffering solutions must be clarified. Thus, future electrified industrial processes pose new “beyond-tomorrow” research challenges for power electronics, requiring close interdisciplinary collaboration with scientists from neighboring disciplines.

title: Geometry control in wire arc additive manufacturing: challenges, strategies, and future perspectives
summary: The deployment of autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) within complex physical systems remains a grand challenge. While intelligent manufacturing aims to address this by infusing industrial processes with real-time adaptation, the prevai
content: The deployment of autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) within complex physical systems remains a grand challenge. While intelligent manufacturing aims to address this by infusing industrial processes with real-time adaptation, the prevailing approach often involves applying machine learning (ML) to isolated, well-defined sub-problems. This component-wise strategy, however, proves insufficient for processes like wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), where geometric fidelity is governed by deeply coupled, multi-scale thermo-fluid dynamics that defy simple predictive modelling. Here, using WAAM as a foundational case study of a complex cyber-physical system, we provide a systematic review of the intelligent strategies required for end-to-end geometry control. We deconstruct this challenge into a unified framework spanning the full process chain—pre-deposition, in-process, and post-deposition—and map the corresponding control methods onto the critical physical scales of the bead, layer, and part. Our synthesis reveals that the primary limitations are not a lack of algorithmic novelty but rather fundamental issues of model generalisation from sparse, high-cost data and the integration of heterogeneous physical priors. This analysis points towards a necessary paradigm shift: moving from static, data-driven prediction towards dynamic, autonomous control architectures. We argue that realising the next generation of intelligent manufacturing requires a focus on integrated systems, such as physics-informed digital twins and multi-sensor fusion platforms, that can holistically manage process complexity in real time.

title: 3D-printed integrated wearable devices with wireless charging batteries and sensors for multimodal physiological monitoring
summary: Wearable electronics require mechanically compliant, highly integrated platforms that combine multiple functional modules to achieve continuous physiological monitoring. However, existing systems remain constrained by wired or unstable powe
content: Wearable electronics require mechanically compliant, highly integrated platforms that combine multiple functional modules to achieve continuous physiological monitoring. However, existing systems remain constrained by wired or unstable power delivery and insufficient system-level integration, leading to poor functional reliability and wearability. Here, we report a self-contained wearable device that integrates wireless charging batteries and multimodal sensors within a single flexible platform. Each functional module is structurally engineered through customized geometric designs and realized using multimaterial direct-ink-writing 3D printing, enabling high performance together with seamless structural and electrical interconnections. The integrated system consists of a rectangular wireless charging coil for efficient energy harvesting, serpentine battery electrodes for flexible energy storage, and a Hilbert-serpentine temperature sensor combined with an interdigital pressure sensor for accurate physiological signal detection. The resulting device is self-contained and skin-conformal, demonstrating real-time monitoring during daily activities, vigorous exercise, and febrile conditions. This study establishes a generalizable architecture for self-contained wearable electronics, offering a pathway toward next-generation intelligent and autonomous wearable electronics.

title: Short-chain ligand-assisted coprecipitation for scalable and green synthesis of monodisperse inorganic nanocrystals: opportunities, mechanisms, and challenges
summary: Monodisperse inorganic nanocrystals are pivotal in catalysis, optoelectronics, energy conversion and storage, and biomedicine, yet an ideal synthesis method that simultaneously satisfies room-temperature operation, green chemistry, ultrafas
content: Monodisperse inorganic nanocrystals are pivotal in catalysis, optoelectronics, energy conversion and storage, and biomedicine, yet an ideal synthesis method that simultaneously satisfies room-temperature operation, green chemistry, ultrafast kinetics, low cost, and large-scale feasibility still remains challenging. This review critically benchmarks solution-phase methods for monodisperse inorganic nanocrystals, including hydrothermal/solvothermal synthesis, hot-injection and heat-up routes, two-phase liquid-liquid synthesis, conventional long-chain ligand-assisted coprecipitation, and short-chain ligand-assisted coprecipitation (SCLAC). In this review, we first summarize the principles, advantages, and limitations of conventional methods, then discuss the formation mechanism of monodisperse nanoparticles, with emphasis on the distinction between classical LaMer-type burst nucleation and non-classical or ligand-mediated nucleation/growth pathways. We then evaluate SCLAC as a promising candidate for green and scalable synthesis. SCLAC uses short-chain fatty acid and aliphatic amine ligands in ethanol/water under ambient conditions and has enabled sub-5 nm rare-earth-doped oxide and fluoride nanocrystals with high photoluminescence quantum yields and batch scales up to the kilogram level. However, its greenness, cost, mechanism, and generality across other material classes require further quantitative validation. We conclude by outlining a roadmap for extending SCLAC to metal sulfides, noble metals, multicomponent systems, and continuous-flow manufacturing, while clearly distinguishing experimentally demonstrated advantages from proposed mechanisms and future opportunities.

title: Psychological Readiness for the Green Energy Transition: A Human-Factors Model for Aviation Maintenance Crews
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: Green-aviation research on battery and alternative-fuel chemistries has advanced rapidly, but a persistent blind spot remains: the psychological readiness of the maintenance personnel who operate these systems daily under safety-critical co
