The results indicate that chemical oxidation and TGA provide similar estimates of vulnerable organic matter, although the fractions identified by both approaches remain operationally defined rather than reflecting in situ degradation processes. The modified chemical oxidation method, therefore, provides an accessible, complementary approach for characterising the relative vulnerability of organic carbon in marine sediments. Incorporating such reactivity-based measurements alongside carbon-stock assessments could improve evaluations of the resilience of shelf-sea carbon stores to disturbance and inform spatial marine management and conservation.

title: Solvent-Mediated Heat-Shock Trapping of Aromatic Carbonyl Guests in Poly(vinylpyrrolidone) Enables White-light Fluorescence, UV and Green-Light-Excited Red Phosphorescence, Delayed NIR Emission
summary: Nonequilibrium polymer processing provides a route to generating emissive states without the need to synthesize new covalent chromophores. We report a simple physical method for encapsulating aromatic carbonyl guest molecules within the car
content: Nonequilibrium polymer processing provides a route to generating emissive states without the need to synthesize new covalent chromophores. We report a simple physical method for encapsulating aromatic carbonyl guest molecules within the carbonyl rich polymer poly(vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP). The resulting host-guest systems display guest dependent fluorescence across the visible region with a white light emitting complex being observed for one of the host/guest combinations with CIE coordinates (0.3147, 0.3244), close to the D65 daylight standard and a CCT of approximately 6430 K. Of the naphthalene derivatives investigated, 4-bromo-1,8-naphthalic anhydride (4-BrNA) displays a very different photo-physical behaviour when encapsulated in the polymer. It gives rise to red room temperature phosphorescence at 613 nm upon excitation at either 360 nm or 500 nm. Control experiments show that the emissive state is only obtained via solvent induced heat shock processing and not simply by dispersing the guest in the polymer. Co-trapping of the NIR emitter IR-783 with PVP/4-BrNA in the polymer leads to delayed near-infrared emission at 824 nm upon excitation at 360 nm, indicating that the emitter is being sensitized by the persistent donor reservoir. This is a rapid, metal free and modular approach which provides a process defined platform for white light fluorescence, visible light excited RTP and time gated NIR emission.

title: A Review of Mechanistic and Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Models for Predicting Pesticide Fate and Transport in Soil and Water
summary: Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poiso
content: Global pesticide use exceeded 3.7 million tonnes in 2023, and residues that persist beyond the treated field drive diffuse soil, surface water, and groundwater contamination linked to ecological harm and an estimated 150,000 pesticide poisoning deaths annually. Because field monitoring of pesticide fate across every soil, climate, and hydrological setting is logistically and financially infeasible at regulatory scale, predictive modelling has become the primary tool for estimating environmental concentrations and associated risk. This review traces the development of the field from traditional process-based mechanisms to hybrid AI frameworks by synthesizing 81 peer-reviewed and technical sources from an initial pool of 1,450 records screened across Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect (2005–2026). We look at the physicochemical and degradation principles that determine the fate of pesticides; the deterministic, mechanistic, process-based, empirical, and statistical models that support the current regulatory risk assessment; the hydrological and transport models that function at the soil profile to watershed scale; and the expanding array of machine learning, deep learning, fuzzy logic, GIS, remote sensing, and IoT-enabled techniques that are transforming precision agriculture and prediction. Case studies from India and other countries demonstrate real-world uses in addition to ongoing limitations in data accessibility and cross-context transferability. We point out important gaps, such as persistent data scarcity in low- and middle-income regions, limited coupling of fate models to downscaled climate projections, and inadequate integration of explainable AI to foster regulatory trust. We identify calibration and validation, particularly probabilistic uncertainty quantification, as essential to the responsible use of both conventional and data-driven models. We conclude that creating accurate, transferable pesticide prediction systems that support the Sustainable Development Goals and safeguard human and environmental health requires combining mechanistic understanding with hybrid, physics-informed AI and climate-resilient precision agriculture technologies.

title: Measurements of Volatile Organic Compounds and Aerosols from Cooking during the CLEAN Home Indoor Field Study
summary: In this study, we present measurements of gas- and particle-phase cooking emissions from the Consumer products, Lights, Environmental Air cleaning in Normal conditions (CLEAN) Home indoor field study. We quantified real-time emissions of 16
content: In this study, we present measurements of gas- and particle-phase cooking emissions from the Consumer products, Lights, Environmental Air cleaning in Normal conditions (CLEAN) Home indoor field study. We quantified real-time emissions of 16 volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during cooking, primarily consisting of small alcohols, carbonyls, and monoterpenes. Emissions were extremely reproducible across the experiments. Emissions of long-chain aldehydes from meat cooking were observed and were consistent with prior measurements. Monoterpene emissions were dominated by ocimene, limonene, and camphene. Calculated emission rates and factors ranged from 0.04–3.77 μg s–1 and 0.06 to 6.04 mg [kg ingredients]−1, respectively. Several postcooking air and surface cleaning activities (germicidal UV lights, bleach cleaning, and a commercial air cleaner) were conducted and had negligible impacts on the decay rates of VOCs in the kitchen. Particle measurements revealed mass loadings of largely organic aerosols, which at times exceeded 300 μg m–3. Differences in cooking protocols (e.g., pan material, stove operation) were found to notably change the emissions of some VOCs and particles. Our results confirm that cooking is a substantial contributor of VOCs and particles indoors and highlight the importance of sufficiently high localized air extraction or ventilation during cooking.

title: Severity dynamics of an invasive forest pathogen: Beech bark disease in an unmanaged old-growth forest
summary: Beech bark disease (BBD) is an invasive insect-pathogen complex causing significant mortality to American beech ( Fagus grandifolia )—one of the most dominant species in temperate forests across eastern North America. BBD disproportionately
content: Beech bark disease (BBD) is an invasive insect-pathogen complex causing significant mortality to American beech ( Fagus grandifolia )—one of the most dominant species in temperate forests across eastern North America. BBD disproportionately affects older and larger beech trees, yet the biotic and abiotic drivers of its spread and impacts are not well-defined. In this study, we assessed the disease severity of American beech trees ( n = 901; ≥10 cm diameter at breast height [DBH]) in a 13.5 ha forest dynamics plot within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) network. We used BBD severity rankings across a four-year period to examine how individual tree characteristics (size, growth rate) and topographic factors (aspect, topographic position index [TPI], topographic wetness index [TWI], and potential diffuse solar insolation) influence symptom severity and disease progression. DBH and relative growth rate (RGR) were identified as significant predictors of disease status, with larger and slower-growing trees at greater risk of severe BBD symptoms. TPI, TWI, and northness were positively correlated with severe BBD symptoms, whereas eastness and potential diffuse solar radiation exhibited negative correlations. Disease progression accelerated with reduced RGR, a pattern also observed among trees on north- and east-facing slopes. Together, these results indicate that tree size, growth rate, and topographically driven microclimates influence BBD dynamics within unmanaged old-growth forests. Notably, large, slow-growing canopy American beech occupying cool, moist, and low-light microhabitats appear particularly susceptible to accelerated disease progression and associated mortality.

title: An Aerogel Composite Cooler with Radiative-Phase-Change Hybrid Cooling for Highly Effective Outdoor Electronics Thermal Management
summary: Conventional radiative cooling suffers from limited cooling capacity, while phase change based temperature control techniques are plagued by material leakage, making them insufficient to satisfy the growing requirements of outdoor electroni
content: Conventional radiative cooling suffers from limited cooling capacity, while phase change based temperature control techniques are plagued by material leakage, making them insufficient to satisfy the growing requirements of outdoor electronics. Herein, we propose a leakproof radiative-phase-change hybrid cooling aerogel composite (RPHCAC) cooler that integrates directionally structured chitosan (CS)/carbon nanotubes (CNTs) aerogel encapsulating beeswax (BW) as the phase change material (PCM) inside a coating of polydimethylsiloxane/hexagonal boron nitride (PDMS/h BN), which achieves a high solar reflectivity of 95.6% with a high latent heat of 163.4 J g-1. Importantly, aerogel composite cooler exhibits a water contact angle of approximately 123.9°, maintaining its water‑repellent character with self‑cleaning functionality. Under direct sunlight, this RPHCAC cooler attains an average temperature reduction of 11.7 °C below ambient and displays a maximum temperature drop of 47.5 °C when further subjected to an intense thermal shock of 2000 W ⋅m−2, which is primarily attributed to the temperature pinning effect of the PCM and the good optical property of the PDMS/h BN coating. By integrating radiative cooling with latent heat storage, this work offers an effective strategy to safeguard outdoor electronics against solar radiation, thus pushing passive thermal management technologies closer to real world deployment.

title: Evidence for persistent net heterotrophy in blackwater estuaries and the importance of depth-resolved community respiration measurements
summary: Blackwater estuaries receive large quantities of terrestrial organic carbon, yet the extent to which this carbon is consumed through estuarine respiration remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate seasonal and vertical variability in
content: Blackwater estuaries receive large quantities of terrestrial organic carbon, yet the extent to which this carbon is consumed through estuarine respiration remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate seasonal and vertical variability in blackwater estuary pelagic metabolism. Both depth-integrated gross primary production (GPP) and community respiration (CR) exhibit pronounced seasonality, with elevated rates during warmer months. CR generally declines with depth. Neglecting vertical variability in CR substantially biases estimates of depth-integrated CR and net community production (NCP). The pelagic community is net heterotrophic (negative depth-integrated NCP) throughout the study period. Net heterotrophy is strongest in summer. These findings show that blackwater estuaries can exhibit persistent pelagic net heterotrophy, suggesting that substantial organic carbon may be processed through pelagic respiration. The observed vertical variability in CR underscores the importance of depth-resolved measurements for accurately quantifying this carbon transformation.

title: A Probabilistic Agent-Based Model of Avascular Tumor Growth by Analysis of Shannon Entropy as a Phenotype Transition Index
summary: A fully probabilistic, two-dimensional model has been developed to simulate avascular tumor growth. In this framework, cell proliferation, phenotype transitions, and spatial relocation of newly formed cells are governed by stochastic proces
content: A fully probabilistic, two-dimensional model has been developed to simulate avascular tumor growth. In this framework, cell proliferation, phenotype transitions, and spatial relocation of newly formed cells are governed by stochastic processes. These biological mechanisms are influenced by the local concentrations of oxygen (O₂) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) within the microenvironment, which encompasses both healthy and tumor tissues. To capture the dynamics of gas diffusion, a system of nonlinear, coupled diffusion equations for O₂ and CO₂ was numerically solved using the finite difference method on a square lattice. Based on the resulting concentration levels, cellular behavior was modeled over a 40-day period. The simulation naturally produced a multilayered avascular tumor structure, consisting of a necrotic core surrounded by concentric layers of quiescent and proliferating cells. Given the probabilistic nature of the model, Shannon entropy was employed as an index to quantify phenotype variability throughout tumor development. Findings show that quiescent and necrotic cells emerge between days 9 and 11, primarily under hypoxic conditions. By the end of simulation, the tumor reached a diameter of approximately 1–2 mm. Entropy peaked between days 11 and 13, reflecting maximal phenotypic diversity, and subsequently oscillated around an asymptotic value. This stabilization indicates a dynamic balance between cell birth and death, which may serve as an early signal of the angiogenic switch and the transition toward vascularized tumor growth.

title: From global evidence to local action: biodiversity impacts and mitigation for wind and solar farms in understudied regions
summary: A rapid transition to renewable energy is essential to address anthropogenic climate change, but its speed and scale may pose new risks to species and ecosystems. The biodiversity impacts of wind and solar facilities are well studied in Nor
content: A rapid transition to renewable energy is essential to address anthropogenic climate change, but its speed and scale may pose new risks to species and ecosystems. The biodiversity impacts of wind and solar facilities are well studied in North America and Europe, but many other regions lack local evidence to guide development. We conducted a global systematic map of 331 field studies on the biodiversity impacts of wind and solar farms and strategies to mitigate them. We also characterised the environments occupied by wind and solar facilities in Australia, where only four field studies of wind farm impacts have been published. Globally, most studies came from temperate North America and Europe and focussed on bird and bat collisions with wind turbines. Fewer studies addressed solar farms, but these highlighted opportunities to restore native plants and invertebrates beneath and around panels. Siting was the most frequently recommended mitigation for both technologies, but depends on land availability and on knowledge of species distributions and movements that is lacking in many regions. Curtailment (turbine shutdown) was the most consistently effective intervention to reduce turbine collisions, though it requires careful implementation to balance trade-offs with energy production. In Australia, wind and solar facilities are concentrated in temperate regions near population centres, mostly on land previously cleared for agriculture, where remaining ecosystems face multiple pressures. Solar farms occupied almost five times the area of wind farms for similar capacity, but these cleared landscapes offer substantial opportunities for restoration alongside development. Global evidence can guide development in understudied regions, but local field research is urgently needed. Priorities include fundamental biodiversity knowledge, open data, indirect and cumulative effects, and testing mitigation and restoration under local conditions. With adaptive management, the renewable energy transition can be both biodiversity friendly and an opportunity to learn more about the species and ecosystems it affects.

title: Identifying new particle formation events by using a simple and low-cost diffusion charger monitor
summary: New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of ultrafine particles (UFPs) in the atmosphere and plays an important role in air quality and human health. NPF events are usually identified from particle number size distribution measured wi
content: New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of ultrafine particles (UFPs) in the atmosphere and plays an important role in air quality and human health. NPF events are usually identified from particle number size distribution measured with complex instruments such as the scanning mobility particle sizer (SMPS) and the Neutral cluster and Air Ion Spectrometer (NAIS). The Naneos Partector2 Pro (P2Pro) measures particle number concentrations (PNC) in eight size bins between 7.8 and 382.4 nm using a unipolar diffusion charger. This study investigated whether this simple and lower-cost instrument can be used for detecting NPF events with performance comparable to reference instruments. To do this, we monitored PNC in Brisbane using a P2Pro over a year. A method was developed and validated by comparing the results with previous studies reported in the same area using the NAIS or SMPS. The analysis was carried out under various combinations of three main sets of criteria – the total PNC, the fraction of particles in the nucleation mode, and the times of occurrence of the events. The results, based on the selected criteria showed that NPF events occurred on 158 (44 %) days of the year. The results showed excellent agreement with previous estimates of NPF events at the same location obtained using an SMPS and NAIS. The outcome of this study offers an affordable alternative to an instrument that can detect NPF events that are important in many aspects such as air quality monitoring and health risk assessment.

title: SynCED: the Synthetic Chemical Exposome Database
summary: The Synthetic Chemical Exposome Database (SynCED) (https://syncedb.ca) is a substantially updated and expanded version of the Toxin and Toxin Target Database (T3DB). SynCED provides rich data on 316 418 synthetic chemicals from diverse chem
content: The Synthetic Chemical Exposome Database (SynCED) (https://syncedb.ca) is a substantially updated and expanded version of the Toxin and Toxin Target Database (T3DB). SynCED provides rich data on 316 418 synthetic chemicals from diverse chemical, toxicological, exposure, and regulatory sources. The synthetic chemical exposome comprises a vast and rapidly expanding range of anthropogenic chemicals, yet information on their sources, uses, biological effects, toxicity, and molecular interactions remains fragmented across numerous resources. SynCED addresses this problem by consolidating this information and linking most known synthetic chemicals with standardized chemical names and identifiers, compound descriptions, predicted or measured physicochemical properties, reference spectral data, exposure and use information, toxicological data, and biological targets or interactions. Literature-derived compound descriptions and functional annotations were built using the Chemical Functional Ontology (ChemFOnt) Fact Finder pipeline, which extracts semantically defined chemical-relation-entity associations while retaining supporting evidence and provenance. In addition to literature-derived biological target information, SynCED also incorporates ligand-based protein-target predictions to extend the coverage of chemicals lacking experimentally characterized interactions. To facilitate compound identification using non-target or suspect screening, SynCED provides extensive search utilities supporting searches by chemical structure, toxicity, text, mass, molecular weight, elemental composition, ESI-MS, EI-MS, and NMR spectra (both measured and predicted) as well as searches by target sequence (protein and DNA). It also supports database browsing by chemical names, ClassyFire chemical taxonomy and exposure source. Together, these features extend T3DB to turn SynCED into a broader, more provenance-aware database, that supports suspect or non-target screening, chemical exposure and hazard assessment, mechanistic studies, and general chemical exposomics research.

title: Soil and environmental gradients driving riparian vegetation structure on two Nile River islands, Luxor Governorate, Upper Egypt
summary: Documenting, updating, and evaluating the phytoremediation potential of natural riparian plants are essential for plant conservation. As part of ongoing floristic surveys on the Nile River islands in Upper Egypt, the present study investiga
content: Documenting, updating, and evaluating the phytoremediation potential of natural riparian plants are essential for plant conservation. As part of ongoing floristic surveys on the Nile River islands in Upper Egypt, the present study investigates vegetation–environment relationships across three ecologically distinct sites on two Nile River islands in Luxor Governorate (Armant Island: sites 1 and 2; Aqalata Island: site 3); and to evaluate phytoremediation efficiency of some macrophytes ( Setaria geminata (Forssk.) Veldkamp, Ceratophyllum demersum L., Myriophyllum spicatum L., Persicaria senegalensis (Meisn.) Soják, and Ludwigia adscendens subsp. diffusa (Forssk.) P.H. Raven) in these islands for non essential heavy metals lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd). Cd and Pb concentrations in the water at all three sites were within safe limits for irrigation water. While Pb in sediments is within the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) safe limit, Cd levels in the sediments exceeded those limits. In contrast, Pb and Cd levels in all studied species fell within the permissible limits during all seasons. The bioaccumulation factors (BAFs) exceeded one for Pb in the submerged species C. demersum and M. spicatum , while the value for Cd exceeded one in M. spicatum only. Translocation factors (TFs) for both metals, Pb and Cd, were less than one, except for Pb in S. geminata and L. adscendens . These results suggest that submerged species, particularly C. demersum , are suitable for phytoextraction, while emergent macrophytes are suitable for biomonitoring. For vegetation analysis, a total of 80 species from 30 families (52 annuals and 28 perennials) were recorded. Poaceae, Fabaceae, Asteraceae, and Brassicaceae are the most diverse families, accounting for 47.50% of the total flora. Therophytes (53.75%) were the most common life form, with a strong cosmopolitan affinity, indicating that widespread species dominate the studied islands. Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) ordination reveals distinct environmental gradients and species distributions across the sampled sites. CCA axis 1 (58.5% variance) clearly separated site 1, characterized by sandy sediments, high pH, and elevated Cd, from the finer-textured, nutrient- and ion-rich sites 2 and 3. The sandy, low-retention environment of site 1 supports a distinct flora adapted to disturbance. CCA axis 2 (41.5% variance) further partitioned site 2 (clay-rich, waterlogged, high organic matter) from site 3 (disturbance-driven). Our findings show that sediment texture, nutrient content, waterlogging, and localized anthropogenic impacts (agricultural runoff, tourism, and related heavy metals) act as cooperative filters, assembling distinct floristic communities on each island. The study expands our understanding of riparian biodiversity in human-influenced arid-region river systems, emphasizing that even small riparian islands serve as sensitive indicators of the interactions between natural and anthropogenic gradien

title: The Seoul Tracer Release Experiment: Investigating Regional Halocarbon Emissions from a Large Metropolitan Area
summary: Halocarbons have hundreds- to thousands-of-times higher global warming potentials than CO2, and reducing some of these emissions is part of the Kigali Amendment. Quantifying these emissions at urban and regional scales remains challenging d
content: Halocarbons have hundreds- to thousands-of-times higher global warming potentials than CO2, and reducing some of these emissions is part of the Kigali Amendment. Quantifying these emissions at urban and regional scales remains challenging due to uncertainties in emission inventories and observation-based estimates. To constrain hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) emissions in one of Asia's most densely populated areas, a regional-scale experiment was conducted with several deliberate tracer-releases from the Seoul (South Korea) metropolitan area during 2024/2025. The compounds HFC-161 and HFO-1336mzz(E) were released as gaseous tracers under controlled conditions, and their dispersion was tracked along the plume trajectories using measurements from two flask-sampling and one in-situ-measurement site. The interpretation of observations was supported by tracer dispersion simulations using the atmospheric transport model FLEXPART. Applying the tracer ratio method, emissions of selected HFCs were determined for the Seoul metropolitan area. They were scaled up to national emissions using population density and then compared with the results of an independent inverse modelling study. The estimates over multiple releases and sites were 2.1±0.6 kt yr−1 for HFC-125, 2.0±0.5 kt yr−1 for HFC-134a, 0.55±0.1 kt yr−1 for HFC-143a, 1.4±0.4 kt yr−1 for HFC-152a, and 1.7±0.5 kt yr−1 for HFC-32. Our estimates agree with those of an independent inverse modelling study within the combined uncertainties. However, significant sampling-site-specific differences were observed for the various releases, presumably due to limitations in the method's applicability, complex meteorology, and technical challenges during some releases.

title: Contrasting Soils Reveal Conserved Setaria viridis Seed Endophyte Communities and Nitrogen‐Cycle Marker‐Gene Patterns
summary: Seed endophytes may act as microbial reservoirs during early plant establishment. Still, it remains unclear whether mature seed endophyte communities primarily reflect soil‐derived microbial inputs or become comparatively constrained within
content: Seed endophytes may act as microbial reservoirs during early plant establishment. Still, it remains unclear whether mature seed endophyte communities primarily reflect soil‐derived microbial inputs or become comparatively constrained within the seed endosphere. We grew Setaria viridis in two contrasting soil contexts, Negev agricultural soil and commercial PotMix, and compared bulk soil, rhizosphere, root, intact seed, and seed endophyte communities using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) quantification of 16S rRNA, nitrogenase‐associated nifH , and bacterial ammonia monooxygenase amoA genes. Soil context strongly affected plant growth and the bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root‐associated microbiomes, whereas seed endophyte communities were comparatively conserved across the two soil contexts. Seeds were enriched in genera with known diazotrophic representatives, showed higher relative nifH marker‐gene abundance than bulk soil, and had rare or undetectable amoA genes. These results indicate that the S. viridis seed endosphere is less responsive to soil context than the bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root‐associated communities. The enrichment of diazotroph‐associated taxa and higher relative nifH marker‐gene abundance suggest nitrogen‐fixation‐associated genetic potential but do not demonstrate active nitrogen fixation.

title: Understanding Fluorine Behavior Across Copper Processing Routes: Mineralogy, Thermodynamics, Process Integration, and Environmental Control—A Critical Review
source: Journal International Review of Research Studies
summary: Fluorine is a process-dependent impurity in copper ores and concentrates because its mineralogical occurrence controls whether it can be rejected during beneficiation, mobilized into acidic process liquors, or redistributed between condense
content: Fluorine is a process-dependent impurity in copper ores and concentrates because its mineralogical occurrence controls whether it can be rejected during beneficiation, mobilized into acidic process liquors, or redistributed between condensed and gaseous products during smelting. This critical review links fluorite, fluorapatite, fluorine-bearing silicates, and texturally associated phases to analytical quantification, comminution and flotation, aqueous speciation, hydrometallurgical and bioleaching responses, thermal transformations, and environmental management. A structured review of a reconciled 132-entry bibliography compares direct copper-system evidence with studies transferable from other mineral and wastewater systems. The analysis distinguishes total fluorine from soluble fluoride and phase-associated fluorine; thermodynamic feasibility from reaction kinetics; selective rejection from contaminant transfer; and laboratory feasibility from industrial implementation. An integrated selection framework centers on mineralogical deportment, copper recovery, fluoride mass balance closure, reagent consumption, corrosion exposure, residue stability, and process integration. The principal finding is that no universal defluorination technology is defensible across copper feeds: preconcentration is preferred for liberated fluorine-bearing gangue, targeted chemical conditioning may be useful for accessible fluoride phases, and robust gas, liquor, and residue management is required whenever fluorine enters downstream circuits. Evidence gaps include representative multi-stream fluorine mass balances, industrial smelter partition data, thermodynamic validation of concentrated electrolytes, and comparative techno-economic assessments.

title: Using a Gaussian process emulator to approximate short-term climate response patterns to greenhouse gas and aerosol forcings
summary: We present a Gaussian process emulator for estimating fast surface temperature response patterns to a range of different climate forcing agents, including both long-lived greenhouse gases and short-lived pollutants such as aerosols. This em
content: We present a Gaussian process emulator for estimating fast surface temperature response patterns to a range of different climate forcing agents, including both long-lived greenhouse gases and short-lived pollutants such as aerosols. This emulator is trained on simulations driven by perturbations to emissions (for short-lived pollutants) and concentrations (for long-lived greenhouse gases) using a full-complexity global climate model and predicts the response in the first five years after the forcing, at a small fraction of the computational cost. We outline the emulator design, including the choice of pollutant perturbations and the input space covered by the training data. We show that the emulator performs well in most regions of the chosen input space, except under very large aerosol perturbations. A global sensitivity analysis is carried out to characterize and understand emission-response relationships for each pollutant. We find similar large-scale patterns of sensitivity to aerosol pollutants released in different regions. Our work demonstrates the potential for rapid climate change projections subject to various climate forcing agents, focusing on the short-term response. This paves the way for the future development of more policy-relevant emulators, that can target decadal and multi-decadal timescales.

title: A framework for decomposing process noise in fineblanking
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: In fineblanking, a mass production process for often safety-critical components, maintaining high-quality sheared surfaces without tears across a tool maintenance cycle is essential. Current modeling techniques assume static process conditi
content: In fineblanking, a mass production process for often safety-critical components, maintaining high-quality sheared surfaces without tears across a tool maintenance cycle is essential. Current modeling techniques assume static process conditions and fail to capture the stochastic variations in real-world sensor data, termed process noise. This work introduces a framework for systematically attributing process noise, establishing an analysis chain from phenomena, through interpretable correlations, to latent driving factors. It combines quality evolution analysis, explainable predictive modeling (XGBoost with SHAP), and latent variable modeling (VAE variant). For 40,450 strokes across eight coils and 1,624 inspected parts at nine geometry features, regression on stroke count and a punch wear proxy shows features ranging from predominantly wear-associated ( $$R^2 \approx 0.74$$ ) to almost entirely unexplained by these trend variables ( $$R^2 \approx 0.02$$ ). For an aggregated tear indicator (relative tear frequency, mean 0.37), progressive coil-wise cross-validation on inspected samples yields a mean MAE of 0.108; errors peak at the first coil with exponential tear accumulation, a regime unseen in training. Restricting features to the shearing phase improves generalization and confirms physical plausibility. Two identified latent factors capture coil-related force offsets and progressive force curve changes, hypothesized to reflect material batch variation and wear dynamics. The framework offers a blueprint for physically attributing process variability in sheet-metal forming.

title: Molecular composition of wintertime haze over the northern Indian Ocean suggests extensive atmospheric processing during transport
summary: Each year during the winter period, a persistent haze forms over the Indian subcontinent and the northern Indian Ocean. This has been shown to influence regional warming, rainfall patterns and air quality. Previous studies have demonstrated
content: Each year during the winter period, a persistent haze forms over the Indian subcontinent and the northern Indian Ocean. This has been shown to influence regional warming, rainfall patterns and air quality. Previous studies have demonstrated that this haze is largely anthropogenic in origin, with its composition dominated by sulfate, organic compounds and black carbon. Nevertheless, to date, information about its composition has largely been limited to bulk chemical composition and low time-resolution data. Here, we aim to characterise aerosol composition over the Indian Ocean on the molecular level, in order to identify the impact of different sources and processing in this region. High-time-resolution measurements were conducted at the Maldives Climate Observatory, Hanimaadhoo (MCOH) using a Time-of-Flight Aerosol Mass Spectrometer (AMS) and Chemical Ionisation Mass Spectrometer with a Filter Inlet for Gases and Aerosols (FIGAERO-CIMS). Results showed a remarkably uniform composition, despite variability in source regions and total concentration, indicating strong regional mixing of air masses. Sulfate accounted for approximately 48 % of non-refractory sub-micron particulate mass. Eighteen sulfur-containing organic compounds were identified, some for the first time in this location. Tracers of some sources were identified in the organic mass spectrum. The organic aerosol was highly oxygenated, with dicarboxylic acids prominent among identified particle phase organic compounds. Our results show the strong influence of long-range transport on aerosol composition over the Indian Ocean, and are consistent with extensive atmospheric processing, including possible heterogeneous sulfate chemistry. This has important implications for understanding radiative forcing and aerosol-cloud interactions in South Asia.

title: Acidification in coastal waters of Adélie Land, Antarctica (1985–2025)
summary: Ocean acidification is expected to be particularly severe in Antarctic continental shelves due to enhanced anthropogenic carbon uptake in cold waters in response to rising atmospheric CO 2 , sea-ice retreat, freshening and climate-change fe
content: Ocean acidification is expected to be particularly severe in Antarctic continental shelves due to enhanced anthropogenic carbon uptake in cold waters in response to rising atmospheric CO 2 , sea-ice retreat, freshening and climate-change feedbacks. Models suggest that undersaturated conditions with respect to aragonite (Ω ar ), a major form of calcium carbonate formed by marine species, could be reached as soon as 2052 for austral winter. Here we present new ocean carbonate system observations from cruises conducted since 2010 in the Adélie Land coastal region in East Antarctica, along with data from a BCG-Argo float and results from a neural network model for the period 1985–2025. The region is a permanent CO 2 sink which was most pronounced since 2006. The CO 2 sink leads to an increase of surface water total CO 2 concentrations ( C T ) (+0.44 ± 0.01 µmolkg-1yr-1) and to a decrease of pH (−0.013 per decade) and Ω ar (−0.035 per decade) for the winter season. The lowest surface Ω ar of 1.2 was observed in winter 2024 from the float data, a critical limit for some marine species such as pteropods. A projection of the C T concentrations in the future, based on observed anthropogenic CO 2 concentrations and emissions scenarios, suggests that aragonite saturation state (Ω ar = 1) will occur in surface waters as soon as 2055 in the Adélie Land region, which is part of a larger area of East Antarctica proposed as a Marine Protected Area by the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources since the early 2010s.

title: Ground-truthing the application of compound-specific stable isotopes of amino acids to planktic foraminifera tests from Santa Barbara Basin
summary: Planktic foraminifera form shells that are preserved in ocean sediments and are used in a variety of paleoproxy and biostratigraphic applications. However, species-specific ecology can complicate the interpretation of planktic foraminifera-
content: Planktic foraminifera form shells that are preserved in ocean sediments and are used in a variety of paleoproxy and biostratigraphic applications. However, species-specific ecology can complicate the interpretation of planktic foraminifera-based proxies, and limited options exist for examining the ecology of extinct species. Here we apply test-bound compound-specific stable isotopes of amino acids (CSI-AA) to examine the trophic ecology of extant planktic foraminifera. We measure CSI-AA in planktic foraminifera shells collected in sediment traps from the Santa Barbara Basin, CA, specifically the three most abundant species in this region: Globigerina bulloides , Neogloboquadrina incompta , and Turborotalita quinqueloba . The nitrogen CSI-AA of all three species suggest that planktic foraminifera have metazoan-like metabolisms, and that trophic position estimates using CSI-AA are appropriate for planktic foraminifera. All three species had trophic positions near 2 (primary consumer), with no evidence for mixotrophy or photosymbionts. Carbon CSI-AA, in combination with a Bayesian stable isotope mixing model, indicates that the three species occupied separate niches based on diet. Globigerina bulloides fed opportunistically on all groups of phytoplankton available in Santa Barbara Basin, adjusting its diet with seasonal changes in phytoplankton assemblage. Turborotalita quinqueloba specialized in diatoms but consumed some heterotrophic bacteria and cyanobacteria. Neogloboquadrina incompta consumed primarily heterotrophic bacteria and some dinoflagellates. Our results align with the current understanding of each species' ecology while further defining their niches. Our findings suggest that CSI-AA is a promising tool for understanding the trophic ecology of planktic foraminifera, and we make recommendations for future applications of CSI-AA to fossil specimens.

title: Significant albedo-induced cooling effects across tropical and subtropical dryland biomes
summary: Terrestrial ecosystems can significantly regulate climate through carbon uptake and alterations in surface albedo. However, current climate mitigation assessments largely focus on carbon sinks while overlooking albedo-induced radiative effe
content: Terrestrial ecosystems can significantly regulate climate through carbon uptake and alterations in surface albedo. However, current climate mitigation assessments largely focus on carbon sinks while overlooking albedo-induced radiative effects. We developed an integrated framework to quantify the net climate effect of global terrestrial ecosystems from 2001 to 2019 by combining net ecosystem productivity with albedo-induced radiative forcing. We estimated the net equivalent carbon dioxide stock change, which incorporates both net cumulative carbon uptake equivalent (NCCE) and the emission equivalent of shortwave forcing. Results show that global terrestrial ecosystems generated a net cooling effect of 397.52 Gt CO 2 e during the study period. Among biomes, tropical and subtropical grasslands, savannas and shrublands, and deserts and xeric shrublands, contributed a cooling effect of 95.33 Gt CO 2 e due to increased albedo, nearly one-quarter of the total NCCE across the 14 biomes, largely driven by declines in photosynthetic vegetation and soil drying in Land use and land cover non-conversion areas. These findings provide new perspectives for re-evaluating the climate value of terrestrial ecosystems and a scientific basis for incorporating surface albedo into future nature-based solutions for climate mitigation.

title: Performance and damage mechanisms of dispersion-strengthened tungsten under H-mode plasma in DIII-D
summary: Dispersion strengthened tungsten (DSW) alloys are promising materials for plasma facing components, displaying improved mechanical properties and microstructure stability compared to pure tungsten. In this work, the performance of DSW reinf
content: Dispersion strengthened tungsten (DSW) alloys are promising materials for plasma facing components, displaying improved mechanical properties and microstructure stability compared to pure tungsten. In this work, the performance of DSW reinforced with 1 wt% transition-metal carbide (TaC, TiC, or ZrC) has been examined under H-mode plasma in the DIII-D tokamak. DSW samples were mounted both flush with the divertor floor and at a 10 ∘ angle towards the incoming plasma fluxes to further increase the heat and particle loading. To simulate the impact of prolonged tokamak operation, similar plasma exposures were repeated on two additional sets of DSW samples: one set pre-implanted with 10 22 m − 2 helium, and another set heated in-situ to an additional 500 ∘ C. Flush mounted samples exhibited good surface stability, with no evidence of melting or cracking regardless of composition or treatment. Carbon redeposition was observed on most samples, likely due to the graphite environment of DIII-D. Under coupled thermal loading and helium implantation, surface nanostructuring developed in some DSW samples; however, DSW containing tantalum dispersion phases showed strong resistance to such surface modification. In contrast, obvious surface melting was observed on 10 ∘ angled samples containing TaC and ZrC dispersoids, likely associated with dispersoid oxidation during fabrication, which reduced thermal conductivity and promoted elevated surface temperatures during plasma exposure. The grain morphology of DSW containing TiC remained largely unchanged, although near-surface dispersoids on the angled TiC sample were missing after plasma exposure. The loss is associated with oxidation of the dispersoids during fabrication, followed by sublimation during plasma exposure. Through systematic comparison of DSW performance under H mode plasma conditions, this study identifies key degradation mechanisms and highlights strategies to improve the performance of DSW as plasma facing materials.

title: Hidden parasites in diatom blooms: high infection rates of Leptocylindrus danicus by the oomycete Miracula nipponica
summary: Parasitic fungi and fungal-like organisms are increasingly recognized as key players influencing diatom dynamics and carbon fluxes in aquatic ecosystems; however, their diversity and ecological roles in coastal environments remain poorly un
content: Parasitic fungi and fungal-like organisms are increasingly recognized as key players influencing diatom dynamics and carbon fluxes in aquatic ecosystems; however, their diversity and ecological roles in coastal environments remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the diversity of fungi and fungal-like organisms over an annual cycle, encompassing spring diatom blooms, in Sagami Bay, Japan, using 18S rDNA metabarcoding, and quantified parasitic infection of diatoms during the spring bloom of May 2022 using fluorescence microscopy and single-spore PCR. The composition of fungi and fungal-like organisms exhibited pronounced seasonal and vertical variations, and the relative read abundances of Chytridiomycota and Oomycota increased during diatom bloom periods. We found that the oomycete Miracula nipponica , recently described from Sagami Bay, infected the bloom-forming diatom Leptocylindrus danicus during the spring bloom. Infection rates varied with depth and reached up to 20.5% of living cells at 10 m (95% confidence interval 17.5–23.9%) and 40% of empty frustules at the surface (95% confidence interval 24.6–57.7%) during bloom conditions. These findings provide quantitative evidence that an oomycete parasite can reach high infection levels in a coastal diatom bloom, and suggest that oomycetes, a previously underappreciated group of parasites, may affect diatom population dynamics and the fate of diatom-derived organic matter in marine ecosystems.

title: Dual-encapsulated liposomal vitamin C increases comparative oral exposure in a randomised crossover study in healthy adults
summary: This study characterised DELT, a rice-protein-associated dual-encapsulation vitamin C powder, and compared its in vitro properties and short-term pharmacokinetic profile with conventional liposomal and reference vitamin C formulations. Phys
content: This study characterised DELT, a rice-protein-associated dual-encapsulation vitamin C powder, and compared its in vitro properties and short-term pharmacokinetic profile with conventional liposomal and reference vitamin C formulations. Physicochemical characterisation included particle size, polydispersity, surface charge, morphology and solid-state analysis. Vitamin C content, operational encapsulation efficiency, in vitro release and accelerated stability were also evaluated. An exploratory, randomised, double-blind, three-treatment, three-period crossover study was conducted in 12 healthy adults following a single oral dose containing 350 mg vitamin C. Re-dispersed DELT had a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 210.0 ± 33.4 nm and a polydispersity index of 0.025. Measured vitamin C content was 71.3 ± 1.0% w/w, and operational encapsulation efficiency was 87.8%. In phosphate buffer at pH 6.8, DELT released 35.0 ± 3.5% of its vitamin C by 8 h, compared with 78.8 ± 4.6% for unformulated vitamin C. During 8 months of accelerated storage at 40 °C/65% relative humidity, vitamin C content changed from 71.23% to 71.17% w/w. In the clinical study, mean baseline-corrected maximum plasma concentrations were 16.90 ± 1.90 µg/mL for DELT, 9.92 ± 1.10 µg/mL for conventional liposomal vitamin C and 2.62 ± 0.76 µg/mL for reference vitamin C. Corresponding areas under the concentration–time curve up to the last measured time point were 126.32 ± 19.60, 68.11 ± 8.46 and 11.43 ± 2.60 µg·h/mL, respectively. Pairwise comparisons were statistically significant ( p < 0.0001). These exploratory findings demonstrate differences in formulation characteristics, release behaviour and measured short-term plasma exposure. Larger studies with longer sampling, validated analytical procedures and compositionally matched comparators are required to confirm the pharmacokinetic findings and investigate the contribution of individual formulation components. Trial registration : Clinical Trials Registry–India, CTRI/2025/12/098688.

title: A Beginner’s Guide to Sustainable Energy Systems Modeling and Optimization
summary: A Beginner’s Guide to Sustainable Energy Systems Modeling and Optimization is a hands-on, tutorial-style reference designed to equip engineers, planners, researchers, and energy professionals with practical tools and methods to tackle energ
content: A Beginner’s Guide to Sustainable Energy Systems Modeling and Optimization is a hands-on, tutorial-style reference designed to equip engineers, planners, researchers, and energy professionals with practical tools and methods to tackle energy planning and decarbonization challenges. The book provides a step-by-step guide to building, analyzing, and optimizing sustainable energy systems—starting from fundamental concepts and progressing through applications using widely accessible platforms like Microsoft Excel, LINGO, P-graph, and Python. By illustrating real-world energy systems, supply chain, and regional/national energy planning problems through a consistent structure across chapters, this book demystifies the modeling and optimization process, helping readers gain confidence in applying what they learn to their specific domains. Bridges the gap between engineering, policy, and sustainability. Offers clear explanations, structured examples, and direct pathways to practical outcomes. Walks the reader through solving the same three types of energy problems using different tools throughout the book, reinforcing learning and enabling direct comparison. Requires no programming experience needed to get started: starts with user-friendly and accessible platforms and gradually introduces more advanced tools. Each section ends with a practical evaluation of the strengths, limitations, and ideal use-cases for the featured tool, providing foundational exposure to readers about when and why to use each platform. Features case studies at three levels of energy problems, ranging from energy system design problems, supply chain synthesis problems to regional/national energy planning problems. Whether transitioning from spreadsheet modeling or looking to expand their toolkit to more sophisticated or open-source platforms, professional engineers in energy systems design, policy, and industrial decarbonization will find this guide particularly valuable for generating data-driven insights, testing different planning scenarios, and optimizing for cost, emissions, and energy efficiency.

title: Life-cycle climate impact of Lepidium campestre (field cress) oil for HVO: Attributional baseline and consequential scenarios for co-product pathways and Nordic land availability
summary: Hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) is central to European Union transport decarbonisation, yet new temperate oilseeds require robust evidence on climate performance and credible co-product pathways. This study evaluates field cress ( Lepidium
content: Hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) is central to European Union transport decarbonisation, yet new temperate oilseeds require robust evidence on climate performance and credible co-product pathways. This study evaluates field cress ( Lepidium campestre ), a newly domesticated Nordic oilseed suited to short-season regions. Under an attributional model aligned with the Renewable Energy Directive (RED), the cradle-to-gate HVO footprint is 34.1 g CO₂-eq MJ⁻¹ , a 63.7% reduction relative to the fossil comparator (94 g CO₂-eq MJ⁻¹) and slightly below the ≥ 65% threshold. A consequential model then quantifies market responses to co-product valorisation, assigning the full upstream burden to the oil for a baseline of 104 g CO₂-eq MJ⁻¹ . Routing press cake to animal feed lowers this to 58.7 g CO₂-eq MJ⁻¹ at full substitution through avoided soybean meal, or 72.6 g CO₂-eq MJ⁻¹ once manure management and soil-carbon return are included. Sequential nitrogen–phosphorus–potassium recovery reaches 74.2 g CO₂-eq MJ⁻¹ , with nitrogen recovery shifting from burden to benefit under the low-carbon Swedish grid. Anaerobic digestion, combining biomethane, avoided-fertiliser, and digestate soil-carbon credits, reaches 65.3 g CO₂-eq MJ⁻¹ , a substantial reduction, though the system remains a net emitter once soil-carbon credits are rigorously bounded. Cultivating field cress on out-of-production fallow land also improves the soil-carbon balance: centennial soil-carbon modelling shows fallow land remaining at its equilibrium (~4.5 kg C m⁻²), whereas a field cress–barley intercrop acts as a net sink, accumulating ~1.8 kg C m⁻² more than the fallow over a century (reaching ~6.3 kg C m⁻²). Monte Carlo and Sobol analyses confirm robustness, with oil content the dominant driver of variance.

title: A porosity threshold shifts rare-earth element uptake mechanisms in deep-sea bioapatite
summary: Deep-sea bioapatite is a major sink for rare earth elements and yttrium (REY), which serve as key paleoenvironmental proxies, yet REY uptake mechanisms remain elusive. Integrating microstructures, X-ray micro-computed tomography, high-resol
content: Deep-sea bioapatite is a major sink for rare earth elements and yttrium (REY), which serve as key paleoenvironmental proxies, yet REY uptake mechanisms remain elusive. Integrating microstructures, X-ray micro-computed tomography, high-resolution elemental mapping, in situ geochemistry, and porosity-based modeling of fossil fish teeth and bones from the northwestern Pacific Ocean, South Pacific Ocean, Indian Ocean, and South China Sea, we identify a universal porosity threshold of ∼7%. Below this threshold, REY uptake is kinetic via diffusion-limited adsorption onto isolated pore surfaces, driving disequilibrium with ambient water; above it, bioapatite approaches equilibrium with pore waters via extensive lattice substitution. Our findings establish porosity as a primary intrinsic control on REY uptake and provide a mechanistic framework for evaluating the reliability of bioapatite REY proxies.

title: Crop-specific manure nitrogen and phosphorus management in US croplands from 1970 to 2025
summary: Manure is the largest organic nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) input to US cropland, but existing long-term data products often estimate manure from broad livestock classes that overlook herd structure and do not resolve crop-specific manage
content: Manure is the largest organic nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) input to US cropland, but existing long-term data products often estimate manure from broad livestock classes that overlook herd structure and do not resolve crop-specific management. This masks two linked processes that matter for nutrient budgets and loss-risk assessments: livestock-based top-down demographic change in manure production and agronomic-surveyed bottom-up variation in timing, method, and treated-area intensity of manure application. Here, we reconstructed a spatially explicit manure N and P management dataset for the contiguous United States by combining an age-group manure production framework, county livestock distributions, state-level crop-specific manure management surveys, treated-area information, and crop distribution maps. The management product reports county-level crop-specific manure N and P use rates on treated area and on all cropland for 1970–2025. Age-group manure production increased from 4.7 to 7.4 Tg N yr−1 and from 0.73 to 1.3 Tg P yr−1 between 1970 and 2021, then declined to 7.0 Tg N yr−1 and 1.2 Tg P yr−1 by 2025. The crop-use application component increased from 0.79 to 1.4 Tg N yr−1 and from 0.25 to 0.53 Tg P yr−1 between 1970 and 2025 (county-crop allocation for corn, soybean, winter wheat, spring wheat, cotton, sorghum, rice, barley, durum wheat, other crops, and cropland pasture), after peaking around 2021–2022. Cross-dataset comparison shows that, among existing national data products, this top-down and bottom-up reconciliation is consistent to the bottom-up crop-management constraints while placing manure N near the lower range of existing products and substantially reducing manure P relative to broad livestock classes estimates. This dataset supports crop-specific nutrient budgets, gridded crop and water-quality modeling, and management-resolved assessments of manure N and P loss risk.

title: Edge ion heat flux as a key parameter of the L-H transition: insights from ion and electron heating experiments on TCV
summary: We investigate the role of the edge ion heat flux $Q_\mathrm{i,edge}$ in the L--H transition on TCV, comparing purely electron-heated (ECRH) and dominantly ion-heated (low-energy NBI) plasmas. The two heating schemes produce different $P_\m
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: We investigate the role of the edge ion heat flux $Q_\mathrm{i,edge}$ in the L--H transition on TCV, comparing purely electron-heated (ECRH) and dominantly ion-heated (low-energy NBI) plasmas. The two heating schemes produce different $P_\mathrm{L-H}$ trends. ECRH discharges exhibit the characteristic non-monotonic density dependence, while NBI discharges show a monotonically increasing power threshold with values up to three times lower at comparable densities. However, when expressed in terms of the edge ion heat flux, both datasets show a monotonic density dependence even at low density, where the electron--ion collisional energy exchange is inefficient, suggesting that the ion heat flux, not the total loss power, plays a key role in the physics of the L--H transition. These results extend the critical edge ion heat flux criterion to a carbon-wall device and to dominantly ion-heated conditions, and support $Q_\mathrm{i,edge}$-based approaches as a physics-grounded complement to conventional $P_\mathrm{L-H}$ scalings.

title: PHYSIOLOGY AND EXTRACELLULAR ELECTRON TRANSFER MECHANISMS IN IRON-OXIDIZING BACTERIA
source: Library, Museums and Press - UDSpace (University of Delaware)
summary: Iron-oxidizing bacteria are important drivers of iron cycling across environments, yet the specific role of iron in physiology is not always known. Most existing studies focus on iron as an electron donor during chemoautotrophic growth of i
content: Iron-oxidizing bacteria are important drivers of iron cycling across environments, yet the specific role of iron in physiology is not always known. Most existing studies focus on iron as an electron donor during chemoautotrophic growth of iron oxidizers, but the role of iron in the metabolism of chemoheterotrophs remains ambiguous. Simultaneous growth on iron and organics is possible in energy mixotrophy among heterotrophs. However, mixotrophy in iron oxidizers is difficult to demonstrate because the capacity for iron oxidation does not demonstrate that the electrons are channeled into the electron transport chain for growth. Leptothrix cholodnii SP-6 is a filamentous organoheterotrophic iron oxidizer present in iron-rich environments. SP-6 is a model organism because it is an easily culturable isolate, with its whole genome sequenced and publicly available. These features of L. cholodnii SP-6 enable exploration of the mechanisms of iron oxidation and extracellular electron transfer (EET) pathways. EET pathways could also enable these iron oxidizers to grow on non-ferrous solid substrates like biochar. Biochar has an electron-storage capacity that allows it to serve as both a donor and an acceptor. The facultative iron oxidizer Sideroxydans lithotrophicus ES-1 can grow on biochar as an electron donor, thereby enabling investigation of EET pathways. Understanding the EET pathways likely involved in biochar-microbe interactions elucidates how biochar could affect microbial communities and soil chemistry, and facilitate alternative metabolic pathways that could influence carbon and iron cycling in the soil. This dissertation addresses knowledge gaps regarding iron's contributions to growth and the underlying mechanisms of extracellular electron transfer pathways for ferrous and non-ferrous substrates. L. cholodnii SP-6 is a filamentous sheath-forming iron oxidizer that can oxidize manganese and iron and has tolerance for elevated iron levels (up to 500 μM). Moreover, L. cholodnii SP-6 iron oxidation mechanisms remain elusive because the genome lacks the validated iron oxidase genes cyc2 and mtoA. This presents an opportunity to study proteins involved in the novel iron-oxidizing pathways of L. cholodnii SP-6. Although L. cholodnii SP-6 is highly responsive to organics, its genome encodes the capacity to fix carbon, suggesting the possibility of using inorganic carbon alongside organics, or carbon mixotrophy. We investigated growth, inorganic and organic carbon utilization, and the expression of potential iron oxidases under different iron and carbon treatments. Our results demonstrated live cells of L. cholodnii SP-6 catalyzed the oxidation of ferrous iron, while killed and abiotic controls did not. Growth experiments showed mixotrophic energy metabolism, as Fe(II) conferred a growth benefit under low-carbon conditions. title: Mountain carbon budgets miss cryosphere hazard events
summary: Warming is destabilizing the mountain cryosphere and triggering more frequent hazard events. These hazards mobilize large stores of carbon as well as rock, ice and water. Yet mountain carbon budgets largely overlook this flux, because routi
content: Warming is destabilizing the mountain cryosphere and triggering more frequent hazard events. These hazards mobilize large stores of carbon as well as rock, ice and water. Yet mountain carbon budgets largely overlook this flux, because routine monitoring rarely operates at the time, location and resolution that hazard events demand. We argue that cryosphere hazards should be treated as carbon events and set out how to close the gap. Here, cryosphere hazard events are mass movements in glacial and permafrost terrain whose onset is abrupt relative to gradual degradation, together with the cascades they trigger (Ding et al., 2021;Zhang et al., 2025). They range from rock-ice avalanches and glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) lasting hours to retrogressive thaw slumps that develop within days to years as a form of abrupt thaw (Turetsky et al., 2020).At high elevations, warming is often amplified (Pepin et al., 2015(Pepin et al., , 2025)). Global glacier mass-loss rates rose by 36 ± 10% between 2000-2011and 2012-2023(Zemp et al., 2025)), and mountain permafrost is warming (Wu and Zhang, 2008;Noetzli et al., 2024) and thawing abruptly (Turetsky et al., 2020). GLOF frequency in the Third Pole has risen since 1980 (Zhang et al., 2023), and global GLOFs from moraine-dammed lakes increased from 5.2 to 15.2 per year between 1981-1990and 2011-2020(Zhang et al., 2025)). Retrogressive thaw slumps are spreading rapidly in alpine permafrost (Xia et al., 2024), driving cascading damage locally and downstream (Ding et al., 2021;Shugar et al., 2021). Existing frameworks recognize erosion, lateral transport, and outgassing as carbon pathways (Chapin et al., 2006;Hilton and West, 2020;Regnier et al., 2022), but lack a way to quantify hazard-driven mobilization and trace its fate (Figure 1a).A complete net ecosystem carbon budget needs vertical exchange from eddy covariance and chambers, and lateral export and outgassing from river and lake sampling (Chapin et al., 2006;Keenan and Williams, 2018), yet these observations rarely capture brief events or hillslope-channel transport.Three monitoring problems limit how cryosphere hazards enter carbon budgets. Temporal aliasing means periodic monitoring misses an event when the sampling interval exceeds a hazard-driven concentration peak. Extrapolation error means that, once a hazard resets sediment and carbon availability, pre-event concentration-discharge relationships no longer predict post-event fluxes. Material selectivity means that sampling of dissolved and suspended loads excludes carbon moved as woody debris, coarse bedload, or buried in deposits. No single method can constrain these fluxes: atmospheric observations cannot resolve lateral transfers, and satellite erosion detection cannot quantify the concentration or reactivity of displaced material. title: The intracellular respiratory burst of plant immunity signaling
summary: Pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) is classically associated with an extracellular respiratory burst generated by plasma membrane-localized NADPH oxidases (RBOHs). Here, we identify an ancient RBOH-independent intracellular respiratory burst
content: Pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) is classically associated with an extracellular respiratory burst generated by plasma membrane-localized NADPH oxidases (RBOHs). Here, we identify an ancient RBOH-independent intracellular respiratory burst driven by central carbon metabolism. Using in vivo biosensors, we demonstrate that receptor activation rapidly triggers sugar catabolism via glycolysis, shifting the NAD pool toward its reduced state. This redox pressure drives a burst in mitochondrial respiratory flux and oxygen consumption. Consequent mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production activates ANAC017-mediated retrograde signaling to induce broader PTI gene expression. This intracellular respiratory burst represents a conserved early hallmark of immunity across land plants and links cellular carbon status to immune activation. It reveals functional parallels between plant immune metabolism and metabolic reprogramming during mammalian immune-cell activation.

title: Decentralized biorefineries for sustainable biochemical production: Techno-economic insights into agro-residue valorization and rural industrialization
summary: Lignocellulosic agro-residues are an underutilized source of biomass for sustainable biochemical production, especially in agricultural economies like India. This review critically examines the potential of decentralized biorefineries for t
content: Lignocellulosic agro-residues are an underutilized source of biomass for sustainable biochemical production, especially in agricultural economies like India. This review critically examines the potential of decentralized biorefineries for the conversion of agricultural residues such as rice straw, wheat straw, sugarcane bagasse, cotton stalks, and coconut biomass to value-added products. It assesses feedstock availability and composition, pre-treatment strategies, conversion pathways, downstream processing, and techno-economic aspects of xylitol, furfural, levulinic acid, nanocellulose, and lignin-derived chemical production. Potential feedstock-product combinations are discussed in terms of biomass composition, regional availability, and conversion requirements. The techno-economic discussion is based on published assessments with available economic indicators, including corncob-based xylitol production and the co-production of ethanol with xylitol or furfural from corn stover. The evidence reviewed suggests that high-value biochemical products could offer attractive revenue opportunities per unit of biomass, but profitability is dependent on conversion yields, recovery and purity of saleable product, plant capacity, capital and operating expenditure, feedstock logistics, and market conditions. Differences in feedstocks, process configurations, production scales, and economic assessment boundaries mean no blanket conclusion can be drawn that decentralized biochemical pathways are more profitable than fuel-oriented systems. The review also includes the models of rural deployment based on the aggregation of biomass, local entrepreneurship, and industrial cooperation. Key barriers are process complexity, scale-up, feedstock logistics, market uncertainty, and policy constraints. Future progress will demand modular process design, digital optimization, integrated resource recovery, and transparent, harmonized techno-economic and life-cycle assessments. In general, decentralized lignocellulosic biorefineries can be a potential route for the valorization of agro-residues and rural bioeconomy development, provided that technical performance, economic viability, and environmental impacts are confirmed under specific conditions.

title: Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in a tropical montane forest in Ecuador under environmental change: Isotopic and stoichiometric assessments
summary: Gelöste organische Substanz (DOM) koppelt den Kohlenstoff- (C), Stickstoff- (N) und Phosphorkreislauf von Waldökosystemen und trägt sie mit dem Abfluss aus. Als mobiler, teilweise bioverfügbarer Anteil der organischen Bodensubstanz reagiert
content: Gelöste organische Substanz (DOM) koppelt den Kohlenstoff- (C), Stickstoff- (N) und Phosphorkreislauf von Waldökosystemen und trägt sie mit dem Abfluss aus. Als mobiler, teilweise bioverfügbarer Anteil der organischen Bodensubstanz reagiert DOM sensibel auf Umweltveränderungen. Dennoch sind Zusammensetzung und Verhalten in tropischen Bergwäldern kaum erforscht. Die Wälder am Rande des Amazonasbeckens im Süden Ecuadors waren einem steigenden Stickstoffeintrag aus dem Verbrennen von Amazonas-Biomasse, einem stetigen Phosphoreintrag durch Staub, häufigeren warmen Tagen und zunehmend trockenen Bedingungen ausgesetzt. Ich untersuchte DOM entlang des Wasserpfads vom Freilandniederschlag über Kronendurchlass, Stammabfluss, Streusickerwasser und die Bodenlösung des Mineralbodens bis zum Bachabfluss mittels dreier komplementärer Ansätze: der Kohlenstoffisotopenzusammensetzung der DOM und der Stickstoffisotopenzusammensetzung des gesamten gelösten Stickstoffs (TDN), jeweils über vier Jahre (2013–2016), sowie der zeitlichen Entwicklung der Konzentrationen, Frachten und stöchiometrischen Verhältnisse von DOC, gelöstem organischem N (DON) und gelöstem organischem P (DOP) über 25 Jahre (1998–2023). Die δ13C-Werte waren im Freilandniederschlag am höchsten und nahmen zum Streusickerwasser ab, da isotopisch leichte Verbindungen aus Blättern und Rinde gelöst wurden. Sie nahmen in der Bodenlösung des Mineralbodens zu, wo Wurzeln und Wurzelexsudate zur DOM beitrugen, während die isotopisch leichtere Fraktion bevorzugt sorbiert und mineralisiert wurde. Da δ13C-Werte und C/N-Verhältnisse der DOM nicht konsistent zusammenhingen, lieferten beide Messungen unabhängige Informationen. Die δ15N-Werte des TDN identifizierten Stickstoffquellen und -senken. Das Kronendach hielt isotopisch schweren N zurück und gab isotopisch leichteres Nitrat und DON ab, sodass der Kronendurchlass leichter war als der Freilandniederschlag. Die δ15N-Werte stiegen dann zum Streusickerwasser an, aufgrund der Auswaschung isotopisch schweren DONs, und nahmen im mineralischen Oberboden ab, da DOM und Ammonium zurückgehalten und Nitrat ausgewaschen wurde. Mit zunehmender Bodentiefe zum Bachabfluss stiegen sie erneut, aufgrund der Denitrifikation isotopisch leichten Stickstoffs. Über die 25 Jahre stiegen die Konzentrationen und Frachten von DON und DOP an, während die DOC/DON- und DOC/DOP-Verhältnisse abnahmen. DOP war jedoch im Freilandniederschlag, in der Bodenlösung und im Bachabfluss nicht nachweisbar. Die δ13C- und δ15N-Werte stiegen in der Festphase parallel an, was einen gekoppelten C- und N-Umsatz widerspiegelt, variierten jedoch unabhängig in der DOM. Insgesamt beleuchteten die drei Ansätze die Quellen, Senken und Transformationen von DOC und TDN. Kohlenstoff- und Stickstoffkreislauf waren in der gelösten Phase weniger eng gekoppelt als in der Festphase, und das Waldökosystem schien auf eine Stickstoffsättigung zuzusteuern, bei der N zunehmend ausgetragen und P zurückgehalten wird. title: Autumn overcompensation following post-drought rewetting advances spring phenology
summary: Global warming and shifting precipitation regimes are increasing the frequency and intensity of post-drought rewetting events, with potentially persistent consequences for forest phenology. Spring phenology is commonly attributed to winter
content: Global warming and shifting precipitation regimes are increasing the frequency and intensity of post-drought rewetting events, with potentially persistent consequences for forest phenology. Spring phenology is commonly attributed to winter and spring temperatures, yet whether recovery from drought during the preceding growing season carries over to regulate subsequent spring phenology remains poorly understood. Here, combining ground observations of 535 tree species across 2,939 sites, three satellite-derived phenology products from 1981 to 2020 across the Northern Hemisphere and controlled post-drought rewetting experiments, we show that rewetting after drought delays autumn phenology and prolongs photosynthetic carbon acquisition, generating an overcompensatory recovery response that advances subsequent spring phenology. This cross-seasonal effect was associated with enhanced carbon gain and storage during post-drought recovery, suggesting that carbon acquired during autumn overcompensation carries over across seasons to promote earlier spring reactivation. CMIP6 projections indicate that this cross-seasonal legacy is likely to persist throughout the twenty-first century and strengthen under greater warming. Our findings identify autumn overcompensation as a previously underappreciated mechanism linking post-drought recovery to subsequent spring phenology, revealing how recovery from hydroclimatic extremes can reorganize seasonal carbon acquisition and phenological timing across years.

title: Technical note: Implementing comprehensive sources and sinks of atmospheric nitrous acid in the Community Earth System Model version 2 (CESM2)
summary: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important tropospheric molecule, influencing the budget of many critical air pollutants and climate forcers. HONO has complicated primary (direct emission) and secondary (chemical production) sources, while its los
content: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important tropospheric molecule, influencing the budget of many critical air pollutants and climate forcers. HONO has complicated primary (direct emission) and secondary (chemical production) sources, while its loss is predominantly controlled by photolysis and deposition. Despite its importance, HONO is not included in many atmospheric and Earth system models, e.g., Community Earth System Model version 2 (CESM2). Here, we reviewed the laboratory and field constraints on atmospheric HONO sources and sinks along with the ranges of critical parameters. We implemented the most critical processes of HONO into the CESM2, including direct emissions (vehicle, ship, biomass burning, and soil), chemical production (homogeneous, nitrogen dioxide uptake on aerosol, nitrogen dioxide uptake on ground surfaces including land, ocean, and ice/snow, as well as iodide-enhanced nitrate photolysis), chemical loss (mainly photolysis), and deposition. Based on our model evaluation, we proposed recommended parameter settings (lower-limit, preferred, and higher-limit) to capture the magnitude and the range of atmospheric HONO abundance. The CESM2 with preferred configurations simulated an annual average surface HONO mixing ratio of 66.0 pptv and a global tropospheric burden of 20.4 Gg N; the simulated HONO levels showed evident spatio-temporal variations, peaking during boreal summer months and over southern Asia. Chemical production prevailed as the dominant HONO source, while photolysis was the main HONO loss. We present the first implementation of HONO-related processes in CESM2 and highlight the need to include HONO processes in future atmospheric and Earth system models to dynamically simulate HONO abundance and its variations.

title: Asymmetric Tourism–Carbon Sink Causality in Tropical Islands: A Geographical Pattern Causality Analysis of Hainan, China
summary: Tourism development and carbon-sink conservation on tropical islands are often framed as a trade-off, yet their spatial causal structure remains poorly understood. Using Hainan, China’s only tropical-island province and an International Tou
content: Tourism development and carbon-sink conservation on tropical islands are often framed as a trade-off, yet their spatial causal structure remains poorly understood. Using Hainan, China’s only tropical-island province and an International Tourism Island, this study applies the Geographical Pattern Causality (GPC) model to 2025 POI kernel-density and net primary productivity (NPP) datasets. While conventional linear methods detect no meaningful association, GPC reveals a robust directional asymmetry: vegetation carbon sinks exert a significantly stronger spatial organizing effect on tourism layout than tourism facilities do on carbon sinks. The dominant causal type is negative for the direction from carbon sinks to tourism facilities, indicating that high-purity carbon-sink cores correspond to opposing local spatial patterns in tourism-facility density; it is positive for the direction from tourism facilities to carbon sinks, reflecting local co-variation within developed tourism mosaics. The directional asymmetry is robust across all tested parameter combinations, although the specific causal subtype labels are parameter-sensitive. Furthermore, pixel-level analyses demonstrate that positive causal strength differs significantly across density zones, while the proportion of positive-causality pixels exhibits only weak density dependence. These findings reframe the tourism–carbon-sink relationship from a simplistic trade-off to an asymmetric spatial coupling, supporting a vegetation-carbon-sink-pattern-first perspective. The results inform one-place-one-policy governance for Hainan and comparable tropical-island destinations, emphasizing that spatial interventions must account for the baseline’s organizing role. Because the analysis relies on a static spatial snapshot, these causal-type labels represent spatial-pattern associations and require future temporal validation.

title: The anti-colonial politics of vernacular desire: Gay goondas and publishing deviance
summary: This article develops a media history of vernacular queer worldmaking by reading Badmash Darpan (1885) as a practice-ensemble of performance, circulation, and framing. Attributed to Teg Ali, the pamphlet adapts Perso-Urdu ghazal conventions
content: This article develops a media history of vernacular queer worldmaking by reading Badmash Darpan (1885) as a practice-ensemble of performance, circulation, and framing. Attributed to Teg Ali, the pamphlet adapts Perso-Urdu ghazal conventions into a Banaras Bhojpuri idiom that stages male–male attachment as publicly repeatable through affective excess—camp bravado, culinary erotics, rivalry, injury, and devotional slippage. I argue that this aesthetic-social method is inseparable from the text’s publication strategy. By exploiting the paratextual and bureaucratic demands of colonial print culture, the pamphlet solicits ethnographic attention and converts the conditions of scrutiny into a pathway for preservation and afterlife.
