Drawing on close reading and literary-historical recovery, and situating the pamphlet alongside Banaras songbooks, Bharatendu Harishchandra’s ‘ Mushaira ’, and later twentieth-century citations, I show how authorship and deviance are performed across a relay that links oral performance to print, and print to archive. The goonda persona crystallizes a vernacular politics of refusal that withholds interpretive closure while making contact. The article thus offers a model of vernacular print as a relay mechanism within a broader performance ecology of queer endurance.

title: Mechanisms of Dissimilarity in Turbulent Transport of Momentum and Heat in the Vegetation Roughness Sublayer
summary: This paper presents an observational analysis of the kinematic and dynamical mechanisms underlying the dissimilarity in turbulent transport of momentum and heat fluxes in the vegetation roughness sublayer (RSL). Using eddy-covariance measur
content: This paper presents an observational analysis of the kinematic and dynamical mechanisms underlying the dissimilarity in turbulent transport of momentum and heat fluxes in the vegetation roughness sublayer (RSL). Using eddy-covariance measurements above a tall Amazon forest canopy, the results show that the transport efficiency (correlation coefficient) of momentum is higher than that of heat even under near-neutral conditions, in contrast to the traditional assumption of a similar momentum--scalar transport in this regime. Quadrant analysis reveals that the reduced efficiency of momentum transport under both unstable and stable conditions is driven by a weakening of downgradient fluxes (primarily sweep events) and strengthening of countergradient interactions, while the increased efficiency of heat under unstable conditions is mostly driven by strengthening of ejections within buoyant plumes. Besides bulk transport efficiencies, lagged cross-correlations indicate that small-scale eddies in the inertial subrange have negligible contribution to net momentum transport, but otherwise actively transport heat fluxes across all stability regimes. Consequently, momentum exchange occurs through larger, more organized motions that exhibit longer decorrelation timescales (eddy lifetimes) than heat-carrying eddies in the RSL. An analysis of the steady-state flux budgets links this contrast in eddy lifetimes to the pressure-scrambling mechanisms that act as the primary sink for both fluxes, where flux relaxation timescales estimated through a Rotta closure closely follow the observed decorrelation timescales and suggest that pressure--temperature-gradient interactions decorrelate the heat flux more rapidly than pressure--strain interactions destroy momentum flux.

title: Insensitivity of the North Pacific oxygen-deficient zone to recent ice age cycle climate changes
summary: The ocean’s oxygen-deficient zones are hotspots of biogeochemical reactions. An important example is water-column denitrification, a process that removes biologically available nitrogen from the ocean. Denitrification discriminates against
content: The ocean’s oxygen-deficient zones are hotspots of biogeochemical reactions. An important example is water-column denitrification, a process that removes biologically available nitrogen from the ocean. Denitrification discriminates against the heavier nitrogen isotope ( 15 N) in favour of the lighter 14 N, leaving a signal of elevated 15 N/ 14 N ratio in the remaining nitrate. Bulk sediment nitrogen isotope records have been interpreted to indicate reduced water-column denitrification and oxygen-deficient zone contraction during the late Pleistocene ice ages. In contrast, we report that foraminifera-bound nitrogen isotopes from the southern margin of the eastern tropical North Pacific are not strongly correlated with global climate, indicating that the southward extent of the eastern tropical North Pacific oxygen-deficient zone was similar between ice ages and interglacials over the last ~265 thousand years. We interpret this disagreement between bulk sediment and foraminifera-bound nitrogen isotopes in the same tropical Pacific sediment cores to arise from effects on bulk sedimentary nitrogen from diagenesis or exogenous nitrogen sources. Rather than varying with global climate, the eastern tropical North Pacific oxygen-deficient zone expanded transiently during the last three deglaciations and other periods with orbital conditions that strengthen the intertropical convergence zone at its northern extreme. Under these conditions, enhanced wind-driven upwelling may have increased eastern tropical Pacific surface productivity and, thus, eastern tropical North Pacific oxygen-deficient zone extent. Our findings differ from foraminifera-bound nitrogen isotope results from the earlier Cenozoic, which associate global cooling with oxygen-deficient zone expansion. The insensitivity of the eastern tropical North Pacific oxygen-deficient zone to late Pleistocene ice ages may reflect thermocline-stabilizing feedbacks that became important once the tropical thermocline had strengthened to late Pleistocene levels. Alternatively, late Pleistocene iron fertilization of the Southern Ocean may have depleted the thermocline nutrient supply to the tropics, counteracting the processes that encourage oxygen-deficient zone expansion in response to cooling.

title: Growth and biochemical variability among Fusarium fujikuroi isolates causing bakanae disease in aromatic rice
summary: During the kharif seasons of 2020 and 2021, a study was conducted at the Department of Plant Pathology, Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, to investigate bakanae disease of aromatic rice, which is a major constra
content: During the kharif seasons of 2020 and 2021, a study was conducted at the Department of Plant Pathology, Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, to investigate bakanae disease of aromatic rice, which is a major constraint on rice production in Haryana and neighbouring states, particularly in early-transplanted crops. During the kharif seasons of 2020 and 2021, 64 isolates were collected from major aromatic rice-growing areas in Haryana. Out of these, 26 isolates were selected to analyse their growth rates and biochemical variability. The growth rate among isolates varied between 12.95–25 mm/48 hr on potato dextrose agar. Isolate FM 18 (25.00 mm/48hr) showed the fastest growth rate, whereas the slowest was observed in FM 31 (12.95 mm/48 h). Maximum colony diameter was shown by FM 18 (83.66 mm) and minimum by FM 31 (55.82 mm). Biochemical constituents (mg/g dry mycelium), including total sugars, total phenols, free amino acids and protein content, were estimated using standard methods. Among the biochemical constituents (mg/g of dry mycelium), total sugars, phenols, free amino acids and protein content varied between 3.77 (FM 53)–12.08 (FM 63), 3.18 (FM 60)–11.98 (FM 20), 26.31 (FM 25)–58.83 (FM 53) and 70 (FM 36)–112 (FM 40) respectively. The present investigation confirms significant biochemical and growth rate variations among the 26 isolates. This characterisation provides a deeper understanding of the pathogen's variation, serving as a vital basis for creating focused management plans and enhancing disease control techniques.

title: Predicting individual tree height in natural Pinus yunnanensis forests: a comparison of generalizability between parametric mixed-effects models and data-driven random forest
summary: Accurate tree height prediction in natural forests requires integrating heterogeneous factors and capturing nonlinear relationships. We compared nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) and random forest (RF) models for predicting individual-tree hei
content: Accurate tree height prediction in natural forests requires integrating heterogeneous factors and capturing nonlinear relationships. We compared nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) and random forest (RF) models for predicting individual-tree height of natural Pinus yunnanensis , identified key predictors, and explored pathways for integrating the two frameworks. We used data from 4,106 trees in 413 permanent plots in Yunnan Province, China, and included variables representing site quality, stand density and competition, stand structure, and climate; plots were split into training and independent test sets at a 70:30 ratio. The NLME model (based on the Hossfeld IV equation with plot-level random effects) included three statistically significant predictors: diameter at breast height (DBH), dominant height ( H d ), and temperature difference (TD). A full-variable RF (RF_full) used all features, whereas a reduced RF (RF_reduced) used the same three predictors to separate algorithm effects from variable-selection effects. Although both RF models fitted the training data better than the NLME model, this advantage did not transfer to independent plots: on the test set, the NLME model (RMSE = 1.66 m, MAE = 1.27 m, MAPE = 14.87%) achieved accuracy nearly identical to that of RF_full (1.66 m, 1.27 m, 14.86%) despite using only three predictors, clearly outperformed RF_reduced (1.75 m, 1.36 m, 16.06%), and produced more balanced residual distributions under heterogeneous plot conditions. The RF_reduced comparison confirmed that the advantage of NLME over RF_reduced arose from the explicit parametric structure with random effects rather than from variable selection. Within the sampled domain, adding features did not improve prediction on new plots: coupling plot-level random effects with a parametric growth equation matched RF_full while using only three predictors, with more stable and interpretable predictions. Because the training and test data were drawn from the same geographic domain, validation in other regions is warranted. We propose incorporating random effects into ensemble learning as cross-level structural constraints, shifting forest growth modeling from method comparison to method integration.

title: Valuation of Carbon Stocks in Forest Area with Special Purpose Gunung Bromo: Efforts to Achieve Indonesia’s FOLU Net Sink 2030
summary: Achieving the 2030 FOLU Net Sink target requires accurate carbon stock estimation and integrated forest health assessment. This study quantified carbon stocks in the Forest Area with Special Purpose (FASP) Gunung Bromo UNS using the USDA ne
content: Achieving the 2030 FOLU Net Sink target requires accurate carbon stock estimation and integrated forest health assessment. This study quantified carbon stocks in the Forest Area with Special Purpose (FASP) Gunung Bromo UNS using the USDA nested-plot design within assessing aboveground tree biomass, litter, understory vegetation, and necromass through tropical allometric equations. Canonical Correspondence Analysis (CCA) examined relationships between carbon stocks and environmental variables, including soil temperature, light intensity, air humidity, and soil pH. Dry secondary forest stored the highest carbon (57.79 tC/ha; 22,582.81 tC across 106.58 ha), followed by shrubland (36.79 tC/ha; 84.19 tC across 0.62 ha) and dryland agriculture (7.36 tC/ha; 487.59 tC across 18.07 ha). Higher stocks were associated with more stable microenvironmental conditions, while open and disturbed areas had lower stocks. These results underscore the need to protect secondary forests, restore shrublands, and strengthen agroforestry systems to support the implementation of FOLU Net Sink 2030.

title: Optimizing electron supply for trichloroethylene reductive dechlorination in a membrane-less bioelectrochemical reactor: Galvanostatic versus potentiostatic approach
summary: This study evaluated galvanostatic control as an alternative to conventional potentiostatic operation for stimulating trichloroethylene (TCE) reductive dechlorination in a bioelectrochemical reactor. A long-term study has been conducted to
content: This study evaluated galvanostatic control as an alternative to conventional potentiostatic operation for stimulating trichloroethylene (TCE) reductive dechlorination in a bioelectrochemical reactor. A long-term study has been conducted to validate the galvanostatic strategy using a model medium (Phase I) and in presence of competing electron acceptors, i.e. nitrate and sulfate (Phase II). In Phase I, shifting from potentiostatic (−450 mV vs SHE) to galvanostatic polarization at −1 mA the coulombic efficiency for reductive dechlorination increased from 0.9 to 31.3% while maintaining complete TCE removal; additionally, the specific energy consumption decreased from 0.61 to 0.001 kWh m −3 . In Phase II, nitrate and sulfate markedly increased the redox demand, indeed, by applying −1 mA to the process, the reductive dechlorination pathway was almost suppressed, whereas −5 mA maintained complete TCE removal and significant dechlorination rate of 40.1 ± 3.2 μeq L −1 d −1 . Potentiostatic operation at −450 mV vs SHE during Phase II restored complete TCE dechlorination but required the highest energy consumption (4.0 kWh m −3 ). The experimental results suggested that the galvanostatic approach is an effective strategy to select microbial metabolisms through the control of hydrogen concentration promoting the activity of dehalogenating microorganisms while suppressing parasitic reactions such as sulfate reduction.

title: The Political Consequences of Stakeholder Governance
summary: We study the political economy of stakeholder governance and corporate lobbying. Lobbying shifts policy toward outcomes that increase the firm's profitability, but it also provokes a backlash from advocacy groups, which push policy back tow
content: We study the political economy of stakeholder governance and corporate lobbying. Lobbying shifts policy toward outcomes that increase the firm's profitability, but it also provokes a backlash from advocacy groups, which push policy back toward the median citizen's preferred outcome. When lobbying is opaque, this backlash generates a ratchet effect: lobbying and backlash escalate, fueling political polarization and instability with little or no policy gain for the firm. To buy quiet, firms adopt stakeholder governance, delegating lobbying to a manager who places less weight on profits and more on citizens' welfare and therefore lobbies less. When the conflict between the firm and society is small, stakeholder governance leads to more socially responsible policies without sacrificing the firm's profits. Paradoxically, when the conflict is large, delegating to a more socially minded manager benefits the firm at society's expense, producing more extreme, socially harmful policies, even when the delegation creates no new agency problems. Our results suggest that stakeholder governance can have unintended political consequences and offer novel implications for corporate governance and lobbying regulation.

title: Topography Shapes Microbial Communities and Functional Potential in Degraded Alpine Meadows
summary: Grassland desertification on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP) strongly alters alpine meadow ecosystems, but the relative roles of topography, and soil water availability in shaping microbial communities along desertification gradient remai
content: Grassland desertification on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau (QTP) strongly alters alpine meadow ecosystems, but the relative roles of topography, and soil water availability in shaping microbial communities along desertification gradient remain unclear. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of degraded alpine meadow soils and investigated microbial taxonomic and targeted functional responses across desertification stages and topographic positions. Environmental variation was primarily structured by soil water content (SWC) and variables related to nutrients. The first principal component explained 66.4% of environmental variation. SWC differed significantly between topographic positions ((F = 43.17, p < 0.001)) but not with degradation stages (F = 2.34, p = 0.106). PERMANOVA showed significant effects of topography on both genus (R² = 0.118, p = 0.043) and targeted functional composition (R² = 0.119, p = 0.031). dbRDA identified SWC as the strongest environmental gradient, whereas variation partitioning analysis indicated larger shared environmental effects for targeted functional profiles (54.6%) and stronger independent soil property effects for genus composition (15.1%). β-diversity was dominated by turnover at both genus (83.5%) and targeted functional (72.5%) levels. These results suggest that topography indirectly shapes microbial community assembly through environmental heterogeneity and that taxonomic and functional responses show partial coupling across alpine meadow soils impacted by desertification.

title: Spatial causal modeling for carbon-aware photovoltaic row spacing in alpine grasslands
summary: Utility-scale photovoltaic power generation is expanding to high-cold meadows, but factors such as panel reflectance, shadows, mixed image elements, local microclimate change and regional warming and humidification trends jointly affect the
content: Utility-scale photovoltaic power generation is expanding to high-cold meadows, but factors such as panel reflectance, shadows, mixed image elements, local microclimate change and regional warming and humidification trends jointly affect the estimation of net ecosystem productivity (NEP). This paper solves the attribution problem through a calculation process: this process corrects the remote sensing pollution of photovoltaic scenes, estimates the NEP constrained by microclimate, uses the spatial PSM-DID method to attribute NEP changes, and converts the estimated ecological response into line spacing boundaries. The positive NEP value indicates the net carbon absorption of the ecosystem, so it is in a carbon sink state. Experiments based on multi-source data from the Qinghai Taratan Photovoltaic Base collected between 2011 and 2025 show that the MC-CASA model achieved an R² of 0.935 and an RMSE of 8.01 g C m⁻² month⁻¹ in 2020, and an R² of 0.976 and an RMSE of 4.26 g C m⁻² month⁻¹ in 2022 (Table 2). Under the PSMDID hypothesis, after excluding climate fluctuation factors, the photovoltaic effect is estimated to be +74.5 g C m⁻² month⁻¹. The layout evaluation based on daylight integral (DLI) further determines that under the specified conditions of ecological light, net ecosystem productivity (NEP) maintenance and capacity density constraints, the minimum feasible line spacing is D = 5.0 m.

title: Effects of post-planting management practices on early Acacia mearnsii stand development and biomass carbon stock in drylands
summary: Land degradation severely depletes dryland biomass carbon, yet the capacity and effectiveness of post-planting interventions involving nitrogen-fixing species for climate mitigation remain poorly quantified. This study evaluated the individ
content: Land degradation severely depletes dryland biomass carbon, yet the capacity and effectiveness of post-planting interventions involving nitrogen-fixing species for climate mitigation remain poorly quantified. This study evaluated the individual and interactive effects of management practices and planting pit sizes on early-stand biomass carbon allocation and predicted soil variables associated with biomass carbon over a two‑year timeline. Acacia mearnsii plantations were monitored under a factorial combination of two pit sizes (30 and 50 cm) and four management regimes: an unmanaged control; watering alone (W); watering with mulching (WM); and integrated watering, mulching, and compost (WMC). Biomass carbon was quantified using destructive sampling and analyzed using generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs). Comprehensive multivariate soil property matrices were simultaneously analyzed across management interventions using R software. Management significantly increased biomass carbon (χ 2 = 42.62, p < 0.001), whereas planting pit size had no significant independent effect. The unmanaged control averaged the lowest total biomass at 47 t CO 2 e ha -1 , whereas WMC achieved a maximum mean of 140 t CO 2 e ha -1 , followed by 116 and 88.4 t CO 2 e ha -1 for WM and W, respectively, in two years. Predictive models demonstrated that Na + , total nitrogen and Available phosphorus explained variance in carbon allocation. Adding WMC reduces soil bulk density and enhances biomass carbon, implying carbon sequestration potential. Root carbon linked with sodium concentration suggests soil chemistry plays a role in carbon allocation and stress buffering. The integrated management (WMC) regime combined with a 50 cm pit size is recommended as the most effective restoration practice in tropical drylands, as this treatment produced the highest aboveground and total biomass carbon stock gains.

title: Considering African savanna elephant conservation as a nature-based climate solution
summary: The conservation of African savanna ecosystems is recognized as making important contributions toward capturing and storing atmospheric carbon in vegetation and in soils to help mitigate climate change. Also, savannas are important for elep
content: The conservation of African savanna ecosystems is recognized as making important contributions toward capturing and storing atmospheric carbon in vegetation and in soils to help mitigate climate change. Also, savannas are important for elephant conservation, which is an increasing priority throughout Africa. However, there is concern that elephants can damage and transform vegetation thereby compromising savanna ecosystems capacities to capture and store carbon. Yet, elephants can have positive effects by releasing body wastes that contribute to nutrient cycling to enhance vegetation productivity (and hence carbon capture). The release of carbon in dung and trampling of soils can enhance long-term carbon storage in soils. Thus, an ecologically holistic assessment of net elephant effects on carbon capture and storage requires accounting for the negative and positive effects together. We report on a holistic assessment of elephant effects using a carbon cycle model that compares savanna ecosystem carbon capture and storage between scenarios with and without elephants. The modeling estimates that elephants at a density of approximately 0.5 individuals per square kilometer could increase average net ecosystem carbon capture by 1.4 times (range of uncertainty of 0.4 to 5.5 times). Elephants are estimated to increase average long-term aboveground carbon stocks by 6.5 times (uncertainty of 2 to 10 times). Average long-term soil carbon storage is estimated to increase by 1.7 times (uncertainty of 0.6 to 5.3 times). The estimated annual carbon capture is large enough to be considered a negative emission in national emissions accounting from land use change, suggesting that savanna elephant conservation should be considered as a nature-based climate solution.

title: Ecotypes matter: photoperiod and site of origin underlie the onset of leaf senescence in Eriophorum vaginatum , an Arctic foundation species
summary: The rapid warming of the Arctic is causing the growing season to expand and the climate to become more unpredictable. This scenario is intensifying a crucial trade-off arctic plants face: maximizing growth during the short growing season wh
content: The rapid warming of the Arctic is causing the growing season to expand and the climate to become more unpredictable. This scenario is intensifying a crucial trade-off arctic plants face: maximizing growth during the short growing season while avoiding freezes at the shoulder seasons. In response, ecotypes have evolved phenological behaviors that are finely tuned to their local climate, which often involves the use of photoperiod cues, especially in the fall. Under the rearrangement of temperature and light regimes, however, such phenological adaptations might prevent native plants from taking advantage of longer growing seasons. To test this phenological mechanism of local adaptation we used a decade-long reciprocal transplant experiment in Northern Alaska and observed the effects of seasonal light and temperature regimes on the leaf phenology of an arctic foundation species, Eriophorum vaginatum . We found that ecotypes rely heavily on site-specific photoperiod cues, but may also use temperature cues. These results indicate that local adaptation of this widespread species to local climates required the evolution of diverging phenological responses to seasonal changes in light. Because light cues will remain stable as the shoulder seasons expand, these adaptations are increasingly maladaptive, and could leave Eriophorum vulnerable to more competitive species.

title: Integrating Biometric, Metabolic, and Photochemical Traits to Identify Candidate Physiological Indicators of Salinity Tolerance and Forage Quality in Alfalfa Cultivars
summary: Salinity limits alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) productivity, yet integrative physiological markers of cultivar tolerance remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify candidate physiological indicators of salt tolerance by integrating g
content: Salinity limits alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) productivity, yet integrative physiological markers of cultivar tolerance remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify candidate physiological indicators of salt tolerance by integrating growth, metabolic, and time-resolved photosynthetic traits across diverse alfalfa cultivars. We exposed nine alfalfa cultivars to a 200 mM NaCl hydroponic shock and monitored their physiological responses over 14 days. We assessed shoot and root growth, leaf Na+/K+ homeostasis, carbohydrate partitioning, dynamic chlorophyll a fluorescence (ChlF), and NIRS-based forage quality. Salinity elicited cultivar-dependent responses. Tolerant cultivars maintained shoot biomass, restricted foliar Na+ accumulation, preserved leaf starch reserves, and progressively recovered Phi2 and linear electron flow (LEF) following initial declines. In contrast, less tolerant cultivars showed persistent growth inhibition, reduced leaf starch, and persistent photochemical impairment. At 7 and 14 dpt, PItotal and Fv′/Fm′ correlated positively with final biomass, whereas PhiNPQ and PhiNO showed negative correlations. Notably, the association between regulated energy dissipation (PhiNPQ) and biomass retention inverted over time, shifting from an early photoprotective mechanism at 1 dpt to a sign of chronic photoinhibitory strain by 7 and 14 dpt. These responses were accompanied by cultivar-specific changes in Na+/K+; balance, soluble sugars, starch, and forage quality. Tracking time-resolved PSII photochemistry reveals that maintaining PItotal and Fv′/Fm′ under saline stress offers an accurate, non-invasive proxy for evaluating cultivar resilience. Their integration into high-throughput phenotyping and breeding programs could facilitate the selection of resilient cultivars. Field validation should consider both biomass production and forage nutritional quality.

title: Solving Regional/National Energy System Planning Problems with Microsoft Excel
summary: This last chapter in Part II introduces another case study in sustainable energy systems modeling and optimization. We further zoom out the energy system supply chain into an even wider context, solving regional/national energy system plann
content: This last chapter in Part II introduces another case study in sustainable energy systems modeling and optimization. We further zoom out the energy system supply chain into an even wider context, solving regional/national energy system planning. The case study uses a carbon-constrained energy planning problem in the Philippines. This type of problem seeks to allocate energy streams from system sources to system sinks, while considering both energy balance and https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 emissions limits. We apply the same model development methodology as in Chapters 5 and 6 . We utilize the same tool, Microsoft Excel ® , to solve the problem. Here we finally illustrate that the modeling strategy we apply can be used at different scales. We also demonstrate that not only raw materials and costs can be constrained or optimized, but also environmental footprints (like https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 ). In energy systems, carbon footprint is one of the most important environmental constraints that we have to consider for sustainability. This chapter introduces the reader to the world of environmentally constrained regional/ national energy system planning for sustainability.

title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host–microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years
summary: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut
content: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysozyme, and secretory immunoglobulin A]. Each of these 51 microbiome models were integrated with a time-point specific male whole-body metabolic model personalized based on LS's weight, blood glucose, and cholesterol. A healthy average (HeAve) community model from 34 individuals provided a reference. Our models predicted methane overproduction from high Methanobrevibacter smithii levels, coinciding with peak CRP and calprotectin. We found that Escherichia coli plays a central role in shaping the predicted metabolome and may promote inflammation through trimethylamine N-oxide and formaldehyde production, out-competing Desulfovibrio piger and Akkermansia muciniphila via active methyl and sulfur cycles. At a later time point, LS experienced a major shift in gut Proteobacteria ecology: E. coli, over-abundant at 675 × HeAve, dropped nearly 80-fold in one month, while Morganella morganii rose by nearly eight times, which coincided with a spike in LS's lactoferrin and lysozyme, a rise in species including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a change in predicted metabolic profile, and increased alpha diversity. We also noted a correlation between postulated inflammation periods and predicted lithocholic acid levels. This work extends two previous studies of 7 and 27 of these time points. Our analysis demonstrates the value of pairing multi-omics time-series data with systems biology approaches in an n-of-1 design, resolving how microbiome composition dynamics shape host–microbiome metabolism and inflammation.

title: Modelling pesticide residues and ecological risks in Kilombero Valley, Tanzania: a SWAT + approach
summary: Thorough pesticide use in tropical agricultural catchments threatens surface and groundwater quality, yet long-term pesticide transport and ecological risks remain poorly understood in data-scarce regions. This study assessed the long-term
content: Thorough pesticide use in tropical agricultural catchments threatens surface and groundwater quality, yet long-term pesticide transport and ecological risks remain poorly understood in data-scarce regions. This study assessed the long-term distribution and ecological risks of chlorpyrifos, profenofos, cypermethrin, and lambda-cyhalothrin in the Kisawasawa catchment, Kilombero Valley, Tanzania, from 2005 to 2035 using the Soil and Water Assessment Tool Plus (SWAT + ). By integrating SWAT + modelling with satellite-derived land use data, global soil datasets, NASA climate records, laboratory-derived pesticide concentrations, and ecological risk assessment, this study provides a long-term spatial assessment of pesticide transport and ecological risks in a tropical, data-limited agricultural catchment in Tanzania. High-risk HRUs for chlorpyrifos, cypermethrin, and profenofos increased from 21% to 41% in 2005 to 63% to 100% in 2035 in surface water, indicating a substantial expansion of ecologically at-risk areas. In groundwater, high-risk HRUs increased from 0-47% to 55-89%, reflecting progressive pesticide migration and persistence in subsurface environments. In contrast, lambda-cyhalothrin declined slightly from 12.7% to 10.4% in surface water, suggesting relatively stable spatial ecological risk. The measured concentrations reached 2.00 µg/L for chlorpyrifos and 0.42 µg/L for profenofos. Ecological risk assessments based on these concentrations revealed risk quotient (RQ) values ≥ 1 at most monitoring sites. Although cypermethrin and lambda-cyhalothrin had concentrations as low as 0.005 µg/L, they still posed significant ecological risks. These results demonstrate the usefulness of SWAT + for projecting long-term pesticide transport trajectories and provide a scientific foundation for targeted mitigation efforts and sustainable water resource management in tropical agricultural catchments.

title: Soil Health, Soil Organic Matter Dynamics, and Carbon Sequestration in Horticultural Ecosystems
summary: Soil health is keystone for achieving sustainable and climate-resilient horticultural production systems. Among its several vital components, soil organic matter (SOM) plays a crucial role in regulating soil physical, chemical, and biologic
content: Soil health is keystone for achieving sustainable and climate-resilient horticultural production systems. Among its several vital components, soil organic matter (SOM) plays a crucial role in regulating soil physical, chemical, and biological properties. This chapter explores the dynamics of SOM in horticultural ecosystems, emphasizing its influence on nutrient cycling, soil structure improvement, water retention, and rhizospheric microbial activity. The processes governing SOM accumulation and decomposition are discussed in relation to management practices such as organic amendments, cover cropping, conservation tillage, and integrated nutrient management. The chapter further highlights the potential of horticultural systems as significant carbon sinks, contributing to climate change mitigation through carbon sequestration. Mechanisms of carbon stabilization, including humification and soil aggregate formation, are critically examined. Emerging approaches such as precision agriculture and microbial interventions are also discussed for enhancing SOM and long-term carbon storage.

title: Herbivore-induced shifts in volatile organic compounds and phytohormone crosstalk are associated with Asian longhorned beetle aggregation on Russian olive
summary: In mixed plantation, Russian olive ( Elaeagnus angustifolia L.) serves as a “dead-end trap tree” for Asian longhorned beetles ( Anoplophora glabripennis ; ALB), attracting adults to lay eggs, and killing their eggs through gum exudation. Fi
content: In mixed plantation, Russian olive ( Elaeagnus angustifolia L.) serves as a “dead-end trap tree” for Asian longhorned beetles ( Anoplophora glabripennis ; ALB), attracting adults to lay eggs, and killing their eggs through gum exudation. Field surveys revealed that ALB preferentially congregates on individual Russian olive trees, with oviposition scars concentrated on 5- to 8-year-old branches, while surrounding trees remain largely uninfested. However, the chemical basis of this dual-level aggregation remains unclear. Volatiles and key phytohormones (ethylene, abscisic acid, jasmonic acid, and salicylic acid) were profiled in healthy, short-term (August) and long-term (June) ALB-infested Russian olive trees using HS-SPME-GC-MS, GC, and UPLC-MS/MS, revealing distinct chemical signatures associated with infestation duration. Volatile profiles differed markedly in both concentration and composition between healthy trees and those under short- or long-term ALB infestation. These chemical shifts reflected coordinated responses, with clustering patterns driven by the combined effects of multiple volatiles. However, within-tree aggregation was not explained by within-tree VOC variation. Biotic stress was associated with a partial reduction in tree ethylene levels, accompanied by decreased levels of JA and SA, and an abnormal increase in ABA level. Therefore, we hypothesize that the abnormal accumulation of ABA under biotic stress may act as a potential "decoy" signal. Under resource-limited conditions, the suppression of the JA/SA pathway collectively may restructure endogenous defense signals in plants and be associated with disrupted external volatile communication, potentially triggering the ecological phenomenon that “infested plants are more susceptible to ALB infestation”.

title: Depth-partitioned oxidation of atmospheric hydrogen, carbon monoxide and methane in a glacier forefield soil
summary: Glacier forefields are model systems for pioneer ecosystem assembly under extreme oligotrophy. Their microbial communities carry widespread genomic potential to oxidize atmospheric trace gases, yet whether this potential is transcribed in s
content: Glacier forefields are model systems for pioneer ecosystem assembly under extreme oligotrophy. Their microbial communities carry widespread genomic potential to oxidize atmospheric trace gases, yet whether this potential is transcribed in situ, and by which lineages, remains largely untested. Here we combined depth-resolved profiling of hydrogen (H 2 ), carbon monoxide (CO) and methane (CH 4 ) at ten locations in the Wildstrubel glacier forefield, Swiss Alps, with mesocosm experiments, long-read metagenomics, and genome-resolved metatranscriptomics. Soils were consistent net sinks for atmospheric H 2 and CH 4 , with fluxes ~2-fold and ~6-fold higher, respectively, in older than in younger terrain. H 2 uptake was concentrated in the upper 20 cm, whereas CH 4 uptake extended deeper. In the field, CO uptake was masked by apparent subsurface production, but in mesocosms lacking this source both CO and H 2 were drawn below atmospheric concentrations. Although 57% of metagenome-assembled genomes encoded trace-gas oxidation enzymes, topsoil transcription was dominated by Group 1h [NiFe]-hydrogenases from a few Actinomycetota populations, in which the CO dehydrogenase coxL was transcribed 20- to 35-fold less. The second most transcribed marker was smoX , most closely related to C 2 -C 6 alkane monooxygenases, suggesting the use of short-chain alkanes of possible subsurface origin. Mobile genetic elements were widely transcribed, matching host transcription, but a 104-kb plasmid-borne coxMSL operon was largely silent. Acetylene perturbation induced no detectable switching between trace-gas pathways. Together, these data suggest that trace-gas metabolism is partitioned across soil depth: atmospheric H 2 scavenging dominates topsoil transcription, whereas methanotrophy and CO production occur deeper. Net surface fluxes, particularly for CO, therefore, underestimate gross trace-gas turnover.

title: Solar radiation modification: Why precaution means non-use
summary: In May 2026 the United Nations Environment Programme released a working paper finding that solar radiation modification (SRM) is not currently a viable climate response, while framing continued research under globally coordinated oversight
content: In May 2026 the United Nations Environment Programme released a working paper finding that solar radiation modification (SRM) is not currently a viable climate response, while framing continued research under globally coordinated oversight as the prudent course. This Perspective argues that this prescription rests on four misconceptions recurring across a decade of high-profile SRM assessments: (1) that more research can resolve what are, at root, political and legal problems; (2) that the precautionary principle licenses experimentation rather than constraining it; (3) that advocating restriction amounts to silencing debate; and (4) that participation in research governance can substitute for the power to decide. Engaging the 2024-2025 advisory opinions of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights and the International Court of Justice, and the human right to science, the Perspective shows that international law supports the opposite conclusion: precaution, correctly understood, means non-use.

title: Unraveling the mRNA-miRNA regulatory network of high photosynthetic efficiency to improve yield potential in Camellia oleifera
summary: Camellia oleifera Abel. ( C. oleifera ) is a premier woody oilseed tree species extensively cultivated in southern China. However, the widespread prevalence of low-yielding plantations severely restricts C. oleifera production. Improving ph
content: Camellia oleifera Abel. ( C. oleifera ) is a premier woody oilseed tree species extensively cultivated in southern China. However, the widespread prevalence of low-yielding plantations severely restricts C. oleifera production. Improving photosynthetic efficiency represents a pivotal strategy for boosting production in C. oleifera . In this study, we selected a key hybrid population developed in our team, and performed leaf physiological and morphological measurements, mRNA-seq and miRNA-seq analyses on leaves from the parental cross YZ-2 × HY3 and five F₁ hybrid progenies. The results demonstrated that YH-5 and YH-10 exhibited high photosynthetic efficiency and high-parent heterosis., YH-1 fell below the low parents and YH-2, YH-4, YZ-2, and HY3 displayed intermediate photosynthetic efficiency. High photosynthetic efficiency of YH-5 and YH-10 relies on elevated light-harvesting efficiency, enhanced carbon fixation capacity, activated phytohormone signaling, enhanced stomatal movement and strengthened photoprotective mechanisms. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified four hub transcription factors- BHLH63 , HSFB1 , NAC078 and ARR2 -as putative regulators of net photosynthetic rate and pigment traits. Integrated miRNA and mRNA analysis revealed that miR393-x and novel-m0437-5p target AFB2 and BCA1 respectively, miR5282 target CYP73A4 , highlighting that stomatal movement and photoprotection mechanisms play key roles in achieving high photosynthetic efficiency. Collectively, this study advances our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying high photosynthetic efficiency traits in C. oleifera , and provides a theoretical foundation for molecular breeding strategies targeting yield improvement.

title: Influence of solitary and combined foliar spray of iron and zinc on fruit-micronutrient biofortification, functional quality and yield of cherry tomatoes
summary: The present study evaluated the effects of supplementary fortnightly foliar applications of iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn), applied individually and in combination (Fe + Zn), on cherry tomatoes. The experiment was conducted under net house conditi
content: The present study evaluated the effects of supplementary fortnightly foliar applications of iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn), applied individually and in combination (Fe + Zn), on cherry tomatoes. The experiment was conducted under net house conditions in an arid region using a factorial randomized block design with three replications. Responses were assessed in red cherry tomato (cv. Pusa Cherry Tomato 1) and yellow cherry tomato (cv. Pusa Golden Cherry Tomato 2) with respect to micronutrient biofortification, growth, yield, and fruit quality. The combined application of Fe and Zn was the most effective treatment, increasing fruit Fe and Zn concentrations by 4.9- and 1.7-fold, respectively, in red cherry tomato, while approximately twofold increases in micronutrient concentrations were observed in yellow cherry tomato (mg/kg DW basis). Foliar application also improved fruit quality parameters, including titratable acidity, soluble solids content, electrical conductivity, and functional quality traits. Shoot dry mass and fruit yield increased by 9% and 16%, respectively, compared with the control. In addition, Fe and Zn application enhanced the accumulation of other nutrients, including potassium, manganese, and copper, indicating synergistic nutrient interactions. Significant fruit type × spray treatment interactions for fruit and leaf micronutrient concentrations indicated differential responses between red and yellow cherry tomatoes. These findings demonstrate the potential of foliar Fe and Zn application as an agronomic biofortification strategy to improve the nutritional and functional quality of cherry tomatoes, thereby contributing to dietary micronutrient enrichment.

title: Conjoint effect of organic formulations and biofertilizers on soil health and fruit quality of citrus (Citrus reticulata Blanco)
summary: The experiment was conducted to investigate the influence of organic manure and biofertilizers on citrus. Trees were treated with different amounts of Azospirillum, including organic manures like jeevamrit, ghanjeevamrit, and FYM. The exper
content: The experiment was conducted to investigate the influence of organic manure and biofertilizers on citrus. Trees were treated with different amounts of Azospirillum, including organic manures like jeevamrit, ghanjeevamrit, and FYM. The experiment was laid out in a Randomized Block Design with seven treatments and three replications to see their effects on the soil properties, tree growth, and fruit quality. Among 7 treatments, T 7 containing FYM (30 kg) + Azospirillum (300 g) showed the maximum increase in plant height, plant spread, and trunk girth. In T 3 , which contains jeevamrit (2.5 L) + Azospirillum (300 g), it gives the maximum increase in fruit weight, fruit size, number of fruits and fruit yield. T 3 gave the maximum efficiency in terms of biochemical analysis and the maximum efficiency in soil pH, soil moisture, soil organic carbon, and EC. The maximum increase in availability of soil nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium was in treatment T 7 . The results indicate that the integration of jeevamrit with Azospirillum is a potential method to improve the quality of fruits, fruit production and the health of the soil as a sustainable option for kinnow mandarin cultivation.

title: DigiSylva: a plot-level dataset of forest attributes integrating field and airborne laser scanning measurements across the boreal-temperate ecotone of the northeastern United States
summary: Enhancing estimates of forest attributes such as structure, composition, volume, and biomass across large spatial extents relies on field inventory measurements to calibrate and validate relationships with metrics derived from airborne lase
content: Enhancing estimates of forest attributes such as structure, composition, volume, and biomass across large spatial extents relies on field inventory measurements to calibrate and validate relationships with metrics derived from airborne laser scanning (ALS) point clouds. However, mixed temperate and boreal forests in the northeastern United States remain underrepresented in publicly available datasets, especially those that co-locate field inventory and ALS observations. In this study, we developed DigiSylva, a spatially explicit database integrating field inventory and various remote sensing products across five representative forest ecosystems within the boreal-temperate ecotone of the northeastern United States. This database includes 308 fixed-area plots spanning inland, managed, experimental, coastal, and northern hardwood forest systems. For each plot, individual tree measurements, including species, diameter at breast height, and spatial position, were recorded. Plot centers were surveyed with sub-meter GNSS accuracy to enable precise spatial alignment with airborne and spaceborne observations. Tree height, aboveground biomass, and stem volume were estimated using multiple allometric methods. Multi-temporal ALS point clouds acquired between 2010 and 2026 were clipped to plot boundaries and processed to derive standardized forest structural metrics. In addition, co-registered NAIP imagery and Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) data were provided for each plot. In total, the dataset contains 6,137 trees, 308 plot-level forest attribute records, and 1,408 plot-level ALS point clouds. This integrated dataset can support forest structural analysis, development of ALS-based forest attribute predictive models (e.g., volume), and multi-temporal biomass monitoring in structurally complex, mixed-species forest ecosystems.

title: The tighter plant-soil coupling coordination predicts greater ecosystem multifunctionality in alpine grasslands
summary: Understanding the maintaining mechanism of ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) under global change is a central challenge.We thus introduce the plant-soil coupling coordination degree (CCD) as a systems-level metric and test its association
content: Understanding the maintaining mechanism of ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) under global change is a central challenge.We thus introduce the plant-soil coupling coordination degree (CCD) as a systems-level metric and test its association with EMF across alpine grasslands on the Tibetan Plateau.Our results showed that CCD was significantly higher in alpine meadows than in alpine steppes.This disparity stemmed from distinct subsystem contributions: plant-driven coordination dominated the alpine meadow ecosystem, whereas soil water availability regulated the alpine steppe ecosystem.Crucially, CCD was strongly associated with EMF across both grassland ecosystems, and increasing CCD corresponded to a transition from decoupled to mutually reinforcing plant-soil interactions, enhancing resource-use efficiency and nutrient cycling.Our finding highlights CCD as a diagnostic indicator of ecosystem multifunctionality, providing a solid basis for shifting management from single ecological components to ecosystem coordination.

title: PERAN GENDER DALAM PENGELOLAAN SUMBER DAYA ALAM DAN PENGUATAN EKONOMI KELUARGA UNTUK MENDUKUNG PENCAPAIAN TUJUAN PEMBANGUNAN BERKELANJUTAN (SDGs) 1 DAN 13
summary: This Community Service Program (PKM) aims to strengthen gender-responsive participation in sustainable natural resource management and strengthen household economic empowerment to support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SD
content: This Community Service Program (PKM) aims to strengthen gender-responsive participation in sustainable natural resource management and strengthen household economic empowerment to support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 1 (No Poverty) and SDG 13 (Climate Action) in Negeri Rutong, South Leitimur Subdistrict, Ambon City. The program was implemented using a participatory and gender-responsive community empowerment approach, comprising community outreach, environmental education, training in generative and vegetative plant propagation, seedling distribution, provision of training modules, and mentoring for Dasawisma groups. Data were collected through observations, interviews, and questionnaires administered to 62 respondents, consisting of 34 men (54.84%) and 28 women (45.16%). The results indicate that the community participates in natural resource conservation, particularly mangrove ecosystem preservation, through planting, maintenance, clean-up, and area monitoring activities. The training also improved community knowledge and skills in plant propagation and the use of home gardens to cultivate vegetables and fruits to help meet household needs and support family income. Women's involvement through Dasawisma groups serves as an empowerment strategy to strengthen community self-reliance, reduce dependence on purchased seedlings, and support environmental rehabilitation. The sustainability of the program is expected to be achieved through regular mentoring and collaboration among higher education institutions, the village government, and the community. Therefore, integrating gender equality, natural resource conservation, and family economic empowerment represents an important approach to improving community welfare while strengthening adaptive capacity to climate change.

title: Organic Heterogeneous Electrosynthesis: Interfacial Catalysis for Selective Organic Transformations
summary: Comprehensive Summary Organic heterogeneous electrosynthesis has emerged as a versatile platform for sustainable organic synthesis, yet its rapidly expanding chemistry remains difficult to interpret using conventional classifications based
content: Comprehensive Summary Organic heterogeneous electrosynthesis has emerged as a versatile platform for sustainable organic synthesis, yet its rapidly expanding chemistry remains difficult to interpret using conventional classifications based on catalyst materials or reaction types. This review introduces a unified Site‐Interface‐Pathway framework to understand how heterogeneous catalytic interfaces regulate reactive intermediates and determine reaction selectivity. Four representative interfacial reaction modes are identified to connect catalyst design with synthetic applications across diverse anodic and cathodic transformations. This framework provides a mechanistic foundation for rational catalyst design and highlights the evolution of heterogeneous organic electrosynthesis from empirical catalyst optimization toward interface‐programmed molecular synthesis. Key Scientists Since the emergence of heterogeneous organic electrosynthesis in the mid‐2010s, the electrode has evolved from a passive electron source into a catalytic interface that controls substrate adsorption, electron and proton transfer, intermediate conversion, and product desorption, with these interfacial processes central to reaction efficiency and selectivity. In 2015, Kubiak and co‐workers incorporated Fe‐porphyrin molecular catalysts into metal‐organic‐framework films for electrochemical CO₂ reduction, demonstrating how molecular active sites could be integrated into solid electrode architectures. [1] Stahl subsequently immobilized a pyrene–TEMPO electrocatalyst on carbon cloth for preparative alcohol oxidation in 2017, providing an early example of reusable molecular catalysis at a heterogeneous interface. [2] Bin Zhang further advanced solid‐electrocatalyst strategies for primary‐amine oxidation to nitriles and selective alkyne semihydrogenation at sulfur‐modified copper interfaces. [3‐4] Mechanistic studies by Shuangyin Wang established design principles for nickel‐based nucleophile electrooxidation and revealed how activated Ni–OH motifs regulate interfacial proton‐coupled electron transfer and subsequent chemical steps. [5‐6] In parallel, Jian Zhang developed Cu nanoarray electrodes for high‐current‐density alkynol semihydrogenation and continuous alkenol production in flow electrolyzers, [7] while Yongwen Tan combined Cu–Au alloying with nanopore confinement to control hydrogen generation, substrate adsorption, product desorption, and over‐hydrogenation. [8] More recently, Dingsheng Wang designed a CuN₃P₁ single‐atom catalyst as a heterogeneous cathodic redox mediator for quinazolinone ring opening and late‐stage natural‐product modification. [9] Collectively, these advances have established heterogeneous organic electrosynthesis as a powerful platform bridging molecular catalyst design with active‐site, interface, microenvironment, and reactor engineering.

title: Protocols in Protein Biochemistry: An Undergraduate Laboratory Manual
summary: Hands-on training in protein biochemistry builds on a small set of core skills: measuring liquids accurately, preparing buffers, quantifying, purifying and analyzing proteins, measuring enzyme activity, and preparing protein crystals. This
content: Hands-on training in protein biochemistry builds on a small set of core skills: measuring liquids accurately, preparing buffers, quantifying, purifying and analyzing proteins, measuring enzyme activity, and preparing protein crystals. This manual presents nine sequenced experiments for an undergraduate biochemistry laboratory that develop these skills in order. Students begin with micropipette calibration by mass and the preparation and pH verification of buffers using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation. They then determine the concentration of cytochrome c by the Bradford assay, purify it by carboxymethyl cation-exchange chromatography, assess purity by SDS-PAGE, and exchange it into a target buffer by dialysis. Next, students determine absolute protein mass from an in-gel bovine serum albumin standard curve using densitometry, measure the Michaelis–Menten kinetics of Trypanosoma cruzi glucokinase with a coupled NADPH assay (Km, Vmax, kcat and kcat/Km), and grow lysozyme crystals by sitting-drop vapor diffusion by screening various concentrations of sodium chloride in the presence and absence of a strand of hair that acts as a nucleating agent. Each experiment provides background, objectives, materials, safety notes, a step-by-step procedure, and data-analysis questions, and the glucokinase assay includes a fluorescence-based assay or an absorbance-based alternative for laboratories without a fluorescence plate reader. The experiments use common reagents and standard equipment, and instructors can adapt them with their laboratory equipment and supplies.

title: Living with ‘The Beast’: The Impact of the Trombe Wall on Homelife
summary: Breakthrough technology is disruptive and can have a meaningful impact on people’s lives. This was the case of Félix Trombe’s solar-mass wall designed for dwellings but untested for homelife. In the early-1970s, Douglas Kelbaugh, a young ar
content: Breakthrough technology is disruptive and can have a meaningful impact on people’s lives. This was the case of Félix Trombe’s solar-mass wall designed for dwellings but untested for homelife. In the early-1970s, Douglas Kelbaugh, a young architect and environmentalist, learned of Trombe’s wall system from an environmental journal. Kelbaugh then designed his family’s house in Princeton, New Jersey (1974–75) around Trombe’s innovation. Lauded for its science, Kelbaugh’s experiment had a significant impact on his homelife. Well-documented over 50 years, nearly all publications describe the technology behind the Kelbaugh House. None before discussed what it was like to live in; how occupants needed to modify living within the house. What soon became evident to Kelbaugh and subsequent owners (including myself) was that you had to live with ‘the Beast’, it did not live with you. This essay seeks not to discuss the Trombe wall’s science, but the life behind it.

title: Beyond the Well Boundary: Strain‐Specific Ammonium Overflow Drives Cross‐Well Nitrogen Transfer in Microalgal Cultures
summary: Ammonia volatilization from microalgal cultures represents an ecologically significant pathway for nitrogen transfer across diverse ecosystems. A 48-well microplate cross-diffusion assay was employed to demonstrate that alkalinization trigg
content: Ammonia volatilization from microalgal cultures represents an ecologically significant pathway for nitrogen transfer across diverse ecosystems. A 48-well microplate cross-diffusion assay was employed to demonstrate that alkalinization triggers profoundly distinct ammonium overflow profiles in Chlamydomonas sp. MACC-216 and Parachlorella sp. MACC-38. Chlamydomonas sp. releases substantial ammonium under both ammonium and nitrate conditions, sufficient to fully sustain the growth of neighbouring nitrogen-free cultures. In contrast, Parachlorella sp. maintains a tight nitrogen economy under nitrate supply. Even under glutamine synthetase (GS) inhibition by L-methionine-DL-sulfoximine (MSX), Parachlorella sp. shows at least ten-fold lower ammonium efflux compared to Chlamydomonas sp. These divergent responses to MSX suggest that ammonium retention in Chlamydomonas sp. depends largely on GS, whereas Parachlorella sp. may rely on additional pathways to prevent nitrogen loss. Collectively, these findings highlight how strain-specific differences in nitrate removal can shape nitrogen availability, with implications for both natural aquatic and designed ecosystems.

title: Post‐Anthesis Drought Intensity Regulates Wheat Grain Weight Through Spermidine‐Mediated Carbon Metabolic Reprogramming After Rewatering
summary: The effect of drought‐rewatering during wheat grain filling on carbon metabolism exhibits intensity‐dependent differences, yet the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Unlike most studies on sustained drought, this work addresses the rewat
content: The effect of drought‐rewatering during wheat grain filling on carbon metabolism exhibits intensity‐dependent differences, yet the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Unlike most studies on sustained drought, this work addresses the rewatering phase and reveals that carbon‐metabolism recovery is critically constrained by preceding drought severity rather than being a simple reversal of stress. Through two‐year field experiments integrating physiological assays, 13 C isotope labelling, transcriptomics and enzymology, our results show that moderate drought‐rewatering enables a metabolic shift from stress‐driven hydrolysis to starch biosynthesis via coordinated regulation of stem fructan and sucrose‐starch enzymes, increasing 1000‐grain weight. This shift was supported by 13 C partitioning data, which confirmed that assimilates were preferentially allocated to spikes, with allocation rates positively correlated with grain width and weight. Severe drought‐rewatering sustains 1‐fructan exohydrolase activity and suppresses starch synthesis genes, reducing 1000‐grain weight. Exogenous spermidine (Spd) enhances source photosynthesis, stem sucrose export and grain starch synthesis while blocking amylolytic degradation, thereby promoting the recovery of 1000‐grain weight under severe drought‐rewatering. The drought‐tolerant genotype XN836 is superior to the drought‐sensitive genotype XN979 in carbon transport and Spd biosynthesis. Therefore, our results demonstrate that Spd may be a key regulator involved in the reprogramming of carbon metabolism under severe drought‐rewatering, providing a target for drought‐resilient cultivation and a framework for precision irrigation and genotype‐specific chemical regulation to mitigate wheat yield losses.

title: Carbon Content and Sequestration of Mangrove Stands and Litter in the Pantai Cemara Mangrove Ecosystem, West Lombok
summary: Mangrove forests play an important role in climate change mitigation through their capacity to store carbon in biomass. This study aimed to estimate carbon stocks and CO₂-equivalent values in mangrove stands and litter in the Pantai Cemara
content: Mangrove forests play an important role in climate change mitigation through their capacity to store carbon in biomass. This study aimed to estimate carbon stocks and CO₂-equivalent values in mangrove stands and litter in the Pantai Cemara mangrove ecosystem, Lembar Selatan Village, West Lombok Regency, Indonesia. An exploratory-descriptive approach was employed, with purposive sampling conducted in two clusters, each comprising three observation transects. Stand biomass was estimated non-destructively using diameter at breast height (DBH) measurements and allometric equations, while litter biomass was measured using 1 × 1 m litter traps over 15 days. Five mangrove species from three families were recorded, with Rhizophora mucronata being the most dominant species, exhibiting Importance Value Indices of 124.24 at the tree level and 165.06 at the sapling level. Estimated stand biomass reached 42.80 t/ha, corresponding to a carbon stock of 21.40 t C/ha and a CO₂-equivalent value of 78.53 t CO₂/ha. Litter biomass averaged 4.06 t/ha, with an estimated carbon stock of 1.90 t C/ha and a CO₂-equivalent value of 6.99 t CO₂/ha. Environmental parameters, including pH, salinity, temperature, and substrate depth, were within ranges considered suitable for mangrove growth. These findings provide estimates of carbon stocks and associated CO₂-equivalent values in mangrove stand biomass and litter, highlighting the potential contribution of the Pantai Cemara mangrove ecosystem to climate change mitigation. Sustainable conservation and rehabilitation efforts are therefore recommended.

title: Synthesis of Sucrose and Glutamate in Systemic Tissues During Rapid Systemic Signaling in Arabidopsis
summary: Plants can transmit chemical/electrical/volatile signals from a single tissue (termed ‘ local tissue’) to all other tissues (termed ‘systemic tissues’), in a process termed ‘systemic signaling’. These can induce whole‐plant acclimation/resi
content: Plants can transmit chemical/electrical/volatile signals from a single tissue (termed ‘ local tissue’) to all other tissues (termed ‘systemic tissues’), in a process termed ‘systemic signaling’. These can induce whole‐plant acclimation/resistance to the abiotic/biotic stressors that were initially sensed by the local tissue. Systemic signals include ‘rapid’ signals, such as the electric, calcium, hydraulic, and reactive oxygen species waves, and ‘slower’ signals, which include metabolites, peptides, RNA/DNA molecules, and proteins. Recent studies reported that metabolic changes can occur rapidly in systemic tissues, but the source of these changes remained unclear. Here we applied 11 CO 2 to radiolabel 11 C‐photoassimilates in rosette leaves and studied rapid systemic signaling in response to local excess light stress, as well as introduced a heavy, stable labelled Glu (Glu‐ 13 C 5 ‐ 15 N 1 ) into local leaves and studied rapid systemic signaling in response to wounding in mature bolting Arabidopsis thaliana plants. Our study revealed that while unlabelled sucrose or Glu accumulated in systemic tissues in response to light stress or wounding, respectively, the accumulation of labelled metabolites was not observed in systemic tissues. Therefore, it appears that metabolites such as sucrose and Glu are not mobilized from local to systemic tissues during rapid systemic signaling in mature bolting plants.

title: Deletion of two candidate depolymerases with overlapping genetic effects increases PHA yield in Rhodopseudomonas palustris TIE-1
summary: Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) is a microbial carbon-storage polymer with potential as a renewable bioplastic, but intracellular remobilization can limit polymer retention. The metabolically versatile bacterium Rhodopseudomonas palustris TIE-1
content: Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) is a microbial carbon-storage polymer with potential as a renewable bioplastic, but intracellular remobilization can limit polymer retention. The metabolically versatile bacterium Rhodopseudomonas palustris TIE-1 accumulates PHA during photoheterotrophic growth, yet the enzymes that control PHA turnover in this organism remain incompletely studied. We identified PhaZ2 (Rpal_0568) as a second candidate PHA depolymerase that is evolutionarily and architecturally distinct from the previously annotated PhaZ1 (Rpal_0578). Deleting either PhaZ1 or PhaZ2 alone did not substantially increase PHA content under tested growth conditions, whereas the double mutant accumulated 2.3-fold and 1.7-fold more PHA than wild type under non-nitrogen-fixing and nitrogen-fixing photoheterotrophic conditions, respectively, supporting overlapping roles in PHA turnover. All deletion strains showed longer doubling times but reached final culture densities similar to wild type. The double mutant showed its strongest retention phenotype under severe but growth-permissive nutrient limitation, including 3.7-fold more PHA than wild type at 33% phosphorus availability. A two-stage cultivation strategy that separated biomass formation from nutrient-limited storage raised volumetric PHA titer to 0.180 mg per mL culture in the double mutant, 1.5-fold more than wild type and approximately 3.4-fold higher than single-stage 33% phosphorus limitation and 4.0-fold higher than single-stage 8% nitrogen limitation (cross-experiment comparison), despite lower PHA content per unit biomass. Finally, an LC-MS-calibrated FTIR spectroscopy model predicted PHA content with an R² of 0.928 ( n = 15) and reproduced the major biological trends. These results identify genetically redundant candidate depolymerases as targets for improving PHA retention in TIE-1 and establish a cultivation and screening framework for strain engineering. Importance Persistent pollution from petroleum-based plastics has intensified the need for biodegradable plastics produced from renewable resources. Polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) is a microbially synthesized bioplastic, but microbial cells can also consume the stored polymer, reducing its net yield. The metabolically versatile, photosynthetic purple non-sulfur bacterium (PNSB) Rhodopseudomonas palustris TIE-1 is a promising production organism because it can photosynthesize, assimilate atmospheric nitrogen, and utilize diverse carbon sources. We show that two candidate PHA depolymerases, PhaZ1 and PhaZ2, likely have overlapping roles in PHA turnover. Removing both candidates increased polymer retention, particularly when nitrogen or phosphorus was limited, and a two-stage cultivation strategy further increased PHA titer to 0.180 mg mL⁻¹ of culture. We also developed a rapid infrared spectroscopy method to track polymer content across strains and growth conditions. These findings offer complementary genetic, cultivation, and screening strategies for

title: Growth–reproduction trade‐offs in woody plants are common but changing: a meta‐analysis
summary: Growth and reproduction draw on a common resource pool, yet empirical studies of woody plants report widely differing relationships between seed production and growth. We synthesized 685 estimates from 78 studies covering 79 woody species,
content: Growth and reproduction draw on a common resource pool, yet empirical studies of woody plants report widely differing relationships between seed production and growth. We synthesized 685 estimates from 78 studies covering 79 woody species, with study locations concentrated at northern temperate latitudes, to test how growth-reproduction correlations vary across time, species, and environments. Growth and reproduction measured within the same year were negatively correlated, suggesting an immediate cost of reproduction. Given the limited and uneven taxonomic sampling, phylogenetic patterns in growth-reproduction correlations remain uncertain. The correlations were not systematically related to functional traits or climate. Trade-offs were strongest in species with high interannual variability in seed production and weakened markedly over recent decades in these species. Together, these results show that growth-reproduction trade-offs in woody plants are common but not fixed, and that shifts in reproductive variability under environmental change can alter how trees balance growth and reproduction, with consequences for long-term forest functioning.

title: Repeated Fire Increases Soil Pyrogenic Carbon Storage in Alaskan Tundra
summary: Pyrogenic carbon in permafrost systems is largely unaccounted for in existing soil carbon inventories and earth system models. We assessed a proxy for pyrogenic carbon along a chronosequence of repeat burns and adjacent, unburned sites in A
content: Pyrogenic carbon in permafrost systems is largely unaccounted for in existing soil carbon inventories and earth system models. We assessed a proxy for pyrogenic carbon along a chronosequence of repeat burns and adjacent, unburned sites in Alaskan tundra. Using Fourier Transformed‐Infrared (FT‐IR) spectroscopy, we quantified aromatic carbon, likely of pyrogenic nature, by aggregating carbon functional groups to create a measure of the relative abundance of aromatic carbon. In addition, we measured total soil organic carbon, total nitrogen concentrations, and carbon to nitrogen ratios, as well as associated soil and environmental characteristics such as thaw depth, O horizon depth, volumetric soil water content, and maximum vegetation height. We found that soil aromatic carbon content increased with the number of burns and accumulated at depths below the soil surface but above the permafrost table. We found inverse relationships between soil aromatic carbon and soil organic carbon and total nitrogen, indicating that pyrogenic carbon likely comprised a larger portion of the carbon pool in areas burned recently or multiple times. The chemical composition and abundance of aromatic carbons attributed to pyrogenic carbon depended on the number of burns and the time since fire. Higher relative abundances of aromatic carbon were positively associated with deeper thaw depths, shallower O horizons, and taller maximum vegetation heights. Lastly, we saw evidence of partial post‐fire regeneration in the oldest site in the chronosequence, but overall, the sites that burned remained fundamentally different from unburned sites in biogeochemical and ecosystem properties. These findings demonstrate the long‐lasting impacts of tundra fire on carbon storage in permafrost ecosystems.

title: Carbonaceous nanomaterials for the removal of hazardous pharmaceutical contaminants from wastewater: mechanisms, recent advances, and future directions
summary: Rising pharmaceutical consumption and the continuous discharge of pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) into aquatic systems have become defining environmental challenges of the present decade. Because conventional wastewater treatment
content: Rising pharmaceutical consumption and the continuous discharge of pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) into aquatic systems have become defining environmental challenges of the present decade. Because conventional wastewater treatment plants were never designed to remove biologically persistent micropollutants, trace residues accumulate in surface water, groundwater and drinking water, where they drive ecotoxicity, endocrine disruption and the dissemination of antibiotic-resistance genes. Therefore, understanding how nanomaterials can not only capture but also destroy these contaminants is central to safeguarding water quality. This review critically examines carbonaceous nanomaterials, such as graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide, carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, carbon dots and biochar, for PhAC removal, organised around the four dominant treatment routes: adsorption, membrane filtration, advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and photocatalysis, the latter treated here as a light-driven hazard-oriented framework that achieves true mineralisation rather than the mere transfer of contaminants to another phase. The best-performing systems for the removal of representative drug classes, such as antibiotics, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, antidepressants, β-blockers and analgesics, are shown to share a common design motif: a conductive, defect-rich and often heteroatom-doped carbon scaffold that concentrates the pollutant, shuttles photogenerated charge carriers and stabilises a redox or light-active phase. Adsorption and membrane filtration routes deliver high capacity but relocate contaminants to a solid or concentrated phase, while carbon-coupled AOPs and S-/Z-scheme heterojunctions achieve contaminant degradation with concurrent antibiotic-resistance-gene reduction. Beyond removal efficiency, this review highlights catalyst stability, regeneration, reusability, total organic carbon (TOC) removal, transformation-product toxicity, energy demand, and performance in real wastewater matrices as critical parameters governing practical applicability. Finally, this review identifies key research gaps and emphasises the need for standardised, hazard-oriented assessment frameworks that integrate degradation efficiency, mineralisation, transformation-product toxicity, and environmental sustainability. Such an approach is essential for advancing carbonaceous nanomaterials from promising laboratory-scale technologies toward reliable and environmentally safe strategies for pharmaceutical-contaminated water remediation.
