title: CASINO Predictions of Polyethylenimine Nanofiber Sample Preparations for SEM
summary: This study presents a method of predetermining the necessary sample preparations, and parameter settings to set a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) for optimal visual detection of morphological imaging of micro- and nanostructured biodegra
content: This study presents a method of predetermining the necessary sample preparations, and parameter settings to set a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) for optimal visual detection of morphological imaging of micro- and nanostructured biodegradable polymers, such as polyethylenimine (PEI) nanofiber, cross-section diameters between 50-500nm. Computational predictions of simulated SEM micro and nano scale images can provide optimization for the characterization of material systems and provide a complementary research observation for training artificial intelligence (AI) models, reducing trial-and-error experimental testing. Micro and nano scale fibers with cross-sectional diameters between 50-500nm serve as building blocks for membrane materials for medical, energy, space, and military applications. This method utilizes the computational prediction software, Monte CA rlo SI mulations of electro N trajectory in s O lid ( CASINO ), to predetermine mounting base and sample coating material for the sample as well as the of number of electrons and voltage of the electron beam from the SEM. The method of employing CASINO reduces the optimization needed to lessen trapped incident beam electrons, electron overcharging of the sample and deterioration of samples during SEM use and provide insight into improving SEM images of various layered materials. Sample preparation optimization using CASINO agrees with consistently used parameters and narrows the range for incongruency across studies, supporting a fabrication standard for increased yield verse expended product used for SEM verification purposes.

title: Reconstrução da vegetação dos biomas brasileiros com baixo de CO2 atmosférico e a existência de fogo no Último Máximo Glacial
summary: O Último Máximo Glacial representa o fim da última glaciação e é marcado pela redução na temperatura média de todo o globo, em comparação as médias atuais. Nesse período, as flutuações climáticas causaram mudanças na vegetação. No entanto,
content: O Último Máximo Glacial representa o fim da última glaciação e é marcado pela redução na temperatura média de todo o globo, em comparação as médias atuais. Nesse período, as flutuações climáticas causaram mudanças na vegetação. No entanto, uma análise que leve em consideração a influencia da baixa concentração de dióxido de carbono (CO2) atmosférico e fogo sobre a vegetação são escassos. Frente a isso, o presente estudo pretende reconstruir a vegetação dos biomas brasileiros para cenários distintos, com diferentes nível de CO2 atmosférico e a existência fogo no Último Máximo Glacial (UMG) e no período Pré-Industrial (PI). Para tanto, foi utilizada como metodologia a simulação de reconstruções da cobertura da vegetação, o modelo Land-surface Process and exchanges (LPX), com dados do modelo Miroc de circulação geral da atmosfera. Foram avaliados quatro cenário de reconstrução da vegetação dos biomas brasileiros, para o período pré-industrial e para o UMG, com mudança da variação da concentração atmosférica de CO2 e a existência de incêndios florestais. Os resultados mostraram fragmentação da vegetação, sobretudo para a redução das florestas tropicais e temperadas, com árvores de grandes portes, substituídas por florestas menos adensadas, com dossel aberto ou regiões com vegetação rasteira ou até mesmo desérticas. A hipótese de aparecimento de Refúgios Amazônicos foi verificado. A mudança na concentração do CO2 e a existência de fogo podem acelerar o processo de fragmentação da vegetação dos biomas brasileiros, acelerando o processo de savanização

title: Sampling decisions for quantifying soil carbon change: resampling the same locations increases efficiency and precision
summary: Quantifying changes in soil carbon commonly relies on sampling designs that either return to new or the same locations in the project area. When the intention is to quantify change caused by adoption of different management practices, these
content: Quantifying changes in soil carbon commonly relies on sampling designs that either return to new or the same locations in the project area. When the intention is to quantify change caused by adoption of different management practices, these same approaches are used but complemented with control areas that function as counterfactual, business-as-usual conditions. For both monitoring and causal estimation, a key design decision underpins the efficiency and precision of a sampling campaign: whether to 1) resample an independent set of samples or 2) resample the same point locations (paired resampling). Using repeated measurements of soil carbon concentrations and stocks from 796 locations across 80 agricultural fields distributed across 20 strata, we first evaluate the sampling efficiency and precision benefits of paired resampling within a monitoring context. In monitoring, we find that resampling the same point locations resulted in an ~2.5-times improvement in precision, which translated to gains in sampling efficiency of 6.7- and 5.5-times fewer samples required to detect change in soil carbon concentrations and stocks, respectively. For causal estimation, where more factors generate uncertainty in the change estimate, paired resampling improved precision by 1.75- and 1.95-times and sampling efficiencies by 3.1- and 3.8-times for concentrations and stocks. Our results are consistent with directional expectations from sampling theory that revisiting sampling locations provides gains in precision and efficiency for quantifying change. However, by testing this theory with a large empirical dataset, we reveal that theoretical benefits translate to real-world, practical benefits of paired resampling designs for overcoming noise generated by the large size and high variability of soil carbon contents to detect the signal of soil carbon change. Our results are relevant for informing the efficiency and precision of designs for regional and national programs focused on tracking and improving soil conditions for soil health, food security and climate mitigation.

title: Innovation and Practice in Teaching Forced Vibration of Packaged Products Under Periodic Excitation Using Context‐Based Instruction and Dialectical Thinking
summary: This study examines pedagogical innovation and practice in teaching forced vibration of packaged products under periodic excitation, grounded in context‐based instruction and dialectical thinking. First, the characteristics and mathematical
content: This study examines pedagogical innovation and practice in teaching forced vibration of packaged products under periodic excitation, grounded in context‐based instruction and dialectical thinking. First, the characteristics and mathematical formulations of periodic excitation are introduced in the context of transport vibration scenarios across engineering domains, and a mathematical model under the periodic excitation is subsequently developed for a practical computer packaged product. Subsequently, an innovative three‐step phenomenon‐based context‐based teaching approach is adopted to systematically structure the teaching content of forced vibration in packaged products under periodic excitation, vividly demonstrating the teaching of forward and inverse problems in forced vibration under periodic excitation. Finally, the optimality of vibration damping in packaging engineering is addressed. Teaching effectiveness is validated through pre‐testing, post‐testing and statistical analysis; the discussion is extended to the cutting‐edge field of modern cushion packaging, centring on optimal balance under multisource uncertainty. Compared with conventional teaching practices, this instructional approach doubles the improvement in students' core professional competencies and self‐learning motivation, providing a replicable framework for pedagogical reform of core courses in packaging engineering.

title: Supercritical-assisted atomization of a dual antioxidant formulation using PVP and HP-β-cyclodextrin as protective carriers
summary: Vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid, AA) and Vitamin E (α-tocopherol, TOC) are widely used in topical formulations because of their antioxidant properties, although their application is limited by poor physicochemical stability. This work investigat
content: Vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid, AA) and Vitamin E (α-tocopherol, TOC) are widely used in topical formulations because of their antioxidant properties, although their application is limited by poor physicochemical stability. This work investigates Supercritical-Assisted Atomization (SAA) as a strategy to improve antioxidant stability and modulate AA release for topical applications. Dual-antioxidant microparticles containing AA and TOC were produced using hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as protective carriers. The effects of the active ingredient-to-carrier ratio and total solute concentration on particle formation and performance were systematically investigated. FESEM analysis showed that both the AA-to-carrier ratio and TOC incorporation had negligible effects on particle morphology, yielding spherical microparticles with mean diameters of approximately 0.40–0.50 μm. In contrast, total solute concentration was the main parameter governing particle size, with an increase to 100 mg/mL producing particles of about 0.80 μm. Mechanistic modeling of the release profiles revealed distinct transport mechanisms for the two carrier systems. Increasing the HP-β-CD content reduced the rapidly available AA fraction, resulting in a more homogeneous and controlled release. Conversely, higher PVP content modified the diffusional properties of the hydrated polymeric matrix, slowing AA transport. TOC incorporation accelerated AA release in both carrier systems, suggesting modifications of the particle microenvironment and enhanced AA mobility. UV–Vis analysis demonstrated that both carriers effectively protected AA against light- and oxygen-induced degradation, while preserving antioxidant performance. These results highlight SAA as a promising technology for producing stable carrier-based antioxidant microparticles with tunable release properties suitable for topical delivery.

title: Lettuce Yield, Quality, and Water Productivity as Affected by Deficit Irrigation and Superabsorbent Polymer Dose
source: New Zealand Journal of Crop and Horticultural Science
summary: Water scarcity is increasingly limiting horticultural production, particularly in Mediterranean environments, making strategies that enhance water productivity (WP) a priority. This study evaluated the effects of four irrigation volumes (10
content: Water scarcity is increasingly limiting horticultural production, particularly in Mediterranean environments, making strategies that enhance water productivity (WP) a priority. This study evaluated the effects of four irrigation volumes (100%, 75%, 50%, and 25% of the water volume required to restore container water capacity, WC) and three doses of a biodegradable, algae‐derived superabsorbent polymer (SAP) (Control, D1: 0.1 g L −1 , D2: 0.2 g L −1 ) on container‐grown lettuce. Compared with 100% WC, total fresh weight was not significantly reduced at 75% WC (−1.4%), whereas it decreased by 34.5% and 76.9% under 50% and 25% WC, respectively. The highest SAP dose (D2) increased total fresh weight by 17.8%, leaf area by 14.2%, and WP by 8.9% compared with the control. No significant irrigation × SAP interaction was detected for growth parameters, indicating an additive effect of the polymer. WP was highest under moderate deficit (75% and 50% WC). A significant interaction was observed only for the flavonol index, which increased under water deficit in control plants, whereas this response was attenuated by SAP. Under the tested conditions, combining moderate deficit irrigation with SAP may reduce irrigation volumes by 25% without yield losses, supporting more sustainable water management in container‐grown vegetables.

title: Native architecture of a mitochondrial oxphosome
summary: Mitochondrial cristae are the primary bioenergetic units of eukaryotic cells, yet the molecular principles that dictate their morphologies remain largely unknown. Using in situ cryo-electron tomography and integrative modeling, we resolve t
content: Mitochondrial cristae are the primary bioenergetic units of eukaryotic cells, yet the molecular principles that dictate their morphologies remain largely unknown. Using in situ cryo-electron tomography and integrative modeling, we resolve the native organization of the respiratory machinery in the diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum. Unlike previously studied animals and green algae, diatoms possess tubular crista, a conserved membrane architecture found in diverse and globally relevant species. We identify several native supercomplexes assemblies, including an oxphosome comprising the entire respiratory chain. Our results, together with molecular dynamics analyses, reveal that these supercomplexes assemble through a lipid-mediated mechanism. We propose that tubular cristae are shaped by the interplay between membrane-bending ATP synthase oligomers that bud the hemispherical crista tips and supercomplexes that act as molecular roadblocks to constrain ATP synthase propagation, thereby balancing membrane curvature and allowing cristae body extension. Furthermore, we show that the diatom Complex I retains ancestral subunits related to fatty acid synthase. Beyond illuminating diatom bioenergetics, our findings reveal a fundamental principle of mitochondrial morphogenesis where ATP synthase-driven membrane curvature is spatially fine-tuned by respiratory supercomplexes.

title: Drought persistence is associated with ecological vulnerability and risk of Heterobasidion species through host suitability under climate change
summary: The mechanisms by which persistent drying trends affect the ecological vulnerability and risk of forest pathogens via host vegetation under climate change remain poorly understood. This study examined three major European Heterobasidion spe
content: The mechanisms by which persistent drying trends affect the ecological vulnerability and risk of forest pathogens via host vegetation under climate change remain poorly understood. This study examined three major European Heterobasidion species (Heterobasidion abietinum, Heterobasidion annosum sensu stricto (s. str.), and Heterobasidion parviporum). A probabilistic framework integrating Random Forest, Vine Copula, and conditional probability analysis was built to evaluated combined effects of temporal moisture persistence and host suitability on pathogen vulnerability and risk of Heterobasidion species across historical periods and various future climate scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, SSP370, and SSP585). The results showed that: (1) Among four drought-related metrics (intensity, frequency, temporal persistence, trend), the temporal persistence of moisture series was the strongest predictor of Heterobasidion suitability. Meteorological drought indices exhibited higher explanatory power than hydrological drought indices, indicating that long-term atmospheric drought stress shapes pathogen distributions. (2) Heterobasidion vulnerability stems from combined drought and host conditions instead of either factor alone. Under the most adverse historical compound conditions, the extremely-high-vulnerability area reached 777.14 × 104 km2 for H. abietinum, 528.67 × 104 km2 for H. annosum s. str., and 306.58 × 104 km2 for H. parviporum, which dropped respectively to 178.68 × 104 km2, 59.67 × 104 km2 and 125.84 × 104 km2 under favourable host-moisture conditions. Higher host suitability tends to mitigate vulnerability, whereas low host suitability amplifies ecological loss risk under similar drought conditions, with distinct interspecific responses. (3) Future climate will substantially alter vulnerability patterns. SSP126 and SSP245 moderately reduce overall vulnerability while SSP370 and SSP585, driven by warming and sustained drying, lead to pronounced vulnerability increases and spatial expansion with non-linear risk amplification. (4) The Ecological Risk Index (ERI) reveals rising potential pathogen risk across European forests in the future, though risk magnitude and spatial patterns vary greatly among species. The temporal persistence of moisture series acts as an important predictor of pathogen vulnerability, and host suitability modulates the transition from climatic stress to ecological risk. This study characterizes couplings in the drought–host–pathogen system using probabilistic compound-driver analysis and provides quantitative tools for forest disease hotspot mapping and adaptive forest management.

title: Outlining the afforestation and reforestation process chain for carbon dioxide removal
summary: Afforestation and reforestation (A/R) are widely promoted as carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies, yet their climate change mitigation potential depends not only on forest establishment but on whether carbon removals remain additional, d
content: Afforestation and reforestation (A/R) are widely promoted as carbon dioxide removal (CDR) strategies, yet their climate change mitigation potential depends not only on forest establishment but on whether carbon removals remain additional, durable and verifiable over time. Here we conceptualize A/R as a ‘process chain’ of coupled decisions, from site selection and establishment pathway, through stewardship, carbon storage, as well as monitoring, reporting, and verification, in which choices made at one stage constrain or shape carbon outcomes at subsequent stages. Our synthesis shows that the climate effectiveness and credibility of A/R-as-CDR are highly contingent on context: carbon sequestration rates vary across climates, soils, species and management regimes, while the durability of stored carbon can be threatened by wildfire, drought, pests, and land-use change, with the latter often driven by shifting governance conditions. Even when tree cover increases, claimed carbon removals can also be undermined by failures in governance and social legitimacy, biophysical and operational readiness, as well as accounting and verification. We therefore argue that A/R should be evaluated not by hectares planted, but by whether it delivers additional, measurable, verifiable, and durable net carbon removals from the atmosphere under conditions of social legitimacy and accountable governance. This framework reveals how risks interact across stages, how failures propagate through the system, and where interventions can improve the durability and credibility of net removals. A/R can therefore contribute meaningfully to climate mitigation, but should complement, rather than substitute for, rapid and sustained emissions reductions.

title: Stage-dependent salt susceptibility of Arabidopsis inositol transporter (INT) gene family mutants
summary: Myo-inositol transporters (INTs) are crucial for plant development and stress responses, but their specific roles in Arabidopsis under salt stress remain unclear. We investigated salt-stress responses in Arabidopsis int1, int2, and int4 mut
content: Myo-inositol transporters (INTs) are crucial for plant development and stress responses, but their specific roles in Arabidopsis under salt stress remain unclear. We investigated salt-stress responses in Arabidopsis int1, int2, and int4 mutants at both seedling and adult stages. In seedlings, int2 and int4 exhibited reduced root growth and increased salt sensitivity, particularly on an inositol-free medium, indicating their importance during early growth under limited inositol availability. In adult plants, salt stress revealed greater susceptibility in int1 and int4 when treated with 200 mM NaCl or higher. These mutants showed stronger leaf wilting, lower PSII quantum yield, and higher nonphotochemical quenching than the wild-type and int2, indicating impaired photosynthetic performance under salinity. Together, these results demonstrate that Arabidopsis INTs make distinct, stage-dependent contributions to salt tolerance: INT2 functions primarily during early seedling growth, INT1 operates in adult leaves, and INT4 is vital at both stages to maintain osmotic and photosynthetic homeostasis.

title: Large variability in aerosol size distribution, chemical composition, and ice nucleating particles over open water and sea ice in the Arctic during melt season
summary: Arctic aerosol particles influence climate directly by interacting with radiation and indirectly by modifying cloud properties, including through their role as ice-nucleating particles (INPs). However, their spatio-temporal variability, che
content: Arctic aerosol particles influence climate directly by interacting with radiation and indirectly by modifying cloud properties, including through their role as ice-nucleating particles (INPs). However, their spatio-temporal variability, chemical composition, and climate-relevant properties over open water, marginal ice zone (MIZ), and pack-ice remain poorly constrained. We investigated aerosol particle size distribution, chemical composition (in ambient air and fog), and INPs (in ambient air, fog, sea-ice, melt-pond, and bulk seawater (BSW)) during ATWAICE (ATlantic WAter pathways to the ICE in the Nansen basin and Fram Strait) expedition aboard RV Polarstern in summer 2022. Aerosol particles over the ice-free ocean were strongly influenced by primary marine emissions, whereas MIZ and pack-ice environments showed larger contributions from aged/secondary aerosol. Fog water composition indicated direct sea-spray activation and scavenging over ice-free ocean, while MIZ and pack-ice fog contained stronger signatures of sea-ice associated dissolved organic matter. INPs in ambient air were found ~43 m⁻³ at -10 °C. INPs in air and fog were predominantly heat-labile, consistent with biological material, whereas BSW, melt-pond, and sea-ice samples contained heat-labile and heat-stable INPs. Case studies combining particle concentration profiles with INP spectra did not indicate a simple and straight forward relationship between INPs and local marine sources. A net emission case (2.2 x 10⁶ m⁻² s⁻¹) showed comparable heat-labile INP fractions in air and BSW, consistent with bubble-bursting or sea-spray production. Conversely, deposition over ice-floes (-0.054 x 10⁶ m⁻² s⁻¹) coincided with ice-active, heat-labile atmospheric INPs absent from BSW, indicating upwind sources, particularly the MIZ and pack-ice environment.

title: Thermodynamic Evaluation of the Extracellular Zinc Chelator ZX1 Reveals Irving–Williams Selectivity and Preferential Sequestration of Cellular Copper
summary: Synthetic chelators are essential tools for investigating the physiological roles of metal ions. The interpretation of their biological effects critically depends on the in vitro characterization of their metal-binding selectivity under bio
content: Synthetic chelators are essential tools for investigating the physiological roles of metal ions. The interpretation of their biological effects critically depends on the in vitro characterization of their metal-binding selectivity under biologically relevant conditions together with direct validation of their cellular activity. In this study, we evaluated the coordination mode, solution dynamics, and binding selectivity of the widely used extracellular Zn(II) chelator ZX1. Titration of ZX1 with Zn(II) confirmed exclusive formation of a complex with 1:1 binding stoichiometry, with line broadening in the 1H NMR spectrum of the ZX1-Zn(II) complex indicating fluxional intraligand exchange dynamics. Spectrophotometric competition titrations across the first-row transition metal series revealed that the thermodynamic affinity of ZX1 strictly adheres to the Irving-Williams series, with affinities progressively increasing from Mn(II) to Cu(II) before decreasing sharply for Zn(II). Consequently, ZX1 binds Cu(II) with more than five orders of magnitude greater affinity than Zn(II). Consistent with these findings, ICP-MS elemental quantification revealed that incubation of 3T3 fibroblasts with ZX1 resulted in up to 70% depletion of total cellular copper, while cellular zinc levels remained statistically unaltered. In addition, cyclic voltammetry studies and binding competition assays with BCS demonstrated that ZX1 can access attomolar buffered Cu(I) through an oxygen-dependent redox-trapping mechanism that closely parallels TPEN-induced copper sequestration. Together, these results demonstrate that ZX1 preferentially coordinates Cu(II) over Zn(II) and acts in cell culture primarily as an extracellular copper sink. These findings not only provide a basis for interpreting the biological effects of ZX1 but also highlight the importance of directly evaluating the metal-binding selectivity and cellular metal levels when applying metal-selective chelators in biological systems.

title: COF-Based S-Scheme Photocatalysts for CO2 Conversion: Interfacial Charge Migration and Molecular Activation
summary: Solar-driven photocatalytic CO2 conversion offers a sustainable route for coupling carbon recycling with solar-to-chemical energy storage. However, its efficiency and product selectivity are limited by rapid charge recombination, inefficien
content: Solar-driven photocatalytic CO2 conversion offers a sustainable route for coupling carbon recycling with solar-to-chemical energy storage. However, its efficiency and product selectivity are limited by rapid charge recombination, inefficient CO2 enrichment and activation, competing proton reduction, and poorly controlled electron/proton transfer during multistep conversion. Covalent organic framework (COF)-based step-scheme (S-scheme) heterojunctions provide a distinctive platform in which selective interfacial recombination can promote charge separation while preserving strongly reducing electrons and oxidizing holes. Meanwhile, the molecular programmability of COFs enables the regulation of interfacial coupling, catalytic sites, and pore microenvironments to facilitate CO2 enrichment and activation and control reaction pathways. This Review examines how COF-based S-scheme interfaces are constructed, how their charge-transfer pathways can be reliably established, and how interfacial charge migration translates into productive CO2 chemistry. Particular attention is paid to interfacial bonding, charge redistribution, built-in electric-field formation, photoinduced carrier migration, and their relationships with intermediate stabilization and multielectron reduction. A central conclusion is that charge separation and catalytic charge utilization are distinct but inseparable design challenges. Future advances will require chemically well-defined interfaces, operando and time-resolved mechanistic validation, and the reaction-specific integration of charge migration, active-site chemistry, proton transfer, and pore microenvironments.

title: Genipin-crosslinked aligned PCL/gelatin/chitosan nanofibre scaffolds functionalised with PEDOT:PSS: electrical characterisation and cytotoxicity assessment using L929 fibroblasts
summary: Electrospun polycaprolactone/gelatin/chitosan (PCL/GE/CS) composite nanofibre scaffolds are attractive for tissue engineering. However, their intrinsic electrical insulation limits electroactive applications. Here, we report aligned PCL/GE/
content: Electrospun polycaprolactone/gelatin/chitosan (PCL/GE/CS) composite nanofibre scaffolds are attractive for tissue engineering. However, their intrinsic electrical insulation limits electroactive applications. Here, we report aligned PCL/GE/CS nanofibre scaffolds fabricated using an acetic acid/acetone-based electrospinning route that avoids chlorinated solvents, crosslinked with genipin and subsequently functionalised by PEDOT:PSS dip-coating. The optimised PCL/GE/CS stock-solution mixing ratio of 80:10:10 (v/v/v), corresponding to final polymer concentrations of 16.0, 1.0 and 0.2% (w/v), produced uniform, bead-free aligned fibres with an average diameter of 356 ± 86 nm. Genipin crosslinking improved aqueous stability, with the scaffolds retaining approximately 98.9 ± 0.2% of their initial dry mass after 14 days in PBS compared with 95.4 ± 0.4% for the corresponding non-crosslinked PCL/GE/CS scaffolds, and reduced the 24 h swelling ratio from 440.8 ± 7.7% to 395.4 ± 9.3%. Subsequent genipin crosslinking and PEDOT:PSS coating slightly increased fibre diameter while preserving the aligned architecture. Surface characterisation confirmed PEDOT:PSS deposition by FTIR and SEM-EDX sulphur mapping. Wettability improved markedly: the water contact angle decreased from 143.2 ± 1.2° for PCL to 104.2 ± 2.4° for PCL/GE/CS and to 41.6 ± 6.2° after genipin crosslinking, while PEDOT:PSS-coated mats showed rapid droplet absorption. The conductivity was anisotropic, reaching 2.22 ± 0.15 S/m parallel to fibre alignment and 1.12 ± 0.06 S/m perpendicular to the fibre axis. In vitro studies with L929 fibroblasts showed no extract-mediated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions. Direct cell culture demonstrated increasing MTT metabolic activity from day 1 to day 7, while representative Live/Dead and DAPI/phalloidin images indicated sustained cell survival, attachment and cytoskeletal organisation. These findings demonstrate measurable electrical functionality together with L929 fibroblast compatibility and support further investigation of the scaffold as a candidate platform for electroactive tissue-engineering studies.

title: Organic amendments for enhancing crop resilience under heavy metal stress: Mechanism, efficacy and implications for food safety
summary: Contamination of agricultural soils by heavy metals impairs the food production system by affecting crop productivity, food chain and ecosystem functioning. However, the remedy for this problem is often assessed in terms of increased metal
content: Contamination of agricultural soils by heavy metals impairs the food production system by affecting crop productivity, food chain and ecosystem functioning. However, the remedy for this problem is often assessed in terms of increased metal immobility rather than its impact on crops. In this review, available evidence regarding the effect of organic amendments, such as compost, manure, biochar, crop residue, biosolid and humic substances, on the resistance of crops to heavy metals is summarised. The review examines four aspects: changes in the soil chemical environment within the rhizosphere; physiological and molecular mechanisms of plant adaptation to heavy metal stress; microbiome interactions induced by organic amendments; and metal uptake by edible plant organs. Organic amendments usually decrease the availability of cationic heavy metals by elevating soil pH and cation exchange capacity (CEC), thereby enhancing adsorption and complexation with carboxyl and phenolic functional groups and shifting metals from exchangeable forms to oxidisable and residual pools. Such soil transformations result in alleviation of oxidative stress, maintenance of mineral balance and photosynthetic activity, as well as activation of antioxidants systems and metal transporters. However, efficiency of the treatment greatly depends on the type of amendment, dose, feedstock, soil type, crop species and metal itself. Some amendments may increase the mobility of oxyanions, introduce additional metals, disturb mineral balance and increase heavy metal concentrations in edible tissues. Collectively, these findings indicate the need to assess success of remediation in terms of crop tolerance, yield and product quality, in addition to heavy metal immobilisation.

title: Tattoo ink wastewater as an overlooked source of organic pigments and metals: potential and limits of microalgae -bacteria consortia for treatment and resource recovery
summary: Synthetic pigments and heavy metals released into urban water systems are a persistent concern for aquatic ecosystems. Textile effluents have been widely studied, but tattoo ink residues remain an almost unexamined source of discharge. Tatt
content: Synthetic pigments and heavy metals released into urban water systems are a persistent concern for aquatic ecosystems. Textile effluents have been widely studied, but tattoo ink residues remain an almost unexamined source of discharge. Tattooing is now common in many countries, and studio waste is expected to enter the sanitary sewer, though disposal practices have not been documented. Tattoo inks combine organic pigments, of which only a part are azo compounds (the others are mainly copper phthalocyanines, quinacridones, diketopyrrolopyrroles and dioxazines), carbon black, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, primary aromatic amines, and metals such as chromium, cadmium, cobalt and nickel in a single, highly concentrated matrix. This review synthesises the available documentation on tattoo ink composition, its regulation in the European Union, the United States, Canada, and Australia, and its pathways into wastewater infrastructure. It provides order-of-magnitude estimates of the associated loads and examines whether microalgae–bacteria consortia, which are well characterised in the treatment of textile effluent, can reasonably be applied to this matrix. We describe the mechanisms involved, compare the biological option with coagulation, adsorption, membranes, advanced oxidation and source collection, and summarise reported performance in a table that separates sorption from degradation. Critically, we identify the properties of tattoo ink effluent that limit direct extrapolation from textile data: insoluble pigment particles, very high pigment loading in the concentrate, co-occurring metals, and dispersed micro-point sources. A documented literature search found no studies testing a microalgae–bacteria consortium on real tattoo ink effluent; the closest work examines single strains or azo dyes in liquid culture. All reviewed performance data come from textile or other industrial effluents, synthetic dye solutions, or simulated metal solutions. Thus, the suitability of consortia for tattoo ink wastewater remains to be investigated. We set out the experimental and regulatory work needed before biomass valorisation within a circular bioeconomy framework can be credibly proposed for this waste stream.

title: Study on the rising trend of groundwater levels in Beijing and its impact on underground space
summary: Most large and medium-sized cities in China are water-deficient. Long-term overexploitation of groundwater has led to the deterioration of the urban geo-environment, whereas recent measures such as ecological water replenishment and groundw
content: Most large and medium-sized cities in China are water-deficient. Long-term overexploitation of groundwater has led to the deterioration of the urban geo-environment, whereas recent measures such as ecological water replenishment and groundwater abstraction control have substantially alleviated this trend. However, groundwater level rise may also cause damage to underground space and affect the development and utilization of underground space resources. Taking the Beijing Plain as an example, this study investigates the trend and patterns of urban groundwater level rise from 2019 to 2025, as well as its impact on the development and utilization of underground space. On this basis, groundwater regulation countermeasures are examined using the marginal analysis method from environmental economics. The results show that ecological water replenishment in Beijing has raised the average groundwater level in the urban plain area by 14.81 m compared with that in 2015. Groundwater level rise exerts multiple damage effects on existing underground space structures, including structural corrosion and deterioration, leakage, anti-uplift failure, increased foundation settlement, and differential hydrostatic pressure-induced damage. It also increases groundwater-related disaster risks during the construction of underground engineering projects and increases the costs of construction dewatering and groundwater cutoff measures. Through a comprehensive benefit analysis of groundwater level rise, this study proposes a multi-level prevention and control framework comprising "dynamic regulation of rising groundwater levels, improvement of anti-uplift design standards, enhancement of underground space resilience, optimization of groundwater control technologies for underground engineering, and establishment of a groundwater level monitoring and early-warning mechanism." This framework can provide a scientific basis for establishing a reasonable urban ecological water replenishment mechanism and achieving the sustainable development and utilization of underground space.

title: Two-Dimensional Ferromagnetic Weyl Half-Semimetal
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnetic topological materials provide appealing platforms for realizing spin-polarized topological states, yet the coexistence of Weyl fermions and robust high-temperature ferromagnetism remains elusive. Here, bas
content: Two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnetic topological materials provide appealing platforms for realizing spin-polarized topological states, yet the coexistence of Weyl fermions and robust high-temperature ferromagnetism remains elusive. Here, based on first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations, we predict monolayer BaMn$_4$O$_8$ to be a dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable ferromagnetic Weyl half-semimetal. \textcolor{blue}{An anisotropic Monte Carlo simulation on a $20\times20\times1$ lattice yields a finite-size transition estimate of approximately 1446~K.} The spin-resolved electronic structure reveals a fully spin-polarized state, in which the spin-up channel hosts linear Weyl band crossings near the Fermi level, whereas the spin-down channel remains insulating. Corresponding Fermi-arc edge states connecting the projected Weyl points (WPs) are clearly observed along the (100) boundary, confirming the nontrivial topology. Importantly, both the Weyl points and their associated Fermi arcs remain robust in the presence of spin--orbit coupling (SOC). \textcolor{blue}{These results identify monolayer BaMn$_4$O$_8$ as a candidate for fully spin-polarized topological transport.

title: Heavy Metal Uptake, Signalling, Detoxification and Environmental Adaptation in Plants: Mechanistic Insights and Emerging Mitigation Strategies
summary: Heavy metal contamination has emerged as a widespread environmental problem that threatens ecosystem functioning, biodiversity and plant performance across natural and managed ecosystems. Toxic elements, including cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), n
content: Heavy metal contamination has emerged as a widespread environmental problem that threatens ecosystem functioning, biodiversity and plant performance across natural and managed ecosystems. Toxic elements, including cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), nickel (Ni), zinc (Zn), aluminium (Al) and other potentially hazardous metals, can accumulate in plant tissues, disrupting growth, development, physiological processes and cellular homoeostasis while posing risks to ecological and human health through trophic transfer. Understanding the mechanisms underlying metal uptake, transport, sequestration and detoxification is therefore essential for increasing plant resilience in metal-stressed environments. This review synthesises current knowledge of plant responses to heavy metal stress, integrating physiological, biochemical, cellular, genetic and molecular mechanisms that contribute to tolerance and adaptation. Particular attention is given to the factors regulating metal accumulation and distribution within plants, including species and genotypic variation, soil physicochemical properties, rhizosphere processes, microbial associations and environmental conditions. This review also evaluates recent advances in strategies to mitigate heavy metal toxicity, including nutrient-based approaches, soil amendments, beneficial microorganisms, biostimulants, phytoremediation technologies, rhizosphere engineering and nanotechnology-assisted interventions. Emerging evidence indicates that plant responses to heavy metals are highly species-specific and strongly shaped by plant-microbe-soil interactions, emphasising the importance of integrated and context-dependent management approaches. Despite substantial progress, significant knowledge gaps remain regarding the regulation of metal partitioning, long-term adaptive responses, cross-tolerance mechanisms and the identification of critical thresholds for maintaining plant health under diverse environmental conditions. Future research integrating multiomics technologies, microbiome engineering, molecular breeding and precision remediation strategies will provide new opportunities to strengthen plant resilience and reduce the ecological risks associated with heavy metal contamination. By consolidating current advances and future directions, this review offers a comprehensive framework for understanding plant adaptation to heavy metal stress and for supporting sustainable ecosystem management in contaminated environments.

title: Branched-chain α-keto acid metabolism is controlled by SLC25A35-mediated mitochondrial import
summary: Liver is considered a primary site for systemic branched-chain alpha-keto acid (BCKA) oxidation due to its abundant dehydrogenase content. However, hepatocytes rely entirely on import of substrate generated elsewhere because they lack intri
content: Liver is considered a primary site for systemic branched-chain alpha-keto acid (BCKA) oxidation due to its abundant dehydrogenase content. However, hepatocytes rely entirely on import of substrate generated elsewhere because they lack intrinsic branched-chain transaminase activity. The mechanisms governing BCKA transit into the mitochondrial matrix remain unknown. We found that mitochondrial import, rather than dehydrogenase activity, determines hepatocellular capacity for BCKA oxidation. We identified MCT1 and MCT2 as transporters required for cellular entry and SLC25A35 as the essential mitochondrial BCKA carrier. Crucially, hepatic SLC25A35 expression is low and limits the liver's contribution to systemic clearance. These findings establish the molecular machinery for BCKA transport and redefine the liver's role in BCKA homeostasis, revealing that mitochondrial transporter abundance, rather than dehydrogenase levels, dictates BCKA metabolic flux.

title: Enabling joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation with an atmospheric foundation model
summary: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but
content: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but assimilating both requires a model that represents chemistry and meteorology together. Existing chemistry-climate models are too expensive for joint data assimilation. Here, we present AuroraChem, a fine-tuned version of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model that jointly simulates meteorology and the GEOS-Chem chemical fields needed to constrain OH. A one-year AuroraChem rollout takes 12 minutes on one GPU. Free rollouts remain stable for one year but do not fully capture seasonal cycles. Using idealized data assimilation, we find that chemical observations can constrain the meteorological state and meteorological observations can constrain the chemical state. Inserting only the chemical fields raises the annual mean spatial correlation of 500 hPa temperature from 0.89 to 0.92 and recovers the moisture and circulation pattern of the Indian summer monsoon. Inserting only the meteorological fields raises the 500 hPa OH correlation from 0.89 to 0.93, close to the 0.94 from inserting the chemical fields themselves, and recovers the OH seasonal cycle. Inserting only NO2 columns sampled at TROPOMI pixels gives an OH correlation of 0.93. These relationships likely reflect learned covariances rather than physical coupling, and covariances are what data assimilation uses to let an observation of one variable update the others. AuroraChem therefore provides a new pathway to joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation.

title: Split-and-Learn: Decoupled Learning for Reactive Transport in Heterogeneous Marine Sediments
summary: Reactive transport in heterogeneous marine sediments couples flow and multicomponent transport with nonlinear chemistry and evolving porosity and permeability, and its simulation over thousands of years is computationally expensive, especia
content: Reactive transport in heterogeneous marine sediments couples flow and multicomponent transport with nonlinear chemistry and evolving porosity and permeability, and its simulation over thousands of years is computationally expensive, especially when uncertain heterogeneity requires many simulations. We develop Split-and-Learn, a framework that keeps the sequential operator-splitting scheme of the full-order model and replaces each stage by a data-driven surrogate with its own structure. Transport is learned on a local data-driven multiscale space, either as a compressed reduced solution map (global inverse atoms) or as coarse-block pieces of the forward operator assembled into a Galerkin or least-squares Petrov-Galerkin system (local atoms). Chemistry is learned through bounded reaction extents with stoichiometric reconstruction, which preserves reaction invariants and nonnegativity. Flow uses learned interface traces and a reduced mixed multiscale solve that enforces coarse-block mass balance. We prove the stability of the split scheme with the evolving medium and bound the error of the learned solver by the accumulated one-step errors of its stages. Numerical experiments in two- and three-dimensional heterogeneous sediment domains show the accuracy and computational cost of the individual and combined learned stages against the full order split solver.

title: Dataset on the regulation of carbon allocation and spike development in wheat under low-temperature stress by exogenous glucose
summary: a. Data Content This dataset contains data on carbohydrates, sugar-metabolising enzymes, culm vascular bundle counts, yield traits and related analyses for wild-type wheat and chlorophyll b-deficient mutants under exogenous glucose and low-
content: a. Data Content This dataset contains data on carbohydrates, sugar-metabolising enzymes, culm vascular bundle counts, yield traits and related analyses for wild-type wheat and chlorophyll b-deficient mutants under exogenous glucose and low-temperature treatments. It supports the identification of site-specific differences in low-temperature damage during the reproductive growth stage, as well as the regulatory role of glucose in source-sink relationships and spike development. b. Purpose of the Dataset To preserve and share data—including measurements, organisation and analysis—from research into the mitigation of low-temperature damage during the reproductive stage of wheat by exogenous glucose, thereby supporting the analysis and verification of relationships between carbohydrate allocation, peduncle structure and yield composition. c. Target Audience This dataset is intended for researchers engaged in crop stress physiology, sugar metabolism, plant development, source-sink relationships, wheat yield formation and agroecology. d. Temporal Scope of Data 2025 e. Spatial Scope of Data The data originate from pot experiments conducted in a controlled climate chamber; the black calcareous soil used in the experiments was collected from the 0–20 cm soil layer of a field at the Gongzhuling Experimental Station.

title: Пороговая бифуркация смены арбускулярной микоризы на эктомикоризу в лесной сукцессионной модели
summary: Сукцессионная смена господствующего фотосинтетического гегемона — широколиственного дерева, поддерживающего арбускулярную микоризу (AM), — на менее продуктивные хвойные с эктомикоризой (ECM) описывается динамической системой из 31 обыкновен
content: Сукцессионная смена господствующего фотосинтетического гегемона — широколиственного дерева, поддерживающего арбускулярную микоризу (AM), — на менее продуктивные хвойные с эктомикоризой (ECM) описывается динамической системой из 31 обыкновенного дифференциального уравнения. Модель построена для лесной делянки площадью около 10 м2 и горизонта 50–60 лет. Показано, что переход имеет характер бифуркации. Хвойный подрост превращается в устойчивые островки; скорость этого превращения называют темпом градации. Равновесная биомасса эктомикоризы устойчивых островков хвойных скачком меняется с 3,9 до 80 г на делянку, и за скачком следует взрывной рост микоризы. Скачок происходит при изменении темпа градации всего на 14%. В ансамбле прогонов исход определяется не скоростью градации. Его определяет углеродный бюджет, который хвойный подрост отдаёт грибу-симбионту. При бюджете ниже порога около 0,0355 г ч−1 подрост не прорывается через критическую массу, нужную для перехода границы бифуркации. Дефицит углерода может компенсироваться мягкой засухой: при низком пороге засухи влага подавляет фотосинтез подроста лишь в самую сухую часть сезона. Граница исходов — трёхмерная поверхность в пространстве углеродного бюджета, порога засухи и темпа градации: слабость одного фактора компенсируется силой другого. Установлено, что в модели бифуркация существует только при открытом семенном потоке. При отсутствии фонового притока всходов оба режима дают вымирание. Для понимания, как минимально получить тот же результат, была построена менее многомерная модель. Редуцированная девятимерная модель построена заново из алгоритмическо- го описания биологических механизмов. Она воспроизводит класс исхода и плато биомассы; год прохождения порога в ней смещается. Расхождение траекторий pH с полной моделью характеризуется среднеквадратичной ошибкой (RMSE) не более 0,12. При включении явного расчёта дефицита давления пара (VPD) порог углеродного бюджета — то минимальное количество углерода, которое подрост отдаёт грибу-симбионту, — смещается вверх: с 0,0355 (без VPD это нижняя оценка порога) до 0,045–0,06. Атмосферная сушащая сила становится четвёртой осью границы исходов.

title: Shifting Landscapes: The Impact of Agricultural Innovation on Deforestation
summary: This paper examines the direct and indirect effects of agricultural technological change on deforestation using the introduction of genetically modified soy in the Brazilian Amazon. Soy production replaced more land and labor-intensive catt
content: This paper examines the direct and indirect effects of agricultural technological change on deforestation using the introduction of genetically modified soy in the Brazilian Amazon. Soy production replaced more land and labor-intensive cattle ranching, slowing local deforestation. However, displaced cattle ranching relocated to connected areas, clearing forest elsewhere and offsetting 39 percent of the forest that was spared locally. Displacement is mediated by the road network, which enables labor mobility and continued access to fixed slaughterhouses. On net, the introduction of genetically modified soy preserved approximately 25,600 square kilometers of forest between 2003 and 2010.

title: Mapping Taliks Beneath Water Tracks Using Ground‐Penetrating Radar Grids
summary: Permafrost is degrading, raising concerns about its impact on global climate. Taliks, year‐round unfrozen layers of ground in permafrost environments, affect hydrological and carbon dynamics and contribute to permafrost degradation. Despite
content: Permafrost is degrading, raising concerns about its impact on global climate. Taliks, year‐round unfrozen layers of ground in permafrost environments, affect hydrological and carbon dynamics and contribute to permafrost degradation. Despite their importance, they are seldom studied because of the difficulty in identifying them. Water tracks (zones overlying permafrost concentrating water flow) have an important role in controlling catchment hydrology, yet their contribution to talik formation remains poorly understood. The objective of this study is to detect and map suprapermafrost taliks using ground‐penetrating radar (GPR) with a specific focus on those located beneath water tracks. Fieldwork was conducted during winter in a discontinuous permafrost area near Eight Mile Lake, Alaska (United States). A GPR with 600 MHz center‐frequency antennas was used along multiprofile grids. Ground‐penetrating radar proved to be a reliable tool for mapping talik extent with a square‐meter spatial resolution. Whereas the top of the taliks was clearly detected with a root mean square error of 17 cm and a 10‐cm uncertainty, their bottoms were less identifiable due to limited signal penetration. Both isolated and lateral suprapermafrost taliks were observed at the site. Importantly, taliks were more present, shallower, and thicker beneath water tracks than in adjacent areas. Additionally, thicker snow cover and topographic depressions were significantly associated with shallower taliks (respective significant correlations of −0.65 and 0.53). Water tracks thus appear to be hot spots for talik formation and expansion, with important implications for winter subsurface hydrological connectivity. These findings highlight the need for increased attention to the processes occurring during the winter in water track environments.

title: Global gridded air-sea oxygen flux inferred from a machine learning-based dissolved oxygen product
summary: We present estimates of the monthly open ocean air-sea O 2 flux from 2004 to 2024 on a 1 ° ×1° grid spanning 64.5° S to 79.5° N. The flux is computed using 4-dimensional ocean dissolved oxygen (DO) fields derived from Argo float and shipboa
content: We present estimates of the monthly open ocean air-sea O 2 flux from 2004 to 2024 on a 1 ° ×1° grid spanning 64.5° S to 79.5° N. The flux is computed using 4-dimensional ocean dissolved oxygen (DO) fields derived from Argo float and shipboard observations via machine learning algorithms (GOBAI-O 2 , Sharp et al., 2023). Flux uncertainties are quantified by generating a large ensemble of flux estimates, first propagating errors from the dissolved oxygen product, then computing fluxes across all combinations of three gas exchange parameterizations that account for bubble-mediated flux and three wind products. We apply DO adjustments to align our resolved global annual mean fluxes with those derived from scaling global ocean heat uptake and regional annual mean fluxes with those derived from ocean inversions. Our results show larger seasonal flux variations at high latitudes than at low latitudes, with clear differences between major ocean basins. Both adjusted and unadjusted annual mean flux estimates exhibit strong ocean O 2 sinks at high latitudes, weak sources in the low-to-mid latitude subtropics, and weak sinks near the Equator. The annual mean adjustment enhances ocean O 2 uptake in the northern high latitudes and reduces outgassing in the tropics and northern subtropics, while slightly weakening uptake in the Southern Ocean. We evaluate our flux seasonal cycles and annual mean values by comparing forward transport simulations with atmospheric O 2 observations from global airborne surveys and surface sampling stations. The simulations reproduce the observed mean seasonal cycles well, but some differences remain in the annual mean latitudinal gradients. We analyze fractional variance contributions from DO, wind, and gas exchange scheme uncertainties and their interactions at regional and hemispheric scales for both climatological monthly and annual mean fluxes. This dataset marks a major improvement over existing air-sea O 2 flux products, as it includes the resolution of interannual variability in the flux seasonal cycle, the use of advanced machine learning-based DO fields that better represent complex spatial and temporal patterns, and robust uncertainty quantification across various scales. This dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22119163 (Jin, 2026).

title: Science-based targets to inform national ocean sustainability gaps
summary: The ocean supports the biosphere and human well-being but is increasingly threatened by global change. Policymakers need tools to assess whether marine ecosystems and environmental functions remain within sustainable levels and to prioritiz
content: The ocean supports the biosphere and human well-being but is increasingly threatened by global change. Policymakers need tools to assess whether marine ecosystems and environmental functions remain within sustainable levels and to prioritize actions. Existing ocean indices assess environmental conditions, but none evaluate sustainability against scientific reference levels incorporating critical natural capital. The Environmental Sustainability Gap (ESGAP) framework offers such a strong-sustainability approach, yet its applications remain broad and lack several dimensions specific to ocean sustainability. Here, we adapted the framework to develop a Blue ESGAP marine indicator set for Indonesia, an archipelagic country highly dependent on the ocean. Through participatory workshops, we selected eight indicators representing four environmental functions: source, sink, life support, and human health and welfare. We assessed them against sustainability reference levels using available data. Results revealed contrasting sustainability gaps. Seawater quality, plastic pollution, and Ramsar site status achieved high scores indicating that targets were met or nearly met, although data quality was moderate for the latter two. Fish stocks showed greater gaps, with only about two-thirds of national and migratory stocks within sustainable levels. Coral reefs and seagrass ecosystems were generally in moderate condition, while the conservation outlook of heritage sites raised significant concerns. The assessment also revealed methodological and data limitations in developing ocean sustainability indicators. The Blue ESGAP provides a science-based, integrated perspective on marine sustainability gaps and trends, complementing ocean accounting and supporting policy prioritization and dialogue towards the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: At the End of the World: A Transdisciplinary Approach to the Apocalyptic Imaginary in the Past and Present
summary: At the End of the World offers a multifaceted effort to unfurl the biblical apocalyptic imaginary as it has played out in Western history. By troubling disciplinary boundaries, it unites leading voices to interrogate continuities between ap
content: At the End of the World offers a multifaceted effort to unfurl the biblical apocalyptic imaginary as it has played out in Western history. By troubling disciplinary boundaries, it unites leading voices to interrogate continuities between apocalyptic motifs of the past and present, thereby providing unique tools for critically understanding the shapes that apocalypse and apocalypticism take in today’s cultural, social, and political spheres.

title: Mekong River sediment decline, downstream reassembly, and weakening sediment exchange with Tonle Sap Lake
summary: Study region Mekong River Basin. Study focus Dam expansion has disrupted Mekong sediment transport, yet mainstream sediment decline, downstream reassembly, and sediment exchange with Tonle Sap Lake are often studied separately. We combine l
content: Study region Mekong River Basin. Study focus Dam expansion has disrupted Mekong sediment transport, yet mainstream sediment decline, downstream reassembly, and sediment exchange with Tonle Sap Lake are often studied separately. We combine long-term suspended-sediment concentration (SSC) observations, period- and hydrograph-limb-specific rating curves, and daily discharge reconstructed by a coupled hydrological–hydrodynamic model at Chroy Chang Var (CCV; delta apex) and Prek Kdam (PK; Tonle Sap gateway). Rating-curve and reconstructed-discharge uncertainties are jointly propagated to quantify changes from pre-dam (1962–1992) to post-dam (2010–2024). New hydrological insights for the region Mean annual suspended sediment load (SSL) at Chiang Saen declined by 85.7%, from 68.00 [95% uncertainty interval: 64.78, 71.46] to 9.75 [9.06, 10.41] Mt yr⁻¹ . Yet post-dam SSL at CCV was 54.55 [50.81, 58.90] Mt yr –1 , of which Chiang Saen represented only 17.9% and cumulative net interstation changes 82.1% [80.6, 86.3%]. These are net reach-scale changes, not identified sediment sources or historical recovery. At PK, mean lakeward SSL was 2.41 [2.26, 2.56] Mt yr –1 and the mean inflow-minus-outflow balance was −0.59 [−0.87, −0.33] Mt yr –1 . Lakeward SSL and reverse-flow volume declined significantly and covaried, although shared discharge dependence partly explains this correlation. Reconstructed flow-weighted SSC showed no significant trend, whereas observation-based evidence for declining SSC was model-dependent. The modern Mekong shows upstream depletion, downstream reassembly, and weakening sediment connectivity with Tonle Sap Lake.

title: GCase deficiency impairs uptake of α-synuclein-loaded ectosome by astrocytes
summary: SUMMARY Parkinson’s disease (PD) involves the prion-like propagation of α-synuclein. One mechanism for the spread of α-synuclein between neurons in PD is ectosomes. But PD is a multicellular disorder in which astrocytes also play a critical
content: SUMMARY Parkinson’s disease (PD) involves the prion-like propagation of α-synuclein. One mechanism for the spread of α-synuclein between neurons in PD is ectosomes. But PD is a multicellular disorder in which astrocytes also play a critical role. How astrocytes take up ectosomes and whether this is affected in PD is unclear. Here we show that GCase-deficiency, as occurs in PD, impairs astrocytic uptake of neuron-derived ectosomes containing α-synuclein. The defect in ectosome uptake by astrocytes is driven by compromised macropinocytosis and can be rescued by reducing glucosylceramides or restoring lysosomal function. These findings identify sphingolipid metabolism as a key regulator of ectosome uptake by primary and iPSC-derived astrocytes. They also support a shift from the uptake and clearance of α-synuclein by astrocytes in health, towards the transmission of α-synuclein pathology towards neurons in PD. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT HIGHLIGHTS GCase-deficiency impairs astrocytic but not neuronal uptake of lipids GCase-deficient astrocytes have impaired uptake of ectosomes containing α-synuclein Impaired uptake by astrocytes mediated by reduced macropinocytosis Reducing glucosylceramide or restoring lysosomal function rescues ectosome uptake

title: Africa and the Politics of Ocean Regions
summary: Much of what has been written about Africa’s place in world politics begins on land. Africa and the Politics of Ocean Regions takes maritime spaces as its starting point. The two-part edited volume explores ocean governance across multiple
tags: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
content: Much of what has been written about Africa’s place in world politics begins on land. Africa and the Politics of Ocean Regions takes maritime spaces as its starting point. The two-part edited volume explores ocean governance across multiple interconnected scales. It demonstrates how marine ecosystems, coastal communities, sovereign states, and international institutions give ocean regions their political character and what this perspective reveals about Africa’s role in international relations. Structured in two complementary parts, it begins by examining the conceptual and legal dimensions of global ocean governance. Understanding that the world’s oceans form an interconnected body of water, Part I interrogate the normative tensions underpinning the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, the governance challenges facing regional seas, including the Arctic and the South Atlantic, and the legal implications of sea-level rise Pacific islands. Part II grounds these conceptual debates in African maritime politics, analysing how African states, island nations and regional organisations navigate ocean governance. It considers their room for manoeuvre and the constraints of limited maritime capacity. Contributors analyse how African states use international law to advance their interests and how African island states assert their maritime identities and their leadership on the blue economy. They also explore the unrealised potential for maritime cooperation within BRICS+, criminal markets in waters where surveillance is limited and the ocean security challenges facing the Southern African Development Community. Bringing together scholars and practitioners, the volume will appeal to scholars of International Relations, African Studies and Maritime Studies and to policymakers working on maritime security, regional cooperation and sustainable ocean development. It carries forward the late Professor Maxi Schoeman’s vision for an African-centred study of ocean politics.

title: Future VLSI Architectures for Neuromorphic Computing, Edge AI and Sustainable Systems
source: International Journal for Multidimensional Research Perspectives
summary: The future of Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) architectures is being fundamentally reshaped by the intersecting demands of Neuromorphic computing, edge artificial intelligence (AI), and sustainable electronic systems. As traditional CMO
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: The future of Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) architectures is being fundamentally reshaped by the intersecting demands of Neuromorphic computing, edge artificial intelligence (AI), and sustainable electronic systems. As traditional CMOS scaling nears its physical limitations, researchers are exploring bio-inspired Neuromorphic designs that mimic the brain's energy-efficient computing mechanisms using spiking neural networks (SNNs), as demonstrated by platforms like Intel’s Loihi and IBM’s True North (Davies et al., 2018; Merolla et al., 2014). In parallel, edge AI is driving the need for VLSI systems capable of performing high-speed, low-latency inference directly on-device, thus reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure. Hardware accelerators such as Eyeriss and Google’s EdgeTPU offer promising solutions through energy-aware architecture and domain-specific design (Chen et al., 2019; Jouppi et al., 2017). These innovations are increasingly evaluated not just on performance, but also on ecological impact. Emerging sustainable VLSI solutions include non-volatile memory technologies like ReRAM and PCM, in memory computing approaches that reduce data movement, and eco-friendly materials like carbon nanotubes and organic semiconductors (Sebastian et al., 2020; Rajendran et al., 2020). However, despite significant advancements, challenges persist in fabrication scalability, algorithm-hardware co-design, and lifecycle sustainability assessment. This paper explores the synergetic evolution of these domains and highlights the critical need for interdisciplinary collaboration to develop future VLSI architectures that are intelligent, efficient, and environmentally responsible. The convergence of Neuromorphic computing, edge AI, and green hardware marks a paradigm shift, positioning VLSI not only as a medium for computation but as a cornerstone of sustainable technological progress.
