title: Logarithmic Normalization and Standard Deviation Modification for Enhanced Sensitivity in Objective Criteria Weighting
source: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making
summary: Objective weighting methods are essential in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) because criterion weights directly influence alternative rankings. However, dispersion-based weighting approaches may assign excessive importance to criteria
content: Objective weighting methods are essential in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) because criterion weights directly influence alternative rankings. However, dispersion-based weighting approaches may assign excessive importance to criteria with high variability, resulting in an imbalanced weighting structure. This study proposes LOGSTA-D, an extension of the Logarithmic Normalization and Standard Deviation (LOGSTA) method that introduces a Dispersion Compression Transformation based on the square root of standard deviation. The transformation is designed to moderate differences in criterion dispersion before logarithmic dispersion is used to derive the final criterion weights. The proposed method is evaluated using a supplier selection dataset consisting of nine alternatives and eight criteria and is integrated with four MCDM methods, namely SAW, MOORA, WP, and WASPAS. The results show that LOGSTA-D produces a more moderated distribution of criterion weights by reducing the dominance of highly dispersed criteria and redistributing importance toward criteria with lower initial weights. Across the evaluated MCDM methods, the resulting rankings exhibit a high degree of consistency, with limited changes among intermediate alternatives. The robustness analysis shows that the LOGSTA-D with MCDM framework achieves a robustness value of 0.9875, compared with 0.9604 for the LOGSTA with MCDM framework, indicating a higher level of ranking consistency under the evaluated conditions. These findings demonstrate that LOGSTA-D provides a controlled dispersion-based weighting mechanism that can support robust decision-making in supplier selection problems.

title: HIVE Weighting: A Novel Heterogeneity-Aware Approach for Criteria Weighting in Multi-Criteria Decision Making
source: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making
summary: Objective criterion weighting plays an important role in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), particularly when decision outcomes depend on how differences among criteria are represented. However, conventional objective weighting approach
content: Objective criterion weighting plays an important role in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM), particularly when decision outcomes depend on how differences among criteria are represented. However, conventional objective weighting approaches may emphasize specific statistical characteristics of the decision matrix without explicitly considering criterion heterogeneity as an integrated concept. This study proposes Heterogeneity-Informed Value Emphasis (HIVE) Weighting, a Heterogeneity-Informed Value Emphasis approach, for objective criterion weighting in MCDM. The method incorporates the mean, standard deviation, and relative variability of normalized criterion values to construct a heterogeneity-based measure of criterion importance. The resulting weights are then integrated with established MCDM methods to examine their applicability in alternative evaluation. A comparative analysis is conducted against Entropy, WENSLO, LOGSTA, CRITIC, and MEREC, followed by evaluations using the SAW and MOORA methods. Sensitivity analysis is further performed by varying criterion weights across multiple perturbation scenarios to examine the stability of the resulting rankings. The findings indicate that HIVE generates a more balanced representation of criterion importance than several comparative weighting approaches while preserving compatibility with different MCDM aggregation procedures. The ranking results obtained through SAW and MOORA show consistent patterns, while the sensitivity analysis indicates that the overall ranking structure is relatively stable under changes in criterion weights. These results demonstrate that HIVE provides an interpretable and flexible framework for incorporating criterion heterogeneity into objective weighting. The proposed approach offers a basis for further research on heterogeneity-aware weighting across diverse MCDM datasets and decision-making contexts, supporting more reliable and transparent weighting practices in complex decision environments.

title: ANALISIS PERBANDINGAN WAKTU DALAM ESTIMASI BIAYA PEKERJAAN STRUKTUR PROYEK GEDUNG PRESISI 5 POLRI: METODE KONVENSIONAL VS BIM 5D
summary: This study compares the cost estimation time for structural work between conventional methods and 5D BIM for the Precision 5 National Police Building Project. Using a quantitative approach and case study, data was obtained from project docu
content: This study compares the cost estimation time for structural work between conventional methods and 5D BIM for the Precision 5 National Police Building Project. Using a quantitative approach and case study, data was obtained from project documentation and simulations. The results show that 5D BIM significantly accelerated the estimation process without compromising accuracy.

title: Adaptive Balanced Entropy Weighting for Mitigating Criterion Weight Imbalance in Multi-Criteria Decision Making
source: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making
summary: Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) relies on criterion weights to represent the relative importance of evaluation criteria in ranking alternatives. However, conventional Entropy Weighting may generate highly imbalanced weights when crite
content: Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) relies on criterion weights to represent the relative importance of evaluation criteria in ranking alternatives. However, conventional Entropy Weighting may generate highly imbalanced weights when criteria exhibit substantially different levels of information variation, potentially causing excessive dominance of particular criteria. This study proposes Adaptive Balanced Entropy (A-Entropy), an objective weighting method that integrates the information-based principle of Entropy Weighting with an adaptive balancing mechanism. The method derives entropy-based weights, measures weight imbalance using a Weight Imbalance Index, and adaptively adjusts the weights according to the identified imbalance level. The effectiveness of A-Entropy is evaluated through two MCDM case studies involving lecturer selection and leasing customer selection. The resulting weights are compared with conventional Entropy Weighting, while their effects on alternative rankings are evaluated using MOORA and PIV, respectively. The results show that A-Entropy substantially reduces weight concentration in the lecturer selection case, where the highest weight decreases from 0.4368 to 0.3333 and the lowest weight increases from 0.0042 to 0.0665. In the leasing customer selection case, the adjustment is more moderate due to its comparatively lower initial imbalance. Furthermore, A-Entropy produces higher Spearman correlations with the original rankings than Entropy, increasing from 0.8303 to 0.9030 for lecturer selection and from 0.9758 to 0.9879 for leasing customer selection. These findings indicate that A-Entropy reduces excessive criterion weight imbalance while preserving meaningful differences in criterion importance and maintaining high ranking consistency. Therefore, A-Entropy provides an adaptive objective weighting approach for MCDM-based Decision Support Systems.

title: Benchmarking Aggregation-Based MCDM Methods: A Comparative Analysis of Ranking Consistency, Stability, and Robustness
source: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making
summary: Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods are widely applied in Decision Support Systems (DSS) to address selection problems involving multiple criteria. However, differences in aggregation mechanisms may affect ranking consistency, sta
content: Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods are widely applied in Decision Support Systems (DSS) to address selection problems involving multiple criteria. However, differences in aggregation mechanisms may affect ranking consistency, stability, and robustness under changing decision conditions. This study presents a benchmarking analysis of five aggregation-based MCDM methods, namely Simple Additive Weighting (SAW), Weighted Aggregated Sum Product Assessment (WASPAS), Additive Ratio Assessment (ARAS), Complex Proportional Assessment (COPRAS), and Multi-Attributive Ideal-Real Comparative Analysis (MAIRCA), for employee selection. Ranking consistency is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation, while stability and robustness are assessed using the Ranking Stability Index and Ranking Retention Rate. SAW, WASPAS, ARAS, and COPRAS achieve perfect consistency with the reference ranking, with a Spearman coefficient of 1.0000, while MAIRCA obtains 0.9879. ARAS and COPRAS achieve the highest stability, with an RSI of 97.22%, and robustness, with an RRR of 86.11%. SAW, WASPAS, and MAIRCA achieve an RSI of 95.56% and an RRR of 77.78%. Ranking changes are mainly limited to an exchange between Candidates 1 and 9, while Candidate 3 remains first across all scenarios. These findings suggest that ARAS and COPRAS exhibit comparatively higher ranking stability under the experimental conditions considered in this study.

title: Conhecimento e práticas sobre sustentabilidade em nefrologia no Brasil
summary: RESUMO Introdução: As mudanças climáticas apresentam uma relação bidirecional com as doenças renais: enquanto fatores ambientais podem aumentar a incidência e a progressão dessas doenças, a terapia dialítica está entre as modalidades de tra
content: RESUMO Introdução: As mudanças climáticas apresentam uma relação bidirecional com as doenças renais: enquanto fatores ambientais podem aumentar a incidência e a progressão dessas doenças, a terapia dialítica está entre as modalidades de tratamento com maior impacto ambiental na área da saúde. Apesar do crescente debate internacional sobre nefrologia sustentável, esse tema permanece pouco explorado no contexto brasileiro. Objetivo: Investigar o grau de conhecimento, as percepções e as práticas relacionadas à sustentabilidade ambiental entre profissionais atuantes na nefrologia no Brasil, bem como identificar barreiras à adoção de estratégias sustentáveis nos serviços de diálise. Métodos: Estudo transversal realizado por meio de questionário online direcionado a profissionais da nefrologia. O instrumento abordou conhecimentos sobre mudanças climáticas e saúde renal, práticas sustentáveis adotadas nos serviços e barreiras institucionais à sua implementação. Resultados: Foram analisadas 180 respostas de profissionais de 20 estados brasileiros e do Distrito Federal, com predomínio de nefrologistas e enfermeiros. A maioria reconheceu a influência das mudanças climáticas sobre a saúde renal; contudo, observou-se conhecimento limitado sobre políticas públicas e estratégias estruturadas de sustentabilidade. As práticas mais frequentemente relatadas envolveram o manejo de resíduos, enquanto iniciativas como reúso de água, uso de fontes de energia renovável e estratégias de transporte sustentável foram menos prevalentes. As principais barreiras identificadas incluíram restrições financeiras, ausência de incentivos institucionais e falta de planejamento estratégico. Conclusão: Os achados evidenciam lacunas entre percepção, conhecimento e implementação de práticas sustentáveis na nefrologia brasileira, destacando a necessidade de políticas, capacitação profissional e estratégias institucionais voltadas à sustentabilidade ambiental no cuidado nefrológico.

title: Seasonal Water-Flow Risk and Business Sustainability in a Mini-Scale Hydropower Enterprise: Evidence from Central Java, Indonesia
source: Scientific Experiences in Business and Entrepreneurship
summary: Fixed-tariff power purchase agreements (PPAs) give small-scale mini-hydropower plant (MHP) entrepreneurs in Indonesia price certainty, but not certainty over the volume of electricity they can sell. This study assesses the production and re
content: Fixed-tariff power purchase agreements (PPAs) give small-scale mini-hydropower plant (MHP) entrepreneurs in Indonesia price certainty, but not certainty over the volume of electricity they can sell. This study assesses the production and revenue vulnerability of an MHP enterprise to streamflow variability through a case study of the Pageruyung-1 MHP (2 MW, run-of-river) in Kendal Regency, Central Java. Recorded daily discharge for May 2023–August 2026 was used to estimate power output, simulate energy and the effective capacity factor (CF), and construct a monthly indicative revenue index; debt service capacity was analysed as a scenario. The lowest monthly mean discharge (431 L/s, October 2023) was only about one-third of the design discharge (1,311 L/s). Simulated annual CF ranged from 43% (May–December 2023) to 88% (2025), while monthly CF fell to as low as 33% in the dry season, below the 60% regulatory benchmark. In 2024, the revenue index of the lowest month was only 44% of that of the highest month (a 56% decline), with a coefficient of variation of 32%, compared with 18% in the wetter year of 2025. Under a level repayment scenario sized at an annual debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.3, the monthly DSCR in 2024 fell below 1.0 for six consecutive months (minimum 0.58); a repayment schedule sculpted to the seasonal pattern reduced this to four months. These findings indicate that the production and revenue vulnerability of MHPs should be assessed on the basis of the monthly distribution rather than annual averages, as a foundation for liquidity and financing planning by small-scale renewable energy entrepreneurs.

title: A Phased Active Frequency Support Strategy Tailored for Wind Power HVDC Transmission Systems
summary: To mitigate the frequency stability challenges arising from insufficient system inertia and inadequate damping capacity, a phased active frequency support control strategy for the sending-end grid with collaborative participation of wind po
content: To mitigate the frequency stability challenges arising from insufficient system inertia and inadequate damping capacity, a phased active frequency support control strategy for the sending-end grid with collaborative participation of wind power and modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) is proposed, which realizes flexible mutual support and efficient utilization of multiple frequency regulation units. For wind power, a macro-variable considering frequency and power deviations is constructed based on cooperative control theory, then an adaptive frequency cooperative control method is designed based on rotor speed and pitch angle adjustment, which realizes differentiated utilization of rotor kinetic energy while fully utilizing the power regulation capability of wind turbines. For MMC-HVDC, an active frequency support control method incorporating the effects of the regulation dead band is proposed, enabling adaptive switching of its frequency regulation performance according to the degree of disturbance. On this basis, a phased frequency coordinated control strategy considering the differences in frequency support characteristics of multi-type resources is proposed to maintain frequency stability while limiting the extent of disturbance influence, where the dead zone values of multi-type resources are designed based on their power regulation margins. Finally, the performance of the proposed control strategies is validated using real-time digital simulation.

title: The Method of Distribution-Microgrid Collaborative Fault Recovery Considering Network Dynamic Reconfiguration
summary: This paper proposes a cooperative fault recovery method for distribution networks and microgrids considering dynamic network reconfiguration. First, an optimization model is constructed with the objectives of minimizing electricity purchase
content: This paper proposes a cooperative fault recovery method for distribution networks and microgrids considering dynamic network reconfiguration. First, an optimization model is constructed with the objectives of minimizing electricity purchase costs, voltage deviations, network losses, load shedding, and microgrid operation costs. The model thoroughly considers operational conditions, including power flow constraints, security operation constraints, and network reconfiguration constraints, within the distribution network. Second, to address the privacy protection requirements of distributed energy resources (DERs) in microgrids, a k-order approximation method is employed to establish an operation feasible region (OFR) model for microgrid operational flexibility resources. This model characterizes the operational characteristics of microgrids through power and energy boundary constraints. Finally, to solve the cooperative optimization problem between the distribution network and microgrids, a non-iterative solution method based on equivalent projection is proposed. This method decomposes the original problem into a distribution network-level optimization and microgrid-level subproblems, eliminating internal variables through equivalent projection technology to achieve cooperative optimization under privacy protection. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively achieve cooperative optimization of distribution network fault recovery and microgrid scheduling while protecting microgrid privacy information, significantly improving the economy and reliability of distribution network fault recovery.

title: Research on Numerical Calibration of Power in Complex Terrain Wind Farms Based on Model Reconstruction
summary: Unlike flat terrain, when air flows through mountainous terrain, it is affected by undulating terrain and ground obstacles, forming complex wind field basins. This leads to the actual power generated by wind turbines being lower than the pr
content: Unlike flat terrain, when air flows through mountainous terrain, it is affected by undulating terrain and ground obstacles, forming complex wind field basins. This leads to the actual power generated by wind turbines being lower than the predicted power. Due to the complexity and uncertainty of the terrain and environment of wind farms, there is a significant difference between the measured power of wind farms and the actual output power of wind turbines. Therefore, studying the influence of complex terrain on wind speed in wind farms is of great significance for the site selection and construction of wind turbines. This paper adopts numerical reconstruction of the actual complex mountain terrain to determine the computational domain of the complex terrain, and compares the existing data to verify the reliability of the model. By changing the ground roughness of the mountain model, the influence of roughness on the wind speed variation at different measurement points in the mountain was analyzed. The variation characteristics of wind speed at various environmental measurement points under different terrain positions and wind turbine operation conditions under complex terrain conditions were mainly studied. Through the numerical calculation of wind speed measurement data and the wind speed variation data table of wind speed measurement points, the accuracy of wind power numerical calibration in wind farms under complex terrain conditions was studied.

title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A con-vergent mixed-methods investigation and the triadic care model
summary: While clinical guidelines strongly endorse psychologically informed physiotherapy (PIP) and cognitive-behavioral techniques (CBT) for musculoskeletal pain, routine clinical uptake remains inconsistent.Most implementation research describes
content: While clinical guidelines strongly endorse psychologically informed physiotherapy (PIP) and cognitive-behavioral techniques (CBT) for musculoskeletal pain, routine clinical uptake remains inconsistent.Most implementation research describes clinician attitudes without modeling the cognitive and systemic mechanisms that impede translation into daily practice.This study investigates the "intention-behavior gap" in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation among Iranian physiotherapists using the COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation -Behavior) framework and introduces the Triadic Care Model as an operational solution.A convergent mixed-methods design (QUAN + QUAL) compliant with the Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study (GRAMMS) guidelines was conducted between 2023 and 2024.The quantitative phase surveyed 450 licensed physiotherapists using the validated Psychological Practice and Skills Tool (PPST).Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) tested hypothesized paths linking psychological self-efficacy, systemic barriers, postgraduate education, and clinical utilization.The qualitative phase comprised semi-structured, in-depth interviews with 20 practicing physiotherapists analyzed via reflexive thematic analysis.Quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated via a joint display matrix.A pronounced intention-behavior gap was identified: 78.2% (n=352) of clinicians strongly endorsed the bio psychosocial model, yet only 24.4% (n=110) routinely implemented psychological techniques.SEM demonstrated excellent fit (χ2/df=2.15,CFI=.96,TLI=.95,RMSEA=.048[90% CI: .041-.055],SRMR=.042).Psychological self-efficacy directly predicted technique utilization (β=.41, p<.001), while postgraduate training indirectly enhanced utilization via self-efficacy (β=.34, p<.001).Systemic barriers exerted a potent negative direct effect on implementation (β=-.46,p<.001).Qualitative synthesis revealed four systemic-cognitive impediments: (1) The Reimbursement Trap and Tariff Disincentives, (2) Sociocultural Stigmatization and Somatic Fixation, (3) Referral Anxiety and Boundary Ambiguity, and (4) Didactic versus Experiential Pedagogical Deficits.Physiotherapists experience high motivational readiness but severe capability and opportunity deficits.Bridging this gap requires moving beyond generic bio psychosocial advocacy toward structural reimbursement reform, experiential micro-skills training, and the adoption of the Triadic Care Model, a structured interprofessional framework linking the physiotherapist, clinical psychologist, and patient through a warm-referral pathway.

title: Towards a Lean-Oriented Multi-Mode Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem with Activity Crashing and Preemption: A Real-Case Study
summary: Integrating lean principles into the multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling problem (MRCPSP) provides a structured approach to eliminate waste of resources. This study introduces a tri-objective mixed-integer linear programming
content: Integrating lean principles into the multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling problem (MRCPSP) provides a structured approach to eliminate waste of resources. This study introduces a tri-objective mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for an extended MRCPSP variant (LMRCPSP) aimed at minimizing project makespan, total cost, and waste of resources (WoR) including both renewable and non-renewable types while ensuring compliance with minimum quality standards. The model incorporates preemptive and crashable activities to improve scheduling flexibility. It also includes rework after activity execution to ensure project quality meets or exceeds the minimum acceptable standard. A real-world construction case study validates the proposed approach, and the AUGMECON2 algorithm is employed to generate Pareto-optimal solutions and explore trade-offs among objectives. A comparative analysis with Microsoft Project schedules, along with sensitivity analyses, further demonstrates the impact of excluding key contributions, confirming that neglecting preemption, rework, or waste reduction leads to higher costs, longer durations, and reduced quality. This underscores the practical value of the proposed framework. Finally, the conclusion and further directions are provided.

title: Heavy-Load Start-Up Compensation for an IPMSM-Driven Gravity Energy Storage Hoisting Unit
summary: The hoisting unit is a key electromechanical energy-conversion component in a hoisting-based gravity energy storage system (GESS). Under heavy-load start-up conditions, an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM)-driven hoisting
content: The hoisting unit is a key electromechanical energy-conversion component in a hoisting-based gravity energy storage system (GESS). Under heavy-load start-up conditions, an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM)-driven hoisting unit may suffer from start-up rollback, delayed torque buildup, and low-speed current fluctuation, which reduce start-up reliability. This paper develops a torque-balance-based adaptive gravity feedforward (AGF) compensation framework for improving the heavy-load start-up performance of an IPMSM-driven GESS hoisting unit. An electromechanically coupled model is established to describe the interaction among the IPMSM drive, transmission mechanism, inclined load, and nonlinear friction. Based on the model, the proposed AGF provides physically matched feedforward compensation for the dominant start-up disturbances while retaining the conventional cascaded feedback structure. Comparative simulations are conducted under conventional proportional-integral (PI) control, fixed feedforward, basic AGF, and improved AGF. Under the 4.8 t full-load condition, conventional PI control produces a maximum start-up rollback of approximately 9.1 mm, while fixed feedforward reduces it to approximately 6.1 mm but introduces a pronounced transient current peak. The improved AGF further reduces the maximum rollback to approximately 0.1 mm and improves low-speed current smoothness. Under the 2.4 t half-load condition, adaptive gravity reconstruction avoids fixed-feedforward overcompensation. Simulations with the motor rotor inertia varied by ±20% around its nominal value show that the proposed strategy retains satisfactory start-up performance under moderate plant-side rotor-inertia variation. The proposed framework provides a practical control approach for improving the heavy-load start-up reliability of IPMSM-driven GESS hoisting equipment without changing the basic hardware topology.

title: Technological Cooperation in the Industrial and Agricultural Sectors between Iran and Afghanistan
source: Journal of Historical Research Law and Policy
summary: Technological cooperation in the industrial and agricultural sectors between Iran and Afghanistan, as two neighboring countries with a shared history and culture, can play a significant role in the economic and social development of both co
content: Technological cooperation in the industrial and agricultural sectors between Iran and Afghanistan, as two neighboring countries with a shared history and culture, can play a significant role in the economic and social development of both countries. However, challenges such as political and security problems, cultural and social barriers, and the lack of adequate infrastructure may hinder the realization of such cooperation. Using a descriptive–analytical method, this study presents proposed solutions for strengthening diplomatic and economic relations, establishing legal and regulatory frameworks, and utilizing regional and international capacities. The findings indicate that Iran, as a country with advanced technology in industry and agriculture, can contribute to improving agricultural and industrial production and processing in Afghanistan through the transfer of technology and technical knowledge. Moreover, research and development cooperation between universities and research centers in the two countries can lead to the creation of joint projects and technological innovations. The results of this study demonstrate that technological cooperation can increase productivity, create employment, and promote sustainable development in both countries, ultimately contributing to an improved quality of life for the people of the region.

title: Kinetically controlled proton removal via bio-inspired hybrid bilayer membrane functionalized electrode for ethylene glycol oxidation to generate C2 products
summary: HBM technology is a transformative strategy for controlling reaction selectivity in complex oxidation pathways. This approach offers a potentially scalable, renewable-energy-powered route for upcycling plastic waste derivatives into high-va
content: HBM technology is a transformative strategy for controlling reaction selectivity in complex oxidation pathways. This approach offers a potentially scalable, renewable-energy-powered route for upcycling plastic waste derivatives into high-value chemical outputs, providing significant translational value for sustainable resource recovery.

title: Electricity Load Growth Projection Based on Customer Sector in Ermera District, Timor-Leste, Using Spatial Projection Method
summary: This study presents an analysis of electricity load growth projections in Ermera District, Timor-Leste, using spatial projection methods. Accurate electricity load growth projection is a vital component of long-term power system planning, i
content: This study presents an analysis of electricity load growth projections in Ermera District, Timor-Leste, using spatial projection methods. Accurate electricity load growth projection is a vital component of long-term power system planning, infrastructure investment, and resource allocation. In developing countries like Timor-Leste, increasing population and economic expansion drive a continuous rise in energy demand. This study develops an electricity load growth projection model based on specific customer sectors (domestic, commercial, industrial, social, and government) in the Ermera District, Timor-Leste, utilizing spatial projection methods integrated with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and the Gompertz growth equation. Ermera District, characterized by its mountainous topography and prominent coffee production sector, currently faces electrification challenges with a regional electrification ratio of approximately 75%, falling below the national average of 83.4%. Historical data from 2021 to 2024 reveals a significant and synchronized expansion of the electricity customer base, surging from 3367 to 8532 customers. The domestic sector consistently represents the primary driver of total energy consumption, accounting for approximately 85% of the total customer base. Spatial analysis identifies the sub-districts of Ermera, Railaco, and Atsabe as the highest customer-density zones and future socio-economic hotspots. By employing a spatial projection method tuned to the regional context, the mathematical models successfully minimized validation deviations against recorded Electricidade de Timor-Leste (EDTL) data to a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) threshold below 10%, highlighting the superior accuracy of spatial modeling over conventional methods in handling topographical variability. The Gompertz equation was applied to model long-term trends, projecting a rapid acceleration phase for the 2025–2030 planning cycle, with predicted cumulative demand escalating from 595,365 kW in 2025 to 1,120,610 kW by 2030. To evaluate network implications, peak demand scenarios were simulated using the Electrical Transient Analyzer Program (ETAP). The power flow simulations exposed recurrent technical limitations across the distribution network, particularly marginal under-voltage conditions (0.38–0.39 kV on the low-voltage side) on peripheral buses along the extended Ermera and Letefoho feeders, alongside transformer loading risks during peak hours. To mitigate these issues and optimize grid reliability, this thesis proposes critical engineering interventions, including the strategic activation of capacitor banks, distribution transformer tap changer optimizations, phase load balancing, and network reconductoring to lower line impedance. Ultimately, these findings offer a comprehensive, spatially explicit framework to support sustainable infrastructure expansion and energy policy formulation in the Ermera District.

title: An Experimental Vision-Based Predictive Framework for Lane Detection and Vehicle Localization Under Low Visibility Conditions During Driving
summary: Reliable lane detection and vehicle localization are essential for advanced driver assistance systems, particularly under low-visibility conditions such as fog, shadows, low illumination, and degraded lane markings. This paper presents a vi
content: Reliable lane detection and vehicle localization are essential for advanced driver assistance systems, particularly under low-visibility conditions such as fog, shadows, low illumination, and degraded lane markings. This paper presents a vision-based predictive framework integrating deep convolutional neural networks, classical image processing, and Kalman filter-based state estimation supported by inertial measurement unit (IMU) data. Lane geometry is estimated from monocular camera images using a CNN-based regression model, while a confidence-adaptive predictive filter exploits vehicle motion to compensate for temporary visual degradation. The system is implemented on low-cost onboard hardware consisting of a forward-facing monocular camera, an IMU, a GPS module, and an embedded processing unit installed on a passenger vehicle. Experimental evaluation is conducted through simulation and real-world driving tests on urban highways using approximately 277000 image frames collected under diverse traffic and visibility conditions. Results demonstrate an average lane detection accuracy of 86.0%, improving to 92.7% with image enhancement. Vehicle localization achieves average lateral errors of 0.24-0.31 m and remains stable for up to 3 s during short-term loss of visual information. Real-time performance is achieved at 30 FPS with an average processing time of 26 ms per frame, confirming suitability for practical ITS deployment.

title: A Hybrid BWM-Entropy-VIKOR Model for Assessing Logistics System Maturity in Large-Scale Steel Industry
summary: Logistics maturity assessment in large-scale industries requires simultaneous consideration of managerial priorities and operational performance—a challenge inadequately addressed by existing single-source weighting models. This study devel
content: Logistics maturity assessment in large-scale industries requires simultaneous consideration of managerial priorities and operational performance—a challenge inadequately addressed by existing single-source weighting models. This study develops a hybrid Best–Worst Method (BWM)–Entropy–VIKOR framework to evaluate logistics maturity across five units of Mobarakeh Steel Company. Five dimensions—Inventory Management, Transportation, Logistics Information Technology, Human Resources, and Financial Performance—were identified through systematic literature review and validated by 15 experts (Content Validity Ratio = 0.62–0.88; Content Validity Index = 0.81–0.94; Cronbach's α = 0.89). To overcome subjectivity bias and inconsistency limitations of conventional pairwise comparisons, subjective weights were derived via the BWM and objectively integrated with Entropy-based weights from operational performance data of 60 logistics units. Final hybrid weights identify Inventory Management (0.295) and Transportation (0.250) as dominant maturity drivers. Units ranked via VIKOR—which balances group utility and individual regret under conflicting criteria—reveal central warehouse as highest maturity (Q = 0.215) and finished goods warehouse as lowest (Q = 0.526), yielding a significant performance gap (ΔQ = 0.311). Unlike prior fuzzy-based models, the proposed framework provides a replicable, data-driven diagnostic tool integrating strategic priorities with empirical variability. Findings enable evidence-based resource allocation and targeted improvement planning in capital-intensive manufacturing contexts.

title: Gearbox Fault Diagnosis in Variable Speed Conditions Using Sensor Fusion and Deep Transfer Learning-based Multi-Channel CNN
summary: This paper presents a novel neural network structure designed for the classification of individual and combined faults in wind turbine gearboxes. This structure features a deep multi-channel convolutional neural network (MC-CNN) that facili
content: This paper presents a novel neural network structure designed for the classification of individual and combined faults in wind turbine gearboxes. This structure features a deep multi-channel convolutional neural network (MC-CNN) that facilitates simultaneous processing of images captured by sensors in different orientations. Therefore, the developed fault diagnoser utilizes a broader range of features for training the network, thereby enhancing the accuracy of fault classification. Subsequently, by incorporating a generalized loss function based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)—a distance metric for comparing probability distributions—along with Deep Domain Confusion (DDC) transfer learning, the proposed method not only detects fault labels but also adapts to features extracted from vibration images at varying speeds. This adaptability preserves the network's functionality under varying load conditions in wind turbines and ensures its effectiveness in low-data scenarios. For testing and evaluating the performance of this method, a wind turbine laboratory testbed was constructed to generate real data in various fault classes. The results demonstrate that the developed method achieves an average accuracy of 99.95% on validation data (used in transfer learning) and 85.15% on test data (have no role in the training process), confirming its superior performance compared to existing approaches.

title: Improving Parameters Affecting Copper Ore Flotation in a Darreh Alu Copper Complex Concentrator
summary: Hydrodynamic components in column flotation have a great impact on the performance and efficiency of the process. Computational fluid dynamics can be used as a powerful numerical method to analyze and predict the components of this process.
content: Hydrodynamic components in column flotation have a great impact on the performance and efficiency of the process. Computational fluid dynamics can be used as a powerful numerical method to analyze and predict the components of this process. Therefore, in this research, the flotation process has been modeled using the commercial software ANSYS Fluent. The modeling has been carried out in two phases and using the volume of fluid (VOF) module. In the design step, the independence of the solution from the grid has been examined, and then the calibration of the developed numerical model has been examined. For different methods of using blades inside the flotation cell, the flow field, bubble diameter, and gas retention have been investigated. The results showed that horizontal blade placement has the best performance in reducing axial mixing in the column, and using this blade placement method, the axial velocity can be reduced by up to 75%. The results also showed that increasing the speed of the agitator from 700 rpm leads to an increase in the separation forces; as a result, the recovery of copper particles inside the flotation cell decreases. On the other hand, increasing the speed of the agitator leads to an increase in the instability of the foam phase. The reason for this can be considered the production of bubbles with a larger diameter due to the increase in the speed of the agitator. Larger bubbles mean more surface energy and, as a result, less recovery of copper particles. Also, as the agitator gets closer to the lower part of the flotation cell, the effect of the turbulence caused by the rotation of the agitator on the phase increases, making the foam phase more unstable and reducing the recovery of copper particles. As the concentration of the foaming agent increases, the size of the bubbles produced decreases; as a result, the stability of the foam phase increases, and with increasing the stability of the foam phase. We can expect an increase in the recovery of copper particles. As the percentage of solids in the pulp increases, the recovery of copper particles also increases.

title: A Hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian Probability Model for Predicting Paraffin Deposits in Ball Valves During High-Paraffin Oil Transportation
summary: This paper develops a hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian probabilistic model for predicting asphaltene-resin-paraffin deposit (ARPD) formation in ball valves. A new approach to describing the deposition process is proposed, in which the carrier pha
content: This paper develops a hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian probabilistic model for predicting asphaltene-resin-paraffin deposit (ARPD) formation in ball valves. A new approach to describing the deposition process is proposed, in which the carrier phase ( highly paraffin oil) is specified by an analytical velocity field, and the dispersed phase is modeled by an ensemble of particles. The key element of the study is the probabilistic function of particle adhesion to the wall, which takes into account three factors: oil supercooling relative to the wax onset temperature (WAT), the distance to the wall, and the local flow velocity. A particle recirculation algorithm is implemented, ensuring the preservation of the total particle number and the statistical significance of the ensemble throughout the simulation. A series of computational experiments showed that the model correctly reproduces the threshold nature of paraffin deposits (deposition begins only at T < WAT ) and allows observing the three-phase dynamics of the narrowing of the flow area. The model revealed that the most intense fouling occurs not in the narrowest cross-section of the ball valve, but in the adjacent transition zones ("seats"), which is explained by hydrodynamic conditions. The model was verified, confirming that the boundary conditions for no-flow are met and particles remain in the system.

title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
summary: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy log
content: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. This algorithm calculates an integrated safety assessment, ranks carriers by risk level, and identifies potential violations. A method of adaptive membership functions has been applied to handle uncertainty and qualitative parameters. A verification study was conducted on theoretical cases covering a range of operational scenarios. A software solution — a Python module for fuzzy inference and visualization has also been implemented, expanding the capabilities of intelligent transportation systems. The results demonstrate that the developed system correctly ranks transport enterprises by risk level. Verification on five theoretical cases (TK1-TK5) confirmed the model's ability to generate an Integrated Safety Assessment (ISA) from 0 to 1, effectively distinguishing between exemplary compliance and systematic critical violations. For instance, a critically problematic scenario (TK4) received a low ISA of 0.34, signaling the need for immediate intervention, while a case with systematic violations (TK5) scored 0.55, near the predefined acceptability threshold of 0.5.

title: A game-theoretic approach for pricing of biomass and biofuel and determining the amount of carbon emission tax in the sustainable supply chain of biofuel
summary: This work focuses on the pricing of biomass and biofuel and on determining the amount of the carbon emission tax. The farmer, the biorefinery, and the government are also involved in this problem. Transportation of biomass between the farm
content: This work focuses on the pricing of biomass and biofuel and on determining the amount of the carbon emission tax. The farmer, the biorefinery, and the government are also involved in this problem. Transportation of biomass between the farm and the biorefinery and biofuel from the biorefinery to the fuel market are considered. The government imposes taxes on carbon emissions caused by biomass production processes. This problem is solved and compared under two scenarios of the game structure with different decision-making orders between the farmer and the biorefinery. In the end, a numerical example is presented, a numerical sensitivity analysis is performed, and the results and management points are stated. The results show that the Nash framework leads to higher biomass and biofuel prices and a higher carbon emission tax compared with the Stackelberg framework. The farmer and the government obtain higher profits under Nash competition, whereas the biorefinery achieves a higher profit under Stackelberg competition. These findings demonstrate that the strategic structure and sequence of decision-making significantly influence pricing, profitability, and environmental outcomes in carbon-regulated biofuel supply chains. Therefore, supply chain coordination and the design of carbon taxation should be considered jointly when developing policies for sustainable biofuel systems. The effect of adopting the technology level and production process is addressed.The attention has been paid to its social impact such as creating employment.We discuss government policy including carbon emission tax using strategic games.The input rate of biomass to biorefinery is effective in adopting technology level.The highest biomass price is obtained when the farmer decides to develop the land. The effect of adopting the technology level and production process is addressed. The attention has been paid to its social impact such as creating employment. We discuss government policy including carbon emission tax using strategic games. The input rate of biomass to biorefinery is effective in adopting technology level. The highest biomass price is obtained when the farmer decides to develop the land.

title: Exergy Analysis and Performance Improvement of the Wasit Thermal Power Plant Using Particle Swarm Optimization with Reduced Exergy Destruction
summary: Increasing electricity demand and the reduced efficiency of steam power plants operating below their design load highlight the need to improve the performance of existing generating units rather than relying solely on constructing new power
content: Increasing electricity demand and the reduced efficiency of steam power plants operating below their design load highlight the need to improve the performance of existing generating units rather than relying solely on constructing new power plants. This study aims to enhance the exergy performance of the Wasit Thermal Power Plant by adjusting controllable operating variables without modifying the existing plant design or equipment. A component-level exergy analysis was first performed using actual steady-state operating data to identify the major sources of irreversibility. The boiler, turbine group, and condenser accounted for approximately 98% of the total exergy destruction. Based on the exergy diagnosis and sensitivity analysis, four controllable operating variables within safe operating ranges were selected because of their direct influence on the major sources of exergy destruction: main steam pressure (13.5–15.5 MPa), main steam temperature (525°C–540°C), reheat steam temperature (525°C–540°C), and condenser pressure (0.007–0.013 MPa). These variables were simultaneously optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to maximize the overall exergy efficiency while maintaining a constant fuel flow rate. Thermodynamic and operational constraints related to low-pressure turbine (LPT) outlet steam quality, heater terminal temperature difference (TTD), and drain cooler approach (DCA), condenser feasibility, and mass balance were imposed to ensure physically realistic and safe operating conditions. The optimal values of the main steam pressure, the main reheat steam temperatures, and the condenser pressure are 13.5 MPa, 540°C, 540°C, and 0.008219 MPa, which achieved the highest overall exergy efficiency and the lowest total exergy destruction. As a result, the overall exergy efficiency increased from 34.7% to 36.3%, total exergy destruction decreased by approximately 11.81 MW, and turbine shaft work increased from 249 to 261 MW. The results demonstrate that diagnosis-driven constrained optimization of controllable operating variables can effectively improve the exergy performance of existing steam power plants without design modifications.

title: Toward Supply Chain Viability in SME Industrial Clusters: A Multi-Dimensional Decision-Making Framework
summary: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in
content: This study develops a multi-dimensional decision-making framework to enhance supply chain viability in small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) industrial clusters operating under recurring disruptions and increasing uncertainty. Grounded in the viable supply chain literature and Industry 5.0 principles, viability is conceptualized as an integrated capacity emerging from the interaction of adaptation, leagility, resilience, sustainability, digitalization, human-centricity, energy-system robustness, and risk mitigation. These high-level capabilities are operationalized through 22 implementation components covering product/design, functional/process, organizational, technological/informational, financial, and energy dimensions. A sequential hybrid methodology is employed to identify, synthesize, structure, evaluate, and operationalize these components. First, a systematic literature review, thematic analysis, and qualitative synthesis are conducted to identify and validate the components contributing to supply chain viability. Second, interpretive structural modeling (ISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to classification (MICMAC) analysis are used to examine hierarchical relationships and influence patterns among the validated components. Third, fuzzy step-wise weight assessment ratio analysis (SWARA) and combined compromise for ideal solution (CoCoFiSo) are applied to assess component importance while incorporating stakeholder preferences, uncertainty, and expert judgment reliability. Finally, the results are integrated into a mixed-integer linear programming model solved using the CBC solver to identify feasible capability portfolios under practical structural and resource constraints.

title: Robust Coordination of Flexible Loads and Energy Storage for Renewable Self-Consumption in Rural Integrated Energy Systems
summary: This paper investigates the problem of enhancing renewable self-consumption in rural integrated energy systems under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation and demand-side participation. High penetration of distributed photovoltai
content: This paper investigates the problem of enhancing renewable self-consumption in rural integrated energy systems under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation and demand-side participation. High penetration of distributed photovoltaic and wind resources in rural communities often leads to pronounced temporal mismatches between supply and demand, exacerbated by limited export capacity and imperfect reliability of flexible loads. To address this challenge, a unified robust optimization framework is developed to jointly coordinate heterogeneous flexible demand and distributed battery storage within a single operational decision model. The formulation explicitly captures intertemporal storage dynamics, diverse load flexibility characteristics, and bilateral uncertainty arising from renewable forecast deviations of up to ±20% for solar and ±35% for wind, as well as demand response participation losses of up to 30%. Budgeted uncertainty sets are employed to represent worst-case yet plausible realizations, and the resulting min–max problem is reformulated into an equivalent single-level optimization model through dualization to ensure computational tractability. A representative rural case study with 120 aggregated users, 1.05 MW of photovoltaic capacity, 350 kW of wind generation, and 1.8 MWh of battery storage demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Compared with deterministic scheduling, the robust strategy increases the average daily renewable self-consumption rate from 73% to 85% and guarantees a minimum self-consumption level of 68% under all admissible uncertainty realizations. Worst-case unserved energy is reduced by approximately 90%, from 1550 kWh to below 200 kWh, at the cost of a moderate increase in daily operational expenditure. These results provide quantitative evidence that coordinated load–storage optimization under uncertainty can transform renewable self-consumption from a highly volatile outcome into a reliable operational service for rural energy systems.

title: Regulatory Provisions for Introducing Phytopharmaceutical Drugs in Indian Market
summary: Plants have been recognized as a very useful and important source of drugs, since time immemorial. However, in the present day, context, usefulness of plants has been questioned, on the grounds of quality control, lack of clinical trials, e
content: Plants have been recognized as a very useful and important source of drugs, since time immemorial. However, in the present day, context, usefulness of plants has been questioned, on the grounds of quality control, lack of clinical trials, etc. Historically, plant drugs listed in "Official books" under "Schedule I" of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, were accepted for marketing in India, without any need for clinical trials. However, such drugs, although marketed in India, could not be marketed as "drugs" in countries like USA, EU, Japan, China, etc., wherein these drugs failed to meet the same standards of quality, consistency and clinical evidence, as chemical drugs. Thus, several Indian "drugs" were introduced in US market as "dietary supplements". This article discusses the concept of "phytopharmaceuticals", as introduced by amendment in the Indian Act, in 2015. The legal provisions related to Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani drugs, in India, are traced out. Recent developments in Indian act, pertaining to phytopharmaceuticals, have been traced out, and compared with those in other countries, such as USA, EU, Japan, China, etc. The recent amendments in Indian act have paved the way towards introduction of "phytopharmaceuticals", meeting the same standards of quality, safety and efficacy, as for chemical drugs, and have brought the quality, safety and efficacy standards for plant-based drugs, at par with those for chemical drugs. It is hoped that this will help in introducing plant -based drugs in several regulated markets.

title: The missing piece in cellulose foam: Process engineering, not more chemistry
summary: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) and polyethylene (PE) foams remain the dominant cushioning materials in protective packaging because of their low density, resilience, and impact-attenuation performance, but their environmental persistence and po
content: Expanded polystyrene (EPS) and polyethylene (PE) foams remain the dominant cushioning materials in protective packaging because of their low density, resilience, and impact-attenuation performance, but their environmental persistence and poor post-consumer recovery are driving increasingly strict packaging regulations. Cellulose-based alternatives — molded pulp, foam-formed and nanofibrillated cellulose (CNF) foams, and mycelium-bound composites — have each achieved partial success, yet none has simultaneously matched EPS/PE-level cushioning performance, cost, and manufacturing scale. This editorial argues that closing this gap depends less on specialty furnish chemistry — surfactants, cross-linkers, or biological cultivation steps — than on process-engineering advances that convert ordinary pulp furnish, using confined-mold vapor expansion and conventional natural binders, into a porous, EPS-like cellular structure, and calls for coordinated industrial investment in that direction.

title: Research on Cavitation and Mechanism of Multistage Pumps Based on Auxiliary Blades
summary: To reveal the cavitation suppression mechanism of front shroud auxiliary blades in five-stage centrifugal pumps under low-flow conditions, comparative numerical simulation and experimental test were carried out. The full-flow CFD model comb
content: To reveal the cavitation suppression mechanism of front shroud auxiliary blades in five-stage centrifugal pumps under low-flow conditions, comparative numerical simulation and experimental test were carried out. The full-flow CFD model combined with standard k-ε turbulence and homogeneous equilibrium cavitation models was established, and external characteristic experiments verified simulation precision. Cavitation performance, pressure distribution, vapor volume fraction and wear-ring leakage were analyzed at 0.3Q low flow rate under varying inlet total pressures. Results show that auxiliary blades reduce critical cavitation margin by 0.69 m at design flow rate, raise cavitation head by 2.89 m and shrink cavitation coverage significantly. Auxiliary blades suppress wear-ring leakage, elevate internal impeller pressure and cut turbulent kinetic energy dissipation. The cavitation expansion rate of auxiliary blades structure is much lower as inlet pressure declines. This study clarifies the cavitation regulation mechanism of auxiliary blades, providing theoretical reference for anti-cavitation structural optimization of multistage centrifugal pumps.

title: Initial SOC Error Recovery with a CC-RLS-PI Hybrid Estimator
summary: Coulomb counting (CC) is open-loop and cannot correct a wrong initial State of Charge (SOC). A scheme that adds recursive least squares (RLS) parameter identification and a proportional-integral (PI) correction to CC was proposed for a 260
content: Coulomb counting (CC) is open-loop and cannot correct a wrong initial State of Charge (SOC). A scheme that adds recursive least squares (RLS) parameter identification and a proportional-integral (PI) correction to CC was proposed for a 260 mAh cell. This study examines that scheme with Thevenin parameters identified offline and held fixed, using Panasonic 18650PF data under static 1C, HWFET and UDDS profiles, initial errors of −2, −20 and −35 percentage points of SOC, and a comparison with CC and with open-circuit-voltage (OCV) initialization. The hybrid estimator first entered the ±2% error band within 1–389 s but never stayed in it. Its mean absolute error (MAE) was 1.5–4.0%, rising to 5.0–7.7% below 40% SOC on the static and HWFET profiles, and it beat CC only when the initial error was at least 2–4 points. In starts at mid-SOC under load without rest, it had a lower MAE than OCV initialization in 7 of 9 cases. The identified polarization resistance changed more than threefold with the forgetting factor. The scheme suits recovery from large initial errors when OCV initialization is unreliable, within an accuracy limit of about 2–4%.

title: Fish-tail-swing-inspired Geometric Optimization of Micro-turbine Blades Using Response Surface Methodology and Computational Fluid Dynamics
summary: To improve the aerodynamic performance of micro air-driven turbine generator rotors, this study proposes a bio-inspired blade design method based on the tail-swing characteristics of carp. Unlike conventional bio-inspired approaches that pr
content: To improve the aerodynamic performance of micro air-driven turbine generator rotors, this study proposes a bio-inspired blade design method based on the tail-swing characteristics of carp. Unlike conventional bio-inspired approaches that primarily reproduce static biological contours, the proposed method translates different tail-swing postures into adjustable blade geometries. The swing angle, front arc angle, rear arc angle, and trailing-edge radius were selected as the design variables. A Box-Behnken design was used to generate 29 blade configurations, and transient CFD simulations were performed to determine the corresponding power coefficients. A response surface model was then established to quantify the individual and interaction effects of the geometric parameters on rotor aerodynamic performance and to identify the optimal blade configuration. The original rotor reached a peak power coefficient of 0.124 at TSR = 0.5. Among the 29 Box-Behnken design cases, the Case 15 rotor achieved a peak power coefficient of 0.315 at TSR = 0.8, representing a 154.0% improvement over the original rotor. The optimized rotor identified by the response surface model reached a peak power coefficient of 0.342 at TSR = 0.8, corresponding to a 175.8% improvement. Sensitivity analysis showed that the influence of the geometric parameters on the power coefficient followed the order: swing angle > rear arc angle > trailing-edge radius > front arc angle, with a significant interaction between the swing angle and rear arc angle. Flow-field analysis revealed that the bio-inspired blade configurations enlarged the high-pressure region over the middle and rear portions of the pressure surface while strengthening the corresponding low-pressure region on the suction surface, thereby increasing the pressure difference across the blade. The optimized blades also produced more continuous high-velocity flow within the inter-blade passages while reducing the extent of the low-velocity region near the trailing edge, promoting more continuous airflow acceleration and enhanced momentum transport. These findings provide a bio-inspired design strategy for improving the aerodynamic performance of micro air-driven turbine rotors and offer guidance for the aerodynamic optimization of small-scale rotating machinery.

title: Technology Research Review: Advancing Interdisciplinary Scholarship in Technological Innovation, Digital Transformation, and Emerging Intelligent Systems
summary: The rapid evolution of modern technologies has transformed industrial systems, governance structures, and societal interactions, creating an urgent need for rigorous and interdisciplinary scholarly inquiry. The Technology Research Review (T
content: The rapid evolution of modern technologies has transformed industrial systems, governance structures, and societal interactions, creating an urgent need for rigorous and interdisciplinary scholarly inquiry. The Technology Research Review (TRR), published by SPIDER Publishing, is an international peer-reviewed journal dedicated to advancing high-quality research in technological innovation, applied systems, and digital transformation. This editorial outlines the journal’s vision to serve as a global platform for theoretical, empirical, experimental, and applied research across diverse domains, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, big data analytics, cybersecurity, blockchain technologies, Internet of Things, robotics, smart manufacturing, and sustainable technologies. TRR emphasizes methodological rigor, originality, and real-world applicability while promoting cross-disciplinary integration among engineering, computer science, data science, and innovation studies. The journal also highlights emerging frontiers such as quantum computing, digital twins, advanced materials, and AI governance, while critically engaging with ethical, regulatory, and societal implications of technological advancement. By fostering research that bridges scientific discovery and practical implementation, TRR aims to contribute to sustainable, inclusive, and responsible technological progress globally. The editorial underscores the journal’s commitment to shaping a knowledge ecosystem that informs academia, industry innovation, and policy development in the era of digital transformation.

title: Retrofiting A Panacea to African Public Transport Terminals Toward the Global Pandemics Mitigation
summary: Public transport in Nigeria and some other African countries is synonymous to road transport system as the government policy seems to give more attention to it than other modes. The few available bus operations in the country are second-han
content: Public transport in Nigeria and some other African countries is synonymous to road transport system as the government policy seems to give more attention to it than other modes. The few available bus operations in the country are second-hand rickety vehicles that are fossil-fuel dependent with all its negative health implications that tend to catalyze SARS-CoV-2 otherwise known as COVID-19 infection that has ravaged the whole world at a pandemic scale. The spatial spread of the virus is mass transport related. This study therefore using direct observatory and internet-based review of literature method to examine the physical state of urban public transport infrastructure adaptation to the new challenges of COVID-19 and its variance. The study revealed that the use of vehicular and terminal retrofitting through IT based social-distancing before and after boarding, and the use of environmental friendly vehicles in line with the global crusade for smart city and green mobility is the panacea to the global epidemiology. African countries like Nigeria should therefore awake from their slumber and join the race toward green mobility and smart city to curtail the spread of epidemic viruses.

title: GEOECONOMIC REVALUATION OF ŠIBENIK’S ROLE IN STRENGTHENING CROATIA’S POSITION IN CANTON 10 OF THE FEDERATION OF BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA - THE STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE OF THE CROATIAN REGIONAL CITY OF ŠIBENIK
summary: his paper analyzes the necessity of transforming the perception of the city of Shibenik from a predominantly tourist center into a key logistical and distribution hub for the hinterland of Western Bosnia (Canton 10). In the context of 2026,
content: his paper analyzes the necessity of transforming the perception of the city of Shibenik from a predominantly tourist center into a key logistical and distribution hub for the hinterland of Western Bosnia (Canton 10). In the context of 2026, marked by the intensification of Bosnia and Herzegovina's EU accession negotiations and the redefinition of global supply chains, Shibenik is positioned as the primary maritime exit for the resource-rich areas of Livno, Tomislavgrad, and Kupres. The central thesis, supported by the author's previous research on geoeconomic pressures from the Italy–Hungary–Serbia triangle, indicates that strengthening the Šibenik–Canton 10 axis is not merely an economic interest but a national security imperative. Utilizing PEST and SWOT analyses, the paper demonstrates how strategic control of the transport route via Knin and Strmica serves as a bulwark against attempts at the regional marginalization of Croatian ports and logistical corridors. Finally, the paper proposes the implementation of a "soft power" model through the development of cross-border economic zones, whereby Shibenik becomes an instrument for the deep integration of the Croatian economic space, ensuring the demographic survival of Croats in BiH and strengthening the overall geoeconomic resilience of the Republic of Croatia.

title: E-Learning in Vietnam: Fact and Solution
source: Journal of Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
summary: E-learning has changed strongly the process of self-learning due to the ability to personalize as well as satisfy demand of learners. E-learning has applied at many universities today, in the 4th industrial revolution era. Many application
content: E-learning has changed strongly the process of self-learning due to the ability to personalize as well as satisfy demand of learners. E-learning has applied at many universities today, in the 4th industrial revolution era. Many application software has been used to replace human beings in imparting knowledge, testing and evaluating the quality of training. In this paper, the authors present some analysis and evaluation of the current online teaching and learning methods and recommend solutions to enhance the interaction and active in the teaching and learning process to improve the quality of online education in Vietnam for the next period.

title: Uloga zelene tranzicije u jačanju konkurentnosti Republike Hrvatske
summary: Republika Hrvatska obvezala se postići cilj Europske unije o postizanju klimatske neutralnosti do 2050. godine. Takav cilj neupitno će utjecati na smjer i intenzitet razvoja hrvatskog gospodarstva. Ispunjenje navedenog podrazumijeva i smanj
content: Republika Hrvatska obvezala se postići cilj Europske unije o postizanju klimatske neutralnosti do 2050. godine. Takav cilj neupitno će utjecati na smjer i intenzitet razvoja hrvatskog gospodarstva. Ispunjenje navedenog podrazumijeva i smanjenje emisije stakleničkih plinova za 55% u odnosu na 1990. godinu. Europska razvojna politika nastavno na navedeno podupire oslanjanje na zelenu tranziciju kroz osiguravanje dovoljne količine proizvodnje obnovljive energije uz povećanje efikasnosti u energetskom, nekretninskom i industrijskom sektoru. Takva politika podupire industrijsku kompetitivnost u čistu energiju i osigurava energetsku autonomiju. Identificiranje nacionalne strategije za obnovljive izvore energije i energetska efikasnost područja su koja posebno trebaju biti u fokusu. Europski ciljevi za 2050. godinu su poznati, međutim intenzitet i način ispunjenja tog cilja još uvijek nije jasno definiran. Jedan od ključnih nedostataka je manjak financijskih sredstava potrebnih za ispunjenje definiranih ciljeva. Glavni cilj ovog rada je analizirati poziciju Republike Hrvatske u mogućnosti ispunjenja zadanog cilja kao i regulatorni te financijski okvir zelene tranzicije.

title: EXPERIENCE ECONOMY AS A CATALYST FOR SUSTAINABLE GEOSITE TOURISM: SERVICE DESIGN MECHANISMS IN THE DUNHUANG DESTINATION SYSTEM, CHINA
summary: This study examines how experience economy perceptions are associated with sustainable geosite tourism intention in Dunhuang, China, through service design mechanisms and place engagement. A cross-sectional visitor survey yielded 452 valid
content: This study examines how experience economy perceptions are associated with sustainable geosite tourism intention in Dunhuang, China, through service design mechanisms and place engagement. A cross-sectional visitor survey yielded 452 valid responses for PLS-SEM analysis, and semi-structured interviews with visitors and frontline staff were completed as contextual support for understanding destination touchpoints. The measurement model demonstrates satisfactory reliability and convergent validity, while discriminant validity is supported, with the EE-SDM HTMT value (0.8925) remaining below 0.90. The structural results show positive relationships for EE→SDM (β=0.824), SDM→SGTI (β=0.385), and EE→SGTI (β=0.457). The indirect association EE→SDM→SGTI is significant (β=0.319, 95% CI [0.241, 0.398]), and place engagement positively moderates the SDM→SGTI relationship (β=0.184, p<.01). The model therefore indicates that memorable destination experiences are linked to sustainable tourism intentions partly through visitors' perceptions of coherent, interpretable, and participation-oriented service design, with the strength of this relationship varying by place engagement. The study contributes a destination-system perspective that connects experience staging, service design, and sustainability-oriented intention across heritage, landscape, transport, and digital touchpoints. Managerially, the findings support touchpoint mapping, interpretive micro-experiences, coordinated digital-physical services, and context-sensitive stewardship cues across the Dunhuang destination network.

title: STRENGTHENING LOCAL ECONOMIES THROUGH ECOTOURISM: EVIDENCE FROM BINTANG DISTRICT CENTRAL ACEH PROVINCE, INDONESIA
summary: This study investigates the role of ecotourism in strengthening local economies in Bintang District, Central Aceh by identifying key potentials within natural and socio-cultural resources. It explores how assets such as Lake Laut Tawar, agr
content: This study investigates the role of ecotourism in strengthening local economies in Bintang District, Central Aceh by identifying key potentials within natural and socio-cultural resources. It explores how assets such as Lake Laut Tawar, agrobased livelihoods, and community enterprises can drive sustainable economic development. The study analyzes stakeholder collaboration, focusing on governance, participation, and community empowerment. It evaluates contributions to income diversification, employment, and micro-enterprise growth while identifying structural and institutional constraints. The research ultimately proposes integrated and sustainable strategies to support resilient, ecotourism-based local economic development.This study employs a mixed methods approach to examine the contribution of ecotourism to local economic strengthening in Bintang District, Central Aceh. Qualitative data were collected through in-depth interviews with key stakeholders to explore governance, collaboration, and community participation. Field observations documented tourism activities, environmental practices, and local economic interactions, with findings analyzed thematically. Quantitative analysis used indicators such as employment, income diversification, enterprise growth, participation rates, and environmental sustainability, supported by secondary data.The integration of these methods ensures triangulation, enhancing validity and providing a comprehensive understanding of ecotourism-driven economic transformation. The findings reveal strong ecotourism potential in Bintang District, particularly around Lake Laut Tawar, supported by rich natural landscapes, biodiversity, agro-tourism, and Gayo cultural heritage. This potential has contributed to emerging income diversification through homestays, culinary enterprises, handicrafts, and local transport services. However, development is constrained by inadequate infrastructure, including accessibility, sanitation, waste management, and digital connectivity. Weak institutional coordination and low community participation further hinder integrated planning and inclusive development. These results highlight the need for improved infrastructure, stronger collaboration, and participatory governance to ensure sustainable local economic transformation.This study concludes that ecotourism in Bintang District, particularly in the Lake Laut Tawar area, holds strong potential to drive local economic strengthening. However, this potential remains underutilized due to inadequate infrastructure and fragmented institutional coordination. Limited community participation further constrains inclusive development and local ownership. The findings highlight the need for integrated strategies combining infrastructure investment, institutional strengthening, and participatory governance. Sustainable ecotourism development requires a balanced approach to economic growth, environmental conservation, and socio-cultural sustainability.

title: EX-POST EVALUATION METHODOLOGIES FOR PUBLIC TOURISM INVESTMENTS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW WITH APPLICATIONS TO HUAMACHUCO, PERU
summary: Public tourism investment plays a strategic role in promoting territorial development, economic diversification, and cultural heritage conservation. However, traditional ex-post evaluation approaches often prioritize economic efficiency whi
content: Public tourism investment plays a strategic role in promoting territorial development, economic diversification, and cultural heritage conservation. However, traditional ex-post evaluation approaches often prioritize economic efficiency while overlooking social, environmental, and governance dimensions. This study systematically analyzes the methodologies, approaches, and limitations of ex-post evaluations of public tourism investments to identify methodological guidelines for sustainable local development in Huamachuco, Peru. A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines. The review covered studies published between 2016 and 2026 and indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed. Of the 135 initially identified records, 37 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the final analysis. The selected publications were examined through thematic coding and bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer to identify methodological trends, conceptual relationships, and research gaps. Approximately 70.6% of the reviewed studies emphasized governance, community participation, and territorial sustainability, whereas 29.4% focused primarily on economic evaluation. Traditional models, including Input-Output analysis and Tourism Satellite Accounts, provide quantitative estimates of economic impacts but frequently overlook environmental carrying capacity, cultural preservation, and equitable benefit distribution. Conversely, governance-oriented approaches emphasize participatory decision-making, institutional coordination, and adaptive management. Bibliometric analysis identifies sustainability as a central theme connecting economic, social, environmental, and governance dimensions. These findings highlight the need for hybrid, multidimensional evaluation frameworks that integrate economic performance with community participation, territorial governance, and sustainability indicators. Such frameworks could strengthen the assessment of public tourism investments and support equitable, resilient, and culturally appropriate local development in emerging Andean destinations such as Huamachuco.

title: Bimodal Pareto Structure in Metaheuristic Tuning of Fractional-order PI Control for A DC Microgrid: An Inverted Oustaloup Realisation and A Threshold-defined Settling-time Objective
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: Direct-current microgrids concentrate photovoltaic, wind and battery conversion behind one lightly buffered bus, and fractional-order PI control is widely used to regulate it.Since s -λ is irrational, every such controller is a rational app
