content: Direct-current microgrids concentrate photovoltaic, wind and battery conversion behind one lightly buffered bus, and fractional-order PI control is widely used to regulate it.Since s -λ is irrational, every such controller is a rational approximation of one.We tune a dual-loop fractional-order PI regulator for a 48 V bus with four multi-objective metaheuristics against steady-state accuracy and settling time, and examine the bimodal Pareto front that results.In the published implementation, the Oustaloup block assigns zeros and poles to a differentiator's grids while carrying an integrator's gain constant, so integral action is absent; the bus parks at the edge of the settling band and the slow cluster is produced by millivolt threshold grazes: 91 % of its points leave the band by less than 5 mV, and a 24 mV change of the band moves 85 % of the front.Correcting the realisation reduces the dip statistic by a factor of 3.1 (hierarchical-bootstrap 95 % CI 2.4-4.0,120 independent runs); the residual two-cluster structure is physical rather than threshold-induced and disappears under tuning on randomised scenarios.Only 3.9 % of the original search box is linearly stable; restricting the search to it removes saturation-driven limit cycles without loss of held-out accuracy.On 150 held-out scenarios, the corrected controller with adequate integral-gain bounds achieves a median IAE of 0.0087 V s, against 0.0146 V s for reconstructed fractional-order sliding-mode and active-disturbance-rejection controllers.All raw results and code are released.

title: Bicycle-inspired Control for Grid-forming Inverters: A Structurally Derived Outer-loop Strategy with Coupled Second-order Dynamics for Active-power Regulation
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: The increasing penetration of inverter-based resources is reshaping the dynamic characteristics of modern power systems, motivating continued investigation of grid-forming control structures with explicit and interpretable dynamics.This pap
content: The increasing penetration of inverter-based resources is reshaping the dynamic characteristics of modern power systems, motivating continued investigation of grid-forming control structures with explicit and interpretable dynamics.This paper introduces Bicycle-Inspired Control (BIC), an outer-loop strategy formulated through coupled second-order equations inspired by the linearized lean-steer dynamics of the benchmark bicycle model.BIC retains explicit coupling between angle and actuator coordinates, providing a structurally coupled representation of activepower/frequency dynamics beyond the conventional single-coordinate swing-equation formulation.The proposed structure is incorporated into a differential-algebraic model of the grid-forming inverter and analyzed using smallsignal methods.A closed-form Routh-Hurwitz stability condition is derived for the full-order BIC dynamics, including the inertial cross-coupling and the washout damping injection.Small-signal eigenvalue and modal analyses are conducted over varying grid-strength conditions, followed by nonlinear time-domain simulations at representative operating points.The results characterize the analytical properties and grid-strength-dependent dynamics of BIC and their correspondence with the observed active-power and frequency transients.

title: Abiotic factors that influence wine terroir
source: Journal of Natural and Agricultural Sciences
summary: The concept of terroir associates wines with their place of origin, since the flavor and aroma of the wine are closely related to the environmental conditions where the vine is produced. Factors such as climate, water and soil have a signif
content: The concept of terroir associates wines with their place of origin, since the flavor and aroma of the wine are closely related to the environmental conditions where the vine is produced. Factors such as climate, water and soil have a significant influence on the organoleptic characteristics of wine, by affecting the development of volatile and non-volatile chemical compounds present in grapes. Climate impacts mainly through variables such as temperature, precipitation and solar radiation, while soil influences through the availability of water and nutrients. Although the process by which these factors determine the quality of wine can be considered intangible and complex, many of the elements involved are measurable and can be monitored in vineyards and wineries. The present work compiles and analyzes different perspectives on the influence of soil, water and climate on wine quality, with the aim of supporting the hypothesis that these factors exert a significant influence on the wines produced in each wine region.

title: Otomobil Kullanıcılarının İnovatif Araçlara Yönelik İlgi ve Beklentileri: Elektrikli Arabalar
summary: Amaç –Teknolojinin hız kazandığı dünyamızda yenilikçi ve çevreci araçların kullanımı artmaya devam etmektedir. Bu araçlar arasında temiz yakıt ve çevreci anlayışa sahip elektrikli otomobillere olan ilgi olumlu yönde olmakla birlikte bazı ye
content: Amaç –Teknolojinin hız kazandığı dünyamızda yenilikçi ve çevreci araçların kullanımı artmaya devam etmektedir. Bu araçlar arasında temiz yakıt ve çevreci anlayışa sahip elektrikli otomobillere olan ilgi olumlu yönde olmakla birlikte bazı yetersizlikleri ve endişeleri de içinde barındırmaktadır. Bu çalışma, sosyo-ekonomik ve kültürel açıdan farklılık gösteren sürücü adaylarının elektrikli araçlara yönelik ilgi, beklenti ve kaygılarını, düşünce ve eylemlerine yansımaları belirlemeyi amaçlamaktadır.Yöntem–Çalışmada, survey (tarama) yöntemin kullanımı benimsenmiş olup, çalışmanın evrenini katı yakıt kullanan, elektrikli ve hibrit özelliğe sahip araç kullanan sürücüler oluşturmaktadır. Örneklem evrenden otomobil kullanan sürücüler arasından kümele örnekleme yoluyla belirlenmiş olan 242 otomobil sürücüsü örneklemi oluşturmaktadır. Araştırma verileri araştırmacının kendisinin geliştirdiği 5’li likert tipinde hazırlanmış 27 maddelik ankete sürücülerin verdikleri yanıtlar oluşturmaktadır. Ölçme aracından elde edilen veriler, bilgisayar ortamına aktarılarak parametrik testlerden korelasyon, t-testi ve ANOVA testi teknikleri ile analiz edilmiştir.Bulgular–Araştırma sonucunda, elektrikli otomobillerin teknik özelliklerinin yanı sıra yönetimlerin uyguladığı çevreci politikalar, yeşil enerji ve finansman politikaları, altyapı yatırımları ve elektrikli otomobillerin gelecekteki konumuna ilişkin izlediği politikalar ve belirsizlikler tüketicilerin beklenti ve endişelerini artırmaktadır. Araştırmada, tüketicilerin elektrikli otomobil satın alma niyetleri üzerine etkileri istatistiksel olarak analiz edilmiştir.Tartışma–Analiz sonucu tüketicilerin elektrikli otomobillerden beklentilerinin oldukça yüksek düzeyli olduğu, ancak bu durum diğer ülkelerin politik uygulamalarının yanı sıra yönetimin tüketici güvenini artıracak politikalara yer vermesi daha da olumlu etki yaratacaktır. Doğal olarak bu sürece bağlı olarak tüketicilerin elektrikli otomobil satın alma niyet ve davranışlarında değişmelere yol açtığı gözlenmektedir. Elde edilen bulgular, literatür verileri çerçevesinde tartışılarak, elektrikli otomobillere yönelik beklentilerin karşılanması ve satın alma davranışının olumlu yönde değişmesi için bazı önerilere yer verilmiştir

title: Termal Turizm İşletmelerinde Bireylerin Algılanan Esenlik ve Yaşam Doyumu Düzeyleri Arasındaki İlişki: Ankara Örneği
summary: Amaç –Bu çalışmanın temel amacı, termal turizm aktivitelerine katılan bireylerin algıladıkları esenlik ve yaşam doyumu düzeylerinin incelenmesidir. Bununla birlikte katılımcıların algılanan esenlik ve yaşam doyumu düzeyleri arasındaki ilişk
content: Amaç –Bu çalışmanın temel amacı, termal turizm aktivitelerine katılan bireylerin algıladıkları esenlik ve yaşam doyumu düzeylerinin incelenmesidir. Bununla birlikte katılımcıların algılanan esenlik ve yaşam doyumu düzeyleri arasındaki ilişkinin tespit edilerek, demografik özelliklerine göre oluşan farklılıkların tespit edilmesi amaçlanmıştır.Yöntem –Nicel bir araştırma olan çalışmada, veri toplama aracı olarak anket formu kullanılmıştır. Katılımcıların algılanan esenlik ve yaşam doyum düzeylerinin belirlenmesi amacıyla “Algılanan Esenlik Ölçeği” (Perceived Wellness Scale) ve Yaşam Doyumu Ölçeği (The Satisfaction With Life Scale) kullanılmıştır. Araştırmanın evrenini Ankara’da ikamet eden ve Ankara’nın termal turizm destinasyonları Kızılcahamam, Beypazarı ve Haymana’yı ziyaret eden bireyler oluşturmaktadır. Toplamda 384 kullanılabilir veriye ulaşılmış ve analize tabi tutulmuştur. Verilerin analizi için SPSS istatistik paket programı kullanılmıştır. Analiz kapsamında ise t-testi, ANOVA testi, korelasyon analizi ile basit ve çoklu doğrusal regresyon analizleri kullanılmıştır.Bulgular–Araştırma sonuçlarına göre; algılanan esenlik ve yaşam doyumu arasında pozitif yönlü bir ilişki tespit edilmiştir. Termal turizm aktivitelerine katılan bireylerin esenlik düzeyleri yaş, medeni durum ve eğitim durumu değişkenlerine göre farklılaşmazken; cinsiyet ve katılım durumu değişkenine göre farklılık göstermektedir. Katılımcıların yaşam doyumu düzeyleri ise; cinsiyet, yaş, medeni durum, eğitim ve katılım durumu değişkenlerine göre farklılık göstermektedir.Tartışma –Araştırma sonuçları termal turizm etkinliklerine katılımın, algılanan esenlik ve yaşam doyumu düzeyleri üzerinde etkili olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır. Bu doğrultuda, termal turizmde sunulan tedavi hizmetlerinin devlet tarafından sağlık sigortası kapsamında karşılanması için şartların genişletilmesi ve yaygınlaştırılması ile termal turizm hizmetlerine erişilebilirliğin artırılması sektöre katkı sağlayacaktır.

title: Green Management Research in Hotels: Examination of Contribution Strategies
summary: Purpose –The study aims to examine the theoretical contribution strategies of articles related to green management in hotels, as one of the early studies. A management approach that has gained increasing interest in the academic literature,
content: Purpose –The study aims to examine the theoretical contribution strategies of articles related to green management in hotels, as one of the early studies. A management approach that has gained increasing interest in the academic literature, within the scope of the study.Design/methodology/approach –The articles were identified from Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect databases using the PRISMA protocol. Based on the contribution claims in the abstract and introduction sections, a systematic review of 33 articles was conducted, and the contribution language used by the authors was evaluated. The contribution claims in the articles were coded into five main categories: revelatory contributions, incremental contributions, replicatory contributions, consolidatory contributions, and differentiated context contributions. Most of the reviewed articles claimed incremental contributions.Results–Neglect spotting, which is part of the incremental contribution strategy, has been the most preferred sub-category. The differentiated contribution strategy is the second most commonly used of the contribution strategies in the articles. No articles were found in the study that claimed to use the replicatory contributions strategy.Discussion –The findings emphasize the importance of clearly and comprehensively expressing theoretical contributions. Additionally, the recommendations include which types of contributions could be emphasized in future studies in the field of green management in hotels. The study is expected to attract the attention of researchers, as the framing of contribution claims is a relatively understudied research topic.

title: BRICS-T Ekonomilerinde Büyümenin Dinamikleri: Ekonomik Karmaşıklık ve Dışa Açıklığın Yapısal Dönüşümdeki Rolü
summary: Amaç –Bu çalışmada, BRICS-T ülkelerinde (Brezilya, Rusya, Hindistan, Çin, Güney Afrika ve Türkiye) 1995-2023 dönemine ait veriler kullanılarak ekonomik büyümenin belirleyicileri analiz edilmektedir. Özellikle, ekonomik karmaşıklık ve ticari
content: Amaç –Bu çalışmada, BRICS-T ülkelerinde (Brezilya, Rusya, Hindistan, Çin, Güney Afrika ve Türkiye) 1995-2023 dönemine ait veriler kullanılarak ekonomik büyümenin belirleyicileri analiz edilmektedir. Özellikle, ekonomik karmaşıklık ve ticari dışa açıklık oranı değişkenlerinin ekonomik büyüme üzerindeki etkilerini incelemektedir.Yöntem–Analizde, yatay kesit bağımlılığı ve heterojen panelleri dikkate alan Dinamik Ortak Korelasyonlu Etkiler (DCCE) yöntemi kullanılmıştır. Analizin ilk aşamasında, yatay kesit bağımlılığının varlığını tespit etmek amacıyla CD_LM testi uygulanmıştır. Test sonuçları, yatay kesit bağımlılığının varlığı ispatlanmış, bu durumda da ikinci nesil birim kök analiz yöntemleri kullanılmıştır. Öncelikle, CIPS (Cross-sectionally Augmented IPS) birim kök testi uygulanmış ve serilerin durağanlık seviyeleri incelenmiştir. Birim kök analizinin ardından, panelin heterojen bir yapıda olduğu Swamy testi ile doğrulanmış sonrasında ise, Westerlund eşbütünleşme analizi ve DCCE tahmin yöntemi kullanılmıştır.Bulgular–Araştırmanın bulgularına göre bağımlı ve bağımsız değişkenlerin uzun dönemde eşbütünleşik hareket ettiği bulunmuş olup, her iki değişkenin de ekonomik büyümeyi pozitif ve istatistiki olarak anlamlı etkilediği tespit edilmiştir. Ekonomik karmaşıklık değişkeninin katsayısı 1.33 olup %5 anlamlılık düzeyinde anlamlı bulunmuştur. Bu bulgu, üretim yapısının daha karmaşık ve bilgi yoğun bir hale gelmesinin ekonomik büyümeyi teşvik ettiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Ticari dışa açıklık oranının katsayısı ise 0.19 olarak hesaplanmış ve %1 anlamlılık düzeyinde anlamlı görülmüştür.Tartışma–Sonuç olarak, bu çalışma, BRICS-T ülkelerinde sürdürülebilir ekonomik büyümenin sağlanması için ekonomik çeşitliliğin artırılması ve ticari dışa açıklığın teşvik edilmesi gerektiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Ekonomik karmaşıklığın artırılması, özellikle bilgi ve teknoloji yoğun üretim yapılarının geliştirilmesi, ekonomik büyümeyi destekleyen temel bir unsur olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Benzer şekilde, dışa açıklık oranının artırılması, uluslararası ticaretin ekonomik büyümeye olan katkısını güçlendirecektir

title: De Gruyter Handbook on the Psychology of Energy Transitions
summary: Limiting climate change will require a global shift in the way energy is produced, distributed, and consumed. While much of the discourse thus far has gravitated toward technological innovation, a successful Energy Transition also depends o
content: Limiting climate change will require a global shift in the way energy is produced, distributed, and consumed. While much of the discourse thus far has gravitated toward technological innovation, a successful Energy Transition also depends on how individuals and communities respond to it, from the technologies they adopt to the projects and policies they support or oppose. This handbook examines the challenges of—and opportunities for—engaging the public in this transition. A distinctive feature of this volume is its practical, modular organization. Instead of a traditional focus on core psychological concepts, content is structured around specific net-zero energy strategies. This approach not only makes the handbook more applied in its focus, but also allows for a layered understanding of concepts. The volume looks at four ways the public engages with the energy transition: managing everyday electricity use, adopting energy efficient and renewable energy technologies, supporting or opposing transition initiatives, and responding to proposals of large-scale, emergent energy and carbon management technologies.

title: Visualization of the Agglomeration Processof Copper Particles Used in the Manufacture of Current-Carrying Cellsof Lithium-Ion Batteries
summary: The present study aims to conduct a comparative analysis of dispersion media used for the synthesis and storage of copper nanoparticles derived from copper formate, and to evaluate their suitability for application in current collectors. Pa
content: The present study aims to conduct a comparative analysis of dispersion media used for the synthesis and storage of copper nanoparticles derived from copper formate, and to evaluate their suitability for application in current collectors. Particle characteristics in two media, namely ethyl alcohol and a mixture of alcohol and ethylene glycol, were investigated using dynamic light scattering, rheological analysis, and refractometry. The results demonstrate that the combined solvent system produces nanoparticles with a smaller average diameter (56.7 nm compared to 107.1 nm in pure alcohol) and a narrower size distribution, with 83.4% of particles falling within the 64-128 nm range. To visualise the data, particle size histograms were constructed, and the distributions were approximated using normal and Pearson distribution models. Experimental findings further indicate that the rate of particle agglomeration in the alcohol - ethylene glycol medium is approximately two times lower than in pure alcohol. On the basis of these results, the alcohol - ethylene glycol mixture can be recommended as a stabilising dispersion medium for the long-term storage of copper nanodispersions intended for use in current collector applications.

title: Advances and Future Directions in Floating Buoy Technologyfor Marine Energy and Environmental Applications
summary: Floating buoy technology has rapidly advanced and is integral to marine science, renewable energy harvesting, and environmental monitoring applications. This study synthesizes recent innovations in buoy designs, energy conversion technologi
content: Floating buoy technology has rapidly advanced and is integral to marine science, renewable energy harvesting, and environmental monitoring applications. This study synthesizes recent innovations in buoy designs, energy conversion technologies, and hybrid system integration. Key advancements include modular construction techniques, bio-inspired and hydrodynamic optimizations for improved stability and efficiency, and novel energy-harvesting mechanisms utilizing oscillating buoys, piezoelectric, and triboelectric systems. The integration of floating buoys with hybrid platforms, such as floating breakwaters and offshore wind turbines, demonstrates considerable potential for cost sharing and enhanced performance. Despite substantial progress, critical gaps remain, particularly in long-term operational validation, real-world performance under extreme conditions, scalability, and comprehensive environmental impact assessments. This study identifies these research gaps and outlines future directions to facilitate the widespread adoption of floating buoy technologies. The insights provided are crucial for guiding ongoing innovation, addressing existing limitations, and supporting sustainable blue-economy initiatives.

title: How to Make Research Reach the Newsroom? Designing Open-Data Platforms Through Boundary Theory
summary: Research increasingly produces openly available datasets with high societal relevance, yet such data remain difficult to reuse beyond their original scientific context. At the same time, data journalism has become an established practice th
content: Research increasingly produces openly available datasets with high societal relevance, yet such data remain difficult to reuse beyond their original scientific context. At the same time, data journalism has become an established practice that relies on openly available data to inform public debate, but rarely draws directly on research data. This study examines how open research data platforms can support journalistic reuse. Building on boundary-spanning mechanisms as a sensitizing and interpretive lens, we analyse reuse as a cross-community challenge in which data must retain meaning across scientific and journalistic contexts. Following a design science research approach, we derive design requirements from interviews with data journalists (n=6), a co-creation workshop with data journalists (n=15), and a formative ex-ante expert evaluation (n=13). The study contributes early design knowledge by showing how syntactic and semantic platform support can enable interpretive reuse across knowledge boundaries.

title: DECARBONIZZAZIONE DEI TRASPORTI MEDIANTE L’IMPIEGO DELL’IDROGENO: PROFILI NORMATIVI E APPLICATIVI
source: Nova Science Publishers (Nova Science Publishers, Inc.)
summary: The decarbonisation of the transport sector represents one of the major challenges of the European energy transition, requiring the development of alternative energy carriers and an adequate regulatory framework capable of supporting techno
content: The decarbonisation of the transport sector represents one of the major challenges of the European energy transition, requiring the development of alternative energy carriers and an adequate regulatory framework capable of supporting technological innovation and infrastructure deployment. In this context, renewable hydrogen has emerged as a strategic energy vector, particularly for transport applications in which direct electrification presents technological or operational limitations. This doctoral thesis investigates the legal and regulatory framework governing the development of hydrogen in the transport sector, focusing on the evolution of European legislation, its implementation in Italy, and the administrative and technical challenges associated with the deployment of hydrogen infrastructure. Particular attention is devoted to the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) and the Renewable Energy Directive (RED III), examining their implications for the development of renewable hydrogen and the establishment of an effective national regulatory and governance framework. The analysis highlights the fragmentation of the applicable legislation, the complexity of administrative procedures, and the lack of uniform operational approaches, which may contribute to regulatory uncertainty and hinder investment. The research adopts an interdisciplinary approach combining legal analysis with technical and environmental assessment. The case study of Capo d’Orlando provides a practical framework for investigating the challenges associated with the implementation of a hydrogen refuelling infrastructure. Through the analysis of the applicable regulatory provisions and administrative procedures, the research identifies the main regulatory, authorisation, technological and economic barriers and develops operational guidelines aimed at supporting the authorisation process and promoting a more consistent and replicable approach to the development of Hydrogen Refuelling Stations (HRS). The thesis also examines the environmental sustainability of hydrogen infrastructure through the analysis of the Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) methodology and Environmental Product Declarations (EPD), based on Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). Their potential contribution to assessing the environmental performance of the technological components of hydrogen infrastructure is explored, together with their role in improving the transparency, comparability and reliability of environmental information supporting regulatory and administrative decision-making. The research demonstrates that the development of hydrogen infrastructure requires an integrated approach in which legal regulation, administrative procedures, technological innovation and environmental assessment are coordinated. Its original contribution lies in the development of an operational and methodological framework combining legal and technical perspectives, with the aim of reducing regulatory uncertainty, i

title: E-Rain Smart Storm Water Inlets Gate The GREEN MANAGEMENT for Smart Cities Roads Drain Rain System
source: Emirati Journal of Civil Engineering and Applications
summary: The E-Rain Smart Gate is a pioneering innovation in the newly defined "Civilectronics" category, integrating civil, electronic, and systems engineering to revolutionize urban drainage. Designed specifically for smart cities and arid environ
content: The E-Rain Smart Gate is a pioneering innovation in the newly defined "Civilectronics" category, integrating civil, electronic, and systems engineering to revolutionize urban drainage. Designed specifically for smart cities and arid environments like the Gulf region, this fully automated system addresses the critical challenges of infrastructure maintenance and street flooding caused by sand, dust, and debris accumulation. The system utilizes advanced rain and water sensors to automatically open inlet gates during rainfall and close them during dry periods to prevent blockages. A key technical feature is the inclusion of distance sensors that electronically measure sand accumulation within the inlets. This data allows utility providers to use specialized software to pinpoint exact maintenance needs, eliminating human error and the need for manual inspections. By integrating with GIS and CMMS, the system enables real-time asset management and predictive maintenance. Economically, the E-Rain system is a "Technology Enabler" within the Industry 4.0 framework. It reduces periodic maintenance costs for municipalities by over 65% and ensures 100% operational efficiency of the drainage network. To ensure financial feasibility, the project utilizes a strategic deployment model focusing on "Wet Spots"—urban zones prone to water accumulation—and offers tiered hardware solutions ranging from USB-connected devices to fully autonomous gates. The efficacy of this "Green Management" solution has been validated through a successful prototype in Shakhbout City, Abu Dhabi. Its technical excellence is further recognized by over 70 international innovation medals from 30 different countries, marking it as a sustainable solution for enhancing public safety and infrastructure longevity.

title: Indonesian Diplomacy in International Institutions: Foreign Policy and Social Strategies in the Globalization Era
summary: This study analyzes Indonesia's diplomatic strategy within international institutions as part of the nation's foreign policy in the era of globalization. Using a qualitative research method with a case study approach on Indonesia's membersh
content: This study analyzes Indonesia's diplomatic strategy within international institutions as part of the nation's foreign policy in the era of globalization. Using a qualitative research method with a case study approach on Indonesia's membership in the United Nations (UN), ASEAN, the G20, and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), this study explores how Indonesia positions itself as a key actor in the architecture of international security and cooperation. The research findings show that Indonesia adopts a multilateral diplomatic strategy based on the principle of free and active, emphasizing its role as a bridge-builder between developing and developed countries. Indonesia consistently utilizes its membership in international institutions to strengthen its geopolitical position, promote democracy, human rights, and champion issues of national interest such as climate change, free trade, and regional conflict resolution. This study contributes to an understanding of the dynamics of Indonesian international politics and the relevance of international institutions in shaping the foreign policies of developing countries

title: Overview of Control and Protection Methods for Enhancing Low-Voltage Ride-Through in Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems
source: SVU-International Journal of Engineering Sciences and Applications
summary: TThis paper provides a comprehensive review of many different methods to improve Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) capability and quality of power for Photovoltaic (PV) and wind hybrid systems. The spread of PV stations and Doubly Fed Inducti
content: TThis paper provides a comprehensive review of many different methods to improve Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) capability and quality of power for Photovoltaic (PV) and wind hybrid systems. The spread of PV stations and Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) wind turbines has witnessed remarkable growth globally, driven by technological advances and growing universal demand for clean power. The ability of the PV system and wind turbine to preserve connection through a fault of grid indicated by LVRT. To improve LVRT and power quality to enhance the dynamic performance of the hybrid system, different methods are used to solve the problem of LVRT and power quality. Among these methods Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System (FACTS) devices and other methods such as crowbar and Direct Current (DC) chopper. FACTS splitted into three group shunt, series, and hybrid connection. These methods are utilized to improve the LVRT capability and quality of power.Keywords: Power Quality; Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT); Hybrid System; Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) Wind Turbine; Photovoltaic (PV); Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System (FACTS); Crowbar; Direct Current (DC) Chopper.

title: Analytical Modelling and Design of a Submersible Threshold Hydraulic Micro-Dam to Evaluate Rural Hydroelectric Production on Non-Diverted Low-Head Rivers
source: Journal of Sustainable Development of Energy Water and Environment Systems
summary: This study presents the analytical modelling, design, and hydraulic validation of a submersible threshold hydraulic micro-dam for rural hydroelectric production on non-diverted low-head rivers. Installed directly in the river, this micro-da
content: This study presents the analytical modelling, design, and hydraulic validation of a submersible threshold hydraulic micro-dam for rural hydroelectric production on non-diverted low-head rivers. Installed directly in the river, this micro-dam offers a technically and economically viable solution to meet the growing electricity demand in rural sub-Saharan communities, particularly in the Republic of Congo, while promoting renewable technologies and sustainable development. This work's contribution is the development and validation of a simplified analytical model derived from the 1D Saint-Venant equations, systematically compared with two-dimensional numerical simulations in COMSOL Multiphysics, applied to a case study of the Douni River in the Republic of Congo. The analytical model enables the estimation of flow speed distributions, pressures, and hydraulic power along the micro-dam channels. Results indicate average flow speeds of 4.46‒9.82 m/s per channel, far exceeding the measured river velocity of 0.297 m/s. Hydraulic power outputs of 7.13 kW to 28.96 kW per channel (14.26‒57.92 kW for a two-channel system) for water depths ranging from 0.22 m to 0.10 m under supercritical flow conditions. The average relative deviation between the analytical and the numerical simulation results remains below 5%, confirming the validity of the proposed simplified method for preliminary design. These values correspond to a maximum slope of 21.8° (40% per channel) and a minimum drop of 1 m. The submersible threshold hydraulic micro-dam demonstrates potential as an integrated hydraulic-hydroelectric solution for small rivers in rural villages, where conventional flow diversion is limited by the absence of natural slopes and high banks. This study is limited to two-dimensional simulations and uniform steady-state flow assumptions and provides a reliable basis for designing low-cost, sustainable micro-hydroelectric systems for electrification in remote areas.

title: From Resource Complementarity to Temporal Integration Behaviour: A Technology-Agnostic Framework for Wind–Solar Hybrid Systems
source: Journal of Sustainable Development of Energy Water and Environment Systems
summary: This study presents a technology-agnostic framework for analysing wind–solar hybridisation from a resource-based perspective, focusing on integration-relevant temporal behaviour. Renewable availability is represented using normalised signal
content: This study presents a technology-agnostic framework for analysing wind–solar hybridisation from a resource-based perspective, focusing on integration-relevant temporal behaviour. Renewable availability is represented using normalised signals, enabling the evaluation of variability and inter-period transition intensity as key indicators of temporal dynamics. The results reveal a non-linear response to the mixing parameter, with variability minimised at balanced wind–solar contributions, while transition intensity reaches its minimum at higher solar shares. This non-coincidence highlights an inherent trade-off between different integration objectives. A demand-aware residual proxy is introduced to assess temporal alignment between renewable availability and electricity demand, indicating improved alignment under hybrid configurations at monthly resolution. The framework operates independently of technology-specific assumptions and dispatch modelling, providing a transparent basis for early-stage planning and hybrid configuration screening. The findings demonstrate how resource complementarity can be systematically linked to integration-relevant behaviour across temporal scales.

title: Overcoming Constraints for Fair Energy: Compatible Solutions in Heritage Protected Urban Centres
source: Journal of Sustainable Development of Smart Energy Networks
summary: Decarbonizing historic urban centres is challenging due to strict architectural and landscape conservation constraints, which limit conventional energy efficiency and renewable solutions. This study investigates three districts in the UNESC
content: Decarbonizing historic urban centres is challenging due to strict architectural and landscape conservation constraints, which limit conventional energy efficiency and renewable solutions. This study investigates three districts in the UNESCO-protected historic centre of Quedlinburg (Germany), assessing the potential of integrated interventions including internal wall insulation, window upgrades, hybrid heating systems, and building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV). Results indicate that envelope improvements combined with hybrid gas boiler–air/water heat pump systems reduce heating demand by over 35%, with a further 10% decrease under projected 2050 climate conditions. BIPV integration contributes to an approximately 30-35% reduction in non-renewable primary energy, depending on roof orientation and available surface area. hDistrict-level analysis confirms the scalability of these measures, demonstrating that conservation-compatible strategies can achieve significant energy and emissions reductions while respecting heritage constraints, providing a replicable framework for other historic centres.

title: Eco-feminism in the modern world: Gender, environment and social transformation
source: International Journal of Research in English
summary: Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary intellectual and social movement that connects gender equality, environmental sustainability and social justice. It examines how systems of patriarchy, economic exploitation, unequal resource distributio
content: Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary intellectual and social movement that connects gender equality, environmental sustainability and social justice. It examines how systems of patriarchy, economic exploitation, unequal resource distribution and environmental degradation can reinforce one another. Emerging prominently during the 1970s and 1980s, eco-feminism has developed from an early emphasis on the symbolic relationship between women and nature toward broader approaches involving environmental justice, political ecology, intersectionality and sustainable development. Contemporary environmental crises such as climate change, biodiversity loss, water scarcity, pollution and food insecurity have renewed interest in eco-feminist perspectives. Women, particularly those living in rural and economically vulnerable communities, may experience environmental changes differently because of unequal access to land, income, technology, political institutions and natural resources. At the same time, women are important agents of environmental protection, community resilience, sustainable agriculture and climate action. The United Nations also recognizes that women's participation in environmental decision-making can strengthen climate-resilient policies. This article examines the relationship between gender and environment, the evolution of eco-feminist thought, women's environmental leadership, climate change, environmental justice and the possibilities for social transformation. It argues that modern eco-feminism should move beyond the assumption that women are naturally closer to nature and instead emphasize equality, participation, rights, knowledge, intersectionality and democratic environmental governance. Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary perspective that examines the interconnected relationship between the oppression of women and the exploitation of nature. It argues that patriarchal, hierarchical, and exploitative social structures often contribute to both gender inequality and environmental degradation. In the modern world, climate change, deforestation, pollution, water scarcity, loss of biodiversity, and unsustainable development have created serious social and ecological challenges, with women—particularly those in rural and marginalized communities—often experiencing disproportionate impacts. Women play important roles in agriculture, household resource management, community health, and environmental conservation, making their participation essential to sustainable development. This article examines the significance of eco-feminism in understanding contemporary gender and environmental issues and explores its potential contribution to social transformation. It highlights the importance of women's environmental knowledge, community participation, political representation, and access to natural and economic resources. The study also emphasizes that environmental sustainability cannot be achieved without addressing gender inequality, poverty, s

title: Flow Dynamics with Jet-induced Vortex Control in a Slotted Vertical-axis Wind Turbine
summary: This study investigates the aerodynamic impact of passive blade slots on the unsteady flow dynamics of a Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) operating at low tip speed ratios. A two-dimensional URANS-based numerical investigation usi
content: This study investigates the aerodynamic impact of passive blade slots on the unsteady flow dynamics of a Darrieus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) operating at low tip speed ratios. A two-dimensional URANS-based numerical investigation using the k–ω SST turbulence model was performed to analyze the creation of slot-induced internal jets and their interaction with the surrounding flow field. An energy-based Jet Strength Index (JSI) was introduced to quantify the momentum injection produced by the slot. The results revealed that the pressure difference between the pressure and suction sides of the blade naturally generated internal jets that injected momentum into the boundary layer and significantly modified the vortex formation. These jets developed primarily on blades 1 and 4, where they weakened the separation-induced vortices identified using the λ₂ vortex criterion and contributed to delaying the dynamic stall. The optimized slotted configuration led to a substantial aerodynamic improvement, with the torque coefficient increasing by up to 89% within the low tip-speed ratio range of λ = 1–2 for a free-stream velocity of 10 m/s. Spectral analysis of the unsteady loads indicated a rotation-driven vortex detachment characterized by a Strouhal number of St ≈ 0.07 and a reduced frequency of k ≈ 0.217 for λ = 1,25. Furthermore, near-wake analysis at λ = 2 primarily weakens separation-induced vortices and reorganizes their spatial distribution in the near wake, leading to reduced vortex strength, delayed breakdown, and more stable wake development, providing new insights into passive flow control mechanisms for enhancing VAWT performance.

title: A Review of Numerical Modeling of Internal Flow, Cavitation, Erosion, and Flow-induced Vibration in Hydropower Valves
summary: Hydropower valves operate under transient, high-pressure conditions in which local throttling, pressure recovery, vortex evolution, and pressure pulsation govern hydraulic performance, cavitation, erosion, and flow-induced vibration. This r
content: Hydropower valves operate under transient, high-pressure conditions in which local throttling, pressure recovery, vortex evolution, and pressure pulsation govern hydraulic performance, cavitation, erosion, and flow-induced vibration. This review synthesizes recent advances in numerical modeling of these coupled phenomena and links internal-flow evolution with hydraulic response, damage initiation, and structural behavior. The evidence base comprised 90 primary studies and five contextual reviews. Twelve primary studies (13.3%) directly addressed hydropower valves or hydropower valve–system interactions, whereas 78 studies (86.7%) provided transferable mechanistic or methodological evidence from related valve and hydraulic systems, highlighting the limited availability of hydropower-specific validation. Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS)-based computational fluid dynamics (CFD) remains the principal engineering method for global hydraulic quantities, whereas large-eddy simulation (LES), multiphase erosion models, and fluid–structure interaction (FSI) methods are more appropriate for unsteady cavitation, particle-induced damage, and structural response. Quantitatively, one direct hydropower butterfly-valve study reported an approximately 10% mean absolute error between CFD predictions and experimental flow-field data. In a transferable three-way globe-valve study, geometric optimization reduced the simulated percentage of cavitation by 49.5%, from 34.90% to 17.62%, while the response-surface model predicted 19.06%. The former supports case-specific confidence in hydropower-valve FSI modeling, whereas the latter demonstrates transferable optimization potential rather than direct hydropower performance. Major limitations include incomplete uncertainty reporting, uneven numerical verification and model calibration, scarce prototype-scale evidence, and limited long-term multiphysics validation. Standardized benchmarks, prototype measurements, and physics-informed monitoring are required to support transferable design and life-cycle decisions.

title: Systemic Quantification And Cascading Biorefinery Engineering Of School Meal Plate Waste
summary: School feeding programs generate large volumes of plate waste, yet most decentralized programs cannot produce comparable and auditable measurements of what is served, consumed, and discarded. Existing research on food-waste measurement, was
content: School feeding programs generate large volumes of plate waste, yet most decentralized programs cannot produce comparable and auditable measurements of what is served, consumed, and discarded. Existing research on food-waste measurement, waste valorization, and sustainability assessment has developed largely as separate streams. This study develops and documents an auditable four-layer framework that links standardized Edge AI computer-vision quantification of school meal plate waste with material characterization, a five-stream cascading bio-valorization pathway, and system-level evaluation, within Indonesia's Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) program. The quantitative, engineering based design covers 50 schools in East Java across five operational zones and 1,200 matched tray pairs, with image-based mass estimates validated against physical scale weights using R², MAE, and MAPE. Waste fractions are characterized through proximate and ultimate analysis and routed to biodiesel, hydroxyapatite, black soldier fly larvae bioconversion, anaerobic digestion, and biochar-compost. Life-cycle and techno economic assessments evaluate the system at a 10 ton/day regional scale. The analysis indicates that standardization at the data-acquisition stage improves downstream comparability and that measured fractions can be linked to differentiated recovery pathways. The numerical results are project reported, the sampling frame is limited to East Java, and the LCA and TEA outputs remain scenario dependent

title: Quaternary adsorption of cadmium(II)/chromium(III)/copper(II)/lead(II) ions from simulated and real wastewater by residual fennel seeds (Foeniculum vulgare) as a removal tool
summary: Proper management of wastewater contaminated with heavy metals through biosorption supports climate change mitigation, green growth, and the circular bioeconomy by generating innovative, biodegradable biosorbents. In this study, lignocellul
content: Proper management of wastewater contaminated with heavy metals through biosorption supports climate change mitigation, green growth, and the circular bioeconomy by generating innovative, biodegradable biosorbents. In this study, lignocellulosic materials derived from residual fennel seeds ( Foeniculum vulgare ), in both virgin (FS) and modified (MFS) forms, were employed for the simultaneous adsorption of Cd, Cr, Cu, and Pb ions from simulated and real wastewaters, for the first time. Physicochemical and instrumental characterisations confirmed the presence of diverse functional groups, high cation exchange capacity, and favourable morphology essential for efficient adsorption. The influence of pH, biosorbent mass, initial concentration, and contact time on the adsorption kinetics and capacity was evaluated. Under optimal conditions (solution pH: 5 (FS)/4 (MFS), initial individual analyte concentration: 50 mg/L, contact time: 20 min with 300 mg of biosorbent), maximum adsorption capacities reached 5.1/7.5 (Cr), 6.1/10.2 (Cu), 3.6/6.7 (Cd), and 7.9/14.7 mg/g (Pb) for FS/MFS, with corresponding removal efficiencies of 50-87.5% (FS) and 50-97.5% (MFS). The metal binding affinity followed the order: Cd < Cr < Cu < Pb. Kinetic analysis revealed a strong correlation with the pseudo-second-order and intraparticle diffusion models (average fit of the removal efficiency values: 99.60% (FS) and 99.85% (MFS), with determination coefficients (R2) close to 1). Overall, the developed biosorption process is cost-effective, environmentally benign, and technically applicable, fully aligning with the principles of green chemistry.

title: A Voltage-Controlled Model Machine Learning Framework for State-of-Charge Estimation in Battery Management System: A Performance Evaluation
summary: Accurate State-of-Charge (SoC) estimation is essential for ensuring the reliability, safety, and efficient operation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), particularly in photovoltaic (PV) applications characterized by intermittent gene
content: Accurate State-of-Charge (SoC) estimation is essential for ensuring the reliability, safety, and efficient operation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), particularly in photovoltaic (PV) applications characterized by intermittent generation. Conventional SoC estimation methods may have limitations in capturing nonlinear and time-dependent voltage behavior under practical operating conditions. This study proposes a data-driven SoC estimation framework that integrates a Voltage-Controlled Model (VCM) with sliding-window temporal feature extraction and multiple machine learning (ML) algorithms. The sliding-window approach transforms sequential voltage measurements into structured lag-based features to represent battery discharge dynamics more effectively. Real-world voltage data were collected from four 45-Ah lead-acid batteries operating in a PV-BESS system from February to December 2024. More than 140,000 charge-discharge records were acquired, from which 6,226 discharge records were extracted for model development and evaluation. Five ML models, namely Support Vector Regression (SVR), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were compared using mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and computation time. The results show that VCM-LSTM achieves the lowest prediction errors, whereas VCM-XGBoost provides the most favorable balance between predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. VCM-XGBoost achieves MSE = 0.0849, MAE = 0.1401, RMSE = 0.2913, and a computation time of 0.94 seconds. These findings indicate that combining sliding-window temporal representation with VCM and ML can support accurate and computationally efficient SoC estimation, highlighting the potential of VCM-XGBoost for resource-constrained BMS applications, particularly in real-world residential PV-BESS environments with limited computational resources.

title: Air pollution in the context of building structure and density in selected Polish cities
summary: The aim of the study was to determine the differentiation of mean annual concentrations of particulate matter PM2.5 and PM10, benzo(a)pyrene (BaP), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and benzene (C₆H₆) in 2018–2024 in the context of the structure and
content: The aim of the study was to determine the differentiation of mean annual concentrations of particulate matter PM2.5 and PM10, benzo(a)pyrene (BaP), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and benzene (C₆H₆) in 2018–2024 in the context of the structure and intensity of development in Gdańsk, Kraków, and Łódź. The analysis also took into account reported pollutant emissions and mean annual wind speed. Data from GIOŚ, KOBiZE, IMGW-PIB, and building data from BDOT10k were used. The highest mean annual concentrations of all analysed pollutants were recorded in Kraków, where the share of built-up area was 49%, and the lowest in Gdańsk, where this share was 30%. After accounting for differences between cities, significant positive correlations between reported emissions and concentration were found for BaP (ρ = 0.90), NO₂ (ρ = 0.60), and PM10 (ρ = 0.55). However, in models accounting for the city effect, reported emissions were not significantly associated with the concentration of any of the analysed pollutants. The mean annual wind speed was highest in Gdańsk (3.98 m/s) and lowest in Kraków (3.08 m/s). The height structure of buildings differed between cities but did not directly correspond to the observed differentiation in concentrations. The results indicate that the differentiation of mean annual air pollutant concentrations between cities co-occurs with differences in building intensity and wind speed. Due to the limited number of cities analysed, these relationships should not be interpreted as causal.

title: Pelatihan dan Implementasi Sistem Kendali Otomatis pada Pompa Air Tenaga Surya untuk Meningkatkan Efisiensi Irigasi Sawah di Desa Ulak Depati
summary: Limited water availability during the dry season and reliance on diesel-powered pumps remain major obstacles to rice field irrigation in Ulak Depati Village, as diesel pumps require high operating costs and inefficient manual operation. Thi
content: Limited water availability during the dry season and reliance on diesel-powered pumps remain major obstacles to rice field irrigation in Ulak Depati Village, as diesel pumps require high operating costs and inefficient manual operation. This community engagement activity aims to design and implement an Arduino-based, solar-powered automatic water pump system that operates according to soil moisture conditions, as well as to improve the partner farmer group's knowledge and skills in operating and maintaining the system. The system consists of solar panels, a solar charge controller (SCC), a battery, an Arduino Uno, a soil moisture sensor, a relay module, a solid-state relay (SSR), and a DC water pump. The implementation stages included socialization, field surveys, system design and assembly, field installation and testing, and training and mentoring for the farmer group. The results showed that the Arduino Uno successfully processed sensor data to control the pump automatically, turning the pump on when the sensor value exceeded 450 and stopping it at values of 450 or below. Field testing delivered 2,513.60 liters of water with a water level of 4.7 cm over 246 minutes, while the training evaluation involving 15 participants achieved an average satisfaction rate of 93%. These findings indicate that the program effectively supports automatic solar-powered rice field irrigation and enhances the farmers' capacity to manage appropriate technology independently

title: A train-the-trainer framework for adapted sports and physical activity in community disability services
summary: People with disabilities face persistent barriers to physical activity, while community disability services often lack staff training and structured approaches to delivering adapted sport. This article presents a train-the-trainer framework
content: People with disabilities face persistent barriers to physical activity, while community disability services often lack staff training and structured approaches to delivering adapted sport. This article presents a train-the-trainer framework designed to equip direct support professionals and community coaches to provide safe, person-centred physical activity. The framework integrates four adaptation domains rules, equipment, environment, and instruction with a population guide, a structured 60-minute session, and four participation levels progressing from initial exploration to community competition. A 16-hour curriculum combines classroom learning, practical activities, and supervised coaching, with competency-based sign-off and a subsequent pathway for training colleagues. Safety, safeguarding, participant choice, and individual care plans underpin delivery. A planned 12-month pilot with Open Arms Care Corporation in Nashville, Tennessee, will examine implementation and participant outcomes through baseline, three-month, and six-month assessments. Measures include physical activity, fitness, movement skills, individual goal attainment, well-being, social participation, safety, and staff capacity. No outcome data are currently available, and the proposed uncontrolled evaluation cannot establish causality. The framework offers a practical model for developing workforce capacity and extending access to adapted sport, subject to evaluation of feasibility, fidelity, sustainability, and participant outcomes.

title: "Bats Are There, But Who Will Protect Them?": Community and Institutional Perspectives on Cave-Dwelling Bat Conservation
summary: Cave-dwelling bats face escalating anthropogenic pressures globally, yet their conservation is frequently compromised by limited community ecological literacy, persistent cultural myths, and inadequate integration of community and instituti
content: Cave-dwelling bats face escalating anthropogenic pressures globally, yet their conservation is frequently compromised by limited community ecological literacy, persistent cultural myths, and inadequate integration of community and institutional perspectives into management. This study investigated community perceptions, staff knowledge, and short-term observations of bat activity at Sudwala Caves, Mpumalanga Province, South Africa, to inform evidence-based conservation strategies. A qualitative socio-ecological design combined reflexive thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with Mankele community participants (n = 31), Sudwala management and tour guide personnel (n = 9), alongside structured field observations conducted by the researchers over three consecutive days in the main cave and exploratory visits to two adjacent unmanaged bat caves. Seven interrelated themes emerged: (1) ambivalent perceptions of bats, (2) cultural myths and misinformation, (3) stakeholder perceptions of declining bat abundance, (4) anthropogenic disturbance as a perceived conservation challenge, (5) gaps in ecological knowledge, (6) conservation willingness contingent on institutional leadership, and (7) bat-tourism interactions. Although a strong majority of community participants expressed willingness to support bat conservation, a substantial proportion demonstrated significant gaps in ecological knowledge, such as the inability to define pollination or identify specific ecological roles of bats. Cultural myths, particularly hair-related misconceptions, were also frequently reported. Both community members and cave personnel similarly perceived a long-term decline in bat abundance, a perception supported by short-term field observations that recorded relatively few visible bats in the main tourist cave. In contrast, exploratory observations of adjacent, low-disturbance caves revealed larger visible bat aggregations, providing comparative ecological context and generating hypotheses about the influence of chronic human disturbance on cave occupancy. These findings indicate that strong community support for bat conservation exists despite limited ecological literacy, and that integrating stakeholder perspectives with preliminary ecological observations can inform adaptive management while highlighting priorities for long-term population monitoring and behavioural studies. The study proposes practical recommendations centred on community education, strengthened institutional collaboration, reduced tourism-related disturbance, and formal protection of adjacent cave habitats. These findings provide an important qualitative baseline for adaptive management and future bat conservation research in South African show caves.

title: Pengenalan Kompor Roket Biomassa pada UMKM Kerupuk Puli UD Sinab di Bangkalan
summary: This article reports the documented introduction of biomass rocket stoves at UD Sinab, Bator Village, Bangkalan, and proposes measurements for subsequent partner evaluation. Primary evidence consisted of an assignment letter and seven origi
content: This article reports the documented introduction of biomass rocket stoves at UD Sinab, Bator Village, Bangkalan, and proposes measurements for subsequent partner evaluation. Primary evidence consisted of an assignment letter and seven original photographs from the ROCKET STOVE folder. Visual analysis identified two black stove units equipped with fans and electrical leads, split firewood, a cooking vessel, and equipment handling. Four photographs showed demonstrations or interactions, while one group photograph displayed the program banner and partner name. The assignment letter scheduled the activity for 22 May 2026, whereas all photograph filenames indicated 16 May 2026 and contained no EXIF capture-time data. Therefore, the exact demonstration date remains unconfirmed. The documentation does not establish participant numbers, production batches, fuel savings, processing-time changes, product-quality improvements, satisfaction, or routine adoption. Proposed follow-up includes an owner-selected heating task, three comparable batches per stove, operator-maintained records, skill and feedback assessments, and mentoring at weeks 2, 4, and 12 from an agreed starting date.

title: Stability and robustness of decision rankings across objective weighting methods in multi-criteria decision-making
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Objective weighting methods derive criterion importance directly from data, but a method producing consistent rankings across aggregation models may not be robust to weight changes. This study jointly evaluates cross-model ranking stability
content: Objective weighting methods derive criterion importance directly from data, but a method producing consistent rankings across aggregation models may not be robust to weight changes. This study jointly evaluates cross-model ranking stability and perturbation robustness in multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) across five objective weighting methods: entropy, criteria importance through intercriteria correlation (CRITIC), method based on the removal effects of criteria (MEREC), principal component analysis (PCA), and standard deviation (SD). Two datasets were used: a renewable energy case (five alternatives and ten criteria) and a supplier-selection case (ten alternatives, eleven criteria) for external validation. Each weight vector was applied to five MCDM aggregation models: visekriterijumska optimizacija i kompromisno resenje (VIKOR), complex proportional assessment (COPRAS), multi-objective optimization on the basis of ratio analysis (MOORA), evaluation based on distance from average solution (EDAS), and technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS). Stability was measured using rank correlation, rank shift, and rank reversal; robustness through criterion-weight perturbation. The two diagnostics are positively associated but not interchangeable. Entropy and MEREC achieved the highest stability and robustness in both cases, whereas PCA was stable across models yet highly sensitive to weight perturbation, indicating that reliability cannot be judged from cross-model stability alone.

title: The effect of dirt and shading on the output power of solar panels at the 50 kWp on-grid rooftop solar power plant
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: The development of solar power plants has penetrated various sectors, both industry and education. Universitas Pamulang has begun using photovoltaic (PV) technology with an installed capacity of 50 kWp in on-grid solar power plants. However
content: The development of solar power plants has penetrated various sectors, both industry and education. Universitas Pamulang has begun using photovoltaic (PV) technology with an installed capacity of 50 kWp in on-grid solar power plants. However, this technology is greatly influenced by environmental factors, not limited to radiation, temperature, tilt angle, wind speed, and direction; the effects of dirt and shading are also important factors that can affect its output power. With this fairly expensive investment, it must be balanced with efforts to maximize energy production, so that there are no losses or damage, especially due to dirt. With these conditions, a comprehensive analysis of the impact of dirt and shade on PV is needed to optimize its output power. This study applied a comparison method between dirty, clean, and shaded PV to analyze their output power. The results showed a decrease in PV output power due to dirt by 4.52% and shading by 3.28% compared to the output power of the cleaned PV, so it can be concluded that dirt and shading have a strong influence on the decrease in output power, and maintenance and cleaning are essential for optimal PV performance.

title: Iterative single-ended fault location in isolated neutral 6–35 kV networks
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: This paper proposes an iterative approach for accurate single-line-to-ground (SLG) fault localization in 6–35 kV distribution networks with isolated neutrals. Such faults account for approximately 80% of network disturbances and are typical
content: This paper proposes an iterative approach for accurate single-line-to-ground (SLG) fault localization in 6–35 kV distribution networks with isolated neutrals. Such faults account for approximately 80% of network disturbances and are typically associated with capacitive fault currents and transition resistances of up to 2000 Ohm. Conventional lumped-parameter representations may result in localization errors of up to 50%, primarily because distributed line capacitance is neglected. The developed approach utilizes an exact ABCD-parameter representation of the line in the zero-sequence domain, where distributed electrical parameters are explicitly considered. A least-squares estimation procedure simultaneously determines fault distance and transition resistance from single-ended voltage and current measurements, accounting for capacitive currents and measurement noise. Monte Carlo analysis yielded an average relative fault-location error of 3.13%, with individual errors ranging from 0.33% to 6.83% across the investigated transition resistance range. Further experimental validation using a 12 km, 35 kV overhead distribution line demonstrated a maximum discrepancy of 0.08 km between simulated and experimental results. Consequently, the proposed iterative approach provides accurate single-ended fault localization without requiring line disconnection, making it highly suitable for reliable fault diagnostics in modern smart-grid distribution systems.

title: Observer-based non-singular terminal sliding mode control for robust regulation of high-gain DC–DC converters
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: High-gain capacitor-based boost converters (HG-CBCs) require robust voltage regulation despite nonlinear internal coupling, parameter variations, and limited feedback sensing. An output-feedback architecture is developed by combining a sign
content: High-gain capacitor-based boost converters (HG-CBCs) require robust voltage regulation despite nonlinear internal coupling, parameter variations, and limited feedback sensing. An output-feedback architecture is developed by combining a signed-power non-singular terminal sliding mode controller (NTSMC) with a linear extended state observer (LESO), which reconstructs the output-voltage derivative and lumped output-channel dynamics from the measured voltage alone. The stability analysis separates finite-time tracking on the ideal sliding manifold from the practical bounded response introduced by observer error and the saturation layer. Real-time implementation on a TMS320F28379D digital signal processor (DSP) demonstrates stable regulation under both steady-state and step-reference operation. At reference voltages of 40 V, 47 V, 57 V, and 87 V, the LESO–NTSMC limits output-voltage ripple to 6.7–8.9%, compared with 9.9–15.1% for conventional sliding mode control (SMC), corresponding to a 31–41% reduction. The experiments further show an average efficiency of 88.7% while requiring only output-voltage feedback, supporting a reduced-sensing solution for high-gain direct current to direct current (DC–DC) conversion in low-voltage renewable energy systems.

title: ANFIS based photovoltaic interconnected smart grid with power quality improvement
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Maintaining power quality is a critical challenge when using microgrids as a primary power source, largely due to their reliance on intermittent renewable energy. During peak loading conditions, these power fluctuations can lead to signific
content: Maintaining power quality is a critical challenge when using microgrids as a primary power source, largely due to their reliance on intermittent renewable energy. During peak loading conditions, these power fluctuations can lead to significant grid instability. The instability is mainly voltage deviations, which are sag, unbalancing and swell. To address this, this article proposes an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) controlled unified power quality conditioner (UPQC), supported directly by photovoltaic (PV) generation. The performance of this intelligent UPQC system is evaluated under standard environmental conditions, with MATLAB 2017b used to simulate and plot the system's effectiveness in mitigating power quality issues.

title: CornLeaf-MIA Net: a novel deep learning architecture for corn leaf disease detection in precision agriculture
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Early detection of corn leaf diseases is important for maintaining crop productivity and supporting precision agriculture. This study proposes CornLeaf-multi-scale intelligent architecture network (CornLeaf-MIA Net), a lightweight convoluti
content: Early detection of corn leaf diseases is important for maintaining crop productivity and supporting precision agriculture. This study proposes CornLeaf-multi-scale intelligent architecture network (CornLeaf-MIA Net), a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) for multiclass classification of blight, common rust, gray leaf spot, and healthy corn leaves. A dataset of 4,013 labeled images was preprocessed through resizing, normalization, and training-stage augmentation. The proposed model was evaluated against MobileNetV2, VGG16, and ResNet50 under identical experimental conditions. CornLeaf-MIA Net achieved 98.38% testing accuracy, with weighted precision, recall, and F1-score of 98.50%, 98.38%, and 98.40%, respectively. The model contains 2,982,052 trainable parameters and achieved a training-validation accuracy gap of 0.71%. It also outperformed MobileNetV2 (94.40%), VGG16 (94.89%), and ResNet50 (95.39%) in testing accuracy. The trained model was implemented in a Flask-based web application using OpenCV and TensorFlow for automated multi-leaf disease diagnosis. The results indicate that the proposed task-specific multi-scale CNN provides high classification performance with a relatively compact architecture and demonstrates practical applicability through web-based implementation.

title: A novel 19-level inverter topology based on a single direct current source and reduced component count
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Conventional multilevel inverters (MLI) provide low harmonic distortion but often require many switches, passive components, and voltage sensors, increasing cost, size, and control complexity. This paper proposes a compact 19-level modified
content: Conventional multilevel inverters (MLI) provide low harmonic distortion but often require many switches, passive components, and voltage sensors, increasing cost, size, and control complexity. This paper proposes a compact 19-level modified split-packed U-cell (MSPUC) inverter powered through one independent direct current (DC) supply source. The proposed configuration employs a reduced number of switches and only three capacitors. Its key contribution is the natural self-balancing of capacitor voltages under sensorless open-loop pulse width modulation (PWM) operation, eliminating the need for additional voltage sensors or auxiliary balancing circuits. In addition, the topology achieves a total standing voltage per unit (TSVpu) of 4.22 and a cost function (CF) of 1.70, indicating reduced voltage stress and improved structural efficiency. MATLAB/Simulink simulations are performed under steady-state conditions, load variations, nonlinear loading, switching-frequency variation, and sudden DC-source disturbances. The obtained results confirm stable capacitor voltage regulation, fast dynamic response, and high-quality output waveforms. Under the nominal condition of R=20 ohm and L=20 mH, the load current total harmonic distortion (THD) is limited to 0.96% without using any external filter. Therefore, the proposed MSPUC inverter provides a compact, cost-effective, and low-complexity solution for efficient power electronic conversion systems.

title: Modelling sump pump energy usage patterns using artificial intelligence
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: Water typically seeps into the basements of buildings that are close to lakes or situated in low-lying areas, and hence these places require continuous pumping to avoid flooding. Such situations very often lead to high energy consumption wh
content: Water typically seeps into the basements of buildings that are close to lakes or situated in low-lying areas, and hence these places require continuous pumping to avoid flooding. Such situations very often lead to high energy consumption which is not well-understood. This research models and analyzes the energy usage patterns of sump pumps installed at Basement 3 of Asia Pacific College (APC) through artificial intelligence techniques. High-resolution (5-minute) and daily aggregated datasets were recorded by SCT013 current sensors and then were converted to energy consumption values. Four prediction models—linear regression, random forest, support vector machine (SVM), and long short-term memory (LSTM)— were trained and tested using root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R²) metrics. For the 5-minute dataset, random forest achieved RMSE=20.78, MAE=2.05, and R²=0.226, whereas LSTM obtained RMSE=18.22, MAE=1.56, and negative R². For the daily dataset, random forest achieved RMSE=299.43, MAE=222.98, R²=0.091, while LSTM reached RMSE=289.80, MAE=208.04, and R²=0.014. The models indicate strong diurnal patterns and show the effect of temporal resolution on predictive performance. All reported LSTM results correspond to direct one-step-ahead forecasting and therefore characterize short-horizon predictive accuracy rather than multi-step deployment performance. The developed framework serves as a steppingstone towards future intelligent pump control and energy-efficient operation.

title: A hybrid Inception-attention VGG and quantum variational learning framework for scalable healthcare data analytics
source: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
summary: The rapid expansion of clinical data requires analytical frameworks capable of handling high-dimensional, heterogeneous, and noisy medical information. Classical deep learning models provide strong feature extraction capabilities but are of
content: The rapid expansion of clinical data requires analytical frameworks capable of handling high-dimensional, heterogeneous, and noisy medical information. Classical deep learning models provide strong feature extraction capabilities but are often computationally intensive and prone to scalability limitations. Conversely, quantum machine learning (QML) offers enhanced representational capacity but suffers from hardware constraints and noise sensitivity. To address these shortcomings, this paper proposes a hybrid deep learning–quantum processing architecture integrating an Inception-attention-based visual geometry group (VGG) network for multiscale feature extraction with a quantum variational classifier (QVC) optimized using parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs). Clinical data from the MIMIC-III dataset undergo min–max normalization, multi-resolution convolutional feature extraction, and quantum-enhanced classification. Experiments demonstrate superior performance compared to classical support vector machine (SVM), quantum support vector machines (QSVM), quantum kernel support vector machine (QKSVM), quantum variational support vector machine (QVSVM), and quantum variational kernel support vector machine (QVKSVM) models. The proposed framework achieves 98.79% accuracy, 98.67% precision, 98.15% recall, and 98.88% F1-score, representing a subtle 0.3% improvement over existing quantum-assisted hybrid models. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid framework within the adopted classical–quantum simulation environment and motivate further validation on real near-term quantum hardware.

title: Nanotexturing of Si Nanopyramid with Enhanced Light Absorption and Improved Hydrogen Gas Yield
summary: In an era defined by climate change and the urgent need for sustainable solutions, the topic of renewable energy has emerged as a beacon of hope and progress. Renewable energy, characterized by its abundant and inexhaustible nature, offers
content: In an era defined by climate change and the urgent need for sustainable solutions, the topic of renewable energy has emerged as a beacon of hope and progress. Renewable energy, characterized by its abundant and inexhaustible nature, offers a viable pathway to meet our energy needs while mitigating the environmental impacts associated with traditional energy sources. Thus, quantitative analysis on the hydrogen gas produced by p-type silicon wafer during water splitting reaction is an important area of research in the field of renewable energy. The process of water splitting involves the separation of water into hydrogen and oxygen gas, which can be used as a clean source of fuel. This current work has unequivocally demonstrated that Si pyramids exhibit superior performance compared to planar Si surfaces in terms of hydrogen gas production. The unique surface morphology of Si pyramids, with its increased surface area and light-trapping capabilities, has been proven in augmenting the water splitting reaction. Si pyramids is fabricated using wet chemical anisotropic etching and hydrothermal method in a stainless-steel autoclave. The manipulated variable for this project is the Si pyramids etching time start from 90 min with 30 min gap until 180 min. Through the characterization and analysis of this project, the Si pyramids with 150 min etching time has shown the optimum absorption intensity, the most uniform pyramid morphology in FESEM, the largest photocurrent density (65.4 mA/cm2 at -1.2V) and produced the highest amount of hydrogen gas which is 10.8 ml with accumulated duration of 60 min during gas chromatography and this value surpass other Si pyramids wafer and planar Si.

title: Reliability-Based Preventive Maintenance Planning of Pressure Regulator Shut-Off Valve Components on CN235 Aircraft
summary: Aircraft component reliability is essential for maintaining flight safety and operational continuity. The Pressure Regulator Shut-Off Valve (PRSOV) is a critical component of the CN235 bleed air system because it regulates and shuts off pre
content: Aircraft component reliability is essential for maintaining flight safety and operational continuity. The Pressure Regulator Shut-Off Valve (PRSOV) is a critical component of the CN235 bleed air system because it regulates and shuts off pressurized air supplied to the aircraft environmental control system. Historical maintenance records indicated 17 PRSOV-related failures during 0–8,952 flight hours, including failures involving the valve, connector, diaphragm, seal O-ring, spring, and solenoid. This study aims to characterize PRSOV reliability, identify dominant failure modes and their causes, and develop reliability-based preventive maintenance recommendations. A quantitative reliability analysis was conducted using a two-parameter Weibull distribution, supported by Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and Fault Tree Analysis (FTA). Weibull analysis indicated a shape parameter greater than one, representing an increasing failure-rate pattern and suggesting the influence of component aging and wear-out mechanisms. FMEA was used to prioritize failure modes based on severity, occurrence, and detection, while FTA was applied to identify the logical relationships among basic failure causes. The integrated results indicate that preventive maintenance intervals should be differentiated according to component-specific reliability characteristics and failure risks rather than relying solely on the manufacturer's general maintenance interval. The proposed approach provides a basis for improving PRSOV reliability, reducing unscheduled maintenance, and supporting CN235 operational safety.

title: Enhanced Multi-criteria Decision-making Framework for Hybrid Super-capacitor Selection in Electric Vehicles using FWZIC and Fuzzy MULTIMOORA
source: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
summary: The move to sustainable transport supports the development of evaluation techniques for Electric Vehicles (EVs) and their energy storage systems.The uncertainty, discrepancies and subjective judgments of experts affect the rankings produced
