title: Carbon-optimal or health-optimal? Air pollution health accounts for data center siting under China’s “East Data, West Computing” initiative
summary: This dataset contains the data and Python code for the article "Carbon-optimal or health-optimal? Air pollution health accounts for data center siting under China's 'East Data, West Computing' initiative" (submitted to the Journal of Cleane
content: This dataset contains the data and Python code for the article "Carbon-optimal or health-optimal? Air pollution health accounts for data center siting under China's 'East Data, West Computing' initiative" (submitted to the Journal of Cleaner Production). The study estimates the additional thermal generation that new electricity demand induces in each Chinese province, combines it with power-sector CO2 emission factors and a provincial PM2.5 source–receptor matrix, and compares the carbon emissions and PM2.5-related premature deaths of data center capacity added before 2030 under alternative siting scenarios. Files: 1. replication_data.xlsx – the only input file, with a README sheet documenting every variable and source. Sheets: (1) provincial parameters for 31 provinces (grid, region, hub status, 2022 average power-sector emission factors, 2021 thermal generation, data center racks in 2019, built racks of the national data center clusters, assumed curtailment rates, 2020 population and per capita GRP); (2) an annual provincial power panel for 2005–2024 (total, hydro, thermal, wind and solar generation and electricity consumption; National Bureau of Statistics); (3–4) power-sector PM2.5 source–receptor matrices of premature deaths for 2020 and 2035 from the replication data of Hu et al. (2024); (5) provincial heating and cooling degree days for 2005–2023 computed from NOAA GSOD station data; (6) provincial area- and population-weighted annual mean temperatures for 2000–2024 from the 1-km dataset of Peng et al. (2019); (7) scalar parameters with sources. 2. replication_code.py – a single script that reproduces all tables, figures and numbers reported in the article.

title: Unveiling livestock tracing and trading dynamics between Brazilian ranchers and slaughterhouses by network science
summary: Beef production plays a central role in the Brazilian agri-food economy, particularly in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul (MS), which is a national reference in cattle herd size and holds strong socio-environmental relevance due to the Panta
content: Beef production plays a central role in the Brazilian agri-food economy, particularly in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul (MS), which is a national reference in cattle herd size and holds strong socio-environmental relevance due to the Pantanal floodplain and its long-standing livestock traditions. Despite this importance, the structural organization of cattle trading interactions between ranchers and slaughterhouses remains poorly understood, especially with respect to the mechanisms shaping network formation and spatial organization. This study analyzes cattle trading transactions based on official Animal Movement Permission records issued between January 2021 and June 2022 in MS. Using these data, we constructed a directed, weighted bipartite network comprising 20,827 nodes and 258,120 edges, representing ranchers and slaughterhouses as distinct node classes. Network science methods were applied to characterize structural properties, centralization patterns, and spatial dependencies, while temporal dynamics were examined on a monthly scale to capture seasonal variations in trading activity. The results reveal a highly asymmetric and centralized network structure, with a small number of slaughterhouses concentrating a disproportionate share of trading connections. Weighted degree distributions display consistent heavy-tailed behavior, with a descriptive power-law exponent (γ) close to 1.2 over time, up to a characteristic weighted-degree threshold between approximately 129 and 256. Although overall network topology remains stable across months, the volume of trades and number of animals per transaction fluctuate in response to market and climatic conditions. Spatial analysis shows that average trading distances increase with node connectivity up to a characteristic scale, beyond which geographic distance becomes weakly associated with connectivity, suggesting the influence of logistical constraints and node-specific advantages. These findings support the hypothesis that Brazilian beef trading networks are shaped by the combined effects of preferential attachment mechanisms and spatial constraints. The resulting hub-and-spoke organization has direct implications for market concentration, resilience, and sustainability. By providing an integrated structural and spatial perspective based on official traceability data, this study contributes to a better understanding of cattle trading dynamics and offers insights relevant to producers, policymakers, and strategies aimed at promoting more sustainable and efficient beef production systems.

title: Energy-Level-Guided Selection ofHole-Collecting Monolayers for p-i-n Perovskite Solar Cells
summary: Harnessing solar energy is crucial for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating climate change. Among emerging photovoltaic technologies, metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted considerable attention owing to thei
content: Harnessing solar energy is crucial for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating climate change. Among emerging photovoltaic technologies, metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their high power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) and low manufacturing costs. In particular, inverted-architecture (p-i-n) PSCs incorporating hole-collecting monolayers (HCMs) have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional (n-i-p) PSCs employing Spiro-OMeTAD-based hole-transport layers, which can suffer from stability issues. These inverted PSCs have improved operational stability and PCEs. A wide variety of HCMs have been developed, but their hole-collection efficiencies depend strongly on the combination of HCM and perovskite materials. Therefore, selecting an appropriate HCM for a given perovskite is essential for achieving high efficiency PSCs. Here, we establish a practical guideline for selecting HCMs based on energy level alignment. We focus on five representative carbazole-based HCMs: 2PACz, MeO-2PACz, Me-2PACz, Me-4PACz, and 3PATAT-C3. By combining experimentally determined energy parameters of these HCMs with the universal energy level alignment model proposed in our previous work, we evaluated the compatibility of these HCMs with given perovskites. We then tested the proposed guideline by examining the correlation between the model-predicted hole-collection efficiencies and previously reported photovoltaic performance. This framework enables rational selection of HCMs for diverse perovskites, thereby minimizing trial-and-error screening in the development of high-efficiency PSCs.

title: Macrofaunal bioturbation modulates microbial metabolic potential in arid mangrove sediments
summary: Bioturbation by benthic organisms substantially alters the physical and biogeochemical properties of mangrove sediments. Through burrowing and sediment reworking, bioturbators increase oxygen penetration into otherwise anoxic, waterlogged s
content: Bioturbation by benthic organisms substantially alters the physical and biogeochemical properties of mangrove sediments. Through burrowing and sediment reworking, bioturbators increase oxygen penetration into otherwise anoxic, waterlogged sediments and redistribute organic matter throughout the sediment profile. Although previous studies have shown that bioturbation modifies microbial community composition, its consequences for microbial functional potential remain poorly understood. Using metagenomics, we confirmed that crab bioturbation reshaped the composition of the sediment prokaryotic community and showed that this restructuring was accompanied by pronounced, depth-dependent shifts in metabolic potential. Gene- and pathway-level analyses indicated that bioturbation redirected bacterial and archaeal functional potential away from anaerobic degradation of complex organic matter and towards more metabolically versatile and oxidative processes, with the enrichment of functions associated with respiratory and central carbon metabolism, the utilisation of diverse carbon- and nitrogen-containing compounds, and traits potentially involved in nutrient mobilisation and plant growth promotion. Consistent with this functional-repertoire transition, diel gas-flux measurements revealed significantly higher CO2 emissions from bioturbated sediments, whereas CH4 emissions were not affected. We propose that these shifts enable sediment microbial communities to exploit newly available substrates, creating a more nutritionally favourable sediment milieu for both microbial communities and other sediment-dwellers, including mangrove trees. Because arid mangroves are typically constrained by patchy nutrient availability and persistent abiotic stress, including high salinity and aridity, these bioturbation-driven microbial functional shifts may play an important role in sustaining mangrove productivity and could represent a general mechanism linking ecosystem engineering to microbiome-mediated nutrient cycling across coastal sediments.

title: Towards Eco-Smart Vertical Cities: Sustainable Skyscrapers in a New Paradigm.
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The concept of Skyscrapers 2.0 represents a paradigm shift in urban planning, expertly blending sustainability, advanced technology, and multifunctionality. Next-generation high-rises are designed to be self-sustaining ecosystems through th
content: The concept of Skyscrapers 2.0 represents a paradigm shift in urban planning, expertly blending sustainability, advanced technology, and multifunctionality. Next-generation high-rises are designed to be self-sustaining ecosystems through the adoption of advanced automation technologies, vertical farming, and renewable energy harvesting. In addition to optimizing energy use and enhancing occupant well-being, they aim to address significant urban concerns such as resource depletion, climate change, and population density. Using modular designs, self-healing materials, biophilic features, and waste-to-resource systems, Skyscrapers 2.0 are intended to be dynamic, resilient, and esthetically pleasing urban environments that contribute to a greener, smarter, and more connected future.

title: Enzymatic Delignification Technology for Bioethanol Production from Ulva reticulata Macroalgae: A Review
summary: Bioethanol is a promising renewable fuel that can reduce dependence on fossil fuels and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. Ulva reticulata has attracted attention as a third-generation bioethanol feedstock because of its carbohydrate-rich b
content: Bioethanol is a promising renewable fuel that can reduce dependence on fossil fuels and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. Ulva reticulata has attracted attention as a third-generation bioethanol feedstock because of its carbohydrate-rich biomass, containing cellulose, hemicellulose-like fractions, and ulvan-rich sulfated polysaccharides that can be converted into fermentable sugars. Although a lignin-like or acid-insoluble fraction has been reported in U. reticulata, this macroalga is generally considered a low-lignin biomass, and its recalcitrance is primarily associated with the ulvan-rich cell-wall matrix rather than a dominant terrestrial-type lignin network. Consequently, the role of delignification in U. reticulata should be viewed as the modification of phenolic or lignin-like residues and the enhancement of cell-wall accessibility rather than the removal of structural lignin. This review critically evaluates the potential of enzymatic delignification technologies to improve bioethanol production from U. reticulata through a PRISMA-guided literature analysis. The findings indicate that ligninolytic enzymes, including laccase, lignin peroxidase (LiP), manganese peroxidase (MnP), and versatile peroxidase (VP), may enhance polysaccharide accessibility and downstream saccharification. Among these enzymes, fungal laccase, particularly from Pleurotus spp., appears promising because it uses molecular oxygen as the electron acceptor and produces water as the primary by-product, offering a potentially more environmentally friendly alternative to peroxide-dependent systems. However, most available evidence is derived from terrestrial lignocellulosic biomass, and direct studies on U. reticulata remain limited. Overall, enzymatic delignification is a promising yet experimental strategy for improving U. reticulata bioconversion. Future studies should validate the effects of ligninolytic enzymes on the modification of phenolic or lignin-like residues, ulvan-matrix disruption, sugar release, inhibitor formation, and ethanol production to establish their practical role in macroalgae-based bioethanol processes.

title: Exploring Business Use Cases for Integrating Electric Vehicles in Electricity Markets and Flexibility Services
summary: Electric Vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a viable solution for mitigating greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the transportation sector. However, integrating EVs into existing power systems presents significant challenges. Adopting EVs will in
content: Electric Vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a viable solution for mitigating greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the transportation sector. However, integrating EVs into existing power systems presents significant challenges. Adopting EVs will inevitably increase energy demand and peak consumption, but EVs also introduce a new source of flexibility that system operators can manage effectively at both the transmission and distribution levels. Several studies have examined the technological, operational, and market challenges of EV penetration in power systems. Most studies do not address how EV penetration can provide flexibility services in real-world scenarios using standard implementations. To address this gap, this paper proposes seven BUCs to support EV integration and deliver the critical services required by the system operator. The seven BUCs are structured using the templates defined in IEC 62559-2 to provide a consistent description of their actors, objectives, interactions, and information exchanges. The resulting conceptual specifications and publicly available repository provide a basis for future assessment and context-specific adaptation; their practical implementation and replicability are not demonstrated in the present study.

title: Bridging Disciplines for Sustainability: Achieving the SDGs Through Collaborative Synergy
source: International journal of research and scientific innovation
summary: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development demands a shift away from traditional, siloed academic approaches toward integrated, cross-sectoral frameworks. This chapter examines how multidisciplinary collaboration in higher education can ac
content: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development demands a shift away from traditional, siloed academic approaches toward integrated, cross-sectoral frameworks. This chapter examines how multidisciplinary collaboration in higher education can accelerate systemic progress toward interconnected Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Grounded in complex adaptive systems theory, institutional governance models, and university case studies, the study evaluates the dynamics of cross-field research. Findings indicate that isolated disciplines are inadequate for addressing complex, systemic challenges like climate disruption, resource depletion, and socio-economic inequity. Conversely, fusing natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and humanities yields scalable, high-impact solutions. Nevertheless, structural barriers—including departmental silos, rigid tenure metrics, and fragmented funding—hinder deep collaboration. To resolve these friction points, we propose institutional reforms: revising faculty incentives to credit joint achievements, funding autonomous interdisciplinary hubs, updating graduate curricula with co-mentorship models, and building strategic public-private-civic partnerships that position higher education as a essential engine for global sustainability.

title: Segmenting Audiences based on Perceptions and Knowledge of Plastic Use Impacts in the United States
summary: Plastic products are an intrinsic and pervasive part of modern human life. Generally, people find plastics convenient and affordable, but largely overlook their environmental impacts due to limited awareness. The purpose of this study was t
content: Plastic products are an intrinsic and pervasive part of modern human life. Generally, people find plastics convenient and affordable, but largely overlook their environmental impacts due to limited awareness. The purpose of this study was to apply audience segmentation using knowledge gap theory to identify the characteristics of segments within the U.S. public with low knowledge and perceptions of the impacts of plastic use. Doing so could inform targeted communication strategies for population segments with limited knowledge and perceptions of plastic use impacts. A two-step hierarchical clustering and K-means clustering analysis was used on a nationally representative sample of 1,235 U.S. residents aged 18 or older. Most respondents had moderate knowledge levels and perceptions of the impacts of plastic use. Five distinct clusters of respondents emerged. Social media integration and socio-demographics differed significantly across the five clusters. The findings suggest that the low knowledge, benefit-oriented segment may represent an important audience for future communication efforts because it was characterized by low knowledge and was more likely to include younger adults, high school graduates, and respondents identifying as politically conservative and Republican. Future research could evaluate whether communication strategies tailored to these audience characteristics improve knowledge, perceptions, and other communication outcomes.

title: Long term yield trends and stability of mechanized rice and wheat establishment systems over two decades in the Indo Gangetic Plains
summary: Rice–wheat farmers in the Indo-Gangetic Plains are being encouraged to replace puddled transplanting and repeated tillage with machine-based establishment, yet few field records show how the alternatives perform over decades. We analysed 22
content: Rice–wheat farmers in the Indo-Gangetic Plains are being encouraged to replace puddled transplanting and repeated tillage with machine-based establishment, yet few field records show how the alternatives perform over decades. We analysed 22 seasons (1998–2020) of a mechanization experiment at Modipuram, India, that compared ten rice and five wheat establishment methods, and we evaluated twenty rice–wheat combinations. Using all seasons with verified records, we estimated yield level, variability, sustainable yield index (SYI), Mann–Kendall trends with Sen slopes and Eberhart–Russell stability, and we tested replicated data from 2016–2019 by analysis of variance. Puddled transplanted rice out-yielded direct-seeded rice by 17% (5.71 vs 4.86 t ha⁻¹). The mechanical transplanter gave the highest mean yield (5.91 t ha⁻¹) and SYI (0.778), whereas rice planted with the manual transplanter declined by 0.49 t ha⁻¹ per decade (p = 0.019). No direct-seeded method declined significantly. In wheat, reduced tillage, strip tillage with the Turbo Seeder and zero tillage yielded 0.46–0.54 t ha⁻¹ more than conventional sowing, and strip tillage was the most stable (CV 5.2%, b = 1.00). With season-specific prices, system rice-equivalent yield fell significantly in 11 of 20 systems, but these falls disappeared at a fixed wheat:rice price ratio because they reflected a declining price ratio rather than lower grain output. The gap between the best transplanted system and zero-till rice–wheat narrowed from 1.6 to 0.4 t ha⁻¹ between the two decades. Machine-based conservation establishment sustained rice–wheat productivity over two decades, while the yield advantage of transplanting is shrinking.

title: Urbanization Doubles Future Compound Heatwave Risk in the Yangtze River Delta Urban Agglomeration Based on a Machine Learning‐Statistical Hybrid Framework
summary: Urbanization intensifies compound heatwaves (CoHot) involving concurrent hot days and nights, yet coarse‐resolution climate projections cannot resolve urban‐scale processes. Dynamical downscaling can bridge this gap but requires substantial
content: Urbanization intensifies compound heatwaves (CoHot) involving concurrent hot days and nights, yet coarse‐resolution climate projections cannot resolve urban‐scale processes. Dynamical downscaling can bridge this gap but requires substantial computing for long‐term projections. Here we introduce a novel and efficient hybrid framework combining daily‐scale stacking ensemble machine learning with monthly‐scale quantile mapping to downscale CMIP6 projections to urban resolution. Applied to China's Yangtze River Delta (YRD), a highly developed urban area, this framework improves simulation of CoHot frequency, duration, and intensity, increasing spatial correlation from −0.26–0.50 to 0.29–0.77 and reducing RMSE by 18%. High‐resolution (5‐km) projections reveal cities as evolving CoHot hotspots, where urban expansion drives shifting spatial patterns. By 2050, city centers could experience about four CoHot events and over 20 CoHot days annually, with total duration twice that in surrounding rural areas. This scalable, efficient tool aids urban heat risk assessment with broad applicability to rapidly urbanizing regions worldwide.

title: Charge-engineered nanohybrid coatings for microbial fouling resistance
summary: Microbial attachment is the gateway to biofouling and microbially influenced corrosion. Yet biocides and passive barrier coatings do not actively regulate the charged metal-microbe interface at which adhesion begins. Here we report a charge
content: Microbial attachment is the gateway to biofouling and microbially influenced corrosion. Yet biocides and passive barrier coatings do not actively regulate the charged metal-microbe interface at which adhesion begins. Here we report a charge-engineered coating, a graphene thin-film nanohybrid (gTFN) on nickel (Ni) forming an asymmetric metal-graphene-metal junction, that suppresses cell attachment through interfacial charge redistribution rather than soluble toxicity. Against the model sulfate-reducing bacterium Oleidesulfovibrio alaskensis G20, gTFN combines an impermeable graphene scaffold, an immobilized low-leaching Ag cap and a serrated topology, reducing microbial surface coverage by 98%, increasing charge-transfer resistance 47-fold and lowering corrosion current 167-fold relative to Ni. Surface-potential mapping and density functional theory reveal interfacial dipoles that pattern the surface potential, while imaging shows graphene wrinkles channeling residual attachment. Transcriptomic profiling reveals downregulation of biofilm-associated and energy-metabolism genes. These results establish interfacial charge redistribution as an active antifouling and anticorrosion mechanism for controlling microbial biointerfaces.

title: Anthropogenic warming intensified the July 2023 North China extreme rainfall event: Roles of moisture transport and convective organization
summary: In late July 2023, North China experienced a devastating extreme precipitation event, resulting in severe flooding and massive economic losses. While extreme circulation patterns, abundant moisture transport, and local topography have been
content: In late July 2023, North China experienced a devastating extreme precipitation event, resulting in severe flooding and massive economic losses. While extreme circulation patterns, abundant moisture transport, and local topography have been identified as the key drivers, the specific role of anthropogenic warming remains elusive. By comparing hindcast simulations of the actual event with a counterfactual scenario representing a climate without anthropogenic interference, we calculate that human-induced warming increased total precipitation by 7.6% and amplified the risk for extreme precipitation at the 400 mm threshold by 9.6%. We further find that anthropogenic warming enhanced water vapor transport to North China, with the largest contributions from the South China Sea and Central China. Additionally, warming facilitated the development of more organized convective systems, characterized by fewer but larger convective clusters, alongside increased precipitation intensity and spatial extent. Our findings reveal the roles of moisture transport and convective structure associated with anthropogenic warming during this extreme rainfall event, highlighting the escalating threats posed by such extremes to communities, infrastructure, and economies.

title: The Sufficiency Perspective on Climate Change Mitigation - Policy Measures towards Transformation in Germany
summary: This dissertation proposes a novel sufficiency perspective on climate change mitigation as a matter of sustainability, with a focus on Germany. Its starting point is a widespread conceptual vagueness regarding sufficiency and a lack of a co
content: This dissertation proposes a novel sufficiency perspective on climate change mitigation as a matter of sustainability, with a focus on Germany. Its starting point is a widespread conceptual vagueness regarding sufficiency and a lack of a comprehensive sufficiency perspective on sustainability issues such as climate protection, beyond individual consumption. Consequently, this dissertation examines the following research questions: How can we investigate climate change mitigation as a matter of sustainability from a comprehensive sufficiency perspective? And what can this perspective teach us about policy implementation in Germany as an example from the Global North? The general idea is that the term sufficiency is utilized by an emerging sufficiency paradigm with a particular perspective on sustainability. As a sustainability paradigm, it consists of a collection of actors (such as scientists and practitioners) with a shared view on sustainability, emphasizing the importance of certain aspects and neglecting others. Hereby, the term sufficiency is used to mark aspects of particular importance for the emerging paradigm, including certain foundational ideas (enoughness, human needs, limits and boundaries), sustainability strategies (sufficiency in a narrow sense, meaning reductions and limitations of consumption and production in the Global North; furthermore equalization and capability empowerment) and socio-economic framework conditions (particularly growth (in)dependence). Hence, investigating climate change mitigation from a sufficiency perspective means 1) understanding climate change as a matter of sustainability, threatening inter- and intragenerational justice, 2) considering the entire portfolio of sustainability strategies, 3) reflecting on the role of socio-economic framework conditions as drivers of (un)sustainability, 4) and doing this from the perspective of the emerging sufficiency paradigm, emphasizing the importance of certain aspects (enoughness, human needs, limits and boundaries, sufficiency in a narrow sense as a sustainability strategy, equalization, capability empowerment, growth (in)dependence), while reflecting on the own assumptions and limitations due to the chosen paradigmatic standpoint. The dissertation contributes to the development and application of this sufficiency perspective on climate change mitigation in Germany with three articles. Article A titled ‘Sufficiency as Relations of Enoughness’ investigates the academic debate on sufficiency and examines the connections between sufficiency and enoughness in detail. It shows that divers uses and understandings of the term sufficiency can be reconceptualized and united through relations of enoughness which embody a shared structure: ‘enough/ too much/ too little of X regarding Y’. Article B titled ‘Sustainability Strategies: What’s in a Name?’ develops a framework of sustainability strategies including and beyond the established triad of efficiency, consistency and su

title: An Economic Analysis of Fiscal Federalism
summary: This chapter reviews the economic reasons for government involvement in a mixed economy, and then, for a federal system, the allocation of the different roles between the central and state governments. With the objectives of greater nationa
content: This chapter reviews the economic reasons for government involvement in a mixed economy, and then, for a federal system, the allocation of the different roles between the central and state governments. With the objectives of greater national production and equity, government economic policy roles include establishing and monitoring property rights, correcting market failures, redistribution, macroeconomic stabilization, and collecting revenues. Economic arguments for the allocation of the general government roles between the central and state governments in a federation consider the mix of attributes of the different general policy roles. Policy attributes include simplicity, economies of scale, heterogeneity of state preferences, and supply capabilities, and opportunities for state competition. Attributes such as simplicity, nationwide public goods, and large economies of scale favour central government. State heterogeneity of preferences and costs of supply and potential benefits of competition to find and implement more effective policy choices favour allocation to the states.

title: Pecha Kucha and conventional presentations for carbon footprint awareness in health sciences students: a controlled trial
summary: Background This study evaluated the effectiveness of Pecha Kucha and conventional presentations in improving carbon footprint awareness among health sciences students. Design A three-arm randomized controlled trial. Methods The study includ
content: Background This study evaluated the effectiveness of Pecha Kucha and conventional presentations in improving carbon footprint awareness among health sciences students. Design A three-arm randomized controlled trial. Methods The study included 122 health sciences students allocated to a Pecha Kucha group ( n = 43), a conventional presentation group ( n = 40), and a control group ( n = 39). Participants in the intervention groups received a four-session carbon footprint education program over two weeks, while the control group received no intervention. Outcomes were assessed using the Carbon Footprint Scale (CFS). Data were analyzed using mixed-design ANOVA and ANCOVA. Results Post-intervention carbon footprint awareness scores were significantly higher in both the Pecha Kucha and conventional presentation groups compared with the control group ( p < 0.05). A significant Group × Time interaction indicated different patterns of change across groups over time ( p = 0.025). Improvements were particularly evident in the waste management dimension of carbon footprint awareness ( p < 0.001). No significant differences were found between the two educational methods. Conclusions Both Pecha Kucha and conventional presentations were associated with improved carbon footprint awareness compared with the control group, although a significant within-group improvement was observed only in the conventional group. No significant difference was found between the two methods, but this should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence. Pecha Kucha may still be a practical approach for sustainability education.

title: HiFi long-read metagenomics reshapes genome-resolved interpretations of activated sludge microbiome
summary: Genome-resolved metagenomics is widely used to characterize activated sludge microbiomes and infer the microbial processes underpinning system performance. However, the reliability of metabolic inferences drawn from fragmented short-read (S
content: Genome-resolved metagenomics is widely used to characterize activated sludge microbiomes and infer the microbial processes underpinning system performance. However, the reliability of metabolic inferences drawn from fragmented short-read (SR) genomes remains insufficiently examined. Using (near-)complete genomes reconstructed from HiFi long-read (LR) sequencing as references, we traced genome recovery through SR assembly and post-assembly processing. Assembly fragmentation and subsequent sequence loss during post-assembly processing compromised the recovery of high-quality genomes despite adequate sequencing depth and breadth of coverage. This incomplete recovery biased inferences regarding denitrification modularity, underestimating complete denitrifier populations and distorting the inferred balance between N2O producers and reducers. Poor recovery of nitrifier and Ca. Accumulibacter genomes, exacerbated by population microdiversity and structurally complex genomic regions, precluded reliable inferences regarding nitrification and phosphorus accumulation. Our findings caution against uncritical interpretation of SR-based microbiome-function linkages and highlight the value of incorporating HiFi LR sequencing into genome-resolved metagenomic analyses.

title: CAMELS-IND-Proj: Daily streamflow projections for 472 Peninsular Indian catchments under future climate scenarios
summary: Climate change is expected to alter streamflow patterns, with important implications for water resources management across Peninsular India. This paper presents the CAMELS-IND-Proj dataset, comprising daily streamflow projections for 472 ca
content: Climate change is expected to alter streamflow patterns, with important implications for water resources management across Peninsular India. This paper presents the CAMELS-IND-Proj dataset, comprising daily streamflow projections for 472 catchments under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways scenarios (SSP126, SSP245, SSP370, and SSP585) for the period 2015 to 2100. The data were generated using a regionally trained Long Short-Term Memory-based hydrological model driven by bias-corrected meteorological projections from 13 CMIP6 global climate models covering India. Catchment attributes from the CAMELS-IND dataset were used to represent catchment characteristics in the model. The dataset provides daily streamflow projections from multiple climate models and climate scenarios, enabling assessments of projected changes in streamflow across a wide range of hydroclimatic conditions. It can support studies of climate change impacts on water resources, flood and drought risk, reservoir planning, agricultural water management, and the design and assessment of water infrastructure. The dataset may also be used for model evaluation, uncertainty analysis, and regional hydrological studies.

title: Barriers to CCUS Deployment in India's Coal Power Sector and a Proposed Energy Pathway: A Review
summary: India’s ambition to become a developed economy by 2047 and achieve net-zero emissions by 2070 creates a structural tension between growth and decarbonization. Coal supplies 60–70% of electricity, contributes roughly half of national CO₂ emi
content: India’s ambition to become a developed economy by 2047 and achieve net-zero emissions by 2070 creates a structural tension between growth and decarbonization. Coal supplies 60–70% of electricity, contributes roughly half of national CO₂ emissions, and underpins regional economies, making rapid phase-out politically and economically challenging. This PRISMA-based systematic review of 185 peer-reviewed studies identifies four mutually reinforcing barriers to CCUS deployment in India’s coal power sector: high capture costs ($4.00–45.00 per tonne) and absent carbon pricing; regulatory gaps in storage liability and permitting; political resistance in coal-dependent states; and social concerns including low awareness and NIMBY attitudes. These constraints have limited progress to a single pilot project despite global expansion. Evidence from international experience supports a four-pillar pathway for India: accelerated deployment of renewable energy; strategic retrofitting of young supercritical plants; robust policy frameworks, including carbon pricing and subsidies; and just transition measures for coal regions.

title: Synthesizing local strategies for the water–energy–food–ecosystem nexus in Mediterranean agriculture: a systematic literature review
summary: The Mediterranean is particularly vulnerable to water–energy–food–ecosystems (WEFE) nexus challenges in agriculture. While local actors are disproportionately affected, there is limited synthesized evidence on how the problems are addressed
content: The Mediterranean is particularly vulnerable to water–energy–food–ecosystems (WEFE) nexus challenges in agriculture. While local actors are disproportionately affected, there is limited synthesized evidence on how the problems are addressed. We conducted a systematic literature review on local solution approaches to WEFE nexus issues in Mediterranean agriculture. Our findings indicate that most studies concentrate on water management, followed by sustainable farming practices. Only a few address energy use in agriculture. We show which governance measures facilitate the implementation of the local solutions, what additional conducive and hindering factors exist, and whether these solutions solve the problems.

title: An Integrated Text Mining and Content Analysis to Inform Climate‐Smart Cocoa Practices
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: Climate‐smart cocoa practices are being championed as a strategy for addressing climate‐related risks in cocoa production systems. Despite growing recognition, adoption remains uneven due to structural, contextual, and knowledge‐related con
content: Climate‐smart cocoa practices are being championed as a strategy for addressing climate‐related risks in cocoa production systems. Despite growing recognition, adoption remains uneven due to structural, contextual, and knowledge‐related constraints. This study integrates evidence from two sources: a systematic review of 60 empirical studies and the first round of a modified Delphi study completed by 14 experts from four cocoa‐producing countries. Text mining of the recommendations extracted from these studies (124 statements consolidated into 60 study‐level documents) identified exploratory themes related to economic resilience, sustainable farming practices and capacity building, climate adaptation and extension services, and agroforestry. A complementary content analysis of the experts' open‐ended responses (54 responses received of a possible 154) revealed nuanced perspectives on the urgency of adoption, local understandings of climate change, implementation challenges, resistance to change, and the role of institutional networks. While both sources converged on the importance of strengthening extension systems and economic support, experts placed greater emphasis on locally grounded experiential knowledge, which was less visible in the literature. Lexical polarity of the literature‐derived recommendations was predominantly neutral or positive and did not differ by topic or by the country of the source study. The findings demonstrate the value of integrating computational and qualitative approaches to inform context‐sensitive and actionable climate‐smart cocoa policies.

title: Historical Evolution and Evaluation of China's Aid to Nigeria's Rail System
summary: This study explored the historical evolution and effect evaluation of China's economic aid to Africa, thereby considering Nigeria in particular. The level of development can be measured on functionality of the rail system. The development p
content: This study explored the historical evolution and effect evaluation of China's economic aid to Africa, thereby considering Nigeria in particular. The level of development can be measured on functionality of the rail system. The development plan for the railway transportation system was examined employing a SWOT matrix approach. Despite the activeness of China in the railway sector in recent years, the sector was neglected and inefficient. The tracks and trains were deteriorating, and the necessary finances were never forthcoming. This study found that the country's economy depends on the modernization of the inefficient tracks and the creation of new links. It also found that despite the negative effects of rail transportation on human health and the environment (such as air and noise pollution, destruction of forests and wildlife habitat, land degradation due to soil erosion of drainage systems and geological formations associated with railway construction), railways continue to play an important role in the development of African and Nigerian economies by transporting freight and passengers at low costs and enabling the growth of mining and agriculture. It is crucial to note that, despite the increased importance of railways in the nation's growth and Chinese engagement in railway infrastructure investment, the challenges are outnumbering the benefits. Therefore, governments at all levels should promote the enabling environment that will drive more investment, security, and channel it the rail to enhance regional complementarity of trade. Nigeria must develop policies that strengthen their ability to monitor and enforce labor, safety, and environmental protections by ensuring that Chinese companies involved in the construction of railways in Africa adhere to global standards and the international labour organization's rules.

title: How to be a Good Neighbor: An Analysis of the Implementation of the EPA’s Good Neighbor Plan of Fossil Fuel Industries
summary: On March 15, 2023, the Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA") promulgated the Good Neighbor Plan in accordance with the Clean Air Act ("the CAA").' The CAA requires twenty-three "upwind" states to reduce emissions and pollution pursuant to
content: On March 15, 2023, the Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA") promulgated the Good Neighbor Plan in accordance with the Clean Air Act ("the CAA").' The CAA requires twenty-three "upwind" states to reduce emissions and pollution pursuant to the 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards ("NAAQS"), the EPA's health-based air quality standard for ground-level ozone (or "smog"). Smog is produced when sunlight mixes with pollution produced by fossil fuel industrial facilities and factories, creating precursor air emissions that ultimately generate harmful ozone pollution.
