summary: Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. However, early-stage formation of passivating oxide shells severely restricts oxygen diffusion, resulting in incomplete
content: Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. However, early-stage formation of passivating oxide shells severely restricts oxygen diffusion, resulting in incomplete oxidation and limited energy utilization. Here, we report a Ce-assisted microstructure design strategy to overcome this long-standing diffusion barrier by constructing three-dimensional oxygen-diffusion scaffolds within aluminum-based fuels through trace cerium addition. Rapidly solidified Al– x Ce powders develop an interconnected Al 11 Ce 3 network, which subdivides the Al matrix into fine domains. During heating and combustion, this Al 11 Ce 3 network is preferentially oxidized into a CeO 2- x /CeO 2 -containing scaffold before extensive Al oxidation, thereby providing continuous oxygen-transport pathways into the particle interior. As a result, Al– x Ce alloy powders exhibit shorter ignition delay, faster flame propagation, shorter combustion duration, and more complete oxidation than pure Al. This work establishes a general and scalable design principle for enhancing metal-fuel combustion through rare-earth-enabled oxygen-diffusion networks.

title: Plasmonic nano-candle platform for phase-resolved optical tracking of Pd hydrogenation with structure-sensitive readout
summary: Hydrogen detection requires platforms that are not only highly sensitive but also capable of tracking inherent gas–matter dynamics. This study reports a Λ-shaped Pd/Au nano-candle array that leverages reverse-tapered nano-slits to amplify l
content: Hydrogen detection requires platforms that are not only highly sensitive but also capable of tracking inherent gas–matter dynamics. This study reports a Λ-shaped Pd/Au nano-candle array that leverages reverse-tapered nano-slits to amplify light–matter interactions and provide dual-mode spectral readouts through extremely strong light localization and enhancement. Resonance shifts were interpreted as being dominated by dielectric variations during Pd→PdH transformation, whereas transmittance changes were used as a structure-sensitive readout to infer model-assisted effective gap evolution under ambient conditions. Comparison between the optical measurements and finite-difference time-domain simulations enabled a model-assisted interpretation of phase-dependent optical responses and effective gap evolution during Pd hydrogenation. The optimized sensing platforms with Pd/Au achieved rapid response (<5 s) and a low detection limit of 0.05% H 2 with high reversibility, outperforming the corresponding Pd-only design. Beyond hydrogen monitoring, this dual-mode nanophotonic strategy offers a broadly applicable framework for analyzing coupled optical and structural responses in functional materials, enabling new opportunities in catalytic sensing, reconfigurable meta-surfaces, and adaptive photonic devices.

title: Cold, dark, and hungry: Dynamic transcriptional regulation across eight months of brumation
summary: Long-term winter dormancy in ectotherms (brumation) defines the annual cycle of many temperate-zone reptiles, yet the transcriptional regulation that supports survival across months of cold and aphagy remains poorly understood. We generated
content: Long-term winter dormancy in ectotherms (brumation) defines the annual cycle of many temperate-zone reptiles, yet the transcriptional regulation that supports survival across months of cold and aphagy remains poorly understood. We generated time-resolved transcriptomic profiles of liver and testis from male red-sided garter snakes (Thamnophis sirtalis parietalis) at five timepoints spanning the eight-month brumation cycle: pre-brumation, early, mid-, and late brumation, and post-arousal under continued aphagy. Time-course negative-binomial regression (maSigPro) followed by gene-set enrichment analysis identified 3,710 transcripts in liver and 5,822 in testis with significant temporal expression structure organized into five overarching temporal patterns: sustained downregulation, downregulation with post-arousal recovery, sustained upregulation, brumation-specific upregulation and cyclic modulation. Liver showed coordinated upregulation of fatty acid mobilization enzymes (ATGL, FOXO1, PPARα) and gluconeogenic regulators (CREBBP, PCK1) coincident with sustained low temperatures. Additionally, low temperature transcriptional activity was suggestive of a shift toward hepatic lipid mobilization and alanine-supported gluconeogenesis. Testis showed sustained suppression of meiosis, reproduction, and DNA-metabolism gene sets that did not fully recover at arousal consistent with this species' dissociated reproductive pattern. Both tissues showed coordinated upregulation of stress-response pathways involving heat-shock proteins, and liver showed upregulation of HIF1α and a glutathione-based antioxidant defense. Interestingly, three vitellogenin transcripts and 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases associated with estradiol-favoring steroid metabolism were upregulated in male liver during late brumation, which is not expected during natural physiology in adult males. Together these data support a framework in which temperature- and prolonged aphagy-associated transcriptional programs contribute to survival of one of the longest, coldest brumations documented in a squamate.

title: Adipocyte GDI2 suppresses lipophagy to restrain adaptive thermogenesis and promotes diet-induced obesity
summary: Promoting the thermogenic remodeling of white adipose tissue (WAT) is a promising strategy to combat obesity. Lipophagy-mediated lipid droplet degradation provides free fatty acids to fuel thermogenesis in beige adipocytes, yet the regulato
content: Promoting the thermogenic remodeling of white adipose tissue (WAT) is a promising strategy to combat obesity. Lipophagy-mediated lipid droplet degradation provides free fatty acids to fuel thermogenesis in beige adipocytes, yet the regulatory mechanisms that link lipophagy to adaptive thermogenesis remain largely unknown. Here, we identify GDP dissociation inhibitor 2 (GDI2) as a previously unrecognized negative regulator of WAT browning and adaptive thermogenesis. GDI2 expression was positively correlated with BMI in humans and was upregulated in the adipose tissue of obese mice, but was downregulated by cold exposure. Adipocyte-specific deletion of Gdi2 in mice promoted cold-induced WAT browning and energy expenditure, and conferred resistance to diet-induced obesity, insulin resistance, and hepatic steatosis. Mechanistically, GDI2 acted as a molecular brake on lipophagy by inhibiting Rab7-dependent late-stage autophagosome-lysosome fusion, independent of the canonical neutral lipolysis pathway. Gdi2 deficiency releases this brake, accelerating the lipophagic degradation of LDs and thereby increasing the supply of free fatty acids. These fatty acids serve as signaling ligands to activate a PPARα-dependent thermogenic program, accompanied by coordinated upregulation of oxidative phosphorylation genes, thereby directing lipid flux toward energy dissipation. Collectively, our findings establish GDI2 as a key inhibitor of adipocyte lipophagy that restrains beige fat thermogenesis, positioning GDI2 as a potential therapeutic target to combat obesity and related metabolic disorders.

title: Innovative Microwave Foamed Egg White-Cork Composite for Enhanced Acoustic Absorption: Valorizing By-Products into Sustainable Construction Materials
summary: This study explores an innovative approach to enhancing the sound absorption properties of cork-based composites for sustainable construction applications. We developed and compared two types of composites: a conventional cork-mortar mixtur
content: This study explores an innovative approach to enhancing the sound absorption properties of cork-based composites for sustainable construction applications. We developed and compared two types of composites: a conventional cork-mortar mixture and a novel composite incorporating microwave-foamed egg white-cork composite. The foamed composite was created by subjecting a mixture of cork granules and liquid egg white to 2.45 GHz microwave radiation, resulting in a highly porous structure. This foamed composite was then embedded in a mortar mix to create the final composite. Acoustic testing revealed significant improvements in sound absorption properties for the composite containing microwave-expanded foamed egg white-cork compared to the conventional cork-mortar mixture. The enhanced performance is attributed to the increased air content and complex pore structure of the foamed composite. Mechanical and morphological tests were conducted to assess the overall material properties of both composites. Additionally, fire resistance tests demonstrated favorable results for both materials, with the foamed composite maintaining good flame-retardant properties. Our findings suggest that this innovative, easy-to-produce composite offers an effective solution for noise attenuation in building applications. The use of potential waste materials (cork by-products and eggs) in the production process further enhances the sustainability profile of this material. This research contributes to the development of eco-friendly, sustainable acoustic materials that align with circular economy principles in the construction industry. The MCEWP composite achieved sound absorption coefficients of up to 0.313 at 4000 Hz and 0.286 at 1000 Hz, with an open porosity of 33.3%, compared to 0.05 and 6.3% porosity for plain mortar, while maintaining flame resistance up to ~ 400°C without ignition. An estimated NRC-like value of 0.15 was obtained for comparative purposes.

title: Large electrocaloric effects in unannealed multilayer capacitors of partially ordered lead scandium tantalate
summary: Multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 with good B-site cation order ( S 111 ~ 0.9-0.96) are driven by supercritical fields of 15.8 V μm −1 in prototype coolers, such that large electrocaloric effects arise over a wide range of temper
content: Multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 with good B-site cation order ( S 111 ~ 0.9-0.96) are driven by supercritical fields of 15.8 V μm −1 in prototype coolers, such that large electrocaloric effects arise over a wide range of temperatures and peak to give thermocouple-measured temperature jumps of |∆ T j | ~ 4.0 K near room temperature. However, the high degree of B-site order requires an energetically expensive 42-day high-temperature anneal that would be economically expensive and environmentally damaging in mass production. Here we report that the performance reduction (4.0 K → 3.1 K) for unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 with partial B-site order ( S 111 ~ 0.6) is surprisingly small because reduced latent heat is mitigated by high-field electrocaloric effects in the induced ferroelectric phase. Eliminating the anneal without unduly compromising performance should render unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 attractive for applications.

title: Dry Surface Decontamination of Nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and Blister (HD) Chemical Warfare Agents Using TiO2/CeO2 Nanosorbents
summary: Dry surface decontamination is a highly practical approach for mitigating chemical warfare agent (CWA) threats without generating liquid waste. Herein, we systematically investigate the dry decontamination performance of nanoscale TiO2, CeO
content: Dry surface decontamination is a highly practical approach for mitigating chemical warfare agent (CWA) threats without generating liquid waste. Herein, we systematically investigate the dry decontamination performance of nanoscale TiO2, CeO2, and mixed TiO2/CeO2 (TiCe) sorbents against nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and blister (HD) agents. Materials characterization confirms that mixing Ti and Ce shifts the microstructure into a highly open, mesoporous network, significantly expanding the total pore volume to 1.01 cm3/g. In dry batch experiments, all nanosorbents achieved rapid, complete depletion of parent extractable G-agents within 10 min, while the Novichok agent A-234 was reduced to <4% within 10 min, exhibiting comparable performance under both ambient daylight and complete darkness. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first demonstration of fully dry Novichok detoxification using metal oxide-based sorbents. Blister agent HD underwent slower degradation, achieving near-complete depletion (with <3% residual) after 480 min. GC-MS analysis confirmed that depletion is driven by safe hydrolytic pathways yielding low-toxicity derivatives, without hazardous oxidation byproducts. When applied to contaminated ceramic tiles, the dry powders successfully transferred and removed all parent CWAs to levels undetectable by GC-FID and GC-MS in both immediate and aged scenarios, except for A-234 on CeO2 (3.7% residue). These findings demonstrate that practical dry surface decontamination is governed by rapid mechanical transfer followed by intra-sorbent degradation. Furthermore, the successful up-scaling of the nanoporous TiO2 synthesis to a kilo-lab scale highlights the straightforward scalability of these materials for real-world applications on delicate equipment.

title: Integrated CO2-EOR and Post-EOR Storage in a Mature Waterflooded UKCS Sandstone Reservoir: Recovery-Retention-Pressure Trade-offs from Compositional Simulation
summary: This study evaluates miscible CO2-enhanced oil recovery, post-EOR CO2 storage, and long-term postinjection behavior in a mature offshore sandstone reservoir using compositional simulation. A PVT-tuned Peng–Robinson model gave a pure-CO2 min
content: This study evaluates miscible CO2-enhanced oil recovery, post-EOR CO2 storage, and long-term postinjection behavior in a mature offshore sandstone reservoir using compositional simulation. A PVT-tuned Peng–Robinson model gave a pure-CO2 minimum miscibility pressure of 2,528 psia by the multiple-mixing-cell method, and reservoir pressure remained above this value in all CO2-EOR cases. Five strategies (continuous CO2; fixed and tapered water-alternating-gas (WAG); a CO2 slug followed by WAG; and simultaneous water-and-gas injection) were compared from a common 2027 reference state. A 36-month CO2 slug followed by alternating six-month CO2 and six-month water periods was preferred: it produced 69.61 MMstb (8.64% of stock-tank oil initially in place), 50.06 MMstb more than continued waterflooding, and retained 9.86 of 21.42 Mt injected CO2 (46.0%). Post-EOR storage at 140 MMscf/d for 15 years, selected from three rate cases because injectivity rather than nominal rate controlled the stored mass, raised the total retained CO2 to 44.81 Mt (79.5% of 56.37 Mt injected); field-average pressure then declined from 6,955 to 6,385 psia over 100 years of shut-in monitoring. Plume expansion was limited, CO2 partitioned progressively into the oleic and aqueous phases, and mobile gas-phase CO2 decreased. The results show that a single mature, heavily waterflooded UKCS reservoir can deliver 6.2 percentage points of additional recovery and retain close to 45 Mt CO2 within its estimated operating-pressure envelope, providing a quantified reservoir-engineering basis for repurposing late-life North Sea oil fields as CO2 storage sites. Geomechanical, well-integrity, surface-processing, economic and lifecycle assessments are required before implementation.

title: A Review of Activated Carbon-Based Materials and Their Performance Tipping Points for Application in CO2 Capture with Future Outlook
summary: Carbon capture technologies have been increasingly demanded to achieve the commitments in the Paris Agreement of capturing 10 Gt CO2 per year. This review examines the many facets of activated carbons for CO2 capture applications. Activated
content: Carbon capture technologies have been increasingly demanded to achieve the commitments in the Paris Agreement of capturing 10 Gt CO2 per year. This review examines the many facets of activated carbons for CO2 capture applications. Activated carbons are popular research materials for CO2 capture applications because of their high surface area, tunable surface characteristics, and widely available feedstocks. Additionally, activated carbon can be deployed at low temperatures and pressures in fixed bed applications. The analysis reveals a range of “tipping points” that we define as the optimal parameters to maximize performance. The first tipping point is that the optimal average pore size for amine-supported carbons is 10 nm, including cyclic stability. Amine-supported carbons with average pores <2 nm perform poorly in all CO2 benchmarking criteria, whereas materials with average pore sizes >10 nm exhibit limited cyclic stability. Amine-supported carbons also exhibit a tipping point with respect to regeneration temperature. As regeneration temperature exceeds 315 K, the net CO2 capacity retention declines by as much as 12%. Tipping points are also observed in relation to adsorption temperature and amine weight loading. For the best-performing combinations of amines supported on mesoporous carbon, the optimum CO2 adsorption temperature is between 70 and 80 °C. An amine weight loading of 60–75% was found to be optimum for mesoporous carbon and results in a high CO2 uptake of up to 5.0 mmol/g. For caustic-impregnated carbons, it is found that increasing the CO2 adsorption temperature always results in a net decrease in CO2 capacity. Carbons impregnated with caustics exhibit the best performance when impregnated with 20–30% by weight of a caustic chemical. A final key observation on “performance tipping points” is that they are closely related to the specific combination of support and surface chemistry being used. Each unique combination exhibits its own unique tipping point characteristics. However, there remain trends that can be extracted from these behaviors that allow us to bracket ideal ranges for certain performance characteristics.

title: A Case Study of Energy-Efficient Industrial Warehousing with Digital Tools
summary: In the domain of industry warehousing, automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS) consist of warehouse racks and stacker cranes that operate in a cartesian coordinate system to achieve a desired product flow. These systems maximize thei
content: In the domain of industry warehousing, automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS) consist of warehouse racks and stacker cranes that operate in a cartesian coordinate system to achieve a desired product flow. These systems maximize their throughput when the devices are operated at their maximum velocity and acceleration constraints. From a product lifecycle management viewpoint, operations with adaptive parameters could reduce energy consumption while meeting temporal constraints. In this paper, we investigate the applicability of two AI tools for sustainable lifecycle management of a stacker crane. We formulate parts of the lifecycle management as a data and AI problem. We divide warehouse management to two categories: Resource allocation and operation optimization. Finally, we perform empirical validation through a warehouse management simulation environment. Our findings benefit lifecycle management strategies and operations of ASRS, contributing to more sustainable industry practices.

title: Interstitial proton buffering enables decoupled transfer dynamics for acidic wastewater decontamination
summary: The remediation of aggressive acidic wastewater is fundamentally hindered by the coupled proton-release/electron-transfer barrier that suppresses high-valent metal-oxo chemistry in conventional advanced oxidation processes. Here we report a
content: The remediation of aggressive acidic wastewater is fundamentally hindered by the coupled proton-release/electron-transfer barrier that suppresses high-valent metal-oxo chemistry in conventional advanced oxidation processes. Here we report an interstitial proton-buffering strategy in which boron is incorporated into a cobalt-manganese phosphide lattice, guiding self-limited reconstruction into a stable oxyhydroxide interface. The interstitial B-regulated interface acts as a local Brønsted-base proton buffer, establishing a proton-acceptor–electron-donor mechanism that enables decoupled proton-electron transfer, as supported by a super-Nernstian E 1/2 -pH response. This pathway stabilizes Co IV -oxo formation and drives complete imidacloprid degradation within 3 min in simulated water. In 80 h continuous-flow treatment of electroplating acid-pickling wastewater at pH 0.85, the system retains 49.48% total organic carbon reduction. These results identify interstitial proton buffering as a route to sustain high-valent oxidation chemistry in strongly acidic water matrices.

title: Rapid fabrication of customizable laser-induced graphene microelectrode arrays
summary: Laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrodes fabricated by CO2 laser scribing have been widely utilized in bioelectronic and sensing applications due to their compatibility with flexible substrates and scalable, cleanroom-free production. The di
content: Laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrodes fabricated by CO2 laser scribing have been widely utilized in bioelectronic and sensing applications due to their compatibility with flexible substrates and scalable, cleanroom-free production. The digitally programmable nature of this process enables rapid and customizable electrode patterning. However, the relatively large spot size of the CO2 laser limits fabrication resolution and prevents device miniaturization. Here, we report a novel dual-laser approach for the direct writing of high-resolution, multiplexed, and integrated LIG microelectrode arrays with tunable structural and electrochemical properties. LIG electrodes were fabricated by CO2 laser scribing of flexible polyimide (PI) films. Optimization of the laser power and scribing speed generated LIG electrode tracks with a low sheet resistance (19.2 ± 0.30 Ω sq−1). Raman spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy confirmed the formation of a three-dimensional, porous graphene-like structure. Device miniaturization was achieved through femtosecond laser micromachining of the PI adhesive insulation layer, producing microelectrode openings with diameters of 20–60 μm. Cyclic voltammetry, differential pulse voltammetry, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) demonstrated a size-dependent enhancement in electrochemical performance. The 30 μm LIG microelectrodes exhibited low electrode-to-electrode and device-to-device variability in 1 kHz impedance (coefficients of variation = 3.13–6.17% and 2.52%, respectively), while maintaining their mechanical integrity, electrical conductivity, and electrochemical performance even after 100 bending cycles at 150° (5.31% ± 2.64% increase in 1 kHz impedance). The rapid, mask-free fabrication of customizable LIG microelectrode arrays highlights the potential of this CO2/fs-laser processing strategy for developing portable, wearable, and disposable electrochemical devices.

title: Flexible Data Access Mechanisms for IoT Ecosystems: From Content-Based Addressing to LLM-Driven Data Acquisition
summary: The continuous development and integration of public and private Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures require flexible and scalable data access mechanisms that ensure seamless access to IoT data regardless of its source of physical addr
content: The continuous development and integration of public and private Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures require flexible and scalable data access mechanisms that ensure seamless access to IoT data regardless of its source of physical address. Traditionally, retrieving data from different physical sources requires rigid, topology-dependent protocols and high technical skills; this may limit accessibility for a wider range of end-users.Content-Based Addressing (CBA) accesses data based on its attributes or content rather than its network location. Users need an intuitive mechanism to extract IoT values from multiple sources (e.g. public and private sources), removing the need for technical database query knowledge. In a similar way to web search (e.g. Google), users ask questions in natural language based on content, location and time without direct reference to the physical location of the IoT devices that provide the necessary information. This paper proposes a novel, hybrid framework for flexible IoT data access that combines CBA with a Large Language Model (LLM)-based conversational interface. The architecture is built on two core pillars: a Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) layer, coupled with a device registry, that unifies heterogeneous data sources, public APIs and private edge devices, into a single content-addressed store secured by a granular Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) mechanism. The second pillar is a Natural Language Query Engine that translates chat-based interrogations into executable system queries.An adaptive imputation service maintains data completeness by detecting missing sensor readings, predicting replacement values, and reconciling predictions when delayed measurements arrive. Together, the framework enables an intuitive experience for IoT data exploration with no technical training needed.

title: Engineering Cas Activity for Clinically Deployable CRISPR Diagnostics
summary: CRISPR-based diagnostics have evolved from proof-of-concept nucleic acid assays to increasingly integrated platforms for streamlined canonical/non-canonical single or multiplex target detection with digital quantification. Here we review th
content: CRISPR-based diagnostics have evolved from proof-of-concept nucleic acid assays to increasingly integrated platforms for streamlined canonical/non-canonical single or multiplex target detection with digital quantification. Here we review these advances according to their ability to regulate Cas activity and dissect key checkpoints of CRISPR activation. We also organize advanced CRISPR-based diagnostic systems by their use of four regulatory dimensions: activation-threshold control, reaction compatibility and temporal coordination, spatial organization, and catalytic signal transduction. This framework reveals common mechanisms and limitations underlying current engineering strategies and provides a conceptual foundation for predictable, standardizable, and clinically translatable Cas activity engineering.

title: Biomass-to-hard carbon for sodium-ion batteries: synthesis strategies, sodium storage mechanisms, and structure–performance relationships
summary: . Among the various anode candidates, biomass-derived hard carbon (BHC) has attracted significant attention owing to its sustainable origin, tunable microstructure, environmental compatibility, and favorable electrochemical properties. This
content: . Among the various anode candidates, biomass-derived hard carbon (BHC) has attracted significant attention owing to its sustainable origin, tunable microstructure, environmental compatibility, and favorable electrochemical properties. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in BHC anodes for SIBs, with particular emphasis on synthesis strategies, precursor engineering, structural characteristics, sodium-storage mechanisms, and electrochemical performance relationships. Different preparation approaches, including direct pyrolysis, activation methods, heteroatom doping, surface engineering, and multi-step carbonization, are critically discussed in relation to their influence on interlayer spacing, porosity, defect density, graphitization degree, and solid electrolyte interphase formation. The role of diverse biomass precursors such as agricultural residues, lignocellulosic materials, algae, and biopolymers is also analyzed to establish structure-property correlations. Furthermore, the review highlights the sodium-storage mechanisms in BHC, including adsorption, intercalation, and pore-filling processes, together with the effects of pore architecture and heteroatom functionalities on ion transport and storage behavior. Current limitations, including low initial coulombic efficiency, structural heterogeneity, ash-related impurities, and scalability challenges, are systematically evaluated alongside recent optimization strategies involving nano-engineering, composite formation, and interface regulation. Overall, biomass-derived hard carbon represents a sustainable and technically viable anode material for next-generation sodium-ion batteries, although further advances in precursor standardization, mechanistic understanding, and scalable manufacturing are required to accelerate practical commercialization.

title: GDL-free multi-phase flow reactors enable stable intermittent CO2 electrolysis
summary: Gas diffusion electrodes (GDE) offer an excellent interface for intensifying mass transfer for fundamental investigations and industrial CO2 electroreduction; however, the operational GDE stability remains a major limitation. GDE flooding,
content: Gas diffusion electrodes (GDE) offer an excellent interface for intensifying mass transfer for fundamental investigations and industrial CO2 electroreduction; however, the operational GDE stability remains a major limitation. GDE flooding, salt precipitation, and catalyst restructuring can worsen under intermittent renewable operation. Here we present a multi-phase flow reactor that controls the reaction microenvironment through flow regimes and eliminates the need for a GDE. Using an optically accessible cell and operando bubble tracking, we studied slug and annular flow over silver for CO2-to-CO conversion. Both flows enhance CO2 transport over single-phase flow (~2x and ~3x peak iCO). We identified boundary-layer renewal, not film thickness, as the governing mechanism, establishing flow velocity and renewal rate as key design levers. The reactor tolerates repeated shutdown and restart, recovering voltage and FE with minimal reconditioning across five days. This study establishes multi-phase flow as a stable flow architecture with guiding design principles for intermittent CO2 electroreduction.

title: Multi-Scale Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Reduced-Order Modeling (ROM) of Metal Membrane Modules for Blue Hydrogen Production and Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS)
summary: Palladium and its alloys are known to enable selective diffusion of hydrogen. This work builds on this property and presents a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling study for the design of a metal-membrane blue-hydrogen separation uni
content: Palladium and its alloys are known to enable selective diffusion of hydrogen. This work builds on this property and presents a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling study for the design of a metal-membrane blue-hydrogen separation unit taking the form of a baffled shell-and-tube mass exchanger. The goal is to maximize the separated blue hydrogen from shifted syngas (syngas subject to a water–gas shift reaction). This separation has two benefits: First, the separated blue hydrogen can be used as fuel. Second, the remaining concentrated carbon dioxide can be captured and either stored permanently rather than emitted to the atmosphere or sold commercially. Thus, the separation unit not only yields a valuable hydrogen commodity but also facilitates carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS). The selective mass transfer process is modeled macroscopically using Sieverts’ law with an Arrhenius-type expression for the permeability. The driving force is the difference in the square root of the hydrogen’s partial pressure between the retentate stream and the permeate stream. We utilize multiple computational modeling tools (mainly the finite volume software Ansys Fluent) to perform three-dimensional RANS (Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes) CFD simulations. These simulations predict the fluid flow and the selective mass transfer process through a palladium metal membrane under different geometric and operational conditions. Additional axisymmetric Ansys Fluent simulations are also performed for experimental test cases having a simpler tubular metal-membrane module. We also apply a system-level, reduced-order model (ROM) to explore off-design operating points for the selective mass transfer process. Our results show that the (zero-dimensional) modeling can substitute the sophisticated three-dimensional CFD modeling if only system-level, scalar performance metrics are sought. The current work is particularly aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy).

title: QM/MM Simulations Reveal Differences in Hydrolysis Mechanisms of Ertapenem and Faropenem in L1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Leading to Different Product Binding Modes
summary: L1, a class B3 metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades β-lactamase inhibitors, both clinically available and those in late-stage trials targeting other MBLs. D
content: L1, a class B3 metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades β-lactamase inhibitors, both clinically available and those in late-stage trials targeting other MBLs. Detailed understanding of the L1 mechanism is necessary to design effective inhibitors. Building on our previous quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) study of L1catalyzed hydrolysis of the penem antibiotic faropenem, we here investigate hydrolysis of a 1β-methyl carbapenem (ertapenem) using MM and enhanced sampling QM/MM MD simulations at the DFTB3 level, comparing the two mechanisms to understand the distinct product binding modes observed crystallographically. The geometry of the transition state for the first, amide bond cleavage, reaction step is similar for both substrates. However, differences are apparent in the subsequent proton transfer step, corresponding to the different binding modes observed crystallographically for the respective products. For faropenem, a bulk water molecule enters the active site, yielding the (2S )-imine-∆1 product via rotation about the C5–C6 bond and protonation at position C2. For ertapenem, the metal-bridging hydroxide is the proton source, and the equivalent rotation is associated with a relatively high barrier. Instead, the more favorable rotation of the C6-carboxyl enables protonation at C2, yielding the (2S )-imine-∆1 product in a distinct binding mode. Long-timescale MM MD simulations indicate rapid dissociation of the ertapenem-derived imine, compared to the faropenem-derived species, from the L1 active site, offering insight into the relative stability of these binding modes. These data reveal how carbapenem and MBL structure influence hydrolysis pathways, and may inform rational MBL inhibitor design.

title: Tear-Down Analysis and Performance of Large Commercial Hard Carbon/NFM Sodium-Ion Batteries
summary: Na-ion batteries with high technology readiness level recently became available. However, the actual low temperature and fast-charging performance of such cells is largely undocumented. In this work, we critically evaluate the performance o
content: Na-ion batteries with high technology readiness level recently became available. However, the actual low temperature and fast-charging performance of such cells is largely undocumented. In this work, we critically evaluate the performance of five types of commercially available Na-ion cells (1.3 Ah-18650, 2 Ah-21700, 10 Ah-cylindrical, 20 Ah-cylindrical, 20 Ah-prismatic) with hard carbon || Na x Ni 1− y − z Fe y Mn z O 2 chemistries. We determine the electrode chemistry and cell design by tear-down analysis as well as production quality aspects via X-ray computed tomography and draw conclusions on drop-in capability in cell production. The behavior of the cathodes in presence of water is tested regarding detachment from the collector foil, Na + /H + ion exchange, pH rise, and H 2 gas evolution. The cell performance is assessed by charge and discharge rate capability tests within the manufacturer’s specification at ambient temperatures of 25 °C and 0 °C. Additionally, cyclic aging of the 20 Ah-prismatic cells was tested. The specific energy and impedance of the Na-ion cells are compared with typical values of Li-ion cells and are rationalized with the support of cell design simulations. A comparison of the historical capacity evolution of 18650 Li-ion cells reveals that Na-ion cells with hard carbon || Na x Ni 1− y −z Fe y Mn z O 2 chemistries currently have capacities similar to those of Li-ion cells from the year 1997.

title: A single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of oocytes and granulosa cells during postnatal folliculogenesis in dairy goats
summary: Early postnatal ovarian development is essential for establishment of the ovarian reserve and female reproductive capacity in mammals. A systematic analysis of the transcriptional programs associated with oocytes and granulosa cells (GCs) f
content: Early postnatal ovarian development is essential for establishment of the ovarian reserve and female reproductive capacity in mammals. A systematic analysis of the transcriptional programs associated with oocytes and granulosa cells (GCs) fate transitions during early folliculogenesis is essential for advancing reproductive biology in dairy goats. Herein, ovarian samples were collected at days 4, 20, and 60, capturing the progression from primordial follicles to Graafian follicles. The final dataset encompasses 90,770 cells, categorized into six major cell types with distinct transcriptional signatures. Specifically, this resource captures the transcriptomic states of four oocyte subtypes and eight GC subtypes, providing high-resolution profiles of sequential germline, meiotic, and paracrine programs, as well as GC maturation trajectories. Furthermore, the dataset contains computationally inferred ligand-receptor interactions and transcription factor regulon activities associated with follicle development. These data provide a valuable resource for investigating the cellular dynamics and putative regulatory networks associated with mammalian folliculogenesis, offering a foundation for future studies on ovarian reserve establishment, oocyte-GC coordination, and the improvement of reproductive efficiency in livestock.

title: Multiple Climate risk shocks and the pharmaceutical manufacturing industry in China: evidence from a joint impulse response function
summary: Introduction Climate risk affects industrial production through multiple indicators simultaneously, and these indicators are interrelated. Co-movement should not be treated as a nuisance to be averaged away, because the standard toolkit tra
content: Introduction Climate risk affects industrial production through multiple indicators simultaneously, and these indicators are interrelated. Co-movement should not be treated as a nuisance to be averaged away, because the standard toolkit traces one shock at a time and therefore cannot explain the effects of a concerted move. Methods This study estimates the joint dynamic response of Chinese pharmaceutical manufacturing value added to simultaneous one-standard-deviation moves in climate policy uncertainty, negative climate sentiment, and positive climate sentiment, using a vector autoregression (VAR) from 2015M03 to 2025M12 and a joint impulse response function. Results The joint response is positive, reaching 0.92 percentage points 3 months after the shock and accumulating to 7.77 percentage points over 12 months. Summing up the three separate generalized impulse responses yields 7.47 percentage points, so the additive calculation understates the joint cumulative response by 0.30 percentage points. The response is also specific to pharmaceutical manufacturing: the same shock leaves the manufacturing industry's median close to zero and with the opposite sign beyond the second month. Discussion Climate information should therefore be monitored as a package rather than indicator by indicator, because the correlations among indicators determine the magnitude of the sectoral response.

title: Achieving Net-zero Operational Energy in High-rise Residential Buildings: A Deep Bioclimatic Design Case Study of the PHANTOM Eco-tower in Miami
source: International Journal of Architectural Engineering Technology
summary: This study presents an integrated design process for achieving high-performance sustainable skyscrapers through Deep Bioclimatic Design. In this study, Deep Bioclimatic Design is defined as an architectural approach capable of enabling buil
content: This study presents an integrated design process for achieving high-performance sustainable skyscrapers through Deep Bioclimatic Design. In this study, Deep Bioclimatic Design is defined as an architectural approach capable of enabling buildings to maintain adequate indoor thermal conditions through passive and climate-responsive strategies, without relying on conventional heating or air-conditioning systems. Furthermore, the additional construction cost of a Deep Bioclimatic Design building is, at most, equivalent to the cost of the conventional heating and air-conditioning systems that it is designed to eliminate. Under appropriate climatic conditions, its application has the potential to substantially reduce operational energy demand, while avoiding substantial additional construction costs. To maximize overall sustainability performance, the study incorporates CEDES, a Green Building Rating System (GBRS) specifically developed to provide a comprehensive assessment of environmental, energy, economic, and occupant-related performance. Previous comparative analyses indicate that CEDES can provide a more effective assessment than currently established GBRSs. The proposed design methodology is applied to the PHANTOM Eco-tower, a skyscraper project developed for Miami, USA. The analysis estimates that the proposed design could reduce operational energy consumption by approximately 57% relative to the selected high-performance multifamily residential benchmark, while eliminating the need for conventional air-conditioning. The case study illustrates how the systematic integration of deep bioclimatic strategies, energy-efficiency measures, and comprehensive sustainability assessment can substantially improve the projected environmental performance of high-rise buildings. These results support the potential of Deep Bioclimatic Design as an effective approach for developing next-generation sustainable skyscrapers while maintaining economic feasibility.

title: A performance-centric progress report on memristor technology
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Memristors have emerged as a promising technology for in-memory and neuromorphic computing, offering a route around the von Neumann bottleneck. As the field diversifies across material systems, the question has shifted from whether a device
content: Memristors have emerged as a promising technology for in-memory and neuromorphic computing, offering a route around the von Neumann bottleneck. As the field diversifies across material systems, the question has shifted from whether a device can switch to how well, how reliably and how efficiently each kind does so. After a brief account of the memristor’s history and the controversies surrounding it, this performance-centric review surveys the landscape of memristor technology, tracing progress in seven categories of resistive-switching material: four defined by composition or structure (oxides, organics, 2D materials and perovskites) and three by switching mechanism (phase-change, ferroelectric and spintronic). The categories are evaluated against a comprehensive set of figures of merit (FoMs) spanning electrical switching, reliability, scalability and synaptic operation. Of these, five key FoMs and the switching and transport mechanisms are compiled, where reported, for 223 devices, with statistical distributions presented for each category so that typical device performance can be read against the best achieved. The remaining FoMs, including the neuromorphic ones, are discussed where reported. The analyses provide a comparative view across categories, highlight trade-offs within them, and relate performance to intrinsic material properties and underlying physical mechanisms. Optoelectronic operation and other notable advances are also covered, and the readiness of each category for industrial use is assessed. The result is a quantitative cross-category reference that lets researchers orient themselves and benchmark new devices.

title: Sustainable low-carbon concrete evaluation through electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and data-driven modeling
summary: The research paper examines the performance of a low-clinker blended binder system including calcite, bentonite and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) in M30 grade concrete. The main aim of the research is to explore the effect of
content: The research paper examines the performance of a low-clinker blended binder system including calcite, bentonite and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) in M30 grade concrete. The main aim of the research is to explore the effect of a combination of calcite, bentonite, and ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS) on the strength and durability properties of M 30 grade of concrete. The cement content was set at 50% with all mixes. A combination of calcite and bentonite, in equal proportions, was used to replace cement at levels of 0%, 5%, 10%, and 15%. The GGBS content was varied to 50%, 45%, 40% and 35% keeping a constant water to cement ratio of 0.45. This study will include an investigation into the fresh concrete properties such as slump and compaction factor, the chemical and mechanical properties, with and without CO 2 sequestration. Moreover, microstructural properties have been taken as a subject of X-Ray Diffraction (XRD). The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and the measurement of alternating current (AC) conductivity is further used to analyze the pore structure of the concrete. Autoregressive and tabular prior data fitting machine learning models were used to predict compressive, split tensile, and flexural strength using only experimental mechanical strength dataset. The models were highly accurate in the testing data with the highest results observed on compressive strength with the use of autoregressive model (R² = 0.9688), split tensile strength with the use of tabular fitting (R 2 = 0.9748) and flexural strength with the use of the autoregressive model (R 2 = 0.9657). These findings prove the possibility of the data-driven method to optimize concrete mix design and improve the sustainability performance. The designed blended binder system is believed to lower the embodied CO 2 emission by about 35–40% relative to traditional M 30 concrete, which is consistent with decarbonization of the world and a sustainable infrastructure objective.

title: The Problem of Speed and Scale in Green Transitions: The Failure of Northvolt and the European Battery Industry
summary: This article examines the rise and fall of Northvolt, which pursued an unprecedented strategy of rapid industrial scaling in Europe’s emerging electric vehicle battery industry. Hailed by European policymakers as a leading example of Europe
content: This article examines the rise and fall of Northvolt, which pursued an unprecedented strategy of rapid industrial scaling in Europe’s emerging electric vehicle battery industry. Hailed by European policymakers as a leading example of Europe’s effort to establish strategic autonomy in lithium-ion battery production, Northvolt sought to challenge an industry long dominated by East Asian firms. Its bankruptcy in 2025 represented a major setback to these ambitions. Situating Northvolt within the broader history of European battery initiatives since 2006, the article traces the company’s development from its founding in 2016 to its bankruptcy in 2025. Drawing on published and unpublished sources and oral history interviews, we examine why Northvolt emerged when it did, why it pursued a strategy of rapid industrial scaling and why it ultimately failed. We argue that Northvolt’s trajectory reveals a fundamental tension between the speed and scale required to compete with established Asian producers and the time needed to develop the technological and organizational capabilities for large-scale manufacturing. Northvolt’s financing model, combining private equity, customer contracts and publicly de-risked loans enabled exceptionally rapid expansion but also generated commitments and pressures to scale production before industrial capabilities had matured. These tensions were compounded by the institutional conditions of European industrial policy and the limited manufacturing experience within Europe’s emerging battery eco-system.

title: Integrating Transboundary Climate Risks into Local Agricultural Adaptation: Evidence from Norway’s Livestock Sector
summary: Global food systems are increasingly exposed to transboundary climate risks (TCRs), yet these risks fall between two stools: omitted from national agricultural policies and overlooked in municipal climate change adaptation planning. Though
content: Global food systems are increasingly exposed to transboundary climate risks (TCRs), yet these risks fall between two stools: omitted from national agricultural policies and overlooked in municipal climate change adaptation planning. Though a qualitative case study in Western Norway, this study explores how incorporating TCRs, specifically linked to imported soybean feed, reshapes climate risk perceptions and discourses, and its potential governance implications for Norway. Drawing on stakeholder interviews, workshops, and a co-production approach, we develop an integrated climate risk framework that links TCRs with physical climate risks and transition risks. Our findings reveal that TCRs resonate with local actors but are difficult to disentangle from broader socio-economic pressures. Introducing TCRs shifts climate discourse from a narrow focus on local hazards and mitigation toward a systemic understanding of global interdependencies. We identify a risk ownership gap in which local actors bear the material consequences of global disruptions while lacking the authority and institutional support to adapt proactively, rendering TCRs a local vulnerability factor. Crucially, incorporating TCRs reveals the potential to reframe grass-based livestock production systems from climate liabilities to resilience assets, emphasizing the strategic adaptive value of local resource use. However, integrating TCRs exposes significant policy tensions and maladaptation risks, particularly between reducing import reliance and managing both local climate hazards and carbon footprint. Because climate risks are experienced locally while authority to address their underlying causes resides elsewhere, effective adaptation requires alignment of national agricultural, climate change mitigation, and adaptation policies to support resilient food systems.

title: Dynamic assessment of boundary lubrication film thickness using contact resistance techniques and its application in complex operating conditions
summary: To enable online, quantitative monitoring of boundary lubricating film thickness in mechanical equipment under complex conditions, the contact resistance method was used for dynamic measurement, calibration, and application of lubricating f
content: To enable online, quantitative monitoring of boundary lubricating film thickness in mechanical equipment under complex conditions, the contact resistance method was used for dynamic measurement, calibration, and application of lubricating film thickness. A contact resistance measurement system was developed for steel ball-steel disc point contact. Spectrum analysis, circuit design optimization, and filtering technology showed a significant decrease in the interference signals between the servo driver and the wires. The standard deviation of zero-value resistance measurement dropped to 0.087 Ω, improving the signal-to-noise ratio and contact resistance measurement resolution, resulting in an optimal film thickness measurement resolution of 7.3 nm. Contact resistance measurements were performed using PAO lubricating oils with different viscosities (60.09 mm²/s to 648.86 mm²/s) under different loads (0.5 GPa to 0.9 GPa) and rolling speeds (2 mm/s to 120 mm/s). Optical interferometry measurements were employed to establish a mathematical model to map the dynamic contact resistance to the film thickness. The model yielded a fitting R² of 0.96 and a standard deviation of 2.33 nm. The self-developed system and mathematical model were employed to assess the film-forming characteristics of the steel-steel point-contact oil-lubrication interface during low-speed reciprocating motion and continuous rotation with starved oil. With its high measurement accuracy, this system effectively captured the point of reversal in reciprocating motion. Even at zero speed, the central film thickness in the contact area remained at 8 nm, attributed to transient confinement of the lubricating oil. Moreover, under starved conditions, continuous contact resistance monitoring reliably tracked the transition from elastohydrodynamic lubrication (~60 nm) to boundary lubrication (~20 nm). This work offers valuable insights for advancing the contact resistance method from qualitative laboratory analysis to quantitative engineering applications.

title: Visible light-responsive green synthesized Chromium-bismuth mixed ferrites for organic pollutant remediation and hydrogen generation
summary: Water is necessary to support all forms of life on Earth. However, the ongoing contamination of water bodies by anthropogenic activities poses an emerging threat to life. Therefore, the development of efficient photocatalysts for pollutant
content: Water is necessary to support all forms of life on Earth. However, the ongoing contamination of water bodies by anthropogenic activities poses an emerging threat to life. Therefore, the development of efficient photocatalysts for pollutant degradation is a widely studied approach. In addition to water pollution, air pollution from burning fossil fuels is also damaging the environment. The quest for alternative, environmentally friendly fuels is also being highly explored. To tackle these issues, the eco-friendly synthesis of chromium-doped bismuth ferrite (Cr/BFO) NPs at 1.25-10% doping of Cr using Brassica oleracea (stalk peel) as a capping agent is reported here. These Cr/BFO NPs were analyzed by UV-Vis, FTIR, PXRD, SEM, EDX, BET, and XPS. Cr/BFO NCs were assessed for their potential applications in water purification and energy generation. The maximum degradation efficiency of 95% was obtained for 5% Cr/BFO NPs, with a corresponding rate constant (k) of 3.39 × 10 -2 min -1 . In the Hydrogen evolution activity, 5% Cr/BFO NPs demonstrated remarkable Formic acid dehydrogenation ability with a TOF of 1509.81 h -1 and an activation energy of +39.49 kJ/mol. These multifaceted applications of highly stable 5% Cr/BFO NPs demonstrated the importance and practicability of the synthesized materials for large-scale applications.

title: AI-Driven Textile Waste Classification and Circular Recovery: A Survey of Computer Vision, Recycling and Policy Literature and a Proposed Platform Architecture
summary: The textile industry and others that use it (such as the retail sector and after-use) produce large amounts of waste at each phase of the value chain, with the majority of this waste going to landfill or incineration. The motives are not my
content: The textile industry and others that use it (such as the retail sector and after-use) produce large amounts of waste at each phase of the value chain, with the majority of this waste going to landfill or incineration. The motives are not mysterious but practical: fibre composition is not usually apparent to the naked eye of the garment, sorting is still predominantly manual, and the manual methods used for the process are cumbersome and inefficient, and presently do not work with blended, contaminated or dark coloured fabrics. This paper summarizes the conclusions of 24 recent studies in automated identification and traceability, AI-based and sensor-based fibre classification, chemical- and thermo-chemical-recycling, value-added material recovery, methodology for assessing sustainability of recycling and policy for a circular economy and puts them together in a set of research gaps. We then developed a Textile Waste Intelligence Platform, an AI-based system that will help classify the fabric type and fibre composition through image analysis, rate it for recyclability and complete circularity, and proposed a recovery route with an estimated environmental value, based on the synthesis. In addition to the narrative synthesis, we extract all accuracy measures from each of the reviewed studies on classification and combine them in one common accuracy framework and quantify a gap which none of the source studies compares itself with. The accuracy drops by a mean decrease of 42.2 percentage points (range 26.6–60.9) when the same method and protocol; clean single-fibre samples change to blended, contaminated or actual post-consumer waste for all 13 accuracy decreases that were aggregated. A second comparison reveals the condition penalty is significantly greater than the 8–10 point penalty for selecting RGB imaging over spectral imaging, meaning realised accuracy is more dependent on condition of the input than the sensing technology itself. The other two patterns that repeat are disjointed classification research and disjointed sustainability scoring on incompatible system boundaries and disjointed research on recycling routes. There are no reviewed papers describing any algorithm for pricing and trading a classified batch after it has been created. Although this is a working prototype, the platform is not yet validated on actual waste streams, the validation process is described in Section 5.5 and no performance data for this platform are claimed in this paper.

title: Analyzing Industry 4.0 Integration Challenges in Sust ainable Supply Chains: A Study of Bangladesh’s RMG Industry Using Fuzzy AHP and BWM
summary: This study examines the challenges of integrating Industry 4.0 technologies into supply chain management to promote sustainable development in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment sector. Although Industry 4.0 offers significant potential, its a
content: This study examines the challenges of integrating Industry 4.0 technologies into supply chain management to promote sustainable development in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment sector. Although Industry 4.0 offers significant potential, its adoption is hindered by multiple interconnected barriers. Through literature review and expert consultation, fifteen key obstacles were identified and prioritized using Fuzzy AHP and the Best-Worst Method. The results consistently highlight leadership and policy-related constraints as the most critical challenges. The study emphasizes the importance of strong institutional support and strategic direction, and proposes a practical roadmap to support digital transformation in labor-intensive industries within emerging economies.

title: Logistics Agglomeration in the US: Public Governance and Environmental Externalities
source: Library, Museums and Press - UDSpace (University of Delaware)
summary: This dissertation investigates the spatial dynamics of the logistics industry in the United States, focusing on the interplay between public governance, market-driven forces, and environmental externalities. Despite growing interest in logi
content: This dissertation investigates the spatial dynamics of the logistics industry in the United States, focusing on the interplay between public governance, market-driven forces, and environmental externalities. Despite growing interest in logistics clusters, the geographical concentration of firms performing supply chain-related activities, research has historically lacked a comprehensive understanding of the institutional variables that influence their development and the socio-environmental impacts they generate. To address these gaps, this dissertation is structured as three interconnected standalone studies. The first study (Paper I, in Chapter 2) consists of a systematic literature review of 17 empirical studies on logistics clustering and sprawl. It reveals that these spatial patterns are highly context-dependent and proposes a novel conceptual model that unifies socioeconomic, infrastructural, and institutional drivers to guide future empirical research. In the second study (Paper II, in Chapter 3), the author evaluates the influence of multi-level government policies (specifically federal transportation grants, state highway spending, and Foreign-Trade Zone designations) on the development of logistics clusters. Utilizing Bayesian mixed-effects logistic regression on longitudinal data for US counties from 2008 to 2022, the results show that top-down financial and regulatory interventions have no discernible direct effect on cluster presence. Instead, agglomeration is overwhelmingly driven by fundamental market forces, including demographic scale, proximity to specialized intermodal rail infrastructure, and historical path dependence. The last study (Paper III, in Chapter 4) uses an extended spatial STIRPAT model to assess localized and regional environmental impacts of logistics agglomeration from 2000 to 2022. The analysis shows that while an increased concentration of logistics employment directly degrades local air quality (AQI) and increases criteria pollutants' concentrations (NO2 and PM2.5), reaching the advanced stage of "clustering" exhibits a mitigating effect on pollution due to economies of scale and shared infrastructure. Furthermore, the study identifies significant spatial spillovers and environmental justice gaps, noting that affluent areas often displace pollutant-heavy activities to vulnerable communities. Overall, this research concludes that laissez-faire market forces are the primary drivers of logistics agglomeration, and that top-down policies are limited in their ability to override these economic realities. Policymakers and public administrators should therefore prioritize horizontal and vertical regional governance to reinforce organically viable clusters and manage the local and regional environmental externalities of logistics agglomeration.

title: Asymmetric Michael reaction for the synthesis of chiral trans -dialkyl nitroalkanals, key building blocks for natural products – a review
summary: The asymmetric Michael reaction converts an alkyl aldehyde and a nitroalkene to a trans -2,3-disubstituted-4-nitroalkanal under mild conditions with high stereoselectivity. The nearly 200 known examples are reviewed herein.
content: The asymmetric Michael reaction converts an alkyl aldehyde and a nitroalkene to a trans -2,3-disubstituted-4-nitroalkanal under mild conditions with high stereoselectivity. The nearly 200 known examples are reviewed herein.

title: Quantity and quality of AI innovation drive renewable energy consumption in Chinese cities
summary: Renewable energy is central to the green transition and to UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 11, and 13. Using a balanced panel of 279 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2007–2021, this study distinguishes AI quantity innovation
content: Renewable energy is central to the green transition and to UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 11, and 13. Using a balanced panel of 279 Chinese prefecture-level cities over 2007–2021, this study distinguishes AI quantity innovation (AI1, AI patent applications, capturing the rate of knowledge creation) from AI quality innovation (AI2, authorized AI patents, capturing inventions that pass substantive examination for novelty, inventiveness and industrial applicability) and examines how each relates to renewable energy consumption. Two-way fixed-effects models are combined with instrumental-variable (IV) identification, two-step mediation, formal cross-group tests, and moderation analysis. Both AI1 and AI2 are positively associated with renewable energy consumption, and the association survives alternative IPC-based patent measures (AI3/AI4), logarithmic specifications, lagged predictors, place-based policy controls, and IV strategies. Three channels-public science-and-technology effort, R&D investment, and energy utilization efficiency-transmit part of the relationship. Effects differ across regions, resource endowments and city sizes, and are amplified by government support and market competition. The results inform differentiated, SDG-oriented AI-renewable policy.

title: Crystallization- and Shear-Induced Structural Evolutions in Polyhydroxyalkanoate-Blend Foams
summary: Crystallization in polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA)-based blends, influenced by the thermal history and shear field, governs the resulting cellular and interfacial morphology of foamed blends. Here, PHA/polycaprolactone (PCL) and PHA/poly(butylen
content: Crystallization in polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA)-based blends, influenced by the thermal history and shear field, governs the resulting cellular and interfacial morphology of foamed blends. Here, PHA/polycaprolactone (PCL) and PHA/poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) foams were prepared by extrusion to examine the roles of melt memory, viscoelasticity, and shear. The crystallization temperature of PHA was shifted from 115 °C after complete melting at 180 °C to 153 °C when melting was restricted to 170 °C due to the retention of residual crystalline nuclei. Such an induced crystallization maximized the crystalline lamellar thickness to 5.0 nm, compared with 4.7 nm at 160 and 180 °C, and resulted in a stiffer, more strain-resistant melt at strains up to 10–15%. This nanoscale crystalline reorganization, compounded by increasing shear rate from 130 to 250 s–1, refined the cellular structure of both blends with divergent shear-dependent minor phase morphologies. PCL discrete particles (1–6 μm) acted as heterogeneous nucleation sites without considerable interfacial debonding, whereas PBS underwent complete in situ fibrillation into an entangled nanofibrillar network (∼600–850 nm fiber diameter) that densified continuously with shear rate. PHA/PBS foam reached a void fraction of ∼32% at 250 s–1, roughly 2 times that of PHA/PCL. The contrasting morphologies, particle-mediated nucleation for PCL versus in situ nanofibrillation for PBS, demonstrated that the minor phase provides an independent effect, alongside melt memory-controlled crystallization and shear rate, for reinforcing the microstructure of PHA-based foams.

title: Evaluation of sensing response of H2S sensing materials toward H2S molecules using artificial neural network and response surface methodology
summary: In this work, temperatures of 25 to 275 °C, times of 6.5 to 4091 s, concentrations of 0.0001 to 400 ppm, and surface areas of 17.11 to 223.6 m 2 /g were simulated through artificial neural network (ANN) and response surface methodology (RSM
content: In this work, temperatures of 25 to 275 °C, times of 6.5 to 4091 s, concentrations of 0.0001 to 400 ppm, and surface areas of 17.11 to 223.6 m 2 /g were simulated through artificial neural network (ANN) and response surface methodology (RSM) for predicting the H 2 S sensor response. The number of collected data points was 548. The optimum values of each parameter were calculated using RSM. The optimized variables were 97.11 ℃ of temperature, 2785 s of response time, 259.77 ppm of H 2 S concentration, and a surface area of 197.78 m 2 /g. Regarding RSM, the dependency of sensor response on the parameters is quadratic. The multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and radial basis function (RBF) models were used in the ANN. Levenberg-Marquardt backpropagation algorithm (trainlm) was used. The numbers of neurons of 49 and 29 were considered for the first and second hidden layers for the MLP network, respectively. The number of neurons was calculated as 198 for the RBF model. The R 2 values of MLP, RBF, and RSM models were attained at 0.9897, 0.9894, and 0.9821, respectively. Also, the % AARD values of the MLP and RBF models are 17.33 and 66.20, respectively. It is concluded that the MLP model could predict the sensor response better than the RBF model. The transfer function for the first and second hidden layers was tansig in the MLP model. The best MSE validation performance of the MLP and RBF networks was 0.001061 and 0.001486 at 69 and 198 epochs, respectively. The MLP 3D diagram also proved that H₂S sensing materials such as Fe 2 O 3 -Ba 0.99 Ce 0.01 TiO 71 , SnCl 2 , and Fe-600 are good candidates for sensing the H 2 S molecules.

title: Market competition strategy optimization model based on the fusion of quantum game theory and multi-agent reinforcement learning
summary: In this paper, a market competition strategy optimization model that combines quantum game theory and multi-agent reinforcement learning is proposed, and its effectiveness is evaluated through simulation experiments based on synthetic Courn
content: In this paper, a market competition strategy optimization model that combines quantum game theory and multi-agent reinforcement learning is proposed, and its effectiveness is evaluated through simulation experiments based on synthetic Cournot competition data. The model enables multidimensional exploration of the strategy space through a quantum superposition state and combines the cooperation-competition mechanism of multi-agent reinforcement learning to achieve rapid convergence to the Nash equilibrium in dynamic games. The simulation results show that the proposed fusion model significantly improves decision-making efficiency, requiring only 24 policy adjustments to converge compared to the 105 times required by traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning methods, while achieving an average market share of 31.4% and an average monthly profit of 7.3 Units, which verifies the expansion ability and robustness of the model in a complex simulated state space. This model provides theoretical support for the transformation of market competition strategy from single-product competition to a more integrated and adaptive competitive-strategy framework. The simulation results suggest that the proposed model can improve market share, profit performance, and strategy stability under synthetic market competition scenarios, providing theoretical and computational reference value for market strategy optimization.

title: Intrusión de agua como reactante: Reformado in situ de metano para la generación de hidrógeno en yacimientos gasíferos
summary: El gas natural ha ocupado históricamente, frente al petróleo, un lugar secundario y, en América Latina, buena parte del gas asociado se quema o se ventea. El reformado in situ de metano (ISMR) propone que la intrusión de agua, hoy motivo pa
content: El gas natural ha ocupado históricamente, frente al petróleo, un lugar secundario y, en América Latina, buena parte del gas asociado se quema o se ventea. El reformado in situ de metano (ISMR) propone que la intrusión de agua, hoy motivo para abandonar pozos, actúe como recurso: el agua reacciona, amortigua los gradientes térmicos y aporta parte del hidrógeno producido. Conforme a PRISMA 2020, se revisaron 48 estudios: 41 de Web of Science, Scopus y ScienceDirect (2020-2025) y 7 mediante búsqueda manual. Los modelos proyectan conversiones de metano del 85 al 92 % entre 550 y 800 °C. En ensayos de laboratorio en medio poroso, esos valores aún no se reproducen. Con agua líquida de intrusión, el requerimiento térmico alcanza, como mínimo, +253 kJ/mol, un 53 % por encima del cálculo con vapor, un término que no se contabiliza en ninguno de los estudios incluidos. Dado que un yacimiento maduro se encuentra entre 80 y 130 °C, el proceso requiere una fuente de calor externa. La retención de CO₂ supera el 95 %; el costo proyectado va de menos de 2,0 a 2,8 USD/kg de H₂ y las emisiones directas disminuyen entre 90 y 95 %. No se identificó ningún estudio latinoamericano a escala de yacimiento que integre simulación, almacenamiento de CO₂ y evaluación técnico-económica.

title: Power harvesting from living solar panels: Crassulacean acid metabolism‐related concentration gradients drive cactus‐produced electricity
summary: Societal Impact Statement Climate change is pressuring the agricultural industry, creating the need for technological innovation. Plant sensors powered by on‐farm energy generation enable farmers to respond to plant stress quickly. Plants u
content: Societal Impact Statement Climate change is pressuring the agricultural industry, creating the need for technological innovation. Plant sensors powered by on‐farm energy generation enable farmers to respond to plant stress quickly. Plants utilizing crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM) exhibit higher drought tolerance through reduced stomatal opening by enabling nocturnal storage of charged organic acid compounds. Our study reveals the environment–photosynthesis relationship driving natural electricity generation in prickly pear cacti, a cultivated CAM crop. We present a new way of remotely detecting CAM crop stress via in situ voltage sensors and show the potential of living cactus‐power harvesting to provide climate‐resilient green electricity to sensors. Summary Power harvesting is the process of capturing tiny amounts of ambient energy from the environment and converting it into usable electrical power. Yet, further development of in situ green energy sources is needed to address power harvesting scale limitations. We describe a new form of power harvesting from plants that utilize crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM). We measured electrochemical gradients across prickly pear cactus ( Opuntia streptacantha ) stems under varying soil, light, and drought conditions. We compared these data to Photosystem II activity and acid concentration differences between stem sides. Results showed strong relationships between voltage and photosynthetic activity driven by light intensity. Acid concentration differences between stem sides, caused by differential photosynthetic activity, were the primary voltage driver. Surprisingly, stem water content did not significantly affect power production. Soil nitrogen additions sustained voltage for longer time periods, likely due to lengthened daily photosynthetic periods. Our generalized linear mixed model suggests that other organic sources besides malic acid may drive electrical charge. Cactus stem voltage shows promise for agricultural stress detection and potential for low‐power harvesting applications, such as in situ sensors.

title: Toward a Process Stable Flame‐Retardant Polyamide 12 Powder for Powder Bed Fusion
source: Journal of Vinyl and Additive Technology
summary: This study aims to develop a halogen‐free, flame‐retardant and process stable polyamide 12 powder for laser‐based powder bed fusion with polymers (PBF‐LB/P). Synergistic systems combining aluminum diethylphosphinate (AlPi) with either zinc
content: This study aims to develop a halogen‐free, flame‐retardant and process stable polyamide 12 powder for laser‐based powder bed fusion with polymers (PBF‐LB/P). Synergistic systems combining aluminum diethylphosphinate (AlPi) with either zinc borate (ZB) or zinc stannate (ZS) were evaluated. Initial screening showed that adding flame‐retardants increased fines content but maintained good powder flowability. Thermal analysis indicated that additives acted as nucleating agents and improved char formation. While the initial blends at best only achieved a UL94 V‐1 rating, increasing the total filler loading to 20 wt% with the 15:1 AlPi:ZB composition led to the desired V‐0 classification. Mechanical testing revealed the typical impact of flame‐retardants as tensile strength and elongation decreased, but stiffness increased. The fabrication of functional parts with a wall thickness of 2 mm seems viable, though dripping limited performance in thinner geometries. Replenishing aged powder with 50% virgin powder resulted in porous parts due to limited coalescence from fragmented flame‐retardant additives and high melt viscosity. However, by refining powder production and mixing processes, the combination of end‐capped polyamide 12 and thermally stable flame‐retardants could offer a viable strategy for creating sustainable flame‐retardant materials for PBF‐LB/P.

title: Adopting Green Innovations: The Case of Zero‐Waste Consumption Practices
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: What are the consumer practices involved in the adoption of green innovations, and how are these processes associated with adoption intentions at different stages? While prior research has identified barriers and drivers of green consumptio
content: What are the consumer practices involved in the adoption of green innovations, and how are these processes associated with adoption intentions at different stages? While prior research has identified barriers and drivers of green consumption, it often overlooks the complex, interconnected practices involved in adoption. This paper investigates green consumer behavior from an “ecosystem adoption of practices over time” (EAPT) perspective, which implies understanding this process as the gradual adoption of interrelated green consumer practices. These practices extend beyond the individual decision‐maker (i.e., the subject of innovation), encompass changes in habits and routines (i.e., the object of innovation), and differ across adoption stages (i.e., the temporality of innovation). Using a mixed‐methods approach, we investigate zero‐waste (ZW) consumption. We combine two qualitative pre‐studies and two field surveys of non‐adopters and early adopters of ZW. The qualitative studies identify four domains of practices—shopping, household, social and general environmental practices—and the surveys examine how perceived changes in these practices are associated with attitudinal beliefs, behavioral control and intentions. Our findings show that general environmental practices are positively associated with attitudinal beliefs in both groups, while household‐practice changes are negatively associated with behavioral control among non‐adopters. Shopping practices are positively associated with intentions among early adopters and show a marginal negative association among non‐adopters. These results provide context‐specific evidence that a practice‐based perspective can complement established adoption models and help businesses and policymakers identify practical barriers to more sustainable consumption.

title: Landscape Heterogeneity Changes and Their Implications for Agriculture in Europe
summary: This dissertation examines the extent and implications of historical changes in landscape heterogeneity in Europe. Landscape heterogeneity is conceptualized as the combination of two complementary dimensions: landscape composition, referrin
content: This dissertation examines the extent and implications of historical changes in landscape heterogeneity in Europe.
