title: Surface Soil Carbon Stocks and Fertility Status of Andisols Under Different Management Practices in Vegetable Cultivation in the Volcanic Highlands of Mount Kerinci
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Andisols are known to hold the highest soil carbon stocks among mineral soil types; they are generally found in highlands, fertile, and suitable for vegetable horticulture. Cultivation practices can deplete soil organic matter, thereby redu
content: Andisols are known to hold the highest soil carbon stocks among mineral soil types; they are generally found in highlands, fertile, and suitable for vegetable horticulture. Cultivation practices can deplete soil organic matter, thereby reducing carbon stocks and soil fertility. This study aims to examinethe impact of land-use intensity and its management in vegetable cultivation on surface carbon stocks and fertility status of Andisol in the Kayu Aro Barat District, Kerinci Regency. A survey method was employed, with observation points and soil samples selected via purposive random sampling. Soil surface carbon stock were estimated using data on soil organic carbon, bulk density, and soil volume at a depth of 0-30 cm. Soil fertility was assessed based on organic carbon concentrations and chemical properties, following the Technical Guidelines for Soil FertilityEvaluation from the Bogor Soil Research Institute. Surface soil carbon storageranged from 73.94 to 129.11Mg/ha, with fertility status ranging from low to high.High soil fertility and surface carbonstock were more prevalent on flat terrain that was intensively cultivated with higher inputs of manure, high-dose chemical fertilizers, and dolomite lime. Conversely, low soil fertility and lower carbon storage were observed on hilly terrain regardless of whether cultivation was intensive or non-intensive where inputs were similar but lacked dolomite. To maintain or enhance soil fertility and carbon stocks and to preservethe role of volcanic highlandsin mitigating soil carbon loss and global warming, it is crucial to educate farmers on adopting soil management practices that align with soil characteristics and crop requirements.

title: Comparative metagenomics reveals diversity and metabolic heterogeneity of sediment microbes from the Great Barrier Reef
summary: Microbial communities in coral reefs are highly connected through benthic-pelagic coupling. Pelagic and host-associated microbiomes have recently been characterised via genome-resolved metagenomics. However, similar characterisation of sedi
content: Microbial communities in coral reefs are highly connected through benthic-pelagic coupling. Pelagic and host-associated microbiomes have recently been characterised via genome-resolved metagenomics. However, similar characterisation of sediment communities has lagged behind due to their higher complexity. Here, using short-and long-read shotgun sequence data, we characterised sediment microbial communities of Australia’s Great Barrier Reef. From 191 samples across 48 broadly distributed sites, we recovered 2,698 prokaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) representing 1,201 species-level clusters, most of which are novel. Compared against their sympatric counterparts in seawater, sediment MAGs exhibited greater phylogenetic diversity and flexibility in metabolic potential, implicating diverse respiration strategies and cycling of nitrogen, sulphur, and hydrogen. They also encode more abundant and novel biosynthetic capabilities, likely reflecting competition and adaptation to intermittent fluctuations in nutrient regimes, and between oxic and anoxic conditions. Our results provide foundational genomic resources for reef sediment microbes, uncovering biodiversity and function that together with planktonic microbes shape the ecological success and stability of coral reef ecosystems.

title: Learning to Read Events for Exact State Tracking with Frozen Language Models
summary: Long event streams require identifying each change and applying the changes in order. We train a selector on a frozen language model to read each transition. With API-only access, we ask the model to list the transitions. An external intege
content: Long event streams require identifying each change and applying the changes in order. We train a selector on a frozen language model to read each transition. With API-only access, we ask the model to list the transitions. An external integer register composes them in order. A confidence rule can flag uncertain updates or retain several candidates. We study products of permutations of five items, a task that fixed-depth, log-precision transformers cannot solve on all input lengths under the standard conjecture that $\mathrm{TC}^0 \ne \mathrm{NC}^1$. On two-event windows, a 27B model answered 3 of 100 correctly without visible reasoning and 96 of 100 when it generated intermediate steps. A frozen 0.8B model with a trained selector read every event in 299 of 299 windows of 43,687 events each. The same package passed 298 of 299 new windows on a fresh machine, missing the target of 0.99 for the one-sided 95% lower confidence bound. A separate follow-up sized to allow one failure yielded 472 of 473. On 1,000-event room-swap documents, three of ten models solved all five documents by reasoning alone. All seven models tested both ways at this length solved all five with extraction and the register, with no chain of thought requested. With concurrent extraction, median wall-clock time fell from 136.1 to 10.4 s for Sonnet 5.5 and from 313.5 to 28.0 s for GPT-6.1 Sol. At fixed per-token rates, mean cost per document fell by 55% for Sonnet 5.5 and 44% for GPT-6.1 Sol. A regular expression with an executor also solved all 15 fixed-format documents. On 500 free-form issue-tracker comments, a separately adapted 4B reader identified the recorded value in 68.8% of cases, compared with 61.0% for a frequency baseline fitted on the same training projects.

title: Ocean technology deployment in the Iberian-Atlantic: regional clusters, innovation and sustainability challenges
summary: Introduction The deployment of ocean technologies (OT) and testing infrastructures is increasingly important for sustainable Blue Economy (BE) development, yet integrated assessments of their spatial distribution, innovation capacity and po
content: Introduction The deployment of ocean technologies (OT) and testing infrastructures is increasingly important for sustainable Blue Economy (BE) development, yet integrated assessments of their spatial distribution, innovation capacity and policy context remain limited. Methods We combined an inventory of 71 OT deployments (1999–2025) in the Iberian-Atlantic with spatial and stakeholder analyses, K-means clustering and multidimensional scaling (MDS) of 13 indicators across 14 NUTS2 regions, and a review of 50 policy and R&D&I initiatives (1970–2026). Results The OT landscape is spatially concentrated but technologically diverse, and dominated by offshore renewable energy. Four regional innovation profiles were identified (metropolitan, industrial-maritime, OT-specialized and emerging), showing that OT specialization is not solely related to economic scale. Policy initiatives influence OT through direct, enabling and indirect pathways. Discussion The findings highlight the importance of place-based innovation capacity, testing infrastructures and coordinated multi-scale governance for sustainable ocean innovation.

title: Photocurrent‐Detected Multidimensional Spectroscopy Reveals Composition‐Dependent Carrier Cooling in Operating Perovskite Solar Cells
summary: Understanding how photogenerated carriers dissipate excess energy in operating perovskite solar cells is essential for connecting ultrafast photophysics with photovoltaic function and provides design principles for engineering next‐generati
content: Understanding how photogenerated carriers dissipate excess energy in operating perovskite solar cells is essential for connecting ultrafast photophysics with photovoltaic function and provides design principles for engineering next‐generation cell architectures. Here, photocurrent‐detected two‐dimensional electronic spectroscopy (PC‐2DES) is used to resolve energy‐dependent carrier relaxation in fully encapsulated, functioning metal halide perovskite solar cells. By comparing devices with the same layer stack structure but different absorber compositions (MAPbI 3 , mixed FAMA, and FAPbI 3 ), it is possible to directly follow the redistribution of photoexcited carriers from initially populated high‐energy states toward lower‐energy band‐edge states. The multidimensional photocurrent response reveals a cascade‐like intraband cooling process whose rate depends on absorber composition, with the slowest relaxation in MA‐based devices, intermediate behavior in mixed‐cation devices, and fastest relaxation in FA‐based devices. A reduced kinetic model incorporating phonon‐mediated intraband scattering, supplemented by a phenomenological many‐body contribution, captures the main energy‐dependent trends. These results establish action‐detected multidimensional spectroscopy as a device‐level probe of ultrafast energy dissipation and show that the composition dependence of hot‐carrier cooling reported for perovskite films and nanocrystals persists in working devices.

title: Discourse diversity in marine protected area management: A Q-methodology analysis of an Atlantic National Park
summary: This study applies Q methodology to examine stakeholder discourses on management actions in the marine–terrestrial Atlantic Islands of Galicia National Park (Spain). A total of 182 participants from diverse actor groups were surveyed, revea
content: This study applies Q methodology to examine stakeholder discourses on management actions in the marine–terrestrial Atlantic Islands of Galicia National Park (Spain). A total of 182 participants from diverse actor groups were surveyed, revealing four distinct discourses: Strict Protection (48%), emphasizing ecosystem protection through visitor quota reduction and restrictions on marine activities; Ecological restoration (13%), focusing on habitat recovery, invasive species removal, and marine pollution control; Education & sustainability (12%), prioritizing environmental education, cultural heritage, and balanced resource use; and Use Regulation (2%), advocating stricter control of marine activities and pollution, with limited support for educational expansion. Consensus emerged in rejecting the expansion of hospitality services and the aesthetic improvement of infrastructure. Stakeholder divergence can be organized along three independent axes: the trade-off between protection and human use, the intensity of ecological intervention, and the choice of management instrument. Socioeconomic factors influenced discourse alignment, with higher education levels increasing the likelihood of identifying with a discourse, while surrounding-area inhabitants and ecotourism actors were less likely to align with a specific discourse. These findings indicate that what divides stakeholders is how strictly to protect, how actively to intervene, and through which instrument to act. Furthermore, they highlight the utility of Q methodology in facilitating adaptive and participatory governance of marine-terrestrial protected areas.

title: Maximize The Reliability of A Distribution System Based on Data Monitoring on Distribution Transformer Power Using The Fuzzy Decision Making Method Based on The Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP)
summary: Distribution transformers are critical components in the electric power distribution system. Transformer failure can cause power outages and economic losses, so a systematic reliability evaluation method is needed. Previous studies generall
content: Distribution transformers are critical components in the electric power distribution system. Transformer failure can cause power outages and economic losses, so a systematic reliability evaluation method is needed. Previous studies generally evaluate reliability based on damage data parameters. The novelty of this study lies in the integration of four operating parameters (voltage, power factor, unbalance, and loading) simultaneously using the Fuzzy Decision Making method based on the Analytical Hierarchy Process. This study aims to analyze and determine the reliability ranking of three distribution transformer units based on monitoring data at Peak Load Time. The AHP weighting results show that power factor has the highest weight (0.47), followed by loading (0.27), unbalance (0.16), and voltage (0.10) with a Consistency Ratio of 0.012 (valid). The analysis results show that the East Transformer has the highest reliability index (73% - Good), the North Transformer (71% - Good), and the South Transformer (50.9% - Sufficient). The South Transformer requires priority repair due to high underload and unbalance conditions.

title: 새만금 RE100 수소·순산소 저장 기반 24시간 무탄소 기저부하 통합 시스템 시뮬레이션

content: 국문 초록 (Korean Abstract) 본 연구는 새만금 지역의 RE100 재생에너지(조력 기반, 태양광 및 해상풍력 보조)를 수소와 순산소로 전환·저장하고, 이를 이용해 24시간 무탄소 기저부하 전력과 액화수소, 산소 및 담수를 동시에 공급하는 통합 시스템을 제안한다. Saemangeum IRUM Simulator v2.4를 이용하여 연간 8,760시간의 물질·에너지 수지와 운전 가능성을 평가하였다. 시스템은 수소 100 t/day 및 산소 793.7 t/day 생산을 위한 수전해, 수소·산소 저장탱크, 10 km 배관, 수소·순산소 직접연소 증기터빈, 배관 차압을 이용한 부분 자기 액화, 조력 구동 해수담수화 및 무방류(ZLD) 농축수 처리 기술을 결합한다. 터빈 입구온도 1,300°C, 1,500°C, 1,700°C에서 수소 생산량의 40%를 발전에 배분하면 각각 29.78 MW, 33.83 MW, 38.46 MW의 연속 기저부하가 산출되었다. 수소에서 전력으로의 블록 효율은 저위발열량(LHV) 기준 53.62~69.25%이며, 수전해를 포함한 왕복 효율은 32.4~41.8%로 평가되었다. 또한 연간 약 610만 m³의 농축수를 처리하는 ZLD 시나리오와 조력·태양광·풍력의 전력 조합, 수소·산소 저장용량을 비교하였다. 본 결과는 합성 기상자료와 선행 시뮬레이션 기반의 개념설계 및 스크리닝 평가이며, 실제 설비의 운전 성능이 입증된 것은 아니다.

title: Behavioural segmentation and short-horizon demand forecasting for a renewable energy community: code and data
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This archive contains the code and input data supporting Chapter 3 of the doctoral thesis "Towards Sustainable Local Energy Initiatives: Integrating Operational Research and Machine Learning" (Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lis
content: This archive contains the code and input data supporting Chapter 3 of the doctoral thesis "Towards Sustainable Local Energy Initiatives: Integrating Operational Research and Machine Learning" (Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa). The workflow tests whether behaviour-based segmentation of smart-meter demand improves short-horizon forecasting of total community demand, and how forecast error differs between behavioural regimes. It covers data loading, rolling-origin fold generation (ten folds), fold-wise imputation and outlier treatment, catch22 feature extraction, UMAP embedding and k-means clustering, forecasting with XGBoost, Random Forest, ANN/MLP and LSTM under aggregate, behavioural and random-control strategies, and cross-fold aggregation of metrics. Contents:- code/: the forecasting and segmentation pipeline (final_pipeline.py and modules)- code/data/: 15-minute electricity consumption for 128 meters and 15-minute weather observations, derived from the public dataset of Monteiro et al. (2024)- benchmark/: seasonal-naive reference forecast evaluated on the same folds, targets and metrics- results/: fold-level metrics of the seasonal-naive reference- environment.yml, requirements.txt, README.md, MANIFEST_SHA256.txt Instructions for reproducing the results are given in README.md. Source data: Monteiro, F. et al. (2024). Electricity consumption dataset of a local energy cooperative. Data in Brief, 54, 110373. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dib.2024.110373 (CC BY 4.0).

title: Copper demand and climate trade-offs of data-centre expansion: model, inputs and outputs (v1.0)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This package reproduces every number, table and figure in the paper "Climate trade-offs of copper demand for global data-centre expansion" (Y. Charabi, submitted to Communications Earth & Environment). The model estimates the copper needed
content: This package reproduces every number, table and figure in the paper "Climate trade-offs of copper demand for global data-centre expansion" (Y. Charabi, submitted to Communications Earth & Environment). The model estimates the copper needed by global data-centre expansion over 2026–2040 in four layers: facility systems, IT equipment, dedicated substations, and the generation and storage that supply the load. It uses the four data-centre capacity cases of the International Energy Agency. It then estimates how much clean-energy abatement is lost when that copper is drawn from a constrained market, and compares this with the emissions saved by renewable rather than gas or nuclear supply. A variance-based (Sobol) sensitivity analysis identifies which parameters drive the result. Contents model/build_audit_tables_v11.py: the model. It reads the inputs and writes audit_tables_v11.xlsx, with one sheet for each table in the paper. scripts/: scripts that write the supplementary tables (CSV), draw the main and supplementary figures, and check the input values against the original IEA workbooks. inputs/: the IEA data-centre capacity data used by the model. outputs/: the workbook, figures and supplementary tables as produced by the code. run_all.sh: a single command that regenerates all outputs in a few seconds. README.md, requirements.txt and CHECKSUMS.sha256. Requirements: Python 3 with the packages listed in requirements.txt. Data sources: all inputs come from public sources cited in the paper (IEA, IRENA, GWEC, IPCC and others). The original IEA workbooks are not redistributed. The verification script checks the transcribed values against them when users download them from the IEA.

title: Grid integrated battery assisted hybrid renewable source with LVRT converter control capability
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The installation and integration of grid-connected hybridrenewable source (PV+WF) based DGSs have increasedsignificantly in recent years. The growing penetration of DGSsinto electrical grids requires their power electronic convertersto poss
content: The installation and integration of grid-connected hybridrenewable source (PV+WF) based DGSs have increasedsignificantly in recent years. The growing penetration of DGSsinto electrical grids requires their power electronic convertersto possess adequate FRT capability. Specifically, the converteris expected to stay synchronized with the grid throughoutvoltage sag events, while injecting suitable reactive power topreserve grid stability. This paper proposes a grid-tied hybridrenewable configuration coupled with battery energy storage,designed to handle both balanced and unbalanced generationand equipped with LVRT capability. A straightforward yeteffective control scheme is adopted so that the DGS convertercontinues operating on the grid under fault conditions andsatisfies the prescribed LVRT requirements. The battery energystorage system is interfaced with the DC link through abidirectional DC–DC converter, which assists in suppressingvoltage variations during disturbances. The proposed controlapproach relies on the positive-sequence components of thegrid current to enable LVRT operation, ensuring the convertercurrent never exceeds its rated limits. The proposed DGSconfiguration and its control strategy are evaluated usingMATLAB/Simulink under voltage sag and varying powergeneration conditions. The simulation results help assess howeffectively the system responds to grid disturbances andmaintains stable and reliable grid-connected operation underdifferent operating conditions.

title: THE ROLE AND IMPORTANCE OF APPLIED MATHEMATICS IN THE GREEN ECONOMY
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The transition to a "green" economy entails the measurement, forecasting, and optimal allocation of resources, energy, and waste; consequently, its scientific foundation relies on applied mathematics. This article demonstrates how challenge
content: The transition to a "green" economy entails the measurement, forecasting, and optimal allocation of resources, energy, and waste; consequently, its scientific foundation relies on applied mathematics. This article demonstrates how challenges associated with the "green" economy can be addressed using optimization methods, statistical forecasting, and differential equations. Each method is illustrated with a numerical example and a corresponding graph; the article also includes an analysis of data concerning renewable energy sources in Uzbekistan.

title: Country-level hourly electricity demand profiles for 54 African countries, 2016–2025 (REPSA)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset provides reconstructed country-level hourly electricity demand profiles for 54 African countries covering 2016–2025, developed as part of the Renewable Energy Planning for Sustainable Africa (REPSA) project. The profiles are ge
content: This dataset provides reconstructed country-level hourly electricity demand profiles for 54 African countries covering 2016–2025, developed as part of the Renewable Energy Planning for Sustainable Africa (REPSA) project. The profiles are generated using a two-stage assign–adapt procedure that matches countries to three African reference demand series from South Africa (2024), Algeria (2019), and Nigeria (2016) based on country characteristics. The assigned profiles are subsequently adapted to reflect socioeconomic, calendar, and weather-related differences, then normalized to preserve annual electricity demand totals from a harmonized country-year dataset. The repository contains hourly electricity demand profiles in CSV format, the harmonized annual dataset with provenance flags, reference-profile assignment metadata, and leave-one-anchor-out validation summaries. These resources support reproducible energy-system modelling, electricity demand analysis, electrification planning, teaching, and comparative studies across African countries. The reconstructed hourly profiles are intended as model-ready estimates where measured national demand data are unavailable and should not be interpreted as independently observed electricity demand.

title: A review of metallurgical approaches for recycling rare earth elements from NdFeB and SmCo permanent magnets
summary: Technological progress, coupled with the rising demand for high-performance materials, has resulted in a considerable expansion of the applications of rare earth elements (REEs). As indicated in the report initially published by the Europea
content: Technological progress, coupled with the rising demand for high-performance materials, has resulted in a considerable expansion of the applications of rare earth elements (REEs). As indicated in the report initially published by the European Commission in 2011 and most recently updated in 2023, REEs are among the metals with the highest supply risk. The production from ore and recycling of these metals represent a significant field of study at the global level. Given the low-grade nature of REE ores, the global dependence on one dominant producer for raw material supply, refining as well as magnet manufacturing, and the significant environmental impact of primary extraction, the recovery of REEs from end-of-life products has emerged as a critical and increasingly researched alternative. Due to the importance of permanent magnets in technological applications and the fact that REEs are listed as critical metals for the European union and several other parts of the world, alternative ways are being sought to supply raw materials. REE-based permanent magnets are key components of numerous advanced technologies, particularly in electrified transportation, renewable energy systems, and high-performance electronic devices. Their combination of strong magnetic performance and technological importance has increased the strategic value of end-of-life magnets as secondary resources for REE recovery. In this context, the number of studies examining the recovery of REEs from permanent magnets is rapidly increasing. The present literature review covers the recovery of REEs from neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) and samarium-cobalt (SmCo) permanent magnets through hydro-, solvo- and pyrometallurgical methods.

title: SSA-RF short-term photovoltaic power prediction method based on correlation-driven feature selection and interpretability enhancement
source: International Conference on Machine Learning, Neural Networks, and Computer Software (MLNNCS)
summary: Photovoltaic power output is highly affected by meteorological conditions and presents strong nonlinearity and stochastic fluctuation, which brings challenges to accurate short-term forecasting. To address the problems of feature redundancy
content: Photovoltaic power output is highly affected by meteorological conditions and presents strong nonlinearity and stochastic fluctuation, which brings challenges to accurate short-term forecasting. To address the problems of feature redundancy, hyperparameter dependence and insufficient interpretability in existing methods, this paper proposes an interpretable SSARF photovoltaic power prediction method based on correlation-driven feature selection. Pearson correlation analysis is first employed to screen key meteorological variables highly related to photovoltaic power, thereby reducing input redundancy and improving feature representation. Then, a random forest regression model is constructed, and the sparrow search algorithm is introduced to optimize critical hyperparameters, including the number of trees, maximum depth and minimum leaf samples. Finally, LIME is used to interpret local prediction results and quantify the contribution of different meteorological factors. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves stable cross-validation performance, efficient parameter optimization, strong fitting ability and accurate time-series tracking. The interpretability analysis further indicates that solar radiation-related factors dominate photovoltaic power prediction. Therefore, the proposed method provides an accurate, robust and interpretable solution for short-term photovoltaic power forecasting and has practical value for smart grid dispatching and renewable energy management.

title: Integrated Regional Forest Biomass Resource Assessment and Aspen Plus Process Simulation for Sustainable Energy Production
source: Journal of the Turkish Chemical Society Section B Chemical Engineering
summary: The sustainable utilization of forest biomass is essential for reducing dependence on fossil fuels while supporting renewable energy production and the transition toward a circular bioeconomy. However, biomass resource assessments and therm
content: The sustainable utilization of forest biomass is essential for reducing dependence on fossil fuels while supporting renewable energy production and the transition toward a circular bioeconomy. However, biomass resource assessments and thermochemical process simulations are generally conducted independently, limiting their applicability to regional bioenergy planning. This study presents an integrated framework that combines spatial assessment of forest biomass resources with Aspen Plus process simulation to evaluate the bioenergy and hydrogen production potential of forest plantation species cultivated in Antalya, Türkiye. The bioenergy potential of Acacia, Pinus, and Eucalyptus species was first assessed using the International Renewable Energy Agency Bioenergy Simulator, followed by the development of an Aspen Plus model incorporating biomass gasification, hydrogen separation, waste heat recovery, and a Rankine cycle for cogeneration. Among the investigated species, Pinus exhibited the highest biomass availability and energy potential, with Pinus pinaster producing approximately 750,000 GJ of bioenergy and 42,000 MWh of electricity, substantially exceeding the best-performing Eucalyptus and Acacia species. Process simulation demonstrated that optimum hydrogen production (6.18 kg/h) and high hydrogen purity (99.1%) were achieved at a gasification temperature of 800 °C and an airflow rate of 20 kmol/h. Increasing steam temperature and pressure enhanced net power generation, while lower cooler outlet temperatures improved hydrogen recovery. The novelty of this work lies in integrating spatial biomass resource assessment with process-level thermochemical simulation, directly linking regional feedstock availability to hydrogen and energy production. The proposed framework supports forest species selection and optimization of biomass-to-hydrogen systems for sustainable regional bioenergy planning.

title: PRODUÇÃO DE BIODISEL A PARTIR DA CATÁLISE HETEROGÊNEA COM CASCA DE OVO
source: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
summary: In recent decades, driven by policies promoting renewable energy and the need to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, biodiesel has emerged as a viable alternative for mitigating climate change and fostering sustainable development. This stud
content: In recent decades, driven by policies promoting renewable energy and the need to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, biodiesel has emerged as a viable alternative for mitigating climate change and fostering sustainable development. This study evaluated the production of methyl biodiesel through heterogeneous catalysis using calcium oxide (CaO) derived from calcined eggshells. The study involved the preparation of the catalyst, followed by the esterification and transesterification of soybean oil with methanol. The results demonstrated an average conversion efficiency of 76,82%, whit the physicochemical properties of the biodiesel within the limits established by the applicable standards, reinforcing the potential of using eggshells as a catalyst in biodiesel production.

title: Solar Powered Hybrid Dryer for Agriculture Product Preservation and Value Addition
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
summary: World is mostly concentrating on new inventions and running with updated technology. Farmers are back bone for every country in the world. Without farmers livelihood is difficult. Solar Powered Hybrid Dryer for Agriculture Product Preservat
content: World is mostly concentrating on new inventions and running with updated technology. Farmers are back bone for every country in the world. Without farmers livelihood is difficult. Solar Powered Hybrid Dryer for Agriculture Product Preservation and Value AdditionThe preservation of agricultural produce through effective drying is essential for reducing post-harvest losses and maintaining grain quality for long-term storage. This project focuses on the design, fabrication, and performance evaluation of an electrically powered, forced-convection multigrain air dryer. The system was developed as a controlled alternative to traditional open-air sun drying, which is often inconsistent and prone to contamination. Methodology & Fabrication The dryer was constructed using a thermally insulated drying chamber to minimize heat loss. The core heating system consists of electric heating coils that raise the temperature of the incoming air to the required levels. A centrifugal blower was integrated to facilitate forced air circulation, ensuring that the heated air is evenly distributed throughout the chamber. To support the grains and allow for maximum air-to-grain contact, the system utilizes multiple perforated plates (trays). These plates were designed with specific hole diameters to provide optimal airflow while preventing grain fall through. Performance Evaluation The performance of the fabricated model was evaluated using different types of grains (such as maize, wheat, and paddy). Key parameters measured included the drying rate, thermal efficiency, and moisture removal rate. Results indicated that the forced-air circulation system significantly reduced drying time compared to natural convection methods.

title: ConvLSTM-DynAE: dynamic deep embedded clustering for smart meter load profiling
summary: The increasing deployment of smart meters has generated large-scale electricity consumption datasets that provide valuable opportunities for data-driven customer segmentation and demand-side energy management. Accurate load profiling underp
content: The increasing deployment of smart meters has generated large-scale electricity consumption datasets that provide valuable opportunities for data-driven customer segmentation and demand-side energy management. Accurate load profiling underpins demand response, peak-load reduction, tariff design, and renewable energy integration. However, conventional clustering methods rely on handcrafted features and predefined similarity measures, while existing deep embedded clustering approaches often overlook temporal dependencies and produce unstable latent representations during optimization. This paper proposes ConvLSTM-DynAE , a dynamic deep embedded clustering framework for smart meter load profiling that integrates a Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) autoencoder with a dynamic clustering objective. The ConvLSTM autoencoder learns robust latent representations by jointly capturing local consumption patterns and long-range temporal dependencies, while the dynamic optimization strategy progressively shifts the learning objective from reconstruction to clustering, mitigating Feature Randomness and Feature Drift to improve clustering stability. The proposed framework is evaluated using two large-scale smart meter datasets from London and Ireland. Clustering performance is assessed using the Silhouette Index, Davies–Bouldin Index, and Calinski–Harabasz Index, together with qualitative analysis of representative load profiles. Comparative experiments against representative conventional and deep clustering methods demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in producing compact, well-separated, and interpretable customer clusters across both datasets. The results demonstrate that ConvLSTM-DynAE provides a robust and effective framework for unsupervised electricity consumption segmentation, generating meaningful customer profiles that support demand response, energy management, and data-driven decision-making in modern smart grids.

title: Milano–Cortina 2026
summary: This chapter examines the Milano–Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games as the first edition to be formally designed under the International Olympic Committee (IOC)’s Agenda 2020 sustainability framework. Drawing on bid documentation, candidatur
content: This chapter examines the Milano–Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games as the first edition to be formally designed under the International Olympic Committee (IOC)’s Agenda 2020 sustainability framework. Drawing on bid documentation, candidature files, governance reviews, and planning materials, the chapter analyses the Games’ pioneering dual-host-city model, which distributed competitions across a polycentric network of venues spanning Lombardy, Veneto, and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano. It evaluates key infrastructure projects – including the Porta Romana Olympic Village, the Cortina Sliding Centre, and the multi-cluster mobility network – and assesses how the Games’ unprecedented territorial scale shaped sustainability governance. A dedicated post-event assessment, written following the conclusion of the Games in February 2026, provides a retrospective verdict: while the edition achieved one of the highest rates of venue reuse in Winter Olympic history and delivered measurable advances in renewable energy sourcing, it also incurred significant cost overruns, governance failures, and environmental shortcuts. The chapter argues that Milano–Cortina 2026 represents a genuinely transitional case – one that confirms both the potential and the structural limits of the Agenda 2020 reform framework.

title: Green Polymers for Energy Conversion: Sustainability, Efficiency, and Future Outlook, International Conference on Statistics, Econometrics, and Mathematics
summary: The expanding need for clean energy and the imperative to address climate change have spurred research into sustainable materials. Green polymers, which are made from renewable feedstocks and are usually biodegradable or recyclable, play a
content: The expanding need for clean energy and the imperative to address climate change have spurred research into sustainable materials. Green polymers, which are made from renewable feedstocks and are usually biodegradable or recyclable, play a vital role in energy conversion devices. This overview emphasizes their role in solar cells, fuel cells, supercapacitors, and thermoelectric devices. Key characteristics like biodegradability, low carbon footprint, and biocompatibility render them desirable substitutes for traditional petrochemical‐based polymers. Challenges in terms of durability, cost, and scalability notwithstanding, breakthroughs in nanostructuring, hybrid composites, and smart polymers hold promise. Hopes for the future are based on molecular innovation, AI‐aided design, circular economy approaches, and robust policy support, opening the door toward sustainable energy technologies.

title: Nanosized versus bulk fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) extract: comparative effects on in vitro rumen gas production kinetics, greenhouse gas productions, nutrient degradability and fermentation end-products
summary: Context Rumen methanogenesis represents a major source of agricultural greenhouse gas productions and a significant loss of dietary energy. Aims This study evaluated the effects of fennel (Foeniculum vulgare Mill.) extract, supplied either
content: Context Rumen methanogenesis represents a major source of agricultural greenhouse gas productions and a significant loss of dietary energy. Aims This study evaluated the effects of fennel (Foeniculum vulgare Mill.) extract, supplied either as a bulk extract or as an oil-in-water nanoemulsion, at inclusion levels of 15, 30 and 45 μL/g dry matter (DM) on in vitro gas production kinetics, methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2) productions, nutrient degradability, and rumen fermentation characteristics. Methods The incubation substrate was a total mixed ration (600 g/kg concentrate feed mixture, 300 g/kg berseem hay and 100 g/kg rice straw, DM basis). Treatments were arranged in a 2 × 3 + 1 factorial design with three incubation runs. Key results Significant form × dose interactions were detected for asymptotic gas production (b), fractional rate of gas production (c), lag time, metabolizable energy, partitioning factor at 48 h and gas yield at 24 h (P < 0.05). Nanosized nanoemulsion 30 μL/g DM produced the greatest fermentation response, yielding the highest b (384.2 mL/g DM), c (0.046 h−1), metabolizable energy (9.97 MJ/kg DM) and gas yield at 24 h (442.9 mL/g DM). In contrast, nanosized nanoemulsion 45 μL/g DM produced the lowest values for these variables, but the highest partitioning factor at 48 h. Both fennel extract forms reduced CH4 production relative to the control, with the nanoemulsion showing greater efficacy. Methane reductions reached 30.0% and 37.7% at nanosized nanoemulsion 30 μL/g DM and nanosized nanoemulsion 45 μL/g DM, respectively (P = 0.001). The nanoemulsion also increased CO2 production per gram of incubated DM compared with the bulk extract (P < 0.001). In vitro DM, neutral detergent fiber and acid detergent fiber degradability, as well as fermentation pH, were significantly affected by the form × dose interaction (P = 0.001). Nanosized nanoemulsion 30 μL/g DM improved degradability, nanosized nanoemulsion 45 μL/g DM reduced it below control values and pH changed only slightly (6.77–6.97). Ammonia-N concentrations declined progressively with increasing fennel extract inclusion (P < 0.001). Conclusions These findings indicate that nanoemulsification enhances the fermentation-modulating and antimethanogenic activity of fennel extract, with 30 μL/g DM providing the most favorable balance between improved fermentation and methane mitigation. Implications Nanoemulsified fennel extract at 30 μL/g DM is a promising, natural phytogenic strategy for enteric CH4 mitigation that warrants confirmation under in vivo feeding conditions.

title: Bitcoin and Ethereum: Computational Analysis of Twelve Years of Social Media Discourse, Sentiment Dynamics, and Sustainability Narratives
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Description This data contains tweet IDs and derived variables for 42.7 million tweets tagged #bitcoin/#BTC (35,791,717 tweets, March 2010 – June 2022) and #ethereum/#ETH (6,873,450 tweets, November 2013 – June 2022), collected with snscrap
content: Description This data contains tweet IDs and derived variables for 42.7 million tweets tagged #bitcoin/#BTC (35,791,717 tweets, March 2010 – June 2022) and #ethereum/#ETH (6,873,450 tweets, November 2013 – June 2022), collected with snscrape in June 2022, before the Ethereum Merge. For every tweet the files give sentiment scores from four methods (VADER, Twitter RoBERTa, CryptoBERT, FinBERT), climate relevance from a keyword dictionary and from ClimateBERT, cleaning flags, simple text counts and engagement counts. For the climate-related subset they add the relevance and stance coded by a large language model (critique, defence, solution, info, promo) and the domains and source types of linked websites. A human-coded validation sample of 1,000 tweets, the keyword dictionary and the coding instructions are included. The files contain no tweet text, usernames or account information. Tweets can be retrieved by their IDs through the X API; the full data are available from the corresponding author for non-commercial academic research under a data use agreement. Files File Rows Contents BTC_derived_climate_sentiment_links.csv 35,791,717 One row per Bitcoin tweet: ID, date, tweet metadata, engagement counts and all derived variables (data dictionary below) ETH_derived_climate_sentiment_links.csv 6,873,450 The same for Ethereum tweets gold_key.csv 1,000 Validation sample: tweet ID, coin, sampling stratum, keyword and ClimateBERT result group_sizes.csv 10 Size of each sampling stratum in the full data, per coin (used to weight recall) gold_codes.csv 1,000 Human codes for the validation sample: relevance, stance, sentiment gold_codes_coder2.csv 250 Second coder's codes for the reliability check keyword_dictionary.md — Climate keyword dictionary: terms, tiers, exclusions codebook.pdf — Coding instructions for relevance, stance and sentiment README.md — This description The two derived files are joined to each other, or to the validation files, on id. A tweet tagged with both coins can appear in both corpora, so use id together with coin when combining them. How the data were collected and processed Collection. Tweets were collected with snscrape in June 2022 using the hashtags #bitcoin and #BTC (Bitcoin corpus) and #ethereum and #ETH (Ethereum corpus). The snscrape search returns original tweets, replies and quote tweets, so the corpora contain no retweets. Engagement counts (likes, retweets, replies, quotes) reflect their values at collection, not at posting. Sentiment. VADER compound scores (vaderSentiment package) were computed on the original tweet text. Twitter RoBERTa, CryptoBERT and FinBERT were run on every tweet, with user mentions replaced by “@user”, links by “http” and texts truncated to 128 tokens. Cleaning flags. Duplicate texts were identified after lower-casing and removing links, mentions, hashtags and extra spaces (the first copy is kept). Tweets with 8 or more hashtags, or more hashtags than half their words, are flagged as hashtag-stuffe

title: Greenness and tropospheric nitrogen dioxide within 47 global cities: Spatially validated satellite evidence and explainable machine learning
summary: Satellite studies often report lower nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) where urban areas are greener, but cross-city models can overstate generalisability and attribute differences between cities to vegetation. We combined TROPOMI tropospheric NO 2
content: Satellite studies often report lower nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) where urban areas are greener, but cross-city models can overstate generalisability and attribute differences between cities to vegetation. We combined TROPOMI tropospheric NO 2 columns (2021–2023) with Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, land cover, built form, population, night lights, ERA5-Land meteorology and EDGAR emissions for 50 screened cities, aggregated to 0.05° cells (about 5 km) that match the TROPOMI footprint. After pre-specified quality control, 47 cities and 3089 cells were analysed. Gradient-boosted models reached R 2 = 0.94 under random cell-level cross-validation, but only 0.11 when whole cities were withheld and −1.13 when whole climate groups were withheld; 81 % of NO 2 variance lay between cities. With city fixed effects, a 0.1 increase in NDVI was associated with 6.9 µmol/m 2 lower NO 2 (95 % CI −10.0 to −3.9), a fifth of the pooled estimate (−32.5). Adding distance to the city centre, a spatial trend surface, night lights or emissions reduced the coefficient by 34–69 %, and by 97 % when distance, emissions, night lights and built form were combined, which indicates that NDVI mainly tracks the urban-core gradient. The city-specific association was negative in 38 of 47 cities but strongly heterogeneous (I 2 = 85 % with spatially robust standard errors) and was not detectably explained by climate group or density. An NDVI knot near 0.32 improved fit, but its interval (0.28–0.58) was wide and the out-of-sample gain was small. The results do not support causal or mitigation interpretations and provide a validation and reporting standard for satellite air-quality studies.

title: Regional landfill siting in northern iran: integrating waste footprint and ecological suitability into a GIS-TOPSIS spatial decision-support framework
summary: Identifying suitable locations for municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal represents a critical challenge for sustainable environmental management. This study investigates the spatial suitability of landfill sites across three northern Irania
content: Identifying suitable locations for municipal solid waste (MSW) disposal represents a critical challenge for sustainable environmental management. This study investigates the spatial suitability of landfill sites across three northern Iranian provinces, Gilan, Mazandaran, and Golestan—and evaluates the potential for integrated waste management using a GIS-based Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) integrated with the TOPSIS method. The methodology integrates a GIS-based weighted overlay analysis for initial suitability screening with an AHP-derived weighting scheme and a TOPSIS-based ranking framework to evaluate candidate sites and classify counties as waste senders, receivers, or independent entities. This research innovatively incorporates "waste footprint" metrics, per capita generation rates and population density, to refine capacity assessment and the decision matrix. A comprehensive set of environmental, socio-economic, and physical-technical criteria was overlaid and weighted. Based on the suitability analysis and projected waste flow patterns, counties were categorized as "senders," "receivers," or "independent" entities. The findings reveal significant spatial variations: Golestan province possesses the largest extent of high-priority land (72,195 ha), followed by Mazandaran (21,960 ha) and Gilan (10,999 ha). Spatial patterns indicate that Gilan exhibits highly centralized suitability, dominated by Rudbar county (>91%), with notable potential for cross-provincial synergy between Rudsar (Gilan) and Ramsar (Mazandaran). In Mazandaran, plain-based counties act as receivers for waste from foothill regions, whereas western areas face severe constraints. Conversely, Golestan demonstrates a balanced distribution, with eastern counties hosting the majority of suitable land (>82%). Despite regional environmental constraints, the study concludes that integrated waste management, driven by inter-county and inter-provincial cooperation, offers a viable pathway for sustainability. This research provides a quantitative, spatially explicit framework to guide policymakers toward more efficient, equitable and environmentally sound MSW management strategies in Northern Iran.

title: A Systemic Functional Analysis of Modality and Power Relations in Bilingual Corporate Sustainability Discourse
source: Journal of English Language and Linguistics
summary: This study investigates modality as a linguistic resource for constructing reality and negotiating power relations in bilingual sustainability reports produced by SET50-listed companies in Thailand. Drawing on Systemic Functional Linguistic
content: This study investigates modality as a linguistic resource for constructing reality and negotiating power relations in bilingual sustainability reports produced by SET50-listed companies in Thailand. Drawing on Systemic Functional Linguistics (SFL), particularly Halliday and Matthiessen’s interpersonal metafunction framework and Humphrey, Droga, and Feez’s modality analysis model, the study employs a mixed-methods approach integrating Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) to examine English and Thai versions of Chairman and CEO messages in 2024 annual reports. Using maximum variation purposive sampling, three companies from different industrial sectors were selected: Thai Oil, Krungthai Bank, and CP ALL. The findings reveal systematic cross-linguistic differences in modality use. English texts predominantly employ higher modality through nominalization, modal adverbials, and modal nouns, projecting institutional certainty, strategic commitment, and organizational credibility aligned with international investor expectations. In contrast, Thai texts rely more heavily on medium and lower modality, particularly through modal verbs such as cha (จะ) and samat (สามารถ), reflecting relational communication strategies, linguistic hedging, and cultural preferences for interpersonal flexibility. Across all sectors, both languages largely avoid coercive high-modality modal verbs, suggesting a shift from authoritarian discourse toward collaborative stakeholder engagement. The study demonstrates that modality functions not only as a grammatical resource but also as a cross-cultural mechanism for managing legitimacy, trust, and power relations in corporate sustainability communication. The findings contribute to research on SFL, corporate discourse, and sustainability reporting in emerging market contexts. Future research should explore cross-linguistic modality shifts across broader ASEAN corporate texts to inform international communication strategies.

title: Attitude, perceived neighborhood accessibility, and travel behavior: A triad of dynamic relationships
source: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
summary: Travel attitude and perceived accessibility are considered influential factors of travel behavior, yet their dynamic relationships remain underexplored. This study investigates the dynamic relationships among travel behavior, travel attitud
content: Travel attitude and perceived accessibility are considered influential factors of travel behavior, yet their dynamic relationships remain underexplored. This study investigates the dynamic relationships among travel behavior, travel attitude, and perceived neighborhood accessibility, using a four-wave panel dataset from the Netherlands. Employing a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model, this study separates stable between-person differences from within-person temporal variations, enabling longitudinal interpretations of how these three factors are associated with each other over time. Three mode-specific models (car, public transportation, and bicycle) are estimated to reveal mode-dependent dynamics. Travel behavior, attitude, and perceived neighborhood accessibility exhibit mode-specific stability, with stable car use, stable perceived neighborhood accessibility for public transportation and bicycle, and a clear disruption in public transportation use in the 2020 wave. Across modes, effects of travel behavior on attitude and perceived neighborhood accessibility are generally stronger than subjective effects on behavior, indicating that changes in travel behavior more often precede changes in perceptions than the reverse. Perceived neighborhood accessibility is closely linked to car attitude in a potential car-oriented lock-in process, shows an initial positive association with later public transportation use, and has weak and inconsistent longitudinal associations with bicycle use. These results extend the traditional attitude–behavior relationship by examining perceived neighborhood accessibility as a distinct construct and showing that its longitudinal associations with travel behavior and attitude vary across modes and periods. This study contributes essential longitudinal insights into promoting sustainable modal shifts.

title: Venezuela Frente al ODS 13 "Acción por el Clima": Desafíos y Oportunidades
source: Revista Venezolana de Economía y Ciencias Sociales
summary: Este ensayo analiza la situación de Venezuela frente al Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS) 13, relativo a la “Acción por el clima”. Con este propósito, se examinan sus metas, los compromisos asumidos por las instituciones públicas y la
content: Este ensayo analiza la situación de Venezuela frente al Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS) 13, relativo a la “Acción por el clima”. Con este propósito, se examinan sus metas, los compromisos asumidos por las instituciones públicas y las capacidades del país para adap­tarse a los efectos del cambio climático. Aunque los informes internacionales señalan que la acción climática es el único ODS que muestra tendencias favorables en Venezuela, se advierte que la disminución de las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero (GEI) no es resultado de una política planificada de transición energética. Por el contrario, parece responder al co­lapso de la producción petrolera y a la profunda contracción económica que se vive desde 2013. Ante la escasez de datos oficiales recientes y dado que Venezuela solo ha presentado un Informe Nacional Voluntario ante la ONU (2016), la investigación evalúa la capacidad na­cional para afrontar desastres socionaturales mediante el Índice de Resiliencia de la Lloyd’s Register Foundation. Los resultados revelan una situación crítica: en 2023, Venezuela ocupó el puesto 126 entre 142 países a nivel mundial. Esta vulnerabilidad se vincula con la precariedad de servicios básicos como el agua y la electricidad, la limitada cobertura de los sistemas de alerta temprana y la profunda desconfianza de la población hacia las instituciones públicas. En conclusión, aunque Venezuela cuenta con un marco constitucional y lineamientos programá­ticos vinculados al ecosocialismo, aún carece de las capacidades operativas e institucionales necesarias para desarrollar una adaptación climática efectiva.

title: Farmers' Climate-Risk Investment Decisions: FICCS Experimental Data and Analysis Code
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository contains the experimental dataset and Python analysis scripts associated with the study “Without outcome feedback, farmers lock into non-investment: Implications for climate services from a repeated-decision simulator.” The
content: This repository contains the experimental dataset and Python analysis scripts associated with the study “Without outcome feedback, farmers lock into non-investment: Implications for climate services from a repeated-decision simulator.” The study examines adaptation and mitigation investment decisions among 50 farmers from Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh, India, using the Farmers’ Interactive Climate Change Simulator (FICCS). Participants completed 20 repeated decision trials under feedback and no-feedback conditions. The repository includes the analysis dataset, Excel workbook, Python scripts for statistical and predictive analyses, and documentation for reproducing the study's results.

title: Experimentation in co-creation for local green solutions
summary: Co-creation is promoted as a collaborative governance approach that can facilitate innovative local green solutions. Experimentation is integral to the green promise of co-creation; experiments create processes and spaces where multi-sector
content: Co-creation is promoted as a collaborative governance approach that can facilitate innovative local green solutions. Experimentation is integral to the green promise of co-creation; experiments create processes and spaces where multi-sector actors can share and develop knowledge, and explore practical solutions. This article interrogates ideas and practices of experimentation in green co-creation, and argues that current understandings are narrowly focused on tools, and lack consideration of the contexts and risks of experiments for sustainability. To expand knowledge on the practical forms and trajectories of experimentation in co-creation, insights are drawn from six cases of green co-creation from around the world. The analysis finds that while collaborative experimentation can be purposefully ‘designed-in’, using plans and tools, it can also unfold via more emergent or adaptive processes. The article calls on advocates of co-creation to be more attentive to the role and limits of designed experimentation for sustainability.

title: Soil Erodibility Factor (K) in Santa Fe Province, Argentina — EPIC Method (0–20 and 0–30 cm)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Descripción Este conjunto de datos proporciona dos mapas georreferenciados del factor de erosionabilidad del suelo (K) para la provincia de Santa Fe, Argentina, estimados utilizando el enfoque empírico EPIC para dos intervalos de profundida
content: Descripción Este conjunto de datos proporciona dos mapas georreferenciados del factor de erosionabilidad del suelo (K) para la provincia de Santa Fe, Argentina, estimados utilizando el enfoque empírico EPIC para dos intervalos de profundidad del suelo: 0–20 cm y 0–30 cm. Los mapas se elaboraron para respaldar las evaluaciones regionales de la posible erosión hídrica mediante la Ecuación Universal Revisada de Pérdida de Suelo (RUSLE), la planificación de la conservación del suelo, el análisis territorial y la modelización ambiental espacial. Metodología La erosionabilidad del suelo se estimó utilizando la formulación empírica EPIC y la información espacial del suelo derivada de SoilGrids, incluyendo la textura del suelo y el carbono orgánico del suelo. Se consideraron dos intervalos de profundidad: 0–20 cm y 0–30 cm. Su inclusión permite comparar la influencia del intervalo de profundidad del suelo seleccionado en las estimaciones regionales de K. Las superficies resultantes representan estimaciones de la erosionabilidad del suelo basadas en modelos y no deben interpretarse como mediciones directas de K sobre el terreno. Contenido del conjunto de datos SF_K_EPIC_020cm_PROVINCIA_5347.tif: Factor de erosionabilidad del suelo K basado en EPIC para el intervalo de profundidad de 0 a 20 cm. SF_K_EPIC_030cm_PROVINCIA_5347.tif: Factor de erosionabilidad del suelo K basado en EPIC para el intervalo de profundidad de 0 a 30 cm. Cada archivo GeoTIFF viene acompañado de un archivo de estilo QGIS correspondiente (.qml). Especificaciones geoespaciales Cobertura geográfica: Provincia de Santa Fe, Argentina. Sistema de referencia de coordenadas: POSGAR 2007 / Argentina 5 (EPSG:5347). Resolución espacial: 250 × 250 m. Dimensiones del ráster: 1499 columnas × 2849 filas. Valor sin datos: −9999. Formatos de archivo: GeoTIFF y QGIS QML. Aplicaciones y limitaciones Los mapas están destinados a evaluaciones a escala regional de la erosionabilidad del suelo, la identificación de patrones espaciales, la planificación de la conservación del suelo y la integración con la erosividad de la lluvia (R) y los factores topográficos (LS) en la modelización basada en RUSLE. La incertidumbre surge de la información subyacente sobre el suelo, la representación de la profundidad del suelo, la resolución espacial, el método de estimación empírica y la heterogeneidad geográfica. Las propiedades derivadas de SoilGrids proporcionan estimaciones regionales espacialmente continuas, pero no reemplazan las observaciones de suelo georreferenciadas, los análisis de laboratorio ni la caracterización del perfil del suelo específica del sitio. El factor K describe la susceptibilidad del suelo a la erosión según el modelo empírico adoptado. No cuantifica de forma independiente la pérdida de suelo. La evaluación de la erosión hídrica potencial requiere la integración con los demás factores relevantes de RUSLE. Creador Mario E. Monti , Ingeniero Agrónomo, Máster en Gestión de Recursos Naturales, Equ

title: Secuencias didácticas sobre cambio climático y conciencia ecológica en estudiantes de segundo de bachillerato: un estudio cuasiexperimental
summary: El cambio climático plantea a la escuela el reto de formar estudiantes que comprendan sus causas y efectos y que estén dispuestos a actuar frente a ellos. Este estudio determinó el efecto de secuencias didácticas de Biología sobre cambio cl
content: El cambio climático plantea a la escuela el reto de formar estudiantes que comprendan sus causas y efectos y que estén dispuestos a actuar frente a ellos. Este estudio determinó el efecto de secuencias didácticas de Biología sobre cambio climático en la conciencia ecológica de estudiantes de segundo de Bachillerato. Se empleó un enfoque cuantitativo, de tipo aplicado y alcance explicativo, con diseño cuasiexperimental de pretest y postest y grupo de control no equivalente. Participaron los 43 estudiantes de segundo de Bachillerato de la Unidad Educativa Paltas, provincia de Loja: el grupo experimental (n = 21) desarrolló cuatro secuencias didácticas centradas en las causas, los efectos locales, la mitigación y la adaptación al cambio climático, y el grupo de control (n = 22) recibió la enseñanza habitual. La conciencia ecológica se midió con un cuestionario de 25 ítems tipo Likert organizado en las dimensiones cognitiva, afectiva, conativa y activa (α = 0,93). En el pretest los grupos fueron equivalentes (p = 0,972). En el postest, el grupo experimental obtuvo una media de 90,62 frente a 77,68 del grupo de control, con una diferencia estadísticamente significativa (t = 4,02, p < 0,001) y un tamaño del efecto grande (d = 1,23); el mayor cambio se observó en la dimensión cognitiva.

title: When goals collide: National-level practitioner perspectives on traffic safety and other transport-policy objectives
summary: This study examines how national-level practitioners perceive synergies and tensions between traffic safety and other transport-policy objectives in Sweden. Although the burden of traffic accidents in Sweden has decreased, the decline has p
content: This study examines how national-level practitioners perceive synergies and tensions between traffic safety and other transport-policy objectives in Sweden. Although the burden of traffic accidents in Sweden has decreased, the decline has plateaued in recent years. To maintain momentum towards the 2030 interim targets and Vision Zero—the ambition that no one should be killed or seriously injured within the transport system—it may be necessary to utilise a more integrated approach and emphasise traffic safety’s potential to contribute to broader societal challenges, such as climate and equality. Seventeen strategists and experts at the Swedish Transport Administration were interviewed, representing traffic safety, health, mobility, environmental sustainability, social sustainability, and national planning. The interviews were analysed using qualitative content analysis, with the conflict-management triangle applied to interpret the substantive, procedural, and relational dimensions of the tensions. Participants generally supported a more integrated approach but raised questions about its reciprocity and implications for traffic safety’s established focus. The analysis identified interactions that were described as predominantly synergistic, broadly compatible desired outcomes with implementation tensions, and persistent measure-specific trade-offs. Many tensions arose not from incompatible goals but from how broadly supported objectives were operationalised through measures, standards, evidence requirements, appraisal practices, and the distribution of benefits and disadvantages. The findings show that traffic safety’s alignment with sustainability and mobility depends on how it is operationalised. Advancing a more integrated approach requires distinguishing between tensions that may be addressed through changes in implementation and persistent trade-offs that need to be recognised and managed transparently.

title: A spatially explicit framework for evaluating resource performance across heterogeneous land-use grid cells
summary: Resource performance evaluation examines how resource inputs are transformed into desirable outcomes while minimising undesirable consequences. Resource performance is spatially uneven, as resource inputs and outputs vary with the human act
content: Resource performance evaluation examines how resource inputs are transformed into desirable outcomes while minimising undesirable consequences. Resource performance is spatially uneven, as resource inputs and outputs vary with the human activities and natural processes associated with different land-use types. Existing evaluations either aggregate performance across administrative units or focus on isolated land-use types. These approaches provide limited evidence on within-region heterogeneity, within-type variability, and temporal changes of resource performance. A land-use-based evaluation framework for resource performance is therefore developed in this study. Each land-use grid cell is treated as a decision-making unit. A data envelopment analysis (DEA) model is applied to evaluate the relative resource performance across spatially heterogeneous land-use grid cells. The framework is applied to the water, energy, and food systems of the Yellow River Basin in 2010, 2015, and 2020 and compared with a city-scale evaluation. The results reveal: (1) spatial variability of relative resource performance within regions; (2) spatial variability of resource performance within a land-use type across locations; and (3) temporal changes in the spatial distribution of resource performance across the three benchmark years. The framework provides a transferable basis for spatially explicit resource management across heterogeneous landscapes.

title: Modeling groundwater salinity evolution and mitigation strategies under stochastic climate forcings in the Comacchio coastal aquifer (Italy)
summary: Coastal aquifers are increasingly threatened by salinization due to climate change and sea level rise, particularly in low-lying Mediterranean environments where groundwater systems are strongly connected with saline and brackish surface wa
content: Coastal aquifers are increasingly threatened by salinization due to climate change and sea level rise, particularly in low-lying Mediterranean environments where groundwater systems are strongly connected with saline and brackish surface water bodies. This study presents a three-dimensional variable-density groundwater flow and transport model of the Comacchio coastal aquifer (northern Italy), integrating climatic datasets to investigate groundwater future response to climate forcings. A monthly transient simulation for the period 2024–2025 was calibrated and validated against piezometric heads and salinity observations, achieving R 2 values up to 0.98 for heads and 0.97 for salinity concentrations. After this step, predictive simulations up to 2050 incorporated climate change projections, including sea-level rise together with stochastic evapotranspiration and recharge derived from a climate models ensemble. Climate uncertainty and unresolved spatial heterogeneity were propagated through the model via DEM-conditioned stochastic downscaling combined with quantile-based climate forcing scenarios. Results indicate that most of the early salinity increase is related to transient model adjustment, whereas climate change acts as a persistent driver of additional salinity by reducing meteoric recharge and enhancing saline inflows and redistribution of pre-existing saline groundwater by 2050. Simulated mitigation scenarios based on upscaled irrigation areas and increased irrigation loadings proved effective in preventing and delaying groundwater salinization.

title: ASSESSMENT OF RURAL FARMERS’ PERCEPTION AND ADOPTION OF CLIMATE SMART AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES IN KWAMI LOCAL GOVERNMENT AREA, GOMBE STATE, NIGERIA
source: Journal of Renewable Agricultural Technology Research
summary: The study assessed rural farmers’ perception and adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in Kwami Local Government Area of Gombe State, Nigeria. It examined the socio-economic characteristics of the respondents, assessed the percep
content: The study assessed rural farmers’ perception and adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in Kwami Local Government Area of Gombe State, Nigeria. It examined the socio-economic characteristics of the respondents, assessed the perception of rural farmers on climate change and climate Smart Agricultural practices, identified the types of climate smart agricultural practices and technologies used and the factors affecting the adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in the study area. A multi-stage sampling technique was employed to sample 277 respondents and the data obtained were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and multiple regression model. The result revealed that majority (75%) of the respondents were within 20-50 years of age, 88.1% were males and most (96.4%) of them were aware about climate change. It further shows that predominant (59.9%) of the respondents had source of information on climate smart agricultural practice through the; fellow farmers, 78.3% of them perceived an increased in temperature and most (92.8%) of them indicated pesticide as smart practice used. The regression result of factors that influence crop yield before and after adoption indicates that the values of R-square were 0.84 and 0.86 which implies 84% and 86% variation in yields before and after adoption respectively were due to variables included in the models, while the remaining 16% and 14% for before and after adoption respectively were accounted by error whereas age, educational level, farm size, extension contact, manure application and farming experience were significantly influences yield before adoption while extension contact, farm size, use of pesticide and manure, early maturing seeds were significantly influenced crop yield after adoption. The study concluded that the understanding of the severity of climate change help farmers in devising effective adaptation strategies, and recommended that more assistance from government is required, especially in sensitizing farmers and supporting them to reduce the cost of adaptation.

title: Compensating for the Removal of Article 22 of the CSDDD Through the Judicial Development of Pre-existing Climate Due Diligence
summary: Article 22 of the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) operationalized broader principles of ‘climate due diligence’ (CDD) in corporate accountability. Although the European Union removed this provision, this article arg
content: Article 22 of the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) operationalized broader principles of ‘climate due diligence’ (CDD) in corporate accountability. Although the European Union removed this provision, this article argues that CDD is not extinguished given its pre-existence. After clarifying that due diligence entails best efforts rather than an obligation of result, this article makes two points: at the state level, the removal raises difficult questions of reconciliation with the CDD duty to regulate corporate actors. At the corporate level, courts may require individual corporations to make best efforts to mitigate climate change, using global climate objectives as relevant benchmarks under tort law or statutory due diligence frameworks, as the rulings in Milieudefensie and Notre Affaire à Tous illustrate. However, it is unclear whether courts can fully compensate for the removal of Article 22, an economy-wide regulation which required transition planning from all corporate actors within its scope.

title: Scaling up power-to-X value chain s: a multi-actor perspective to economic sustainability
summary: Power-to-X (PtX) technologies, which convert renewable electricity into green hydrogen and further into its derivatives, are among the most credible pathways for decarbonizing hard-to-abate industrial sectors. Despite strong policy support
content: Power-to-X (PtX) technologies, which convert renewable electricity into green hydrogen and further into its derivatives, are among the most credible pathways for decarbonizing hard-to-abate industrial sectors. Despite strong policy support and technically mature components, large volumes of planned PtX capacity remain stranded at the pilot stage, suggesting that the barriers to large-scale deployment are economic and institutional rather than technological. Existing research, dominated by techno-economic analyses that assess cost efficiency at the system level, has largely overlooked the multi-actor nature of PtX value chains and how risk evolves across the lifecycle of their assets. This dissertation develops an integrated, multi-actor and lifecycle-oriented understanding of the economic sustainability of PtX value chains, addressing three research questions on the drivers and barriers to actor participation, the advancement of economic sustainability from a multi-actor perspective, and the asset lifecycle risk sources shaping implementation. The dissertation is article-based, combining a systematic literature review, an abductive multiple case study of PtX actors interpreted through the Multi-Level Perspective, a cashflow-based multi-actor techno-economic method developed through Design Science Research, and a case study of asset lifecycle risk in hydrogen-integrated steelmaking. The results show that PtX value chains can scale when three interdependent layers, the value chain, the actor, and the asset, are simultaneously in balance: aggregate competitiveness, viable business cases for each required value chain actor, and manageable collective risk across asset lifecycles. Profitability is often distributed asymmetrically among actors, and risk is distributed unevenly over the asset lifecycle and the value chain. The dissertation contributes an integrative theoretical framework, the Path2X modeling method, and managerial and policy guidance for structuring economically sustainable and scalable multi-actor PtX value chains.

title: Livestock Waste Management and Biodigester-Based Resource Recovery in the Akaki Sub-Basin, Ethiopia
source: CGSPace A Repository of Agricultural Research Outputs (Consultative Group for International Agricultural Research)
summary: Livestock waste management is a growing concern in Ethiopia’s Akaki sub-basin, which drains Addis Ababa and the surrounding areas. This study looked at how livestock waste is managed in the sub-basin and the problems involved. It also devel
content: Livestock waste management is a growing concern in Ethiopia’s Akaki sub-basin, which drains Addis Ababa and the surrounding areas. This study looked at how livestock waste is managed in the sub-basin and the problems involved. It also developed a business plan for a cooperative-based biodigester as a circular economy solution. The study combined a representative household survey in Addis Ababa and Sheger City with six focus group discussions. Findings show that livestock waste management is largely unregulated, and few households use improved practices. The most common approaches are dumping, discharging waste into rivers, and traditional composting, which mostly happens in the dry season. These practices pollute the environment and miss the chance to recover useful resources from waste. On average, households keep about 12 dairy livestock. Small-scale farmers keep 5 to 10 adult animals, and large-scale farmers keep 10 to 20. Biodigesters were identified as a feasible way to recover resources, turning livestock waste into biogas and organic fertilizers. Three small- to medium-scale models were considered suitable under different conditions: private individual-farmer, cooperative-based, and independent youth-led. Large-scale centralized biodigesters were also identified as a possible option for integrated waste management across the wider area. Farmers strongly preferred the cooperative-based model, so a business plan was developed for it. The plan covers cooperative structure, feedstock and other resource needs, expected outputs, and financial viability. Based on direct financial benefits, the analysis found a benefit-cost ratio of 1.3, which indicates that the biodigester is viable under the assumptions used. Wider benefits, such as less pollution, better public health, resource recovery, and jobs, were not quantified. Cooperative biodigesters offer a promising way to improve livestock waste management and advance the circular economy in the Akaki sub-basin.

title: Surface-mediated reduction of Cr(VI) on aged polyamide microplastics: Leaching behavior and interaction mechanisms
summary: Microplastics (MPs) can interact with toxic heavy metals, thereby altering their environmental behavior and ecological effects. This study investigated the adsorption–transformation and leaching behavior of Cr(VI) by UV-aged polyamide micro
content: Microplastics (MPs) can interact with toxic heavy metals, thereby altering their environmental behavior and ecological effects. This study investigated the adsorption–transformation and leaching behavior of Cr(VI) by UV-aged polyamide microplastics (UV-PA) under the combined effects of light irradiation and dissolved oxygen (DO). SEM-EDS and XPS analyses demonstrated that photo-oxidative conditions increased the surface roughness of UV-PA, promoted amide bond cleavage, and generated more oxygen-containing functional groups, thereby enhancing Cr(VI) adsorption. CV, EIS, pH, and ORP analyses further confirmed that UV-PA possessed Cr(VI) reduction capability, with the highest electron transfer efficiency observed under UV+aerobic conditions. Probe compound experiments revealed that the generation of O was maximized under these conditions, effectively promoting Cr(VI) reduction. In the presence of Cr(VI), dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and total nitrogen (TN) concentrations increased to 15 mg/L and 6 mg/L, respectively, indicating that Cr(VI) accelerated the leaching of UV-PA. EEM-PARAFAC analysis showed that the leachates were mainly composed of protein-like and humic-like substances, while NO was detected only in Cr(VI)-containing systems. LC–MS results further indicated that Cr(VI) could selectively cleave PA molecular chains and promote the formation of specific organic compounds.
