title: ESG PRINCIPLES BUSINESS REPORTING ISSUES IN THE AUDIT CONTEXT
summary: Auditing as a science has evolved over the centuries, overcoming the demands of the times and constantly expanding its functions. Currently, the audit organizations is faced with the challenges of assessing the reliability of sustainable de
content: Auditing as a science has evolved over the centuries, overcoming the demands of the times and constantly expanding its functions. Currently, the audit organizations is faced with the challenges of assessing the reliability of sustainable development information. On the one hand, the sustainable development information published in organizations is not yet clearly regulated, on the other hand, the audit interpretations of ESG developments are still awaiting their regulation. Currently, IFRS-S international financial reporting standards related to sustainable development are in force, which clearly outline the information requirements that also apply to businesses operating according to ESG principles. At the same time, it is also worth noting that the approaches by which the credibility of this reporting will be assessed have not yet been clarified from an audit perspective. Determining the format of the audit report is also important, since ESG reporting includes not only financial but also non-financial information. The article makes recommendations aimed at improving the formation of sustainable development audit conclusions, which enable stakeholders to form a reasonable opinion about the sustainable development information published by organizations and make sound decisions.

title: Conceptualizing a Work-Readiness Teacher Training Curriculum for Education 4.0 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Systems Thinking and Design Thinking Approach
summary: Purpose: This study proposes a Work-Readiness Teacher Training Curriculum to prepare teachers in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) and emerging Education 4.0 demands. Methodology: A descriptiv
content: Purpose: This study proposes a Work-Readiness Teacher Training Curriculum to prepare teachers in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) and emerging Education 4.0 demands. Methodology: A descriptive literature review synthesized peer-reviewed studies, policy documents, evaluation reports, and theoretical works published mainly from 2000 to 2025. Sources were identified through ERIC, JSTOR, SAGE journals, Google Scholar, and institutional sources and analysed using qualitative thematic synthesis. Findings: The synthesis identified professional, pedagogical, digital, socio-emotional, collaborative, problem-solving, creative, entrepreneurial, and adaptive competencies as important for 4IR-oriented teacher preparation. The proposed curriculum integrates these competencies through learner-centered, experiential, collaborative, inquiry-based, and context-responsive pedagogies. Systems Thinking provides a holistic perspective on education-to-employment linkages, while Design Thinking supports participatory and iterative curriculum development. Unique Contribution to Theory, Policy and Practice: The study proposes a context-responsive teacher training framework linking teacher competencies, innovative pedagogy, and workforce requirements. The framework may inform teacher education, professional development, and curriculum reform aimed at strengthening education-to-employment alignment in the DRC.

title: From Integrity to Entangrity: A Diffractive Reading of a Sustainability Manager’s Entangled Subjectivity
summary: Integrity is one of the key concepts in business ethics and has conventionally been understood as a quality of the autonomous ethical subject. Relational approaches have challenged this view by showing how integrity is shaped through everyd
content: Integrity is one of the key concepts in business ethics and has conventionally been understood as a quality of the autonomous ethical subject. Relational approaches have challenged this view by showing how integrity is shaped through everyday human encounters and organisational practices. Feminist post-humanist thinking takes this challenge further by questioning human-centred understandings of ethical subjectivity itself. Drawing on Karen Barad’s articulations of entanglement and diffraction, this paper explores what happens to integrity when ethical subjectivity is understood as emerging through more-than-human entanglements. Through a collaborative diffractive reading of theoretical discussions on integrity and entanglement, alongside a sustainability manager’s empirical account, we trace three recurring patterns of entangled subjectivity: sensing that something is not right, carrying the weight of responsibility, and aspiring towards more liveable entanglements. These patterns show how integrity comes to matter through embodied, affective, material, and organisational entanglements. Building on these patterns, this research develops ‘entangrity’ as a relational and lively reconceptualisation of integrity, understood as an expression of entangled subjectivity. Entangrity renews questions surrounding ambiguous ethical subjectivities by pointing to the way ethical tensions are dwelt within, rather than ‘navigated’. It also exemplifies how diffractive reading can enable conceptual development whilst keeping different and even ontologically distinct theoretical perspectives in play. Thus, we invite thinking-with the possibilities of what ethical subjectivity and response-ability might become as posthuman business ethics continues to be developed.

title: Traditional Food Items of SHGs: A Study of their Marketing Channel and Constraints in the Context of Assam, India
source: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
summary: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) play a vital role in promoting marketing of traditional food items and empowers rural communities through small-scale food processing, local marketing, and sustainable micro-enterprises. Commercialisation of traditio
content: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) play a vital role in promoting marketing of traditional food items and empowers rural communities through small-scale food processing, local marketing, and sustainable micro-enterprises. Commercialisation of traditional food of Assam would certainly help a section of its people to become economically independent and also enable them to maintain a decent standard of living. Based on both primary and secondary sources of information, this paper investigated the marketing channel of traditional food items and problems faced by the SHGs while marketing these products. Ninety (90) members from 18 purposively selected SHGs of Assam were interviewed to collect required information and Garrett’s Ranking Technique was used to rank the problems faced by the SHG members while marketing the traditional food items. The study identified three channels of marketing traditional food items of which use of retail channel is the most. The tough competition from the other products produced by big companies has been found as the most significant problem faced by the SHGs with the highest Garrett mean value followed by limited financial resources and lack of knowledge on proper packaging.

title: Towards a dose-response model for weather-induced colour change in Norway spruce wood: a weather dose concept, universal curve of weathering and response function
source: European Journal of Wood and Wood Products
summary: The aim of this study is to develop a dose-response modelling framework to quantify the influence of geographical location on the visual appearance of wood materials under outdoor exposure. For this purpose, spruce wood specimens were expos
content: The aim of this study is to develop a dose-response modelling framework to quantify the influence of geographical location on the visual appearance of wood materials under outdoor exposure. For this purpose, spruce wood specimens were exposed to natural weathering at 18 different locations for a period of 12 months. Climatic parameters, including solar radiation, air temperature, relative humidity, precipitation, and wind speed, were selected as dose variables. The CIE L* coordinate was adopted as the response variable to represent changes in surface appearance. Among the CIE colour coordinates, L* exhibits a monotonic and continuous behaviour during weathering, which makes it particularly suitable for dose-response modelling. Therefore, the relationship between cumulative climatic dose and colour change was described using a universal first‑order asymptotic solution. The dose has been defined as a cumulative weighted sum of normalized weather indicators. The weighting coefficients associated with individual climatic variables and their interactions, together with the kinetic reaction constant, were treated as decision variables. These parameters were optimized by minimizing the mean squared error between measured and predicted CIE L* values. The high coefficient of determination of the dose response model R² = 0.89 suggests that the variability in CIE L* is sufficiently explained by the model. The proposed approach enables the development of location-sensitive predictive models for assessing long-term colour alterations of wood surfaces under varying climatic conditions.

title: The Rhetorical Power of Political Slogans: Perceived Influence on Public Opinion and Governance
source: Journal of Media Journalism & Mass Communication
summary: Political slogans shorten political identities, policy statements and emotional appeals through a condensing process so that they can be easily recognized and repeated. This study investigates the perception of the audiences about the impac
content: Political slogans shorten political identities, policy statements and emotional appeals through a condensing process so that they can be easily recognized and repeated. This study investigates the perception of the audiences about the impact of slogans on public opinion, political judgment and political governance. Two hundred and eight respondents participated in an on-line, cross-sectional, quantitative survey with a structured questionnaire comprising of 15 closed-ended questions. Descriptive percentages were used as the sample is very small and cannot be generalized to the population level as this is a non-probability sample. Results show good perceived effects. The percentage of respondents who said that slogans impact the perceptions about the government policy was around three quarters, whereas 85.7% said that slogans impact the assessment of the effectiveness and trustworthiness of the government. 75.0% thought that emotional language had a greater influence than neutral language, and 92.8% said that the emotional impact had partial or full significance when assessing the impact of slogans. The media, amplification and historical context were also considered significant. Meanwhile, 92.1% agreed that slogans can be too simple to formulate complex political issues and can lead to misleading the public. The findings thus suggest that slogans are ambivalent democratic tools, because they can be used to draw attention, create a sense of community and mobilize involvement, but they also can replace affective surety for policy specifics. The study provides a theoretically integrated interpretation, based on the ELM, SIT, agenda-setting and framing. Its findings remain tentative and could be studied with larger-probability samples and experiments and by longitudinal design.

title: Associations of protected area residence with nutritional status and nutrient intake among school-aged children in northeastern Cambodia
summary: This study assessed nutritional status and nutrient intake among 500 children aged 6–12 years living inside and outside protected areas in northeastern Cambodia. Adjusted models showed no significant association between residence in protect
content: This study assessed nutritional status and nutrient intake among 500 children aged 6–12 years living inside and outside protected areas in northeastern Cambodia. Adjusted models showed no significant association between residence in protected areas and anthropometric Z-scores. However, wild food collection was negatively associated with height-for-age Z-scores (HAZ) and body mass index-for-age Z-scores (BAZ), while household size was positively associated with HAZ. Most children in both groups did not meet the Cambodian recommended dietary allowances for energy and nutrients. These findings highlight the need for further research and context-specific strategies to improve nutrition among school-aged children in remote communities.

title: NatureScaping™: An integrated framework to address modern world environmental challenges
summary: Environmental challenges such as biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, water insecurity, climate change and unsustainable land use are outcomes of interacting ecological, social, economic and institutional processes. Addressing these ch
content: Environmental challenges such as biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, water insecurity, climate change and unsustainable land use are outcomes of interacting ecological, social, economic and institutional processes. Addressing these challenges requires planning approaches that consider landscape functions and human well-being together. This paper proposes NatureScaping™ as a place-based, science-informed and participatory framework for organising the assessment, planning, implementation and adaptive management of interventions in human-influenced landscapes. The framework is informed by six Rajasthan precedents documented through a combination of practitioner accounts, project materials and institutional conservation experience: the Abu Model; Chak Ramnagar/Project Boond-V; the Dholpur Model; Bharatpur–Keoladeo conservation and water-management experience; Rajputana’s Shakuntalam; and nature-integrated planning associated with Vizrama Eco-Resorts. These precedents are treated as antecedent practices that informed conceptual development of the framework. NatureScaping™ proposes four assessment dimensions, namely ecological, social, economic and institutional and a seven-stage intervention cycle: LISTEN, MAP, RESTORE, INTEGRATE, EMPOWER, MEASURE and ADAPT. Eight potential application domains are identified, ranging from cities and watersheds to biodiversity corridors, campuses, hospitality, rural settlements and knowledge institutions. The framework is positioned as complementary to established approaches including ecological restoration, biodiversity conservation, Nature-based Solutions and integrated landscape management. Its potential alignment with selected Sustainable Development Goals and the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework is discussed as a planning opportunity rather than evidence of target achievement. The framework remains a conceptual and operational proposition requiring prospective pilot applications, standardised indicators, independent monitoring and comparative evaluation.

title: Reconciling Customary Law with Constitutional Guarantees: Women’s Property and Inheritance Rights in Nigeria
source: American Journal of Society and Law
summary: Succession and inheritance represent the core legal mechanisms through which the rights, duties, obligations and property of a deceased individual are transferred to surviving beneficiaries, including heirs, spouses and relatives, in accord
content: Succession and inheritance represent the core legal mechanisms through which the rights, duties, obligations and property of a deceased individual are transferred to surviving beneficiaries, including heirs, spouses and relatives, in accordance with established legal principles. In Nigerian jurisprudence, succession and inheritance are inextricably linked concepts governing post mortem assets distribution. However, customary law in Nigeria has historically been anchored in deeply entrenched patriarchal traditions and the customary rule of male primogeniture, which systematically position women as subordinate to men and disentitle female offspring and wives from inheriting immovable property. A significant paradigm shift occurred with the landmark Supreme Court of Nigeria 2014 decision in Ukeje v. Ukeje, wherein the apex court invalidated discriminatory customary rules for failing the statutory repugnancy test and violating constitutionally guaranteed fundamental rights to equality and freedom from discrimination enshrined under the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Although this historic judicial pronouncement affirmed equal property inheritance rights for women regarding immovable estate, judicial activism alone remains insufficient to dismantle deep seated cultural biases or guarantee widespread socio legal compliance across rural communities in Nigeria. This study adopts the doctrinal method of legal research and critically analyses the existing legal framework governing female gender rights and property inheritance under Nigerian customary law. The paper found that most of the cultural hereditary practices are firmly entrenched and intertwined with religion or superstition and high rate of illiteracy, especially among the rural population. In addition, rules of customary law are unwritten, uncertain and undefined and as such difficult to be enforced. The research contends that judicial precedents must be accompanied by comprehensive policy reforms and targeted public sensitization to fully operationalise, enforce and institutionalise gender equity in property succession in Nigeria.

title: ÖZBEKISTONDA YAŞIL IQTISODIYOTGA ÖTIŞ JARAYONIDAGI ÖZGARIŞLAR VA RIVOJLANIŞ ISTIQBOLLARI
summary: Maqolada Özbekistonda yaşil iqtisodiyotga ötiş jarayonidagi özgarişlar qayta tiklanuvçi elektr energetikasi, suv resurslaridan foydalaniş, çiqindilarni boşqariş, yaşil moliyalaştiriş va iqlimga moslaşuv misolida örganildi. Normativ hujjatla
content: Maqolada Özbekistonda yaşil iqtisodiyotga ötiş jarayonidagi özgarişlar qayta tiklanuvçi elektr energetikasi, suv resurslaridan foydalaniş, çiqindilarni boşqariş, yaşil moliyalaştiriş va iqlimga moslaşuv misolida örganildi. Normativ hujjatlar va rasmiy hisobotlar qiyosiy hamda tavsifiy usulda tahlil qilindi. 2024–2025-yillarda quyoş va şamol elektr stansiyalarida işlab çiqariş 4,86 mlrd kVt·soatdan 10,50 mlrd kVt·soatga, ularning jami elektr işlab çiqarişdagi uluşi 5,96 foizdan 12,11 foizga oşgani aniqlandi. 2025-yil yakunida suv tejovçi texnologiyalar 2,6 mln gektarni qamrab oldi. Çiqindi xizmatlari böyiça aholi va mahalla kesimidagi qamrov tafovuti, şuningdek, Orolböyi va Toşkent misolida ekologik natijalarni ölçaş masalalari körib çiqildi. Tahlil natijalari asosida elektr tarmoqlarini modernizatsiya qiliş, suv sarfini ölçaş va yaşil loyihalarning ekologik samarasini oçiq hisobotlarda yoritiş böyiça takliflar işlab çiqildi.

title: The informational effects of institutional crowding: Evidence from zombie election monitors
summary: How do governments manage the political costs of scrutiny from international organizations? We introduce the concept of institutional crowding , whereby governments simultaneously affiliate with multiple international bodies sharing the sam
content: How do governments manage the political costs of scrutiny from international organizations? We introduce the concept of institutional crowding , whereby governments simultaneously affiliate with multiple international bodies sharing the same ostensible mandate but varying in capacity and value commitments. We develop this argument in the context of international election observation, where governments facing higher domestic electoral risk benefit from inviting not only credible election observation missions (EOMs) but also ‘zombie’ groups whose assessments are anticipated to be more lenient. The primary effects of this strategy are informational: When multiple EOMs are present, the resulting range of evaluations gives media greater latitude to present international assessments favorably, or to obscure negative findings behind conflicting signals. Using original media-based data on the presence and assessments of EOMs across 621 executive elections in 114 countries from 1998 to 2018, we show that governments facing greater domestic electoral risk — particularly where opposition strength is growing and previous elections sparked protests — are more likely to host multiple EOMs of varying quality. Notably, this pattern is not driven by autocracies alone, reflecting a broader political survival logic that cuts across regime types. Consistent with our theoretical mechanism, we show that elections hosting multiple EOMs are associated with more positive depictions of election observer assessments in the media, even as divergence among different missions increases. Beyond election observation, the logic of institutional crowding travels to any domain where institutional proliferation creates opportunities for information management.

title: Coaching and Inclusive Lifelong Learning within an AI-Supported Skilling System
summary: This paper first explains how skilling systems improve workers' and firms' capacity to adapt to changing labour markets by helping them develop adequate skills, measure progress, and reward practice in distinct tasks. Coaching within skilli
content: This paper first explains how skilling systems improve workers' and firms' capacity to adapt to changing labour markets by helping them develop adequate skills, measure progress, and reward practice in distinct tasks. Coaching within skilling systems supports managers and employees in improving performance, managing workplace challenges and transitions, pursuing life goals, and developing leadership skills. Lifelong learning helps employees and employers remain successful within their own job and generally in the labour market. Inclusive lifelong learning within a skilling ecosystem ensures that continuous education, upskilling, and reskilling opportunities reach all people regardless of background, age, or employment status. AI-supported skilling systems, like those described in this paper, use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve coaching and lifelong learning by delivering personalized coaching and removing traditional barriers to education. This also helps to identify skill gaps and adapt educational content. Multilingual translations and real-time language conversions using AI make training more inclusive and available to marginalized groups and those with basic skill gaps. AI-based chatbots and mentors support "learning in the flow of work," continuous coaching and mentoring. AI can identify industry trends, and upskilling or reskilling programs can align with existing needs. Inclusive skilling ecosystems, which are also described in the paper, use artificial intelligence to support learning, job training, and career growth fairly and are open to all people.

title: Climate Challenges and Sustainable Development in Iraq: National Strategies for Adaptation and Alignment with the UN 2030 Agenda
summary: Purpose: This study examines Iraq’s escalating climate vulnerabilities, water scarcity, rising temperatures, desertification, and pollution, while assessing the effectiveness of national adaptation strategies in alignment with the UN 2030 A
content: Purpose: This study examines Iraq’s escalating climate vulnerabilities, water scarcity, rising temperatures, desertification, and pollution, while assessing the effectiveness of national adaptation strategies in alignment with the UN 2030 Agenda, particularly Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 6, 7, and 13. Recent assessments confirm that Iraq is among the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries, particularly to heatwaves, drought and water stress (Atlantic Council, 2023). Design/Methodology/Approach: A descriptive-analytical and comparative methodology is employed using national reports, international databases, and institutional assessments to evaluate governance, finance, and institutional responses. Iraq’s national adaptation strategy builds on a sequence of UNDP-supported diagnostics and capacity-building programmes (UNDP, 2022). Findings: Results reveal significant adaptation gaps caused by weak coordination, fragmented data, and heavy reliance on external funding, which undermine resilience-building and sustainable development goals. Original/Value of the Paper: The research provides an integrated policy-oriented roadmap that links Iraq’s national climate challenges with global sustainability frameworks, highlighting governance reforms, green finance tools, and energy transition strategies. This approach is consistent with the sustainable development paradigm linking poverty reduction, environmental protection and inclusive growth (Sachs, 2015). Research Limitations/Implications: The analysis is limited by insufficient national data systems and the conditional nature of Iraq’s international commitments. Updated diagnostics underscore the need to link climate action with economic reform and institutional modernisation (World Bank, 2024). Practical Implications: Recommendations include establishing a National Climate Council, scaling renewable energy, modernising irrigation, and integrating climate justice into policy frameworks. Achieving Iraq’s energy-transition targets will require major investment in grid modernisation and renewable capacity (IEA, 2025). Keywords: Climate Change; Iraq; Climate Policy; Resilience; SDGs; Adaptation Strategies; Water Security; Energy Transition; Climate Governance; Climate Justice; 2030 Agenda Citation: Thari H. H. (2026): Climate Challenges and Sustainable Development in Iraq: National Strategies for Adaptation and Alignment with the UN 2030 Agenda. World Sustainable Development Outlook 2025, Vol. 21, pp. 353-365. WASD: London, United Kingdom.

title: Youth as Catalysts of Climate Action: Advancing Environmental Sustainability and the SDGs Beyond 2030
summary: Purpose: This paper analyses how youth-driven initiatives are reshaping global climate governance and sustainable development beyond the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) timeline. It examines the mechanisms, barriers, and instituti
content: Purpose: This paper analyses how youth-driven initiatives are reshaping global climate governance and sustainable development beyond the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) timeline. It examines the mechanisms, barriers, and institutional conditions affecting youth influence in climate decision-making. Design/Methodology/Approach: Using a conceptual and comparative case study framework, the paper systematically reviews youth-led climate initiatives (2011-2025) from the Global South and North. It assesses mobilisation, agenda setting, co-production of policy, climate finance, and litigation as key pathways, supported by empirical cases from Africa, Europe, and Asia. Findings: Youth activism has shifted from symbolic protest to substantive participation in governance. However, tokenism, institutional exclusion, and resource inequality persist. The study identifies three key barriers, institutional, political, and socio-economic, and presents scalable solutions such as co-governance mandates and equitable finance models. Original/Value of the Paper: The paper reframes youth as strategic co-architects of sustainability rather than peripheral actors, integrating ethical, political, and practical dimensions of intergenerational equity. Practical Implications: Embedding youth participation in law, simplifying access to finance, and aligning education with green-economy pathways are essential to institutionalising intergenerational collaboration and accelerating equitable climate action beyond 2030. Keywords: Youth Empowerment; Climate Governance; Intergenerational Equity; Climate Justice; Sustainable Development Goals; Renewable Energy Transition; Global South; Adaptation; Mitigation; Environmental Policy Citation: Alzain, H. M. and Majuto, K. (2025): Youth as Catalysts of Climate Action: Advancing Environmental Sustainability and the SDGs Beyond 2030. In Ahmed, A. (Ed.): United Nations: What Next After 2030 Agenda and SDGs. World Sustainable Development Outlook 2025, Vol. 21, pp. 367-385. WASD: London, United Kingdom.

title: Analysis of PT BNI’s Financial Health for 2021-2024 Based on The RGEC Method and Its Implications for Bank Sustainability
source: Advances in economics, business and management research/Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research
summary: This study aims to analyze the financial health of PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BNI) using the RGEC method, which consists of four main components: Risk Profile, Good Corporate Governance (GCG), Earnings, and Capital. In addition
content: This study aims to analyze the financial health of PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BNI) using the RGEC method, which consists of four main components: Risk Profile, Good Corporate Governance (GCG), Earnings, and Capital. In addition, this research explores the relationship between BNI’s RGEC assessment and its commitment to sustainable banking. The method employed is descriptive quantitative, utilizing secondary data derived from BNI’s annual financial reports for the period 2021–2024. The findings show that BNI’s financial health improved significantly over the period. (1) The Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratio declined from 3.7% to 2.0%, indicating better credit risk management. The Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR) remained within the “Fairly Healthy” range at 96%. (2) GCG maintained a consistent score of 2 (Healthy), reflecting transparency, accountability, and sound governance practices. (3) Earnings performance also improved, with Return on Assets (ROA) increasing from 1.3% to 2.4%, and (4) the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) averaged 20.59%, classified as “Very Healthy.” Overall, BNI’s composite health score rose from “Healthy” (80–84%) to “Very Healthy” (88%). These results demonstrate that BNI’s financial soundness aligns with the key principles of sustainable banking, particularly in economic and governance aspects. Strong financial fundamentals allow the bank to support green financing, manage risks effectively, and contribute to long-term financial system stability. It highlights that consistent improvement in RGEC indicators can serve as a foundation for Enhancing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance in the banking industry.

title: Factors for Ensuring Sustainable Economic Growth Through the Development of Green Economy in Uzbekistan
source: Advances in economics, business and management research/Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research
summary: This study examines the role of green economy development in fostering sustainable economic growth in the Republic of Uzbekistan, focusing on renewable energy expansion, water use efficiency, industrial energy savings, green investment, and
content: This study examines the role of green economy development in fostering sustainable economic growth in the Republic of Uzbekistan, focusing on renewable energy expansion, water use efficiency, industrial energy savings, green investment, and green employment. Employing a mixed-method approach that combines a systematic literature review, comparative cross-country analysis, and empirical assessment of national statistical indicators for 2023, the study develops a Green-based Sustainable Growth Index (GSI) through a linear regression model incorporating five normalized variables: Renewable Energy Ratio, Water Use Efficiency, Energy Saving Efficiency, Green Investment Index, and Employment in Green Sectors. The calculated GSI value of 0.4377 indicates that Uzbekistan currently operates at approximately 43.8% of its green growth potential, reflecting an intermediate stage of transformation. Results reveal that energy saving efficiency and renewable energy share are the most influential drivers, jointly accounting for over 63% of the index, while green investment and green employment exert comparatively moderate effects. Water use efficiency, particularly in agriculture, also emerges as a strategically significant factor given Uzbekistan’s water scarcity challenges. These findings confirm the effectiveness of current national policies, including the Green Energy Strategy 2023–2030, while identifying priority areas for further intervention. The study concludes that achieving the national target of 30% renewable electricity generation by 2030 requires coordinated cross-sectoral policies, expanded green financing, and sustained international cooperation, and proposes the GSI as a practical monitoring tool for tracking progress toward inclusive, climate-resilient economic growth.

title: Elizabeth Stuart's self-fashioning and dynastic ambitions : an analysis of the importance of visual and material culture
summary: This thesis is an investigation of how an elite noblewoman in seventeenth-century Europe was able to fashion an image for herself to further her dynastic ambitions at a time of considerable political and religious turmoil. By analysis of vi
content: This thesis is an investigation of how an elite noblewoman in seventeenth-century Europe was able to fashion an image for herself to further her dynastic ambitions at a time of considerable political and religious turmoil. By analysis of visual and material culture and corroborated by epistolic evidence I show how Elizabeth Stuart (1596-1662), daughter of James I of England and VI of Scotland, Electress of the Palatinate and sometime Queen of Bohemia, crafted and maintained a majestic self-image throughout a forty-year exile in the Dutch Republic against substantial financial and political odds. I demonstrate how she took the lead from the strong female role models of her mother Queen Anne of Denmark and her godmother Queen Elizabeth I on the importance of appearance, dress and jewellery to construct an identity. I explore how she gained agency in widowhood by building networks of friends and diplomatic relations to garner support and raise money for her cause to regain the Palatinate lands for her family. By commissioning portraits of herself and her family (living and dead), in which she represented herself as historical and biblical heroines and by staging politically astute theatrical masques Elizabeth was able to substantiate her royal position and exert influence to aid her cause. Her strategic choice to dress continually in black allowed her to show the strengths of a male ruler whilst maintaining the socially accepted virtues of an ideal royal consort. Her astute exploitation of the printed image was key to the dissemination of her message. I illustrate that Elizabeth was well-schooled in the importance of soft-diplomacy and the art of gift-giving that allowed her to build an influential court in The Hague and sustain advantageous pan-European relationships. Although her official status as monarch was short-lived the majestic image she crafted and maintained her whole life, in large part through deployment of visual and material culture, was instrumental to her success in achieving the restitution of the Palatinate lands (albeit partially) to her son. Through the study of the visual and material culture my research deepens our understanding of seventeenth-century society, ideas and values. By applying a broad interdisciplinary methodology, the study shows the myriad ways that a female monarch could use visual imagery and objects to fashion an identity to further both her political and religious ambitions. It also recognises Elizabeth’s underappreciated contribution to the restoration of the Stuart monarchy.

title: Models for agroforestry and related land uses – development and applications
summary: Agroforestry (AF) and related land use (LU) models are increasingly important for understanding complex interactions between ecological processes, socio-economic drivers, LU dynamics, and to support science-based decision-making for sustain
content: Agroforestry (AF) and related land use (LU) models are increasingly important for understanding complex interactions between ecological processes, socio-economic drivers, LU dynamics, and to support science-based decision-making for sustainable land management. Using systematically selected 103 academic articles; we trace and discuss modelling development and applications. Publications on AF modelling have increased notably since 2020, although LU modelling remains dominant. Seven model categories were identified. The results showed that optimization/economic models were the most frequent (22.3%), followed by cellular/spatially explicit (20.4%), process-based (19.4%), integrated or hybrid (15.5%), and empirical/statistical models (13.6%), while agent-based (4.9%) and machine learning models (3.9%) were less common. Methodological developments indicate a shift toward integrated frameworks incorporating ecological, economic, and social dimensions, although multi-scale integration remains limited. While many models have decision support systems (DSS) potential, only a small proportion (6%) are operationalized into formal DSS tools. Key challenges include data scarcity, inadequate validation, scale mismatches, model complexity, sensitivity to parameter choice, insufficient representation of farmer behavior and institutional factors. Specific gaps persist in validation, uncertainty handling, cross-system integration, and policy relevance. Established and emerging technologies, including GIS, remote sensing, and artificial intelligence, offer significant potential to advance model accuracy, scalability, and real-world applicability, although their combined application remains limited. Future research should enhance the quality of input data, integrate multiple model types, rigorous calibration, stronger alignment with decision-making needs, and improve stakeholder relevance. This is crucial for advancing evidence-based policy to support resilient AF systems and sustainable LU planning under dynamic global conditions.

title: Static and ensemble-dependent thermodynamics of the strain-induced parity anomaly in gapped graphene
summary: Static strain in sublattice-gapped graphene generates a pseudomagnetic field that couples with opposite signs to the two valleys. The opposite Dirac chiralities then make the zeroth pseudo-Landau level shift in the same direction in both va
content: Static strain in sublattice-gapped graphene generates a pseudomagnetic field that couples with opposite signs to the two valleys. The opposite Dirac chiralities then make the zeroth pseudo-Landau level shift in the same direction in both valleys. At fixed chemical potential, all higher levels cancel in the grand-potential difference between opposite pseudofields, leaving an equilibrium response determined by the zeroth level. The static charge response forms a thermally broadened plateau within the gap. Near a band edge, field reversal changes the entropy by the Boltzmann constant times the natural logarithm of two per unsplit zeroth-level state. The heat-capacity difference has two lobes near each band edge at fixed chemical potential and a finite low-temperature edge value at fixed carrier number. A finite gate capacitance interpolates between these limits. We propose differential calorimetry and quantum-capacitance measurements on gated, gapped graphene. The protocol switches between opposite trace-free triaxial strain patterns at zero applied magnetic field and records the differences as the gate voltage is swept through the band edges.

title: Water stress as a pathway between climate vulnerability and fiscal sustainability in the European Union
summary: Climate vulnerability can affect fiscal sustainability through both direct effects and environmental pressures. This study examines whether water stress provides a pathway linking climate vulnerability to fiscal sustainability in the EU-27
content: Climate vulnerability can affect fiscal sustainability through both direct effects and environmental pressures. This study examines whether water stress provides a pathway linking climate vulnerability to fiscal sustainability in the EU-27 over 2003–2023. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first EU-wide studies to examine water stress as a mediating mechanism between climate vulnerability and fiscal sustainability. A Fiscal Sustainability Index is constructed using Principal Component Analysis, and panel estimation methods are used to examine the main relationships while accounting for dynamic effects and potential endogeneity. Structural Equation Modeling is then used to assess whether water stress mediates the relationship between climate vulnerability and fiscal sustainability. The results show that greater climate vulnerability is associated with higher water stress, and higher water stress is associated with lower fiscal sustainability. The indirect effect of climate vulnerability on fiscal sustainability through water stress is negative and statistically significant, indicating significant mediation. However, the direct effect of climate vulnerability on fiscal sustainability is not statistically significant in the dynamic estimation. This suggests that water stress may be an important pathway through which climate vulnerability affects fiscal sustainability. The results point to the need for closer integration of climate adaptation, water management, and fiscal planning in the EU. Improving water infrastructure, increasing water-use efficiency, maintaining fiscal buffers, and accounting for climate- and water-related risks in public investment and budgeting can help strengthen fiscal sustainability, particularly in countries exposed to higher climate and water stress.

title: Valorization of Vineyard Pruning Residues through Biochar Production: Effects on Soil Productivity, Long-Term Carbon Sequestration, and Circularity in Viticulture
source: Advances in Environmental and Engineering Research
summary: Viticulture generates large volumes of woody pruning residues that are commonly burned or landfilled, so that both their material value and their potential as a carbon sink are lost. Pyrolytic conversion into biochar has been proposed as a
content: Viticulture generates large volumes of woody pruning residues that are commonly burned or landfilled, so that both their material value and their potential as a carbon sink are lost. Pyrolytic conversion into biochar has been proposed as a route that simultaneously addresses waste management, soil productivity, and climate mitigation. This review assesses how far the evidence supports these three claims for biochar made from vineyard prunings. A narrative synthesis of 55 sources (2014-2026), identified in Scopus and by targeted supplementary searches, was organized along five axes. Quantitative values were extracted, checked for internal consistency, and classified as measured, proxy, or modeled. Between 300 and 600°C, mass yield fell from 45.2% to 32.3% and total carbon rose from 66.5% to 77.9%, while the fixed carbon recovered per unit of feedstock was unchanged (25 g per 100 g). In vineyard field trials (8-44 t ha-1), none of which is documented as having used vineyard-pruning biochar, yield responses ranged from none to +66% and soil organic carbon rose by 36% to more than 200%. Biochar recovered after 15 years retained an inertinite fraction of 93.7% (94.8% initially), whereas century-scale persistence (60-100%) is model-based. Meta-analytic sequestration rates were 8.96 Mg CO2-eq ha-1 yr-1 for biochar and 2.82 for returned prunings. On-farm prunings would supply only 0.6-0.9 t biochar ha-1 yr-1, and a cost-benefit analysis found negative net present value without carbon-credit revenue. Vineyard-pruning biochar is a credible option for circular, climate-smart viticulture, provided that process control, site-specific management and supportive economics are in place. Field trials with the vineyard-derived material, industrial-scale life-cycle assessment and vineyard-specific economics are the principal gaps.

title: Provincial and Sectoral CO₂ Emissions and Provincial Indicators in China, 2005–2022
summary: This dataset covers 30 province-level regions in China, excluding Tibet, from 2005 to 2022. The Excel workbook contains eight worksheets. Two report annual direct CO₂ emissions across seven sectors and annual provincial CO₂ emission totals,
content: This dataset covers 30 province-level regions in China, excluding Tibet, from 2005 to 2022. The Excel workbook contains eight worksheets. Two report annual direct CO₂ emissions across seven sectors and annual provincial CO₂ emission totals, both in megatonnes. The other six report resident population, energy intensity, urbanisation rate, the tertiary sector’s share of nominal GDP, population density, and the share of coal in energy use. Emissions data were obtained from the Center for Carbon Neutrality (CCN) dataset. Provincial indicators were compiled from the China Statistical Yearbook and provincial statistical yearbooks.

title: Lattice Distortion and Defect-Associated Functional Properties of Ba₁₋ₓFeₓCrO₃ Perovskites: Linking Microstructural Disorder with Optical and Dielectric Responses
summary: Ba₁₋ₓFeₓCrO₃ (x = 0.1–0.4) perovskite ceramics were synthesized by the conventional solid-state route to investigate their composition-dependent structural, optical, dielectric, and electrical properties. X-ray diffraction (XRD) indicated a
content: Ba₁₋ₓFeₓCrO₃ (x = 0.1–0.4) perovskite ceramics were synthesized by the conventional solid-state route to investigate their composition-dependent structural, optical, dielectric, and electrical properties. X-ray diffraction (XRD) indicated an orthorhombic perovskite framework across the investigated compositions, with no detectable secondary crystalline phases within the measurement limits. Five XRD line-broadening methods yielded model-dependent coherent-domain size estimates of approximately 31–78 nm, highlighting the sensitivity of microstructural parameters to the analytical approach. Complementary FTIR spectra provided supporting information on metal–oxygen lattice vibrations. Tauc analysis showed a decrease in the estimated optical band gap from 3.22 to 2.99 eV with increasing Fe content, indicating a composition-dependent shift in the optical absorption edge. Dielectric measurements revealed frequency-dependent responses, with BFC-1 exhibiting comparatively lower dielectric loss. AC conductivity also varied with composition and frequency, with BFC-3 and BFC-4 showing higher conductivity at high frequencies. A non-monotonic conductivity feature around 1–1.5 MHz was observed, although its underlying mechanism could not be established. Within the adopted structural model, Fe is considered predominantly associated with the Ba/A-site; however, partial B-site incorporation cannot be excluded because direct site-occupancy characterization was not performed. Possible oxygen nonstoichiometry and associated defect contributions remain unverified. Overall, the results reveal composition-dependent correlations among structural, optical, dielectric, and electrical properties while highlighting the need for further structural and transport characterization to clarify the underlying mechanisms.

title: Beyond lead: iodide leaching as an overlooked environmental pathway from perovskite solar cells
summary: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are the fastest-evolving photovoltaic technology; however, their great promise is challenged by lead content and potential pollutant release. While previous studies have focused primarily on lead, the environme
content: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are the fastest-evolving photovoltaic technology; however, their great promise is challenged by lead content and potential pollutant release. While previous studies have focused primarily on lead, the environmental behavior of other constituents remains poorly understood. We evaluate chemical leaching from conventional lead-based PSCs and newly developed low-lead PSCs (50% lead reduction) under environmentally relevant leaching conditions. The test showed encapsulated intact devices released negligible metals, demonstrating effective containment. Fractured (damaged) devices released measurable lead; however, the concentrations remained below the U.S. EPA hazardous waste threshold (5 ppm). Most notably, we discovered substantial iodide leaching from damaged PSCs, with concentrations reaching up to 3 ppm, several orders of magnitude higher than typical iodide levels in surface water. This is a critical finding, as iodide is a precursor for highly toxic iodinated disinfection byproducts (I-DBPs) formed during drinking water treatment. This pathway represents a previously overlooked environmental risk associated with PSCs. Our findings highlight the need to expand environmental risk assessments of PSC technologies beyond heavy metals to include halide release and its implications for drinking water to ensure a truly sustainable solar energy transition.

title: Direct conversion of industrial off gas to green carbonate and H2
summary: Decarbonization of steel and coal-chemical industries, a major CO 2 emitter, is crucial for achieving carbon neutrality. Escaping the grip of combustion, separation and hydrogenation, is a formidable challenge on the path to industry net-ze
content: Decarbonization of steel and coal-chemical industries, a major CO 2 emitter, is crucial for achieving carbon neutrality. Escaping the grip of combustion, separation and hydrogenation, is a formidable challenge on the path to industry net-zero carbon emissions. Here we suggest a non-hydrogenated new route for directly converting industrial off-gas and methanol into green dimethyl carbonate (DMC) and clean H 2 via coupling off-gas conversion and methanol upgrading. In the design, the CO in off-gas reacts with the byproduct H 2 O generated during CO 2 -to-DMC synthesis, continuously pulling DMC synthesis equilibrium forward following Le Chatelier's principle, while yielding H 2 as a valuable co-product. This process exhibits significant advantages in carbon retention, cost-effectiveness and H 2 production, and covers various compositions of steelmaking and gasification off-gases. Notably, a DMC yield of 76.8 mmol/g with > 98% selectivity is obtained on the new route, which represents 7.8-fold higher than conventional sole CO 2 route, together with 74.6 mL/g H 2 . The strategy converts the industrial off-gases utilization from a costly separation and high H 2 demand challenge into a reaction advantage for simultaneous DMC synthesis and H 2 production, providing a new approach for industrial decarbonization and MeOH upgrading.

title: Legal governance of blue carbon credits in China’s voluntary carbon market
summary: Introduction Blue carbon credits are increasingly advocated as a way to finance the conservation and restoration of coastal ecosystems; however, the development of carbon markets does not necessarily guarantee credible climate mitigation. T
content: Introduction Blue carbon credits are increasingly advocated as a way to finance the conservation and restoration of coastal ecosystems; however, the development of carbon markets does not necessarily guarantee credible climate mitigation. This article examines the legal governance of blue carbon credits in China's national voluntary greenhouse gas emission reduction market. Methods Combining doctrinal legal analysis, institutional comparison, and qualitative risk assessment, the study operationalizes a six-part framework covering additionality, quantification accuracy, permanence, leakage control, prevention of double counting, and independent validation, verification, and transparency. This analysis reviews China's CCER regulatory framework and the Ecological and Environmental Code, along with the methodologies for mangrove afforestation, coastal salt marsh restoration, and seagrass bed restoration. Results It finds that existing rules establish basic safeguards for project eligibility, carbon accounting, third-party verification, and centralized registration; however, they do not fully address the interaction between pre-existing conservation obligations and additionality, baseline uncertainty, long-term reversal liability, cross-mechanism information coordination, and ecological accountability. These gaps show that neither formal compliance with regulatory requirements nor project registration is sufficient to ensure the environmental integrity of issued credits. Discussion The article recommends more specific eligibility requirements, stronger monitoring, reporting, and verification, enforceable reversal-risk management, better-coordinated information systems, and clearer legal responsibilities that integrate carbon credit governance with marine ecosystem protection. The article concludes that effective blue carbon governance must move beyond market expansion and toward life-cycle legal safeguards that can secure credible and durable mitigation outcomes while also supporting marine ecosystem conservation.

title: THE COMPREHENSIVE CHINESE REFERENCE ON SUSTAINABLE FINANCE AND ESG GOVERNANCE REGULATORY MECHANISMS, LEGAL ACCOUNTABILITY, AND IMPLEMENTATION PATHWAYS TOWARD DUAL CARBON GOALS 2026 TO 2060
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: THE COMPREHENSIVE CHINESE REFERENCE ON SUSTAINABLE FINANCE AND ESG GOVERNANCE: REGULATORY MECHANISMS, LEGAL ACCOUNTABILITY, AND IMPLEMENTATION PATHWAYS TOWARD DUAL CARBON GOALS 2026 TO 2060 This monumental reference establishes the definiti
content: THE COMPREHENSIVE CHINESE REFERENCE ON SUSTAINABLE FINANCE AND ESG GOVERNANCE: REGULATORY MECHANISMS, LEGAL ACCOUNTABILITY, AND IMPLEMENTATION PATHWAYS TOWARD DUAL CARBON GOALS 2026 TO 2060 This monumental reference establishes the definitive legal, regulatory, and operational framework for sustainable finance and ESG governance in China. Structured across five major parts and nine specialized appendices, it provides legislators, corporate boards, financial institutions, and international investors with actionable tools for navigating China's historic transition toward peak carbon by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Part One covers legislative foundations including the Ecological Civilization doctrine and the unified 2025 Green Finance Catalogue. Part Two addresses corporate governance and the Chinese Sustainability Disclosure Standards. Part Three examines legal accountability under the groundbreaking 2026 Ecological and Environmental Code. Part Four analyzes sustainable financial instruments including central bank green lending and the China National Emissions Trading System. Part Five explores the international dimension, focusing on the Green Belt and Road Initiative and cross-border compliance. The nine appendices deliver groundbreaking practical tools: a quadrilingual glossary, legislative registry, interoperability mapping between Chinese, European, and international standards, governance templates, quantitative carbon footprinting equations, and a strategic guide for Middle East and Africa markets. The work includes nine comprehensive reference matrices covering regulatory architecture, disclosure and materiality, financial engineering, governance and liability, green financial technology, China versus European Union comparison, implementation roadmap, Green Belt and Road Initiative, and key performance indicators. The 100-indicator China ESG Maturity Scorecard enables institutions to precisely diagnose compliance gaps and develop multi-year corrective action plans. This reference transforms the complex Chinese regulatory landscape into a navigable, enforceable, and strategically actionable architecture for the global green transition. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24483011

title: Sustainable food consumption as policy objective: where does the European Union stand?
summary: Sustainable food consumption is a priority of the EU's Farm to Fork strategy, yet gaps remain in understanding consumer sustainable choices. Drawing on Eurobarometer data, this paper analyzes environmental perceptions of respondents by soci
content: Sustainable food consumption is a priority of the EU's Farm to Fork strategy, yet gaps remain in understanding consumer sustainable choices. Drawing on Eurobarometer data, this paper analyzes environmental perceptions of respondents by socioeconomic characteristics, categorizing consumers into two groups based on food purchasing priorities. Probit results show that higher education and better economic conditions increase the likelihood of prioritizing health and environmental concerns. However, pro-environmental factors are not uniformly understood across groups. Therefore, awareness campaigns emerge as effective drivers of sustainable consumption, suggesting policymakers should expand existing initiatives, develop long-term educational programs, and tailor interventions to consumer segments.

title: Fault Diagnosis of Natural Ester Oil Filled Transformers Using Mechanism Inspired Structured Tokens and Auxiliary Supervision with Full Window Trends
summary: The pursuit of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality has increased demand for environmentally friendly natural ester oil-filled transformers. Abnormal dissolved gas levels can compromise their operational reliability, making dissolved gas an
content: The pursuit of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality has increased demand for environmentally friendly natural ester oil-filled transformers. Abnormal dissolved gas levels can compromise their operational reliability, making dissolved gas analysis (DGA) and fault diagnosis essential to stable operation. This study proposes a three-class diagnostic method that integrates mechanism-inspired structured tokens, a full-window trend residual, and auxiliary supervision of thermal and discharge components to diagnose thermal, discharge, and combined electrical–thermal faults in natural ester oil-filled transformers. Using 900 training sequences and 120 test sequences, with 0 min as the normal baseline and evaluation at 10–60 min, the method achieved mean accuracies of 93.47% and 93.19% at 20 and 30 min, respectively, across six runs. These values exceeded those of the model without auxiliary supervision using the same observation window by 0.56 and 1.25 percentage points. The benefits of auxiliary supervision were not observed at every diagnostic time point. In a fixed reference run, the accuracies at successive time points were 95.83%, 95.83%, 93.33%, 92.50%, 90.00%, and 87.50%. At later time points, missed combined faults were predominantly classified as discharge faults, whereas all 40 discharge-fault sequences were correctly identified at every time point. The study provides a theoretical basis and technical support for DGA-based diagnosis of natural ester oil-filled transformers and may contribute to their operational stability. However, generalization across experimental batches and the benefits of component-level supervision require further validation.

title: Nationwide high-resolution assessment reveals the underestimated carbon sink of Chinese parks
summary: Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and promote carbon neutrality, parks, as Nature-based solutions, are often underestimated in their collective carbon sequestration function. Here we establish a high-resolutio
content: Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and promote carbon neutrality, parks, as Nature-based solutions, are often underestimated in their collective carbon sequestration function. Here we establish a high-resolution (30 -meter) carbon accounting framework for 8,137 parks across mainland China from 2010 to 2020, incorporating previously overlooked small parks. We show that parks constitute a substantial carbon sink. The total carbon sequestration based on Net Primary Productivity of parks nationwide reaches 52.7 million tonnes of carbon in 2020. Within the 5,425 urban parks, large parks exceeding 100 hectares (hm²) contribute over 90% of the total urban park sequestration, whereas parks of 10–50 hm 2 drive the 2010–2020 shift from carbon sources to sinks. Medium and small sized parks show greater synergy between carbon sequestration and recreation services, informing locally tailored planning.

title: Carbon quota adequacy analysis and regulation strategy for coordinated electricity–carbon scheduling
summary: High renewable penetration and the carbon‐peaking and carbon‐neutrality goals subject power‐system operation scheduling to the dual pressure of maintaining power and energy balance while ensuring carbon quota adequacy. Random renewable fluc
content: High renewable penetration and the carbon‐peaking and carbon‐neutrality goals subject power‐system operation scheduling to the dual pressure of maintaining power and energy balance while ensuring carbon quota adequacy. Random renewable fluctuations propagate to source‐side carbon emissions through thermal‐power adjustments, making deterministic annual quota decomposition unsuitable for risk control in coordinated electricity–carbon plans. This study proposes a carbon quota adequacy analysis method and dynamic regulation strategy. First, a carbon‐emission deviation uncertainty model expresses source‐side deviations as a linear function of renewable disturbances. Linear random-vector mapping and finite-lag covariance propagation yield the first and second central moments of cumulative deviations and a component quota adequacy index. Second, an intertemporal inventory state equation exploits the long settlement cycle of carbon quotas to convert static component constraints into mutual-aid constraints across time windows while conserving the total quota. Third, a distributionally robust coordinated electricity–carbon scheduling model represents adequacy risk by a chance constraint over a carbon-emission deviation ambiguity set. A generation-order table endogenously determines chronological marginal-unit emission factors, enabling a second-order cone reformulation. Case studies reveal the complex effects of quota adequacy conditions on electricity–carbon decisions and verify that the method improves operation–plan quota adequacy under source-side emission uncertainty.

title: Safeguarding the Last Mile in the Transition to New Energy: Innovations in High-Value Recycling of Retired New-energy Devices
source: 中国科学院院刊：英文版
summary: The Research Center for High-Value Recycling of Emerging Solid Wastes (RC-HRESW) at the Guangzhou Institute of Energy Conversion focuses on the circular utilization of retired new-energy devices, thereby contributing to China’s energy trans
content: The Research Center for High-Value Recycling of Emerging Solid Wastes (RC-HRESW) at the Guangzhou Institute of Energy Conversion focuses on the circular utilization of retired new-energy devices, thereby contributing to China’s energy transition and resource sustainability, and supporting its carbon-neutrality goals. Building on a thermochemical deconstruction-reconstruction framework for organic solid wastes, the Center has developed full-chain technologies covering intelligent dismantling, clean thermochemical conversion, and high-quality metal recovery. This article summarizes the Center’s recent advances in the recycling of retired new-energy devices, together with over 20 engineering demonstration projects for solid waste recycling. By integrating fundamental research, key technologies, large-scale demonstration, and major infrastructure projects, the Center is striving to establish a circular new-energy system and to provide scalable solutions for clean, low-carbon development.

title: What Sustainability Disclosures Disclose
summary: Sustainability disclosures are the backbone of corporate sustainability efforts. If stakeholders want companies to compete over how “good” they are for society, they need a way to see what companies are doing and trying to do. But these dis
content: Sustainability disclosures are the backbone of corporate sustainability efforts. If stakeholders want companies to compete over how “good” they are for society, they need a way to see what companies are doing and trying to do. But these disclosures have been widely criticized for their lack of credibility and comparability. To improve them, nonprofits and companies have developed voluntary reporting frameworks that many firms have now adopted and that have informed mandatory disclosure regulations. These critiques and regulatory debates have proceeded, however, without basic facts about what these disclosures contain and whether voluntary tools help. Answering these questions has been difficult because of the non‐standardized nature of these disclosures. This project overcomes these barriers through the use of large language models and provides the most comprehensive analysis of sustainability disclosures to date. We evaluate over 15,000 sustainability disclosure documents issued by more than 2100 Russell 3000 firms spanning 1998–2023. We construct measurable indicators based on characteristics that stakeholders have identified as relevant: specificity, quantitative evidence, fluff (~puffery), negative news, and data table and figure counts. Five patterns stand out. First, sustainability reporting and the adoption of external assurance and voluntary frameworks (GRI, SASB, TCFD, CDP, SBTi) surged after 2015. Second, firms often adopt multiple frameworks at once, and adoption is sticky. Third, as reporting mainstreamed, reports became less specific, less quantitative, and fluffier. Fourth, longer‐reporting firms produce more concrete reports (more specific and quantitative, with more tables and less fluff) with more negative news, but these differences largely reflect which firms began reporting early and broad calendar trends rather than learning by doing. Fifth, frameworks show mixed and non‐uniform associations with our measures—some with less fluff, more negative news, and more tables, but also with lower quantitative density. We find no consistent evidence that adoption leads to improvements along the dimensions we study. The results underscore the potential importance of the rules vs. standards dichotomy in sustainability reporting. Firms unraveled across rule‐like margins (whether to report or to adopt a framework) but stalled on more standard‐like asks (e.g., for more concrete reporting), for which performance is harder to evaluate.

title: A signaling game for green bonds
summary: We build a signaling game model of a firm’s decision to acquire a costly green label which enables it to emit a green bond. A greenium may compensate it for the incurred cost. That cost is higher for non-green firms. With an investor that p
content: We build a signaling game model of a firm’s decision to acquire a costly green label which enables it to emit a green bond. A greenium may compensate it for the incurred cost. That cost is higher for non-green firms. With an investor that prefers a clean environment and dislikes being fooled into believing in a fabricated green label, there are equilibria featuring green bonds by either both firm types, only the green firm or neither. The type of equilibrium we can expect hinges predominantly on the relative size of the greenium. In green bond pooling equilibria, the non-green firm optimally acts as a greenwasher. Allowing side payments undermines stability of all equilibria where a green label is acquired. A neutral rather than a green investor considerably decreases the number of conceivable equilibria, as does uncertainty about the investor type. The equilibria of the baseline model are preserved if we allow two investors, a green and a neutral one, to decide on their respective purchase of the bond sequentially. Lastly, if investors hold all market power, no green labels will be observed at all.

title: Modified Switched‐Inductor DC/DC Converter With Wide Voltage Conversion Range for Fuel Cell Vehicles
source: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications
summary: To match the voltage of high power fuel cell stacks (300–600 V) with the vehicle DC bus (400–800 V) in fuel cell vehicles (FCVs), this paper proposes a modified switched‐inductor buck‐boost converter. By redesigning the switched‐inductor im
content: To match the voltage of high power fuel cell stacks (300–600 V) with the vehicle DC bus (400–800 V) in fuel cell vehicles (FCVs), this paper proposes a modified switched‐inductor buck‐boost converter. By redesigning the switched‐inductor impedance network and adding two capacitors (C 1 and C 2 ), the converter enables parallel charging and series discharging of both the inductors and capacitors, with continuous input current and a common ground, greatly extending the voltage conversion range. After steady‐state analysis and comparison with existing topologies, a 200‐W scaled‐down prototype was built. Experimental results verify a conversion ratio of 0.8–5, an input voltage range of 40–250 V, and an input current ripple below 1 A. Dynamic tests under input voltage steps from 180 to 220 V and load steps from 100% to 50% show minor voltage overshoot and a settling time of less than 150 ms. The peak efficiency reaches 95.1%. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed DC/DC converter. Trial Registration: Not applicable

title: Contested Sustainability: Analysing Civil Society Organisations' Mobilisation on EU Sustainable Finance
source: JCMS Journal of Common Market Studies
summary: This article aims to shed light on the mobilisation of civil society organisations (CSOs) in European Union (EU) sustainable finance policy as a new area of the EU single market in finance. As both the definition and the policy instruments
content: This article aims to shed light on the mobilisation of civil society organisations (CSOs) in European Union (EU) sustainable finance policy as a new area of the EU single market in finance. As both the definition and the policy instruments of sustainable finance are contested, we investigate CSOs' positions in the EU's Platform on Sustainable Finance (Platform) and the extent to which these positions reflect two distinctive policy logics: a ‘financial’ one and a ‘sustainability’ one. We find important differences between CSOs inside and outside the Platform, with the largest divergence between finance CSOs inside the Platform and environmental CSOs outside it. The analysis suggests that CSOs within the Platform self‐selected or were socialised into more mainstream, economic positions, speaking to recent findings that increased civil society engagement from the inside of financial regulation may lead to a ‘financialisation’ or ‘marketisation’ of civil society.

title: Interface‐to‐Bulk Grain Regulation Enables Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 Solar Cells Exceeding 11% Efficiency
summary: Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) represents an emerging thin‐film photovoltaic absorber owing to the excellent stability, tunable bandgap (1.1–1.7 eV), and high light absorption coefficient (> 10 5 cm −1 ). Hydrothermally deposited S
content: Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) represents an emerging thin‐film photovoltaic absorber owing to the excellent stability, tunable bandgap (1.1–1.7 eV), and high light absorption coefficient (> 10 5 cm −1 ). Hydrothermally deposited Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cells have broken the 10% efficiency bottleneck, yet as‐prepared Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 films suffer from small grains (typically ∼400 nm) with abundant grain boundaries (GBs) that introduce dense defect states, inducing severe non‐radiative recombination and hindering further efficiency enhancement. Here we develop an interface‐to‐bulk grain regulation strategy to achieve ultra‐large (exceeding 3 µm) columnar grains spanning the entire absorber. This strategy combines buried‐interface Sb pre‐deposition to tailor initial hydrothermal deposition and rear‐interface Se‐mediated two‐step post‐annealing to drive grain coalescence and growth through a sequential infiltration‐reaction‐coalescence mechanism. We also found that this grain engineering also leads to the passivation of bulk deep‐level and interfacial defects, and optimized heterojunction band alignment, which collectively suppresses non‐radiative recombination and in turn delivers an ultralow open‐circuit voltage deficit of 0.483 V. Consequently, the ultra‐large‐grain Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 solar cell delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 11.04%, which is the highest efficiency ever reported for antimony chalcogenide‐based solar cells. This study establishes an integrated strategy for regulating grain growth in Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 films toward efficient devices.

title: Biomimetic Carbonate Aerogel via γ‐Dicalcium Silicate Mineralization for Concurrent CO 2 Sequestration and All‐Season Building Thermoregulation
summary: The decarbonization of the built environment demands strategies that simultaneously reduce operational energy and sequester atmospheric CO 2 , yet these functions remain decoupled in existing construction materials. Here, we demonstrate a b
content: The decarbonization of the built environment demands strategies that simultaneously reduce operational energy and sequester atmospheric CO 2 , yet these functions remain decoupled in existing construction materials. Here, we demonstrate a biomimetic carbonate aerogel fabricated from γ‐dicalcium silicate (γ‐C 2 S)—a model system representative of carbonation‐reactive calcium silicate phases in alkaline industrial wastes—via carbonation‐directed assembly. In situ mineralization of γ‐C 2 S under pressurized CO 2 (0.3 MPa, 75% RH, 24 h) sequesters 334 mg CO 2 g −1 whilst generating a hierarchical CaCO 3 nano‐array architecture that functions as a broadband photonic platform. The resulting aerogel achieves a solar reflectance of 93.2% and mid‐infrared emittance of 94.5%, delivering a daytime net cooling power of 76.3 W m −2 . An ultra‐low thermal conductivity of 0.046 W m −1 K −1 mitigates the indoor overcooling impact in winter through superior envelope insulation. The inorganic‐dominated composition confers excellent flame resistance under direct flame exposure exceeding 7 min and a 1476.5% carbonation‐induced increase in compressive strength. EnergyPlus simulations across 30 cities spanning all Köppen‐Geiger climate zones demonstrate annual building energy savings of 7.68%–67.75%. These results establish carbonation‐directed assembly as a proof‐of‐concept materials strategy for coupling CO 2 mineralization with radiative and conductive thermal management.

title: Boosting Green Hydrogen Cycling with Atomic Raft Catalyst Featuring Strong Metal-Support Interaction
summary: Coupling green hydrogen evolution with fine chemical production is highly important for reducing the carbon footprint and promoting the sustainable development of human society, which requires efficient and stable catalysts. Herein, we pres
content: Coupling green hydrogen evolution with fine chemical production is highly important for reducing the carbon footprint and promoting the sustainable development of human society, which requires efficient and stable catalysts. Herein, we present efficient green hydrogen cycling (GHC) from water to fine chemicals via a Pt atomic raft (PtAR) catalyst, which consists of a strongly correlated Cr 2 O 3 matrix with atomically thin Pt rafts distributed across its surface (PtAR/Cr 2 O 3 ). Benefiting from strong metal-support interaction, the PtAR/Cr 2 O 3 catalyst demonstrates dual functionality in dehydrogenation and hydrogenation, exhibiting high intrinsic activity for both the hydrogen evolution from water and the selective hydrogenation of halogenated nitrobenzene. Mechanism investigation revealed that such high GHC performance originated from the moderate binding energy between the reaction intermediates and the cooperative PtAR active sites.

title: Room Temperature Processed and Inkjet‐Printed Oxide Nanoparticle‐Based Diodes for Wireless Paper Electronics
summary: At a time when plastic and electronic waste are increasingly impacting human health, even a modest transition toward eco‐friendly paper‐based electronics can meaningfully reduce the footprint of non‐biodegradable electronic waste. In this r
content: At a time when plastic and electronic waste are increasingly impacting human health, even a modest transition toward eco‐friendly paper‐based electronics can meaningfully reduce the footprint of non‐biodegradable electronic waste. In this regard, we report room‐temperature‐printed high‐performance oxide‐based heterojunction diodes and demonstrate wireless charging of supercapacitors with different architectures, capacitance, and energy density values, paving the way for future wireless paper electronics. The printed diodes are fabricated on glass or paper substrates with indium gallium oxide (IGO) nanoparticle ink, at room temperature, using a chemical curing method, where the surfactants on the nanoparticle surface of a heavily stabilized nanoparticle ink are removed chemically by interaction with halide ions to provide a compact nanoparticulate film. The diodes printed on glass and paper substrates demonstrate current densities of 358 and 6 A cm −2 at 1 V, respectively; whereas the diodes printed on paper can rectify AC signals up to 10 MHz. Moreover, the diodes printed on paper exhibit excellent stability against 1000 dynamic bending cycles with 2.5% tensile strain and promising long‐term storage stability under inert atmosphere for over 600 days. Finally, wireless charging of supercapacitors using these diodes is demonstrated at 125 kHz, enabling direct AC‐DC rectification and on‐device energy storage.

title: Upcycling Granulated Blast Furnace Slag into Sustainable Geopolymer Catalysts for Photo-Fenton Water Treatment: An ESCAPE Assessment
summary: Iron-functionalized geopolymer catalysts incorporating granulated blast furnace slag (GBFS), an iron and steelmaking by-product, were developed and investigated for the photo-Fenton treatment of real wastewater. Catalysts were prepared by a
content: Iron-functionalized geopolymer catalysts incorporating granulated blast furnace slag (GBFS), an iron and steelmaking by-product, were developed and investigated for the photo-Fenton treatment of real wastewater. Catalysts were prepared by alkali activation of 1:1 metakaolin/GBFS blends under different activation and curing conditions, followed by iron impregnation. The materials were tested in two untreated industrial wastewater matrices: scrubber wastewater and the liquid fraction of digestate (LFD). The best-performing formulations removed 97.1% of the initial total organic carbon (TOC) from scrubber wastewater and 60.9% from LFD after 30 min; a metakaolin-only reference achieved approximately 43% TOC removal from LFD under the reported comparison conditions. An LFD pretreatment with Amberlyst® 15 followed by photo-Fenton treatment increased TOC removal to 77.6% after 30 min and 86.2% after 60 min. The ESCAPE assessment of catalyst production identified a favourable result for the room-temperature NaOH-activated formulation (RT8M; ESCAPE Index 1.18), whereas the sodium-silicate formulation (TSS; 0.03) fell within the method’s neutrality range. The study connects an industrial by-product stream with the treatment of real wastewater and develops iron-functionalized, monolithic geopolymer catalysts.
