This experimental demonstration provides a basis for industrial symbiosis between steelmaking and wastewater-treatment operators and points toward future three-dimensional catalytic architectures.

title: Systematic ground-effect bias in heat transfer coefficient estimation
summary: Data-driven building energy models often represent the building envelope using a single effective heat transfer coefficient (HTC), implicitly assuming uniform boundary conditions. In practice, this assumption is violated because floors are
content: Data-driven building energy models often represent the building envelope using a single effective heat transfer coefficient (HTC), implicitly assuming uniform boundary conditions. In practice, this assumption is violated because floors are thermally coupled to the ground, whose temperature differs systematically from outdoor air temperature. This work examines how omission of ground coupling introduces bias in HTC estimation. A time window-level expression for the ground-effect relative bias is derived for a simplified RC network representation and shown to depend on both the floor share of total envelope conductance and an accumulated ground-effect factor over the estimation window. The effect is then investigated using synthetic high-resolution data generated from detailed Modelica simulations of archetypal single-family houses, with 2R2C models identified on moving 21-day windows. Results show that the empirical relative bias scales systematically with floor heat-transfer share and that its seasonal variation is closely tracked by the derived ground-effect bias. At the same time, the mean bias across buildings remains close to zero, indicating cancellation between competing structural bias components. The findings show that omitted physics can produce systematic, yet interpretable parameter bias, even when predictive performance is strong, underscoring the need for bias-aware model formulations in building energy performance assessment.

title: Calibrated intra-era archetypes for the Swedish multi-family housing stock
summary: Urban building energy models (UBEM) often represent a whole construction era with a single archetype. This misses within-era variation and leaves sensitive parameters such as infiltration to absorb residual errors between model predictions
content: Urban building energy models (UBEM) often represent a whole construction era with a single archetype. This misses within-era variation and leaves sensitive parameters such as infiltration to absorb residual errors between model predictions and measured energy performance (EP) during calibration. This study tests whether intra-era archetypes improve agreement with measured EP for Gothenburg’s 1955–1975 multi-family housing (MFH) stock and how to select representative buildings for archetype calibration within the subgroup. The method is demonstrated on 2,020 buildings. The results show that splitting one era into multiple archetypes reduces prediction error more reliably than calibrating a single era-wide model: simply partitioning the stock based on ventilation systems and renovation status lifts the share of buildings within 20 % of measured EP from 25.7 % to 60.9 %, while residual-median anchor calibration (selecting the representative building whose pre-calibration simulated/measured EP ratio is closest to the subgroup median) of the partitioned model reduces city-wide bias from 32.45 % to 6.42 % normalised mean bias error (NMBE). Choosing the representative building carefully matters: a poor choice shifts the entire group in the wrong direction. Because it relies only on building footprints and energy certificate data, the method is in principle applicable to other Swedish municipalities. Within each group, however, one calibrated archetype is still too simple when buildings vary widely.

title: A Literature Synthesis on Circularity in the Construction Sector
summary: The construction sector is a major contributor to global energy use, carbon dioxide emissions, raw material consumption, and waste generation. These impacts are expected to increase as population growth and urbanisation drive demand for bui
content: The construction sector is a major contributor to global energy use, carbon dioxide emissions, raw material consumption, and waste generation. These impacts are expected to increase as population growth and urbanisation drive demand for buildings and infrastructure. Despite its environmental significance, the sector largely follows linear production models. Achieving a more resource-efficient built environment therefore requires a transition toward circular principles, including reduction, reuse, repair, remanufacturing, and recycling to extend material lifetimes and reduce waste. Research on circularity in the construction sector has expanded rapidly, creating a need for synthesis to consolidate existing knowledge and identify remaining gaps. To address this need, a systematic literature review was conducted, combining an analysis of Swedish research projects identified through the Swecris database with an international review of studies retrieved from Scopus. The synthesis focused on four thematic areas: digitalisation, environmental and economic incentives, application domains across micro-, meso-, and macro-levels, and policy frameworks. The review reveals persistent gaps, including limited exploration of advanced digital technologies beyond BIM and material passports, incomplete life-cycle coverage in incentive analyses, a strong emphasis on micro-level applications, and uncertainty regarding the effectiveness of existing policy instruments. Addressing these gaps is essential to support the broader adoption of circularity in the construction sector.

title: Intrafibrillar mineralization of muscle fibers via CaP ion cluster as a precursor for bone regeneration
summary: Imitating the structure of bones has already attracted great attentions, but the complex hierarchical structure and unique organic-inorganic interface of bones have remained sophisticated to replicate to this day. Here, utilizing the natura
content: Imitating the structure of bones has already attracted great attentions, but the complex hierarchical structure and unique organic-inorganic interface of bones have remained sophisticated to replicate to this day. Here, utilizing the naturally muscles with hierarchical structures as the template and CaP ion clusters as the mineralization precursors, we successfully achieved intracellular mineralization and fabricated a CaP-muscle scaffold for bone defect repair. Based on the hydrogen bond interactions between proteins and CaP ion clusters, the CaP phase in mineralized muscle can maintain an amorphous state even when ethanol and TEA have completely evaporated. Through various indicators, it has been verified that this type of CaP-muscle scaffold can effectively promote the repair process of large bone defects.

title: Review of waste refrigerant treatment and valorization technologies for climate change mitigation: From physical separation to thermochemical conversion
summary: This review systematically examines recent advances in waste refrigerant treatment and valorization technologies for climate-change mitigation and circular refrigerant management. The reviewed technologies are categorized into physical sepa
content: This review systematically examines recent advances in waste refrigerant treatment and valorization technologies for climate-change mitigation and circular refrigerant management. The reviewed technologies are categorized into physical separation, non-catalytic thermochemical destruction, catalytic decomposition and conversion, and hybrid processes. Physical separation methods—including extractive distillation, adsorption, and membrane separation—preserve refrigerant molecules and enable their recovery, reclamation, and reuse; however, their performance depends strongly on mixture composition, purity requirements, and regeneration energy. Non-catalytic destruction methods, such as incineration and plasma decomposition, can achieve high destruction and removal efficiencies but require substantial energy and downstream control of corrosive byproducts such as HF and HCl. Catalytic processes can lower the required reaction temperature and, in selected systems, direct refrigerant-derived species toward recoverable products, although catalyst fluorination, deactivation, and long-term stability remain important limitations. Hybrid approaches integrating separation, catalysis, plasma, photothermal activation, or in situ halogen fixation offer potential improvements in energy efficiency and byproduct management. This review brings physical separation, thermochemical destruction and conversion, and hybrid treatment approaches into a common assessment of waste refrigerant management. It contributes by synthesizing reported performance data, refrigerant-dependent treatment behavior, and opportunities for integrating separation and conversion, while identifying limitations in comparability and evidence for environmental and economic feasibility. • Classifies refrigerant treatments into physical, non-catalytic, and catalytic types • Evaluates mechanisms and limits of physical separation and non-catalytic destruction • Catalytic conversion enables efficient upcycling into high-value compounds • Proposes hybrid systems and multifunctional catalysts to achieve carbon neutrality

title: Active Flow Control for Aerodynamic Efficiency Enhancement in Transonic Flow
summary: Die vorliegende Arbeit befasst sich mit der aktiven Strömungskontrolle zur Verbesserung der aerodynamischen Effizienz in kompressiblen und transonischen Strömungen. Untersucht werden die beiden Kontrollmethoden des wand-normalen homogenen A
content: Die vorliegende Arbeit befasst sich mit der aktiven Strömungskontrolle zur Verbesserung der aerodynamischen Effizienz in kompressiblen und transonischen Strömungen. Untersucht werden die beiden Kontrollmethoden des wand-normalen homogenen Ausblasens und Absaugens sowie die in Strömungsrichtung wandernden Wellen von spannweitiger Geschwindigkeit (streamwise travelling waves of spanwise velocity). Beide Methoden zeigen in kanonischen Strömungen eine Verringerung des Widerstands, wobei die zugrundeliegenden Mechanismen im transonischen Bereich noch nicht vollständig verstanden sind. Der erste Teil der Arbeit präsentiert eine umfassenden numerische Untersuchung des wandnormalen Ausblasens und Absaugens, die auf einem Tragflügel im subsonischen und transonischen Strömungsbereich angewendet wird. Es wird eine Parameterstudie über einen großen Bereich an Variablen, wie der Machzahl, Anstellwinkel, Kontrollposition und Kontrollgröße durchgeführt. Die Analyse berücksichtigt die energetischen Kosten der Kontrolle. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass die Wechselwirkung zwischen Stoß und Grenzschicht das Verhalten der Kontrolle grundlegend ändert. In Gegensatz zu Beobachtungen der Kontrolle im subsonischen Strömungsbereich zeigen die Ergebnisse, dass ein Absaugen auf der Oberseite des Tragflügels die aerodynamische Effizienz deutlich verbessern kann. Die Erhöhung der Effizienz kann durch eine Verringerung des Gesamtwiderstands aufgrund einer stromabwärts Verschiebung des Stoßes erreicht werden. Im zweiten Teil der Arbeit wird die Frage beantwortet, warum unterschiedliche Methoden der aktiven Strömungskontrolle trotz verschiedener Effekten auf den lokalen Reibungswiderstand zu vergleichbaren Verbesserungen der aerodynamischen Effizienz führen. Es werden direkte numerische Simulationen durchgeführt, um wand-normales Absaugen mit StTW unter identischen transsonischen Strömungsbedingungen zu vergleichen. Während beide Methoden zu einer Verbesserung der Effizienz führen, reduzieren StTW den lokalen Reibungswiderstand, während Absaugen ihn erhöht. Eine detaillierte Analyse der Strömungen zeigt, dass der dominierende Mechanismus, der zur Effizienzsteigerung führt, nicht die lokale Veränderung der Wandschubspannung ist, sondern eine Verringerung der Impulsdicke stromaufwärts des Stoßes zusammen mit einer Verschiebung des Stoßes in Richtung der Hinterkante sowie einer Zunahme des Auftriebs. Die Ergebnisse der vorliegenden Arbeit liefern neue Erkenntnisse über die Mechanismen, die für die Verbesserung der Effizienz mit aktiver Strömungskontrolle in transonischen Strömungen verantwortlich sind. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass eine lokale Verringerung der Wandschubspannung kein ausreichendes Kriterium für eine Verbesserung der Effizienz ist und dass eine Wechselwirkung zwischen Stoß und Grenzschicht eine bedeutende Rolle spielt.

title: Crossing the biological hierarchy with 2D materials-based biomedical devices
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have attracted significant attention owing to their distinctive physicochemical properties arising from their ultrathin planar architectures. While the term "2D materials" is traditionally associated with atom
content: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have attracted significant attention owing to their distinctive physicochemical properties arising from their ultrathin planar architectures. While the term "2D materials" is traditionally associated with atomically thin or few-layer systems, such as graphene, MXenes, and transition metal dichalcogenides, recent advances have demonstrated that materials with thicknesses spanning from several nanometers to micrometers can also exhibit characteristic two-dimensional behavior when their thickness remains sufficiently small relative to their lateral dimensions. Under this expanded definition, polymeric nanosheets and microscale thin films emerge as important members of the broader 2D material family for biomedical applications. In this review, we survey recent advances in biomedical devices and systems based on 2D materials across a wide range of thickness scales. To provide a unified perspective, the discussion is organized according to biological hierarchy, spanning from ions and small biomolecules to organs and organ systems. This framework enables a systematic examination of how 2D materials can be utilized across the biological hierarchy by maintaining their two-dimensionality across different length scales. Finally, we discuss the challenges associated with the translational potential of 2D materials and future research directions, including their multihierarchical integration.

title: Automated production route selection for responsible manufacturing: A case study in wooden furniture production
summary: Under growing pressure to support the sustainable development goals , manufacturers must balance sustainability with operational efficiency. Achieving balance requires the continuous optimization of production routes in response to changing
content: Under growing pressure to support the sustainable development goals , manufacturers must balance sustainability with operational efficiency. Achieving balance requires the continuous optimization of production routes in response to changing operational conditions and customer demands. However, existing approaches struggle to accommodate these dynamic and often conflicting criteria. To address the challenge, the study proposes an integrated framework for responsible manufacturing that combines AI-based route generation with AHP and TOPSIS for multicriteria decision-making and uses SCOR metrics to evaluate performance. The framework was applied to evaluate trade-offs between conflicting objectives, particularly CO₂ emissions and production costs at the pre-production stage. It comprised four stages: (1) automatically generating a production route, (2) predicting operational runtimes, (3) evaluating alternative routes against conflicting criteria, and (4) recommending the highest-ranked route. A manufacturing case study was conducted to validate the framework and assess its ability to reduce decision-making time, align production routes with organizational and customer requirements, and make trade-offs between criteria transparent. Current research shows that applying AI and automation to pre-production activities results in greater operational efficiencies, subsequently enhancing supply chain performance. Automated production preparation enables early assessment of workstation workloads, thereby enhancing planning accuracy, resource utilization efficiency, and the speed of generating commercial proposals. Consequently, companies can strengthen their reputation and boost customer satisfaction by aligning production processes with customer preferences.

title: Deciphering the device physics and performance limits of FTO/TiO2/CsBiSI2/Spiro-OMeTAD/Ag photovoltaics: A device-level multi-parameter investigation
summary: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) exhibit high efficiencies but still suffer from multiple issues, such as toxicity, ion migration, and interfacial recombination. This work explores a quaternary chalco-halide perovskite, CsBiSI₂, synthesized by
content: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) exhibit high efficiencies but still suffer from multiple issues, such as toxicity, ion migration, and interfacial recombination. This work explores a quaternary chalco-halide perovskite, CsBiSI₂, synthesized by partially replacing iodide with sulphur (anion-splitting) to combine the favorable optoelectronic properties of Cs₃Bi₂I₉ with improved stability and band-gap tuning. Numerical SCAPS-1D simulations coupled with impedance spectroscopy (Nyquist, capacitance-voltage, and Mott-Schottky analyses) have been employed to study how the back-electrode work function, operating temperature, and parasitic resistances affect carrier dynamics and photovoltaic performance. Increasing the metal work function improves charge extraction and built-in potential, yielding higher open-circuit voltage and power-conversion efficiency, but benefits saturate beyond ~5 eV due to larger interfacial resistances. The simulated Nyquist semicircle becomes larger with increasing temperature from 290 to 400 K, while V OC , FF, and PCE decrease. These findings provide guidelines for designing lead-free perovskite devices with optimized contacts and mitigated parasitic losses.

title: Temperature-compensated plasmonic resonance in graphene bolometric quantum barrier THz detectors
summary: Graphene/narrow gap semiconductor quantum barrier heterostructures provide a promising platform for terahertz (THz) bolometric detection because graphene supports tunable plasmonic resonances, while the adjacent barrier converts carrier hea
content: Graphene/narrow gap semiconductor quantum barrier heterostructures provide a promising platform for terahertz (THz) bolometric detection because graphene supports tunable plasmonic resonances, while the adjacent barrier converts carrier heating into a measurable thermionic current. Existing descriptions of such detectors often start from the linear Dirac dispersion of graphene and the bias controlled zero temperature carrier density, but the finite temperature shift of the chemical potential and its effect on plasmonic detuning remain less explicit. Here we develop an analytical model for the temperature dependent plasmonic response of monolayer graphene quantum barrier THz detectors. Starting from the exact Fermi-Dirac relation between carrier density, chemical potential, and temperature, combined with charge conservation under an applied bias, we derive a self consistent equation for the thermally shifted chemical potential and use it to evaluate the detuning between the plasmon resonance and a fixed THz driving frequency. The analysis shows that there exists a temperature 𝑇 m i n at which this detuning is minimized, and that 𝑇 m i n admits a closed form perturbative expansion in terms of bias voltage and device geometry. The resulting series yields an explicit convergence criterion expressed as a threshold voltage and provides a design rule for temperature compensated plasmonic resonance. These results identify the temperature of minimum detuning as an analytically tractable target quantity for frequency selective THz detection in graphene quantum barrier bolometric plasmonic structures. Temperature is not an independent external tuning knob. The operating temperature of the device is given, and the resulting detuning is compensated in coordination with the applied bias voltage.

title: Purification and Structural Modification of Spent Lithium-Ion Battery Graphite via Organic and Inorganic Acid Leaching: A Comparative and Statistical Study
summary: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are a promising secondary resource for graphite anode recovery; however, recovered graphite is often contaminated with transition metals, inorganic residues, binder-derived species, and electrolyte decomposition
content: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are a promising secondary resource for graphite anode recovery; however, recovered graphite is often contaminated with transition metals, inorganic residues, binder-derived species, and electrolyte decomposition products, which degrade material quality. This study systematically compares selective leaching with inorganic acids (H₂SO₄, HCl, and HNO₃) and organic acids (acetic, ascorbic, and citric acids). It uses multivariate statistical analysis to evaluate graphite purification and metal separation from the LIB black mass. The results show that H₂SO₄ at 0.5 M was the most effective leaching system, producing the most ordered graphite structure, as indicated by a d-spacing of 3.3354 Å and a degree of graphitization of 98.83%. Multicriteria evaluation using the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) confirms H₂SO₄ as the optimal leaching agent, consistent with the recovery distribution observed in the normalized heatmap for all target metals (Co, Cu, Mn, Fe, Ni, and Pb). Main-effect-plot analysis further reveals heterogeneous metal-specific leaching mechanisms. These findings emphasize the importance of selecting an appropriate leaching medium and integrating statistical approaches to optimize graphite purification from LIB waste within a circular-economy framework.

title: Electrothermal Impact of Resistive Aging in Supercapacitor-Based Fast-Charging for Electric Vehicles Using an Equivalent-Circuit Model
summary: A theoretical and computational electrothermal framework is presented to investigate the effects of resistive aging in a supercapacitor-based fast-charging station coupled with an electric vehicle. Aging is localized in the station-side sup
content: A theoretical and computational electrothermal framework is presented to investigate the effects of resistive aging in a supercapacitor-based fast-charging station coupled with an electric vehicle. Aging is localized in the station-side supercapacitor bank and is represented by an exponentially time-dependent internal resistance characterized by the parameters ξ and λ, which determine the magnitude of the aging-related resistive contribution and its effective growth rate, respectively. The governing circuit equation is solved analytically in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, making the dependence of the electrical response on the aging parameters and circuit coefficients explicit. The results show that ξ mainly attenuates and advances the current peak, whereas λ accelerates the post-peak decay and shortens the effective charging interval. Increasing resistive aging also limits voltage equalization and lowers energy transfer efficiency by increasing dissipation along the station-side power path. The efficiency response exhibits a coupled dependence on (ξ,λ), such that different parameter combinations can produce comparable efficiency levels when their cumulative resistive effects are similar to each other. A first-order lumped thermal model driven by cell-level Joule dissipation predicts that the cell temperature increases during the dominant charging interval and subsequently approaches the ambient temperature as the current becomes negligible. Over the investigated parameter range, the temperature increase is substantially more sensitive to ξ than to λ, whose increase produces a slight reduction in the accumulated temperature increase. The results provide analytical verification and literature-based corroboration of the proposed framework rather than direct experimental validation.

title: Trans-cinnamaldehyde alleviates hepatic steatosis and pyroptosis via SIRT1 activation in acute alcoholic liver injury
summary: BACKGROUND Acute alcoholic liver injury (ALI) is a hepatic disorder caused by excessive alcohol intake. The typical pathological features of ALI include hepatic lipid droplet accumulation, hepatocyte death, and inflammatory cell infiltratio
content: BACKGROUND Acute alcoholic liver injury (ALI) is a hepatic disorder caused by excessive alcohol intake. The typical pathological features of ALI include hepatic lipid droplet accumulation, hepatocyte death, and inflammatory cell infiltration. Trans-cinnamaldehyde (TCA) is a natural aldehydic organic compound that exerts antibacterial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and lipid metabolism-regulating effects. However, whether TCA can alleviate acute ALI remains unclear. AIM To investigate the therapeutic targets of TCA for the treatment of acute ALI through transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation. METHODS We established a mouse model of acute ALI in vivo by oral gavage administration of ethanol (5 g/kg, 50% v/v) to investigate the protective effects of TCA against ethanol-induced hepatic steatosis and cell death. In vitro , we explored the mechanisms by which TCA regulates the sirtuin 1/peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (SIRT1/PPARα) pathway, fatty acid β-oxidation, and pyroptosis through SIRT1 gene silencing. RESULTS Our study found that TCA treatment (40 mg/kg) significantly reduced serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase activities, as well as hepatic total cholesterol and triglyceride levels in mice with acute ALI. Furthermore, TCA treatment markedly attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and hepatocyte death. Analysis of the Gene Expression Omnibus database (GSE28619) from patients with alcoholic hepatitis revealed significant enrichment of the adenosine 5’-monophosphate-activated protein kinase and PPAR signaling pathways. Mechanistically, TCA activated SIRT1/PPARα signaling. Notably, SIRT1 silencing abrogated the protective effects of TCA against acute ALI, including the amelioration of hepatic steatosis, enhancement of fatty acid β-oxidation, and suppression of ER stress-related proteins such as glucose-regulated protein 78, phosphorylated inositol-requiring enzyme 1α, C/EBP homologous protein and pyroptosis-associated proteins such as NOD -like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3, cleaved cysteinyl aspartate specific proteinase-1 (cleaved caspase-1), N-terminal gasdermin D. CONCLUSION TCA alleviated hepatocyte lipid deposition, ER stress and cell death in acute ALI by promoting SIRT1 activity, suggesting that TCA is a potential therapeutic agent for ALI.

title: Nanostructured propolis attenuates experimental liver fibrosis and is associated with changes in LC3 and p62 expression
summary: BACKGROUND Liver fibrosis is characterized by persistent activation of hepatic stellate cells and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, and effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. AIM To investigate whether nanostructuring enh
content: BACKGROUND Liver fibrosis is characterized by persistent activation of hepatic stellate cells and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, and effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. AIM To investigate whether nanostructuring enhances the antifibrotic efficacy of propolis against carbon tetrachloride (CCL4)-induced liver fibrosis and examined its association with changes in the autophagy-related markers microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3) and sequestosome 1 (p62). METHODS Male Sprague-Dawley rats were exposed to CCL4 for eight weeks with or without concomitant administration of conventional propolis or propolis nanoparticles. Biochemical, histopathological, oxidative stress, and molecular analyses were performed, including assessment of LC3 and p62 expression at the mRNA and immunohistochemical protein levels. RESULTS CCL4 administration induced marked hepatic injury, oxidative stress, and liver fibrosis, accompanied by increased LC3 expression and reduced p62 expression. Both propolis formulations attenuated these alterations; however, propolis nanoparticles produced more pronounced improvements in biochemical, histopathological, oxidative stress, and molecular parameters than conventional propolis and were associated with partial attenuation of the CCL4-induced changes in LC3 and p62 expression. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that nanoformulation may improve the antifibrotic efficacy of propolis in experimental liver fibrosis. The observed alterations in LC3 and p62 were associated with the protective effects of propolis nanoparticles; however, because autophagic flux was not directly assessed, these findings should be interpreted as changes in autophagy-related marker expression rather than definitive evidence of altered autophagic activity. Further studies are warranted to clarify the underlying mechanisms and evaluate the translational potential of this approach.

title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: Investigating the role of interstellar dust, gas, and stars in high-z galaxies at kiloparsec scales
summary: A comprehensive understanding of galaxy evolution requires a detailed analysis of gas and dust, including their distribution and evolution within galaxies. In this work, we analyse spatially resolved (∼,1-2,kpc) rest-frame C ii and dust con
content: A comprehensive understanding of galaxy evolution requires a detailed analysis of gas and dust, including their distribution and evolution within galaxies. In this work, we analyse spatially resolved (∼,1-2,kpc) rest-frame C ii and dust continuum ALMA observations together with JWST/NIRSpec IFU data of a sample of six massive galaxies at z,∼,4-5. We focus on deriving and comparing the spatial distributions of atomic and molecular gas masses, dust and stellar masses, star formation rates (SFR), and metallicity. The oxygen abundance maps have median values in the range of 12+log(O/H),sim8.1-8.3 with variations of the order of 1,dex within the same galaxy. In four galaxies of our sample, the oxygen abundance shows a minimum at the peak of the Hα emission and an enhancement in the outer parts. The calibration used in this study to estimate the atomic gas mass in our galaxies seems to overestimate the atomic gas mass surface densities by up to one to two orders of magnitude. However, a calibration based on a spatially resolved C ii conversion factor gives a more robust estimation of the total gas mass. The dust-to-gas surface mass density ratio varies between łog Σ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.2 ^ +0.24 _ -0.19 and łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.69^ +0.21 _ -0.16 , while the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio ranges from łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.01^ +0.13 _ -0.12 to łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.91^ +0.13 _ -0.13 . A detailed analysis of the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and the gas mass fraction versus metallicity revealed that galaxies exhibiting signatures of strong outflows have a lower dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and lower gas mass fractions than the galaxies with no outflow signatures. While the latter is consistent with these galaxies ejecting part of their gas reservoir to the circumgalactic medium, the low dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratios also suggest that part of the dust content is expelled outside the galaxy, which reinforces previous theoretical suggestions of dust removal by stellar feedback or radiation pressure to explain the high UV luminosities in galaxies at very high redshifts. Some galaxies of our sample have almost an order of magnitude higher ratios of dust-to-gas and dust-to-stellar surface mass density than galaxies in the local Universe, suggesting that a large dust reservoir has been built up already at timescales of sim1,Gyr in these galaxies.

title: Inferring accretion bursts in intermediate-mass protostars from asteroseismic imprints
summary: During star formation, objects may gain the majority of their final mass through regular and intense bursts of mass accretion. For burst events of the FU Orionis-type (FUor), accretion rates can climb as high as 10^ -3 in short windows of t
content: During star formation, objects may gain the majority of their final mass through regular and intense bursts of mass accretion. For burst events of the FU Orionis-type (FUor), accretion rates can climb as high as 10^ -3 in short windows of time, amounting to just a few percent of the main accretion phase. Some bursters had not been observed in the preceding quiescent stage, making their classification as FUors difficult. To study the occurrence of such events observationally, signatures of the current accretion bursts and tracers of recent bursts are crucial. In this work, we investigate the potential to identify current accretion bursts and detect recent bursts in protostars and pre-main sequence (pre-MS) stars of intermediate mass using asteroseismology. The aim is to characterize theoretical period-spacing diagrams of pre-MS gravity-mode (g-mode) pulsators that have undergone accretion bursts. We used the stellar structure and evolution code to evolve stellar models from the protostellar seed phase of 0.01 MESA and 1.5 ̊sun up to 4.0 with a constant accretion rate of 10^ -6 A single accretion burst was initialized during the accretion phase. The stellar oscillation code GYRE was employed to compute the resulting asteroseismic properties of the models. Accretion bursts of up to 10^ -3 are sufficient to cause the convective cores of the models to recede, leaving behind a chemical trace that is manifested in the form of quasi-periodic dips in the g-mode period spacing. This effect is strongest during the outburst, but also lingers for up to 475 years before the convective core is re-established and the dips are gone. Our experiment shows that a single accretion burst leaves an imprint in the deep interiors of protostars and pre-MS stars of intermediate mass and that this imprint can be captured with asteroseismology. Well-resolved g-mode pulsations of young stellar objects may therefore help identify current and recent accretion bursts. Our results are most conclusive for burst magnitudes greater than 1 -4 corresponding to FUor-type bursts.

title: The long-period central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455
summary: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer-period central stars are scarcer. We characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455, which has previously
content: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer-period central stars are scarcer. We characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455, which has previously been claimed to be an intermediate-period binary with a period of approximately 12 days. We studied archival and catalogue photometry to probe the previously reported photometric variability and binary spectral energy distribution. We used long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring to measure the radial velocity curves of the two components of the central binary, and to derive their atmospheric parameters. We also undertook kinematical and chemical abundance analyses of the nebula itself. The orbital period of the central binary of exceeds five years and is highly eccentric. The binary comprises a relatively low-temperature sdO-type central star and a spun-up K-type giant companion. The Kiel mass of the central star is approximately half the dynamical mass derived from the radial velocities. While the systemic velocity and inclination of the nebula are consistent with the radial velocities of the binary, its abundance pattern adds support for a lower-mass progenitor that did not experience hot bottom burning (and is thus more consistent with the Kiel mass than the mass derived from the radial velocities). To the best of our knowledge, the central star of is only the fourth planetary nebula central star to have a spectroscopically confirmed orbital period longer than one year.

title: Impact performance of nanoclay-reinforced balsa-core carbon/epoxy sandwich composites
summary: Balsa-core sandwich structures are widely used in fields such as aerospace, marine, and automotive, where weight savings and high performance are essential. In this study, the low-velocity impact performance of sandwich composites with nano
content: Balsa-core sandwich structures are widely used in fields such as aerospace, marine, and automotive, where weight savings and high performance are essential. In this study, the low-velocity impact performance of sandwich composites with nanoclay-reinforced carbon/epoxy face sheets and a balsa core was experimentally investigated in detail over the 25–200 J impact energy range. Carbon/epoxy sheet materials were manufactured by hand lay-up and vacuum bagging with neat resin and with nanoclay additions of 1, 2, and 3 wt.%. Then, sandwich composites were formed by bonding face sheets and a balsa core. The findings indicate that a 1 wt.% nanoclay reinforcement increased the maximum peak force by up to 59 %, the perforation energy threshold by 48 %, and improved the damage area by up to 6.5 % and the damage depth by up to 60 % of sandwich composites.

title: Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
summary: Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that saf
content: Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management.

title: SATAY-based chemogenomic screening uncovers antifungal resistance mechanisms and key determinants of ATI-2307 and chitosan sensitivity
summary: Multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens are a serious threat to public health and global food security. Mitigation requires the discovery of antifungal compounds with novel modes of action, along with a comprehensive understanding of the molec
content: Multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens are a serious threat to public health and global food security. Mitigation requires the discovery of antifungal compounds with novel modes of action, along with a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing antifungal resistance. Here, we apply SAturated Transposon Analysis in Yeast (SATAY), a powerful transposon sequencing method in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, to uncover loss- and gain-of-function mutations conferring resistance to 20 different antifungal compounds. These screens identify a diverse array of novel resistance mechanisms and multiple modes of action. SATAY is performed in drug-sensitive strains to generate chemogenomic profiles for compounds that lack activity against conventional laboratory strains. This study therefore provides a significant resource for exploring cellular responses to chemical stresses. We discover that the natural antifungal Chitosan electrostatically interacts with cell wall mannosylphosphate, and that the transporter Hol1 concentrates the novel antifungal ATI-2307 within yeast. This latter finding presents an avenue for drug design initiatives, but also unveils a straightforward evolutionary path to ATI-2307 resistance with minimal fitness cost.

title: Mesophase-induced vitrification in coordination polymers via aliphatic chain dynamics
summary: Hybrid glasses of coordination polymers promise a fusion of processability and structural functionality, yet their formation is limited by poor thermal stability and high melting points. Here, we show mesophase-induced vitrification in a se
content: Hybrid glasses of coordination polymers promise a fusion of processability and structural functionality, yet their formation is limited by poor thermal stability and high melting points. Here, we show mesophase-induced vitrification in a series of magnesium-based coordination polymers with aliphatic dicarboxylate linkers of varying chain length. Upon thermal desolvation, these frameworks transition into a mesomorphic state that retains the long-range order of the parent framework while disordering the organic substructure. This intermediate state enables a direct glass transition without melting. In contrast, only the longest-chain analogue melts, and its melt-quenched glass has lower stiffness owing to partial dissociation of the metal–organic backbone, indicating that mechanical properties are governed by the integrity of the coordination network. Spectroscopic and structural analyses show that vitrification proceeds through mobilisation of the aliphatic linker within an intact coordination network, paralleling semicrystalline polymers. These findings establish a design strategy for vitrifiable coordination networks that integrates principles from polymer dynamics and mesomorphism.

title: Modeling forest age and NPP and developing site index tables for the Manas River Basin, Xinjiang
summary: Introduction The dynamic variation of net primary productivity (NPP) with forest age is crucial for evaluating forest productivity and potential carbon input. In arid regions, this process is likely modulated by water availability and site
content: Introduction The dynamic variation of net primary productivity (NPP) with forest age is crucial for evaluating forest productivity and potential carbon input. In arid regions, this process is likely modulated by water availability and site heterogeneity, although the present study focuses on characterizing the age -NPP relationship rather than directly attributing it to a specific hydrological driver. Using the Manas River Basin in Xinjiang as a case study, this research aimed to characterize the age -NPP relationships and site quality patterns of dominant tree species under arid conditions and their implications for global ecosystems of similar types. Methods This research established a forest age-NPP relationship model for four dominant tree species ( Spruce , Poplar , Elaeagnus angustifolia , and Populus euphratica ) and one mixed stand type ( Mixed wood ), and developed a site index table. Based on multi-period forest resource survey data, we systematically compared the fitting performance of five models (SEM, SDP, L, M, and Γ) and employed the guide curve method to fit tree height growth processes for compiling the site index table. Results (1) Among the five candidate models, SEM and Γ functions showed the best performance in describing the NPP -forest age relationship in arid regions, although their predictive skill varied among tree species and the mixed stand type. Different tree species exhibit distinct NPP accumulation patterns: Spruce shows a "progressive saturation type," maintaining continuous growth and stabilizing over 140 years; Elaeagnus angustifolia enters a high -productivity maintenance phase early; Populus euphratica exhibits a 'growth -sudden decline' pattern; this pattern may be consistent with, but does not directly demonstrate, interruption of carbon accumulation due to water stress or physiological senescence, because hydrological and physiological variables were not measured in this study. These patterns highlight species -specific differences in NPP accumulation under arid conditions. (2) The established site index table showed an internal consistency of ≥ 94%, indicating a distinct spatial gradient in site quality within the watershed. Spruce shows a wide site index range, reflecting its sensitivity to moisture and topography, whereas Poplar has a concentrated range (15 -19 m), indicating strong adaptability. The site index shows a significant correlation with stand age-related NPP trends. Discussion The site index is consistent with the interpretation that site quality reflects water and nutrient availability, and that site quality is therefore an indicator --rather than a regulator --of forest productivity potential in this arid inland basin. The model and site index table developed in this study provide a quantitative tool for assessing NPP -based productivity potential and for differentiated forest management in the Manas River Basin. This approach can inform adaptive forest management and ecological restoration

title: Bisureido ester of 2‐(methylthio)ethanol: A novel lead against triple‐negative breast cancer inducing apoptosis via pH‐gradient–triggered chloride transport
summary: Dysregulation of transmembrane chloride flux has emerged as a promising strategy for inducing cancer cell death through disruption of intracellular pH gradients and subsequent apoptosis. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of novel o
content: Dysregulation of transmembrane chloride flux has emerged as a promising strategy for inducing cancer cell death through disruption of intracellular pH gradients and subsequent apoptosis. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of novel ortho ‐phenylenediamine ( o ‐PDA) bisurea derivatives bearing carboxyl ( 5a–f ) and 2‐(methylthio)ethyl ester ( 6a,b ) groups for pH‐gradient‐induced anion transport and resultant anticancer activity. Esterification of 5c–f proved synthetically challenging due to an unprecedented CDI‐catalyzed intramolecular cyclization that yielded the 4‐oxo‐benzo[ d ][1,3,6]oxadiazepines 8a , b ; the process was rationalized via a DFT‐supported mechanism involving anion‐binding catalysis. All target compounds demonstrated 1:1 chloride ion‐binding as shown by 1 H NMR titration results and a pH‐gradient‐induced transmembrane chloride transport (as shown by vesicular transport studies) which was enhanced by electron‐withdrawing groups (EWGs) on the terminal phenyl rings. Ester derivatives 6a , b exhibited significantly higher chloride binding and up to ∼67‐fold increased transport efficiency over their carboxylic acid analogs. Compound 6b emerged as a new lead, combining efficient chloride binding ( K a = 163 M −1 ), potent transport (EC 50 = 0.007 mol%), and superior antiproliferative activity (IC 50 = 6.34 μM) against resistant breast cancer cells via apoptosis induction. These findings establish 6b as a promising lead for chloride‐transport‐mediated cancer therapy, with further optimization recommended via EWG diversification and theoretical consideration of the cyclization pathway in retrosynthetic design.

title: Tunnel-Barrier Control of Ultrafast Demagnetization and Spin Transport in Graphene/TiOx/Co Heterostructures
summary: Heterostructures combining graphene with 3 d transition metal ferromagnets (FMs) enable various spin-based phenomena at ultrafast timescales. However, challenges such as the interfacial impedance mismatch, FM deposition-induced defect gener
content: Heterostructures combining graphene with 3 d transition metal ferromagnets (FMs) enable various spin-based phenomena at ultrafast timescales. However, challenges such as the interfacial impedance mismatch, FM deposition-induced defect generation, and interface modification by interfacial coupling or hybridization can impede their functionalization for spin-orbitronics. In this work, we utilize insulating TiO x barrier layers to modify the interfacial spin conductance structurally, disentangle spin pumping and magnetic proximity effects, and establish external control over ultrafast magnetization dynamics in single-layer graphene/TiO x /Co systems. All-optical time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements of femtosecond to nanosecond spin dynamics reveal systematic tunability of ultrafast magnetic parameters via barrier engineering. The thickness-dependent modulation of Co damping indicates efficient spin pumping, with substantial interfacial spin transparency retained even in the presence of an ultrathin TiO x barrier. Notably, a 0.8 nm TiO x barrier suppresses the magnetic proximity effect while allowing spin transfer into graphene. These findings demonstrate that tunnel-barrier engineering can help separate proximity-induced magnetism from spin transport, providing a practical route to control ultrafast magnetization dynamics in graphene-based heterostructures.

title: Turnovers Drive Supported Metal Nanoparticle Catalyst Surface Reconstruction to Kinetically Trapped Metastable Structures
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Supported metal catalysts often operate with high adsorbate coverages that can alter nanoparticle structures as compared to the clean catalyst. Such restructuring is typically described within an equilibrium picture that assumes that nanopa
content: Supported metal catalysts often operate with high adsorbate coverages that can alter nanoparticle structures as compared to the clean catalyst. Such restructuring is typically described within an equilibrium picture that assumes that nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages adopt their thermodynamically preferred state. Here, we challenge this assumption and propose that under conditions of high adsorbate coverage and fast turnovers of surface species, supported metal nanoparticle structures and adsorbate coverages can become kinetically trapped in metastable states. We studied CO adsorption–desorption quasi-equilibrium on Pt/γ-Al2O3 using in situ IR spectroscopy and chemisorption as a function of temperature (300–650 K), CO pressure (10–2–10–4 bar), and visible photon flux (0–2 W cm–2 440 nm photons). The adsorbed CO IR band area increases with temperature and photon flux, contrary to equilibrium predictions of decreasing coverage. Estimates of apparent Pt dispersion and CO desorption rates, along with the reversibility of IR spectral changes, support the hypothesis that when CO turnovers are faster than Pt atomic rearrangements to their equilibrium state, the catalyst is driven into metastable states. We estimate atomic rearrangements time scales of 10–1–10–3 s on CO-covered Pt nanoparticles at ∼500–600 K. Grand-canonical sampling calculations show that equilibrium Pt–CO structures cannot reproduce the experimental IR trends, implying the presence of off-equilibrium coverages, structures, or both. By matching the experimental trend, theory identifies a plausible flat, nonequilibrium free-energy region that can facilitate kinetic trapping of metastable catalyst states. These results highlight the need for theoretical and experimental approaches targeting nonequilibrium structures to establish structure–function relationships in heterogeneous catalysis.

title: A new paradigm for high-level radioactive waste disposal: intrinsic radionuclide properties and comparative hazard
summary: Disposal regulations and technologies for high-level radioactive waste have evolved separately from other hazardous wastes, despite shared concerns about long-term risks. This study compares these historical trajectories and reassesses the
content: Disposal regulations and technologies for high-level radioactive waste have evolved separately from other hazardous wastes, despite shared concerns about long-term risks. This study compares these historical trajectories and reassesses the hazard profile and physical/geochemical properties of key radionuclides. Long-lived radionuclides have low specific activity and emit little or no penetrating radiation; their risks arise primarily from internal exposure, analogous to chemical carcinogens disposed of in the shallow subsurface. Actinides have carcinogenic potency comparable to dioxin but are strongly immobilized under reducing conditions, whereas mobile long-lived radionuclides have lower potency. These findings support a paradigm shift in disposal strategies: (1) shifting the long-term safety basis from heavily engineered systems toward inherent geochemical/physical mechanisms; (2) considering trade-offs between hypothetical future risks and present-day environmental impacts; and (3) harmonizing regulatory requirements for disposal, including long-term stewardship. Such a unified, lifecycle-aware framework will enhance overall environmental protection and improve the sustainability of energy systems.

title: Allergic Conjunctivitis and Rhinitis in Saudi Arabia Using Google Trends: Associationwith Air Pollution and Meteorological Factors
source: Journal of Epidemiology and Global Health
summary: Climate changes and air pollution are potential drivers for allergic conjunctivitis and rhinitis. In arid region such as Saudi Arabia, limited studies have explored the influence of environmental factors on health diseases. This study aims
content: Climate changes and air pollution are potential drivers for allergic conjunctivitis and rhinitis. In arid region such as Saudi Arabia, limited studies have explored the influence of environmental factors on health diseases. This study aims to investigate seasonality of allergic conjunctivitis and rhinitis, and to explore association with air pollutants and meteorological factors in Saudi Arabia using Google Trends (GTs). Quasi-Poisson Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) combined with Distributed Lag Non-linear Model (DLNM) were used to explore the effect of air pollution and meteorological factors on population-level interest on allergic conjunctivitis and rhinitis. Both allergic diseases demonstrated seasonal pattern, with peak in autumn and spring. Relative risks (RRs) for ocular allergy given increase in PM2.5, PM10, NH₃, CO, and BC at lag 0 (RR = 1.114, 95% CI: 1.020–1.217), (RR = 1.079, 95% CI: 1.007–1.155), and (RR = 1.286, 95% CI: 1.081–1.530), (RR = 1.011, 95% CI: 1.003–1.019), and (RR = 1.506, 95% CI: 1.118–2.028), respectively. Ocular allergy may be more sensitive to ambient environmental irritants. In contrast, allergic rhinitis search interest was governed primarily by seasonality. This study highlights associations between both allergic conjunctivitis and rhinitis search interest with air pollution and meteorological factors. This can offer evidence for regional air quality policy decisions and implementing preventive measures to reduce the risk of allergies burden.

title: Topological tunneling magnetoresistance from type-II Weyl-like states in a room-temperature half-metallic Janus Mn 2 PC monolayer
summary: Integrating room-temperature half-metallicity with topological carriers that can serve as spin-selective tunneling channels remains a key challenge for two-dimensional spintronics.Here, based on first-principles and quantum-transport calcul
content: Integrating room-temperature half-metallicity with topological carriers that can serve as spin-selective tunneling channels remains a key challenge for two-dimensional spintronics.Here, based on first-principles and quantum-transport calculations, we identify tetragonal Janus Mn 2 PC as a candidate platform that combines intrinsic half-metallicity and spin-polarized type-II Weyl-like states, with an estimated Curie temperature of 554 K. Its spin-up bands form strongly tilted Weyl-like crossings near the Fermi level, whereas the spin-down channel is insulating, leaving a large half-metallic gap. Wannier-based tight-binding calculations reveal topological edge states associated with these nodal crossings. Spin-orbit coupling opens a small gap of 11.2 meV at the crossings, producing concentrated Berry curvature and a sizable anomalous Hall conductivity. These coupled half-metallic and topological features motivate a Mn 2 PC-based magnetic tunnel junction. Quantum-transmission calculations using a low-energy effective Hamiltonian show that the parallel state conducts through fully spin-polarized Weyl-like channels, whereas the antiparallel state is strongly blocked by the half-metallic gap, yielding a large topological tunneling magnetoresistance within the coherent spin-conserving limit. The accompanying anomalous Hall response provides an accessible transport signature of the conducting topological carriers, suggesting a route to room-temperature topological spintronic functionality.

title: Opioid-sparing postoperative analgesia after impacted mandibular third molar surgery: a double-blind randomized clinical trial of intra-socket biodegradable extended-release bupivacaine hydrogel
summary: Postoperative pain following mandibular third molar extraction is commonly managed using systemic nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and opioids; however, these agents are associated with adverse effects and potential overuse. Th
content: Postoperative pain following mandibular third molar extraction is commonly managed using systemic nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and opioids; however, these agents are associated with adverse effects and potential overuse. The present study aimed to develop and clinically evaluate a biodegradable bupivacaine/Carbopol hydrogel as a sustained-release local analgesic system for postoperative pain control after mandibular third molar surgery. This single-center, double-blind, split-mouth randomized clinical trial was conducted at the outpatient clinic of Qazvin University of Medical Sciences. Sixteen patients (7 men and 9 women; mean age: 23.2 years) with bilaterally impacted mandibular third molars were enrolled. Following extraction, intra-socket administration of either bupivacaine/Carbopol hydrogel or placebo hydrogel was performed. Postoperative pain intensity was assessed using a 10-point visual analog scale (VAS) at 2, 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours after surgery. Rescue analgesic consumption was recorded daily for 3 postoperative days. Statistical analysis was performed using repeated-measures ANOVA in SPSS version 24, with the significance level set at α = 0.05. Repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant effects of time, treatment group, and time × group interaction on postoperative VAS pain scores (all P < 0.05). Except during the first 2 postoperative hours, the bupivacaine/Carbopol hydrogel group exhibited significantly lower pain scores at 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours compared with the placebo group. Although postoperative analgesic consumption was consistently lower in the hydrogel group, no statistically significant differences in rescue analgesic intake were observed between the groups over time (P > 0.05). No adverse local or systemic reactions were identified during the follow-up period. The biodegradable bupivacaine/Carbopol hydrogel demonstrated sustained postoperative analgesic effects following mandibular third molar extraction and may represent a promising adjunctive strategy for localized, opioid-sparing pain management in oral surgery. Further large-scale clinical trials and comprehensive physicochemical and toxicological evaluations are required to validate these findings and optimize the formulation for broader clinical application. The study was conducted in accordance with the WMA Declaration of Helsinki and approved by the Research Ethics Committee of Qazvin University of Medical Sciences (approval ID: IR.QUMS.REC.1402.102) and the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (approval ID: IRCT20221201056682N1, 2023-07-17).

title: Marine volatile organic compounds air-sea exchange dynamics across a summer-to-autumn ecosystem transition
summary: Marine ecosystems influence atmospheric chemistry and climate by exchanging volatile organic compounds (VOCs) with the atmosphere, yet the chemical diversity and the environmental controls of the exchanged compounds remain poorly constraine
content: Marine ecosystems influence atmospheric chemistry and climate by exchanging volatile organic compounds (VOCs) with the atmosphere, yet the chemical diversity and the environmental controls of the exchanged compounds remain poorly constrained. This gap persists because most marine observations are targeted, short-term, and narrow-suite measurements that seldom deliver chemically broad, continuous fluxes. Here we show that marine VOC exchange is chemically diverse and changes in magnitude and composition on event‑to‑season timescales. Using continuous flux measurements of 73 m/z features in the Baltic Sea, we observe a pronounced reorganization of net exchange: early organosulfur emissions diminish as cyanobacterial biomass declines (indicating water-side source limitation), while oxygenated and nitrogen-containing VOCs exhibit mixed behaviors ranging from deposition to episodic emissions (often dominated by wind-driven gas transfer kinetics). Together, these results demonstrate that chemically diverse marine VOC exchange is closely coupled to wind-induced mixing, water‑column structure, and phytoplankton community succession, highlighting the need to resolve these dynamic ecosystem states to predict future atmospheric composition.

title: Correlated Charge Order Intertwined With Time‐Reversal Symmetry‐Breaking Nodal Superconductivity in the Kagome Superconductor CeRu3Si2
summary: Kagome materials provide a platform for exploring flat‐band‐driven symmetry‐breaking quantum states. Here, we introduce CeRu 3 Si 2 , a kagome superconductor in which our first‐principles calculations show the coexistence of Ru ‐orbital kag
content: Kagome materials provide a platform for exploring flat‐band‐driven symmetry‐breaking quantum states. Here, we introduce CeRu 3 Si 2 , a kagome superconductor in which our first‐principles calculations show the coexistence of Ru ‐orbital kagome flat bands and flat bands derived from ‐states. X‐ray diffraction reveals a dominant 1/2 charge order with a much weaker 1/3 component persisting up to room temperature. Deep within the charge‐ordered state, magnetoresistance emerges below 80 K and strengthens further below 30 K. Zero‐field muon spin‐rotation measurements show no time‐reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking in the normal state, in contrast to and . However, an applied magnetic field induces weak magnetism. Across the family (=La, Y, Ce), the superconducting transition temperature scales linearly with the onset temperature of normal‐state TRS breaking and the magnitude of the field‐induced magnetic response, revealing a direct positive correlation between normal‐state symmetry breaking and superconductivity. Furthermore, we identify that is the first 132‐type kagome compound to host nodal superconductivity together with spontaneous internal magnetic fields, suggestive of intrinsic TRS breaking in the superconducting state. These results establish as a unique platform where kagome‐derived ‐ and ‐electron flat bands coexist with rich hierarchy of electronic orders.

title: Forecasting the flame: simulating future wildfire regimes in the Northeast Mediterranean
source: Natural hazards and earth system sciences
summary: Despite a global decline in total burned area, high-impact wildfire events continue to pose growing threats to ecosystems and human communities. As climate change amplifies hydroclimatic extremes, cycles of precipitation-driven fuel build-u
content: Despite a global decline in total burned area, high-impact wildfire events continue to pose growing threats to ecosystems and human communities. As climate change amplifies hydroclimatic extremes, cycles of precipitation-driven fuel build-up followed by persistent drought are increasing the likelihood of severe wildfires. Moving beyond estimates of total burned area, this study aims to answer “where, and how often, will future landscapes burn?” by quantifying wildfire hazard through fire probability and fire return intervals for the northern segment of the Eastern Mediterranean Basin (34–46° N, 24–50° E), a region where such extremes are expected to fundamentally alter fire regimes. Potential changes in fire activity were investigated for the period 1961–2100 using the process-based dynamic vegetation model LPJ-GUESS coupled with SIMFIRE–BLAZE wildfire modules. Terrestrial vegetation was represented using regionally parameterised Plant Functional Types, and simulations were forced with ERA5-Land reanalysis for the historical period (1961–2025) and an ensemble of five CMIP6 climate projections under a high-emissions scenario (SSP5-8.5) for exploratory future analysis (2015–2100). Benchmarking against MODIS MCD64A1 observations revealed that while the model successfully reproduced domain-scale burned area magnitudes and interannual variability, weak spatial agreement highlighted the strong influence of localised anthropogenic ignition and suppression processes not represented in the natural-potential experimental design. Future projections indicated that changes in fire probability and return intervals are unlikely to be spatially uniform. Instead, simulation results highlight a fundamental reorganization of fire regimes driven by the interplay between hydroclimatic change, vegetation dynamics, and landscape structure. By combining temporally explicit reanalysis data with ensemble climate projections, this study distinguishes between the role of observed hydroclimatic extremes in shaping historical fire activity and the importance of long-term climate trajectories in constraining future risk. The findings suggest that climate change may not simply increase overall wildfire activity in the Northeast Mediterranean, but rather systematically redistribute fire risk across its distinct ecoregions, with urgent implications for anticipating emerging hotspots and adapting fire management strategies.

title: A global 3D chlorophyll a dataset derived from multimodal deep learning reconstruction
summary: Chlorophyll a (Chl a ) is a key variable for characterizing marine phytoplankton biomass and upper-ocean biogeochemical variability. Existing global products are generally limited to the ocean surface and therefore cannot adequately resolve
content: Chlorophyll a (Chl a ) is a key variable for characterizing marine phytoplankton biomass and upper-ocean biogeochemical variability. Existing global products are generally limited to the ocean surface and therefore cannot adequately resolve subsurface vertical structure. In this study, a multimodal Profile-Surface Transformer (PST) framework was developed by integrating Biogeochemical-Argo (BGC-Argo) Chl a profiles, Core-Argo temperature-salinity profiles, and satellite-derived surface Chl a to reconstruct the three-dimensional (3D) vertical structure of Chl a from 10 to 500 m depth. A global monthly mean 3D Chl a dataset at 1° spatial resolution for January 2005–June 2025 was subsequently constructed. Evaluation of the dataset demonstrates that PST exhibits robust stability and effective profile reconstruction capability across various generalization scenarios. The coefficients of determination under random split, year-based split, and spatial cross-validation are 0.89, 0.87, and 0.86 ± 0.01, respectively. Furthermore, independent external validation using ship-based observations confirms that the model maintains good generalization performance across different observing systems. The constructed dataset successfully reproduces known global patterns of Chl a vertical structure and its subsurface chlorophyll maximum (SCM), as well as their seasonal variability. Variability in SCM depth is primarily characterized by regionally heterogeneous redistribution superimposed on a persistent zonal background, rather than by a pronounced monotonic change in the global mean depth. Overall, the constructed long-term 3D Chl a dataset integrates surface observations and discrete biogeochemical profiles, delivering a new observationally constrained global product. This dataset is well-suited for studies on the vertical ecological structure of phytoplankton, long-term ocean biogeochemical variability, and the responses of upper-ocean ecosystems to climate change. The dataset is publicly available from Zenodo (Meng et al., 2026a) at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22726410.

title: Millimeter-wave Detections of Symbiotic Stars in SPT and ACT Data
summary: We present the results of a joint targeted search of candidate symbiotic stars at millimeter wavelengths using the South Pole Telescope (SPT) and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Candidates are selected from the New Online Database of
content: We present the results of a joint targeted search of candidate symbiotic stars at millimeter wavelengths using the South Pole Telescope (SPT) and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Candidates are selected from the New Online Database of Symbiotic Variables, restricting to objects that are within either the SPT-3G or ACT~DR6 footprint, covering most of the southern hemisphere and up to a declination of + 20 ∘ . Forced photometry on the 828 candidate symbiotic star locations in SPT and ACT data results in 31 unique objects detected with more than a 3 σ significance using two frequency bands: 18 confirmed and 13 suspected symbiotic stars. We provide the SPT and ACT 95/98, 150, and 220~GHz light curves, along with optical and infrared light curves from 2016–2026, as well as spectral energy distributions, physical parameters from the literature, and brief summaries regarding the nature of each individual object. Using Herschel SPIRE data from 2013, we place upper limits on millimeter flux for CN Cha near the beginning of the optical rise in its 2012/2013 nova, which suggests a strong variability and lag at millimeter wavelengths and results in a rare observance of a potential Galactic millimeter slow transient. In addition, we provide coadded thumbnails and light curves for the remaining 797 candidate symbiotic stars that did not pass our detection thresholds. Millimeter-wave emission from symbiotic stars is primarily a combination of free-free emission of the ionization region and optically thick blackbody emission of the cooler dust components of the system. When combined with contemporaneous multi-wavelength observations, millimeter-wave observations can be used to test binary models of symbiotic stars and provide insight on the geometry and physical properties of these systems.

title: Quasi-degenerate cation occupation enables oxygen-vacancy defect healing in nonlinear optical crystals
summary: Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which
content: Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which couple with dopants and obscure or degrade the intrinsic properties. Therefore, chemical substitution that enables atomically precise engineering of materials without generating defect structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to overcome this detrimental coupling and successfully apply it to the langasite-family nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal, La 3 TiGa 5 O 14 (LGTi). Therein, the cross-site occupation of Ti and Ti 3+ /Ti 4+ redox flexibility improves the kinetic accessibility of oxygen-vacancy ( V O ) defects associated with cation disorder, enabling their removal during oxidative annealing. The oxidized LGTi single crystal has a V O -related defect concentration below the electron paramagnetic resonance detection limit, with a laser damage threshold of 2.53 GW/cm 2 and a large NLO coefficient of 3.51 pm/V, both exceeding the previously reported values for bulk langasite-family crystals. Overall, this work provides a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to mitigate substitution-induced defects in structurally complex crystalline systems and has great prospects in enhancing material performance.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Pretrained Vision-Foundation Models for Post-Stack Seismic-Data Denoising
summary: We present a parameter-efficient workflow for denoising post-stack seismic data with pretrained vision encoders, including the self-distillation with no labels (DINO) family. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) branches and reconstruction components
content: We present a parameter-efficient workflow for denoising post-stack seismic data with pretrained vision encoders, including the self-distillation with no labels (DINO) family. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) branches and reconstruction components are trained on synthetic pairs; the decoder is then adapted to noisy field patches without clean targets. On test data from a progressive growing generative adversarial network (PGGAN), DINOv2 achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 41.46 dB across three training seeds using 1.79 million trainable parameters, compared with 42.21 dB for U-Net and 41.93 dB for the denoising convolutional neural network (DnCNN). In an independent reflectivity-based test without further training, U-Net gave the highest PSNR under Gaussian noise, whereas DINOv3 without LoRA ranked first under coherent linear and stripe noise. Comparisons based on China land and Mobil amplitude variation with offset (AVO) field sections showed reduced incoherent background noise and clearer dominant reflections, alongside spectral narrowing and reflection-aligned residuals that indicate a risk of losing fine detail. The workflow provides a reproducible baseline for adapting pretrained vision encoders to post-stack seismic denoising.

title: Marine organic aerosols reflect ecosystem variability from phytoplankton functional types to micronekton
summary: Marine organic aerosols remain a major source of uncertainty in aerosol cloud-climate interactions, in part because marine ecosystem structure and biological drivers are typically reduced to bulk chlorophyll- a . Here, a full year of high-r
content: Marine organic aerosols remain a major source of uncertainty in aerosol cloud-climate interactions, in part because marine ecosystem structure and biological drivers are typically reduced to bulk chlorophyll- a . Here, a full year of high-resolution aerosol mass spectrometry measurements at Mace Head (west coast of Ireland) is combined with HYSPLIT air-masses exposure and gap-free phytoplankton functional type (PFT) fields to explore influences on primary marine organic aerosol (PMOA) and methanesulphonic acid (MSA). During the spring-summer diatom climax, PMOA correlates with dominant bloom taxa ( R =0.62–0.70) and micronekton ( R =0.55). Strong PFTs covariance, however, prevented robust attribution to a single species. Cross-entropy showed PMOA maxima at 0–2 d for bloom-forming taxa and micronekton at 14 d, consistent with early labile release and later lysis/grazing while MSA also showed lagged associations to both PFT and micronekton. Mechanical forcing was evaluated from source-region wave Reynolds number, whitecap coverage and bubble-plume penetration. Across the three selected case studies, PMOA reflected the balance between ecosystem state and air-sea transfer. Spring–summer 2018 case combined high sea-surface particulate organic carbon (POC) and nutrients drawdown with sufficient air-sea transfer; August 2018 had stronger forcing, but lower POC while August 2009 combined higher POC and the strongest air-sea transfer. These findings support considering ecosystem composition and nutrients alongside air-sea transfer when representing natural marine aerosols and motivate future research vessel campaigns and mesocosm experiments to explicitly manipulate PFT interactions.

title: Electron-Beam Induced Methane Decomposition for in Situ Carbon Doping of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
summary: Controlling the spatial incorporation of carbon into hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is essential for engineering optically active defects, yet existing approaches lack nanoscale precision and control over the carbon supply. We demonstrate a
content: Controlling the spatial incorporation of carbon into hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is essential for engineering optically active defects, yet existing approaches lack nanoscale precision and control over the carbon supply. We demonstrate a method for carbon doping hBN using electron-beam irradiation in a low-pressure methane atmosphere in which the beam simultaneously generates vacancies and decomposes methane into carbon and hydrogen atoms. Using annular dark-field (ADF) scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), we show that increasing methane partial pressure suppresses pore growth and drives the formation of triangular boron-terminated pores through preferential hydrogen etching of nitrogen. Time-resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping reveals progressive carbon incorporation into the lattice, accompanied by boron and nitrogen depletion. Carbon incorporation is largely confined to the irradiated area, arranging in a hexagonal pattern in patches not exceeding ∼1 nm in size, with modifications to the local electronic environment visible in their EEL fine structure spectra.

title: An uncertainty-aware geospatial framework for climate-resilient cultivation planning of Panax notoginseng in Northern Vietnam
summary: High-value medicinal plants with narrow ecological tolerances are increasingly threatened by climate change, yet cultivation planning often overlooks climate-model uncertainty and land-use constraints. We developed an uncertainty-aware geos
content: High-value medicinal plants with narrow ecological tolerances are increasingly threatened by climate change, yet cultivation planning often overlooks climate-model uncertainty and land-use constraints. We developed an uncertainty-aware geospatial framework to support climate-resilient cultivation planning for Panax notoginseng in northern Vietnam. The framework integrates GIS-based fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (fuzzy-AHP) modelling, non-compensatory ecological thresholds, five CMIP6 climate models, two high-emission scenarios (SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5), model–scenario consensus analysis, and land-use exclusion masks. The baseline suitability model, independently evaluated using 27 published occurrence records, achieved an AUC of 0.68 and a continuous Boyce index of 0.93. Under baseline conditions, highly suitable land covered approximately 7250 km 2 (7.9% of the valid study area). By 2041–2070, the ensemble-mean highly suitable area decreased to approximately 2330 km 2 under SSP3-7.0 and 1580 km 2 under SSP5-8.5, representing reductions of 68% and 78%, respectively.
