Although individual projections identified broader suitable areas, high-confidence climate-stable S1 cores were much smaller, declining from 3830 km 2 at the weakest agreement threshold to 139 km 2 under full agreement. Increasingly stringent model–scenario agreement was the main driver of the reduction in candidate land; after land-use exclusions, potentially available cultivation land ranged from 3360 to 127 km 2 across consensus thresholds, and most excluded stable-core land was conservation-designated. The framework provides uncertainty-aware decision-support maps for climate-smart cultivation and conservation planning, while recognizing that field validation, tenure, accessibility, and socioeconomic feasibility remain necessary before site-level implementation.

title: Mapping Gender (In)Justice in the European Green Transition: a Comparative Analysis of Eco-Social Indicators
summary: The green transition is frequently evaluated through narrow technocratic or economic lenses, overlooking the gendered distribution of power and resources. The study aims to map the gendered domains of the European green transition, revealin
content: The green transition is frequently evaluated through narrow technocratic or economic lenses, overlooking the gendered distribution of power and resources. The study aims to map the gendered domains of the European green transition, revealing how gender-blind policy design may reproduce existing social inequalities. Integrating eco-feminist and intersectional perspectives, the research identifies critical intersections between environmental and social goals, and investigates the selected domains of the green transition: mobility, housing and green labor market. Utilizing secondary data from Eurostat and the European Institute for Gender Equality, we select and evaluate eleven gender-sensitive indicators across the EU-27. Descriptive analysis is used to map gender gaps and hierarchical cluster analysis is applied to classify national performance profiles. The findings reveal systemic gender inequality across the EU. While men dominate the green labor market, women remain more dependent on public transport and bear a disproportionate housing-related burden. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the achievement of gender justice is deeply contingent upon prevailing welfare state models. The analysis identifies four profiles: North-Western group demonstrating horizontal professional segregation despite egalitarian pragmatism; Continental group reflecting a conservative compromise with moderate gender gaps across all analyzed domains; Central-Eastern group marked by high horizontal labor segregation and significant internal variation in both sustainable mobility and housing; South-Eastern group exhibiting the highest gender pay gaps and a significant risk of transport poverty for women. We argue that achieving just sustainability requires shifting towards policies that explicitly address structural gender imbalances, both though policy design and indicators used for evaluation.

title: Systematic Electrochemical Investigation of Iron Removal from Coal Fly Ash Acid Leaching Solution by Electrodeposition
summary: Electrodeposition is a clean, efficient method for separating Al and Fe from coal fly ash acid leachate. This study systematically investigates Fe electrodeposition removal. Thermodynamic and electrochemical analyses confirm theoretical fea
content: Electrodeposition is a clean, efficient method for separating Al and Fe from coal fly ash acid leachate. This study systematically investigates Fe electrodeposition removal. Thermodynamic and electrochemical analyses confirm theoretical feasibility, Pb, Cu, Ni co-deposit with Fe, while Na, K, Ca, Mg, Li, Zn, Ga, Cr, Ti do not interfere. Increasing temperature and Fe 2+ concentration shifts Fe 2+ /Fe reduction potential positively, promoting deposition. Titanium and lead electrodes suppress hydrogen evolution. High AlCl 3 concentration effectively suppresses hydrogen evolution without significantly inhibiting Fe deposition. Kinetics show that both Fe 2+ /Fe and Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ reductions are diffusion-controlled, with diffusion coefficients ∼2.4 × 10 −5 and 1.0 × 10 −6 cm 2 s −1 . With increasing applied potential, Fe nucleation changes from progressive to instantaneous, reducing grain size and transforming morphology from irregular flakes to star-shaped pentagonal structures. This work provides electrochemical theoretical support for optimizing Fe electrodeposition removal from coal fly ash acid leachate.

title: Cataclysmic variables from Gaia XP spectra: The Gaia emission-line magnitude (GEM) diagram
summary: Gaia DR3 opens a new window for the census of Galactic stellar populations in all-sky surveys, specifically for identifying cataclysmic variables (CVs). While the majority of CVs are distributed below the main sequence on the Gaia HR diagra
content: Gaia DR3 opens a new window for the census of Galactic stellar populations in all-sky surveys, specifically for identifying cataclysmic variables (CVs). While the majority of CVs are distributed below the main sequence on the Gaia HR diagram, identifying them among dominant background stellar populations remains a significant challenge. Here, we present the Gaia Emission-line Magnitude (GEM) diagram - a tool designed to isolate CV candidates from background stars located below the main sequence. Using Gaia photometric data and low-resolution BP/RP (XP) spectra, we construct the GEM diagram by plotting the extinction-corrected absolute magnitude ( M G 0 ) against the pseudo-equivalent width of the H α line ( p g E W H α ), which is computed via a Gaussian line-profile approximation. We find that known CVs and major stellar background populations, including white dwarfs, hot subdwarfs, and white dwarf-main sequence binaries, occupy distinct regions on the GEM diagram, reflecting both their physical properties and the low-resolution nature of the Gaia XP spectra. We define an empirical selection line on the GEM diagram to separate true H α -emitting CVs from background contaminants. As a proof of concept, we apply the GEM diagram to a Gaia volume-limited sample within 250 pc ( G < 17.5 mag) distributed below the main sequence, recovering known CVs. Additionally, we identify three new CV candidates whose accreting nature is supported by archival X-ray data and optical variability. Compared to traditional optical color-based selection techniques, the GEM diagram uses Gaia’s low-resolution spectra for initial target identification in all-sky surveys. This provides a more reliable framework for the statistical selection of CV candidates prior to ground-based spectroscopic follow-up and can be scaled to future Gaia data releases to map Galactic emission-line star populations.

title: Efficient Mitigation of Copper-Induced Oxidative Stress Using Chitosan-Based Iron Oxide Nanoparticles for Applications in Agriculture
summary: Copper (Cu) is an essential plant micronutrient; however, its accumulation in agricultural soils due to mining, industrial discharge, and intensive agrochemical use can cause phytotoxicity. Excess Cu promotes reactive oxygen species (ROS) a
content: Copper (Cu) is an essential plant micronutrient; however, its accumulation in agricultural soils due to mining, industrial discharge, and intensive agrochemical use can cause phytotoxicity. Excess Cu promotes reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, disrupts cellular functions, and impairs plant growth. Conventional mitigation approaches include soil amendments, phytoremediation, antioxidant supplementation, and chelation, while engineered nanomaterials offer additional possibilities for metal-stress management. This study introduces a multifunctional nanoparticle-based approach for Cu binding and mitigation of associated oxidative stress. We developed functionalized iron oxide (Fe3O4) nanoparticles (MIONPs) through sequential surface modification of Fe3O4 nanoparticles with chitosan, glutathione, and 3-mercaptopropionic acid. MIONPs exhibited a Cu-binding efficiency of 47.6%, compared with 11.8% for bare Fe3O4 nanoparticles (BIONPs) under the tested conditions. In Cu-stressed Solanum lycopersicum seedlings, MIONPs treatment improved germination rates from 5.3 to 14.6 day−1 under 100 μM Cu stress and from 3.2 to 15.9 day−1 under 200 μM Cu stress, compared with 15.7 day−1 in the untreated control. MIONPs treatment also reduced ROS-associated fluorescence and was associated with improved mitochondrial fluorescence patterns and better-preserved nuclear organization. These findings highlight the potential of surface-functionalized Fe3O4 nanoparticles for agricultural applications.

title: Depth Control of Room-Temperature Quantum Emitters in Gallium Nitride
summary: Bright quantum emitters are key components for quantum communication systems. Radiative point defects in gallium nitride (GaN) are promising candidates for room-temperature single-photon emission, operating from the visible to the telecom O
content: Bright quantum emitters are key components for quantum communication systems. Radiative point defects in gallium nitride (GaN) are promising candidates for room-temperature single-photon emission, operating from the visible to the telecom O-band. Despite their potential, their integration into photonic structures has remained limited, with experimental photon extraction efficiencies far below simulated predictions. To identify the origin of this limitation, we characterize visible and near-infrared quantum emitters in GaN epilayers grown on c-plane sapphire substrates exhibiting narrow linewidths (∼5.8 nm), high photon count rates (>2 MHz), and strong antibunching, reaching g(2)(0) values as low as 0.06 at room temperature. We find that these emitters are located near the GaN/substrate interface, thereby limiting their coupling to optical modes. Building on this observation, we show that the insertion of a thin low-temperature GaN interlayer enables the formation of quantum emitters at arbitrary depths with sub-60 nm accuracy, independent of the substrate. The intentionally introduced emitters exhibit room-temperature optical properties comparable to naturally occurring ones, including narrow linewidths (∼5.6 nm), saturation count rates exceeding 1.5 MHz, high Debye–Waller factors (0.45–0.99), and strong antibunching. The resulting epilayer fully coalesces within less than 250 nm, ensuring compatibility with GaN-based cavity fabrication and enabling emitter placement within intrinsic regions of p–i–n diode architectures. These results mark a decisive step toward efficient emitter-cavity coupling, enabling the realization of cavity-enhanced quantum emission in GaN.

title: Site-selective activation of near-infrared emitters in hBN
summary: Near-infrared (NIR) emitters in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) have recently emerged as bright and spectrally stable light sources, but they have so far been found at locations set by the local defect environment rather than by design. Here
content: Near-infrared (NIR) emitters in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) have recently emerged as bright and spectrally stable light sources, but they have so far been found at locations set by the local defect environment rather than by design. Here we show that NIR emitters can be activated at predefined sites by combining single-shot femtosecond laser writing with annealing in an oxygenrich environment. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of site-selective activation of NIR emitters in hBN. The written matrices are recovered in post-anneal photoluminescence maps, including in collection bands centred at 800 and 900 nm. Site-resolved spectra under 532, 635 and 785 nm excitation show narrow lines extending to 1 µm; 83% of the spectra acquired at written sites under 785 nm excitation and 71% under 635 nm excitation contain at least one resolved peak above 810 nm. The integrated emission increases with writing-pulse energy over the range studied, and many sites host more than one emitter, which identifies lower writing energies as the route to single-emitter occupancy. Photon-correlation measurements on selected sites show antibunching, with a raw, uncorrected second-order correlation value g (2) (0) of 0.31 in a band centred at 850 nm. Spectral time series reveal bands that persist over the recorded intervals together with intermittent emission beyond 900 nm. Comparison with identically written, argon-annealed samples indicates that the annealing atmosphere controls the spectral range of the activated emitters, while the laser defines where they form.

title: Synthesis of MnO2 nanostructures as efficient electrode materials for supercapacitors: effect of calcination temperature
source: Materials for Renewable and Sustainable Energy
summary: To assess the impact on the physicochemical and electrochemical characteristics of manganese oxide (MnO 2 ) nanostructures (NSs), a hydrothermal technique was used to synthesize nanostructures, which were then thermally annealed at differen
content: To assess the impact on the physicochemical and electrochemical characteristics of manganese oxide (MnO 2 ) nanostructures (NSs), a hydrothermal technique was used to synthesize nanostructures, which were then thermally annealed at different temperatures. The successful synthesis of MnO 2 NSs was confirmed by structural and morphological characterization. According to electrochemical characterization, the pseudocapacitive behavior of the MnO 2 -based electrode is significantly influenced by the calcination temperature, with 400 °C (MO-1), 500 °C (MO-2), and 600 °C (MO-3) as the respective temperatures. In a 1 M KOH electrolyte, the optimized MO-1 electrode showed a specific capacitance of 280 F/g at 10 mA/cm 2 . Additionally, after 5000 GCD cycles, the MO-1 electrode showed outstanding cycling stability, with nearly 82.3% retention of its initial capacitance. An asymmetric supercapacitor (ASSC) device assembled with MO-1 as the positive electrode and activated carbon as the negative electrode delivered a specific capacitance of 126.7 F/g at 10 mA/cm 2 and maintained 95.4% of its capacitance over 10,000 cycles. The ASSC device also achieved an energy density of 39.6 Wh/kg and a power density of 3750 W/kg at 10 mA/cm 2 .

title: Ultrathin BN layers grown on sapphire by molecular beam epitaxy at low and high temperature
summary: Ultrathin boron nitride (BN) layers have been synthesized by nitrogen plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on c-plane sapphire substrate at two low (50 °C) and high temperature (1000 °C), respectively. Sharp and clear light absorption pea
content: Ultrathin boron nitride (BN) layers have been synthesized by nitrogen plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on c-plane sapphire substrate at two low (50 °C) and high temperature (1000 °C), respectively. Sharp and clear light absorption peaks very close to 200 nm with nearly zero absorbance in the range of 225−700 nm have been measured, irrespective of the growth temperature. The present study demonstrates the formation of sp 2 -hybridized BN material at both temperatures, albeit with different polytypes. The hexagonal BN polytype was mostly developed when the layers are grown at the higher temperature, whereas the less ordered turbostratic BN polytype formed primarily when the layers are grown near room temperature (RT). We observe a noticeable enhancement in Young modulus and hardness for the sample grown near RT, suggesting that the deposition of ultrathin BN material at low temperature is a meaningful strategy to further increase the sapphire surface resistance against mechanical damage yet preserving its transparency.

title: Monolithically integrated flexible multimodal healthcare electronics on perovskite piezoelectric thin film for human motion and physiological signal monitoring
summary: Integrating multiple sensing modalities into a compact, mechanically compliant platform is essential for wearable healthcare electronics aimed at monitoring human motion and physiological signals. However, conventional multimodal sensors ty
content: Integrating multiple sensing modalities into a compact, mechanically compliant platform is essential for wearable healthcare electronics aimed at monitoring human motion and physiological signals. However, conventional multimodal sensors typically rely on rigid, multilayered architectures that limit flexibility, increase fabrication complexity, and introduce mechanically vulnerable interfacial boundaries. Here, we present a monolithically integrated flexible multimodal healthcare electronics (f-MHE) platform fabricated on a perovskite piezoelectric thin film, enabling dual-parameter detection of pressure and temperature within a single-layer architecture. The platform integrates an interdigitated-electrode piezoelectric pressure sensor for pulse-wave detection and a serpentine thermoresistive temperature sensor for skin-temperature measurement. The monolithic design eliminates multilayer stacking and repeated alignment/etching steps, thereby simplifying fabrication, reducing interfacial boundaries, and enhancing mechanical integrity. As a result, the f-MHE achieves an ultrathin (< 5 μm), mechanically compliant form factor that enables conformal attachment to curved and deformable surfaces, including human skin. The device exhibits a pressure sensitivity of 24.1 mV·kPa−1 with a resolution of < 0.1 kPa over 0.1–25 kPa, and a temperature sensitivity of 5.03 Ω·°C–1 with a resolution of < 0.1 °C over 25–45 °C. Robust linearity, stability, and durability are maintained under repeated mechanical deformation. Multimodal sensing is further validated through real-time, simultaneous monitoring of pulse waves, respiration, and body motion. This work provides a structurally simple yet highly efficient and reliable strategy for multifunctional sensor integration and highlights the potential of monolithic thin-film platforms for next-generation wearable health monitoring.

This work represents a rapid and affordable analytical approach for analyzing complex lipid mixtures in situations where conventional chromatography cannot be used, including analysis on a portable mass spectrometer.

title: Arsenite (Trisenox) Bridges the Redox Centers of Thioredoxin Reductase
summary: Arsenic trioxide (Trisenox) is an effective treatment for acute promyelocytic leukemia and is being explored for broader anticancer applications, yet our understanding of the molecular basis of its anticancer activity remains incomplete. Un
content: Arsenic trioxide (Trisenox) is an effective treatment for acute promyelocytic leukemia and is being explored for broader anticancer applications, yet our understanding of the molecular basis of its anticancer activity remains incomplete. Under physiological conditions, arsenic trioxide forms arsenite, As(OH)3, which has been proposed to target the thioredoxin system. Here, we investigate the structural basis of arsenite interaction with mammalian thioredoxin reductase 1 (TrxR1, TXNRD1), a flavoenzyme selenoprotein essential for maintaining cellular redox homeostasis. Arsenic and selenium K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy, including high-energy resolution fluorescence detected (HERFD)-XAS, were combined with site-directed mutagenesis and density functional theory calculations. Wild-type TrxR1 forms a well-defined As(SeR)(SR)2 coordination environment in which arsenite binds the catalytic selenocysteine residue Sec498 and bridges the C-terminal and N-terminal redox centers of the enzyme. Replacement of Sec498 by cysteine yields an As(OH)(SR)2 species, whereas substitution by serine abolishes detectable binding. These results provide the first direct structural characterization of arsenite bound to TrxR1 and reveal a mechanism by which arsenite inhibits catalysis through cross-linking of the enzyme’s redox centers. The findings establish a molecular basis for targeting of the thioredoxin system by arsenic trioxide and provide new insight into the chemistry underlying its anticancer activity.

title: How government spending relates to eco-social outcomes: a global comparative analysis from 2005 to 2019
summary: Governments play a central role in achieving eco-social outcomes, understood as the joint attainment of social wellbeing and environmental sustainability. Yet empirical evidence on how government spending relates to eco-social outcomes rema
content: Governments play a central role in achieving eco-social outcomes, understood as the joint attainment of social wellbeing and environmental sustainability. Yet empirical evidence on how government spending relates to eco-social outcomes remains limited. This study examines the relationship between government spending, human needs satisfaction, and carbon implications across 116 countries between 2005 and 2019 using input-output and regression analyses. To account for global climate justice, we adjust carbon intensities (CO 2 e/US$) according to countries’ fair shares of the remaining global carbon budget. These equity-adjusted carbon intensities capture both the carbon efficiency of spending and countries’ position relative to their fair carbon budgets. We find that higher government spending is generally associated with better social outcomes, although returns diminish at higher spending levels and depend on spending composition. Spending on education and recreation, social protection , and public administration is linked to better social outcomes and comparatively low equity-adjusted carbon intensities. By contrast, industry -related government spending consistently exhibits high intensities, suggesting potential carbon lock-ins. For most spending categories, intensities tend to be lower in countries with better social outcomes, with housing as a notable exception. Order and defense spending is associated with lower social outcomes despite substantial carbon impacts. Across key welfare sectors, including education and recreation, health and environment , and social protection , government spending is linked to more favorable eco-social outcomes than household spending, suggesting advantages of public and collective provisioning.

title: Effect of quark-hadron phase transitions on the neutron star mass distribution
summary: The neutron star (NS) mass distribution serves as a crucial probe of the dense matter equation of state (EOS) and core-collapse supernova explosion mechanisms. Although observations reveal a bimodal NS mass distribution, existing theoretica
content: The neutron star (NS) mass distribution serves as a crucial probe of the dense matter equation of state (EOS) and core-collapse supernova explosion mechanisms. Although observations reveal a bimodal NS mass distribution, existing theoretical simulations often struggle to naturally reproduce the high-mass peak, and the impact of the quark-hadron phase transition (PT) in high-density nuclear matter remains largely unexplored. Employing the 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamics code GR1D with hybrid EOSs incorporating a first-order PT (RDF1.1 and RDF1.2), we systematically simulate core-collapse supernovae for progenitors with zero-age main-sequence masses ranging from 13 to 120 M⊙. Our results reveal a threefold impact of the PT onset density on the final supernova fate: in low-compactness progenitors, an early PT truncates accretion and produces less massive NSs; in the critical-compactness regime, it facilitates successful explosions; and in high-compactness progenitors, it accelerates black hole formation. Compared with the ∼ 1.4 M⊙ peak typical of the conventional core-collapse scenario, the inclusion of the PT produces NSs with masses centered around 1.70 M⊙ for RDF1.1 and within 1.55–1.70 M⊙ for RDF1.2. Furthermore, we identify a novel formation channel whereby low-compactness progenitors with failed initial shocks can form more massive NSs via a PT induced second shock. Due to the fixed nature of the PT boundary, the final NS masses exhibit a pronounced clustering effect. This study elucidates the critical role of the quark-hadron PT in shaping the NS mass distribution, providing important astrophysical constraints on the properties of high-density nuclear matter and the formation mechanism of massive NSs.

title: Tailoring pore microenvironments in scalable classic COFs boosts solar H 2 O 2 production and antibiotic remediation
summary: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising for solar-driven chemical synthesis and environmental remediation, yet their practical application is constrained by the trade-off between structural sophistication and synthetic scalability.
content: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising for solar-driven chemical synthesis and environmental remediation, yet their practical application is constrained by the trade-off between structural sophistication and synthetic scalability. In this work, we develop a pore microenvironment engineering strategy on classic COF skeletons to boost photocatalytic performance without relying on intricate monomer design. Two isostructural hexagonal COFs (TTA-DMA and TTA-DHA) are synthesized via a facile, cost-effective autoclave solvothermal route using commercially available linkers, achieving gram-scale yield while preserving high crystallinity and uniform pore channels. Combined advanced transient spectroscopies and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that hydroxyl functionalization on pore walls rationally modulates localized electronic states, extending light harvesting, suppressing radiative charge recombination, accelerating charge separation, and lowering the O2 activation energy barrier. The optimized TTA-DHA delivers an exceptional solar H2O2 production rate of 14,562 μmol·g−1·h−1 with an apparent quantum yield of 9.1% at 400 nm. The in situ generated H2O2 further drives a concurrent advanced oxidation cascade, achieving 85%–97% degradation of five representative recalcitrant antibiotics within 1 h under visible light. This work bridges scalable material fabrication with efficient solar energy conversion, providing a practical blueprint for functionalizing classic porous frameworks toward multipurpose applications.

title: Seawater Oxidation on Submicron-Crystalline Boron-Doped Diamond Electrodes
summary: Herein, we investigate selectivity of submicron-crystalline boron-doped diamond (SC BDD, ca 150 nm grain size) toward synthetic seawater oxidation. In seawater, Cl − oxidation reaction (ClOR) competes with water oxidation. We demonstrate th
content: Herein, we investigate selectivity of submicron-crystalline boron-doped diamond (SC BDD, ca 150 nm grain size) toward synthetic seawater oxidation. In seawater, Cl − oxidation reaction (ClOR) competes with water oxidation. We demonstrate that ClOR dominates at current densities of 20–100 mA cm −2 , producing ClO − and HClO (ClO − /HClO) species with ca 60% faradaic efficiency (FE). Concentrations of toxic byproducts ClO 3 − and ClO 4 − were found to be lower than that of ClO − /HClO by factors of 20 and 10 5 , respectively. Comparison of ClO − /HClO FEs to that of MC BDD ( ca 20 µm grain size) [Baturina et al., J. Electrochem. Soc. , 173, 146,501 (2026)] shows 25% decrease in the FE for the former material. We hypothesize that sp 2 carbon played a major role in suppressing the ClO − /HClO generation on SC BDD vs MC BDD. Comparison of polarization curves measured on SC BDD electrodes in seawater and 0.5 M NaCl shows a positive shift in the onset potential of Cl − oxidation accompanied by lower currents in the entire potential region for the former solution. This was attributed to competition of seawater constituents such as SO 4 2− for the sp 2 carbon active sites. XPS characterization shows surface oxidation to ether/hydroxyl, carbonyl and carboxyl groups after anodic oxidation.

title: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations
content: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties. We use a large grid of thermochemical models to predict the fluxes of 48 transitions from eight species observable with ALMA, spanning a wide range of system properties and external FUV fields of 102–105 G0. At fixed stellar and disk properties, all transitions generally brighten with increasing FUV field strength. HCO+ and CO fluxes increase monotonically in virtually all disks, whereas lower-excitation lines, particularly those of C2H and N2H+, respond weakly and non-monotonically. However, variations in stellar mass and disk size introduce substantial degeneracies, limiting the usefulness of individual line fluxes as tracers of external irradiation. We therefore assess all pairwise line flux ratios, which can significantly reduce these degeneracies, evaluating their correlation with the external field, the magnitude of their change across the FUV range, and predicted ALMA detectability. We identify 135 promising ratios, including several combining strong FUV sensitivity and high detectability with efficient single-tuning ALMA observations. The strongest diagnostics either contrast high- and low-excitation lines of the same or co-spatial species (e.g. CO J=8-7/J=1-0), probing different regions of the photoevaporative wind, or pair an FUV-sensitive wind tracer with comparatively insensitive emission arising closer to the disk (e.g. HCO+ J=3-2/C2H N=3-2). Our results provide a framework for identifying externally photoevaporating systems from spatially unresolved emission and constraining their incident FUV field strengths.

title: Nanoscale Architecture−Dependent Sulfur Utilization and Interfacial Evolution in Coaxial Electrospun Sulfurized Polyacrylonitrile Nanofibers for Lithium−Sulfur Batteries
summary: Coaxial electrospinning offers a versatile strategy to regulate the nanoscale internal architecture of fiber-based electrodes. In this work, sulfurized polyacrylonitrile (SPAN) nanofibers with dense, hollow, and collapsed structures are con
content: Coaxial electrospinning offers a versatile strategy to regulate the nanoscale internal architecture of fiber-based electrodes. In this work, sulfurized polyacrylonitrile (SPAN) nanofibers with dense, hollow, and collapsed structures are constructed by tuning the core flow rate. The characteristic nanoscale dimensions include an average shell thickness of 193 nm for H-SPAN and an average flattened layer thickness of 190 nm for C-SPAN. Although all samples exhibit similar chemical bonding configurations, their distinct internal architectures lead to markedly different electrochemical behaviors and interfacial evolution characteristics. Among the investigated structures, the hollow SPAN (H-SPAN) delivers the highest reversible capacity of 1042 mA h g−1 and maintains approximately 770 mA h g−1 after 100 cycles at 0.2C, together with a high-rate capacity exceeding 838 mA h g−1 at 1C. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals reduced charge-transfer resistance and improved interfacial kinetics in H-SPAN during cycling. Post-cycling morphology and depth-profile XPS analyses further demonstrate that the hollow architecture promotes more uniform sulfur participation while suppressing the formation of lithium-containing inactive species. In contrast, the collapsed structure (C-SPAN) exhibits increased interfacial resistance, sulfur signal attenuation, and limited electrochemical accessibility. These findings reveal the critical role of nanoscale internal architecture in governing sulfur utilization and interfacial evolution in SPAN-based electrodes, providing insights into the structural design of polymer-derived sulfur cathodes for lithium−sulfur batteries.

title: Polynomial regression model for wear rate of different nanocomposite coatings morphology
source: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
summary: This study evaluated how wear rate of electroless NiP nanocomposite coatings' is affected by deposition conditions, nodule size, hardness and friction coefficient. The changes in structure, composition, morphology, thickness, hardness, coef
content: This study evaluated how wear rate of electroless NiP nanocomposite coatings' is affected by deposition conditions, nodule size, hardness and friction coefficient. The changes in structure, composition, morphology, thickness, hardness, coefficient of friction and wear rate were investigated. The electroless (NiP-NPs) was performed at (75 0 C for 30 min), (75 0 C for 60 min), (75 0 C for 90 min), (85 0 C for 30 min), (85 0 C for 60 min), (85 0 C for 90 min), (95 0 C for 30 min), (95 0 C for 60 min), and (95 0 C for 90 min) first with (5 g l −1 ) of TiC NP, followed by (5 g l −1 ) of SiC NP. Finally, adding a mixture of ( 2.5 g l −1 ) of TiC NP and (2.5 g l −1 ) of SiC NP to the deposition solution. The scanning electron microscope results show that compared to the nodular structures formed with TiC nanoparticles, the presence of SiC nanoparticles in the plating solution results in a coating with smaller, denser nodules and more uniform surface. While, the presence of the both nanoparticles result in a coating with a different size, density, and agglomeration state depending on the incorporation level of each NP. The coating hardness of the EL NiP-TiC that was prepared at 90 min 95 0 C shows the highest hardness value and a best wear rate, and coefficient of friction. While EL NiP-SiC that was prepared at 90 min 75 0 C shows the highest hardness value. Otherwise, the best wear rate and the average coefficient of friction are obtained at 90 min at 95 °C. For the EL NiP-TiC-SiC, the highest hardness value was obtained at 30 min 95 °C,as well as the best wear rate and the average coefficient of friction. The wear rate was simulated using a polynomial regression model. The polynomial regression model achieved an in-sample (R 2 ) = 0.9233, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 0.0088, and (RMSE) of 0.0107. The results demonstrate consistency with experimental data and highlight the model’s ability to capture meaningful physical trends and variable interactions. This shows a high degree of agreement with experimental data and outstanding predicted accuracy.

title: Airborne Exposure of Human Primary Alveolar Cells to Benzo[a]pyrene Induces Acute Cellular Stress and Remodeling
summary: The majority of world’s population is exposed to air pollution levels that exceed WHO guidelines. Air pollution poses a significant threat to human respiratory health. Fine and ultrafine particles can penetrate deep into the respiratory tra
content: The majority of world’s population is exposed to air pollution levels that exceed WHO guidelines. Air pollution poses a significant threat to human respiratory health. Fine and ultrafine particles can penetrate deep into the respiratory tract and reach the alveoli, the primary site of gas exchange in the lung. As a result, the alveolar epithelium is particularly vulnerable to inhaled toxic pollutants. In this study, optimized Air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures of human primary alveolar cells were apically exposed to either a single, high-dose or to repeated low-doses of benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), a major constituent of air pollution, to mimic acute and chronic exposure, respectively. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enriched pathways of DNA repair and oxidative phosphorylation after acute or chronic exposure. Remarkably, only chronic exposure induced changes in inflammatory signaling and epithelial remodeling signatures, including enhanced DNA repair and altered mitochondrial activity. These findings were supported by immunofluorescence staining of the proliferative marker Ki67 and DNA damage marker γ-H2AX. Collectively, our data demonstrate that human primary alveolar cells are physiologically relevant to model airborne pollutant exposure and our studies highlight the importance of chronic exposure models for studying the impact of air pollutants. Interestingly, chronic exposure of primary alveolar cells elicited a qualitatively distinct response from acute exposure, and suggests that chronic exposure brings alveolar cells in a primed immunological state. This could have clinical implications as people living in polluted areas may be more vulnerable and at higher risk to additional triggers.

title: Effects of spectroscopically and thermochemically characterized dietary microplastics on growth, feeding behavior, and tissue histology of tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
summary: Microplastic contamination has emerged as a critical environmental issue in aquatic ecosystems. Yet, limited experimental evidence exists on the dietary effects of microplastics on fish growth, behavior, and tissue integrity under controlle
content: Microplastic contamination has emerged as a critical environmental issue in aquatic ecosystems. Yet, limited experimental evidence exists on the dietary effects of microplastics on fish growth, behavior, and tissue integrity under controlled conditions, as well as on the physicochemical characterization of test feeds and fish muscle. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of dietary polyvinyl chloride (PVC) microplastics (MPs) compared with inert kaolin clay particles on growth performance, feeding behavior, biochemical characteristics, and histopathology in Oreochromis niloticus . Five experimental feeds were formulated: a control feed (T0), feeds containing 3% and 6% kaolin (T1, T2), and feeds containing 3% and 6% PVC MPs (T3, T4). Fish were fed the experimental feeds for 49 days under controlled laboratory conditions. Physicochemical characterization of test particles, feeds, and fish muscle tissues was performed using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and Differential Scanning Calorimetry/Thermogravimetric Analysis (DSC/TGA). Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) was used to characterize PVC-MPs to assess their surface morphology, particle shape, and size. Growth indices, including weight gain, specific growth rate, feed conversion ratio, survival, and condition factor, were recorded alongside behavioral observations. Feeding behavior was assessed using standardized scores for feed acceptance (1–5), feeding activity (1–5), feeding latency (s), feed intake (g/fish/day), and feeding attempts (observed/day). FTIR analysis confirmed the structural integrity of PVC MPs and kaolin, as well as their presence in feeds and fish tissues. At the same time, DSC/TGA revealed reduced thermal stability in MPs and kaolin- supplemented feeds. SEM images showed irregular and fragmented MPs surfaces with size ranging approximately from 50 to 90 µm. Growth performance was significantly affected by dietary treatments, with notable differences in final weight (p = 0.037), weight gain (p = 0.040), feed conversion ratio (p = 0.011), and condition factor (p = 0.01). Feeding behavior was markedly impaired in MPs-fed groups, including reduced feed acceptance and feeding activity (p < 0.001), increased latency (p = 0.0003), and altered feed intake (p = 0.04). Although water quality parameters remained within optimal ranges, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, and salinity exhibited significant treatment-related interactions (p < 0.001). Histopathological examination revealed bundle dissociation, necrosis, segmentation, and atrophy in muscle, epithelial detachment, filament disruption, and lamellar loss in gills, and epithelial degeneration, mucosal disruption, and inflammatory infiltration in the gut of MPs-fed fish, whereas kaolin-fed groups showed minor alterations. In conclusion, dietary exposure to PVC microplastics adversely affected growth performance, feeding behavior, and tissue integrity in O. niloticus , even at relatively low inclusio

title: Assessing burned area trends in the Western Mediterranean: insights from long-term inventory and satellite data over the 1985–2025 period
summary: Background Burned area (BA) estimates are widely used to represent fire activity, yet their comparability across historical inventories and satellite-derived products remains limited. Few studies have systematically compared multiple BA dat
content: Background Burned area (BA) estimates are widely used to represent fire activity, yet their comparability across historical inventories and satellite-derived products remains limited. Few studies have systematically compared multiple BA data sources, which limits the robust assessment of spatial and temporal patterns and the comparison of trends, particularly in highly fire-prone regions. Aims To compare BA estimates across multiple data sources in Western Mediterranean Europe (WME) and assess their consistency in terms of patterns and trends. Methods A multi-source comparison was conducted between a historical inventory and three widely used satellite products, considering BA estimates across all land cover and their filtered versions (excluding agricultural and urban areas). Analyses were performed at annual, fire-season and off-season scales, using overlapping and extended periods, and applying trend and correlation analyses to evaluate consistency across sources. Key results Clear differences emerged in absolute BA values among products, with one satellite dataset consistently reporting higher estimates. Nevertheless, interannual variability and spatial patterns were broadly consistent across sources, with high agreement during annual and fire-season periods. Trend analyses indicated a general decline in BA over the last two decades, although off-season signals were more variable and less consistent. Conclusions and implications These findings highlight the value of integrating historical and satellite-based data to obtain a more comprehensive picture of fire activity in a region increasingly shaped by climate change and anthropogenic transformation. Cross-comparisons between data sources improve the identification of areas of convergence and uncertainty, strengthening the assessment of recent BA trends.

title: Evolution of the pore structure of activated coal-based activated carbon following activation pretreatment and its phased inhibition effect on spontaneous combustion
summary: Coal-based activated carbon is porous and easily oxidized. Under stacking conditions, it is prone to heat-storage oxidation and spontaneous combustion, which are dangerous. This study investigated the effects of particle size and H 3 PO 4 /
content: Coal-based activated carbon is porous and easily oxidized. Under stacking conditions, it is prone to heat-storage oxidation and spontaneous combustion, which are dangerous. This study investigated the effects of particle size and H 3 PO 4 /CH 3 COOK ratio on the pore structure development of coal-based activated carbon. The activated carbon with the most developed pore structure was subsequently treated with Na 2 S 2 O 8 solutions at different concentrations to evaluate the inhibition performance of Na 2 S 2 O 8 and to verify changes in pore structure during the inhibition process. The results showed that the adsorption capacity of activated carbon increased with decreasing particle size and first increased, then decreased, as the H 3 PO 4 /CH 3 COOK ratio increased. The 0–0.074 mm sample activated at an H 3 PO 4 /CH 3 COOK ratio of 1:3 exhibited the most developed pore structure and the highest adsorption capacity. That sample was treated with Na 2 S 2 O 8 at different concentrations. Among them, a 5% Na 2 S 2 O 8 yielded the best inhibition results, increasing the ignition temperature by 33.4℃and reducing the total heat release by 67.68 J/g. Under 5% Na 2 S 2 O 8 treatment, both heat release and mass loss during the oxidative heat accumulation and combustion phases were minimized, while the ignition temperature during the oxidative pyrolysis phase reached its maximum, and the activation energy for each stage was maximized. Furthermore, 5% Na 2 S 2 O 8 maintained a high adsorption capacity while passivating active sites. However, excessive concentration can cause micropores and mesopores to coalesce, destroying the pore structure of activated carbon and reducing adsorption capacity. This study supports the safe storage, transportation, and application of coal-based activated carbon.

title: Cascading Hybrid Metaheuristic Maximum Power Point Tracking for Photovoltaic Systems Under Partial Shading Conditions: A PSO–FPA–CSA–GWO Approach
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Partial shading conditions (PSC) distort the power–voltage characteristic of a photovoltaic (PV) array into a multipeaked surface, causing single-stage maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods to stagnate at local peaks. This paper propo
content: Partial shading conditions (PSC) distort the power–voltage characteristic of a photovoltaic (PV) array into a multipeaked surface, causing single-stage maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods to stagnate at local peaks. This paper proposes a cascading hybrid MPPT controller sequencing four metaheuristics with warm-started population handoff: particle swarm optimisation (PSO) for global exploration, the flower pollination algorithm (FPA) for neighbourhood narrowing, cuckoo search (CSA) for Lévy-flight refinement, and the grey wolf optimiser (GWO) for local convergence. The controller was evaluated on a single-diode model of a KC200GT module string under seven shading patterns, including two six-module patterns with competitive local peaks (peak ratio down to 0.56), against perturb-and-observe, incremental conductance, standalone PSO, and standalone GWO, over ten seeds per pattern (70 runs per method). The proposed cascade achieved a global-peak success rate of 100% (70/70 runs), a mean efficiency of 99.98% ± 0.03%, and a worst-case efficiency of 99.77%, versus 56.7% for standalone PSO and 51.3% for P&O/INC. Mean settling time was 0.042 s, matching the fastest single metaheuristic, with the lowest steady-state oscillation (0.058 W). A paired t-test confirmed a significant efficiency gain over GWO (p = 3.2 × 10⁻⁴) with significantly lower variance (Levene p = 4.0 × 10⁻⁴). An ablation study showed that removing CSA reduced the success rate to 98.6% and worst-case efficiency to 72.5%, confirming Lévy-flight refinement as the primary source of robustness. Staged metaheuristic composition, rather than any single algorithm, delivers consistently high tracking accuracy across a wide range of shading severities.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF REDUCED GRAPHENE OXIDE (rGO)-MODIFIED ELECTRODES FOR ELECTROCHEMICAL DETECTION OF LEAD (Pb2+)
source: Sainsmat Jurnal Ilmiah Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam
summary: Contamination of water bodies with lead (Pb2+) is a major concern for ecosystems and human health, requiring the development of sensitive, rapid and cost-effective analytical methods for its identification. In this work, an electrochemical
content: Contamination of water bodies with lead (Pb2+) is a major concern for ecosystems and human health, requiring the development of sensitive, rapid and cost-effective analytical methods for its identification. In this work, an electrochemical sensor based on screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) modified with reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was created for the detection of Pb2+ using cyclic voltammetry (CV) technique. The surface modification was done through the rGO incorporation into SPCE surface to enhance the electrical conductivity, increase the electroactive surface area and accelerate the electron transfer kinetics. Electrochemical characterization with K3[Fe(CN)6] redox probe showed great improvement in the performance of the electrode as there was an increase in the anodic peak current (Ipa) from 26.29584 μA to 37.57084 μA and a decrease in the peak to peak separation (ΔEp) from 0.632 V to 0.284 V after modification, suggesting an increase in the electrochemical activity and electron transfer rate. The fabricated sensor demonstrated a linear response to Pb2+ ions in the concentration range of 0.0010-0.0225 ppm with regression equation of y = 1090x - 2.734 (R2 = 0.99) and limit of detection (LoD) of 0.00254 ppm. These results show that the modification of SPCE by rGO remarkably enhances the electrochemical performance, which improves the sensitivity and simplifies the charge transfer. The fabricated SPCE-rGO sensor is a simple, sensitive and reliable platform for the determination of Pb2+, and it exhibits great potential for rapid environmental monitoring and on-site heavy metal analysis.

title: Effect of High‐Speed Railway Operational Conditions on the Dynamic AC Corrosion Behavior and Mechanisms of Pipeline Steel
summary: High‐speed railway operation induces dynamic AC interference on nearby buried steel pipelines, with periodic operating and shutdown periods. A dynamic AC corrosion simulation system incorporating AC current density, cathodic protection leve
content: High‐speed railway operation induces dynamic AC interference on nearby buried steel pipelines, with periodic operating and shutdown periods. A dynamic AC corrosion simulation system incorporating AC current density, cathodic protection level, and shutdown period is established to investigate corrosion behavior and mechanism. The corrosion rate increases with increasing dynamic AC current density and first decreases and then increases with a negative shift in cathodic protection potential. Increasing the shutdown period from 0 to 6 h reduces corrosion rates under different cathodic protection conditions. Under a 5 h shutdown period, 300 A/m 2 AC interference, and −1.15 V SCE cathodic protection, the corrosion rate decreases from 1.047 mm/y after 19 h operation to 0.932 mm/y after 5 h shutdown and further stabilizes at approximately 0.52 mm/y after multiple operating–shutdown cycles. Shutdown‐period cathodic protection promotes corrosion product film stabilization and enhances corrosion resistance, revealing the mitigation mechanism of dynamic AC corrosion during high‐speed railway operational cycles.

title: Genomic and biological characterization of exopolysaccharides produced by Streptococcus thermophilus CCASU-ST-S3 and CCASU-ST-S52, with statistical optimization and preliminary spectroscopic characterization of EPS-STS3
summary: Background Streptococcus thermophilus is a key dairy starter capable of producing exopolysaccharides (EPS) with strain-dependent biosynthetic and biological properties. Two EPS-producing strains, STS3 and STS52, isolated from yogurt, were c
content: Background Streptococcus thermophilus is a key dairy starter capable of producing exopolysaccharides (EPS) with strain-dependent biosynthetic and biological properties. Two EPS-producing strains, STS3 and STS52, isolated from yogurt, were characterized genomically, and their partially purified EPS preparations underwent preliminary biological evaluation. Methods Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analyses were used to confirm strain identity, assess safety-associated genomic features, and characterize EPS biosynthetic potential. Partially purified EPS preparations were evaluated for antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, cytotoxic effects, wound closure, and antimicrobial activity. EPS production by STS3 was optimized using one-factor-at-a-time screening followed by response surface methodology. The unoptimized EPS-STS3 preparation was separately subjected to preliminary spectroscopic characterization. Results Both strains contained Wzx/Wzy-dependent EPS biosynthetic loci with multiple glycosyltransferase- and Eps-associated genes; STS52 additionally carried a putative pel-like polysaccharide locus. Genome annotation identified nucleotide-sugar precursor pathways. Neither strain harbored acquired antibiotic resistance genes or virulence determinants. EPS-STS3 and EPS-STS52 preparations exhibited 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl radical-scavenging activity (90.1% and 88.9%, respectively) and inhibited albumin denaturation. Both preparations produced dose-dependent reductions in cell viability, with greater effects in Caco-2 cells than WI-38 fibroblasts. The Caco-2 half-maximal inhibitory concentrations were 462.2 and 437.8 µg/mL, respectively. EPS-STS52 produced greater wound closure than EPS-STS3. EPS-STS3 produced promising antibacterial activity against tested Gram-negative bacteria; none was observed for EPS-STS52 or against Gram-positive bacteria or Candida . Optimization raised EPS-STS3 yield to 3.77 g/L (~ 23.56-fold above basal yield) under 3.8% sucrose, 5.8% peptone, pH 5.5, 47 °C, 32 h, and 3% inoculum. The optimized temperature exceeded that commonly reported for S. thermophilus EPS production. Ultraviolet analysis of EPS-STS3 showed no absorbance attributable to proteins or nucleic acids, while Fourier-transform infrared and ¹H/¹³C nuclear magnetic resonance data supported the carbohydrate nature. Conclusion The two locally isolated S. thermophilus strains exhibited distinct EPS biosynthetic features, and their partially purified EPS preparations showed measurable biological activities under the tested conditions. EPS production by STS3 was substantially improved through statistical optimization, while preliminary spectroscopic characterization supported the carbohydrate nature of EPS-STS3. These findings support further structural characterization and biological evaluation of S. thermophilus -derived EPS using more specific and quantitative approaches.

title: Dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma delays postharvest senescence of sweet corn via an AsA–GSH-mediated multi-pathway synergistic network
summary: Harvested sweet corn ( Zea mays L.) have high respiration rates and are susceptible to water-loss and shriveling, loss of sweetness and color as well as kernel hardening (increased firmness). The effects of dielectric barrier discharge (DBD
content: Harvested sweet corn ( Zea mays L.) have high respiration rates and are susceptible to water-loss and shriveling, loss of sweetness and color as well as kernel hardening (increased firmness). The effects of dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma (10.5 kV, 10 min) on the senescence of 'Nongkenuo 336' sweetcorn kept at 20°C and 90% ± 2% relative humidity for up to 8 days were investigated. Physiological measurements were combined with transcriptomic, widely targeted metabolomic, and proteomic analyses to dissect the molecular mechanisms by which DBD plasma affects sweet corn metabolism. DBD treatment suppressed kernel hardening, weight loss, and loss of soluble solids content and color. 1196 differentially accumulated metabolites were identified and DBD treatment inhibited the progressive accumulation of deterioration-associated metabolites senescenceover time, while maintaining flavor- and nutrition-related metabolites. Transcriptomics showed that DBD treatment repressed starch-hydrolyzing genes ( AMY , BAM ), ethylene signaling genes ( ETR , EIN2 , EIN3 ), and the cell wall degradation gene, PME . DBD treatment maintained expression of phenylpropanoid pathway genes ( PAL , HCT , COMT , CAD , POD ), the ABA receptor, PYL , and the response factor, ABF , while downregulating the signal amplifier SnRK2 . Proteomics revealed significant enrichment of defense-related proteins, including glutathione S-transferase family proteins and UDP-glucuronosyl/UDP-glucosyl transferase family proteins. Notably, ascorbate–glutathione (AsA–GSH) metabolism was enriched across all three omic measurement: GlcAK expression recovered, and antioxidant metabolites such as L-ascorbic acid were maintained. Together, these results indicate that DBD plasma activates an antioxidant network centered on the AsA–GSH cycle. This network coordinately regulates hormone signaling, sugar metabolism, cell wall metabolism, and secondary metabolism, converting exogenous RONS-induced oxidative signals into protective physiological responses that are associated with the systematic delay of senescence.

title: GERMINATION AND EARLY GROWTH PERFORMANCE OF KHAYA SENEGALENSIS (DESR.) A. JUSS. UNDER VARYING LIGHT INTENSITIES
summary: This study assessed the effects of four pre-sowing treatments seeds: dewinging and soaking, dewinging only, soaking only, and untreated seeds control; on germination dynamics over 19 days. The study also determined the effect of four light
content: This study assessed the effects of four pre-sowing treatments seeds: dewinging and soaking, dewinging only, soaking only, and untreated seeds control; on germination dynamics over 19 days. The study also determined the effect of four light intensity regimes (100%, 75%, 50% and 25% of full sunlight) on early growth, chlorophyll content, and biomass allocation in seedlings, over eighteen weeks. The main effects of period of experiment, pre-sowing treatment and their interactions were significantly different for germination rate (p < 0.001). Dewinging alone produced the most rapid and synchronised germination, confirming primarily physical seed dormancy. Light intensity significantly influenced seedling height (p = 0.006), with seedlings under 25% light attaining the highest height (2.205 ± 0.172 cm). In addition, leaf area was significantly affected (p < 0.001) by light intensity and nearly doubled under 25% light (560.95 cm 2 ), when compared with 100% light intensity (284.61 cm 2 ). Chlorophyll content showed a progressive inverse relationship with irradiance, and this was consistent with shade acclimation. The species is confirmed as a non-pioneer light demander with a juvenile shade tolerance optimum of 25–50% of full sunlight. A two-stage nursery protocol --seed dewinging followed by cultivation under 50% shade is recommended for producing high-quality seedlings for reforestation.

title: Nanoparticle and Microplastic Exposure in Textile Manufacturing: Neurotoxicological Mechanisms, Occupational Mental Health, and a Public Health Research Agenda for South Asia
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Textile manufacturing is one of the world’s largest employment sectors, with the International Labour Organization estimating approximately 90 million workers in the global textile and garment industry, more than half of whom are women and
content: Textile manufacturing is one of the world’s largest employment sectors, with the International Labour Organization estimating approximately 90 million workers in the global textile and garment industry, more than half of whom are women and many of whom are concentrated in South and Southeast Asia (International Labour Organization, 2025). Workers involved in textile finishing, stitching, coating, and mechanical processing may experience occupational exposure to engineered nanoparticles and nanoscale microplastic fragments generated during textile production and processing. Despite growing concern regarding such exposures, their potential implications for workers’ psychological and neurological health remain insufficiently understood. This narrative review synthesizes four interconnected evidence streams—occupational exposure assessment, mechanistic nanotoxicology, human biomonitoring, and textile-worker mental health—to examine whether a testable public health question emerges at their intersection. Experimental evidence from animal and cell-culture studies indicates several biologically plausible pathways through which nanoparticle exposure may influence neurological and behavioral functioning, including blood–brain barrier translocation, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammatory processes. However, the exposure levels used in many experimental studies substantially exceed those documented in occupational settings, limiting direct extrapolation to workers. Human biomonitoring studies among nanomaterialexposed workers have demonstrated physiological changes, but available evidence has not established significant neurobehavioral associations and has rarely integrated exposure biomarkers with validated psychological assessment instruments. In parallel, research on textile workers has documented elevated levels of depression, anxiety, and occupational stress, although these outcomes have predominantly been attributed to psychosocial and organizational working conditions rather than potential environmental or nanomaterial exposures. This evidence gap highlights the need for an integrated occupational health framework that simultaneously considers chemical, physical, and psychosocial determinants of workers’ mental health. Pakistan’s Sialkot region represents a potentially valuable setting for such research because of its extensive textile and adjacent manufacturing activities and the availability of relevant occupational and biomonitoring infrastructure. We therefore propose a staged cohort study that combines objective exposure biomarkers with validated psychological and neurobehavioral instruments while controlling for psychosocial job strain and other relevant occupational and demographic confounders. Such an approach could help determine whether occupational exposure to engineered nanoparticles and nanoscale textilederived particles is associated with measurable psychological or neurobehavioral outcomes and, ultimately, facilitate evidence-based oc

title: Weighted Multi-Model Ensemble Projections of Temperature under Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) in the White Volta Basin, Ghana
summary: Increasingly susceptible to the effects of climate change (CC), the White Volta Basin is a vital source of water for West Africa and could worsen already existing hydroclimatic issues. Consequently, CC assessment is becoming difficult in da
content: Increasingly susceptible to the effects of climate change (CC), the White Volta Basin is a vital source of water for West Africa and could worsen already existing hydroclimatic issues. Consequently, CC assessment is becoming difficult in data-scarce areas, especially in the northern part of Ghana. To evaluate the CC of the basin under different climatic scenarios as described by the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs), this study used statistically bias-corrected CMIP6 climate model outputs to estimate maximum and minimum temperature (Tmax and Tmin) variations within the Ghanaian part of the basin. Only temperature is analysed. This study employed 15 different Global Climate Models under the 6th IPCC Report’s Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios (SSPs) of the CMIP6 (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5), which were bias-corrected over the basin using data sourced from the Ghana Meteorological Agency stations as well as 9 virtually generated stations using ERA5 data. A weighted multi-model ensemble was subsequently developed using model performance (correlation-based weights at the GMet stations) and, for the virtual stations, model independence and performance through the ClimWIP approach. The individual bias-corrected models were evaluated against the same observations used to fit the correction (no independent validation period) using R², RMSE, and PBIAS, indicating goodness of fit rather than out-of-sample skill. For the bias-corrected data, R² ranged from 0.83 to 0.99 for Tmax and 0.91 to 0.99 for Tmin, compared with 0.00 to 0.59 for the raw data. RMSE for bias-corrected Tmax and Tmin ranged from 0.01 to 0.38°C and 0.00 to 0.25°C, respectively. PBIAS ranged from 0.00 to 0.48% for bias-corrected Tmax and Tmin (-16.9 to 20.0% for the raw data; positive values indicate overestimation). Under the high-emission scenario (SSP5-8.5), the projected warming could intensify pressure on water resources, agricultural productivity, ecosystem health, and overall water security (these impacts were not modelled in this study). The study revealed seasonal and spatial variations in temperature, with warming under SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5; apparent post-2060 decreases under SSP1-2.6 are probably processing artefacts and are not interpreted as cooling. The findings of the study are expected to help decisionmakers make tangible decisions in addressing SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), and 13 (Climate Action) in the White Volta Basin. Clinical trial number: not applicable.

title: A flexible in planta transformation platform for grapevine functional genomics
summary: Grapevine (Vitis vinifera) transformation remains a bottleneck for functional genomics and targeted breeding owing to slow, genotype-dependent protocols. Here we develop ViDeT (Vitis de novo induction-based Transformation), a tissue culture
content: Grapevine (Vitis vinifera) transformation remains a bottleneck for functional genomics and targeted breeding owing to slow, genotype-dependent protocols. Here we develop ViDeT (Vitis de novo induction-based Transformation), a tissue culture-free, in planta Agrobacterium delivery strategy that uses developmental regulators to trigger de novo regeneration concomitant with transgene delivery. Across eight cultivars, ViDeT achieved shoot induction rates of 8-79% and transgenic efficiency of 40-96%, enabling recovery of transgenic shoots within 6-8 weeks, from both semi-lignified and fully lignified canes of twelve genotypes. ViDeT-mediated VvMYBPA1 overexpression enabled multi-omics profiling and regulatory validation of transcriptional programs, whereas VvL-IdnDH (L-idonate dehydrogenase) overexpression increased tartaric acid and decreased L-malic acid and showed interactome enrichments in central carbon metabolism. Together, ViDeT converts grapevine transformation from a longstanding constraint into an enabling step for hypothesis-driven functional genomics and precision breeding in this woody perennial.

title: BaTiO3/SrTiO3 Heterostructures: Structure, Electronic Properties and Photocatalytic Application
source: Eurasian journal of physics and functional materials
summary: Perovskite oxides based on BaTiO3 (BTO) and SrTiO3 (STO), as well as their heterostructures, are considered highly promising materials for photocatalytic water splitting and solar fuel production owing to their tunable band structure, ferro
content: Perovskite oxides based on BaTiO3 (BTO) and SrTiO3 (STO), as well as their heterostructures, are considered highly promising materials for photocatalytic water splitting and solar fuel production owing to their tunable band structure, ferroelectric properties, and good chemical stability. In this study, a comprehensive analysis of recent literature was carried out, encompassing synthesis methods, electronic structure, and photocatalytic performance of pristine perovskites, doped systems, and heterostructures. Special attention was paid to first-principles DFT calculations of key electronic parameters, including the band gap. The review shows that pulsed laser deposition and molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) with in situ RHEED control, including hybrid MBE, provide unit-cell-level control of BTO/STO interfaces, whereas atomic layer deposition (ALD) offers low-temperature, conformal growth suitable for integration with Si. The reviewed computational and experimental data show that doping and heterostructure formation enable targeted modification of the electronic properties, significantly improving charge carrier separation, reducing the band gap, and enhancing overall photocatalytic activity. These findings highlight the potential of interface engineering in ferroelectric perovskites and may help researchers select synthesis techniques and computational approaches, since the calculated band gap depends strongly on the chosen exchange–correlation functional.

title: Parabolic modeling of gene expression and essential oil in Thymus kotschyanus along the altitudinal gradient of Sabalan Mountain
summary: Thymus kotschyanus is one of the pharmacologically important plants known for its bioactivity of secondary metabolites; however, little information exists on the impact of altitude along with interannual variability of climatic conditions o
content: Thymus kotschyanus is one of the pharmacologically important plants known for its bioactivity of secondary metabolites; however, little information exists on the impact of altitude along with interannual variability of climatic conditions on its terpene biosynthesis pathway. The objective of this research was to examine the spatiotemporal gene expression of geranyl diphosphate synthase ( GPPS ) and terpene synthase ( TPS ) as well as the essential oils composition in T. kotschyanus over three consecutive years (2022–2024) at 17 altitudes (2150–3250 m) of Sabalan Mountain, Iran. RT-qPCR revealed that both genes transcript levels followed a non-linear, parabolic developmental response along the vertical gradient, peaking at an optimal elevation threshold of approximately 2780m concurrently, and GC-MS analysis demonstrated that oxygenated monoterpenes dominated the essential oil profile within these intermediate altitudes. Integration of synoptic meteorological data showed that interannual expression peaks in 2023 strongly correlated with macroclimatic anomalies, specifically an exceptionally wet early spring followed by a severe summer drought transition. Multivariate hierarchical clustering of 51 spatiotemporal units distinguished ecological cohorts based on climate plasticity and metabolic yields. These findings demonstrate that terpene biosynthesis and essential oil accumulation in T. kotschyanus are finely co-regulated by a strict interplay between altitudinal boundaries and microclimatic dynamics.

title: Data for: Calibrated Stochastic Simulation and NSGA-II Optimization for Bamboo Plantation Expansion: Evidence from a Smallholder Estate in East Java, Indonesia
summary: The dataset supports the research paper "Calibrated Stochastic Simulation and NSGA-II Optimization for Bamboo Plantation Expansion: Case Study in a Smallholder Estate in East Java, Indonesia." This dataset contains 2024 observations from a
content: The dataset supports the research paper "Calibrated Stochastic Simulation and NSGA-II Optimization for Bamboo Plantation Expansion: Case Study in a Smallholder Estate in East Java, Indonesia." This dataset contains 2024 observations from a 120-hectare bamboo plantation in East Java together with assumptions, simulation input variables, output, and NSGA-II Pareto optimal solutions. The purpose is to analyze if plantation expansion is profitable without incurring downside risk and increasing the amount of carbon. Given the assumptions and under the 20-year horizon period of analysis, no expansion strategy analyzed provides positive expected incremental NPV although the revenue from the carbon credit lowers the expected losses. The set of Pareto optimal solutions will show trade-offs between expected NPV, CVaR5% downside risk, carbon stocks, probability of loss, and peak capital requirements. Since there is no harvest per plot observation data available, production is simulated using sales data.

title: Microscale controls on bacterial biodegradation of dispersed oil droplets
summary: Bacteria contribute to the removal of oil from water by degrading hydrocarbons in dispersed droplets. For degradation through direct contact, bulk measurements of oil loss alone cannot distinguish time spent reaching droplets from delays be
content: Bacteria contribute to the removal of oil from water by degrading hydrocarbons in dispersed droplets. For degradation through direct contact, bulk measurements of oil loss alone cannot distinguish time spent reaching droplets from delays before detectable depletion after attachment. This Mini Review compares imaging studies of individual droplets with mathematical models and chemical measurements to examine how bacterial colonisation affects oil persistence. A shorter depletion phase does not necessarily mean faster overall oil removal. A model of bacterial encounters and oil consumption predicts that smaller droplets can persist longer when the increase in encounter time outweighs the decrease in consumption time. Imaging experiments show that a longer post-attachment lag can more than offset a shorter subsequent depletion phase. After attachment, bacteria can also form biofilms that change droplet shape, oil dispersion and droplet transport. These physical changes can redistribute oil, so chemical measurements are needed to establish whether droplet loss reflects hydrocarbon transformation or mineralisation. Models of oil persistence could be tested using measurements of both bacterial colonisation timing and the loss of target hydrocarbons.

title: Data and results for cost and carbon tradeoffs in highway microgrids with delayed electric vehicle charging demand
summary: This record provides the inputs, reconstructed charging-demand profiles, saved dispatch solutions, trajectories, optimality certificates and result tables supporting the study "Cost and carbon tradeoffs in highway microgrids with delayed el
content: This record provides the inputs, reconstructed charging-demand profiles, saved dispatch solutions, trajectories, optimality certificates and result tables supporting the study "Cost and carbon tradeoffs in highway microgrids with delayed electric vehicle charging demand." Six modules cover capacity and operating tradeoffs across 81 deterministic scenarios; validation using public charging transactions; frozen rolling control; retrospective reachability diagnosis; a rejected guard-release ablation; and paired offline validation under fixed nonzero carbon and electricity-import limits. Paired dispatch costs are compared under the same equipment, demand, carbon budget, full-service requirements and terminal storage conditions. The transaction analysis uses 121 dates with three power reconstructions and two target protocols. Under the fixed nonzero targets, each reconstruction is feasible on 120/121 dates, with an incremental operating cost no greater than 5% on 119/121 dates. These are import-cap compliance counts, not counts of days with an actual peak reduction. Daily hindsight targets are reported separately. The 30 controller-selection dates and 28 retrospective diagnostic dates have distinct roles; the rejected ablation has no new-date evaluation. Failed cases are retained.Charging power is reconstructed from transactions. Equipment, demand-propagation parameters and overlaid photovoltaic and projected carbon inputs define the modeled operating conditions. Whole-session energy is conserved, while cross-midnight sessions can produce different calendar-day energy allocations across reconstructions.Computational reproduction requires the companion software record.
