summary: Purpose This paper aims to explore whether land-use planning and environmental regulations in seven African countries – Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda and Ethiopia – can effectively manage the use of land for carbon d
content: Purpose This paper aims to explore whether land-use planning and environmental regulations in seven African countries – Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda and Ethiopia – can effectively manage the use of land for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) technologies. It examine how planning law handles competing land uses for afforestation, bioenergy with carbon capture and storage and soil carbon sequestration, and assesses whether current frameworks address spatial justice, participatory governance and fair land access. Design/methodology/approach The study uses à socio-legal approach that combines three methods: analyzing land use planning laws, environmental regulations and climate policies in the seven countries; reviewing interdisciplinary literature on land governance, legal pluralism and climate mitigation; and examining national policy documents like nationally determined contributions, spatial plans and land tenure laws. The analysis draws on spatial justice theory and legal pluralism. Since the study is based on documents rather than fieldwork, its findings reflect the legal and policy record. Further research would be needed to confirm how these laws work in practice at the community level. Findings In all seven countries, land-use planning systems are not set up to manage CDR projects effectively. There are three main problems: no clear carbon rights in property law, a gap between climate goals and planning laws and not enough protections for communities whose land rights are affected by carbon removal. These issues perpetuate land inequalities and make green grabbing more likely. The paper proposes a five-part framework for fair CDR governance, including integrating spatial justice, linking climate and planning laws, clarifying carbon rights, managing trade-offs and legally recognizing different tenure systems. Originality/value This paper contributes to the discussion on property law, planning law and climate governance by showing that African planning systems struggle with CDR due to underlying values, not just technical issues. These systems focus more on state development than on fair distribution. The article introduces the idea of spatially just carbon removal governance as a framework for analyzing and reforming these systems, building on African constitutional and international climate law and expanding research on green grabbing and spatial justice to include negative emissions.

title: A framework for holistic development of sustainability in higher education institutions
source: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
summary: Purpose Nations are implementing systematic approaches to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Higher education institutions (HEIs) can serve as powerful catalysts in supporting these efforts and driving progress towards the
content: Purpose Nations are implementing systematic approaches to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Higher education institutions (HEIs) can serve as powerful catalysts in supporting these efforts and driving progress towards the agenda. However, existing Sustainable Assessment Tools (SATs) were unable to meet the needs of developing nations’ HEIs. This study aims to analyse five major SATs and propose a holistic Environmental Social and Governance (ESG)-aligned framework for HEIs, with India as a validation case study. Design/methodology/approach A mixed method approach was used, and data were collected from sources like research articles, ranking and accreditation agencies. Five SATs (QS, UI GM, THE, USAT and STARS) were classified and analysed. The qualitative method involved mapping SAT towards 169 indicators of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG). The quantitative method involved charting the proportion of the five SATs indicators and metrics towards ESG. Findings The analysis showed major contribution was towards environmental segment and less towards social and governance. Social SDGs, particularly SDG 8 (Decent work) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) received near zero coverage. The proposed framework includes segments such as social, economic and governance which also aligns with SDGs. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to analyse five SATs through both SDG and ESG charting providing an analysis for existing gaps. The expected impact was highest in the environmental segment by curbing emissions to 5.7 from 7.1 kg CO2eq. per capita per day. Incorporating the proposed framework with a ranking body, like NIRF in India will promote sustainability in HEIs and eventually contribute towards the 2030 Agenda for sustainable development of the nation.

title: Transforming Legacy Oilfield Infrastructure for Hydrogen Transport: Integrating Advanced Technologies and Green Finance
source: SPE Annual Caspian Technical Conference and Exhibition
summary: The urgent need for climate change mitigation and low-carbon energy transition creates a strategic opportunity to repurpose existing oilfield infrastructure for grey and blue hydrogen production, processing, and transportation. This study e
content: The urgent need for climate change mitigation and low-carbon energy transition creates a strategic opportunity to repurpose existing oilfield infrastructure for grey and blue hydrogen production, processing, and transportation. This study evaluates how legacy oil and gas (O&G) facilities and pipeline networks can be converted into hydrogen-ready assets to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, minimize flaring, and support sustainable energy-system transformation. Repurposing legacy oil and gas infrastructure for hydrogen service is often presented as a low-cost route to early hydrogen markets, yet the decision is frequently made before material compatibility, lifecycle emissions and financing eligibility are evaluated on a common basis. This paper develops a gate-based screening method that links pipeline requalification, system performance, lifecycle greenhouse-gas intensity and financeability. Three representative asset archetypes are assessed: a documented dry-gas transmission line, an ageing gathering line with incomplete integrity records, and a former liquid-hydrocarbon line. A 200,000-trial Monte Carlo analysis propagates uncertainty in retrofit expenditure, retained energy throughput, operating-cost uplift, carbon-capture performance and upstream methane loss. For the dry-gas archetype, the median retrofit capital ratio was 0.336 relative to a new hydrogen pipeline, and the median normalized delivery burden was 0.484; all sampled cost cases remained below the new-build reference, subject to passing the structural-integrity gate. The ageing gathering line produced a median burden of 1.266 and was below the new-build reference in only 8.1% of trials. The former liquid line produced a median burden of 2.593 and did not reach cost parity. For natural-gas-derived hydrogen, median lifecycle intensity was 1.65 kg CO2e/kg H2 for integrated capture supplied by low-leakage gas, 4.01 kg CO2e/kg H2 for uncertain upstream performance, and 6.06 kg CO2e/kg H2 for partial capture and high leakage. Capture fraction and methane loss were the dominant carbon variables. The analysis also shows that the often-cited global flaring quantities are system-wide upper bounds, not project outcomes: 167 bcm was flared globally in 2025, whereas a project must be evaluated from site-specific recoverable volume, composition and operating continuity. The proposed framework provides a reproducible basis for selecting assets, defining monitoring requirements and linking finance claims to measured technical and carbon performance.

title: Synthesizing mixed-integer linear programming models from natural language descriptions
source: INFOR Information Systems and Operational Research
summary: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) is a powerful tool for solving numerous real-world decision-making problems. However, the formulation process typically requires substantial expert effort. This study investigates whether it is possib
content: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) is a powerful tool for solving numerous real-world decision-making problems. However, the formulation process typically requires substantial expert effort. This study investigates whether it is possible to automatically recognize constraints and generate accurate MILP formulations from unstructured textual descriptions. We propose a multi-stage framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) and mathematical modeling techniques. The framework comprises three stages: (1) identification of decision variables, (2) classification of objectives and constraints with fine-tuned LLMs, and (3) generation of mathematical expressions based on templates, including implicit constraints for logical relations. We conduct numerical evaluation on a new dataset of 30 problems comprising 177 paragraph-level descriptions. The proposed framework is able to generate correct models for 29 of 30 instances and 176 of 177 mathematical expressions. Compared with direct prompting and recent automatic model generation methods, including a training-based framework and an agentic system, our approach achieves 7 to 24 additional accurate models and produces consistent results across multiple trials. Error analysis shows that competing methods often fail to capture implicit constraints or logical relations. Our framework enhances the automation of MILP formulation and also offers opportunities for developing training tools for operations research practitioners and supporting automatic decision problem solving in practice.

title: QAMNet: Co-designing deep learning with complex-valued computing machines
summary: The energy consumption of inference has become critically important with the growing adoption of deep neural networks (DNNs). Analog optical neural networks (ONNs) can reduce the energy of matrix-vector multiplication below that of digital
content: The energy consumption of inference has become critically important with the growing adoption of deep neural networks (DNNs). Analog optical neural networks (ONNs) can reduce the energy of matrix-vector multiplication below that of digital electronics. However, this promise is limited by digital-to-analog (DAC) conversion: even at low bit precision b , encoding the 2 b levels of weights and inputs into the analog domain requires specialized, power-hungry electronics. Quadrature-Amplitude Modulation (QAM), the dominant format in modern telecommunications, encodes information on both the in-phase and quadrature axes of a carrier. A consequence of this two-dimensional signaling is a quadratic O ( N 2 ) → O ( N ) saving in modulation energy over intensity-only modulation. Inspired by this advantage, we introduce QAMNet, an ONN architecture and hardware that fully utilizes the complex amplitude of light with QAM to achieve superior modulation-energy scaling. Using physics-based simulations of conventional telecommunications equipment, we show that QAMNet accelerates complex-valued DNNs with accuracies indistinguishable from digital hardware. Compared to standard ONNs, QAMNet ONNs: (1) attain higher accuracy above moderate total bit precision, (2) are more accurate above low energy budgets, and (3) are optimal when hardware bit precision is limited.

title: Impacts of snowpack on winter ecosystem respiration across the Northern Hemisphere
summary: Climate-driven snowpack dynamics across the Northern Hemisphere introduce substantial uncertainty into the global carbon budget, but how winter ecosystem respiration (Reco winter ) responds to this critical driver remains unclear. In this s
content: Climate-driven snowpack dynamics across the Northern Hemisphere introduce substantial uncertainty into the global carbon budget, but how winter ecosystem respiration (Reco winter ) responds to this critical driver remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the impact of seasonal snowpack on Reco winter across the Northern Hemisphere (NH, > 30 ° N) using multi-source datasets. Our analysis revealed that in 34.71 % of NH ecosystems, snowpack (depth, density, and duration) exerted the most critical impact on respiration. Incorporating snowpack indicators progressively improved model R 2 compared with no-snowpack models. Applying a single indicator improved R 2 by 0.19–0.22 over 18.85 % –32.96 % of the study area, and the combined use of all three indicators improved R 2 by an average of 0.24 over 50.18 % of the study area, demonstrating the necessity of adopting a multi-indicator approach. By applying structural equation models, we further demonstrated that snowpack impacts Reco winter through direct, thermal, and moisture pathways, with the direction and relative contribution of each pathway exhibiting significant regional differentiation under varying hydrothermal conditions. The thermal pathway was predominantly positive across the NH (69.53 % of ecosystems), the direct pathway shifted from a negative impact in cold zones to a positive impact in warm zones, and the moisture pathway was negative in most of the study area. These findings highlight the complex and spatially heterogeneous nature of snowpack impacts on winter ecosystem carbon fluxes, and underscore the importance of adopting a multi-indicator, multi-mechanism perspective in understanding ecosystem responses to snowpack.

title: Trophic state assessment of a phosphorus-enriched pre-sanctuary estuarine reach using Carlson TSI, Bayesian network modelling, and Shannon entropy analysis
summary: Estuarine reaches immediately upstream of protected habitats intercept nutrient and pollutant loads before they reach the protected zone, yet their trophic status is rarely monitored. This study provides a field-based trophic assessment of
content: Estuarine reaches immediately upstream of protected habitats intercept nutrient and pollutant loads before they reach the protected zone, yet their trophic status is rarely monitored. This study provides a field-based trophic assessment of the Tulabhagya River reach, a 6.8-km distributary of the Godavari Delta (Andhra Pradesh, India) immediately upstream of the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary (CWS), India's second-largest contiguous mangrove forest. Water samples were collected from ten stations across 6 months (January–June 2025); total phosphorus (TP), chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), and Secchi disk depth (SDD) were measured to compute Carlson’s Trophic State Index (TSI). A Bayesian Network (BN) model was developed for probabilistic scenario analysis under four TP loading conditions, and Shannon entropy analysis quantified spatial and temporal variability across 60 station-month observations. Results confirm persistent hypertrophic conditions throughout the transect (TSI(Avg): 68.84–79.50; mean = 74.71 ± 2.69), driven by TP concentrations (mean 1733 ± 512 µg L −1 ) exceeding the eutrophic threshold by up to 31-fold. TSI(Chl-a) remained oligotrophic, near the mesotrophic threshold, evidencing turbidity-mediated phytoplankton suppression. The BN model indicated 70% eutrophic–hypertrophic probability under high-TP conditions, shifting to 77% oligotrophic–mesotrophic probability when TP was reduced to 1000 µg L −1 . Shannon entropy reached its theoretical maximum for SDD and TSI(Avg) (H = 1.585 bits). A strong relationship between TSI(TP) and TSI(Avg) (R 2 = 0.602, p < 0.001) identifies TP as the dominant trophic driver. These findings provide a probabilistic evidence base for targeted phosphorus abatement to safeguard the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary.

title: Present and future responses of near-surface wind speed to different land-use and land-cover types in China
summary: Near-surface wind speed (NSWS) is highly sensitive to land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). However, previous studies have mainly focused on overall LULCC effects, leaving the attribution of wind variations to individual land transitions
content: Near-surface wind speed (NSWS) is highly sensitive to land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). However, previous studies have mainly focused on overall LULCC effects, leaving the attribution of wind variations to individual land transitions and management poorly constrained. Here, we utilize simulations from the latest Land-Use Model Intercomparison Project to disentangle and quantify the responses of NSWS to different types of LULCC over China from 1970 to 2014. We demonstrate that the primary-to-grazing transition is the dominant factor contributing to LULCC-induced NSWS variability, followed by fertilizer use, while urbanization makes the smallest contribution among the examined LULCC types. Future projections further suggest that land-use pathways can substantially perturb wind patterns, with low-emission pathways combined with minimally regulated land use producing more pronounced alterations than high-emission pathways combined with sustainable land use. These results highlight the importance of resolving LULCC in attributing and projecting NSWS changes, with implications for climate modeling, wind-energy assessment, and land-use policy.

title: Combined Rhizophagus irregularis and Bacillus megaterium inoculation enhances root hydraulics and potassium acquisition and improves maize tolerance to drought stress and potassium deficiency
summary: In this study we investigated the effectiveness of combined inoculation with the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus R. irregularis and the PGPR B. megaterium in improving maize tolerance to combined potassium (K) deficiency and drought stress. T
content: In this study we investigated the effectiveness of combined inoculation with the arbuscular mycorrhizal fungus R. irregularis and the PGPR B. megaterium in improving maize tolerance to combined potassium (K) deficiency and drought stress. Thus, maize plants inoculated with these microorganisms or maintained as uninoculated controls were cultivated either under deficient K supply (0.3 mM K) or under ample K fertilization (6 mM K). Half of plants was maintained under well-watered conditions during the entire experiment and the other half was subjected to drought stress for 15 days before harvest. Results showed that under K deficiency, the combined inoculation of R. irregularis plus B. megaterium allowed maize plants to overcome the problem of K limitation and to reach a similar biomass production than uninoculated control plants cultivated under normal K levels. This effect was observed both, under well-watered and under drought stress conditions. The mechanisms underlying these effects on plant growth include enhanced root hydraulic conductivities, improved photosynthetic capacity and efficiency of photosystem II, reduced oxidative damage to lipids, and enhanced K uptake and accumulation. This indicates that, for important crops such as maize, the inoculated microorganisms can contribute to reducing the use of chemical fertilizers under the influence of additional abiotic stresses such as drought.

title: A digital twin and XR framework for heritage access by visitors with mobility limitations
summary: Balancing heritage authenticity with accessibility presents a "double constraint" for historical sites restricted by complex topography and strict preservation laws. This study addresses this challenge by proposing a non-invasive "Scan-to-S
content: Balancing heritage authenticity with accessibility presents a "double constraint" for historical sites restricted by complex topography and strict preservation laws. This study addresses this challenge by proposing a non-invasive "Scan-to-Service" framework that integrates LiDAR, Digital Twin (DT), and Extended Reality (XR) to revolutionize inclusive smart tourism. Using Taipei’s Treasure Hill Artist Village as a testbed, we developed a high-fidelity Digital Twin and an accessibility-optimized XR interface, subsequently validating the system's efficacy through the Task-Technology Fit (TTF) model with 36 elderly and mobility-impaired participants. Empirical results demonstrate that the virtual system significantly outperforms traditional physical tourism experiences. Notably, a surge in "Technology Utilization" scores confirms that such advanced tourism technology successfully unlocks latent demand previously suppressed by physical barriers, while business model analysis indicating a user preference for pay-per-use services suggests long-term economic sustainability. By establishing a comprehensive engineering workflow, this research theoretically extends the TTF model to the domain of inclusive heritage and demonstrates how automation can empirically realize spatial justice and cultural equity for marginalized groups.

title: Unveiling carbonate dissolution in coastal sediments and its influence on seawater buffering capacity with δ 13 C DIC and 224 Ra– 228 Th disequilibria
summary: Organic carbon mineralization is generally recognized as the primary source of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) released from sediments in coastal seas. The CO 2 accumulation or the formation of corrosive microenvironment induced by organic
content: Organic carbon mineralization is generally recognized as the primary source of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) released from sediments in coastal seas. The CO 2 accumulation or the formation of corrosive microenvironment induced by organic carbon degradation can promote the dissolution of calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) in sediments, complicating the efficiency of carbon burial and total alkalinity (TA) inputs to aquatic environments. However, quantitative assessments of sediment CaCO 3 dissolution and its impacts on the seawater carbonate remain poorly constrained. In this study, we selected typical high-productivity regions, mariculture farms, and applied the 224 Ra– 228 Th disequilibrium approach to quantify the effluxes of DIC and TA across the sediment-water interface. The stable carbon isotope of DIC ( δ 13 C DIC ) was employed to trace DIC sources in porewater. The results showed that CaCO 3 dissolution in the sediment accounted for 29±13 % to 55±10 % of the benthic DIC effluxes. Notably, a high contribution of CaCO 3 dissolution did not coincide with strong organic carbon degradation across sites, suggesting that dynamic disturbance in the sediment, which weakened the metabolic CO 2 accumulation in porewater, was also a crucial factor affecting carbonate dissolution. According to the evaluation of the influence that benthic DIC and TA effluxes exerted on the seawater CO 2 content, the TA supplied by the CaCO 3 dissolution was identified to enhance the carbonate buffering capacity of seawater and counteracted the acidification driven by organic matter remineralization. This indicates that CaCO 3 dissolution in sediments should be involved in coastal carbon cycling and assessments on coastal ecosystem resilience under the risk of CO 2 elevation.

title: RMG-Py v4: 17 Years of Open-Source Reaction Mechanism Generation
source: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling
summary: Kinetic modeling describes reacting chemical systems through networks of elementary reactions and their associated rate parameters. Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG-Py) automates the construction of these networks by simulating reaction fl
content: Kinetic modeling describes reacting chemical systems through networks of elementary reactions and their associated rate parameters. Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG-Py) automates the construction of these networks by simulating reaction fluxes to identify dominant chemical pathways in silico. RMG-Py v4.0.0 marks 17 years of open-source reaction mechanism generation, introducing substantial improvements in performance, usability, and chemical scope. Benchmarks demonstrate higher throughput in constructing combustion models relative to prior versions, alongside streamlined installation via Docker and binary distributions. Key new capabilities include automated library selection, improved species selection algorithms, integration with the Julia-based ReactionMechanismSimulator.jl for simulating arbitrary reactor configurations, and PySIDT-based property estimators. Heterogeneous catalysis support is improved by the addition of new adsorbate thermophysical property data, new reaction families, resonance templates of surface-bound species, and uncertainty quantification for parameter sensitivity analysis. The release also extends RMG-Py into new chemical domains, including electrochemical mechanisms for battery and CO2RR applications, and an automated fragment-based modeling framework for the pyrolysis of large molecules. Together, these advances improve new users’ experience, expand the range of tractable systems, and maintain RMG-Py at the forefront of computational kinetic modeling.

title: Coverage Effects in Heterogeneous Catalysis: From Fundamental Understanding to Predictive Modeling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calcu
content: Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calculations suffer from vast combinatorial complexity on crowded surfaces, while machine learning methods require large training data sets and have limited physical interpretability. We reveal a physics-based linear correlation mapping complex coverage-dependent adsorption energies directly to computationally inexpensive gas-phase pairwise interactions that are evaluated via Mie potentials. This correlation is governed by bond order conservation: as surface−adsorbate interactions weaken under crowding, adsorbate−adsorbate interactions strengthen. This correlation generalizes across metal surfaces having diverse crystal facets, surface tensions, and single- and multicomponent adsorption classes (e.g., dissociative S*, N* + O*, and nondissociative CO*). This correlation predicts coverage-dependent reaction thermodynamics for NO* dissociation and for atomic-adsorbate diffusion. Coverage-dependent trends in adsorption energies of CO*/Pt(111) agree with experimental calorimetry. Ultimately, these gas-phase pairwise interactions are a descriptor for lateral interactions of atomic and structurally simple adsorbates on structurally stable metal surfaces. The generalizability and physical interpretability of this descriptor open new avenues for modeling adsorption and reaction energies on crowded metal surfaces.

title: Reconciliation through Integration: A Source-Level Bayesian Framework for Developing Measurement-Integrated Methane Inventories
summary: Bottom-up (BU) inventories and top-down (TD) aerial measurements at midstream natural gas facilities frequently diverge, and this discrepancy remains a central challenge for methane accounting in the sector. Previous approaches typically re
content: Bottom-up (BU) inventories and top-down (TD) aerial measurements at midstream natural gas facilities frequently diverge, and this discrepancy remains a central challenge for methane accounting in the sector. Previous approaches typically reconcile this divergence by treating BU and TD data as independent estimates of a single true quantity to be adjusted toward agreement, rather than as evidence that each captures only part of a more complex underlying system. This complexity arises from methane emissions being strongly governed by equipment operational state and therefore instantaneous aerial “snapshots” translate poorly to annual inventories. We argue instead that BU and TD are complementary sources of evidence that should be integrated. We present a source-level Bayesian framework that constructs BU prior distributions for each emission source category and updates them with attributed aerial detections through an empirical data-augmentation procedure. The resulting posterior distributions were propagated through unit-level activity data and source-specific information via Monte Carlo simulation to produce annual estimates. Across 64 compressor stations, measurement-integrated annual estimates were 84% higher than the BU inventory, a difference driven almost entirely by compressor vents (rod packing and seal vents) and leakage through blowdown and isolation valves, which together accounted for 90% of the asset-level revision. The revision was heterogeneous across stations and source categories, emphasizing the importance of source-level, station-specific integration when developing an emissions inventory.

title: Green ambidexterity, SDG disclosure and social reputation in Indonesian listed firms
summary: This study examines whether green ambidexterity, comprising green exploitation and green exploration, is associated with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) disclosure among Indonesian listed firms and whether SDG disclosure is associated wi
content: This study examines whether green ambidexterity, comprising green exploitation and green exploration, is associated with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) disclosure among Indonesian listed firms and whether SDG disclosure is associated with social reputation. The sample comprises 989 firm-year observations of non-financial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2020–2024, retained from an initial 4,770 after excluding financial firms and observations with missing data. Green exploitation, green exploration and social reputation are measured through content analysis and archival data from sustainability reports, and SDG disclosure through an index-based approach. Panel data regressions control for firm, governance and financial characteristics. Green exploitation and green exploration are each positively and significantly associated with SDG disclosure when entered separately, and their additive combination is also positively associated with disclosure, although neither dimension shows a significant independent association when both are entered jointly. Higher SDG disclosure is associated with stronger award-based social reputation. These associations are consistent with, but do not establish, a pathway from green orientation through disclosure to formal stakeholder recognition. Board size and the presence of a sustainability committee are positively associated with SDG disclosure in the GLS and pooled OLS estimations but not in the firm fixed effects models. The findings suggest that firms communicate both dimensions as a combined orientation in SDG reporting. The study contributes to the green ambidexterity literature by distinguishing their roles in SDG disclosure and by examining award-based social reputation as a correlate of SDG disclosure in an emerging market.

title: Supply-Chain Carbon Responsibility in Voluntary Carbon Markets: Input-Output Incidence and the Capital-Reallocation Channel in Five Economies
summary: Environmentally extended input–output analysis shows that carbon responsibility depends on the accounting boundary, but the economic consequences of that choice for voluntary carbon markets have not been quantified. This study compares thre
content: Environmentally extended input–output analysis shows that carbon responsibility depends on the accounting boundary, but the economic consequences of that choice for voluntary carbon markets have not been quantified. This study compares three responsibility rules (direct emissions, domestic supply-chain responsibility and imports-inclusive total-requirements responsibility), normalized to the same national carbon quantity, for Korea, France, Italy, the Netherlands and Canada over 2005–2022. Annual harmonized input–output tables, industry emissions, capital and investment data and observed voluntary carbon-market prices are combined with a coverage bound calibrated to registry retirements. The rules reallocate 18.6–37.5 percentage points of national responsibility across sectors in every year, systematically shifting responsibility from electricity, primary and fuel-using sectors toward construction and food processing. Applying a single-year input–output table to other years misstates Korean incidence by 21–23 points, so annual tables matter for historical responsibility accounting. By contrast, predicted five-year investment reallocation is at most 0.016 percentage points in any country-year at market-consistent coverage, about 0.011 points in 2022 if energy firms retire all credits, and 0.014 points with an investment elasticity of 1.0. A 0.1-point shift would require prices of 11–15 US dollars per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent at full coverage. Responsibility accounting therefore changes who bears the cost far more than where capital flows.

title: Data underlying the publication: A novel approach for incorporating carbon emissions into sustainable optimal reliability of engineering structures
summary: Code and data for the case study belonging to "A novel approach for incorporating carbon emissions into sustainable optimal reliability of engineering structures", to be submitted to Structure and Infrastructure Engineering. The case_study.
content: Code and data for the case study belonging to "A novel approach for incorporating carbon emissions into sustainable optimal reliability of engineering structures", to be submitted to Structure and Infrastructure Engineering. The case_study.ipynb notebook file contains the implementation of the case study, where the optimal reliability of a beam is calculated using both the conventional and proposed novel method. Several analyses are performed on the two-objective optimisation problem. This notebook uses the classes defined in the Python files beam_class_optimal.py and beam_class_concrete.py. It also uses several pickled (.pkl) files containing pre-calculated data for the reliability analysis used in the optimisation objective functions, which speeds up calculations. The code allows these to be re-calculated if desired. The intention is to have this data available immediately with the first submission of the paper. Because of that, adjustments could still be made as part of the peer review and revision process, including the final title and doi of the publication. These adjustments will be recorded in the README file.

title: A Proposed Phenomenological Material–Energy Scaling Framework for Recovery-Constrained Solvent Sustainability
summary: Solvents constitute a major material and environmental burden in pharmaceutical manufacturing, yet sustainability assessment is still largely based on proportional metrics such as Process Mass Intensity (PMI) and aggregated life-cycle indic
content: Solvents constitute a major material and environmental burden in pharmaceutical manufacturing, yet sustainability assessment is still largely based on proportional metrics such as Process Mass Intensity (PMI) and aggregated life-cycle indicators. Building on our previously published solvent-centric sustainability framework, which integrated PMI, circular PMI (cPMI), Global Warming Potential (GWP), and Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) for solvent-focused process assessment, the present study develops a phenomenological material–energy scaling formulation for recovery-constrained solvent sustainability. The proposed relationship is formulated as a testable phenomenological scaling framework, with its present scope limited to a system-specific relationship rather than a universal physical law. The framework represents the total sustainability burden, L(η), as a combination of a material-driven contribution and a recovery-associated nonlinear contribution: L(η) = c + kM(η) + β[ηn/(1 − η)], where M(η) is solvent material intensity, η is the recovery fraction, c is an intercept, k is a material-impact coefficient, β represents system-specific recovery-associated sensitivity, and n is a phenomenological recovery exponent. A dimensionless form is: L* = c* + αM* + λ[ηn/(1 − η)], where L* = L/L0, M* = M/M0, c* = c/L0, α = kM0/L0, and λ = β/L0. The nonlinear coordinate, Φ(η;n) = ηn/(1 − η), is used as a practical representation of recovery-associated asymptotic behaviour rather than as a first-principles thermodynamic equation. The parameters β, λ, and n are therefore expected to depend on the solvent, process configuration, recovery technology, operating conditions, response being measured, and system boundary. A seven-record pharmaceutical case-study dataset was used to examine the linear material relationship, the proposed nonlinear recovery coordinate, and an extended material–recovery interaction. Across the records, solvent mass decreases from 150 to 45 kg·kg−1 API as recovery increases from 30% to 92%, while energy use decreases from 520 to 380 MJ·kg−1 API. The linear model explains most of the observed variation (R2 = 0.979), whereas adding the nonlinear recovery term provides only a small improvement (R2 = 0.981), is penalized by information criteria, and gives an exponent at its imposed upper limit. An extended interaction model gives a closer fit to the seven observations, but its five-parameter structure relative to only seven observations does not support claims of independent predictive performance. These results therefore provide a basis for treating the proposed formulation as a testable phenomenological scaling hypothesis, rather than as evidence for a universal material–energy law. A complementary step-resolved analysis examines how solvent-related material and environmental burdens are distributed across individual process operations and how recovery may shift the balance between material use and recovery-associated energy requirements. Thi

title: The selective impact of tobacco genotypes on the microbial diversity and structure in the rhizosphere during the floating seedling cultivation
summary: Rhizosphere microorganisms are crucial for plant growth, development, and stress adaptation, and plant genotype can shape rhizosphere microbial communities through genotype-dependent differences in root traits and rhizodeposition. In this s
content: Rhizosphere microorganisms are crucial for plant growth, development, and stress adaptation, and plant genotype can shape rhizosphere microbial communities through genotype-dependent differences in root traits and rhizodeposition. In this study, three cultivated tobacco varieties, Yunyan 87 (YY87), K326, and Honghuadajinyuan (HD), one local variety, Chuanpihongda (CP), and one wild species, Nicotiana repanda (YS), were selected to investigate temporal changes in rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities under a floating seedling system. The results showed significant differences in bacterial and fungal alpha diversity between tobacco genotypes and the unseeded control. Specifically, bacterial diversity in all tobacco varieties exceeded that of the unseeded control only in the later stages of cultivation, whereas fungal diversity in these varieties consistently remained higher than that of the control throughout the entire period. PCoA and PERMANOVA indicated that both genotype and sampling time significantly affected bacterial and fungal community composition, with sampling time explaining a larger proportion of variation. At the phylum level, bacterial communities were mainly dominated by Pseudomonadota, Bacillota, Actinomycetota, Chloroflexota, and Acidobacteriota, whereas fungal communities were mainly represented by Ascomycota, Basidiomycota, Chytridiomycota, and Mucoromycota. Genotype-associated differences were also observed at the genus level and in co-occurrence network patterns. Functional prediction suggested that metabolism-related categories were dominant across samples, and CP showed relatively higher predicted abundances of several metabolic pathways, including terpenoid and polyketide metabolism. These findings provide a reference for understanding genotype-associated rhizosphere microbial variation in tobacco floating seedling systems and for future studies on microbial regulation during seedling production.

title: Fuel-Economy Efficiency Gaps Across Indonesian Transport Modes: A Stochastic Frontier Analysis
source: Journal of the Civil Engineering Forum
summary: Improving fuel economy is a critical but underexplored dimension of urban transport decarbonisation in developing countries. This study presents an exploratory frontier-based assessment of observed fueleconomy heterogeneity across Indonesia
content: Improving fuel economy is a critical but underexplored dimension of urban transport decarbonisation in developing countries. This study presents an exploratory frontier-based assessment of observed fueleconomy heterogeneity across Indonesian urban transport modes, estimating how far individual performance falls below a conditional mode-specific frontier and whether those gaps are evenly distributed across users. Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA) is applied to survey data from 1,610 vehicle owners/drivers across surveyed Indonesian urban areas, estimating separate frontiers for each mode using 1,242 internal combustion observations. Primary mode-level frontier estimates are designated for five of the six modes; candidate fits for small cars are reported in the sensitivity analysis, but no sufficiently robust primary estimate is designated. Trucks with three or more axles show the largest frontier-relative efficiency gap (24.0%), followed by motorcycles (22.1%), two-axle trucks (21.6%) and medium/large cars (20.5%), while buses at 11.4% operate closest to their frontier. A sensitivity analysis across four outlier-trimming rules and two inefficiency distributions (48 fits, of which 25 satisfy all diagnostic criteria) shows that the freight estimates are highly stable and the motorcycle and medium/large-car estimates are moderately sensitive. For motorcycles, user characteristics are jointly associated with the one-sided frontier-deviation component: ride-hailing riders operate closer to the frontier (16.6%) than all other occupation groups (23.7% to 29.8%), which are not statistically distinguishable from one another. Occupational coefficients attenuate substantially after conditioning on reported annual VKT, although most remain statistically significant. The gaps provide a consistent comparative benchmark but may reflect a combination of behaviour, vehicle condition, maintenance, operating circumstances, omitted heterogeneity and reporting error; they therefore help identify priorities for diagnostic and intervention testing rather than directly measuring the savings achievable through any single intervention.

title: N2O emissions and potato yield responses to organomineral, inhibitor-based, and deep-placement fertilizer in East Midlands England
summary: Nitrogen (N) fertilization is essential for potato production but can increase soil nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions, creating trade-offs between marketable yield and emission intensity. Finding a balance between potato productivity and climat
content: Nitrogen (N) fertilization is essential for potato production but can increase soil nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions, creating trade-offs between marketable yield and emission intensity. Finding a balance between potato productivity and climate mitigation is critical. Unlike conventional mineral fertilizers, carbon capture organomineral fertilisers (CCOMFs) offer a low-carbon alternative that integrates recycled organic matter with mineral nutrients to sustain crop productivity while reducing the overall carbon footprint. Therefore, we evaluated the effects of five fertilizer type and application strategies; band-placed ammonium nitrate (AN) + N inhibitor (Didin, dicyandiamide; DCD), surface-broadcast AN, band-placed AN, surface-spread CCOMF each applied at 160 kg N ha − 1 and an unfertilized control on marketable tuber yield, yield-scaled N 2 O-N emission, and agronomic N efficiency metrics in a commercial field trial. Results show that fertilizer treatment altered both the magnitude and timing of N₂O emissions. Cumulative N₂O-N emissions were lowest with AN + DCD (2.4 ± 0.2 kg N₂O-N ha⁻¹) but higher with CCOMF (7.9 ± 1.0 kg N₂O-N ha⁻¹) and surface-broadcast AN (7.4 ± 2.7 kg N₂O-N ha⁻¹). Nevertheless, CCOMF produced the highest marketable tuber yield (62.0 ± 1.6 t ha⁻¹), total biomass (93.2 ± 2.6 t ha⁻¹), partial factor productivity (387.5 ± 10.0 kg tuber kg⁻¹ N) and agronomic N use efficiency (26.9 ± 10.0 kg tuber per kg⁻¹ N). Yield-scaled N₂O-N emissions did not differ significantly among treatments. Our findings demonstrate that low carbon footprint organomineral fertilizer (CCOMF) outperformed mineral fertilizer and mineral fertilizer combined with N inhibitor with respect to tuber yield and N use. Further, CCOMF reduced N₂O emissions and offset emission intensity by increasing potato tuber yield. Our findings validate CCOMF as a viable alternative to conventional fertilizers at farm scale.

title: IoT-Driven Enterprise Energy-Efficiency Optimization Model and Financial Performance Analysis: Path Analysis for Promoting a Green Economy
source: International Journal of Intelligent Information Technologies
summary: At present, most businesses lack systematic solutions for leveraging real-time Internet of Things energy data to optimize efficiency and financial performance. The authors propose an Internet of Things–driven framework that integrates three
content: At present, most businesses lack systematic solutions for leveraging real-time Internet of Things energy data to optimize efficiency and financial performance. The authors propose an Internet of Things–driven framework that integrates three modules: (a) a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network with an attention mechanism for high-precision time series forecasting, (b) a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm for scheduling with the intent of realizing dual energy cost and carbon emission objectives, and (c) an improved entropy-weight Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution model for the comprehensive evaluation of energy-financial benefits. Experimental results showed a prediction mean absolute percentage error of only 0.48%. After optimization, energy cost dropped from 0.195 to 0.160 yuan/kWh, carbon emission intensity decreased from 0.220 to 0.184 CO2/kWh, unit energy cost dropped from 1.02 to 0.828 yuan/kWh, and profit margin rose from 12.8% to 17.6%. This framework achieves multidimensional integration of technology, economics, and sustainability, thus offering a scalable pathway for enterprises' green transformation.

title: Greener Valorization of the Seaweed Ulva lactuca: Efficiency and Sustainability of Microwave-Assisted Carotenoid Extraction Using Alternative-Solvents
summary: The recovery of bioactive compounds through green technologies is essential for sustainable industrial development. This study evaluated the efficiency of microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) compared to conventional maceration for recoverin
content: The recovery of bioactive compounds through green technologies is essential for sustainable industrial development. This study evaluated the efficiency of microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) compared to conventional maceration for recovering carotenoids from the seaweed Ulva lactuca. Six solvents were compared: green alternatives (2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF) and ethyl lactate), food-grade solvents (ethanol and ethyl acetate), and traditional options (acetone and hexane). Overall, MAE increased carotenoid recovery approximately 2.2-fold compared with conventional maceration, with solvent-dependent improvements ranging from 1.7- to 5.2-fold. Significant differences in extraction capacity were observed among solvents; hexane and 2-MeTHF yielded the highest carotenoid content (32.35 ± 1.35 and 29.03 ± 0.86 µg/g dw, respectively). Response surface methodology (RSM) optimized MAE conditions at 290 W, 5 min, and a 35.8 mL/g solvent-to-sample ratio, achieving a carotenoid content of 34.82 ± 0.89 µg/g. Environmental assessment revealed that MAE reduced the carbon footprint five-fold compared to the conventional method (5.05 vs. 25.25 g CO2 eq./g of seaweed) due to lower electricity consumption. 2-MeTHF exhibited the lowest environmental burden (0.26 g CO2 eq./µg carotenoid), outperforming hexane (0.46) and ethyl lactate (13.20) due to its superior extraction efficiency and lower emission factor. These findings position MAE combined with 2-MeTHF as a high-performance, eco-friendly strategy to produce marine-derived carotenoids in the food, nutraceutical, and health industries.

title: Influence of OPGW Structure on Ice-Melting Characteristics and Optical fiber Temperature under DC
summary: Considering Joule heating, convective and radiative heat losses, ice-water phase change and dynamic evolution of air gap, a finite-element model is developed in this paper. The characteristics of electrical heat input, heat-transfer pathway
content: Considering Joule heating, convective and radiative heat losses, ice-water phase change and dynamic evolution of air gap, a finite-element model is developed in this paper. The characteristics of electrical heat input, heat-transfer pathways, and fiber thermal response for OPGWs are analyzed. The effects of cable outer diameter, aluminum area fraction, and optical-unit location on ice-melting characteristics are investigated. It indicates that the air gap gradually expands during ice melting after applying a direct current (DC). Its thermal resistance would produce a nonlinear optical fiber temperature response, with a rapid initial increase followed by a slower rise. As the cable outer diameter increases from 13.6 to 16.8 mm, the ice-melting time increases from 3298.4 s to 4828.2 s whereas the optical fiber temperature decreases from 83.83 to 52.08 ℃. Increasing the aluminum area fraction from 0.30 to 0.52 increases the ice-melting time by 21.2% but decreases the optical fiber temperature by 23.90℃. The effect of outer diameter is governed jointly by electrical heat input and thermal and structural factors, whereas aluminum area fraction primarily affects ice melting by changing the equivalent resistance. The difference in ice-melting time with different optical-unit configurations is less than 1%, and their optical fiber temperature differences arises mainly from local heat-transfer pathways and thermal resistance variations. This study provides references for making ice-melting strategy and optimizing the OPGW structure.

title: Isotope evidence for changing methane sources at high northern latitudes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: The renewed increase of methane (CH 4 ) in the atmosphere since 2007 is an imminent threat to the stability of the climate system and undermines climate policy goals. A reversal in the trend of its carbon isotopic composition ( δ 13 C CH4 )
content: The renewed increase of methane (CH 4 ) in the atmosphere since 2007 is an imminent threat to the stability of the climate system and undermines climate policy goals. A reversal in the trend of its carbon isotopic composition ( δ 13 C CH4 ) in the 21st century indicates a fundamental shift in the global CH 4 cycle. Here, we investigate the origin of this δ 13 C CH4 trend by determining isotope source signatures of CH 4 emissions based on high and mid-northern latitude observations. A clear latitude gradient and seasonal cycle of the source signatures reflect the spatially and temporally varying contributions of the different sources, each with distinct signatures. We find a large shift in the source signature after 2007 between −3.6 and −5.1‰ at high northern latitudes, and a moderate change between −0.4 and −0.9‰ at mid-northern latitudes. The decrease in δ 13 C CH4 source signature is likely caused by a shift from thermogenic and pyrogenic to microbial sources, accompanied by a likely decrease in the isotopic signature of the microbial emissions, possibly resulting from climate change. Our results suggest that current inverse models may underestimate the shift between fossil and microbial emissions at high northern latitudes, or that microbial methanogenesis pathways change much more strongly than currently believed. Source changes at high latitudes have a disproportionate contribution to the observed trend in atmospheric δ 13 C CH4 .

title: Replacing Hazardous Solvents with Eco-Friendly Alternatives: Advancing Green Chemistry for Sustainable Industrial Processes
summary: Solvents play a critical role in chemical synthesis, pharmaceutical manufacturing, coatings, petrochemicals, agriculture, and numerous industrial processes. However, many conventional solvents—including benzene, toluene, dichloromethane, ch
content: Solvents play a critical role in chemical synthesis, pharmaceutical manufacturing, coatings, petrochemicals, agriculture, and numerous industrial processes. However, many conventional solvents—including benzene, toluene, dichloromethane, chloroform, and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF)—pose significant environmental and human health risks due to their toxicity, volatility, persistence, and contribution to atmospheric pollution. Growing concerns regarding occupational safety, environmental sustainability, and regulatory compliance have intensified efforts to identify and implement eco-friendly solvent alternatives. This paper examines the scientific principles, technological developments, industrial applications, and challenges associated with replacing hazardous solvents with greener substitutes. The study explores bio-based solvents, water-based systems, supercritical fluids, ionic liquids, deep eutectic solvents, and solvent-free technologies through the lens of Green Chemistry principles. Furthermore, the paper evaluates industrial case studies, economic implications, regulatory frameworks, and future research directions aimed at accelerating the transition toward sustainable solvent systems. The findings indicate that while significant progress has been achieved, widespread adoption requires continued innovation in solvent design, lifecycle assessment, process optimization, and industrial scalability.

title: jzzhou1207/Soil-aggregate-integrity-and-hierarchy: Soil aggregate integrity and hierarchy offer a potential pathway for managing greenhouse gas emissions under warming
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Soil aggregate integrity and hierarchy offer a potential pathway for managing greenhouse gas emissions under warming Overview This repository accompanies the manuscript Soil aggregate integrity and hierarchy offer a potential pathway for ma
content: Soil aggregate integrity and hierarchy offer a potential pathway for managing greenhouse gas emissions under warming Overview This repository accompanies the manuscript Soil aggregate integrity and hierarchy offer a potential pathway for managing greenhouse gas emissions under warming, prepared for submission to Carbon Balance and Management. It provides the summary datasets and Python plotting scripts for Figures 3–6 and documents the intended data processing and figure-reproduction workflow. The study examines how aggregate size, structural integrity, and the arrangement of macroaggregates and microaggregates influence soil carbon dioxide (CO₂), nitrous oxide (N₂O), methane (CH₄) emissions, and their combined global warming potential (GWP) under different warming conditions. It combines soils from an approximately ten-year open-top-chamber (OTC) field-warming experiment in a Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau alpine meadow with controlled laboratory aggregate reconstitution and incubation. The management motivation is to evaluate whether maintaining or modifying soil aggregate structure may influence greenhouse gas responses to warming. Repository status. The four figure_*.csv tables included here were reconstructed directly from numeric values embedded in the four supplied plotting scripts.
