title: Optical GeoAI and spatial modeling enable urban-canopy mapping and resilience screening in Davis, California
summary: Cities need spatially explicit canopy information to connect urban greening with surface-temperature context, mobility, and neighborhood planning. We developed an optical GeoAI workflow for Davis, California, using 2022 National Agriculture
content: Cities need spatially explicit canopy information to connect urban greening with surface-temperature context, mobility, and neighborhood planning. We developed an optical GeoAI workflow for Davis, California, using 2022 National Agriculture Imagery Program (0.6 m RGB + NIR). DeepForest generated crown candidates, which were filtered with NDVI and non-maximum suppression, refined with box-prompted Segment Anything Model (ViT-B), and expanded with a transparent NDVI-texture infill. Analyses used the 25.92 km 2 Census TIGER municipal boundary and a 100 m grid. The workflow retained 11,741 candidate crowns and mapped 7.71 km 2 of canopy (29.8% of the city). On the identical extent, reference-relative agreement with the 2022 USDA/CAL FIRE LiDAR-assisted canopy product reached 0.804 pixel precision, 0.873 pixel recall, 0.719 intersection over union, and 0.837 Dice, while 97.4% of candidate centers coincided with reference canopy. Approximately 49% of candidates occurred within 15 m of a road. Canopy was inversely associated with land-surface temperature from the 11 May 2022 Landsat 8 scene (Spearman ρ = −0.477; partial ρ = −0.551 controlling for built probability), and spatial modeling identified neighborhood structure. Two transparent screening surfaces identified locations where canopy need, heat, and contextual indicators co-occur. The framework links open Earth-observation and urban data to reproducible, updateable, urban-informatics screening products for follow-up assessment, rather than site-level planting prescriptions.

title: Anthropogenic Contaminants in Commercial Fish from Brazil and Mozambique: µ-Raman Characterization and Market-Associated Distribution Patterns
summary: Contaminants in commercially important fish provide relevant information on environmental exposure in coastal urban systems. This study investigated materials detected in the gastrointestinal tracts of croaker (Micropogonias furnieri) and h
content: Contaminants in commercially important fish provide relevant information on environmental exposure in coastal urban systems. This study investigated materials detected in the gastrointestinal tracts of croaker (Micropogonias furnieri) and horse mackerel (Trachurus trachurus) marketed in Santos, Brazil, and Maputo, Mozambique, integrating microscopy combined with Raman spectroscopy (µ-Raman), frequency analysis, and correspondence analysis with market categories and market-associated socioeconomic profiles. µ-Raman analysis included 68 spectral acquisitions, yielding 124 component assignments, including carbonaceous materials, synthetic polymers, cellulosic materials, pigments, dyes, and other chemical signatures. Carbon and graphite were the most frequent components, while polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyester-related materials predominated among synthetic polymers. Both study areas showed comparable spectral-occurrence patterns, particularly for PET, graphite, and cellulosic materials. Global chi-square tests showed no statistically significant dependence between material occurrence and either market categories or socioeconomic profiles. However, adjusted standardized residuals and correspondence analysis revealed localized distributional patterns involving specific materials and market categories, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than causal relationships. Integrating µ-Raman spectroscopy and multivariate analysis provides a useful framework for characterizing chemically diverse materials associated with gastrointestinal exposure in commercially important fish. Nevertheless, their occurrence in gastrointestinal tissues provides evidence of environmental exposure and may be relevant to ecological risk, which requires dedicated toxicological assessment. Because we analyzed only gastrointestinal tissues, the findings do not demonstrate contamination of edible muscle tissues, human dietary exposure, or health risk.

title: Conceptualising brand purpose as a multidimensional marketing and management construct: a qualitative framework
summary: Brand purpose has been explored across organisational, stakeholder, authenticity, sustainability and brand-equity research but remains difficult to define consistently. This paper aims to create a combined multidimensional model of brand pu
content: Brand purpose has been explored across organisational, stakeholder, authenticity, sustainability and brand-equity research but remains difficult to define consistently. This paper aims to create a combined multidimensional model of brand purpose and create an initial set of items for further validation. By conducting a concept-based literature review we identified eleven tentative domains. Through an iterative two-round expert consultation process these domains were questioned and adjusted. We used a combination of deductive-inductive and grounded theory coding techniques when analysing the data from our 15-member panel of experts (made up of both academics and practitioners). An additional expert panel of 11 provided written input which was used to inform initial item creation. As the focus of the expert round was to challenge and improve upon our domains, this should not be considered validation of the items. Our domains can be grouped into four themes: a beyond-profit core, internal embedding, stakeholder experience, and impact and brand outcomes. Theoretically, our paper integrates these domains and clarifies boundaries between similar concepts. Managerially, it provides a structured basis for reflecting on brand purpose. Lastly, we created a set of items that require future validation.

title: The Role of the State in Economic Development: A Comparative Analysis of Capitalism, Communism, and Islamic Political Economy
source: Global Review of Islamic Economics and Business
summary: The debate over the role of the state in economic development is generally polarized between capitalism, which emphasizes minimal state intervention, and communism, which places the state as the sole controller through a command system. Bot
content: The debate over the role of the state in economic development is generally polarized between capitalism, which emphasizes minimal state intervention, and communism, which places the state as the sole controller through a command system. Both have produced significant achievements, but they leave behind structural problems such as inequality, cyclical crises, inefficiency, and stagnation. This study addresses the research problem that comparative analyses positioning capitalism, communism, and Islam within a single political-economic framework remain limited, so that the role of the state in Islamic economics has not been positioned as an equal paradigm, but merely as a normative complement. This research gap encourages research to reformulate the role of the state in Islamic economics based on maqaṣid al-shariah. The research uses the library research method with a comparative political economy and normative synthesis approach. Data was collected from primary literature, classical economic texts, the writings of Islamic scholars, and secondary literature in the form of international journals, development reports, and contemporary theories. The analysis was conducted through content analysis, cross-paradigm comparative evaluation, and normative synthesis. The findings show that capitalism has evolved from a minimal state to a market-oriented state, while communism positions the state as a hegemonic actor that controls all economic sectors but risks causing authoritarianism and stagnation. In contrast, Islamic economics positions the state as an authority.

title: AI and Overdetermination: The Real Source of Responsibility Gaps
summary: As AI systems become increasingly embedded in medicine, policing, warfare, and other high-stakes domains, their harmful outputs raise a pressing question: who, if anyone, is morally responsible? A common worry is that AI can generate respon
content: As AI systems become increasingly embedded in medicine, policing, warfare, and other high-stakes domains, their harmful outputs raise a pressing question: who, if anyone, is morally responsible? A common worry is that AI can generate responsibility gaps: cases in which morally significant harms occur, human agents acted suboptimally, and yet no individual seems to satisfy the conditions for accountability. Such gaps are troubling because they threaten practices of blame, compensation, deterrence, and moral repair. But when and why do responsibility gaps arise? Existing discussions often locate the source of the gap in either the opacity of AI systems or the involvement of many human contributors. This paper argues that both diagnoses miss the mark. The real source of AI responsibility gaps, we argue, is overdetermination. In many AI contexts, harmful outcomes may occur regardless of what any particular individual does, because other agents, firms, institutions, or systems would have produced materially similar outcomes. This structure undermines the control condition on moral responsibility. The diagnosis matters for our evaluations of remedies: transparency-based solutions target the wrong sort of problem, and individual gatekeeper models may simply reproduce the same overdetermination structure at a higher level. Collective-level solutions, by contrast, are at least structurally suited to closing the gap.

title: When the internet cools crops: the mitigating effect of digital infrastructure on heat-induced grain losses in China
summary: High temperatures are increasingly threatening the stability of grain output and food security in the context of climate change. Yet there is currently a lack of empirical evidence to show whether the development of digital infrastructure c
content: High temperatures are increasingly threatening the stability of grain output and food security in the context of climate change. Yet there is currently a lack of empirical evidence to show whether the development of digital infrastructure can help mitigate the adverse effects of high temperatures on grain output. Using data from 294 prefecture-level cities in China over the period 2010–2023, we estimated the effect of high-temperature risks and digital infrastructure on grain output. We also examined whether digital infrastructure moderates the relationship between high-temperature disasters and grain output. We find that high-temperature risks significantly suppressed grain output; there is an inverted U-shaped relationship between digital infrastructure construction and grain output; digital infrastructure can mitigate the loss of grain output caused by high-temperature risks, and its buffering effect is mainly concentrated in the central and western regions as well as regions with lower exposure to high temperatures. Improving agricultural information acquisition, optimizing the allocation of production factors, enhancing digital risk sharing and financial security, and accelerating the adoption of climate-adaptive technologies are important mechanisms for the functioning of agricultural digital resilience. This paper incorporates digital infrastructure construction into the agricultural climate adaptation framework, clarifies the conditions for the effective functioning of agricultural digital resilience, and provides insights for the development of digital infrastructure in grain-producing regions exposed to high-temperature risks.

title: Data from: Sheep grazing within regenerative perennial systems accelerates soil carbon and nitrogen accrual
summary: Vineyard producers are increasingly adopting regenerative production models in response to the sustainability challenges of input-based conventional production. Integrating livestock onto cropland is a central regenerative practice. It offe
content: Vineyard producers are increasingly adopting regenerative production models in response to the sustainability challenges of input-based conventional production. Integrating livestock onto cropland is a central regenerative practice. It offers a route to building soil health and reducing input and labor costs, while creating new markets and added value. Integrated sheep vineyard systems (ISVS) are gaining traction in California's coastal regions. Systems-level data from working farms remain scarce, however, as do knowledge-sharing platforms for producers grazing across a conventional to regenerative gradient. That gap limits best-management guidance and our understanding of the benefits and trade-offs involved.This three-year on-farm study compared vineyards integrating sheep grazing with those that did not, along a conventional to regenerative management gradient. It was designed through extensive consultation with growers and sheep operators, and builds on the team's previous work. The study pursued five objectives. It established a landscape-scale, on-farm participatory research platform. It quantified the effects of grazing and grazing intensity on vineyard soil health, biodiversity, vine health, yield, berry quality, forage quality and input use. It analyzed the economic performance of these systems and developed a cost-return planning tool. It identified benefits and trade-offs by evaluating interactions among the chemical, physical, biological and economic components of the vineyard. And it disseminated results to producers in English and Spanish through field days, presentations, a best-management-practice guide, and social media.The study network comprised commercial vineyards in northern and central California. These ranged from sites with grazing legacies of at least three years to sites with no grazing history. Grapes are California's third-highest-grossing crop at close to one million acres, and vineyard understories are an increasingly important forage source as drought reduces rangeland production. Working across a commercial network allowed management strategies, input use, soil health and crop yield outcomes to be assessed against real edaphoclimatic variation rather than under experimental control. Recent assessments of nature-based climate solutions have identified this kind of on-farm evidence on stacked sustainable practices as a priority.Items in this project hold the data, code and documentation released from the study. The first release covers soil carbon and nitrogen accrual under sheep grazing across 49 vineyards. It accompanies Fenster et al., Carbon Balance and Management.Within this dataset are two data sheets and the map used for creating figure 1 of the manuscript. Additionally, there is the associated R code and Readme file.Data files:1.) Transect-level soil carbon, nitrogen and management data from 49 California wine grape vineyards under contrasting grazing and regenerative managementFile Name: 2026-10-20_Public_D

title: Effects of CO₂ Carbonation Stabilization Parameters on the Performance of Lake Sediment
summary: To investigate the effects of CO₂ carbonation parameters on lake sediment stabilization, a ternary binder of reactive MgO, slag, and silica fume was used in a full-factorial two-factor, three-level experiment. Carbonation times of 0.5, 1.0,
content: To investigate the effects of CO₂ carbonation parameters on lake sediment stabilization, a ternary binder of reactive MgO, slag, and silica fume was used in a full-factorial two-factor, three-level experiment. Carbonation times of 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 h and CO₂ pressures of 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 MPa were evaluated. Compressive strength, shear strength, and mass gain ratio were measured after 7, 14, and 28 d. All three responses generally increased with carbonation time and CO₂ pressure. Two-way ANOVA showed significant main effects of both factors at all curing ages (p < 0.001), whereas the interaction depended on the response and age. At 0.6 MPa, increasing carbonation time from 1.0 to 1.5 h increased the 28 d compressive strength only from 7.06 to 7.12 MPa. Therefore, 1.0 h–0.6 MPa provided a favorable balance between strength and treatment duration.

title: Framing Climate Governance in Türkiye-EU Relations
summary: This chapter examines how the European Union’s (EU) European Green Deal (EGD) projects climate norms beyond the Union and how Türkiye receives, reframes, and selectively internalizes these norms under conditions of asymmetric interdependenc
content: This chapter examines how the European Union’s (EU) European Green Deal (EGD) projects climate norms beyond the Union and how Türkiye receives, reframes, and selectively internalizes these norms under conditions of asymmetric interdependence. Bringing together a policy-framing approach with theories of norm diffusion and localization, it asks how EU climate rules are narrated in Türkiye’s official policy discourse and what patterns of strategic alignment emerge as climate objectives become intertwined with market access and regulatory risk. Empirically, the chapter focuses on the 2019–2025 period, tracing key EU instruments—the European Climate Law, the Fit for 55 package, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and sustainable-finance rules (Taxonomy and SFDR)- alongside Türkiye’s main planning and coordination texts, including the Eleventh and Twelfth Development Plans and the Green Deal Action Plan. While Türkiye aligns with EU standards in areas affecting export resilience and investment access, it adopts a selective approach in high-cost areas, emphasizing fairness and burden-sharing. Consequently, this chapter conceptualizes “strategic alignment” as a selective alignment pattern focused on competitiveness, energy security, and regulatory risk. At the implementation level, it defines Türkiye-EU cooperation priorities in areas such as green finance and technology partnerships.

title: Why Do Reforestation Systems Collapse? Governance Failure, Utility Insolvency, and Livelihood Trajectories of Green Infrastructure in the Great Green Wall Sahelian Drylands
summary: The success of restoration projects generally depends on planted area or canopy cover. Infrastructure that is responsible for sustaining the life of seedlings (such as vehicles, water source, pumps and processing units) receives very little
content: The success of restoration projects generally depends on planted area or canopy cover. Infrastructure that is responsible for sustaining the life of seedlings (such as vehicles, water source, pumps and processing units) receives very little attention. This paper asks why infrastructure built under Pillar 3 (“Climate-Resilient Infrastructure”) of the Great Green Wall (GGW) stops working, and who is able to repair it. We present a qualitative case study of three sites in the Ferlo region of northern Senegal (Widou Thiengoly, Koyli Alpha, Mbaye Awa) and, for comparison, a field observation and documentary case study of Tigray, Ethiopia, where armed conflict prevented comparable fieldwork. The Senegal data are based on (N = 120) semi-structured interviews, (N = 7) focus group discussions and structured infrastructure inspection conducted between September 2025 and February 2026. We organised and interpreted them using categories drawn from the Social-Ecological Systems framework and Access Theory. At the Senegal sites we found: a shrinking vehicle fleet at the Widou station; water cut-offs after the GGW agency fell behind on payments to the rural water utility (SDE-R); solar pumps without storage and an idle milk-processing unit; and administrative control that blocked women’s groups from funding their own water storage. For Tigray, published studies report deliberate destruction of nurseries and water schemes during the war. Seedling loss and abandoned assets therefore look alike in both places but have different causes: administrative neglect in Senegal and armed conflict in Tigray. We conclude that restoration funding should cover maintenance, utility bills and spare parts, not only planting.

title: The Tragedy of Sand Commons and Environmental Justice in India’s Riverine Ecosystems
summary: Riverbed sand, a vital ecological component and an indispensable resource for India’s infrastructure boom, has become the site of a profound constitutional and environmental crisis. The unregulated and extensive extraction of sand epitomize
content: Riverbed sand, a vital ecological component and an indispensable resource for India’s infrastructure boom, has become the site of a profound constitutional and environmental crisis. The unregulated and extensive extraction of sand epitomizes the ‘Tragedy of Sand Commons’, where developmental imperatives override ecological and community interests creating a crisis of law and sustainability. The foundational legal flaw is the classification of sand as a "minor mineral" under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. This framework prioritises revenue over ecology, creating a systemic failure of governance and a profound implementation gap in the State's constitutional mandate to protect the environment under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), particularly Article 48A. The Supreme Court's landmark judgment in Deepak Kumar v. State of Haryana (2012) and subsequent interventions by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) recognised the massive ecological damage caused by unregulated extraction and closed the exemption under which minor mineral leases below five hectares had escaped environmental appraisal altogether. This judicial activism is rooted in the Public Trust Doctrine, which reframes the State’s role from a mere licensor to a trustee, constitutionally bound to protect rivers as a public resource. This paper situates riverbed sand mining within the broader discourse of constitutional environmentalism, exploring how India’s environmental jurisprudence has evolved to recognise nature’s intrinsic rights and the state’s duty as trustee of natural resources. It also critically examines the "SDG Paradox": the aggressive pursuit of SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) is proceeding at the cost of progressive degradation of riverine ecosystems, directly undermining SDG 14 (Life Below Water) and SDG 15 (Life on Land). Through doctrinal and policy analysis, the paper argues that achieving true environmental justice requires a doctrinal shift: legally re-classifying riverbed sand from “minor mineral” to a “vital ecosystem component” under a unified national legislation, and embedding ecological restoration and community participation within the legal framework.

title: The role of participatory neighbourhood processes in establishing energy cooperations based on two case studies from Switzerland
summary: Decarbonising the existing building stock is a major challenge for sustainable and climate-neutral cities, particularly in neighbourhoods characterised by a high prevalence of single- and (small-sized) multi-family housing and fragmented ow
content: Decarbonising the existing building stock is a major challenge for sustainable and climate-neutral cities, particularly in neighbourhoods characterised by a high prevalence of single- and (small-sized) multi-family housing and fragmented ownership structures. While neighbourhood-scale energy solutions promise technical, economic, and social benefits, in Switzerland, they are rarely realised in practice. This paper examines how participatory approaches can support the emergence of neighbourhood-level energy cooperations in such contexts. The paper presents a comparative case study of two Swiss pilot projects where the QUBE methodology, a process-focused intermediary methodology that supports coordination and joint action towards renewable energy solutions, was developed and applied. QUBE targets a critical but underexplored transition space between new solutions for individual buildings and institutionalised energy communities, enabling coordination among homeowners through structured participatory processes. The findings suggest that neighbourhood-based participatory processes can generate momentum for local energy transitions by activating residents, strengthening local networks, and enabling informed decision-making. Crucial to this process is intermediary support that helps clarify feasible options, build trust, and facilitate both individual and collective action, while also contributing to the emergence of targeted support structures at community and municipal levels. However, the scope of owner-led energy cooperation remains more limited than expected, as persistent barriers such as financial constraints, regulatory complexity, and heterogeneous owner preferences hinder coordinated action. By foregrounding process- and governance-related outcomes, the paper provides transferable insights and lessons learned to inform the design and implementation of participatory approaches that support socially accepted, place-based pathways to decarbonise existing suburban neighbourhoods.

title: Legal Architecture of Carbon Trading through the Carbon Exchange in Indonesia: An Analysis of POJK 14/2023, SEOJK 12/2023, and Regulatory Dynamics 2025-2026
summary: This article examines Indonesia's legal framework for carbon trading through the carbon exchange, anchored in OJK Regulation No. 14/2023 and OJK Circular Letter No. 12/SEOJK.04/2023, and situates it within the 2025 to 2026 regulatory shift
content: This article examines Indonesia's legal framework for carbon trading through the carbon exchange, anchored in OJK Regulation No. 14/2023 and OJK Circular Letter No. 12/SEOJK.04/2023, and situates it within the 2025 to 2026 regulatory shift comprising Presidential Regulation No. 110/2025, OJK Regulation No. 10/2026, and OJK Board of Commissioners Member Regulation No. 6/2026. Employing a normative-juridical methodology combined with descriptive secondary market analysis, the study reveals three core findings. First, classifying carbon units as securities imports capital-market governance including licensing, fit-and-proper tests, supervision, and administrative sanctions directly into the carbon market. Second, the initial 2023 architecture underwent substantial revision in 2025 and 2026 through the replacement of the single registry with the decentralized Carbon Unit Registry System (SRUK), the expansion of eligible carbon units, explicit financial consumer protection, and the revocation of Circular Letter No. 12/SEOJK.04/2023. Third, regulatory maturity has not yet translated into market liquidity, as cumulative trading value stood at approximately IDR 94.20 billion by October 2026. The article concludes that Indonesia's policy agenda is transitioning from market creation toward market integrity and depth while requiring explicit benefit-sharing mechanisms for communities surrounding carbon-generating ecosystems.

title: Effective Intrusion Detection and Classification in VANET Environments Using Deep Learning Model with Optimization Algorithms
source: International Journal of Computer Science and Engineering
summary: VANET (Vehicular Ad Hoc Network) is an innovative transportation technology that improves road safety and traffic management through communication and data sharing between vehicles. The attackers create various kinds of assaults to oppose t
content: VANET (Vehicular Ad Hoc Network) is an innovative transportation technology that improves road safety and traffic management through communication and data sharing between vehicles. The attackers create various kinds of assaults to oppose the operational tasks of the network environment in VANET. Then, identifying the attacks in VANET method is extremely essential to give reliable and secure communication among each vehicle within the system. Because of this, the Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is needed in VANET to offer safety from outside attacks like Botnet, Denial of Service (DoS), and so on. These may identify assaults and provoke a response, lowering the effects on the target system. This paper develops an Intelligent Intrusion Detection and Classification using Deep Learning Model and Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithms (IIDC-DLMMOA) method in VANET Environments. The main intention of IIDC-DLMMOA technique relies on developing an effective structure for IDS in VANET communications. The hiking optimization algorithm (HOA) performs feature selection by identifying the input features that contribute most to the classification process. For the classification process, the proposed IIDC-DLMMOA designs a spatial-temporal attentive with long short-term memory (STA-LSTM) system. At last, the hyperparameter tuning optimizes a classification model of STA-LSTM method through a Multi-Objective Mantis Search Algorithm (MOMSA) by selecting the best parameter values. The developed IIDC-DLMMOA system is verified on the real-time benchmark database, and the stimulated outcomes are in comparison with other advanced techniques.

title: Innovative alkalinity neutralization approaches improve tomato yield, quality and influence soil properties in semi–arid agroecosystems with irrigation (bi)carbonates hazard
source: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
summary: Introduction Irrigation alkalinity with high residual sodium carbonate (RSC) adversely affects soil chemical properties, nutrient availability, and tomato fruit quality. This study evaluated the effectiveness of neutralization strategies su
content: Introduction Irrigation alkalinity with high residual sodium carbonate (RSC) adversely affects soil chemical properties, nutrient availability, and tomato fruit quality. This study evaluated the effectiveness of neutralization strategies such as acid neutralizer (AN), liquid sulphur (LS), and CSSRI elemental sulphur (S°) reaction product (CSRP) mixed with irrigation water (RSC 3 and 6 me L –1 ) to bring the RSC equivalent to 1 me L –1 in improving soil ionic composition, nutrient availability, and the nutritional quality of tomato under alkali–irrigated sodic soil. Methods Treatments were allocated in a randomized block design in lysimeters filled with sodic soil (pH 1 : 2 9.88, EC 1 : 2 2.1 dS m –1 ). Irrigation water was applied through drip based on the crop coefficient and evapotranspiration demand of the summer–season tomato crop. Results and Discussion Neutralization approaches significantly increased Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , and SO 4 2– concentrations and reduced carbonate/bicarbonate [H(CO 3 ) n– ], soil pH and alkalinity. The CSRP was most effective in increasing Ca 2+ 12.9 and SO 4 2– (49.0 meq L –1 ) content in soil solution and lowering soil pH. CaCl 2 –S also increased under CSRP treatment. The soil improvement significantly enhanced tomato yield and fruit quality by increasing total soluble solids, pulp pH, and total antioxidants. Under CSRP, lycopene and total soluble solids were 3.80 mg 100 g –1 fresh weight and 7.27° Brix, respectively. Changes in soil properties due to RSC irrigation neutralization explained about 81% ( P = 0.046) of the variability in yield and fruit quality. Dissolved reactive P, exchangeable sodium percentage, and pH were the most important factors affecting yield and quality under sodic soil with RSC irrigation. The findings concluded that the alkalinity–neutralizing amendments such as acid neutralizer, liquid sulphur, and CSSRI elemental sulphur (S°) reaction product effectively improve crop performance in alkali irrigated sodic soils. These amendments also improved S and P availability and alleviated sodicity stress, thereby improving tomato nutritional quality. Overall, the results indicated that alkalinity neutralization can effectively improve soil properties and support vegetable production in alkalinity—affected agroecologies.

title: Divergent Dynamics of Farmland Rents and Local Employment under Utility-Scale Solar Expansion: Evidence from U.S. Counties
summary: Utility-scale solar expansion creates competing demands for land while generating local investment and employment opportunities. Land rental costs and employment gains may, however, follow different time paths. This study links georeference
content: Utility-scale solar expansion creates competing demands for land while generating local investment and employment opportunities. Land rental costs and employment gains may, however, follow different time paths. This study links georeferenced solar projects with agricultural cash rents and employment in 1,403 U.S. counties (12,627 county-year observations) during 2016–2024. Using doubly robust staggered difference-in-differences, dynamic event studies, and spatial exposure comparisons, we examine responses to the first entry of a qualifying ground-mounted solar project. During the commissioning year and the following two years, real nonirrigated cropland cash rents rise by an estimated 7.12%, while private-sector employment increases by 1.26%. Rent effects strengthen over time, whereas employment gains diminish after commissioning; construction employment exhibits a pronounced initial response. Rent effects are larger where reliance on rented land or the cropland share is higher, while employment gains are stronger in counties with larger manufacturing sectors. Neighboring-county solar exposure is associated with smaller positive responses in rents and employment. These findings highlight divergent timing and spatial patterns of agricultural land costs and local employment returns, informing solar siting and sustainable land-use planning.

title: When Governance Unlocks Green Performance: Revisiting ESG Effectiveness in Resource‐Abundant Economies
summary: As environmental, social, and governance (ESG) frameworks gain traction in global financial markets, questions persist about their true environmental effectiveness, especially in resource‐abundant economies where governance weaknesses preva
content: As environmental, social, and governance (ESG) frameworks gain traction in global financial markets, questions persist about their true environmental effectiveness, especially in resource‐abundant economies where governance weaknesses prevail. This study revisits the ESG–environment nexus through the lens of institutional enrichment, asking whether governance quality can unlock the environmental potential of ESG systems. Using panel data for 20 extractive economies spanning 2000–2023, we employ cross‐sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) and method of moments quantile regression (MMQR) techniques to capture both long‐run dynamics and distributional heterogeneity across carbon emissions, ecological footprint, and green innovation. The results reveal that ESG scores alone often correlate positively with environmental degradation, suggesting symbolic compliance rather than substantive sustainability. However, when interacted with governance quality—and particularly its squared term—ESG frameworks begin to exert a significant mitigating influence on emissions and ecological pressure while enhancing innovation performance. This demonstrates that institutional enrichment functions as a threshold mechanism, converting ESG disclosure into genuine environmental progress. The study reframes ESG not as a standalone sustainability signal but as a conditional financial governance instrument dependent on institutional strength. By linking corporate sustainability strategy with institutional capability, the research offers a governance‐based explanation for ESG heterogeneity and provides strategic insights for policymakers, investors, and firms seeking credible pathways toward green performance in resource‐dependent contexts.

title: Beyond Emission Reduction: Carbon Tax, Climate Resilience, and Cultural Heritage Protection in Indonesia Toward SDG 13
summary: One of the considerations for passing Law Number 32 of2009 concerning Environmental Protection and Management is global warming. The existence of negative externalities in the form of greenhouse gas emission pollution represents a market fa
content: One of the considerations for passing Law Number 32 of2009 concerning Environmental Protection and Management is global warming. The existence of negative externalities in the form of greenhouse gas emission pollution represents a market failure caused by the fact that the cost of environmental damage is not borne by polluters. Instead, this cost is borne by the general public and culturale heritage building. Based on the polluter pays principle, legal tax instruments emerged to internalize these costs into production cost structures. In line with SDGs 13 regarding climate change, which focuses on curbing greenhouse gas emissions, one of the Indonesian government's efforts to prevent climate change is through the imposition of a carbon tax. The government responded to this condition by enacting Law Number 7 of2021 concerning the Harmonization of Tax Regulations. Article 13 paragraph (9) sets a very low carbon tax rate of at least IDR 30.00 per kilogram of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO 2 e) or an equivalent unit Based on normative research using a statutory approach and a conceptual approach, findings reveal that the rate of IDR 30,000/ton (CO 2 e) does not yet meet the Kaldor-Hicks economic efficiency standard. This is because its value is far below the global social cost of carbon. Consequently, the internalization of negative environmental externalities remains sub-optimal, preventing the potential net social gain which should compensate for the social loss caused by carbon emission pollution from being fully realized.

title: Зелёное финансирование и низкоуглеродная трансформация обрабатывающей промышленности Китая: механизмы, вызовы и направления развития
summary: Введение. Обрабатывающая промышленность Китая находится на ключевом этапе перехода от модели экстенсивного роста с высоким энергопотреблением и значительными выбросами к экологически устойчивой, низкоуглеродной и высокоэффективной модели хо
content: Введение. Обрабатывающая промышленность Китая находится на ключевом этапе перехода от модели экстенсивного роста с высоким энергопотреблением и значительными выбросами к экологически устойчивой, низкоуглеродной и высокоэффективной модели хозяйствования. Зелѐные финансы, опирающиеся на кредитное финансирование, инвестиции в облигации и механизмы углеродного рынка, обеспечивают направленное перераспределение капитала в пользу экологически чистых проектов и формируют устойчивый импульс к трансформации промышленного сектора КНР. Несмотря на совершенствование институциональной системы зелѐных финансов, обрабатывающая промышленность страны сталкивается со структурными вызовами, в числе которых индустриализация зелѐных технологий, оптимизация структуры высокоуглеродных отраслей и трансмиссия углеродных издержек. Материалы и методы. На основе актуальных данных 2024–2025 годов о развитии зелѐного финансирования в Китае и низкоуглеродной трансформации обрабатывающей промышленности с использованием методов анализа научной литературы и институционально-политического анализа в работе исследована роль зелѐных финансов в поддержке экологически устойчивого развития промышленного сектора КНР, рассмотрены текущее состояние и ключевые вызовы данного процесса. Эмпирическая база сформирована на основе официальных данных Народного банка Китая, Государственного статистического управления и Министерства промышленности и информационных технологий КНР. Результаты исследования. По состоянию на конец второго квартала 2025 г. остаток зелѐных кредитов в национальной и иностранной валютах в Китае достиг 42,4 трлн юаней с приростом 21,7% в годовом исчислении; доля кредитов, направленных на сокращение выбросов углерода, составила 67,5%. Совокупный объѐм эмиссии зелѐных облигаций превысил 4,1 трлн юаней, а кумулятивный объѐм торгов на национальном углеродном рынке достиг 696 млн т. В период XIV пятилетнего плана в Китае сформировано 6430 национальных зелѐных заводов и 491 зелѐный промышленный парк, на долю которых приходится более 20% совокупного объѐма продукции обрабатывающей промышленности. Однако сохраняются три ключевые проблемы: отставание индустриализации зелѐных технологий, медленные темпы оптимизации высокоуглеродной структуры отраслей и существенное давление трансмиссии углеродных издержек. Обсуждение и заключения. В статье обоснованы четыре направления развития: повышение эффективности коммерциализации зелѐных технологий, ускорение структурной оптимизации энергоѐмких отраслей, совершенствование механизмов внутреннего учѐта углеродных издержек и укрепление кадрового обеспечения в сфере экологичных технологий. Зелѐные финансы и низкоуглеродная трансформация обрабатывающей промышленности КНР должны формировать синергетический механизм, обеспечивающий высококачественное экологически устойчивое развитие отрасли посредством сопряжения технологических инноваций, структурной оптимизации, управления издержками и кадрового обеспечения. title: ESG FINANCING AND CARBON CREDITS AS A MECHANISM FOR THE RENATURALIZATION OF RECREATIONAL AREAS IN FOREST ECOSYSTEMS
summary: The article examines the possibility of applying ESG financing instruments and the carbon units market for the restoration of forest areas subject to recreational digression. The transition from a subsidy-based model of nature management to
content: The article examines the possibility of applying ESG financing instruments and the carbon units market for the restoration of forest areas subject to recreational digression. The transition from a subsidy-based model of nature management to an -investment model is substantiated, where renaturalization becomes a source of environmental assets. Based on the analysis of international cases and Russian regulatory initiatives (the "Nature Unit" mechanism), a methodological scheme for assessing the carbon potential of recreational zones is proposed. The modeling results show a positive economic return on projects subject to verification requirements and long-term lease of forest plots.

title: Industrialization in middle Africa: do renewable energy, finance, trade, electricity access, environmental taxation, and FDI matter?
summary: Background This study examines the effects of renewable energy consumption (REC), financial development (FD), trade openness (TO), access to electricity (AE), environmental tax (ETX), and foreign direct investment (FDI) on industrialization
content: Background This study examines the effects of renewable energy consumption (REC), financial development (FD), trade openness (TO), access to electricity (AE), environmental tax (ETX), and foreign direct investment (FDI) on industrialization. Methods Drawing on a panel dataset of eight Middle African countries covering the period from 2000 to 2021, the analysis employs panel FMOLS, DOLS, and RLS estimators, complemented by pairwise Granger causality tests to assess both the robustness and causal direction of the relationships. Findings The findings reveal that REC exerts a positive and statistically significant influence on industrialization across all estimation techniques, a result further reinforced by Granger causality evidence indicating a bidirectional relationship between REC and industrialization. Likewise, FD emerges as one of the most influential drivers of industrialization, displaying positive effects that remain significant at the 1% level across all models, together with unidirectional Granger causality running from FD to industrialization. Similarly, TO also has a positive and statistically significant effect on industrialization, while the Granger causality confirms a unidirectional causal relationship from TO to industrialization. Furthermore, AE exerts a positive and significant influence on industrialization under every method, accompanied by bidirectional causality between AE and IND. In contrast, ETX consistently exerts a negative and statistically significant impact on industrialization, although the Granger causality results reveal a bidirectional causal relationship between ETX and industrialization. Lastly, FDI exhibits a negative and statistically significant effect on industrialization, with no evidence of causality in either direction. Summary Overall, renewable energy consumption, financial development, trade openness, and access to electricity promote industrialization, whereas environmental tax and foreign direct investment exert negative effects.

title: How Often Should Forest Carbon Credits Be Verified? Replication Data and Code

content: This dataset contains the replication data and code for "How Often Should Forest Carbon Credits Be Verified? title: In-Transit Ripening of Mangoes: Optimising CO2 Management
summary: Efficient in-transit ripening of mango (Mangifera indica L.) fruit is essential for preserving quality and meeting market demands. This study investigated the application of RipestufTM, an ethylene-releasing powder, and hydrated lime [Ca(OH
content: Efficient in-transit ripening of mango (Mangifera indica L.) fruit is essential for preserving quality and meeting market demands. This study investigated the application of RipestufTM, an ethylene-releasing powder, and hydrated lime [Ca(OH)2] to absorb excess carbon dioxide (CO2) produced by fruit respiration within refrigerated truck containers to optimise ripening conditions during road transport in Australia. Over two mango seasons, eleven consignments were monitored, including six treated with RipestuffTM and hydrated lime and five untreated controls. Air and pulp temperature, ethylene, CO2, O2 and relative humidity (RH) concentrations were continuously monitored throughout transport. In year 1, ethylene-treated consignments transported at 14–16 °C exhibited CO2 accumulation up to 20% despite the inclusion of lime, which was associated with reduced ripening uniformity. Subsequent laboratory experiments identified key limitations in CO2 control, including insufficient gas permeability of the lime packaging materials, reduced lime utilisation at depth, and variability in lime activity. In year 2, an optimised lime application system incorporating improved packaging permeability and reduced lime bed depth effectively limited CO2 concentrations to below 5% during transport, even at elevated temperatures of 18–19.5 °C. Ethylene concentrations were maintained above 10 ppm for 2–3 days, resulting in accelerated and uniform ripening compared with untreated fruit. This study underscores the importance of managing temperature, ethylene, and CO2 levels during transit to achieve consistent ripening and high fruit quality. It is recommended that fruit respiration rates and container free air volume be quantified prior to determining the required quantity of lime for commercial application. Only freshly manufactured hydrated lime with an activity above 85% and depth of ≤ 40 mm in highly porous packaging should be used to maximise CO2 absorption efficiency.

content: XülasәTәdqiqatın mәqsәdi.Bu mәqalәnin yazılmasında mәqsәd müasir aqrar fәaliyyәtlәr sistemi kimi aqroekosistemin idarә edilmәsindә rәqәmsal mühit üstünlüklәrinin reallaşdırılması istiqamәtlәrini müәyyәn etmәkdir.Qarşıya qoyulan mәqsәdә nail olmaq üçün ilk dәfә olaraq, aqroekosistemdә baş verәn proseslәrin idarә edilmәsi mәsәlәlәrinә ayrı-ayrılıqda baxılmış, idarәetmәnin rәqәmsal aspektlәrdә tәkmillәşdirilmәsi istiqamәtlәri müәyyәn edilmişdir.Tәdqiqatın metodoloji bazasını elmi abstraksiya, müqayisәli tәhlil, sintez, mәntiqi ümumilәşdirmә metodları, habelә rәqәmsal texnologiyalardan istifadәnin verilәnlәr bazasının formalaşması vә inkişafını xarakterizә edәn yanaşmalar tәşkil etmişdir.Tәdqiqatın tәtbiqi әhәmiyyәti әldә edilmiş nәticәlәrin aqroekosistemlәrin idarә edilmәsinin rәqәmsallaşması prosesindә, idarәetmә mexanizminin tәkmillәşdirilmәsi istiqamәtindә görülәn tәdbirlәrin hazırlanması vә icrasında istifadәsi imkanlarında ifadә olunur.Tәdqiqatın nәticәlәrinin aqroekosistemlәrdә müxtәlif fәaliyyәtlәrin rәqәmsal idarә edilmәsi tәcrübәsindә aqrar fәaliyyәtlәrin sәmәrәliliyini yüksәltmәyә xidmәt edәcәyini söylәmәk olar.Xülasә edilәn müddәalar göstәrir ki, aqroekosistemlәrin rәqәmsal idarә edilmәsi tәkmillәşdikcә sahәnin dayanıqlı inkişafına ciddi töhfә verә bilәr.Tәdqiqatın orijinallığı vә elmi yeniliyi.Aqroekosistemlәrin rәqәmsal idarә edilmәsinin sәmәrәliliyinin yüksәldilmәsi, rәqәmsal mühit üstünlüklәrinin reallaşdırılmasının müәyyәn edilmiş iqtisadi vә institusional istiqamәtlәrindә atılacaq davamlı addımlardan asılı olacağı aşkar edilmişdir. title: Research on integrated risk measurement of China’s carbon market based on Copula-VaR-QIDE model
summary: As an emerging financial market, China’s carbon market is characterized by strong nonlinear dependence among multiple risk factors, fat-tailed return distributions, and frequent extreme volatility, posing significant challenges to conventio
content: As an emerging financial market, China’s carbon market is characterized by strong nonlinear dependence among multiple risk factors, fat-tailed return distributions, and frequent extreme volatility, posing significant challenges to conventional risk measurement methods. Existing approaches either rely on restrictive distributional assumptions or suffer from boundary bias in nonparametric density estimation, limiting their ability to accurately characterize tail risks. To address these limitations, this study proposes a nonparametric integrated risk measurement framework, namely the Copula-VaR-QIDE model, by integrating Value at Risk (VaR), quasi-interpolation density estimation (QIDE), and Copula theory. Specifically, QIDE is employed to estimate the marginal distributions of risk factors without restrictive distributional assumptions, while Copula theory is used to model their nonlinear dependence structure. Using a two-factor risk framework comprising carbon price and exchange rate returns, the proposed model is applied to four representative Chinese carbon markets (Guangdong, Beijing, Hubei, and Shanghai). Empirical backtesting results demonstrate that the proposed model consistently outperforms traditional VaR and Copula-VaR-KDE models in terms of predictive accuracy and stability. The proposed framework provides a flexible and robust approach for integrated carbon market risk measurement and offers practical implications for carbon market regulation and financial risk management.

title: Ontological conflict and system hacking: Indigenous agency and relational-aquatic spatiality among Anak Rawa of Riau
summary: This article examines how the Anak Rawa, an Indigenous community inhabiting the coastal peatlands of Penyengat Village, Siak Regency, Riau, negotiate identity, living space, and environmental governance amid overlapping state and corporate
content: This article examines how the Anak Rawa, an Indigenous community inhabiting the coastal peatlands of Penyengat Village, Siak Regency, Riau, negotiate identity, living space, and environmental governance amid overlapping state and corporate territorial regimes. Moving beyond the materialist framework that dominates agrarian conflict scholarship, the study advances the concept of ontological spatial conflict to explain the epistemic contest between geometric-productive spatial planning and a relational-aquatic customary spatiality grounded in hydrological continuity, seasonal mobility, and intergenerational ecological practices. Unlike scholarship on political ontology and land control, which foregrounds competing claims over a shared object, this concept specifies how the territorial unit itself is constituted differently by each party. Drawing on critical ethnography involving twelve purposively selected informants, participatory mapping data generated through a Participatory Land Use Planning (PLUP) process, and secondary data on peatland restoration, the study triangulates community narratives with independently produced datasets. The findings reveal that the Anak Rawa exercise strategic agency through system hacking, repurposing bureaucratic instruments to sustain hydro-ecological continuity. This process is mediated by cultural brokers whose authority is unevenly distributed within a demographically plural village. The article contributes a context-specific explanatory mechanism of ontological conflict in coastal peatlands, conceptualizes system hacking as a form of agency with traceable outcomes, and identifies reforms needed to operationalize hydro-legal recognition.

title: From Anticipation to Implementation: Time–Frequency Reconfiguration of the Carbon–Freight Nexus under the EU ETS
summary: This study examines how the relationship between European Union allowance (EUA) prices and dry-bulk freight returns changes as maritime carbon regulation moves from anticipation to implementation. The analysis uses 714 weekly observations f
content: This study examines how the relationship between European Union allowance (EUA) prices and dry-bulk freight returns changes as maritime carbon regulation moves from anticipation to implementation. The analysis uses 714 weekly observations from January 2013 to September 2026 and applies wavelet coherence and phase-difference methods across four regulatory stages: pre–Fit for 55, the 2021–2023 transition, maritime inclusion in the EU Emissions Trading System in 2024, and the subsequent EU ETS–FuelEU Maritime period. Despite a near-zero full-sample return correlation, local dependence differs in sign and horizon. Positive EUA-leading configurations dominate statistically significant 2–8-week cells during 2021–2024. In 2025–2026, statistically significant 8–32-week coherence is predominantly negative and EUA-leading. These configurations remain visible under alternative wavelet resolution, winsorization and Brent-adjusted partial coherence, although a 1% threshold sharply reduces significant coverage. The findings show that maritime carbon-market integration is characterized by a reconfiguration of the carbon–freight relationship rather than a uniform strengthening. For shipping businesses and policy analysis, the results underline the need to distinguish allowance exposure, freight-market conditions and the horizon over which market information is incorporated.

title: Exclusion before displacement and the reorganization of waste access in Makassar’s waste-to-energy transition
summary: Makassar’s waste-to-energy (WtE) transition is promoted as a technological response to urban waste and clean-energy challenges, yet its social consequences remain insufficiently examined. This study investigates how planned WtE development
content: Makassar’s waste-to-energy (WtE) transition is promoted as a technological response to urban waste and clean-energy challenges, yet its social consequences remain insufficiently examined. This study investigates how planned WtE development restructures power relations, access to waste resources, and livelihood security among waste-dependent communities around the Tamangapa disposal site. A qualitative case study combined in-depth interviews with eight key informants, an informal small-group discussion, participant observation, and document analysis, supported by a descriptive survey of 98 purposively selected respondents. Findings indicate that planned WtE arrangements position municipal waste increasingly as industrial feedstock alongside existing informal material-recovery practices. This creates an anticipatory mechanism of material exclusion through reduced or uncertain access to recoverable waste and procedural exclusion through unequal access to project information and environmental-risk knowledge. Survey findings show substantial livelihood vulnerability, limited understanding of WtE technology, high perceived ecological risk, and strong support for community monitoring and protection mechanisms. Conceptually, the study shows that exclusion can emerge through the reorganization of practical access before formal displacement occurs, revealing an anticipatory form of environmental inequality rather than completed displacement. A just WtE transition therefore requires livelihood safeguards, transparent and verifiable information, substantive participation, and participatory monitoring.

title: Цифровая трансформация управленческого учёта проектных затрат: от регламента управленческой отчётности к BI-дашборду
summary: Введение. В статье рассматривается переход от ручных форм управленческого учѐта проектных затрат к автоматизированным цифровым платформам как методическая, а не только техническая задача. Показано, что метод освоенного объѐма (EVM) применит
content: Введение. В статье рассматривается переход от ручных форм управленческого учѐта проектных затрат к автоматизированным цифровым платформам как методическая, а не только техническая задача. Показано, что метод освоенного объѐма (EVM) применительно к проектно-ориентированным организациям должен интерпретироваться с учѐтом стадии жизненного цикла проекта – создания актива или его последующей операционной эксплуатации, поскольку именно от этого зависит состав показателей, подлежащих автоматизированному расчѐту. Материалы и методы. На основе анализа российских учѐтных платформ и методологии проектного управления рассмотрена логика перехода от ручных инструментов к цифровым. На примере внутреннего регламента еженедельной управленческой отчѐтности консалтинговой компании «Консилиум» показано преобразование ручного формата планфактного отчѐта в техническое задание для цифрового дашборда. Систематизированы цифровые инструменты автоматизации учѐта проектных затрат и пять уровней зрелости автоматизации. Результаты исследования. На примере «Консилиума» удалось показать: цифровая трансформация управленческого учѐта буксует не там, где нет подходящего программного продукта, а там, где не формализована сама отчѐтность. Автоматизировать можно лишь то, что уже живѐт в регламенте: конкретный перечень показателей, фиксированную периодичность, закреплѐнные аналитические разрезы. Переработка такого регламента в техническое задание на BI-дашборд – это не изобретение нового, а перевод уже работающей практики в цифровую форму, что и делает подход практически реализуемым. Обсуждение и заключения. Описанный подход рассчитан в первую очередь на проектно-ориентированные компании среднего масштаба, то есть те, у кого нет ни бюджета на разработку с нуля, ни ресурса на длительное внедрение ERP. Таким организациям важно опереться на уже сложившуюся отчѐтную практику, а не заменять еѐ целиком. Дальнейшие исследования, на наш взгляд, стоит направить на отраслевую конкретизацию: нужны сценарии перехода между уровнями зрелости с реальными оценками затрат и сроков для каждого шага. Introduction. Project cost accounting is routinely described as a technology problem. This paper argues it is not. The transition to digital platforms fails – or stalls at half-measures – not because of software limitations but because management reporting was never formalised to begin with. A further argument concerns EVM: applied to project-oriented organisations, the method only makes sense when differentiated by lifecycle stage, since asset creation and operational use call for entirely different indicator sets. Materials and Methods. The study combines a review of Russian accounting platforms and EVM methodology with direct analysis of practice. The core empirical material is an internal weekly reporting procedure from Consilium Consulting Company. title: Ethnobotanical uses of Helichrysum species: A review of traditional medicinal practices
summary: Background: The genus Helichrysum Mill. (Asteraceae) comprises approximately 500–600 species and has a long history of traditional medicinal use. This review aimed to evaluate the geographical distribution, plant parts, preparation methods,
content: Background: The genus Helichrysum Mill. (Asteraceae) comprises approximately 500–600 species and has a long history of traditional medicinal use. This review aimed to evaluate the geographical distribution, plant parts, preparation methods, and medicinal indications associated with Helichrysum species. Methods: A literature review was conducted between April and September 2026 using Scopus, PubMed, and TR Dizin, supplemented by Google Scholar and ResearchGate. Publications identifying Helichrysum taxa and documenting traditional medicinal uses were eligible. Of 110 sources, 10 were excluded, 80 were included in the ethnobotanical analysis, and 20 were retained as supporting references. An ethnobotanical record represented a documented traditional medicinal use associated with an identifiable taxon. Data were analyzed descriptively, and medicinal indications were classified using the WHO ICD-11 Browser. Uses without classifiable medical indications were excluded from ICD-11 analysis. Results: ICD-11 classification yielded 275 chapter assignments, primarily involving symptoms, signs or clinical findings (n = 75; 27.27%), followed by genitourinary (n = 49; 17.82%), digestive (n = 32; 11.64%), and respiratory diseases (n = 31; 11.27%). Türkiye and South Africa were prominent geographical locations. Flowers and aerial parts were commonly used, while infusion and decoction predominated as preparation methods. Conclusions: Helichrysum species exhibit diverse traditional medicinal uses. Further pharmacological, toxicological, and clinical studies are needed to establish their efficacy and safety.

title: Моделирование затрат на строительство социальных объектов с учетом региональных экономических циклов (Республика Татарстан)
summary: Введение. Точность прогнозной оценки затрат на строительство социальных объектов имеет прикладное значение для регионального бюджетного планирования, однако традиционные сметные расчѐты, опирающиеся на базовые индексы и нормативы, не учитыв
content: Введение. Точность прогнозной оценки затрат на строительство социальных объектов имеет прикладное значение для регионального бюджетного планирования, однако традиционные сметные расчѐты, опирающиеся на базовые индексы и нормативы, не учитывают фазовых колебаний строительной активности. В Республике Татарстан, где реализуются масштабные программы возведения школ, поликлиник и других объектов социальной инфраструктуры, недоучѐт циклических удорожаний ресурсов и контрактных рисков приводит к систематическим отклонениям фактической стоимости от плановой. Цель исследования – обоснование подхода к прогнозированию затрат на строительство социальных объектов, включающего индикатор регионального экономического цикла в качестве корректирующего фактора. Материалы и методы. Методологическую основу исследования составляют действующая Федеральная сметно-нормативная база (далее – ФСНБ) ценообразования в строительстве, приказы Минстроя, данные Федеральной государственной информационной системы ценообразования в строительстве (далее – ФГИС ЦС) и региональные индексы цен строительных ресурсов. Для выделения циклической составляющей применяется фильтр Ходрика – Прескотта к рядам объѐмов строительных работ в сопоставимых ценах; разрыв (gap) трактуется как отклонение фактической строительной активности от тренда. Эконометрическая спецификация построена как динамическая регрессия с лагами, где зависимая переменная – темп изменения сметной стоимости, а регрессоры включают официальные индексы, инфляцию материалов, динамику оплаты труда и gap-индикатор. Результаты исследования. Предложена трѐхкомпонентная модель затрат: базовая смета, умноженная на индекс изменения стоимости и экспоненту от циклической поправки. Для типового объекта (школа/поликлиника) выполнены сценарные расчѐты, показывающие, что в фазе перегрева удорожание может достигать 15–22% против 8– 13% при замедлении. Разработан алгоритм калибровки параметра чувствительности γ по историческим данным и порядок интеграции модели в расчѐт начальной максимальной цены контракта. Область применения – корректировка региональных инвестиционных программ, управление закупочными процедурами и формирование резервов на непредвиденные расходы. Обсуждение и заключения. Введение циклического компонента переводит детерминированную сметную оценку в вероятностный интервал, что повышает обоснованность бюджетных решений. Ограничения метода связаны с зависимостью оценок разрыва от выбора фильтра и длины выборки, а также со спецификой уникального оборудования, слабо коррелирующего с общими индексами. Перспективы развития модели видятся в переходе к панельной оценке по типам объектов и использовании режимно-сменных спецификаций для учѐта структурных сдвигов. Introduction.
