title: How Green Bond Issuance Shapes Corporate Environmental Ratings and Emissions: Transmission Channels and Dynamic Responses in China
summary: Green bonds finance corporate environmental projects. Using a 2012–2025 panel of firms listed on China’s A-share markets, we examine changes in environmental ratings and emissions around firms’ first green bond issuance. The Sun–Abraham est
content: Green bonds finance corporate environmental projects. Using a 2012–2025 panel of firms listed on China’s A-share markets, we examine changes in environmental ratings and emissions around firms’ first green bond issuance. The Sun–Abraham estimates show relative gains in Huazheng environmental (E) scores in the issuance year and the following year. In the bond-issuer comparison with firm-specific linear trends, the gains for green bond issuers exceed those for ordinary bond issuers by 1.69 and 2.47 points, respectively. Green invention patent applications and grants, along with quantitative environmental disclosure, are positively associated with E scores. Both the two-way fixed effects and Sun–Abraham estimates show an increase in quantitative disclosure. Larger firms and firms with more pre-issuance media coverage show greater E-score gains. The estimated post-issuance change in log absolute emissions is smaller for firms with higher initial carbon intensity. On a sample with ratings, disclosure, and emissions data, Sun–Abraham estimates show relative increases in E scores and absolute emissions. At longer horizons, carbon intensity declines relative to control firms as estimated growth in operating revenue outpaces that in absolute emissions. These findings help investors and regulators interpret ratings and carbon intensity alongside absolute emissions over the life of green bonds.

title: Leveraging Digital Technology for the Carbon Performance of a Manufacturing Firm Using Affordance Actualization Theory
summary: Digital technology offers new opportunities for manufacturing firms to improve their carbon performance. However, research on how digital technology influences different dimensions of carbon performance and its underlying mechanisms remain
content: Digital technology offers new opportunities for manufacturing firms to improve their carbon performance. However, research on how digital technology influences different dimensions of carbon performance and its underlying mechanisms remain limited. To address this gap, we investigate how digital technology affordances enhance firms’ carbon performance and identify the mechanisms through which these affordances are actualized. Using a longitudinal dataset covering 312 A-share listed firms in China’s electrical machinery and equipment manufacturing industry from 2013 to 2023, we find that digital technology affordances positively affect carbon performance, including carbon efficiency and green revenue. Empirical analyses reveal differentiated mediating mechanisms: operational process optimization mediates the relationship between digital technology affordances and carbon efficiency, whereas business partnership and managerial myopia mediate their effects on green revenue. Moreover, the effects are heterogeneous: the impact of digital technology affordances is stronger in firms located in resource-based cities and highly marketized regions. Further analysis extends the significantly positive effect of digital technology affordances to external stakeholders, such as green reputation and green investors’ attention. This study provides novel and concrete insights into carbon performance, highlights the role of digital technology affordances in corporate sustainability, and offers practical guidance for firms pursuing digital-enabled green transformation.

title: Rethinking the Classification of Forest Carbon Sink Potential: A Co-Benefit Potential Perspective
summary: International carbon market experience and China’s forest carbon sink development indicate that unlocking the potential of co-benefits is an important pathway toward the high-quality development of forest carbon sinks. From the perspective
content: International carbon market experience and China’s forest carbon sink development indicate that unlocking the potential of co-benefits is an important pathway toward the high-quality development of forest carbon sinks. From the perspective of co-benefit potential, this study applies the biomass conversion factor method and the present value (PV) method to estimate the forest carbon sink potential and co-benefit potential of 304 cities in China, respectively, and further grades and classifies forest carbon sink potential based on the estimation results. We find that cities differ substantially in both carbon sink potential and co-benefit potential, and both are higher in western than eastern China. Based on the ratio of co-benefit potential to forest carbon sink potential, the sampled cities were classified into five quality grades (I–V) of forest carbon sink potential, and the numbers of cities across the different quality grades were ranked as follows: Grade IV (88) > Grade II (73) > Grade III (65) > Grade I (43) > Grade V (35). Forest carbon sink potential can be classified into eight types: the social–economic high-potential type, social–ecological high-potential type, ecological–economic high-potential type, ecological high-potential type, economic high-potential type, social high-potential type, general-development type, and overall low-potential type. The findings provide new insights into the diversified, innovative, and quality-oriented development of forest carbon sink products and help avoid social welfare losses resulting from efficiency-oriented forest carbon sink development.

title: Investigation of Root Causes and Supply Chain Factors Associated With Premature Chassis Rusting in South African Vehicles Exported to Europe
summary: Premature chassis corrosion in vehicles exported from South Africa to Europe increases warranty costs, compromises reliability, and reduces customer satisfaction. This study investigated its root causes using a mixed‐methods approach integr
content: Premature chassis corrosion in vehicles exported from South Africa to Europe increases warranty costs, compromises reliability, and reduces customer satisfaction. This study investigated its root causes using a mixed‐methods approach integrated with the Lean Six Sigma DMAIC methodology. Quantitative data from warranty records, supplier audits, quality inspections, and production records were combined with qualitative document and process analyses. Chi‐square tests, ABC analysis, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Fuzzy FMEA, and gravimetric and electrochemical tests were used to assess and prioritise corrosion risks. Findings identified improper coating application, inadequate surface preparation, material incompatibility, supplier variability, and weak process control as key contributing factors. The study establishes a baseline for evaluating proposed interventions and presents a data‐driven framework to improve chassis durability, reduce corrosion defects and warranty costs, minimise material waste, and strengthen the competitiveness of South African automotive exports.

title: Advancing nutraceutical delivery through microencapsulation: hybrid systems, controlled release, and machine learning‐driven optimization
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: Bioactive constituents have strong potential for nutraceutical applications, but their use in functional products is often limited by poor stability, low water solubility, low bioavailability, degradation during processing and storage, and
content: Bioactive constituents have strong potential for nutraceutical applications, but their use in functional products is often limited by poor stability, low water solubility, low bioavailability, degradation during processing and storage, and undesirable sensory properties. Microencapsulation can help overcome these limitations by protecting bioactive compounds and improving their delivery. However, the wide range of wall materials and encapsulation techniques makes it difficult to select the most suitable system for each application. This review critically evaluates microencapsulation strategies for nutraceutical constituents by examining the relationships between bioactive properties, wall materials, encapsulation techniques, release mechanisms, and functional performance. Current evidence shows that there is no single encapsulation technique that is suitable for all constituents. Successful encapsulation depends on compatibility between the bioactive compound, wall material, processing conditions, and the intended application. Conventional techniques, especially spray drying and freeze drying, remain widely used, while lipid-based carriers, structured emulsions, and emerging systems provide additional options for improving stability and delivery. However, industrial application may be limited by scale-up challenges, processing complexity, cost, regulatory requirements, and the lack of standardized evaluation methods. Machine learning also offers new opportunities for formulation optimization, release prediction, and process design, although its application remains at an early stage. Overall, future research should focus on rational material and process selection, scalable and sustainable technologies, and standardized performance assessment to support the development of effective and commercially practical nutraceutical delivery systems. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Porous Organic Frameworks for Overall Photosynthesis H 2 O 2
summary: Solar‐to‐H 2 O 2 conversion represents one of the most promising avenues for sustainable development, while overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via the dual pathways of simultaneous ORR and WOR holds significant scientific value. This review fir
content: Solar‐to‐H 2 O 2 conversion represents one of the most promising avenues for sustainable development, while overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via the dual pathways of simultaneous ORR and WOR holds significant scientific value. This review first systematically summarizes the recent advancements of porous organic frameworks (POFs) for overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Starting with a concise overview of the fundamental principles of H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via ORR and WOR, as well as dual‐channel H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, the evaluation protocols and key factors are briefly discussed. Thereafter, the advantages, development, and typical design strategies of POFs for this process are summarized. Subsequently, various smart POFs for dual‐pathway photosynthesis H 2 O 2 are introduced. In the past year alone, diverse molecular design strategies have driven continuous gains across all performance metrics, with records reaching a H 2 O 2 production rate of 17.25 mmol·g −1 h −1 , an accumulated concentration of 82.3 mM, an AQY of 40%, and an SCC efficiency of 4.7%. Last but not least, conclusions, challenges, and long‐term outlooks of this field are revealed with a focus on POFs design, computer‐assist, H 2 O 2 decomposition, and mechanism investigations. This review aims to offer in‐depth insights and guidelines for POFs in efficient overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis.

title: Cellulose Microfibrils as a Secondary Reinforcement Enabling High Untreated Coir Fiber Loadings in Bio‐Based Rigid Polyurethane Foams
summary: Untreated lignocellulosic residues degrade the mechanical performance of rigid polyurethane foams (RPUF), and the surface treatments normally used to avoid it add cost and chemical burden. This work examines whether glycerol‐dispersed cellu
content: Untreated lignocellulosic residues degrade the mechanical performance of rigid polyurethane foams (RPUF), and the surface treatments normally used to avoid it add cost and chemical burden. This work examines whether glycerol‐dispersed cellulose microfibrils (MFC), used as a secondary reinforcement, can offset that penalty. MFC was transferred from aqueous suspension to glycerol by sequential solvent exchange and added at 0.2 wt% to castor oil‐based RPUF containing 5, 10, or 15 wt% untreated coir ( Cocos nucifera ) fiber (CF). Under free‐rise conditions, CF alone left the apparent density unchanged (43.4–45.7 vs. 44.3 kg m −3 for the neat foam) but reduced the compressive strength (by 53% at 15 wt%) while raising the compressive modulus. Adding 0.2 wt% MFC refined the cellular structure, densified the foams by 21%–31%, and reversed the strength loss, with 5.CF.MFC reaching 158.2 kPa, 39% above the control. Normalization by density revealed an asymmetric reinforcement: the specific modulus rose by 241%–285%, whereas the specific strength of the best hybrids only matched the control, showing that the strength gain is largely density‐driven. FTIR indicated hydrogen bonding between MFC and the urethane hard segments. A low MFC content enables high untreated CF loadings without a mechanical penalty.

title: Bamboo‐Derived Oxygen‐Rich Porous Carbon Cathode Enabling High‐Performance Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
summary: Four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries (4eZIBs) are promising for high‐energy aqueous energy storage, yet their practical performance is limited by the instability of reactive I + species and the associated irreversible iodine loss. Herein, an
content: Four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries (4eZIBs) are promising for high‐energy aqueous energy storage, yet their practical performance is limited by the instability of reactive I + species and the associated irreversible iodine loss. Herein, an oxygen‐rich hierarchical porous carbon (PC) derived from bamboo powder is developed as an iodine host to regulate interfacial iodine chemistry. A zinc nitrate hexahydrate assisted solution combustion carbonisation strategy simultaneously constructs interconnected micro/mesopores and enriches oxygen‐containing surface functionalities. The resulting PC‐15 provides abundant accessible sites for iodine immobilisation, whereas its oxygen‐rich surface modulates the local iodine coordination environment and mitigates I + hydrolysis. The synergistic regulation of pore confinement and surface chemistry leads to enhanced iodine utilisation and favourable interfacial reaction kinetics. Consequently, the PC‐15 cathode delivers a specific capacity of 447.9 mAh g −1 at 0.8 A g −1 and retains a high rate capacity of 340.9 mAh g −1 at 8 A g −1 . Upon prolonged cycling at 5 A g −1 , it retains a capacity of 182.8 mAh g −1 after 4000 cycles with an average coulombic efficiency of 99.6%. These results demonstrate that integrating hierarchical pore confinement with oxygen‐rich surface chemistry can effectively reconcile iodine retention with rapid redox conversion, providing a practical materials design principle for high utilisation aqueous iodine cathodes.

title: Nash Equilibrium in Tariff Setting: The 2018-2020 U.S.-China Trade War and Its Global Impacts
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This study analyzes the 2018–2020 U.S.-China trade war through a game-theoretic lens to understand how countries reach a Nash equilibrium in tariff setting and its implications for global trade flows. Employing a non-cooperative game model
content: This study analyzes the 2018–2020 U.S.-China trade war through a game-theoretic lens to understand how countries reach a Nash equilibrium in tariff setting and its implications for global trade flows. Employing a non-cooperative game model with payoff functions πU(tU, tC) = WU − αtU − βtC − γtU tC for the U.S. and πC(tU, tC) = WC − δtC − ϵtU − ζtU tC for China, where tU and tC are tariff rates, we identify a Nash equilibrium of mutual high tariffs (18.6% for the U.S., 15% for China). This equilibrium, resembling a Prisoner’s Dilemma, led to a 51.65% reduction in bilateral trade, with U.S. imports from China falling 52.3% and exports to China dropping 49.3%. Trade diversion increased exports to third countries like Mexico and Vietnam, while global value chain disruptions raised freight mileage by 0.23%–0.34%. Welfare losses were 0.2% for the U.S. and 1.7% for China. The findings highlight the suboptimal outcomes of non-cooperative tariff strategies and underscore the need for multilateral frameworks, such as the World Trade Organization (WTO), to foster cooperative trade policies and mitigate global trade disruptions. Keywords: Nash Equilibrium. U.S.-China Trade War, Tariffs, Game Theory, Trade Diversion. Title: Nash Equilibrium in Tariff Setting: The 2018-2020 U.S.-China Trade War and Its Global Impacts Author: Hossen Md Sayed, Romi Md Tamim Anaj, Nurul Md Islam International Journal of Recent Research in Commerce Economics and Management (IJRRCEM) ISSN 2349-7807 Vol. 13, Issue 4, October 2026 - December 2026 Page No: 99-109 Paper Publications Website: www.paperpublications.org Published Date: 21-November-2026 DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24415451 Paper Download Link (Source) https://www.paperpublications.org/upload/book/Nash%20Equilibrium%20in%20Tariff%20Setting-21112026-3.pdf

title: Divergent evolutionary trajectories of Lactobacillus crispatus and Lactobacillus iners in the Chinese vaginal microbiome
summary: The vaginal microbiota is central to women’s reproductive health, yet its population structure and evolutionary history remain underexplored in non-western populations. We conducted a multicentre study of 212 vaginal samples from women acro
content: The vaginal microbiota is central to women’s reproductive health, yet its population structure and evolutionary history remain underexplored in non-western populations. We conducted a multicentre study of 212 vaginal samples from women across six provinces in China to interrogate community composition, geographic stratification and strain-level evolution. Overall, Chinese vaginal communities displayed low alpha diversity and were most frequently dominated by Lactobacillus . Longitudinal sampling across menstrual cycles indicated that most participants maintained stable community state types, with a subset exhibiting state shifts, highlighting both resilience and context-dependent dynamics. Geographic analysis revealed a higher prevalence of Lactobacillus crispatus in northern regions. Strain-resolved genome reconstruction and phylogenomic analysis suggested that Chinese L. crispatus lineages cluster with western counterparts, consistent with a relatively recent introduction and expansion in China, potentially following China’s accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001. In contrast, Chinese Lactobacillus iners formed a divergent branch with markedly greater genetic diversity (40-fold higher than L. crispatus ), supporting its status as an indigenous colonizer. Pangenome analysis indicated species-specific accessory functions consistent with local adaptation. Together, these findings delineate a geographically structured and evolutionarily distinct vaginal microbiome in Chinese women, with recent emergence of L. crispatus alongside long-standing, diverse L. iners lineages.

title: Quantum flow algorithm: Quantum simulations of chemical systems using reduced quantum resources and constant depth quantum circuits
summary: We assess the performance of the Quantum Flow (QFlow) algorithm employing cost-effective solvers based on the unitary coupled-cluster Ansatz with single and double excitations (QFlow-SD). The resulting energies are benchmarked against those
content: We assess the performance of the Quantum Flow (QFlow) algorithm employing cost-effective solvers based on the unitary coupled-cluster Ansatz with single and double excitations (QFlow-SD). The resulting energies are benchmarked against those obtained with an analogous QFlow formulation defined in the same active spaces but augmented by higher-rank excitations, including triples and quadruples (QFlow-SDTQ) within a matrix-based implementation, to isolate the effect of excitation rank. Across all molecular systems considered, QFlow-SD closely reproduces the QFlow-SDTQ energies thereby requiring substantially fewer variational parameters while preserving the reduced-qubit footprint of the QFlow algorithm. For this implementation, we perform a series of calculations, including a composite two-step downfolding workflow for H2O. To enable simulations beyond the matrix implementation, we introduce and demonstrate a second-quantized many-body formulation of QFlow. Using this formulation, we perform QFlow calculations of larger problems, including H8 in 6-31G, H2O in 6-31G, and a 4 × 4 two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model, reducing the parent qubit requirements (26-32 qubits) to eight-qubit active-space subproblems. We compare our results against benchmark DMRG energies and show rapid convergence over QFlow cycles and recovery of a large fraction of correlation energy.

title: Giant dielectric permittivity in Nb-doped rutile crystals
summary: Dielectric properties of Nb-doped (∼1.5 at.%) rutile single crystals were studied in the 10–300 K temperature range (at frequencies below the MHz range down to 0.3 K) in a broad frequency range, including terahertz and infrared range, to un
content: Dielectric properties of Nb-doped (∼1.5 at.%) rutile single crystals were studied in the 10–300 K temperature range (at frequencies below the MHz range down to 0.3 K) in a broad frequency range, including terahertz and infrared range, to understand the origin of its giant permittivity. The results were fitted, modelled and compared with those of the undoped rutile crystal measured in the terahertz and infrared ranges. The primary effect originates from the near-electrode depletion layer of lower conductivity compared to the bulk (surface barrier-layer capacitor effect), which causes a strong thermally activated relaxation in the MHz dielectric spectra. In the higher frequency range, the main difference between doped and undoped crystals is the presence of an overdamped microwave excitation (central mode) in the doped crystal for both polarizations, persisting down to 10 K and not thermally activated. This accounts for the previously reported increased permittivity values down to 2 K—where all lower-frequency relaxations are frozen—compared to undoped crystals. It also explains why our low-frequency permittivity at 0.3 K exceeds its THz value. In similar Nb-doped rutile single crystals it was quite recently ascribed [V. A. Dinh et al , Phys. Rev. B 114 , 024112, (2026)] to MW tunnelling of molecular polarons. Polar phonons are affected only by a slightly increased damping.

title: “What’s SUPP”: developing an in vitro model for healthy oral biofilms
summary: Oral diseases such as caries and periodontitis coincide with dysbiosis of oral plaque biofilms enriched for oral pathogens typically present in low abundance in health. Many available in vitro sup ragingival p laque (SUPP) models favor the
content: Oral diseases such as caries and periodontitis coincide with dysbiosis of oral plaque biofilms enriched for oral pathogens typically present in low abundance in health. Many available in vitro sup ragingival p laque (SUPP) models favor the growth of oral pathogens via several factors, including anaerobic incubation, non-saliva media, or assembled consortia that do not well represent species abundant in healthy SUPP. Here we present a low-cost, high-throughput in vitro SUPP model designed to study healthy commensal interactions. Saliva-coated hydroxyapatite discs, inoculated with donor SUPP, were incubated aerobically under a thin layer of medium. In this context, we performed an iterative 16S rRNA microbiome profiling-guided refinement of medium and incubation conditions to best match donor SUPP composition. Using a 25% saliva medium, we obtained in vitro SUPP community diversity over 3–5 days that more closely resembled in vivo diversity than those using rich media or anaerobic incubation. Using these initial model conditions, we were able to determine how filter vs boiling sterilization of saliva impacted community composition in vitro . Furthermore, we were able to use the model to quantify the fitness of the fluorescently labeled Corynebacterium matruchotii wild-type and lut -operon mutant, demonstrating their integration into the in vitro SUPP biofilm and the necessity of lut expression in vitro in a far more complex community than we had previously investigated. This model enables a low-cost mechanistic investigation of polymicrobial interactions in a structurally complex, health-relevant biofilm context at suitable sample sizes for microbiome assessment independent of host immune responses. IMPORTANCE Multiple oral diseases coincide with a shift in the oral microbiota that occurs during a complex transition, which can also be impacted by changes in the host environment and immune response. We currently know relatively little of interactions and mechanistic relationships within polymicrobial communities in oral health compared to disease. While the focus on disease research is rightfully justified, the understanding of what mechanisms might serve to stabilize or restore healthy communities may be a promising avenue for disease prevention and treatment. The significance of this study is that it provides an initial, accessible in vitro model to study these mechanisms of interaction separate from host responses. Use of this model will enable discovery of microbial-driven factors that may preserve or restore oral health.

title: A graph state space model jointly predicts optical density and tyrosine concentration during fermentation
summary: Measurements of biomass and product concentration in microbial fermentation often require offline assays, which limits their availability for real-time process monitoring. We propose G-Mamba, a framework that uses process knowledge and onli
content: Measurements of biomass and product concentration in microbial fermentation often require offline assays, which limits their availability for real-time process monitoring. We propose G-Mamba, a framework that uses process knowledge and online measurements to jointly predict optical density at 600 nm (OD600), a proxy for biomass, and tyrosine concentration. The framework combines a bidirectional Mamba branch for temporal representation learning with a graph convolutional branch that uses a predefined process graph and a learnable adjacency matrix. The predefined graph encodes operational relationships, dependencies in derived-variable calculations, and biologically motivated associations. The two branch representations are concatenated and passed to a multilayer perceptron. We evaluated the framework on 30 Escherichia coli fermentation batches using five-fold batch-wise cross-validation and three training seeds. Among the compared models, G-Mamba achieved the lowest mean MAE in all four evaluated tasks and the lowest mean MSE in the 2→4 and 3→4 tasks. Joint training reduced mean MSE for both targets, although improvements were not uniform across all metrics. The efficiency measurements indicate a favorable accuracy-cost trade-off relative to several strong baselines. Further validation is needed to assess performance under other strains and cultivation conditions.

title: The Springback Effect in Pre-Densified Sulfidic Solid Electrolyte/Binder-Sheets and Its Implication for All-Solid-State Batteries
summary: Cell components that enable high energy density, the reduction of operation pressure, and the adaptation of established production processes are important for the breakthrough of Li-ion all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Slurry-based proces
content: Cell components that enable high energy density, the reduction of operation pressure, and the adaptation of established production processes are important for the breakthrough of Li-ion all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). Slurry-based processing, adapted from Li-ion battery technology, represents a promising production route. Although slurry-based fabrication of separators has been reported, the influence of the operation pressure on their conductivity and the effect of the mechanical properties of the polymer binder in composite separators remains elusive. Here we report a slurry-based process to obtain free-standing solid electrolyte (SE)/binder composite sheets as ASSB separators, employing different contents and types of binder. Using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, we investigate their ionic conductivity as a function of fabrication pressure (yielding different separator porosities) and operation pressure. Using a novel cell-setup approach, we quantify the conductivity loss for fully densified composite SE/binder-sheets when measured at practically relevant, reduced operation pressures, comparing it with the maximum conductivity attained at very high operation pressures. The conductivity loss is related to a “springback” effect, whereby the pressure release after fabrication leads to a volumetric expansion of the polymer phase, resulting in decreased ionic conductivity. The extent of this effect strongly depends on both the type of binder and its content.

title: The protein phosphatase 2A catalytic subunit Pph22 partners with Tap42 and Rrd2 to control viability and virulence in Cryptococcus neoformans
summary: Protein phosphatase 2A regulates eukaryotic signaling, but the function of its associated regulators remains poorly understood in the human fungal pathogen Cryptococcus neoformans. Here, we used affinity purification coupled with mass spect
content: Protein phosphatase 2A regulates eukaryotic signaling, but the function of its associated regulators remains poorly understood in the human fungal pathogen Cryptococcus neoformans. Here, we used affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry and identified 81 candidate proteins associated with the catalytic subunit Pph22, including the scaffold subunit Tpd3, the regulator Tap42, and the protein phosphatase methylesterase 1. Conditional-expression and meiotic spore analyses supported an essential role for TAP42 in viability. We identified CNAG_05505 as the Rrd2 ortholog and detected an interaction between Rrd2 and Pph22 in a yeast two-hybrid assay. Deletion of RRD2 impaired thermotolerance, altered responses to multiple stresses and antifungal agents, reduced melanin and capsule production, delayed sexual development, and inhibited titan cell formation. Mutants also displayed altered cell wall staining and reduced expression of genes involved in chitin synthesis and deacetylation. RRD2 deletion increased basal Hog1 phosphorylation, whereas PPH22 overexpression reduced it. Double-mutant analysis revealed phenotype-dependent genetic interactions between RRD2 and HOG1. Although RRD2 deletion did not significantly alter overall survival in the Drosophila infection assay, it markedly attenuated virulence in mice: all mutant-infected mice survived the 70-day observation period, and fungal burdens were reduced across multiple organs at 21 days post-infection. These findings distinguish the essential contribution of Tap42 from the broad roles of Rrd2 in stress adaptation, morphogenesis, cell surface organization, and mammalian virulence, extending the functional analysis of the cryptococcal protein phosphatase 2A regulatory network.

Crucially, to bridge the gap between static electronic structure models and real-time behavior, these static calculations were coupled with first-principles molecular dynamics based on the Car-Parrinello formulation (CP-MD). This combined static-dynamic approach provides a comprehensive view, allowing us to evaluate the structural stability and dynamic fluctuations of the interaction network under realistic thermal conditions.

title: The Emerging Crosstalk Between Nrf2 and the cGAS–STING Pathways: A Novel Axis in Neuroinflammation and Immune Regulation
summary: The pathophysiological basis of neurodegenerative and immune disorders is common and is distinguished by chronic inflammation and oxidative stress. Two major players in these pathways are the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf
content: The pathophysiological basis of neurodegenerative and immune disorders is common and is distinguished by chronic inflammation and oxidative stress. Two major players in these pathways are the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), a master regulator of antioxidant defenses, and the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, a key pathway mediating innate immune sensing of cytosolic DNA. While both axes have been studied extensively in separate settings, growing evidence suggests that Nrf2 and cGAS–STING interact in a context-dependent manner to regulate neuroinflammation and immune modulation dynamics. The objective of this review is to provide an extensive overview of the current knowledge on the crosstalk between Nrf2 and the cGAS–STING axis, with a particular focus on neurodegenerative diseases and neuroinflammatory conditions. We suggest a new theoretical framework in which the crosstalk acts as a regulatory barrier, controlling the balance between neuroprotection and neurotoxicity, and opening new therapeutic avenues. This term does not imply a defined physical or molecular barrier; rather, it describes a potential functional balance between Nrf2-mediated antioxidant and cytoprotective responses and cGAS–STING-mediated innate immune activation.

title: Inhibition of soluble epoxide hydrolase alleviates silver nanoparticle-induced pulmonary inflammatory response in a mouse model of metabolic syndrome
summary: Introduction Nanosized particles pose health risks following inhalation exposure. Epidemiological studies indicate that individuals with metabolic diseases are more susceptible to particulate air pollution, leading to increased inflammation
content: Introduction Nanosized particles pose health risks following inhalation exposure. Epidemiological studies indicate that individuals with metabolic diseases are more susceptible to particulate air pollution, leading to increased inflammation and lung injury. Previously, we found that silver nano particles (AgNPs)‐exposed metabolic syndrome (MetS) mice had elevated lung inflammation and altered inflammatory lipid mediators, linked to increased levels of soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH). sEH degrades anti‐inflammatory epoxyeicosatrienoic acids (EETs), so inhibiting it may improve EET bioavailability and help resolve pulmonary inflammation. 1‐Trifluoromethoxyphenyl‐3‐(1‐propionylpiperidin‐4‐yl) urea (TPPU), a potent sEH inhibitor, has shown efficacy in preclinical models of various chronic inflammatory diseases. Our current study hypothesizes that inhibiting sEH with TPPU can alleviate inflammation induced by AgNPs in susceptible mouse model of MetS. Methods To test this hypothesis, C57BL/6J male mice were fed either a healthy diet or a high‐fat Western diet for 14 weeks. Subsets of mice were treated with TPPU (10 mg/L) via drinking water for 1 week prior to AgNP exposure to inhibit sEH activity. After 1 week of treatment, mice were exposed to 50 µg/mouse AgNP via oropharyngeal aspiration. Endpoints of pulmonary inflammation and toxicity were evaluated 24 h following AgNP exposure. Results AgNP‐exposed MetS mice treated with DMSO showed significantly exacerbated pulmonary inflammation than healthy mice. TPPU treatment reduced this excess neutrophil infiltration, along with lower expression of pro‐ inflammatory cytokines (IL‐6, CCL2, CXCL2). DMSO‐treated AgNP‐exposed mice showed reduced IL‐10 (a resolution‐phase cytokine), which TPPU restored in both mouse models. Lipidomic analysis demonstrated AgNP exposure altered specific phospholipid classes linked to autophagy and inflammatory signaling, along with shifts in polyunsaturated fatty acid profiles, with different patterns in healthy versus MetS mice. TPPU treatment restored several of these lipids and PUFA changes along with related inflammatory markers (IL‐6, IL‐10, COX‐2, iPLA2), suggesting sEH inhibition works partly by restoring normal lipid and fatty acid signaling. Discussion Inflammatory responses to particulate exposure may be treated via modulation of lipid mediators, benefiting susceptible subpopulations.

title: Permission Theory: A Framework for Regulated Access to Latent Capability in Complex Systems
summary: Permission Theory argues that a system’s latent capability and its regulatory access to that capability are distinct dimensions of explanation. The paper develops an operational framework separating capability, admission, execution and obse
content: Permission Theory argues that a system’s latent capability and its regulatory access to that capability are distinct dimensions of explanation. The paper develops an operational framework separating capability, admission, execution and observed expression, with access distributed across initiation, continuation and establishment. It proposes a conditional relationship between system coupling, failure propagation and selective restriction, while allowing modularity and containment to expand accessible change. Evidence from developmental buffering, tooth development, cardiac renewal, cellular reprogramming and artificial-agent governance illustrates both the framework’s reach and its limits. A formal model and seven intervention-oriented research designs distinguish permission release from capability acquisition, interacting gates from simple inhibition, and activation from durable integration. This manuscript substantially revises an earlier Permission Theory manuscript hosted in the author’s OSF project (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/ANZR8). It offers a cross-domain causal framework and a testable research programme, not a new clinical dataset.

title: Hepatopulmonary syndrome and liver transplantation: Current evidence and practical considerations
summary: Hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a pulmonary vascular complication of liver disease and/or portal hypertension, defined by an arterial oxygenation defect caused by intrapulmonary vascular dilatations (IPVDs). HPS is reported in 10%–30% of
content: Hepatopulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a pulmonary vascular complication of liver disease and/or portal hypertension, defined by an arterial oxygenation defect caused by intrapulmonary vascular dilatations (IPVDs). HPS is reported in 10%–30% of patients evaluated for liver transplantation (LT), and in 21%–37% of a uniformly phenotyped prospective cohort, yet it remains underdiagnosed because most patients have only mild hypoxemia and nonspecific symptoms. Recent prospective multicenter data show that even mild HPS is associated with reduced functional capacity and with an approximately twofold higher risk of death after adjustment for liver disease severity. No gradient by the degree of hypoxemia was detected, although the analyses were not powered to exclude one, and the excess risk was observed mainly in patients who did not undergo LT. Mechanistically, HPS reflects pulmonary vasodilator excess together with dysregulated angiogenesis, and human studies have identified circulating angiopoietin-2, von Willebrand factor, and reduced bone morphogenetic protein-9 signaling as candidate mediators. Because pulse oximetry is insensitive, we favor arterial blood gas analysis combined with contrast-enhanced echocardiography in LT candidates, although guideline panels have not reached consensus on routine bubble echocardiography and the yield of universal testing is unproven. HPS and portopulmonary hypertension may coexist or develop sequentially, which requires attention both before and after LT. No medical therapy has proven effective, and LT remains the only treatment that reliably reverses HPS. Post-LT survival is good across most of the spectrum of pretransplant hypoxemia but is lower in recipients with the most severe hypoxemia, and patients with very severe hypoxemia or large shunt fractions remain at risk of severe posttransplant hypoxemia, a complication with high perioperative mortality. This review summarizes current evidence on HPS, focusing on transplant candidacy, organ allocation, living donor LT, and perioperative management, and highlights knowledge gaps relevant to Korea.

title: Multi-Pass Focused Helium Ion Beam Processing for Reducing Ga-FIB-Induced Surface Damage in Single-Crystal Diamond
summary: Single-crystal diamond has attracted considerable attention for applications in quantum information processing, nanophotonics, and microelectromechanical systems. However, focused gallium ion beam (Ga-FIB) milling introduces near-surface st
content: Single-crystal diamond has attracted considerable attention for applications in quantum information processing, nanophotonics, and microelectromechanical systems. However, focused gallium ion beam (Ga-FIB) milling introduces near-surface structural damage and gallium implantation, which may adversely affect the performance of diamond-based nanostructures. In this study, focused helium ion beam (He-HIM) post-processing was investigated as a potential approach for reducing Ga-FIB-induced surface damage in single-crystal diamond. The effects of helium ion dose, beam current, and multi-pass processing conditions on the damaged-layer thickness were systematically examined using cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (TEM), high-resolution TEM (HRTEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED). The results showed that helium ion irradiation at a dose of 5 × 10¹⁵ ions/cm² reduced the local damaged-layer thickness from 200.39 ± 1.46 nm to 192.97 ± 1.06 nm, whereas higher doses resulted in increased damaged-layer thickness. Beam-current experiments revealed that regions processed at 13–29.67 pA exhibited thicker damaged layers than the 12 pA reference regions, although no monotonic dependence on beam current was observed. Based on these findings, two six-pass He-HIM processing strategies were implemented using progressively reduced beam currents or ion doses. Compared with corresponding Ga-FIB-only reference regions, the multi-pass treatments reduced the local damaged-layer thickness by approximately 5.6% and 8.0%, respectively. These findings suggest that carefully controlled He-HIM post-processing can moderately reduce Ga-FIB-induced surface damage, while excessive irradiation may introduce additional structural defects. This study provides experimental guidance for optimizing helium ion beam post-processing of diamond nanostructures.

title: Spatio-temporal differentiation of comprehensive performance of pollution reduction, carbon mitigation, green expansion and economic growth in counties of Guangxi
summary: Coordinated development of pollution reduction, carbon mitigation, green expansion, and economic growth is an essential pathway for China to achieve a qualitative improvement in eco-environmental quality from quantitative change. Defining “
content: Coordinated development of pollution reduction, carbon mitigation, green expansion, and economic growth is an essential pathway for China to achieve a qualitative improvement in eco-environmental quality from quantitative change. Defining “comprehensive performance” as the composite measure of the four-dimensional level, this paper uses panel data (2011–2023) for 111 county-level administrative units in Guangxi. Adopting entropy-weighted TOPSIS, Dagum Gini coefficient, and other approaches, it identifies the spatiotemporal evolution pattern and driving factors of county-scale comprehensive performance. The results show that: (1) The comprehensive performance index rises by 145.10%, showing a spatial pattern of high values in northern-southern Guangxi and low values in eastern-western Guangxi, with marked imbalance across the four dimensions. (2) Global Moran’s I fluctuates upward from 0.2448 to 0.2549, with High-High (H–H) clusters centered on the Beibu Gulf Urban Agglomeration. (3) The overall Gini coefficient falls from 0.3388 to 0.3222, indicating a fluctuating reduction in regional disparities. Net inter-regional disparity dominates total disparities from 2011 to 2022, while intensity of transvariation contributes slightly more in 2023, implying intensified cross-overlap between high-value and low-value regions. (4) Under the DPSIR framework, driving factors including urbanization rate, sown area of crops, and annual mean temperature exert significantly spatially differentiated effects on the comprehensive performance index. Finally, zonally differentiated policy recommendations are proposed to support green-low-carbon transition and coordinated governance for Guangxi’s counties during the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

title: Hypoxia‑induced uncoupling of membrane contact sites in male infertility: From organelle stress to network failure (Review)
summary: Hypoxia represents a well‑established pathological and environmental driver of male fertility decline. However, current paradigms centered on oxidative stress only partially explain the progressive deterioration of the testicular microenvir
content: Hypoxia represents a well‑established pathological and environmental driver of male fertility decline. However, current paradigms centered on oxidative stress only partially explain the progressive deterioration of the testicular microenvironment. Through the integration of multidisciplinary evidence, a pathological framework centered on the uncoupling of organelle membrane contact sites (MCSs) is proposed. We hypothesize that hypoxia impairs tethering proteins, initiating two concurrent events: Uncoupling of mitochondria‑associated endoplasmic reticulum membranes within Leydig cells, which disrupts cholesterol trafficking and impairs steroidogenesis, and uncoupling of peroxisome‑mitochondria contact sites within Sertoli cells, which interrupts lipid metabolic coupling and induces lipotoxic injury. This bimodal cellular insult synergistically drives the progressive functional collapse of the testicular microenvironment through a ‘Leydig‑Sertoli‑germ cell’ cascade. Considering the unique properties of the testis, temperature sensitivity and immune privilege, the scope and rationale for extrapolating this mechanism is defined and potential interventional strategies targeting MCSs are proposed. Accordingly, the present review provides a theoretical basis for overcoming the limitations of conventional antioxidant therapies. Notably, this framework relies on theoretical inference from cross‑tissue evidence and lacks direct empirical validation. However, it provides a novel and testable subcellular perspective for future research.

title: Diagnostic-Anchored Neural State-Space Modeling of Electrochemical Degradation and Load-Dependent Voltage Loss in Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
summary: Understanding proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) durability requires connecting electrochemical degradation to voltage loss under different operating loads. We develop a diagnostic-anchored neural state-space model that represents c
content: Understanding proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) durability requires connecting electrochemical degradation to voltage loss under different operating loads. We develop a diagnostic-anchored neural state-space model that represents catalyst/interface, protonic/ionic, ohmic, and oxygen-transport responses through four evolving state coordinates. Material descriptors, accelerated-stress conditions, and beginning-of-test characterization condition state evolution. Diagnostic-specific observation masks enable learning from measurements acquired at different aging stages, while a load-structured decoder predicts voltage loss at five current densities. Using 37 curated aging trajectories, repeated cell-grouped fivefold cross-validation yielded a mean voltage-loss MAE of 12.34 mV across five loads and R2 = 0.901 at 1.0 A cm-2. The model reconstructed electrochemically active surface area loss with R2 = 0.809. Replacing the structured decoder increased mean voltage-loss MAE to 15.50 mV. Across 13 nominally matched comparisons, raising the upper potential limit from 0.95 to 1.15 V was associated with median increases of 0.294 in active-area-loss fraction and 0.159 V in voltage loss at 1.0 A cm-2. This framework unifies electrochemical diagnostic reconstruction and load-dependent performance prediction for comparative cathode durability assessment within the investigated accelerated-stress conditions.

title: Multi-omics and biochemical analyses reveal nonlinear growth and redox responses of Morchella sextelata mycelia to potassium carbonate
summary: Mineral nutrient availability influences substrate colonization and biomass accumulation by morel mycelia, but the dose-dependent effects of exogenous K₂CO₃ on mycelial growth and the associated molecular responses remain poorly understood.
content: Mineral nutrient availability influences substrate colonization and biomass accumulation by morel mycelia, but the dose-dependent effects of exogenous K₂CO₃ on mycelial growth and the associated molecular responses remain poorly understood. In this study, Morchella sextelata mycelia were exposed to low, medium, and high doses of K₂CO₃, together with an untreated control. Mycelial radial growth and biomass accumulation were assessed together with transcriptomic, proteomic, and targeted biochemical analyses. Both low- and medium-dose treatments promoted mycelial growth. Relative to the control, the medium-dose treatment increased mycelial growth rate and dry weight by 43.6% and 23.2%, respectively, whereas the high-dose treatment reduced these parameters by 23.9% and 70.4%, respectively, demonstrating a pronounced nonlinear dose response to K₂CO₃. Under the respective screening criteria, HK yielded the largest DEG and candidate DEP sets, with changes involving substrate transport, membrane lipid metabolism, peroxisomal processes, and glutathione metabolism. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a gene module that was significantly and positively correlated with both mycelial growth rate and dry weight and was primarily associated with carbohydrate metabolism, the cell cycle, and intracellular turnover processes. Integrative transcriptomic and proteomic analysis further associated the treatment responses with pentose and glucuronate interconversions, the pentose phosphate pathway, nucleotide precursor formation, and ribosome-related processes. Under the high-dose treatment, the responses of several carbon metabolic nodes and ribosome-related components did not parallel the observed changes in mycelial growth. Biochemical assays showed that the NADPH/NADP + ratio was highest and ROS-associated DCF fluorescence and MDA content were lowest under the medium-dose treatment, whereas the high-dose treatment showed the opposite pattern despite having the highest G6PDH activity. These findings characterize concentration-dependent responses of morel vegetative mycelia to K₂CO₃ and identify candidate molecular processes for further investigation under controlled culture conditions.

title: 3D-printed electrochemical platforms for early diagnosis of cancer and therapy monitoring
summary: Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, making early diagnosis and continuous monitoring of disease progression and treatment response essential. Therapy monitoring is essential for evaluating treatment efficacy and guiding decis
content: Cancer remains a leading cause of death worldwide, making early diagnosis and continuous monitoring of disease progression and treatment response essential. Therapy monitoring is essential for evaluating treatment efficacy and guiding decisions. Liquid biopsy combined with electrochemical biosensors enables minimally invasive biomarker detection for decentralized healthcare. In this context, 3D printing provides versatile manufacturing capabilities for developing electrochemical platforms with tailored architectures and functionalities. This review examines the evolution of 3D-printed electrochemical platforms, with particular emphasis on fused deposition modeling and alternative additive manufacturing techniques, covering fabrication strategies, material selection, post-processing approaches and electrode architectures ranging from individual electrodes to integrated sample-to-answer systems. Applications involving clinically relevant cancer biomarkers, including proteins, microRNAs and extracellular vesicles, are discussed alongside cellular models and emerging opportunities for therapy monitoring, while key challenges and future perspectives highlight the potential of sustainable, autonomous and clinically translatable 3D-printed electrochemical platforms for cancer diagnosis and monitoring.

title: A System Solution for Selection and Optimization of Concrete Compositions at the Design Stage Using a Digital Model and a Combined Machine Learning Model
summary: Statement of the problem. This work aims to address the technological gap between the growing requirements for the design of resource-efficient and environmentally friendly concrete and the limitations of traditional experimental laboratory
content: Statement of the problem. This work aims to address the technological gap between the growing requirements for the design of resource-efficient and environmentally friendly concrete and the limitations of traditional experimental laboratory methods. The goal is to create a digital product model capable of not only predicting properties but also solving multifactor optimization problems, taking into account technological, strength, and economic constraints, including cost minimization. Results. A digital assistant for concrete composition selection has been developed. It is based on an intelligent system that combines several mathematical approaches to provide the most accurate and understandable strength prediction. The model demonstrated high prediction accuracy: the coefficient of determination R² = 0.913, and the mean absolute error MAE = 3.32 MPa. To explain the predictions, a factor influence analysis was used, identifying the key influencing factors. Conclusions. The model serves as an effective tool for transitioning from traditional composition selection to digital parametric design. This ensures significant cost reductions (e. g., cement consumption) and development time by minimizing full-scale testing. The proposed solution provides a practical basis for creating resource-efficient and environmentally friendly concrete mixtures.

title: Anatomical, physiological, and metabolic trait adjustments in tea leaves under different intercropping systems: implications for ecological tea garden management
summary: Introduction Intercropping is widely used to promote sustainable tea cultivation, but how different companion-tree configurations are associated with tea leaf functional traits remains insufficiently understood. This study compared leaf tra
content: Introduction Intercropping is widely used to promote sustainable tea cultivation, but how different companion-tree configurations are associated with tea leaf functional traits remains insufficiently understood. This study compared leaf trait responses across four tea-based intercropping systems. Methods A replicated field experiment was conducted in a tea plantation in Zhejiang, China, comparing tea monoculture (CK), tea–persimmon (T+P), tea–pecan (T+H), and tea–persimmon–pecan (T+P+H), with three replicate plots per treatment. Leaf anatomical traits, stomatal density and dimensions, soluble protein, soluble sugars, starch, antioxidant-related indicators, and photosynthetic pigments were measured. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to summarize multivariate trait variation. Results Intercropping generally reduced epidermal and mesophyll thickness. Relative to CK, T+P had 50.2% lower stomatal density but 32.8% longer and 35.7% wider stomata. It was also associated with 15.1%, 30.1%, and 17.4% higher soluble protein, soluble sugar, and starch concentrations, respectively, 79.6% higher total chlorophyll, and 12.1% lower malondialdehyde (MDA). In contrast, T+P+H showed the greatest mesophyll thinning and the highest MDA concentration. The first two PCA axes explained 55.77% of total trait variation and indicated clear multivariate differentiation between T+P and CK. Discussion These findings indicate that tea-based intercropping configurations are associated with coordinated changes in leaf anatomy, stomatal morphology, metabolism, oxidative status, and pigment profiles. Under the conditions examined, T+P showed the most balanced integrated leaf-trait profile, suggesting its potential for ecological tea-garden management. However, light environment, gas exchange, resource competition, yield, and processed-tea sensory quality were not directly measured, and companion-tree identity was confounded with planting geometry and plot location. The observed responses should therefore be interpreted at the configuration level and validated through multi-season, multi-site studies before broader management recommendations are made.

title: How Does implicit debt shape local governments’ low-carbon governance? A public value conflict perspective
summary: Against the backdrop of accelerating green development and low-carbon transition, governments worldwide face challenges balancing economic development and low-carbon governance. Particularly when faced with fiscal pressure and public debt a
content: Against the backdrop of accelerating green development and low-carbon transition, governments worldwide face challenges balancing economic development and low-carbon governance. Particularly when faced with fiscal pressure and public debt accumulation, local governments often confront public value dilemmas. This study examines how implicit debt affects local governments’ low-carbon governance efficiency via public value conflict, and further analyzes the effect of local leadership turnover frequency on this mechanism. Results show that implicit debt intensifies public value conflict in local low-carbon governance, thereby inhibiting low-carbon governance efficiency. Moreover, a higher frequency of local leadership turnover further strengthens this mechanism.
