content: Anaerobic corrections to RothC remain insufficiently tested across paddy regions. Standard and modified RothC were compared using paired 1980s–2010s soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks at 104 Chinese sites. Published decomposition multipliers of 0.2 in assigned flooded months and 0.6 otherwise were applied without refitting. Simulated and observed stocks were standardized to 0–20 cm, and external precipitation and reference evapotranspiration were re-extracted from matched-period monthly climate products. Mean inferred carbon inputs were 4.67 and 1.75 t C ha ⁻1 yr ⁻1 . In a leakage-free benchmark of 1,469 external cropland profiles, modification reduced pooled root mean square error from 24.37 to 22.80 t C ha ⁻1 (6.4%) and mean bias from +8.93 to +7.33 t C ha ⁻1 . Both pooled R 2 values remained negative, and RMSE increased in Northeast China. Literature budgets contextualize inferred inputs without validating site-level additions. The correction strongly changes model-equivalent input requirements but provides only modest aggregate stock improvement; regional application requires independent carbon budgets, water-management records, and repeated SOC observations.

title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
summary: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors p
content: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO 2 /H 2 O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. This work offers a route toward self-correcting scientific databases and toward database curation driven by large language models.

title: Governed Synchronization of Adaptive Digital Twins for Industrial Biomanufacturing: Application to Penicillin Fermentation
summary: Digital twins are increasingly used in biomanufacturing to support real-time monitoring and decision-making. However, maintaining long-term synchronization between the digital twin and the physical twin remains a significant challenge becau
content: Digital twins are increasingly used in biomanufacturing to support real-time monitoring and decision-making. However, maintaining long-term synchronization between the digital twin and the physical twin remains a significant challenge because biological processes continuously evolve due to batch-to-batch variability, process drift, and measurement uncertainty. Existing approaches rely on repeated model retraining or high-dimensional adaptive models, increasing computational complexity and reducing interpretability and industrial deployability. This work proposes a Governed Adaptive Digital Twin (GADT) framework for industrial penicillin fermentation that relies on a validated symbolic process model synchronized through a low-dimensional governed adaptation layer. The structural model is developed offline using multi-gene genetic programming (MGGP), while online synchronization is achieved by adaptively updating only two interpretable parameters, gain and bias, using normalized prediction error. The adaptation process incorporates scheduling, innovation filtering, guardrail constraints, parameter bounding, and batch lifecycle management to ensure robust industrial operation. The proposed framework was evaluated using pseudo-online streaming data generated from 90 simulated fed-batch fermentation campaigns based on the industrial-scale IndPenSim benchmark, labelled as representing approximately three years of simulated production campaigns in the IndPenSim benchmark. Compared with a conventional digital twin, the proposed GADT achieved higher prediction accuracy and trajectory-level synchronization while effectively compensating for long-term process drift without recursive model correction or structural model retraining. Ablation studies further demonstrate that the proposed governance mechanisms are essential for stable and physically consistent adaptation. The results demonstrate that governed synchronization, rather than continuous structural model evolution, enables sustained digital twin performance and provides an interpretable, computationally, industrially deployable architecture for adaptive digital twins in biomanufacturing.

title: Editorial: Utilizing well-instrumented critical zone sites: infrastructure, data integration, and advancements in earth system research
summary: Critical Zone (CZ) science brings together disciplines such as hydrology, soil science, geochemistry, ecology, and earth-surface processes to understand Earth's shallow skin as an interconnected system. By examining interactions among water
content: Critical Zone (CZ) science brings together disciplines such as hydrology, soil science, geochemistry, ecology, and earth-surface processes to understand Earth's shallow skin as an interconnected system. By examining interactions among water, rocks, soils, the atmosphere, and living organisms, CZ science research advances our understanding of the processes that govern ecosystem functioning and inform applications ranging from water-resource management to sustainable agriculture and carbon cycling (Brantley et al., 2007;Banwart et al., 2013;Stolze et al., 2024). Addressing these complex interactions requires observations that capture the spatial heterogeneity and temporal dynamics of CZ processes across a range of scales (Kumar et al., 2023). Open-source monitoring infrastructure, innovative sensing, and low-cost instrumentation can expand access to environmental data and reveal dynamics and subsurface heterogeneity that might otherwise remain unresolved. This Research Topic brings together five contributions that illustrate these complementary advances, spanning environmental monitoring networks, soil moisture and CO₂ flux measurements, soil carbon dynamics, and subsurface flow pathways. Below, we synthesize these contributions, highlighting their methodological innovations and the scientific insights they offer.Of the five publications in this Research Topic, three focus on how open-source infrastructure, innovative sensing techniques, and low-cost instrumentation can improve the spatial and temporal resolution of CZ observations while expanding access to environmental data. Dessimond et al. present the Environmental Sensing and Data Network (ESDN), a multisite environmental monitoring infrastructure in eastern North Carolina that integrates legacy and modern sensors using LoRaWAN telemetry, a self-hosted ThingsBoard Internet of Things (IoT) platform, and cloud-based data archiving. Since its deployment in mid-2024, the network has expanded to 110 sensors and 14 communications gateways across diverse settings, including urban and suburban neighborhoods, agricultural lands, forests, and coastal wetlands, supporting applications ranging from flood and groundwater monitoring to soil moisture, nutrient cycling, and community science. By supporting diverse sensors while reducing reliance on proprietary platforms, recurring telemetry fees, and vendor-specific systems, the ESDN offers a flexible alternative to conventional commercial monitoring systems. Such networks have the potential to lower technical and financial barriers to environmental monitoring and broaden participation among educators, community organizations, and local stakeholders.Susanto et al. developed a hybrid inversion approach that combines signal processing and numerical modeling to estimate soil moisture from passively heated fiber-optic distributed temperature sensing (FO-DTS). After testing the approach with synthetic data generated using HYDRUS-1D, they applied it to a 60-m hills

title: Mangrove Ecosystem Quality Index: Combining Field-Based Vegetation Structure and Water Quality to Assess Mangrove Ecosystem Condition in Segara Anakan, Cilacap, Indonesia
summary: Comprehensive mangrove health assessments require evaluating both historical vegetation structure and dynamic water quality, yet these domains are rarely integrated into a single field-based index. This study develops the Mangrove Ecosystem
content: Comprehensive mangrove health assessments require evaluating both historical vegetation structure and dynamic water quality, yet these domains are rarely integrated into a single field-based index. This study develops the Mangrove Ecosystem Quality Index (MEQI) to address this gap, applying it to 45 sampling points in the Segara Anakan lagoon, Indonesia. The MEQI combines a Vegetation Structure Index (ISV) and a Water Quality Index (IWQ), each comprising six parameters weighted empirically through principal component analysis (PCA). Point-level scores were mapped utilizing inverse distance weighting on a hexagonal grid. Results indicate an average MEQI of 51.76, with 2 stations classified as Very Good, 26 as Good, 15 as Moderate, and 2 as Poor. Spatially, ecosystem health was strongest in the north-central and western sectors but degraded along the eastern arm due to anthropogenic loads. Notably, evaluating the sub-indices independently revealed a statistically significant divergence: vegetation structure (average ISV 40.77) was substantially more degraded than water quality (average IWQ 62.75). Relying solely on the composite MEQI risks a masking effect, where functional aquatic conditions obscure historically degraded vegetation. The PCA weights highlighted carbon stock, biomass, pH, and dissolved oxygen as primary ecosystem drivers. The MEQI serves as a practical, field-deployable tool that robustly complements remote-sensing approaches like the Mangrove Ecosystem Health Index (MEHI). For effective conservation, managers must utilize such integrated indices to periodically monitor the disparate recovery timelines of structural and aquatic mangrove dimensions.

title: An Injectable Hydrogel With Dynamic Anchoring of Salvianolic Acid B Enables Sustained Co‐Delivery With Bevacizumab for Retinal Trifunctional Recovery in Diabetic Retinopathy
summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is driven by oxidative stress, pathological angiogenesis, and retinal neurodegeneration, yet current anti‑VEGF therapies fail to address upstream oxidative damage or neuronal injury and require frequent injections.
content: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is driven by oxidative stress, pathological angiogenesis, and retinal neurodegeneration, yet current anti‑VEGF therapies fail to address upstream oxidative damage or neuronal injury and require frequent injections. Moreover, the distinct pharmacokinetic behaviors of small molecules and biologics hinder their synchronized delivery. Herein, an injectable hydrogel exploiting salvianolic acid B (SaB) as a dynamic molecular anchor is developed for sustained co‑delivery with bevacizumab (Bev). Through multivalent dynamic boronate ester interactions, SaB functions simultaneously as a therapeutic cargo and a dynamic network participant, restricting its rapid diffusion and reducing the release-rate mismatch with Bev to enable sustained co-delivery for over 6 weeks. Sustained SaB scavenges reactive oxygen species, activates Nrf2/HO‑1 signaling and suppresses the ROS/MAPK/HIF-1α/VEGF cascade, thereby reduces endogenous VEGF production, whereas Bev continuously neutralizes extracellular VEGF. By integrating upstream oxidative stress regulation with downstream angiogenic inhibition, this strategy achieves trifunctional retinal recovery characterized by oxidative stress alleviation, pathological angiogenesis suppression, and retinal neuroprotection. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats, a single intravitreal injection effectively suppresses pathological angiogenesis, reduces oxidative damage, preserves retinal structure and function, and exhibits excellent ocular biocompatibility. This SaB-enabled dynamic anchoring hydrogel provides a promising long-acting co-delivery strategy for multifactorial DR therapy.

title: Rhizosphere Resource–Niche Coupling Mediates A Respiratory Trade‐Off in Microbial Carbon Use Under Contrasting Agricultural Management
summary: The rhizosphere constitutes a critical hotspot for terrestrial carbon transformation, yet the mechanistic linkage between contrasting agricultural management and coordinated shifts in rhizosphere resources, microbial niches, and carbon-use
content: The rhizosphere constitutes a critical hotspot for terrestrial carbon transformation, yet the mechanistic linkage between contrasting agricultural management and coordinated shifts in rhizosphere resources, microbial niches, and carbon-use strategies remains poorly resolved. Here, we established a unified resource-niche coupling framework and validated it using a seven-year field experiment with crop rotations of contrasting diversity and two fertilization regimes (mineral vs. manure). We quantified rhizosphere vs. bulk soil effects across three resource axes: resource quantity, microbial stoichiometric demand, and enzyme-based carbon-processing allocation. Fertilization dominated the stoichiometric-demand axis, enriching labile metabolites (amino acids, peptides, lipids), accelerating bacterial community turnover, and driving high respiration investment per unit microbial biomass alongside carbohydrate-specialized carbon use. By contrast, diversified crop rotation affected resource quantity and carbon-processing strategy axes, accumulating polyphenolic and glycosylated secondary metabolites, expanding fungal niche breadth, and homogenizing substrate utilization across carbon substrates. We identified a community-level trade-off between respiratory intensity and substrate-use evenness associated with rhizosphere resource-niche coupling: mineral fertilization favored respiration-intensive carbon use, whereas crop diversification promoted more balanced substrate utilization. This unifying mechanistic framework predicts rhizosphere carbon partitioning under agricultural management and offers actionable guidance for climate-smart farming to strengthen long-term soil carbon retention.

title: Catalytically Active Species and Sites in CO 2 Hydrogenation Identified by Modulation Excitation Spectroscopy
summary: Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO 2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design
content: Thermocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation has developed into an important sustainable route toward valuable fuels and chemicals, thereby reducing the greenhouse gas CO 2 and supporting the energy transition. For a rational design of more efficient, selective, and stable catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation, detailed knowledge of the reaction mechanism, including key intermediates and active sites is required. Modulation excitation spectroscopy (MES) has emerged as a powerful tool to discriminate between catalytically active and (nonparticipating) spectator species and to identify active sites, and has been shown to provide important new mechanistic findings not accessible by steady‐state approaches, contributing to the very intense debate on CO 2 hydrogenation mechanisms. Despite its broad applicability, the MES method is still rarely used in catalysis research and has contributed to the mechanism of CO 2 hydrogenation mainly by its combination with infrared spectroscopy. In this Minireview, the potential of MES for providing mechanistic insight on catalytic CO 2 hydrogenation will be illustrated based on the current literature, followed by an outline of potential methodical extensions. Future prospects for the application of MES to mechanistic studies on CO 2 activation beyond thermal catalysis, including photo‐ and electrocatalysis, as well as other areas of research will be discussed.

title: Thermal Dynamics as a Non‐Invasive Indicator for Cycle Life Prediction of LiFePO 4 /Graphite Batteries Under Fast‐Charging
summary: Resistance‐induced overpotential and the associated heat generation are critical factors affecting cycle life of lithium‐ion batteries under fast‐charging conditions. In this study, we propose a temperature‐based prognostic approach for the
content: Resistance‐induced overpotential and the associated heat generation are critical factors affecting cycle life of lithium‐ion batteries under fast‐charging conditions. In this study, we propose a temperature‐based prognostic approach for the early prediction of battery cycle life, focusing on LiFePO 4 /graphite cells cycled under a fixed family of multistep fast‐charging protocols at 30°C. The charging process was segmented into four state‐of‐charge (SoC)‐resolved constant‐current regions (CC1–CC4). Voltage and temperature analyses revealed that the initial SoC region (CC1) is particularly sensitive to overpotential development, where a high current density is associated with a premature transition to the constant‐voltage (CV) mode and intensified heat generation. At advanced stages of cycling, temperature behavior exhibited correlations with cycle life consistent with voltage responses. Based on these observations, temperature evolution during the early cycles (third to 10th) was employed to construct a cycle life prediction model. Among the CC‐resolved regions, temperature‐related features from CC1 and CC4 showed higher predictive relevance than those from CC2 and CC3. These results suggest that non‐invasively measured surface temperature can serve as a physically meaningful indicator for early‐stage cycle life prognosis under the studied fast‐charging conditions. The proposed framework provides an interpretable approach for battery health monitoring and fast‐charging protocol design.

title: Steric Effect of Branch Grafting Enables Highly Soluble and Stable Phenazines in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
summary: Phenazine-based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one-step two-electron redox reaction. However, the highly co
content: Phenazine-based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one-step two-electron redox reaction. However, the highly conjugated structure of phenazine reduces molecular polarity and limits the solubility in electrolytes. Herein, we introduced a branched chain to achieve a highly stable and soluble phenazine derivative for AOFBs. The branched structure can effectively suppress the π-π interaction of the phenazine conjugation system but also inhibit the hydrolysis of the ether bond by steric hindrance, which significantly enhances the structural stability. The AOFB using a 1.0 mol/L electrolyte of 2,2'-(phenazine-2,3-diylbis(oxy))dipropionic acid exhibited a high discharge capacity of 45.5 Ah/L and a low-capacity decay rate of 0.00017% per cycle, with stable operation for more than 42 days (1200 cycles). Furthermore, a pilot-scale stack demonstrated excellent cycling stability, with negligible capacity degradation after 400 cycles. The outstanding AOFB performance suggests its promise for large-scale energy storage applications.

title: Optimizing Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Performance of MoSe₂ through Strategic Transition-Metal Doping: A Density Functional Theory Analysis
summary: Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising candidates for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) because of their high specific surface areas and mechanical flexibilities. However, the catalytic activities
content: Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising candidates for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) because of their high specific surface areas and mechanical flexibilities. However, the catalytic activities of pristine TMDs are limited by the chemical inertness of their basal planes. In this study, spin-polarized density functional theory calculations are performed to investigate the effects of 3d- and 4d-transition-metal doping on the HER performance of the MoSe2 basal plane. Transition-metal doping in MoSe2 confirms the thermodynamic stability of the resulting systems; specifically, doping with early transition metals offers the highest lattice stability, whereas doping with late transition metals induces greater electronic perturbations. The adsorption energetics reveal that pristine MoSe2 provides the weakest binding energy toward H (1GH∗ = 1.40 eV), whereas Zn doping gives the strongest binding energy (1GH∗ = −0.40 eV). Moreover, doping of Cd and Ag in the nearest-neighbor configuration drastically reduces the Gibbs free energy of H adsorption to near-optimal values of – 0.02 and –0.16 eV, respectively. Finally, electronic structure analysis and d-band center scaling indicate that these dopants trigger a semiconductor-to-metal transition and optimize the orbital hybridization between the metal d-states and H s-orbitals. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the development of high-performance, earth-abundant electrocatalysts for sustainable, green H2 production.

title: Are fungi and their enzymes effective for biodegradable microplastics in wastewater? Linking particle retention to polymer-carbon conversion
summary: Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) can persist through wastewater treatment and be transferred from water to sludge without substantial polymer degradation, posing potential risks to aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Fungi can colonize bi
content: Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) can persist through wastewater treatment and be transferred from water to sludge without substantial polymer degradation, posing potential risks to aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Fungi can colonize biodegradable polyester particles and produce extracellular enzymes capable of depolymerization, but their effectiveness in continuous municipal wastewater treatment remains uncertain. This critical review examines the relationships among particle retention, fungal enzyme activity, polymer hydrolysis, and the fate of released carbon. We distinguish physical capture from depolymerization, assimilation, and mineralization, drawing on evidence from fungal cultures, isolated enzymes, and mixed microbial systems. Three potential treatment configurations are evaluated: recoverable fungal pellets, attached fungal growth, and enzymatic hydrolysis of concentrated BMP fractions. Their feasibility depends on sustained particle–enzyme contact, catalytic activity under non-sterile conditions, and downstream utilization or recovery of hydrolysis products. We propose evaluation criteria incorporating polymer-specific inventories across effluent, sludge, and retained solids; isotope-based carbon tracing; matched experimental controls; and energy and material accounting. This framework identifies the evidence needed to determine whether fungal interventions achieve genuine reductions in residual polymer discharge rather than merely transferring biodegradable microplastics between environmental compartments.

title: Oxygen Vacancies as a Reaction Switch for Cocatalysts‐Free CO 2 Photoreduction on CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 Hybrid Without Sacrificial Agent
summary: Photocatalysis offers an energy‐efficient and renewable approach of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) conversion into sustainable fuels and chemicals. However, the cutting‐edge photocatalysts mostly rely on sacrificial electron donors, whereas noble‐m
content: Photocatalysis offers an energy‐efficient and renewable approach of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) conversion into sustainable fuels and chemicals. However, the cutting‐edge photocatalysts mostly rely on sacrificial electron donors, whereas noble‐metal cocatalysts hinder the progress of this field to real‐world applications. Developing photocatalysts that could work in the absence of sacrificial agents as well as noble‐metal cocatalysts is highly desirable, but remains challenging. As such, this work demonstrates a Z‐scheme photocatalyst having abundant oxygen vacancies (OVs) in a flower‐shaped CeO 2 /Manganese oxide (Mn 3 O 4 ) hybrid to facilitate the CO 2 photoreduction via exposure to visible light. The CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 hybrid with OVs promotes visible light absorption and charge carrier separation. The optimized 9CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 catalyst yields 12 μmol h −1 of CO and 2.2 μmol h −1 of CH 4 without any noble‐metal catalysts or sacrificial agents, which is ∼13 times greater than that of pristine Mn 3 O 4 . The 9CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 catalyst exhibits robust structural stability with fully regenerable activity. While per‐hour yield declines due to intermediate adsorption, mild thermal treatment at 425 K completely restores catalytic performance over multiple cycles. The optimized photocatalytic efficiency of 9CeO 2 /Mn 3 O 4 is primarily due to its expanded range of light‐absorption capacity and effective charge carrier retention, as demonstrated by ultraviolet–visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, photoluminescence analysis, transient photocurrent spectra, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Therefore, this discovery has the potential to facilitate the fabrication of photocatalysts for CO 2 reduction to biofuels and synthetic compounds.

title: Exploiting the Potential of Large Language Models in NLP : A Survey of Methods and Applications
source: Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have proven to be a revolutionary concept in the field of natural language processing (NLP). The development of transformer‐based models and the advances in related directions, such as large‐scale pre‐training,
content: Large language models (LLMs) have proven to be a revolutionary concept in the field of natural language processing (NLP). The development of transformer‐based models and the advances in related directions, such as large‐scale pre‐training, instruction tuning, preference optimization, retrieval augmentation, and parameter‐efficient adaptation, have led to the creation of extremely capable and versatile language models. At the same time, the rapid growth of the LLM makes it hard to track and understand the relationships between different models, their training procedures, adaptation methods, applications, and evaluation techniques. This survey presents a unified taxonomy of LLMs organized around three core dimensions: architectural paradigms, training methodology, and fine‐tuning and adaptation techniques. In addition, the survey examines LLM capabilities across major NLP tasks and analyzes the evaluation techniques used to assess their performance, robustness, and generalization. This distinction between core taxonomy dimensions and complementary analytical dimensions provides a structured perspective on the development, adaptation, application, and evaluation of LLMs. For each category, the paper analyzes the current trends, advantages, and limitations and provides a taxonomy of the main approaches and directions. Moreover, this paper also discusses the key limitations of the state‐of‐the‐art LLMs. Altogether, the study provides a holistic view of the LLM that can help understand the research directions in the LLM field.

title: Astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D regulates hippocampal memory through extracellular matrix remodeling
summary: Astrocytes contribute to hippocampal cognitive functions, but how astrocyte-derived factors regulate memory formation remains unclear. Here, we identify astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D (CtsD) as a regulator of hippocampal learning and memory
content: Astrocytes contribute to hippocampal cognitive functions, but how astrocyte-derived factors regulate memory formation remains unclear. Here, we identify astrocyte-secreted Cathepsin D (CtsD) as a regulator of hippocampal learning and memory. Proteomic profiling of hippocampal astrocytes upon learning identified candidates predicted to be secreted, among which we focused on CtsD, whose extracellular brain functions are unknown. Neutralizing extracellular CtsD or astrocyte-selective CtsD knockdown (aCtsD-KD) impaired hippocampal long term potentiation (LTP) and memory acquisition, suggesting an extracellular role for astrocytic CtsD. In aCtsD-KD mice, these deficits were accompanied by alterations in excitatory transmission and synaptic structures. aCtsD-KD also caused abnormal extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, and its partial digestion by chondroitinase ABC rescued the memory deficit, indicating that astrocytic CtsD-dependent ECM degradation contributes to hippocampal memory. Together, our findings suggest a CtsD-dependent astrocyte-matrix-synapse axis regulating hippocampal memory.

title: FlexibleCommunity: An Incentive-Based Dynamic Flexibility Management Simulator
summary: This paper introduces FlexibleCommunity, an incentive-based energy management simulator for investigating demand-response strategies of communities and generating high-resolution datasets capturing both explicit and implicit participation.
content: This paper introduces FlexibleCommunity, an incentive-based energy management simulator for investigating demand-response strategies of communities and generating high-resolution datasets capturing both explicit and implicit participation. The simulator can be configured to represent an arbitrary number of buildings, enabling scalable modeling of communities with heterogeneous dwellings equipped with price-responsive heating systems of varying types and capacities. It also integrates photovoltaic (PV) systems, electric vehicles (EVs), and battery storage to represent multiple flexibility mechanisms. FlexibleCommunity includes stochastic occupant behavior to improve realism and capture uncertainty in energy use patterns. The generated datasets contain time-series data on energy consumption, price signals, weather conditions, and solar irradiance, supporting applications such as load forecasting and flexibility assessment. To improve accessibility, it includes a graphical user interface (GUI) for configuration, visualization, and dataset generation.

title: Developing Actual Occupancy Profiles for Mosques
summary: Building occupancy profiles are essential for optimizing energy performance, yet standardized data for mosques remains scarce despite their unique, intermittent usage patterns. This study addresses this gap by evaluating a cost-effective, r
content: Building occupancy profiles are essential for optimizing energy performance, yet standardized data for mosques remains scarce despite their unique, intermittent usage patterns. This study addresses this gap by evaluating a cost-effective, real-time occupancy monitoring system using Raspberry Pi and computer vision. By capturing headcount data at 30-second intervals, the system demonstrated high responsiveness in tracking complex dynamics within a mosque environment. The analysis reveals that weekend attendance generally exceeds weekday levels, with weekdays showing sharper post-prayer declines due to professional and academic obligations. A primary divergence occurs during the Friday Jummah congregation, which reached a peak of 110 occupants, saturating the hall’s capacity. This surge exhibited a wider temporal footprint than standard prayers due to the mandatory pre-prayer sermon (Khutbah). Quantitative results show that weekday occupancy peaked at 60 during the Maghrib prayer, while weekend peaks reached 75. On average, worshippers arrived 5 minutes before the prayer and departed 20 minutes after, resulting in a total stay of 25 minutes. These findings validate the system’s ability to provide high-resolution, empirical data, offering a foundation for demand-controlled environmental management and more energy-efficient operational strategies in religious facilities.

title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no
content: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

title: Effect of spring maize hybrids on ruminal degradation kinetics of dry matter, fiber and protein in silages
summary: Increasing the role of home-grown forages in animal feeds is of utmost importance for a more appropriate recycling and re-utilization of nutrients, and to reduce dependency on imported concentrated ingredient and provide long-term sustainab
content: Increasing the role of home-grown forages in animal feeds is of utmost importance for a more appropriate recycling and re-utilization of nutrients, and to reduce dependency on imported concentrated ingredient and provide long-term sustainability to dairy production systems.However, with agricultural land shrinking and food sector competition increasing, efficient use of available land and feed resources is critical.In this regard, silage production from whole crop maize and optimizing its utilization in animal ration can play a key role by ensuring continuous and uniform supply of good quality forage throughout the year and optimizing animal productivity.In this context, current research was designed to investigate the rumen fermentation kinetics of dry matter (DM) and nutrients of maize silages produced from different genotypes of spring maize.Ten maize genotypes were cultivated for silage production in sixty plots within two fields with three replicates per field, using Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD), at the research fields of Livestock Research and Development Station Surezai Peshawar.The maize were grown under uniform growing condition using standard agronomic practices.Crop growth was monitored, and samples were taken from a 1 m long strip of two adjacent rows of each plot when the DM content reached 335 g/kg.The samples were chopped into small (1-1.5 cm) particles and fermented in 1.5 L silos.The silos were packed layer by layer and the compacted and closed air tightly.After 60 days silos were opened and subsamples were collected for in situ studies.The samples were air-dried in oven, ground (2 mm particle size) and stored for in situ trial.Samples (5 g) of each silage were incubated in the rumen of a cannulated cow for 0, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24, and 36 hours to determine in situ fermentation kinetics.The residues and samples were analysed for DM, crude protein (CP), and neutral detergent fibre (NDF).The degradation rate of DM (Kdm) of maize genotypes varied from 1.99% in (P-3025W) to 5.72% (CS200).The effective rumen degradable DM (EDDM) varied from 44.05% in (P-30k08) to 36.22% in (CS200).The kd of CP (Kdcp) of maize hybrids ranged from 2.50% in (M-Garanan) to 8.83% (Azam).The effective rumen degradable CP (EDcp) ranged from 72.32% in P-2Y10 to 36.35% in 3025W.The kd-NDF of maize genotypes ranged from 1.56% (P-3025W) to 7.32% (M-Gorilla).The effective rumen degradable NDF (EDNDF) fraction varied from 36.07%(P-3025W) to 14.12% (P-2Y10).The results of this study revealed that the degradation of DM, CP, and NDF of maize silage in the rumen differed depending on maize cultivars, indicating that there is a higher potential for utilising this knowledge in ration design to improve livestock productivity.

title: Conscious coins: an interpretive structural approach to understanding behavioral drivers of green cryptocurrency investment
summary: Purpose This study systematically aims to explore and structures the key enablers driving green cryptocurrencies adoption. Design/methodology/approach The study uses interpretive structural modelling approach to delve into the complex inter
content: Purpose This study systematically aims to explore and structures the key enablers driving green cryptocurrencies adoption. Design/methodology/approach The study uses interpretive structural modelling approach to delve into the complex interplay between psychological, technological, financial and regulatory factors, revealing both direct and indirect influences on investment decisions. Findings Drawing on a comprehensive literature review and insights from 20 domain experts, the research identifies 19 critical factors influencing green cryptocurrency adoption. These factors are organised into a five-tier hierarchical structure, uncovering their causal relationships and classifying them according to their influence levels. Research limitations/implications The present research is constrained by expert-driven analysis, which may affect the objectivity of the findings. Further quantitative validation of the identified factor interrelationships is warranted. The exclusion of demographic and psychographic influences restricts user segmentation insights, while the static view limits generalisability. Practical implications From a practical perspective, the study provides actionable recommendations for businesses, policymakers and environmental advocates by helping to promote sustainable practices, address key barriers and foster a more resilient green cryptocurrency ecosystem. Social implications The study emphasises that advancing green cryptocurrency adoption can drive a collective shift towards sustainable digital finance, fostering eco-conscious investment behaviour, enhancing financial literacy on environmental responsibility and reinforcing the social norm of aligning technological innovation with sustainability values. Originality/value The findings contribute to the broader theoretical discourse on sustainable digital finance by integrating micro- and macro-level influences within a unified framework. Furthermore, the study introduces a novel conceptual model grounded in the means-end chain theory, offering deeper insights into the dynamics of green cryptocurrency investments.

title: Green finance investments in the era of geopolitical uncertainty: moderation and mediation effects
summary: Purpose This study investigates the effects of environmental knowledge, corporate social responsibility (CSR) scepticism and media intervention on willingness to invest in green finance products (WGF) through the mediation of greenwashing p
content: Purpose This study investigates the effects of environmental knowledge, corporate social responsibility (CSR) scepticism and media intervention on willingness to invest in green finance products (WGF) through the mediation of greenwashing perception. Furthermore, the study examines the moderating role of geopolitical uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 372 Islamic Bank customers via a questionnaire and evaluated using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings The study reported a positive relationship between environmental knowledge, CSR scepticism, media intervention and greenwashing perception. In addition, the results show a negative relationship between greenwashing perception and WGF. Furthermore, geopolitical uncertainty negatively moderated the relationship between greenwashing perception and WGF. Practical implications This study proposes pragmatic approaches for Islamic banks to enhance the adoption of green finance and effectively tackle greenwashing amid geopolitical uncertainty. By implementing focused sustainability education, individuals are empowered to make well-informed investment decisions and better understand greenwashing. Engaging in collaborative media initiatives and employing transparent marketing strategies can bolster trust among environmentally conscious customers, increasing their involvement in sustainable banking. Originality/value The article makes novel contributions by examining Islamic banking customers' opinions on green finance and their reactions to greenwashing amid geopolitical uncertainties. By incorporating variables such as environmental knowledge, CSR scepticism and media intervention, the study will provide insights into the behaviours related to sustainable finance in the context of Islamic banking. This study introduces innovative theoretical viewpoints to sustainable finance research through multi-theoretical frameworks.

title: Credible CSR and credit ratings: how state-led CSR enhances firm creditworthiness
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine whether participation in China’s large-scale, government-led corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative, the Targeted Poverty Alleviation (TPA) campaign, affects firm credit ratings. It also explores
content: Purpose This study aims to examine whether participation in China’s large-scale, government-led corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative, the Targeted Poverty Alleviation (TPA) campaign, affects firm credit ratings. It also explores the mechanisms through which such participation enhances creditworthiness. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel dataset of 1,177 listed firms in China from 2009 to 2021, the authors use coarsened exact matching (CEM) to construct a matched sample and then apply a staggered difference-in-differences (DiD) framework to estimate the causal effect of TPA participation on credit ratings. We also conduct mediation analyses to identify the roles of environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance and media reputation, and perform robustness checks including PSM-DiD, placebo tests and heterogeneity analyses. Findings Firms participating in the TPA campaign receive higher credit ratings. The effect is stronger among non-state-owned enterprises, firms in underdeveloped regions, and those rated by international joint-venture agencies. Greater investment intensity in the program further amplifies the benefit. Improved ESG performance and media favorability partially mediate the relationship, suggesting that rating agencies value the reputational and sustainability signals conveyed through government-aligned CSR. Research limitations/implications This study addresses the “credibility gap” in CSR by shifting focus from voluntary actions to high-visibility, state-monitored mandates like China’s TPA campaign. It demonstrates that in emerging markets, institutional legitimacy and political alignment are vital nonfinancial determinants of credit risk. Future research should examine how macroeconomic risks moderate this relationship and explore other firm-level outcomes. In addition, testing the generalizability of these findings in different institutional contexts is essential. Finally, as data improves, explicitly comparing the differential impacts of voluntary versus government-led CSR on firm performance will provide deeper insights into corporate sustainability and creditworthiness. Practical implications The findings provide insights for firms seeking to improve creditworthiness and for policymakers aiming to align CSR incentives with development goals in emerging economies. For corporate managers, the findings demonstrate that aligning CSR strategies with national development goals can yield tangible financial benefits, specifically improved credit ratings and reduced borrowing costs. For investors and credit rating agencies, the study highlights that government-endorsed CSR provides a more reliable and externally validated benchmark for assessing a firm’s long-term stability and operational risk than opaque, self-reported composite CSR scores. title: Searching for nearby supermassive black hole binaries with GRAVITY
summary: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with <16.5% for <9.2%. We compared these results with predictions from the Horizon-AG
content: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with <16.5% for <9.2%. We compared these results with predictions from the Horizon-AGN simulation, finding comparable binary fractions. We also noted that the expected fraction strongly depends on the assumed distribution of individual SMBH accretion rates within binaries, which is currently unresolved in cosmological models. Our results demonstrate the potential of infrared interferometry to identify parsec-scale binary AGN candidates. Moreover, the results motivate future + observations to expand the sample and follow up on known candidates in order to help confirm their nature and distinguish genuine binaries from asymmetric nuclear structures. on Very Large Telescope Interferometer. We investigated parsec-scale asymmetric emission by modeling the squared visibilities and closure phases with a single circular Gaussian component plus a background point source for the central AGN, and we searched for additional compact companions through grid-based binary models. The robustness of the search was validated using injection--recovery simulations and point-spread-function diagnostics. We identified several features in the initial significance maps, but only one candidate of the 20, NGC 3783, showed a persistent compact asymmetry, corresponding to an observed incidence of 5%. title: Structural Inertia of Energy Inefficiency: Can Islamic Finance Close the Energy Efficiency Gap in Java's Provincial Economies, Indonesia?
summary: Java faces a dilemma between the demand for high economic growth and a chronic dependence on fossil energy. This study examines the persistence of the energy efficiency gap across five provinces in Java from 2017 to 2023 and tests the role
content: Java faces a dilemma between the demand for high economic growth and a chronic dependence on fossil energy. This study examines the persistence of the energy efficiency gap across five provinces in Java from 2017 to 2023 and tests the role of Islamic finance in narrowing it. Energy efficiency is measured using the Slack-Based Measure Data Envelopment Analysis (SBM-DEA) with undesirable output. The persistence of the gap and its determinants are estimated using the one-step System Generalised Method of Moments (GMM). The results reveal pronounced performance polarisation among provinces. DKI Jakarta, East Java, and West Java reach the best-practice level, whereas Banten and Central Java remain locked at low efficiency levels. The energy efficiency gap is highly persistent, with a coefficient of 0.748. The adjustment rate is only 25.2% per year, with a half-life of approximately 2.4 years. Green sukuk significantly narrows the gap, while economic growth has no significant effect. These findings indicate that Islamic finance can help close the energy-efficiency gap but operates within strong structural inertia. Energy policy should therefore be differentiated across provinces, and green sukuk allocation should target provinces with the widest gaps.

title: Viscophoretic Nanoparticle Transport
summary: Viscosity is a fundamental property of liquids and sets the diffusivity of suspended particles. When viscosity varies in space, diffusivity does too; under isothermal conditions, stochastic thermodynamics predicts a particle drift term v =
content: Viscosity is a fundamental property of liquids and sets the diffusivity of suspended particles. When viscosity varies in space, diffusivity does too; under isothermal conditions, stochastic thermodynamics predicts a particle drift term v = ∂xD(x) arising from position-dependent viscosity. Here, we impose steep, stable viscosity gradients in a microfluidic channel and directly image nanoparticle motion at the single-particle level using high-resolution microscopy. We find viscous-gradient-driven drift velocities that exceed Stokes–Einstein-based estimates, and we quantify this discrepancy through simultaneous measurements of local diffusivity and drift extracted from the same trajectories. We then illustrate how such controlled gradients enable passive focusing in a phoretic trap that combines viscophoresis with diffusiophoresis. Our measurements provide a quantitative single-particle characterization of viscous-gradient-driven transport that is of importance in any system and any application exhibiting viscosity gradients, from membrane separation processes to inter- and intracellular biomolecular transport.

title: Ozone decrease observed in the upper atmosphere following the 11 May 2024 Mother's Day and the 8 June solar storms
summary: On 11 May 2024, a succession of coronal mass ejections merged and struck the Earth, inducing large-scale perturbations in the magnetosphere. During this event, satellite observations revealed that an extreme geomagnetic storm occurred along
content: On 11 May 2024, a succession of coronal mass ejections merged and struck the Earth, inducing large-scale perturbations in the magnetosphere. During this event, satellite observations revealed that an extreme geomagnetic storm occurred alongside a moderate solar proton event (SPE). Simultaneously, atmospheric ozone and temperature were measured by the AURA/MLS instrument. In this work, we present the first observations of the effect of the extreme storm of May and the subsequent SPE of 8 June on ozone concentration and temperature throughout the atmosphere. The observations of the MLS instrument show that the event of May led to stronger depletion of O 3 in the mesosphere and lower thermosphere (MLT) than in June and that noticeable depletion mainly occurred in the Southern Hemisphere. This difference is explained by the type and intensity of energetic particle precipitation (EPP) that occurred during the two events, with both protons and electrons in May and only protons in June. In May, mesospheric ozone depletion peaked at 60 % at 80 km and reached 30 % at 75 km, lasting for 5 d. The SPE of June also caused a decrease of mesospheric ozone that lasted for 2 d down to 70 km. Below 60 km, no significant changes in ozone volume mixing ratio (vmr) were observed after either event.

title: Generalized Wright Analysis: Stochastics and Applications
summary: In this paper, we investigate the stochastic counterpart of the generalized Wright analysis introduced in Beghin et al.~ in Integral Equations and Operator Theory, 97, 2025. We define a new class of non-Gaussian and non-Markovian processes,
content: In this paper, we investigate the stochastic counterpart of the generalized Wright analysis introduced in Beghin et al.~ in Integral Equations and Operator Theory, 97, 2025. We define a new class of non-Gaussian and non-Markovian processes, called the generalized Fox-H process, which extends well-known processes such as fractional Brownian motion and generalized grey Brownian motion. We study their joint probability density and covariance, showing the stationarity of their increments. In addition, this process has H{\"o}lder continuous paths and is represented as a time-change of fractional Brownian motion. We characterize the generalized Fox-$H$ noise as an element in the distribution space $(\mathcal{S})^{-1}_{\mu_\Psi}$. We conclude by establishing the existence of local times and discussing their anomalous diffusion properties. MSC Classification: 33E12 , 60E05 , 60G18 , 60G20 , 60G22

title: Combining geodetic data and summer MODIS albedo anomalies for annual glacier mass balance estimation
summary: Annual glacier mass balance time series are essential for understanding the impacts of climate change on glacierized regions. Satellite-based observations enable consistent and regionally comprehensive monitoring of glacier mass balance. Wh
content: Annual glacier mass balance time series are essential for understanding the impacts of climate change on glacierized regions. Satellite-based observations enable consistent and regionally comprehensive monitoring of glacier mass balance. While geodetic methods yield robust estimates over decadal timescales, their application at annual resolution is limited by measurement uncertainty. In this study, we propose an approach that combines 20 years geodetic mass balance data with glacier-wide average summer albedo anomalies from MODIS to produce reliable annual glacier mass balance estimates for land-terminating glaciers. We generated time series from 2000 to 2019 for 2748 glaciers across three regions: the European Alps, Scandinavia, and Svalbard. Validation against 1108 available in-situ mass balance measurements yielded root mean square errors (RMSE) of 0.44, 0.72, and 0.39 m w.e. and coefficients of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.62, 0.54, and 0.44 for the European Alps, Scandinavia, and Svalbard, respectively. These results demonstrate the method's effectiveness and its potential for application in other glacierized regions.

title: Sub-shot-noise emission statistics of a CW-excited single photon source
summary: Shot noise sets a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of classical optical measurements, with coherent emitters achieving the lowest possible shot-noise level. Emission from sub-Poissonian light provides a pathway to surpass this limit, an
content: Shot noise sets a fundamental limit on the sensitivity of classical optical measurements, with coherent emitters achieving the lowest possible shot-noise level. Emission from sub-Poissonian light provides a pathway to surpass this limit, and single-photon sources provide a natural platform for generating such light. However, it is commonly assumed that off-resonance continuously excited solid-state single-photon sources exhibit Poissonian statistics over large exposure periods, owing to their strong coupling to the host lattice. In this work, a theoretical model of a continuously driven two-level single-photon source is developed, treating both excitation and radiative decay as stochastic processes. The analysis demonstrates that photon emission can display sub-Poissonian statistics when excitation and decay rates are comparable, showing that continuous excitation does not inherently preclude nonclassical emission. The model is further extended to include finite detection efficiency and detector dead time, illustrating how these practical non-idealities can affect the experimental observation of sub-Poissonian statistics.

title: Metal-dependent thermodynamics of histidine-mediated protein immobilization revealed by quantum chemical calculations
summary: Quantum chemistry and experiment show that His-mediated enzyme immobilization is governed by first-shell metal–imidazole thermodynamics, coordination number and Fe 3+ hydrolysis, reproducing the observed order Ni 2+ > Zn 2+ > Co 2+ > Fe 3+
content: Quantum chemistry and experiment show that His-mediated enzyme immobilization is governed by first-shell metal–imidazole thermodynamics, coordination number and Fe 3+ hydrolysis, reproducing the observed order Ni 2+ > Zn 2+ > Co 2+ > Fe 3+ .

title: Mitigating numerical stiffness in least-squares formulations of elliptic PDEs for physics-informed neural networks
summary: Residual-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) combine interior PDE and boundary residuals using mean squared errors (MSE). For elliptic boundary value problems, these formulations can show numerical stiffness causing slow training
content: Residual-based physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) combine interior PDE and boundary residuals using mean squared errors (MSE). For elliptic boundary value problems, these formulations can show numerical stiffness causing slow training. We study a residual formulation that combines an H 0 − 1 interior residual with an H 1 / 2 boundary residual for nonzero Dirichlet boundary data. For finite-dimensional test spaces in H 1 ( Ω ) , we introduce two finite-dimensional approximations, the subspace-induced negative-order Sobolev seminorm (SINOS) and its dual counterpart (D-SINOS), and quantify their stiffness through a stiffness ratio defined with respect to the H 1 -norm. We establish continuity and coercivity estimates for both formulations and show that, for polynomial spaces of degree n , the stiffness ratios of SINOS and D-SINOS grow at most as O ( n 2 ) and O ( 1 ) , respectively. Numerical experiments recover rates of n 2.00 and n 0.05 , compared with n 6.95 and n 5.68 for MSE and L 2 -based residual losses. PINN experiments for the Poisson equation, a stationary convection–diffusion–reaction problem, and the stationary incompressible Navier–Stokes equations show that SINOS achieves consistently strong convergence and accuracy, while D-SINOS improves over MSE but does not attain the performance of SINOS. These results demonstrate that negative-order Sobole

title: Suppressing cavity frequency noise using a Kerr nonlinearity
summary: Resonance-frequency fluctuations can limit the sensitivity and stability of superconducting microwave cavities used for qubit readout, optomechanical displacement sensing, and magnetic flux detection. Here, we demonstrate the suppression of
content: Resonance-frequency fluctuations can limit the sensitivity and stability of superconducting microwave cavities used for qubit readout, optomechanical displacement sensing, and magnetic flux detection. Here, we demonstrate the suppression of resonance-frequency fluctuations by locking a noisy nonlinear superconducting microwave cavity to a strong pump tone. The Kerr nonlinearity of this system, whereby the resonance frequency depends on the intracavity field amplitude, gives rise to an intrinsic feedback mechanism that enables passive stabilization without active external feedback. Using two-tone spectroscopy, we experimentally characterize the intrinsic nonlinear feedback mechanism and investigate its temporal stability through Allan deviation analysis. The frequency fluctuations of the locked cavity mode are reduced by nearly two orders of magnitude, reaching the 1/f noise floor, without continuous frequency tracking or active control. Kerr locking provides a general approach for self-stabilizing nonlinear microwave resonators by suppressing low-frequency cavity noise while preserving sensitivity to signals outside the locking bandwidth. This approach may benefit a broad range of systems, including superconducting quantum interference device-based resonators, optomechanical devices, and parametric amplifiers.

title: Effective neutrino mass and apparent phantom crossing
summary: Recent cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses have reached, and in some analyses fallen below, the minimum value implied by the normal mass ordering, suggesting a possible tension with neutrino-oscillation measurements. We i
content: Recent cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses have reached, and in some analyses fallen below, the minimum value implied by the normal mass ordering, suggesting a possible tension with neutrino-oscillation measurements. We investigate whether this discrepancy can be alleviated in a mass-varying-neutrino (MaVaN) cosmology in which a canonical pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone boson (pNGB) drives late-time cosmic acceleration and controls the masses of massive neutrinos through an exponential coupling. Using current cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and type Ia supernova data, we reconstruct the neutrino-mass evolution and show that the cosmologically inferred effective neutrino mass can fall below the present-day normal-ordering floor while remaining consistent with oscillation constraints. The same interaction produces a distinctive late-time signature, with 96% of the posterior expansion histories exhibiting a crossing of the apparent phantom divide, wapp = −1, at zcross = 0.90+0−0.2813 within 68% C.L. The underlying scalar field nevertheless remains canonical, with wϕ ≥−1. Our results therefore show that neutrino mass variation can simultaneously alleviate the apparent neutrino-mass tension and generate the phantom-crossing behavior favored by current cosmological data, without introducing a phantom field or violating the null energy condition.

title: The Digitalization–Fraud Paradox: Asymmetric Effects of Strategic Digital Orientation
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping organizational governance, yet its ethical implications for corporate misconduct remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how strategic digital orientation (SDO), defined as a firm’s strategi
content: Digital transformation is reshaping organizational governance, yet its ethical implications for corporate misconduct remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how strategic digital orientation (SDO), defined as a firm’s strategic commitment to developing and integrating digital capabilities, is associated with corporate fraud. Using 34,320 firm-year observations of Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2022, we construct a multidimensional measure of SDO through textual analysis of Management Discussion and Analysis disclosures and measure corporate fraud using complementary regulatory databases. The results provide robust evidence of an asymmetric relationship between SDO and corporate fraud. Firms exhibiting relatively low to intermediate levels of SDO are associated with higher observed fraud risk, whereas the positive association weakens at higher levels of SDO. Moderation analyses show that internal control quality and innovation capability weaken the positive association between SDO and fraud, potentially by reducing governance misalignment associated with digital transformation. Mediation analyses reveal multiple competing governance mechanisms—audit quality, information asymmetry, technology intensity—with indirect effects that are statistically significant but economically modest. These findings are consistent with an asymmetric ethical risk framework in which technological opacity, accountability diffusion, and governance lag create ethical vulnerabilities that are partially offset by stronger monitoring and governance capabilities at higher levels of SDO. This research contributes to business ethics research by demonstrating how digital transformation reshapes accountability structures, redistributes moral responsibility, and generates asymmetric patterns of misconduct risk across firms exhibiting different levels of SDO.

title: ArchaeoBench: a large-scale archaeological question-answering benchmark for large language models
summary: Despite the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in data-intensive disciplines, archaeology lacks public, large-scale benchmarks, and its spatio-temporally fragmented knowledge resists integration into model parameters. Here we in
content: Despite the rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in data-intensive disciplines, archaeology lacks public, large-scale benchmarks, and its spatio-temporally fragmented knowledge resists integration into model parameters. Here we introduce ArchaeoBench, a hierarchically structured benchmark built from 63 official excavation reports across 20 Chinese provinces, comprising over 9.2 million training question-answer pairs and 1,698 evaluation questions spanning multiple cognitive levels. Fine-tuning seven open-source LLMs on this benchmark yields substantial gains, approaching commercial baselines on several question types, whereas chain-of-thought prompting brings only marginal improvements on fact- and text-grounded questions, suggesting that archaeological question answering is constrained primarily by access to reliable domain knowledge rather than reasoning depth. Motivated by this finding, we propose a knowledge-graph-based retrieval-augmented generation framework that injects curated structured evidence to enhance spatio-temporal and cultural-linkage reasoning. ArchaeoBench converts excavation reports into reusable, machine-readable knowledge infrastructure for the discipline.

title: Dimensions of Brand Activism as Predictors of Customer Purchase Intention: A Study of Multinational Brands in Nigeria
summary: The research evaluated the effect of brand activism on customer purchase intention toward multinational companies’ products in South-West Nigeria. The research adopted a cross-sectional survey research design. The study's population was lim
content: The research evaluated the effect of brand activism on customer purchase intention toward multinational companies’ products in South-West Nigeria. The research adopted a cross-sectional survey research design. The study's population was limited to customers of multinational companies in South-West Nigeria. The sample size of 384 participants was selected for the study. It was determined using the Cochran formula. The study used the judgmental sampling technique. The data for this study were generated from the primary source through the use of a structured questionnaire. The study used internal consistency reliability. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical techniques in order to arrive at a conclusion. The findings revealed that value-driven communications have a positive and significant effect on customer purchase intention (β = 0.139, p < 0.05), indicating that ethical and value-based messaging can influence consumers, though with a relatively modest impact. Brand authenticity emerged as the strongest predictor of customer purchase intention (β = 0.721, p < 0.05), underscoring the critical role of perceived sincerity, consistency, and credibility in shaping consumer trust and emotional attachment. In contrast, woke-washing was found to have a negative and significant effect on customer purchase intention (β = −0.080, p < 0.05), suggesting that consumers penalize brands perceived to engage in superficial or insincere activism. The study concludes that while value-driven communications are important, authentic and consistent brand activism is far more influential in driving purchase intentions, whereas woke-washing undermines trust and weakens brand–consumer relationships. It therefore recommends that multinational companies align activism messages with tangible actions, prioritize authenticity, and ensure transparency and long-term commitment to social causes to enhance customer purchase intention.

title: ESG Information Credibility and Retail Investors’ Allocation Intention: The Roles of Sustainability Awareness and Greenwashing Perception
source: Journal of Economics Entrepreneurship Management Business and Accounting
summary: Purpose – This study examines the relationship between ESG information credibility and retail investors’ ESG investment allocation intention, considering sustainability awareness and greenwashing perception as potential mediators.Design/met
content: Purpose – This study examines the relationship between ESG information credibility and retail investors’ ESG investment allocation intention, considering sustainability awareness and greenwashing perception as potential mediators.Design/methodology/approach – A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among Indonesian retail investors from January to April 2026. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4, including direct, indirect, serial mediation, and predictive analyses using PLSpredict.Finding/Results – ESG information credibility is positively associated with investment allocation intention, sustainability awareness, and greenwashing perception. Sustainability awareness positively relates to greenwashing perception but not significantly to allocation intention. Unexpectedly, greenwashing perception positively relates to allocation intention. Mediation through sustainability awareness is insignificant, whereas mediation through greenwashing perception and serial mediation are statistically significant. However, these indirect associations do not confirm the hypothesized mechanisms because key relationships differ from their predicted directions.Originality/Value – This study highlights the complex relationships among ESG credibility, sustainability awareness, greenwashing perception, and investment intentions. It challenges conventional assumptions about greenwashing as an investment deterrent and emphasizes the distinction between statistical mediation and theoretical confirmation, providing directions for further research on investor behavior and ESG information exposure. intentions.

title: Digital Trade Transitions: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Economic Networks and Innovation Ecosystems
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF INNOVATIONS & RESEARCH ANALYSIS
summary: Digital trade has emerged as an innovative economic strategy that transcends traditional and cross-border electronic commerce. Research Objectives: This research performs an extensive bibliometric examination to review and synthesize availa
content: Digital trade has emerged as an innovative economic strategy that transcends traditional and cross-border electronic commerce. Research Objectives: This research performs an extensive bibliometric examination to review and synthesize available research at the convergence of digital commerce, international economic networks, and innovation systems. Methodology: Employing the Scopus database, the study investigates a collection of 877 academic publications from 2010-2026 adhering to PRISMA guidelines. To extract the data, four crucial phrases “International Business”, “Global Trade”, “Economic Integration” and “Innovation” are utilised. Through performance analysis and scientific mapping methodologies, using VOSviewer software, the researcher examined prominent cited authors, disciplines, top universities, significant journals, citation analysis, bibliographic network of leading nations and keyword clusters over time. Key Findings: The results indicate a notable increase in scholarly production 158 in 2025 regarding digital trade, propelled by technological upheaval in this domain. Top Scopus subject areas include ‘Business, Management and Accounting’ having 383 documents, ‘Social Sciences, 267’, ‘Economics, Econometrics and Finance’, 261 and so on. Co-citation of most cited authors include Porter M.E., Goto M., Teece D.J. among top most productive and quoted writers with highest link strength. United States lead with 105 documents, China 86, India 66 followed by other 107 nations. Most frequent keywords are ‘International Trade’ with 361 occurrences, ‘Innovation’, 166, ‘Sustainable Development’ 126, ‘Global Market’, 72 and so on. The research reveals a significant transformation from company-focused evaluations of digital trade adoption to knowledge dissemination and sustainable economic integration, unveiling a vibrant and swiftly evolving domain. Implications: The bibliometric identification of AI, blockchain, and platform-based business models as dominant clusters offers a clear directive for MNEs. The findings have serious implications for policymakers, business strategies, and innovators. Further studies need to be done to look at the impact of digital trade shift on specific industries such as green energy technology, FinTech, and Industry 5.0.

title: Gendered Experiences of Crop Loss in Rice Farming, India
summary: This study examines the gendered impacts of rice crop loss in Odisha, India, drawing on evidence from 409 farming households across eight rice-producing districts. Using household surveys, focus group discussions, and key informant intervie
content: This study examines the gendered impacts of rice crop loss in Odisha, India, drawing on evidence from 409 farming households across eight rice-producing districts. Using household surveys, focus group discussions, and key informant interviews, the research explores how crop loss affects livelihoods, food security, health, education, migration, and household wellbeing. The study identifies significant gender disparities in exposure to crop loss impacts and access to recovery resources, with women disproportionately affected by increased unpaid labour, food insecurity, financial stress, and limited access to insurance, compensation, and advisory services. The findings highlight the need for gender-responsive policies and interventions to strengthen resilience, improve equitable access to support systems, and promote inclusive recovery among rice-farming households.

title: Financing Green Residential Retrofits: An Ex Ante Cost–Benefit Analysis of Energy Affordability in Thessaloniki
summary: This study appraises external-wall insulation for lower-income apartment households in Thessaloniki under financing assumptions drawn from Greece’s Exoikonomo 2025 programme. It adapts the C40 Healthy and Efficient Retrofitted Buildings (HE
content: This study appraises external-wall insulation for lower-income apartment households in Thessaloniki under financing assumptions drawn from Greece’s Exoikonomo 2025 programme. It adapts the C40 Healthy and Efficient Retrofitted Buildings (HERB) model using regional household profiles, census floor areas and Greek multifamily archetypes. Under the engineering benchmark, discounted retail bill savings do not cover installation costs for either insulation package. The lower-cost package can exceed break-even in the partial economic appraisal when avoided direct carbon emissions are valued at European Investment Bank shadow prices, depending on rebound and the costs included. Grants improve household financial returns, but the higher-cost package has negative mean household returns at the lower ordinary grant rate. At a binding grant ceiling, the lower-cost package reaches more dwellings and delivers greater aggregate bill savings. Targeting the higher-cost package by affordability-gap relief yields a slightly larger reduction in the gap. The estimates describe conditional programme outcomes rather than observed energy-poverty reduction.

title: Global Labor Market and Artificial Intelligence (AI) WILL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) CAUSE JOB CUTS?
source: Innovative Research in the Modern World
summary: This article investigates whether the rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models will lead to widespread job cuts across the global economy. Drawing on contemporary labor economics and international instituti
content: This article investigates whether the rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) and large language models will lead to widespread job cuts across the global economy. Drawing on contemporary labor economics and international institutional forecasts, it distinguishes between task-level automation and full occupational displacement, analyzing vulnerable routine and clerical professions alongside emerging AI-augmented roles. The paper further examines skills transformation in language and knowledge industries, cross-country disparities between advanced and emerging economies, and risks of wage polarization, demonstrating that proactive reskilling, inclusive governance, and human-AI collaboration are essential to prevent structural unemployment.

title: Financing Broader Sustainable Transition: Green Finance Policies and Cross-Regional Green Innovation Spillovers Along Supply Chains
summary: In the pursuit of sustainable development, whether green finance policies can transcend geographical boundaries and reshape resource allocation to generate cross-regional green innovation spillovers along supply chains deserves in-depth inv
content: In the pursuit of sustainable development, whether green finance policies can transcend geographical boundaries and reshape resource allocation to generate cross-regional green innovation spillovers along supply chains deserves in-depth investigation. This study conducts an empirical analysis using a difference-in-differences (DID) approach. The results show that: (1) the establishment of green finance pilot zones in the regions where upstream supply chain firms are located significantly promotes green innovation among downstream firms outside the pilot zones, confirming the existence of a cross-regional spillover effect of green finance policies. (2) The establishment of green finance pilot zones significantly alleviates financing constraints for firms within the pilot zones. Supported by a "push-pull" theoretical framework, credit transmission among supply chain firms provides a channel for capital flows, enabling the incentive effects generated by green finance policies to spill over to downstream firms outside the pilot zones. (3) Further analysis reveals that the cross-regional green innovation spillover effect driven by positive corporate credit transmission is influenced by multiple factors at the firm, supply chain, and environmental levels. These findings not only provide theoretical insights into corporate green transformation but also offer empirical support for leveraging green finance policies to achieve broader sustainable development goals (SDGs).

title: A Formal Model of Wealth–Power Feedback with Eight Classes: Thresholds of Elite Capture, Class Mobility and Policy Counter-Levers, with an Illustrative Calibration for Urban Punjab
summary: This paper develops a dynamic political-economy model in which wealth and political power reinforce one another across an ordered structure of eight economic classes. Each class converts population, wealth and organisational capacity into p
content: This paper develops a dynamic political-economy model in which wealth and political power reinforce one another across an ordered structure of eight economic classes.
